jobs.title: Director, Internal Controls
jobs.description:
About Xanadu:

Xanadu’s mission is to build quantum computers that are useful and available to people everywhere.

At Xanadu, we are learners, innovators, researchers, collaborators and problem solvers. We are creating something that has never been built before. What we are doing is extremely hard, the classic moon shot. Few people in their life will be able to be a part of something like this, where if we are successful, the technologies we develop will solve some of the world’s most challenging problems, and literally change the world. And that is something to be excited about!

Your role and responsibilities:

The Director, Internal Controls and projects is responsible for supporting management in the design, implementation, execution, and continuous improvement of the Company's processes and internal control programs, including the Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) compliance program. This role will partner with finance, operations, information technology, Internal Audit, External Audit, IT and business process owners to strengthen the control environment, support regulatory compliance, and drive process improvement initiatives.

The Director will lead internal controls activities on management’s behalf, assist with management's evaluation of internal controls over financial reporting (ICFR), deliver training to control owners and stakeholders, and participate in other finance projects as required such as financial and system transformations.

You will:
Internal Controls and SOX Compliance:

Support management in the implementation, maintenance, and enhancement of the Company's internal control and SOX compliance programs.
Coordinate related planning activities, risk assessments, process reviews, and control rationalization in collaboration with internal audit.
Assist management in evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal controls including for SOX compliance.
Partner with process owners to improve processes and related control documentation, and prepare and maintain control documentation.
Coordinate management testing activities and monitor the timely execution of key controls.
Track control deficiencies, remediation plans, and management action items to ensure timely resolution.
Support management's quarterly and annual control certification processes.
Evaluate control implications arising from changes in business processes, organizational structures, systems, and regulatory requirements.
Promote continuous improvement of internal controls through the identification and implementation of best practices, process improvements, and automation opportunities.

Audit Collaboration:

Collaborate closely with Internal Audit and External Audit to support SOX compliance, control assessments, and audit activities.
Coordinate with Internal Audit and External Audit on testing plans, documentation requirements, walkthroughs, and evidence requests.
Facilitate management responses to audit observations and assist in the development and execution of remediation plans.
Foster alignment among management, Internal Audit, and External Audit regarding key risks, control design, testing approaches, and remediation activities.
Support efforts to maximize audit efficiencies and reliance opportunities through high-quality documentation and control execution.

Training and Business Partnership:

Develop and deliver training programs related to SOX compliance, internal controls, governance, and risk management.
Provide guidance and support to control owners and business stakeholders regarding internal control responsibilities and expectations.
Promote a strong culture of accountability, compliance, and risk awareness throughout the organization.
Act as a trusted advisor to management on internal control, governance, and compliance matters.

Systems Implementations and Special Projects:

Participate in various finance projects including system implementation and upgrades, digital transformation initiatives, and other technology-enabled projects.
Support the design and implementation of controls within new business processes.
Assess risks and control requirements associated with system implementations and significant business changes.
Collaborate with project teams to ensure appropriate governance, security, and control considerations are incorporated into project plans.
Lead or participate in special projects, including process improvement initiatives, and other strategic initiatives.
Support management in evaluating the internal control impact of business transformation programs.

Reporting and Stakeholder Management:

Build and maintain strong working relationships across finance, IT, operations, Internal Audit, External Audit, and executive leadership teams.
Communicate internal control and SOX program progress, risks, key findings, and remediation activities to relevant stakeholders including internal and external audit.

Basic qualifications and experience:

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, Information Systems, or a related discipline.
8+ years of progressive experience in SOX compliance, internal controls, internal audit, risk management, external audit, or public accounting.
Strong understanding of NI 52-109, SOX 302 and SOX 404 requirements, COSO framework, and internal control best practices.
Experience supporting public company compliance and financial reporting environments.
Experience working with Internal Audit, External Audit, senior management, and Audit Committees.
Experience with business process redesign, and systems and digital transformation projects.
Deep knowledge of internal controls, SOX compliance, governance, and risk management.
Strong project management and organizational capabilities.
Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills.
Exceptional verbal and written communication skills.
Ability to influence and collaborate effectively across all levels of the organization.
Strong business process, financial reporting, and systems knowledge.
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic and fast-paced environment.
High degree of professionalism, integrity, and attention to detail.

Preferred qualifications and experience:

jobs.title: Executive Vice President of Project Management
jobs.description:
Executive Vice President of Project Management

Detailed Job Description

Job Overview

The Executive Vice President (EVP) of Project Management is responsible for providing comprehensive leadership and oversight of the company’s project management framework, project portfolio, and the execution of major projects. The EVP defines enterprise-level project management strategy, ensuring that all projects are implemented successfully in alignment with established strategic goals, budgetary plans, timelines, and quality standards. This role holds full accountability for project planning, execution, resource allocation, budget control, risk management, team leadership, and performance monitoring, with the objective of driving the standardization, formalization, and efficiency of the company’s project management system.

The EVP of Project Management is tasked with translating the company’s strategic objectives into actionable project plans, overseeing cross-departmental and cross-business-unit collaboration, and ensuring that major initiatives are delivered on time, within budget, and to the required quality standards. Working closely with the CEO, COO, CFO, heads of business units, and senior project management teams, the EVP provides strategic project management support for major investments, business transformation initiatives, and long-term development strategies, while continuously enhancing the organization’s overall project delivery capabilities.

Key Responsibilities

I. Project Management Strategy and Executive Leadership

Develop and implement an enterprise-wide project management strategy, ensuring that project management objectives are aligned with the company’s corporate strategy, operational plans, and long-term business goals. Provide comprehensive leadership to the project management department and relevant management teams, establishing unified standards, workflows, and execution mechanisms. Determine the direction, management priorities, and resource allocation plans for key projects based on the company’s business development needs. Monitor the execution of the project management strategy and provide regular reports to the CEO and senior leadership team regarding overall project progress, critical issues, and the outcomes of strategic implementation.

II. Project Portfolio Management and Prioritization

Assume full responsibility for the management and oversight of the company’s project portfolio. Evaluate the strategic value, commercial viability, resource requirements, and expected returns of individual projects to ensure that investments remain aligned with the company’s overall business objectives. Establish mechanisms for project initiation, approval, prioritization, and periodic review, while optimizing the allocation of resources and the sequence of execution across various projects. Oversee interdependencies, resource conflicts, and schedule coordination among multiple projects, adjusting the portfolio management plan as necessary. Collaborate with finance and business units to ensure that key projects receive the appropriate funding, personnel, and technical support. III. Project Planning and Execution Oversight

Lead the overall planning and execution management of major projects, ensuring that project scope, objectives, timelines, budgets, deliverables, and the division of responsibilities are clearly defined. Oversee project managers and their teams to ensure work progresses according to approved project plans, while conducting regular reviews of project milestones, task completion, and the quality of deliverables. For complex, cross-departmental, or high-priority projects, participate directly in key decision-making and execution oversight, addressing major issues that arise during implementation in a timely manner. Ensure that every phase of the project—from initiation, planning, and execution to monitoring and final delivery—complies with the company’s management requirements.

IV. Budget Management and Resource Allocation

Manage budget planning, cost oversight, and resource allocation at the project management level, collaborating with the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and the finance department to establish project budgets, funding requirements, and cost-control plans. Monitor variances between actual expenditures and approved budgets, analyze the causes of any cost overruns, and develop appropriate corrective measures. Coordinate human resources, technical equipment, external vendors, and other necessary resources to ensure project teams possess the capabilities and conditions required to complete their tasks. Promote resource sharing and cross-project optimization to enhance resource utilization, reduce execution costs, and ensure that project investments yield the expected business value.

V. Project Performance and Schedule Management

Establish a unified corporate project performance management system and define key performance indicators (KPIs)—such as project completion rates, milestone achievement rates, budget and schedule variances, delivery quality, and project returns. Organize regular project review meetings to assess execution progress, cost status, and actual outcomes. Ensure that project managers submit timely progress reports, risk assessments, and performance analyses, enabling management to maintain an accurate understanding of project status. For projects experiencing delays, budget overruns, or quality issues, coordinate with relevant teams to develop recovery plans and improvement strategies, ensuring that projects are brought back on track.

VI. Cross-Departmental Coordination and Stakeholder Management

Foster effective collaboration between project management teams and various business functions—including operations, finance, engineering, technology, procurement, sales, marketing, and human resources—to ensure alignment on project objectives, resource allocation, and delivery requirements. Resolve conflicts regarding responsibilities, communication barriers, resource contention, or execution challenges that may arise in cross-departmental projects. Responsible for high-level communication with clients, suppliers, partners, and other key stakeholders to ensure that project requirements are accurately understood and critical matters are addressed in a timely manner. In the event of major project disputes or issues impacting overall delivery, organize relevant management personnel to develop and implement solutions.

VII. Project Risk, Quality, and Compliance Management

Establish an enterprise-level project risk management framework, overseeing project teams as they identify, assess, and manage potential risks related to schedules, budgets, technology, contracts, supply chains, and operations. Develop mechanisms for project risk reporting, issue escalation, and contingency response to ensure that significant risks are escalated promptly and resolved effectively. Collaborate with legal, compliance, quality management, and internal audit departments to ensure project execution adheres to applicable laws, regulations, contractual requirements, industry standards, and internal company policies. Supervise project quality control and delivery acceptance processes, drive the implementation of corrective and preventive actions, and mitigate the risks of project failure or operational losses.

VIII. Project Management System Optimization and Team Development

Continuously refine the company’s project management policies, standardized processes, and management tools, while advancing the development and operational capabilities of the Project Management Office (PMO). Introduce appropriate project management methodologies, digital management platforms, and data analytics technologies to enhance efficiency in project planning, schedule tracking, resource management, and performance reporting. Lead the development of project management talent, establishing performance evaluation, professional training, and succession planning mechanisms for project managers. Consolidate experience and best practices from major projects to foster knowledge sharing and continuous process improvement, thereby elevating the company’s professional standards in project management and its overall delivery capacity.

Work Experience

Typically requires 18+ years of experience in project management, project execution, engineering management, or corporate operations.

At least 8 years of senior management experience, with a proven track record of leading large-scale project management departments, Project Management Offices (PMOs), or multiple project teams.

Extensive experience in managing large project portfolios, complex cross-departmental projects, and enterprise-level strategic initiatives.

Practical management experience in areas such as strategic project planning, budget management, resource allocation, risk control, and project performance monitoring.

Preference will be given to candidates who have held positions such as Vice President of Project Management, Director of Project Management, Head of a Project Management Office (PMO), Head of Project Execution, or other senior leadership roles. Experienced in communicating and collaborating with CEOs, COOs, CFOs, and members of the Board of Directors.

Preference will be given to candidates with experience in managing cross-regional or international projects, or large-scale corporate transformation initiatives.

jobs.description:
Executive Director,
Victoria Brain Injury Society (VBIS)
Location:
Victoria, BC
Employment Type:
Full-time (37.5 hours/week)

$85,000–$95,000 annually, commensurate with experience

December 2026 

﻿The full job description is available at: https://vbis.ca/careers/

________________________________________________________________________________________

At the Victoria Brain Injury Society (VBIS), we believe in compassion, accountability, and community. We’re a small but mighty team that supports people with acquired brain injuries through personalized programming, advocacy, education, and connection. Our values guide us in everything we do—from peer support groups and clinical services to public awareness campaigns and housing advocacy. 
We’re looking for our next Executive Director: someone who brings a deep sense of empathy and leadership to the role, and who’s ready to build on the strong foundation we’ve established. If you have experience in community health, disability advocacy, or systems change work, we’d love to hear from you. 

As Executive Director, you’ll be the strategic and operational leader of VBIS. You’ll work closely with our Board of Directors and senior staff to advance our mission, ensure effective program delivery, and build partnerships that create lasting impact across the region. You don’t have to be an expert fundraiser, but you should be comfortable representing VBIS publicly and helping to steward donor relationships. A strong understanding of nonprofit operations, team leadership, and advocacy is essential. 

What You’ll Be Doing 

• Guiding organizational strategy and leading day-to-day operations 
• Supporting and empowering staff, volunteers, and clients 
• Overseeing finances, HR, and compliance 
• Collaborating with partners and funders 
• Representing VBIS in public, media, and government spaces 
• Championing awareness of brain injury and its impact in our community 

What We’re Looking For 

• 3–5 years of leadership experience in nonprofit, public health, or community-based roles 
• A background in social work, rehabilitation, public policy, or similar field 
• Values-driven leadership with a strong equity and inclusion lens 
• Excellent communication and systems-thinking skills 
• A flexible, responsive approach - you’re comfortable navigating complexity and change 

Why VBIS?

We have two offices, but you’ll work out of our downtown Victoria office, close to green spaces, transit, and community amenities. You’ll join a team that genuinely enjoys working together, and a board that is thoughtful and engaged. We work hard, we laugh often, and we care deeply about what we do. 

How to Apply

Please submit your resume and a cover letter outlining why this role resonates with you to both Sharlene and Shannon at sharlenel@vbis.ca and skowalko25@gmail.com. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? Coinbase is building the future of finance for people, institutions and their agents, with one place to trade crypto, equities, derivatives and prediction markets, use stablecoins, and connect AI agents with clear controls. The bar is high and the pace is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency. It's a place to be pushed past your perceived limits and do the best work of your career. If you're ready to build the future of finance with a championship team who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote\-first, but not remote\-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for in\-person working sessions


Coinbase Canada is seeking a Head of Finance, Canada to lead the financial and regulatory reporting function for our Canadian regulated business. Reporting to the Director of Reporting and Technical Policy within the Accounting organization, you will serve as the enterprise Finance authority for Canadian reporting, regulatory capital, and OSC and CIRO submissions.



This strategic leadership role defines the target\-state operating model, sets scalable reporting and control standards, and represents Finance with senior leaders, the Board, the OSC, and CIRO. The role requires direct ownership of both Form 31\-103F1 and CIRO Form 1, from data sourcing through review, submission, and remediation.


#### **What You'll Do**


* Own the strategy, governance, and process architecture for Coinbase Canada's financial and regulatory reporting function.
* Lead audit\-ready preparation of Form 31\-103F1, CIRO Form 1, and applicable OSC and CIRO submissions.
* Set standards for IFRS books, parallel ledgers, reconciliations, capital calculations, and supporting documentation.
* Represent Finance in OSC and CIRO examinations, inquiries, meetings, filings, and remediation matters.
* Advise executives and the Board on financial performance, regulatory capital, liquidity, control health, and emerging risks.
* Partner across Tax, Treasury, Legal, Compliance, Operations, Product, and Technology to align reporting, capital, liquidity, and strategy.
* Build organizational capability through talent development, succession planning, outsourced\-provider governance, and KPI/SLA accountability.
* Drive responsible automation and AI adoption that improves reporting quality, efficiency, control effectiveness, and auditability.

#### **Required Skills and Experience**


* 13\+ years of progressive finance, accounting, or regulatory reporting experience within a Canadian investment dealer, securities dealer, bank, fintech, regulator, or professional services firm.
* Successfully passed the Chief Financial Officer Qualifying Examination and the Partners, Directors and Officers Qualifying Examination, each administered by the Canadian Securities Institute (CSI) and the Canadian Investment Regulatory Organization (CIRO).
* 5\+ years of direct ownership and preparation of both CIRO Form 1 and Form 31\-103F1 for a Canadian regulated entity.
* Direct experience managing the filing lifecycle, including calculations, accounting judgments, review and sign\-off, submission, regulator follow\-up, and remediation.
* Experience in a self\-clearing or introducing broker\-dealer environment, with expertise in dealer capital adequacy, regulatory capital, liquidity, and related controls.
* CPA or equivalent accounting designation required.
* Expert knowledge of IFRS, NI 31\-103, Form 31\-103F1, CIRO capital adequacy, and Canadian securities\-regulatory reporting.
* Demonstrated enterprise\-level leadership, regulator\-facing judgment, executive communication, and Board influence.
* Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business\-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality.

jobs.title: Research Director, Agentic AI Platforms
jobs.description:
Overview

About the Role & Team

IDC is seeking a Research Director to join our established worldwide artificial intelligence, data and automation (AD&A) research domain to focus on agentic AI tools and platforms. The candidate will have to demonstrate deep existing knowledge of both the existing and future capabilities across all types of agentic AI tools and platforms, including those that can build, manage, orchestrate and govern AI agents for use in the enterprise. The candidate will also collaborate with other analysts covering adjacent technologies including other forms of AI and Automation technologies. Research will include understanding market drivers and trends, buying behaviors, and the business value impact of these technologies. The candidate will employ IDC research methodologies to size markets and forecast market growth.

What You’ll Do

Identify key market trends in agentic AI, as well as broader AI technology and market developments.

Developments. Additional Responsibilities Include

Analyze competitive market strategies and conduct market segment and sizing studies.
Contribute to ongoing research to analyze trends in these segments, including the competitive strategy and financial performance of technology providers, and end user demand for those offers.
Provide industry expertise for client-facing engagements and client inquiries.
Partner with sales and drive incremental revenue through subscription and custom solutions for our AD&A group.
Utilize knowledge of key digital transformation drivers as well as key enterprise IT challenges in software development, business automation, integration, and AI (predictive, interpretive, and generative).
Respond to client requests for market/competitive data across these agentic AI tool and platform technology markets.
Collaborate with other analysts, particularly in other AI research areas, in creating research documents and forecasts.
Present to senior management including C-Level executives across the domain as well as interviewing/interacting with a wide range of IT and technology vendor decision-makers and senior level audience.

What You Bring

Bachelor’s degree is required; Master’s degree preferred.
Experience working in a technical and/or business transformation capacity implementing AI projects.
First-hand experience using AI tools is a strong plus.
Strong knowledge of the overall AI technology sector is required, along with the ability to analyze trends and provide actionable guidance to technology providers and buyers. Direct experience in this area is ideal.
Up-to-date knowledge of innovations in AI foundation models, agent technologies and the AI industry more broadly.
Knowledge of AI deployment models and the advantages and disadvantages of each.
Demonstrated ability to analyze survey data and provide clear, concise summaries and recommendations.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to analyze, present, and articulate complex data sets.
Strong interpersonal and organizational skills, with the capacity to work both independently and within a team.
Proven ability to read and evaluate financial reports to analyze key drivers that impact companies’ ability to differentiate and remain competitive.
Ability to travel 25-30% for client meetings, industry events, and customer projects.
This role offers the flexibility to work remotely from an approved U.S. location, or onsite at our corporate office in Boston, MA.

Why This Role Stands Out

At IDC, your work helps shape how the world understands technology and where it goes next. You collaborate with curious, high-caliber colleagues who value rigor, integrity, and shared success. As the premier global provider of trusted technology intelligence, IDC equips business and technology leaders with the evidence they need to make confident decisions. Our insights inform strategy, investment, and innovation across industries and regions.

Recognized by IIAR as Analyst Firm of the Year for five consecutive years, IDC sets the standard for credibility and impact. With more than 1,000 analysts worldwide and a truly global perspective, we combine deep expertise with practical relevance. Here, your ideas matter, your voice is heard, and your contributions provide the insights leaders rely on every day. It is meaningful work, backed by a culture that supports growth, collaboration, and long-term career development with a globally respected brand.

What We Offer

15 vacation days per year (increases with tenure; carryover allowed)
10 paid sick days per year
1 week paid new parenting leave
Flexible work options (remote, part-time, flexible hours)
Health, dental, vision, and paramedical coverage for you and your family
Annual healthcare spending account
Employee Assistance Program for counseling and support
Best Doctors medical second opinions
Life, AD&D, and long-term disability insurance
Retirement savings plan with company match (up to 4% of salary)
$75/month technology allowance for home office or phone expenses
Company-paid cell phone plan

Compensation Transparency

At IDC, we are committed to fair and equitable pay practices. Employees are compensated equitably for their work, aligned with their skills and experience. Salary and incentive structures are determined through a rigorous process that considers experience, education, certifications, role-specific requirements, internal equity, and verified Canada market data from an independent third-party partner. The expected total annual compensation, depending on location and experience, is between 110,200 CAD – 137,700 CAD, inclusive of base salary and variable compensation. If this role relocates to a different country, the salary range will be updated to reflect that country's range, rather than a currency conversion of the original range.

Equal Opportunity Employer

jobs.title: Director, Digital Marketing
jobs.description:
You are as unique as your background, experience and point of view. Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered and challenged to be your best self. You'll work with dynamic colleagues - experts in their fields - who are eager to share their knowledge with you. Your leaders will inspire and help you reach your potential and soar to new heights. Every day, you'll have new and exciting opportunities to make life brighter for our Clients - who are at the heart of everything we do.

At Sun Life, we're driven by our Purpose: helping our Clients achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. Our values shape how we work: caring, authentic, bold, inspiring, and impactful.

When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.

Discover how you can make a difference in the lives of individuals, families and communities around the world.

Job Description:

Reporting to the AVP Marketing, Sun Life Global Investments (SLGI), the Director, Digital Marketing is responsible for leading a team of managers and specialists focused on the development and execution of the strategic direction of all aspects of our digital client experience across both the retail and institutional businesses.

This includes providing leadership to key internal stakeholders on the introduction and evolution of technology applications and initiatives that enable SLGI to maintain market differentiation in the investment industry as well as responsibility for overseeing all digital work for SLGI including developing strategic/integrated digital marketing plans and creating an overall digital strategy encompassing Web, Social Media, SEO/SEM and CRM Strategy and Digital Communications.

In addition, in their capacity as a senior member of the SLGI marketing team, the incumbent will represent SLGI in a variety of cross business unit capacities and effectively collaborate with other team leaders in other business units on key marketing strategies and initiatives.

What will you do:

Proactively lead the development and execution of the overall digital marketing strategy and annual/multi-year plans for SLGI to support business objectives
Oversee the execution of all digital projects and priorities within SLGI and ensure focus on projects that have the most impact to the business and long-term growth
Build and manage critical relationships with IT, operations and the back office to ensure marketing operational excellence and successful implementation/resolution of business requirements/challenges
Provide technical expertise and manage the relationships when working with vendors on our various digital properties
Work closely with key areas of the business (Enterprise Services, Corporate Marcom, Individual, etc.) and build a collaborative relationship to ensure that SLGI is aligning with and leveraging the best practices of other digital opportunities
Leverage insight and information/feedback received from advisors, sales, investors and key internal partners to help inform the digital strategy and marketing tactics
Actively participate in content planning and development for all SLGI web properties to ensure consistent messaging and the application of best practices
Lead the development of integrated digital marketing strategies for SLGI web properties and digital projects including social media, content marketing, email marketing, etc.
Develop and maintain online sales aids, tools and calculators designed to help our clients evaluate investment opportunities, and confidently select products that help their clients meet their financial goals
Help our distribution team both attract and retain assets and clients, through our digital experiences and journey’s
Measure and report metrics and analytics to demonstrate awareness and consideration by target audience and to help inform and optimize future campaigns and marketing strategies/tactics
Lead, manage and coach a team of high performing digital marketers including championing training programs and development opportunities that further build the expertise of the team

What do you need to succeed:

Creative and technical problem solver with a successful track record of helping a company grow their business through website development, client/user experience optimization, content
strategy, analytics and social media marketing
University degree with 8 years + experience as a digital marketing professional in the investment industry
Previous experience within the financial services industry, specifically the investment area.
Specific understanding and knowledge of investment funds, wealth insurance products as well as both the retail advisor channel and the institutional market (consultants, plan sponsors)
Strong understanding of digital technologies and communications, including digital marketing, web analytics and measurement and SEO/SEM
Self-confident and strong ability to work effectively and independently within tight deadlines, adapt to changing deadlines and ability to prioritize multiple deliverables within a cross functional team environment with a variety of reporting levels and varying skills/competencies
Flexible individual with creative problem-solving & strong analytical skills
Ability to confidently build relationships and effectively engage with junior colleagues through to senior executives
At least 3 years experience leading and managing a team of senior and junior colleagues
A positive leader who inspires high performance and leads by example
Familiar with best practices in digital strategy, planning and execution
Diplomacy and negotiation skills – Sun Life is a large, complex organization that requires collaboration across teams within the marketing department, across departments within the business unit, and across business units within the parent company

The Base Pay range is for the primary location for which the job is posted. It may vary depending on the work location of the successful candidate or other factors. In addition to Base Pay, eligible Sun Life employees participate in various incentive plans, payment under which is discretionary and subject to individual and company performance. Certain sales focused roles have sales incentive plans based on individual or group sales results.

Diversity and inclusion have always been at the core of our values at Sun Life. A diverse workforce with wide perspectives and creative ideas benefits our Clients, the communities where we operate and all of us as colleagues. We welcome applications from qualified individuals from all backgrounds.

Persons with disabilities who need accommodation in the application process, or those needing job postings in an alternative format, may e-mail a request to thebrightside@sunlife.com.

We are proud to be a hybrid organization that offers our employees the choice and flexibility to work from both the office and virtually based on the needs of the business, our Clients and you.

We may use artificial intelligence to support candidate sourcing, screening, interview scheduling.

We thank all applicants for showing an interest in this position. Only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

BMO Capital Markets is a leading, full\-service financial services provider. We offer corporate and investment banking, treasury management, as well as research and advisory services to clients around the world. \#bmocapitalmarkets


We are looking to bring on a VP into our Global Finance Risk team, to be based out of the Toronto office.


This person will be responsible for managing risk across prime, counterparty credit, and business and developing the risk framework, which includes margin risk methodologies. The person will also collaborate across teams, including trading, credit, market risk, counterparty, and the front office to work cohesively and collaboratively to ensure all risk coverage. * Balances the Bank's risk appetite with the client needs in making recommendations/proposals
* Manages firm’s risk and takes action to reduce exposure in developing and delivering client strategies
* Take measured risks while protecting the bank by applying our Risk Management Framework in the execution of your role, in line with our Risk Culture and within our approved Risk Appetite, making sound and risk informed decisions that align to business strategy, protect assets, and adhere to applicable policy documents (Frameworks, Policies, Standards, Procedures and Supporting documents), laws and regulations.

* Global platform includes Prime Brokerage and Swap offerings across US, Canada and the UK.
* Client portfolios comprise of a broad range of asset classes and investment strategies, including: Equities (incl. Common Stock, ETFs, ADRs, MLPs, REITs), Corporates (IG \& HY), Convertible Bonds, Options \& Indexes
Hedge fund and real money counterparties  
* 

  

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Daily management of client portfolio exposures and counterparty\-related risk issues
* Support of operational risk and platform trade processing associated with client counterparty risks

* High level of engagement with Sales, Trading and other members of the business as it relates to client management and ongoing business initiatives
* Thoughtful and complete analysis and communication of risk concerns both internally within the business and among control function partners
* Identifying and escalating emerging risks – credit, market, operational or legal – to senior management and Global Finance management. Continuously assessing and adapting to new products and market stress events and proactively proposing risk solutions
* Facilitating new client trades and managing existing portfolio exposures to ensure that risks, primarily market\-driven counterparty risk, but also documentation, legal and reputational risks are well\-controlled
* Work closely with Counterparty Credit, Credit Risk Management and other key stakeholders on onboarding of new clients, implementation of margin methodology, as well as maintaining ongoing dialogue and promptly escalating issues with existing clients
* Develop strategic risk solutions, analytics and platform enhancements to help advance BMO’s competitive advantage
* Maintain a positive culture within the team by cultivating a productive and collaborative work environment

Ensure full compliance with risk procedures and other Global Finance or Global Markets policies  

* 

  

**Qualifications:**

* B.S. – Quantitative Finance, Financial Engineering, Finance / Statistics or related discipline.
* Between 5 \- 7 years of experience in Prime Finance risk or general experience with Delta One and Global Prime Finance trading
* Experience with VaR and stress testing.
* Strong data querying and quantitative analysis skills are required, knowledge of Python, SQL and AI Development tools.
* Comfort with using data querying skill set to design risk dashboards, graphic user interfaces linked to internal databases and enhanced risk reporting.
* Exposure to and strong understanding of equities products, such as Delta One, Swaps, and derivatives across all asset classes. Experience with Synthetic Prime is a plus.
* Strong understanding of market risk and counterparty risk processes and metrics.
* Knowledge of relevant Prime financing platforms, asset types, market structure and client investment strategies.

jobs.title: Director, Content & Curriculum - Elementary (K-6)
jobs.description:
At Nelson, we've been supporting teaching and learning across Canada for more than a century. As Canada's leading K–12 educational publisher and digital learning provider, we work alongside educators to develop trusted, curriculum\-aligned resources, digital learning solutions, and assessment tools that meet the evolving needs of classrooms.


From our longstanding publishing heritage to innovative platforms like Edwin, we bring together quality content, technology, and practical support to help educators create equitable, inclusive, and engaging learning experiences for every student.


Behind this work is a team of passionate, collaborative, and forward\-thinking people who care about making a difference in Canadian education. We're always looking for curious, creative individuals who bring fresh perspectives, embrace new ideas, and want to make a meaningful impact.


If that sounds like you, we'd love to hear from you! Apply to join our team today.


Let's Create Possible, one learner at a time.

 **About the Role**


You lead Nelson’s English elementary (K–6\) portfolio in Edwin, our digital learning platform. Reporting to the VP, Content \& Curriculum, you set the grade\-band roadmap and priorities, allocate people and budget across course teams, and build the team of Product Managers and Program Specialists who deliver.


Each Product Manager owns their course end to end, and each Program Specialist owns instructional design and quality. Your job is to make sure the portfolio adds up: the right courses, in the right order, with the right people, meeting the standards the VP sets across Content \& Curriculum. You are the coach, the escalation point and the tie\-breaker. While the team is being built, you also personally lead priority products as needed.


You work closely with the VP, the Secondary and French Directors, the Assessment Lead, and the Commercial, Engineering, Classroom Success and Content Services teams. As the face of the elementary portfolio, you build strong relationships with customers and educator thought leaders.


This posting represents an existing vacancy.

 **Requirements** **Key Accountabilities**


Portfolio strategy and roadmap (20%)

* Own the K–6 English portfolio roadmap and priorities, within the VP’s cross\-portfolio strategy. Build it with Product Managers and Commercial, grounded in market research, curriculum change, usage data and competitive analysis.
* Approve course business cases and development budgets prepared by Product Managers, and present portfolio recommendations to the VP and senior leadership.
* Decide priorities for refreshing existing outdated content across the portfolio, with Commercial. Product Managers and Program Specialists carry out the refreshes.
* Make sure every course in the portfolio has assessment built in from the start, and set priorities for retrofitting assessment into existing courses.
* Own the portfolio’s efficacy evidence, with the Assessment Lead: studies, outcome data and case studies that Commercial, boards and ministries can rely on.
* Lead acquisition, licensing and partnership work for the grade band, with the VP accountable.
* Set one unified vision for your team, aligned with Nelson and Edwin principles.


Portfolio delivery and resourcing (25%)

* Allocate people, budget and shared resources, including the freelance and contract bench, across teams to deliver the highest\-value priorities, and shift them quickly when market or corporate priorities change.
* Hold Product Managers accountable for delivering their courses to the agreed scope, schedule, budget and quality. Review status and risks with them regularly.
* Decide escalations that change a launch date or budget or affect more than one team, and break ties between a Product Manager and Program Specialist on instructional quality.
* Report portfolio status, risks and financials to the VP and senior leadership.
* Roll out our standard content development workflow and templates across the grade band, in partnership with Content Services.
* Work with the Secondary and French Directors and the Assessment Lead to align roadmaps, share resources and best practice, and deliver a coherent K–12 experience across grades and languages.


Team leadership (30%)

* Hire, coach and develop Product Managers and Program Specialists, and through the Program Specialists the Content Producers. Set clear goals and hold the team accountable for results.
* While the team is being built, personally lead priority products as needed.
* Build Product Managers’ ability to lead teams through influence, and Program Specialists’ ability to lead their producers.
* Build a high\-performing, collaborative and inclusive team culture.
* Lead on assessment strategy and instructional design for the grade band, drawing on current research in teaching and learning.
* Continuously improve how the team plans and builds, including better tools for building content and iterative development.


Market presence and expertise (25%)

* Represent Nelson as a trusted voice in elementary education with Ministry of Education contacts, Directors of Education, principals, subject consultants, teacher associations and assessment experts, including at conferences and events.
* Stay close to teachers, administrators, boards and ministries to spot customer needs, curriculum shifts, and instructional and assessment practice.
* Make sure the portfolio builds strong foundations in literacy and numeracy, and readies students for the intermediate grades, with learning that is concrete, developmentally appropriate and connected to their lives.
* Bring early\-years assessment expertise, including the role of screeners, to the Assessment Lead’s K–12 strategy and to K–6 course teams.
* Build the network of educator thought leaders and subject\-matter experts that Product Managers draw on.
* Identify platform features that would drive teacher and student usage across the portfolio, and bring them to the platform p

jobs.title: Director, Engineering
jobs.description:
CircleCI is the platform that powers continuous integration and delivery for the world's best engineering teams — helping them build, test, and ship software quickly, safely, and confidently, including the new generation of AI\-assisted development. Do you want to lead the teams that set that example for customers?



The Director, Engineering is a strategic leader who directs operational units across the engineering organization. You will own the technical strategy and multi\-quarter roadmap for your engineering organization (typically 4\-5 teams including engineering managers), collaborating on organizational engineering strategy and partnering across functions to deliver measurable business impact.



This is a broad, high\-impact seat — you'll partner closely with the VP of Engineering and peer leaders across the org to shape structure, roadmap, and operating standards for a group that's growing and evolving fast.



This role balances technical depth with strategic thinking, people development with execution, and short\-term delivery with long\-term sustainability. You will work with Product, Go\-to\-Market teams, customers, and executive leadership to drive CircleCI's mission forward.


**Strategic Planning**
----------------------


### **Your Strategic Responsibilities:**


* Lead and grow a multi\-team engineering organization, with ownership of its structure, headcount, and provide input for product strategy
* Partner with the VP of Engineering and cross\-functional stakeholders on technical strategy and multi\-quarter roadmap for your organization, ensuring alignment with company objectives.
* Raise the bar on engineering practices, operating standards, and delivery quality across the group
* Build and develop a strong management layer — hiring, coaching, and growing engineering managers and leads
* Define operating metrics and team goals; craft strategies to scale infrastructure and meet business objectives
* Cultivate a culture of excellence that closes the gap between business/roadmap commitments and what gets delivered
* Lead distributed engineering teams to deliver highly available, highly secure experiences at scale
* Bring real AI competency to the role — not just personal use of AI tools, but building the systems and practices that let your teams get genuine leverage from AI
* Represent your organization's roadmap, tradeoffs, and constraints clearly to Product and other cross\-functional partners

### **Your Decision\-Making Authority:**



You have full authority to:


* Hire, promote, and performance\-manage all engineers and managers within your organization
* Make final decisions on administrative and operational matters within your domain
* Approve technical architecture decisions that impact your organization alongside highly experienced senior engineers
* Prioritize and sequence engineering work; allocate budget for team tools, training, and resources
* Represent engineering in cross\-functional forums and make commitments on behalf of your organization

**What We're Looking For**
--------------------------



This is a key role with significant impact on CircleCI's engineering organization and business outcomes.


* 5\+ years in engineering leadership, including direct management of managers
* Ability to translate business objectives into technical strategy and enable teams to deliver reliable, resilient, and secure features at scale
* A proven track record of building strong, aligned teams across varied technical surfaces
* Thorough understanding of developer tools market, practices, competition, and trends
* Genuine fluency with AI\-assisted engineering workflows and what it takes to operationalize them at a team level
* Expert manager with ability to mentor and develop individual contributors and managers; build high\-performing teams through recruiting, coaching, and creating growth opportunities
* Drive frameworks for people development, performance, inclusion, and belonging across your organization
* Data\-driven problem solver who handles risk and uncertainty; coordinates work spanning departments with alignment to organizational goals
* Strong verbal and written communication skills; ability to influence teams, peers, leaders, executives, and customers
* Comfortable working with globally distributed teams across multiple time zones using synchronous and asynchronous communication, and making hard structural and personnel calls, not just process improvements
  


We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.


**About CircleCI**



CircleCI is the world's largest continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) platform, and the hub where code moves from idea to delivery. As one of the most\-used DevOps tools \- processing more than 3 million jobs a day \- CircleCI has unique access to data on how the most effective engineering teams work, and the tools to help software companies successfully leverage the power of AI into their commercial applications. Companies like Hinge, HuggingFace, and Samsung use us to improve engineering team productivity, release better products, and get to market faster.

  

Founded in 2011 and headquartered in downtown San Francisco with a global, remote workforce, CircleCI is venture\-backed by Base10, Greenspring Associates, Eleven Prime, IVP, Sapphire Ventures, Top Tier Capital Partners, Baseline Ventures, Threshold  

Ventures, Scale Venture Partners, Owl Rock Capital, Next Equity Partners, Heavybit, and Harrison Metal Capital.

jobs.title: Director, Digital Marketing & eCommerce
jobs.description:
**The Company**

  

We are a leading global company committed to bettering lives through cannabis.

  

At Canopy Growth, quality, consistency and trust guide everything we grow, make and deliver. From cultivation to consumer, we take a long\-term view, with the ambition to help set the standard for the industry.

  

We're looking for principled, driven people who want to do meaningful work and help shape what comes next. We invest in our people, support their growth and value the different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives they bring.

  

We believe the best of this industry is still ahead \- and we intend to lead it there. Come join us.

  

  

  

**The Opportunity**

  

Reporting to the Head, Medical Product \& Marketing, the Director, Digital Marketing \& eCommerce Marketing is responsible for end\-to\-end ownership of Canopy’s medical digital ecosystem, including eCommerce platforms, clinic channels, and digital acquisition.

  

  

This role leads the strategy, execution, and performance of all digital growth initiatives to acquire, convert, and retain patients, while driving scalable, data\-driven growth across the Spectrum and clinic businesses. This also includes execxuting on best in class Ecommerce practices across Spectrum \& Abba Medix Ecommerce shops.

  

  

The Director will lead a team (including Customer Growth / eCommerce) and partner cross\-functionally to deliver a best\-in\-class digital experience in a regulated environment.

  

  

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

  

* Own the end\-to\-end digital growth strategy across eCommerce, clinics, and acquisition channels.
* Develop and execute integrated digital strategies to drive acquisition, conversion, retention, and lifetime value.
* Translate business objectives into digital roadmap, go\-to\-market plans, and execution priorities.
* Own performance of eCommerce platforms and clinic digital channels, including traffic, conversion, revenue, and retention.
* Oversee website experience, UX, content, and digital journeys across patient, clinic and HCP touchpoints.
* Ensure timely execution of digital initiatives, product launches, and platform enhancements.
* Own and scale digital acquisition programs (paid media, SEO, partnerships) to drive patient growth.
* Oversee customer lifecycle strategy, including onboarding, engagement, retention, and reactivation.
* Establish a data\-driven performance culture, including KPIs, dashboards, and reporting frameworks.
* Measure and optimize ROI across all digital channels and programs.
* Partner with Sales, Medical, IT, Product, and external agencies to align on priorities and execution.
* Ensure digital platforms reflect real\-time supply, regulatory, and operational requirements
* Ensure all digital marketing activities comply with regulatory, legal, and industry standards.
* Oversee governance of medical content, digital assets, and digital patient\-facing materials.
* Lead and develop a high\-performing digital team, including eCommerce and customer growth functions
* Provide coaching, direction, and performance management to drive results and team development
* Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.
* Other duties as assigned.
  

  

**Experience \& Skills**
------------------------

  

* 7–10\+ years in digital marketing, eCommerce, or growth roles, with leadership responsibility
* Proven track record of owning and scaling digital businesses or DTC/eCommerce channels
* Deep expertise in digital acquisition, lifecycle marketing, and website optimization
* Strong analytical capability with experience managing performance metrics and ROI
* Experience in regulated industries (healthcare, pharma, cannabis) preferred
* Demonstrated ability to lead cross\-functional teams and complex initiatives

jobs.title: Head of Talent
jobs.description:
**About Qorsa**


Qorsa is a Canadian post\-quantum cryptography and cybersecurity company building CasQade — a crypto\-agile security platform protecting sovereign government, defence, financial, and critical\-infrastructure networks against current and emerging cryptographic threats. We are headquartered in Waterloo, Ontario, with a European subsidiary in The Hague, Netherlands. Our work spans post\-quantum cryptography, explainable AI, AI\-driven threat intelligence, cryptographic agility, hardware security, and distributed systems, with active engagements across Canadian defence, NATO, and allied partner organizations.  

  

**The Role**


You'll own how Qorsa hires. You'll build the processes the whole company will use to hire the people they need, and make Qorsa a place strong technical people want to join. We hire across cryptography, PKI, silicon design, DevOps, customer delivery, security certification, and AI development, in Waterloo and at our subsidiary in The Hague. Many of our customers are in defence and government, so many roles need people who can obtain Government of Canada or NATO security clearance.

**Responsibilities**

* Build the structures, pipelines and strategies that will support Qorsa's talent acquisition efforts
* Work with hiring managers to identify their recruitment needs and create tailored plans for hiring the talent they need.
* Run every candidate search end to end with the hiring manager: job description, posting, sourcing, screening, interview scheduling, references, offer and close
* Source directly for scarce profiles, including cryptographers, PKI specialists, silicon engineers and cleared customer\-facing engineers
* Build a structured interview process for each role with its hiring manager: question banks, scorecards, take\-home assessments with follow\-up interviews, and debriefs that reach a decision within days
* Train hiring managers and interviewers to run that process consistently
* Run our applicant tracking system and report pipeline status, time to hire and offer acceptance against the hiring plan
* Check citizenship and clearance eligibility at the start of each process, and work with our company security officer so personnel clearance applications start as soon as an offer is accepted
* Run the intern program, including university co\-op relationships and an intake every term
* Build our employer brand: careers page, postings, and a presence at the universities, conferences and communities where cryptography, security and hardware people gather
* Give leadership market data for planning: compensation benchmarks, candidate supply, and lead times for hard\-to\-fill and cleared roles
* Recommend agencies, contractors or additional recruiting staff when hiring volume calls for them
* Hand each new hire to their manager with paperwork, clearance applications and appropriate onboarding in place

**\#\# Qualifications**

* 6\+ years in technical recruiting or talent acquisition, including time as the first or lead recruiter at a growing technology company
* A record of filling senior engineering or research roles through direct sourcing
* Experience building a hiring process: structured interviews, scorecards, ATS setup and pipeline reporting
* Experience hiring for defence, government or other regulated employers, including roles that require security clearance
* Enough technical fluency to discuss a candidate's work with them and with our engineers, and to sell deep\-tech roles to people holding several offers
* Working knowledge of Ontario employment standards and of offers that combine salary and stock options
* Clear, persuasive writing for postings and outreach
* Eligible for Government of Canada security clearance

**\#\# Nice to have**

* Experience with the PSPC Contract Security Program or the Controlled Goods Program
* University and co\-op recruiting, particularly with the University of Waterloo
* A network in the cryptography, cybersecurity or semiconductor communities
* Experience growing a recruiting team

**Compensation**


We compensate exceptionally well — a strong base salary plus meaningful stock options in a rapidly growing company.

**Benefits**

* Dental care
* Extended health care
* Vision care
* On\-site parking

**Work Location:** In person in Waterloo, Ontario, if you're local. Remote work will be considered if occasional onsite periods in Waterloo are acceptable.

jobs.description:
Reports to: Chief Executive Officer | Location: Toronto, Ontario [hybrid] | Full-time, permanent

About Us

Appficiency is a global technology and professional services firm that solves complex business challenges through the intelligent application of enterprise software, automation, and AI. We're a proud Oracle NetSuite Alliance Partner; Salesforce Crest Partner; Microsoft Gold Certified Partner, and much more: our evolution has taken us well beyond a single platform, making us a multi-technology advisory and implementation partner across ERP, CRM, cloud platforms, and AI-driven solutions. What sets us apart is a "technical-first" approach, teams who understand both business logic and deep system architecture paired with a genuine belief that our people are our greatest strength, and that's who we invest in first.

The Opportunity

As our first CFO, you will be the senior-most financial leader of the organization — owning financial strategy, acquisition strategy and the overall fiscal health of the business as we navigate our next phase of growth as a services-led technology firm, scaling through both organic growth and acquisitions. You'll work closely with the CEO and the executive team to drive sustainable revenue growth and profitability, improve financial performance and build a finance function that gives leadership timely, reliable information for decisions. Our day-to-day finance operations are sound; this role adds the senior leadership layer above them. It suits a seasoned finance executive who can do three things well: build the function (processes, reporting and budgeting), develop the team and lead acquisitions from screening through integration.

What You'll Do

Develop and execute financial strategies that align with the company's growth objectives, including a growth plan that separates organic growth from acquisition-driven growth and tracks both against actual results
Oversee all financial operations, including FP&A, accounting, treasury, budgeting, and risk management across our Toronto and Philippines teams
Lead the strategic financial planning process, including long-term projections and capital allocation decisions made with the CEO
Act as the CEO's senior deputy on financial and operational matters, able to represent the company and lead decisions in the CEO's absence
Build and deliver a monthly management reporting package (results, budget-to-actual analysis, key performance indicators and commentary) on a fixed calendar, so leadership receives the information it needs without having to request it
Lead the annual budget with department heads so each leader understands and owns their budget, and connect it to the unit economics of the business
Oversee company cash flow, investments, and capital structure optimization
Manage financial reporting and ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, including tax, payroll and statutory filings in each country where we operate
Set revenue recognition, billing and project accounting policies for fixed-fee, time-and-materials and software resale contracts
Lead mergers and acquisitions from end to end: set acquisition criteria; screen opportunities sourced by our advisors; lead valuation, financial due diligence and deal structuring; and plan post-acquisition integration
Manage relationships with banks, lenders, auditors and external advisors; lead any future financing
Build and lead the finance and accounting team; coach and develop current team members into larger roles and add capability (such as FP&A) as the business grows
Analyze key professional services metrics (utilization, realization, project margin, backlog, collections) and software metrics (recurring revenue, renewals, churn) to drive profitability and growth decisions
Partner with the CEO and executive team on strategic decision-making and operational efficiency
Collaborate with the CTO and other executives to align financial and technology strategy
Partner with the leader of our internal transformation program so finance processes and reporting support company-wide operating improvements
Identify financial risks, maintain effective internal controls and develop mitigation strategies to protect company assets
Prepare the business for potential future milestones (e.g. significant acquisitions, major growth investments or a future transaction)

What You'll Bring

Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, or related field; Master's degree or MBA preferred
12-15+ years of progressive finance experience, including significant time as a CFO or senior finance executive in a professional services or technology firm, ideally an IT consulting or systems integration business
CPA designation (or equivalent international accounting designation) required; CFA an asset
Executive experience with professional services and software business models and associated revenue recognition
Proven experience scaling a mid-market business toward $100M in revenue, including growth through acquisitions
A builder's track record: designing finance processes, management reporting and budgeting from the ground up, ideally as a company's first CFO
Strong track record driving financial strategy in high-growth, founder-led or owner-managed environments
Deep understanding of professional services economics (utilization, rates, project margin) and software metrics and their strategic implications
Excellent leadership skills, with experience building and scaling finance teams and mentoring early-career finance leaders
Outstanding communication skills, comfortable engaging the CEO, department heads, lenders and acquisition counterparties; able to explain financial results clearly to non-financial leaders
International finance experience (multi-country teams and foreign currency) is a plus
Hands-on experience with Oracle NetSuite (or a comparable cloud ERP) is a strong asset

What Will Set You Apart

A track record of successfully leading acquisitions of professional services or technology businesses, from screening through integration
Deep fluency in services and software unit economics and how they inform strategic decision-making
A reputation for clear, credible financial communication with owners, lenders and leadership teams
Experience preparing a company for significant milestones (acquisition, major scale-up)
A collaborative, tech-forward mindset — comfortable partnering with product and technology leaders
Experience coaching a high-potential finance manager into a senior leadership role
Comfort stepping into a finance framework established by an interim CFO or external advisors and making it your own

What Success Looks Like

The company's financial strategy directly enables and accelerates growth objectives
The CEO and leadership team view you as a trusted, credible voice on financial health and strategy
Leadership receives a monthly management reporting package on a fixed calendar, without having to request it
Department heads own their budgets and use them to run their areas
Acquisition opportunities are screened against clear criteria and the transactions you lead are executed and integrated smoothly
The finance team operates as a strategic partner to the business, not just a reporting function
The Finance team has grown into larger roles, with clear accountabilities and succession in place
Financial risk is proactively managed, and the company is well-positioned for its next growth milestone

jobs.description:
You’ve built dashboards. Tracked milestones. Chased vendors. Flagged risks. But your reports hit a ceiling. You weren’t the one making the calls.

2 Hour Learning is building an AI-powered education model designed to help students achieve a full day of academic progress in just two hours. Making that model work at scale requires dozens of initiatives, technology partners, contracts, and investment decisions to move in sync. Your job is to make the execution layer trustworthy enough for executives to act on it.

You will own the operating outputs behind those decisions: portfolio dashboards that expose slippage before it becomes a surprise, vendor scorecards tied to real contractual commitments, competitive bid packages that make trade-offs clear, and contract controls that prevent unsupported spend. AI will be part of your daily workflow, helping you standardize updates, detect anomalies, compare bids, analyze vendor performance, and validate invoices.

This is not a PMO role built around meetings, process compliance, or polished status decks. It is for an operator who wants their work to have consequences. When a vendor underperforms, your evidence should make that obvious. When spend drifts from the contract, your controls should catch it. When executives need to make a $5M decision, your outputs should give them the confidence to make it fast. If that sounds like the level of ownership you have been looking for, apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Own portfolio-level dashboards across 10+ concurrent initiatives, using AI to standardize updates, detect slippage, expose blockers, and maintain a trusted executive view of delivery, budget, and risk
Run recurring vendor performance reviews and maintain rubric-based scorecards that combine delivery, quality, cost, contractual commitments, and qualitative performance signals
Lead competitive technology-vendor procurement, including structured bid packages, normalized comparisons, scoring rubrics, SOW development, and evidence-backed recommendations
Govern contracts and invoices by tracking fee caps, milestones, acceptance criteria, and amendments, then validating invoices against signed terms before spend is approved
Use AI daily to analyze portfolio data, detect anomalies, surface underperformance, draft decision-ready outputs, and reduce manual PMO administration

What You Won’t Be Doing

Producing status reports that executives read but never use to make decisions
Running a meeting-heavy PMO where coordination matters more than measurable execution
Treating vendor management as relationship maintenance while missed commitments go unchallenged
Passing contracts, SOWs, invoices, or procurement decisions to someone else because they look too commercial or technical
Using AI as an occasional productivity trick instead of a core part of how you operate

VP Portfolio Operations Key Responsibilities

As VP Portfolio Operations, you will produce reliable, AI-powered dashboards, scorecards, procurement packages, and contract controls that give executives the clarity and leverage to hold vendors accountable, control costs, and accelerate delivery across a $50M EdTech portfolio.

Basic Requirements

Personally owned execution across 10+ concurrent initiatives with at least $5M in portfolio budget responsibility, tracking spend and making evidence-backed recommendations on budget allocation, vendor selection, and initiative priorities. Final approval authority and P&L ownership are not required
Managed 5+ external technology vendors at the same time, such as SaaS providers, AI/ML platforms, marketing agencies, or engineering firms
Built and maintained portfolio-level dashboards covering metrics such as delivery health, budget burn versus forecast, milestone completion, and major risks or blockers
Can point to a case where C-suite leaders used your portfolio data to make a go/no-go decision on a vendor renewal, budget reallocation, or initiative deprioritization
Directly led competitive technology procurement, including structured bid evaluation, vendor scoring, negotiation, and recommendations for executive approval
Authored or co-authored SOWs with measurable deliverables, milestone payments, SLAs, acceptance criteria, or other performance-based terms
Negotiated commercial terms such as pricing, penalties, fee caps, or exit clauses and enforced those terms through invoice validation or corrective action
Strong written communication skills, with the ability to turn complex financial and operational data into concise recommendations executives can act on
Able to analyze financial and vendor-performance data quickly enough to recommend optimization, reallocation, or vendor elimination
Able to work US business hours

Nice-to-have Requirements

Experience using AI-enabled dashboards, anomaly detection, predictive alerts, or natural-language analysis in portfolio management
Experience in EdTech, technology, consulting, or another environment managing complex portfolios of external technology partners
Fluency with portfolio and delivery tools such as Linear, Jira, or similar systems

About 2 Hour Learning

Education is broken, but 2 Hour Learning is proving it doesn’t have to be. They’re tearing down the outdated one-size-fits-all model and replacing it with AI-driven personalized learning that helps kids master academics in just two hours a day.

With students consistently ranking in the top 1-2% nationally and the top 20% achieving an astonishing 6.5x growth, they’re proving that smarter learning is possible. At 2 Hour Learning, it’s talent and performance that matter.

They offer a dynamic, on-campus and remote-friendly environment where innovators, educators, and AI specialists can be a part of fixing a broken school system.

2 Hour Learning is reprogramming learning for the AI era.

Here’s How They’re Fixing It.

Vantage Group is a global leader in airport and transportation investment, development, management, and advisor services. Since 1994, Vantage's corporate and network-wide team has managed an award-winning portfolio, building strong partnerships that integrate global expertise and local know-how to solve complex transportation challenges at every network location. Over three decades, Vantage has built a track record of creating customized solutions to transform airports and transportation centers that benefit the passengers, stakeholders, and communities they serve.
