More information: www.cyqm.ca

The Role

The Greater Moncton International Airport Authority (GMIAA) is seeking a strategic and collaborative Director, Finance & Administration to serve as the organization’s senior financial leader and trusted advisor to the President & CEO, Board of Directors, and Audit Committee. This role is responsible for driving financial strategy, business planning, budgeting, risk management, and financial performance while ensuring strong governance and accountability across the organization.

As a key member of the senior leadership team, the Director oversees all finance and administrative functions, including corporate finance, audits, insurance, pension and benefits programs, and corporate governance. The role also provides leadership and direction for the Human Resources function, supporting the development of a high-performing and engaged workforce. Working closely with internal teams, airline partners, vendors, and stakeholders, the successful candidate will help shape the airport’s long-term strategy and contribute to the continued growth and success of one of Atlantic Canada’s most important transportation hubs.

Key Responsibilities

Achievement of Financial Goals

As a member of the senior leadership team, partners with the CEO to translate the airport's strategic vision into long-term plans, annual business objectives, and measurable financial outcomes; leads initiatives that support sustainable growth and long-term financial viability.
Leads the annual business planning, budgeting, and forecasting processes, working collaboratively with all departments to develop financial plans that support organizational priorities.
Provides strategic financial analysis, insights, and recommendations to support operational, commercial, and capital investment decisions across the organization.
Leads the financial evaluation, negotiation, and ongoing performance monitoring of commercial agreements with airlines, concessionaires, tenants, and vendors.
Develops business cases and financial models for new projects, investments, and growth initiatives, ensuring informed decision-making and effective resource allocation.
Oversees capital planning and budgeting, including the development and maintenance of the airport's long-term capital plan.

Management & Performance Reporting

Serves as the primary financial advisor to the Board of Directors and Audit Committee, preparing and presenting financial reports, forecasts, business analyses, and recommendations.
Leads the development and continuous improvement of organizational performance measurement and reporting frameworks, ensuring key metrics effectively support accountability and strategic decision-making.
Ensures all organizational, financial, and regulatory reporting obligations are completed accurately and on time.

Finance & Administration Function

Provides overall leadership and accountability for the Finance & Administration function.
Oversees financial reporting, accounting operations, internal controls, treasury management, payroll oversight, tax compliance, and cash flow management.
Leads all external financial audits and serves as the primary liaison with auditors, financial institutions, and lending partners.
Manages the organization's insurance portfolio and enterprise risk management program, identifying and mitigating risks to support operational and financial objectives.
Serves as the organization's subject matter expert on airport fees and charges, Airport Improvement Fees (AIF), lease structures, and commercial pricing.
Ensures compliance with the Federal Ground Lease and related reporting, procurement, insurance, and public accountability requirements.

Leadership & Team Development

Leads the Finance & Administration team in a collaborative, high-performance environment, setting clear expectations and supporting employee growth, development, and succession planning.
Provides strategic leadership and oversight for the Human Resources function through the HR Manager, including workforce planning, employee relations, labour relations, and organizational effectiveness.
Oversees the Corporate Board Secretary function, ensuring effective governance processes, accurate board records, and administrative support for the Board of Directors.

Qualifications & Experience

Education

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Commerce, or a related field.
Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation required.
Additional education or professional development in leadership, governance, risk management, or human resources would be considered an asset.

Experience

Minimum of 8 years of progressive leadership experience in finance and accounting, including at least 5 years in a senior management role.
Experience serving as a key member of a senior leadership team, contributing to organizational strategy, business planning, and decision-making.
Demonstrated success leading financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, audits, treasury management, and risk management functions.
Experience presenting financial results, strategic recommendations, and business cases to Boards of Directors, Audit Committees, or similar governance bodies.
Experience evaluating, negotiating, and managing commercial agreements and business relationships with customers, vendors, tenants and airlines.
Experience providing leadership and oversight to human resources functions, including workforce planning and organizational development; direct HR leadership experience and labour relations is considered an asset.
Experience in the airport, aviation, transportation, infrastructure, or other capital-intensive industries would be considered an asset.
Bilingualism in English and French would be considered an asset.

Skills and Capabilities

Strategic and commercially minded leader with strong financial and business acumen.
Strong leadership, coaching, and team-building skills, with a track record of driving performance, accountability, and engagement.
Ability to lead organizational change and influence stakeholders at all levels, including executives, Board members, business partners, and external stakeholders.
Collaborative and approachable leadership style with a hands-on, solution-oriented approach.
Excellent verbal, written, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.
High degree of integrity, professionalism, accountability, and sound judgment.

The expected annual compensation for this position includes a base salary of $130,000 to $155,000, plus eligibility to participate in the Company's annual incentive program. Beyond competitive compensation, we offer career progression opportunities, access to a global team of talented professionals, and boundless opportunities to make your mark within our organization. If you share our sense of adventure, we invite you to join us on the journey.

jobs.description:
At a glance

Location: Montréal, QC. Hybrid, with about half your time on-site.
Employment: Full-time, permanent.
Reporting to: CFO.

About Nomic

Nomic was founded to make biology easier to measure—and to enable scientists to extend lives by making proteomics accessible, scalable, and routine. Our story began at McGill University, where our co-founders and early team developed breakthrough technology that would change the way proteins are measured.

Today, Nomic is powered by our proprietary nELISA® platform—an end-to-end technology that delivers high-throughput, quantitative, and affordable protein data at unprecedented scale. With the launch of Omni 1000, we are making the $50 proteome a reality, breaking down barriers that have limited the field for decades. For the first time, large-scale, quantitative proteomics is accessible to any scientist, supporting everything from drug discovery and translational research to AI-enabled therapeutic development.

Since our launch, we’ve partnered with leaders in pharma, biotech, and academia—including GlaxoSmithKline and the Broad Institute—and have profiled more than 500,000 samples across diverse applications. Our growth is fueled by over $60 million in investment from top-tier backers, including our recent $42 million Series B.

We’re building a team of world-changers—scientists, engineers, and problem-solvers who believe that accessible proteomics can help shape the future of medicine. If you want your work to have real impact, we’d love to meet you.

Learn more in our Series B announcement.

The role

As Director, Supply Chain, you will oversee end-to-end supply chain operations, including procurement, logistics, and inventory management. You will drive the development and execution of strategies to optimize performance, reduce costs, and improve reliability across systems and workflows. This role involves close collaboration with cross-functional teams to align production schedules, streamline material flow, and mitigate supply risks. You will also lead data-driven forecasting, manage supplier relationships, and establish clear metrics to monitor and continuously improve supply chain effectiveness. This role is ideal for someone with a strong track record in a high-growth environment, particularly in life sciences, and experience operating at the intersection of manufacturing and services.

What You’ll Do

Procurement

Own our material and product costs within our standard cost model, analyzing cost structure and inventory variances and leading improvements in cost efficiency.
Design and maintain procurement workflows that are scalable, automated and audit-ready, including for materials used in quality-controlled processes.
Develop sourcing strategies and manage supplier relationships, from negotiation to ongoing performance oversight.
Work with Sales, Manufacturing and Service Lab leaders to forecast material needs, using data-driven models and increasingly automated tools.

Sales and operations planning

Lead materials and supply planning with operational leaders, aligning production plans, raw material supply, inventory and supplier capacity with the sales forecast.
Build and maintain operational and capacity models that support resource planning and budgeting.
Own our ERP as its subject matter expert: data integrity, accuracy and how well it serves the business.

Inventory

Own our inventory systems and processes, with tight integration between the ERP and Nomic’s internally developed LIMS, the central hub for our operational data.
With your peers, set inventory carrying strategies that balance operational performance and financial stewardship.
Oversee receiving: intake, verification and system entry of inbound materials.
Keep physical inventory accurate across all storage sites, including temperature-controlled storage, and own material movement, reconciliation and audit readiness.
Track raw materials, work in progress and finished goods end to end, including lot traceability and shelf life.

Logistics

Build and run outbound logistics for our kit business: order fulfillment, packaging, shipping, temperature-controlled distribution, delivery tracking and returns.

What You’ll Bring

You’re naturally curious, quick to learn and energized by solving problems with people across disciplines. You think end to end, from planning and procurement to inventory and logistics, and you want to design systems that work well and scale from day one. You bring an engineering mindset, you’re comfortable with technology, and you care about making things run smoothly, reliably and transparently. You approach operations practically and iteratively, always looking for the next improvement.

You’ve seen what good looks like in a fast-growing manufacturing organization like ours. You know when to move fast, when to push back and when to step in and fix something yourself. You adapt how you work with others, handle change and ambiguity well, and colleagues trust you to bring structure without rigidity. You’re excited to be one of the first leaders of this function, knowing your work will help scientists better measure and understand biology.

Relevant experience. 7+ years in supply chain, operations or manufacturing roles supporting manufacturing. Life-science tools experience is strongly preferred; we also welcome candidates from other industries with strong technical adaptability.
Leadership and building experience. Experience leading and developing people. Building scalable processes in a high-growth company or having led a supply chain function is a plus.
Procurement and cost expertise. Experience owning strategic sourcing and supplier negotiations, and working with standard costing and variance analysis. Experience developing procurement practices in a quality-controlled environment is a plus.
Planning and inventory experience. Experience connecting sales forecasts to production and materials planning, with ownership of manufacturing inventory control. Experience shipping temperature-controlled goods is a plus.
ERP expertise. Subject matter expertise in an ERP system; NetSuite is highly desirable.
Cross-functional communication. You work effectively with scientific, operational and commercial teams and can turn complex requirements into practical processes.
Education. An advanced degree (for example an MSc) in engineering, the life sciences or a related technical field is a plus.
Location. You can work on-site in Montréal about half the time. Working proficiency in French and English is an asset.

Why join us

Real ownership. You’ll set the direction for Supply Chain and shape the processes, systems and workflows that support Nomic’s growth.
Work that matters. Our platform helps pharma, biotech and academic scientists understand disease and develop new medicines. A reliable supply chain is what keeps it running.

___

Directeur(trice), chaîne d'approvisionnement

Le poste en bref

Lieu de travail — Montréal (Québec). Mode hybride, avec environ la moitié de votre temps sur place.
Type d'emploi — Poste permanent, à temps plein.
Supérieur immédiat — Chef de la direction financière.

À propos de Nomic

Nomic a été fondée pour faciliter la mesure biologique et permettre aux scientifiques de prolonger la vie en rendant la protéomique accessible, évolutive et courante. Notre histoire a commencé à l'Université McGill, où nos cofondateurs et notre équipe initiale ont mis au point une technologie révolutionnaire qui allait changer la façon dont les protéines sont mesurées.

Aujourd'hui, Nomic s'appuie sur notre plateforme exclusive nELISA®, une technologie de bout en bout qui fournit des données protéiques à haut débit, quantitatives et abordables à une échelle sans précédent. Avec le lancement d'Omni 1000, nous faisons du protéome à 50 dollars une réalité, brisant ainsi les barrières qui ont limité ce domaine pendant des décennies. Pour la première fois, la protéomique quantitative à grande échelle est accessible à tous les scientifiques, soutenant tout, de la découverte de médicaments et la recherche translationnelle au développement thérapeutique basé sur l'IA.

Depuis notre lancement, nous avons établi des partenariats avec des leaders du secteur pharmaceutique, des entreprises de biotechnologie et du secteur académique, notamment GlaxoSmithKline et le Broad Institute, et avons profilé plus de 500 000 échantillons dans diverses applications. Notre croissance est alimentée par plus de 60 millions de dollars d'investissements provenant de bailleurs de fonds de premier plan, dont notre récente série B de 42 millions de dollars.

Nous constituons une équipe de personnes qui changent le monde : des scientifiques, des ingénieurs et des solutionneurs qui croient que la protéomique accessible peut contribuer à façonner l'avenir de la médecine. Si vous souhaitez que votre travail ait un impact réel, nous serions ravis de vous rencontrer.

Pour en savoir plus, consultez notre annonce de financement de série B
.

Votre rôle

À titre de directeur ou directrice de la chaîne d'approvisionnement, vous superviserez l'ensemble des activités de la chaîne d'approvisionnement, y compris l'approvisionnement, la logistique et la gestion des stocks. Vous piloterez l'élaboration et la mise en œuvre de stratégies visant à optimiser le rendement, à réduire les coûts et à améliorer la fiabilité des systèmes et des processus. Ce rôle exige une collaboration étroite avec des équipes interfonctionnelles afin d'harmoniser les calendriers de production, de simplifier la circulation des matériaux et d'atténuer les risques d'approvisionnement. Vous dirigerez également les prévisions fondées sur les données, gérerez les relations avec les fournisseurs et établirez des indicateurs clairs pour suivre et améliorer continuellement l'efficacité de la chaîne d'approvisionnement. Ce poste conviendra parfaitement à une personne qui a fait ses preuves dans un environnement en forte croissance, en particulier dans les sciences de la vie, et qui a l'habitude d'évoluer à la jonction de la fabrication et des services.

Vos responsabilités

Approvisionnement

Assumer la responsabilité des coûts de nos matériaux et de nos produits dans le cadre de notre modèle de coût standard, en analysant la structure des coûts et les écarts d'inventaire et en dirigeant les initiatives d'amélioration de l'efficacité des coûts.
Concevoir et maintenir des processus d'approvisionnement évolutifs, automatisés et prêts pour les audits, y compris pour les matériaux utilisés dans des processus soumis au contrôle de la qualité.
Élaborer des stratégies d'approvisionnement et gérer les relations avec les fournisseurs, de la négociation au suivi continu du rendement.
Collaborer avec les responsables des ventes, de la fabrication et du laboratoire de services afin de prévoir les besoins en matériaux, à l'aide de modèles fondés sur les données et d'outils de plus en plus automatisés.

Planification des ventes et des opérations

Diriger la planification des matériaux et des approvisionnements avec les responsables des opérations, en harmonisant les plans de production, l'approvisionnement en matières premières, l'inventaire et la capacité des fournisseurs avec les prévisions de ventes.
Établir et maintenir des modèles opérationnels et de capacité qui appuient la planification des ressources et la budgétisation.
Assumer la responsabilité de notre ERP à titre d'expert ou d'experte en la matière : intégrité et exactitude des données, et capacité du système à bien servir l'entreprise.

Inventaire

Assumer la responsabilité de nos systèmes et processus d'inventaire, en assurant une intégration étroite entre l'ERP et le LIMS développé à l'interne par Nomic, plaque tournante de nos données opérationnelles.
Avec vos pairs, définir des stratégies de détention des stocks qui concilient rendement opérationnel et saine gestion financière.

jobs.title: Head of Fraud Investigations
jobs.description:
Every great career move starts with the right conversation. Humans of HR is a Canadian-owned search firm, and we partner with respected organizations across the country to find the leaders who make a real difference to their teams. We take the time to understand what matters to you, not just what’s on your résumé, and every conversation is handled with complete discretion.

The People You’d Join

Our client is a large, long-established and highly respected organization headquartered in Metro Vancouver. It’s purpose-driven, financially strong and in the middle of a real transformation, with serious investment going into data, digitization and AI. Its senior leaders describe the culture as one of the most collaborative and supportive they’ve worked in, with a genuine commitment to people and a clear appetite to keep raising the bar.

The Work You’d Own

This is a director-level role. Reporting to the Chief Compliance and Risk Officer, you’ll lead the organization’s fraud investigations function and a team of about ten investigators, including four senior investigators and a data scientist. You’ll own the full fraud program, end to end, and you’ll be the person who decides how it runs next.
Lead every file from detection and triage through investigation, findings, recovery and, where needed, civil action with external counsel
Find the control gaps that let fraud happen, and lead the strategies that prevent and deter it
Shape the department’s methodology, key performance indicators and analytics strategy, using a newly implemented AI-enabled case management platform
Bring long-standing files to resolution and shorten the time from first flag to final outcome
Guide recovery negotiations and settlements, and review recovery correspondence
Build a culture of mentorship, where senior investigators actively develop the rest of the team
Set the department’s annual plan and budget, and report results clearly to senior leadership and the board’s audit committee
Join client meetings and proposals as part of the leadership team, and work closely with legal counsel and, when required, law enforcement

The Human We’re Looking For

10+ years of experience in fraud investigations, internal audit, forensic accounting, financial crimes or a related field
7+ years in progressively senior leadership roles, with a track record of building and developing high-performing teams
A sharp investigative mind that connects information across sources, spots patterns and knows where to focus effort
Strong data literacy, with the ability to work with data yourself or direct a team that does
Experience negotiating settlements, and sound knowledge of administrative law and procedural fairness
Executive presence and political savvy, with the credibility to advise executives, clients, legal counsel and law enforcement
The judgment to work with a high degree of independence and to raise issues early
A Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE) designation is a strong asset

Where and How You’d Work

Metro Vancouver, BC. This is a hybrid role, with three days a week on site and flexible hours, Monday to Friday. The office has on-site parking, a gym and a cafeteria. You’ll need to live in British Columbia.

The Full Picture on Pay

Base salary of $150,000 to $200,000, depending on experience
Annual bonus with a 15% target
A very generous employer contribution to a defined contribution pension plan, with no employee contribution required
Comprehensive health, dental and life coverage, with premiums that can be fully paid by the employer depending on the plan you choose
Four weeks’ vacation to start, increasing with service, plus extra vacation at service milestones
A dedicated budget for professional development and growth
Wellbeing perks, including virtual health care for you and your family, an on-site gym and a yoga room

Why We Like This One

Leadership roles like this rarely come with so much room to build. The executive you’d report to is fully invested in this role, the technology investment is already in place, and success is measured by the rigour and quality of the team’s work rather than recovery targets alone. If you’ve ever wanted to put your own stamp on a fraud program, this is the one.

Your Next Step

If this opportunity resonates, we’d love to hear from you. Every application is read by a real person on our team, and if there’s a fit, we’ll reach out to talk about the role and what matters to you in your next move. Everything you share stays confidential, and nothing goes to our client without your consent. We believe hiring works best when it’s done with care and intention, and that starts with you.

Not quite the right role for you? We’re always working on new searches, so stay in touch. And if you’re an employer looking to grow your team, we’d be glad to help. You can follow Humans of HR on LinkedIn.

About Us

The Department of Health and Wellness offers opportunities to grow and advance in a dynamic sector that touches the lives of all Nova Scotians. Along with our partners, including the Nova Scotia Health Authority and the IWK Health Centre, we are committed to continually improving our healthcare system. The Department is thinking differently about how to plan, fund, legislate and monitor to improve access and service delivery. To do this, we need leaders at all levels of the organization who embrace a challenge and believe in their ability to make a difference.

About Our Opportunity

As the Director of Accountability and Analytics
, you will have an opportunity to influence how physician services are planned, funded, monitored and improved across Nova Scotia’s health system.

Reporting to the Executive Director, you will be a key member of the leadership team advancing strategic priorities across the physician services portfolio. Your leadership will span two connected areas: strengthening accountability for physician remuneration and funded programs, including support for major negotiations, and building the branch’s data and analytics capability to enable stronger, evidence-informed decisions.

This is an opportunity for a strategic and collaborative leader who is comfortable working at the intersection of policy, funding, accountability, analytics and health-system transformation
. You will lead multidisciplinary teams, work with senior partners across government and the health system, and translate complex financial, operational, policy and analytical information into practical frameworks, meaningful insights and clear advice.

Your work will help strengthen performance and accountability while building the data and analytical capabilities needed to support the future of physician services in Nova Scotia.

Primary Accountabilities

In this role, you will provide strategic leadership to complex initiatives that strengthen accountability and expand the use of data in physician services planning, funding and performance management.

You will lead multidisciplinary teams, establish priorities and create the conditions for high-quality, decision-focused work. Working across the Department, government, Nova Scotia Health, IWK Health and external organizations, you will bring partners together to move initiatives from design through implementation, measurement and continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities Include

Strengthening accountability by designing and improving frameworks, performance measures and monitoring approaches for physician remuneration models and funded initiatives.
Leading complex initiatives that establish clear outcomes, roles, decision-making responsibilities, reporting requirements and approaches to managing risk.
Supporting major negotiations through scenario analysis, costing, evidence synthesis, mandate development and recommendations related to Physician Agreement and Clinical/Academic Funding Plan negotiations.
Building analytics capability by advancing a branch data and analytics strategy focused on data quality, governance, access and integration, including the transition to modern cloud-based platforms.
Turning data into insight by overseeing dashboards, Power BI reporting, forecasting tools and provincial measures related to financial performance, service delivery, access, health human resources and outcomes.
Ensuring analytical integrity through appropriate methods, controls and documentation that support reliable and well-governed analysis.
Leading and developing people while building capability in project delivery, accountability, business intelligence and advanced analytics.
Building trusted partnerships and collaborative approaches to complex issues where perspectives and priorities may differ.
Influencing decisions by translating complex information into clear briefings, presentations and recommendations for senior audiences.

Qualifications And Experience

You are a strategic and collaborative leader who can bring clarity to complex issues and turn evidence into action. You are comfortable working with senior leaders and system partners, guiding multidisciplinary teams, and translating complex analytical, financial, operational and policy information into clear advice.

You have a Bachelor’s Degree
in a relevant field such as public or business administration, health administration, data or health analytics, economics, finance, engineering, computer science or a related discipline, plus significant years of progressively responsible experience
. This includes at least three years in a leadership or management role
involving complex projects, organizational change, accountability, performance measurement or data-informed decision-making in the public, health or a similarly complex sector. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.

You Bring Demonstrated Experience In

Leading and developing professional or multidisciplinary teams.
Leading complex, cross-functional initiatives from design through implementation, measurement and continuous improvement.
Building or strengthening organizational, accountability or analytical capabilities.
Designing accountability frameworks, performance measures or evaluation approaches.
Translating complex data, policy, financial and operational information into clear advice for senior decision-makers.
Building productive relationships with senior partners where perspectives, priorities or implementation considerations may differ.

Experience supporting complex negotiations, health-system funding or physician remuneration is considered an asset. A Master’s Degree in a complementary discipline is also an asset.

Experience with modern data and business intelligence platforms such as Microsoft Fabric, Microsoft Azure, Power BI or comparable technologies
is an asset. Hands-on technical development experience is not required; however, you must be able to lead technical specialists, assess analytical approaches and ensure data products align with business and policy needs.

At elockers, we are on a mission to make live events smarter, easier and more enjoyable.

From world-class festivals and stadiums to iconic concert venues, we provide innovative self-service locker solutions that give visitors the freedom to enjoy unforgettable experiences without worrying about their belongings.

Founded in the Netherlands, elockers is rapidly expanding across Europe and North America. We are an ambitious, entrepreneurial company with big plans, strong partnerships and a passion for the live entertainment industry.

Lock in. Own the operation.

Your mission

You take ownership of our operations and key client relationships across Canada. Based in Toronto, you keep our existing venues and festivals running smoothly while building the operational structure for what comes next. This is a hands-on leadership role. You make decisions independently, represent elockers in the Canadian market and are just as comfortable on a festival site at 6 a.m. as in a meeting with a venue operator.

What you'll build

Operations that run.
You own the planning, preparation, execution and evaluation of our venue and festival operations across Canada, managing multiple projects from A to Z.
Boots on the ground.
Logistics, installations, maintenance, event support and breakdowns. When needed, you're onsite helping with installations and troubleshooting.
Strong client relationships.
You are the key contact for our venues, festivals and partners. You manage expectations, solve issues and keep satisfaction high.
Growth with existing partners.
You spot opportunities to expand partnerships and work closely with our commercial team on renewals and new projects.
A reliable local network.
You build and manage a flexible pool of part-time staff, freelancers, transport companies, warehouses and technical service providers.
A lean structure that scales.
You recruit, train and coordinate local teams, and set up operations that grow efficiently without an unnecessarily large permanent team.
Grip on performance.
You own operational planning, budgets, quality and reporting, and improve processes as the business grows.
One international team.
You work closely with our European team on logistics, technology, operations and commercial opportunities.

What you bring

Several years of operations experience in live events, festivals, venues or a comparable fast-paced environment.
Experience leading teams and managing external partners, freelancers and suppliers.
You've built something from the ground up before and enjoy doing it again.
You take ownership, act independently and solve problems before they become problems.
Strong client skills. You're comfortable with major venue operators and festival organizers.
Based in or around Toronto, with the flexibility to travel to venues and events across Canada.

What you get

Ownership of the Canadian operation in an international scale-up.
Real impact on how we grow in North America.
A competitive package that reflects your level.

About Destination Canada

Tourism is the heartbeat of communities from coast to coast to coast. At Destination Canada, our aspiration for the tourism industry is to generate wealth and wellbeing for all of Canada and enrich the lives of our guests. Our mission is to influence supply and build demand for the benefit of locals, communities and visitors through leading research, alignment with public and private sectors, and marketing Canada nationally and abroad. We seek diverse, ingenious thinkers teeming with intellectual curiosity and a deep desire to grow Canada's tourism industry – strengthening the socio-cultural, environmental and economic vitality tourism brings to Canada.

About the role:

Reporting to the Senior Vice President, Marketing Strategy & Chief Marketing Officer, the Regional Managing Director, Asia Pacific provides strategic direction and leadership for Destination Canada's activities across China, Japan and South Korea. The role translates Destination Canada's 2030 Vision and Go-to-Market Strategy into regional priorities and initiatives that strengthen Canada's brand, build demand among high-value travellers and contribute to organizational objectives.

The Regional Managing Director leads regional teams and operations, develops strategic partnerships across the travel and tourism ecosystem, and connects regional opportunities with global initiatives and travel corridors. Working closely with colleagues in Canada and international markets, the role uses market intelligence, partner insights and performance data to guide decisions, oversee resources and deliver measurable results.

Key accountabilities

Regional Strategy: Develops and implements regional strategies for China, Japan and South Korea, translating Destination Canada's 2030 Vision and Go-to-Market Strategy into market priorities that contribute to global objectives and high-value travel demand. As organizational priorities evolve, assesses opportunities in additional markets and provides strategic recommendations to inform future market engagement and investment decisions.
Strategic Partnerships: Develops long-term partnerships with airlines, travel brands, media, distribution platforms and other organizations, connecting regional opportunities with broader partnership ecosystems to extend reach, share capabilities and deliver measurable impact.
Marketing and Discoverability: Oversees integrated marketing initiatives that strengthen Canada's cultural relevance, build destination demand and improve Canada's discoverability across evolving digital, search and AI-enabled travel planning channels, in collaboration with global teams and partners.
Trade Engagement: Guides regional travel trade and distribution strategies, strengthening industry relationships, advocacy and collaboration to increase awareness of Canadian tourism experiences and support travel conversion.
Market Intelligence: Uses consumer research, travel flow insights, partner data and emerging insights into AI-enabled discovery and traveller behaviour to identify opportunities, inform regional priorities and support investment decisions.
Global Integration: Collaborates with headquarters, international markets and strategic partners to connect regional activities with global initiatives, including opportunities across travel corridors, aviation networks and emerging distribution channels.
People Leadership: Leads and develops regional employees and external representatives, setting priorities, managing performance and fostering collaboration across markets and with headquarters teams.
Performance Management: Establishes regional performance objectives, monitors results and applies insights from marketing, partnership and operational activities to improve effectiveness, resource allocation and measurable outcomes.
Financial Oversight: Oversees regional operating and program budgets, resource allocation, forecasting and contract management, ensuring effective stewardship of resources and compliance with organizational policies.
External Representation: Represents Destination Canada with government officials, tourism industry leaders, strategic partners and other stakeholders, advancing organizational priorities and strengthening Canada's position within the regional tourism ecosystem.

What you need

Graduation from a recognized university in marketing, business, tourism or another relevant discipline, or an acceptable combination of education, training and experience.
At least 8 years of relevant senior management experience, including responsibility for developing and delivering marketing, sales or market development strategies and programs across multiple international markets.
International marketing and market development: Experience developing and implementing integrated consumer marketing, business-to-business, distribution and partnership initiatives that build demand and support measurable outcomes.
Regional market expertise: Demonstrated knowledge of Asian markets, including experience developing business relationships and navigating commercial and cultural considerations relevant to China, Japan and South Korea.
People and operational leadership: Experience leading geographically dispersed teams, managing external representatives and agencies, and overseeing operations across multiple countries or markets.
Strategic partnership development: Experience identifying, developing and managing partnerships involving multiple organizations, aligning shared objectives, negotiating agreements and coordinating joint initiatives.
Brand and demand development: Experience using audience insights, brand positioning, content, media and digital distribution channels to build consumer interest, improve destination discoverability and support progression from awareness to travel consideration and conversion.
Financial and performance management: Experience overseeing operating and program budgets, managing financial forecasts, assessing performance and making resource allocation decisions.
Research and analytical capabilities: Ability to interpret market research, consumer insights, travel trends and performance data to identify opportunities, assess risks and recommend strategic adjustments.
Executive communication and stakeholder engagement: Ability to present strategic recommendations clearly, influence decisions and build effective relationships with senior government, industry and business stakeholders across cultures.

It would be great if you also had

A Master of Business Administration (MBA).
Experience working in the international travel and tourism industry.
Established relationships with travel trade, tourism industry or other relevant partners in Asian markets.

jobs.description:
Permanent Full Time

We are looking for a Director, Portfolio Management & Governance within the Technology Project Management Office.

The Director, Portfolio Management & Governance reports to the AVP, Program Management & Governance and is accountable for the integrated planning, governance, and delivery oversight of technology investments within the Canada Operations & Business Enablement portfolio. The Director works closely with senior business and technology leaders to establish priorities, evaluate investment trade-offs, manage portfolio-level risks and dependencies, and ensure initiatives deliver measurable business value within approved financial and capacity constraints. The role leads a team of Program Managers and Project Managers and serves as a trusted advisor and escalation point for portfolio delivery.

The Director, Portfolio Management & Governance is outcome-focused and capable of leading high-profile, highly complex, or ground-breaking programs of work while providing clear, credible advice to senior leadership.

What you will do:

Planning:

Lead the development of the annual portfolio delivery plan and budget within Technology, and work with business partners to refresh a multi‑year delivery roadmap that aligns with strategic priorities.
Collaborate with Technology and Business Portfolio Leaders to assess and socialize priorities, ensuring visibility into impacts across systems, processes, and other portfolios.
Support the creation of an integrated cross‑portfolio delivery plan by aligning project investments with business and technology strategies.
Partner with divisional leadership to identify resource needs and staff programs and projects with appropriately skilled team members.
Work closely with Technology leaders to define priorities, objectives, scope, and deliverables that support enterprise goals and desired business outcomes.

Delivery Oversight & Governance:

Oversee the successful delivery of complex technology programs and projects within the assigned portfolio, ensuring alignment to business value, timelines, and budget.
Analyze incoming demand and structure it into programs, projects, or epics as appropriate.
Apply appropriate Governance Frameworks to guide business case development and ensure required documentation and approvals are in place.
Lead and develop a team of Program Managers and Project Managers accountable for delivery execution.
Conduct regular program retrospectives and post‑implementation reviews to drive continuous improvement and capture lessons learned.
Manage portfolio‑level risks and issues, ensuring effective analysis, mitigation, communication, and resolution.
Synthesize portfolio performance, financial forecasts, risks, dependencies, and delivery outcomes into clear, concise, and decision-oriented communications for senior leadership and governance forums. Proactively surface emerging concerns, articulate business impacts, and recommend practical courses of action.
Maintain detailed portfolio‑level spend plans and ensure strong financial governance across all initiatives.
Serve as the escalation point for all delivery‑related issues, risks, decisions, and changes within the portfolio.
Manage resource capacity, workload balancing, and team assignments to ensure optimal delivery performance.
Apply the most appropriate delivery methodologies—Waterfall, Agile (Scrum/Kanban), Hybrid, etc.—to achieve optimal business outcomes, ensuring adherence to enterprise standards and methodologies.

What you will bring:

A university or college degree in a relevant field.
A minimum of eight years of progressive technology delivery experience within financial services, insurance, fintech, or a comparably complex organization, including at least three years leading multi-million-dollar programs, portfolios, or enterprise initiatives. Experience with application development and technology modernization is preferred.
Proven ability to build strong, collaborative relationships with colleagues and external stakeholders, influencing outcomes with confidence and credibility.
Proven executive-level communication skills, with the ability to translate complex portfolio, delivery, financial, and risk information into clear, concise, decision-oriented messages for senior leaders. Demonstrated experience preparing and delivering executive presentations, facilitating governance forums, influencing senior stakeholders, and communicating difficult issues or recommendations with confidence, sound judgment, and appropriate transparency.
Demonstrated portfolio management experience, including investment planning, prioritization, financial forecasting, capacity planning, dependency management, and the evaluation of competing initiatives against business value and strategic outcomes.
Proven ability to apply sound judgment and constructive challenge within governance forums, including testing assumptions, identifying gaps, escalating concerns, and helping senior leaders make informed investment and delivery decisions.
Demonstrated experience leading and developing delivery professionals, including setting clear accountabilities, coaching performance, building succession capability, and creating an environment of transparency, inclusion, and continuous improvement.
Ability to work across organizational boundaries and influence business and technology leaders with competing priorities, building alignment around enterprise outcomes rather than optimizing for a single project, function, or portfolio.
A strategic mindset with the ability to evaluate programs through the lens of business value and enterprise outcomes.
Strong comfort with ambiguity and change, with the ability to navigate uncertainty by seeking clarity from diverse stakeholders and available information.
Exceptional multi‑tasking and prioritization skills, thriving in a fast‑paced and demanding environment.
A passion for building, developing, and empowering high‑performing teams; a leader who models continuous learning, innovation, and an entrepreneurial mindset.

jobs.title: Vice President, Financial Controller
jobs.description:
Company Description

Classic Fire + Life Safety is an industry leader in fire protection and life safety services, supporting commercial, industrial, and institutional clients across Canada. With a strong reputation built on safety, reliability, and technical expertise, the company continues to scale through organic growth, value accretive acquisitions and partnerships, and operational excellence.

Our goal is to partner with our customers, to ensure their building, and the people in them are safe, from new building construction activities, modernization activities, and demand for system upgrades, through to preventative maintenance and service

Why join the Classic team?

CFLS is a caring company who values our staff.
CFLS is local and is part of the community.
CFLS is a full-service fire protection contractor.

Overview

We are seeking an experienced and hands-on Vice President, Financial Controller to lead the controllership, accounting, treasury, tax, audit, compliance, and shared services functions while acting as a key strategic partner to the CFO and executive leadership team.

Position Summary

The Vice President, Financial Controller is responsible for the integrity of the company's financial reporting, internal controls, treasury management, tax compliance, and accounting operations.

The successful candidate will combine strong technical accounting expertise with practical functional leadership. This individual will oversee all financial control activities while driving process improvements, automation, systems optimization, and finance transformation initiatives that support continued growth.

This role requires a leader who can operate both strategically and tactically, providing executive-level guidance while remaining close to the details.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Reporting & Controllership

Own all monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reporting processes.
Ensure timely and accurate consolidation of financial results across all business units.
Support preparation of management reporting packages, lender, and board reporting.
Ensure compliance with Canadian accounting standards for private enterprises (ASPE), IFRS (if applicable), GAAP, and regulatory requirements.
Develop and maintain accounting policies and technical accounting guidance.

Internal Controls, Governance & Risk Management

Design, implement, and continuously enhance internal control frameworks.
Lead annual audit planning and execution.
Coordinate relationships with external auditors and advisors.
Oversee risk management initiatives related to financial governance and credit agreement compliance.

Shared Services & Transactional Finance

Provide leadership over:
Accounts Receivable / Collections
Accounts Payable
Master Data Governance

Establish service-level expectations and performance metrics.
Improve efficiency through process standardization and automation.
Improve data quality and financial discipline throughout the organization

Treasury & Cash Management

Oversee corporate treasury operations and liquidity management.
Monitor working capital performance and cash flow forecasting.
Manage banking relationships and lender compliance requirements.
Optimize cash management structures across multiple legal entities.
Support debt financing initiatives and covenant reporting.

Tax Leadership

Oversee corporate income tax, sales tax, and other statutory compliance requirements.
Manage year-end tax provisions and related disclosures.
Ensure compliance across all provinces and jurisdictions in which the company operates.

Acquisition Integration

Support accounting integration of acquired businesses.
Standardize financial reporting and control environments following acquisitions.
Ensure successful transfer of accounting and reporting processes into the corporate finance structure.

Leadership & Talent Development

Lead, mentor, and develop the finance organization.
Establish performance standards and succession plans.
Foster a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.
Recruit and develop future finance leaders.

Qualifications

Required

CPA designation (CPA, CA preferred).
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field.
Minimum 12-15 years of progressive finance and accounting experience.
Minimum 5 years in a senior leadership role such as: Controller, Director of Finance, VP Finance, VP Controller.
Experience in cross-border, multi-site service environments, such as field services, facilities services, industrial services, or related sectors.
Financial reporting knowledge.
Strong understanding of: Revenue recognition, Work-in-progress accounting, Project accounting, Audit and internal controls, Treasury management, Corporate taxation
Experience with ERP implementations and finance transformation initiatives.
Advanced Excel and financial systems capabilities.

Leadership Competencies

The ideal candidate will demonstrate:

High integrity and sound judgment.
Strong business partnership skills.
Ability to influence across all levels of the organization.
Exceptional communication and presence.
Continuous improvement mindset.

We thank all applicants who apply, but only those candidates who meet the above qualifications will be contacted for an interview.

Salary placement within the stated range is determined by evaluating the candidate’s relevant experience, skills, and qualifications, along with internal equity and prevailing market conditions. These factors are applied consistently to support transparent and equitable compensation practices in Ontario.

No part of our hiring process uses AI or automated screening technology, all candidate reviews and applications are evaluated manually and hiring decisions are completed by human staff, to ensure a fair and transparent assessment.

jobs.description:
Do you have a knack for building connections, developing trusted relationships, and turning your network into meaningful business opportunities?

Join Tedy and help us build and scale our partner network across Canada, directly contributing to our growth.

About Tedy

Tedy is a unified financial platform that helps businesses manage employee benefits, rewards, stipends, retirement savings, and expenses through AI-powered automation, embedded financial services, and integrated payments.

We’re an AI-native company, not only in what we build but also in how we work. Everyone at Tedy is empowered to experiment, build their own tools, automate workflows, and rethink how things get done.

We’re looking for an ambitious, fully bilingual professional who combines exceptional relationship-building skills with an entrepreneurial and AI-native mindset.

The Role

You will own and scale one of Tedy’s most important growth channels: our national partner ecosystem.

You’ll develop relationships with HR consultants, total rewards advisors, insurance brokers, consulting firms, and technology partners across Canada.

Working directly with our founders, you’ll help define our partnership strategy, develop new commercial opportunities, and build the systems that allow our partner network to scale efficiently.

You’ll have the autonomy to experiment, make decisions, and turn your ideas into action.

What You’ll Do

Identify, recruit, and develop strategic partners across Canada.
Build lasting relationships across the HR and employee benefits ecosystem.
Equip and support partners with the resources, training, and tools they need to succeed.
Develop joint commercial initiatives and go-to-market strategies.
Build AI-powered workflows to improve partner discovery, outreach, onboarding, engagement, and performance tracking.
Create and continuously improve your own tools and processes to scale your impact.
Turn strategic partnerships into measurable revenue and sustainable growth.
Represent Tedy at industry events, conferences, and strategic meetings.
Collaborate directly with our Sales, Marketing, and Product teams.

What We’re Looking For

Experience in partnerships, business development, or B2B sales.
A natural ability to establish trusted relationships and develop professional networks.
Strong commercial instincts and the ability to turn opportunities into results.
Full professional fluency in French and English, both written and spoken. This is mandatory.
An entrepreneurial mindset, intellectual curiosity, and a high degree of autonomy.
The ability to thrive in a fast-moving technology company.
Experience working within an HR technology company, consulting firm, insurance brokerage, or HR team is a strong asset.

AI-Native Mindset (Mandatory)

At Tedy, AI proficiency is a core competency, regardless of your role. We’re looking for someone who already integrates AI into the way they think, work, and solve problems.
Hands-on proficiency with large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini.
Ability to design AI-powered workflows, build custom assistants, and automate repetitive business processes.
Comfort experimenting with AI agents, no-code and low-code platforms, and emerging AI technologies.
Ability to independently prototype tools and solutions that improve productivity and commercial performance.
Strong judgment when working with AI-generated outputs, business data, and confidential information.
A genuine curiosity for emerging technologies and a continuous drive to improve how you work.

You don’t need to be a software engineer. But you should be a builder, someone who can identify a problem and leverage AI to create a solution rather than wait for someone else to build it.

We expect candidates to demonstrate concrete examples of how they have used AI to improve their work, build tools, or solve business problems.

Why Tedy?

Trusted by more than 600 businesses.
A fast-growing Canadian fintech with North American ambitions.
An AI-native environment where experimentation and initiative are encouraged.
A culture that values autonomy, execution, and great ideas over bureaucracy.
Direct access to the founders and real influence over strategic decisions.
Competitive compensation with a performance-based component.
Flexible employee benefits, naturally.

Let’s Build What’s Next.

We’re not looking for someone to simply manage partnerships. We’re looking for someone who builds relationships, creates opportunities, and constantly finds smarter ways to scale their impact.

If that’s how you work, we’d love to meet you.

jobs.description:
Program Director

Program Directors at Havas CX have two primary objectives: 1 - Define the vision and structure of client programs and overseeing its execution by our team of project managers, and 2 – Continuously improve and refine the delivery practice. As a Program Director, you may be involved in overseeing multiple projects, across multiple brands or clients to ensure the overall project health in their portfolio (financials, resources, risks, relationships), or overseeing one large portfolio-sized account.

The Program Director serves as "Lead" on large client accounts and is accountable for the delivery management team's organization, operational efficiencies, and health within their assigned accounts. Within that role, the Program Director may be responsible for supervising one or more project managers and/or senior project managers. Program Directors will interface heavily with senior creative, technical, and executive management within the client to assure that the solution is understood and addresses the customer's business requirements. They will also ensure that the challenges and requirements are understood by the team and will participate in the solution developed by the team.

The Program Director will be responsible for delivering accurate financial management of the accounts/brands to which he/she is assigned and for delivering improved account margins. In addition to the project responsibilities, Program Directors will also participate in the business development process and will be a key member of the business development team where appropriate. They will proactively manage risk to ensure project success.

Responsibilities
Planning

Has a deep understanding of the client’s business needs, expectations and requirements
Leads the project team in determining the approach, deliverables, schedule, and tools to deliver multiple projects streams within established constraints
Works with client team as well as members of the assigned project team to estimate costs and timing for tasks such as project strategy, functional design, visual design, technology requirements, etc., utilizing established estimating process and tools.
Ensures the feasibility of project delivery given scope, time and budget constraints.

Execution

Coordinates activities of the project management team and has overall responsibility for quality output
Performs timely review, and approval of invoices and timesheets
Leads the creation and delivery of SOWs and CRs
Ensure that the Program meets and exceeds the company’s internal project delivery standards
Ensures that the project management team is handling core functions of the PM role, such as scheduling and facilitating project-related team meetings (i.e. kick-offs, status, internal/client reviews, etc.), communicating action steps to the team, and delivering weekly status reports to project team, the client and management
Helps update processes and standards for project documentation and ensures that the project management team is developing, maintaining, reviewing and/or disseminating all project documentation
Is a contributor to the content and presentation of key client deliverables as required to ensure relevancy, strategy, quality, and timeliness

Monitoring
– Scheduling, Financials and Risk Management

Ensures adherence to processes for scope management and change control
Oversees project management team to ensure that projects in the assigned accounts are completed according to schedule and within budget
Responsible for accuracy and overall financial health throughout the project lifecycle including estimates, revenue forecasts, invoicing, payables, receivables, etc.
Responsible for delivering work with sold margins
Responsible for identifying and driving solutions to project risk challenges at the account and project levels
Is also responsible for developing and adhering to processes for project and account financial management
Is the point of contact for all team and client escalations

Client Communication

Establishes relationships with key client team members and owns all client communications
Champion a client focused culture to deepen client relationships and leverage broader company relationships, systems and knowledge.

Team Management

Works closely with direct reports to ensure they understand expectations of their performance and helps them identify commitments; providing direction and feedback via regular meetings and as needed
Champions a high-performance environment and contributes to an inclusive work environment.
Builds team expertise by mentoring junior team members and offering training in relevant methodologies, techniques, frameworks, etc.
Works with the Discipline lead, Solution Leads, Practice Leads and other team members to develop and/or promote best practices for the discipline

Qualifications
10+ years’ experience managing multiple large, complex and cross-functional interactive projects, preferably in an agency environment
Solid understanding of agile best practices is required
Experience managing pharma brands is a plus
Certification in an agile methodology is a bonus
Excellent understanding and performance of project delivery best practices including budget, scope and time management
Expert knowledge of one or more of the following: software development life cycles, web/mobile technologies, web/mobile development processes and the delivery of solutions with creative and engineering components, digital strategy projects
Excellent verbal and written communication skills
Excellent organizational and time management skills
Experience in working closely with Creative and UX teams
Preferably have a background or understanding of IT
Expert understanding of project management methodology including the ability to identify and resolve issues, manage risk, develop detailed work plans and specifications, perform resource allocations and run team meetings
Ability to work on multiple projects and manage multiple project managers and/or senior project managers at one time
Demonstrated ability to motivate staff/project/account team, inspire teamwork and take a leadership role
Ability to solve complex account-wide problems with keen instincts and organizational experience
Must be able to simultaneously focus on the big picture, details, and driving results
3-5 years of people management experience

About Havas CX Canada

Havas CX is a global network of digital agencies dedicated to creating meaningful experiences across the customer journey. With deep capabilities in business transformation, experience design, CRM, and technology, we partner with leading brands to deliver exceptional digital products and services across B2B and B2C markets.

We are deeply committed to investing in the professional development of our team members, providing ample opportunities to expand skills, take on diverse challenges, and contribute to high-impact projects. **SUMMARY**

The Senior Vice President, IT Operations is accountable for the stability, performance, resilience, secure operation and continuous improvement of the technology environment that supports BGIS operations and the business\-critical solutions we deliver to our clients. Reporting to the Chief Technology Officer, this executive leads four operational domains: Application Support, Infrastructure (including Service Desk and End User Support), Financial Application Support, and the Legacy Software Development Platform (operational enhancements). The individual sets the operational strategy and service model for these domains, directs a team of directors, managers and technical professionals across onshore and offshore teams, and partners with business unit leaders, client\-facing teams and vendors to ensure that services meet or exceed contractual SLAs and client expectations. The individual drives a culture of operational excellence and continuous improvement, using automation, standardization, data\-driven KPI management and modern IT service management practices to increase reliability, reduce cost, and improve the client and end\-user experience. The role is a member of the IT leadership team and reports regularly to senior and executive management on operational performance, risk and investment priorities.  



**KEY DUTIES \& RESPONSIBILITIES**

Leadership


Directs the IT Operations organization through a team of directors and managers, spanning onshore, offshore and third\-party resources across all four domains.


Demonstrates strong, competent leadership for team members to guide them in reaching their full potential and meeting their objectives, which supports achievement of our corporate goals. Specifically, these responsibilities include but not limited to:


* Full involvement with recruiting talent.
* Provides mentoring, coaching and guidance to all team members.
* Objectively recommends compensation adjustments.
* Manages all aspects of performance.
* Builds leadership bench strength and succession plans across all four IT Operations domains.
* Develops the technical capabilities of the organization, including reskilling and upskilling staff for cloud, automation and AI\-enabled operations.
* Defines the workforce and sourcing strategy, determining the right balance of in\-house, offshore and managed service resources.
Fosters an environment of teamwork, accountability, innovation and client service to meet business objectives.  
* 

IT Operations Strategy \& Service Excellence


* Defines and executes the multi\-year IT Operations strategy and roadmap, aligned with BGIS business objectives, client commitments and the broader IT strategy.
* Partners with the Chief Technology Officer and Architecture to shape the enterprise technology roadmap and standards, and leads the operational integration of acquired businesses and new technology platforms.
* Holds overall accountability for the availability, performance and resiliency of business\-critical solutions that support our clients, ensuring contractual SLAs and KPIs are consistently met or exceeded.
* Establishes a unified operating model, service catalogue and support structure (L1\-L3\) across Application Support, Infrastructure, Financial Application Support and the Legacy Software Development Platform.
* Establishes demand intake, prioritization and resource capacity planning across all four domains, balancing day\-to\-day operations, operational projects, CISO\-requested security work and client commitments, and ensures operational projects are delivered on time, on budget and with minimal service disruption.
* Establishes governance for ITSM processes, including incident, major incident, problem, change, release, configuration and request management, and ensures timely root\-cause analysis and corrective action.
* Ensures 24x7 operational coverage for business\-critical services, including monitoring and event management, and on\-call and after\-hours support.
* Serves as the executive escalation point for critical client\-impacting incidents; directs response, client communication and post\-incident reviews.
* Builds relationships with senior business unit leaders and client\-facing teams to understand business direction, anticipate operational needs and manage expectations.
* Provides service performance insights to account and client\-facing teams to inform client governance discussions and shape the support model, and ensures IT services comply with client contractual, audit and data protection requirements.
* Establishes and enforces IT Operations policies, standards and procedures, and ensures adherence to enterprise IT standards (i.e. Security, IT Governance, Service Management, Architecture).
* Manages operational risks through mitigation strategies, and plans or implements contingencies where necessary.
Provides regular reporting to senior and executive management on SLA and KPI performance, operational risk, capacity and investment priorities.  
* 

Application Support


* Directs the support, maintenance and operational health of the enterprise and client\-facing application portfolio, including integrations, middleware and SaaS platforms.
* Ensures applications that support client service delivery are monitored, supported and maintained to meet defined service levels and business continuity requirements.
* Partners with Business Technology, product and development teams to ensure smooth transition of new solutions into production support, including defining operational acceptance criteria early in the delivery lifecycle.
* Sets the strategy for application lifecycle management, including patching, upgrades, license compliance, and the rationalization and decommissioning of redundant applications.
Oversees database administration and data operations, including performance, backup and restore, and data retention, in line with BGIS and client requirements.

Senior Director, Information Technology
jobs.description:
Vacancy Status
: Full Time, 14 Month Contract 

Position Description:
The Toronto Region Board of Trade is seeking a Senior Director, Information Technology for a 14-month contract to lead the Board's IT team. Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, you will ensure the Board's systems remain secure, reliable and well-supported, and serve as a trusted technology partner across all levels of the organization. This role oversees IT operations, business applications, vendor partnerships, cybersecurity and in-flight technology initiatives within a Microsoft-centred environment that includes Azure, Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365 and the Power Platform. In addition to progressive IT leadership experience, the ideal candidate will be a clear communicator, highly collaborative, and able to step into an established environment quickly, combining sound strategic judgment with a hands-on approach to day-to-day operations.

Key Responsibilities:
Technology Leadership & Execution

Serves as the senior technology advisor to the Chief Financial Officer and leadership team, providing clear, concise updates and recommendations.

Ensures technology priorities remain aligned with organizational goals and carries forward in-flight initiatives to agreed milestones.

Maintains a strong understanding of the organization’s technology environment and remains actively involved in the execution and resolution of day-to-day technology matters.

Identifies opportunities to improve technology effectiveness, reliability and user experience, with a focus on practical solutions appropriate for a 50-100-person organization.

AI Implementation & Adoption

Supports the implementation of agentic AI solutions across the organization, working with business teams and external partners to identify practical use cases, configure and test solutions, and integrate them into everyday workflows.

Manages and supports the Board’s AI tools, including Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini, overseeing licensing, access, configuration and technical support.

Coordinates the technical requirements for AI implementation, including system integrations, data access, testing and deployment, ensuring appropriate security controls and human oversight in accordance with the Board’s AI use policy.

Provides practical guidance, training and troubleshooting to help employees adopt AI tools and apply them effectively in their work.

Team Leadership & Cross-Functional Collaboration

Leads, supports and develops the IT team, setting priorities and managing performance and KPIs.

Provides service to all areas of the Board by applying business partner skills and a client service outlook.

Allocates work effectively across the team and ensures appropriate coverage for operational priorities, projects and employee support.

Documents key decisions and changes to support a smooth transition at the end of the contract

Vendor Management, Security & Compliance

Manages the relationships with key technology partners, including the managed services providers; monitors performance and oversees renewals and negotiations.

Leads vendor escalations and ensures unresolved service issues are addressed quickly and effectively.

Maintains the Board's cybersecurity posture across Azure and Microsoft 365, including identity, access and data protection.

Upholds IT policies, including the Board's AI use policy, and supports compliance with accessibility (AODA) and privacy requirements.

IT Operations & Service Delivery

Oversees the reliable day-to-day operation of IT infrastructure and technology services at both the Board’s event space at 100 Queens Quay and corporate office at 21 Melinda, including network connectivity, Wi-Fi, end-user services, collaboration tools and telephony.

Takes a hands-on role in addressing operational issues, troubleshooting escalated concerns and coordinating resolution with internal team members and external vendors.

Manages the IT operating calendar, including renewals, reviews and as needed event support.

Maintains service levels and resolves escalated issues promptly.

Oversees technology onboarding and offboarding, hardware and software provisioning, access management and equipment lifecycle requirements.

Business Applications & Data

Oversees the Board's infrastructure including: CRM, marketing automation, finance, event management system, payments, website and related platforms.

Works directly with business teams and vendors to troubleshoot issues, manage enhancements and ensure systems are configured to support operational requirements.

Coordinates system upgrades, integrations, implementations and changes, ensuring appropriate testing, communication, documentation and employee support.

Supports reporting and analytics through Power BI and champions low-code solutions on the Power Platform where they add value.

Identifies opportunities to automate manual processes, simplify workflows and improve productivity using existing technology.

Your experience includes:

10+ years of progressive IT experience, including experience leading IT teams.

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Strong working knowledge of a Microsoft-centred environment, including Azure, Microsoft 365 and Dynamics 365.

Practical experience implementing or supporting AI tools and workflow automation, including technical deployment and employee adoption; experience with agentic AI solutions considered an asset.

Experience managing IT infrastructure, connectivity, audiovisual systems and technology support across multiple locations, including corporate office and event environments.

Proven experience managing managed service providers and external agencies, including contracts and performance.

Solid grounding in cybersecurity practices for a cloud-first organization.

Experience managing an IT budget and reporting to senior executives.

Strong oral and written communication skills; experience explaining technical matters to partners at all levels.

Ability to work cross-functionally and collaboratively with business units.

Experience with Business Central, Power BI, ClickDimensions, CMS considered an asset.

You’re often described as:

A steady, pragmatic leader who builds trust quickly with a new team

A business partner first, able to translate organizational needs into practical technology solutions

Highly organized and able to navigate competing priorities and deadlines

A self-starter who can work independently from a structured handover

A strong communicator, collaborative with colleagues from all levels and departments

Security-minded, detail-oriented and accountable

Working Conditions:

Full-time position, hybrid with 3-4 days in office.

May require occasional evening and weekend work for system maintenance or emergencies.

On-call availability for critical system issues.

Compensation & Benefits

TRBOT is committed to fair, equitable pay that matches the responsibility and expertise behind every role.

This role has an annual salary range of $120,000-$170,000.

At TRBOT, performance plays an important role in pay progression. As you build your skills, take on new challenges, and make an impact, your compensation will evolve to reflect that progress. Regular development check-ins with your manager keep your path clear and your momentum strong.

We encourage open dialogue about compensation at every stage of the interview proto ensure transparency and trust. Ask us anything—we want you to feel informed and confident from day one.

About the Toronto Region Board of Trade

At Toronto Region Board of Trade, you work closely with a collaborative, results-driven team of city builders. You will be centre stage on the issues that matter to the region. Working at Toronto Region Board of Trade gives you an opportunity to work with thought leaders, while collaborating with our dynamic, diverse membership.

Our culture is grounded in core values that include:

Accountability – We are accountable to our Members, stakeholders and each other.

Collaboration – We are our strongest when we work together.

Connections – We engage and build communities.

Learn more about the exciting work the Board is doing at bot.com.

We look forward to hearing from interested candidates. Only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

The Board welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodation is available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process.

As part of our recruitment process, TRBOT may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support the screening of applications. Participation is optional, and candidates can choose to opt out as part of the application process.
