jobs.title: Senior Capital Projects Director
jobs.description:
Company Overview

K’awat’si Consulting and Management Services (KCMS)
is an Indigenous-owned consulting and management organization based in Port Hardy, British Columbia. KCMS supports the economic development and long-term goals of the Gwa’sala-’Nakwaxda’xw Nations through professional services, business management, project support, and strategic initiatives.

Purpose

To lead the planning, coordination, and delivery of capital projects, infrastructure improvements, renovations, and other major organizational and client projects. The Senior Capital Project Director is responsible for developing project scopes, budgets, schedules, procurement strategies, and implementation plans while coordinating with stakeholders, consultants, engineers, architects, contractors, and funding partners. The position ensures projects are effectively planned and delivered within approved scope, budget, timelines, safety requirements, and organizational objectives.

Work Location
- Port Hardy, BC
Company/Department
-K’awat’si Consulting and Management Services
Reports To
-Executive Director

What We Offer:

1 month of covered accommodations in a hotel room for individuals relocating from outside of Northern Vancouver Island.
Relocation assistance
Enrollment in the company benefits plan after 3 months of employment
Career growth and educational development opportunities
Company events and holiday parties
Wellness incentives, including discounted gym membership and access to free in-person counselling services.
3 weeks of vacation

Position Summary

As the Owner’s Representative for major capital projects, you will act as agent for project owners (organization) in delivering complex built-asset programs. You will lead from feasibility to funding application to procurement and through to project close-out, ensuring scope, schedule, cost and quality objectives are achieved, risks are managed, and the asset is delivered aligned with operational requirements and strategic goals. You will lead project reporting to project owners, and hold accountability for working with project execution teams to ensure on-time and on-budget project delivery. Your expertise in engaging and working with consultant teams is a key driver of success in this position.

Key Responsibilities

Establish and maintain the project governance, delivery framework and stage-gate methodology (feasibility → design → procurement → construction → commissioning → handover).
Develop and maintain the master budget and schedule (in CAD, metric units) and monitor performance with regular forecasts and variance reporting.
Serve as the owner’s single point of accountability: review and challenge designs, review and approve procurement strategy, oversee contract negotiations and award, manage contract administration on behalf of the owner.
Interface with architects, engineers, general contractors, internal stakeholders and external authorities (regulatory, permitting, First Nations governments, provincial government, federal government).
Conduct risk management: maintain a risk register, identify and track major risks (e.g regulatory permitting, funding changes, inflation), develop mitigation plans.
Monitor construction progress: review and approve payment applications, change orders, claims; validate cost back-up; ensure alignment with budget and owner’s interest.
Implement quality assurance and commissioning processes; ensure as-built documentation, warranties, operations & maintenance handover and asset lifecycle considerations.
Lead stakeholder engagement: provide executive‐level updates to board/council, prepare capital project reports, highlight KPIs (cost per m², schedule adherence, change-order %, sustainability metrics, Indigenous employment/contracting %).
Manage sustainability, supplier diversity and Indigenous involvement mandates (embedding design and procurement criteria accordingly).
Ensure compliance with health‐care facility standards (if applicable), building codes, safety regulations, environmental requirements, and owner’s internal standards.
Mentor and lead a team of project managers, cost/schedule controllers, and admin staff; build capacity internally to elevate capital delivery maturity.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Architecture, Construction Management or equivalent; Master's degree an asset.
Minimum 10 years of capital project delivery experience (≥ CAD $10 million+ portfolio preferred) in commercial, healthcare, infrastructure or First Nations contexts.
Demonstrated experience acting as Owner’s Representative or equivalent agency/owner’s-advisor role. Experience with Procore is an asset.
Strong financial acumen: budget development and control, cash-flow management, cost forecasting, change-order oversight.
Excellent contract and procurement experience: RFP development, bid evaluation, contract negotiation, claims/change-control.
Familiarity with delivery models (Design-Bid-Build, Design-Build, Construction Management) across the full suite of Canadian Construction Documents Committee (CCDC) methods.
Proven track record in stakeholder management, working with indigenous governments, board/council reporting and working in complex governance structures.
Strong leadership, communication, negotiation and problem-solving skills; ability to translate technical/contractual issues into executive-level decisions.
Professional certification (PMP, CCM, or equivalent) and membership in relevant associations an asset.
Experience in deploying and managing projects in Microsoft Project.
Flexibility to travel to project sites and work occasional extended hours as needed.

Key Metrics/Performance Indicators

Percentage of capital projects delivered on time (schedule variance ≤ +5 %).
Percentage of projects delivered within budget (cost variance ≤ +3 %).
Change-order ratio as percent of contract value (target < 5 %).
Indigenous contracting/spend % (for First Nations-partnered projects).
Procurement cycle time (days from RFP to award).
Handover completeness (as‐built documentation, warranty registration, O&M manuals delivered and accepted).

Preferred Attributes

Experience in Canadian health-care infrastructure and Indigenous-government capital partnerships.
Skilled at operating in ambiguity and shaping governance frameworks rather than just execution.
Ability to lead through influence (given many external consultants/contractors).
Track-record of embedding sustainability, resilience and whole-life cost thinking into capital project delivery.

Join us in supporting sustainable aquaculture practices that benefit our community! We value motivated individuals ready to contribute their energy and skills toward meaningful environmental stewardship and community development. This paid position offers a dynamic work environment where your efforts directly impact local prosperity.

jobs.description:
Vice President, Property Management

Toronto, ON

The Opportunity

Reporting to the Managing Director, Residential Services, the Vice President, Property Management provides strategic and operational leadership across BGO’s residential property management platform. The role is responsible for driving financial and operational performance, resident experience, and key initiatives in support of client and company objectives.

The Vice President provides leadership and guidance to residential teams to ensure service standards are maintained and established programs, policies, and operating practices are consistently executed.

This is an onsite position located in Toronto, ON.

What You Will Do

Residential Operations & Performance

Provide strategic and operational leadership for residential property management operations, including general operations, maintenance, resident experience, administration, capital management and financial performance.
Lead the preparation and review of strategic business and operating plans for residential properties and identify opportunities to improve operational and financial performance.
Provide leadership to Directors, Regional Property Managers and other senior property management leaders within the assigned scope.
Ensure accountability for financial results and KPIs against annual budgets and established business targets.
Provide guidance and direction for accurate, timely and comprehensive property budgets, operating reports and other required reporting.
Drive improvements in property financial performance through analysis of property operations, leasing and marketing activity, rental rates, vacancies, operating expenses and input from property teams.
Lead the review and enhancement of operating practices, policies and procedures and develop new processes where required.
Ensure strong resident communications and relations and maintain appropriate service standards across the residential portfolio.
Ensure compliance with applicable property legislation and regulations and BGO policies and procedures.

Portfolio & Client Leadership

Liaise with property teams to ensure market positioning and strategic direction align with portfolio, client and company objectives.
Maintain strong relationships with internal and external clients and ensure owner objectives are being satisfied within established parameters.
Oversee the onboarding of new properties and development properties into the residential portfolio, ensuring effective transitions.
Support the development of pro-forma budgets and work with the acquisitions team on due diligence for prospective acquisitions and development properties.
Collaborate with Technical Services to ensure capital plans are executed effectively and within established timelines.
Collaborate with Marketing on property marketing plans and initiatives.

Leadership

Provide leadership, direction and senior management expertise to residential leaders and their teams.
Develop and mentor leaders, building accountability and supporting the continued development of talent within the residential business.
Foster collaboration between property teams and corporate/divisional departments and support groups.
Participate in national and regional initiatives to advance property management practices and operational effectiveness.
Maintain strong functional relationships across internal teams and with clients and other external stakeholders.

Business Development

Work alongside the Managing Director and other residential leadership to identify potential new clients and third-party residential property management opportunities.
Build and maintain strong, long-term relationships with existing BGO clients.
Maintain awareness of residential industry trends, market conditions and competitors to identify opportunities for growth.
Represent BGO with clients, prospective clients, industry members and at relevant industry events and networking functions.
Act as an ambassador for BGO’s residential property management offering and organizational values.

Sustainability

Support BGO’s commitment to environmental and social responsibility and the integration of sustainability practices within residential operations.

Who You Are

Key Qualifications

Education - University degree combined with relevant experience.
Experience - Minimum 10 years of progressive experience in property management and real estate operations, including hands-on property management experience and responsibility for multiple properties and large teams.
Licences / Certifications: CPM and/or CMRAO Limited or General License designation supplemented by relevant leadership and industry education is considered an asset
Industry / Functional Knowledge
Experience with new developments, property onboarding and lease-up activity.
Strong knowledge of property management regulations and compliance requirements across Canada

Software: Microsoft Office, Yardi, RentCafé
Strong financial acumen, including budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting and analysis of property performance.
Strong knowledge of residential operations, including leasing, resident experience, property performance and operating requirements.
Demonstrated experience developing and executing property business plans, operating budgets and financial strategies.
Experience supporting acquisitions and development opportunities, including pro-forma budgeting and due diligence.
Experience working with internal and external clients, understanding owner objectives and delivering against business priorities.
Experience identifying and supporting new business and third-party property management opportunities.

Other Skills And Behaviours

Client & Stakeholder Leadership: Builds strong relationships, understands priorities, and communicates effectively with clients and stakeholders.
Influence & Collaboration: Works across functions to build alignment and advance initiatives without direct authority.
Change & Continuous Improvement: Identifies and implements improvements to practices, policies and processes while maintaining effective operations.
Team Leadership & Supervision: Provides clear direction, sets expectations, and leads employees and service providers effectively.
Accountability & Follow-Through: Ensures work meets established standards for quality, safety, timelines and performance.
Work Planning & Delegation: Prioritizes, schedules and delegates work to balance operational needs, team capacity and resident service.
Business Development: Represents the residential business with clients, prospects and internal and external stakeholders.
Police Clearance: A criminal verification check is required for employment.

BGO is a global leader in real estate investment management, partnering with more than 750 institutional clients to invest in and manage high-quality real estate across office, industrial, residential, retail, and hospitality sectors. jobs.title: Associate Director, Funding
jobs.description:
About KV Capital

At KV Capital, we have established ourselves as industry leaders in real estate debt and investment, driven by our unwavering commitment to excellent, trusted partnerships, and innovating solutions. Since our founding in 2006, we have expanded our business across three connected areas of service: real estate private equity, real estate lending, and private equity investments in real estate supply chain businesses. Managing a robust portfolio of +$1.8 billion in funded investments, accompanied by +$1 billion in assets under management, our dedicated team of finance experts is driven by a shared goal to cultivate prosperity for our clients, investment partners, and communities. We have office locations in Edmonton, Calgary, and Toronto, and continue to expand our reach nationally.

Real Estate Debt (“RED”)

Since its inception, our Real Estate Debt division has funded and/or advised on $2.5B+ of commercial deals. We provide financing solutions for land, subdivision financing, multi-family, retail, industrial, office, hospitality, mixed-use properties, and specialty financing, such as equity and structured finance deals.

Role Summary

Reporting to the Vice President, Investment Management, the Associate Director, Funding is responsible for the oversight and execution of the Funding function within the Real Estate Debt division. This includes reviewing and approving conditions precedent, reviewing initial loan fundings and construction progress advances, and coordinating the loan funding process with internal and external stakeholders. The Associate Director, Funding has primary responsibility for credit and transactional oversight of the advances that KV Capital funds towards approved investments. The Associate Director, Funding ensures all funding activity is accurately reflected in KV Capital’s systems and investor reporting, and leads continuous improvement in funding controls, processes, and technology.

Responsibilities

Loan Funding & Coordination
Oversee and perform the final review of conditions precedent prior to initial advances for new mortgage loan investments. This includes title, security documents, insurance, appraisals, environmental and geotechnical reports, cost consultant reports, and equity verification.
Review and approve construction progress advance requests within delegated authority. This includes quantity surveyor and cost consultant reports, cost-to-complete recalculations, holdback review, lien searches, and title sub-searches. Loan program "exception" requests and higher-risk advance requests are escalated to the Vice President, Investment Management, where necessary.
Oversee team members responsible for instructing external solicitors, reviewing solicitor reports, and coordinating funding with borrowers, brokers, legal counsel, consultants, and syndicate and institutional partners.
Ensure fundings are executed in accordance with participation, syndication, servicing, and interlender agreements, including timely partner approvals, funding notices, and pro rata advances.
Review funding packages issued to investors, including KV Mortgage Fund, for accuracy and completeness.
Ensure all loan advances are accurately recorded in the system, enabling proper calculation of LTV, LTC, interest reserves, and remaining commitments.
Work with the Capital Markets and Corporate teams to forecast funding requirements and committed undrawn balances for liquidity planning.
Monitor commitment letter conditions and ongoing covenants throughout the funding period, and flag defaults, budget overruns, or adverse changes in project status.

Builder Lines of Credit (BLOC)
Oversee the credit and transactional administration of the BLOC portfolio from approval through renewal and repayment.
Review underwrites prepared by Origination and Investment Management for new BLOC facilities and renewals. Reviews cover:
Builder track record, experience, and capacity;
Corporate financial statements, tax filings, and work-in-progress schedules;
Guarantor net worth, liquidity, and contingent liabilities;
Inventory levels, absorption, and sales history; and
Market conditions in the builder's target geographies and product types.
Review and approve requests to add projects, lots, or units to existing facilities. Each request is assessed against facility terms, including eligible product types and geographies, per-unit and aggregate sub-limits, spec-to-presale ratios, LTV/LTC, budget reasonability, permits, and title.
Review BLOC draw requests against unit-level budgets, cost-to-complete, and margin or borrowing base requirements.
Monitor ongoing facility compliance, including aggregate limits, speculative unit limits, unit aging and maximum hold periods, concentration limits, and reporting covenants. Recommend curtailments, paydowns, or suspension of availability where warranted.
Oversee unit sale repayments, partial discharges, release prices, and re-advances under revolving availability, ensuring net sale proceeds are applied in accordance with facility terms.
Review amendments, extensions, renewals, and annual reviews of BLOC facilities in coordination with Origination and legal counsel.
Conduct or coordinate periodic site visits and inventory inspections for BLOC facilities.
Recommend enhancements to BLOC program guidelines, documentation, and reporting templates based on portfolio performance and market conditions.

Credit Review & Analysis
Review credit applications on an ongoing basis, separately or in conjunction with Funding responsibilities, to evaluate:
Market value reasonability;
Borrower credibility and repayment ability;
Project feasibility and exit strategy viability; and
Market outlook, economic fundamentals, and risk factors.
Review Letters of Interest, Commitment Letters, and amendments to confirm that funding mechanics are clear and administrable, including advance conditions, holdbacks, reserves, and release provisions.
Identify key risks and mitigants in transactions, ensuring appropriate security and documentation structures.
Support the management of high-risk and distressed files by providing funding history, cost-to-complete analysis, and recommendations on protective advances.

Process Improvement & Compliance
Develop, implement, and maintain funding controls, checklists, and approval matrices to enhance accuracy in funding calculations and approvals.
Ensure compliance with company policies, investor guidelines, KV Mortgage Fund Board resolutions, syndicate agreements, and regulatory, legal, and ethical standards related to funding.
Monitor key operational metrics related to funding processes and recommend strategic improvements.

Special Projects & Strategic Initiatives
Lead or participate in initiatives focused on optimizing funding operations, BLOC administration, and credit analysis methodologies.
Support technology and automation enhancements to streamline funding workflows.
Provide insight and recommendations for special projects, including market research and process improvements.
Support the day-to-day operations of the Funding team by providing mentorship, technical guidance, and assistance to Funding Analysts, including support with work prioritization and ongoing training and development.
Drive team engagement and ensure KVC's culture and values are embedded within the Funding team.

Requirements

jobs.title: Chief Administration Officer
jobs.description:
Trusted Leadership. Public Service That Matters. A Special Place To Live.

An opportunity to support an elected Board, lead a complex public service organization and make a lasting contribution to communities across central Vancouver Island.

With the upcoming retirement of the current Chief Administrative Officer, the Regional District of Nanaimo (RDN) is seeking an accomplished, forward-thinking executive to serve as its next Chief Administrative Officer (CAO).

Located on the central east coast of Vancouver Island, the RDN encompasses the City of Nanaimo, the District of Lantzville, the City of Parksville and the Town of Qualicum Beach, together with seven electoral areas extending from Cassidy in the south to Bowser in the north, and from the Strait of Georgia coast and Gabriola, DeCourcy and Mudge Islands in the east to the edge of Cathedral Grove and Nanaimo Lakes in the west.

Situated within the traditional territories of several first nations, including Snuneymuxw, Snaw-Naw-As and Qualicum First Nations, the RDN recognizes the rich cultural heritage of these communities and the importance of respectful, collaborative relationships.

Home to approximately 170,000 residents, the region is experiencing significant growth. Its distinctive combination of urban centres, coastal communities, rural landscapes, and natural environments creates both opportunities and complex decisions about its future.

Few local government executive positions offer this combination of regional complexity, community diversity, and opportunity for meaningful public service.

The Opportunity

Reporting directly to the Regional Board, the CAO serves as the organization's senior administrative leader and principal professional advisor. The successful candidate will work closely with the Board to translate its strategic direction into results, provide sound professional advice, lead a capable administrative team, and strengthen relationships across the region.

The role calls for an executive who understands the complexities of regional governance, including the distinct interests of municipalities and electoral areas, the challenges of growth and infrastructure investment, and the importance of fiscal sustainability and responsive public services.

The Leadership We Are Seeking

The RDN is seeking an accomplished public-sector executive who brings:
Professional courage and integrity
— The judgment to provide measured, independent, and evidence-informed advice, including when that advice may differ from the Board's preferred direction.
Political acuity and relationship-building
— The ability to understand diverse perspectives, build trust and work effectively with elected officials.
Strategic and operational leadership
— The experience to translate Board priorities into organizational results while maintaining financial and operational discipline.
Exceptional communication
— The ability to navigate complex and sensitive issues with clarity, diplomacy, and sound judgment.
Collaborative leadership
— A commitment to supporting the Board's governance role, fostering organizational excellence, and strengthening relationships across the region.

What You Will Bring

You will be a seasoned executive with significant senior leadership experience in local government or a similarly complex public-sector environment.

You will demonstrate:
A strong understanding of local government governance, administration, and financial management.
Proven experience leading multidisciplinary organizations and delivering complex public services.
The ability to support an elected Board with balanced, objective professional advice and sound judgment.
Experience navigating organizational change, community expectations, and competing priorities.
A commitment to transparent, accountable, and effective public administration.
The interpersonal skills to build productive relationships with elected officials, employees, first nations, community partners, and other governments.

Above all, you will bring the maturity, judgment and leadership presence to earn trust, support effective governance, and guide the organization through both opportunities and challenges.

Why the Regional District of Nanaimo?

Few executive leadership opportunities offer this combination of professional challenge, community impact, and lifestyle. The RDN serves a region that brings together growing urban centres, distinctive rural communities, remarkable natural environments, and a strong sense of place. The next CAO will have the opportunity to help shape how the organization responds to growth, infrastructure needs, environmental stewardship, financial sustainability, and evolving community expectations.

For the right leader, this is an opportunity to combine meaningful public service with a rewarding personal and professional life on Vancouver Island.

The salary range for this position is
$281,986 to $323,585 with comprehensive benefits.

December 11, 2026

jobs.title: Director, Finance Business Partner
jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE

When it comes to health, we’re always looking for ways to push for better. It’s why we were founded in the first place. In 1957, our founder, pharmacist William Wilkinson, witnessed a mother sacrifice her health by forgoing her own medicine to pay for her sick daughter’s prescription. He knew there had to be a better way. So, he introduced North America’s first prepaid drug plan, and GreenShield was born as a non-profit with a mission to support better health for all Canadians.
We aren’t just a health and benefits company. We’re the only non-profit social enterprise that brings worlds of coverage and care together, all in one place.
We’re noble challengers, purposefully building a better way and we need the best people to help us create a more holistic approach that takes care of the mind and body.

Our mission is to create better health for all Canadians, and we know that starts with our employees.

THE ROLE IN A NUTSHELL

The Director, Finance Business Partner is a senior strategic advisor accountable for shaping financial performance, decision quality, and value creation across the Payer portfolio, including Insurance, Benefits Administration, Third Party Administration, and Claims Adjudication. Operating at the intersection of strategy, performance, and finance, this role partners closely with the EVP and senior leaders to frame decisions, challenge assumptions, assess trade-offs, and align priorities to enterprise objectives.

The role brings an enterprise-wide, forward-looking perspective—connecting pricing, claims trends, margin, cost, risk, and reinsurance considerations to strategic choices and performance outcomes.

Success in the role requires strong business judgment, influence, and the ability to translate complex financial and insurance insights into clear actions, accountability, and measurable outcomes. Success is measured through stronger decision support, improved financial and insurance performance, earlier visibility to risk and opportunity, and sustained performance improvement across the portfolio.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Advisory & Decision Support

Serve as a trusted advisor to the EVP and senior leaders, shaping decisions through insight, challenge, and clear articulation of trade-offs across growth, margin, cost, and risk.

Financial & Insurance Performance Leadership

Lead planning, forecasting, performance management, and business insight across the portfolio, with a strong focus on pricing, claims trends, margin drivers, cost discipline, operational efficiency, and reinsurance implications.

Performance Improvement & Value Creation

Identify and advance actions that improve performance and value realization, including business cases, scenario analysis, productivity opportunities, and disciplined follow-through on results.

Governance, Integration & Operating Rhythm

Embed financial discipline, transparency, and integrated planning into leadership routines and governance forums, ensuring decisions are informed by sound analysis, clear accountability, and enterprise priorities.

Early Day Objectives & Outcomes

Establish a clear performance baseline and strengthen visibility into the financial and insurance drivers that matter most, including pricing, claims trends, margin, cost, and risk
Improve forecasting, decision support, and leadership insight by aligning financial analysis more closely to business realities and emerging trends
Identify and begin advancing priority actions that improve performance, sharpen accountability, and support value creation across the portfolio

Decision Authority & Scope

Leads financial planning, performance insight, and strategic advisory across the assigned portfolio, shaping priorities, targets, and decision frameworks
Influences enterprise decisions through structured insight and challenge, while execution accountability remains with business leaders

People Leadership

No direct reports initially
Leads through influence in a complex, matrixed environment, building strong partnerships across business lines and functions.

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Bachelor’s degree in finance, Accounting, Business, or a related field; CPA, CFA, ASA, FSA
7–10+ years of progressive experience in finance, FP&A, or strategic business partnering, ideally within insurance, health benefits, or other regulated financial services environments
Strong insurance domain expertise, including pricing, trend analysis, claims and margin drivers, and reinsurance concepts and implications
Strong understanding of revenue, cost, and operational performance drivers, with the ability to translate complex data into actionable business insight
Experience supporting senior leaders, influencing decisions, and leading through complexity in a matrixed organization
Strong analytical judgment, strategic thinking, and ability to assess trade-offs, risks, and opportunities

NICE TO HAVE

MBA preferred

THE CULTURE

We believe a career should be meaningful. Not just a means to earn a living. Our culture is one where everyone's voice is heard and valued. Because that’s what it takes to create better health for all. We dare to challenge the status quo. And we’re driven by people who have challenged theirs. We believe that your workplace should empower you to be the best version of yourself. That’s why we provide a place where you can be inspired, challenged, and rewarded.

Where your growth means our growth.
Where your voice is heard and valued.
Where your work has purpose. And purpose matters.

We believe our people are critical to our overall success. Inclusivity makes us a stronger, smarter and more informed organization. Being intentionally inclusive of diverse backgrounds, perspectives and experiences will enhance our company culture to positively impact how we support our communities. A career at GreenShield isn’t just about personal achievements, it's about making a difference together.

Here’s to Better Health for All!
A FEW MORE DETAILS

Proficiency in English is required for this position. As part of this role, you will be required to communicate with colleagues or customers who use English as their primary language. By requiring English proficiency for this position, we aim to ensure that our employees can excel in their roles, collaborate, and communicate effectively, and contribute to the success of our organization.
GS supports diversity, equity and inclusion in our teams and communities, and we value the unique contributions made by all. Even if your experience doesn’t align perfectly to every requirement, we invite you to apply. jobs.title: Senior Director - Performance Marketing (Remote)
jobs.description:
Ready to own Puffy’s $1M+ monthly ad budget and use AI to decide which campaigns to launch and where to spend more to grow sales profitably?

Total annual cash compensation:
Up to USD $240,000 + comprehensive benefits
Base salary up to USD $200,000/year + monthly performance bonus of up to 20% of base
Location:
Remote (Global)

Potential career path:
Senior Director – Performance Marketing → VP of Performance Marketing → Chief Marketing Officer.

Career progression that takes 4-5 years elsewhere can happen in 1-2 years here for high performers.

The Opportunity:

Puffy is a technology-driven e-commerce business with over $1 billion in lifetime sales, powered by analytics, data and artificial intelligence.Our teams bring together software development, quality assurance, machine learning and AI, marketing, design, conversion rate optimisation, talent augmentation, HR, operations, legal, finance and customer success.

Reporting directly to the CEO, you’ll lead paid media across Google and Meta, owning capital allocation, measurement, creative testing and the performance marketing team. You’ll use AI to support analysis and challenge spending decisions, applying your commercial judgment to decide where to scale, hold or pull back. You’ll build the decision systems that help the team act consistently and remain accountable for growing sales while protecting contribution margin.

The Problems You'll Own:

Primary: Decide what to launch and where the budget goes:
A multi-million-dollar monthly budget runs across Google and Meta, and every standard campaign type is already live and optimized: brand and non-brand search, PMax, Meta prospecting and retargeting, Shopping and feed. Growth now has to come from what isn't running: new campaign structures, new creative, a different mix of spend.

Secondary: Build the system that runs the scaling decisions:
Design and document the rules that govern spend, when to pause, when to increase budget, when to pull back, and the measurement each decision depends on. The system should run the scaling without day-to-day executive oversight.

What You'll Own:

Capital allocation:
Allocate multi-million-dollar monthly budgets across Google and Meta based on what the next dollar earns, not average platform-reported return on ad spend (ROAS). Bring a weekly recommendation to the CEO showing where to move spend, the expected return and the risks.
Measurement and profitability:
Own one view of paid media performance. Reconcile platform attribution with actual orders and revenue, track the marketing efficiency ratio (MER), and use incrementality tests to see which sales ads actually caused. Measure contribution margin after product returns and financing costs.
Bidding and budget rules:
Build and document rules for bidding, budget limits, and when to pause, hold, scale or pull back. Specify how much evidence each decision needs and when to escalate. Make the playbook usable by any team member before automating repeatable steps.
Creative testing:
Build a pipeline of concepts and briefs. Label tests so the team can distinguish a new idea from a variation, and analyze what gets viewers to stop and what keeps them watching. Apply those findings to the next round of ads, including user-generated content (UGC) and creator-authorized ads (whitelisting).
Retail promotions:
Plan when to concentrate spend around the retail calendar, how to present financing offers, and which messages shoppers should see from first impression through checkout. Test whether a promotion adds profitable sales.
New campaigns and channels:
Launch new structures and creative on Google and Meta. Identify paid channels beyond them, rank each opportunity by its investment case, and design pilots with a budget, a success measure and a clear decision to stop or scale.
Team leadership:
Set priorities, coach and assess senior direct reports and specialists, and develop the skills the function needs. Work with Analytics on measurement and the creative team on briefs. Recommend hires, reporting lines or restructuring to the CEO for sign-off.
AI-assisted decisions:
Use AI to diagnose performance, compare spending scenarios, develop creative concepts, and prepare forecasts and reports. Link the AI review in every proposal to the CEO. Check calculations and creative claims against their sources and own the final recommendation.

In your first year, put the budget rules, measurement and testing routines into use. Start with a baseline and agree targets with the CEO. You can change targeting, bids, creative priorities and spend within approved limits; escalate material risks early and get approval before increasing total spend, committing unallocated funds to a new channel or changing commercial guardrails.

What This Can Mean for Your Career:

Your model informs how much capital the CEO commits to growth next quarter. As you prove where additional spend turns into profit, your scope can expand across the paid channels you select and bring capital allocation, creative strategy and P&L ownership together.

What You'll Need:

7+ years in performance marketing, with sustained ownership of at least $1M per month on Google and at least $1M per month on Meta, concurrently or across roles. Ownership means you controlled strategy, campaign structure and budget, even when your team handled execution.
Hands-on Google Ads experience in the PMax era: campaign structure, Shopping feed management, and the different economics of brand and non-brand search.
Experience marketing purchases with average order values of $1,000 or more, where conversions are infrequent and customers take time to decide.
A bidding, budgeting and pause playbook you personally built at scale, rather than inherited. Be ready to present it and explain the business results of a decision you made with it.
The ability to design incrementality tests, set thresholds and decide when there is enough conversion data to act. Explain how you weigh stopping a promising test too early against wasting spend.
Experience running creative tests at scale since Apple’s App Tracking Transparency (ATT) changes, separating concepts from variations and using creative performance data to decide what to test next.
Experience managing senior direct reports and building or restructuring a performance marketing team. Be ready to show what improved through your leadership and coaching.
A structured way to select a new paid channel, set a pilot budget and decide in advance what evidence would justify stopping or expanding the test.
Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed.

Good to Have:

Experience scripting against the Meta and Google Ads APIs, or using Google Ads Scripts.
Experience in both agency and in-house performance marketing teams.
Experience with emerging paid channels such as TikTok, connected TV or affiliate partnerships.
Direct-to-consumer e-commerce experience in home goods, furniture or another high-order-value category.

The Resources to Build On:

Puffy has been AI-first since December 2023. You’ll have company-provided AI tools, including ChatGPT and Claude, AI agents, bots, plugins, AI projects and automations through platforms such as n8n.You’ll also receive relevant department tools, data, assets and specialist support. Use them to challenge a forecast against actual orders and costs before you put the team’s budget behind it.

The Puffy DNA:

We’re ambitious, fast-paced and focused on turning ideas into results.
Be the Owner:
Take responsibility for outcomes and follow work through completion.
Execute with Urgency:
Make thoughtful decisions quickly and act decisively.
Demand Excellence:
Solve difficult problems and keep improving your craft.
Be AI-First:
Use multi-turn AI conversations to challenge assumptions and improve your work.
Go All-In:
Work together when the mission demands it.

✨ Your Total Compensation & Benefits:

💰 Compensation:
Total Annual Package: Up to USD $240,000 + comprehensive benefits (Base salary + monthly performance bonus of up to 20% of base)

Annual salary review every January
🏥 Health & Protection:
Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance (based on country of hire)
🌴 Time Off:
Generous Paid Time Off (PTO) + Public holidays

💼 Work Environment:

AI-First organization with access to AI-native tool stack
Remote First: Work from the comfort of your home office
Learning & development opportunities
International team collaboration across 16+ nationalities. Your assumptions get challenged daily.

🏆 Rewards & Recognition:

Eligibility for selection to the Leaders Club, an elite recognition program featuring premium wellness memberships, exclusive networking with senior leadership, and annual leadership retreats
Eligibility for nomination as 'We Are' Champion of the Month, monthly recognition with gift vouchers and company-wide celebration for exceptional contributions

Ready to Put Your Paid Media Expertise to Work?

Click “Apply” to submit your application. Tell us about a Google or Meta budget decision you owned: why you increased, held or cut spend, how you used AI to test your assumptions, and how you verified the impact on sales and contribution margin.

jobs.title: Director, Issuing Solutions Sales & Business Development
jobs.description:
About Us 
Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid.

 At Visa, you'll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world.

 Join Visa and do work that matters – to you, to your community, and to the world. Progress starts with you.

 Job Description 

 The Director, Issuing Solutions Sales & Business Development, Canada will be responsible for accelerating the growth of Visa's Value-Added Services business across the Canadian market. 

 This is a client-facing commercial role combining sales, business development, market development and consultative solution selling. The Director will identify new opportunities, build qualified pipeline, develop senior client relationships, shape solutions and actively advance opportunities through the sales cycle to deliver commercial outcomes. 

 The successful candidate will operate at the intersection of client strategy, technology and sales execution. They will engage Canadian issuers to understand strategic priorities and business challenges, identify whitespace, lead client discovery, develop compelling business cases and solution strategies, and bring together the appropriate Visa capabilities to address client needs. 

 Working closely with Visa's Account Executives, Specialist Sellers, Product, Visa Consulting & Analytics (VCA), Solutions Engineering and other cross-functional partners, this individual will help clients navigate opportunities across Visa's evolving portfolio while maintaining clear accountability for pipeline creation, sales execution and revenue growth. 

 The role requires a hands-on commercial leader who is equally comfortable creating an opportunity, shaping the solution and selling the value proposition. 
 Essential Functions 

 Sales & Commercial Execution 
 Develop, own and advance a pipeline of Issuing Solutions opportunities across Canada, with accountability for revenue growth and commercial outcomes. 
 Lead client engagements throughout the sales cycle, including prospecting, discovery, opportunity qualification, solution positioning, business-case development, commercial discussions and close. 
 Build and maintain senior-level relationships across existing and prospective Canadian issuer clients. 
 Proactively uncover new client needs and translate those needs into actionable sales opportunities. 
 Develop compelling value propositions and commercial narratives that connect Visa capabilities to measurable client business outcomes. 
 Partner closely with Visa Account Executives and Specialist Sellers to establish account strategies, coordinate client engagement and progress opportunities. 
 Maintain strong sales discipline around pipeline management, forecasting, opportunity progression, risks and next steps. 

 Client Discovery & Solution Development 
 Lead structured client discovery to understand strategic priorities, operational challenges, technology environments and modernization needs. 
 Translate client challenges into integrated solution strategies across Visa's broader portfolio rather than approaching clients solely through individual products. 
 Develop client-specific business cases that clearly articulate strategic value, expected outcomes and commercial rationale. 
 Provide consultative and technical sales leadership throughout complex opportunities, engaging product and technical specialists when deeper solution expertise is required. 
 Help bridge client strategy, business requirements, Visa capabilities and technical feasibility to accelerate opportunities through the decision-making process. 
 Navigate complex client environments involving multiple decision-makers and business and technology stakeholders. 

 Canada Market Development & Go-to-Market 
 Identify whitespace across Visa's Canadian issuer relationships and translate that whitespace into targeted commercial opportunities. 
 Develop account-level and market-level go-to-market strategies reflecting the unique structure and dynamics of the Canadian payments ecosystem. 
 Create qualified opportunities across Pismo, Verifi, VCA, fraud and risk, digital enablement, network solutions, post-purchase experiences and other relevant Visa capabilities. 
 Develop executive relationships that position Visa as a strategic business and technology partner. 
 Identify emerging client needs and market trends and translate those insights into actionable sales strategies. 
 Bring Canadian market and client insights back into Visa to help inform commercialization strategies, product priorities and future go-to-market approaches. 
 Work across Visa's broader organization to create coordinated client strategies and bring the appropriate resources and expertise to priority opportunities.  

 Leadership Profile 

 The ideal candidate will combine the commercial drive of a seller, the structured thinking of a consultant and the solution orientation of a sales engineer. 

 This individual should be comfortable walking into an issuer with an open-ended business challenge, leading discovery, identifying where Visa has a credible right to play, developing the business case, mobilizing product and technical expertise, advancing commercial discussions and ultimately helping close the business. 

 The successful candidate will have a builder mindset and strong sales orientation. They will be energized by identifying opportunities that are not yet fully formed and creating the strategy, relationships and internal alignment necessary to convert those opportunities into revenue. 

 Key Measures of Success 

 Success in this role will be demonstrated through: 
 Building and converting a healthy pipeline of Canadian Issuing Solutions opportunities. 
 Generating new sales and contributing directly to Canada revenue objectives. 
 Identifying previously untapped whitespace within Visa's issuer relationships. 
 Converting discovery and strategic client conversations into qualified commercial opportunities. 
 Developing strong executive relationships across priority Canadian financial institutions. 
 Building compelling business cases and solution strategies for larger, complex or multi-solution opportunities. 
 Accelerating commercial opportunities across Pismo, Verifi, VCA and Visa's broader Value-Added Services portfolio. 
 Strengthening coordination across Account Executives, Specialist Sales, Product, VCA and technical teams. 
 Establishing a scalable foundation for continued growth of Visa's Issuing Solutions business in Canada. 

 Visa requires at least 3 days in office, expectations of these days will be confirmed by your Hiring Manager.

 Qualifications 

 Basic Qualifications 
 Significant experience in sales, business development, market development, management consulting, solution engineering, financial services, payments, fintech or enterprise technology. 
 Demonstrated experience developing and advancing complex B2B sales opportunities. 
 Proven ability to establish and maintain relationships with senior client executives and key decision-makers. 
 Strong commercial orientation with experience identifying potential opportunities, developing value propositions and progressing opportunities through a structured sales process. 
 Experience leading client discovery and translating complex business challenges into actionable solutions and business cases. 
 Ability to understand technically complex products and effectively connect technology capabilities to business outcomes. 
 Strong communication, executive presentation, negotiation and stakeholder-management skills. 
 Demonstrated ability to operate successfully in a highly matrixed organization and influence across teams without direct authority. 

 Preferred Qualifications 
 Experience within the Canadian banking, payments, fintech or financial-services ecosystem. 
 Experience working directly with financial institutions, issuers, payment processors, fintechs or technology platforms. 
 Demonstrated understanding of the Canadian payments landscape and the dynamics associated with established domestic payment infrastructure. 
 Experience selling or developing opportunities involving payments technology, issuer processing, digital payments, fraud and risk, consulting or other enterprise technology solutions. 
 Experience combining commercial selling with consultative discovery and solution-oriented sales methodologies. 
 Demonstrated ability to build new markets, develop whitespace opportunities or commercialize emerging solutions. 
 Ability to work comfortably across business, product and technology stakeholders. 

 Visa is an EEO Employer 
 Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status. Visa will also consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with EEOC guidelines and applicable local law.

 Visa welcome and encourages application from persons with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process.

jobs.description:
Job Description 

 What will you do? 
 Governance Frameworks & Accountabilities: Develop and maintain enterprise AI risk governance frameworks and guidance aligned with RBC's Enterprise Risk Management Framework and applicable policies. Clarify accountabilities, decision rights and escalation expectations across business and technology teams, supporting clear ownership of AI risks within each business, function and technology domain.
 Governance Guidance & Advisory: Interpret policy and advise on emerging AI governance questions in partnership with Legal, Privacy, Security, Model Risk, Data Governance and other specialist teams. Translate complex requirements into clear enterprise guidance and advise accountable owners on how to apply it across the AI lifecycle.
 Governance Forums & Decision-Making: Support the Enterprise AI Risk Council through decision papers and follow-up on commitments, and guide business and functional AI risk councils on decision authority, risk triage and escalation. Partner with AI Risk Champions to promote consistent interpretation of enterprise guidance.
 AI Risk Assessment Governance & Improvement: Guide the evolution of AI risk assessment approaches across the enterprise and support business and functional owners in establishing and operationalizing AI risk governance. Partner with assessment, technology and operational teams to make assessments more consistent, proportionate and effective.
 AI Taxonomy & Governance Evolution: Partner with AI Architecture and relevant business, technology and risk teams to develop AI terminology, taxonomy and classification, coordinating enterprise input to ensure consistent definitions and application. Develop related inventory guidance, evolve governance as AI capabilities and risks change and support audit and regulatory responses.
 Team Leadership & Partnerships: Lead and develop the governance team, set priorities and coach colleagues. Build effective partnerships across business, technology and risk functions to align governance expectations and support informed risk decisions.

What do you need to succeed? 
 Must-have
 Experience in risk management, governance or a control function within a complex organization, with strong knowledge of enterprise governance, technology risk and regulatory expectations.
 Demonstrated experience developing or enhancing governance frameworks and translating policy requirements into practical guidance, clear accountabilities and decision-making processes.
 Sound judgement in ambiguous situations, with the ability to evaluate emerging technology risks and develop practical recommendations.
 Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills, including experience resolving competing priorities across business, technology and risk teams.
 Strong executive communication skills, including written recommendations, decision papers, governance materials and presentations.
 People leadership experience, including coaching colleagues, setting priorities and leading initiatives across functions.
 Undergraduate degree in finance, business, computer science, engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
 Nice-to-have
 Data governance experience, including data ownership, quality, lineage and controls.
 Knowledge of software development lifecycle practices and related risk and control requirements.
 Experience with AI governance, AI risk assessment or the risks of generative and agentic AI.
 Experience as a business process owner or leading improvements to risk assessment processes.
 A relevant risk, audit or AI governance designation, such as CRISC, CISA, CISSP or AIGP.

 We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.
 The opportunity to shape enterprise AI governance and support the responsible use of AI across RBC.
 Work with business, technology and specialist risk teams on emerging AI challenges.

 Leaders who support your development through coaching and managing opportunities.

jobs.title: Head of Data and AI, Wealth Management Canada
jobs.description:
Job Description 

 What is the opportunity? 
 Wealth Management is seeking a Head of Data and AI to set the scientific direction and lead the applied AI research and development agenda for our Canadian business. As the senior AI scientist and technical authority on our Wealth Management Data and AI team, you will decide how we solve ML and AI problems rigorously, and how we prove the results are accurate, safe and valuable to advisors and clients.

 We are looking for a deeply technical AI leader with a research-grade understanding of modern machine learning and generative AI, and a track record of turning that science into production systems at scale. You will lead and grow a team of AI scientists, ML researchers, data scientists and ML engineers, partner closely with product, technology and business leaders across Wealth Management and RBC, and work with RBC’s broader AI research community to bring frontier techniques into the hands of advisors.

 ​ What will you do? 
 Define and own the AI/ML science roadmap for Wealth Management Canada, covering generative AI, agentic systems, predictive modelling, personalization, forecasting and optimization.
 Identify where emerging research (foundation models, reasoning, retrieval, agents, multimodal, small and fine-tuned models) can create a durable advantage in wealth management, and turn it into funded, testable bets.
 Make build, buy and fine-tune decisions on models, architectures and platforms based on evidence, benchmarking and a clear view of cost, latency, risk and performance.
 Represent Wealth Management’s AI science externally and across RBC, including partnerships with research institutes, universities and technology partners.
 Provide hands-on technical leadership across the model lifecycle: problem framing, data and feature design, training, fine-tuning, prompting and orchestration, evaluation, deployment and monitoring.
 Establish the standards for experimental design, offline and online evaluation, A/B testing and statistical validity, so that results are reproducible and claims are defensible.
 Build robust evaluation frameworks for LLM and agent-based systems, including accuracy, groundedness, hallucination, bias, robustness and red-teaming, tied to real advisor workflows.
 Review the technical work of scientists and engineers, coach them on research quality, and raise the bar on how models are designed, tested and explained.
 Own the scientific approach to responsible AI in a regulated environment, including explainability, fairness, privacy, safety guardrails, model risk and ongoing performance monitoring.
 Work with Model Risk, Legal, Compliance, Privacy and Technology to translate emerging regulation and internal policy into practical technical controls and validation methods.
 Communicate model capabilities, limitations and uncertainty clearly and honestly to senior leaders, regulators and non-technical stakeholders.
 Develop and retain AI scientists, researchers and ML engineers, and create a culture of curiosity, scientific debate and learning by experimentation.
 Create career paths and mentoring for technical talent, and build a strong research-to-production pipeline with engineering and product partners.
 Champion a test-and-learn approach where hypotheses, experiments and data drive decisions, and where failed experiments are shared and learned from.
 Define the data requirements AI needs to succeed, and partner with data and technology teams on high-quality domains, a consistent data dictionary and a unified client view that serve both AI and operational use cases.
 Work with product and business leaders across Global Wealth Management, WMC and RBC to translate advisor and client problems into well-posed scientific questions, and scientific results into shipped products.

 What do you need to succeed? 
 Must-have: 
 Advanced degree (Master’s required, PhD strongly preferred) in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Engineering or a related quantitative field;
 8+ years of experience building and applying machine learning and AI, including leading scientists or researchers in a top-tier technology company, research lab or leading financial institution;
 Deep, hands-on expertise in modern ML and generative AI, including LLMs, retrieval-augmented generation, agentic systems, fine-tuning and evaluation, with a strong grounding in statistics and experimental design;
 A track record of research or applied-science impact, such as peer-reviewed publications, patents, open-source contributions or production models that moved a business metric;
 Proven ability to take models from prototype to production in an enterprise environment, with working knowledge of MLOps, scalable data and compute platforms, and model monitoring;
 Experience with responsible AI, explainability, model risk management and AI governance, ideally in a regulated industry;
 Strong leadership skills, with experience hiring, coaching and leading high-calibre scientific and engineering talent;
 Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to explain complex scientific concepts and trade-offs to executives and non-technical stakeholders;

 Nice-to-have: 
 Understanding of the banking industry, preferably Wealth Management, is an asset.

 What's in it for you? 
 We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

jobs.description:
Overview:

When our square shaped burgers made their first sizzle on the scene more than 50 years ago, people knew our approach wasn’t like any other. Same goes for the way we support our employees. Our culture of openness, flexibility, and inclusiveness allows everybody to flourish in their own way. If you’re looking for a career where you can be part of the action as we continue to grow our iconic brand – We got you!  

Yes, Wendy’s really serves only fresh, never frozen beef in all of our restaurants throughout Canada, and Wendy's is looking for the person who wants to help buy that beef (and all the other good stuff we need in Wendy’s restaurants)! The Director – Canadian Procurement will contribute to the growth and profitability of The Wendy’s Company and their Canadian franchisees by leading purchasing strategies, optimizing programs and processes, and building supplier relationships. They will act as Wendy’s Restaurants of Canada’s brand liaison and procurement subject matter expert, whilst leading a team of category managers that has responsibility for the full scope of categories (food, packaging, and indirect). This individual is an experienced procurement professional and will provide strong leadership in the areas of strategy, cost management, commodity program development, supplier management, project management and internal/external customer service. Additionally, they will ensure timely supply of high\-quality products, while focusing on cost reduction initiatives and strategies to move categories forward and ensure no one has to ask, “Where’s the Beef?”
Responsibilities:
* In consultation with the Vice President of Canadian Supply Chain, develop and implement 3\-5 year sourcing strategies for assigned categories. Manage sourcing processes for assigned categories, in order to ensure an uninterrupted supply of products and services. Guarantee that materials meet or exceed Wendy’s, QSCC, industry, and CFIA regulations and guidelines.
* Create a cross\-functional working environment to engage suppliers, internal key stakeholders – both Wendy’s and QSCC – and other strategic development partners in order to drive continuous innovation.
* Understand various industry and product dynamics, such as influential component prices, seasonality, demand, menu changes, trends, forecasting, and industry and business trends. Develop forward\-thinking strategies to drive cost certainty/predictability/savings for franchisees.
* Cultivate and sustain strategic supplier partnerships that drive mutual value, foster collaboration, and consistently reflect the organization's values and high ethical standards..
* Develop and implement key performance metrics for the category, including supplier partnerships. Conduct benchmarking activities, business reviews and evaluation programs for assigned categories
* Evaluates supplier capabilities, operations, and product offerings to identify opportunities for value creation, risk mitigation, quality improvement, and supply continuity. Conducts supplier site visits, distribution center assessments, and restaurant field visits to assess performance, strengthen supplier partnerships, and ensure alignment with business requirements.
* Lead, develop, and inspire a high\-performing team by setting clear expectations, fostering accountability, and aligning individual contributions with organizational objectives. Serve as a coach and mentor to employees and leaders, building capabilities, supporting career growth, and cultivating a culture of continuous learning and development.
* Other duties as assigned


Qualifications:
* Minimum of eight years of experience in Protein Procurement and Supply Chain Management (strongly preferred).
* Bachelor’s Degree in Business, Supply Chain Management or Logistics (or equivalent combination of education and experience). MBA in Economics, Supply Chain or Finance preferred.
* Demonstrated understanding of (Commodity) Risk Management programs and strategies.
* Demonstrated understanding of end\-to\-end Supply Chain, including programs, distribution \& logistics, procurement, QA, culinary, and commercialization.
* Broad understanding of the Foodservice Industry and supplier community.
* Elevated standards related to communication and customer service. Experience communicating with and influencing senior\-level leadership.
* Informed and up to date on US and Canadian government and industry regulations and guidelines.
* Intuitive and strategic thinker.

 **Expected Work Location (In Office)**: It is expected that you will primarily perform work at the Wendy's Canadian Restaurant Support Center 5515 North Service Rd STE 201 Burlington ON L7L 6G4 Canada or at other location(s) as designated by the Company. You are required to work in the office at least 3 days a week. Changes to work location arrangements are subject to managerial approval and business needs. \#LI\-Onsite  

Wendy’s was built on the premise, "Quality is our Recipe®," which remains the guidepost of the Wendy's system. Today, Wendy's and its franchisees employ hundreds of thousands of people across more than 7,000 restaurants worldwide with a vision of becoming the world's most thriving and beloved restaurant brand.

Job Type & Duration:
Full-time, Permanent

Shift Information:
Monday to Friday, 35 hours per week

Affiliation: Non-represented

1

Position Description

The Director of Finance is a senior finance leader responsible for the integrity, stewardship, and governance of ESA’s financial operations and financial reporting. This role ensures accurate and timely accounting, compliance with statutory and regulatory requirements, effective cash and balance sheet management, and robust internal controls. They will be responsible for all day-to-day finance operations, including functional responsibility over general accounting, accounts payable, accounts receivable, pension administration, treasury, investments.

The Director of Finance is responsible for audit readiness by ensuring robust policies, systems, and procedures are in place, and by supporting the external audit process as required.

In addition, the Director of Finance will partner with the CFO, senior leadership, and staff to improve progam or process integration to enhance efficiently and effectiveness in achieving program objectives, In relation to any system or process changes, the Director of Finance will collaborate with respective business areas to positively impact design and operational effectiveness in support of business objectives as well as financial and management reporting objectives.

Role Description

Financial Accounting and Reporting

Provide financial and accounting leadership for ESA’s Finance function and business areas. Oversee all accounts, ledgers, and reporting systems and changes thereto, ensuring continued compliance with appropriate GAAP standards and regulatory requirements.
Design and maintain internal controls and safeguards related to revenue (billings and receipts) and expenditures.
Oversee the preparation and integrity of monthly, quarterly and annual financial reports in accordance with GAAP.
Lead the month end and year end close processes, ensuring timeliness, completeness, and accuracy.
Lead the annual ESA external financial statement audit, including planning, fieldwork and reporting while keeping the CFO apprised of any issues on a timely basis.
Develop, maintain, and enforce accounting policies, procedures and documentation, maintaining an appropriate audit trail for the external auditors.
Monitor and assess potential changes in NFPO accounting standards and or gaps in ESA’s accounting policies and provide data driven, clear guidance and recommendations to the CFO.
Prepare materials for Board/A&IC briefings as part of regular quarterly meetings and/or as required.

Internal Controls, Compliance and Audit

Design, implement, and maintain a strong internal control framework over financial reporting.
Ensure compliance with statutory, regulatory, tax, and reporting requirements.
Act as the primary liaison with external auditors, regulators, and other external stakeholders on accounting and control matters.
Lead the preparation of audit schedules and support external audit activities through to successful completion.
Identify, assess, and mitigate financial reporting and operational financial risks.

Accounts payable and Accounts Receivable

Provide strategic and operational oversight of the accounts payable and accounts receivable functions.
Ensure efficient, accurate, and timely processing of vendor payments and customer billings and collections.
Establish and monitor key controls over disbursements, collections, credit management, and reconciliations.
Oversee the management of aged receivables and support resolution of complex or escalated issues.
Continuously improve processes to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and compliance.
Collaborate with cross-functional business areas on review of manual journal entries.

Treasury, Cash Management & Banking

Oversee daily cash management, bank relationships, and banking structures.
Ensure appropriate controls over cash receipts, disbursements, and account reconciliations.
Monitor liquidity and working capital from an operational and control perspective, in alignment with CFO direction.
Authorize banking arrangements and ensure compliance with signing authorities and delegated limits outlined in the Organizational Authority Registrar.

Investments Oversight (Outsourced Chief Investment Officer Governance)

Provide financial governance and oversight of ESA’s investment activities managed by an outsourced Chief Investment Officer (OCIO), in accordance with approved investment policies, mandates, and governance frameworks.
Act as the secondary finance liaison with the OCIO to ensure the accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of investment‑related financial information and reporting. The CFO is the primary point of contact for investment-related activities.
Review and assess investment valuations, and accounting treatments prepared under the OCIO’s management for compliance with applicable accounting standards and investment policies.
Monitor adherence to internal controls related to investment transactions, custody, valuation, and financial disclosures, including controls executed by the OCIO and third‑party service providers.
Coordinate with the OCIO, custodians, external managers, actuaries (where applicable), and auditors to support audit activities and regulatory reporting related to investments.
Ensure appropriate investment disclosures are prepared for financial statements
Support the CFO and relevant board committee by conducting a detailed review of quarterly reports provided by the outsourced Chief Investment Officer (OCIO). This includes assessing the completeness, accuracy, and clarity of reporting related to portfolio performance, asset allocation, valuation methodologies, compliance with the Investment Policy Statement, and key risk exposures.
Liaise with the OCIO to obtain clarifications, supplemental analysis, or follow‑up information as required to support informed oversight and governance discussions at the committee level.

Pension And Other Post Employment Benefits Accounting

Oversee accounting, reporting, and compliance related to pension plans and post‑employment benefits.
Liaise with external actuaries, pension administrators, and external auditors on valuation, disclosures, and funding matters.
Ensure accurate recording of pension assets, liabilities, expenses, and associated disclosures.
Support governance and oversight of pension plans in accordance with applicable legislation and policies.

Payroll

Provide strategic leadership and oversight over ESA’s payroll function, with operational payroll processing executed by senior payroll professionals.
Set strategic direction, governance standards, and control expectations for payroll operations to ensure accuracy, compliance, and consistency.
Establish and maintain ESA’s payroll policy.
Ensure robust internal controls are designed, implemented, and operating effectively over payroll processing, payroll changes, reconciliations, and access management to ESA’s payroll system.
Oversee payroll accounting and financial integrity, including review of payroll reconciliations and confirmation of accurate recording of payroll‑related expenses, liabilities, and accruals.
Review and challenge escalated payroll issues, exceptions, or control matters, approving resolution approaches and escalating material risks to the CFO as appropriate.
Sponsor continuous improvement initiatives related to payroll systems, processes, controls, and reporting to enhance efficiency, risk management, and employee experience.

People Management

Lead, mentor, and develop a high performing finance team.
Set clear performance expectations and foster a culture of accountability, accuracy, and continuous improvement and customer service to cross-functional business units

Other

Effectively represent the Finance team as a Senior Management Team Member on board committees or internal committees as required.

Qualifications

CPA designation required
Strong oral and written communication skills.
At least 10-12 years of progressive experience in accounting and finance.
Demonstrated experience in financial reporting, internal controls, accounts payable, accounts receivable, investments and pension accounting.
Experience supervising a team of finance professionals.
Experience with non-government not for profit accounting and a solid knowledge and

understanding of GAAP and accounting for pensions.

Analytic, organization, and problem-solving skills for strategic data interpretation.
Strong emotional intelligence and self-awareness is essential.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills required to effectively communicate complex

issues to senior leadership.

The ability to translate complex financial concepts to individuals at all levels including finance and non-finance managers.
Requires demonstrated listening and negotiating skills and the ability to work effectively with people inside and outside the organization to achieve the required results.

Winnipeg Foundation is For Good. Forever. We help people give back to our shared community by connecting generous donors with causes they care about For Good. The Opportunity

This new position will report to the Vice President, Community Impact. TWF is seeking a Director of Endow Manitoba to lead the Endow Manitoba program and related provincial initiatives that strengthen the sustainability, effectiveness, and growth of Manitoba’s community foundations.The successful incumbent will be a strategic, people-focused leader and relationship builder with strong communication, financial, analytical, project management, and decision-making skills.The Director will be accountable for the development, implementation, evaluation, and continuous improvement of provincial capacity-building programs and ensure that Endow Manitoba remains responsive to emerging opportunities, risks funding requirements, and long-term sector needs.
