At Crescent Hotels & Resorts, we are a team of hospitality professionals that are deeply connected to & proud of the exceptional experiences we provide for our guests. More than that, we know our Associates are the shining stars of what we do! We understand what it takes to be a part of something great. We will encourage you to bring your true self to work every day, we will celebrate you and we will cheer you on as you shine bright in your career journey. Whether it be our health & wellness programs, best in class learning and development or our travel discounts that ‘feed your inner explorer’, we work hard to create and deliver on what YOU need. We are ready for you to start your journey with us where You Belong. We Care. Shine Bright.

We Are Looking For Our Next Great Team Leader To Join Us On Our Food & Beverage Team. We Are Committed To Providing You With

Competitive wages - An annual salary of $120,000
An exceptional benefit plan for eligible associates & your family members
RRSP matching program (for eligible associates)
Flexible scheduling to allow you to focus on what is important to you
Discounts with our Crescent-managed properties in North America for you & your family members
Discounts with Marriott properties globally for you & your family members
Eligible associates will receive a seasonal ski pass benefit
The opportunity to work at a luxury ski-in/ski-out resort, experience an incredible winter season, and be part of the vibrant community at RED Mountain

Position Summary

The Director of Food & Beverage leads the dining and beverage experience across RED Mountain Resort and The Josie Hotel, from mountain dining and après-ski to upscale restaurant service, weddings and special events.

This hands-on leadership role brings people, service and operations together to create memorable guest experiences, grow the business and build strong teams. The Director will help shape the future of both properties by strengthening standards, developing talent and finding opportunities to work smarter together while preserving each property's unique character.

Major Responsibilities

Top Priorities

Stabilize daily F&B operations and establish clear management routines across both RED Mountain Resort and The Josie Hotel.
Deliver consistent service, culinary quality, atmosphere and cleanliness across every outlet and event, while respecting the different service expectations of mountain dining and an upscale boutique hotel.
Build an accountable F&B leadership team and a reliable seasonal workforce.
Improve revenue, average cheque, labour productivity, cost of sales and departmental profitability.
Strengthen collaboration among Culinary, Service, Banquets, Sales, Events, Rooms and Finance.
Develop beverage, menu, event and après-ski programs.
Create a positive team culture focused on standards, communication, safety and development.
Build relationships with Rossland producers, suppliers, partners and the local community.
Identify shared purchasing, staffing, training, supplier and operational efficiencies across both businesses.
Develop a cohesive F&B strategy that strengthens the overall RED destination experience while maintaining the distinct positioning of each outlet.

Food and Beverage Leadership

Lead the F&B business plan, budget, forecast, service strategy and operating priorities for both businesses, with separate financial accountability and reporting for each.
Maintain visible leadership during peak periods, special events, après-ski and service recovery.
Lead daily and weekly meetings covering forecasts, staffing, reservations, events, product and guest feedback.
Set clear accountability for restaurant, lounge, banquet, culinary, stewarding and beverage leaders.
Provide timely operating updates, risks, results and recommendations to the respective General Managers and senior leadership.
Establish a clear management structure and delegation of responsibilities to ensure both businesses receive consistent leadership and operational oversight.
Work closely with both General Managers to align priorities, resources, budgets and guest experience standards.

Guest Experience And Outlet Operations

Set and inspect standards for greeting, seating, service sequence, menu knowledge, timing, billing and farewell.
Review reservations, covers, groups, events, occupancy, weather and mountain activity to plan each service.
Resolve significant guest concerns, authorize appropriate recovery and correct recurring causes.
Maintain strong outlet presentation, music, lighting, uniforms, cleanliness, equipment and opening and closing controls.
Partner with Rooms and Guest Services on VIPs, amenities, packages, special occasions and in-house communication.
Review guest feedback and online sentiment and turn findings into clear coaching and improvement actions.
Ensure The Josie's F&B operations meet applicable Marriott Autograph Collection brand standards and guest expectations.
Develop distinct service standards appropriate to each outlet, from casual mountain dining to elevated restaurant and hotel experiences.

Culinary and Beverage Partnership

Partner with culinary leaders on menu development, quality, consistency, food cost, production and kitchen execution.
Ensure menus balance guest appeal, local identity, seasonality, operational capacity and financial return.
Lead beverage strategy, pricing, purchasing, inventory, controls, supplier relationships and team education.
Review menu mix, contribution, waste, yields, portioning and availability; act quickly on performance gaps.
Coordinate menu and beverage changes with training, point-of-sale updates, marketing, signage and launch plans.
Identify opportunities to leverage combined purchasing volumes, supplier agreements and beverage partnerships across RED and The Josie.
Oversee the development of distinctive wine, cocktail and beverage programs appropriate to each property's positioning.
Evaluate opportunities for shared culinary resources, menu development and operational efficiencies without compromising quality or service.

Banquets Events and Commercial Performance

Lead F&B execution for meetings, weddings, groups, seasonal activations and hotel events.
Partner with Sales and Events on menus, pricing, service standards, labour, space use and event profitability.
Review banquet event orders and ensure complete handoffs among Sales, Culinary, Service, Rooms and Engineering.
Develop packages, promotions, signature events and local partnerships that grow demand and strengthen positioning.
Track outlet and event revenue, covers, average cheque, pace, mix and conversion against forecast.
Develop a coordinated wedding, conference, group and special events strategy across the resort and hotel, maximizing revenue opportunities for both businesses.
Work with Sales, Marketing and Revenue Management to develop dining experiences, packages and activations that drive incremental visitation, guest spending and destination appeal.
Identify opportunities to improve banquet profitability, event execution and cross-selling between RED and The Josie.

Rebuild People & Culture

Assess structure, talent, procedures and recurring failures; maintain a sequenced improvement plan with both General Managers.
Recruit, onboard, schedule, coach and retain F&B leaders and seasonal employees.
Re-establish pre-shifts, training plans, menu testing, quality checks, labour reviews and manager handovers.
Set clear goals, provide direct feedback, recognize strong performance and address performance concerns promptly.
Build product knowledge, sales confidence, responsible service, food safety and leadership capability.
Create a respectful, inclusive workplace with strong communication and sustainable management coverage.
Build leadership depth at each property, ensuring capable managers are empowered to run day-to-day operations independently.
Develop shared training standards, leadership development opportunities and seasonal staffing strategies where appropriate.
Work with Human Resources to improve recruitment, retention, employee engagement and succession planning across both operations.

Financial Controls Safety and Asset Care

Manage revenue and expenses to budget and forecast, with close attention to labour, food cost, beverage cost and waste.
Review daily sales, discounts, voids, promotions, gratuities, cash, payment activity and operating variances.
Maintain purchasing, receiving, storage, inventory, recipe, portion and point-of-sale controls.
Lead budgeting, forecasting, month-end reporting, capital planning and corrective action for assigned areas.
Ensure compliance with food safety, liquor service, employment, accessibility, privacy, fire and occupational safety requirements.
Protect outlets, kitchens, equipment, smallwares and inventories through disciplined maintenance and asset stewardship.
Maintain separate departmental budgets, financial reporting and performance measures for RED Mountain Resort and The Josie Hotel.
Work with Finance to establish transparent and appropriate allocation of shared costs, labour and purchasing between the two businesses.
Identify opportunities for consolidated procurement, improved supplier pricing and operational efficiencies.
Partner with Engineering and Finance to prioritize deferred maintenance, equipment replacement and capital improvements across F&B operations.

Measures of Success

Guest satisfaction, online sentiment, complaint recurrence, recovery time, service timing and quality consistency.
Outlet and banquet revenue, covers, average cheque, menu mix, upselling and event conversion.
Labour productivity, overtime, food cost, beverage cost, waste, inventory accuracy and departmental profitability.
Health inspection, food safety, responsible service, cash control, inventory and workplace safety performance.
Leadership stability, seasonal staffing readiness, retention, attendance, training completion and internal development.
Completion of agreed rebuild milestones and reduction in repeat service, product and control failures.
Improvement in F&B profitability at both RED Mountain Resort and The Josie Hotel, measured independently.
Demonstrable purchasing savings and operating efficiencies achieved through appropriate shared services.
Growth in banquet, wedding, group and special event revenue across both properties.
Successful development of a stable management structure capable of supporting two distinct F&B operations.

Key Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Education

Post-secondary education in business administration, hospitality, tourism, culinary arts, or a related field is preferred; equivalent relevant experience will be considered.
Additional hospitality, food safety, or responsible beverage service education or certification is an asset.

Experience

Seven or more years of progressive F&B leadership experience, preferably including senior management responsibility within a full-service hotel, resort or multi-outlet hospitality operation.
Experience leading multiple outlets and supervising managers or supervisors across culinary, service, bar and event operations.
Demonstrated experience with budgets, forecasting, labour management, inventory control, menu costing and pricing, and improving financial performance.
Experience with point-of-sale systems and scheduling, inventory, reservation, event and other business software.
Experience overseeing both hotel F&B operations and high-volume casual dining or resort outlets is strongly preferred.
Demonstrated success improving underperforming operations, developing management teams and implementing sustainable operating standards.
Experience with banquets, weddings, conferences and group business is strongly preferred.
Experience with Marriott or another internationally branded hotel is an asset.

Physical And Other Requirements

Ability to meet the physical demands of an active resort and hotel environment, with reasonable accommodation where required.

jobs.title: Vice President, Edmonton Manufacturing Operations and Site Head
jobs.description:
At Gilead, we’re creating a healthier world for all people. For more than 35 years, we’ve tackled diseases such as HIV, viral hepatitis, COVID-19 and cancer – working relentlessly to develop therapies that help improve lives and to ensure access to these therapies across the globe. We continue to fight against the world’s biggest health challenges, and our mission requires collaboration, determination and a relentless drive to make a difference.

Every member of Gilead’s team plays a critical role in the discovery and development of life-changing scientific innovations. Our employees are our greatest asset as we work to achieve our bold ambitions, and we’re looking for the next wave of passionate and ambitious people ready to make a direct impact.

We believe every employee deserves a great leader. People Leaders are the cornerstone to the employee experience at Gilead and Kite. As a people leader now or in the future, you are the key driver in evolving our culture and creating an environment where every employee feels included, developed and empowered to fulfill their aspirations. Join Gilead and help create possible, together.

Job Description

The Vice President, Edmonton Manufacturing Operations and Site Head is accountable for the strategy, culture, performance, and operational execution of Gilead’s Edmonton site. The role leads the cross-functional Site Leadership Team and provides direct or matrixed leadership across Manufacturing, Packaging, Analytical Operations, Quality, Engineering and Maintenance, Supply Chain, Technical Operations, Finance, Human Resources, Legal, Information Technology, and Public Affairs. The Vice President ensures safe, compliant, reliable, and cost-effective clinical and commercial supply; translates enterprise and Pharmaceutical Development and Manufacturing priorities into site strategy; and serves as the primary legal representative and a director of Gilead Alberta ULC (GAULC).

This site-based role is in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada, and requires periodic international business travel, including travel to the United States. The Vice President is a member of the PDM Manufacturing Leadership Team and partners across the Global Manufacturing network to shape enterprise strategy and deliver shared business outcomes.

Responsibilities

Lead the Edmonton Site Leadership Team and align directly managed and matrixed functions around clear priorities, decision rights, performance expectations, and shared accountability for site outcomes.
Translate enterprise and Global Manufacturing priorities into medium- and long-term site strategy, annual operating plans, resource requirements, and measurable performance objectives.
Ensure site operations are executed safely, compliantly, reliably, and efficiently to meet product demand, quality, service, cost, and financial commitments; establish management routines that enable timely decisions and transparent accountability.
Build and develop a high-performing, inclusive, feedback-rich leadership team; strengthen succession pipelines and critical capabilities; and foster an environment in which employees are included, developed, empowered, and accountable.
Establish a culture and management system of operational excellence and continuous improvement, using data, digital capabilities, automation, and new technologies to improve safety, quality, reliability, productivity, cost, and speed.
Sponsor transformational change, simplify and scale processes, and build cross-functional commitment to new capabilities and ways of working.
Provide strategic oversight for clinical and commercial drug-substance manufacturing, packaging, analytical testing and release, maintenance, engineering, supply chain, technical operations, scale-up, technology transfer, registration, and product launch activities at the Edmonton site.
Contribute to CMC strategy, governance, and decision-making for the commercial portfolio through active partnership with PDM product teams and functions including Quality, Technical Development, CMC Regulatory, Product Strategy, PDM Strategy and Operations, and Global Supply Chain.
Ensure inspection readiness and sustain compliance with applicable cGMP, health, safety, environmental, employment, legal, fiscal, and statutory requirements.
Develop and manage operating and capital budgets, capacity plans, workforce plans, and investment priorities in alignment with site and network requirements.
Establish proactive business-continuity and risk-management plans that protect employee safety, regulatory compliance, product supply, critical operations, and site service commitments.
Serve as a senior member of the PDM Manufacturing Leadership Team and as executive sponsor for strategic, operational excellence, and people initiatives that extend beyond the Edmonton site.
Guide the preparation, review, and approval of CMC sections for regulatory filings and support agency interactions, product-related inspections, and commitments arising from those activities.
Provide technical and strategic support to internal and external cGMP manufacturing and testing operations.
Fulfill legal and fiscal responsibilities as a director of GAULC in accordance with Canadian law and company governance requirements.
Represent Gilead with government officials, regulatory authorities, industry organizations, educational institutions, community partners, suppliers, and other external stakeholders, strengthening the Edmonton site’s reputation and strategic relationships.
Perform other responsibilities consistent with the scope and accountability of Edmonton Site Head.

Qualifications

BA or BSc degree in business, science, engineering, or related discipline and a minimum of 14 years of relevant experience; alternatively, an MSc, MA, MBA, or other advanced degree and a minimum of 12 years of relevant experience. Equivalent combinations of education and experience may be considered.
Senior leadership experience in a complex pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or similarly regulated manufacturing environment, including accountability for clinical or commercial drug-substance manufacturing or related operations.
Demonstrated success leading direct and matrixed functions, building high-performing senior teams, developing successors, and influencing across a global enterprise.
Experience developing and executing site or enterprise strategy, operating plans, budgets, capital priorities, workforce plans, and performance-management systems.
Experience leading operational excellence, transformation, technology adoption, and continuous-improvement initiatives with measurable business outcomes.
Experience supporting regulatory filings, agency interactions, and product-related inspections, with knowledge of U.S., Canadian, Japanese, and other applicable global regulatory expectations.
Knowledge of ICH guidelines and cGMP requirements for the development and manufacture of small-molecule active pharmaceutical ingredients, as well as current industry trends and regulatory expectations.
Experience working with external manufacturing and testing organizations and managing business continuity, supply, quality, and operational risk.
Strong financial, scientific, technical, and operational acumen, with the ability to make sound decisions in ambiguity and balance patient, compliance, people, supply, and business considerations.
Exceptional executive communication, collaboration, judgment, and stakeholder-management skills, including the ability to simplify complex issues, explain the rationale for decisions, build trust, and influence without direct authority.
A leadership approach grounded in integrity, inclusion, accountability, enterprise thinking, disciplined execution, and commitment to Gilead’s values and Leadership Commitments.

Leadership Expectations

Model Gilead’s values and Leadership Commitments in decisions, actions, and relationships.
Create an inclusive environment in which diverse perspectives are sought, respected, and translated into stronger decisions.
Set clear direction, connect teams to purpose, and maintain accountability for results and behaviors.
Develop talent, invite candid feedback, and strengthen organizational capability and succession.
Collaborate across boundaries and act with an enterprise mindset in service of patients and shared outcomes.

As an equal opportunity employer, Gilead Sciences Inc. is committed to a diverse workforce.

People Leader Accountabilities

Create Inclusion: Model inclusive leadership and embed diversity, equity, and inclusion into how the team operates, makes decisions, and develops talent.
Develop Talent: Understand employees’ skills, aspirations, and potential; provide coaching, feedback, and opportunities that grow both current performance and future readiness.
Empower Teams: Align goals to enterprise and R&D priorities, clarify decision rights, remove barriers, and connect the team to the broader Public Affairs and R&D ecosystem.

For Current Gilead Employees And Contractors

Please apply via the Internal Career Opportunities portal in Workday.

**Full job description**


**Kemp Care Network** is a compassionate community dedicated to supporting the emotional, physical, and social needs of individuals living with a serious illness, facing their final chapter, or grieving a death. Through our commitment to exceptional care, meaningful connections, and unwavering support, we help individuals and families navigate some of life’s most challenging moments with dignity and compassion.


We are seeking a leader to join our team as **Director of Operations** of our soon to be open **Keaton’s House – Paul Paletta Children’s Hospice**.


The Director of Operations provides strategic and operational leadership for all services, ensuring the delivery of safe, high\-quality, family\-centred care for children with life\-limiting illnesses and their families. This role oversees all aspects of hospice operations, clinical practice, staffing, quality improvement, risk management, program development, and regulatory compliance. In this role you will work closely with healthcare providers, community partners, and the leadership team to advance organizational priorities and foster innovation in children’s hospice care. Most importantly, this leader will ensure that the voices, experiences, and needs of children and families remain at the heart of every decision.


If you are a purpose\-driven leader who is ready to help build the regional centre of excellence for children’s hospice and palliative care, we invite you to join us in shaping a future where every child and family receives exceptional care, compassionate support, and meaningful moments together.


Total Rewards package includes: base salary of ($115,000 – $135,000 based on experience), fully employer paid health and dental benefits, sick days, personal days, robust Employee Assistance Program and more!


**In this role you will:**


* Provide leadership and oversight for all clinical services, programs, and care delivery
* Ensure the provision of safe, high\-quality, evidence\-informed, and family\-centred care for all patients and families
* Recruit, orient, mentor, coach, and support members of the interdisciplinary clinical and support teams
* Conduct performance reviews, establish development goals, and address performance concerns in accordance with organizational policies.
* Support employee engagement, retention, succession planning, and professional development initiatives
* Lead quality improvement initiatives to enhance clinical outcomes, guest experience, and organizational effectiveness
* Oversee incident reporting, investigation, and follow\-up activities
* Ensure compliance with accreditation standards, legislation, professional practice requirements, and organizational policies
* Promote a culture of continuous quality improvement, risk management, and patient safety
* Support the collection, analysis, and reporting of program and clinical outcome data
* Champion a family\-centred approach to care that respects the unique needs, values, cultures, and preferences of children and families
* Address guest and family concerns and contribute to the resolution of complex clinical situations
* Serve as a member of the senior leadership team and contribute to organizational strategy and decision\-making

**Qualifications:**


* Current registration in good standing with the College of Nurses of Ontario (CNO) as a Registered Nurse (RN).
* Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BScN) required; Master’s degree in Nursing, Health Administration, Leadership, or a related field is an asset.
* Minimum 5 years of progressive healthcare leadership experience, including oversight of clinical operations and interdisciplinary teams.
* Experience in palliative care, hospice care, pediatric complex care, community nursing, or a related healthcare setting preferred.
* Strong knowledge of clinical practice, family\-centred care, quality improvement, risk management, patient safety, and relevant healthcare legislation and standards.
* Demonstrated ability to lead teams, manage complex situations, drive program development, and support organizational priorities.
* Experience with strategic planning, quality initiatives, and budget or resource management.
* Commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion, and culturally safe care.
* Ability to participate in an on\-call leadership rotation and work occasional evenings and weekends as required
* This is a future vacancy but the successful applicant should be available to start in early 2027
* AI may be used in the recruitment process

jobs.description:

People & Culture

British Columbia, Canada (Hybrid)

Description

Photonic is building the world’s first commercial-scale quantum computer, and we are growing fast to do it. We are seeking an exceptional Chief People Officer (CPO)
to serve as the CEO’s trusted partner and a leading voice on the executive team, shaping the decisions that determine who we hire, how we lead, how we reward, and how ready we are when investors, acquirers, or public markets look closely. This is not a back-office seat. It is a seat at the table for someone who can influence at the top, move quickly, and build. This role is based in Coquitlam, BC, with 2–3 days per week in the office.

Please include a cover letter with your resume (in one file) describing how you would be a great fit at Photonic and what attributes you could bring to our growing team.

What We Need You To Do

Executive Partnership & Influence

Act as the CEO’s thought partner on company strategy, organizational design, and the people decisions that shape Photonic’s trajectory.
Represent people and culture in the boardroom, advising the Board and its committees on executive compensation, succession, and talent risk.
Advise and coach the executive team through growth, transformation, and high-stakes decisions with candour and credibility.
Translate business strategy into a multi-year workforce plan, and give leadership the insight to act on it.

Talent Acquisition & Leadership Pipeline

Set the strategy for winning highly specialized scientific and engineering talent (PhDs, quantum, photonics) in a fiercely competitive global market.
Build the leadership bench and succession pipeline that will carry Photonic through its next stages of growth, and protect our promote-from-within culture.
Establish Photonic as a global employer of choice for the people who will build the future of computing.

Compensation, Benefits & Total Rewards

Define a global rewards philosophy across Canada, the US, and the UK that attracts and retains world-class talent.
Steward equity and executive compensation strategy so it is competitive, defensible, and built to withstand investor and acquirer due diligence.
Partner with the CEO and CFO to align people investment with financial strategy.

Organizational Readiness & Governance

Build the people governance and compliance framework that a company under investor, acquirer, or public-market scrutiny is expected to have.
Anticipate and manage people-related risk, including employment, regulatory, and reputational risk, as we expand globally.
Ensure our people infrastructure scales ahead of the business as headcount accelerates.

Culture & Organizational Leadership

Champion a culture rooted in our values of Fearless Ambition, Accountability, Growth, and Respect as we scale across borders.
Build and lead a high-performing HR organization across talent acquisition, HR operations, total rewards, and business partnership.
Own the strategy for engagement, performance, and retention, and hold leaders accountable for results.

What You Bring To Our Team

15+ years of progressive HR leadership, including at least 5 years leading an HR function at the senior leadership level in a scaling technology or deep tech environment.
Bachelor’s degree in HR, BA, or a related field, with an MBA or equivalent advanced degree. CPHR designation or equivalent (e.g., SHRM-SCP, CIPD). A combination of education and senior executive experience will be considered.
A proven trusted advisor to CEOs and boards, with the executive presence and judgment to match.
Proven ability to build and scale HR processes and teams through periods of rapid growth (100→500+ employees).
A strategic, enterprise-level thinker who connects people decisions to business outcomes and investor expectations.
Experience leading HR across multiple geographies (Canada required; US and/or UK strongly preferred).
Strong knowledge of Canadian employment law; familiarity with US and UK employment regulations is a significant asset.
Strong command of Canadian employment law and the judgment to navigate complex, sensitive matters with discretion.
Comfortable with the pace, ambiguity, and shifting priorities of a company at this stage of growth.
A bias to action and a genuine love of building.
A fit with our values: Fearless Ambition, Accountability, Growth, and Respect.

An Exceptional Candidate Will Bring

Experience scaling an organization through rapid growth (100→500+ employees) and preparing it for investor, acquirer, or public-market scrutiny.
Experience leading organizational design and change through a transition from research to commercialization.
Experience advising a Board or its compensation committee, including equity strategy.
Working knowledge of US and UK employment frameworks.

WHY YOU SHOULD WORK WITH US

Work closely with some of the brightest innovators in quantum technologies to drive breakthroughs that redefine computing
Join at a pivotal moment and help shape and lead an organization through one of the most exciting phases a company can experience
Inclusive company culture that values collaboration
Clear career paths, with 80% of our managers and directors promoted from within
Regular social events and fun activities keep our global team connected
Competitive compensation package including base salary, stock options, and relocation assistance for global talent
Comprehensive benefits including extended health, dental, life, long term disability, an employee assistance program, parental leave top-ups, a flexible spending account, and unlimited wellness leave

The description above is what we think an ideal candidate would look like for this role. At Photonic, we understand that everyone has a different work and life journey. jobs.title: Associate Director, Enterprise Crisis Management
jobs.description:
Job Description 

 What is the opportunity? 
 The Enterprise Crisis Management Team is responsible for delivering and enhancing RBC's operational and reputational crisis management programs and achieving best-in-class global crisis response practices to support the overall resilience of the organization.

 The Associate Director, Enterprise Crisis Management provides subject matter expertise to support the Director, Enterprise Crisis Management in the preparation of playbooks, assessments, trainings, and other materials to ensure the organization is collectively prepared to respond to crises. The Associate Director will work closely with teams in the 1st and 2nd line to support the implementation of strong risk management practices across the organization.

 What will you do? 

 (a) Support the Implementation of Crisis Management Practices 
 Support crisis management team activities designed to manage operational and reputational risk through prevention, preparedness, response, and recovery. 
 Contribute to setting the overall strategic direction for RBC’s enterprise approach to crisis preparedness and response, including providing strategic and tactical support through the crisis management lifecycle.
 Prepare playbooks, guides, and supporting materials to help ensure the organization is collectively prepared to respond to low likelihood, high severity events.
 Manage the logistics and lead the development of tabletop exercises for the crisis management teams and support business and regional tabletops through coaching and thought leadership.
 Lead a structured approach to crisis response, including coordination, preparing materials, both standard and ad hoc, and scribing through to resolution.
 Support the development and execution of Crisis Management awareness and training across the enterprise with key stakeholders.

 (b) Monitor top & emerging risks and provide advice and guidance 
 Maintain a strong understanding of the threats and hazards facing the financial services sector and proactively identify potential operational and reputational risks.
 Lead proactive outreach and monitoring of incidents, both emerging and ongoing.
 Build strong relationships across the organization to ensure effective information sharing and collaboration.
 Consistently demonstrate behaviours that embed a strong risk management culture. 

 (c) Enable program execution and reporting 
 Manage program metrics, procedures, risks and controls.
 Develop and maintain the annual training and testing calendar.
 Track action items resulting from Crisis tabletops and activations.
 Document key findings in post-incident reviews (PIRs)
 Support engagement with regulators and external committees.
 Coordinate with Incident Management Teams and Business Continuity central team as required.

 (d) Champion Strategy & Culture 
 Support a high-performing culture focused on operational excellence and risk awareness 
 Work collaboratively across teams, contributing to an engaged workforce who are effective, knowledgeable and adaptable

 What do you need to succeed? 

 Must Have: 

 Experience in Crisis Management, Emergency Management, Physical or Cybersecurity, or related field. 
 Experience in financial services or highly regulated industries, with demonstrated success in large-scale global matrixed environments. 
 Experience directly supporting senior leadership and strong executive stakeholder management and communications skills. 
 Ability to work in high pressure environments, adapt effectively, and communicate clearly. 
 An understanding of risk management frameworks, control environments, and governance structures. 
 Ability to balance competing priorities with exceptional time management and results orientation. 
 Excellent critical thinking skills with demonstrated ability to challenge assumptions at senior levels. 
 Strong interpersonal, relationship-building, and communication capabilities. 
 Strong facilitation and presentation skills; demonstrated ability to engage stakeholders and committees. 

 Nice-to-Have: 

 Industry professional accreditation or certification 
 Experience in Corporate Communications, Operational Resilience, Business Continuity and/or Incident Management

jobs.title: Technology Director
jobs.description:
Requirements

Description & Requirements

who we are

lululemon is an innovative performance apparel company for yoga, running, training, and other athletic pursuits. Setting the bar in technical fabrics and functional design, we create transformational products and experiences that support people in moving, growing, connecting, and being well. We owe our success to our innovative product, emphasis on stores, commitment to our people, and the incredible connections we make in every community we're in. As a company, we focus on creating positive change to build a healthier, thriving future. In particular, that includes creating an equitable, inclusive and growth-focused environment for our people.

About This Team

The lululemon cybersecurity team helps protect the trust our guests, employees, and partners place in us. We work across technology and the business to understand risk, build practical security capabilities, and enable teams to move quickly and responsibly. We are looking for a Director of Security Operations to lead our Security Incident Response Team (SIRT), Threat Intelligence, Security Observability, and Detection Engineering capabilities. This leader will build an operation that treats detections as software: versioned, tested, measurable, and continuously improved.

Core Responsibilities

You will lead a global team of security engineers, analysts, threat hunters, intelligence practitioners, and incident responders. You will set the strategy and operating model for detecting, investigating, and responding to threats across lululemon’s technology environment. You are as comfortable discussing telemetry and detection logic with engineers as you are explaining business impact and response decisions to executives. You know that effective security operations is not measured by how many alerts a team can generate. It is measured by how reliably we identify meaningful threats, respond to them, and improve the systems around us.

Lead incident response

Own the SIRT strategy, incident response lifecycle, and operational readiness across cloud, SaaS, identity, endpoint, network, and application environments.
Lead coordination during significant incidents, establishing clear decision-making, escalation, communications, and recovery processes.
Partner with technology teams, Legal, Privacy, Communications, Risk, and other stakeholders to manage incidents and their business impact.
Run exercises and post-incident reviews that result in owned, tracked improvements to detection, response, and resilience.
Establish a sustainable global coverage model, including on-call and external partnerships where appropriate.

Build detection as code

Set the direction for a detection engineering program that manages detection logic, queries, rules, and response workflows as version-controlled code.
Establish engineering practices for peer review, automated testing, deployment, documentation, tuning, and retirement of detections.
Use threat modeling, incident learnings, threat intelligence, and adversary behavior to prioritize detection coverage against meaningful risks.
Validate detections continuously through simulation, replay, purple teaming, and other appropriate testing methods.
Reduce alert fatigue by improving signal quality, enriching context, and automating repeatable work while retaining human judgment for consequential decisions.

Own security observability

Define the telemetry strategy needed to investigate threats across identities, systems, applications, cloud services, and data flows.
Partner with engineering and platform teams to build reliable, secure, and cost-conscious telemetry pipelines, including clear ownership, data quality, retention, and access controls.
Identify and address visibility gaps, including those created by changes in infrastructure, SaaS adoption, and emerging technologies.
Guide the evolution and consolidation of security operations tooling, including decisions about what to build, buy, retain, or retire.

Turn intelligence into action

Lead a threat intelligence capability that identifies and communicates threats relevant to lululemon’s business, technology, and operating environment.
Translate intelligence into prioritized detections, hunts, defensive improvements, and incident readiness.
Build trusted relationships with industry peers, partners, and relevant information-sharing communities.

Build the team and program

Hire, develop, and retain a diverse, high-performing team. Create clear career paths and a healthy operating environment for people doing demanding work.
Set a multi-year roadmap, operating budget, and investment priorities aligned with business risk and technology strategy.
Define meaningful measures of effectiveness, such as detection coverage and validation, telemetry health, alert quality, time to detect and contain, and completion of post-incident improvements.
Communicate security operations performance, material risks, and investment tradeoffs clearly to technical teams and executive leaders.
Work with security and technology partners to meet applicable regulatory and contractual obligations, and provide evidence of operational effectiveness.

Qualifications

Approximately 8 years of experience in technology, including at least 5 years leading security operations, incident response, detection engineering, or closely related teams.
Experience building or evolving security operations capabilities for a complex, global organization.
Demonstrated experience leading significant security incidents and coordinating technical responders and business stakeholders through investigation, containment, and recovery.
Strong technical understanding of detection engineering and security observability, including logging pipelines, detection logic, security analytics, and automation.
Experience applying software engineering practices to security operations, such as version control, code review, automated testing, and continuous integration and deployment.
Experience detecting and responding to threats across cloud, SaaS, identity, endpoint, and application environments.
Experience using threat intelligence and adversary frameworks, such as MITRE ATT&CK, to inform detection priorities and assess coverage.
Experience designing or operating incident response processes informed by frameworks such as NIST, and measuring whether those processes work in practice.
Sound judgment in balancing security outcomes, operational workload, cost, privacy, and business impact.
Ability to influence across organizational boundaries, communicate clearly under pressure, and translate technical risk into actionable business decisions.
A track record of developing people and creating inclusive, accountable teams.

Valuable Additional Experience

Building or scaling purple-team, threat-hunting, or detection validation programs.
Applying AI and automation to security operations with appropriate testing, oversight, and access controls.
Working with managed detection and response providers, incident response partners, or globally distributed operations.
Investigating threats involving software supply chains, development pipelines, and machine or service identities.

must haves

Acknowledge the presence of choice in every moment and take personal responsibility for your life.
Possess an entrepreneurial spirit and continuously innovate to achieve great results.
Communicate with honesty and kindness and create the space for others to do the same.
Lead with courage, knowing the possibility of greatness is bigger than the fear of failure.
Foster connection by putting people first and building trusting relationships.
Integrate fun and joy as a way of being and working, aka doesn’t take yourself too seriously.

Additional Notes

Authorization to work in Canada is required for this role.

Compensation And Benefits Package

lululemon’s compensation offerings are grounded in a pay-for-performance philosophy that recognizes exceptional individual and team performance. The typical hiring range for this position is from  $196,600 - $258,100
annually
; the base pay offered is based on market location and may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and internal equity. As part of our total rewards offering, permanent employees in this position may be eligible for our competitive annual bonus program and equity offerings , subject to program eligibility requirements.  

At Lululemon, Investing In Our People Is a Top Priority. We Believe That When Life Works, Work Works. We Strive To Be The Place Where Inclusive Leaders Come To Develop And Enable All To Be Well. Recognizing Our Teams For Their Performance And Dedication, Other Components Of Our Total Rewards Offerings Include Support Of Career Development, Wellbeing, And Personal Growth

Paid time off
Savings and retirement plan matching
Generous employee discount

Parenthood top-up
Extensive catalog of development course offerings
People networks, mentorship programs, and leadership series (to name a few)

Note: The incentive programs, benefits, and perks have certain eligibility requirements. The Company reserves the right to alter these incentive programs, benefits, and perks in whole or in part at any time without advance notice.

Unlock your ambition, turn ideas into world-changing realities, and join an organization where every voice makes a difference, and every difference builds a healthier world.

Own the Pharmacovigilance (PV) Audit Program: Develop, implement, and maintain the global PV audit strategy, ensuring alignment with regulatory expectations (e.g., EMA, FDA, MHRA, PMDA) and industry best practices.
Manage Audit Operations: Oversee scheduling, planning, execution, reporting, and follow-up for PV audits, including internal audits and audits of service providers and affiliates. Fully participate in the audit program; actively owning and executing PV audits.

Master’s degree and 5+ years in pharmacovigilance or pharmaceutical industry; or Bachelor’s degree and 10+ years relevant experience.

Strong oral and written communication skills in English.
Integrity: Accepting and adhering to high ethical, moral, and personal values in decisions, communications, actions, and when dealing with others.
Ability to travel globally up to 15%.

Our salary and benefits are everything you’d expect from an organization with global strength and scale, and you’ll be surrounded by career opportunities in a culture that fosters care, collaboration and support.

At Agnico Eagle, our values never waver. We believe in trust, respect, equity, family and responsibility. Why? And, we value your commitment to treat every person on our team with respect, helping us to operate safely, protect the environment and make a positive contribution to our local communities.

Canadian\-based and led, Agnico Eagle is Canada's largest mining company and the second largest gold producer in the world. It produces precious metals from operations in Canada, Australia, Finland and Mexico and has a pipeline of high\-quality exploration and development projects. Agnico Eagle is a partner of choice within the mining industry, recognized globally for its leading sustainability practices. Agnico Eagle was founded in 1957 and has consistently created value for its shareholders, declaring a cash dividend every year since 1983\.


Want to learn more about our operations and projects? Click here!

------------------------

Reporting to the Corporate Director, Finance Technology, you will be part of the Finance Department. You will provide product leadership for Finance Technology, translating strategy into an integrated roadmap and driving execution, adoption and continuous improvements across the organization. Your decision's will impact the company’s finance capabilities across Agnico Eagle’s global portfolio. You will enable the Company to operate more efficiently, generate better insights, and make faster, more informed decisions.

  

In this hands\-on leadership role, you will lead a team while working closely with business stakeholders from Operations, Finance and IT to translate business needs into scalable technology solutions. You will drive capabilities across budgeting and forecasting, long\-range planning, reporting, automation, advanced analytics and AI.

  

* End\-to\-End product ownership and execution within the Finance Technology strategy


	+ Drives the product, translates finance needs into priorities, coordinates delivery and is accountable for the execution and outcomes
	+ Serve as a key member of the Finance Technology leadership team, providing strategic advice and recommendations to the Corporate Director and VP on product strategy, investment priorities, technology capabilities and governance.
	+ Own the product roadmap and backlog
	+ Drive adoption and realization of expected benefits
	+ Own stakeholder engagement and product governance processes
	+ Accountable for the daily decisions to drive the product(s)
  

* Partner with business leaders to identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, automate, and improve Finance\-related processes


	+ Requires enterprise\-wide stakeholder management and balancing competing priorities across Finance, Technology and the needs of operations.
  

* Lead product delivery from business requirements and prioritization through solution design, implementation, adoption, and continuous improvement
  

* Own and evolve Finance capabilities across budgeting, forecasting, long\-range planning, reporting, automation, advanced analytics and AI
  

* Identify and prioritize AI and advanced analytics opportunities for Finance, leveraging Databricks in partnership with Data and Technology teams
  

* Ensure Finance solutions are supported by trusted, governed, and integrated data
  

* Manage competing priorities and ensure investments are aligned with business value and strategic objectives
  

* Lead and develop a Product Owner team while remaining actively involved in key initiatives.
  

* Communicate product strategy, progress, risks, and outcomes to senior Finance and Technology stakeholders
  

**WHAT YOU NEED TO SUCCEED**
----------------------------

  

* Bachelor’s Degree in finance, IT or other relevant field of study required.
  

* CPA, MBA, or technology related specialisation.
  

* Knowledge of the mining industry is considered an asset.
  

* 15\+ years of progressive experience in Finance Technology, Finance Transformation, product management, enterprise applications, or related areas.
  

* Strong understanding of finance processes, including budgeting, long\-range planning, forecasting, management reporting, and performance management.
  

* Experience leading complex technology products or Finance transformation initiatives.
  

* Knowledge of EPM, ERP, enterprise data platforms, analytics, automation, and AI technologies.
  

* Familiarity with JD Edwards, Anaplan, Hyperion or similar is considered an asset.
  

* Experience with Databricks or similar modern data and analytics platforms is an asset.
  

* Strong product management, stakeholder engagement, and prioritization skills.
  

* Demonstrated ability to operate at both a strategic and hands\-on delivery level.
  

* Strong leadership, communication, and problem\-solving capabilities.
  

* Proficiency of the French language is considered an asset.

jobs.title: VP, Social Commerce
jobs.description:
At **Viral Nation,** we specialize in building social\-first ecosystems for brands to connect with the modern consumer journey. Our integrated solutions align strategy, talent, media, and technology with culturally relevant creativity to scale the world's fastest\-growing digital brands. Viral Nation offers a fluid, creative, and growth\-oriented environment that will support your ambitions to apply your talents in an open, collaborative, and fast\-paced culture. Our ability to stay at the forefront of the industry has fuelled our success and will guide us in paving the path forward. We're driven to push boundaries and think beyond today to deliver strategies, and we're just getting started.



While we continuously exceed our goals, we need your help – our success is only as great as our people. Strong performance leads to high expectations, and we must keep raising the bar!


Viral Nation is seeking a **Vice President, Social Commerce** to build and lead our social commerce practice. You'll turn enterprise demand into creator\-led commerce programs that Viral Nation can sell, deliver and scale profitably.



Start with a creator affiliate and build on our existing TikTok Shop work. Choose the right path to purchase for each client: retailer or marketplace affiliate, direct\-to\-consumer commerce, or in\-platform checkout. Base that choice on the product, shopper behaviour, unit economics and the client's existing retail and ecommerce partnerships.



You'll lead the commerce work from the investment recommendation through launch and the decision to scale. Decide what Viral Nation should build, where partners are better placed to deliver, and when to hold off.


**Responsibilities:**


### **Lead social commerce strategy**


* **Set the direction** for the practice, including the services we sell, how we staff them and what we need to deliver them well.
* **Choose the right path to purchase** across retailer and marketplace affiliate, direct\-to\-consumer programs and native checkout, including TikTok Shop.
* **Assess launch readiness** across product margin, offer, inventory, fulfillment, returns, client approvals and access to usable data.
* **Shape programs around the client** by connecting creator content and paid amplification to the point of purchase. Define how the work fits alongside existing partners.

### **Advise clients and shape opportunities**


* **Lead senior client conversations** on launch readiness, investment and learning goals.
* **Qualify opportunities** with Growth and Client Services, and build a pipeline of pilots with a credible path to recurring revenue.
* **Price and staff the work** with Growth and Finance, with clear scope, delivery capacity and margin expectations before we commit.
* **Recommend where to invest** based on acquisition, sales and contribution, and be willing to recommend against a channel when the economics don't work.

### **Build the offering and guide delivery**


* **Build repeatable delivery playbooks** for creator recruitment and activation, incentives, tracking, approvals, disclosures and payout reconciliation.
* **Lead the commerce workstream** with Client Services, Strategy, Creator Relations, Creative, Paid Media and Analytics. Define who owns each handoff and escalation.
* **Apply SocialAI and VN Secure** to identify creators and content that fit target shoppers and to support brand safety vetting. Use campaign data to test which combinations drive purchases.
* **Choose tools and partners** based on creator reach, workflow, data access and cost. Brands or partners own inventory, fulfillment and returns unless the scope of work explicitly assigns them to Viral Nation.
* **Develop the team** and identify the specialist capacity we need to deliver reliably as the practice grows.

### **Drive measurable performance and learning**


* **Measure client outcomes** with Analytics and Finance. Track net sales after returns, customer acquisition or repeat purchase as relevant, and client contribution after relevant costs such as creator incentives, fees and media spend.
* **Separate attributed sales from incremental impact** and design tests with Analytics to estimate lift where the data and program allow it.
* **Decide what to scale, refine or stop** based on performance, commercial contribution and operational readiness.
* **Track the health of the practice** through qualified pipeline, pilot conversion, recurring revenue and delivery margin.


**Skills and Qualifications:**


* Senior experience building and running creator commerce programs through launch and optimization, with direct accountability for results.
* Deep creator affiliate expertise and direct responsibility for launching or operating TikTok Shop.
* Experience choosing between retailer or marketplace affiliate, brand\-owned commerce and native checkout, and working with existing partners.
* A track record of turning a client opportunity into a business case, then leading delivery and using the results to decide what to scale.
* Strong commercial judgment across commissions, discounts, creator compensation, media, returns, acquisition cost and contribution margin.
* Credibility with senior clients and the ability to lead discovery, pitches and performance discussions.
* Experience building a team or service and mobilizing specialists across functions.
* Ability to diagnose delivery issues and make clear trade\-offs across client, creator and partner teams.
* Experience across multiple brands, categories or markets is an asset.


**What success looks like**


* In the first 30 days, map the pipeline, existing delivery capabilities and partners. Identify what we can launch, what needs support and what to decline.
* By day 60, give Growth and Client Services a costed affiliate\-first offer and a TikTok Shop option for clients that meet launch criteria. Define staffing, handoffs and the pilot scorecard.
* By day 90, have a staffed pilot ready to launch, with tracking, approvals

jobs.title: Director, Finance
jobs.description:
**Director of Finance**
=======================

**Full\-Time \| Remote**

**Lead the Numbers. Shape the Future. Grow with GraceMed.**
-----------------------------------------------------------


GraceMed is a growing, multi\-location healthcare and aesthetics organization offering a wide range of plastic and cosmetic surgeries, dermatology services, aesthetic treatments and medical\-grade skincare.


As we continue to expand, we are looking for an experienced finance leader to help shape the next stage of our growth. This is an opportunity to take ownership of our financial reporting and accounting operations while playing an important role in strategic planning, business performance, organizational transformation and the integration of new clinics and acquisitions.


Working closely with executive leadership, physicians and clinic managers, you will help strengthen our financial infrastructure, build scalable processes and translate financial information into meaningful business insights.


If you are a hands\-on finance leader who enjoys balancing technical accounting expertise with strategic thinking, operational partnership and people development, we would love to hear from you.

**Why Join GraceMed?**
----------------------

* **Make a meaningful impact:** Play an influential role in shaping the financial operations and future growth of an expanding healthcare organization.
* **Be part of the bigger picture:** Work directly with executive leadership and operational teams, contributing to business strategy and important organizational decisions.
* **Build and improve:** Take ownership of financial processes, systems and controls, with the opportunity to introduce improvements and build scalable practices.
* **Grow with us:** Be part of an evolving organization with opportunities for professional development and increased leadership responsibility.

**The Opportunity**
-------------------


Reporting directly to the Vice President, Finance, the Director of Finance will lead GraceMed's accounting and financial reporting functions, ensuring strong financial governance, accurate reporting and effective financial operations across the organization.


This role will play a key part in supporting GraceMed's continued growth and evolution by providing financial insight, strengthening internal controls, driving process improvements and supporting the financial integration of new clinics and acquisitions.


As a trusted financial partner to the executive team, you will prepare and present financial results, strategic priorities and recommendations to support organizational decision\-making. You will also work closely with clinic managers, physicians and operational leaders to ensure finance is viewed as a collaborative and value\-added business partner.


This is a hands\-on leadership opportunity for an experienced finance professional who combines strong technical accounting expertise with commercial acumen, exceptional communication skills and a people\-centred leadership approach.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

### **Financial Reporting and Analysis**

* Lead the general ledger and monthly, quarterly and annual financial close processes, ensuring accurate and timely financial reporting.
* Oversee journal entries, accruals, reconciliations and financial statements to ensure accuracy and compliance with applicable accounting standards.
* Prepare consolidated financial statements, management reporting packages and monthly financial variance analysis.
* Provide meaningful financial insights and recommendations to senior leadership, including analysis of revenue, expenses, labour, EBITDA and cash flow.
* Prepare and present financial performance, strategic priorities, key business drivers and recommendations to the executive leadership team.
* Support executive, Board, investor and lender reporting requirements.

### **Budgeting, Forecasting and Financial Planning**

* Lead the annual budgeting process across clinics and corporate departments.
* Develop and maintain financial forecasts, models and business cases to support strategic initiatives and operational decisions.
* Monitor financial performance against budgets and forecasts, identifying risks, opportunities and areas for improvement.
* Provide financial analysis and recommendations to support business growth, investment decisions and cash management.

### **Clinic Operations and Business Integration**

* Partner with clinic managers, physicians and operational leaders to understand financial performance and identify opportunities to improve profitability and efficiency.
* Build strong internal customer relationships, providing responsive, practical financial guidance and support to operational stakeholders.
* Lead and support the financial integration of newly acquired and established clinics, including accounting systems, banking, payroll, accounts payable and internal controls.
* Support acquisition due diligence, financial analysis, purchase price accounting and integration activities.
* Standardize financial reporting, accounting practices and processes across clinic locations.
* Identify opportunities to streamline financial workflows and improve reporting accuracy and efficiency.

### **Treasury and Financial Operations**

* Oversee cash management, banking activities, accounts payable, accounts receivable and working capital management.
* Review payroll processing and related reconciliations in collaboration with internal teams and external providers.
* Ensure timely and accurate completion of statutory remittances, tax filings and financial payments.
* Maintain appropriate financial controls and approval processes for banking transactions and expenditures.

* Develop, implement and maintain financial policies, procedures and internal controls across the organization.
* Strengthen month\-end and quarter\-end close processes, financial documentation and reporti

jobs.title: Director, Software Engineering - Remote
jobs.description:
Optum Tech is a global leader in health care innovation. Our teams develop cutting\-edge solutions that help people live healthier lives and help make the health system work better for everyone. From advanced data analytics and AI to cybersecurity, we use innovative approaches to solve some of health care's most complex challenges. Your contributions here have the potential to change lives. Ready to build the next breakthrough? Join us in making healthcare work better for everyone through people\-led, responsible AI while **Caring. Connecting. Growing together.**

  

Within Enterprise Insight Engineering and Enterprise Imaging, the Stratus Imaging Archive (SI Archive) serves as Optum's cloud\-native Vendor Neutral Archive (VNA) and the foundation of our Enterprise Imaging strategy. We are seeking a Director of Software Engineering to own SI Archive end to end and scale it into the market\-leading cloud VNA\-expanding our customer footprint, leading complex cloud migrations, and embedding AI capabilities into both our imaging platform and our engineering workflows on Google Cloud.

  

You'll enjoy the flexibility to work remotely \* from anywhere within Canada (except for the Saskatchewan province) as you take on some tough challenges.

 **Primary Responsibilities:**

* Own and drive the SI Archive VNA product, partnering with Product Management to set the engineering strategy, roadmap, and execution plans while providing coaching and mentorship across engineering teams
* Define and execute strategic technical initiatives that expand VNA capabilities, customer footprint, and revenue, including DICOM and non\-DICOM ingestion, lifecycle management, routing, image exchange, and interoperability (DICOMweb, HL7, FHIR, IHE)
* Oversee large\-scale engineering programs, including PACS and archive migrations and new\-customer onboarding, ensuring compliance (QARA), system quality, architectural integrity, budgets, and delivery timelines are consistently met
* Balance customer commitments, product roadmap priorities, operational reliability, and technical modernization while owning the availability, performance, security, and cloud cost of a petabyte\-scale archive on Google Cloud backed by solid SLOs, observability, and disaster recovery
* Design, develop, and deploy AI\-powered solutions that make SI Archive AI\-ready (governed, de\-identified imaging data, AI orchestration, intelligent search), with a solid emphasis on responsible AI practices
* Use enterprise\-approved AI tools across the SDLC to streamline workflows, automate routine processes, and drive continuous improvement in engineering velocity and quality, while reviewing AI\-assisted and software outputs for accuracy, security, and performance
* Evaluate emerging imaging, cloud, and AI trends to inform solution design, system resilience, and strategic innovation, and represent SI Archive engineering with customers and senior leadership from executive briefings to escalations
* Foster a culture of technical rigor, collaboration, and high standards by hiring, developing, and growing a high\-performing organization of engineering managers and engineers

  

You'll be rewarded and recognized for your performance in an environment that will challenge you and give you clear direction on what it takes to succeed in your role as well as provide development for other roles you may be interested in.

**Required Qualifications:**

* 10\+ years of software engineering experience, including 5\+ years of progressive leadership managing large, distributed teams (20\+) and delivering complex, large\-scale software solutions
* Hands\-on experience designing, building, and operating scalable, cloud\-native software platforms on GCP, AWS, or Azure
* Demonstrated experience delivering AI\-enabled capabilities in a product or leading AI adoption across an engineering organization
* Working knowledge of DICOM, DICOMweb, HL7, FHIR, and IHE standards
* Proven track record of partnering with Product Management on product roadmaps, execution, project timelines, engineering budgets, and quality/compliance standards

 **Preferred Qualifications:**

* Hands\-on experience with Google Cloud Platform (GCP)
* Experience with large\-scale imaging data migrations and enterprise customer onboarding
* Experience implementing Agentic AI at enterprise scale, such as de\-identification, AI orchestration, or model\-ready data pipelines
* Engineering leadership experience for a VNA, PACS, or enterprise imaging product
* Demonstrated leadership capability in building high\-performing engineering teams and coaching, mentoring, and developing technical talent and leaders

* All employees working remotely will be required to adhere to UnitedHealth Group's Telecommuter Policy

 **Canada Residents Only:** The salary range for Canada residents is $127,500 \- $264,700 annually. Pay is based on several factors including but not limited to education, work experience, certifications, etc.

 *At UnitedHealth Group, our mission is to help people live healthier lives and help make the health system work better for everyone. Together, we are shaping the future of healthcare by harnessing technology and innovation to make care simpler to navigate, more affordable and more connected for the people we serve. We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcomed, valued, heard and respected, empowering people to bring their authentic selves to work and strengthening our collective impact through diverse talents, backgrounds, experiences and perspectives.*

jobs.title: Global Director, Growth Marketing
jobs.description:
**Who we are:**
---------------


Founded in 2013, Ignition is the leading revenue and billing automation platform for firms and agencies. We automate proposals, invoicing, payments and workflows in a single AI\-powered platform, empowering businesses to sell, bill and get paid faster.  

  

Ignition automates proposals, engagement letters, invoicing, payments and workflows in a single AI\-powered platform, empowering 8,500\+ businesses to sell, bill and get paid for their services with ease.
  

  

To date, Ignition customers have managed relationships with over 2\.4 million clients and earned $13b in revenue via the platform. Ignition's global workforce spans Australia, Canada, New Zealand, the Philippines, US and the UK.

**Company Values:**
-------------------

* We are better everyday
* We work without ego
* We are smarter together
* We hero our customer

**About the Role**
------------------


Ignition helps accounting firms price confidently, bill everything and get paid faster. Ignition runs the revenue side of 8,500\+ accounting firms. We’re looking for the person who builds the digital engine that finds the next 10,000, in every region we sell. You will own the pipeline Ignition generates through digital channels, in every region we sell. You'll lead performance marketing (SEO, AEO (answer engine optimization), paid search, paid social), lifecycle and nurture, and the website, co\-owning pipeline and revenue with our sales leaders in every region.


This is a hands\-on, test\-and\-learn leadership role where AI is at the core of how marketing gets done: enabling you to run the work, build reporting, and quickly spot and fix issues. This role goes beyond channels and you’ll help shape how marketing and sales work together, along with working closely with RevOps, Product Marketing and regional marketing teams across AMER, APAC and the UK.

  

**Where and How We Work**
-------------------------


We're a global team across Canada, the US, Australia and the UK. We work asynchronously where we can and offer flexible hours to make cross\-time\-zone collaboration work.

  

**What You’ll Do**
------------------

**Own and grow the global digital pipeline:**

* Co\-own the digital pipeline and revenue targets for AMER, APAC and UK, with AMER as the largest market.
* Set the global channel strategy and adapt it by region and segment, from SMB to mid\-market and enterprise firms.
* Grow self\-serve trials and signups alongside sales\-led pipeline initiatives
* Manage and optimize the paid media budget across search, social and other CPC channels, quickly reallocating spend to the best\-performing campaigns.
* Partner with regional marketing and product marketing in every region so digital programs amplify launches, campaigns and events.

**Co\-own pipeline and revenue with Sales:**

* Build a true partnership with regional sales leaders; sharing digital funnel ownership and revenue accountability for joint success.
* Shape how marketing and sales work together: lead definitions, routing, prioritization, follow\-up and feedback loops, with RevOps.
* Influence sales process and campaign builds so marketing demand converts to revenue.
* Use sales and customer insight to decide where to invest and what to test next

**Lead performance, lifecycle and the website:**

* Lead organic search, AEO, paid search and paid social via both in\-house and through agencies.
* Own lifecycle and nurture programs, moving leads to qualified pipeline and reengaging stalled or lost opportunities.
* Own the website as our primary conversion asset. Use insights from sales calls, live chat and customer conversations to sharpen messaging, improve visibility in AI\-driven search results, and deliver a consistent roadmap.
* Launch an automated and consistent online review program on G2 and Capterra to drive positive online sentiment

**Run marketing with AI:**

* Use AI and agents to do real work: content and ad variants, campaign builds, analysis, scenario planning and reporting.
* Help the team adopt AI in their own workflows, so the team can experiment and ship faster.
* Build reporting that lets you see quickly where the funnel is off track, by region, channel and segment, and act on it.

**Lead, Build, and Mentor a High\-Performing Team**:

* Lead a team covering paid and organic search, lifecycle marketing and website development, plus agency partners.
* Foster a culture of experimentation with clear priorities, regular cadence, and transparent readouts.
* Report weekly and quarterly to leadership on pipeline, channel performance, conversion and ROI.
* Build, coach and grow a high\-performing remote team.

**What you need to succeed:**

* **Experience:** 10\+ years in B2B growth or demand generation at a high\-growth SaaS company, including 3\+ years leading a team. You've owned pipeline targets across more than one region.
* **Performance marketing depth:** Hands\-on with SEO, paid search and paid social, and confident managing paid budgets and CPC economics. You know what AEO is and have a point of view on how to win in AI search.
* **Lifecycle and conversion:** You've built nurture programs and improved website conversion through steady testing.
* **AI fluency:** You use AI tools daily and can show how they changed your output. You're comfortable connecting tools like Claude or ChatGPT to your marketing stack, building agents or AI workflows, and teaching your team to **do the same.**
* **Analytical agility:** You can pull your own data, find where the funnel broke, and make a call. HubSpot and a BI tool (Looker, Tableau or similar) are part of your day.
* **Global performance:** Owned pipeline targets across more than one region
* **Leadership and partnership:** You build strong remote teams. You have a track record of co\-owning pipeline and revenue with sales leaders, earning their trust and influencing how the two teams work together. You communicate performance clearly to executives.
* **Mindset:** Y

 Job Description: 
 You are the bridge between what Critical Mass makes and what Adobe builds. 

 This role is embedded simultaneously in the Adobe product team and the Critical Mass creative team. You are a strategic partner — the person who knows what Adobe is building before it ships, understands what the creative team is capable of, and finds the opportunity between those two things. Your presence closes the distance between “we could” and “we do.” You do that by knowing how, or figuring it out. You are a creative director who builds. Your instinct when an idea enters the room is “yes, and”… and  you can follow through. You make the idea exist fast enough to influence the direction, not just validate it.

 You Will: 
 The Job - You operate in multiple swim lanes: you work with the strategy team to understand the landscape of the business needs and what’s possible. You’re embedded in creative team concepting: bringing technical knowledge into briefs early, prototyping ideas quickly enough to shape direction, and raising the ambition of what the team believes is possible. You run your own work: identifying platform and partnership opportunities, building new statements of work, and sitting at Adobe’s product roadmap table as a voice from the creative side. Mentorship runs through the role: you’re actively building the technical fluency of the creative team around you.

 What You Produce - Rapid prototypes that make abstract concepts concrete for creative teams and clients. A sustained, strategic point of view on where Adobe’s product capabilities create creative opportunity, translated into the agency’s output and business development. New business territory: expanded statements of work, platform partnerships, and product-adjacent engagements developed from your proximity to both sides. Active investment in the prototype-forward capabilities of the creative team.

 The Standard - The measure of this role is not how impressive the work is in isolation: it’s how much further the creative team goes because you’re in the room. Your job is to enable teams and expand the creative space on what’s possible. You are a practitioner, not an observer.  And you build client relationships at the same time. 

 You Have: 
 Genuine creative ambition.
 Pushing creative possibilities through an uncertain and constantly changing landscape of technologies.
 You are deeply curious and have the agency to act on it.
 You explore new technologies and how they can support, augment, and amplify teams.
 You have a portfolio of built things: real examples of concepts you made concrete, ideas you moved from “what if” to something a client could react to.
 Experience at the boundary of creative and product teams, with relationships on both sides and a track record of using that position to expand what’s possible.
 The communication skills to present confidently in a product roadmap meeting and in a client creative review, and to be taken seriously in both.

 What We Offer: 
 Global maternity and parental leave

 Vacation, compassionate leave, personal/sick days, and flex days

 Early Dismissal Friday’s (off at 3:00 PM local time every Friday)

This role develops new tools and processes to optimize flow, inventory, capacity, service, and cost across the supply chain, leveraging global relationships and best practices while using data, analytics, and scenario modelling to inform strategic decisions.

This position leads a team responsible for creating and validating integrated supply chain plans and forecasts, aligning logistics, replenishment, store operations, and eCommerce activities. The Director also manages strategic activities such as seasonal and promotional flow plans, collaborating with 3PL partners and internal teams to balance customer availability, operational capacity, inventory, speed, and cost-effectiveness.

Reporting to the SVP of Solutions, Strategy & Growth, this leader ensures our intelligence fuels new business, deepens client relationships and sharpens how we sell and deliver our solutions.

Key Responsibilities

Unify thought leadership across the company

Build and run a single intelligence agenda that draws on expertise from every connected capability leader and agency.
Partner with capability and agency leaders to surface, sharpen and package their best thinking into a consistent company point of view.

Bachelor’s degree required in a relevant discipline such as business, finance, human resources, law, accounting or actuarial science; an MBA or other relevant advanced degree is preferred, and a professional compensation designation such as CCP, or equivalent, is an asset
