**Design the Next Century: An Enduring Leadership Legacy at Hudbay**  



For you, mining has never been just a job—it has been a life passion. It was more than the financial advantage or the multicultural opportunities; it was more than a school where you became a master of your domain. It was your source of knowledge, your greatest adventure, and the primary path upon which you built your life.  



You understand the fundamental truth of our industry: "If it can’t be grown, it must be mined." At this stage of your journey, you aren’t just looking for another role; you are looking for the opportunity to steward the future of a sector that has been your life’s work, ensuring the pride you take in this foundational industry is passed down to the next generation of leaders.  


**Why Hudbay?**  

Hudbay provides the metals the world needs. We work sustainably, transform lives and create better futures for communities. We live this purpose every day.  



Hudbay is a company where a century of resilience meets a 100\-year vision for the future. As we turn 100 in 2027, we are seeking visionary leaders who will steer our next hundred years. While none of us will be here to see the end of that next century, the legacy of your leadership will be sure to leave a positive and indelible mark.  


At Hudbay, you will be the vital driver of business decisions that translate into millions of dollars in investment, direct impacts on local communities, and the economic prosperity of the countries where we operate. With a world\-class portfolio across Canada, Peru, and the United States, we offer a prestigious platform to leave a multi\-generational mark. At Hudbay, your leadership is the cornerstone of a sustainable, global legacy—one that will stand long after your career is complete.

The Director, Government Relations leads, designs, and executes Hudbay’s Canadian government relations strategy and policy advocacy. **Director of Marketing — Job Description**

**MedixSafe \| Full\-Time \| Reports to the President**

*This role is hybrid and will require you to work in office up to 3 days per week.*

**About MedixSafe**

MedixSafe provides secure medication storage and narcotics tracking for EMS agencies, fire departments, hospitals, and healthcare organizations. Our intelligent security hardware and cloud software help organizations store, track, and audit controlled substances safely and in compliance with regulatory requirements.

New DEA regulations are changing how EMS agencies handle controlled substances, and our newest product extension delivers vial\-level tracking without disrupting medic workflow. We are scaling, and we need a marketing leader to make MedixSafe the category leader in controlled substance compliance and inventory intelligence.

**The Role**

The Director of Marketing owns MedixSafe's marketing strategy, pipeline generation, and category positioning, and is accountable for marketing's contribution to revenue. You will turn regulatory change and operational risk into messaging that drives demand from enterprise EMS agencies, fire departments, and healthcare systems.

**This is a hands\-on leadership role in a lean team.** You will work directly with the President and Sales, and lead a Marketing Coordinator who you will share day\-to\-day execution and marketing operations (the Coordinator also supports Customer Activation). AI is central to how we operate: we use tools like Claude daily and expect you to build a function that does more with less.

**What You'll Own**

**Strategy, Positioning \& Category Leadership**

* Set the marketing strategy, plan, and budget, prioritized against revenue goals.
* Define and communicate our value proposition \- in close collaboration with our CTO who also leads Product
* Lead competitive positioning and educate EMS and healthcare leadership on regulatory change and medication diversion risk.
* Build executive thought leadership through speaking, industry research and benchmarking, and analyst and media engagement.

**Demand Generation \& Pipeline**

* Build a scalable demand engine, including account\-based marketing for large EMS agencies and multi\-site healthcare organizations.
* Own paid and organic acquisition: our established Google Ads program, the launch of Meta Ads, SEO, and Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) for AI\-powered search.
* Lead integrated campaigns across content, email nurture, webinars, events, and channel partners.
* Own HubSpot strategy, attribution, and reporting on pipeline, cost per lead, and ROI.

**Product Launch \& Sales Enablement**

* Lead positioning, messaging, and launch campaigns for new products, including vial\-level tracking.
* Equip sales with playbooks, battlecards, enterprise collateral, ROI tools, and case studies that shorten deal cycles.
* Set conference and trade show strategy and measure what each event returns.

**Team \& AI\-Enabled Operations**

* Lead and develop the Marketing Coordinator, who executes campaigns, webinar production, event logistics, website and HubSpot updates, and Canva asset creation.
* Build AI\-assisted workflows and automation so a lean team delivers high output while protecting accuracy, brand consistency, and customer data.
* Manage agencies and vendors where specialist help is needed.

**How Success Is Measured**

* Growth in marketing\-sourced pipeline, especially enterprise opportunities.
* Cost\-efficient customer acquisition and faster sales cycles.
* Market recognition as the leader in controlled substance compliance.

**What You Bring**

**Required**

* 5–10 years of B2B marketing experience, including ownership of pipeline targets and a marketing budget.
* A track record building demand programs, ABM, and product launches that supported enterprise sales teams.
* Hands\-on command of digital performance marketing: Google Ads, SEO, conversion tracking, and campaign analytics.
* Advanced HubSpot experience across campaigns, automation, lead management, and reporting.
* Experience directing or mentoring at least one marketer, coordinator, or agency
* Ability to turn complex regulatory topics into simple, compelling messaging, with strong writing and a sharp eye for on\-brand design.
* Practical, daily use of AI tools such as Claude or ChatGPT to raise productivity and quality.

**Preferred**

* Experience marketing hardware plus SaaS, IoT, or medical technology.
* Experience in regulated markets such as healthcare, compliance, or public safety.
* Experience with Meta Ads, AEO, GA4, Google Search Console, and Google Tag Manager.
* Experience running webinar programs, trade shows, and channel partner marketing.

**How You Work**

* Entrepreneurial and hands\-on: you set the plan and roll up your sleeves to execute it.
* Analytical and outcome\-driven, with decisions grounded in data.
* Collaborative with sales leadership and comfortable in a scaling company.

jobs.title: Director, Sales - Bulloch POS
jobs.description:
At Dover Fueling Solutions (DFS), we are taking fueling and convenience retail to the next level. We are passionate about cultivating excellence in everything we do, but what really fuels us is our people. They’re the heart of our company. As an employee, our promise to you is that you’ll work on new and innovative products and solutions, be mentored by managers and teammates who are collaborative, caring, and act with integrity, and have the opportunity to grow in ways that are meaningful to you. Unique and interesting projects – both locally and globally – will challenge you and allow you to pursue different and rewarding career paths.

We are #EnergizedByGrowth.

DFS is part of a legacy of leadership that spans back generations, made up of some of the most trusted, leading-edge brands in the industry. As part of Dover Corporation and with our talented, innovative, outstanding people, we are doing great things and redefining what is possible in fueling and convenience retail. Providing advanced fuel-dispensing equipment, including clean energy solutions, systems and payment, automatic tank gauging and wet stock-management solutions, DFS comprises the product brands of Wayne Fueling Systems, OPW Fuel Management Systems, ClearView, Tokheim, ProGauge, Fairbanks, LIQAL, AvaLAN, and Bulloch Technologies. Headquartered in Austin, TX, DFS has a significant technology development and manufacturing presence worldwide, including facilities in Brazil, China, India, Italy, Poland, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom and the United States.

The Opportunity

Dover Fueling Solutions is seeking a commercial leader to shape the next phase of growth

for Bulloch POS in Canada. Bulloch is a proven point-of-sale technology platform with a

strong position in the Canadian market.

The immediate mandate is clear: build and embed a disciplined, scalable account

management model that deepens our most important customer relationships, strengthens

execution, and creates durable growth.

The Director will engage senior IT and business leaders at large enterprise accounts,

translate their priorities and technology roadmaps into actionable account strategies, and

coordinate DFS resources to deliver long-term customer value.

Additional focus will be selective new-logo growth with Canadian retailers not currently

using Bulloch. These are strategic pursuits with sales cycles that can extend several years

and require thoughtful relationship development, technical credibility, and disciplined

opportunity management.

The Director will lead a team and have significant exposure across DFS. After establishing a

strong Canadian account management framework and demonstrating sustained

execution, the successful candidate may have opportunities to contribute to Bulloch’s

longer-term U.S. growth agenda.

What You Will Own

Build the account management system. Design and implement a consistent

framework for account planning, customer governance, opportunity management,

executive engagement, and performance reviews across Bulloch Canada.

Lead and grow strategic accounts. Develop multi-year plans connecting customer

technology priorities with Bulloch capabilities, investments, and measurable

business outcomes.

Become a trusted partner to enterprise technology leaders. Build credibility with

senior IT, technology, operations, and business stakeholders and understand their

roadmaps, integration requirements, risks, and priorities.

Create disciplined customer governance. Establish executive business reviews,

account health assessments, stakeholder maps, opportunity pipelines, and clear

accountability for customer commitments.

Drive retention, expansion, and lifetime value. Identify opportunities to deepen

relationships through additional deployments, software, services, and evolving

customer requirements.

Win targeted new logos. Lead selective pursuits with Canadian retailers not

currently using Bulloch, recognizing the strategic and long-term nature of these

opportunities.

Lead regional selling directly. Take an active role in solution positioning, deal

shaping, qualification, negotiation, and closing with smaller regional and

independent retailers.

Develop a high-performing team. Coach direct reports in strategic account

management, commercial discipline, executive engagement, and opportunity

development.

Orchestrate cross-functional execution. Work across Product, Engineering,

Implementation, Customer Success, Support, Service, Marketing, and Finance to

remove obstacles and deliver a consistent customer experience.

Bring the market into the business. Translate customer feedback, competitive

dynamics, and technology trends into actionable insights for product and business

leadership.

Operate with commercial rigor. Own forecasting, pipeline quality, account KPIs,

quarterly planning, and transparent reporting of opportunities and risks.

What Success Looks Like

Within The First 12–18 Months

A repeatable account management framework is operating across Canada and

actively used by the team.

Strategic customers have clear account plans, governance cadences, stakeholder

maps, and documented growth priorities.

Bulloch strengthens retention and share of wallet while building credible long-term

pipelines with targeted new customers.

Customer commitments are better coordinated across DFS, with clearer ownership

and fewer execution gaps.

The team demonstrates stronger commercial discipline and executive-level

customer engagement.

Bulloch’s Canadian business is positioned to scale without relying on tribal

knowledge or individual relationships.

What You Bring

7+ years of progressive B2B sales, strategic account management, or commercial

leadership experience, ideally in enterprise software, SaaS, POS, payments, retail

technology, or another complex technology environment.

Demonstrated success building or materially improving strategic account

management practices, rather than simply operating within an established process.

Experience managing large enterprise customers with complex stakeholder groups

and long-term technology roadmaps.

Confidence engaging senior IT and business leaders and translating technical

requirements into commercial strategy.

Strong commercial judgment across account planning, opportunity qualification,

negotiation, forecasting, and long-cycle selling.

Experience developing people and creating accountability within a small, high

impact team.

Ability to influence effectively across Product, Engineering, Customer Success, and

Other Functions Without Relying On Formal Authority.

Strong written and verbal communication skills with an ability to distill complexity

into clear decisions and actions.

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
Ability to travel as required to customers and DFS locations.

Preferred Experience

Canadian retail, convenience, fuel, or multi-site enterprise technology experience.
POS, payments, forecourt, or adjacent retail technology experience.
Challenger, MEDDPICC, or another disciplined enterprise-selling methodology.
Experience working within a global technology organization and distributed cross

functional teams.

Why This Role

This is an opportunity to shape how a market-leading technology business manages its

most important customer relationships.

The successful candidate will have the mandate to build, not simply maintain—creating

the account management discipline that supports Bulloch’s next stage of growth while

gaining exposure to senior customers and leaders across Dover Fueling Solutions.

For a high-potential commercial leader, the role provides a platform to demonstrate

enterprise leadership and expand into broader growth responsibilities over time.

Founded as a community initiative and registered as a charitable, not-for-profit society in 1992, Augustine House Society owns and operates Augustine House, a special seniors’ residence that is home to 150 wonderful residents. The residence offers a distinctive continuum of independent living, assisted living and long-term residential care, allowing residents to access additional support as their needs evolve while remaining in a familiar, home-like community. As a private-pay facility, Augustine House benefits from a strong financial and physical foundation, underpinned by a deep commitment to dignity, compassion, individual well-being and excellence in care. The organization seeks a leader who is passionate about being visible and engaged with residents and families, and who is recognized for fostering a positive, supportive, accountable and compassionate work environment that attracts and retains exceptional staff.

Reporting to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director will provide the strategic vision and leadership to support the continued growth and financial stewardship of Augustine House, with full P&L accountability. The Executive Director will champion a culture grounded in quality, service, transparency and, above all, engagement. Working closely with a dedicated Board and a passionate, committed management team, the Executive Director will translate the Society’s vision, mission and priorities into clear strategic and operational plans, while overseeing resident services, care, human resources, labour relations, finances, marketing, facilities and organizational performance. Description

Job Overview:

The Vice President, General Ledger Accounting
will lead the General Ledger Accounting function for an assigned portfolio of markets and regions. The Vice President is accountable for the overall performance of the GL teams that prepare, review and deliver monthly financial statements and related client deliverables for the communities supported within that portfolio.

Reporting to the SVP, Client Accounting, the Vice President will establish the strategic direction, operating priorities and performance expectations for the assigned GL organization. The role will work closely with market and regional leaders, Financial Management leadership and Client Accounting Shared Services partners to ensure financial statements are accurate, timely and supported by consistent processes, strong controls, effective issue escalation and disciplined performance management.

The Vice President will lead transformation and standardization across the assigned portfolio while ensuring the operating model remains responsive to local market needs, management agreements, governing documents and client expectations. The ideal candidate is a strategic, technically strong and service-oriented leader who can develop leaders, create accountability, resolve complex reporting issues and improve the quality, consistency and efficiency of financial statement delivery.

Due to the global nature of this position, the Vice President should be comfortable working across multiple time zones (Pacific Standard Time to Eastern Standard Time), within reason.

Job Responsibilities

The job duties listed are typical examples of the work performed by positions in this job classification. Not all duties assigned to every position are included, nor is it expected that all positions will be assigned every duty.

General Ledger Accounting

Provide executive ownership of the monthly close and financial statement reporting cycle for all communities within the assigned portfolio, ensuring accurate and timely delivery in accordance with internal policies and procedures, regulatory requirements, management agreements, property governing documents and client expectations.
Establish the portfolio’s operating rhythm, reporting timetables, quality standards, review protocols, escalation paths and delivery-tracking requirements for monthly financial statements.
Ensure the integrity of general ledger activity, including account reconciliations, accruals, prepaid expenses and amortization, fixed assets, interfund and reserve activity, cost recovery billings and other client deliverables.
Serve as the senior escalation authority for complex accounting matters, financial statement exceptions, late or at-risk deliverables and significant client or operational issues within the assigned portfolio.
Oversee GL support for annual client audits and budgets, special assessments, loans, mortgages and other significant client financial obligations.
Establish and monitor service level and key performance indicators for financial statement delivery
Drive leadership accountability for results against service-level and key performance indicators, reviewing performance regularly and leading corrective action plans where targets are missed.
Build the leadership capability, succession plans, organizational structure and workforce capacity required to support client growth, retention and changing business needs.
Attract, develop and retain high-caliber leaders and accounting professionals while promoting a culture of collaboration, accountability, trust and service excellence.

Business Partner

Serve as the senior Client Accounting business partner for market presidents, regional leaders, Financial Management leadership and other senior stakeholders within the assigned portfolio.
Partner with the VP, Accounts Receivable and Resales; VP, Accounts Payable; Senior Director, Treasury Services; and other Client Accounting leaders to ensure cohesive end-to-end service delivery and timely resolution of cross-functional issues.
Translate portfolio performance, operational trends and accounting risks into clear recommendations and decisions for the SVP, Client Accounting and senior market leadership.
Build strong relationships with supported markets to understand local culture, client requirements and operating needs while reinforcing enterprise standards and shared-services objectives.
Act as a senior resource for board members, property and association managers and other stakeholders by leading the resolution of significant accounting and financial reporting matters.
Represent General Ledger Accounting in senior leadership forums, cross-functional initiatives and major business decisions affecting client accounting and reporting.

Financial Planning

Develop and manage the GL operating budget for the assigned portfolio, including headcount planning, forecasts, productivity assumptions and variance analysis.
Align staffing, leadership capacity and workload to the monthly close cycle, client growth, market transitions and service requirements.
Develop business cases and investment recommendations for organizational changes, systems, automation, training and process improvement initiatives.
Monitor portfolio capacity and cost-to-serve indicators and take action when workload or service demand exceeds available resources.

People Management

Lead a team of 125+ associates through a senior leadership structure within North America
Attract, develop and retain diverse, high-caliber talent, while developing an engaged team to build the capabilities required for the organization to perform at high levels.
Promote a culture of collaboration, trust and support.
Clearly define and communicate performance responsibilities, goals, expectations and objectives.
Regularly evaluate teams to determine performance and whether company standards for work performance are met. If expectations are not met, are responsible for coaching and corrective actions.
Conduct ongoing performance management activities by providing constructive feedback and coaching through regular check-ins, structured one-on-one meetings, mid-year touchpoints and annual reviews.

Project Management

Provide executive sponsorship and governance for large-scale GL initiatives affecting the assigned portfolio, including market integrations, client transitions and accounting platform migrations.
Establish project objectives, decision rights, accountability, milestones, risks and escalation paths in partnership with project and functional leaders.
Ensure market and GL team readiness through effective planning, communication, training, change management and post-implementation support.
Provide clear status updates to senior leadership on timeline, accomplishments, decisions, risks, issues and required support.

Business Process Improvement

Lead the standardization and continuous improvement of GL processes, review practices, controls and workflows across the assigned markets and regions.
Establish and maintain standard operating procedures, service-level expectations, process documentation and governance for the GL function.
Partner with the Business Transformation and technology teams to define business requirements, prioritize enhancements, improve reporting capabilities and support adoption of enterprise accounting platforms.
Evaluate opportunities to automate, centralize or redesign work while maintaining accountability, control integrity and service quality.
Develop dashboards that provide visibility into financial statement delivery, quality, productivity, backlog, capacity, risk and technology adoption.
Use performance data, root-cause analysis and market feedback to identify systemic issues and implement sustainable corrective actions.
Share and implement leading practices across the GL organization and collaborate with peer functional leaders to improve end-to-end Client Accounting processes.

Compliance & Governance

Maintain an effective internal control environment over the general ledger and financial reporting functions, including segregation of duties, review controls, documentation standards and escalation procedures.
Ensure GL processes adhere to applicable accounting standards, federal and state requirements, company policies, standard operating procedures, management agreements and client-specific obligations.
Coordinate with internal and external auditors on audit requests, control reviews, year-end support and remediation activities.
Monitor regulatory, accounting and industry developments that may affect client accounting operations and lead implementation of required changes across the assigned portfolio.
Ensure the appropriate handling of sensitive and confidential information and safeguard client and company assets.

Additional Duties

Partner with the SVP, Client Accounting and other GL leaders to carry out the strategy, operating model and priorities for General Ledger Accounting.
Practice and adhere to FirstService Residential Global Service Standards.
Always conduct business with the highest standards of personal, professional and ethical conduct.
Anticipate needs across supported markets and manage department resources to provide timely and reliable service; prioritize and communicate when requests exceed capacity.

Strong analytical skills to perform data collection and benchmarking against best practices.

Ability to communicate a clear strategy and vision for General Ledger Accounting across our organization and have experience in leading change management initiatives that bring people, process, and technology together from different functional areas to deliver a quality financial services customer experience necessary.
Passion for gaining efficiency through process change while creating a positive team environment where we can recruit, develop, and retain talent.
Comfort with rolling out new technologies, automation and outsourcing to third parties to improve accuracy, timeliness and maximize efficiencies a must.
Knowledge leader in both financial accounting and the Condo/HOA industry. Sound business acumen and the ability to present practical solutions is a key requirement.
Experience interacting with or working through change management items with field operations personnel.

jobs.title: Strategy & Corporate Development Director (CA)
jobs.description:
At PointClickCare our mission is simple: to help providers deliver exceptional care. And that starts with our people. As a leading health tech company that’s founder-led and privately held, we empower our employees to push boundaries, innovate, and shape the future of healthcare.

With the largest long-term and post-acute care dataset and a Marketplace of 400+ integrated partners, our platform serves over 30,000 provider organizations, making a real difference in millions of lives. We also reinvest a significant percentage of our revenue back into research and development, ensuring our employees have the resources to innovate and make a lasting impact. Recognized by Forbes as a top private cloud company and honored as one of Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, we offer flexibility, growth opportunities, and meaningful work.

At PointClickCare, we empower our people to be the architects of a smarter healthcare future; one that is human-first and accelerated by AI to create meaningful and lasting change. Employees harness AI as a catalyst for creativity, productivity, and thoughtful decision-making. By integrating AI tools into our daily workflows, collaboration is enhanced, outcomes are improved, and every team member has the proficiency to maximize their impact. It all starts with our hiring practices where we uncover AI expertise that complements our mission, and we continue to invest in training and development to nurture innovation throughout the employee journey.

Join us in redefining healthcare — so it doesn’t just survive, it thrives. To learn more about PointClickCare, check out Life at PointClickCare and connect with us on Glassdoor and LinkedIn.

Travel to Office expectations**

For Remote Roles
: If this role is remote, there will be in-office events that will require travel to and from the Mississauga and/or Salt Lake City office. These will include, but not limited to, onboarding, team events, semi-annual and annual team meetings.

For Hybrid Roles
: If this role is Hybrid, there will be an expectation to reside within commutable distance to the office/location specified in the job listing. This will include, but not limited to, weekly/bi-weekly/monthly events in the office with your specific team. This is a requirement for this role.

Team Summary

Strategy & Corporate Development is a small team that partners directly with PointClickCare’s Executive Team to decide where the company plays and how it wins over the next 3 – 5 years. This team owns the full arc from insight generation to stakeholder alignment—shaping long-range strategy and financial planning; tracking market, competitive, and regulatory shifts across long-term and post-acute care; sizing our highest-impact new growth opportunities; and deciding whether to build, buy, or partner to capture these opportunities. When the answer is buy, the same team sources, evaluates, negotiates, and closes relevant transactions (M&A, joint ventures), setting them up for successful integration and performance against underwriting theses. This is a small, but high-impact team with consistent opportunities for driving impactful decisions and meaningful senior leadership-level exposure.

The team operates in a hybrid model, with most roles based in Toronto and a few remote across the US, consisting of one SVP, two Directors, one Senior Manager, one Manager, and one Senior Analyst.

Job Summary

As PointClickCare approaches $1 billion in ARR, ensuring the whole company aligns behind a clear, coherent strategy becomes ever more critical.

The Strategy & Corporate Development Director leads enterprise-level strategy initiatives that shape PointClickCare’s long-term growth agenda, portfolio priorities, and investment decisions. The Director independently frames complex and ambiguous strategic questions, integrates perspectives across end-markets and functions, and develops recommendations for the Executive Team and Board. As a strategic thought partner to the SVP, Strategy & Corporate Development, the Director leads major components of long-range and annual planning, drives alignment on enterprise priorities, and provides direction and quality oversight to other team members supporting strategic initiatives.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the identification, stack-ranking prioritization, and provide recommendations to the organization around our highest-potential growth opportunities that support the company’s aspirations through whitespace analyses, market inventory and pricing outlooks, and assessment of how customers’ business models are evolving
Lead strategic assessments of market, customer, competitive, and regulatory developments. Synthesize and frame major, future-weighted headwinds and tailwinds into clear hypotheses, supported by proprietary intelligence, advising the Executive Team on the “What? So What? Now What?”
Lead major components of PointClickCare’s enterprise strategic planning process, translating long-term strategic priorities into financial assumptions, enterprise objectives, investment requirements, and measurable performance indicators. Integrate inputs across end-markets and functions, challenge inconsistent assumptions, and escalate material risks, gaps, and trade-offs for Executive Team decision.
Formulate, refine, and cascade our play-to-win strategy across all end-markets to the organization, ensuring senior leadership buy-in on where the company will play, how it will win, and what it will deprioritize, and establish mechanisms to monitor execution against agreed strategic priorities.
Contribute to and inform portfolio management and capital allocation decisions, including building the case for major organic and inorganic investments, evaluating M&A and joint ventures, and assessing divestitures and wind-downs. Develop and present investment recommendations, articulate financial and strategic trade-offs, challenge underlying assumptions, and advise senior leadership on whether and how PointClickCare should proceed.
Coach and mentor junior team members, providing guidance and feedback that strengthens strategic thinking, analytical rigor, executive communication, and independent judgment.

Required Skills & Experience

7+ years of experience at a top management consulting firm, private equity, investment bank, or in-house strategy experience at a scaled, sponsor-backed business
Successful track record leading or contributing to evaluation of expansion in existing and new segments, including market entry options for new businesses, go-to-market strategy for new product offerings, and build-buy-partner assessments
Demonstrated qualitative (market research, synthesis, hypothesis development) and quantitative (Excel, financial modeling) analytical skills
Strong financial acumen and ability to understand core business levers
Exceptional communicator, able to convey complex ideas in a clear, concise manner both verbally and in writing
Self-starter who thrives and can manage multiple workstreams in fast-paced environments

Preferred Experience

Familiarity with the US healthcare system
Exposure to SaaS and HCIT business models and metrics
Experience working directly with Executive Teams, Boards, and investors

PointClickCare Benefits & Perks

Benefits starting from Day 1!

Retirement Plan Matching

Flexible Paid Time Off

Wellness Support Programs and Resources

Parental & Caregiver Leaves

Fertility & Adoption Support

Continuous Development Support Program

Employee Assistance Program

Allyship and Inclusion Communities

Employee Recognition … and more!

jobs.title: Director, Data Management
jobs.description:
The Director, Data Management will have overall responsibility for the Data Management team, including Clinical Data Managers, Clinical Data Coordinators, Clinical Study Builders and Clinical Data Coders.

The Director, Data Management, will provide strategic leadership and oversight of data management resources, processes, and deliverables, ensuring the quality, integrity, and timely delivery of clinical trial data.

The Director, Data Management will oversee and participate in all clinical data management activities required to ensure that data captured in clinical trials undertaken, or managed by Indero, are collected, managed and reported clearly, accurately and securely. In addition, this position is required to conduct all these activities in conformance with applicable regulatory requirements, industry guidelines and Indero’s SOP while respecting Indero’s commitment to sponsor’s requirements and timelines.

More specifically, the Director, Data Management must:

Strategic Leadership and Collaboration

Inspire, lead and develop all functions within Data Management by helping to formulate a clear vision for the future and attracting and retaining top talent.
Define and drive the Data Management strategy and roadmap, including innovation, standardization and automation initiatives that support the company’s business objectives.
Collaborate with Biostatistics, Risk-Based Study Management, Project Management and other function leaders to align strategies, processes and tools, and to ensure integrated delivery of clinical trial data.
Represent Data Management in sponsor and client meetings and manage the escalation of study risks and issues related to Data Management deliverables.
Monitor industry trends and regulatory changes in clinical data management.
Provide leadership and accountability to study teams assigned to the dedicated client portfolio.

People and Resource Management

Provide direct oversight of data management operations, including planning and assigning work, overseeing the performance of direct reports and conducting performance reviews.
Evaluate the performance of assigned project personnel.
Oversee and provide ongoing training/mentoring to data management and programming staff and review/approve documentation generated by staff, as necessary.
Ensure that all trainings assigned to oneself and to direct and indirect reports are completed on time, and provide direct and indirect reports with appropriate support.
Oversee resource allocation for Data Management activities across clinical trials and internal initiatives.
Lead the development of flexible resourcing strategies, including internal and external resources, to meet the evolving demands of the company.
Adhere to and promote company values and related expected behaviors and follow company SOPs and processes for all deliverables.

Financial Management and Oversight

Oversee budget and resources allocated for Data Management.
Lead the annual Data Management budget planning.
Be responsible for the operational and financial health of Data Management-supported clinical trials by monitoring key operational metrics and supporting budget oversight and forecasting.
Participate in the review of Master Service Agreements (MSA) and work orders with external service providers, process and track payment requests to ensure accordance with the budget and the needs of the study.
Develop Work Orders with external service providers, process and track payment requests to ensure accordance with the budget and the needs of the study.
Oversee activities performed by external service providers to ensure they are done in accordance with effective Work Orders, applicable regulations and Indero SOPs (if applicable).
Oversee the selection, implementation and ongoing management of Data Management systems (e.g., EDC) and strategic technology vendors.

Operational Excellence, Quality and Compliance

Oversee development and optimization of Data Management processes with specific focus on efficiency and quality, while maintaining or exceeding industry best practices.
Define, analyze and monitor Data Management key performance indicators (KPIs) and quality metrics to ensure quality, compliance and timely delivery, and report on performance to senior leadership.
Ensure that Data Management standards, SOPs, processes and trainings are aligned with applicable ICH-GCP guidelines, regulatory authority requirements and industry best practices.
Oversee the definition, writing and updating of data management SOPs.
Monitor timelines and ensure that data management deadlines are met.

Clinical Data Management Delivery

Provide escalation support and expertise to project teams, sponsors and external vendors on complex data management matters, as needed.
Provide support and close oversight to data management team activities for clinical trials from the development of study protocols to the completion of study reports.
Oversee the development of eCRF specifications (including data capture screens and edit check specifications) needed to build a study-specific clinical database/electronic data capture (EDC) system.
Oversee the programming and ongoing maintenance of the clinical database.
Oversee the validation and testing of the clinical database e.g. User Acceptance Testing.
Oversee the development of eCRF completion guidelines and other training material required to train site users and monitors.
Oversee the development of data transfer agreements and specifications with vendors providing external data (e.g. laboratory results).
Oversee the review/development of the data management plan (DMP), and other clinical data management related documentation.
Oversee ongoing data review/cleaning during study conduct.
Ensure that data management documentation is complete and up-to-date in the eTMF.
Oversee the archiving of the clinical database and related documents.

Employee may be assigned to other responsibilities that do not pertain to their former description, if they have the required experience, are qualified and/or have received adequate training.

Requirements:

B.Sc. or M.Sc., or related field;
Minimum of 8 years of leadership experience, plus at least 15 years of clinical trials experience in biotechnology, pharmaceutical or CRO industry.
Proven experience leading and developing data management teams and managing multiple studies and sponsor portfolios.
Demonstrated experience leading global or cross-functional initiatives and influencing strategy across multiple stakeholders.
Experience with budget planning and resource management, including the oversight of external vendors.
Experience in the setup, validation and oversight of EDC systems and other clinical data systems.
Experience supporting sponsor audits and regulatory inspections is an asset.
Strong knowledge of ICH-GCP, CDISC standards (CDASH, SDTM), and applicable data protection regulations.
Strategic thinking, with the ability to define a vision and translate it into operational plans.
Strong leadership and coaching skills, with the ability to teach, train and mentor employees at all levels.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence at all levels of the organization and with external stakeholders in a matrix, cross-functional environment.
Strong organizational and planning skills, with the ability to prioritize multiple competing demands in a fast-paced environment.
Sound judgment, problem-solving and decision-making skills.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English; French is an asset.
Good knowledge of good clinical practices, and applicable Health Canada and Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulations/guidelines.

Our company:

At Indero, you will work with brilliant and driven colleagues. Our values are collaboration, innovation, reliability and responsiveness. We offer a stimulating work environment and attractive advancement opportunities.

In this position, you will be eligible for the following perks:

Permanent full-time position
Flexible schedule
Vacation
Home-based position
Ongoing learning and development

﻿About Indero

A Global Clinical Leader In Dermatology!

﻿Formerly known as Innovaderm, Indero is a world-renowned expert and clinical research leader in dermatology. We have more than two decades of experience serving a broad range of indications, patient populations, administration routes, and drug classes, and a global footprint.

﻿Indero is a dual-focus CRO for dermatology and rheumatology, with 25+ years’ experience in clinical research and trial delivery. Our full-service approach – which includes everything from protocol design and patient recruitment to trial monitoring and biometrics – provides biotech and pharmaceutical sponsors with the rigorous scientific foundation and tailored expertise their studies need to reach the finish line efficiently and effectively. With capabilities in North America, Europe, Asia Pacific and Latin America; vast, continuously growing relationships with investigators and patients; and a dedicated research clinic through which we design and execute our own studies, Indero is the ideal CRO partner for clinical needs at global scale.

﻿Indero is committed to providing equitable treatment and equal opportunity to all individuals. As such, Indero will provide accommodations throughout the recruitment and selection process to applicants with disabilities, upon request.

﻿Indero only accepts applicants who can legally work in Canada.

jobs.title: Vice President of Service Management Operations
jobs.description:
The Vice President of Service Management and Operations leads the company’s overall service management and operational ecosystem. This role oversees service delivery, process management, customer support operations, quality control, operational performance, and resource allocation, ensuring that all company services are delivered efficiently, consistently, and sustainably in accordance with established standards.

Focusing on operational efficiency and service delivery quality, this position serves as a key link between customer service, business operations, technical support, product, sales, and quality management teams. By establishing standardized service management policies, operational monitoring mechanisms, and performance evaluation systems, the role drives improvements in service response efficiency, customer satisfaction, service quality, and overall operational performance.

Core Responsibilities

I. Service Operations Strategy
- Define the company’s service management strategy, annual operational goals, and execution plans.
- Develop a service operations management framework aligned with the company’s business growth.
- Establish service management policies, service standards, and operational guidelines.
- Optimize the service organizational structure and operational management model.
- Enhance the scalability and long-term operational sustainability of the service ecosystem.

II. Service Delivery and Operations Management
- Oversee all customer-facing and internal service delivery activities.
- Supervise service requests, task allocation, and the execution of service delivery.
- Establish service delivery workflows and quality management standards.
- Ensure service teams meet agreed-upon service levels.
- Manage and resolve critical service delivery issues and operational anomalies.

III. Service Process and Quality Management
- Develop standardized service processes and operational procedures.
- Monitor service quality, adherence to standards, and compliance with workflows.
- Implement mechanisms for service quality audits and continuous improvement.
- Analyze issues arising during service delivery and drive root-cause remediation.
- Streamline service processes to reduce redundant tasks and operational delays.

IV. Service Performance and SLA Management
- Define service operations KPIs and performance evaluation frameworks.
- Monitor compliance with Service Level Agreements (SLAs).
- Track key metrics such as service response times, resolution times, and completion rates.
- Maintain service operations dashboards and management reporting systems.
- Guide underperforming teams in developing and executing improvement plans.

V. Resource and Capacity Management
- Coordinate human resources and workload planning for the service team.
- Allocate personnel and operational resources effectively based on service demand.
- Monitor team utilization, service capacity, and staffing requirements.
- Optimize service scheduling, task distribution, and workflows.
- Establish a long-term forecasting and capacity management system for service resources.

VI. Customer Support and Service Experience
- Oversee customer support and the resolution of service-related issues.
- Coordinate the handling of major customer complaints and complex service challenges.
- Implement processes for collecting customer feedback and driving service improvements.
- Continuously enhance customer service standards and the overall service experience.
- Improve customer satisfaction, retention rates, and service recognition.

VII. Operational Cost and Budget Management
- Develop annual budgets and cost plans for service operations.
- Monitor personnel costs, outsourcing expenses, and general operational expenditures.
- Analyze service cost structures and resource utilization efficiency.
- Identify opportunities for cost optimization and drive improvement initiatives.
- Balance service quality, operational efficiency, and cost control.

VIII. Cross-functional Coordination and Systems Management
- Coordinate across customer service, technical support, product, and business operations teams.
- Promote the unified adoption of service management systems and ticketing platforms.
- Establish standards for service data, operational reporting, and information management.
- Resolve issues related to cross-departmental service delivery and resource coordination.
- Ensure that service operations remain aligned with the company’s overall business objectives.

IX. Team Leadership and Organizational Development
- Lead the service operations team and relevant departmental managers.
- Build a talent pipeline and develop management personnel within service operations.
- Define team goals, performance standards, and professional development plans.
- Cultivate talent in the areas of service quality, operational management, and customer support.
- Foster a service-oriented culture that is efficient, professional, and customer-focused.

Education
- Bachelor’s degree or higher in Business Administration, Operations Management, Service Management, Information Technology, or a related field.
- An MBA, EMBA, or a Master’s degree in a management-related discipline is preferred. - Certifications such as ITIL, PMP, or Lean Six Sigma are preferred.

- 20+ years of experience in service management, service operations, customer service, or enterprise operations management.
- 15+ years of experience in service operations or managing large-scale service teams.
- Experience in multi-departmental service delivery and service quality management.
- Proficient in SLA management, service performance evaluation, and operational process optimization.

jobs.title: Head of Product
jobs.description:
About Charitable Impact

Charitable Impact started as a bold idea and evolved quickly into an unwavering belief: everyone should have access to resources that help them build the brighter future they imagine. We provide a donor-centric giving platform, supported by a donor advised fund, that helps people amplify their generosity to create the change they want to see in the world. We simplify the giving process, allowing donors to manage all of their giving from one place, access timely tax receipts, and donate in a variety of ways including cash, publicly traded stocks, company shares, and many other options. Anyone can use it to find and give to their favourite charities from one place, give with friends and others, and get support with making their biggest impact possible. So far, Canadians across the country have donated more than $1.6 billion through our platform. 

We take care of each other

Our team members enjoy competitive salaries, purposeful perks, and a culture that gives back and has fun doing it. We're proud to have been named one of Canada’s Most Admired™ Corporate Cultures of 2024 and winner of the Gamechanger: Company Culture Award at BC Tech's 2026 Technology Impact Awards. We support each other, learn from one another, and grow together. We're on an adventure to make giving an intentional and meaningful part of daily life. So, come and join us, and let's build a brighter future together.

What you’ll do

The Head of Product is a high-impact leadership role with broad influence across Charitable Impact. Leading both Product Management and UX, and reporting to the VP, Experience & Growth, this role sits at the intersection of product vision, organizational priorities, and execution. Working closely with our founder, who plays a central role in shaping product direction, the Head of Product is responsible for understanding that vision deeply, translating it into clear priorities, and creating the conditions for teams to carry it forward with focus and coherence.

A major part of the role is orchestration across our seven product streams. The Head of Product maintains a clear view of how the different parts of the product fit together: where work intersects, where dependencies exist, where sequencing matters, and where trade-offs need to be made. You help ensure individual streams do not operate as isolated bodies of work, but contribute to a connected product direction and a consistent experience for our users.

The role is accountable for the effectiveness and output of both Product Management and UX teams. You'll maintain a clear and ongoing view of product health, using data, experimentation, and performance measures to understand what's working, where the product is underperforming, and where teams should focus next.

You'll work closely with Engineering, Marketing, Donor Engagement & Experience, Business Development, Data, and the broader Leadership team to connect product decisions with the needs and priorities of the organization. This is a role for an experienced product practitioner who is also willing to deeply learn the context of our product: what makes it unique, the charity context in which it exists, its history, strengths, constraints, dependencies, and opportunities - and use that understanding to guide teams as Charitable Impact continues to evolve and mature its product practice.

We're a hybrid office and this role requires PCT availability and in-office attendance once per quarter in our Vancouver office. This role will lead distributed teams across Canada and India and will require time-zone flexibility (early morning/evenings PCT).

Your responsibilities

Product Strategy & Portfolio Leadership

Work closely with our founder to translate product vision and strategic direction into clear priorities, roadmaps, and executable plans.
Maintain a coherent portfolio view across all seven product streams, including sequencing, dependencies, trade-offs, and performance measurement. 
Lead quarterly product planning and help translate company priorities into clear product and experience OKRs.
Ensure related work across streams is coordinated rather than developed in isolation.
Represent Product and UX in leadership forums and company-wide planning.

Product + UX Leadership

Lead Product Management and User Experience as an integrated product-development function.
Inspire and mentor the team, creating a collaborative and inclusive culture.
Develop a culture of creativity, innovation, and continuous improvement within the team.
Lead by example, demonstrating a relentless commitment to excellence.
Develop annual and quarterly departmental plans and objectives.
Cultivate a strong sense of ownership and accountability within the team, empowering team members to take initiative and drive projects forward.
Foster strong cross-functional partnerships with other teams and stakeholders to align departmental efforts with company goals and objectives.
Continue to support our environment of care and compassion for one-another, and nurture our culture that values considerate and empathetic collaboration.

Product Performance, Data & Experimentation

Establish a clear framework for product performance, including activation, adoption, engagement, retention, conversion, and feature usage.
Ensure major product initiatives have clear success measures and appropriate instrumentation before release.
Build stronger connections between product strategy, behavioural data, UX research, and user insight.
Establish a regular cadence for reviewing product performance and identifying where iteration is needed.
Build A/B testing and controlled experimentation into product development where appropriate.
Help teams translate assumptions into testable hypotheses, measurable outcomes, and evidence-based decisions.
Partner with Engineering and Data to improve the quality, accessibility, and reliability of product analytics.

Capacity, Velocity & Product Development Effectiveness

Partner with Engineering leadership to calibrate realistic delivery expectations based on capacity, complexity and dependencies. 
Improve the flow of work from strategy and discovery through UX, technical planning, implementation, measurement, and iteration.
Use delivery and capacity data to improve quarterly planning, forecasting, and sequencing.
Improve velocity without reducing performance to simplistic activity metrics or story points.

Cross-Functional Execution

Establish strong Product, UX, and Engineering partnerships across the product streams.
Work closely with Engineering on feasibility, architecture, sequencing, and technical dependencies.
Connect product work with Marketing, Donor Engagement & Experience, Operations, Data, and other business teams where needed.
Provide senior support on difficult scope, prioritization, dependency, and product trade-offs.

What success looks like

Product strategy is translated into a coherent portfolio of work across the seven streams.
Leadership and the broader organization have clear visibility into what we are building and how it is performing.
PM and UX function as a unified unit with greater effective capacity.
Major product investments are instrumented, measured, and evaluated after release.
A/B testing and experimentation are used rigorously where they can improve decisions.
Product data routinely influences prioritization and iteration.

What we're looking for

10+ years of progressive product leadership experience, including managing and developing high-performing Product and UX teams.
Experience leading combined Product + UX/Product Design teams and coaching senior leaders. 
Strong understanding of UX, product design, prototyping, usability testing, and experience quality.
Proven experience translating high-level or founder-led strategy into coordinated product portfolios, roadmaps, and priorities.
Experience managing multiple product areas, streams, or squads.
Deep experience with product analytics
Strong experience with A/B testing and experimentation, including hypothesis development, instrumentation, success criteria, and interpretation.
Experience using product data to drive prioritization, iteration, and investment decisions.
Experience with complex SaaS products involving data, APIs, permissions, multiple user types, and cross-platform functionality.
Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to make complex product and technical work clear to both technical and non-technical audiences.
A confident, steady leadership style that creates clarity.
Strong AI literacy and a practical understanding of how emerging tools can improve product development, UX, analytics, and team productivity.

Bonus points

Fintech, payments, charitable giving, or regulated environments experience.
Marketplace, platform, or B2B/B2C hybrid experience.
API and data-platform experience.
Product-led growth experience.

Compensation

The expected starting salary range for this role is $195,000 - $215,000/year
.

Total rewards

Extended health care benefits.
Vision, dental, paramedical, and life insurance.
Annual health spending account.
To spend on what's important to you.
Professional development.
We believe in supporting our team members in achieving their professional goals.
RRSP matching.
To encourage you to save for your future.
Monthly donation & volunteer matching.
To encourage you to give. 
Rest and relaxation.
Minimum three weeks paid annual vacation and unlimited sick days.
Flexibility.
Flexible work schedules and remote work options.

Our people make us great

We love working with creative and open-minded people who bring imagination and courage to work, who treat others with respect and kindness, and who act on their generosity each day. We're committed to building an equitable, inclusive, and collaborative workplace that welcomes and encourages members of traditionally underrepresented groups to join our team. About Us

The Alberta Public Service works to build a stronger province for current and future generations. We make a difference in the lives of Albertans through rewarding career opportunities.

The Ministry of Jobs, Economy, Trade and Immigration leads the efforts to grow Alberta's economy by delivering strategic programs and services to support Alberta's entrepreneurs and job creators, attract investment, expand and diversify trade, and ensure Alberta has an innovative and competitive business environment.

For further information, visit the ministry website at https://www.alberta.ca/jobs-economy-trade-and-immigration

Role

Reporting to the Assistant Deputy Minister (ADM), the Executive Director (ED), Employer and Program Services is accountable for delivering workforce programs, building relationships with partners to help them build capacity to fill in-demand jobs, develop and retain workers, facilitate investment in skills training, prepare their workforces for the future, and find solutions to labour market issues, including workforce adjustment and resiliency.

The Executive Director is accountable to work with other provincial and federal governments to coordinate labour market programming, including delivery and implementation of Canada-Alberta Labour Market Transfer Agreements, including managing the performance measurement framework, on behalf of five ministries across the Government of Alberta. The Executive Director also leads labour supports in government-wide investment attraction efforts and oversees an Operational Excellence unit to lead client-experience improvement projects in the department.

The Executive Director is responsible for identifying and meeting client needs including workers, employers, industry, employee organizations, and third-party service providers that deliver training and employment programs and services. This includes gathering and using labour market intelligence, informing strategic workforce direction across government, and influencing industry action.

Taking broad systems thinking and problem-solving approaches, the Executive Director enables critical improvements of and informs program design in an effort to support labour market development and effective resource use considering future implications to Alberta's workforce needs. The Executive Director provides leadership and direction to a team of about 60 professional and program staff, inclusive of relevant budget accountability and actively contributes as a member of the Division leadership team.

You have demonstrated experience in strategic and systems thinking, creative problem solving and experience leading strategic initiatives to produce positive change. A Bachelor’s degree is required and academic training at a Master’s Level is advantageous.

Position: Executive Director
Employment Type: Part-Time (20 hours/week), Independent Contractor
Compensation: Commensurate with experience and qualifications
Reports To: Board of Directors
Location: Work from Home

Must be available to travel to meetings across the counties we serve. Preference to individuals living in one of the regions we serve or within 50 km of any of the regions we serve (eg. Oxford, London, Middlesex, Huron-Perth, Grey-Bruce). 

Must be eligible to work in Canada, and hold a class G drivers licence. 
The successful candidate will be asked to complete an OPP record check, including a vulnerable sector screening. 

Deadline to Apply: 

Applications will be reviewed and assessed on an ongoing basis until the position has been filled. 
Please submit a cover letter and resume to: info@facilefutures.ca and include the Subjectline “Application to Facile Executive Director Position” 

About Facile Futures

At Facile Futures, we believe everyone deserves to live a meaningful, connected, and self-directed life. As a family-founded and family-led organization, we recognize individuals and families as experts in their own lives, with unique strengths, experiences, and aspirations.
Through relationships, collaboration, and person-directed approaches, we work alongside people and families to navigate challenges, strengthen connections, and create opportunities for belonging, inclusion, and possibility. Our work is grounded in dignity, self-determination, equity, and the belief that stronger communities are built when people are heard, valued, and empowered.

The Opportunity

This is an exciting time for Facile! After three years of growth and expansion, we’re looking for the right leader to take our organization forward. Facile Futures is seeking a compassionate, collaborative, and values-driven Executive Director to lead organizational operations while working alongside individuals and families. With a 15 year history of walking alongside people with a disability and their families, we are a trusted source for planning and facilitation. Families depend on us for creative solutions, innovation leadership and strategic advocacy. Balancing nonprofit administration with relationship-based family support, the Executive Director will collaborate with the Board, staff, families, and community partners to strengthen sustainability, advance inclusion, and create meaningful opportunities for growth and connection.

What's in it for You?

Flexible, self-directed schedule and work-from-home arrangement
Purposeful work supporting family-led, community-driven initiatives
Continuous learning and paid professional development opportunities
A creative, welcoming culture committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion

Key Responsibilities

Person-Directed and Family-Focused Leadership
Build trusting, respectful relationships with individuals and families, honouring their unique experiences, choices, and aspirations
Lead and mentor a team of facilitators supporting person-directed planning, self-determination, and supported decision-making
Create opportunities for families to connect, share experiences, and strengthen supportive networks
Ensure people with a disability and their families have a meaningful influence on organizational priorities, programs, and decisions
Respond to emerging needs with empathy, creativity, and collaborative problem-solving
Strengthen connections to community resources and services without imposing predetermined definitions of success

Organizational Leadership and Operations
Lead day-to-day operations, ensuring effective administration, organizational accountability, and alignment with Facile Futures' mission
Collaborate with the Board to implement strategic priorities, establish measurable goals, and identify opportunities for innovation and growth
Develop and maintain organizational policies, procedures, systems, and records
Oversee budgets, expenditures, financial reporting, and coordination with accounting supports
Ensure compliance with applicable legal, regulatory, funding, and reporting requirements
Supervise and support team members and volunteers, fostering a culture of trust, inclusion, accountability, and continuous learning
Manage organizational priorities and resources effectively within a part-time leadership structure

Community Partnerships and Advocacy
Develop relationships with community organizations, service providers, school boards, funders, and Ministry stakeholders
Represent Facile Futures in community networks, partnerships, and collaborative initiatives
Support families in navigating systems and accessing opportunities aligned with their goals
Advocate for inclusive, equitable, and person-directed approaches that reflect the voices and priorities of people with disabilities and their families
Identify opportunities to strengthen community capacity, accessibility, and meaningful participation

Fund Development and Sustainability
Collaborate with the Board to strengthen financial sustainability through funding, partnerships, and entrepreneurial opportunities
Develop grant applications, funding proposals, and fundraising initiatives
Cultivate relationships with funders, donors, and community supporters
Explore diversified revenue opportunities that support Facile Futures' independence and unencumbered service status
Communicate organizational impact through meaningful outcomes and stories that respect individual dignity, privacy, and consent

Board Relations and Governance
Maintain a transparent, collaborative, and accountable relationship with the Board of Directors
Provide timely operational updates, financial information, and strategic recommendations
Support Board meetings, annual reporting, recruitment, and governance activities
Respect the distinction between governance and operational leadership while encouraging shared learning and thoughtful decision-making

Who We're Looking For

We recognize that effective leadership develops through diverse professional, personal, and community experiences. Candidates may bring backgrounds in nonprofit leadership, entrepreneurship, disability advocacy, family support, community development, or related fields.

Values and Leadership Approach
Strong commitment to person-directed, co-creative, and family-led practices, equity, inclusion, and self-determination
Ability to listen deeply, build authentic relationships, and respect the expertise of individuals and families
Compassionate, collaborative, and ethical leadership grounded in trust, transparency, and accountability
Creativity, adaptability, initiative, and an entrepreneurial approach to problem-solving and organizational growth

Experience and Skills
Experience in nonprofit management, entrepreneurship, community programming, family support, advocacy, or a related field
Strong administrative, financial management, organizational, and communication skills
Experience collaborating with families, community partners, and diverse stakeholders
Demonstrated ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and lead within a part-time role
Experience in strategic planning, project management, fundraising and grant writing is essential. Candidates must demonstrate proficiency in written and spoken English. Language proficiency may be assessed as part of the recruitment process.
Knowledge of disability services and systems (e.g., DSO, ODSP), person-directed planning, and community inclusion is an asset
Experience working with a volunteer Board of Directors is an asset

We value lived experience. People with disabilities, family members, caregivers, and others with relevant lived experience are encouraged to apply. Formal education may be an asset, but we welcome candidates whose skills, knowledge, and leadership abilities have developed through diverse pathways.

Working Arrangements and Compensation

This is a part-time, independent contractor position (20 hours per week) offering flexible scheduling and a work-from-home arrangement. The role combines organizational administration, strategic leadership, and meaningful engagement with individuals, families, and community partners.
Compensation will reflect the successful candidate's experience, qualifications, and agreed-upon responsibilities.

jobs.title: Director of AI Applications Development
jobs.description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients. 

 At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute. 

 To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com 

 What you'll be doing 

 As part of CIBC’s technology team, you’ll lead our AI Applications Development function and guide a high-performing team of AI engineers, developers, and quality assurance specialists who build and support enterprise-grade AI solutions. As Director, you’ll provide technical and people leadership to drive the design, development, deployment, and ongoing evolution of advanced AI applications across the bank. You’ll work closely with technology and business partners to shape solution architecture, define integration requirements, and deliver solutions that align to strategic priorities and enterprise standards. You’ll help ensure our AI-driven applications are secure, scalable, reliable, and well monitored, with a strong focus on cloud-native delivery, observability, and compliance. You’ll also foster a culture of innovation, collaboration, continuous improvement, and strong documentation practices while supporting your leaders and teams in delivering high-quality solutions that enhance the client experience.

 At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. Details on your work arrangement (proportion of on-site and remote work) will be discussed at the time of your interview. 

 How you'll succeed  
 People leadership - Lead and develop a team of leaders, AI engineers, developers, and quality assurance specialists by setting clear direction, providing meaningful coaching, and creating opportunities for growth. Build an inclusive, high-performing environment where team members are supported, accountable, and connected to CIBC’s priorities.
 Strategic partnership - Build trusted relationships with technology and business partners, vendors, and senior stakeholders to understand business needs, translate them into practical AI solutions, and influence decisions through clear, business-focused communication.
 Technical leadership - Guide architecture and engineering decisions for enterprise AI applications, with a focus on security, scalability, performance, and reliability. Support the development and deployment of modern AI solutions using tools and technologies such as Python, FastAPI, JavaScript frameworks, Azure AI services, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), large language models (LLMs), and agentic AI frameworks.
 Quality and platform excellence - Champion strong engineering practices across cloud infrastructure, continuous integration and continuous delivery, observability, documentation, and test automation to help ensure solutions are resilient, maintainable, and ready for enterprise scale.
 Delivery leadership - Work with internal partners to prioritize, plan, and deliver initiatives on agreed timelines and budgets. Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, encourage reuse across teams, and help shape a shared AI strategy that scales across the enterprise.

 Who you are  
 You are a hands-on builder first. You have recently designed, built, and shipped production AI applications yourself, and you still enjoy writing code, reviewing pull requests, and solving production issues alongside the team.
 You bring strong technical depth. You have hands-on experience with Python, FastAPI, JavaScript (Vue.js or React.js), SQL, Redis, and Azure Cloud services, including Azure OpenAI / AI Foundry and API Management. You are comfortable with CI/CD tools such as GitHub Actions and QA automation frameworks such as Playwright, Cypress, or Selenium.
 You know modern AI engineering. You have built solutions using large language models (LLMs), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), prompt and context engineering, tool calling, and agentic frameworks such as LangGraph, LangChain, LangSmith, or equivalent. It’s an asset if you have experience with Databricks, LLM evaluation, and observability for AI agents in production (e.g., Splunk, OpenTelemetry).
 You build for the enterprise. You design for security, scalability, reliability, and compliance, and you understand what it takes to run AI safely in a regulated environment.
 You are ready to grow as a people leader. You mentor engineers, set technical direction, and raise the engineering bar. You are excited to grow into leading a team of engineers and QA specialists as the function scales.
 Your influence makes a difference. You build trusted relationships with business and technology partners, translate business needs into practical AI solutions, and explain complex ideas clearly to non-technical audiences.
 You're digitally savvy. You are curious, adapt quickly to new tools and trends, and take ownership of outcomes in a fast-moving space.
 You live your values. You bring high standards, genuine care to your relationships, and want to grow with an employer that shares your values and brings out your best.

 What CIBC Offers 

 At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.
 We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.

 Our spaces and technological toolkit will make it simple to bring together great minds to create innovative solutions that make a difference for our clients.

 We cultivate a culture where you can express your ambition through initiatives like Purpose Day; a paid day off dedicated for you to use to invest in your growth and development.

 *Subject to plan and program terms and conditions

 What you need to know 
 CIBC is committed to creating an inclusive environment where all team members and clients feel like they belong. We seek applicants with a wide range of abilities and we provide an accessible candidate experience. If you need accommodation, please contact Mailbox.careers-carrieres@cibc.com 

 CIBC is committed to clarity in our hiring process. All roles posted are opportunities we’re actively recruiting for, unless stated otherwise.

 You need to be legally eligible to work at the location(s) specified above and, where applicable, must have a valid work or study permit.

 We may ask you to complete an attribute-based assessment and other skills test (such as simulation, coding, French proficiency). 

 We use artificial intelligence tools during the recruitment process. Our goal for the application process is to get to know more about you, all that you have to offer, and give you the opportunity to learn more about us.

Regular
