jobs.title: VP Finance
jobs.description:
SIRIUS INSTRUMENTATION AND CONTROLS INC.

THE ORGANIZATION

Sirius designs and manufactures chemical injection systems and instrumentation packages for upstream and midstream oil and gas operators. Their equipment runs in some of the harshest production environments in the world - Western Canada, the Permian, and increasingly the Middle East, Africa and Latin America - where precision matters and downtime costs money. Their technologies help eliminate greenhouse gas emissions, improve injection accuracy, and reduce manpower and chemical costs - two of their customers’ largest expenses. The portfolio includes solar-powered and AC chemical injection systems, environmentally friendly tank systems, and advanced automation technologies.

Founded in April 2003 in Alberta, Canada, Sirius is headquartered in Edmonton with U.S. operations in Midland, Texas (operating as Sirius Controls Inc.) since 2017. Sirius is a registered corporation with APEGA (Association of Professional Engineers) and was awarded the 2018 “Clean Technology Innovation” Award by CETAC-West. Since December 2024, Sirius has been backed by a private equity sponsor and is executing a multi-year growth plan that targets a doubling of revenue across both countries, while adding key international markets.

Sirius’s Core Values define their culture, drive their work, and guide their commitment to excellence. They are the operating standard for every member of the team - and the Vice President, Finance is expected to model and reinforce them.

Core Values:

Continuous Innovation
: Innovation begins with listening to understand and transforms curiosity into impactful solutions. It is a continuous improvement loop that channels learning back into our products, processes, and people.
Integrity:
We do what we say we will do. We take responsibility for our actions and own our commitments to become trusted advisors that clients rely on.
Collaboration:
We achieve excellence by working together with trust, humility, open communication, and a shared purpose. Collaboration means ownership across every step of the process.

For more information on Sirius Instrumentation & Controls, please visit their website at: https://www.siriuscontrols.com/.

THE OPPORTUNITY

The Vice President, Finance (“VP Finance”) is a senior finance leader accountable for the integrity, accuracy, and effectiveness of accounting, reporting, and financial operations across both Sirius entities: Sirius Instrumentation and Controls Inc. (Canadian parent) and Sirius Controls Inc. (U.S. subsidiary). The VP Finance also partners closely with leaders across the Company to strengthen effectiveness and optimize performance.

Reporting directly to the Chief Financial Officer (“CFO”), the VP Finance serves as the CFO’s deputy and designated backup, ensuring continuity across board, sponsor, lender, banking, insurance, and audit relationships, and acting on the CFO’s behalf as delegated or required.

The VP Finance retains direct ownership of the accounting function while progressively delegating close and transactional execution to the Assistant Controller as that role continues to develop. The scope will expand across financial planning and analysis, treasury, tax compliance coordination, and strategic finance, including key initiatives such as ERP implementation.

RESPONSIBILITIES

In support of the organization's strategic objectives, the successful candidate will be accountable for the following key responsibilities:

Financial Reporting and Technical Accounting

Accountable for the consolidated month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close across both entities, including intercompany eliminations and FX translation (IAS 21); ensure timely, accurate consolidated reporting under IFRS.
Accountable for all IFRS technical positions including but not limited to - IFRS 15 revenue recognition, IAS 2 standard costing and WIP valuation, IFRS 16 leases, IAS 12 deferred tax, and IFRS 3 acquisition accounting carry-forward; prepare technical memos and defend positions to auditors.
Responsible for the primary external audit relationship - planning, PBC management, technical defense, and year-end coordination.
Ensure compliance with tax, regulatory, and Board of Directors-specific reporting requirements.

Internal Controls, Risk, and Governance

Responsible for the internal control environment across all transactional cycles (revenue/receivables, purchases/payables, payroll, inventory, fixed assets, treasury, close and reporting); and progress the framework toward SOX-lite (COSO 2013).
Establish and maintain accounting policies, procedures, and controls documentation.
Partner with the CFO on risk management and audit committee reporting.

Accounting Operations and Delegation

Accountable for the accuracy and completeness of accounts receivable, accounts payable, payroll, inventory, and treasury activities across both entities.
Progressively transition close execution, transactional review and AR/AP Admins to the Assistant Controller against a defined development plan, retaining review authority and overall accountability for the function.
Supervise tax compliance - GST/HST, U.S. state sales and use tax, and cross-border requirements-coordinating with external advisors on transfer pricing, withholding, and treaty application.
Collaborating with sales department, legal counsel and clients to ensure timely and optimal Master Services Agreements.

Financial Planning and Analysis; Board and Sponsor Reporting

Responsible for the completion of the board reporting packages: monthly flash, quarterly board pack, sponsor reporting, and covenant compliance certificates.
Build and lead the FP&A capability - annual budget, rolling 12-month forecast (quarterly), budget-versus-actual and variance analysis, and KPI reporting - to support decision-making.
Assume Budget Master role while partnering with the CFO to deliver the annual budget.
Provide insight on financial performance, margins, working capital, and risk areas as a Partner to the executive team.

Treasury and Cash Management

Responsible for working capital management, and CAD/USD exposure monitoring.
Manage day-to-day banking relationships, credit facility reporting, and intercompany funding, escalating covenant and liquidity matters to the CFO.

Systems and Process Improvement

Lead the finance workstreams of the ERP implementation - requirements, chart of accounts design, data migration, UAT, cutover, and post-go-live stabilization - through the transition from QuickBooks.
Collaborate with supporting the Plant Controller and Senior Vice President Operations, operationalize standard costing in the make-to-order manufacturing environment, including BOM accuracy, overhead absorption, and variance analysis.
Drive process automation and continuous improvement of the close, reporting cadence, and documentation base to support margin improvement.

Leadership and Team Development

Manage, mentor, and scale the accounting team; foster a culture of accountability, process improvement, and cross-functional collaboration.
Develop the Assistant Controller on a defined succession track toward financial controller-level ownership of the close; establish SOPs, training milestones, and cross-training pairs.
Build a documented and defensible finance function.

Strategic Partnership and CFO Redundancy

Act as the CFO’s deputy: represent Finance with the board, sponsor, lenders, and auditors as delegated, and assume the CFO’s operating responsibilities in the CFO’s absence.
Support M&A activity - diligence, integration, and acquisition accounting - including vendor due diligence and quality of earnings readiness.
Support international expansion structuring (Middle East and beyond) with external advisors as it progresses.
Collaborate with the sales, operations, and engineering teams, to be a Business Partner supporting financial decision making, cost savings initiatives, and strategic decision making

MEASURES OF SUCCESS

Audit-Ready Financial Reporting:
Consolidated IFRS reporting is delivered accurately and on schedule, with a clean external audit and no material adjustments or control deficiencies.
Scalable, Audit-Ready Finance Function:
Strong controls, clear documentation, and a successfully implemented ERP that position the business well.
Seamless CFO Continuity and Team Succession:
The VP Finance is trusted by the Board, sponsor, lenders, and auditors as the CFO’s deputy, while the Assistant Controller progresses to independent ownership of the close.

THE INDIVIDUAL

Given the pivotal role this individual will be expected to play in achieving the strategic objectives of the company and in supporting the success of the organization, it is essential that the successful candidate possess the following education, experience, competencies and attributes:

Education

A university degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, or a related field is required; an MBA is considered an asset.
Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation in good standing is required.
Strong working knowledge of IFRS is required, including the application of complex technical accounting standards.
Knowledge of U.S. GAAP or cross-border reporting experience would be considered an asset.
Commitment to ongoing professional development, particularly in IFRS, tax, and financial systems.

Experience

Must-have:

A minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in accounting and finance, including senior leadership responsibility for the accounting and reporting function.
Demonstrated expertise in IFRS, including consolidated reporting across multiple entities, intercompany eliminations, foreign currency translation, and preparation of technical accounting positions.
Proven experience leading the external audit relationship and delivering clean, timely audits.
Track record of building and strengthening internal controls, accounting policies, and finance processes.
Experience preparing Board, lender, or investor reporting, including budgeting, forecasting, and variance analysis.
Demonstrated success leading, mentoring, and developing accounting teams, including succession planning and delegation.

Nice-to-have:

Manufacturing experience is strongly preferred, ideally within a make-to-order or engineered products environment, with a solid understanding of standard costing, inventory valuation, and overhead absorption.

En joignant le Groupe Adag, vous intégrerez une équipe dynamique et ambitieuse qui vous permettra d'apprendre, de vous développer et de progresser professionnellement
. Notre organisation est en pleine croissance et transforme son industrie tout en misant sur une culture de collaboration et de plaisir au travail. Si vous êtes reconnu(e) pour votre sens de l'organisation, votre rigueur et votre capacité à mobiliser les gens, nous aimerions vous rencontrer !

Rôle, responsabilités et objectifs

Développer, maintenir et être responsable du modèle financier de projet répondant aux exigences des prêteurs, ainsi que coordonner son audit indépendant.
Diriger l'exécution des financements par dette et par capitaux propres, incluant la préparation du mémorandum d'information, la gestion de la salle de données (data room), les vérifications diligentes des prêteurs et la négociation des feuilles de modalités (term sheets).
Collaborer avec les conseillers juridiques, l'ingénieur indépendant, les agences de notation et les preneurs fermes jusqu'à la clôture financière des projets.
Évaluer la bancabilité des baux de locataires, des ententes d'approvisionnement énergétique et des contrats de construction, et intégrer les résultats aux négociations commerciales.
Après la clôture du financement, gérer les décaissements de construction, le suivi des coûts à terminer (cost-to-complete), le respect des clauses financières (covenants) et les obligations de reporting auprès des prêteurs.

Recruter, encadrer et développer une équipe spécialisée en financement de projets.

Expert(e) en modélisation financière, capable de présenter et de défendre un modèle financier devant des prêteurs et des agences de notation.

Présence obligatoire au bureau trois (3) jours par semaine
.

.

répond à la demande croissante pour les centres de données et les infrastructures critiques, stimulée par l'essor du télétravail, des services infonuagiques et de l'intelligence artificielle. jobs.title: Vice President, Supply Chain and Inventory Management
jobs.description:
Vice President, Supply Chain & Inventory Management

About Delta Group

Delta Group is a Western Canadian wholesale distribution and solutions platform serving waterworks and water infrastructure, agricultural irrigation, pumps and motors, water treatment, wastewater and related markets. Delta combines multi-branch wholesale distribution with specialist technical solutions, engineered systems, projects and service. Through acquisitions and organic growth, the group has an opportunity to integrate supply-chain practices while maintaining the market knowledge and relationships of its operating businesses.

Position mandate

Lead Delta’s end-to-end group supply-chain strategy, with executive accountability for procurement, inventory investment and quality, demand planning, vendor economics, replenishment and network efficiency. Build one disciplined operating framework across multiple companies and branches without impairing customer service or project execution. This is an operational change-leadership position, not simply a senior purchasing appointment. This role can be based in Calgary or Chilliwack, BC.

Group supply-chain strategy and governance

Design and implement group-wide policies for inventory, purchasing, approvals, stock allocation and supplier engagement.
Clarify central versus local authority, escalation rules, exception management and performance accountability.
Partner closely with General Managers, Finance, sales and operations; lead monthly supply-chain performance reviews.
Integrate acquired businesses and branch practices into a scalable operating model.

Inventory investment, productivity and controls

Own group inventory productivity, target-setting and action plans by branch, segment, category and SKU.
Drive reduction of excess, obsolete, slow-moving and duplicate inventory through transfers, vendor returns, disposition and prevention.
Set service-sensitive reorder points, safety stocks, inventory classifications and replenishment policies.
Establish consistent cycle counts, inventory accuracy and inventory ownership controls; coordinate valuation and reserves with Finance.
Protect strategic, seasonal and critical long-lead stock while improving inventory turns and cash generation.

Procurement and supplier management

Coordinate category strategy, purchasing scale, approval limits and controls for committed purchases.
Negotiate supplier terms, pricing, rebates, freight, returns, vendor-managed/consignment arrangements and service commitments.
Implement supplier scorecards and contingency planning for critical products and manufacturers.
Improve purchase-order visibility, interbranch-first decisions and special-order controls; prevent unsupported speculative buys.
Maintain the relationships needed to protect exclusive lines and the commercial advantage of Delta’s technical product portfolios.

Demand planning and major projects

Create rolling forecasting processes using sales patterns, seasonality, known projects and credible customer commitments.
Differentiate recurring wholesale replenishment from project-specific purchasing for pivots, pipe, pumps and engineered packages.
Coordinate purchasing with project managers, installation schedules, deposits and supplier lead times.
Manage cancellations, unallocated project material, foreign-exchange and supply risks through clear ownership and exit plans.

Warehousing, distribution and logistics

Evaluate branch stocking, regional hubs, stock transfers, warehousing productivity and freight economics.
Standardize receiving, storage, picking, shipping and transfers where it creates measurable value.
Build evidence-based business cases for any warehouse consolidation, logistics outsourcing or network redesign.

Systems, master data and analytics

Serve as executive business owner for supply-chain processes.
Establish item-master governance: duplicates, naming, UOMs, vendor references, product attributes, inactive SKUs and status.
Build reliable dashboards for aging, turns, fill rate, demand accuracy, outstanding POs, project stock and supplier performance.
Drive practical system-based replenishment and useful automation rather than spreadsheets without accountability.

Working capital and financial accountability

Develop annual and rolling plans for inventory cash release, purchasing efficiencies and inventory-related operating costs.
Coordinate with VP Finance on cash forecasting, open commitments, vendor terms and independently verified savings.
Evaluate investments against inventory carrying cost, service levels, gross margin, liquidity and project risks.
Report monthly to the CEO with financial outcomes, constraints and corrective actions.

People leadership and transformation

Assess and develop existing branch purchasing, inventory and supply-chain employees; recommend an appropriate group structure.
Hire, coach and hold accountable functional leaders and analysts as approved.
Work constructively with GMs while challenging unsupported inventory and purchasing decisions.
Lead branch-level adoption through training, site visits, clear metrics and consistent follow-through.

Required experience and qualifications

12–15+ years of relevant progression in supply chain, inventory, procurement or wholesale distribution operations, including at least five in a senior multi-branch leadership role.
Demonstrable responsibility for material inventory investment across multiple branches, with quantified improvements in turns, aged inventory, cash flow and service.
Strong track record in vendor negotiations, category strategy, purchase controls and operational change after acquisitions.
Commercial understanding of distribution gross margin, inventory carrying cost, cash conversion, stockouts and service economics.
Hands-on experience implementing effective ERP-based replenishment and master-data management.
Ability to lead effectively through influence and formal authority in decentralized technical distribution businesses.
Relevant degree or equivalent operating experience; SCMP, CSCP or CPIM an asset; regular Western Canadian travel required.

Preferred background

Industrial, waterworks, plumbing, pump and motor, agricultural equipment, irrigation, electrical or HVAC wholesale distribution; acquisition integration; regional distribution network optimization; and balancing project procurement with standard branch replenishment.
Leadership profile
Commercially astute, financially disciplined and decisive; credible at branch and warehouse level; analytically strong, capable of difficult conversations with respected GMs, and equally focused on supplier relationships, customer service and sustainable cash release. Comfortable with ambiguous data but unwilling to accept unsupported conclusions.

Key measures of success

Inventory investment and turns by business, branch and category, adjusted for commercial conditions and service needs.
Aged, obsolete and duplicate stock reduction; inventory accuracy and shrinkage.
Working-capital release and annualized procurement/freight/rebate savings validated by Finance.
Customer fill rates, on-time delivery, backorders and project material availability.
Purchasing compliance, forecasting reliability, supplier performance and inventory transfer effectiveness.
Business Central item-master quality, supply-chain reporting and adoption of replenishment processes.
Strength and accountability of supply-chain leadership and branch operating practices.

First-year priorities

First 30 days: establish validated baselines, purchasing commitment visibility, risk/opportunity ranking and assessment of current team. By 90 days: institute buying authority, interbranch-first controls, aged-inventory program and CEO dashboard. Months 4–6: demonstrate measurable cash release, supplier and forecasting improvements. By 12 months: deliver sustained financial and service outcomes and an approved second-year improvement plan. Specific financial targets will be agreed with the CEO and VP Finance after verifying opening conditions.

Why join Delta

The opportunity is to shape the supply-chain economics of a substantial Western Canadian technical distribution platform, turn scale into meaningful procurement and inventory advantage, and build a disciplined, scalable organization. The role carries senior leadership visibility, operating influence and direct accountability for measurable results.

GreenShield is a proudly Canadian, national non-profit health care and insurance organization, driven by our mission of Better Health for All. As a non-profit social enterprise without shareholders, we reinvest our excess earnings to directly support underserved communities. Through GreenShield Cares, we positively impacted the health and well-being of over one million Canadians between 2020 and 2025. What’s driving us now is the commitment to measurably impact an additional three million Canadians by 2030 – across mental health, essential medicines, and chronic disease management – through scalable initiatives that deliver meaningful change in pursuit of our mission of Better Health for All.

**Job Title**


AVP, Data Governance**Job Description**

**Role Overview**

  

Pacific Life Re is progressing a major business, technology and data transformation across Divisional Business Services. The Divisional Data Team is delivering the governed data foundations, warehouse, data governance \& quality, and reporting capabilities required to support Project Unify, regulatory and management reporting, operational resilience and future analytics including AI enablement.

  

The AVP, Head of Data Governance role provides strategic and delivery leadership for data governance and data quality across Pacific Life Re. The role translates the Data Strategy and Data Governance and Management Programme into practical standards, controls, operating practices and measurable outcomes, ensuring that data is trusted, understood, appropriately controlled and fit for operational, regulatory and strategic use.


Working with and across all business functions, Technology, Risk, Legal, Compliance, Internal Audit and Pacific Life enterprise teams. The role embeds governance into our business\-as\-usual practices and project delivery, considering the wider information management lifecycle, including data management, handling, security, privacy, retention and ensures alignment with enterprise divisions. A central expectation is to communicate progress, risks, dependencies, decisions and business outcomes clearly to executive sponsors, governance forums, delivery teams and data users.

 **This role and is on\-site 4 days per week and work from home 1 day per week in Toronto, ON.**

 **Role Responsibilities**

 *Strategy, framework and accountability*

* Lead the execution of the divisional Data Governance strategy, framework, operating model and roadmap, aligned with the PL Re Data Strategy and relevant enterprise standards.
* Develop and maintain clear decision rights, accountability and escalation routes across Data Owners, Business Data Managers, Data Stewards, Business Process Owners and Technology Owners.
* Chair the Data Governance Forum and ensure that decisions, actions, standards, exceptions and escalations are recorded, communicated and progressed.
* Define and report measures for governance maturity, adoption, control effectiveness and the resolution of material data issues.

 *Programme delivery*

* Support the VP for Data, in delivering the Data Governance and Management Programme, including mobilisation, analysis, target\-state design, investment planning, prioritised remediation and transition into sustainable implementation.
* In collaboration with strategic projects and business workstreams, embed data requirements, definitions, ownership, quality thresholds, lineage, controls, acceptance criteria and governance sign\-off throughout delivery.
* Maintain an integrated delivery view of milestones, dependencies, risks, issues, resources, budgets, benefits and readiness, escalating decisions promptly and constructively.
* Provide executive sponsors and governance bodies with concise, evidence\-based updates on progress, outcomes, residual risks and decisions required.

 *Data Quality*

* Develop and implement the divisional data quality strategy and operating model, covering critical data, quality rules, measures, controls, scorecards, root\-cause analysis and remediation prioritisation.
* Lead the adoption of metadata, business glossary, lineage and data catalogue capabilities, ensuring that priority data assets are discoverable, consistently defined and supported by accountable business roles.
* In collaboration with Business Analysts, Data Engineering, Reporting and Architecture, embed governance by design into data products, semantic models, workspaces and reporting solutions.
* Direct the effective use and integration of strategic governance and data quality technologies, including Collibra and Informatica IDMC, with a focus on control outcomes and business adoption.

 *Risk, lifecycle \& assurance*

* Lead data lifecycle governance, including retention, classification, discoverability, permitted access, defensible disposition and remediation of identified control gaps.
* Act as the senior Data Governance contact for regulatory, audit and risk activity, coordinating evidence, management responses, remediation plans and reporting through the appropriate governance routes.
* In collaboration with Legal, Data Protection, Information Security, Risk and Technology, translate policy and regulatory requirements into proportionate, implementable data controls.
* Monitor material data risks and issues, challenge remediation plans and support accountable business and technology leaders in reaching documented decisions on residual risk. Working closely with legal and risk functions.

 *People, engagement and capability*

* Build and lead a high\-performing Data Governance team, setting clear objectives, developing capability, delegating effectively and creating succession depth.
* Develop and maintain an engagement and communication plan that translates governance priorities into clear executive narratives, adoption messages, training and role\-based guidance.
* Establish and support an active stewardship community that shares good practice, resolves cross\-functional issues and embeds governance in day\-to\-day business activity.
* Manage specialist partners and contractors against clear deliverables, quality expectations, knowledge\-transfer requirements and value outcomes.

 **Skills \& Experience**

* Extensive experience in data governance, data management, data quality and data leadership within a complex, regulated organisation.
* Demonstrable success in moving governance from policy and framework design into practical delivery, adoption, and measurable business outcomes.
* Strong programme and change delivery experience, with the ability to coordinate concurrent workstreams, dependencies, risks, resources and budgets.
* Strong knowledge of data ownership and stewardship, metadata, business

About Axya 
 Axya is a technology company modernizing the source-to-pay process for the manufacturing industry. Our SaaS platform streamlines and automates procurement, making it faster, simpler and more cost-effective for companies sourcing custom parts. By digitizing traditionally manual processes, Axya helps manufacturers operate with greater efficiency and competitiveness. Axya recently closed a $17 million CAD Series A funding round, a milestone that fuels our next stage of growth as we expand our team, accelerate product development and bring our platform to more manufacturers. 
 We are proud to cultivate an inclusive and collaborative work environment that supports innovation, growth and professional development. As a member of our team, you will work alongside passionate, forward-thinking professionals and contribute directly to transforming procurement in the manufacturing sector. Role Overview 
 As the Director of Marketing (Growth & Demand) at Axya, you will own and drive our go-to-market engine. 
 You’ll define positioning and messaging, build impactful campaigns, and create compelling marketing 
 collateral that fuels pipeline generation and expansion opportunities. 

 This is a hands-on, individual contributor role with the opportunity to evolve into a managerial position as 
 the marketing function scales and the team grows. If you have a proven background in SaaS marketing, 
 particularly in manufacturing, procurement, or supply chain, and thrive in a fast-paced, high-growth 
 environment, this is your opportunity to make a measurable impact. 

 Key Responsibilities 
 - Build the marketing foundation: Define Axya’s positioning, messaging, and target segments 
 within manufacturing and procurement. 
 - Create impactful collateral: Develop high-quality presentation decks, customer one-pagers, 
 case studies, and other materials that drive pipeline creation and expansion opportunities. 
 - Own demand generation: Lead inbound (content, SEO, paid, social) and outbound (email, 
 LinkedIn, ABM) campaigns, as well as co-marketing and event initiatives. 
 - Develop field marketing: Plan and execute targeted conferences, executive roundtables, and 
 other high-impact experiential events. 
 - Optimize the funnel: Establish and monitor MQL → SAL → SQL definitions, track conversion 
 metrics, and ensure high-quality lead flow to sales. 
 - Collaborate cross-functionally: Partner with Sales and BDR teams to align campaigns, 
 prioritize accounts, and refine messaging based on real-time market feedback. 
 - Leverage tools & data: Manage Axya’s CRM/marketing automation stack (HubSpot preferred), 
 maintain data integrity, and report on campaign performance. 
 - Be both strategic and hands-on: Execute day-to-day tactics while laying the groundwork for 
 scalable growth 

 What We’re Looking For 
 - Proven B2B SaaS marketing experience, ideally within manufacturing, procurement, or supply 
 chain technology. 
 - Demonstrated success in demand generation and pipeline building through inbound and 
 outbound strategies. 
 - Strong communication and storytelling skills: able to craft clear, compelling messaging and 
 visuals. 
 - Product marketing experience creating sales and marketing collateral such as decks, one-pagers, 
 and campaign materials. 
 - Proficiency with CRM and marketing automation platforms (HubSpot preferred) and data-driven 
 decision-making. 
 - Strategic thinker who can execute tactically and thrive in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial 
 environment. 
 - Self-motivated, collaborative, and eager to take ownership of growth initiatives. 

 Why Join Axya 
 🏖  Unlimited vacation policy: because we believe in balance. 
 🏥  Comprehensive health insurance: your well-being matters. 
 🕒  Flexible work schedule: results matter more than hours 
 🏡  100% remote: get the job done wherever you prefer.

jobs.title: Director, Brand Activation
jobs.location: Dallas Infomart Office DAI; Toronto; Denver; Tampa
jobs.description:
Who are we? 
 Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.   

A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future. 

A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work. 

 Job Summary 
 Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company, and the brand has to work as hard as the business does. This role is where brand strategy becomes something people can see: in our channels, at our events, in our product names, on our merchandise, and in the way our agencies and partners bring the brand to life.

 The Director, Brand Activation owns how the Equinix brand is executed and activated across all of Global Marketing. You will be the connective tissue across the whole organization: Web, Social, Paid Media, and Thought Leadership, and equally the demand campaigns, the field and partner programs in every region, and the events where customers meet us in person. Wherever the brand shows up, you set the standards the work is built from and make sure it adds up to one company.

 You will manage our external creative and brand resources as a single portfolio, build and run the AI agents that handle brand intake, review, and operational work, own brand naming and trademark management, run the company store, and lead how the brand shows up at events.
 This is a senior individual contributor role with a wide remit and real authority. It suits someone who has led brand or creative teams and now wants to lead through standards, partners, and influence rather than headcount. You will report to the Sr. Director, Brand, and work daily with peers across the Brand & Digital pillar, Revenue Marketing, Field & Partner Marketing, Global Events, Product Marketing, Communications, and Legal.

 Responsibilities 
 What you will do
 Brand activation across Global Marketing
 Be the single point of accountability for how the Equinix brand shows up across the whole marketing organization, and the person every team goes to when they need the brand to work harder for them
 Translate brand strategy into activation plans that Web, Social, Paid Media, and Thought Leadership can execute, and set the brand standards each of those teams builds from
 Make sure demand and product campaigns carry the brand as well as the offer, partnering with Revenue Marketing and Product Marketing from the brief rather than at the final review
 Bring consistency to field and partner activation in every region, giving regional teams the standards, assets, and judgment they need to adapt the brand locally without fragmenting it
 Lead brand activation at events, including Connect (our global sales kickoff), flagship industry and customer events, and the partner and field events that carry our brand into the market, in partnership with Global Events
 Partner with Communications on brand narrative, including the company’s position on data centers and the communities they operate in
 Do all of this through standards, partnership, and influence. You set how the brand works; the channel, campaign, field, and events teams run their own programs

 Agency and resource management
 Own the brand agency roster, contractor pool, and associated budget as one portfolio: selection, scoping, briefing, performance, and spend
 Direct agency work so that external partners deliver to brand standards and to the priorities of the organization, not team by team or region by region

 AI agents and the brand operating model
 Design, deploy, and manage the AI agents that run the brand’s day to day operations: request intake and triage, brand review and compliance checks, asset and template retrieval, and first drafts of routine creative and copy
 Own the self service operating model that lets teams across Equinix create on brand work through agents and templates rather than routing every request through a central creative team
 Set the guardrails: what agents can approve on their own, what routes to a human, and how brand standards are encoded so the agents enforce them consistently
 Measure and improve the model: request volume, turnaround, review accuracy, and adoption across teams, and retire what is not working
 Partner with Marketing Ops and IT on tooling, data, and governance so brand agents fit the broader Marketing AI stack rather than sitting beside it

 Brand naming and trademark
 Own brand naming for Equinix: product and service names, program and initiative names, and internal naming requests, running a clear process with Product Marketing and Legal
 Manage the trademark portfolio with Legal, including clearance, filings, renewals, and enforcement of brand usage

 Company store and brand merchandise
 Own the Equinix company store end to end: assortment and design, vendor and fulfillment management, quality, and the way merchandise reflects the brand
 Brand governance
 Maintain and evolve brand standards, messaging governance, and the tools and templates that keep the brand consistent at scale
 Be the person people come to when something is off brand, and the person who makes it easy to get it right

 Qualifications 
 What you bring
 10 or more years in brand, creative, or integrated marketing, including several years leading brand execution for a global B2B company. Technology or infrastructure experience is a plus, not a requirement
 A track record of activating a brand across the full marketing mix: owned and paid channels, demand campaigns, field and regional programs, and live events. You have done this with teams that do not report to you
 Hands on experience managing agencies and external creative resources, including scoping, budgets, and holding partners to a standard

jobs.title: Director, Data Science
jobs.description:
Our Purpose 

 Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential. 

 Title and Summary 

Director, Data Science 

Overview

The Security Solutions Data Science team is responsible for delivering Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) models that support Mastercard’s Identity and risk products across the payment networks. These models are designed to be production-ready and to power high-value capabilities that protect digital transactions and enable trusted decisioning at scale.

Beyond model development, the organization is responsible for building scalable, repeatable, and resilient data science capabilities that cover the end-to-end lifecycle of machine learning solutions, from data acquisition and feature engineering through experimentation, validation, deployment, and monitoring. These systems must not only perform effectively in production, but also be built in a way that is industrialized, maintainable, and aligned with broader business and platform needs.

Services within Mastercard is responsible for acquiring, engaging, and retaining customers by managing fraud and risk, enhancing cybersecurity, and improving the digital payments experience. Within this mission, the Identity Data Science portfolio plays a significant role in developing intelligence-driven solutions that improve how risk is understood and managed across the merchant lifecycle.

We are looking for a highly skilled and strategic Director to lead a Data Science team that focuses on solving merchant risk during onboarding and monitoring. This role is critical in driving the research and development of a merchant registry and profiling capability within the Identity Data Science portfolio. This includes setting the strategy for how merchant intelligence is built and scaled, guiding the development of reusable data science assets and profiling frameworks, and ensuring strong execution across product, engineering, and data science partners. You will help shape both the technical direction and operational model needed to turn this capability into a durable and scalable advantage.

Role
Key responsibilities include:
• Define and execute the strategy for solving merchant risk during onboarding and monitoring through the research and development of a merchant registry and profiling capability
• Lead, coach, and develop high-performing teams of Data Scientists, including hiring, mentorship, and performance management
• Build a strong team culture focused on collaboration, accountability, and continuous learning
• Guide the design of scalable machine learning and analytical systems using modern data and cloud platforms such as Databricks and Sparks.
• Establish best practices for problem framing, technique selection, experimentation, and validation across the team
• Ensure teams identify appropriate approaches for business problems and rigorously validate solutions against both technical and business outcomes
• Partner closely with Product, Engineering, and other stakeholders to translate strategic needs into data science roadmaps and deliverables
• Drive Agile delivery practices that support iterative development, measurable outcomes, and continuous improvement
• Promote reusable data assets, standardization, and scalable workflows that strengthen long-term execution
• Communicate strategy, progress, trade-offs, and business value clearly to senior leadership
• Balance long-term vision with near-term delivery to maximize impact and time-to-value

All About You
Essential Skills to be successful:
• Advanced degree (Master’s or PhD preferred) in Data Science, ML, or related field
• Extensive experience leading a Data Science team and drive innovation with inspiration.
• Experienced being a great people leader but able to dig into the work where necessary
• A proven track record of deploying high performance machine learning models at scale in a production environment
• Strong proficiency with Python, SQL, along with experience using scalable Machine Learning and Cloud frameworks
• Strong ability to guide teams in identifying appropriate techniques and validating solutions rigorously
• Critical thinking and a drive to produce high-quality work, ensuring that all solutions meet rigorous standards
• Demonstrated success translating complex business problems into strategic data science initiatives. Ability to lead through ambiguity and change
• Strong understanding of Agile methodologies, with the ability to drive iterative delivery across cross-functional teams
• Excellent stakeholder management, communication to both technical and non-technical audiences, and leadership skills
• Proven ability to build teams, influence roadmaps, and deliver measurable business value in complex environments
• High-energy and self-driven orientation

Nice to Have
• Experience building or scaling shared data science platforms, registries, or enterprise data assets
• Familiarity with merchant risk, fraud, or identity ecosystems
• Experience driving cross-team standardization and reusable capabilities
• Exposure to governance frameworks for model validation and AI systems 

Mastercard is a merit-based, inclusive, equal opportunity employer that considers applicants without regard to gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, disabled or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We hire the most qualified candidate for the role. In the US or Canada, if you require accommodations or assistance to complete the online application process or during the recruitment process, please contact reasonable_accommodation@mastercard.com and identify the type of accommodation or assistance you are requesting. Do not include any medical or health information in this email. The Reasonable Accommodations team will respond to your email promptly. 

 Corporate Security Responsibility 

All activities involving access to Mastercard assets, information, and networks comes with an inherent risk to the organization and, therefore, it is expected that every person working for, or on behalf of, Mastercard is responsible for information security and must:
 Abide by Mastercard’s security policies and practices;

 Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed;

 Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and

 Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.

In line with Mastercard’s total compensation philosophy and assuming that the job will be performed in Canada, the successful candidate will be offered a competitive pay based on location, experience and other qualifications for the role and may be eligible to participate in a discretionary annual incentive program. This is a pipeline posting for future opportunities within our team.

Articulates annual SMART goals and outcomes the team can deliver to drive achievement of business objectives. Challenges the status quo, including with focus on speed of decision making and digital, innovative thinking.  Seeks to understand business/function opportunities and obstacles and strives to be in front of the business partnering on people & talent changes.  Supports prioritization and makes decisions to focus on highest impact work, including identifying work that (whilst potentially a good idea) is not a current priority.  Drives achievement of ambitious goals through test & learn, measurement, refinement, and holding others accountable, as needed.

Embraces and promotes the use of technology, including AI and digital tools, to enhance HR processes, employee experience, productivity, and careers.  Fosters a digital mindset and supports the development of digital skills across the organization. Operates with curiosity and openness in how AI-enabled tools can evolve the work of the HR function, capturing efficiencies and driving more focus on outcomes and impact.

 People Leadership: Leads and inspires a BOLDER, winning team with the mindset, expertise, and capability to achieve our People & Culture strategy, including developing great leaders.  Provides context for goals and how the work of the team aligns to and supports achievement of Sunlife’s Purpose, Ambition, and strategies.  Promotes team adaptability, resilience, and a psychologically safe work environment.  Cultivates a development culture with direct feedback, coaching, opportunities to cross and upskill, and gain stretch opportunities, in which performance concerns are addressed directly and promptly.  Models and sets expectations for talent scouting and desire to build the best HR team.  Showcases team talent and work.

 Data and Measurement Focus: Grounds decisions in facts, leverages data to generate new insights and opportunities, clearly defines and measures business outcomes to identify course corrections and measure success.  Informs strategies and decisions through knowledge of current external research and trends.  Encourages action based on best data available versus defaulting to comprehensive analyses.

Position Summary

The Software Engineering Director will lead the engineering organization responsible for Finance, Admin, Insights and Embedded Analytics Reporting to the SVP, Engineering, this leader will oversee a team of 5 Engineering Managers and approximately 60 engineers.

The Director will partner closely with Product Management to define roadmaps, align engineering strategy with business priorities, and build a cohesive, high-performing organization. This role requires a strategic engineering leader who can mentor leaders, strengthen talent density, drive technical architecture decisions, and help scale AI-powered products and platforms within a cloud-based ecosystem.

Key Responsibilities

Partner with Product Management to develop and execute roadmaps that balance product innovation, technical investments, operational excellence, and long-term platform strategy.
Lead and unify multiple engineering teams into a cohesive organization, establishing clear priorities, shared objectives, and strong cross-functional collaboration.
Develop and execute engineering strategies that support current and future business needs while ensuring scalable, reliable, and secure platform capabilities.
Drive technical architecture decisions across Core and Application & Platform Services technology stacks, partnering with architecture and shared services teams.
Coach, mentor, and develop managers and senior managers, building leadership capability and increasing organizational effectiveness and talent density.
Guide teams in evaluating and prioritizing technical initiatives by clearly articulating business value and aligning investments with strategic objectives.
Lead hiring, workforce planning, and succession planning efforts to attract, retain, and develop top engineering talent.
Collaborate with engineering, product, sales, customer success, and executive stakeholders to successfully deliver complex, large-scale initiatives.
Champion Agile and Kanban development methodologies and foster a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, and technical excellence.
Support the development and scaling of AI-driven products and services, helping create an integrated data ecosystem that enables innovation across the organization.

Required Skills & Qualifications

15+ years of progressive software engineering experience, including significant leadership experience within complex technology organizations.
Proven experience leading large engineering organizations through multiple layers of management, including managers and senior managers.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field.
Demonstrated success partnering with Product Management and executive stakeholders to define strategy, prioritize investments, and deliver business outcomes.
Experience defining and implementing software engineering best practices across the full software development lifecycle.
Strong track record of organizational leadership, including coaching leaders, driving change, and building high-performing teams.
Experience delivering large-scale cloud-based solutions using Azure, AWS, and/or Google Cloud Platform.
Familiarity with modern AI technologies, with preference given to candidates who have successfully built and scaled AI-enabled products or platforms.
Strong technical architecture background with the ability to evaluate trade-offs and guide strategic technology decisions.
Demonstrated ability to influence across engineering, product, sales, customer success, and executive teams.
Excellent communication, problem-solving, organizational, and stakeholder management skills.
Strong sense of ownership, urgency, accountability, and commitment to delivering results.

jobs.title: Sales Director, Aspirational Big Bets
jobs.description:
Strength in Trust

OneTrust’s mission is to enable innovation through the responsible use of data and AI. We believe that ensuring data is trusted shouldn’t slow teams down—it should accelerate what’s possible. This led us to develop the first technology platform for responsible data use in 2016. Today, with AI representing the latest and most impactful expansion of data yet, OneTrust is once again redefining what responsible innovation looks like. OneTrust, the AI‑Ready Governance Platform™, unifies regulatory intelligence, automation, and connected governance workflows so businesses can continue to move at the speed of AI while ensuring good governance to prevent data misuse at scale. Trusted by thousands of organizations worldwide, OneTrust is shaping the future where trusted data becomes a transformative force for business and society.

The Challenge

We are looking for a Regional Sales Director for our Aspirational Big Bets (New Logo) Enterprise team. Regional Sales Directors have a critical role and responsibility to develop and manage a team of Account Executives (Sales reps) to help them meet and exceed individual and team goals and metrics. Your team will be focused predominantly on new-customer acquisition: identifying high-potential organizations, developing trusted relationships with senior stakeholders, and leading complex sales from first conversation through close.

We invest heavily in our Sales Team through demand generation, methodology-driven sales philosophy, weekly sales trainings, customer-driven roadmaps, and a readily-available executive team to help close deals. This is a high value opportunity with uncapped commission and a competitive salary.

Your Mission

The Regional Sales Director is responsible for developing and managing a productive team of Aspirational Big Bets Account Executives. You will demonstrate the ability to train, motivate, and coach the team to successfully deliver or exceed quota for your patch. You will also qualify sales opportunities, setting proper customer expectations and quarterbacking deal negotiations.

As a Regional Sales Director, You Will

Demonstrate a knowledgeable understanding of OneTrust’s products and services, and how the different offerings can be leveraged to address different sets of customer pain points
Manage, hire, and train a team of Account Executives, driving an inclusive team dynamic and high-performance team culture focused exclusively on acquiring new customers
Develop a leverageable understanding of customer needs to assist with prospecting and qualifying potential buyers
Develop and maintain robust pipelines for future business for yourself and your team, set and hold to commits and accurately forecast delivery against those pipelines
Engage with high priority accounts for OneTrust, identifying and driving strategic engagement with the buyer, adjusting your / your team’s approach based on buyer persona and company context and leveraging OneTrust leadership accordingly to support deal close
Partner consistently with collaborating organizations (e.g., Business Development, Specialist Sales, Solution Engineering, Partner Sales, Marketing) throughout the deal cycle to increase deal close rates and deliver a coordinated prospect experience
Track and report on metrics for your team, utilizing data and regular pipeline inspection to prioritize actions and surface risks early
In partnership with HR, support the leadership team in ensuring equitable experiences, strengthening inclusion acumen, and promoting a culture of inclusivity and belonging that embraces the contributions of all team members

You Are

You are someone who’s both a player and coach with a hunting mentality and consultative approach. You enjoy motivating and driving others to perform while still exceeding yourself. You approach problems with the utmost creativity and perspective, and are well-disciplined in sales processes and CRM hygiene.

Your Experience Includes

Bachelor’s degree or comparable experience
10+ of proven sales experience, ideally selling B2B Enterprise-level software or related technologies
5 years of people management experience
Proven ability to engage across corporate functions and work with partner ecosystems and cross-functional deal teams
Effective customer-facing communication skills and experience communicating with C-Level Executives effectively
Experience managing complex, consultative sales cycles with multiple stakeholders and senior decision-makers
A strong prospecting and pipeline-generation discipline, with the resilience and ownership to create opportunities rather than rely solely on inbound demand
Commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion through continuous development, modeling inclusive behaviors, and proactively managing bias

Extra Awesome

Experience with Salesforce CRM
Experience selling into privacy, security, governance, risk, compliance, or other trust-related business areas

For California, Colorado, Connecticut, Nevada, New York, Rhode Island, and Washington-based candidates: the annual base pay range for this role is listed below. Within this range, individual pay is determined by several factors, including location, job-related skills, work experience, and relevant education and/or training. This role may also be eligible for discretionary bonuses, equity, and/or commissions, as well as benefits.

Salary Range

$153,750—$205,000 USD

Where we Work

We are embracing an office-first culture, encouraging three days a week in office for most roles, with meaningful opportunities to collaborate and celebrate in person.

Each role may have specific requirements or flexibility depending on the scope of the position, so we encourage you to verify this with your recruiter during your first interview.

Benefits

As an employee at OneTrust, you will be part of the OneTeam. That means you’ll receive support physically, mentally, and emotionally so that you can do your best work both in and out of the office. This includes comprehensive healthcare coverage, flexible PTO, equity RSUs, annual performance bonus opportunities, retirement account support, 14+ weeks of paid parental leave, career development opportunities, company-paid privacy certification exam fees, and much more. Specific benefits differ by country. For more information, talk to your recruiter or visit onetrust.com/careers.

Resources

Check out the following to learn more about OneTrust and its people:

OneTrust Careers on YouTube
@LifeatOneTrust on Instagram

Your Data

You have the right to have your personal data updated or removed. You also have the right to have a copy of the information OneTrust holds about you. Further details about these rights are available on the website in our Privacy Overview .
You can change your mind at any time and have your personal data removed from our database. In order to do this you must contact us and let us know you wish to be removed. The request should be made on the Data Subject Request Form.

Recruitment fraud warning: OneTrust is aware of scams involving false offers of employment with our company. The fraudulent jobs, interviews and job offers use fake websites, email addresses, group chat and text messages. Be aware that we never ask candidates for personal information, IDs or bank information during the interview process. We do not interview prospective candidates via instant message or group chat, and do not require candidates to purchase products or services, or process payments on our behalf as a condition of any employment offer. Please note that any legitimate interview availability requests will come directly from a OneTrust recruiter with an "@onetrust.com" email address. You may also receive legitimate emails from "@us.greenhouse-mail.io". Recruiters will only reach out to candidates who have applied for a role through our ATS (Greenhouse) or prospects via LinkedIn InMail. Job offers will come from a recruiter and may have a "@docusign.net" email address. For more information or if you have been targeted please reach out to askrecruiting@onetrust.com.

Our Commitment to You

When you join OneTrust you are stepping onto a launching pad — the countdown has begun. The destination? A career without boundaries working alongside a diverse and inclusive crew who is passionate about doing meaningful work. As a pioneer, your voice and expertise will help chart the direction of an entirely new category. Our commitment to putting people first starts with you. Your growth is part of the mission. Our goal is to give you the power to embark on the next phase of your uniquely, unique career.

You will guide enterprise resource planning modernization, including NetSuite and the broader enterprise application landscape, while establishing

technology direction for Manufacturing and the Integrated Supply Chain in alignment with Finance, Human Resources, and Commercial capabilities. You will also evaluate emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, software-as-a-service solutions, automation, Industrial Internet of Things, and cloud and edge technologies, to determine how they can support the future of work and deliver measurable business value.

What You Will Do

Partner with Enterprise Business Engagement Managers and Business Relationship Managers to translate business priorities into integrated process, data, and technology strategies, capability roadmaps, and investment priorities.
Develop and maintain three-to-five-year technology roadmaps for enterprise resource planning, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, and other key enterprise functions.

Define technology strategies and target-state architectures for Supply Chain, Manufacturing, and Digital Plant capabilities in alignment with Finance, Human Resources, and Commercial priorities.

Participate in future-of-work discussions and identify emerging technology opportunities that can improve productivity, resilience, scalability, and sustainability.

Practical experience applying artificial intelligence, machine learning, generative artificial intelligence, advanced analytics, or intelligent automation to enterprise business processes.
Experience evaluating and implementing software-as-a-service platforms and emerging enterprise technologies.
Knowledge of The Open Group Architecture Framework, ArchiMate, capability-based planning, and architecture governance.
Demonstrated ability to connect strategy and execution, influence across organizational boundaries, and advise senior leaders as a trusted partner.

jobs.title: Chief Actuary
jobs.description:
Overview

Reporting to the Vice President and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and operating under the oversight of the Chief Executive Officer (CEO), the Chief Actuary is a senior leader accountable for the Corporation’s claims & premiums forecasting, rate setting, policy liability valuation, investments, asset-liability management, stress testing capital, and reinsurance.

The Chief Actuary represents the Corporation before the Public Utilities Board (PUB) during the annual General Rate Application (GRA), providing actuarial expertise and expert testimony. The role has oversight from the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) also serves as a strategic advisor to the CEO and Executive Management team, leveraging actuarial analysis and statistical research to support key business decisions and organizational change. In addition, the Chief Actuary contributes to governance through participation on committees overseeing claims, investments, and enterprise risk management.

Responsibilities

Strategic Planning & Transformation:
Lead the development of strategies for pricing and capital management, reserving, forecasting, reinsurance and investments.
Provide expert advice and guidance on the Corporation’s financial forecasting, rate setting, valuation of policy liabilities, investments, asset and liability management, stress testing of capital and reinsurance.
Oversee the design, implementation, and reporting of the Corporation’s Asset and Liability Management strategy.
Develop and implement processes to ensure a current understanding of new and emerging trends, practices and solutions.
Develop and implement processes and practices to evaluate MPI’s ability to meet needs and address future conditions or issues.
Create strategies to position the Corporation in the future by anticipating and acting on trends.
Translate the strategic plans into operational and business plans for pricing, capital management, reserving, forecasting, reinsurance and investments and set operational objectives to all employees.

Operational & Performance Leadership:
Determine actuarially sound rates for the Basic line of business and provide professional opinion on the appropriateness of these rates to the PUB.
Determine actuarially sound rates for the Extension line of business.
Determine actuarially sound rates for Commercial lines and collaborate with key stakeholders to incorporate strategic, operational, and competitive requirements into the proposed rates.
Ensure the effective design, maintenance, controls, and output of key pricing models.
Testify at the PUB rate hearings on behalf of the Corporation.
Perform quarterly reviews of the Corporation’s policy liabilities for all lines of business.
Work collaboratively with the External Appointed Actuary to obtain an external signed actuarial opinion on the policy liability reviews.
Monitor claims reporting and reserving guidelines, in collaboration with key internal stakeholders.
Contribute to the forecasting process by providing actuarial forecasts by line of business and include premiums, claims costs, expenses, and investment income.
Lead the design, maintenance, and on-going enhancement of the Corporation’s financial forecasting model.
Provide financial modelling and scenario analysis for strategic decisions from the Executive and the Board of Directors.
Lead the design, maintenance, and output of the stochastic models used to simulate the behaviour of claims, interest rates, investment returns, and other economic variables.
Perform Financial Condition Testing for each line of business to stress test the capital for satisfactory financial condition and provide a signed actuarial opinion.
Oversee the Corporation’s Asset and Liability Management program to meet the programs’ objectives.
Perform commutation analysis for the Corporation’s reinsurance contracts and participate in the negotiation of reinsurance contracts.
Monitor investment performance and report investment performance to the Investment Committee of the Board of Directors.

Organizational & People Leadership:
Establish and maintain an effective organizational structure that supports the strategic delivery of services, ensuring alignment with corporate priorities and operational excellence.
Foster a unified and high-performing leadership team that is collaborative, future-focused, and committed to advancing the Corporation’s mission through continuous service improvement and innovation.
Champion a culture of accountability, inclusion, and excellence, where diverse perspectives are valued, calculated risks are embraced, and employees are empowered to deliver exceptional service and contribute meaningfully to the Corporation’s success.

Qualifications

Education:
Fellow of the Canadian Institute of Actuaries (FCIA) and Fellow of the Casualty Actuarial Society (FCAS).
The CFA designation and/or strong investment knowledge is considered as an asset.

Experience:
Ten (10) years of senior leadership experience at the Director or Senior Director level, including five (5) years in a senior actuarial leadership capacity within the property and casualty insurance industry, with accountability for strategic rate setting, reserving, enterprise risk management, and actuarial governance.

Technical Knowledge and Skills:
Exceptional leadership skills with a proven ability to form, lead and develop high performing teams, and demonstrate successes in leading change.
Superior negotiation skills along with excellent interpersonal skills and proven success in public speaking and formal presentations.
Proven experience effectively and critically assessing different product and coverage scenarios and determining creative solutions that meet customers’ needs while demonstrating clear understanding of root cause, impacts and consequences of decisions on both customers and the corporation.
Strong organizational skills along with the ability to plan and manage multiple complex projects and tasks simultaneously will contribute to success in this role.
Capable of positively engaging executive management, the Board of Directors as well as influential external stakeholders (e.g. Government of Manitoba, strategic business partners, interest groups with diverging interests) and operate with the highest level of integrity and business ethics.

The role is accountable for profitable growth, portfolio mix and capital efficiency; underwriting appetite, standards and governance; pricing and portfolio performance; coverage intent and product strategy; material referrals and exceptions; emerging-risk and claims-trend oversight; talent and technical capability; and senior market leadership. PFR comprises several distinct specialist businesses. The PLL must have strong financial and professional lines expertise and sufficient technical breadth to understand, challenge and lead across the portfolio. Deep expertise in one or more

PFR areas is an asset, but identical specialist depth across every product is not required. The PLL remains accountable for underwriting standards, coverage intent, guidelines and product direction, while increasingly leading detailed development and execution through product specialists, underwriters and internal or external resources. The role works closely with Field teams and functional partners to build technical and leadership depth and ensure decisions are made at the appropriate level.

What part will you play?

If you’re looking for a place where you can make a meaningful difference, you’ve found it. The work we do at Markel gives people the confidence to move forward and seize opportunities, and you’ll find your fit among our global community of optimists and problem-solvers. We’re always pushing each other to go further because we believe that when we realize our potential, we can help others reach theirs. Join us and play your part in something special!

The opportunity~

We are seeking a senior underwriting leader to lead the strategy, performance and health of our Professional & Financial Risks (PFR) portfolio in Canada. This is an exciting opportunity to shape the future of Markel Canada’s PFR portfolio, influence broader organizational strategy and strengthen our presence across specialty areas, customer segments and distribution channels. PFR brings together several distinct specialist businesses, including across our E&O, D&O and Cyber product lines. This role leads them collectively as one portfolio, while recognizing that each requires its own technical expertise, market knowledge and underwriting strategy. You will be accountable for sustainable profitable growth, portfolio mix, underwriting direction and the technical capability of the PFR business. As a senior leader, you will collaborate with other product line leaders, Field distribution teams, and other functional teams across global operations. Working closely with the Markel Canada leadership team, you will join a values-driven culture with integrity and accountability at its core, with significant onward career opportunities.

If you are an underwriting leader who builds strong businesses and technical capability, brings sound judgment to a complex portfolio, and excels at creating value and market impact, this is your opportunity to make a difference.

This is an opportunity to join a growing and ambitious business in a high-impact and visible role at a pivotal time in our journey. You will lead the development and delivery of Markel’s Professional & Financial Risks (PFR) strategy in Canada, building greater growth, cohesion and performance across the PFR portfolio.

As part of the Product Leadership team, reporting into the SVP Underwriting, you are the senior leader responsible for the PFR underwriting strategy at Markel Canada. PFR brings together a range of specialist products, including Professional Indemnity/E&O, Management Liability (D&O, EPL, Fiduciary), Cyber, Crime, and Tech E&O and Fintech packages. The role is accountable for the full PFR product line, written through our specialty teams, Sectors, Digital Portal and Delegated Underwriting. Markel intends to profitably grow the PFR portfolio, in coordination with other lines of business, by strengthening our presence in our areas of expertise and creating new avenues for growth.

The role works closely with Field underwriting teams and with Claims, Actuarial, Data and Analytics, Operations and Distribution, as well as the International OCUO (Office of the Chief Underwriting Officer) and other UK-based colleagues and, occasionally, US-based colleagues, connecting Canadian opportunities with Markel’s broader international capabilities.

What you'll be doing~

Own the strategy, performance and health of the Professional & Financial Risks (PFR) portfolio, delivering sustainable profitability and growth across its component businesses.
Translate the goals established by the President & Managing Director and SVP of Underwriting into a clear, prioritized PFR agenda, and communicate it across the business.
Set portfolio mix and allocation across the PFR businesses, with clear accountability for underwriting appetite, pricing adequacy and portfolio economics, and direct portfolio remediation where needed.
Champion the technical capability of PFR, working with Field leaders and people managers on development, coaching and succession for PFR talent, and supporting specialists and senior underwriters to take ownership so that technical decisions are made at the appropriate level.
Set the direction for underwriting guidelines, sector-specific underwriting frameworks, product and coverage development, underwriting authorities and training priorities, with detailed development led by the appropriate product and sector specialists, underwriters and Field teams.
Manage technical wordings & endorsements, product development, underwriting guidance and governance for the PFR portfolio, including oversight of underwriting authorities, periodic guideline updates, and conducting audits to uphold technical standards.
Elevate Markel’s presence and reputation in the Canadian financial, cyber and professional lines market through senior broker and client relationships, a strong read of market dynamics, thought leadership and participation in industry events.
Decide on material referrals, novel risks and significant exceptions within PFR, applying technical rigour and considering the implications for the overall portfolio.
Provide oversight of emerging risks, claims trends, volatility and aggregation across PFR, ensuring appropriate mitigation strategies are in place for professional, financial and cyber exposures.
Proactively identify new market opportunities and product offerings within PFR, including innovative solutions for emerging and complex risks in areas such as professional services, technology, and financial institutions, and development of risk mitigation offerings.
Act as an active senior underwriting leader with Field underwriting teams, helping them make better decisions and connecting them with the right expertise and resources, both locally and across Markel’s international network.
Work closely with PFR product and underwriting leaders across Markel’s international businesses, sharing ideas, products, underwriting experience, portfolio performance and best practice, and drawing on one another’s expertise to strengthen results in each market.
Set clear direction and expectations, challenge appropriately and create accountability, building a positive, collaborative and high-performing underwriting culture across PFR.
Ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and company standards related to PFR business.
Collaborate with Claims, Actuarial, Data and Analytics, Operations, Distribution and executive leadership to drive portfolio performance and strengthen underwriting practice within PFR.
Define the underwriting requirements, priorities and intended outcomes for digital, operational and process initiatives, working with the teams responsible for implementation.

Our must haves~

Proven ability to leverage data and analytics to enhance underwriting strategies and drive improvement in PFR portfolio results.
Strong financial and professional lines underwriting expertise and credibility, including complex, layered and shared programme structures, and experience in technical leadership roles within the sector.
Technical breadth across the PFR portfolio to understand, challenge and lead its component businesses, including medium and large organisations and cross-border and foreign exposures. Deep expertise in one or more financial, cyber or professional lines is an asset.
Proven track record of managing sophisticated PFR portfolios and executing strategies that deliver profitable growth and sustainable performance.
Strong portfolio-management judgment, with a clear understanding of how pricing, claims trends, appetite, coverage, portfolio mix, volatility and capital considerations interact.
The judgment to recognize when deeper specialist expertise is required, and the leadership ability to draw on the right internal or external expertise.
Strong grasp of claims, actuarial, and loss control functions as they relate to professional and financial risks.
Established senior broker and client relationships within the Canadian Professional & Financial Risks marketplace, and a strong understanding of Canadian market dynamics.
Strategic mindset with a proactive, entrepreneurial approach to identifying solutions and addressing challenges in the PFR space.
A track record of leading through others and through influence, without relying on direct reporting lines~ developing technical capability, giving specialists meaningful ownership and enabling teams to execute.
Minimum of 10+ years of professional and financial risks (PFR) insurance underwriting and leadership experience.
Undergraduate degree preferred. Graduate degree and/or relevant industry designations would be highly advantageous.
Outstanding verbal and written communication abilities, with a collaborative approach and strong relationship-building skills.
Excellent strategic acumen with a proven ability to think long term and lead transformational change.
Energetic, service oriented, proactive self-starter with a strong sense of urgency and the ability to anticipate the future needs of the business.
Proven ability to set and achieve objectives, and to influence and secure buy-in from senior leaders, peers and underwriters.
Adaptable, with the ability to zoom out from an individual underwriting issue and consider its implications for the overall portfolio.
Interpersonal skills necessary to achieve business objectives and interact effectively, combined with high levels of confidence, integrity, energy, enthusiasm, executive presence, and a personality aligned with the “Markel Style.”
Willingness and ability to travel.

If you’re ready to make an impact, we’d love to hear from you!

Who we are~

Markel Group (NYSE – MKL) a Fortune 500 company with over 60 offices in 20+ countries, is a holding company for insurance, reinsurance, specialist advisory, and investment operations around the world.

We’re all about people | We win together | We strive for better | We enjoy the everyday | We think further

What’s in it for you?

A great starting salary plus annual bonus potential & strong benefits package.
20 vacation days plus additional floater days per year.
Fantastic company RRSP, extended health and dental coverage, life insurance, travel insurance, vision care and wellness initiatives.
There are countless opportunities to learn new skills and develop in your career and we can provide the support needed to do just that!

This is a replacement role.
