jobs.title: Senior Director Finance
jobs.description:
Senior Director of Finance

Markham, Ontario

Our client is a successful, privately held Canadian company with a well-established business and an entrepreneurial, growth-oriented culture. They are looking for a Senior Director of Finance to join their leadership team and take on a broad, highly visible mandate.

This is not a traditional accounting-focused finance role. While ensuring strong financial discipline remains important, the real opportunity is to become a strategic and commercial partner to the business — helping leadership better understand performance, identify opportunities and make stronger, data-driven decisions.

The Opportunity

Reporting to the President, the Senior Director of Finance will lead the finance function while spending significant time working across the organization.
The mandate will include:
Leading financial planning, budgeting, forecasting and performance analysis
Providing meaningful insight into revenue, margins, pricing, costs and profitability
Developing and enhancing KPIs and management reporting
Partnering with operational and commercial leaders to support better decision-making
Evaluating business cases, capital investments and growth opportunities
Identifying opportunities to improve processes, controls and overall efficiency
Leveraging technology, automation and AI to improve the way financial information is produced and used
Ensuring accurate and timely financial reporting and maintaining appropriate financial controls
Leading, developing and mentoring the finance team
Acting as a trusted financial advisor to senior leadership

The Ideal Candidate

You are a CPA
with progressive finance leadership experience and a strong understanding of a manufacturing or similarly operational business.

You bring strong technical fundamentals, but your real strength is your ability to connect the numbers to the business. You are curious, analytical and commercially minded, and you naturally dig beneath financial results to understand what is driving them.
You are equally comfortable rolling up your sleeves and getting into the details as you are sitting with senior leaders and helping shape a decision.

Experience working within a privately held, entrepreneurial or mid-sized organization would be particularly valuable.

Why Consider This Opportunity?

This is an opportunity to join a successful organization where Finance has a meaningful seat at the table. You’ll have the ability to influence how the business operates, improve the tools and information used to make decisions, and help shape the continued evolution of the finance function.

For someone who enjoys building, improving and influencing — rather than simply maintaining — there is a lot to sink your teeth into here.

Work Model:
Predominantly onsite

jobs.title: Head of Revenue
jobs.description:
Head of Revenue - Full-time, Remote

Application Deadline: November 29th, 2026 @ 11:59pm EST

Build the revenue engine that takes BeMo to the next stage of growth.

Why BeMo?

At BeMo, our mission is rooted in the belief that education is a universal right, not a privilege. We help students pursue highly competitive professional programs through admissions consulting, test preparation, and technology-enabled services. Our team is remote, fast-moving, data-driven, and focused on measurable student and business outcomes.

The Role:

We are looking for a commercially rigorous Head of Revenue to own the full revenue system across demand generation, sales, expansion, lifecycle revenue, and revenue operations. This is not a traditional sales-leadership role. Your job is to identify the biggest constraint on profitable growth, quantify the opportunity, prioritize the highest-leverage initiatives, and lead cross-functional execution.

You will be accountable for increasing cash and revenue while protecting the quality and economics of growth. You will work directly with the CEO and lead the revenue organization toward BeMo's long-term growth trajectory.

What You Will Own:

Company-wide revenue growth across marketing, sales, direct/self-serve revenue, upsells, cross-sells, downsells, saves, referrals, and reactivation.
Demand generation economics, including qualified lead volume, cost per qualified request, CAC, ROI/ROAS, and channel-level growth efficiency.
Sales performance, including completed consultations, revenue per completed call, conversion rate, AOV, show efficiency, response speed, and forecasting accuracy.
Pricing, packaging, offers, promotions, and lifecycle monetization designed to increase customer value without relying on short-term pull-forward tactics.
Revenue operations: attribution, dashboards, lead tracking, funnel measurement, forecasting, QA, and reliable experiment measurement.
A disciplined testing program across acquisition, landing pages, sales, follow-up, email/SMS/direct mail, offers, and expansion revenue.
Cross-functional prioritization: decide where the next dollar and the next hour of team capacity create the highest expected incremental value.
Revenue leadership systems that reduce dependence on any single individual and create repeatable, scalable execution.

How Success Will Be Measured:

The role carries a significant performance-based component aligned with the same outcomes the role controls. Performance is evaluated across three dimensions:
Cash growth: durable improvement in actual cash received.
Demand generation: growth in qualified demand and channel economics, not traffic or lead volume in isolation.
Strategic execution: completion and quality of the systems, experiments, reporting, automation, and longer-term initiatives required to compound revenue growth.

These outcomes are also subject to a company growth-driver score that prevents one strong metric from masking deterioration elsewhere in the revenue system. The objective is sustainable progress toward BeMo's long-term growth trajectory, not local optimization of one department.

What You Will Do:

Diagnose the revenue funnel and identify the highest-value constraint before prescribing solutions.
Build quarterly revenue plans with quantified assumptions, targets, owners, timelines, and expected impact.
Lead the Sales Manager and coordinate tightly with marketing, operations, support, finance, and DevOps.
Set and monitor leading and lagging KPIs across acquisition, sales, and expansion revenue.
Design and review experiments with defined hypotheses, controls, success metrics, guardrails, and decision rules.
Improve the economics of paid and organic acquisition while maintaining sufficient qualified demand for the sales organization.
Increase revenue per lead and revenue per customer through better conversion, AOV, offers, upsells, cross-sells, and reactivation.
Build accurate forecasting, attribution, and executive reporting so decisions are based on trusted data.
Use AI and automation where they improve speed, conversion, decision quality, or operating leverage.
Develop leaders, delegate execution appropriately, and hold teams accountable for both results and quality.

We’d Love to Hear From You if You…

Have 7+ years of progressively senior revenue, growth, commercial, sales, or marketing leadership experience.
Can demonstrate material revenue growth you personally helped cause, with baseline, endpoint, time period, and measurable contribution.
Have owned more than one part of the revenue system - ideally demand generation plus sales, lifecycle/expansion, or RevOps.
Are highly quantitative and can translate funnel changes into incremental revenue, cash, CAC, and contribution economics.
Have managed leaders and teams rather than relying on personal heroics.
Can distinguish correlation from causation and are comfortable changing your view when the data contradicts your initial hypothesis.
Know how to prioritize aggressively and can explain what should not be done yet.
Have strong attention to detail, forecasting discipline, and operating cadence.
Are comfortable in a remote, high-accountability environment and can work across functions without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.

Compensation & Location:

Remote role. Potential total annual compensation up to $300,000+ CAD, including competitive base compensation and a significant performance based bonus tied to cash growth, demand generation, strategic execution, and progress against the company's long term revenue growth plan. Final compensation will depend on experience and performance.

Our Hiring Process:

Our hiring process includes multiple steps. You will progress to each step if we believe there's a good match for both parties. The process includes a review of your application, a skills assessment test, a virtual OR phone interview, a face-to-face interview with select members of our team via video conference and lastly, reference calls.

How to Apply:

Simple. Click "Apply" and fill out the short application form.

We won’t be able to individually respond to all applicants, but if we feel that you’re a strong match, we will be in touch via email to proceed with your application. Thanks, and we look forward to hearing from you!

--

BeMo is strongly committed to inclusion and diversity within its community and welcomes all applicants including but not limited to: visible minorities, all religions and ethnicities, persons with disabilities, LGBTQ persons, and all others who may contribute to the further diversification of ideas.

jobs.title: Director, Client Success and Adoption US
jobs.description:
Jacobian builds AI-powered radiology reporting software, including Fluency for Imaging (FFI) and SmartAssist. Our customers are US health systems, imaging centers and radiology groups that rely on FFI every day to produce patient reports.

This director brings together two teams with a shared mission: helping customers realize measurable value from FFI and grow into long-term partners. Client Success Managers own the commercial relationship, account health and renewals. Adoption Specialists drive radiologist and administrator enablement, including SmartAssist rollouts. The director runs both as one motion, with the Client Success Manager accountable for the account and the Adoption Specialist work planned against each account's goals.

As Jacobian's US customer base grows, this director will scale both teams to match. That means planning headcount ahead of demand, hiring and onboarding new team members, and building repeatable playbooks and coverage models so service quality holds as account and site volume increase. The role partners closely with Implementation, Support, Sales, Marketing, and Product teams. Drive growth through our existing customers by ensuring each one is live, engaged, and achieving measurable clinical and operational results, earning their renewal, expansion, and advocacy.

This is a remote role based in the US or Canada.

Key Responsibilitites

Operating model: Define US customer segmentation (high-touch, scaled, digital), the engagement model and coverage ratios for each tier, and the customer lifecycle from the go-live handoff through renewal.
Team leadership: Hire, onboard, coach, and retain Client Success Managers and Adoption Specialists. Define role profiles and career paths between the two roles, run a regular performance-management cadence, and plan headcount ahead of customer growth
Training and adoption: Lead new-customer training on Fluency for Imaging, from administrator onboarding through radiologist go-live. Run adoption programs for AI features such as SmartAssist, own speech recognition tuning and troubleshooting, and set utilization benchmarks by product
Customer health and risk: Build health scores in HubSpot from FFI usage, SmartAssist adoption, speech recognition performance, support trends, and sentiment. Set early-warning signals, and own how at-risk accounts are identified, escalated, and recovered
Value and retention: Lead executive business reviews that show customers the clinical and operational value they are getting. Own the US renewal calendar and forecast
Build and run a US reference radiologist network through the Adoption Specialists and CSMs: recruit continuously (including via the SmartAssist rollout), match members to Sales and Marketing needs, give back through fees or non-financial benefits, and measure participation and impact on renewals
Growth and advocacy: Partner with Sales on expansion opportunities and clean pre- and post-sale handoffs, and with Marketing on references and customer advocacy
Cross-team handoffs: Own the customer relationship across Implementation and Technical Support. Set exit criteria for the go-live handoff from Implementation, and coordinate with Technical Support on escalations and recurring issues so customers get one consistent experience
Scaled engagement: Serve smaller accounts efficiently through HubSpot-driven touchpoints, triggered playbooks, AI-assisted account preparation, and meeting capture
Voice of the customer: Bring structured customer feedback to Product, Clinical, and the executive team. Close the loop on adoption friction and feature requests, and represent customers in roadmap discussions
Financial accountability: Accountable for gross and net revenue retention, churn, and renewal and expansion targets for US accounts. Contributes to the Client Success budget and headcount plan with the VP, Client Success
Quality and compliance: Make sure customer feedback that may be a complaint is routed into Jacobian's complaint-handling process. Partner with Legal, Security, and Compliance on protecting customer data under HIPAA

Requirements

8+ years in customer success, account management, or professional services, including 3+ years leading customer-facing teams
Experience working with health systems or radiology groups, ideally in clinical software, imaging IT, or speech recognition and reporting
Credibility with clinical stakeholders (radiologists, department leaders) and IT stakeholders, up to the executive level, including handling escalations
A track record of improving retention and adoption, with measurable results
Comfort with data, metrics, and CS tooling (CRM, customer success platforms), and a systems thinker who builds repeatable processes
Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience

Preferred

Familiarity with radiology workflows
Hands-on experience with speech recognition tuning and troubleshooting
Experience rolling out AI features or ambient documentation tools to physicians
Experience building a CS function or CS Operations capability from an early stage
Experience in a regulated environment such as medical device software or HIPAA-covered healthcare

Benefits

Join a fast-growing, mission-driven team shaping the future of AI in radiology - building products that improve workflows and patient outcomes worldwide
This role is open to fully remote candidates based anywhere in the US or Canada
Comprehensive health insurance available from day one
401k contributions, employer match up to 5%
20 days PTO + sick days
Enhanced parental leave and pay

Here’s What You’ll Be Focusing On

Operationalize business strategy to drive profitable growth.

Build, develop, and lead an organization that can consistently deliver sustainable financial results and an exceptional customer experience.

Excellent business and financial acumen.

jobs.description:
About the role

McCann is seeking a Strategy Director, Performance & Creative Integration to lead strategies that connect brand building, creative ideas and measurable business outcomes. Rooted in our Truth Well Told ethos, you will turn business, audience and cultural insight into clear strategic direction, then work with creative, media, analytics, CRM and commerce partners to bring that direction to life. You will lead client relationships, guide strategists and help grow our clients and the agency.

What you will do:

Lead strategy and creative development

Understand client business and marketing problems. Draw on consumer, cultural, category, media and performance data to find meaningful truths and opportunities.
Develop integrated strategies that connect brand objectives, customer needs, acquisition and measurable business results.
Write clear briefs and strategic narratives that inspire original creative work across channels and customer journeys.
Partner with Creative and Business Leadership to develop ideas, give constructive feedback and carry the strategic story from opportunity through execution and impact.
Stay close to digital behaviour and social conversation. Explain what people do and why it matters for the work.

Connect performance and creative

Bring creative, media, analytics, CRM and commerce teams together around shared audience insight, campaign objectives and measurement.
Shape demand generation, lead generation, customer acquisition and digital commerce strategies where they serve the client’s business.
Use campaign results to identify creative opportunities, guide versioning and personalization, and recommend what to test next.
Develop practical approaches to testing and iteration, including dynamic creative optimization where appropriate.

Lead clients and the team

Present persuasive strategic recommendations and lead confident, productive conversations with clients and internal teams.
Bring proactive thinking to client relationships, new business opportunities and agency growth.
Mentor strategists, adapt your coaching to their needs and give clear feedback that helps people and the work grow.

What you bring

At least eight years of relevant strategy experience, including agency experience and leadership of client work.
A record of turning insight into strong creative work and clear business outcomes.
Working knowledge of media, audience strategy, analytics and measurement, with experience in performance marketing, lead generation, CRM, customer acquisition or digital commerce.
The ability to decide which data matters, explain what it means and translate it into creative direction.
Strong writing, storytelling, presentation and client leadership skills.
Curiosity about culture and digital behaviour, sound judgment, and an open approach to collaboration and feedback.
Experience guiding or managing strategists and helping multidisciplinary teams work together.

Success in this role

Your strategies will help clients build their brands and achieve measurable business results. Teams will use your direction to create connected work, learn from its performance and improve what comes next. You will strengthen strategic talent, client relationships and McCann’s reputation for effective creative work.

jobs.title: Director Customer Success
jobs.location: St John’s, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada
jobs.description:
Why SiftMed
SiftMed is an AI company in St. John’s, Newfoundland. Insurance carriers, independent medical examiners and legal teams use our platform to review medical records in claims. It finds the facts a case turns on, like pre-existing conditions, treatment gaps and causation evidence, across thousands of pages. Each finding links to its source page, and customers cut review time by 50 to 70 percent. We handle some of the most sensitive data there is, so security and privacy shape every product decision.

Revenue grew 10X in 2025. In July 2026 we closed a round led by Staircase Ventures, with the founders of Verafin, bringing our total funding to more than $10 million. We’re opening a new office and have more customer demand than people to meet it. Titles and comp are flexible for the right person. If you want your work to matter from your first week and want to help build a company that started in Newfoundland, we’d love to talk.

The role
You'll own the full customer lifecycle at SiftMed: pilots, onboarding, adoption, retention and expansion. You'll write the playbook for how we work with every customer, from strategic accounts to smaller ones, and make sure each one gets real value from SiftMed long after the contract is signed.

You'll report to our VP, Product and work closely with Sales, Product and Engineering. To start, you'll run pilots and onboarding yourself. As SiftMed grows, you'll build and lead a customer team to take on more of that work.

What you'll do

Pilots and onboarding
Design the playbook for how we manage every SiftMed customer, from first pilot to renewal
Run pilots during the sales cycle with Sales and Product, and manage strategic pilots end to end as program manager
Build and scale our onboarding process, and handle configuration for new customers

Adoption and retention
Design adoption, training and outreach plans for priority customers and smaller accounts
Define customer health scores from product usage and engagement, and flag at-risk accounts well ahead of renewal
Confirm new customers have fully replaced their old review process, and retrain accounts when key stakeholders change
Own how we announce new releases to customers, and use them to re-engage quiet accounts

Expansion and product
Find growth opportunities in existing accounts and run expansion plans with Sales and Product
Turn feedback across accounts into roadmap priorities, scope fixes for adoption blockers with Engineering, and tell customers what we built for them
Use AI to analyze usage data and customer feedback, and to draft customer communications

Who you are
You build a process, then run it yourself until someone else can.
You notice when an account goes quiet, and you act on it long before renewal.
You can turn scattered customer feedback into a clear priority for the product team.
You work well across Sales, Product and Engineering, and you get things done without needing to manage everyone involved.
You want to grow into leading a team.

This role probably isn't right for you if you want a team in place on day one.

What you bring
You use AI tools every day to work faster and better, and you can show us how. This is required for every role at SiftMed.
10+ years in customer success, account management or implementation for B2B software
Experience designing and running onboarding and adoption programs across a full book of customers
Experience running pilots or proofs of concept with enterprise customers during a sales cycle
Experience defining customer health metrics and using product usage data to manage retention
Experience working with Product and Engineering to turn customer feedback into product changes

Bonus points
Background in insurance, legal or healthcare software
Experience building or leading a customer success team
Experience with Salesforce or product analytics tools

If you don't match every item here, apply anyway.

Your first six months
First month: Learn the product in depth and meet our customers alongside Sales and Product
Within 3 months: Run your first pilot and onboard new customers using a playbook you've written
Within 4 months: Launch customer health scores across our full customer book
By 6 months: Own the customer lifecycle end to end, with an adoption and expansion plan for every priority account

What you get
Behind every medical file we review is a person waiting on a decision about their claim. We take that seriously. We don’t take ourselves too seriously. Everyone has a seat at the table, whatever their role. Your ideas shape what we build, and you’ll have the trust and autonomy to act on them.

Four times a year, the whole company heads out of the office for “Boil-Up.” In Newfoundland, a boil-up means stopping to boil the kettle over an open fire for tea and a bite to eat. Ours is a week of strategic planning and fun, where everyone helps set direction for the months ahead. Between Boil-Ups, you’ll find us on the pickleball court, laughing together and celebrating life's special occasions.

We offer flexible, hybrid work because we trust our people. You won’t need to ask twice to do school drop-off or get to a mid-day appointment. We serve a wide range of people, so we need a team with a wide range of backgrounds and perspectives. We welcome applicants from every background. If you need an accommodation at any point in the hiring process, let us know and we’ll make it work.

jobs.description:
Are you looking to make your mark and grow your career with a company on the rise? We'd love to have you on our team!

Equinox Gold
is a growth-focused gold producer headquartered in Vancouver, British Columbia, operating a diversified portfolio of high-quality, long-life mines in Canada, Mexico, Nicaragua, and United States. Guided by our core values of integrity
, excellence
, accountability

Reporting to the SVP, Accounting and Reporting, the Director, Operations Accounting and Reporting plays a key role in the timely and accurate preparation of the Company’s monthly financial statements and quarterly financial reports. Continuous Improvement

Required Experience And Skill Set

10+ years of experience, preferably with a high-growth, multi-jurisdictional public company or Big 4 firm; 3+ years of supervisory experience.

Strong analytical, problem-solving and research skills.
Strong communication skills with the ability to explain complex accounting issues to key stakeholders.
Strong attention to detail and organizational skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines.
Advanced Excel and financial systems skills; accounting system implementation experience is an asset.
Self-motivated team player able to build partnerships and motivate teams across the organization.
High ethical standards and commitment to integrity in financial reporting.

Job Conditions

Fluency in Spanish is an asset.
Willing to travel to company sites as needed.

CPA, or equivalent designation.

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related discipline.

jobs.title: Director of FP&A
jobs.description:
Senior FP&A leadership opportunity with a large, well-established North American manufacturing and distribution company headquartered in Vancouver. Excellent opportunity for an experienced finance leader who enjoys combining strategic financial oversight with hands-on analysis, developing high-performing teams, and influencing executive-level decision-making. Competitive compensation, excellent benefits, and a collaborative corporate culture.

Who- the Company:

Our client is a very well-established and successful manufacturing and distribution company with operations across North America, 2000 employees, 10+ legal entities, 30+ operating sites across Canada and the US, etc. They have a great reputation among their happy customers and partners. The 40+ person finance team is collaborative and friendly, and the leaders promote productive workdays with plenty of communication and organization to limit unnecessary overtime.

The company is recognized for its commitment to operational excellence, continuous improvement, and professional development. Its finance team works collaboratively with senior leadership and business stakeholders to support organizational performance and long-term growth.

What- the Role:

Our client seeking a new Director of Financial Planning & Analysis
to lead its enterprise-wide FP&A function. Reporting to the Vice President of Strategy, this is a hands-on leadership position responsible for overseeing financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, and analysis across a large and complex North American organization.
The Director will lead and develop the FP&A team while partnering closely with the VP, CFO, executive leadership, Finance Business Partners, and other cross-functional stakeholders to strengthen financial planning discipline, improve forecasting accuracy, and deliver meaningful financial insights that support business decisions.

Key Responsibilities include:

Budgeting & Forecasting:
Lead enterprise-wide budgeting, forecasting, and long-range financial planning, including cash flow forecasting.
Financial Analysis & Reporting:
Oversee financial consolidation, performance analysis, and executive and Board reporting, identifying key business drivers, risks, and opportunities.
Financial Modelling & Capital Planning:
Lead scenario analysis, capital investment evaluations, and business case development to support strategic decision-making.
Business Partnership:
Collaborate with senior leadership and cross-functional stakeholders to evaluate performance, challenge assumptions, and provide actionable financial insights.
Process Improvement & Team Leadership:
Enhance FP&A processes, reporting standards, and forecasting accuracy while leading and developing a high-performing team.

SWIM will provide interested candidates with a detailed job description.

Who- the Candidate:

We are seeking a well-rounded senior-level FP&A professional with at least 10-15 years’ of progressive work experience, including around 5 years in people management. Canadian CPA designation and/or CFE will be viewed very favourably, as would MBA-Finance from a reputable University.
Qualified candidates will bring extensive experience leading financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, financial modelling, and management reporting functions, ideally within a large, complex, multi-site organization operating across Canada and the United States, and/or globally… i.e. $500M+ in revenues, 1000+ employees, and/or operations across multiple countries.
Experience within manufacturing, distribution, or other inventory-intensive industries
would be particularly relevant, given the organization's operational scale and complexity.

The successful candidate will demonstrate:

Proven experience leading enterprise-wide budgeting and forecasting processes, including cash flow forecasting, and improving financial planning accuracy and discipline.
Strong financial modelling capabilities, including long-range planning, scenario analysis, capital investment evaluations, and business case development.
Experience consolidating financial information across multiple business units, regions, and operating entities.
Confidence presenting financial insights and recommendations to senior executives and influencing strategic business decisions.
A demonstrated ability to lead, coach, and develop finance professionals while remaining comfortable working hands-on with complex financial analysis.
Strong proficiency with financial systems, including SAP or comparable ERP platforms, and enterprise planning, reporting, and performance management tools. Experience with OneStream, Tableau, or similar platforms is an asset.
Beyond technical expertise, the ideal candidate is analytical and a collaborative leader, with strong business acumen
who can balance enterprise-level strategic thinking with attention to financial detail. Strong communication, business judgment, critical thinking, and the ability to constructively challenge assumptions are essential.
We are seeking someone who can build credibility with senior stakeholders, navigate ambiguity, drive continuous improvement, and develop a strong, accountable FP&A team.

How Much:

Competitive base salary commensurate with level of skills, experience, and education, likely in the range of $170,000 to $190,000, possibly with some upwards flexibility for highly qualified candidates who have many/most of the “nice to haves.” The company will provide their new Director of FP&A with a solid overall compensation package, including a generous variable compensation program, professional development support, and excellent health, dental, & vision benefits.

Where:

Corporate office in the heart of downtown Vancouver, working from office 4-5 days/week to allow for plenty of in-person relationship building, presentations/meetings, and collaboration. It is anticipated that there will be around 5% business travel in this role (within Canada and US).

Deliver accurate, concise and action-oriented weekly, monthly and quarterly performance reporting and insight.

Analyse revenue, margin, cost, pipeline, backlog, wins, losses, utilisation and productivity to identify trends, risks, opportunities and corrective actions.
Provide scenario and option analysis, clearly setting out assumptions, sensitivities, trade-offs, risks and recommended actions.

Company Description
Endacho Healing Society (EHS) is an Indigenous-led organization advancing innovative approaches to trauma healing in the Northwest Territories. EHS is developing a culturally grounded healing program and a first-of-its-kind, bed-based Trauma Healing Lodge in the NWT. The Lodge will integrate Indigenous knowledge, land-based approaches, and Western therapeutic practices to support individuals and communities. EHS is focused on addressing a significant gap in services for people living with the impacts of residential schools and other forms of colonial trauma. Team members join a mission-driven environment committed to healing, cultural safety, and community wellness.

The Project Director is a 2-year full-time, role. The project is located in Yellowknife, but a remote/hybrid working location may be considered for the right candidate. Your work will span strategic planning, partnership development, funding, financial stewardship, and support to the Board of Directors. As part of a small, nimble organization, you will take an active role in both strategic leadership and the day to day activities that keep everything moving forward. Demonstrated experience working respectfully with Indigenous governments, organizations or communities, ideally in the North, and an understanding of colonial impacts, cultural safety and trauma-informed practice.

The Director of Enterprise Architecture is a strategic leadership role responsible for defining and advancing SE Health’s enterprise architecture vision. The Director leads enterprise-wide architecture decisions that drive agility, scalability, security, and measurable business outcomes. The Director ensures successful architecture and integration of platforms such as Alayacare and Workday, while driving adoption of best practices, standards, and governance across technology domains. jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
The Ontario Historical Society is seeking a new Executive Director, a unique and exciting opportunity to work with the diverse peoples of Ontario and make a significant contribution to the heritage sector in Canada.

What is the Ontario Historical Society?

Founded in 1888, The Ontario Historical Society (OHS) is a not-for-profit corporation and registered charity; a non-government group bringing together people of all ages, all walks of life and all cultural backgrounds interested in preserving some aspect of Ontario’s history.

The OHS is unique in its provincial mandate and very different to other provincial organizations. In 1899, the Legislative Assembly of Ontario granted OHS the legal power and responsibility to incorporate not-for-profit historical organizations. The Society is the only not-for-profit in North America with this legal tool to establish and incorporate other not-for-profit historical corporations.

The OHS is an inclusive, extensive membership-based organization, dedicated to working with all cultures, all religions and with Indigenous peoples. It is the largest organization of its kind in Canada that is growing through grassroots community engagement focused on the protection and promotion of Ontario’s history. 

The OHS headquarters is located at the historic John McKenzie House (built 1913) in Willowdale (Toronto), Ontario. John McKenzie House and its adjacent stable s and milk-house are all designated under the Ontario Heritage Act (1993). All buildings and adjacent properties (including Parkview Neighbourhood Garden) are subject to a heritage conservation easement (2013).

The OHS is governed by an all-volunteer board of directors. The Society is supported by and supports over 800+ member organizations and institutions located in communities across Ontario.

What does the OHS do?

●        Provides advice on all matters relating to good governance for historical not-for-profit corporations, including reviewing and revising constitutions and by-laws, surrendering charters, facilitating corporate name changes, consulting on the dissolution of assets, and supporting member applications for federal charitable tax status;
●        Oversees an insurance program at reduced cost to members in good standing;
●        Maintains corporate archives of all affiliated societies, which number over 335 not-for-profit organizations and growing;
●       Publishes in print and online the widely read peer-reviewed scholarly journal Ontario History (established 1899);
●        Provides consultations and other services to its affiliated societies and member organizations which includes, but is not limited to examining strategic directions, providing references for grant applications, consulting on heritage designations and conservation easements, and providing webinars and workshops on topics of heritage matters to both members and the broader heritage community;
●       Runs an awards program to honour individuals and organizations who have contributed significantly to the preservation and promotion of Ontario’s heritage;
●        Acts as an advocate in partnership with our member organizations, supporting the preservation and designation of heritage assets in local communities across the province;
●        Is the guardian of the public interest in regard to cemetery preservation in the province as it relates to The Funeral, Burial and Cremation Services Act, 2002 (FBCSA), formerly Cemeteries Act (Revised 1990). Compiles a detailed list of all unregistered cemeteries in Ontario as requested by the Government of Ontario; and
●        Maintains a reference library of over 5,600 books reflecting Ontario’s historical and cultural diversity.

Position Description:

The Executive Director reports to the Society’s board of directors and is charged with management roles, strategic leadership, and public advocacy that are needed to fulfill the unique mission and vision of the Society. In working to preserve, protect, and promote Ontario’s history and heritage, the Executive Director collaborates with the board of directors, with the Society membership, and with the affiliated societies, staff, and sector partners. The Executive Director is an effective leader, a trusted advisor and resource person, and a mentor to historical organizations throughout the province. The standard working hours for this position are 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday to Friday in office. Flexibility is required to accommodate evening and weekend commitments, as necessary. In order to fulfill and advance the Society’s mission, willingness to travel throughout Ontario is part of the role.

Role and Responsibilities:

●        Oversees the unique legal responsibilities of the Society and represents the interests of historical organizations throughout the province.
●       R esponsible for the overall administration and financial management of the Society.
●       Cultivates productive working relationships with all levels of government and embraces public visibility and advocacy roles and responsibilities.
●       Serves as the Society spokesperson to address the public, policy makers, partners, and the media.
●       Collaborates with members and stakeholders to enhance public support and financial resources for OHS and its affiliates.
●       Leads and facilitates philanthropic activities, donor relations, and funding opportunities.
●       Oversees the maintenance and operation of the historic John McKenzie House property.
●       Guides, supervises, and evaluates organizational operations and personnel, delegating authority as is deemed appropriate to other staff.
●       Mentors staff and volunteers, maintaining a positive, productive, and collaborative working environment.
●       Oversees strategic planning and evaluation (including the effectiveness of programs, services and communications), and central office operations.
●       The Society’s new strategic plan is focused on expanding capacity building programs, supports, resources, and events for its members. The Executive Director will lead the organization in building new partnerships and strengthening existing operations to advance this strategic direction. 
●       Ensures adherence to policies, procedures, and performance standards; ensuring the Society is fully compliant, accountable, and transparent in regard to federal, provincial, and municipal laws and regulations.

●       Supports the work of the Editor and Book Editor of the Society’s scholarly journal Ontario History

Required Qualifications:

Qualified applicants must have a bachelor’s degree, with a master’s degree strongly preferred, and a minimum of eight ( 8
) years of leadership experience in the not-for-profit sector. Experience in public policy development and a successful advocacy track record at the federal, provincial, or municipal level is required. A broad knowledge of the public benefits and roles that government and philanthropic support play in advancing positive impacts provincially is fundamental. A comprehensive understanding and sensitivity of the mandates, values, and environments in which the Society, its affiliates and members function.

Salary Range:

The expected compensation range for this role is $80,000 to $95,000
annually. Placement within the range will be based on demonstrated skills, and relevant experience.

How to Apply:

Qualified candidates should apply by submitting a cover letter and resume to the Chair of the Board and President of the Society, Dr. Jenna Kirker, at hr@ontariohistoricalsociety.ca
no later than 11:59 pm EST on Wednesday, December 23, 2026. Interviews will be scheduled for the second week of January. We thank everyone for their interest, but only those selected for an interview will be contacted. References will be requested at the time of the interview.

The Ontario Historical Society is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment and welcomes applications from all qualified individuals including women, racialized persons, Indigenous people, persons with disabilities and other equity-seeking groups. All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however, Canadian citizens and permanent residents will be given priority. This is in accordance with Canadian immigration requirements.

Residential and commercial mortgage lending represent a significant component of the institution’s business and balance sheet, making deep expertise in both areas essential to success in this role.

Reporting directly to the President & CEO, the successful candidate will provide strategic and operational leadership across mortgage origination, credit underwriting, portfolio management, risk oversight and product development. This individual will play a pivotal role in shaping the institution’s lending strategy, strengthening broker and referral relationships, enhancing operational effectiveness and ensuring a disciplined approach to sustainable portfolio growth, credit quality and risk management.

This is an opportunity for an accomplished lending executive with extensive knowledge of both residential and commercial mortgage lending, strong commercial acumen and sound credit judgment. Combining strategic vision with hands-on leadership, the successful candidate will be well positioned to lead a high-performing team, identify new market opportunities and contribute directly to the institution’s long-term growth and financial performance.

Location:
West end of the GTA
Work Arrangement:
On-site, five days per week

Senior Vice President

Strategic Leadership & Business Performance

Develop and execute the annual lending strategy, operating plan and budget in alignment with the institution’s broader business objectives.
Partner with the President & CEO and senior leadership team to establish lending priorities, growth targets and performance measures.
Monitor business performance, portfolio trends and budget variances, providing regular reporting, insights and recommendations to senior management.
Identify opportunities to expand lending activities, strengthen market positioning and improve operational efficiency.

Residential & Commercial Lending

Oversee residential and commercial mortgage lending, including origination, credit adjudication, underwriting, modifications, subordinations and ongoing portfolio administration.
Ensure lending decisions align with established credit policies, risk appetite, underwriting standards and business objectives.
Drive responsible portfolio growth while maintaining strong credit quality, effective arrears management and appropriate risk controls.
Strengthen origination channels and referral relationships, including mortgage brokers and other business partners, to support sustainable business development.

Credit Risk, Governance & Regulatory Compliance

Identify emerging credit and operational risks, assess portfolio performance and recommend appropriate mitigation strategies.
Ensure lending practices, processes and documentation adhere to applicable legislation, regulatory expectations and internal standards.
Provide senior management with insight into portfolio quality, arrears, credit trends and other key risk indicators.

Product Development & Market Strategy

Monitor residential and commercial lending markets, competitor offerings, pricing trends and evolving customer and broker needs.
Recommend and implement lending product enhancements, pricing strategies and new product initiatives that support competitiveness and profitability.
Identify opportunities to improve the lending experience, streamline processes and strengthen the institution’s value proposition.
Oversee the implementation of approved lending initiatives, ensuring effective communication, training and execution.

Operational Excellence & Technology

Oversee lending administration, systems and processes to support efficient, consistent and scalable operations.
Partner with technology and other internal stakeholders to identify system enhancements, improve workflows and support the implementation of approved initiatives.
Establish appropriate performance measures and reporting processes to monitor productivity, service levels, turnaround times and overall departmental effectiveness.

Leadership & Talent Development

Lead, mentor and develop a high-performing lending team across origination, underwriting and administration.
Establish clear performance expectations, departmental objectives and individual development plans.
Oversee recruitment, succession planning, employee development and performance management.
Foster a collaborative, accountable and service-oriented culture that supports business growth, sound credit practices and continuous improvement.

Business Development & Industry Engagement

Monitor business pipelines and lending activity to support current and future funding and portfolio objectives.
Represent the institution at relevant industry events, business development initiatives and promotional activities.
Identify emerging opportunities and market developments that may influence lending strategy and future growth.

Qualifications & Experience

Significant (15+ years) senior-level experience in residential and commercial mortgage lending, ideally within a bank, non-bank financial institution or other established lending organization.
A proven track record of leading lending operations, credit underwriting, portfolio management and business development.
Strong knowledge of mortgage credit adjudication, underwriting standards, lending policies, risk management and regulatory compliance.
Demonstrated ability to develop and execute lending strategies that balance portfolio growth, profitability, credit quality and risk.

jobs.description:
Salary: $120,000 - $170,000 per year.

Harlo Entertainment is a Toronto-based operator, management and private equity company, delivering value over 30 years of aggregate experience in both the hospitality and entertainment industry. With first-hand insights and perspectives, Harlo Entertainment defines best-in-class, luxury experience and is deeply committed to the highest level of guest satisfaction.  

We are a collection of diverse individuals with unique skill sets and subject matter expertise focused on building and scaling ventures. As a member of our team, you will have the opportunity to work across multiple high-profile, growing brands including Shake Shack Canada, Kasa Moto, MIMI Chinese, Sunnys Chinese, Linny's, The Playbook Commons, Valerie, Roses Social and more. Check out our website to learn more: www.harloentertainment.com  
We are a people-first culture. We strive to create great outcomes and establish win-win partnerships through integrity, reliability, inclusivity, and great communication. Our greatest asset is our people, as they are the powerhouses behind our outcomes. 

Role Overview
We are looking for a dynamic, creative and experienced Head of Communications and Marketing to be part of a growing team who will lead the marketing efforts across our portfolio of restaurant and hospitality brands. This role owns the full growth engine: brand and multi-channel marketing, strategic partnerships, SEO and digital presence, performance analytics, and PR. The ideal candidate uses data to decide where to invest, can lead cross-functional projects such as new openings and concept launches from idea to execution, and is measured on results: traffic, covers, revenue and brand strength.

Key Responsibilities
Marketing Strategy & Brand
Develop and own the marketing strategy and budget for each brand in the portfolio, tied to clear traffic, cover and revenue targets.
 Oversee the execution of marketing initiatives across all channels (digital, social, email/CRM, in-venue, partnerships and PR) and own the portfolio marketing calendar.
Direct content and creative across social, email and web, holding internal teams and creative partners accountable for quality and each brand's distinct voice.
Manage external partners (creative, PR, paid media, SEO), holding them to clear deliverables and KPIs.
Ensure all materials and activations follow established brand guidelines, and work with leadership to implement approved brand direction.
Maintain quality control across all guest-facing touchpoints and support the rollout of brand standards across new and existing locations.
Data, Digital & Performance
Build and maintain a marketing performance dashboard for each brand (traffic, reservations/covers, guest acquisition cost, ROAS, CRM, social and search) and report regularly to leadership.
Use guest, reservation, sales and campaign data to decide where to invest, what to test and what to stop, and set success metrics for every campaign, partnership and activation before launch.
Oversee SEO and digital presence across all brands (local search, Google Business Profiles, websites, booking paths and online reviews), holding partners accountable for results.	
Oversee paid media (search, social, display) and manage spend against ROI targets.
Develop guest segmentation and CRM programs that drive repeat visits and guest lifetime value.
Strategic Projects & Openings
Lead cross-functional projects from ideation through execution, including new openings, concept development and business initiatives.
Lead the marketing and launch plan for every new opening and concept.
Partner with leadership and operations teams to identify and prioritize high-impact opportunities.
Develop project plans, timelines and budgets, and ensure projects are delivered on time and to a high standard.
Act as a central point of coordination across departments to drive alignment and accountability.
Strategic Partnerships
Identify, develop and manage partnerships that drive brand awareness and business growth.
Negotiate and execute collaborations with aligned brands, media, creators and community partners.
Oversee partnership activations from concept through execution, ensuring strong ROI and brand alignment, and report on results.
PR & Communications
Set PR strategy that supports openings, launches and business milestones, and oversee PR partners in execution.
Build and maintain relationships with media, journalists and influencers, and serve as the primary point of contact for media inquiries.
Maintain crisis communication plans and manage issues response alongside leadership.
Keep internal teams informed and aligned on key initiatives, campaigns and launches.
Represent the portfolio at industry events, conferences and public forums.
Other duties as assigned.

What Success Looks Like in Year One
Within the first year, you will have built a clear marketing plan and KPI dashboard for every brand in the portfolio, delivered successful launches for new openings and concepts on time and on budget, grown traffic and covers through data-led campaigns and partnerships with measurable ROI, strengthened organic search and digital presence across all brands, and built a high-performing network of agency and media partners.

Skills and Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Public Relations, Communications, Journalism, Marketing or a related field (Master’s degree preferred).
7+ years of experience in public relations, with at least 3 years in a leadership role.
Proven track record of successful media relations and PR campaign execution.
Proven track record of executing successful digital and brand marketing campaigns. 
Strong copywriting, content planning, and creative direction skills. 
Proficiency in social media management tools and analytics platforms (e.g., Hootsuite, Buffer, Sprout Social, Google Analytics). 
Experience managing paid advertising campaigns across platforms (Google Ads, Meta, TikTok, etc.). 
Excellent communication, collaboration, and project management skills. 
Strong crisis management and problem-solving abilities.
Ability to build and maintain relationships with media and key stakeholders.
Experience in the food and beverage industry is a plus.
Strong interpersonal skills and ability to collaborate effectively with our portfolio teams, cross-functional departments, and stakeholders.  
Proficiency in PR analytics and tools

What we offer:
Competitive compensation, including comprehensive benefits, spending account and professional development program.
Opportunity to develop skills and gain experience in multiple disciplines in a fast-paced environment.
Dynamic and fun office culture with colleagues who share the same core values.
Exclusive perks from our portfolio companies.
Unlimited vacation policy. 

Harlo Entertainment is an equal opportunity employer.  
All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, creed, age, disability, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, gender expression, medical condition, genetic information, marital, military and veteran status.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer – Digital Assets & Capital Markets
jobs.description:
Salary: CAD $225,000 - $300,000 per year.

Chief Financial Officer – Digital Assets & Capital Markets 
 Company: Secure Digital Markets (SDM)
 Location: Toronto, Ontario
 Compensation: Target $225,000-$300,000 + performance bonus + equity participation
 Employment Type: Full-Time | Executive Leadership
 About Secure Digital Markets 
 Secure Digital Markets (SDM) is an institutional digital asset and financial services firm providing sophisticated clients with access to digital asset liquidity, execution, lending, and capital markets solutions.
 Operating at the intersection of cryptocurrency, institutional trading, and financial markets, SDM serves a global client base that demands speed, expertise, discretion, and institutional-grade execution.
 As we enter our next stage of growth, we are seeking a strategic Chief Financial Officer to strengthen our financial infrastructure, optimize capital deployment, and help drive long-term enterprise value.
 The Opportunity 
 This is not a traditional accounting-focused CFO position.
 We are seeking a commercially minded, capital-markets-oriented finance executive who understands how financial businesses create value and how capital can be strategically deployed to accelerate growth.
 Reporting to and partnering closely with the CEO, the CFO will oversee corporate finance, treasury, liquidity, capital allocation, financial reporting, investor relations, and strategic transactions.
 The successful candidate will bring sophisticated financial expertise, ideally gained within institutional digital assets, cryptocurrency trading, market making, exchanges, hedge funds, or related capital markets environments.
 Given SDM's international operations, the CFO must also understand the complexities of managing financial operations across Canada and the United States.
 This is an opportunity to shape financial strategy, influence major investment decisions, and build the financial foundation for SDM's next stage of growth.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Capital Strategy, Treasury & Investments
 Lead SDM's enterprise-wide treasury, liquidity, and capital allocation strategy.
 Optimize balance-sheet management, capital reserves, collateral utilization, and risk exposure across trading, lending, and investment activities.
 Evaluate capital deployment opportunities based on profitability, risk-adjusted returns, and long-term shareholder value.
 Oversee banking, custody, counterparty relationships, regulatory capital requirements, and financial oversight of fund and investment initiatives.
 Strategic Finance, Reporting & Performance 
 Develop financial models, budgets, forecasts, and scenario analyses to guide strategic decisions.
 Establish clear visibility into revenue, profitability, margins, and return on capital across business lines.
 Build scalable financial reporting systems, management dashboards, internal controls, and financial processes.
 Ensure accurate financial reporting and readiness for audits, regulatory reviews, and investor diligence.
 Partner with leadership to evaluate new products, investments, hiring decisions, and resource allocation.
 Cross-Border Finance & Regulatory Coordination 
 Oversee financial operations, reporting, and consolidated financial oversight across Canadian and U.S. entities.
 Manage cross-border financial considerations, including intercompany transactions, transfer pricing, taxation, and capital movement.
 Coordinate with legal, tax, compliance, and regulatory advisors to support effective corporate structures and regulatory compliance.
 Investor Relations & Capital Raising 
 Lead financial strategy and execution supporting investor relations, fundraising, and capital partnerships.
 Develop financial models, investor presentations, diligence materials, and a compelling financial narrative for institutional investors.
 Represent SDM in investor discussions, communicating financial performance, capital strategy, risk management, and growth opportunities.
 Strategic Transactions & Executive Partnership 
 Lead financial evaluation, due diligence, valuation, and structuring for acquisitions, investments, and strategic partnerships.
 Maintain institutional-quality financial information and transaction readiness.
 Serve as a trusted strategic partner to the CEO and shareholders, providing independent financial judgment and constructively challenging investment and operating decisions.
 Ideal Candidate & Qualifications 
 We are seeking an accomplished finance executive with 12+ years of progressive experience in financial leadership, treasury, or capital markets, including meaningful senior management responsibility.
 The ideal candidate will bring:
 Digital Assets & Capital Markets: Direct experience in institutional cryptocurrency, digital asset trading, market making, exchanges, hedge funds, brokerage, or sophisticated capital markets environments.
 Treasury & Capital Management: Strong expertise in liquidity management, capital allocation, balance-sheet risk, collateral management, and financial risk oversight.
 Cross-Border Financial Expertise: Demonstrated experience managing financial operations across Canada and the United States, including multi-entity reporting, taxation, and regulatory considerations.
 Strategic Financial Leadership: Proven ability to build financial models, forecasting frameworks, reporting infrastructure, and financial decision-making processes.
 Investor Relations & Transactions: Experience supporting institutional capital raises, investor communications, M&A, or strategic transactions.
 Executive Experience: Previous leadership as a CFO, Deputy CFO, Treasurer, Head of Finance, VP Finance, or comparable senior finance executive.
 Experience with institutional lending, investment funds, or structured financial products is highly desirable.
 CPA, CFA, MBA, or equivalent professional qualifications are beneficial but not required.
 Leadership Profile 
 The successful candidate combines financial rigor, commercial judgment, and an entrepreneurial mindset.
 You are analytical, intellectually independent, and comfortable challenging assumptions when financial evidence does not support a proposed strategy.
 You can communicate complex financial information clearly, build credibility with institutional investors, and work effectively alongside entrepreneurial founders and executive leadership.
 Above all, you take ownership. You establish accountability, make sound decisions under pressure, and turn financial analysis into meaningful business outcomes.
 Compensation 
 SDM offers a competitive executive compensation package based on experience and demonstrated results.
 Miami: CAD $225,000–$300,000 base salary*
 Annual Incentive: Performance-based bonus
 Long-Term Incentive: Equity / ESOP participation
 *Exceptional candidates may be considered outside the stated salary ranges. 
 Why Secure Digital Markets? 
 This is an opportunity to play a central role in shaping the future of an established institutional digital asset business.
 Rather than inheriting a mature finance organization, you will help determine how capital is allocated, how financial decisions are made, and how SDM scales its operations.
 Working directly with entrepreneurial leadership, you will influence strategic investments, strengthen institutional financial infrastructure, and help position the company for its next phase of growth.
 For the right executive, this is an opportunity to have a direct and measurable impact on enterprise value.

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Machine Learning Frameworks & Operations
jobs.description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients. 

 At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute. 

 To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com 

 Summary: 
 We are seeking a leader that can balance vision with execution to a newly formed enterprise MLOps team. The Director, Enterprise Machine Learning Frameworks & Operations will lead the design, development, and scaling of our enterprise-wide machine learning operations (MLOps) capability. This role is critical to establishing AI at scale, driving efficiency, reliability, and compliance across the model development lifecycle—from experimentation to production. 

 The ideal candidate combines deep technical expertise with strong stakeholder engagement and can execute on a strategic vision. You will contribute to the MLOps strategy, enforce strict adherence to enterprise governance, and lead the implementation of tooling and frameworks to enable secure, scalable, and repeatable AI/ML delivery across the bank. Success will be built on defining the technical activities to mature and standardize the capability and in driving a measurable impact to build influence with stakeholders. 

 What you’ll be doing 

 The Director, Enterprise Machine Learning Frameworks & Operations will lead the design, development, and scaling of enterprise-wide ML Operations (MLOps / LLMOps) capabilities. This role is pivotal in establishing AI at scale by driving operational efficiency, reliability, and compliance throughout the entire model development lifecycle (from experimentation to production deployment). You will shape the MLOps strategy and oversee the implementation of tooling, frameworks, and engineering standards that ensure secure, scalable, and repeatable delivery of AI/ML and LLM solutions across the bank. You will architect and build reusable platform capabilities, reference architectures, deployment patterns, and platform services that support both traditional machine learning and large language model use cases across multiple lines of business. Success will be measured by your ability to define and standardize technical activities, mature operational practices, and drive measurable business impact and stakeholder adoption. The ideal candidate possesses deep technical expertise in MLOps, hands-on engineering leadership, and strong stakeholder engagement skills to deliver on a strategic vision for enterprise-scale AI operations. 

 At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. You’ll have the flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you’ll spend 1–3 days per week on-site, while other days will be remote. 

 How you’ll succeed 
 Technical Leadership and Contribution -  Translate strategic capability roadmaps into actionable technical deliverables, including the design and implementation of CI/CD pipelines, end-to-end MLOps workflows, and automated ML pipelines for data ingestion, training, validation, and deployment. Ensure workflows are compliant with regulatory and enterprise governance requirements, including approval gates, automated monitoring and alerts, and audit-ready processes. Oversee the development of enterprise-grade, production-ready, and standardized MLOps capabilities to support scalable and reliable AI delivery across the organization. Set and communicate best practices and guidelines to ensure consistency and high-quality delivery. Drive the creation of reusable frameworks, platform services, engineering standards, and deployment patterns that accelerate AI delivery while reducing operational complexity and duplication across teams. 
 Stakeholder Management and Collaboration -  Build strong relationships and collaborate with business partners, technology teams, and cross-functional stakeholders to gather requirements, prioritize initiatives, and align MLOps solutions with business objectives. Partner with AI governance, Compliance, and technology teams to ensure all solutions adhere to regulatory and internal standards. Participate in code reviews, identify updates to and the need for new documentation, and share best practices. Stay current with emerging AI/ML tools and techniques, actively contributing to a culture of experimentation and continuous improvement. Advise on the MLOps strategy and capability roadmap based on stakeholder feedback and emerging needs. Act as the primary point of contact for business and technical stakeholders regarding MLOps delivery. 
 MLOps/ LLMOps Development and Production Deployments–  Lead the end to end model deployment pipeline management. Develop and sustain production-ready deployments (including support for APIs and open-source models). Oversee Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines. Partner with AI and Enterprise technology teams to ensure alignment on reusable technology components across all use cases, incorporating compliance requirements early to avoid delays, and maintaining lineage and version tracking. Assess models to prevent performance degradation and establishing monitoring frameworks to analyze inference latency, optimize token usage, and detect potential hallucinations in real time 
 People & Culture - Champion a culture of innovation, collaboration, and continuous learning within the MLOps team and across the enterprise. Upskill and mentor cross-functional teams on MLOps tools, frameworks, and best practices. Exhibit strong influencing, negotiation, and conflict resolution skills, with the ability to align diverse stakeholders around common goals. 

 Who you are 
 You can demonstrate 8+ years of experience in software engineering, platform engineering, data platforms, AI/ML engineering, or MLOps, with at least 2 years in a leadership role. Proven track record delivering scalable ML platforms in a highly regulated environment. It’s an asset if you have experience in financial services or other regulated industries. You have relevant knowledge and deep expertise with cloud-native architectures and technologies (e.g., Azure ML, Databricks, Kubernetes). Expertise with CI/CD, monitoring, model governance, and observability frameworks. 
 You have a degree in. Computer Science, Statistics, Engineering, or a related field. You have a strong software engineering and platform engineering foundation with experience building production-grade platforms, distributed systems, AI/ML services, developer platforms, or enterprise-scale automation frameworks. 
 Your influence makes a difference. You are comfortable operating as a hands-on technical leader who can balance strategic direction with deep technical discussions, architectural design, engineering trade-offs, and implementation guidance. 
 You’re driven by collective success. You have experience partnering with model risk, audit, and data governance teams. 
 You live your values.  You bring high standards, genuine care to your relationships, and want to grow with an employer that shares your values and brings out your best. 

 What CIBC Offers

jobs.description:
As AVP, Actuarial AI & Data Governance, you will lead the strategy, governance and enablement required to accelerate responsible adoption of AI and strengthen data capabilities across Actuarial.

 Reporting to the VP, Actuarial Innovation, you will partner with Actuarial leaders, enterprise AI and Data teams, Data Governance, Technology, Risk and other partners to establish and embed data governance, along with lead the shift from individual AI use cases to embedding AI and trusted data into core actuarial workflows and ways of working.

 You will lead the evolution of Actuarial data governance, establishing clear ownership and stewardship, strengthening data quality management, and creating greater transparency and accountability for the data that underpins critical actuarial processes. You will work across Actuarial and enterprise partners to ensure data issues are identified, prioritized and addressed, while aligning Actuarial practices with broader enterprise data standards and governance.

 You will also establish the frameworks and capabilities that enable Actuarial to innovate responsibly and at scale, including AI portfolio prioritization, citizen-led development, responsible AI governance, capability building and value realization. You will provide a trusted view of the Actuarial AI portfolio and help leaders determine where to invest, accelerate, scale, redirect or stop initiatives based on business value, feasibility and risk.

 The role will be instrumental in developing an AI- and data-enabled actuarial function, improving productivity, quality and speed of insight while strengthening the governance and accountability required to maintain trust in actuarial data and AI-enabled processes.

 Position Responsibilities 
 AI & Data Strategy and Transformation 
 Develop and execute the Actuarial AI and Data strategy, aligned with broader Actuarial priorities and enterprise AI, Data and Technology strategies.
 Partner with Actuarial leaders to identify and redesign priority workflows where AI, automation and better use of data can materially improve how actuarial work is performed.
 Establish a clear roadmap for AI and Data capability development, balancing near-term opportunities with longer-term transformation priorities.
 AI Portfolio Governance & Value Realization 
 Establish and evolve a transparent governance and prioritization framework for the Actuarial AI portfolio, including intake, assessment, prioritization, decision rights and pathways for delivery.
 Maintain a trusted view of the AI portfolio, including strategic alignment, expected value, delivery progress, dependencies, risks and realized outcomes.
 Lead structured portfolio reviews and provide recommendations on which opportunities should be accelerated, scaled, redirected, paused or stopped.
 Develop and maintain a value-realization framework with measurable baselines and outcomes,
 AI Enablement, Adoption & Capability Building 
 Build Actuarial AI literacy and capability through a structured learning, experimentation and adoption program.
 Partner with learning and talent teams to embed AI capabilities into broader Actuarial skill development. 
 Drive the transition from individual AI use cases toward repeatable capabilities and transformed workflows that can be adopted and scaled across the function.
 Data Governance & Data Capability 
 Define and evolve the data governance framework for Actuarial, aligned with enterprise policies, standards and controls.
 Establish clear data ownership and stewardship models for critical actuarial data, with explicit accountability for data quality and effective use.
 Develop practical mechanisms for identifying, logging, prioritizing and resolving material data-quality issues.
 Partner with enterprise Data, Technology and business teams to improve the accessibility, reliability and usability of data required by Actuarial.
 Provide governance and strategic direction without duplicating enterprise ownership of data platforms and technical infrastructure.
 Leadership & Stakeholder Engagement 
 Serve as a strategic advisor to senior Actuarial leaders on AI, data and emerging technology, translating complex topics into clear choices, implications and actions.
 Engage leaders to establish shared ownership of workflow transformation and measurable business outcomes
 Lead and develop a small, high-impact team and extend its reach through partnerships across Actuarial, enterprise AI, Data, Technology, HR/Learning and other functions.
 Communicate progress, outcomes, risks and strategic choices clearly to senior leadership.

 What we are looking for: 
 FSA/FCIA designation, or equivalent
 Deep understanding of actuarial processes, supported by hands-on experience across core actuarial workflows.
 Strong understanding of how AI, advanced analytics and modern data capabilities can be applied to knowledge-intensive business processes.
 Leadership and management skills, leading both direct and indirect teams
 Strong business acumen with an aptitude for strategic, critical, and analytical thinking
 Strong verbal and written communications skills
 Strong relationship management skills and ability to work within and across departments
 Understanding the needs of various stakeholders across the organization
 Ability to manage multiple projects of varying priorities levels and scope

 We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want.
 We’ll recognize and support you in a flexible environment where well-being and inclusion are more than just words.
 As part of our global team, we’ll support you in shaping the future you want to see.

jobs.title: Director of Sales
jobs.description:
Help enterprises put AI agents to work in customer experience. 
 Most enterprise support teams have spent years building on platforms they rely on every day. Those platforms hold their tickets, workflows, knowledge and customer history. What’s missing is AI that can actually do the work: resolve issues, take action across systems and hold up at enterprise scale.
 That’s what Botpress does. We’re the enterprise-grade AI agent platform for customer experience, backed by a $25 million Series B. Over 1 million AI agents run in production on Botpress, and more than 4,000 customers use the platform, including American Express and GE. We pioneered tool calling for AI agents and were the first to bring a commercial retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) offering to market. 
 We work alongside the systems our customers already use, integrating and partnering with them to make them work better.
 At Botpress, everyone is an owner, bringing their unique perspective and talents. We work fully in-office in Montreal. If you want to help build what comes next, we’d like to meet you.

 About the Role 
 We’re hiring a Director of Sales to lead our team of three account executives through a pivot into a more consultative, sales-led motion with mid-market and enterprise companies. You’ll report to our CRO and work closely together to find product-market fit in a new category, then build the team to scale it. This is a hands-on role: you’ll be in deals alongside your AEs at critical moments, and you’ll grow the team with us, with a seat in hiring from day one. The role is based in our Montreal office.
 Responsibilities 
 Lead and develop the sales team. Coach and lead our account executives as a hands-on leader, and grow the team with us. Set clear expectations and build a culture of curiosity, accountability and consistent execution.
 Own the forecast and pipeline. Run a weekly operating rhythm with rigorous forecasting, pipeline reviews and deal inspection in HubSpot. Translate our revenue goals into account priorities, pipeline targets and coverage, and drive the team to hit them.
 Guide complex deals from discovery to signature. Coach sellers through multi-stakeholder buying committees using MEDDPICC or a similar framework, and engage directly at critical moments. Bring in Solutions Engineering, security, legal and leadership for business cases, technical validation, pricing and negotiation.
 Turn pilots into contracts. Make sure each pilot has a clear scope, agreed success measures, a defined spend cap and terms that convert it to an annual contract. Help the team navigate budget timing, procurement and security reviews, and lead deal reviews that surface risk early and turn it into clear next steps.
 Help define product-market fit. Test what resonates with mid-market and enterprise buyers, read the signals in our pipeline, and tell us plainly what’s working and what isn’t. Bring market signals and customer feedback to Product and leadership to shape where Botpress goes next.
 Partner with outbound and Marketing. Work with our outbound team and Marketing on account segmentation, targeting, messaging and account-based plays. Give them regular, specific feedback on what converts so pipeline quality improves every month.
 Build a repeatable go-to-market motion. Turn what works into stages, playbooks, enablement and metrics the team can run without you in the room. Once product-market fit is established, build the hiring model and capacity plan: headcount, ramp and pipeline coverage.
 Lead an AI-native sales team. Embed AI into how the team researches accounts, develops outreach, prepares for calls, plans deals and forecasts. Model it yourself, share what works, and help sellers spend more time on judgment, strategy and customer relationships.
