jobs.title: Chief Marketing and Strategy Officer
jobs.description:
THE OPPORTUNITY

We have a dynamic opportunity for a Chief Marketing and Strategy Officer (CMSO) to join the Executive Leadership Team at Alberta Municipalities in Edmonton, Alberta. Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, the CMSO is the enterprise integrator for strategy, corporate planning and governance, strategic project management, growth and innovation, and marketing and communications. This is a great role for a leader that thrives in a fast paced and complex senior leadership role, managing multiple competing priorities, in an agile decision-making hub for member priorities. The corporate governance oversight and accountabilities associated with the role are significant and deep experience with Board governance is necessary for success.

The CMSO leads five direct reports: four Senior Directors, responsible for Corporate Planning and Governance, Project Management, Growth and Innovation, and Marketing and Communications, and a Project Coordinator/Executive Assistant. Working in a multifaceted environment, the CMSO makes sense of complex and emerging issues, frames them for decisions by the Chief Executive Officer, the Executive Leadership Team, Boards and Committees, and leads the plans, programs and projects that turn strategy into measurable results for members.

THE IDEAL CANDIDATE

The ideal candidate is a senior strategic leader who thrives in complexity, is a strong and effective communicator and has a deep background in corporate governance. The CMSO will turn ambiguous and competing information into clear strategy and plain language so that Boards, elected officials and executives can act on and set priorities across the organization aligning resources where they create the most value. They bring strong business and corporate service acumen along with a delivery focused mindset that can balance delegating vs perfection, and the judgement and diplomacy to advise on sensitive matters. They will also have the experience and background to effectively work with internal and external partners and stakeholders as well as elected officials and various levels of government.

As a true partner and a leader of people, the successful candidate brings strong emotional intelligence, integrity, a corporate services mindset, earns trust, and builds alignment through influence. They adjudicate objectively between competing views, support productive debate, contribute to dialogue constructively, lean into difficult conversations and step in directly when the team is stretched. They coach senior leaders, draw on the experience of the team, model the organization’s values, and strengthen a collaborative, accountable and high-performing culture, staying calm and fact based in a fast-moving, political environment. They also need to be passionate about the work of municipalities and the people they lead.

THE ORGANIZATION

Founded in 1905, Alberta Municipalities (ABmunis) is the province’s largest municipal association. It represents 264 of Alberta’s 334 municipalities, from small summer villages to major cities and specialized municipalities, which together are home to more than 85% of Albertans. It advocates on shared municipal issues and helps members build resilient communities. It also pools its members’ purchasing power to secure better pricing on employee benefits, insurance, energy and other services, with the proceeds helping fund its advocacy work. Its business services and its advocacy reinforce each other, and it works through partnerships to build common solutions with its members.

Governance

Alberta Municipalities is led by a Board of Directors elected by member municipalities during each annual convention. The Board is comprised of representatives from Alberta’s cities, towns, villages, summer villages, and specialized municipalities.

Additional information about Alberta Municipalities and key resources relevant to this opportunity are available below:
Alberta Municipalities website
2026 Advocacy Priorities
ABmunis Media Releases
ABmunis 2025 year in review

RESPONSIBILITIES

Strategic Leadership and Issues Management

Lead how the organization identifies, assesses and responds to complex and emerging issues, risks and opportunities, drawing on governance, member, advocacy, business, financial, operational, technology and reputational perspectives.
Distill ambiguous issues into clear problem statements, strategic choices and recommendations, and advise the Chief Executive Officer, the Executive Leadership Team and the Boards on significant and sensitive matters.
Develop frameworks, strategies and roadmaps with clear priorities, accountabilities and measures of success, and lead cross functional work on issues that span departments, entities or governance bodies.
Help develop advocacy strategies that advance member priorities with different levels of government and stakeholder groups, building alignment among people with different mandates and perspectives.

Corporate Planning and Governance

Provide executive leadership for governance across multiple (5) Boards, (9) committees and legal entities, respecting their distinct mandates and regulatory requirements, including agenda planning, decision support, appointments and the implementation of Board direction, and ensure Board and committee meetings are well run, with timely, high-quality materials.
Lead strategic planning and evaluation with the Chief Executive Officer, the Executive Leadership Team and the Boards, turning Board direction into organizational priorities, initiatives and performance measures.
Direct environmental scanning of political, economic, social, regulatory, member, market and technology trends, and advance governance effectiveness and Board development.
Oversee the corporate policy framework so policies are developed, reviewed, approved, communicated and applied consistently, in line with legislation and strategy, and oversee Board election processes, including Returning Officer responsibilities.

Strategy Execution and Program/Project Management

Lead the Project Management Office, setting the approach to prioritization, intake, governance, resourcing, risk and reporting, and the level of involvement based on an initiative’s complexity, risk and impact.
Oversee a portfolio of strategic and operational initiatives, including digital transformation (enterprise systems, data, CRM, automation), organizational and process transformation, governance initiatives, business growth, member programs, advocacy and public policy campaigns, and complex regulatory and compliance implementations.
Ensure major initiatives have clear objectives, scope, accountabilities, resources, timelines, risks and success measures before implementation, resolve competing priorities and capacity constraints with sponsors, and keep senior leaders and Boards informed of progress, risks and results.

Growth and Innovation

Lead the department that advances growth, innovation and sustainable revenue, strengthening existing business lines and developing new profitable ones through new markets, partnerships, customer segments, products, services and pricing.
Ensure opportunities are supported by market, financial, operational, governance, legal, tax and risk analysis, and turned into business cases and plans for the Executive Leadership Team and Boards that fit strategy, capacity and mandate.
Lead the adoption of artificial intelligence across the organization with sound governance, privacy, security, risk and change management and training, and watch for emerging technologies and business models that create member value.

Marketing and Communications

Provide strategic direction for marketing, brand, communications and major events, aligned with strategy, advocacy priorities, business objectives and member needs, with resources focused on the greatest value and a clear view of the return on major marketing spend.
Oversee major campaigns and events, including advertising, the annual Convention, advocacy and election campaigns, member engagement and brand initiatives, and guide internal communications so employees receive clear, timely and consistent information.
Translate complex organizational, policy and business issues into clear messages for members, elected officials, partners and other audiences.
Direct sensitive communications issues and media relations, shaping positioning and messaging with other executives to protect the organization’s reputation in a dynamic political environment.
Oversee marketing and brand strategy to strengthen awareness of Alberta Municipalities and its services and support the growth and positioning of its business lines.

Executive and People Leadership

Contribute to the leadership, direction and performance of the organization as a member of the Executive Leadership Team, and act on behalf of the Chief Executive Officer when assigned.
Coach the Senior Directors, set clear expectations and performance measures, and hold leaders accountable for results.
Build a collaborative, accountable and high performing culture that values member focus, strategic thinking, innovation and continuous improvement, and support strong relationships across departments, entities, Boards and committees.

QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum of 15 years of progressively senior experience in strategic planning, corporate governance, organizational strategy, program or project management, public administration or a similarly complex environment.
Significant experience leading enterprise strategic and corporate planning and delivering major cross functional programs and projects involving multiple departments, stakeholders and competing priorities.
Demonstrated experience working within complex governance and decision-making structures involving multiple Boards, committees, organizations or stakeholder groups.
Strong financial and business acumen, including assessing business cases, budgets, contracts, revenue opportunities, costs and risks.
Knowledge of governance practices, change management and innovation, with a strong understanding of economic, social, environmental, technological and political trends and their impact on members.
A degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Political Science, Strategic Management, Organizational Leadership or a related field.

Assets include
:
Master’s degree.
Project Management Professional (PMP), Prosci change management certification or related professional designation.
Experience in a government, municipal, association, regulatory, political or other multi stakeholder environment.
Executive oversight of corporate planning and governance, growth and innovation, a project management office, or marketing, communications, engagement, brand strategy and major events.

KEY COMPETENCIES

Sets long-term strategy with other leaders, owns strategic goals and plans, presents strong business cases for initiatives and resource allocation, and anticipates obstacles and business disruptions.
Analyzes ambiguous information, applies frameworks where there is little precedent, seeks diverse views and makes sound decisions with organization wide consequences.
Delivers clear strategic messages at the enterprise level, explains complex issues in plain language to senior executives and gains buy in and consensus from people with widely different views.
Builds alliances inside and outside the organization and uses a deep understanding of their network to connect people in ways that create value.
Sets performance goals and metrics, approves budgets and investments in line with financial goals, holds leaders accountable and pushes the organization to higher standards.
Anticipates member needs and builds service into goals, programs, products and processes, and fosters a service orientation across the management team.
Breaks down silos and builds an inclusive, consultative culture of collaboration across departments, entities and partners, taking ownership of team and organizational outcomes.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer & Vice President, Administrative Services
jobs.description:
Saskatchewan Polytechnic is the province’s only polytechnic and its primary institution for post-secondary applied education and research. Proudly situated in the homeland of the Métis people and on Treaty 4 and Treaty 6 Territory, Saskatchewan Polytechnic serves more than 26,000 learners across its campuses in Moose Jaw, Prince Albert, Regina, and Saskatoon.

Saskatchewan Polytechnic is a dynamic, future-focused institution offering more than 150 programs that power careers and strengthen communities. Through various credentials, program partnerships, and learning pathways, Saskatchewan Polytechnic opens meaningful opportunities for every learner. Its accomplished and innovative faculty lead programs and applied research deeply connected to industry, ensuring graduates are job ready and in demand. As a proud member of Polytechnics Canada, the institution champions a student-centred and industry-responsive model of education that drives innovation, fuels economic growth, and shapes the workforce of tomorrow.

The Chief Financial Officer & Vice President, Administrative Services provides strategic financial leadership and operational vision that will shape the organization's trajectory for years to come. This pivotal role provides enterprise-wide leadership to ensure the institution’s long-term financial stability, operational resilience, and capacity to invest strategically in academic excellence, innovation and growth. Working in close partnership with executive leadership, the CFO & VP, Administrative Services translates financial insight into strategic action, informing major decisions and supporting key growth initiatives. This role integrates disciplined financial management with strategic investment, revenue diversification, infrastructure optimization, and prudent financial risk leadership. This role leads a diverse portfolio encompassing financial services, human resources, facility services, strategy, communications marketing and retail services, and information technology services, integrating these functions into a cohesive, high-performing operation that enables staff and programs to excel. The successful incumbent will champion a culture of accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement across all administrative functions.

The ideal candidate is a strategic, results-oriented finance executive with a track record of leading complex financial and administrative functions within multi-faceted organizations. Along with a CPA, they bring deep expertise in financial management, including budgeting, forecasting, audit, and risk mitigation, paired with strong business acumen and the ability to translate financial insight into forward-looking strategy. As a proven leader, the successful candidate has built and developed high-performing teams, fostered cross-functional collaboration, and guided organizations through periods of change. They are a confident, polished communicator capable of engaging and influencing senior stakeholders, including boards and executive teams, and are recognized for sound judgment and accountability. Highly organized and adaptable, they bring a continuous improvement mindset and an unwavering commitment to operational excellence, innovation, and service delivery across the organization.

To Apply

To fill this position, Saskatchewan Polytechnic has partnered with leadership advisory firm Odgers. Applications are encouraged immediately and should be submitted online at https://careers.odgers.com/en-ca/31264.

We would like to thank all applicants but regret that we are only able to personally contact those individuals whose backgrounds best match the requirements for the role.

Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion

Saskatchewan Polytechnic considers the diversity of our workforce to be one our leading strengths and greatest assets. Our employee diversity enhances our ability to meet the needs of an increasingly diverse student population. Currently, approximately 10% of our students are Indigenous. A continued emphasis on the development of a representative workforce is one of Sask Polytech's strategic priorities and, as an organization, we are making significant efforts to attract and retain Indigenous employees.

Saskatchewan Polytechnic is an equal opportunity employer. English Description Follows

À propos du rôle (sommaire du poste) :

McKesson Canada est à la recherche d’un(e) directeur(trice) principal(e), Stratégie commerciale et partenariats stratégique et axé(e) sur les résultats pour stimuler la croissance des revenus, l’acquisition de nouveaux clients et le développement de partenariats stratégiques au sein de notre portefeuille Santé spécialisée.

Relevant de la haute direction, vous dirigerez une équipe de développement des affaires hautement performante responsable d’accroître notre part de marché, de repérer de nouvelles occasions commerciales et de renforcer les relations au sein de l’écosystème des soins de santé. Ce rôle combine leadership stratégique, exécution des ventes et collaboration interfonctionnelle afin de soutenir une croissance durable et de consolider la position de McKesson comme chef de file des solutions de santé spécialisée.

Ce que vous ferez (responsabilités) :

Élaborer et mettre en œuvre la stratégie de développement des affaires et de ventes pour le secteur Santé spécialisée afin d’atteindre les objectifs de croissance des revenus et d’expansion du marché.
Assumer la responsabilité du budget de développement des affaires de Santé spécialisée, des prévisions de ventes et de la performance du pipeline commercial.
Stimuler la croissance de nouvelles affaires en repérant, évaluant et sécurisant des partenariats stratégiques ainsi que de nouvelles occasions auprès de la clientèle.
Soutenir et accompagner les membres de l’équipe lors des rencontres avec les clients, de l’élaboration de solutions, des présentations et des négociations.
Assurer un suivi de la santé du pipeline, de la performance des ventes, de l’exactitude des prévisions et des indicateurs d’engagement de la clientèle.
Élaborer des analyses de rentabilité, des modèles financiers et des propositions commerciales afin de soutenir les occasions de croissance.
Analyser les tendances du marché des soins de santé, les renseignements concurrentiels et les connaissances client afin d’orienter la prise de décisions stratiques.
Collaborer avec les équipes du marketing, des opérations, des finances, des produits et d’autres partenaires interfonctionnels afin d’offrir des solutions centrées sur les besoins de la clientèle.
Établir et maintenir des relations de niveau exécutif avec des clients clés, des partenaires et d’autres parties prenantes de l’industrie.
Assurer l’excellence des interactions avec la clientèle, de la préparation des propositions et des présentations destinées à la haute direction.
Tirer parti de l’expertise de spécialistes internes afin de proposer des solutions novatrices favorisant l’atteinte des objectifs de la clientèle et de l’entreprise.

Exigences de base :

Baccalauréat en administration des affaires ou dans un domaine connexe, ou expérience professionnelle équivalente.
Plus de 15 ans d’expérience démontrée en vente et/ou en marketing, avec un historique constant d’atteinte et de dépassement des objectifs d’affaires dans l’industrie des soins de santé.
Expérience au sein de l’industrie pharmaceutique (médicaments d’origine, génériques ou biosimilaires) ou dans le secteur des soins de santé spécialisés.
Historique éprouvé d’atteinte et de dépassement des objectifs de ventes, de revenus et de croissance.
Succès démontré dans l’élaboration et l’exécution de plans stratégiques de développement des affaires.
Expérience dans la gestion de cycles de vente complexes et de relations avec une clientèle de niveau entreprise.
Excellentes aptitudes en communication, en présentation et en gestion des parties prenantes.
Expérience au sein d’organisations matricielles et dans la direction d’initiatives interfonctionnelles.
Forte présence exécutive et capacité à influencer les dirigeant(e)s et décideur(euse)s du secteur des soins de santé.
Expertise en négociation contractuelle et en développement de partenariats stratégiques.

Compétences et expérience privilégiées :

Expérience dans la direction d’équipes de vente importantes, performantes et réparties sur plusieurs territoires.
Solide sens des affaires et excellente maîtrise des aspects financiers, notamment en matière de prévisions, de budgétisation, d’élaboration d’analyses de rentabilité et d’évaluation du rendement des investissements (ROI).

Le/la titulaire de ce poste aura à soutenir de façon quotidienne des clients internes et/ou externes à l’extérieur du Québec et/ou aux États-Unis. Par conséquent, ce poste requiert une maîtrise de l’anglais à l’écrit et à l’oral. Veuillez noter que le nombre de postes dont les tâches requièrent une connaissance de la langue anglaise a été restreint dans la mesure du possible.

About the Role (Job Summary):

McKesson Canada is seeking a strategic and results-oriented Sr. Director, Commercial Strategy & Partnerships to lead revenue growth, new client acquisition, and strategic partnerships across our Specialty Health portfolio.

Reporting into senior leadership, you will lead a high-performing business development team responsible for expanding market share, identifying new commercial opportunities, and strengthening relationships across the healthcare ecosystem. This role combines strategic leadership, sales execution, and cross-functional collaboration to drive sustainable growth and reinforce McKesson's position as a leader in specialty healthcare solutions.

What You'll Do (Responsibilities):

Develop and execute the Specialty Health business development and sales strategy to achieve revenue growth and market expansion objectives.
Own the Specialty Health business development budget, sales forecast, and pipeline performance.
Drive new business growth by identifying, evaluating, and securing strategic partnerships and customer opportunities.
Support and coach team members in customer meetings, solution development, presentations, and negotiations.

Collaborate with Marketing, Operations, Finance, Product, and other cross-functional partners to deliver customer-focused solutions.
Build and maintain executive-level relationships with key customers, partners, and industry stakeholders.
Ensure excellence in customer interactions, proposal development, and executive presentations.

Basic Requirements:

Experience within the pharmaceutical industry (brand, generic, or biosimilar) or within the Specialty space.
Proven track record of achieving and exceeding sales, revenue, and growth objectives.
Demonstrated success developing and executing strategic business development plans.
Experience managing complex sales cycles and enterprise-level customer relationships.
Exceptional communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.
Experience working within matrixed organizations and leading cross-functional initiatives.
Strong executive presence with the ability to influence senior healthcare leaders and decision-makers.
Expertise in contract negotiations and strategic partnership development.

Preferred Skills/Experience:

Experience leading large, geographically dispersed, high-performing sales teams.
Strong financial acumen, including forecasting, budgeting, business case development, and ROI analysis.

The incumbent of this position will provide daily support to internal and/or external clients outside Quebec and/or in the United States. est à la recherche d’un(e) Directeur(trice), Gouvernance des données
stratégique et expérimenté(e) pour diriger les programmes de gouvernance des données à l’échelle de l’entreprise afin d’améliorer la qualité des données, la conformité réglementaire, la confiance des parties prenantes et l’excellence opérationnelle. Cette personne définira et mettra en œuvre des stratégies de gouvernance couvrant la gouvernance des données, la gestion des métadonnées, le catalogage des données, la qualité des données, la gestion des données maîtres (MDM) et les capacités de traçabilité des données (data lineage).

Le ou la titulaire collaborera étroitement avec les équipes d’affaires, technologiques, de gestion des risques, de conformité et de données afin d’établir des cadres de gouvernance, des normes, des politiques et des contrôles soutenant la prise de décisions fondée sur les données et le respect des exigences réglementaires. Ce rôle requiert une solide combinaison de leadership, d’influence, d’expertise en gestion des données et d’engagement des parties prenantes au sein d’un environnement organisationnel complexe.

Ce que vous ferez

Diriger la stratégie de gouvernance des données à l’échelle de l’entreprise, y compris le modèle opérationnel, les politiques, les normes et les mécanismes de contrôle.
Favoriser l’adoption et l’optimisation des plateformes de gouvernance et de catalogage des données.
Établir et superviser les programmes de qualité des données, de gestion des métadonnées, de gestion des données maîtres et de traçabilité des données.
Collaborer avec les équipes des Risques, de la Conformité, de la Protection de la vie privée, de la Sécurité et de l’Audit afin d’assurer la conformité réglementaire et la maturité des pratiques de gouvernance.
Développer des indicateurs de gouvernance, des KPI de santé des données et des rapports destinés à la haute direction.
Travailler avec les parties prenantes de l’entreprise pour définir la propriété des données, l’intendance (data stewardship), la reddition de comptes et les priorités de gouvernance.
Diriger des équipes multidisciplinaires responsables d’initiatives d’envergure en gouvernance et en gestion des données.
Recruter, développer et mobiliser des équipes performantes en favorisant une culture de responsabilité, de collaboration et d’amélioration continue.

Exigences de base

Plus de 12 ans d’expérience professionnelle en gouvernance des données, gestion des données, architecture des données, analytique, conformité ou dans un domaine connexe, dont au moins 4 ans d’expérience en gestion d’équipes.
Baccalauréat ou expérience professionnelle équivalente.
Expérience dans la direction de programmes et de modèles opérationnels de gouvernance des données à l’échelle de l’entreprise.
Expérience dans l’implantation ou la gestion de plateformes de catalogage, de gestion des métadonnées ou de gouvernance des données.
Expérience en gestion de la qualité des données, traçabilité des données, intendance des données et contrôles de gouvernance.
Expérience de collaboration avec des équipes de conformité, de gestion des risques, de protection de la vie privée, d’audit ou de réglementation.
Capacité démontrée à diriger des initiatives transversales et à influencer des parties prenantes de haut niveau.
Expérience dans l’élaboration de politiques, de normes, de KPI et de cadres de reddition de comptes en matière de gouvernance.

Compétences et expérience privilégiées

Maîtrise en gestion de l’information, informatique, administration des affaires, analytique des données ou dans un domaine connexe.
Expérience dans des secteurs réglementés tels que les soins de santé, les produits pharmaceutiques, les services financiers ou l’assurance.
Connaissance de plateformes de gouvernance des données telles que Collibra, Alation, Informatica, Microsoft Purview ou des outils similaires.
Expérience avec les principes DAMA-DMBOK et les cadres de gestion des données d’entreprise.
Connaissance des règlements en matière de protection des données, des mécanismes de gouvernance et des cadres de gestion des risques.
Expérience à diriger des initiatives de transformation des données à l’échelle de l’entreprise.
Excellentes compétences en communication auprès des dirigeants et en gestion du changement organisationnel.
Certifications pertinentes en gouvernance des données, gestion des données, protection de la vie privée ou technologies infonuagiques.

Déplacements, environnement de travail et exigences physiques

Capacité à voyager jusqu’à 20 % du temps, selon les besoins de l’entreprise.
Modalités de travail hybrides ou à distance pouvant être offertes selon les besoins de l’entreprise et la situation géographique.
Capacité à participer à des réunions virtuelles et en personne et à travailler efficacement dans un environnement soutenu par la technologie.

jobs.title: Associate Director, Compliance
jobs.description:
Purpose Unlimited
is an independent financial services company with an unrelenting focus on customer-centric innovation, delivered through technology-driven solutions. Led by entrepreneur Som Seif, the company is developing a diversified product platform aimed at addressing historically underserved segments of the market. Purpose Unlimited’s businesses include Purpose Investments, Advisor Solutions by Purpose, and Driven.

Who is Steadyhand?

Steadyhand Investment Funds Inc.'s
mission is to help Canadians build their wealth through a better, more human experience.

Vacancy Status:
This is for a current opening.

Compensation:
$145,000 - $165,000

Job Description

Who You Are

The Associate Director, Compliance is the operational leader of SIFI’s Compliance function and is accountable for the day-to-day management, execution and continuous enhancement of the compliance program for its CIRO-regulated mutual fund dealer activities. The role translates the compliance risk assessment and annual plan into effective monitoring, testing, reporting, remediation and regulatory support.

Reporting to the Chief Compliance Officer (CCO), the Associate Director provides technical leadership, provides day to day management of Compliance resources, establishes program standards and quality controls, and escalates material, complex or unresolved matters. The role maintains independent second-line challenge while partnering constructively with the Branch Manager, Operations and other business functions.

Steadyhand Investment Funds Inc. (SIFI) is seeking an Associate Director, Compliance to help lead and continuously enhance its compliance program.

Reporting to the Chief Compliance Officer, this role serves as the operational leader of the Compliance function and manages the day-to-day compliance program for a CIRO-regulated mutual fund dealer. The Associate Director provides leadership across monitoring and testing, branch reviews, registrations, complaints, governance reporting, regulatory examinations, policy management and regulatory change implementation.

The successful candidate will combine technical compliance expertise with people leadership, program management and practical business partnership. This role offers meaningful responsibility and a potential development path toward future Chief Compliance Officer responsibilities.

ROLE BOUNDARY -
This is a second-line compliance leadership role. Day-to-day supervision of Approved Persons, new-account approvals, trade reviews and suitability decisions remain with the Branch Manager role. The Associate Director assesses whether supervisory systems are operating effectively and does not replace first-line supervision.

Responsibilities: What You Will Do/ What You Will Own

Compliance program leadership

Lead the day-to-day operation of the firm’s compliance program and manage execution of the annual compliance plan.
Maintain the compliance risk assessment, compliance calendar and risk-based testing framework.
Establish monitoring methodologies, documentation standards, quality controls and escalation protocols.
Prioritize resources and continually enhance the effectiveness, efficiency and scalability of the compliance function.

Monitoring and testing oversight

Design and oversee risk-based monitoring and testing of compliance and supervisory controls.
Design and oversee risk-based reviews of Operations processes and related controls for compliance, including money and securities movement, books-and-records activities, client reporting and reconciliations.
Review testing results, trends, recurring deficiencies and emerging risks.
Challenge supervisory effectiveness and oversee remediation plans and validation testing.
Escalate material findings, high-risk matters and unresolved issues to the CCO.

Branch review program management

Approve the annual review schedule, risk-based scope and testing approach.
Review and approve branch review reports and assess the significance of findings.
Monitor management responses, remediation commitments and overdue actions.
Ensure branch review coverage remains appropriate as the business evolves.

Registration, licensing and continuing education oversight

Oversee registration, licensing, NRD administration, onboarding and termination activities.
Review complex registration matters, restrictions and outside activity disclosures.
Oversee the continuing education, proficiency, annual training and attestation programs.
Ensure registration and proficiency records remain complete, accurate and regulator-ready.

Complaints, investigations and regulatory reporting

Oversee complaint handling, investigations, resolution recommendations and regulatory event assessments.
Review required regulatory notifications, filings and reporting submissions.
Ensure matters are handled consistently, fairly and within applicable requirements.
Escalate material complaints, reportable events and significant conduct concerns to the CCO.

Regulatory examinations and reviews

Lead operational preparation for CIRO examinations, regulatory reviews, audits and information requests.
Coordinate document production, response drafting, examination logistics and internal stakeholders.
Oversee deficiency responses, remediation plans and progress reporting.
Support the CCO in regulator interactions and on material examination matters.

Regulatory change, policies and training

Monitor regulatory developments and conduct impact assessments and gap analyses.
Coordinate implementation of regulatory changes across policies, procedures, controls and business practices.
Maintain compliance policies, guidance and communications and oversee the annual policy review cycle.
Develop and deliver practical training and awareness initiatives.

Governance and reporting

Prepare clear, decision-useful compliance reporting for senior management and governance forums.
Develop dashboards, metrics and key risk indicators and maintain issue and remediation tracking.
Assist the CCO with annual compliance reporting and other governance materials.
Ensure significant matters are escalated on a timely basis.

Team leadership and development

Manage and develop Compliance Officer(s) and future compliance resources.
Establish clear goals, priorities, performance expectations and quality standards.
Review work product and provide coaching, feedback and mentorship.
Build team capability, accountability and succession depth.

Strategic advisory and broader regulatory support

Advise business leaders on regulatory requirements, compliance risks and practical controls for new initiatives and operational changes.
Provide oversight and guidance across AML, privacy, FATCA/CRS, CASL, marketing and communications, conflicts of interest, personal trading, outside activities, registered plans and estate-related controls.
Act as a constructive and pragmatic business partner while maintaining independent compliance judgment and effective challenge.

Financial planning compliance oversight

Lead the development and ongoing maintenance of the compliance framework supporting the firm’s financial planning offering.
Establish compliance standards for the approved service scope, permitted activities, planner titles and credentials, jurisdictional requirements, client disclosures, fees, conflicts, referrals, privacy and record keeping.
Design risk-based monitoring and testing of financial planning activity, including plan-file reviews, supervision evidence, implementation consistency and remediation.
Oversee controls for planner proficiency, training, continuing education and authorization and assess provincial title-protection requirements as the service expands across jurisdictions.
Assess whether planning information is appropriately reconciled to dealer KYC and whether resulting investment recommendations and actions are consistent with KYP, costs, available alternatives and suitability obligations.
Provide compliance oversight of planning tools, methodologies, assumptions, templates, marketing materials and client communications.
Analyze findings and complaints, identify trends or systemic issues, challenge first-line supervision and escalate material matters to the CCO.
Advise on the compliance implications of new planning services, technology, specialist referrals and changes to the delivery model.

Decision rights and escalation expectations

May establish monitoring and testing methodologies, documentation standards, quality controls and escalation protocols consistent with the approved compliance framework.
May assign and prioritize Compliance resources, review and approve routine work product, and require management responses and remediation evidence.
May close routine findings where satisfactory evidence has been obtained and closure is within delegated authority.
Must escalate material non-compliance, actual or potential client harm, systemic or repeat deficiencies, overdue high-risk remediation, potential reportable events, significant conduct concerns and matters requiring CCO or legal judgment.
Does not replace Branch Management’s first-line supervision, make decisions reserved to the CCO, or commit the firm to a regulatory position unless expressly authorized.

Expected work products and records

Compliance risk assessment, annual plan and compliance calendar

jobs.title: Director of Finance - Mining
jobs.description:
The Opportunity:

ML6 is partnering with a publicly traded mining organization to identify a Director of Finance to join its growing leadership team.

This individual will play a critical role in overseeing the company's financial reporting, technical accounting, regulatory compliance and internal control environment across its Canadian and international operations.

Reporting directly to the Chief Financial Officer, the Director of Finance will lead the financial reporting function, oversee external audits and ensure the integrity of consolidated financial statements and regulatory disclosures. The position will also provide financial leadership across international subsidiaries, supporting the complexities of operating within a global mining and mineral processing business.

This is an excellent opportunity for a technically strong accounting leader who combines public company reporting experience with a hands-on approach to financial management. The successful candidate will be comfortable navigating complex IFRS matters, working directly with external auditors and providing guidance to operational teams, while also identifying opportunities to strengthen processes, improve reporting capabilities and develop the finance function.

What You'll Be Doing:

Oversee the preparation and delivery of consolidated quarterly and annual financial statements, management discussion and analysis (MD&A), and other required public company disclosures.
Manage financial reporting and statutory accounting requirements across international subsidiaries, ensuring compliance with local regulations and consistency with corporate reporting standards.
Maintain oversight of IFRS accounting practices and Canadian reporting requirements, evaluating new accounting standards and determining their impact on the business.
Lead the annual external audit process, coordinating with audit firms, managing documentation requirements, addressing technical accounting questions and ensuring timely completion of audit deliverables.
Establish and maintain effective accounting policies, procedures and internal controls to support financial accuracy, regulatory compliance and risk management.
Deliver financial reporting, analysis and insights to the CFO, executive leadership and Board of Directors to support business planning, strategic initiatives and corporate decision-making.
Oversee cash flow forecasting, banking relationships, intercompany transactions, payment processes and broader treasury activities across the organization.
Partner with internal stakeholders on accounting considerations related to corporate transactions, acquisitions, divestitures and other complex business activities.
Lead and develop the finance team, establishing clear expectations, building technical capabilities and fostering a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.
Identify opportunities to improve financial reporting processes, automate manual activities and strengthen the effectiveness of accounting systems and controls.
Act as a subject matter resource for accounting and financial reporting matters, providing guidance to finance and operational teams across multiple jurisdictions.

What You'll Need to Be Successful:

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance or a related discipline.
CPA designation is required.
Minimum of 5 years of public accounting experience, specifically auditing mining companies.
At least 5 years of progressive experience in financial reporting and accounting leadership roles, ideally within a publicly traded mining or resource-based organization.
Strong background overseeing consolidated financial statements, MD&A and regulatory filings for publicly listed companies.
Demonstrated experience managing external audits and maintaining effective relationships with external audit firms.
Experience overseeing financial reporting across international subsidiaries and navigating multiple regulatory and accounting environments.
Advanced technical knowledge of IFRS and Canadian financial reporting requirements.
Strong understanding of TSX listing requirements, Canadian securities regulations and public company disclosure obligations.
Experience developing accounting policies, strengthening internal controls and improving financial reporting processes.
Advanced Microsoft Excel capabilities and experience with ERP and financial reporting systems.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex accounting matters to executive leadership and operational stakeholders.

Compensation Range:
$190,000 - $210,000 base salary + bonus

jobs.description:
About us

 Qualio is a unified quality and compliance management platform that helps regulated organizations get products to market faster with reduced risk. Trusted by biopharma, medtech, and diagnostics companies worldwide, Qualio eliminates fragmented systems that create audit delays and compliance blind spots. Our platform enables audit readiness in weeks through multi-standard automated gap analysis and evidence reuse across ISO and FDA requirements. Qualio is ISO 27001, ISO 9001, and ISO 27701 certified, reflecting our commitment to security, quality, and privacy.

 The Qualio team is all-remote, and currently distributed across North America, Europe and Australia.

 What's the opportunity?

 At Qualio, the people we hire shape how life science companies bring safer products to market. As Talent Acquisition Director, you’ll own recruiting end to end and build something we’ve never had: an in-house executive search capability that replaces our reliance on outside firms. You’ll partner directly with our CEO and senior leadership team to land the Director, VP and C-level leaders who will define Qualio’s next chapter, and you’ll set the standard for how we hire at every level.

 This is an individual contributor role with real influence, reporting to the VP Finance. 

You'll redesign and automate the recruiting process end to end, mapping workflows and using AI, rather than running a traditional, manual, relationship-driven function. Build and scale recruiting operations, not just manage existing systems, while keeping people involved where judgment and respect matter most, such as interviews and executive recruiting. The right candidate naturally challenges conventional hiring habits and puts efficiency and AI-assisted recruiting first.

You won’t manage a team, but you’ll be the person leadership turns to when a critical hire can’t miss. You’ll work closely with a Europe-based recruiter who also supports People Ops, splitting the load strategically and building practices together. We’re small enough that your impact is immediately visible, and collaborative enough that you won’t be figuring it out alone.

 What will I be doing?

 Apply AI where it demonstrably improves efficiency or hiring quality.

 Lead role kickoffs, scorecards, sourcing, interviews, debriefs, offers and onboarding handoffs.

 Personally source, assess and close Director+, VP and C-level talent.

 Run weekly hiring priorities, monthly metrics and quarterly quality-of-hire reviews.

 Own Greenhouse hygiene, templates, interviewer training and shared documentation standards.

 Maintain critical-role target lists and continuous sourcing/referral programs.

 Protect the hiring bar and provide a candidate experience that wins people with competing options.

 What skills do I need?

 10+ years in talent acquisition, with 5+ focus in executive search/hiring.

 Proven direct sourcing and closing of VP/C-level hires without dependence on retained search.

 Experience building recruiting processes, administering an ATS and using funnel metrics; Greenhouse experience is a plus.

 Hiring experience across North America and Europe, with awareness of differing employment norms.

 Strong structured interviewing, analytical skills, executive communication and stakeholder influence.

 Active, demonstrable use of AI in recruiting workflows.

 Self-directed and effective in a remote, fast-changing, cross-time-zone environment.

 A plus: experience recruiting in life sciences, regulated industries or SaaS for regulated customers.

 Benefits

 The opportunity in helping life-saving products get to market faster

 Medical coverage (with premiums for our most popular plan fully covered for you and your eligible dependents)

 Dental and Vision coverage

 Dependent Care & Health FSA, HSA, Short/Long Term Disability, Basic & Voluntary Life Insurance

 Studies have shown that women and people of color are less likely to apply for jobs unless they believe they meet every single one of the qualifications as described in a job description. jobs.description:

Whether the job entails interacting with our customers, driving digital growth, or providing vital behind-the-scenes support, we’re all here for the same reason – to roll up our sleeves and create happiness through cooking and sharing good food.

Sur La Table is seeking a Director, Ecommerce and Marketing Analytics
to define how data, insight, and AI drive decision-making across the company.

This role serves as the analytical hub of the organization
, supporting eCommerce, Marketing, Finance, Retail, Merchandising, Inventory Planning, and Operations. While embedded within the eCommerce organization, the mandate of this role is company-wide: to transform data into insight, insight into implications, and implications into clear recommendations that drive action.

This is not a reporting role. It is a foundational leadership role responsible for establishing analytical standards, governing AI-enabled workflows, ensuring data integrity, and elevating how decisions are made across the business.

This position will report into the Senior Director of Ecommerce.

What you get to do:

Company-Wide Insight Leadership

Serve as the primary analytics leader across eCommerce, Marketing, Finance, Retail, Merchandising, Inventory Planning, and Operations.
Own problem definition for analytics - determining which business questions matter and what decisions insights should inform.
Move analysis beyond “what happened” to “why it happened,” “how it happened,” and “what we should do next.”
Proactively mine data to identify risks, opportunities, inefficiencies, and performance drivers.
Influence senior leaders through clear implications and actionable recommendations.

Establish validation frameworks to pressure-test AI-generated outputs against source data, historical performance, customer behavior, and commercial logic.

You will own the end-to-end marketing measurement process for major client accounts, from assessing data quality and building analytical models to presenting findings and guiding investment decisions. You will combine technical execution, client communication, and cross-functional collaboration to establish measurement practices that continuously improve over time.

 Assess client CRM, tracking, and marketing data to determine what can be measured immediately, what requires further development, and which data issues must be addressed first.

 Define the most meaningful business outcomes for each model, selecting measurable funnel stages with sufficient and consistent volume in collaboration with client operations teams.

 Direct tracking and CRM implementation improvements, including conversion tracking, UTM and click ID capture, lead source fields, lifecycle stage definitions, and system integrations.

 Validate implementation changes and ensure data quality before incorporating information into measurement models.

 Manage inconsistencies in historical data, including changes in definitions, broken tracking, and missing or undated events.

 Build and continuously refine Bayesian marketing mix models using tools such as Google Meridian, including prior selection, calibration, diagnostics, and back-testing.

 Translate model outputs into practical budget allocation scenarios, accounting for diminishing returns and channel constraints.

 Design and manage quarterly incrementality experiments suited to B2B environments, including target-account holdouts, geographic splits, budget increases, and platform lift studies.

 Conduct power analysis, establish break-even thresholds, and agree on decision rules before experiments begin.

 Evaluate experiment results objectively, including inconclusive findings, and use them to improve model accuracy and narrow forecast ranges over time.

 Collaborate with data, machine learning, and platform engineers to integrate measurement methodologies into client-facing products and workflows.

 Use AI tools and agents to improve analytical efficiency while independently validating outputs and protecting client information.

 Develop and present monthly Revenue Narratives with account directors, explaining performance, model findings, and recommended investment decisions in language accessible to marketing leaders and finance executives.

 Present quarterly experiment findings and coordinate future testing roadmaps with channel teams.

 Clearly communicate the limitations of available data and models, avoiding unsupported conclusions or misleading claims.

 Document analytical decisions, assumptions, and trade-offs while maintaining rigorous quality standards for all client-facing deliverables.

 Support new business and account expansion by explaining measurement capabilities and helping account and channel teams apply marketing science effectively.

 Requirements: 

 You bring substantial experience in marketing science, analytics, or data science, with a proven ability to turn sophisticated measurement into business decisions. You are comfortable building models independently, working with complex B2B data, and communicating analytical findings to senior stakeholders. You combine strong technical expertise with sound judgment, curiosity, and the ability to manage several client engagements simultaneously.

 Significant professional experience in marketing science, analytics, or data science within an agency, consultancy, or growth-focused organization.

 Demonstrated ownership of measurement initiatives that have directly influenced marketing budgets or business decisions.

 Hands-on experience building and maintaining marketing mix models using Google Meridian, Robyn, PyMC-Marketing, or comparable frameworks.

 Practical experience designing, analyzing, and interpreting incrementality experiments, including statistical power analysis and predefined decision criteria.

 Experience measuring B2B marketing outcomes using CRM platforms such as Salesforce or HubSpot, particularly in environments with long sales cycles and low weekly conversion volumes.

 Experience directing tracking and CRM implementation projects and ensuring the reliability of marketing data.

 Some experience mentoring colleagues, managing a small team, or directing specialist contributors.

 Strong proficiency in Python and SQL, with experience working with weekly data from advertising platforms, CRM systems, and web analytics tools.

 Familiarity with data and cloud infrastructure such as BigQuery, dbt, Amazon SageMaker, or Google Vertex AI is an advantage.

 Working knowledge of web tracking and CRM technologies, including Google Tag Manager, Google Analytics 4, server-side tracking, Salesforce, and HubSpot.

 An AI-forward mindset, with regular use of AI tools and agents, the ability to independently assess their outputs, and an interest in identifying new applications for these technologies.

 Ability to transform complex datasets into clear deliverables that influence client or executive decisions.

 Strong understanding of full-funnel performance and marketing investment across channels, rather than focusing on isolated campaign metrics.

 Excellent storytelling and communication skills, including the confidence to explain when available evidence cannot support a requested conclusion.

 Strong analytical judgment, curiosity, and the ability to challenge assumptions constructively.

 Excellent organizational skills and the ability to oversee measurement activities across multiple client accounts.

 Annual base salary ranging from CAD 110,000 to CAD 140,000, with potential eligibility for a bonus. Actual compensation depends on relevant skills, experience, and qualifications.

 Fully remote working arrangement from a home office in Canada.

 Medical, dental, and vision insurance, along with disability and life insurance coverage for employees and their families.

 Employer-paid insurance coverage for employees, with a 50% employer contribution toward dependent coverage.

 Access to certified therapists through Spring Health and a Headspace membership.

 Physical well-being resources, including physical therapy through Omada and virtual workouts through Aaptiv.

 Complimentary One Medical membership for primary and virtual care.

 Unlimited paid time off, with a two-week minimum, in addition to paid company holidays.

 Birthday leave and an end-of-year company recharge period from December 24 to January 1.

 Paid parental leave.

 Traditional and Roth 401(k) retirement plans with a 3% company match.

 Annual bonus opportunities that increase over time based on tenure.

 Annual company-wide retreat.

 A remote-first and inclusive work environment that supports professional development, collaboration, and individual well-being.

jobs.description:
Job Description 

 What is the opportunity?   
 At RBC Insurance, AI is fundamental to transforming how we operate, serve our customers, and compete in a rapidly evolving financial services landscape. To realize this opportunity, we need a visionary leader who can simultaneously architect and enable enterprise AI capabilities, modernize and enhance our data platforms, and transform our legacy integration infrastructure into a nimble, scalable foundation.
 As Senior Director, AI and Data & Integration Platforms, you will own the strategy and end-to-end delivery across all three domains. You'll be responsible for building the intelligent, data-driven foundation that enables RBC Insurance to unlock AI-driven intelligence to enhance customer experiences, and fundamentally transform our business model. This is your opportunity to lead one of the most consequential technology transformations in our organization's history.

 What will you do?   

 Own enterprise AI strategy and delivery: Develop and execute the long-term vision for AI capabilities across RBC Insurance IT and business operations. Identify frontier, game-changing AI use cases that drive competitive advantage, serve as the expert for emerging AI technologies, and position RBC Insurance as an AI-first organization.
 Architect and modernize data platforms: Lead the strategic transformation of our global data foundation, stabilizing and enhancing both on-premises and cloud data platforms. Build a scalable, secure, resilient data architecture that serves as the foundation for AI, analytics, and business intelligence. Ensure data governance, quality, and accessibility across the enterprise while optimizing cost and performance.
 Transform legacy integration platforms: Champion the modernization of our integration infrastructure, moving from legacy systems to API-first, event-driven architectures. Design integration platforms that enable seamless data flow, real-time decision-making, and agile business capability delivery.
 Drive strategy into delivery at scale: Translate strategic vision into executable roadmaps and quarterly milestones. Lead end-to-end execution of transformational initiatives spanning AI implementation, data platform migration, and integration modernization. Establish accountability for delivery excellence, quality, and measurable business outcomes.
 Build and lead high-performing teams: Provide strategic leadership to data architects, AI engineers, integration specialists, and technical teams. Foster a high-performance culture of innovation, collaboration, and continuous learning. Coach technical leaders on strategic thinking, delivery excellence, and career development. Build a team of thought leaders who stay at the forefront of AI, data, and integration technologies.
 Build strategic partnerships and stakeholder alignment: Serve as the trusted delivery partner to business leaders, IT executives, and technology teams. Cultivate strong relationships across Technology, Digital Channels, Business Operations, and Product teams. Align organizational priorities, remove obstacles, and drive speed to impact through collaborative leadership..
 Champion continuous learning: Cultivate a team of technical thought leaders who stay at the forefront of industry trends, emerging technologies, and digital platform best practices, ensuring RBC Insurance maintains competitive advantage and drives innovation across digital channels.

 What do you need to succeed? 
 Must Have 
 10+ years of progressive leadership in AI, data, and/or technology transformation, with 5+ years leading technical teams delivering enterprise-scale IT solutions. Demonstrated track record of executing transformational business strategy and delivering measurable organizational impact.
 Deep expertise in artificial intelligence and machine learning: Proven experience architecting, implementing, and scaling AI solutions in production environments. Strong understanding of GenAI and Agentic AI applications across business operations, including predictive analytics, automation, and intelligent decision-making. Ability to translate AI capabilities into business value and organizational efficiencies.
 Expert-level data platform leadership: Extensive experience designing, building, and modernizing enterprise data platforms (data lakes, data warehouses, cloud platforms). Proficiency with both legacy and modern data technologies. Strong foundation in data governance, quality, integration, and analytics.
 Integration platform and modernization expertise: Experience leading the transformation of legacy integration infrastructure to modern architectures. Deep understanding of API-first design, event-driven systems, and hybrid technology ecosystems
 Enterprise delivery and execution excellence: Demonstrated ability to lead complex, multi-year transformational programs at enterprise scale within financial institutions or regulated industries. Strong foundation in software development lifecycle, budgeting, resource allocation, and delivery governance.
 Executive leadership and stakeholder influence: Exceptional ability to lead diverse technical teams and influence senior stakeholders through data-driven decision-making, compelling communication, and strategic facilitation. Strong executive presence and ability to operate at the C-level.

 Nice to Have   
 Prior experience in financial services or regulated industries, with deep understanding of compliance, risk management, and enterprise governance frameworks.
 Hands-on experience with specific AI/ML platforms (e.g., cloud AI services, Agentic AI, LLMs, GenAI, MCP, etc), modern data platforms (e.g., Databricks, Snowflake), and integration technologies (e.g. Apache Kafka, APIGee, event streaming, etc).
 Experience in leading AI adoption and scaling development practices. Established and/or Chaired AI Centers of Excellence that drove organizational AI adoption.
 Experience leading successful data modernization programs on multi-platform hybrid environments in large enterprises.

 What’s in it for you?   
 We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

The Role We are seeking a Head of PCI DSS Advisory to lead OBRYN GUARD’s PCI DSS and payment-security advisory function.

You will work closely with our Head of Security, Engineering, Product, QA, Solutions and Leadership teams to ensure OBRYN GUARD’s PCI-related workflows are technically accurate, operationally practical and appropriately positioned as readiness and advisory support.

jobs.title: Director, Integrated Planning & Procurement
jobs.description:
Reporting to

President & COO

Direct Reports

4 direct reports; approximately 8 team members in total

Purpose

The Director, Integrated Planning & Procurement is accountable for translating commercial demand into reliable material, procurement, production and inventory plans. This leader owns Select Foods’ end-to-end planning operating system, including demand planning, materials planning, procurement, production planning, inventory control, S&OP and the business ownership of SAGE MRP.

This is a hands-on executive leadership role in a lean, growing organization. The successful candidate must be equally comfortable developing long-term supply-chain strategy, leading an Executive S&OP discussion, coaching managers and personally working through an MRP implementation, supplier shortage, inventory imbalance or production-planning issue when required.

Responsibilities

Own and Lead S&OP
: Own, chair and continuously improve the monthly S&OP cycle: Demand Review, Supply and Capacity Review, Procurement and Materials Review, Integrated Reconciliation and Executive S&OP.

Establish one credible production plan, document assumptions and risks, and ensure unresolved service, capacity, inventory, cost and supply decisions are escalated to the Enterprise Leadership Team.

Connect volume plans to financial commitments, working-capital expectations and operating priorities.

Maintain clear meeting charters, calendars, inputs, decision rights, actions and follow-up disciplines.

Demand Planning:
Establish a disciplined demand planning process in partnership with Sales and Finance.

Create and maintain the unconstrained demand plan, incorporating baseline demand, customer intelligence, promotions, new business, losses and one-time events.

Monitor forecast accuracy and bias at useful product and customer levels; lead root-cause actions where performance falls outside agreed tolerances.

Challenge assumptions constructively and ensure demand changes are translated into supply, materials, capacity and inventory implications.

Materials Planning and SAGE MRP:
Act as the business owner of SAGE MRP and ensure it produces trusted, actionable recommendations.

Own planning policies and parameters, including lead times, safety stocks, order quantities, minimums, planning horizons, yields, scrap factors and make/buy settings.

Ensure BOM, master data, supplier and inventory data are sufficiently accurate to support reliable planning.

Lead root-cause correction to shortages rather than relying on manual workarounds.

Develop team capability and standard work for running, interpreting and maintaining MRP.

Production and Capacity Planning:
Convert the agreed demand plan into feasible medium-term capacity plans and executable production schedules.

Balance service, labour, equipment capacity, changeovers, material availability, shelf life, cost and inventory.

Establish planning time horizons, schedule change rules and a clear handoff from planning to operations.

Lead recovery plans when demand, supply or capacity deviates from plan.

Procurement and Supplier Performance:
Lead procurement strategy and execution for raw materials, packaging and other assigned categories.

Improve material availability, supplier reliability, lead times, commercial terms and supply resilience.

Implement supplier scorecards, regular performance reviews, risk mitigation and structured escalation.

Ensure purchasing decisions reflect total cost, minimum order quantities, working capital, service risk and quality requirements.

Inventory Strategy and Control:
Develop differentiated inventory strategies for make-to-stock and make-to-order products, raw materials, WIP and finished goods.

Segment items using demand variability, lead time, service expectations, shelf life, margin, MOQ, production frequency and supply risk.

Establish safety-stock, reorder, lot-sizing and coverage policies with clear ownership and review frequency.

Lead initiatives to reduce excess, obsolete and slow-moving inventory while protecting customer service and production continuity.

Manage overage, obsolete materials cost effectively including charge backs to customer as appropriate.

Partner with Finance and Operations to improve inventory accuracy, governance and working-capital performance.

Warehouse Operations and Carrier Management:
Oversee warehouse operations ensuring safe, efficient and compliant practices.

Align warehouse capacity, labour and processes with the production plan, customer service requirements and inventory policies.

Monitor warehouse and carrier performance through clear KPIs, regular reviews and corrective actions.

Lead carrier strategy and negotiate carrier contracts, rates and service terms to balance cost, reliability and customer commitments.

People and Functional Leadership:
Lead four direct reports and an overall team of approximately 8 across planning, procurement, warehouse and inventory control.

Set clear accountabilities, decision rights, standard work and performance expectations.

Coach managers and planners to solve problems independently while remaining close enough to the work to identify weak processes, data or controls.

Build succession, cross-training and technical capability across demand planning, supply planning, MRP, procurement and inventory.

Strategy and Continuous Improvement:
Develop and execute a multi-year roadmap for planning maturity, inventory, sourcing, capacity, systems and team capability.

Lead practical improvement initiatives that deliver measurable benefits in service, schedule adherence, inventory, supplier performance, cost and productivity.

Contribute to enterprise decisions bringing an integrated commercial, operational and financial perspective.

Translate strategy into clear priorities, owners, milestones and sustained operating routines.

Qualifications

10+ years of progressive leadership experience across supply chain planning in a manufacturing environment, with direct exposure to demand, materials and production planning.

Post-secondary degree in supply chain, operations, business, engineering or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.

APICS / ASCM CPIM or CSCP, SCMP, Lean Six Sigma or comparable professional development is an asset.

Demonstrated ownership or leadership of S&OP / IBP processes and cross-functional decision making.

Strong practical command of MRP logic, planning parameters, master data and exception management; experience with SAGE is preferred, while transferable ERP/MRP expertise is essential.

Experience developing inventory policies for both make-to-stock and make-to-order products.

Meaningful procurement and supplier-management experience, including performance, risk and commercial trade-offs.

Proven ability to lead managers and technical teams while remaining personally effective in detailed operational problem solving.

Ability to translate data into clear decisions for Sales, Finance, Operations and Leadership.

Strong change leadership, communication, analytical judgment and execution discipline.

Leadership Profile

Strategic and practical: sees the long-term system while understanding today’s details.

Enterprise-minded: optimizes the total business rather than one function.

Data-driven and decisive: converts imperfect information into clear, timely choices.

Coach and operator: develops people without becoming disconnected from the work.

Constructively challenging: tests assumptions and surfaces risks early.

Accountable and resilient: follows through and leads calmly through shortages, changes and competing priorities.

jobs.description:
HSB Canada, part of Munich Re, is Canada's premier engineering-driven specialty insurer and provider of inspection, engineering and technology services that set the standard for excellence in the market. Our constantly evolving offerings lead the market in cyber, equipment breakdown, renewable energy, technology services, engineering based risk management and inspection services. We bring technical expertise to help our clients stay ahead of complex, emerging and technology-based risks. We dare to think big and we are continuously innovating on behalf of our clients. We recognize Diversity, Inclusion, and Belonging as key priorities and a culture that welcomes different thoughts and opinions.

HSB is much more! It’s insurance. Engineering. Technology. To learn more about us, please visit www.hsb.ca

Primary Objectives

Director, Product Innovation acts as a strategic catalyst and internal innovation & strategy consultant—turning market signals, data, and emerging risks into new insurance products/coverages and tech-enabled risk solutions/services for Canada. This leadership position carries enterprise-wide responsibilities and direct visibility to the CEO and Executive Leadership Team, with work that significantly influences the organization’s growth and innovation agenda.

This role reports to the VP, Strategy & Innovation and sits within the Senior Leadership Team, with high visibility to the CEO and Executive Leadership Team, and will have 1–2 direct reports (Product Innovation Strategists. This role will be integral in shaping our bold 2030 ambition by accelerating innovation outcomes, strengthening innovation governance, and launching 1–2 new products to market.

Job Responsibilities

Enterprise product innovation strategy & pipeline
Build and maintain an enterprise innovation roadmap across multiple lines, translating strategy into a prioritized portfolio of product and service opportunities.
Lead structured market and customer discovery—synthesizing broker/customer insights, competitor intelligence, market research, and emerging risk trends into clear product hypotheses and recommendations.
Develop executive-ready business cases and investment recommendations, managing research and insights budget.
IoT Solution Strategy
Define the IoT solution strategy for Canada: priority use-cases, target segments, value proposition, required data/telemetry, and partner ecosystem.
Shape bundled offerings that combine insurance with technology and value-add services (prevention, monitoring, response), in line with HSB’s broader IoT and technology-enabled risk approach.
Incubation Operating Model
Run a hypothesis-driven “test & learn” approach—designing low-risk experiments to validate desirability, viability, and feasibility before scaling.
Build and own a repeatable incubation playbook (problem framing → customer discovery → prototype/P&L → underwriting/claims/legal review → pilot → launch), reinforcing speed with discipline.
Innovation Governance & Decision Velocity
Steward and continuously improve the established innovation governance process—intake criteria, prioritization, stage gates, and transparent decision documentation—to drive throughput and quality.
Establish meaningful metrics and dashboards for pipeline health, launch progress, and measurable outcomes.
End-to-End Product Launch
Lead cross-functional delivery of 1–2 new products per year from concept to launch: coverage design/wording, underwriting appetite, pricing approach, operational readiness, and go-to-market enablement. Define product KPIs and performance monitoring plans and translate insights into iteration post-launch.
Product Mechanics: Rigor & Credibility
Partner with Underwriting, Actuarial, Claims, Legal/Compliance, and Technology to ensure new and evolving products are implementable, governed, and aligned with underwriting intent and risk appetite.
Bring structured thinking to profitability and sustainability—supporting segmentation, rate adequacy discussions, and portfolio insights as needed.
Executive Advisory & Stakeholder Influence
Serve as a trusted advisor to senior leaders—framing decisions, facilitating alignment, and telling a clear story from data to recommendation. Manage complex senior stakeholder dynamics across the business and with global partners, ensuring strong alignment and decision velocity.
Leading, coaching, and developing team of Product Innovation Strategists
Establishing team operating rhythms and removing delivery blockers

Qualifications

University-level education in finance, business administration, economics, risk management, or equivalent professional experience; MBA or equivalent graduate degree an asset
8–12 years demonstrated experience in strategy, innovation, or product roles; insurance or broader financial services
Structured, hypothesis-driven problem solving: ability to frame ambiguity, develop options, assess trade-offs, and drive to clear decisions.
Strong analytical capability: extracting insights from data and market research and translate them into strategy and action.
Multi-workstream leadership: proven ability to manage multiple initiatives in parallel while maintaining quality, pace, and stakeholder alignment.
People leadership experience (formal or informal): ability to coach talent, delegate effectively, and drive accountability in a small, high-performing team.
Executive communication: ability to produce crisp, compelling materials and present complex topics simply and persuasively to senior audiences.
Strong P&C insurance (or broader financial services) product knowledge—coverage/wordings, underwriting appetite, pricing fundamentals, and regulatory considerations is an asset
Prior strategy consulting experience (e.g., strategy consulting Engagement Manager/Senior Manager level) or equivalent internal strategy/innovation consulting experience is an asset
Experience building ecosystems/partnerships (vendors, data providers, technology partners) to enable product and service innovation is an asset

Together, we engage with everything we have and are, to help humankind act braver and better. Go further with HSB.

An engaging and collaborative environment that promotes continuous learning and development

jobs.title: VP of Performance Marketing (Remote, Calgary)
jobs.description:
Blacksmith Agency

Marketing
Full time
Remote (USA, Canada or South Africa)

About The Role

Blacksmith Agency runs PPC and SEO for clients across multifamily, B2B and technical verticals. As VP of Performance Marketing you lead that department. The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist report to you and they are the specialists in their channels. Right now nobody owns this function, which is the whole reason this seat is open.

This is a management seat, not a senior individual contributor one.
You will not be building campaigns, and on technical SEO your strategist will know more than you do. That is the arrangement, not a gap. You carry channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale. The strategists carry the execution of it, and you carry whether the department delivers.

What You Own

The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist: their quality bar, their development, their reviews, and the call when someone is not going to get there.
The standard the work is held to. What a good audit looks like, what gets checked before work leaves the agency, how an account is reported. You write it and you hold two specialists to it.
Client results across the whole function, including whether our reporting is honest. Nobody here is auditing attribution and GA4 accuracy today.
The escalation when an account is at risk. You diagnose it, you direct the strategist who fixes it, and you are on the call with the client.
Channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale.
What we tell sales we can credibly deliver, before it gets sold.
The hiring plan for the department, and first-round interviews for your own team, within about a quarter.

What You Need

Strategists or specialists who have reported to you, where their reviews, their development and the decision when someone was not working out were yours. Managing accounts is not this.
7+ years across paid media and SEO. Owning one channel while sitting beside the other does not count here.
Enough depth in Google Ads, GA4, Search Console, Meta and Microsoft Ads to tell good work from work that merely looks good. That is a lower bar than doing it and a higher bar than reading a report.
One account you turned around that you can talk through: the metric, the figure before, the figure after, and why the change worked. Whose hands were on the keyboard matters far less than whether the diagnosis was yours.
Comfortable being the client-facing owner when an account is underperforming. That call comes to you, not to the strategist.
Agency experience carrying many accounts at once.

Please do not apply if

Nobody has ever reported to you, or you have never owned someone's review or had to performance-manage anyone.
You have only ever run one channel.
All of your experience is in-house on a single brand.
What you actually want is to keep building campaigns yourself. That is not a lesser ambition, it is a different job, and this is not it.

None of these are preferences we bend on. They are how we screen, so applying anyway costs you an hour and gets you a no.

Process

Three conversations, then a decision. A thirty minute screen with our recruiter, a first round with the founder this seat reports to, and a final. No take-home project and no panel interview.

How To Apply

Four fields at the link, then a short 6 minute Predictive Index assessment. Use the same email throughout. No cover letter.

Sales

Remote (USA or Canada)

No direct reports. This is an individual contributor seat going after strategic, multi-location accounts: large companies you open and close yourself.
