jobs.title: Director, Executive Compensation & Board Advisory Consulting
jobs.description:
Description

Are you an experienced, technically adept Canadian tax or accounting practitioner who wants to broaden their focus and solve high-impact challenges for companies of all sizes and levels of complexity? Are you looking to apply your hard-earned technical skills to a new field, move into management consulting and join a multi-disciplinary team of high-performing professionals advising many of Canada’s leading companies?

As a Director in our Executive Compensation and Board Advisory (ECBA) practice, you will bring your expertise in Canadian tax and accounting to collaborate with some of the industry’s top consultants and provide first class executive compensation support and innovative solutions to our client. In return, you will develop deep and cutting-edge technical knowledge and skills in executive compensation. You will be a go-to resource for our Canadian and broader North American teams on Canadian tax and accounting issues that impact executive compensation, manage consulting projects and provide input to senior colleagues while overseeing and quality-reviewing junior staff’s work. You will learn compensation consulting skills and technical knowledge from some of Canada’s leading practitioners, working on engagements that range from the routine to the exceptional, but all of which serve to create a key link between company performance and executive pay. As you learn, you will graduate to serve as project lead on projects of smaller scope within this role.

The scope of our projects will range from those focused solely on executive compensation and board and committee effectiveness, (e.g., rewards strategy, competitive compensation analyses, annual and long-term incentive program design, pay-for-performance analyses, shareholder engagement strategy and preparation) to those involving other lines of business such as M&A due diligence and integration, total rewards strategy design and optimization assessments. Client engagements will typically be with the relevant committee(s) of the Board, senior management, or both.

You will also participate in and contribute to activities that support continued revenue growth of the Work & Rewards line of business and WTW overall. These activities may include supporting local, regional and/or national marketing events, performing industry/topical research and developing intellectual capital, and participating in our firm’s industry and/or topical teams.

Note: Employment-based non-immigrant visa sponsorship and/or assistance is not offered for this specific job opportunity.

The Role

While every day and assignments are somewhat different, some of your main responsibilities will include:

Delivering effective, consistent project management for multiple, marquee clients.

WTW does not provide tax or accounting advice to clients, but our work rests on a clear and accurate understanding of tax, accounting and other regulatory frameworks. You will be pivotal in providing accurate, authoritative advice and guidance to our consulting teams on Canadian tax and accounting issues that arise in relation to executive compensation matters
Using your technical skills to support the design of innovative solutions to client compensation challenges, with a particular emphasis on long-term incentive plans including various equity-based incentives
Drafting statements of work, project plans and budgets involving multiple workflow streams and client teams.
Serving as the day-to-day project lead, ensuring progress of the team against established objectives, budget, timeline, deliverables and quality standards.
Leveraging to and managing the work of junior staff, providing coaching and on-going feedback.
Operating as the key contact to clients on delivery of services; managing client expectations and raise appropriate issues to Senior Consultants.
Collaborating and contributing to the development, design and implementation of compensation programs that include total rewards strategy, competitive benchmarking, annual and long-term incentive plan design, employment contract review, change-in-control agreements, overall competitive pay analysis and pay-for-performance alignment.
Contributing to the development of new tools and approaches.
Supporting the generation of new business as part of the broader team by:
Assisting with new business development activities.
Participating in discovery discussions with prospects and developing / delivering proposals.
Establishing collaborative relationships with clients to understand their business and issues to better inform our consulting and to expand WTW’s relationship into new service areas.
Contributing to the external visibility of WTW’s brand through intellectual capital generation, drafting articles, and attending and speaking at relevant conferences.

Qualifications

The Requirements

A minimum of 7 years of tax and / or accounting experience in an established corporate advisory firm, and a genuine interest in broadening your skills in management consulting and executive compensation.
A strong technical knowledge and understanding of applicable tax and accounting requirements – regulatory and legal expertise would be advantageous.
Experience advising on the tax and accounting implications of annual, equity, stock and other long- and short-term incentive programs is desirable.
Creative, analytical and results-driven orientation, demonstrated through the ability to draw conclusions, themes, and trends from data analysis and communicate results effectively.
Proven experience successfully managing multiple, multi-faceted projects and producing quality deliverables on time and within budget.
An executive presence with polished and well-developed communication skills, including experience making presentations and “sell” ideas to colleagues and management.
Self-starter attitude and ability to work within ambiguity.
Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment.
Excellent Excel and PowerPoint skills and clear, concise written and verbal communication skills.

Compensation

The base salary compensation range being offered for this role is $110,000 CAD -$150,000 CAD per year.

This role is also eligible for an annual short-term incentive bonus.

Company Overview

Fengate Asset Management is a leading alternative investment manager focused on infrastructure, private equity, and real estate strategies. Founded in 1974 in Hamilton, Ontario, and with over 250 team members across Canada and the U.S., Fengate is one of the most active real asset and growth equity investors in North America. The firm currently manages over C$10 billion in capital commitments in support of more than C$40 billion in gross asset value, on behalf of over 60 institutional investors across North America, Europe, and Asia.

The firm believes that acting responsibly to its stakeholders and communities is fundamental. Fengate is a signatory of both the Institutional Limited Partners Association (ILPA) Diversity in Action initiative and the United Nations-supported Principles for Responsible Investment, integrating environmental, social and governance (ESG) principles into all stages of the firm’s investment process. In 2021, Fengate established its ESG Committee and its EBID (Equity, Belonging, Inclusion and Diversity) Think Tank, consisting of leaders and employees of all backgrounds and levels throughout the firm, to advance and govern the ESG and EBID objectives.

Fengate has achieved Platinum Club member status as one of Canada’s Best Managed Companies, retaining this designation since 2007, and has been certified as a Great Place to Work®. Over the past year, Fengate was named one of Canada’s Best Workplaces™ (#4 for companies with 100-999 employees) and as a Best Workplace™ for Financial Services & Insurance, Inclusion, Women, Today’s Youth, Mental Wellness, Giving Back, and Most Trusted Executive Teams.

The firm has also been recognized with Waterstone Human Capital’s 2022 Most Admired Corporate Cultures™ award. This program recognizes best-in-class organizations for having cultures that have helped them enhance performance and sustain a competitive advantage. Only 50 organizations are awarded this prestigious corporate culture award each year.

OPPORTUNITY

The Head of Public-Private Partnerships is a senior leadership role within Fengate’s Infrastructure Investments team, responsible for leading the firm’s P3 and infrastructure concessions platform across North America. Reporting to the Managing Director, Infrastructure Investments, this leader will combine market origination and public-sector relationship development with hands-on commercial execution, guiding complex transactions from opportunity identification and triage, procurement strategy and consortium formation through bid, investment approval, financial close and transition to asset management. The role will integrate P3 activity into Fengate’s broader enterprise and investment strategy, working in close partnership with leaders across Investments, Legal, Finance, Responsible Investment, Asset Management and Investor Relations. This individual will lead and develop the P3 team, create disciplined pursuit and bid-governance practices, and advance infrastructure projects that generate durable value for communities and investors.

Define and lead Fengate’s North American P3 and infrastructure concessions strategy, aligning market priorities, origination, resource allocation and sector coverage with the firm’s infrastructure funds and broader enterprise objectives
Originate, assess and advance opportunities across Canada and the United States, including traditional availability-payment P3s, infrastructure concessions and other alternative or collaborative delivery models
Lead complex pursuits and transactions from market development, procurement strategy, consortium formation and bid planning through commercial structuring, investment committee approval, negotiations, financial close and handover to asset management
Provide senior commercial leadership across RFQ and RFP processes, including bid governance, risk allocation, financing strategy, project agreements, consortium arrangements, pricing, procurement compliance and negotiation strategy
Lead, coach and develop P3 investment professionals, bid directors and pursuit teams, establishing clear accountabilities, and consistent execution standards
Partner across Investments, Legal, Finance, Responsible Investment, Asset Management, Investor Relations and Value Creation to ensure opportunities are investable, financeable, operationally sound and aligned with labour, responsible investing, and investor expectations
Build and maintain executive-level relationships with government agencies, procurement authorities, developers, contractors, operators, lenders, institutional investors and professional advisors; represent Fengate at industry forums and stakeholder engagements
Monitor P3 policy, procurement models, infrastructure priorities and competitive activity across sectors such as transportation, social infrastructure, public facilities, utilities and other essential infrastructure, translating market intelligence into strategic recommendations
Support fundraising, investor engagement and senior leadership communications by articulating the firms’ P3 strategy, pipeline, risk framework, market differentiation and transaction track record

Key Qualifications

10+ years of progressive experience across infrastructure development, investment, project finance, P3/PPP, concessions or alternative delivery, including senior accountability for complex North American pursuits and transactions
Demonstrated track record leading transactions end to end, from origination, procurement assessment and bid development through consortium formation, commercial close, financial close and transition into delivery, operations or asset management
Deep knowledge of P3/PPP, DBFM, DBFOM, concessions and other collaborative or alternative delivery models, including procurement, project agreements, consortium governance, lifecycle and O&M considerations, risk allocation and public-sector decision-making
Strong commercial, financial and investment judgment, with the ability to assess bankability, risk-adjusted returns and delivery risk; challenge assumptions; negotiate complex agreements; and make disciplined pursuit and capital-allocation recommendations
Established relationships across public authorities, infrastructure developers, contractors, operators, lenders, institutional investors, technical advisors and legal counsel in Canada and/or the United States
Proven enterprise leadership and people-management capability, including building and developing teams, coaching senior professionals, setting pursuit governance and influencing across investment, legal, finance, responsible investment and asset-management functions
Exceptional executive communication, stakeholder-management and negotiation skills, with credibility in government, consortium, investment committee, board and institutional-investor settings
Undergraduate degree in business, finance, engineering, law, economics or a related discipline; an MBA, CFA, P.Eng., legal qualification or other relevant graduate degree or professional designation is preferred

jobs.title: Director of Technology Operations
jobs.description:
Coinspaid Dev is the engineering brand behind the technology, infrastructure, and R&D expertise built within Coinspaid. With more than 120 engineersand over 11 years of industry experience, Coinspaid Dev brings together software engineering, infrastructure, security and R&D teams with experience building distributed systems and blockchain infrastructure operating across more than 20 blockchain networks.

Coinspaid Dev emerges as an independent engineering brand with a straightforward mission: to advance blockchain infrastructure engineering and contribute practical expertise back to the industry. The structure is new. The experience behind it is not.
 
Director of Technology Operations
We are building the next operating model for a ~150-person technology organization behind production-critical financial infrastructure.
We are looking for a Director of Technology Operations to lead that transformation.
This is not a traditional infrastructure or IT operations role. The mandate is to evolve Technology Operations from a primarily reactive model toward a scalable organization built around clear ownership, platform engineering, automation, self-service, operational excellence, resilience and measurable outcomes.
You will initially lead several established technology functions through their existing Heads and Leads, with approximately 25 people across Platform/DevOps, Corporate IT and Operational Excellence. The mandate is broader than the initial team size: you will help shape the operating model of a ~150-person technology organization and build capabilities designed to scale significantly beyond today's structure.
Your responsibility will go beyond managing these teams. You will help shape how the broader technology organization operates: how production services are owned, how incidents and changes are managed, how engineers consume infrastructure capabilities, how operational risks are identified, and how recurring manual work is systematically eliminated.
A major part of the role is organizational transformation. We expect you to assess the current model, challenge it where necessary, define the target state, develop the leaders underneath you, and deliver measurable improvements rather than simply introduce new processes.
The goal is straightforward: as the company grows, Technology Operations should become more reliable, resilient and scalable while requiring less manual coordination, less operational toil and less executive intervention.
What you will do
Lead the transformation of Technology Operations across Platform/DevOps, Corporate IT and Operational Excellence, moving the organization from reactive operations toward ownership, automation, self-service and measurable outcomes.
Define the Technology Operations strategy, target operating model, organizational structure, responsibilities, priorities and transformation roadmap.
Lead multiple established technology functions through Heads, Leads and other managers, creating clear accountability and developing leaders who can operate with increasing autonomy.
Lead the evolution of DevOps toward a Platform Engineering model that reduces operational toil, increases self-service and improves developer productivity while maintaining reliability and security.
Partner with Engineering to establish a "you build it, you own it" model, where product teams retain ownership of their services in production while Technology Operations provides the platform, standards, tooling and operational framework that enable them to operate reliably.
Develop Service Management toward Operational Excellence: strengthen service ownership, incident and problem management, introduce risk-based change governance, reduce unnecessary manual controls, and use operational data to eliminate systemic causes of failures.
Transform Corporate IT toward a secure, automated employee technology model, with strong identity and access lifecycle management, device management, governance and employee self-service.
Continuously assess the current organization, technology landscape and operating model, identify structural and operational gaps, and turn them into concrete improvement initiatives.
Improve the maturity, reliability, scalability and efficiency of technology operations supporting production-critical systems.
Define meaningful operational metrics and use them to identify systemic problems, measure transformation outcomes and drive improvements rather than simply report performance.
Own the Technology Operations contribution to digital operational resilience, including ICT business continuity, disaster recovery, backup and restoration, resilience testing, recovery objectives, crisis readiness, and remediation of findings from incidents and resilience exercises.
Partner with Security, Risk and Compliance to maintain an effective ICT risk management and control environment, including technology risk identification, critical service dependencies, ICT third-party risk, resilience testing, audit readiness and regulatory remediation.
Ensure operational and technology risks are identified early, understood, prioritized and addressed appropriately.
Support the company through audits, certifications, regulatory requirements and other controls relevant to financial and technology organizations.
Own and optimize budgets, technology vendors, infrastructure investments and external partnerships within the function.
Partner closely with Engineering, Security, Risk, Compliance, Product, Finance and other business functions.
Represent Technology Operations in cross-functional and executive discussions and communicate complex technology and operational topics clearly to different audiences.
Help prepare the technology organization for the next stage of the company's growth, including increasingly complex enterprise customers, new products and a larger engineering organization.
What we are looking for
Significant leadership experience in Technology Operations, IT Operations, Infrastructure & Operations, Platform/Production Operations, Platform Engineering or a comparable technology function.
Experience as a manager of managers, with responsibility for several teams or functions through Heads, Engineering Managers, Team Leads or equivalent leadership roles.
Previous experience as a Technology Director, VP/Head of Technology Operations, Platform/Infrastructure leader or in a comparable senior role within a product engineering organization is highly relevant.
Proven examples of significant organizational or technology transformation: changing operating models, building or restructuring functions, introducing new capabilities, increasing operational maturity, scaling teams or materially changing how technology organizations operate.
Experience leading or evolving DevOps, SRE or infrastructure capabilities toward Platform Engineering, including developer self-service, automation and reduction of operational toil.
Strong understanding of modern production ownership models and the relationship between Platform Engineering and product engineering teams.
Experience with production-critical systems where availability, reliability, security and operational failures have direct business impact.
Experience with IT and Service Management in modern product/engineering environments, including incident, problem and change management.
Experience transforming Corporate IT or employee technology environments, including identity/access lifecycle, endpoint/device management, automation, governance and employee self-service.
Practical experience with business continuity, disaster recovery and operational resilience in production-critical environments, including BIA, RTO/RPO, backup and restoration, resilience testing and remediation.
Experience working with Security, Risk and Compliance teams and managing technology and operational risks.
Exposure to audits, certifications, regulatory requirements and operational controls relevant to financial institutions or other regulated environments.
Working knowledge of regulatory frameworks relevant to technology operations in financial services, such as DORA, and the ability to translate regulatory requirements into pragmatic engineering and operational controls, is a plus.
Experience managing budgets, vendors, contracts and technology investments.
Ability to operate effectively when requirements, organizational boundaries or the final solution are not yet fully defined.
Track record of developing leaders and building teams that can operate without constant escalation or executive intervention.
Ability to move between strategic topics and operational problems: understand what requires executive attention, delegate what should be owned by your leaders, and personally step in when the situation requires it.
Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, including the ability to work effectively with technical teams, senior business stakeholders and executive leadership.
Experience in fintech, payments, banking, financial infrastructure or another regulated and production-critical technology environment would be highly valuable.
How we think about this role
We are not looking for a traditional IT or infrastructure leader whose primary focus is maintaining existing systems and following established processes.
We need someone who is comfortable entering an environment where not everything has already been defined — and who sees that ambiguity as part of the mandate.
You should be able to understand how the organization actually operates today, distinguish symptoms from systemic problems, bring the right people together, make decisions with incomplete information, and turn those decisions into measurable organizational and technology improvements.
You will not be expected to solve every problem personally. A major part of your role will be to build strong Heads and Leads who can own their areas independently, while you focus on the most important organizational, strategic and cross-functional challenges.
At the same time, limited resources, legacy approaches or imperfect processes should be constraints to work with — not reasons why progress cannot happen.
What success looks like
Within the first 6–12 months, we expect to see measurable movement in addition to plans:
reduced recurring operational toil;
increasing developer and employee self-service;
stronger and clearer service ownership;
fewer repeated incidents and systemic operational failures;
more risk-based and automated change management;
improved developer and employee experience;
clearer operational and resilience metrics;
measurable progress toward a Platform Engineering model;
stronger operational resilience and risk management;
and Heads and Leads operating with greater autonomy.
You will have established a clear target operating model and transformation roadmap, but success will not be measured by the existence of the roadmap itself. It will be visible in how the organization operates.
Success means the organization requires less manual coordination and executive intervention while becoming more reliable, resilient, faster and more scalable.

jobs.title: AVP, Corporate Development
jobs.description:
Canadian Tire Corporation, Limited (“CTC”) is one of Canada’s most trusted companies and one of the country’s most recognized retail brands. Across Canadian Tire Retail, Mark’s, SportChek, Triangle Rewards, and Canadian Tire Bank, we are focused on creating long-term value and delivering on our True North strategy.

We are seeking a commercially minded, strategic leader to help shape and execute corporate development opportunities across CTC, including acquisitions, divestitures, investments, and strategic partnerships.

Reporting to the Vice President, Corporate Development, the AVP will lead complex transactions from opportunity assessment through execution and transition. This role works closely with senior business leaders and external advisors, provides clear recommendations to executives and the Board, and leads a team of Managers and Senior Analysts.

What You Will Do

Shape corporate development strategy

Partner with the VP, Corporate Development and business leaders to identify and prioritize inorganic growth, portfolio, and strategic partnership opportunities.
Assess strategic fit, commercial potential, risks, and value creation opportunities in support of CTC’s True North strategy.
Build investment theses and practical recommendations that connect enterprise priorities with actionable opportunities.

Lead complex transactions end to end

Own acquisitions, divestitures, investments, and partnership mandates from screening, valuation, and due diligence through negotiation, approvals, signing, closing, and transition planning.
Lead cross-functional transaction teams spanning Finance, Legal, Tax, Treasury, Strategy, Operations, and business units, alongside external advisors and counterparties.
Direct financial models, valuations, business cases, and risk assessments; challenge assumptions and maintain high standards for decision-making.
Lead commercial negotiations and advise on terms, risk allocation, and transaction documents in partnership with Legal.

Advise and influence senior stakeholders

Develop compelling investment cases, decision memoranda, and Board materials with clear recommendations, trade-offs, and sensitivities.
Build trusted relationships with executives, business leaders, prospective partners, sellers, investors, and advisors, often in confidential and high-stakes situations.
Provide sound judgment and direction when information is incomplete, priorities shift, or negotiations become complex.

Deliver value beyond the transaction

Oversee integration readiness, value creation plans, investment performance, governance, and strategic portfolio reviews as required.
Strengthen transaction governance, playbooks, knowledge sharing, and analytical practices across the Corporate Development team.

Lead and develop the team

Manage, coach, and develop Managers and Senior Analysts, setting clear expectations and quality standards.
Allocate resources across concurrent mandates and build a collaborative, accountable, high-performing team.

Key relationships

VP, Corporate Development and senior leaders across CTC’s businesses
Finance, Legal, Tax, Treasury, Strategy, Operations, and other cross-functional partners
Executive leadership and Board stakeholders
External investment banks, advisors, investors, transaction counterparties, and strategic partners

What You Will Bring

8+ years of relevant experience in corporate development, investment banking, private equity, transaction advisory, consulting, or a comparable transaction-intensive environment.
A demonstrated record of independently leading material M&A, investment, divestiture, or strategic partnership processes through negotiation and execution.
Advanced financial and commercial acumen in valuation, modelling, transaction structuring, business cases, risk assessment, and value creation.
Strong strategic judgment and the ability to turn financial, operational, and market complexity into practical recommendations.
Executive-level communication, negotiation, and influencing skills, including experience preparing materials for senior leadership and Board audiences.
Experience leading cross-functional teams, managing external advisors, and balancing multiple high-priority mandates.
Proven people leadership, coaching and talent development capabilities.
Excellent written communication and presentation skills, with advanced Excel, PowerPoint, and market research capabilities.
Post-secondary education in a relevant discipline.

Additional Assets

Knowledge of the Canadian retail landscape, CTC’s businesses, and its strategic priorities.
An advanced degree or relevant professional designation.

Leadership attributes

Enterprise-minded with strong commercial instincts
Decisive and comfortable operating with ambiguity
Credible, collaborative, and influential with senior stakeholders
Analytical, disciplined, and accountable for execution
Committed to developing talent and building inclusive, high-performing teams

This posting represents an existing vacancy within our organization.

We may use artificial intelligence tools as part of our recruitment process to assist in the initial screening of resumes. All hiring decisions, including candidate evaluation, selection, and disposition, are made by human recruiters.

About Us

Canadian Tire Corporation, Limited (“CTC”) is one of Canada’s most admired and trusted companies. With more than 90 Owned Brands, over 1,600 retail locations, financial services, exemplary e-commerce capabilities, and exciting market-leading merchandising strategies. We dream big and work as one to innovate with purpose for our customers at every level of our business, investing in new technologies and products, and doubling down on top talent to drive the company forward. We offer competitive salaries and wages to CTC employees, as well as store discounts, supported learning through our Triangle Learning Academy, Canadian Tire Profit Sharing, and retirement and savings programs for eligible employees. As part of our enhanced flex benefits program, we offer mental health benefits in the amount of $5,000 per year for benefits-eligible employees and their families, including total well-being, and mental health tools and resources for all employees. Join us in helping to make life in Canada better through living and working our Core Values: we are innovators and entrepreneurs at our core, outcomes drive us, inclusion is a must, we are stronger together and we take personal responsibility. It is an especially exciting time to join CTC and its family of companies where career opportunities are wide-ranging! Join us, where there's a place for you here.

Our Commitment to Diversity, Inclusion and Belonging

We are committed to fostering an environment where belonging thrives, and diversity, inclusion and equity are infused into everything we do. We believe in building an organizational culture where people are consistently treated with dignity while respecting individual religion, nationality, gender, race, age, perceived ability, spoken language, sexual orientation, and identification. We are united in our purpose of being here to help make life in Canada better.

Accommodations

We welcome and encourage candidates from equity-seeking groups such as people who identify as racialized, Indigenous, 2SLGBTQIA+, women, people with disabilities, and beyond. Should you require any accommodation in applying for this role, or throughout the interview process, please make them known when contacted and we will work with you to help meet your needs.

**Job Description**  

  

**Director, Solutions Architecture \- Enterprise Architecture**  

  

Fitch Group is seeking a Director, Solutions Architecture based in our Toronto office, reporting to the Lead Enterprise Architect for the Fitch Group line of business you support.
  

  

This is a hands\-on architecture role built around one core relationship: engineering squads. You'll partner directly with the teams building technology across your line of business, helping them design solutions, navigate architecture standards, and build with confidence. You'll also help build our internal automated governance agents, contributing hands\-on to the tools that support technology evaluation, PR review, and standards enforcement across the organization. This is an individual contributor role \- no direct reports \- for someone who leads through influence, expertise, and relationship.
  

  

**What We Offer:*** Direct Engineering Partnership: Serve as the architecture partner engineering squads actually want to talk to \- someone who helps them solve real problems, not someone who shows up to gate their work.
* Hands\-On Contribution to Automated Governance: Build agents alongside the EA team \- PR review, ARB submission support, technology evaluation \- using your own experience with agent orchestration, observability, and MCP tooling.
* Influence Without Bureaucracy: Shape how engineering teams adopt architecture patterns through demonstrated value, not mandate. You earn trust by being useful.
* AI\-Native Engineering at Scale: Help define how an entire line of business builds software with AI \- from coding assistants to agentic development workflows \- and set the practices other teams follow.

**How You'll Make an Impact:*** Be the Architect Engineers Call First: Provide direct architecture guidance to the engineering squads in your line of business \- solution design, trade\-off analysis, pattern selection \- in the flow of their actual work.
* Support ARB and JAD Sessions When It Matters: Step in to help squads prepare when a new technology or a new pattern is entering the picture \- pressure\-testing the design and reducing back\-and\-forth before formal review.
* Build Agents for the EA Lifecycle: Contribute directly to the agents that power technology evaluation, PR review, standards enforcement, and ARB submission support.
* Translate Standards Into Practice: Take architecture principles and the Tech Roadmap (Invest/Maintain/Divest/Research) and make them concrete and actionable for engineers building real systems.
* Prototype Before You Recommend: Build working examples of patterns before asking teams to adopt them. Credibility here comes from having built it yourself.
* Partner Across Engineering: Work closely with engineering leads to understand their constraints and tailor architecture guidance to their specific context \- what works for one squad won't work for all of them.
* Champion AI\-Based Development: Help squads adopt AI\-assisted and agentic development \- coding assistants, AI\-driven testing, and agentic workflows \- and establish the patterns, guardrails, and metrics that let them ship faster with confidence rather than treating AI as a novelty.
* Drive Down Technical Liabilities: Use the Tech Roadmap (Invest/Maintain/Divest/Research) and the enterprise architecture graph of dependencies to give squads a clear view of their technical debt \- what to retire, what to modernize, and where hidden coupling creates risk before it becomes an incident.
* Automate Upgrades and Modernization: Help teams stand up automated dependency upgrades, patching, and modernization pipelines \- so keeping systems current becomes a routine, low\-effort habit instead of a stop\-the\-world project.

* Hands\-On Agentic AI Experience: Real experience building AI agents, working with LLMs, and applying agentic patterns \- orchestration, observability, tool use \- to production workflows.
* Influence\-Based Leadership: Demonstrated ability to drive adoption across teams without direct authority \- earning buy\-in through trust and results, not org\-chart power.
* Customer\-Facing Orientation: You think of engineers as your customers. You want to understand their problems and help solve them, not enforce a checklist.
* Governance at Scale: Experience defining and evolving technical standards across many teams \- knowing how to get consistent buy\-in without slowing everyone down.
* Track Record Driving AI Adoption: Demonstrated success introducing AI\-based development practices \- coding assistants, agentic workflows, or developer\-productivity tooling \- to engineering teams and getting real, sustained usage rather than shelfware.
* Technical Debt and Dependency Management: Experience mapping system dependencies and leading modernization or automated\-upgrade programs across a codebase or platform.

jobs.description:
**About Nu**
============


Nu serves more than 143 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human\-centered services.

  

Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability.  

  

Visit our Institutional Page

**Head of Design, Global App Platforms (Core)**
===============================================

**ABOUT THE ROLE**
------------------


Core is the team that defines what great design means at Nu. It's a small, deliberately elite group of designers with two jobs: set the bar for design across the company today, and decide where that bar is headed next.


Core delivers the vision for the Nu app as it launches across countries. Right now that means designing the next version of the app, and the version after that. But vision alone isn't the job. Everything Core builds has to be adoptable by every market. When Core ships a new experience, it defines the guidelines, hands them to our teams in Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia, and partners with them as they tailor it to their customers.


As Senior Design Manager, you'll lead this team. It's a high\-craft environment made up of some of the strongest individual contributors in the company, many of them from the most design\-led companies in tech. You'll be hands\-on in the work while giving the team the structure, focus, and air cover it needs to do the best work of their careers.

**WHAT YOU'LL DO**
------------------

* **Set the Bar:** Define and raise the standard for design quality across Nu, and make that standard legible enough that every team can work toward it.
* **Lead the Next Generation of the App:** Shape the vision and execution for the next versions of the Nu app, from early concepts through launch\-ready guidelines.
* **Stay Hands\-On:** Get into the work with your team. Critique, prototype, push the craft, and help solve the hardest design problems directly.
* **Build for Adoption:** Make sure everything Core creates can scale across Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia. Partner with local teams so global guidelines become experiences that fit each market's customers.
* **Partner Across Design:** Work closely with the Design System team and other design leaders so Core's vision and the system that delivers it move together.
* **Lead and Grow a World\-Class Team:** Manage a small team of senior, high\-craft designers. Give them clarity, protect their focus, and help them grow.
* **Manage Stakeholders:** Represent Core's work to product, engineering, and business leaders, align them on direction, and remove the blockers that slow great work down.

**WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR**
--------------------------

### **Required:**

* **Exceptional Craft:** A portfolio that shows world\-class product and visual design, with consumer, mobile\-first work at scale.
* **Vision You've Shipped:** Experience defining the future direction of a product and seeing that vision through to launch.
* **Hands\-On Leadership:** You lead from inside the work. Formal people\-management experience is a plus, not a requirement; we care more that you've raised the bar for the designers around you.
* **Stakeholder Management:** A track record of influencing senior cross\-functional partners and driving alignment across teams that don't report to you. This isn't a lone\-wolf role.
* **Systems Thinking:** Experience creating guidelines, patterns, or frameworks that other teams adopted and built on.
* **Global Mindset:** Comfort designing experiences that balance global consistency with local relevance across markets and cultures.

### **Nice to Have:**

* Experience leading a small team of very senior ICs.
* Experience designing financial products or other high\-trust consumer experiences.

**OUR BENEFITS**
----------------

* Opportunity of earning equity at Nu
* Medical Insurance
* Dental and Vision Insurance
* Life Insurance and AD\&D
* Extended maternity and paternity leaves
* Nucleo \- Our learning platform of courses
* NuLanguage \- Our language learning program
* NuCare \- Our mental health and wellness assistance program
* 401K
* Saving Plans \- Health Saving Account and Flexible Spending Account
* Work\-from\-home Allowance
* Relocation Assistance Package, if applicable.

**WORK MODEL FOR THIS ROLE**
----------------------------


Our hybrid work model brings us to the office 3x per week, on strategic days designed to maximize team connection and collaboration. For more details, visit https://building.nubank.com/nu\-hybrid\-work\-model/


This role can be based in any of our US offices: Palo Alto, Miami, or McLean.

**COMPENSATION**
----------------


Palo Alto, CA: The **total compensation** range for this role in Palo Alto is roughly $450k to $725k USD, comprised of both base salary and equity (in the form of RSUs: 3\-year vest, 1\-year cliff). Final compensation is determined by level, experience, and location.


Our recruitment process may involve the use of artificial intelligence–enabled tools, such as automated interview transcription and analysis, to support the evaluation process. Artificial intelligence is not used to make final hiring decisions; all decisions are made by human reviewers.  

  

To maintain a consistent and fair process for every candidate, Nu does not provide individualized technical feedback. See how our policy works here

jobs.title: Director, Finance & Accounting
jobs.description:
BERMANFALK Hospitality Group
is a "design driven" manufacturer of custom casegoods and seating for the hospitality industry. At BERMANFALK we are passionate about design and bringing our client's visions to life. We are looking to add like-minded professionals to our team who are excited by contributing to a fast-paced company and who excel with management of details and customer service. www.bermanfalk.com

About BERMANFALK Hospitality Group

BERMANFALK Hospitality Group delivers custom casegoods and seating to the hospitality industry, including hotels, resorts, and restaurants; primarily focused on the 3+ to 5 star market. We manage every project from design phase, approvals and shop drawings through to manufacturing, quality control, logistics, delivery and installation. Our model depends on a trusted network of manufacturing partners, which makes precise cost control, disciplined project accounting, and sound supply-chain ﬁnance central to our success.
We are growing and evolving high paced business, and we are looking for a ﬁnance leader who can run rigorous day-to-day project and cost accounting while shaping the ﬁnancial strategy that will carry the company to its next stage.

ROLE SUMMARY

The Director, Finance & Accounting is the senior ﬁnance leader at BERMANFALK and owns every part of the company's ﬁnancial function. The role has two equal halves:

Operational ﬁnance:
building and running cost-based and project-based accounting so that every project's true cost, margin, and cash position is known in real time, from quote to ﬁnal invoice.
Strategic ﬁnance:
leading ﬁnancial planning, capital structure, banking relationships, risk management, and growth strategy for the company as a whole.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who is as comfortable reconciling a landed-cost variance on a guestroom package as presenting a ﬁve-year plan to ownership and lenders.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Project & Job-Cost Accounting

Own the full project accounting lifecycle, including project setup, budgets, cost tracking, change orders, billing, and close-out.
Design and maintain a job-costing structure that captures manufacturer costs, freight, duties, brokerage, warehousing, installation, samples, and allocated overhead by project and by line item.
Ensure change orders and scope changes are priced, approved, and billed promptly so that margin does not erode.
Deliver project proﬁtability reporting that compares estimated and actual results, identiﬁes variances, and feeds lessons back into estimating.

Cost Accounting & Supply-Chain Finance

Build accurate landed-cost models for outsourced production, covering FOB pricing, ocean and inland freight, tariffs and duties, customs brokerage, insurance, and FX.
Partner with procurement to manage manufacturer deposits, payment milestones, letters of credit, and supplier terms.
Monitor and mitigate foreign-exchange exposure on supplier payments and customer contracts, including hedging strategy where appropriate.
Track tariff and trade-policy changes and model their impact on pricing, sourcing decisions, and open contracts.
Support estimating and sales with cost data, pricing models, and margin guardrails for bids and proposals.
Evaluate manufacturing partners from a ﬁnancial perspective, including cost competitiveness, ﬁnancial stability, and risk concentration.

Financial Operations & Controls

Lead month-end and year-end close, producing accurate and timely ﬁnancial statements.
Prepare consolidated Balance Sheets, Income Statements, and Cash Flow Statements.
Coordinate and lead all annual external audits, ensuring robust internal controls and GAAP/IFRS compliance.
Maintain 13-week cash-ﬂow forecasting and working-capital management across overlapping projects.
Maintain direct oversight over global banking accounts and treasury management across 4 countries.
Oversee Indirect Tax Compliance & Remittances – US Sales & Use Tax, Canadian provincial and federal sales taxes and UK VAT returns.
Lead corporate income tax compliance and statutory filings with the CRA, IRS and HMRC.

Strategic Finance & Leadership

Develop and own the annual budget, rolling forecasts, and long-range ﬁnancial plan.
Serve as a strategic advisor to the Executive Team and ownership on growth, pricing strategy, market expansion, and investment decisions.
Build KPI dashboards covering backlog, gross margin by project and client, projects rolling forecast.
Evaluate strategic opportunities including new product categories, partnerships, acquisitions, and vertical integration.
Lead the selection, implementation, or optimization of ERP and project accounting systems that connect estimating, procurement, and ﬁnance.
Build, mentor, and lead the ﬁnance and accounting team as the company scales.
Establish standard operating procedures (SOPs), clear performance metrics, and workflow efficiency across global finance functions.

QUALIFICATIONS

Required

CPA designation (Canada) or equivalent professional accounting credential is preferred.
10+ years of progressive ﬁnance experience, including at least 5 years in a senior leadership role (Controller, Director of Finance, or VP Finance).
Deep, hands-on expertise in project-based and job-cost accounting, WIP reporting, and percentage-of-completion or milestone revenue recognition.
Experience in manufacturing, contract furniture, FF&E, millwork, construction, or another project-driven industry.
Working knowledge of import/export ﬁnance, including landed costs, duties, FX, and international supplier payments.
Proven experience managing banking relationships, credit facilities, and cash-ﬂow planning.
Strong command of ﬁnancial modelling and advanced Excel, plus experience with ERP or project accounting systems.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain ﬁnancial results to project managers, sales teams, and ownership alike.

﻿Preferred

Experience with outsourced or offshore manufacturing (e.g., Asia, Mexico, Europe) and the related supply-chain ﬁnance.
Background in the hospitality FF&E, contract furniture, or hotel development sector.
Experience leading an ERP implementation.
Familiarity with FX hedging, trade credit insurance, letters of credit, and surety bonding.
Experience in a privately held or family-owned company during a period of growth.

What Success Looks Like in the First Year

Every active project has an accurate, current cost-to-complete and margin forecast.
Month-end close is completed on a consistent, reliable timeline with project-level reporting.
Landed-cost and pricing models are standardized and used by estimating on every bid.
A rolling cash-ﬂow forecast and KPI dashboard are in place and reviewed with leadership regularly.
A clear multi-year ﬁnancial strategy and systems roadmap has been presented to and adopted by ownership.

Why Join BERMANFALK

A senior seat at the leadership table with direct inﬂuence on the company's direction.
The opportunity to build and shape the ﬁnance function of a growing hospitality business.
Work on high-proﬁle projects across the hospitality sector on a global scale.
Competitive compensation, performance bonus, and beneﬁts package.

COMPENSATION:
Salary Range: $150,000 - $175,000 CAD per year

BENEFITS

Comprehensive extended health & dental benefits plan with a health spending account
Paid time off including vacation
Flexible working environment - Hybrid & Remote option depending on the role
Supplementary maternity and parental leave top-up
Beautiful open office space in Langley with full kitchen - offering coffee, snacks and refreshments
Tuition reimbursement program and various growth opportunities
Casual dress
Company social events and fun team-bonding activities
Employee assistance programs

Our business is guided by honesty and integrity. We offer competitive wages and a progressive, collaborative and creative work environment. While we laugh a great deal, we have high expectations of each other, and top-level performance is essential.
BERMANFALK Hospitality Group is an equal opportunity employer.

HYBRID WORK

BERMANFALK is a hybrid company where employees have the flexibility to work from the
office or remotely based on the specific needs of the company. We feel this model empowers employees to work where they feel most productive, while maintaining a strong connection with their team and encouraging company-wide collaboration.  

We empower our employees to shape their work themselves, so that they can achieve quality results and deliver excellence to our team and clients. When done well, we become better collaborators, communicators, ultimately enriching our work-life balance.

Full in-office attendance will be expected during onboarding and training.

We’re one of Canada’s largest pension investors, with CAD$320.6 billion of net assets as of March 31, 2026.

We invest funds for the pension plans of the federal public service, the Canadian Forces, the Royal Canadian Mounted Police and the Reserve Force. Headquartered in Ottawa, PSP Investments has its principal business office in Montréal and offices in New York, London and Hong Kong.

Capturing and leading complex global investments requires us to work as one to seize valuable opportunities, in close collaboration with some of the world’s top companies. What if your new chapter started here?

The Ministry of Education and Childcare supports students, parents, teachers and administrators from Early Childhood Services (ECS) through Grade 12. Through safe and respectful schools for all students, Alberta’s government is making life better by investing in education, one of the most important investments we can make in our future. The Ministry has the following responsibilities: developing curriculum and setting standards; evaluating curriculum and assessing outcomes; supporting teacher development and certification; supporting students with diverse learning needs; funding and supporting school boards; advancing First Nations, Métis, Inuit and francophone education; and overseeing basic education policy and regulations.

Reporting to the Executive Director, this position ensures branch functions and programs are integrated, coordinated and in compliance with relevant legislation, policies and business plans.

The Director is accountable for ensuring that the department, school authority and childcare financial reporting system is effectively developed, maintained and monitored and for financial reporting for the Ministry including quarterly and annual reporting and Public Accounts Committee reporting.

The Director develops policies relating to department, childcare and school authority financial reporting and information systems used to report school authority budgets and audited financial statements. He/she provides information to support internal and external financial accountabilities and works with business areas across Alberta Education and childcare to lead the completion of financial analysis and reporting accountabilities, including provision of associated advice and expertise.

Prepare and deliver briefings and presentations on financial issues and analysis to senior management, stakeholders, MLA task teams, Treasury Board, Executive Team and Legislative Standing Committees.
Provide leadership, coaching, mentoring, and professional development opportunities to support staff growth, performance, and continuous improvement.
Represent the Ministry on internal, cross-ministry, government, and external committees, task forces and working groups.

Working with associations across the country, CAUT brings national and international perspectives to help solve local challenges. They also bring local priorities to the national agenda, influencing federal policy and investments in research and post-secondary education.

The Director coordinates the work of these functions, aligns resources and priorities with organizational objectives, and oversees the development and implementation of their budgets, operational plans, policies, and processes. As a member of the management team, the Director contributes to strategic, operational, and financial planning and coordinates progress on cross-functional initiatives. The role combines financial stewardship, sound people management, effective technology and information management, and oversight of facilities and administrative services. The Director leads and develops a team of professional and administrative staff, provides guidance on complex matters, and keeps the Executive Director informed of progress, emerging issues, and resource requirements.

The ideal candidate is a highly adaptable, bilingual executive who thrives in a hands-on, multifaceted leadership role and can serve as a trusted partner to the Executive Director. Working closely with Category Directors, Store Concepts, Operations, Marketing, external agencies, and brand partners, the Director will translate strategic priorities into compelling customer experiences and commercially successful initiatives. The role requires a combination of strategic thinking, commercial acumen, creativity, and strong executional leadership.

 **Key Responsibilities**

 **Brand Experience, Events \& PR Partnerships**


Lead the planning and execution of key Prestige Beauty events that strengthen brand partnerships, showcase innovation, and elevate the Shoppers Drug Mart beauty proposition.

* Lead planning for the annual September Beauty Conference, partnering with brand vendors, external agencies, and internal teams to deliver an engaging experience that reinforces business priorities and inspires Beauty Specialists.
* Partner with Marketing, PR, and external agencies to plan and execute the P2 PR Event, showcasing brand innovation, product launches, and strategic initiatives.
* Collaborate with brand partners on event participation, sponsorships, product showcases, and educational activations.
* Oversee event budgets, timelines, logistics, agency relationships, and cross\-functional coordination to ensure successful execution.

 **Corporate Programs \& Commercial Innovation**


Lead the development and execution of innovative, multi\-brand programs that drive product discovery, incremental sales, and profitability.

* Own the end\-to\-end strategy and execution of signature programs, including Discovery Sets, Beauty Bundles, and the Beauty Advent Calendar.
* Lead program development, including concept creation, brand participation, product curation, pricing, forecasting, packaging, and execution.
* Partner with Marketing, Merchandising, Supply Chain, Finance, and brand vendors to ensure successful program delivery.
* Manage annual program calendars, timelines, and commercial objectives.
* Monitor sales and profitability, identifying opportunities to optimize performance and improve future programs.

 **Beauty Boutique Strategy, Store Concepts \& Merchandising**


Lead the evolution of the Beauty Boutique retail environment, ensuring store concepts and merchandising strategies deliver a premium customer experience and support profitable growth.

* Partner with Category Directors and Store Concepts to evolve Beauty Boutique formats, store layouts, brand adjacencies, and space allocation.
* Participate in capital planning discussions, supporting new store openings, renovations, and brand rollouts.
* Lead the development of multi\-brand planograms and merchandising standards, balancing brand priorities, customer navigation, and store productivity.
* Collaborate with Store Concepts, Operations, and brand partners to ensure successful execution of new store openings, renovations, and merchandising initiatives.
* Oversee Beauty Boutique promotional calendars, merchandising direction, and grand opening activities.
* Leverage customer insights, competitive trends, and store performance to continuously elevate the in\-store experience.

 **Cross\-Functional Leadership \& Business Performance**


Serve as a key connector across Category Management, Operations, Marketing, Store Concepts, and brand partners to ensure alignment and effective execution of Prestige Beauty priorities.

* Build strong internal and external partnerships to advance business initiatives and strengthen execution.
* Partner with Store Operations to communicate priorities, support Beauty Specialist engagement, and gather field feedback.
* Participate in vendor planning meetings, operational calls, and key business events.
* Monitor performance across corporate programs, merchandising initiatives, and store projects, identifying risks and opportunities.
* Drive process improvements, clear accountability, and timely execution across multiple initiatives.

**Qualifications \& Experience**

* University degree in Business, Marketing, Retail Management, or a related field.
* Significant progressive experience in retail, category management, merchandising, brand marketing, or commercial strategy, preferably within beauty or prestige retail.
* Proven ability to lead complex, cross\-functional projects from strategy through execution.
* Strong commercial acumen, including financial planning, forecasting, and performance analysis.
* Experience with retail store concepts, merchandising, customer experience, or large\-scale event management.
* Strong relationship\-building, negotiation, communication, and influencing skills.
* Strategic thinker with strong analytical capabilities, creativity, and attention to detail.
* Ability to manage multiple priorities, navigate ambiguity, and deliver results in a fast\-paced environment.

jobs.description:
Job Description 

 What is the opportunity? 

 The Operational Excellence Associate Director drives execution of audit remediation activities and operational excellence initiatives within the Client Lifecycle Management pillar. This role serves as a primary "doer" embedded within CLM operations, responsible for executing audit responses, managing action plans, and implementing control improvements. Unlike a governance function, this role maintains accountability into CLM Pillar heads for work execution and prioritization, ensuring audit requirements translate into concrete operational improvements.

 The Associate Director coordinates audit responses across regulatory examinations, manages compliance-related documentation, and ensures sustainability of implemented controls. This position bridges the centralized Audit Engagement team and day-to-day CLM operations, ensuring timely resolution of identified issues while preventing recurring deficiencies.

 What will you do? 

 Audit Response Planning & Execution 
 Coordinate with 1st, 2nd line and 3rd line groups on review & exam scheduling and work planning
 Participate in quarterly advance planning sessions to anticipate regulatory examination cycles
 Support centralized intake management by providing pillar-level resource availability and capacity
 Maintain work inventory and prioritize activities aligned with internal review and external regulatory exam timelines
 Serve as the primary point of contact for assigned audit areas; coordinate directly with CLM Pillar heads & Head of Operational Excellence on work scope and priorities
 Develop detailed audit response narratives with supporting documentation, process maps, and data samples
 Track and manage audit action plans from initiation through completion and validation
 Maintain audit-ready documentation with clear evidence of control effectiveness and remediation status
 Respond to auditor inquiries and follow-up requests within agreed timelines

 Control Assessment, Design & Governance 
 Identify control gaps and design preventive or detective controls aligned with operational risk and regulatory expectations
 Recommend process improvements to CLM Pillar heads with supporting business cases
 Participate in self-identified issues management (EIM) to document and remediate deficiencies
 Support RCSA (Risk Control Self-Assessment) reviews and attestation processes
 Chairing and Coordination of CLM Monthly Risk and Control Forum.
 Perform periodic analysis of OREs, Breaches & Complaints to drive strategic remediation
 Coordinate with 1LODb & 2LOD teams to review CLM specific training requirements

 Regulatory and Compliance Knowledge 
 Maintain current knowledge of regulatory expectations in regulatory exams, KYC/AML requirements
 Work with the CLM Leadership & Head of Operational Excellence to translate regulatory findings into operational remediation activities
 Support privacy impact assessments, operational resilience reviews, BIA/BCP plan updates & Intragroup Outsourcing Documentation
 Ensure compliance with regulatory examination protocols and timelines
 Escalate emerging regulatory trends or examination focus areas to CLM leadership

 Issue Management and Sustainability 
 Ensure comprehensive documentation of identified issues, root causes, and remediation plans
 Assess sustainability of implemented controls and recommend enhancements
 Monitor duplicate issue identification and coordinate resolution with central audit team
 Track remediation metrics and provide status updates to CLM Pillar heads
 Identify systemic risks requiring structural or process-level changes

 Decision Making 
 Determines scope of audit response work and required supporting documentation; prioritizes remediation activities in consultation with CLM Pillar heads and central audit team
 Assesses control design and operating effectiveness; recommends process improvements and enhanced control procedures
 Makes go/no-go decisions on completeness and accuracy of audit response documentation before submission
 Escalates emerging regulatory expectations or examination risks to Head of Operational Excellence and CLM Pillar heads
 Prioritizes work activities based on regulatory examination timelines and pillar operational capacity

 Execution 
 Recommends specific remediation actions and control enhancements to CLM Pillar heads and process owners
 Advises on regulatory examination preparation and required evidence packages
 Suggests process improvements to reduce audit findings and control deficiencies
 Recommends resource allocation and timeline adjustments based on examination complexity and scope

 What do you need to succeed? 

 Must have: 
 Minimum 3-7 years in regulatory examination response, KYC/AML compliance, or Client Due Diligence functions
 Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Law, Compliance, Business Administration, or related field
 Direct experience with regulatory exams (National Futures Association, FINRA, SEC, or OCC preferred) or equivalent international regulatory frameworks
 Strong understanding of AML/KYC processes, client data governance, and regulatory requirements
 Demonstrated ability to interpret regulatory expectations and translate into operational remediation activities
 Proven execution track record in completing audit responses and remediation activities

 Nice to have: 
 Prior experience in 1st or 2nd line compliance, risk, or audit functions
 Compliance, anti-money laundering, or financial regulatory certifications (AML, KYC, CAMS, CIP, or equivalent)
 Exposure to operational resilience frameworks, BIA/BCP, or privacy impact assessment processes
 Experience with process improvement, control design, or operational risk management
 Familiarity with trading operations, client onboarding, or KYC platforms
 Advanced Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Visio); data management and reconciliation
 Strong written and verbal communication; ability to explain complex control designs to auditors and operational teams
 Detail-oriented with ability to manage multiple overlapping audit requirements and timelines
 Problem-solving mindset with focus on practical, sustainable solutions
 Ability to work collaboratively with pillar heads, risk, compliance, and auditors
 Time management and ability to balance audit response demands with BAU operational activities

 We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

jobs.description:
Your work days are brighter here. 

 We’re obsessed with making hard work pay off, for our people, our customers, and the world around us. As a Fortune 500 company and a leading AI platform for managing people, money, and agents, we’re shaping the future of work so teams can reach their potential and focus on what matters most. The minute you join, you’ll feel it. Not just in the products we build, but in how we show up for each other. Our culture is rooted in integrity, empathy, and shared enthusiasm. We’re in this together, tackling big challenges with bold ideas and genuine care. We look for curious minds and courageous collaborators who bring sun-drenched optimism and drive. Whether you're building smarter solutions, supporting customers, or creating a space where everyone belongs, you’ll do meaningful work with Workmates who’ve got your back. In return, we’ll give you the trust to take risks, the tools to grow, the skills to develop and the support of a company invested in you for the long haul. So, if you want to inspire a brighter work day for everyone, including yourself, you’ve found a match in Workday, and we hope to be a match for you too.

 About the Team 
Workday is building a new specialized sales team focused on selling platform, data, analytics, AI, and extensibility solutions into the Office of the CIO. This team will partner with enterprise customers to help IT leaders modernize their technology strategies, unlock business value from Workday’s platform, and align innovation roadmaps to strategic business outcomes.

The Revenue organization at Workday balances integrity, innovation, accountability, and collaboration. We are looking for an experienced sales leader who can build trusted executive relationships, coach high performing sellers, and help accelerate market adoption in a dynamic growth area for Workday 
 About the Role 

 You are an experienced enterprise sales leader who combines technical fluency, executive presence, and disciplined sales execution. You have led teams through complex, multi stakeholder sales cycles and are comfortable engaging directly with CIOs, CTOs, and senior IT leaders. 

 You know how to coach sellers, orchestrate internal resources, shape executive-level value propositions, and create accountability around pipeline generation, forecast accuracy, and revenue performance. You bring credibility in conversations about cloud architecture, data strategy, AI, integration, security, and enterprise transformation, and you can help your team position Workday as a strategic platform within a customer’s broader technology ecosystem. 

 Key Focus & Responsibilities 
 Team Leadership & Coaching: Use your experience to lead, coach, and mentor a field sales team of specialized Account Executives. Drive a culture of accountability, performance, and continuous development. 
 Deal Strategy & Orchestration: Lead a team focused on driving complex platform sales cycles ($500K+ ARR) by orchestrating internal teams of pre-sales, value management, bid management, and sales support from initial discovery through negotiation and closing. 
 SOW, Roadmap, & Deal Governance: Oversee your team's operational accountability for generating and executing formal AI/Platform Statements of Work (SOWs) and delivering 1–3 year phased technology roadmaps. 
 Forecasting & Business Modeling: Maintain accurate forecasting data and business modeling for senior leadership, while helping your team operationalize a "time to engage" strategy based on corporate triggers. 
 Hyperscaler & Partner Co-Selling: Employ effective selling strategies by pulling together different business units to maximize sales, guiding your team to co-sell joint platform solutions with cloud hyperscaler partners (AWS, GCP) and Global System Integrators (GSIs).

 About You

 8+ years experience selling cloud/SaaS/ERP/analytics solutions, with a specific focus on complex platform, enterprise data, or AI/analytics solutions directly to the Office of the CIO or CTO. 
 8+ years experience managing complex sales cycles from start to finish with a track record of successful revenue/quota attainment. 
 5+ years experience as a leader in a team selling environment.

 2+ years of field sales management experience at a SaaS company, ideally focused on new business acquisition, with an additional 8+ years as a field sales representative.

 5+ years experience as a leader in a team selling environment. 

 Other Qualifications 
 Domain & Technical Fluency: Strong technical credibility in modern enterprise IT architectures, cloud data foundations, API orchestration, data privacy/security, and AI/ML platform integration. 
 oCIO Persona Fluency: Speaks the language of IT leadership. Understands the strategic competitive landscape by staying up to date with trends and customer needs so you can effectively coach your team to position Workday solutions. 
 Cross-Functional Orchestration: Proven experience pulling together different business units to maximize on sales and position Workday's extensibility, analytics, and autonomous agent capabilities as an interoperable component of a client's wider IT stack. 
 Dynamic Leadership: Self-starter attitude with the ability to work in a dynamic environment, empowering your team to challenge legacy IT assumptions, frame clear TCO models, and align technology roadmaps to strategic business goals. 

 Workday Pay Transparency Statement 

 Workday pay ranges vary based on work location. As a part of the total compensation package, this role may be eligible for the Workday Bonus Plan or a role-specific commission/bonus, as well as annual refresh stock grants. Recruiters can share more detail during the hiring process. Each candidate’s compensation offer will be based on multiple factors including, but not limited to, geography, experience, skills, job duties, and business need, among other things. For more information regarding Workday’s comprehensive benefits, please click here. 

Primary Location: CAN.ON.Toronto 

Primary Location Base Pay Range: $170,000 CAD - $255,000 CAD 

Primary CAN Base Pay Range: $170,000 - $255,000 CAD 

 Our Approach to Flexible Work 

 With Flex Work, we’re combining the best of both worlds: in-person time and remote. Our approach enables our teams to deepen connections, maintain a strong community, and do their best work. This means you'll have the freedom to create a flexible schedule that caters to your business, team, and personal needs, while being intentional to make the most of time spent together.
