jobs.title: Senior Director, Marketing & Communications
jobs.location: Dorval Head Office, Dorval, Quebec, Canada
jobs.description:
Founded in 2000 by three former Royal Canadian Air Force (RCAF) CF-18 fighter pilots who identified an opportunity to improve military readiness training, Top Aces has since established itself as the world leader in contracted adversary air (ADAIR) services and joint terminal attack controller (JTAC) training.

 We pride ourselves on our unblemished safety record, having flown an industry leading 160,000+ hours of operational training without accident in support of customers worldwide, including Canada, the U.S., Germany, and multiple other NATO allies and international partner nations.

 Our vision is to be the most trusted provider of innovative defense training solutions, continuously elevating standards in an industry where "Experience Matters." This commitment to innovation and technology ensures we remain adaptable, training allied militaries to succeed against evolving threats.

 Top Aces’ dynamic team contributes to delivering on our purpose of training the next generation of combat leaders by living our values of Service, Integrity, Excellence, and Together every day!

 Join our team!

 Position Summary 

 The Senior Director, Marketing & Communications is responsible for developing and leading Top Aces' marketing, brand, and communications strategy. The role leads a team of marketing and communications professionals and ensures that the company's messaging, brand presence, employee communications, and external profile support corporate priorities and business growth.

 The position also provides strategic oversight of government relations activities through the direction and management of external Government Relations advisors. The Senior Director establishes priorities, aligns advisor activities with business objectives, monitors performance, and coordinates internal support for advisor-led advocacy and stakeholder engagement initiatives. The role is not intended to execute day-to-day lobbying activities.

 The Senior Director serves as a trusted advisor to executive leadership on marketing, reputation, executive communications, media relations, employee communications, brand positioning, and strategic stakeholder engagement.

 Key Responsibilities 

 Marketing Strategy & Brand Management 

 Develop and execute a global marketing strategy for showcasing the company’s capabilities in line with corporate priorities, growth objectives, and business development needs.

 Lead brand positioning and ensure consistent use of approved brand standards across the business, regions, channels, and external materials.

 Oversee the development of marketing campaigns, presentations, digital content, videos, advertising, promotional materials, and customer-facing collateral.

 Lead the strategy for corporate events, trade shows, conferences, partnerships, and sponsorships.

 Partner with Business Development and executive leadership to support customer pursuits and strategic initiatives.

 Monitor market trends, audience insights, competitor activity, and emerging opportunities to strengthen positioning and campaign effectiveness.

 Internal Communications 

 Develop and execute an internal communications strategy that supports employee engagement, culture, organizational alignment, and change initiatives.

 Lead the preparation of executive messages, employee announcements, leadership updates, All Employee Calls, and communications for major corporate initiatives.

 Advise leaders on communication approaches for organizational changes and employee-facing initiatives.

 Measure the reach and effectiveness of internal communications and continuously improve channels and content.

 External Communications & Media Relations 

 Develop and implement an external communications strategy to strengthen Top Aces' visibility, credibility, and reputation.

 Lead the preparation of corporate messaging, press releases, media statements, website content, social media, corporate announcements, and executive communications.

 Lead media relations and manage relationships with relevant industry and business media.

 Support senior leaders with interviews, speeches, presentations, strategic messaging, and public-facing engagements.

 Lead crisis communications planning and coordinate communications responses during business-critical situations.

 Ensure consistent messaging across markets, audiences, and communication channels.

 Government Relations Agency Oversight 

 Establish annual Government Relations priorities in consultation with executive leadership, Strategy, and Business Development.

 Direct and manage external Government Relations advisors responsible for executing the company's Government Relations activities.

 Set clear advisor mandates, budgets, and reporting expectations.

 Review and approve advisor-developed stakeholder strategies, engagement plans, briefing materials, advocacy campaigns, and government-facing messaging.

 Coordinate internal subject-matter experts and executives to support agency-led government outreach and stakeholder meetings.

 Ensure Government Relations activities are aligned with business objectives, customer pursuits, corporate messaging, and reputation considerations.

 Monitor relevant government, defence, procurement, policy, and regulatory developments through agency reporting and other appropriate sources.

 Assess advisor performance, manage contracts and budgets, and recommend changes to external support where required.

 Ensure activities are conducted in accordance with applicable lobbying, transparency, ethics, and reporting requirements.

 Team Leadership & Functional Management 

 Lead, coach, and develop an agile marketing and communications team.

 Establish clear priorities, objectives, accountabilities, and development plans for team members.

 Foster collaboration across functions and ensure the team provides responsive, high-quality support to internal stakeholders.

 Manage the departmental operating budget and allocate resources according to business priorities.

 Select and manage external marketing, communications, creative, digital, media, and related service providers.

 Establish meaningful performance indicators and regularly report on results, risks, priorities, and resource requirements.

 Education 

 Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Communications, Public Relations, Journalism, Business Administration, Political Science, or a related field.

 A master's degree or relevant professional designation is considered an asset.

 Experience 

 Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience in marketing and communications, including senior leadership accountability.

 Demonstrated experience leading internal and external communications, brand strategy, media relations, and integrated marketing initiatives.

 Proven experience leading and developing teams and managing cross-functional initiatives.

 Experience managing external agencies, consultants, contracts, budgets, and performance expectations.

 Experience overseeing Government Relations agencies, public affairs advisors, or stakeholder engagement programs is a strong asset.

 Experience in defence, government-facing, or a highly regulated industry is considered an asset.

 Skills, Knowledge & Behaviours 

 Strategic marketing and communications leadership.

 Brand stewardship and reputation management.

 Exceptional written, verbal, presentation, and executive communication skills.

 Strong agency governance, contract management, and budget oversight capabilities.

 Sound judgement and the ability to navigate sensitive, complex, or high-profile matters.

 Strong business acumen and ability to translate strategy into clear communication and marketing priorities.

 Executive presence and ability to advise and influence senior leaders.

 Effective people leadership, coaching, delegation, and prioritization.

 Strong project management and ability to lead multiple initiatives in a fast-paced environment.

 Collaborative, adaptable, creative, and results-oriented approach.

 Bilingualism in English and French, with strong English writing skills, is preferred.

 Working Conditions 

 Domestic and international travel required.

 Availability to support events, stakeholder engagements, or urgent communications outside regular business hours.

 Eligibility to obtain required security clearances and Controlled Goods access may be required.

 Security Clearance Requirements/ CGP / ITAR: 

 Position requires Controlled Goods Clearance and Level 2 Secret Clearance

 By joining Top Aces, you will find: 

 A work environment in which service, integrity, excellence and teamwork are highly valued;

 Opportunities for development and growth;

 Multidisciplinary and multicultural collaboration at a local and global level;

 A flexible schedule;

 Attractive benefit plan.

 Come share your passion with us! Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered, and challenged to be your best self.

 Equal Employment Opportunity 

 At Top Aces, all employees are welcome regardless of race, nationality, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, disability or age. The masculine form may be used in this job description solely for ease of reading but refers to men, women and gender diversity.

jobs.title: Financial Director
jobs.description:
Our client is a multi-entity agribusiness with commercial greenhouse operations producing tomatoes and bell peppers. The Director of Finance will lead the finance and accounting function across both locations, taking hands-on responsibility for financial reporting, controls, cash flow and lender reporting. As a trusted advisor to the Chief Executive Officer, the Director will work with ownership and senior leaders on forecasting, operating performance, capital planning and investment decisions. The role offers direct mentorship from the CEO and room to take on broader responsibility as the business grows. Depending on the candidate’s experience, the company may consider an appointment at the Controller or Chief Financial Officer level, with title, scope and compensation aligned accordingly.

Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, you will:

Lead accounting operations and the month-end and year-end close across multiple entities. Oversee the general ledger, chart of accounts, accounts payable and receivable, biweekly payroll and bank reconciliations, with support staff handling daily transactions.
Deliver monthly, interim and annual consolidated financial statements under Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE), including intercompany eliminations. Apply accounting policies consistently and review proposed changes with the CEO.
Lead annual budgeting and rolling forecasts. Explain variances and report revenue and EBITDA against forecast to support performance and incentive reporting for senior leadership and ownership.
Partner with growing, operations and other department leaders to develop financial and operational metrics, monitor costs and profitability, and assess capital investments, pricing, product decisions and contracts.
Forecast and manage cash flow, maintain banking and lender relationships, prepare lender reporting packages and monitor compliance with debt covenants. Support financing, capital planning and long-term budgeting.
Maintain documented accounting policies, procedures and internal controls that safeguard assets and support accurate reporting. Identify and help manage financial and credit risks.
Coordinate annual reviews or audits with external accountants and oversee tax filings, payroll remittances and government reporting.
Lead, coach and develop the accounting team and manage outsourced accounting relationships.
Improve accounting processes, ERP systems and management reporting to increase accuracy and efficiency.

Your background includes:

A bachelor’s or master’s degree in accounting, finance, business administration or an equivalent qualification. A CPA designation is strongly preferred.
Six to eight years of progressively responsible finance or accounting experience, including experience leading or supervising staff.
Working knowledge of ASPE, multi-entity consolidation, internal controls, budgeting, forecasting and cost control.
Experience with lender reporting and debt covenant compliance.
Proficiency with financial reporting software and ERP systems, along with advanced Excel skills. Experience with Sage 300 is an asset.
The ability to explain financial results clearly to non-finance leaders and owners, work constructively through disagreements and maintain accuracy under pressure.
A hands-on approach, sound judgment and discretion with confidential information. You take ownership of your work, welcome feedback and pursue ongoing professional development.
Experience in agriculture, agribusiness, greenhouse or food production, or another seasonal, capital-intensive business is an asset. Experience in a family-owned or owner-managed business is also an asset.

The role works across two locations (Chatham, ON and Dresden, ON) and is structured around a 40-hour work week, with flexibility required during reporting, budgeting and lender deadlines.
Periodic remote work may be considered after onboarding.

Litherland & Co. is dedicated to fair and equal opportunities for all applicants. Candidates are selected upon the highest level of equity, diversity, and inclusion across the organization and throughout its hiring process. If you are selected for an interview and require accommodations, arrangements will be made for your convenience throughout the recruitment.

jobs.description:
President | Global Manufacturing

Confidential Executive Search

Hamilton (Stoney Creek), Ontario

Own the P&L. Lead the operating companies. Decide where the business grows next.

If you’ve led manufacturing businesses across borders, grown revenue profitably, and built leadership teams that deliver, this is a chance to do it at the president level. You’ll take the helm of a profitable manufacturing division within a privately held, Canadian family-owned group. You’ll report directly to the CEO, lead an established executive team, and have full P&L accountability across a portfolio of businesses serving Tier 1 suppliers and OEM customers.

The mandate is to grow the businesses that have earned their place in the market, identify where the group can win next, and put capital and talent behind those opportunities.

Why are we looking for you?

Our client wants a President who can walk a plant floor and see where the business can improve, sit down with a major customer and uncover where it can grow, and make a clear case to the Board for where it should invest. We’re looking for someone who can point to the decisions they made, the teams they built, and the results they delivered.

What will you do?

Set the growth agenda.
Decide which markets, customer relationships, partnerships, and new business lines warrant investment, then lead the work to turn those decisions into profitable growth.
Own the financial and operating results.
Lead the division’s P&L and set clear priorities for margin improvement, capital investment, automation, and performance across its international operations.
Lead the leaders.
Coach and challenge the executives running the operating businesses, give them clear ownership of their results, and develop the next generation of leadership.
Get close to the business.
Spend time with plant teams and key customers to understand what’s driving performance and where better products, processes, or technology can create an advantage.
Work directly with the CEO and Boards.
Present performance, investment recommendations, and strategic trade-offs to the parent company’s Board and lead the operating company boards.

What do you bring?

10+ years of senior leadership in manufacturing
, with experience overseeing multiple plants or operating businesses across international markets.
Full P&L ownership
and a record of growing a manufacturing business profitably, with specific examples of the revenue, margin, or operating gains you led.
Experience serving Tier 1 or OEM customers
and building commercial relationships at the executive level. Automotive, rail, and food manufacturing are especially relevant.
Sound judgment on capital allocation, automation, and continuous improvement
, with the ability to explain the business case and see the investment through.
A track record of developing senior leaders, building succession plans, and earning trust
with employees, customers, owners, and Boards.
A bachelor’s degree in engineering or business. A relevant master’s degree is an asset.

What’s in it for you?

You’ll lead a profitable division with established customer relationships, an experienced executive team, and operations across North America and Asia. You’ll have the scope to shape the portfolio and make decisions that matter to the long-term owners of the business.

Compensation:
Executive base salary plus a performance-based bonus.
Travel:
Regular domestic and US travel plus quarterly international trips to Asia.

Interested in a confidential conversation?

Apply with your resume or reach out directly to MT Talent Solutions (Guillaume Miszczak)
. We’d like to hear about a manufacturing business you helped grow and the decisions you made to get it there. All inquiries and applications will be handled confidentially.

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
Help shape the future of Thunder Bay’s Waterfront District

The Waterfront District is home to independent businesses, restaurants, arts and culture, and one of Thunder Bay’s greatest assets: Lake Superior. It is a place with a strong identity and considerable potential. It also faces real challenges, from vacant properties and pressure on local businesses to the need for more activity, investment, and coordinated action.

The Waterfront District Business Improvement Area (BIA) is looking for an Executive Director who

can bring people together, represent local businesses, and turn priorities into visible progress.
This is a hands-on leadership opportunity for someone who enjoys working directly with people and wants to make a difference in a neighbourhood they can see and experience every day.

The opportunity

Working with the Board of Management, you will lead the BIA’s work to strengthen the district as

a vibrant place to visit, do business, live, and invest.
You will be a visible presence among members
and community partners, a practical advocate for the district, and the person who keeps the organization focused on results.

What you will help achieve

▪ Strategic leadership.
Turn the BIA’s strategic priorities into achievable plans, make sound choices
about where to focus limited resources, and keep the Board informed of progress and emerging
opportunities.
▪ Member relationships and advocacy.
Build trust with business and property owners. Work
constructively with the City and community partners to advance shared priorities, including cleaner,
more welcoming public spaces, stronger support for businesses, and conditions that encourage
investment.
▪ Programs and district development.
Build on the Waterfront District’s cultural and culinary
strengths through events, promotions, and partnerships that bring people downtown throughout the
year. Help advance conversations about vacant properties, residential growth, and a more active
mixed-use district, recognizing that many of these outcomes depend on partners.
▪ Organizational management and Board support.
Keep day-to-day operations, communications,
and finances well managed. Support the Board with clear information and recommendations, and
explore practical ways to strengthen the BIA’s funding and capacity over time.

You may be a good fit if you…

▪ Build strong working relationships with people who have different interests and perspectives.
▪ Can move from a conversation with a business owner to a meeting with City staff or the Board, and
communicate effectively in each setting.
▪ Are organized, resourceful, and comfortable taking responsibility for both plans and practical follow-through.
▪ Understand budgets, priorities, and accountability, and know when to seek advice or support.
▪ Care about local business, downtown development, and the future of Thunder Bay.

Experience and potential

Experience in leadership, business, community development, economic development, association
management, or a related field would be valuable. Familiarity with municipal processes, Board governance, advocacy, events, or marketing would be an asset. We are interested in what you have accomplished, how you work with people, and your ability to learn.

We recognize that strong candidates may bring different combinations of experience and skills. If you have the judgment, initiative, and relationship-building ability this role requires but are still
developing in some areas, we encourage you to apply. For the right candidate, the Board is open to discussing a scope of responsibility and development plan that allows you to grow into the full

Executive Director mandate.

What success could look like in your first year

▪ Members see an accessible, responsive BIA that understands their priorities.
▪ The Board has a realistic action plan, clear reporting, and evidence of progress on its strategic
priorities.
▪ District events and partnerships support more consistent activity and a stronger Waterfront identity.
▪ The BIA has strengthened its working relationships with the City and other partners on issues it
cannot resolve alone.

Compensation and how to apply

The salary range is $60,000–$75,000, with the starting salary and responsibilities to be discussed based on experience and the agreed scope of the role.

Please submit a resume and brief cover letter explaining your interest in the Waterfront District and the results you would bring to this role.

Apply to:
melissa@compassleadership.ca
Deadline:
December 11, 2026

The Waterfront District BIA welcomes applications from candidates with diverse backgrounds and experiences. Only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.description:
**ABOUT US**



SickKids Foundation, with over 50 years of philanthropic impact is Canada's largest charitable funder of child health research, learning and care, raising over $200 million last year. As a national charity, SickKids Foundation invests in national and international initiatives to benefit children in Canada and around the world. As the fundraising partner to The Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids), we are aligned in supporting Precision Child Health (PCH), the future of tailoring medicine to each child's unique traits so SickKids can diagnose faster, treat smarter, and predict better.



We are driven by our core values of integrity, collaboration, excellence, innovation, and inclusion, with goals of delivering a superior donor experience, investing in our people and culture, driving innovative and sustainable fundraising, and disrupting the market through data and technology.



SickKids Foundation is committed to an inclusive culture by embedding equity, diversity and inclusion in our policies, practices, and behaviours. We aim to build awareness and skills in this area, both internally and with our partners. Our commitment extends to creating a safe, positive work environment. For details on our Equity, Diversity \& Inclusion commitment, please click here. (https://www.sickkidsfoundation.com/aboutus/equitydiversityandinclusion)



We’re committed to attracting and retaining passionate individuals to help create a healthier future. That’s why SickKids Foundation is looking for a new Associate Director, Development Analytics.


**Description of the Position**



Fundraising is a sales function. It has a pipeline, defined stages, conversion rates, cycle times and coverage ratios—and a frontline team whose time is one of the organization’s scarcest resources.



The Associate Director, Development Analytics owns the analytics behind that pipeline. The role makes fundraising performance visible and measurable, identifies where opportunities exist to improve it, and translates those insights into clear, actionable recommendations for fundraising leaders.



This is a hands\-on role for a sales and pipeline analytics professional. The successful candidate is comfortable working directly with data, building reporting and dashboards, and developing analytical or predictive models when they add value. But the role goes beyond producing reports and models. Its real value is in the analysis: knowing which metrics matter, identifying where the pipeline is performing well or breaking down, uncovering opportunities within fundraiser portfolios, and helping leaders understand what actions they can take as a result.



The role also connects Research Services with frontline fundraising. It translates prospect intelligence and analytical signals into clear, prioritized opportunities so fundraisers can focus their time and effort on the prospects with the greatest potential.



The Associate Director, Development Analytics is a key role within the Business Intelligence \& Analytics team. Reporting directly to the Director, Development Analytics, you will provide functional leadership for Development Analytics, serve as the authoritative advisor to Development leadership, and partner across the analytics function: with Data Science \& Engineering to ensure development data is well modelled and accessible, with Research Services to turn prospect intelligence into action, and with Marketing Analytics to build end\-to\-end visibility from donor acquisition through the development pipeline.



You will play a central role in delivering the Foundation's Data \& Analytics Strategy (DAS) for Development, setting the analytics roadmap, standards and priorities and executing key use cases that build analytics maturity and drive measurable value for fundraising and the broader organization.


**Key Responsibilities**


**Functional Leadership \& Roadmap**


* Provide functional leadership for Development Analytics, integrating pipeline, portfolio, revenue, campaign and donor analytics across Development.
* Establish and maintain the Development Analytics roadmap, operating model, methodologies, standards and tools within the approved Development strategy and the DAS.
* Own the development analytics intake process: prioritize, approve, defer or redirect analytics requests so that priorities are clear, timelines are met and the team is set up to deliver with consistency and quality.
* Serve as the authoritative advisor to Development leadership on forecasting, portfolio optimization, prospect strategy, performance measurement and the effective allocation of fundraising resources.
* Maintain and enforce analytics processes and standards, and hold stakeholders accountable for agreed data inputs and business requirements.
* Measure and report on the adoption and impact of analytics products.
* Resolve conflicting business requirements, data limitations and competing analytical priorities across Development, determining when existing approaches should be adapted or replaced.
* Anticipate emerging business needs and initiate analytical work that may challenge current assumptions, practices or resource\-allocation decisions.


**Pipeline, Portfolio \& Performance Analytics**


* Own development pipeline analytics: stage progression, conversion and win rates, cycle time and velocity, coverage ratios, average gift size and slippage, by fundraiser, portfolio, segment and campaign.
* Independently identify and frame where the funnel is underperforming and why, including emerging issues where the problem and approach are not yet defined, and bring forward specific, prioritized recommendations rather than describing the numbers.
* Partner with fundraising leadership on portfolio construction and optimization: right\-sizing portfolios, balancing prospect capacity against fundraiser bandwidth, surfacing under\-worked or misassigned prospects, and analyzing frontline productivity to improve return on fundraiser tim

jobs.title: Executive Vice President of Regional Management
jobs.description:
Position Overview

The Executive Vice President of Regional Management is responsible for overseeing the company's regional business operations, developing regional management strategies, and ensuring effective execution of corporate objectives across assigned geographic markets.

This executive provides strategic direction to regional leadership teams, monitors regional business performance, manages operational priorities, and identifies opportunities for business expansion and organizational development.

The role works closely with the CEO, COO, and other senior executives to align regional activities with corporate strategies, strengthen management accountability, improve operational performance, and support the company's long-term growth.

The ideal candidate has extensive executive leadership experience, a strong understanding of regional business management, and a proven ability to oversee multiple business units, geographic markets, and senior management teams.

Key Responsibilities

1. Regional Strategy and Executive Leadership

Develop and implement regional management strategies aligned with the company's overall corporate objectives.

Establish regional business priorities, management objectives, and long-term development plans.

Translate corporate strategies into actionable regional execution plans.

Provide strategic direction and executive oversight to regional directors, managers, and business unit leaders.

Evaluate regional market conditions and identify opportunities for business growth and operational improvement.

Advise the CEO and senior leadership team on regional business performance, expansion opportunities, and management priorities.

2. Regional Business Operations Oversight

Oversee business operations across assigned geographic regions and regional business units.

Ensure regional teams operate in accordance with corporate policies, operational standards, and established business objectives.

Monitor regional operational performance and address issues affecting business continuity or execution.

Establish consistent management practices and operating procedures across regional offices.

Coordinate regional operational initiatives to improve organizational efficiency and business performance.

Ensure regional management teams have the resources and support necessary to achieve their objectives.

3. Regional Performance and Accountability

Establish regional performance targets and key performance indicators (KPIs).

Review regional financial and operational results against established business objectives.

Evaluate revenue performance, operating expenses, productivity, and regional business growth.

Hold regional executives and department leaders accountable for performance outcomes.

Identify performance gaps and direct the development of corrective action plans.

Present regular regional performance assessments and strategic recommendations to executive leadership.

4. Regional Market Development and Expansion

Identify new geographic markets and business opportunities for regional expansion.

Evaluate market conditions, competitive environments, and regional business potential.

Develop regional growth strategies in collaboration with business development and corporate strategy teams.

Oversee the execution of regional expansion initiatives and new market development programs.

Build relationships with regional business partners, industry stakeholders, and strategic organizations.

Assess the operational and financial requirements associated with regional expansion.

5. Senior Management and Organizational Development

Recruit, lead, mentor, and develop regional senior management personnel in coordination with the appropriate departments.

Establish leadership expectations, management responsibilities, and organizational accountability.

Evaluate regional leadership effectiveness and identify succession planning needs.

Strengthen communication and coordination between corporate headquarters and regional management teams.

Develop management structures that support regional growth and organizational scalability.

Promote a results-oriented leadership culture across all assigned regions.

6. Financial and Resource Management

Oversee regional budget planning and resource allocation in coordination with the finance department.

Review regional operating budgets, financial forecasts, and expenditure performance.

Ensure regional resources are aligned with corporate priorities and business requirements.

Identify opportunities to improve cost efficiency and operational productivity.

Evaluate the financial implications of regional business initiatives and expansion plans.

Work with finance leadership to maintain appropriate financial oversight and budget accountability.

7. Cross-Functional Executive Coordination

Collaborate with the COO, CFO, regional directors, and other senior executives to coordinate corporate and regional priorities.

Ensure effective cooperation between regional operations, finance, marketing, sales, customer experience, and business development teams.

Resolve major cross-regional management challenges and organizational issues.

Facilitate communication between corporate headquarters and regional business units.

Coordinate strategic initiatives that require participation from multiple departments or geographic markets.

Ensure regional execution remains consistent with company-wide business strategies.

8. Risk Management and Corporate Governance

Oversee regional management practices to ensure alignment with corporate governance requirements.

Identify regional operational, financial, and business risks and coordinate appropriate mitigation strategies.

Ensure regional management teams follow established company policies and internal control procedures.

Work with legal, compliance, and internal audit teams on regional governance matters.

Escalate significant regional business risks and management issues to executive leadership.

Promote transparency, accountability, and responsible decision-making across regional operations.

9. Executive Reporting and Strategic Decision-Making

Provide regular reports on regional business performance, operational results, and strategic initiatives.

Present regional management updates and recommendations to the CEO and executive leadership team.

Evaluate the effectiveness of regional strategies and recommend adjustments when necessary.

Provide executive-level insights into market developments, organizational performance, and expansion opportunities.

Lead high-priority regional management initiatives and monitor their implementation.

Support corporate strategic planning through regional business intelligence and management analysis.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Management, Finance, Economics, or a related field.

Master's degree in Business Administration (MBA) or a related discipline is preferred.

Minimum of 20 years of professional experience in business management, regional operations, or executive leadership.

At least 10 years of experience in senior management, multi-regional leadership, or executive-level operational oversight.

Demonstrated experience managing multiple geographic markets, regional business units, or senior leadership teams.

Strong knowledge of business strategy, regional management, operational performance, and organizational development.

Proven ability to develop and execute regional business plans.

Experience managing budgets, performance targets, and organizational resources.

Excellent executive communication, negotiation, and decision-making skills.

Ability to lead complex business initiatives and coordinate cross-functional executive teams.

jobs.location: New York City Office NYO1; Redwood City; Toronto; Dallas Infomart Office DAI
jobs.description:
Who are we? 
 Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.   

A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future. 

A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work. 

 We are looking for a Senior Director to lead our AMER Enterprise Customer Success Management organization at an important point in the evolution of Customer Success Management at Equinix.  This leader will be responsible for translating our global Customer Success Management strategy into a value-led, data-driven regional operating model that strengthens customer relationships, improves value realization, identifies and mitigates risk, and drives predictable retention, renewals and growth.  

 The role requires more than operating an established Customer Success Management organization. We are looking for a builder and transformation leader who can help shape how Customer Success operates - combining high-touch customer engagement with data, digital capabilities, automation and AI to create a more proactive and scalable customer experience.  The Senior Director will lead CSM teams across AMER and serve as a senior Customer Success partner to AMER Sales leadership and teams across Equinix. Success will require the ability to set a clear vision, simplify complexity, develop strong leaders, and turn strategy into consistent execution across a diverse region.

 Key Responsibilities: 

 Lead a value-led Customer Success organization 
 Build a culture in which Customer Success begins with understanding customer priorities and desired outcomes. Ensure CSMs translate those priorities into Success Plans, value realization, adoption strategies, executive engagement and measurable customer outcomes. 
 Own retention, renewals and commercial performance 
 Be accountable for regional retention and renewal performance and predictability. Establish disciplined renewal management, forecasting and risk practices while strengthening CSM commercial acumen and accountability. Partner closely with Sales on renewal strategy, expansion opportunities and long-term customer value. 
 Build a proactive, data-driven engagement model 
 Use customer health, risk, lifecycle, commercial and behavioral signals to help CSMs prioritize where and how they engage. Drive a shift from reactive account management toward proactive engagement focused on value, risk, renewal and growth. 
 Operationalize the global Customer Success Management model across AMER 
 Translate global coverage, segmentation and engagement standards into disciplined regional execution while accounting for the needs of AMER customers and markets. Establish clear expectations engagement models and ensure consistent execution of core Customer Success Management motions. 
 Scale Customer Success through digital, automation and AI 
 Champion the use of technology to increase CSM capacity and improve the customer experience. Partner with global teams to incorporate digital journeys, automation, AI and agentic capabilities into the Customer Success operating model allowing CSMs to focus their time where human relationships, judgment and expertise create the greatest value. 
 Create consistent customer engagement and value rhythms 
 Drive consistent execution of Success Planning, Customer Business Reviews, health and risk management, renewal readiness and executive engagement. Ensure these motions are focused on customer outcomes rather than activity completion. 
 Partner deeply with AMER Sales and cross-functional leaders 
 Serve as the senior Customer Success counterpart to AMER Sales leadership. Build strong partnerships across Sales, Service Management, Renewals, Support, Product, Marketing, Operations, Finance and other teams to create a coordinated post-sale customer experience and remove barriers to customer outcomes. 
 Clarify CSM and Service Management accountability 
 Help establish clear accountability between value-led Customer Success Management and operational Service Management. Reduce unnecessary handoffs, eliminate ambiguity and ensure CSM capacity remains focused on customer value, retention and growth. 
 Manage material customer and commercial risk 
 Provide executive oversight for significant customer, relationship and renewal risks that cannot be resolved at the account or manager level. Ensure risks are identified early, clearly understood and addressed cross-functionally. 
 Build and develop an exceptional regional leadership team 
 Lead and coach CSM leaders across the AMERs. Build leadership capability in value articulation, commercial acumen, executive engagement, change leadership and disciplined execution. Own regional workforce planning and ensure organizational capabilities evolve alongside the Customer Success model. 
 Lead transformation and continuous improvement 
 Create belief in the future-state Customer Success model and translate transformation strategy into clear expectations and behaviors. Challenge legacy practices, remove barriers to change, and establish a culture of measurement, experimentation and continuous improvement. 

 Skills, Experience & Qualifications 
 We are looking for a leader who brings:
 Extensive experience leading Customer Success or related GTM organizations. 
 Demonstrated experience building and operationalizing value-led Customer Success motions, including Success Planning, value realization, adoption, customer health, risk management and executive engagement. 
 Proven accountability for retention, renewals, renewal forecasting and commercial performance. 
 Experience leading segmented Customer Success Management models and operating across differentiated coverage approaches such as high-touch, pooled and digital. 
 Experience using data, customer signals and analytics to prioritize engagement and improve customer outcomes. 
 Strong understanding of how digital Customer Success, automation and AI can increase scale and improve customer experience without sacrificing important human relationships. 
 Experience leading significant operating-model or organizational transformation and bringing teams through meaningful change. 
 Demonstrated ability to build strong partnerships with Sales and senior cross-functional leaders. 
 Experience developing leaders and building high-performing Customer Success Management organizations. 
 Bachelor's degree in a business-related discipline or equivalent experience. 

 Leadership Characteristics 
 The successful candidate will be:
 A builder and operator who can move comfortably between strategy and execution. 
 A customer- and value-first leader who understands the connection between customer outcomes, retention and growth. 
 A strong commercial leader who is comfortable owning renewal performance and predictability. 
 A digital-first thinker who sees technology, automation and AI as ways to enhance, not replace, the customer relationship. 
 A strong simplifier who can turn complex strategies into clear priorities and operating expectations. 
 A confident leader of leaders with a strong coaching and talent-development mindset. 
 Highly effective at influencing across organizational boundaries and building alignment with Sales and other functions. 
 Data-informed and comfortable using signals and metrics to drive decisions. 
 Comfortable operating with ambiguity and leading through significant transformation. 
 Willing to roll up their sleeves when necessary to turn a vision into an operating reality. 

 Equinix Benefits 
 As an employee, you become important to Equinix’s success. We ensure all your benefits are in line with our core values: competitive, inclusive, sustainable, connected and efficient. We keep them competitive within the current marketplace to ensure we’re providing you with the best package possible. So, wherever you are in your career and life, you’ll be able to enhance your experience and bring your whole self to work.

 Employee Assistance Program: An Employee Assistance program is available to all employees.

US Benefits: - Insurance: You may enroll in health, life, disability and voluntary plans that are designed for you and your eligible family members. - Retirement: You and Equinix may contribute to a retirement plan to help you plan for your financial future. - Paid Time Off (PTO) and Paid Holidays: You will receive an accrued amount of PTO each pay period along with various paid holidays for you to rest and recharge. Eligibility requirements apply to some benefits. Benefits are subject to change and may be subject to specific plan or program terms.

Canada Core Benefits: - Insurance: You may enroll in healthcare coverage that is designed to complement the provincial healthcare system, along with life, disability and optional benefit plans that are designed for you and your eligible family members. - Retirement: You may also enroll in Equinix-sponsored retirement or savings plans: Defined Contribution Pension Plan (DCPP), Group Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP) and Tax-Free Savings Plan (TSFA). - Vacation and Paid Holidays: Equinix offers both vacation and personal time, along with various paid holidays for you to rest and recharge. Eligibility requirements apply to some benefits. Benefits are subject to specific plan or program terms, and to change at Equinix discretion.

 What is the opportunity? 
 As a strategic leader, you will support the transformation of the organization's operational readiness for the next AI era. You will pivot the organization from passive analytics toward human-controlled, Agentic AI operations—autonomous, multi-agent systems capable of reasoning, planning, tool usage and workflow execution, while maintaining controls and managing risk. You will support transformation and change management teams, bridging the gap between technical AI capability and human-centred organizational adoption. By establishing continuous learning ecosystems, supporting change management, leading AI governance frameworks and supporting PCO AI strategy, you will ensure employees are equipped, confident, excited and proactive in co-working alongside intelligent software agents. 

 What will you do? 
 AI Transformation Strategy & Roadmap: Align with Operations leaders on the transformation vision and support execution of a multi-year roadmap for moving teams from static generative AI tools to autonomous agent workflows; manage and improve frameworks for identifying high-value processes for agent-based automation.
 Agent Governance Framework Lead the development and maintenance of governance for operations agent development, including approval workflows, maintenance standards, and risk assessment criteria.
 Risk, Guardrails & Compliance Oversee risk review processes for user agent deployment, define operational guardrails and safety protocols from an operational perspective, and work with Ops risk, Risk and Compliance to ensure regulatory and internal control alignment. 
 AI Learning & Capability Development Deploy and maintain role-based AI learning tracks, from foundational AI literacy to advanced human-in-the-loop system design, and collaborate with internal, academic, vendor, and training partners to keep content current. 
 Adoption Support change management efforts to address role displacement concerns and build trust in autonomous systems. 
 Strategy Communication & Forum Facilitation Coordinate communication of the PCO AI strategy and programs with strategy and enablement teams, and organize and facilitate strategic AI meetings and forums, including agendas, minutes, and action tracking. 
 Leadership Support & Operations Provide administrative and operational support to the VP of Ops Data and AI to keep the team engaged and compliant.

 What do you need to succeed? 
 Must-have 
 Agentic AI and automation: Hands-on exposure to autonomous agents, workflow orchestration, or human-in-the-loop system design
 Operations transformation: Experience partnering with operational leaders to redesign processes and drive adoption
 Stakeholder management: Experience influencing senior executives and coordinating across risk, compliance, legal, and business units
 Data and AI strategy: Experience setting multi-year roadmaps for AI, analytics, or digital transformation in a large organization
 Governance and risk: Familiarity with model risk, AI governance, or technology risk frameworks, ideally in a regulated industry such as banking

 Nice-to-have 
 Change management: Experience leading workforce adoption or change initiatives, including communicating role impacts 
 Regulatory knowledge: Understanding of Canadian AI and banking regulation, such as OSFI guidance and privacy requirements

jobs.title: VP Product Innovation, Modern Campus
jobs.description:
About Modern Campus 
 Modern Campus empowers institutions to move with confidence across the modern learner journey. Our platform spans web content management, curriculum and catalog management, student engagement and lifelong learning — giving more than 1,700 colleges and universities the infrastructure they need to support the entire learner-to-earner lifecycle and deliver personalized, scalable experiences. 

  We partner with the education community to create new pathways for learning and opportunity, reimagining how institutions serve the modern learner and shape the future of education. 

 Our purpose — our north star — is to empower institutions to confidently serve and support the modern learner. 

  This mission and purpose come to life through how we show up every day: 
 We exist to create empowerment through education. 
 We lead with honesty and empathy. 
 We shape the future through innovation. 
 We become trusted partners. 
 We make the complex feel possible. Position Summary 
 Modern Campus is seeking a visionary and execution-oriented Vice President, Product Innovation to identify, validate, build, and scale new product opportunities while transforming how we develop products through AI-enabled and agentic practices. 

 This leader will serve as the company's innovation catalyst, balancing customer discovery, strategic product incubation, and organizational transformation. The Vice President, Product Innovation will lead the creation of new offerings that expand our portfolio while establishing scalable, AI-native product development capabilities that accelerate speed, quality, and customer value across the organization. 

 The role partners closely with Product Management, Engineering, Design, Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, and Executive Leadership to drive growth through both new products and new ways of building products. 
 What You'll Do 
 Product Innovation & New Venture Development 
 Identify, validate, and launch innovative software products that address emerging challenges and opportunities in higher education. 
 Lead customer discovery, market research, and rapid experimentation to assess new market opportunities. 
 Build and test MVPs, prototypes, and pilot programs to validate customer demand and commercial viability. 
 Define business models, pricing strategies, and go-to-market approaches for new offerings. 
 Partner with Product, Engineering, Design, Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success teams to successfully transition validated concepts into scalable businesses. 
 Develop and manage an innovation portfolio that balances incremental improvements with transformative growth opportunities. 
 Foster a culture of experimentation, learning, and innovation across the product organization. 
 AI-Enabled Product Development Leadership 
 Define and champion Modern Campus's vision for AI-enabled and agentic product development. 
 Establish best practices for leveraging AI across the product lifecycle, including customer research, discovery, requirements gathering, prototyping, documentation, testing, experimentation, and product operations. 
 Evaluate emerging AI technologies and identify opportunities to improve how product teams operate and deliver value. 
 Develop repeatable frameworks, playbooks, governance models, and adoption strategies for responsible AI implementation. 
 Partner with Product, Engineering, and Design leaders to embed AI-native practices into day-to-day product development workflows. 
 Measure and continuously improve the impact of AI-enabled practices on customer outcomes, delivery speed, and organizational effectiveness. 
 Promote a culture of experimentation, continuous learning, and responsible AI adoption across the company. 
 Executive Leadership & Collaboration 
 Influence company strategy through innovation insights, customer feedback, and emerging market opportunities. 
 Communicate vision, strategy, business cases, and outcomes effectively to executive leadership and key stakeholders. 
 Build alignment across departments to accelerate innovation initiatives and organizational transformation. 
 Serve as a thought leader on AI, product innovation, and emerging technology trends. 
 What You'll Bring 
 Required Qualifications 
 Proven experience leading software products from concept through customer validation, commercial launch, and post-launch scaling. 
 Experience building and managing innovation portfolios, product incubators, or venture-style product development initiatives. 
 Demonstrated success delivering revenue-generating software products, including business model development, pricing strategy, and go-to-market execution. 
 Deep understanding of artificial intelligence technologies and their application to software product development. 
 Hands-on experience leveraging AI tools and agentic workflows to accelerate product development and decision-making. 
 Strong executive presence and communication skills with the ability to influence strategy and organizational change. 
 Proven ability to operate effectively in fast-paced, ambiguous, and rapidly evolving environments. 
 10+ years of progressive product leadership experience within a software organization. 
 Experience leading cross-functional teams, major product launches, and strategic initiatives. 
 Preferred Qualifications 
 MBA or advanced business degree. 
 Experience in higher education, education technology, SaaS, or other complex B2B software markets. 
 Experience scaling AI-enabled product organizations. 
 Track record of launching net-new businesses, platforms, or product categories. 
 Success in This Role 
 Within the first 12–24 months, successful outcomes may include: 
 Launching three or more new product experiments into market. 
 Creating a repeatable and measurable innovation pipeline from idea to commercialization. 
 Generating meaningful new revenue streams from newly launched offerings. 
 Increasing product team effectiveness through AI-enabled workflows and agentic development practices. 
 Improving speed-to-market and customer value realization across the product portfolio. 
 Establishing Modern Campus as a leader in AI-enabled product innovation within higher education technology. 
 Why Join Modern Campus? 
 At Modern Campus, we're transforming how higher education institutions engage learners throughout the entire student lifecycle. We believe meaningful growth comes from understanding our customers, connecting their challenges to the right solutions, and creating experiences that deliver measurable value. 
 This role offers an opportunity to shape the future of demand generation at Modern Campus, building innovative, data-driven marketing strategies that strengthen customer engagement, accelerate growth, and connect marketing impact to business outcomes.

jobs.title: VP of Business Operations
jobs.description:
We're the all-in-one agentic marketing platform. AI-native from day one. We're not joining a category, we're defining it.

We're looking for our CEO's second in command. This role owns the operating system of the company and ensures every department has clear priorities, measurable goals, and accountable leadership.
If you want real ownership, to move fast, and raise the bar every week, keep reading. If you want a big title and a seat at the table without actually running anything, this isn't it.

What you'll own

Manage all department heads. Set expectations, hold them to their numbers, and keep work moving smoothly across teams without bottlenecks.
Turn the CEO's strategy into quarterly plans with clear owners and deadlines.
Oversee the finance team: cash flow, forecasting, reporting and vendor spend.
Own legal and compliance: contracts, employment matters and outside lawyers.
Run our EOS meetings, quarterly goals (rocks) and company scorecards.
Lead AI and automation across the company. Decide what AI agents handle and get every team using them.
Document how work gets done so it doesn't depend on one person. Roll out new tools and processes with People Ops.

What we're looking for

About 8 years of operations experience, including a senior leadership role (Director, VP, COO or similar).
Experience managing other managers or department heads.
Experience overseeing finance: budgets, cash flow, forecasting and reporting.
Experience handling contracts, employment matters and outside lawyers.
Experience running EOS or a similar planning system (quarterly goals, scorecards, weekly leadership meetings).
Hands on experience using AI to automate real work, like AI agents, connected tools or dashboards that update themselves.
Based in the US or Canada, working primarily Eastern hours and can flex for critical company needs, launches, and leadership situations.

You'll thrive here if...

You've run operations across a whole company, not just one team.
You can tell a department head their numbers are off and still have a good working relationship on Monday.
You get a real kick out of turning chaos into a system someone else can run.
You don't wait to be told what to do. You see the gap and you move.
Deadlines don't rattle you. Ambiguity doesn't either.
You're an AI power user, not someone who's "open to learning it someday."
You communicate clearly, especially when things are unclear.
You have opinions and you're not afraid to bring them.
You can laugh at a chaotic week on Friday and mean it.

What working here actually looks like

High expectations. Real ownership. Things change fast and we don't apologize for it. You'll work with smart people who push you, a product that keeps getting better, and a team that's genuinely building something new.
We'll probably give you more to own than you expected. That's on purpose.
We use AI every day, across every function. That's just how we work.

We're the all-in-one agentic marketing platform, AI-native from day one. Our tools help marketing teams move faster, make smarter decisions, and do more with less. We're defining a new category and we're looking for people who want to be part of it.

Join EY and help to build a better working world.

Payroll is a business\-critical function, and organizations are looking for more efficient, technology\-enabled ways to deliver it.

  

We’re looking for a senior payroll or employment tax professional who knows the market, sees where it’s going and wants to turn those insights into growth.

This is an opportunity to combine payroll leadership, client delivery and commercial thinking while helping shape the growth of EY’s Payroll Operate business in Canada and contribute to the global business.

**Qualifications**

**Ideally, you’ll also have,**

Are you ready to shape your future with confidence? Apply today.

NTT DATA strives to hire exceptional, innovative and passionate individuals who want to grow with us. If you want to be part of an inclusive, adaptable, and forward-thinking organization, apply now.

We are currently seeking a Chief Architect & Design Authority to join our team in Remote, British Columbia (CA-BC), Canada (CA).

Purpose of the role

Global Platforms is moving to a product-led platform organization in which AI agents run more and more of the service-management work, under clear governance. This Chief Architect & Design Authority position will be the single design authority for that platform. This role sets the architecture, standards and certification that every team builds and deploys against, independently of any one build or delivery team. The role reports to the Head of Core Engineering because its standards apply equally across all four pillars. Keeping design authority separate from build and run accountability means standards stay consistent and reusable, and are never relaxed to meet one team's delivery pressure.

Key Responsibilities

Architecture and standards
Own the Global Platforms reference architecture: One NTT Platform foundation, One Experience Platform, Composable modules, cloud tools and client tools.
Define and maintain the Agentic Service Management reference model: ITIL 4 practices as the process map, IT4IT as the reference architecture, and a standard decomposition from process to vendor adapter.
Set vendor-neutral interface standards (including MCP-based tool interfaces) and adapter conformance tests.
Define the action envelope standard.
Design authority and certification
Chair the platform design authority.
Certify agents, automations and action envelopes before production or delivery.
Own the agent and automation registry standard.
Agentic platform architecture
Lead the architecture of the NTT-owned control plane.
Provide technical oversight of the Incident process PoC and Phase 2 design.
Keep portable process specifications and envelope catalogue outside any single vendor.
Technology strategy and vendor architecture
Advise on build, buy or integrate decisions.
Shape partner architecture relationships with ServiceNow, Microsoft, LogicMonitor, Cisco and hyperscalers.
Own cloud tools architecture.
Provide tooling rationalization input.
Engineering standards
Set architectural guardrails for CI/CD, testing, IaC, SRE and golden paths.
Ensure self-service capabilities support engineering and composable modules.
Client and security engagement
Represent architecture to client boards.
Work with the CISO office on security architecture.
Innovation and people
Assess innovation funnel opportunities.
Lead and develop the architecture team and community of practice.

Key relationships

Global Head of Platform Technology & Innovation.
Head of Engineering, Global Platform: line manager.
Pillar leads: peers and consumers of standards.
Release & Service Introduction lead: joint owner of certification.
C&S delivery, sales and solution architecture leadership.
CISO office.
Partners: ServiceNow, Microsoft, LogicMonitor, Cisco, hyperscalers.

Decision rights

Decides: reference architecture, standards, approvals and certification outcomes.
Recommends: build/buy/integrate, vendor choices, investment priorities.
Escalates: disputed design authority decisions and exceptions.

Success measures (first 12 months)

Reference architecture and Agentic Service Management standards adopted.
Design authority and certification operating with production agents registered and certified.
Phase 1 Agentic Operation delivered and Phase 2 approved.
Interface standards and conformance tests in use.
Architecture input into license rationalization and FY27 planning.
Architecture community established.

Experience And Capabilities

Senior enterprise or platform architect with 15+ years experience.
Experience setting and enforcing architecture standards.
Knowledge of ITIL 4 and IT4IT or equivalent.
Experience with automation, AIOps, observability and agentic/GenAI systems.
Knowledge of ServiceNow and hyperscaler AI platforms.
Integration architecture experience.

If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.

You’ll define how partners onboard, build expertise, deliver customer value, and grow their businesses while shaping lifecycle programs, operating models, and measurable success outcomes. By helping partners deliver secure, reliable experiences for their customers, you’ll extend 1Password’s mission to more organizations.

We’re using AI to work smarter and align teams faster, from drafting partnership proposals and generating intelligence briefings to creating product mock-ups and demos that support impactful cross-functional work. AI also helps us bring clarity and consistency to our day-to-day operations, giving us more time for strategic thinking, relationship-building, and meaningful collaboration across 1Password.

What We're Looking For

Bring 12+ years of experience in partner success, customer success, channel operations, or related roles in Business-to-Business (B2B) software, including experience leading teams and managing managers. Experience within an AI-forward organization is considered a strong asset.
Demonstrate success building or scaling a partner-facing organization with measurable improvements in partner productivity, customer retention, expansion, and satisfaction.
Understand partner business models, particularly managed service providers and resellers, including recurring revenue, service delivery, and the economics of a profitable partner practice.

Apply strong commercial judgment and analytical skills to connect partner engagement and customer adoption with revenue outcomes and investment decisions.
Build trust with partner leaders, lead complex escalations, and influence priorities across Sales, Customer Success, Product, Marketing, Support, Operations, and Finance.
Translate strategy into repeatable processes, lead through change, and establish clear accountability in a growing organization; experience in cybersecurity, identity and access management, or another technically complex Software as a Service (SaaS) category is a plus.

What You Can Expect

Develop joint success plans and executive business reviews that connect partner capability, customer adoption, service delivery, and commercial growth.
Partner with enablement and technical teams on training, certification, deployment readiness, and repeatable practices that help partners deliver successful customer outcomes.
Identify partner and customer risk early, coordinate recovery plans and growth opportunities, and clarify ownership across renewals and commercial execution.

 BMO Capital Markets is a leading, full-service North American-based financial services provider, with over 2,700 professionals in 30+ locations around the world, including 20 offices in North America, offering corporate, institutional and government clients access to a complete range of investment and corporate banking products and services. BMO Capital Markets is a member of BMO Financial Group (NYSE, TSX: BMO), one of the largest diversified financial services providers in North America with US$1.1 trillion total assets and approximately 53,000 employees as of April 30, 2026. #bmocapitalmarkets

 We are hiring a Vice President, Energy Origination to join the Commodities business team in Calgary. The role will help grow BMO's commodities franchise by originating and executing physical and financial energy solutions for corporate and commercial clients. The successful candidate will combine energy market knowledge, commercial judgment and quantitative skills to identify client needs, develop risk-management and financing ideas, and coordinate transactions from initial dialogue through approval and execution. Working closely with Commodities Sales and Trading, Investment and Corporate Banking, Commercial Banking, Credit, Legal and other product partners, the Energy Origination team develops solutions informed by clients' capital structures, operating exposures, physical commodity flows and strategic priorities. The role provides direct client exposure and increasing ownership of relationships and transactions, with support from senior originators and product specialists on more complex mandates.

 KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES

 Client Origination and Relationship Management
 Develop and deepen relationships with a portfolio of existing and prospective energy and commodities clients.
 Identify commodity exposures and commercial objectives through an understanding of clients' operations, physical flows, capital structures, and financing needs.
 Prepare client pitches, market analysis and transaction proposals in partnership with senior originators, trading, structuring and banking coverage teams.
 Support pricing, negotiation and execution of live transactions, taking increasing ownership as experience and product knowledge develop.

 Transaction Structuring and Analysis
 Perform quantitative, financial, credit and documentation analysis for energy transactions.
 Develop customized hedging and risk-management analyses using swaps, options and structured products.
 Work with internal partners to assess market liquidity, optionality, basis risk, regulatory requirements and execution considerations.
 Support the development and commercialization of new solutions that address evolving client needs and commodity-market opportunities.

 Execution, Governance and Risk Management
 Coordinate internal approval and execution processes across Credit, Market Risk, Legal, Documentation, Compliance, Client Onboarding and Operations.
 Develop an understanding of the principal terms of market trade-governing agreements (ISDA, EDI, NAESB etc), including credit support and transaction-specific documentation.
 Apply sound judgment regarding counterparty risk, CVA/FVA, capital, liquidity, suitability, regulatory and conduct considerations.
 Maintain high standards of accuracy, controls and follow-through throughout the transaction lifecycle.

 Collaboration and Franchise Development
 Partner closely with Commodities Sales and Trading to share market intelligence, develop client ideas and solve transaction-specific problems.
 Build productive relationships with Investment and Corporate Banking, Commercial Banking and other Global Markets and Global Origination partners to identify cross-product opportunities.
 Contribute to strategic initiatives, client-planning discussions and market-development efforts for the energy and commodities franchise.
 Support the development of Analysts and Associates through collaboration, knowledge sharing and review of work product.

 QUALIFICATIONS
 Knowledge and Experience
 Relevant experience in commodities, energy markets, derivatives, corporate banking, investment banking, commercial banking, risk management or a related field; direct client-facing experience is preferred.
 Strong understanding of North American energy markets and the commercial exposures of producers, midstream companies, refiners, utilities, industrial users and other market participants.
 Working knowledge of financial and physical commodity products, with experience in OTC derivatives and options considered an asset.
 Familiarity with transaction documentation, counterparty credit and regulatory considerations applicable to commodity transactions.
 University degree in finance, economics, engineering, mathematics, science or another relevant discipline.
 Skills
 Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex market and product concepts into practical client solutions.
 Commercial mindset and demonstrated interest in business development, relationship management, and energy markets.
 Strong quantitative, financial-modeling, and analytical skills, with careful attention to detail.
 Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint and other Microsoft Office applications; experience with Bloomberg, VBA, Python or other analytical tools is an asset.
 Ability to manage multiple priorities, exercise sound judgment, seek guidance when appropriate and adapt to changing market conditions and transaction demands.
 Collaborative approach and ability to work effectively across trading, banking, credit, legal, risk and operational teams.
 High standards of integrity, ownership, accuracy, and client service.

jobs.title: Senior Vice President, Strategy Director
jobs.description:
Edelman is a voice synonymous with trust, reimagining a future where the currency of communication is action. Our culture thrives on three promises: boldness is possibility, empathy is progress, and curiosity is momentum.

At Edelman, we understand diversity, equity, inclusion and belonging (DEIB) transform our colleagues, our company, our clients, and our communities. We are in relentless pursuit of an equitable and inspiring workplace that is respectful of all, reflects and represents the world in which we live, and fosters trust, collaboration and belonging.

 Edelman is a trusted voice helping organizations earn trust through action. Through the Edelman Trust Barometer, the definitive global study of trust, we inform and advise leaders across business, government, media, and civil society on how trust shapes growth, reputation, and societal expectations. Our work is consistently recognized at the industry's highest levels, including Cannes Lions, WARC, and the IPA Effectiveness Awards.

 We are looking for a Senior Vice President, Brand Strategy to join our team in Canada, leading strategic thinking for some of the world's most recognized consumer brands.

 This is an opportunity to shape brand strategy across North America while collaborating with global teams to deliver culturally relevant, insight-driven work that connects brands with consumers in meaningful ways.

 As a senior strategic leader, you will work at the intersection of brand, culture, creativity, and commerce, helping clients navigate evolving consumer behaviours, identify new opportunities, and build brands that earn attention, trust, and relevance.

 You'll partner closely with senior client leaders, creative teams, strategists, and specialists across Edelman's integrated network to develop ambitious ideas grounded in consumer understanding and designed to drive business impact.
 This is a role for someone who loves the craft of strategy as much as the opportunity to lead it. You'll be hands-on in shaping the work, a trusted advisor to clients, and an inspiring mentor to the next generation of strategic talent.

 Who You Are
 You're a strategic thinker and brand builder who understands what makes consumers care, what drives culture, and how brands can show up meaningfully in people's lives.

 You bring deep experience working with consumer brands, ideally within CPG, and know how to turn complex business challenges, consumer insights, and cultural tensions into clear, compelling strategies that inspire creative thinking.
 You're equally comfortable working directly with senior clients, collaborating with creative teams, and rolling up your sleeves to develop the strategic thinking behind the work.

 You thrive in collaborative environments, bring curiosity and fresh perspectives to challenges, and enjoy working across markets and disciplines to create work that makes a difference.

 What You'll Do
 Lead brand strategy for major CPG clients, developing insight-led approaches that strengthen brand positioning, cultural relevance, consumer engagement, and business growth.
 Shape strategic thinking across North America, collaborating with Canadian, U.S., and global teams to connect local market understanding with regional and global brand ambitions.
 Turn consumer and cultural insights into creative opportunities, drawing on research, data, audience behaviours, category dynamics, and emerging trends to uncover compelling brand platforms and communications strategies.
 Partner with creative and integrated teams to inspire distinctive, culturally relevant ideas and campaigns that connect with consumers across earned, social, digital, and other brand touchpoints.
 Build trusted relationships with senior clients, providing strategic counsel, challenging conventional thinking, and helping brand leaders navigate evolving consumer expectations and business challenges.
 Drive strategic excellence and business growth, identifying opportunities to expand client partnerships, contributing to new business pitches, and championing work that delivers measurable impact.
 Lead and develop strategy talent, mentoring strategists, fostering collaboration, and building an inclusive environment where diverse perspectives and bold thinking can thrive.
 Champion innovation and connected thinking, bringing together expertise from across Edelman's North American and global network to explore new methodologies, tools, and approaches to brand-building.

 What We're Looking For
 10+ years of experience in brand strategy, communications strategy, advertising, integrated marketing, consulting, or a related discipline, including experience leading strategy for major consumer brands.
 Strong understanding of the CPG landscape, consumer behaviours, brand-building, and the cultural and commercial dynamics shaping categories such as food, beverage, personal care, and household products.
 Proven ability to develop compelling brand positioning, creative briefs, communications platforms, and integrated strategies that translate insights into distinctive, effective work.
 Experience leading large, complex client relationships and collaborating with senior stakeholders across multiple markets, ideally including North America.
 A track record of inspiring creative work and translating strategic thinking into measurable brand or business outcomes.
 Strong leadership, communication, storytelling, and presentation skills, with the ability to influence clients, inspire creative teams, and mentor strategic talent.
 A collaborative, curious, and entrepreneurial approach, with the ability to bring together diverse perspectives and navigate complex, cross-functional environments.

 Life at Edelman
 At Edelman, you'll have the opportunity to shape the future of some of the world's most recognized brands while working alongside talented colleagues across strategy, creative, communications, data, and digital.

 Our global network brings together different perspectives, expertise, and capabilities to solve complex challenges and create work that matters.
 Our culture is built on three promises: boldness is possibility, empathy is progress, and curiosity is momentum. 

 We're committed to creating an inclusive environment where people feel respected, supported, and empowered to bring their perspectives and ideas to the table.

 We believe that great strategy starts with curiosity, thrives through collaboration, and creates impact when it challenges what's possible.

 We are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your experience doesn’t perfectly align with every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

À propos de Systemex

Systemex est une organisation mondiale en pleine croissance qui réunit des expertises complémentaires en automatisation industrielle et en services-conseils industriels. Systemex Automation (SA)

Systemex Industries Conseils (SIC)
