Cette opportunité fait partie de Systemex Industries Conseils (SIC)

À propos du poste

Systemex Industries Conseils (SIC) est à la recherche d’une personne d’expérience pour assurer la direction des opérations, notamment la gestion des ressources humaines, le développement du personnel et la performance opérationnelle de l’ensemble de ses lignes de services.

Relevant de la direction générale, vous serez responsable de la gestion du personnel technique et spécialisé, de l’optimisation des ressources ainsi que de l’efficacité opérationnelle, de la rentabilité, de la satisfaction de la clientèle et de la croissance durable. En tant que membre de l’équipe de direction, vous collaborerez étroitement avec les directions techniques et les autres départements afin d’assurer l’adéquation entre les compétences disponibles et les besoins de l’entreprise.

Principales responsabilités

Diriger la planification, l’affectation, la répartition, la mobilisation et l’optimisation des ressources pour l’ensemble des lignes de services, en fonction des besoins des projets.
Piloter le processus de planification des ventes et des opérations (S&OP) afin d’aligner les occasions d’affaires, les engagements liés aux projets, la capacité des équipes et les besoins de recrutement.
Encadrer le personnel technique et spécialisé, notamment en matière de performance, de développement professionnel, de mobilisation, de fidélisation, de recrutement et d’intégration, en collaboration avec les ressources humaines et les directions techniques.

Contribuer à l’élaboration des budgets, aux prévisions financières et aux propositions commerciales, tout en favorisant l’efficacité opérationnelle, la rentabilité et la croissance durable.
Entretenir de solides relations avec la clientèle, gérer les enjeux opérationnels nécessitant une escalade et collaborer avec le développement des affaires et les équipes techniques afin de favoriser la fidélisation, la croissance des comptes et les occasions d’affaires récurrentes.
Standardiser et améliorer les processus de gestion des ressources, d’administration des projets, les systèmes opérationnels, les outils de suivi et les processus interfonctionnels.
Promouvoir une culture de responsabilisation, de collaboration, d’amélioration continue et de santé et sécurité au travail, tout en veillant au respect des politiques internes et des exigences réglementaires.

Qualifications et expérience

Diplôme universitaire en génie, en administration des affaires ou dans un domaine connexe.
Minimum de 10 ans d’expérience pertinente, dont une expérience significative en gestion d’équipes techniques.
Expérience démontrée en gestion des ressources, en planification opérationnelle et en réalisation de projets dans un environnement industriel ou de services techniques.
Solides compétences en leadership, en communication, en planification et en résolution de problèmes, ainsi qu’une bonne compréhension des enjeux financiers et une expérience de travail au sein d’une organisation matricielle.

Job Description

Leader Amélioration des Données / Data Improvement Lead

English job description follows***

Description De L'emploi

Vous avez une expérience confirmée dans l'analyse de données et la gestion de la performance, vous avez travaillé sur l'amélioration de processus et la digitalisation, et vous souhaitez évoluer tout en développant de nouvelles compétences ? Ce poste est pour vous !

Le programme d'avions commerciaux A220 recherche un Leader en amélioration des données pour rejoindre notre équipe Performance Management basée à Mirabel (Québec, Canada), où vous collaborez étroitement avec les analystes de performance, les équipes des Opérations et l'équipe de digitalisation.

Vous ferez partie de l’équipe Performance Management chargée de développer la standardisation et l'amélioration de la qualité des données de performance pour la chaîne de valeur A220, tout en soutenant la feuille de route de digitalisation. L'organisation de l'équipe est établie de manière à promouvoir la collaboration transversale et l'autonomie, dans un esprit de soutien mutuel et d'apprentissage collectif.

Dans ce rôle, vous agirez en tant que point de contact central et facilitateur entre les analystes de la performance opérationnelle et l'équipe de digitalisation. Votre mission sera d'optimiser l'efficacité des processus d'assemblage de l'A220 en coordonnant l'amélioration des données provenant de divers flux : approvisionnement secondaire, SDO ( Supplier Disruption Over Cost ), coûts récurrents (RC) et CVAT ( Customer Value Added Time ). Vous identifierez les besoins en automatisation, harmoniserez les méthodes d'analyse et assurerez la transition des analyses manuelles vers des solutions digitales robustes pour améliorer la rentabilité globale.

Votre Environnement De Travail

Le siège du programme d'avions commerciaux A220 est situé à Mirabel, dans la région métropolitaine de Montréal, à deux pas de la ville dynamique de Montréal. Réputée pour son environnement paisible et sûr, la région offre une grande qualité de vie aux jeunes professionnels ou aux professionnels expérimentés, ainsi qu'aux familles, en équilibrant parfaitement les opportunités de carrière et les activités de plein air, ce qui en fait un endroit vraiment spécial où il fait bon vivre.

Parce Que Nous Prenons Soin De Vous

Avantages financiers: Salaire attractif, bonus annuel, régime d’assurances collectives, régime de retraite et régime d’achat d’actions.
Équilibre vie privée / professionnelle: Une politique de travail hybride (selon les besoins opérationnels), une cafétéria sur site, une politique de congés très concurrentielle.
Bien-être / santé: Programme d’Aide aux Employé.e.s (PAE), programme de rabais, service médical sur site, accès à un service de navette publique entre Laval (station de métro Montmorency) et Mirabel, et une application de covoiturage.
Développement individuel: des opportunités d’évolution et des possibilités de formations nombreuses (catalogue de plus de 10.000 e-formations disponibles en libre accès pour développer votre employabilité, certifications, programmes de développement accéléré, mobilité nationale et internationale).

Chez Airbus, nous vous aidons à travailler, à vous connecter et à collaborer plus facilement et de manière plus flexible. Partout où cela est possible, nous favorisons la flexibilité dans nos modes de travail afin de stimuler l'esprit d'innovation.

Vos Défis

Assurer le lien principal entre les analystes (Performance, SDO, RC, CVAT) et l'équipe de digitalisation pour traduire les besoins métiers en solutions automatisées;
Garantir la qualité, la cohérence et l'exactitude des données de performance issues des flux d'approvisionnement et de production;
Harmoniser la définition et le suivi des indicateurs clés de performance (KPI) à travers les différents flux pour assurer une vision transverse de la performance;
Identifier les opportunités d'automatisation des rapports de performance (hebdomadaires, mensuels, trimestriels) et superviser leur mise en œuvre par l'équipe technique;
Consolider les points de blocage majeurs identifiés par les analystes du pôle Performance Management afin de prioriser la feuille de route de digitalisation selon l'impact sur la performance des opérations;
Préparer et présenter des feuilles de route claires et des visualisations de données aux parties prenantes pour soutenir la planification stratégique;
Collaborer avec les départements Opérations, Finances et Qualité pour optimiser la performance globale de la chaîne de valeur.

Votre Profil

Vous détenez un baccalauréat en ingénierie;
Vous détenez un minimum de 10 ans d’expérience dans un système industriel;
Vous possédez une expérience pertinente en analyse de données, en gestion de la performance ou en amélioration de processus;
Vous maîtrisez les outils d'analyse et de visualisation de données tels que Power BI, Skywise et Python;
Vous avez une connaissance approfondie des entrepôts de données, de l'analytique en nuage et de l'automatisation des processus;
Vous possédez de solides compétences en résolution de problèmes et une capacité démontrée à collaborer avec des équipes interfonctionnelles;
Vous avez la capacité de vulgariser des concepts de données complexes pour les rendre accessibles aux équipes opérationnelles et de direction;
Vous avez une expérience confirmée dans la définition de cadres de mesure de performance et la création de structures d'analyse complexes.

Ce poste peut impliquer des déplacements professionnels.

Déplacements Requis

Ce travail nécessite une prise de conscience liée à tous les risques potentiels de conformité et à un engagement à agir avec intégrité, ces valeurs sont le fondement du succès, de la réputation et de la croissance durable de l'entreprise.

Donnez une nouvelle dimension à votre carrière en soumettant votre candidature en ligne maintenant !

Job Description

You have proven experience in data analysis and performance management? Have you worked on process improvement and digitalization, and are you looking to grow and develop new skills? This role is for you!

The A220 Commercial Aircraft Program is seeking a Data Improvement Leader to join our Performance Management team based in Mirabel (Quebec, Canada), where you will collaborate closely with performance analysts, Operations teams, and the digitalization team.

You will be part of the Performance Management team responsible for developing standardization and improving performance data quality for the A220 value chain, supporting the digitalization roadmap. The team is structured to promote cross-functional collaboration and autonomy, fostering mutual support and collective learning.

In this role, you will act as a central point of contact and facilitator between operational performance analysts and the digitalization team. Your mission will be to optimize the efficiency of the A220 assembly processes by coordinating data improvement across various streams: secondary supply, SDO (Supplier Disruption Over Cost), Recurring Costs (RC), and CVAT (Customer Value Added Time). You will identify automation needs, harmonize analytical methods, and ensure the transition from manual analysis to robust digital solutions to improve overall profitability.

The A220 commercial aircraft Programme is headquartered in Mirabel, in the greater Montreal area, where the vibrant city of Montreal is just a stone’s throw away. Individual development: Great upskilling opportunities and development prospects with unlimited access to +10.000 e-learning courses to develop your employability, certifications, accelerated development programmes, national and international mobility.

Your Challenges

Act as the primary liaison between analysts (Performance, SDO, RC, CVAT) and the digitalization team to translate business needs into automated solutions;
Ensure the quality, consistency, and accuracy of performance data collected from supply and production flows;
Harmonize the definition and monitoring of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) across various flows to guarantee a cross-functional view of performance;
Identify automation opportunities for performance reporting (weekly, monthly, quarterly) and oversee their implementation by the technical team;
Consolidate major roadblocks identified by the Performance Management analysts to prioritize the digitalization roadmap based on its impact on Operational Performance;
Strategic Communication: Prepare and present clear roadmaps and data visualizations to stakeholders to support strategic planning;
Collaborate with Operations, Finance, and Quality teams to optimize the overall value chain performance.

You hold a Bachelor’s degree in Engineering;
You have a minimum of 10 years of experience in an industrial system;
You possess relevant experience in data analysis, performance management, or process improvement ;
You are proficient in data analysis and visualization tools such as Power BI, Skywise, and Python;
You have in-depth knowledge of data warehousing, cloud analytics, and process automation;
You possess strong problem-solving skills and a demonstrated ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams;
You have the ability to simplify complex data concepts for operational and executive leadership teams;
You have proven experience in defining performance measurement frameworks and creating complex analytical structures.

Business Travel May Be Required For This Position.

Why WestJet

Since our story took off in 1996, WestJet has strived to enrich the lives of everyone in our world; a career with us is no exception. We’re proud to be one of Canada’s most admired and respected corporate cultures and continuously aim for the highest standards of service and success.

Join us, this is where your career story takes off.

Overview Of Role

Reporting to the VP, People, this role is accountable for the design of the WestJet Group Total Rewards strategy.

Leading teams of compensation, benefits, and savings/pension professionals, the role ensures the design, development, and operational execution of all programs and plans aligned with WestJet's strategic objectives. The role ensures these programs are progressive, legislatively compliant, and financially sustainable over the long term.

This role is accountable for developing a comprehensive Group Total Rewards strategy by collaborating with the business to ensure programs support the organization's culture and strategic objectives. Drive compensation, benefits, and savings/pension strategy across all employee groups, from executives to frontline employees, ensuring alignment with organizational goals. Identify opportunities to simplify plans wherever possible while ensuring long-term value and cost effectiveness.

Lead Total Rewards teams and maintain and further a culture of effective collaboration with other teams within the People function.
Foster strong relationships with key stakeholders by delivering subject matter expertise through a team of high-performing, experienced professionals.
Support CBA negotiations for both compensation and benefit provisions. Implement negotiated CBA provisions into plan rules and systems requirements, including retroactive adjustments where applicable.
Oversee the organization's pay equity program, including plan development and maintenance, stakeholder collaboration, pay equity analyses, and implementation of required adjustments, ensuring ongoing legislative compliance and group-wide equitable compensation practices.
Deliver executive compensation and incentive plan materials to the Compensation & Governance Committee, enabling informed Board-level decisions that support attraction, retention, and pay-for-performance principles.
Oversee benefit renewals, funding arrangements, claims trends, insurer performance, eligibility administration, and escalations.
Perform comprehensive financial modeling to generate actionable insights and deliver strategic recommendations to business leaders. Identify key cost drivers and uncover opportunities for cost containment. Contribute to Total Rewards benchmarking initiatives and monitor industry trends to inform future program design and strategy.
Oversee strategic partnerships with external consultants, actuaries, carriers, and benefits providers to ensure service excellence, cost effectiveness, and alignment with organizational objectives.
Continuous Improvement & IPO Readiness: Lead and implement projects involving technology-driven solutions and develop change management plans to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of Total Rewards programs. Monitor program performance to ensure Total Rewards offerings are comprehensive, financially responsible, and support the organization's successful transition from a private to a public company.
Oversee the development of engaging communication materials and information sessions for leaders and employees, ensuring a comprehensive understanding of the organization's total compensation philosophy and practices.
Stay informed of legislative requirements that affect compensation, benefits, pension, and savings policies, and develop action plans to ensure governance, compliance, and implementation.
Participate in and lead project work that may involve the development or redesign of programs to support the WestJet Group's growth plans or meet governance requirements.
Lead group-wide Total Rewards transformations and change initiatives as required.

Experience And Qualifications

A bachelor's degree in a related discipline (Human Resources, Finance, or Commerce).
15+ years of direct experience leading Total Rewards programs and teams in a large, complex organization, including experience in privately held and/or publicly traded enterprises.
Demonstrated ability to build highly effective and collaborative working relationships at all levels of the organization.
Dedicated team player who is highly organized, self-motivated, and able to work independently while taking initiative.
Experience with labour bargaining and operationalizing associated collective agreements from a Total Rewards perspective.

Excellent analytical and critical thinking skills, with a proven track record of completing complex data analysis and transforming it into actionable insights and strategic recommendations.
Ability to work in a time-sensitive environment with strong attention to detail.
Well-developed communication skills, along with a high degree of discretion, tact, and diplomacy when dealing with sensitive matters.
Advanced knowledge of Microsoft applications, including Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.
CCP and/or CEBS designation considered an asset.

A fun and friendly culture with colleagues who work together to win

Savings and Benefit programs that are flexible to meet your specific needs

WestJet took to the skies in 1996 with just over 200 employees and three aircraft operating service to five destinations. jobs.title: Senior Director, Revenue Management
jobs.description:
At Saputo, we bring good to the table by making high-quality products, investing in our people, and supporting communities around the world . As a top 10 global dairy processor, we value contributions that matter and strive to foster an inclusive, growth-driven work environment. Ready to bring your best?

Overview of the role:

Saputo is seeking a Senior Director, Revenue Management – North America.

The Senior Director, Revenue Management leads Saputo North America’s revenue management agenda across Canada and the United States to deliver sustainable, profitable growth across customers, channels, categories, and products. This role integrates pricing, trade investment, promotion effectiveness, mix and assortment, and portfolio profitability into one disciplined commercial framework. The Senior Director partners with Sales, Marketing, Finance, Supply Chain, Operations, Category & Product Management, Commercial R&D, and Technology to translate market, customer, commodity, and cost dynamics into fact-based decisions and consistent execution.

As a senior commercial thought leader, the Senior Director establishes governance, analytics, tools, and decision forums that improve pricing accuracy, strengthen return on trade investment, accelerate insights, and build an integrated revenue management capability across Saputo North America while enabling market-specific execution in Canada and the United States.

How you will make contributions that matter:

Revenue Management Strategy & Governance

Own and evolve the Saputo North America revenue management strategy, operating model, multi-year roadmap, and performance scorecard in alignment with business and commercial priorities.
Integrate the core revenue growth levers of pricing, promotions, trade terms, mix, assortment, channel strategy, and portfolio optimization.
Align North American standards with country-specific market conditions, customer structures, commercial practices, and business priorities to drive consistency without limiting local agility.
Establish decision rights, approval thresholds, guardrails, and governance for pricing, trade investment, promotions, bids, contracts, and new business opportunities.
Define clear North American and country-level decision rights, escalation paths, and accountability across the Canadian and U.S. businesses.
Lead pricing and revenue management forums, ensuring decisions, assumptions, risks, approvals, and follow-up actions are documented and communicated.
Serve as a trusted advisor to senior Sales, Finance, Category & Product, Marketing, Operations, and Supply Chain leaders, constructively challenging assumptions and recommending action.

Pricing Strategy, Architecture & Execution

Lead market-based pricing strategies that reflect commodity movements, inflation, supply chain costs, cost-to-serve, competitive dynamics, and customer value.
Oversee periodic and event-driven price reviews, scenario modeling, financial evaluation, sales materials, customer transition plans, and execution of approved price changes.
Develop and maintain price corridors, floors, exception protocols, validation controls, and pricing policies that improve consistency and reduce value leakage.
Optimize ERP-enabled price data, maintenance routines, and controls to improve pricing accuracy, transparency, and monthly price-change execution.
Partner with Sales on complex negotiations and customer conversations, balancing profitable growth, customer needs, and volume risk.

Trade Investment & Promotion Effectiveness

Own the governance and optimization of total trade investment, including planning standards, approval criteria, accrual alignment, performance tracking, and post-event review.
Establish consistent pre- and post-promotion evaluation methods using incremental volume, revenue, margin, return on investment, and strategic objectives.
Identify non-productive spend, value leakage, and underperforming events; partner with commercial teams to redirect investment toward higher-return opportunities.
Maintain promotional guidelines and embed lessons learned into customer plans, annual planning, and future investment decisions.

Customer, Channel & Portfolio Profitability

Lead recurring diagnostics across Canada and the United States, including customers, channels, categories, brands, and SKUs to identify performance drivers, risks, and corrective actions.
Advance category and portfolio profitability by prioritizing opportunities in mix, assortment, product rationalization, and route-to-market economics.
Develop actions for the highest- and lowest-performing customers and SKUs, including margin improvement, cost-to-serve, terms, freight, and commercialization opportunities.
Create clear North American executive reporting that connects price, volume, mix, trade, freight, currency, and cost movements to net sales and margin outcomes, with visibility to consolidated and country-level performance.

New Business, Bids & Commercial Decision Support

Support the financial and strategic evaluation of bids, new customers, private label, co-manufacturing, innovation, and other business development opportunities.
Apply defined guardrails and scenario analysis to assess profitability, capacity, factory utilization, service requirements, risk, and incremental growth.
Maintain scalable bid and tender tools, decision records, and post-launch scorecards to confirm performance against approved business cases.

Planning, Forecasting & Performance Management

Co-lead North American net sales and customer margin planning with Sales Operations and Finance, including consolidated, country, channel, customer, category, and product views.
Lead in-year forecasting and scenario planning for price, volume, mix, trade, freight, commodity exposure, and customer margin performance.
Provide timely diagnostics for weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual business reviews, highlighting causals, outlook, risks, opportunities, and recommended actions.
Partner with Finance on close-related revenue management activities, including customer expense classification, true-ups, pricing factors, and relevant commodity or hedging impacts.

Data, Digital Enablement & Advanced Analytics

Define the North American revenue management data, reporting, and technology roadmap, including ERP, trade promotion, customer, syndicated market,.
Improve data quality, common definitions, master data, model governance, and controls so leaders can make decisions from trusted information.
Harmonize revenue management definitions, performance measures, and reporting across Canada and the United States to enable comparable insights and coordinated decision-making.
Champion responsible use of advanced analytics, automation, and AI-enabled decision support for elasticity, scenario modeling, promotion optimization, forecasting, and opportunity identification.
Ensure analytical methods remain explainable, validated, appropriately governed, and paired with commercial judgment.
Drive adoption of self-service dashboards and standardized tools while preserving clear accountability for decisions and outcomes.

You are best suited for the role if you have the following qualifications:

10+ years of progressive experience in revenue management, commercial finance, sales operations, pricing, category management, or a related commercial discipline.
Leadership experience in consumer-packaged goods, food and beverage, dairy, or another complex, customer-driven manufacturing environment.
Bachelor’s degree in business, Finance, Economics, Marketing, Analytics, Supply Chain, or related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience. Master's degree or advanced professional qualification in Business, Finance, Analytics, or a related field, is preferred.
Demonstrated experience leading teams and influencing senior cross-functional stakeholders.
Demonstrated ability to lead through a matrixed, multi-country organization and influence senior stakeholders across Canada and the United States.
Deep experience in pricing, trade investment, promotion analytics, customer profitability, forecasting, and commercial decision support.
Experience translating complex data into clear recommendations, business cases, and executable commercial actions.
Working knowledge of commodity- and cost-driven pricing dynamics, customer negotiations, and commercialization processes.
Experience with ERP and commercial analytics environments; ability to lead processes, data, and technology improvement.
Experience with SAP and trade promotion, pricing, syndicated data, visualization, and advanced analytics platforms.
Experience establishing or maturing a multi-country revenue growth management capability across multiple channels, customer segments, and business models.
Exposure to elasticity modeling, assortment optimization, AI-enabled analytics, and model governance.

Posting Information:

Who We Are

For 150 years, London Health Sciences Centre (LHSC) has been a leader in world-class care. As an acute tertiary and quaternary teaching hospital, LHSC provides leading-edge medical care to people from across western Ontario and beyond. LHSC is located just two hours from Toronto and two hours from Detroit in the city of London which is known for its beautiful and walkable downtown core located on the Thames River, a vibrant culinary scene and scores of activities that highlight local arts, culture and music. Our team of more than 17,000 physicians, staff, learners and volunteers works tirelessly to support patients as they navigate their unique health-care journeys. As one of Canada’s largest acute-care teaching hospitals, LHSC is a renowned centre of innovation with a history of groundbreaking research that has influenced how people are cared for around the world. With nearly 1 million annual patient visits across University, Victoria and Children's Hospitals, LHSC provides compassionate leading-edge care and is proud of our strong regional, national and international partnerships. For more information, please visit www.lhsc.on.ca.

The Business Support team provides portfolios with operational budgeting, reporting, forecasting and analysis support. This team plays an important role in assisting LHSC leadership in making informed financial decisions, and provides sound advice in financial practices and organizational policy.

The Capital Finance team supports the capital asset needs of LHSC. The team works closely with Corporate Accounting to ensure accurate, efficient and timely recording of capital transactions. The culture of teamwork and respect drives the team to support the capital needs of patient care at LHSC.

What the Role is

The Director, Business Support and Capital Finance provides strategic and operational leadership for business management and capital planning practices across London Health Sciences Centre (LHSC) to maximize delivery of high quality, safe, and efficient patient care within available budgets. The role provides hospital-wide leadership and oversight for business planning, financial management, reporting, and control practices to safeguard organizational assets and strengthen financial performance. The Director also provides strategic financial stewardship of LHSC's capital planning, capital accounting, and capital funding activities and ensures compliance with internal and external audit requirements related to capital financial reporting.

The Director leads and drives systems transformation through encouraging and supporting innovation and championing and orchestrating change, challenging the status quo. The role leads Managers and Business Managers and develops and sustains healthy work environments and effective teams within a performance-driven culture. The Director organizes program activities, directs resources, executes operational initiatives, formulates policies and procedures, and strategically plans for the future. The Director develops purposeful coalitions with internal and external stakeholders.

Reporting to the Vice President, Finance (CFO) & Performance , the Director, Business Support and Capital will translate decisions of our senior level into execution by utilizing systems thinking strategic planning and relationship management by developing purposeful coalitions with internal and external partners. This position requires someone with a proven track record for leading and driving systems transformation through encouraging and supporting innovation and championing and orchestrating change. developing and sustaining healthy work environments and effective teams while leading in a performance-driven culture. You will organize program activities, direct resources, execute operational initiatives, formulate policies & procedures, and strategically plan for the future.

You will demonstrate strong business acumen including management of multi-million dollar operating and capital budgets. This leader will have exceptional analytical and critical thinking skills that contribute to identifying problems and issues, evaluating the interdependence of decisions, questioning and challenging the status quo, and designing and implementing processes for improvement.

You foster a healthy, safe and engaging work environment where others have meaningful opportunities to contribute, collaborate, and cooperate to achieve results. You inspire and motivate your leaders and teams by aligning with our mission, vision and values and modelling performance and service excellence. Spotting and developing talent is a strength, as is your ability to coach, mentor, support and challenge others to achieve professional and personal goals.

Who You Are

You are self-aware of own assumptions, values, principles, strengths and limitations
You manage and develop self while modeling qualities such as honesty, integrity, resilience, and confidence
You engage and support others to foster development, personal goals and encourage a healthy organization
You achieve results by strategically aligning direction, decisions, actions and evaluation with the vision, values and evidence
You facilitate an environment of collaboration and cooperation
You create connections, build partnerships and networks
You demonstrate a commitment to the organizational vision, mission, values and service excellence
You are a transformational thinker that encourages and supports innovation
You have exceptional analytical skills that contribute to effective decision-making
You are self-directed, courageous, and highly motivated with excellent interpersonal and effective communication skills

What You Will Bring with You

Successful completion of a recognized Master's Degree in Business, Commerce, Finance or a related discipline, preferred*
Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation, which can also include a recognized legacy Chartered Accountant (CA), Certified Management Accountant (CMA), or Certified General Accountant (CGA) designation in good standing with CPA Ontario required
Strong knowledge of Canadian Public Sector Accounting Standards and Financial reporting
Minimum of 8 to 10 years' leadership experience, preferably in progressively more responsible leadership position(s)
Minimum five (5) years' previously related demonstrated experience and understanding in a healthcare-related discipline, preferably in Finance
Strong knowledge of Ontario Healthcare Reporting Standards (OHRS) preferred
Previous leadership in Capital Planning and/or Finance preferred
Member of the Canadian College of Health Leaders (CCHL) who have, or are in process of attaining the Canadian Health Executive (CHE) Select certification program preferred
Fluent and computer literate with computer systems such as email and Microsoft Office applications (MS Word, Excel & PowerPoint)
Demonstrated ability to attend work on a regular basis

*Consideration for an interview will be given to a Baccalaureate and prior experience assessment

How to Apply

Apply through London Health Sciences Centre’s career website at https://www.lhsc.on.ca/careers, Job ID #111503

Submission Requirements ( please submit as a PDF document )

Cover Letter, Resume and Listing of Education, Credentials, Certifications and References.

As part of the assessment process applicants may be required to complete a written profile, presentations, etc. Please be advised that reference checks may be conducted as part of the selection process.

Immunization Requirements

Before beginning employment at LHSC, all new hires must provide documentation related to LHSC’s Health Review Requirements. For more information and a detailed list of requirements, please visit Health Review Requirements | LHSC.

Additional Information

London Health Sciences Centre fosters a culture of patient and staff safety whereby all employees are guided by LHSC's Mission, Vision, Values and Code of Conduct.

LHSC does not use artificial intelligence (AI) to screen, assess or select applicants for a position.

Developing and reviewing complex financial models, valuation analyses, forecasts, discount rates and other financial inputs
Analyzing financial and non-financial information and identifying issues relevant to the valuation or quantification of economic damages
Conducting and directing economic, financial, industry and company-specific research
Preparing and reviewing expert reports and other written analyses
Preparing and reviewing rebuttal analyses that assess the analyses and conclusions of other experts
Communicating directly with clients and counsel regarding analyses, information requirements, findings and engagement progress
Managing project plans, staffing, timelines, budgets and deliverables
Supervising, reviewing and developing junior team members, including providing technical guidance and feedback
Preparing for and attending hearings, trials and mediations
Supporting testifying experts throughout the engagement and hearing process and contributing to business development and practice-building initiatives

Qualifications

A bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, economics, business or another relevant discipline from a recognized post-secondary institution
A CBV, CPA, CFA, ACA/ACCA or equivalent international professional designation
Approximately seven to ten years of relevant professional experience
Prior professional experience in business valuation, economic damages, forensic accounting, dispute advisory or economic consulting
Strong analytical and quantitative skills in business valuation and financial analysis, and the ability to develop practical and creative approaches to complex financial and commercial problems
The ability to interpret financial statements and other financial and non-financial information and identify issues relevant to an engagement
Advanced Microsoft Excel skills
Excellent written, verbal and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate complex financial concepts clearly and concisely
Experience managing projects or significant workstreams and working effectively under competing deadlines
Experience supervising, reviewing and developing junior professionals
A willingness to travel domestically or internationally when required

Experience preparing expert reports or other analyses for litigation or arbitration proceedings
International arbitration, direct client and counsel interaction, business development, practice-building experience.
Experience with financial databases such as S&P Capital IQ and Bloomberg
Experience with VBA and/or python
Additional language skills, reflecting the international nature of our practice

Our culture and people are driven by passion, pride, and performance. Passion for the clients we serve, the work we deliver, and the communities we live in. jobs.title: Head of Consumer Segment, NAM (Canada)
jobs.description:
Description

At Xe, we live currencies
. Founded in 1993, Xe is a global leader in currency exchange and international money transfers. What began as a simple currency converter has grown into a platform trusted by over 300 million people each year. We provide a comprehensive range of currency services and products, including our real-time exchange rates, Currency Converter, Market Analysis and Currency Data API, supporting 130+ currencies across 190+ countries with quick, easy, secure Money Transfers for individuals and businesses. We leverage technology to deliver these services through our website, mobile app, and by phone. Backed by Euronet, we process more than $115 billion in global payments annually. Xe is profitable, product-led, and focused on building reliable, user-first tools that make moving money across borders easier for everyone.

Our Principles

At Xe, we value people who take initiative, think big, and follow through. We’re curious by nature and not afraid to ask what if or try something new. Everyone’s voice matters here. We expect people to speak up, bring ideas, and take ownership of their work. We don’t micromanage. We trust each other to make good calls, take responsibility, and move fast when it counts. And we care about community. Not in a vague corporate way, but in the sense that we have each other’s backs, stay open to feedback, and build a culture of trust and real collaboration.

Ambition. We dream big, try things out, and always ask “why not?” and “what if?” We’re ambitious in our thinking and our delivery.
Responsibility. We get involved, bring our perspective, and are always open to new ideas. We take personal responsibility.
Community. We value a sense of belonging, trusting each other, and encouraging authenticity. We contribute to our community.

The Role.
The Head of Consumer is the senior owner of Xe’s Consumer business in the United States and Canada, accountable for its strategy, proposition and commercial performance. Product, Marketing and Growth sit in global teams, so you will lead through influence: aligning them, along with Pricing, Sales, Customer Success, Care and Operations, behind the North America plan.

Responsibilities

This is a builder’s role. You will run the NAM Consumer business like a founder, owning revenue, profitability, acquisition, activation, retention, wallet share and customer lifetime value — and opening new channels to reach more customers. The role suits a digitally fluent leader with a background across product, marketing and growth in a fast-paced startup or scale-up. You know what great looks like in each function and can push global teams to deliver it for North American customers. Responsibilities include:

Consumer Strategy & Commercial Performance

Set and execute the North America Consumer strategy across the US and Canada, with clear plans to grow market share, revenue, customer value and profitability.
Own end-to-end commercial performance across the customer lifecycle: acquisition, activation, engagement, retention, wallet share and lifetime value.
Define the priorities, targets and operating rhythm for the Consumer business, and align regional and global stakeholders behind them.
Track a fast-moving competitive set — digital money transfer apps, neobanks, big tech wallets and incumbent banks — and spot new pockets of growth, such as high-value corridors and underserved diaspora communities.

Channel Expansion

Identify, build and scale new acquisition and distribution channels for Consumer in the US and Canada — for example, affiliate and referral programs, embedded and B2B2C distribution, community, diaspora and employer channels, and marketplaces.
Build the business case for each channel, run pilots, and scale those that hit CAC, volume and margin targets.
Lead commercial discussions with channel partners, including RFPs, and manage those relationships for ongoing performance.
Work with Compliance and Operations so each new channel launches safely and integrates cleanly into the customer journey.

Influencing Product, Marketing, Growth & Pricing

Be the voice of the NAM consumer with global Product, Marketing and Growth teams: bring market insight, set regional priorities, and secure roadmap and investment commitments.
Develop and own Customer Value Propositions for each Consumer segment in the US and Canada, and brief global teams on the features, benefits, pricing and service levels each segment needs.
Own regional go-to-market and in-market delivery of new products and propositions, coordinating cross-functional teams to maximize uptake and commercial return.
Champion test-and-learn on NAM funnels, onboarding and messaging, and hold partner teams to agreed outcomes.
Partner with Global Pricing on pricing and FX margin strategies that balance adoption, competitiveness, revenue, margin and retention.

Customer Experience & Service Delivery

Lead consumer service and sales performance across Customer Success and Digital Sales, ensuring service and sales SLAs are consistently met or beaten.
Partner with Care leadership so the global Care function serves NAM customers well, meets service levels and resolves complaints quickly.
Use customer feedback, app reviews, NPS, service data and root-cause analysis to remove friction across the journey.

Operational & Cross-Functional Leadership

Work with global Revenue Operations and Sales Operations to align regional strategy, global programs, annual targets and performance reporting.
Partner with North America Compliance leadership so the Consumer business meets its US and Canadian regulatory obligations — including state money transmitter licensing, CFPB remittance rules, FinCEN, FINTRAC and Bank of Canada requirements — while keeping the experience fast and customer-centric.
Build, lead and develop a high-performing team and create clear cross-functional accountability across regional and global stakeholders.

Performance Management & Reporting

Build and run a Consumer performance framework covering acquisition, conversion, activation, transactions, active customers, retention cohorts, revenue, profitability, CAC, LTV, channel performance, customer experience and product adoption.
Give senior leadership regular, insightful reporting that turns data into clear recommendations and actions.
Use data, customer insight and commercial analysis to guide investment decisions and close performance gaps.

How Success is Measured.
Success in the role will be measured through a combination of commercial, customer and operational outcomes, including:

Growth in Consumer revenue, margin and market share across the US and Canada.
Growth in active Consumer customers and transaction volumes.
Volume, revenue and unit economics from new channels launched and scaled.
Improved acquisition, conversion and activation, from sign-up to first transfer.
Increased retention, repeat usage and wallet share.
Adoption and commercial performance of new products and propositions in NAM.
Improved customer experience and service performance (e.g. NPS, app ratings, SLAs).
Stronger cross-functional execution and delivery of NAM priorities by global teams.

What You Bring

A digital-first operator who thinks in funnels, cohorts and experiments, and lives and breathes modern consumer apps.
Hands-on leadership experience across Product, Marketing and Growth — ideally having owned or run more than one of these functions.
A track record in a high-growth, fast-paced startup or scale-up environment, ideally in consumer fintech, payments, money transfer, neobanking or another digital consumer business.
Proven results scaling a consumer product: driving acquisition, activation, retention and monetization with measurable impact.
Fluency with the modern growth stack — product analytics, experimentation platforms, CRM and lifecycle tools, attribution and paid acquisition channels.
Strong commercial and analytical skills, with a firm grasp of unit economics (CAC, LTV, payback, contribution margin) and data-driven decision-making.
Experience building and leading high-performing, cross-functional teams, and comfort influencing in a matrixed global organization.
A bias for action: you move fast, ship, learn and iterate, while keeping the bigger strategic picture in view.
Excellent communication and storytelling, from team stand-ups to senior leadership.
Understanding of, or a strong appetite to learn, regulated financial services in the US and Canada.
Deep customer empathy and familiarity with US and Canadian consumer markets.

Perks & Benefits (Canada)

Competitive salary and incentive.
Vacation+ personal days + day off for your birthday + sick time + holidays
Volunteering day for a charity of your choice
Healthcare
Life & Disability insurance
Plumm Mental Health and Wellbeing
Matched employer RRSP contribution (subject to limits)
Discounted Euronet Employee Share Purchase Plan (ESPP)
A chance to grow your career in a mission-driven global company.

Why Join Us?
You'll be part of a fast-moving team where your contributions directly impact growth. We invest in our people with tools, mentorship, and opportunities to level up fast-whether that's moving into closing roles or leadership paths. You'll also play a key role in shaping how we go to market in the competitive payments space, using real insights and industry benchmarks to stay ahead of the curve. Xe offers a competitive salary and benefits package. Actual compensation is based upon factors such as the candidate’s skills, qualifications, and experience. In addition, Xe offers a wide range of best-in-class, comprehensive and inclusive employee benefits for this role, including healthcare, dental and vision benefits, retirement plan, paid vacation/sick leave and more.

Xe values diversity and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We provide equal opportunities to all employees and applicants, regardless of race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. At Xe, we are committed to making our recruitment practices barrier-free and as accessible as possible for everyone. This includes adjustments or changes for disabled people, neurodiverse people or people with long-term health conditions. If you would like us to do anything differently during the application, interview or assessment process, including providing information in an alternative format, please contact us at recruitment@xe.com. It is not to be taken as a complete statement of responsibilities or requirements. Job Description 

 What is the Opportunity? 
 The Associate Director, Market Risk (FRTB Capital) will play a pivotal role in building and leading RBC’s market risk regulatory reporting infrastructure under the Basel 3 Endgame (B3EG) framework. The individual will architect end-to-end production of critical US IHC regulatory submission including the FFIEC 102 (weekly FRTB capital reporting), FR Y-9C Risk-to-Finance reconciliations, and CCAR Market RWA projections for FRY-14A. This high-impact role offers ownership over establishing automated reporting workflows, partnering with IT on system implementations and data pipeline enhancements, and driving strategic initiatives such as FRTB calculator improvements and IMA vs. SA approach analysis. The ideal candidate brings 5+ years of market risk reporting or regulatory capital experience, strong technical capabilities in Python and SQL, and a track record of delivering accurate regulatory submissions in production environments.

 What will you do? 
 Lead the design, implementation, and ongoing production of Market Risk regulatory reports under B3EG, including the FFIEC 102 and weekly FRTB capital reports and CCAR Market RWA 9-quarter projections; establish automated reporting views and dashboards to support granular schedule-level reporting – 25%.
 Partner with IT and Group risk Analytics team on FRTB Standardized Approach (SA) calculator enhancements for jurisdictional changes, system implementations, and data pipeline automation; coordinate UAT testing, production validation and reporting infrastructure improvements – 20%•.
 Build and maintain the Risk-to-Finance reconciliation framework (FR Y-9C), perform comprehensive data analysis across market risk exposures, capital calculations, and reporting datasets; including root-cause analysis of breaks and develop automated reconciliation tools and validation checks– 20%. 
 Design and implement controls automation solutions for reporting and capital calculation processes; build automated validation checks, exception monitoring tools, and alerting mechanisms to enhance data quality, control effectiveness, and reduce manual intervention – 15%.
 Conduct FRTB Internal Models Approach (IMA) impact analysis and desk-level feasibility assessments; collaborate with trading desks and modelling teams to evaluate capital benefits, backtesting performance, and P&L attribution requirements; provide recommendations on optimal approach selection (IMA vs. SA) by desk – 10%.
 Develop and maintain reporting documentation including data lineage, process flows, line-item mapping, and methodology descriptions; monitor regulatory developments, participate in FRB data collection exercises (e.g., HPE/QIS), and support internal audit, RCSA, and regulatory examination processes – 10%.

 What do you need to succeed? 
 Bachelor’s degree in finance, Engineering, Mathematics, or related quantitative discipline; advanced degree preferred.
 5+ years of experience in market risk management at a financial institution with hands-on involvement in regulatory reporting and FRTB implementation.
 Deep understanding of market risk capital frameworks (Basel III/IV, FRTB SA/IMA approach) and associated regulatory reporting requirements. 
 Proven experience designing and maintaining reconciliation frameworks between risk systems and general ledger/finance platforms; ability to identify, investigate and resolve complex data breaks.
 Advanced proficiency in data analysis and automation using Python, SQL, and Excel to manipulate large-scale datasets, build validation tools and streamline reporting workflows.
 Hands-on experience with Business Intelligence and reporting tools (Tableau, OBI, or equivalent) and market risk systems; ability to translate data into actional insights through dashboard and visualizations.
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills with demonstrated ability to synthesize complex regulatory and technical concepts for senior management and regulators, and cross-functional stakeholders.
 Ability to manage recurring production processes under tight weekly deadlines while maintaining accuracy and completeness.
 Autonomous, highly motivated, and able to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.

jobs.description:
Venture outside the ordinary - TMX Careers

The TMX group of companies includes leading global exchanges such as the Toronto Stock Exchange, Montreal Exchange, and numerous innovative organizations enhancing capital markets. United as a global team, we’re connecting cross-functionally, traversing industries and geographies, moving opportunity into action, advancing global economic growth, and propelling progress. Through a rich exchange of ideas, meaningful collaboration, and a nimble operating model, we're powering some of the nation's most critical systems, fueling capital formation and innovation, bringing increased opportunity to business visionaries, product ingenuity to consumers, and career exploration to our team.

Ready to be part of the action?

The Chief Compliance Officer (CCO)
holds a key position responsible for designing, implementing, and maintaining a robust compliance program to ensure that CDS Clearing and Depository Services Inc. (CDS) and the Canadian Derivatives Clearing Corporation (CDCC) each operate within their applicable legal and regulatory frameworks. This mandate covers the complete end-to-end compliance framework for both entities.

The CCO ensures an integrated compliance strategy by coordinating with the Businesses, Risk Management, Internal Audit and Enterprise Compliance functions, as well as with the TMX General Counsel’s Office. Providing assurance on the effectiveness of post-trade compliance, the CCO reports directly to the Board of Directors and the Vice President, Regulatory Affairs and Enterprise Compliance.

Given that CDS and CDCC are recognized clearing agencies and designated systemically important Financial Market Infrastructures (FMIs), the CCO is tasked with ensuring strict adherence to applicable legal and regulatory requirements, including those stemming from such federal designation and provincial recognitions. In this role, the CCO also liaises directly with key regulators.

Work Location:
We are open to candidates being located in one of the following Canadian office locations: Toronto or Montreal.

Key Accountabilities

Compliance Strategy & Oversight
Ensure the continued development of a strong, credible, robust culture of compliance through leading the function with excellence, practicality, and strong relationships with the businesses, risk management, legal, TMX affiliates, and external stakeholders
Assess the overall compliance framework for CDS and CDCC and adapt it to the evolution of the post-trade businesses and their regulatory requirements, accounting for the systemically important nature of these businesses and their similarities and differences; and on an ongoing basis, reassess the compliance framework to ensure it continues to be fit for purpose
Serve as a strategic advisor on the compliance impact of changes to post-trade businesses, including changes to rules, risk frameworks and IT infrastructure
Maintain and oversee written policies, procedures and controls to ensure compliance with applicable federal and provincial laws, regulations (including National Instruments), Recognition Orders, and Oversight Agreements and international obligations (collectively the Regulatory Requirements), and monitor regulatory and industry trends affecting the FMIs
Ensure timely and appropriate review of written policies and procedures is undertaken regarding the operation of the clearing agencies, develop and conduct training and monitoring to ensure policies and procedures are understood and complied with
Collaborate with the Chief Risk Officer (CRO) to ensure that compliance risks are identified, assessed, and mitigated within each FMI's overall enterprise risk management framework
Lead the management and delivery of annual disclosures against international standards designed to ensure the safety, efficiency, and resilience of clearing, payment, and settlement systems (i.e., the Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures (PFMI)), including ensuring that appropriate senior clearing agency staff are identified to "own" each key consideration of an applicable PFMI principle, that each owner understands and applies the required PFMI assessment methodology, and periodically assessing the PFMI compliance program including by benchmarking against global peers
Meet, as appropriate, with staff at the Canadian Securities Administrators (CSA) and the Bank of Canada (BoC) to discuss compliance matters, coordinate with the General Counsel’s Office and other stakeholders to respond to questions from relevant regulators and maintain relationships with such regulators
Act as a trusted advisor on compliance matters to CDS and CDCC, including responding to early warning questions, establishing trust and open communication with the businesses to allow for proactive detection and remediation; and advise business lines on compliance regarding Participants’ and Clearing Members’ adherence to rules, procedures and manuals
Coordinate responses to due diligence questionnaires from Participants covering a variety of areas, including AML, KYC, politically exposed persons, cyber security
Governance & Board Reporting
Prepare and certify an Annual Compliance Report assessing the overall health of the compliance programs, including the FMIs’ compliance with regulatory requirements for submission to the Board and regulators
Engage with the relevant Boards as needed regarding, apprising the Board of material non-compliance that poses a risk to market participants or the broader financial system
Meet in camera with the Board and/or designated committees, as needed, and at least once annually to discuss the state of the compliance program
Incident/Crisis Management
Monitor and report any breaches of regulatory requirements to applicable stakeholders on a timely basis
Respond promptly and assist as needed in incident management or crisis scenarios, coordinating with risk management, legal, business, operations, technology and other internal stakeholders in the execution of post-trade controls, surveillance, incident management and reporting
Collaborate with business lines to periodically update recovery and wind-down plans, which ensure systemic stability by detailing how FMIs manage severe stress, allocates uncovered losses, or safely winds down operations, and participate in default management and recovery plan simulations

Must Have(s)

Experience: Minimum 10 years of compliance experience within a regulated entity, including at least 3 years in a primary compliance leadership role
Regulatory Engagement/Oversight: Proven experience liaising directly with capital markets, banking, or other regulators (e.g., Bank of Canada, CSA, OSFI), and developing and executing compliance frameworks in a complex regulatory environment
Industry Knowledge: Deep expertise in compliance requirements for regulated entities, such as financial market infrastructures or financial institutions
Leadership & Collaboration: Track record of driving strong compliance culture, and collaborating effectively across legal, enterprise risk, operations, business and finance functions
Communication: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the proven ability to communicate effectively to all levels in an organization, including C-suite executives and Boards of Directors

Nice to Have(s)

Domain Expertise: Specialized experience and strong operational familiarity with Canadian securities, derivatives, clearing, and settlement systems
Language Skills: Professional proficiency in French is an asset

In the market for…

Growth

jobs.description:
About Cheaper Inference Cheaper Inference is a drop-in, OpenAI-compatible API that charges developers about 30% below provider list price
. We save money in two ways:
Marketplace pricing.
Providers with spare LLM capacity compete on price. We send each request to the cheapest healthy offer and pass the discount on to customers.
Fewer wasted tokens.
Our optimization pipeline uses current research to cut tokens from each request. Every customer can see exactly what each request saved.

Our customers are developers and technical teams running production workloads through our API. When something goes wrong, such as a failed request, a surprising bill or a confusing savings number, they need fast, accurate, technically credible help. Support is part of the product.

The role You'll build and lead customer support at Cheaper Inference from the ground up. You'll handle tickets yourself at first, then design the systems, tools, documentation and team that let support grow with the company. You'll be accountable for how fast we respond, how well we resolve issues, how satisfied customers are and how much of what you learn gets back to the product team.
You'll work closely with the founders and engineering. A large share of our support is technical. You'll often be the first to spot an API issue, a billing edge case or a confusing part of the dashboard.

What you'll do Own the support function.
Set up support channels (email, in-app chat, Discord or Slack communities), choose and configure the tools, and define SLAs, priority levels and escalation paths.
Handle tickets directly at first.
Answer technical questions about API integration, streaming, rate limits, errors, model availability, request headers, prompt A/B experiments and billing.

jobs.title: Head of Supply Partnerships (Inference Providers)
jobs.description:
About Cheaper Inference Cheaper Inference is a drop-in, OpenAI-compatible API that charges developers about 30% below provider list price
. We help our customers save money in two ways:
Marketplace pricing.
Providers with spare LLM capacity compete on price. We send each request to the cheapest healthy offer and pass the discount on to customers.
Fewer wasted tokens.
Our optimization pipeline uses current research to cut tokens from each request. Every customer can see exactly what each request saved.

Our supply of inference capacity limits how far we can grow. The more good, reliable, low-cost capacity we have, the bigger the discount, the more models we can offer and the more customers we can serve.

The role You'll be the first person focused full-time on the supply side of the business. You'll find, sign, onboard and manage our relationships with inference providers. These include GPU clouds, model labs, resellers, enterprises with reserved capacity they don't use and neoclouds. You'll be accountable for how much capacity we have, what it costs, how reliable it is and how many models it covers.
You'll work closely with the founders and engineering. In this job, commercial deals and technical details go together: a good deal on a slow or unreliable endpoint is a bad deal.

What you'll do Build the supplier pipeline.
Find and rank providers with surplus or discountable capacity across models, regions and hardware. Run outreach from first contact to a live integration.
Negotiate and close.
Set pricing, volume commitments, rate limits, SLAs, payment terms and data-handling terms. Structure deals that keep us below list price while staying fair and sustainable for providers.
Onboard providers.
Work with engineering to connect new providers to our routing layer. Meet latency and throughput targets and report accurate usage.
Manage live relationships.
Track each provider's uptime, latency, error rates, fill rates and how competitive their prices are. Run regular business reviews, handle escalations and expand the relationships that work.
Protect supply resilience.
Avoid relying too heavily on one provider, keep backup capacity for our most popular models and plan ahead for demand spikes and new model launches.
Track the market.
Follow GPU and token pricing, new model releases, provider roadmaps and competitors. Turn what you learn into a supply strategy and pricing recommendations.
Own trust and compliance with partners.
Make sure providers meet our standards for data retention, privacy, security (e.g., SOC 2) and acceptable use. Work with legal on contracts and DPAs.
Shape the marketplace.
Help design incentives, pricing mechanics and provider-facing tools and processes that attract and keep good capacity.

What success looks like First 90 days:
A mapped list of target providers, at least 3–5 new providers signed and live, and a clear view of the health of current supply.
First year:
A deep, diverse provider base covering all major models, measurable gains in price and reliability, and a repeatable process for bringing on new providers.

What we're looking for 4+ years
in partnerships, business development, supply or procurement, ideally at an AI infrastructure company, cloud or GPU provider, or a two-sided marketplace.
An existing network across inference providers, GPU clouds or model labs, or a clear plan for building one fast.
A strong commercial sense. You're comfortable with unit economics, margin, usage-based pricing and capacity commitments.
Enough technical depth to discuss tokens per second, time to first token, rate limits, quantization, context windows and API compatibility with engineers on both sides.
A track record of negotiating and closing complex contracts.
Comfort with data. You can build the dashboards and models you need to manage supply (SQL or spreadsheets).
An owner's mindset and comfort with ambiguity at an early-stage company.

This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Director of Product, Shopper based in Canada.

As Director of Product, Shopper, you will define and lead the product vision, strategy, and execution of a growing consumer shopping platform. You will oversee a multidisciplinary team of engineers, product managers, and designers responsible for delivering seamless mobile shopping experiences. Your mission will be to drive customer acquisition, activation, conversion, retention, and repeat purchases while making affordable shopping accessible to a wider audience. You will own the product roadmap, identify growth opportunities, and use data-driven experimentation to continuously improve the shopper journey. Working closely with Growth, Marketing, Retail, Data, and Engineering teams, you will shape innovative discovery and personalization experiences. This is an exciting leadership opportunity to scale a purpose-driven consumer marketplace while contributing to food waste reduction and more sustainable retail practices.

Accountabilities

Define product vision and strategy: Establish the long-term vision and strategic direction for the shopper experience, making affordable products increasingly accessible through an intuitive and engaging consumer platform.
Own product roadmap and priorities: Translate strategic objectives into a data-driven roadmap, identifying, evaluating, and sequencing opportunities based on customer needs, business impact, and growth potential.
Lead and develop cross-functional teams: Manage, mentor, and develop a multidisciplinary Shopper team comprising engineers, product managers, and designers. Support recruitment, leadership development, and organizational growth.
Drive business performance: Own key product and business metrics, including shopper acquisition, activation, conversion, repeat purchase rates, retention, and revenue growth.
Optimize the shopper journey: Oversee the complete customer funnel, from app installation and onboarding to product discovery, search, browsing, checkout, and post-purchase engagement.
Lead experimentation and continuous improvement: Establish a consistent testing and optimization process through A/B testing, funnel analysis, customer insights, and measurable product experiments.
Strengthen customer acquisition and engagement: Collaborate with Growth and Marketing teams on acquisition strategies, referrals, promotional campaigns, loyalty initiatives, and lifecycle communications.
Improve product discovery and personalization: Enhance search functionality, browsing experiences, merchandising, recommendations, and personalized offers to help shoppers find relevant products and local deals.
Leverage customer insights: Regularly engage with shoppers through interviews, behavioral analytics, session recordings, and customer support feedback to identify friction points and uncover opportunities.
Champion AI-driven innovation: Partner with Data and Machine Learning teams to integrate personalization, intelligent recommendations, demand signals, and AI-powered capabilities into the shopping experience.
Collaborate across business functions: Work closely with Retail and other departments to align product availability, inventory information, item data, and the overall customer experience.
Drive product excellence: Establish high standards for product specifications, decision-making, execution, prioritization, and post-launch performance evaluation while contributing to senior-level product and engineering leadership.

At least 8 years of experience in product management, ideally within consumer marketplaces, e-commerce, retail technology, or grocery-related businesses.

Strong understanding of consumer e-commerce fundamentals, including funnel optimization, search and merchandising, checkout experiences, customer acquisition, and lifecycle marketing.

Strong leadership and communication skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders, manage competing priorities, and build alignment across multidisciplinary teams.

Experience in grocery delivery, food retail, or marketplaces managing limited, perishable, or frequently changing inventory.

**Location:** Ontario, Canada


**Function:** Service Delivery

 **About Sitero**



Sitero is an emerging leader in clinical services and software solutions for the life sciences industry. We bring experience and expertise across a diverse range of therapeutic areas and focus on innovative, technology\-enabled solutions that let our clients concentrate on their core strengths. From early\-phase studies through Phase III clinical trials, our team delivers high\-touch services and technology that protect the safety of everyone across the clinical research community, with an emphasis on ethics, compliance, and innovation.

 **The Opportunity**



The Associate Vice President, Service Delivery leads how Sitero delivers its eClinical systems and services (such as RTSM, CTMS, Site Payments, EDC and eConsent) and owns the Project Management Office (PMO), which now sits within Service Delivery. The role is accountable for the service delivery organization’s strategy, financial performance, quality, and client outcomes. It also oversees the Director, PMO, and the PMO function, which brings governance, visibility, and execution discipline to every engagement from initiation through project closure.



This senior leadership role works closely with Clinical Services (including Data Management and Biostatistics), Business Development, Product Management, Finance, Quality, and HR. Together they make sure that what Sitero commits to commercially is delivered well.

 **What You Will Do**

 **Service Delivery Leadership \& Strategy**


* Set the vision, strategy, and operating model for Service Delivery, in line with Sitero’s corporate goals.
* Direct and manage all eClinical system delivery activities, including implementation, study build, configuration, and support for CTMS, RTSM, Payments, EDC, eConsent, and related platforms.
* Define, standardize, and continuously improve delivery processes across the eClinical portfolio.
* Direct and coordinate day\-to\-day activities across Service Delivery teams so that execution, delivery, and communication are effective.
* Lead the evaluation and adoption of new technology and delivery tools to improve efficiency, quality, and scalability.

  


**PMO Ownership \& Oversight**


* Lead the move of the PMO into Service Delivery and make it an integrated part of the delivery organization.
* Provide direct oversight of, and serve as the reporting manager for, the Director, PMO, including goal setting, performance management, and development.
* Approve and champion the PMO strategy, operating model, governance framework, and service offering.

Job Title

AVP, R&D

Job Description

We have a great opportunity to join our Global R&D function as a leader of a team of five actuaries and analysts. You will be leading the development of biometric assumptions for a range of different global reinsurance markets. We are looking for someone who can influence key stakeholders in the business to maximize the value of assumption knowledge.

In this role, you'll work with colleagues across the company on both Longevity and Protection markets in Europe and North America, giving you diverse exposure and the opportunity to make a real impact. You will be responsible for all aspects of the delivery of assumptions, from planning, team management, technical direction, stakeholder engagement and implementation.

A key focus over the next few years will be to scale the team capabilities for the increase in volume of assumptions which we need to produce. This will come through being courageous in improving economies of scale and standardizing and sharing capabilities.

You will lead stakeholder relationships with people across the business:

R&D teams across multiple geographies
Savings & Retirement and Protection teams inside the Reinsurance Division to support on Pricing and Product developments
Division teams such as Corporate Actuarial, Operations and Risk
Biometric teams in other Divisions on shared assumptions related to the US market

We are a collaborative and friendly team who thrive to provide their best. You will report to the VP, R&D.

How You’ll Help Move Us Forward

You'll be a recognized leader in actuarial assumption development — setting the direction, raising the bar, and leaving a visible mark on how we work across global markets.
Redefine what market-leading looks like. You'll bring genuine intellectual curiosity to assumption development — challenging inherited methodologies, pioneering new analytical approaches, and setting a standard that competitors will follow.
Build a team that scales with ambition. You'll be accountable for growing a high-performing function — streamlining how we work, eliminating inefficiency, and developing the next generation of actuarial talent.
Influence decisions at the highest level. You'll forge strong relationships with senior stakeholders across Pricing, Product, and beyond — translating complex technical judgements into clear, compelling recommendations that drive real business decisions.
Be the function's critical voice. You'll provide rigorous, independent challenge to Pricing assumptions — ensuring intellectual honesty sits at the heart of everything we do.
Shape the profession, not just the company. Through thought leadership, academic partnerships, and research initiatives, you'll help define where actuarial thinking goes next.

Desirable Skills & Experience

Demonstrable exposure to assumption development with a reinsurer, life company or consultancy. This could be through working directly in a pricing or basis setting team or through a review function.

Report writing and verbal communication skills, including ability to present to senior managers and to forge close relationships with other teams.

Organised and deadline focused.
Interest and understanding of programming and comfortable with or willing to learn software packages, such as Tableau, SQL (or comparable database language) and R.
Experience with people management or mentoring, and interest in coaching and developing junior staff.

The District of Peachland is seeking an experienced and community-minded leader to join our team and help serve Canada’s Kindest Community. As a member of the Senior Leadership Team, the Director advises the CAO, departmental leaders, and Council on budgeting, asset management, and funding, and leads the Finance Department through the Deputy Director of Finance.

This is a full-time permanent role with an anticipated start date by February 2027.

Financial Strategy & Governance

Oversee financial bylaws, policies, and reporting, and accounts payable and receivable, including invoicing for all departments.

Exceptional leadership, communication, and relationship-building skills, with political and organizational acumen.
