jobs.title: Managing Director, Housing & Infrastructure
jobs.description:
The Inuvialuit Regional Corporation (IRC) is a uniquely positioned Indigenous organization dedicated to enhancing the economic, social, and cultural well-being of Inuvialuit beneficiaries through the implementation of the historic Inuvialuit Final Agreement (IFA). Established in 1984 and headquartered in Inuvik, Northwest Territories, IRC represents the collective interests of six Inuvialuit communities, including 35,000 square miles of Inuvialuit-owned lands. Today, IRC is a significant and multifaceted organization with more than 180 employees, $1.9 billion in assets, and a broad mandate spanning land stewardship, investment, economic development, health, education, culture, and community development. Through its diverse operations, subsidiaries, programs, and partnerships, IRC plays a central role in advancing Inuvialuit participation in the northern economy while supporting the long-term prosperity, self-determination, and well-being of Inuvialuit communities.

Reporting directly to the Chair and Chief Executive Officer, the Managing Director, Housing & Infrastructure will lead IRC’s capacity to plan and deliver housing, community facilities, and major infrastructure across the Inuvialuit Settlement Region. This is represented by four key functions: Programme Planning and Controls, Housing Delivery, Owner’s Engineering and Assurance, and Infrastructure Delivery. Housing represents the most immediate and substantial priority, with more than 150 units currently forecast to 2030, and a further assessed need of more than 1,000 units by 2040. Beyond delivering individual projects, the Managing Director will help establish the longer-term master planning, standardized approaches, project controls, procurement strategies, and supply-chain solutions needed to accelerate housing and infrastructure development across IRC’s communities. They will also act as owner’s representative for several infrastructure projects related to NORAD’s Forward Operating Location in Inuvik working closely with the Canadian Department of National Defense. And they will plan and deliver additional infrastructure in the region to support the projected population growth and increased activity.

The role will require breadth as much as scale. IRC’s growing capital portfolio spans housing, community, energy, transportation, logistics, commercial, and other major infrastructure. Each element of this portfolio is shaped by the realities of remote northern delivery, short construction seasons, constrained logistics, and limited resupply windows. As the ideal candidate, you bring extensive experience leading complex, multidisciplinary capital programs across the full project lifecycle and, ideally, demonstrated experience delivering in the North or Arctic. Exceptional leaders from similarly remote, logistically constrained, or uniquely complex environments will also be relevant. Above all, the Managing Director will hold the owner’s seat, and be responsible for setting requirements, challenging designers and contractors, managing cost and schedule, and ensuring projects are delivered safely, practically, and to IRC’s expectations.

This is an opportunity to build an enduring infrastructure capability within IRC and leave a lasting positive impact across the entire region and the nation. The Managing Director will establish and lead each of the four key functions, building a permanent internal team while effectively directing seconded personnel and external delivery partners. For a practical, purpose-driven leader attracted to complex delivery and northern development, the opportunity combines immediate execution with the chance to create the systems, capability, and Inuvialuit capacity required to support IRC’s communities and ambitions for decades to come.

To explore this opportunity further, please click ‘apply’.

Few organizations have the reach, relationships and opportunity to shape community well-being across British Columbia quite like United Way British Columbia ("UWBC"). As one of the province's most recognized and influential charitable organizations, UWBC brings together people, resources, expertise and partners to tackle ever-evolving and pressing social challenges. Built on a proud legacy of community leadership, UWBC is unique in its ability to offer both deep local expertise and the reach and influence of a province-wide organization.

Not the United Way you may think you know.

Founded on a federated fundraising/grantor model and largely based on workplace campaigns, the organization has very deliberately moved toward partnered program delivery, community mobilization and solutions designed around demonstrated gaps. The impact of this shift can be seen in every corner of the province. An historic amalgamation of regional United Way organizations, as well as a merger with BC211, has enhanced the strategic capability of the organization. Today, UWBC is what most social impact organizations can only aspire to be: a high profile social impact organization with local presence; provincial scale; specialist expertise; strong government relationships at all levels, and enviable capacity to innovate.

Reporting to the Board of Directors, the Chief Executive Officer (“CEO”) will lead UWBC into an exciting new chapter. Following the tenure of a long-serving leader, the next CEO joins at an exciting juncture. With an opportunity to shape the development of the next strategic plan, and supported by a committed Board and team, this leader will play an important role in advancing United Way BC’s mission and strengthening its high-profile impact across the province. The Board is looking to the next CEO to sharpen the organization’s strategic focus, strengthen financial sustainability and funding opportunities and establish greater clarity around where UWBC can deliver the greatest impact.

As the next CEO, you are a proven, forward-thinking and values-driven leader who has demonstrated an ability to lead an organization through ongoing change. Collaborative and inspiring, you have a track record of translating strategy into results, building capacity at an enterprise level and fostering partnerships that drive organizational success. Combining financial and operational acumen with exceptional leadership, relationship-building skills and political awareness, you bring the credibility, courage and commitment to advance UWBC's mission and strengthen its impact at a time when communities across British Columbia are facing increasingly complex social challenges. The power of collective action has never been more important. About the Opportunity

MERE HR & Consulting
is pleased to partner with an established and respected electronics manufacturing organization in Markham, Ontario, in the search for an accomplished Director of Supply Chain
.

Our client specializes in providing comprehensive electronic manufacturing and design services, supporting customers through printed circuit board (PCB) assembly, electronic component integration, product testing, prototyping, and low-to-mid-volume manufacturing. Operating in a technically demanding environment, the organization places significant emphasis on product quality, manufacturing efficiency, supply chain reliability, and customer satisfaction.

As the organization continues to strengthen its operational capabilities, it is seeking a highly experienced supply chain leader who can bring strategic direction, financial discipline, strong supplier relationships, and proven leadership to its supply chain operations.

This is an excellent opportunity for a results-oriented professional who understands the complexities of electronics manufacturing and is prepared to take ownership of supply chain performance at both the strategic and operational levels.

The Position

Reporting directly to the Chief Operating Officer, the Director of Supply Chain will provide overall leadership and direction for the organization's supply chain function, encompassing strategic procurement, inventory management, material planning, supplier performance, and the movement of components and finished products throughout the manufacturing process.

The successful candidate will play an important role in balancing customer delivery commitments with inventory investment, procurement costs, supplier reliability, and operational efficiency.
Beyond managing day-to-day activities, this individual will be expected to evaluate existing systems and practices, identify opportunities for improvement, establish sustainable processes, and develop a high-performing supply chain team capable of supporting changing manufacturing demands.

The ideal candidate combines strategic business thinking with hands-on electronics manufacturing experience
, understands the challenges associated with global component sourcing, and can translate business priorities into measurable operational results.

Key Responsibilities

1. Supply Chain Strategy & Executive Leadership

Develop, implement, and continuously refine an integrated supply chain strategy aligned with the organization's operational objectives, financial priorities, and customer service expectations.
Provide senior-level oversight of purchasing, material planning, inventory management, supplier relationships, and supply chain execution.
Take accountability for supply chain operating costs, inventory investment, supplier performance, and the organization's ability to meet customer delivery commitments.
Identify opportunities to reduce overall supply chain costs while maintaining product quality, continuity of supply, and customer satisfaction.
Partner with the COO and other members of senior management on operational planning, business improvement initiatives, and strategic projects.

2. Strategic Procurement & Global Supplier Management

Direct purchasing and sourcing activities for electronic components, printed circuit board assemblies, semiconductor products, electro-mechanical components, and other manufacturing materials.
Develop and maintain strong commercial relationships with domestic and international suppliers, contract manufacturers, and strategic business partners.
Lead supplier negotiations involving pricing, commercial terms, lead times, material availability, and service expectations.
Evaluate supplier capabilities, performance, cost structures, and associated operational risks.
Develop sourcing strategies to minimize exposure to global supply disruptions, extended procurement lead times, and supplier capacity constraints.
Work closely with suppliers and internal stakeholders to resolve material availability, quality, pricing, and delivery challenges.

3. Inventory Management, Material Planning & Supply Chain Performance

Oversee the planning and movement of materials throughout the supply chain, from initial purchasing and supplier delivery through manufacturing and final customer shipment.

Lean manufacturing principles and continuous improvement practices.
Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) and Material Requirements Planning (MRP) systems to improve planning accuracy, inventory controls, and operational visibility.
Develop standardized processes and reporting practices to improve consistency, accountability, and decision-making.
Identify and eliminate process bottlenecks that affect purchasing efficiency, material flow, inventory management, or customer delivery.
Encourage data-driven decision-making supported by meaningful operational and financial performance measures.
Lead or participate in strategic improvement projects assigned by executive leadership.

, including significant responsibility for procurement, inventory management, material planning, and supply chain operations.

, with demonstrated responsibility for managing supply chain teams and operational performance.

jobs.title: Chief of Staff, Client Families
jobs.description:
About Us

Mayfair is a private family office. We design, build and run the office that sits around a principal’s wealth and their life, so the people who created that wealth don’t have to run it themselves.

The people who join now will shape what Mayfair becomes, from how we bring on new principals to how we work together. Your work will show up in the company as much as in the principals you serve.

The Role

You’ll run the office for each principal you serve. You’ll be their single point of contact and direct the work across our five verticals. You’ll sit beside the principal, not three layers below them, and see the whole picture rather than one slice of it. Your judgment shapes real outcomes for the people we serve. You’ll work with a small number of principals. How many depends on the level of service each one has chosen. You become the person they call first. When something needs a decision, you bring it to them with the work done and the options framed. The decisions stay with them.

You won’t carry the work alone. Our own people run the five verticals behind you, and AI handles much of the research, reporting, and document prep underneath. That leaves your time for the principal and the judgment calls.

You don’t need to be an expert in all matters. You need to know when a question calls for a specialist, bring in the right people, and make sure the principal has what they need to decide. Knowing who to call matters more than knowing every answer.

What You'll Do

• Become the principal’s right hand, and build the relationship over years, not quarters.
• Run the reporting and meeting cadence so the principal knows what’s coming before it arrives.
• Keep the decision log. When something needs a decision, bring it with the work done and the options framed.
• Have the difficult conversations when they come up, whether that’s telling a principal a plan won’t work, holding an advisor to a missed deadline, or helping family members work through a disagreement.
• Direct our Asset Administration & Reporting, Banking & Treasury, Financial Operations, Wealth Oversight and Tax & Structures teams so the work gets done well and on time. In a given month that might mean signing off the bill pay schedule, approving a capital call, reviewing the monthly close and cash forecast, or planning the tax work ahead of a business sale.
• Oversee the life side of the office: property managers, household staff, aviation, travel, IT and security.
• Put governance and controls in place, from approval limits to how payments are authorized, and keep them working.
• Hold the principal’s lawyers, accountants, bankers and investment managers accountable to one plan and one set of facts.
• Spot early when a situation needs a specialist. You don’t need to be the expert, but you need to know when one is needed. If a principal is heading toward a sale, the tax and legal team should be in place months before the deal, not the week it closes.
• Lead triage for new principals: map every advisor, account, entity and asset, learn the principal’s values, and set up how they want approvals to work.
• Help shape how Mayfair onboards, reports and runs reviews as the company grows.

What We're Looking For

• Five or more years at manager or senior manager level in a Big Four private client group, or a comparable role in private banking, wealth advisory or a multi-family office, including leading complex, multi-advisor projects for ultra-high-net-worth individuals and families.
• Strong emotional intelligence. You read people well and earn trust quickly. You notice what a principal isn’t saying, stay steady when a conversation gets difficult, and can tell them something they don’t want to hear. This matters more than anything else on this list.
• Ease with significant wealth. You’re comfortable with founders, executives and multi-generational families, and you hold your own with them and with their lawyer, accountant and banker in the same room.
• A generalist’s curiosity. One week it’s a pre-sale reorganization, the next it’s an aircraft purchase, a new trust or a renovation. You don’t need to be the expert in each. What matters is learning enough to run it and knowing when to bring in someone who is.
• Clear, simple communication. You can take something complex and make it simple. A principal should be able to read your summary in five minutes and know the options, the trade-offs and what needs deciding.
• A CPA, TEP, CFA or equivalent professional designation.
• Flexibility to work across North American time zones. Some travel is required, in Canada and the US.
• You live in Canada and are legally entitled to work in Canada.

Nice to Have

• Experience at an early startup, ideally one still defining its own operating model while building.
• Background in wealth tech, legal tech, or fintech.
• Working familiarity with family office concepts: trusts, entity structures, investment policy statements, manager oversight, and how those pieces interact.
• Experience working alongside a small team without a large product organization or established tooling around you.
• A CPA In-Depth or Master of Taxation, Canada and US cross-border experience, or time in a family office.

Logistics

• Remote, based anywhere in Canada. Full-time and permanent.
• Base salary range: $165,000 to $185,000 CAD per year. Where you land in the range reflects your experience.
• Standard business hours, with flexibility across North American time zones.
• Some travel is required, in Canada and the US.

How We Hire

Five values guide how we work:
Do What Is Right.
Be In The Arena.
Earn The Right.
All In. One Team.
Fear Nothing. Solve Everything.
They are the first filter for anyone who joins us, ahead of the interview and ahead of skills.

Because this role approves client payments and other financial transactions, the process includes a background check, including a credit check, with your written consent.

We give everyone we interview an answer.

How to Apply

Apply through LinkedIn with your resume. We highly recommend a cover letter. Make it the first page of the same PDF you upload as your resume.

In the first line of your cover letter, tell us your favourite restaurant, or a place you would take a visitor, in the city where you live.

Mayfair welcomes applications from all qualified candidates. If you need an accommodation at any point in the process, tell us and we’ll work with you.

A trusted partner to the entire UBC Community - including the President and executive team, Board of Governors, Host Nations, Deans and senior leaders, student leaders, campus residents and alumni community - the VPFO will translate institutional priorities into sustainable multi-year financial and operating strategies in service of the University’s academic mission. The role calls for a leader who builds and engages strong teams, communicates complex choices clearly, has successfully demonstrated change in a complex environment, and balances institutional consistency with the needs of a distributed academic environment.

At Visa, you'll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world.

Join Visa and do work that matters – to you, to your community, and to the world. Progress starts with you.

Job Description

Company Description

Visa is a world leader in payments and technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories. Our mission is to connect the world through the most innovative, convenient, reliable and secure payments network, enabling individuals, businesses and economies to thrive.

Make an impact with a purpose-driven industry leader. Join us and experience Life at Visa.

The Canada Strategy & Operations team helps shape how Visa Canada grows and executes against its market priorities. Working closely with Canada market leadership, Sales, Business Lines, Finance and regional teams, the team connects strategy with execution and helps ensure we focus on the opportunities that matter most. The team’s remit spans market and commercial strategy, sales operations, business planning and performance management, with a focus on continuously improving how we serve clients and drive growth.

What a Director, Strategy & Operations does at Visa Canada

The Director, Strategy & Operations is responsible for strengthening commercial strategy, sales effectiveness and operating discipline across the market, serving as a key partner to the sales organization and Canada leadership team. Reporting to the Vice President, Strategy & Operations, the Director will translate Canada’s strategic priorities into commercial action, strengthen performance management, and continuously evolve how we sell as client expectations, competition and technology change.

The role requires someone who can move comfortably between strategy and execution, identifying where and how we should grow and translating those opportunities into clear priorities and measurable outcomes.

Sales & Commercial Strategy

Translate Canada’s market priorities into clear sales and commercialization strategies.
Support client segmentation, account prioritization and coverage strategy.
Partner with Sales and Business Lines to identify and accelerate priority growth opportunities.
Help evolve Canada’s sales and coverage model as client needs, competition and the payments landscape change.

Commercial Performance & Execution

Own the Canada sales operating rhythm, including forecasting, performance management and business reviews.
Track performance against revenue, payment volume and sales objectives, providing clear, forward-looking insights.
Support the Canada Leadership Team operating rhythm, ensuring discussions are anchored in business performance, strategic priorities, key risks and clear actions.
Identify performance gaps, commercial risks and growth opportunities and drive actions to improve outcomes.
Provide leadership with a clear view of business performance and areas requiring intervention.

Improve how the frontline sells, including account planning, opportunity management, pipeline discipline and CRM adoption.
Strengthen the connection between account plans, commercial opportunities, investments and business outcomes.
Simplify processes, remove friction and increase seller capacity, improving productivity and commercial effectiveness.
Leverage data, automation and AI to strengthen insights, streamline work and enable better client engagement and decision-making.
Partner with regional and global teams to bring relevant tools, capabilities and best practices into Canada.

Strategic Leadership & Partnership

Serve as a trusted thought partner to Canada leadership and account executives.
Bring a fact-based, forward-looking perspective to commercial priorities, investments and resource decisions.
Influence across a highly matrixed organization to translate priorities into action and measurable results.

10+ years of experience in strategy, sales operations, commercial management, consulting, financial services, payments or a related field.

Strong commercial and financial acumen, with experience in sales planning, forecasting, pipeline management, performance management and/or commercialization.
Experience in payments, banking, fintech or a complex B2B commercial environment preferred.

Demonstrated ability to translate strategy into execution, turning complex business priorities into clear plans, actions and measurable outcomes.

Job Description

Why should you join our team?

Innergex Renewable Energy Inc. is an independent renewable energy producer with an extensive and growing portfolio of assets in Canada, the United States, France and Chile. The Corporation develops, acquires, owns and operates hydroelectric facilities, wind farms, solar farms and energy storage facilities.

We are convinced that generating power from renewable sources will lead the way to a better world. We remain committed to responsible growth that balances people, our planet, and prosperity. We believe in offering an engaging, inclusive and supportive work environment where each team member can thrive.

Your contribution!

The Director of Financial Reporting provides strategic and operational leadership for the Financial Reporting function. The incumbent is responsible for the quality, integrity, completeness, and compliance of the consolidation, financial disclosure, and financial reporting processes under his or her responsibility, in accordance with applicable accounting standards, current regulatory requirements, and company policies. They remain ultimately responsible for the quality of these reports, including the proper application of IFRS, the consistency of financial disclosures, and the appropriateness of the accounting positions adopted prior to their approval by the Corporate Controller.

They also play a key role in talent development, succession planning, the ongoing improvement of processes, systems, and controls related to financial reporting, as well as in supporting strategic initiatives related to growth, restructuring, financing, and acquisitions.

Your day-to-day!

Provide strategic and operational leadership for the Financial Reporting function and ensure its continued development to meet the organization's current and future needs.
Be accountable for the quality, integrity, completeness, and compliance of the consolidated financial statements, the statutory financial statements under their responsibility, and the related financial disclosures, as well as for the appropriate application of accounting standards, the consistency of financial disclosures, and the appropriateness of the accounting judgments and positions adopted.
Ensure that financial information complies with IFRS, applicable regulatory requirements, financing agreements, company policies, and best practices in financial disclosure.
Serve as the internal authority on consolidation, financial reporting, and technical accounting for significant transactions, including acquisitions, divestitures, restructurings, financing, strategic projects, and complex commercial agreements.
Make recommendations to senior management regarding accounting policies that have a significant impact on the organization's financial statements, financial performance, or disclosure requirements.
Ensure the governance of data, consolidation structures, and financial disclosure processes that support the organization's financial reporting.
Serve as the primary point of contact for external auditors regarding financial statements, significant accounting policies, internal controls over financial reporting, and other matters within the scope of the position.
Support the organization's strategic initiatives, including acquisitions, divestitures, corporate restructurings, financing, growth projects, and organizational transformations that impact financial reporting.
Develop talent, ensure succession planning for the Financial Reporting function, and continuously strengthen the team's skills.
Promote continuous improvement, automation, and process standardization to enhance the quality, efficiency, agility, and resilience of the Financial Reporting function.

Your skills, our requirements!

At least 10 years of progressive experience in financial accounting, financial reporting, and consolidation.
Bachelor's degree in accounting.
Hold a professional accounting certification (CPA).
Proven experience in complex consolidation environments involving a large number of legal entities, multidimensional corporate structures, partnerships, non-controlling interests, complex joint venture or investment structures, and frequent corporate reorganizations.
Proven experience in cost accounting, including analyzing and documenting accounting positions related to complex transactions.
Significant experience in preparing, reviewing, and overseeing consolidated financial statements in accordance with IFRS. Experience with US GAAP is a plus.
A proven ability to design and refine processes that simultaneously improve operational efficiency, the quality of financial reporting, and the robustness of controls.
Experience in management and team development.
Experience with leading financial consolidation tools.
A recognized leader capable of mobilizing teams of professionals and exerting credible influence with internal and external stakeholders on complex issues related to financial reporting, financial disclosure, and technical accounting.
Strong professional judgment and a proven ability to analyze, challenge, and defend positions, conclusions, and recommendations related to complex issues of consolidation, financial reporting, and financial disclosure to external auditors, management, and other stakeholders.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills (French and English; Spanish is a plus), including the ability to explain complex financial and accounting issues in layman’s terms to people at various levels within the organization.
Strong ability to fulfill a governance role, manage risks related to financial reporting, and strike a balance between rigor, operational performance, and business needs.
Strategic thinking that enables one to anticipate the financial, accounting, and organizational impacts of business decisions and transformation projects.
Recognized leadership in talent development, succession planning, employee engagement, and building high-performing teams.
Ability to operate effectively in an environment involving complex transactions, corporate restructurings, acquisitions, financings, or other events requiring a high level of expertise and judgment.
Extensive knowledge of Oracle Fusion or a comparable integrated ERP system.
Very good knowledge of a financial consolidation tool such as OneStream, HFM, or an equivalent tool.
Very good knowledge of a financial disclosure tool such as Workiva or an equivalent tool.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and financial analysis tools.
Ability to leverage automation, data analytics, and artificial intelligence tools to improve the efficiency, quality, and reliability of financial reporting processes.
Bilingualism (French and English, both spoken and written) is required to facilitate ongoing collaboration with various stakeholders outside Quebec.

Additional considerations!

The position is based at the Company’s headquarters in Longueuil, conveniently located steps from the Longueuil–Université-de-Sherbrooke metro station.

jobs.title: Director, Solutions Architecture
jobs.description:
About Coursera + Udemy

Coursera and Udemy are now one company, bringing together two mission-driven brands to create the world’s most powerful platform for turning learning into progress. Together, we help more than 300 million learners and 12,000+ enterprise customers build the skills they need for a world being reshaped by AI. Read more about the combined company by visiting our blog.

Why join us now?

AI is transforming how people learn, work, and grow, and the need for new skills has never been greater. Coursera brings trusted content and credentials from leading university and industry partners, while Udemy brings a dynamic skills marketplace and global network of real-world experts. By combining these strengths, we can connect more people and organizations to the skills they need, when they need them.

Shape What Comes Next

By joining our team, you’ll have the opportunity to reshape how the world learns and applies skills—and help millions of people participate in the new economy. Bring your ideas, expertise, and perspective to meaningful work that can make a difference at global scale.

How We Work

Coursera + Udemy lets you choose the best way to work, whether it’s from home, an office, or a collaboration space. We’re a globally distributed team that comes together intentionally for collaboration, complex problem-solving, and key milestones — creating opportunities for teams to come together. If you’re ready to make a global impact, help scale unique products across Coursera + Udemy, and grow your career, apply below.

Job Overview:

Within Professional Services, you'll lead the Solutions Architecture team through a fundamental change: from a technical intake team that passes integration work to third parties to a team that designs and builds the integrations we choose to own on Workato. You'll decide which integrations are strategic to own and which third parties can deliver faster, and you'll balance capacity across Coursera and Udemy technical work. You'll lay a foundation to build from, so that integrations are productized and reusable rather than one-offs, and you'll upskill the team to design, build, and test the way an engineering team does. You'll also take ownership of integrations built by third parties for both Coursera and Udemy, and decide what, if anything, to migrate in house. This is a highly operational role. You'll redesign how the team works with Product, Partnerships, Presales, and Customer Support, define workflows that are not yet defined, and build the delivery discipline, capacity model, and metrics that make the function run like a well-oiled machine. You'll report to the Senior Director of Professional Services and partner closely with the Director of AI Innovation to streamline how the team works.

Responsibilities:

Lead the shift from a technical intake team that routes work to third parties to a team that builds the integrations we choose to own, and set the criteria, service levels, and pricing for what we own versus what third parties deliver.
Own the integration roadmap and prioritization with Product, Partnerships, Engineering, and Support, and make capacity and load-balancing tradeoffs across Coursera and Udemy technical work.
Establish the Workato foundation and productize what we can, with shared standards and reusable components, and a custom layer on top that is easy to adapt. Build reuse into design review.
Take ownership of the inherited integrations, six years of third-party work on the Coursera platform and a handful on Udemy. Document them, decide what, if anything, to migrate, retire, or keep, and steward the code and its environment.
Hire and upskill the team to design, build, and test like engineers, aligned with Coursera Engineering's standards. Use AI-assisted development deliberately so the team builds fundamentals first, and manage token usage.
Redesign how the team works, including Jira, intake, and workflows with Product, Partnerships, Presales, and Support, and train Support to deflect development-related tickets.
Own the run and support model for what we build, including monitoring, maintenance, versioning, and service levels. Meet security, contractual, and data privacy standards, and serve as the senior escalation point for high-risk issues.
Partner with Presales on early scoping and own the technical handoff from Sales into delivery. Work with the Director of AI Innovation and Solutions on the pilot-to-PS transition review and on streamlining the team's work.
Run utilization and project tracking, manage the technical service catalog, pricing, SOWs, and margin, and build metrics that show impact on deal size, time to production, retention, and quality.

Basic Qualifications:

8+ years of experience in solutions architecture, technical professional services, or integration consulting, with a strong focus on API integrations (REST, SOAP, GraphQL) and cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud.
Proven experience leading and developing technical teams, ideally globally distributed, and running a technical delivery function, including capacity planning, utilization, and cross-team workflows.
Experience building reusable, productized integrations on an iPaaS platform and designing for reuse across customers.
Experience applying engineering standards (SDLC, design and code review, testing) to integration delivery, and coaching a team to adopt them.
Experience taking over third-party-built or inherited code and making build, buy, partner, and migrate decisions, including managing third-party partners.
Direct experience in pre-sales activity for technical services, including discovery, scoping, and SOW creation.
Strong communicator with stakeholders from engineers to executives. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Preferred Qualifications:

Hands-on experience with Workato, or a comparable iPaaS platform such as MuleSoft, Boomi, Jitterbit, or Tray.io.
Integration experience with SSO, ERP, HRIS, and LMS/LXP systems.
Experience integrating teams, codebases, or service portfolios through a merger or acquisition.
Proficiency in data analytics and SQL.

Compensation

Coursera offers competitive pay and fair compensation practices across all regions. Job titles may span multiple career levels, and the targeted hiring base salary range for this role in Canada is $175,000 - $218,000. Actual compensation will depend on factors such as experience, education, transferable skills, business needs, and location. This range may be adjusted over time and may include eligibility for variable pay, equity, and comprehensive benefits.

Application Window:
December 7, 2026

We anticipate the application window will be open until December 7, 2026. Based on business needs, this opportunity may remain posted beyond or closed before the anticipated application window.

For more information about how Coursera collects and uses your personal information, please see our Coursera + Udemy Global Applicant Privacy Notice.

jobs.description:
Business Introduction

GSK remains committed to achieving bold commercial ambitions for the future. By 2031, we aim to deliver £40 billion in annual sales, leveraging our existing strong performance momentum to significantly increase our positive impact on the health of billions of patients globally. Our Ahead Together strategy is centered on early intervention to prevent and alter the course of disease, thereby protecting people and supporting healthcare systems. Our diverse portfolio consists of vaccines, specialty medicines, and general medicines. Through continuous innovation and a dedicated focus on scientific and technical excellence, we strive to develop and launch new, groundbreaking treatments that address critical health challenges.

Position Summary

Are you energized by leading one of Canada's most significant oncology businesses while shaping the future of lung cancer care through multiple innovative launches?

If so, this Commercial Director, Lung Cancer role may be the ideal opportunity to leverage your strategic leadership capabilities while driving transformational growth across one of GSK Canada's most important oncology portfolios.

As a member of the Canadian Oncology Leadership Team, the Commercial Director will provide strategic and operational leadership for the Lung Cancer business, including responsibility for the successful launch of multiple pipeline assets. This individual will lead a high-performing commercial organization and work across Medical, Market Access, Regulatory, Commercial Excellence, Finance and Global teams to ensure patients receive timely access to innovative therapies. The Commercial Director will play a pivotal role in shaping GSK Canada's oncology strategy and delivering sustainable business growth while building organizational capability for the future.

Responsibilities

This role will provide YOU the opportunity to lead key activities to progress YOUR career. These responsibilities include some of the following:

Strategic Leadership & Business Performance

Develop and execute the long-term strategic vision for the Lung Cancer portfolio, ensuring sustained growth and market leadership.
Lead commercial strategy development and execution for pipeline assets.
Own portfolio performance, including sales growth, market share, profitability, forecasting accuracy, and business planning.
Establish strategic priorities and resource allocation decisions that maximize patient impact and business outcomes.
Drive annual planning, forecasting, and commercial investment decisions across the portfolio.

Launch Leadership

Lead launch readiness and commercialization activities for multiple upcoming oncology launches.
Oversee development and execution of comprehensive launch strategies across sales, marketing, medical, market access, diagnostics, and external stakeholder engagement.
Ensure robust launch governance, performance measurement, and optimization processes.
Partner closely with Global and Regional teams to influence launch strategies and share best practices.

Cross-Functional Enterprise Leadership

Lead and inspire a high-performing cross-functional oncology team consisting of Sales, Marketing, Medical Affairs, Market Access, Regulatory, Finance, Commercial Excellence, Digital, Analytics and Operations.
Build strong alignment across internal stakeholders to accelerate business performance and execution excellence.
Serve as a key member of the Canadian Oncology Leadership Team, contributing to broader business unit strategy and organizational priorities.
Effectively influence senior leaders both within Canada and globally.

People Leadership

Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team and leadership bench.
Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, inclusion, and continuous improvement.
Attract, develop, and retain top commercial talent.
Build organizational capability to support current and future oncology growth opportunities.

External Engagement

Develop relationships with key external stakeholders, including healthcare professionals, cancer centers, advocacy organizations, healthcare decision makers, and industry partners.
Ensure deep customer and market understanding informs business decisions.
Champion a patient-centered approach to strategy development and execution.

Why You?

Basic Qualifications

We are seeking professionals with the following required skills and qualifications to help us achieve our goals:

Bachelor's degree.
12+ years of progressive pharmaceutical or biotechnology commercial experience.
Significant sales and marketing leadership experience within specialty pharmaceuticals.
Proven oncology commercial leadership experience, including launch and lifecycle management.
Demonstrated success leading large, complex businesses with multiple strategic priorities.
Strong experience in strategic planning, forecasting, business performance management, and commercial investment planning.
Experience leading and developing high-performing teams and people leaders.
Demonstrated ability to influence across a matrix organization and successfully partner with Global stakeholders.
Exceptional communication, executive presence, and stakeholder management skills.
Strong analytical and strategic thinking capabilities with the ability to translate insights into action.

Preferred Qualifications

If you have the following characteristics, it would be a plus:

Lung cancer or thoracic oncology experience.
Experience leading multiple concurrent product launches.
Launch excellence experience within oncology.
MBA or advanced business degree.
Market Access and reimbursement experience in Canada.
Strong understanding of diagnostic and biomarker testing landscapes.
Experience working across Canadian, Regional, and Global commercial organizations.
Bilingual (English/French).

Leadership Success Profile

The successful candidate will demonstrate:

Enterprise and strategic mindset.
Courageous leadership and decision-making.
Strong commercial acumen.
Ability to thrive in ambiguity and manage complexity.
Talent development and coaching excellence.
Exceptional cross-functional leadership.
Customer and patient focus.
Proven ability to deliver results through others.

Work Arrangement

This role is based in Mississauga, Ontario and offers a hybrid working model. You will join us in the office regularly to collaborate with your team and partners while having the flexibility to work remotely when suitable.

How To Apply

We want to hear from you. Please submit your resume and a brief cover letter to share why this role excites you and how your experience fits. We review applications fairly and promptly. If you have questions, please reach out through the application platform. Join us and be part of a team that is passionate about improving patients’ lives every day.

Skills

Business Planning, Data to Insights, Digital Fluency, Launch Excellence, Scientific Literacy, Strategic Planning

Why GSK?

Uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together.

GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. We aim to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade, as a successful, growing company where people can thrive. We get ahead of disease by preventing and treating it with innovation in specialty medicines and vaccines. We focus on four therapeutic areas: respiratory, immunology and inflammation; oncology; HIV; and infectious diseases – to impact health at scale.

People and patients around the world count on the medicines and vaccines we make, so we’re committed to creating an environment where our people can thrive and focus on what matters most. Our culture of being ambitious for patients, accountable for impact and doing the right thing is the foundation for how, together, we deliver for patients, shareholders and our people.

This ensures that all qualified applicants will receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, gender identity, and sexual orientation), parental status, national origin, age, disability, genetic information (including family medical history), military service or any basis prohibited under federal, state or local law. jobs.title: VP, Engineering Operations
jobs.description:
Who We Are

We're Redis. We built the product that runs the fast apps our world runs on. (If you checked the weather, used your credit card, or looked at your flight status online today, you’re welcome.) At Redis, you’ll work with the fastest, simplest technology in the business—whether you’re building it, telling its story, or selling it to our 10,000+ worldwide customers. We’re creating a faster world with simpler experiences. You in?

Why would you love this job?

Engineering Operations is a high-leverage function within the CTO organization. Its purpose is to make Engineering and Cloud Operations execution legible, commitments durable, and leadership time scalable—primarily through clarity, technical depth, and strategic influence.

As VP, Engineering Operations, you will build and evolve the operating system of the CTO organization while steering the AI transformation of our engineering and cloud infrastructure operations. You will work across Engineering, Cloud Ops, and product partners to create confidence in delivery, surface technical risks early, drive modern AI-enabled engineering workflows, and empower leaders to focus on long-term strategy and architectural outcomes.

This is a highly visible role for a deeply technical operator who can move comfortably between software architecture, cloud platforms, AI-driven automation, data, and organizational dynamics. You will succeed not by adding bureaucracy, but by introducing intelligent, modern structures for better architectural decisions, clear ownership, and scalable execution.

What You’ll Do

Own the Engineering operating system

Design, run, and continuously improve the CTO organization’s operating cadence, including quarterly business reviews, initiative and program reviews, goal-setting cycles, leadership forums, and internal communications.
Establish lightweight, reusable standards for agendas, pre-reads, synthesis, status, risk and confidence language, ownership, dependencies, decision capture, and follow-through.
Turn fragmented execution signals into concise, decision-ready narratives for the CTO and Engineering leadership.
Ensure forums drive decisions and tradeoffs—not simply status updates.

Create execution visibility and confidence

Make Engineering priorities, commitments, dependencies, and risks visible across the company.
Improve the quality and timeliness of early risk detection and escalation.
Use data and qualitative signals together to distinguish real progress from activity or optimism.

Align priorities, people, and investment

Partner with the CTO, Engineering leaders, Finance, People, Product, and other functions to connect strategy, priorities, capacity, headcount, funding, and operating norms.
Support workforce and headcount planning, financial and investment alignment, and organizational planning with clear analysis and decision materials.
Improve cross-geo and cross-functional operating norms so expectations are explicit rather than assumed.

Provide leverage on strategic and special initiatives

Bring structure to ambiguous, cross-cutting, or high-risk initiatives that do not yet have a natural program home.
Support high-impact company priorities such as major transformations, IPO readiness, M&A diligence, or other initiatives requiring CTO-level coordination.
Know when to stay involved, when to escalate, and when to exit so Engineering Operations does not become a permanent dependency.

Build durable operating muscle

Institutionalize good judgment into reusable systems, templates, and standards.
Use automation, analytics, and AI-assisted workflows thoughtfully to improve signal quality and operating leverage.
Socialize changes effectively and build adoption through clarity, usefulness, and trust—not compliance theater.

Drive AI Transformation in Engineering and Cloud Operations

Architect and execute strategic initiatives that integrate AI technologies into software development lifecycles, CI/CD pipelines, and cloud operations to accelerate innovation and developer efficiency.
Establish frameworks and benchmarks to evaluate the adoption, effectiveness, and impact of AI tools across engineering and cloud infrastructure teams.
Lead cross-functional programs focused on automated observability, AI-driven incident management, and intelligent cloud resource optimization.

What will you need to have?

Deep technical background in software engineering, distributed systems, or cloud infrastructure operations alongside experience in a strategic leadership or business operations role.
A demonstrated ability to turn ambiguous, cross-functional problems into clear decisions, ownership, operating mechanisms, and measurable outcomes.
Experience designing and running operating cadences, business reviews, planning processes, leadership forums, or comparable mechanisms that improve execution.
The ability to influence without relying on formal authority and to build trust across geographies, functions, and levels of the organization.
Comfort working in a fast-changing environment with incomplete information and competing priorities.

Extra Great If You Have

Experience supporting a CTO, VP Engineering, or comparable technology executive in a high-growth or transformation environment.
Experience with annual planning, portfolio management, headcount planning, financial modeling, or investment reviews.
Experience supporting IPO readiness, M&A diligence, organizational transformation, or other enterprise-scale change.
Experience building operating standards, metrics, dashboards, or lightweight automation that materially improves decision quality.
Hands-on experience designing or deploying AI tooling, LLM integrations, AI-assisted coding, or automated ops platforms within large-scale engineering or cloud environments.

We Give Back To Our Employees

Our culture is what makes Redis a fun and rewarding place to work. To support you at work and beyond, we offer all our US team members fantastic benefits and perks:

Competitive salaries and equity grants
Unlimited time off to promote a healthy work-life balance
H/D/V coverage along with 401K, FSA, and commuter benefits
Frequent team celebrations and recreation events
Home internet & phone stipend
Learning and development opportunities
Ability to influence a high-performance company on its way to IPO

jobs.title: Director, Technology & Product
jobs.description:
About Univerus

Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Burnaby, British Columbia, Univerus is a fast-growing enterprise software company specializing in vertical market solutions. With over 300 employees, more than 20 acquisitions, and a global customer base exceeding 3,500 organizations, Univerus delivers mission-critical technology across public and private sectors. Our flagship product, Unity ERP, powers operations in local government, utilities, construction, manufacturing, health and safety, education, and beyond.

Learn more at univerus.com.

About Bu

Since 1981, Baragar Systems has partnered with K–12 school districts across Canada and the United States to provide data-driven planning tools that transform complex enrolment, boundary, staffing, and demographic data into clear, confident decisions. Serving more than 100 school districts, Baragar has built a reputation for deep educational planning expertise and meaningful impact on how education leaders plan for the future. Our product suite includes Demographic Dynamics (enrolment forecasting), GeoSchool (boundary planning and analysis), ThemeMap (geographic data visualization), District Intelligence (data dashboards and reporting), Staff Allocator, School Locator and School Boundaries Online. All tools purpose-built for the unique planning challenges school districts face. Baragar has historically operated as a service-first organization. Each year, the team delivers custom geospatial and demographic data packages, assembled by experienced data analysts and GIS specialists, alongside an annual software deliverable. Deep client engagement, hands-on support, and tailored training are central to how Baragar works. This model has created strong, trust-based relationships, and that expertise remains a core part of who we are.

Baragar operates as a focused business unit within Univerus, combining the intimacy and expertise of a specialist team with the scale and investment of a growing global organization.

Learn more at baragar.com

Position Details

Hours: 40 hours per week, Monday to Friday

Salary Range: $120,000 to $145,000 CAD per year

Location: Surrey, BC, Canada - Hybrid

This is a replacement position.

Role Overview

Baragar is entering a new chapter, one that builds on decades of service excellence while developing stronger internal accountability for its technology and product direction. The domain expertise, client relationships, and delivery capability that define Baragar today are what we’re building from, and what we’re committed to protecting as we grow. We are now establishing clearer in-house leadership over product direction, a more deliberate approach to technology decision-making, and the capacity to develop internal technical capability alongside our existing development partnerships.

We are seeking a Director, Technology & Product to lead that work. This is a senior role spanning five core areas: leading change, technology leadership and modernization, product and delivery management, building internal capability, and budget and governance. The successful candidate will hold both the strategic and the operational; someone who understands legacy systems, manages vendor and delivery relationships with confidence, brings clear technology judgment, and has the presence and discipline to drive meaningful change in an organization with a long operational history. This is a role focused on forward momentum, building on what works while creating the conditions for meaningful change. It is not a purely strategic role; the person who succeeds here will be equally comfortable doing the work as directing it: writing requirements, staying close to delivery, and investing the time to deeply understand Baragar’s domain, its data, and how the organization operates before

driving change. They will have a direct hand in shaping what Baragar’s technology foundation looks like over the next several years. The expectation, and the commitment from the organization, is that this investment of time and understanding comes first.

Organizational Relationship

This role reports directly to the EVP of Baragar Systems and operates as the senior internal technology voice for the business unit. The Director, Technology & Product works closely with external development partners who currently deliver all of the product work, as well as with Baragar’s data analysts, GIS specialists, and client-facing staff. The role operates within Baragar’s structure as a focused business unit of Univerus but will engage with

Univerus technical leadership on strategic alignment and collaborate with counterparts in other business units.

Key Responsibilities

Leading Change

Act as the senior internal technology voice in leadership discussions, vendor discussions, and strategic planning, bringing clarity and confidence to complex technical decisions.
Hold the organization accountable to transformation milestones, engaging teams and leadership with clarity and credibility, while respecting the expertise and customer value already built into the business.
Communicate technology direction, progress, and change clearly across the broader organization ensuring parties at all levels understand the why, not just the what.

Technology Leadership & Modernization

Develop a deep understanding of Baragar’s existing products, development workflows, codebases, data structures, and hosting environments.
Lead the development and execution of a practical modernization roadmap for Baragar’s product suite, sequencing technology improvements in a way that reduces technical debt, ensures customer value is protected, and remains within approved budget parameters.
Evaluate options for cloud hosting, application architecture, database strategy, integrations, APIs, reporting, and security, and develop business cases to support recommendations.
Provide internal leadership of technical decision-making, building stronger in-house capability to complement existing development partnerships and ensure Baragar has clear internal direction on core product and architecture decisions.
Establish, evolve, or maintain development standards, release processes, documentation practices, code review expectations, QA processes, and security practices.

Product & Delivery Management

Stay actively involved in delivery at a working level, reviewing specifications, participating in development cycles, and maintaining enough technical depth to make informed decisions and spot problems early.
Lead the planning, resourcing, timelines, and delivery across multiple software products.
Oversee backlog management, release planning, and production support.

Employment Type

Job Description

Director, Finance Systems

Plusgrade is scaling across global entities and building toward public-company readiness, and our Finance systems need an architect who can turn complex accounting and control requirements into clean, automated infrastructure. If you want to own the Finance-side design of NetSuite and our broader financial tech stack from the ground up rather than maintain someone else's legacy setup, this seat is yours.

What You'll Be Doing

Lead current- and future-state Finance process design with domain leaders, applying modern, best-fit technology to reduce manual effort, improve accuracy, and accelerate cycle times. Translate needs into requirements and control criteria; define and track value and outcomes for related system, integration, and automation changes, including AI use cases.
Partner with the VP, Finance Technology & Automation and Finance leaders on roadmap and prioritization. Lead Finance-side discovery, process and control design, and initiative coordination.
Lead Finance-side evaluation and implementation of NetSuite and related platforms. Partner with the Director, Finance Automation and technical teams on architecture, integrations, configuration, testing, and launch; validate process and control fit and audit readiness before go-live.
Define Finance needs for data quality, reconciliations, and reporting; partner with technical and data teams to ensure Finance data flows are complete, reliable, and audit-ready.
Partner with application specialists and technical owners to maintain operational readiness for Finance systems, including user support, documentation, adoption, escalation paths, incident coordination, releases, and upgrades.
Lead, develop, and coach the team, setting clear expectations and building the capabilities needed to deliver Finance systems initiatives.
Set control requirements for finance systems and processes affecting financial reporting, including data integrity, access, segregation of duties, approvals, and change management. Partner with IT on SOX, ITGC, ICFR, and ITACs.
Lead audit readiness for Finance systems and application controls; coordinate evidence and track remediation with control owners, IT, and Finance to support public-company readiness.
Coordinate Finance-facing vendor relationships, including service reviews, escalations, and renewal or change recommendations.

What You Bring

10+ years of progressive experience in finance systems, enterprise applications, or a related field, including at least 5 years leading teams or major programs.
A track record of leading Finance-side requirements, process design, controls, and adoption for ERP implementations or transformations. NetSuite experience is strongly preferred, including partnering with technical owners on configuration, integrations, and change governance.
A bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Information Systems, Business, or a related field; CPA or equivalent accounting designation is preferred.
Experience supporting global, multi-entity environments, ideally including M&A or business integrations.
Experience supporting a public company or pre-IPO environment is preferred.
Strong knowledge of Finance processes, accounting operations, financial reporting, and internal controls, including SOX/ITGC/ICFR, IT application controls (ITACs), and segregation-of-duties concepts; able to translate these into practical process and system requirements.
Experience with integrations, data architecture and governance, system security, and process automation. EPM, BI, or data-warehouse experience is an asset.
Clear communication and sound initiative leadership—you can facilitate process design with Finance leaders, define success measures and control requirements, influence across functions, and partner effectively with technical teams while balancing strategic direction with practical execution.
Experience evaluating or implementing AI-enabled solutions in Finance or Accounting workflows—such as transaction matching, reconciliations, invoice processing, close, reporting, or anomaly detection—with appropriate human review, data privacy, auditability, and control safeguards is an asset.

Why Plusgrade

Travel is about the moments that make a journey feel personal. At Plusgrade, we build the technology that makes those moments possible, from upgrade offers and loyalty experiences to revenue tools used by 575+ airline, hospitality, cruise, rail, and financial services partners worldwide.

The work is global, complex, and rewarding. You will solve meaningful problems, take ownership from idea to outcome, and work alongside people who are smart, curious, and committed to doing great work.

We also give our teams access to AI tools and the encouragement to use them thoughtfully, to move faster, explore ideas, and build better ways of working.

We trust our teams to do their best work. That means autonomy, flexibility, and room to grow.

Come help us shape the future of travel.

Job Information

Job Title: Director Emerging Resources.

Job Requisition ID: 89476

Ministry: Energy and Minerals

Location: Edmonton or Calgary

Full or Part-Time: Full-time

Hours of Work: 36.25 hours per week

Permanent/Temporary/Wage: Permanent

Scope: Open Competition

Closing Date: November 29, 2026

Classification: Senior Manager, Zone 2

Salary: $5,139.30 - $6,526.16 bi-weekly ($134,135 - $170,332/year)

The Alberta Public Service works to build a stronger province for current and future generations. We make a difference in the lives of Albertans through rewarding career opportunities.

The Ministry of Energy and Minerals is responsible for sustaining the interests of Albertans through the stewardship and responsible development of energy and mineral resource systems.

Please review Energy and Minerals to learn more and what it has to offer.

The Strategy and Market Access (SAMA) Division is responsible for developing Alberta's strategic direction to deliver on energy mandates including natural gas infrastructure development, market access, energy market diversification, strategic foresight, economic analysis, and stakeholder engagement.

The Energy Futures Branch leads the development and implementation of strategies related to natural gas infrastructure, value-add initiatives, export opportunities including liquefied natural gas (LNG) and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), critical minerals, emerging resources, and pipeline regulatory processes

The Unit of Emerging Resources is responsible for strategy development and implementation of Alberta’s critical minerals and geo-thermal resources.

Role Responsibilities

Are you a strategic thinker and collaborative leader? Energy Futures is looking for a Director, Emerging Resources to provide strategic leadership and advance Alberta’s critical minerals, geothermal energy, and other emerging resource opportunities.

Reporting to the Executive Director, Energy Futures, this position provides strategic leadership for the Department’s mandated initiatives related to critical minerals, geothermal and other emerging opportunities. The position leads professional teams responsible for strategy and legislative development, complex projects, and work across government and with external partners to advance complex policy, investment, regulatory, and market priorities.

In This Role, You Will

Provide strategic advice, analysis and recommendations, for policies, programs, and initiatives related to critical minerals, geothermal energy, and other emerging resources.
Lead strategy planning, legislative and regulatory development, implementation planning and evaluation for Alberta’s Critical Minerals Strategy and Action Plan and other emerging resource development initiatives.
Direct the preparation of decision documents, briefing notes, correspondence, cabinet and Treasury Board materials, key messages and other executive products.
Lead complex, cross-ministry and cross-jurisdictional initiatives including engagement with federal, provincial and territorial partnerships on critical minerals.
Build and sustain trusted relationships with federal counterparts and industry to advance Alberta’s interests and strategic outcomes on critical minerals and other emerging opportunities. Lead, coach, and develop managers and staff while fostering a collaborative, accountable, and results-oriented work environment.
Identify opportunities to strengthen Alberta’s competitiveness, attract investment, and support mineral exploration, development, processing, and value-added opportunities.
Direct complex policy, economic, technical, regulatory, and market analysis and provide evidence-based recommendations to senior and executive leadership.
Represent the department on intergovernmental committees, working groups, industry forums, and other strategic initiatives.
Lead unit operations, workforce planning, financial oversights, priority setting, staff development, issues management and coordination oversight and continuous improvement while managing competing priorities and emerging issues.

This is an exciting opportunity for a strategic and collaborative leader to influence Alberta’s energy and mineral future. Your leadership will help shape policies, strengthen partnerships, attract investment, and advance the responsible development of Alberta’s emerging resources.

The Job Description is provided for further details on this position.

APS Competencies

Competencies are behaviors that are essential to reach our goals in serving Albertans. We encourage you to have an in depth understanding of the competencies that are required for this opportunity and to be prepared to demonstrate them during the recruitment process.

Systems Thinking: You will consider the broader economic, regulatory, competitive, and market environment when developing strategies for critical minerals, geothermal energy, and emerging resources.
Build Collaborative Environments: You will build strategic relationships with industry, Indigenous organizations, regulators, other governments, and cross-ministry partners to advance emerging resource priorities.
Develop Self and Others: You will provide clear direction, coaching, and mentorship to managers and staff, empowering your team to deliver on complex priorities. This aligns with the APS emphasis on achieving results through others and setting clear expectations.
Creative Problem Solving: You will analyze complex policy, economic, regulatory, and market issues and develop practical, evidence-based options and recommendations for senior leadership.
Drive for Results: You will establish clear priorities and lead the delivery of high-profile strategic initiatives while balancing competing priorities and maintaining accountability for results.
Agility: You will anticipate and respond to emerging issues, changing government priorities, and evolving energy and mineral markets while providing timely strategic advice.

Qualifications

University graduation in Public Administration, Business Administration, Economics, Engineering, Science, or a related field, supplemented by seven (7) years of progressively responsible experience required in Leading complex strategic initiatives, and issues management

Related experience or education may be considered as an equivalency on a one for one basis

Assets

Knowledge of Alberta, North American and global energy landscape.
Experience with investment attraction, market development, or resource competitiveness.
Experience working with industry, Indigenous organizations, governments, regulators, international investors or other strategic partners.
Experience managing human and financial resources and leading organisational change.
Advanced writing, briefing, engagement and presentation skills.
Ability to brief and present to senior leaders and Ministers.
Demonstrated ability to develop strategies, legislation, regulations and government decision documents such as cabinet reports.
Strong policial and financial acumen.

Minimum recruitment standards outline the minimum education and experience required for appointment to a job classification.

Notes

Hours Of Work

36.25 hours per week (full time) Monday to Friday.

Term Of Employment

This is one full-time permanent position.

Location:

Petroleum Plaza Building, North Tower, Edmonton

or

AMEC Place, Calgary

Final candidates will be required to undergo a criminal records check (CRC).

Successful candidates will be required to disclose any business or financial interests, including the owning of shares or financial investments in the energy sector, to comply with the Department of Energy & Minerals’ Supplementary Code of Conduct.

Any costs associated with obtaining the required documents/checks as noted or interview travel expenses, will be the responsibility of the candidate. Out-of-province applicants can obtain the required documents/checks from the province they currently reside in.

Working for the Alberta Public Service .

Alberta Public Service Benefit Information .
Professional learning and development .
Research Alberta Public Service Careers tool .
Positive workplace culture and work-life balance.

How To Apply

Applicants are advised to provide information that clearly and concisely demonstrates how their qualifications meet the advertised requirements, including education, experience, and relevant examples of required competencies.

Candidates are required to apply online. Please see Job Application Resources for more information.

In your resume, please include dates (including months and years) associated with all education and work experience. For example, January 2006 - June 2009 (part-time). This example is provided for illustrative purposes only. Applicants are encouraged to present their information clearly and thoroughly, using a format that best conveys their experience.

It is recommended applicants who have completed post-secondary studies from outside of Canada obtain an evaluation of their credentials from the International Qualifications Assessment Service (IQAS) or from a recognized Canadian Credential Evaluator; please visit the Alliance of Credential Evaluation Services of Canada for more information.

It is also recommended that applicants include the assessment certificate from IQAS or any other educational assessment service as part of their application.

Closing Statement

This competition may be used to fill future vacancies, across the Government of Alberta, at the same or lower classification level.

We thank all applicants for their interest. All applications will be reviewed to determine which candidates' qualifications most closely match the advertised requirements.
