jobs.description:
Job Title: Vice President, M&A Integration and Clinic Onboarding

Department: Operations

Scope: National – Canada

Reports to: Chief Growth Officer

Location: Toronto, Ontario (4 Days in Office, 1 Day Remote)

About 123Dentist

At 123Dentist, we are one of Canada’s largest and fastest-growing dental support organizations, supporting more than 500 clinics and 10,000 team members across the country. Growth through acquisition is central to that story, and our M&A Integration and Clinic Onboarding team makes sure every practice that joins the network is set up for success from day one.

Position Overview

123Dentist is seeking an accomplished executive to lead its national M&A Integration and Clinic Onboarding function. This leader will be responsible for bringing together the existing teams into a unified, scalable operation that ensures newly acquired dental practices transition successfully into the 123Dentist network, maintain operational continuity and deliver against acquisition objectives.

Reporting to our Chief Growth Officer, the Vice President M&A Integration and Clinic Onboarding will oversee the full integration lifecycle, from pre-close planning through operational stabilization and transition to Regional Operations. The role will also drive post-acquisition value creation in partnership with Finance and Operations, while ensuring a positive integration experience for partner dentists, clinic leaders and employees. Success will require strong commercial judgment, operational execution and the ability to lead cross-functional teams in a highly acquisitive, multi-site environment.

Key Accountabilities

Integration Strategy & Executive Leadership

Lead the national M&A Integration and Onboarding function, with accountability for its strategy, operating model, resources, priorities and overall performance.
Establish scalable integration processes, governance frameworks and standards that support multiple concurrent acquisitions across the network.
Exercise delegated decision-making authority over integration priorities, approved budgets and resources, ensuring alignment with organizational growth objectives.
Provide executive leadership with visibility into integration performance, material risks, resource requirements and strategic opportunities.

Acquisition Integration & Operational Readiness

Oversee the end-to-end operational integration of acquired practices, from permitted pre-close planning through Day 1 readiness, stabilization and formal operational handoff.
Establish acquisition-specific integration plans, milestones, accountabilities and risk mitigation strategies based on the complexity and needs of each practice.
Ensure effective coordination across clinic operations, HR, Finance, IT, Marketing, Procurement and other functions to maintain operational and patient care continuity.
Identify and resolve integration challenges, ensuring acquired clinics transition efficiently into the 123Dentist network.

Post-Acquisition Value Creation & Financial Performance

Lead the development and execution of post-acquisition value creation plans aligned with each acquisition’s investment case and the organization’s growth strategy.
Partner with Finance, Regional Operations and functional leaders to establish measurable revenue, growth, productivity and cost-efficiency initiatives.
Monitor integration-related financial and operational performance, identify variances and drive corrective actions with accountable business leaders.
Ensure financial value realization is appropriately tracked and validated by Finance, with ongoing performance accountability clearly transitioned to Regional Operations.

People, Culture & Partner Experience

Establish a consistent, relationship-focused onboarding experience for acquired practice owners, partner dentists, clinic leaders and employees.
Partner with HR and Regional Operations to identify and address critical talent retention risks, leadership transitions and workforce integration requirements.
Lead integration-related change management and communication efforts, promoting engagement, cultural alignment and trust throughout the transition.
Preserve strong local practice relationships while supporting the adoption of 123Dentist’s operating standards and organizational values.

Integration Governance & Operational Handoff

Establish cross-functional integration governance, including clear decision rights, accountabilities, milestones, escalation protocols and performance expectations.
Lead alignment among Corporate Development, Operations, Finance, HR, IT, Legal and other functions to ensure effective integration execution.
Establish formal integration completion and handoff criteria, ensuring operational readiness and clear ownership of outstanding risks and initiatives.
Partner with Regional Operations to ensure a seamless transition of accountability and sustainable clinic performance following integration.

Team Leadership & Organizational Development

Lead the consolidation of the existing M&A Integration and Clinic Onboarding teams into a unified national function.
Establish an effective organizational structure, clear leadership accountabilities and resource plans aligned with the acquisition strategy.
Build, coach and develop high-performing teams capable of managing multiple integrations and delivering measurable results.
Drive continuous improvement through standardized processes, performance reporting and scalable integration capabilities.

Qualifications & Experience

Significant progressive leadership experience in M&A integration, multi-site operations or operational transformation, ideally including 12–15 years of relevant experience.
Proven experience leading multiple acquisitions and integrating businesses within complex, geographically distributed organizations.
Demonstrated ability to build and lead integration teams, establish governance and deliver measurable operational and financial outcomes.
Strong financial and commercial acumen, including investment-case execution, performance measurement and value realization.
Experience leading cross-functional teams and influencing senior executives, operational leaders and key stakeholders.
Strong relationship management and change leadership capabilities, particularly when integrating acquired businesses and retaining critical talent.
Proven ability to balance strategic priorities with hands-on execution in a fast-paced, decentralized environment.
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Operations, Finance or a related field; MBA or equivalent advanced qualification considered an asset.

Preferred Experience

Experience in highly acquisitive, multi-location organizations, including dental support organizations, veterinary networks, pharmacy, optometry, healthcare services or other decentralized service businesses. Experience in private equity-backed or high-growth acquisition environments is highly desirable.

What Sets You Apart

You thrive in a highly acquisitive, fast-paced, decentralized environment, balancing strategy with hands-on execution. You bring sound commercial judgment, lead cross-functional teams, influence senior executives, and build trust with partner dentists, clinic leaders and employees as practices join the network.

Why Join 123Dentist?

Lead a national function with real ownership, including delegated decision-making authority over integration priorities, budgets and resources
Build something new by bringing the existing M&A Integration and Clinic Onboarding teams together into one unified, scalable operation
Play a central role in the growth of one of Canada’s largest and fastest-growing dental support organizations
Partner with executive leadership, Finance and Regional Operations to turn each acquisition’s investment case into measurable results
Shape the experience of partner dentists, clinic leaders and employees as new practices join the network

jobs.title: Director, FinOps (35690)
jobs.description:
Director, FinOps (Cloud Financial Management)

Location:
Toronto, Ontario

Work Model:
Hybrid – Minimum 3 Days Onsite per Week

Employment Type:
Permanent, Full-Time

Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced Director, FinOps (Cloud Financial Management)
to build, lead, and mature an enterprise FinOps program focused on delivering measurable and sustainable cloud cost optimization
without compromising reliability, security, or engineering productivity.

This is a strategic and hands-on leadership role
requiring a strong combination of FinOps, cloud financial management, Azure cost optimization, financial analysis, forecasting, governance, and cross-functional leadership
.

The Director will own the FinOps strategy, operating model, cost optimization pipeline, forecasting discipline, governance cadence, and savings targets
, while partnering closely with Engineering, Cloud Operations, Product, Finance, and senior leadership
.

This role requires someone who can operate at the executive level while remaining hands-on with analysis, tracking, optimization, reporting, follow-up, and governance
. Success will depend heavily on the ability to influence technical and business teams and establish a culture of cloud cost accountability and cost-aware decision-making
.

Key Responsibilities

FinOps Strategy & Cloud Cost Optimization

Own and evolve the enterprise FinOps strategy, operating model, and governance framework across Azure and platform services.
Build and manage a structured cloud cost optimization pipeline covering opportunity identification, impact analysis, prioritization, execution, savings verification, and regression prevention.
Drive quarterly and annual cloud savings targets using transparent methodologies for hard savings, unit-cost improvements, and cost avoidance.
Identify cloud cost drivers and translate findings into practical, measurable optimization initiatives.
Establish appropriate cost ownership and accountability across teams.

Financial Management, Forecasting & Unit Economics

Lead cloud budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis, and scenario planning.
Develop and mature showback/chargeback practices and cost-allocation methodologies.
Define and track unit economics, including measures such as cost per customer, transaction, environment, or deployment.
Improve financial discipline through tagging standards, allocation accuracy, commitment planning, anomaly detection, and benefits tracking.
Develop business cases and evaluate ROI and financial impact for optimization initiatives.
Establish defensible baselines and methodologies for measuring and reporting realized savings.

Azure Optimization & Engineering Partnership

Partner with Engineering and Cloud Operations to incorporate cost considerations into architecture reviews, backlog prioritization, release planning, and operational decision-making.
Drive optimization across areas including:
Azure compute and infrastructure
AKS/Kubernetes
Rightsizing and scheduling
Storage tiering
Networking
Reserved Instances and Savings Plans
Observability and monitoring costs

Translate technical architecture and infrastructure decisions into financial impact and cost-to-serve implications.
Establish practical cost-efficiency policies and guardrails aligned with engineering delivery.
Support Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and GitOps practices where appropriate.

FinOps Tooling, Automation & Cost Observability

Implement and mature cloud cost visibility, reporting, dashboards, alerts, and automation using Azure-native tooling and/or FinOps platforms.
Develop processes for anomaly detection, automated cleanup, cost monitoring, and optimization tracking.
Establish cost-observability practices across technologies including Azure Monitor, Log Analytics, and Application Insights.
Improve the quality and availability of financial and operational cloud-cost data used for decision-making.

Governance & Executive Reporting

Own the regular FinOps governance cadence, including analysis, tracking, follow-up, and optimization reviews.
Develop executive-level reporting covering cloud cost drivers, risks, savings progress, forecasts, KPIs, and recommendations.
Provide clear recommendations and trade-offs to senior leadership.
Drive outcomes across Engineering and Finance primarily through influence, governance, data, and accountability rather than direct authority over technical teams.

Team & Cross-Functional Leadership

Lead and mentor a small FinOps team/function, with the opportunity for the function to grow.
Establish team goals, operating cadence, accountability, and continuous-improvement practices.
Work cross-functionally with Engineering, Cloud Operations, Product, Finance, and senior leadership.
Develop training and enablement initiatives that improve FinOps awareness and cloud cost literacy across technical and product teams.
Build trusted relationships with both technical and business stakeholders.

Required Qualifications

10+ years of experience across cloud/platform technology, finance/FP&A, technology operations, FinOps, or closely related disciplines.
3+ years of leadership experience at the Director, Head, Lead, or comparable level.
Demonstrated experience building, leading, or materially contributing to FinOps / Cloud Financial Management programs.
Proven track record delivering material, measurable cloud savings across multiple quarters and improving cost-to-serve.
Strong experience with Azure cloud economics, cost drivers, and optimization.
Solid technical understanding of Azure architecture, including compute, AKS/Kubernetes, storage, networking, and observability.
Strong financial expertise across budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis, scenario planning, business casing, ROI, and savings measurement.
Experience developing cloud cost allocation, tagging, showback/chargeback, and/or unit-cost models.
Ability to translate complex technical decisions into financial impact and actionable business recommendations.
Strong analytical capabilities with the ability to identify true cost drivers and measure optimization outcomes.
Demonstrated ability to influence Engineering, Finance, Product, and Cloud teams without relying solely on direct authority.
Strong hands-on capability across analysis, tracking, reporting, optimization follow-up, and governance.
Executive-level written and verbal communication skills, including KPI reporting, recommendations, decision support, and senior stakeholder presentations.
Ability to operate effectively in an environment requiring structure, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Core Competencies

FinOps Strategy & Governance
Azure Cloud Cost Optimization
Cloud Financial Management
Budgeting, Forecasting & Variance Analysis
Cloud Cost Allocation & Unit Economics
Showback / Chargeback
Cost Optimization & Savings Measurement
AKS / Kubernetes Cost Management
Cloud Cost Observability
Executive Reporting & KPI Management
Cross-Functional Influence
Financial & Technical Analysis
Team Leadership & Mentorship
Hands-On Operational Leadership

Nice to Have

FinOps Foundation certification – Practitioner and/or Professional.
Relevant Microsoft Azure certifications.
Experience implementing showback/chargeback and unit-cost models at scale.
Experience working in IaC/GitOps environments, including technologies such as Terraform and Argo CD.
Experience integrating cloud cost controls and governance into engineering and delivery pipelines.

What Success Looks Like

About Us

The Department of Health and Wellness offers opportunities to grow and advance in a dynamic sector that touches the lives of all Nova Scotians. Along with our partners, including the Nova Scotia Health Authority and the IWK Health Centre, we’re committed to continually improving our health care system. With a focus on collaborative primary health care, improved supports for mental health and addictions, digital health, capital infrastructure, and more, the department is thinking differently about how to plan, fund, legislate and monitor to improve access and service delivery. To do this, we need leaders at all levels of the organization who embrace a challenge and believe in their ability to make a difference.

About Our Opportunity

Reporting to the Senior Executive Director, Public Health, the Director, Public Health Emergency Management will provide strategic leadership for Nova Scotia’s approach to preparing for, responding to, and recovering from public health emergencies. Your work will help protect the health of Nova Scotians and strengthen the province’s readiness for pandemics, major incidents, and other emerging public health threats.

Leading a team of public health emergency preparedness professionals, you will oversee the development and delivery of emergency preparedness plans, strategies, policies, and accountability frameworks aligned with departmental and government priorities and the Health Protection Act.

This is a highly collaborative and influential leadership role. You will work across government and with provincial, federal, and other partners to strengthen public health emergency preparedness, identify emerging risks and opportunities, and provide evidence-informed advice and recommendations to senior leaders. Your ability to see the bigger picture, build relationships, and translate complex issues into clear strategies will be essential to your success.

Build strong partnerships across government and with federal, provincial/territorial, community, professional, and other external organizations.
Represent the Department on committees, working groups, project teams, conferences, and intergovernmental initiatives.

Unity Health Toronto is one of Canada’s largest Catholic healthcare networks serving patients, residents and clients across the full spectrum of care, spanning primary care, secondary community care, tertiary and quaternary care services to post-acute through rehabilitation, palliative care and long-term care, while investing in world-class research and education.

Research is a cornerstone of Unity Health Toronto’s mission, bringing together world-class scientists, clinician-researchers, trainees, and research staff to advance discoveries that improve patient care and strengthen health systems. With internationally recognized strengths across clinical, scientific, and population health research, Unity Health is committed to translating innovative research into meaningful impact for patients, communities, and the broader healthcare system.

THE OPPORTUNITY

Clinical trials are a key part of Unity Health Toronto's Exceptional Care Without Exception strategic plan, advancing research excellence across the network while providing patients with access to innovative therapeutics that may not otherwise be available. SPHERE CRO , one of Canada's leading academically-affiliated Contract Research Organizations (CRO), complements this work by delivering end-to-end clinical research services to academic, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and industry partners, including site management, project management, data management and technologies, regulatory affairs, biostatistics, and patient engagement.

A newly-created role reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, Research, and overseeing a team of approximately 50 people, the Senior Director will lead the execution of Unity’s clinical trials strategy, including the build of the Central Clinical Trials Unit, the adoption of key technologies such as the enterprise deployment of the clinical trials management system, and initiatives that position Unity’s sites as a global leader in clinical trials performance. jobs.title: Director, Discretionary Portfolio Management Supervision
jobs.description:
Join a financial services firm where your contributions are valued. Edward Jones is a Fortune 500¹ company where people come first. With over 9 million clients and 20,000 financial advisors across the U.S. and Canada, we’re proud to be privately-owned, placing the focus on our clients rather than shareholder returns.

Behind everything we do is our purpose: We partner for positive impact to improve the lives of our clients and colleagues, and together, better our communities and society. We are an innovative, flexible, and inclusive organization that attracts, develops, and inspires performance excellence and a sense of belonging.

People are at the center of our partnership. Edward Jones associates are seen, heard, respected, and supported. This is what we believe makes us the best place to start or build your career.

View our Purpose, Inclusion and Citizenship Report.

¹Fortune 500, published June 2024, data as of December 2023. Compensation provided for using, not obtaining, the rating.

This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced Supervising Portfolio Manager to build, design, hire for and launch a new Supervising Portfolio Management team. By way of background, at Edward Jones we have been rapidly evolving and growing our Managed Account offering, and we are now launching an advisor-managed discretionary offering that allows our financial advisors to be licensed as Portfolio Managers and manage client portfolios on a discretionary basis.

To make this possible, and meet more clients' needs at scale, we need to stand up a Canadian Supervising Portfolio Management team who will have full responsibility for the design, implementation and ongoing execution of the supervisory framework governing the program.

What You'll Do

As we're just getting started, you will be asked to design our supervisory policies and procedures, set the standard advisors must meet to be admitted to the program, and figure out how the Supervising Portfolio Management team needs to be structured for enduring success.

As the functional leader and a licensed Supervising Portfolio Manager, once the team is launched, you will lead the team with overall responsibility for supervising financial advisors licensed as Portfolio Managers (PM) and Associate Portfolio Managers (APM), ensuring investment decisions made on behalf of clients align to Edward Jones' investment philosophy and meet a fiduciary standard.

To deliver on this, you will build out a team of licensed Portfolio Managers who bring deep expertise in portfolio construction, suitability and risk management, and who demonstrate the judgment and conviction to act whenever an investment decision is not in the client's best interest. Your team's responsibilities will include pre-approving APM models and trades, conducting account-level oversight against each client's Investment Policy Statement, and determining when an advisor is ready to be released from heightened supervision.

Just as important, you and your team will be a trusted partner to our financial advisors and branch teams, coaching advisor PMs and APMs and providing the feedback and development that elevates the quality of advice across the program. You will partner with Compliance, Legal, Operations and Technology to build supervisory controls that are automated and scalable, so Edward Jones can grow advisor-led discretionary management with confidence that every client receives high-quality advice and investment decisions.

Key Responsibilities

Lead and build the Supervising Portfolio Management team, including the design, implementation and ongoing governance of the supervisory framework, policies and procedures for the firm's advisor-managed discretionary offering.
Act as the designated supervisory principal for the program, with final authority to approve or decline advisor entry into the program, and to determine when a newly licensed advisor is released from heightened supervision. Set the standard advisors must meet to be admitted and coach applicants to reach it.
Overall responsibility for how the team conducts ongoing supervisory reviews of advisor Portfolio Manager (PM) and Associate Portfolio Manager (APM) activity within discretionary accounts, identifying and resolving exceptions in a timely manner. Note that portfolios are centrally traded and centrally rebalanced, so supervision focuses on program-level oversight rather than individual trade execution.
Monitor portfolio activity across advisor-managed discretionary accounts for suitability, concentration risk, and adherence to client Investment Policy Statements (IPS). As portfolios are centrally designed and rebalanced in a uniform manner, supervision emphasizes program-level consistency rather than individual portfolio rebalancing.
Review and approve new discretionary models and pre-approve APM models and trades, ensuring they adhere to the firm's investment guidelines, and the diversification, risk and expected return characteristics are appropriate for the selected risk profile.
Attract, develop and engage talent, cultivating an inclusive environment, and own the development and execution of the team business plan.
Serve as the primary investment resource to advisor PMs and APMs, providing constructive feedback on the model portfolios, investment proposals and rebalancing strategies they develop, and coaching newly licensed APMs until they are proficient as full Portfolio Managers.
Oversee the performance measurement process for central models, acting as a data steward to ensure accurate and reliable returns are reported and used in marketing and client-facing materials.
Meet CIRO obligations as a permanent standing member of the Managed Account Committee (MAC), maintain supervisory records, and serve as the point of contact for regulatory examinations, internal audits and Compliance inquiries.
Continuously improve supervisory procedures to scale with the growth of the offering, partnering with Compliance, Operations, Wealth Platforms and Technology to automate controls and oversight.
10+ years of experience in portfolio management, including supervision of discretionary or managed accounts
Currently licensed or immediately able to be licensed as a Portfolio Manager with CIRO, with supervisory responsibilities
Bachelor's Degree or higher-level education
CFA Charter holder
Expert knowledge of CIRO rules governing managed and discretionary accounts and the fiduciary standard of care owed to discretionary clients.
Deep expertise in designing supervisory frameworks, written supervisory procedures (WSPs) and controls that scale program-level oversight.
Extensive knowledge of asset allocation, portfolio construction, risk management and IPS review, with the depth to assess and coach advisor investment decisions.
Proven ability to build a new function where no precedent exists, including the operating model, standards and team.
Seasoned judgment to make final supervisory decisions on behalf of clients and hold the line on standards, including declining an advisor's entry into the program, while preserving the relationship.
Demonstrated ability to coach licensed professionals, providing direct, constructive feedback that builds competency and elevates the quality of advice.

At Edward Jones, we are building a place where everyone feels like they belong. We're proud of our associates' contributions to the firm and the recognitions we have received.

Check out our U.S. awards and accolades: Insights & Information Blog Postings about Edward Jones

Check out our Canadian awards and accolades: Insights & Information Blog Postings about Edward Jones

If you're a strategic sales leader who knows how to develop people, build strong customer partnerships and turn opportunities into results, we'd like to hear from you.
  
This role is based in our head office in Oakville.
  
  

What You'll Do
  
* Lead the development and execution of a national sales strategy, translating business priorities into clear regional goals, plans and accountability.
* Coach and develop Regional Sales Managers, strengthening leadership capability, sales execution and team performance.
* Drive national revenue and gross margin performance, maintaining a healthy sales pipeline, accurate forecasts and clear performance expectations.
* Build consistency across regions through effective sales practices, territory planning and customer account management.
* Strengthen relationships with key, strategic and national accounts, ensuring the right resources and expertise are brought together to meet customer needs.
* Champion a team\-selling approach by connecting Sales with Service, Market Segment Managers and other internal specialists to deliver complete customer solutions.
* Use Salesforce and business insights to monitor performance, identify opportunities and support informed decisions.
* Partner with Commercial Operations and Service leadership to improve sales effectiveness, customer retention and growth opportunities.
* Build a strong sales leadership pipeline by developing talent, supporting succession planning and creating opportunities for growth.
* Lead change and foster a collaborative, accountable and customer\-focused sales culture.


What You'll Bring

* A track record of developing and executing sales strategies that deliver profitable growth across multiple regions or territories.
* Strong business and financial acumen, with experience managing revenue, gross margin, forecasting and sales performance.
* Experience with strategic account management, territory planning and complex customer relationships.
* A proven ability to coach, motivate and develop leaders and high\-performing teams.
* Strong CRM experience, preferably Salesforce, with an understanding of how data supports sales effectiveness and decision\-making.
* Excellent communication, influencing, negotiation and relationship\-building skills.
* A collaborative leadership style and the ability to build strong partnerships across different business functions.

Choose the Safe Way, Always
  
Safety is at the heart of everything we do. As a leader, you'll champion a strong safety culture and ensure safe decision\-making is part of how our sales organization operates.
  
You'll follow all company and customer health and safety requirements, including safe driving practices and required safety procedures when visiting customer sites, branches and other locations.
  
  

Why Levitt\-Safety?
  
At Levitt\-Safety, we believe our people are our greatest strength. When you join our team, you'll be part of an established Canadian company with 90 years of experience, a strong reputation and a shared commitment to helping people work safely.
  
  

**Here's what you can look forward to:**  

* Competitive annual base salary of $160,000 \- $190,000, commensurate with skills and experience and aligned with internal equity, plus an annual bonus opportunity.
* Comprehensive benefits package including health, dental and vision coverage to support you and your family's well\-being.
* Company\-matched RRSP program as well as profit\-sharing.
* Opportunities to grow your leadership capabilities and advance your career while helping shape the national sales strategy, develop leaders and make a measurable impact on business growth.
* A collaborative team to work alongside; knowledgeable people who value teamwork, accountability and doing what's right.
* A purpose\-driven organization where safety isn't just what we do; it's what we stand for.


Application \& Hiring Process
  
  

Levitt\-Safety may use AI\-enabled tools to support the screening and assessment of applications.

jobs.title: Sr. Director of ISV Business Development
jobs.description:
**Job Description** The Senior Director, ISV Business Development is the global craft leader for Sage’s ISV ecosystem. You will act as the single accountable owner for turning solution strategy into ecosystem\-led, commercially\-governed growth. Operating as the head of the ISV craft, the role holds unified accountability for solution\-strategy alignment, commercial contracting, go\-to\-market (GTM) success support, executive relationship management, and partner performance across every business unit, franchise and region.
  

  

This role sits at the intersection of Product Management, Product Marketing, Growth, Enablement, Performance Marketing, Trading, Legal, Finance and Regional Revenue teams. It exists to ensure that the BUILD / Partner / Buy decision is made deliberately and consistently, that the resulting commercial relationships are contracted on scalable terms, and that partners are launched, supported and held to measurable annual targets – so that ecosystem investment is always tied directly to customer outcomes and revenue.
  

  

This is a Hybrid position based in\-office 3 days per week.
  

**Key Responsibilities** Solution Strategy Alignment (BUILD / Partner / Buy)
  

  

- Own the partner voice in solution strategy – partner with Product Management and Product Marketing to bring clarity to the BUILD, Partner or Buy decision for each capability gap, ensuring the right capability reaches customers through the right commercial model.
  

- Steward the Solution Maps – maintain the partner component of Sage’s global solution maps, translating identified capability gaps into a prioritized ecosystem investment and recruitment plan.
  

- Guard the BUILD boundary – ensure that where Sage chooses to build, ISV extensibility, AI\-gateway readiness and self\-funding business\-development principles are designed in, so partner strategy strengthens rather than duplicates the core roadmap.
  

- Governance – run the quarterly connect / review cadence that keeps Product, Growth, Marketing, Enablement, Sales and Commercial Partner teams aligned to a single, consistent solution strategy across geographies.
  

  

Commercial Contracting
  

  

- Chief commercial contracting authority for ISV – lead negotiation of global reseller, referral, OEM, white\-label, marketplace, co\-sell and strategic alliance agreements.
  

- Scalable frameworks – develop and institutionalize standard commercial frameworks, pricing structures, revenue\-share and API\-monetization models, and policy standards that apply consistently across all Sage products and regions.
  

- Cross\-functional integrity – partner closely with Legal, Finance, Product and Operations to ensure commercial consistency, sound unit economics and end\-to\-end alignment to signed commitments.
  

  

GTM Success Support
  

  

- Launch readiness – drive the five\-phase activation lifecycle (approval and scope, commercial and systems readiness, product and technical readiness, GTM enablement and launch, post\-GA performance management) so every partnership is commercially viable, technically sound and operationally ready before launch.
  

- Enablement and handoff – ensure clean handoff to Commercial Operations, Enablement and field sellers (direct and channel), with playbooks, positioning and rules of engagement that let sellers support and position ISV solutions independently.
  

  

- Field execution support – work with regional revenue and growth teams so strategic partners receive the visibility, overlay capacity and commercial guidance needed to convert strategy into pipeline and attach.
  

  

Relationship Management
  

  

- Executive sponsorship – maintain trusted executive\-level relationships and governance for Sage’s most strategic ISV partnerships, representing Sage as a senior partner in the market.
  

- Joint business planning – develop and execute joint business plans, and lead Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) and executive steering committees with top ISV partners.
  

- Final escalation point – act as the ultimate escalation owner for strategic partner matters, resolving complex commercial, product, legal and GTM issues and protecting long\-term mutual growth.
  

  

Partner Performance – Annual Target Setting \& Performance Reporting
  

- Annual target setting – work with partners and regional revenue leaders to set annual ISV targets, ensuring ISV revenue is budgeted as an explicit subset of franchise revenue with assigned sales targets rather than left as unowned aspiration.
  

- Performance reporting – own the ISV scorecard and regular reporting to leadership – tracking ISV\-sourced and ISV\-influenced ARR, net revenue and margin contribution, attach rate, retention/expansion, activation and churn.
  

  

Course correction – run monthly and quarterly performance reviews to track partners against target, and recommend investment, expansion or corrective action to keep the portfolio performing.
  

  

Qualifications:
  

- Approximately 15\+ years of relevant industry experience, particularly in ISV business development.
  

- Proven experience leading people, beyond individual contributor success.
  

- Leadership Approach: A “first among equals” leadership style, guiding four largely self\-directed, director\-level professionals.
  

- Ability to act as a mentor, sounding board, and advisor rather than relying on detailed direction or hands\-on management.
  

- Leverages experience to provide guidance, anticipate challenges, and help the team navigate risks.
  

  

Plenty of perks:
  

- 100% paid premiums for health, dental, and vision coverage.
  

- RRSP contribution match (100% up to 4%).
  

- 35 days paid time off (11 paid holidays, 16 vacation days, 3 personal days, 5 sick days).
  

- 18 weeks of paid parental leave for birth, adoption, or surrogacy offered 1 year after the start date.
  

- 5 days paid yearly to volunteer (through Sage Foundation).
  

- $5,250 tuition reimbursement per c

jobs.title: Director, Finance

jobs.title: Director, FP&A
jobs.description:
At Range Group
we believe in the power of the professional travel advisor. We represent over $4.5 billion in annual travel sales. All our investments stem from a common thesis, that travel advisors add real value to a trip. Travel advisors when equipped with technology and 24/7 support are irreplaceable. Equally important is our philanthropy. Range Foundation channels 10% of group profits to social impact. From exploration grants, improved access to education, new discoveries on sea and land, cultural infrastructure, and helping our global neighbors in times of need — we are investing to build a better future.

About The Role

This is a hands-on senior finance leadership role for someone who operates at the intersection of strategy, analytics, and execution. You’re as comfortable building a complex multi-entity model from scratch as you are presenting the story behind the numbers to the executive team.

As Director, FP&A, you will own the analytical engine that supports decision-making across Range Group’s portfolio of travel brands — leading enterprise planning and forecasting, managing a small team, and working directly with senior leadership to evaluate opportunities, navigate risks, and drive performance.

What You’ll Do

Financial Modelling & Planning

Build, maintain, and continuously improve financial models covering consolidated Group performance, brand-level P&Ls, cash flow forecasting, and scenario analysis.
Own the Group-level cash flow tracker and EBITDA bridging model, ensuring accuracy and timeliness week over week.
Lead the annual budgeting, forecasting, and long-range planning processes across the organization.
Support ad hoc financial analysis — acquisition modelling, business case development, and covenant compliance.
Drive continuous improvement in financial planning frameworks, forecasting methodologies, and analytical tools.

Performance Management & Executive Insights

Own enterprise-wide performance reporting — financial reviews, KPI dashboards, executive scorecards, and variance commentary.
Lead monthly and quarterly business reviews with senior leadership.
Translate financial results into clear, decision-ready insights that prompt action.
Identify and proactively flag emerging risks, opportunities, and performance trends across the portfolio.

Strategic Business Partnership

Partner with executive and business leaders to align financial plans with strategic priorities and growth objectives.
Evaluate investments, business initiatives, and strategic opportunities through modelling and scenario analysis.
Provide financial leadership on strategic initiatives, business cases, and investment decisions.
Support executive and Board reporting requirements.

Treasury & Foreign Exchange Management

Own foreign exchange exposure tracking, reporting, and scenario analysis across the Group's multi-currency operations.
Partner with treasury, banking partners, and external advisors to evaluate foreign exchange risks and mitigation strategies.
Assess the financial impact of currency fluctuations on forecasts, budgets, cash flow, and business performance.
Develop recommendations and decision-support materials for leadership regarding FX risk management and capital planning.
Monitor market trends and currency movements, proactively identifying risks and opportunities that may impact business performance.

Team Leadership & Capability Building

Lead a small finance team — including a Finance Manager and intern — as a player-coach: owning models and analysis end-to-end while delegating and developing where appropriate.
Foster a high-performance, analytically rigorous culture within the team.
Support ERP and reporting tool improvements from a finance data and output perspective.
Champion the evolution of finance from a reporting function to a true strategic business partner.

What You’ll Bring

8+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, Corporate Finance, Strategic Finance, or Finance Business Partnering — with a track record of owning complex models in a multi-entity environment.
Advanced Excel skills — non-negotiable. You build models from scratch, structure them for auditability, and are fast and precise in the tool.
Strong accounting foundation: you understand how the P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow statement connect inside a model.
Proven experience leading enterprise budgeting, forecasting, and long-range planning processes.
Experience analyzing foreign exchange exposure, multi-currency financial impacts, and scenario modelling within a corporate FP&A, finance, or strategic finance environment.
Strong executive presence, comfortable presenting to senior leadership and capable of influencing and constructively challenging stakeholders.
Experience in multi-entity and multi-currency operating environments.
CPA designation strongly preferred; candidates without the designation will be considered where technical skills and experience are strong.
Background in travel, technology, hospitality, or another fast-paced, multi-brand environment is an asset.

Who You Are

You are a builder. You prefer to own models end-to-end and take pride in work that is structured, auditable, and built to last.
You are intellectually curious and detail-oriented, but able to zoom out and connect the numbers to a broader business narrative.
You operate well with ambiguity and can manage competing priorities without losing accuracy or composure.
You are a collaborative leader who still wants to be close to the work — energized by doing, not just directing.
You communicate with a low-ego, peer-level style — credible with senior stakeholders, collegial with the broader team, and proactive about surfacing issues.

Why Join Range Group

This is a rare opportunity to bridge corporate finance and executive strategy in a multi-brand travel and technology portfolio. You’ll have genuine influence — shaping how capital is allocated, how performance is communicated, and how the finance function evolves as the company grows.

The role carries real complexity: multi-entity consolidations, multi-currency exposure, and a direct reporting line to the Chief Finance Officer. You’ll lead a small team and have the space to build the frameworks and processes that become the foundation for the company’s next phase.

Hybrid Work Model

We’re based in Toronto and targeting three days in office per week, with flexibility built in.

We provide a competitive compensation package with a strong pay for performance rewards approach. Employees have the opportunity to participate in incentive programs and compensation tied to business and individual performance. The actual compensation may vary depending on local market conditions, geography and relevant job-related factors such as knowledge, skills, qualifications, experience, and education/training.

We are committed to providing employment accommodation in accordance with the Ontario Human Rights Code and the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act. If you require accommodation due to a disability at any stage of our hiring process, please advise us when completing your application.

The Range Group may use artificial intelligence throughout the recruitment process to screen, assess or select applicants for this position. These tools assist our hiring team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans.

We thank all candidates for their interest however only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.title: Director, Trust & Anti-Fraud // Directeur, Confiance et Anti-fraude
jobs.description:
Mistplay est l'application de fidélité n°1 pour les joueurs mobiles. Notre communauté de millions de joueurs mobiles engagés utilise Mistplay pour découvrir de nouveaux jeux et gagner des récompenses. Les joueurs sont récompensés pour le temps et l'argent qu'ils consacrent aux jeux et peuvent échanger ces récompenses contre des cartes cadeaux. Mistplay a pour mission d'être le meilleur moyen de jouer à des jeux mobiles pour tous, partout dans le monde ! Téléchargez Mistplay sur le Google Play Store  ici  et suivez-nous sur  Instagram ,  Twitter  et  Facebook .

📍 Veuillez noter :
Au Canada 🇨🇦, Mistplay suit un modèle hybride de 2 jours/semaine en bureau à Toronto (400 University Ave) & Montréal (1001 Blvd. Robert-Bourassa)

Mistplay is the #1 loyalty app for mobile gamers. Our community of millions of engaged mobile gamers come to Mistplay to discover new games to play and earn rewards. Gamers are rewarded for their time and money spent within the games and can redeem those rewards for gift cards. Mistplay is on a mission to be the best way to play mobile games for everyone everywhere! Download Mistplay on the Google Play Store  here  and follow us on  Instagram ,  Twitter  and  Facebook .

📍 Please Note:
In Canada 🇨🇦, Mistplay follows a 2 days/week in-office hybrid model in Toronto (400 University Ave) & Montreal (1001 Blvd. Robert-Bourassa)

🇫🇷  La description en français est ci-dessous ⬇️ 
Overview
Mistplay is the loyalty platform for mobile gamers. Players earn real rewards for playing games on Android and iOS, game studios pay us to acquire players who stay, and our LoyaltyPlay offerwalls extend that economy into other publishers' apps. A rewards economy can sometimes attract people who want the rewards without the play, and the ways they try keep changing: device farms, emulators, multi-accounting, referral abuse, account takeover, spoofed playtime and purchases, and low-quality traffic on the supply we sell to advertisers.

AI has changed the nature of that fight. Attackers now use it to generate accounts, mimic real play sessions, write convincing appeals and automate offerwall completions at a scale and speed that rule-based defences were never built for. We believe the answer is to be better at AI than they are. We're looking for a leader who will build stronger detection, prevention and mitigation, including through the use of AI: agents that triage and investigate, models that learn faster than attackers adapt, and tooling that lets a small team cover a large and shifting surface.

You will be accountable for our fraud strategy, our fraud roadmap and the metrics demonstrating ongoing and improved fraud prevention the company runs on, and you'll report on all three to the Senior Leadership Team and the board. You won't do it alone. You'll work in a tight coordination with our Fraud Analytics Manager and an Engineering Manager, who bring the analysts and engineers; together you define the roadmap, and you are the one accountable for landing it, working with Product to get it into plans and shipped.

This is a hands-on role in the sense that matters: you'll be in the data, running investigations, prototyping detection logic, shaping enforcement policy and running the response when an attack hits. It starts as a senior individual contributor position, and we expect it to grow: as the function matures there is room for this person to take on direct reports.

What You'll Be Doing

Own the fraud strategy and roadmap. Keep a clear, current picture of where we're exposed and what it costs, decide what we tackle this quarter and next, and turn that into a roadmap the Fraud Analytics, Engineering and Product teams commit to. Bring new features, offers and reward mechanics through an abuse review before they launch, and push back when something isn't ready

Be the accountable owner of Mistplay's fraud metrics. Define how we measure loss, prevalence and false positives, make sure the numbers are trusted, and deliver regular updates on our fraud posture, strategy and progress to the Senior Leadership Team and the board

Lead detection and enforcement work with the Fraud Analytics and other cross-functional teams. Set the investigation agenda, dig into live attack patterns alongside the analysts, prototype the rules and models that stop them, and hand clean specs to engineering to productionise. Own the enforcement ladder, from warnings and holds through to account and device bans, and the appeals policy behind it, so that real players aren't the collateral. You’ll also work cross-functionally with our commercial and marketing teams to ensure coordination and resolution with our clients and our marketing channels

Stand up fraud on-call and incident response. Build the on-call rotation and the incident response playbooks and procedures for fraud events, with clear severity levels, escalation paths and communication to the business. When an incident happens, run it: contain the attack, coordinate analytics, engineering, support and finance, and keep leadership informed. Afterwards, own the post-incident review and report, and make sure the mitigations that prevent a repeat get prioritised and shipped

Protect the quality of what we sell. Set traffic-quality standards for LoyaltyPlay and our third-party offerwall publishers, decide how we score and act on publisher-level fraud, and own the install-quality story we tell advertisers, including how we handle disputes

Make the function AI-native. Bring LLM and coding agents into day-to-day fraud work, from triage and evidence gathering to first-pass investigations, with people making the final enforcement calls. Help the analytics team adopt them, and keep an eye on AI-driven abuse as a threat in its own right

Own our platform and vendor choices. Decide how we use Play Integrity, App Attest and our MMP's fraud tooling, evaluate device-intelligence and bot-detection vendors against measured results, and make the call on what we buy

Influence across the company. Fraud touches Commercial, Marketing, Engineering, Product, UA, Supply, Support, Finance and Legal. You'll be the person who keeps everyone clear on what good looks like and what they own, without needing formal authority over any of them

What We're Looking For

10-12 or more years in fraud, risk, trust and safety or anti-abuse, much of it at a consumer platform, mobile ad network, MMP or rewards business. You've personally dealt with several of the threats above and can talk in detail about what worked and what didn't

Comfortable and current in the data. Strong SQL, enough Python to prototype and analyse, and a track record of designing detection logic that ran in production, even if someone else deployed it

Sharp analytical and critical reasoning: you can size a loss, weigh it against the cost of a control, and make a call you can defend to a CFO

Experience owning a fraud or risk strategy and roadmap, and presenting it to senior leadership or a board

You've run fraud or security incidents end to end, ideally having set up the on-call and incident response process yourself, and you can show how your post-incident work stopped the same thing happening twice

Proven ability to get things done through teams you don't manage, and to partner well with analytics and engineering leaders who do

AI-forward in practice: you use LLM and coding agents in your own work, you've applied AI to detection or investigation before, and you have a grounded view of where it helps and where a human has to decide

Working familiarity with Play Integrity, App Attest or DeviceCheck, MMP fraud suites and the device-intelligence vendor landscape

Strong communication and collaborative skills, including strong follow-through

Nice to have: Rewarded gaming, offerwall or incentivized UA experience; Databricks or Spark; graph or link analysis; mobile client security knowledge; prior people management or a desire to grow into it

What Mistplay Offers

Real ownership of a domain that protects revenue, player trust and advertiser relationships, and presenting fraud strategy and results directly to the Senior Leadership Team and the board.

A Fraud Analytics team and an Engineering Manager as your day-to-day partners, inside an AI forward, fast paced engineering culture 

A role designed to grow with you, including the option to build and lead a team as the function expands

Competitive compensation and benefits package.

Interview Process
A conversation about your experience, a fraud strategy case & a hands-on data exercise (AI assistants welcome), and an onsite conversation with the CTO & Fraud Analytics Manager & Fraud Engineering Manager where you walk through your case the way you would on-the-job with senior leadership.

🇫🇷 Description en français

Aperçu du poste
Mistplay est la plateforme de fidélisation pour les joueurs mobiles. Les joueurs gagnent de vraies récompenses en jouant à des jeux sur Android et iOS, les studios de jeux nous paient pour acquérir des joueurs engagés, et nos mur d'offres LoyaltyPlay étendent cette économie aux applications d'autres éditeurs. Une économie de récompenses peut parfois attirer des personnes qui souhaitent obtenir des récompenses sans jouer, et leurs méthodes évoluent continuellement : fermes d'appareils, émulateurs, comptes multiples, abus de parrainage, prise de contrôle de compte, falsification du temps de jeu et des achats, et trafic de faible qualité sur l'inventaire que nous vendons aux annonceurs.

L'IA a modifié la nature de cette lutte. Les fraudeurs l'utilisent désormais pour générer des comptes, imiter de vraies sessions de jeu, rédiger des appels convaincants et automatiser la réalisation d'offres à une échelle et une vitesse auxquelles les défenses basées sur des règles n'ont jamais été préparées. Nous croyons que la solution consiste à être meilleurs qu'eux en matière d'IA. Nous recherchons un leader qui saura bâtir une détection, une prévention et une atténuation plus fortes, notamment grâce à l'utilisation de l'IA : des agents qui trient et enquêtent, des modèles qui apprennent plus vite que les fraudeurs s'adaptent, et des outils permettant à une petite équipe de couvrir une surface vaste et évolutive.

Vous serez responsable de notre stratégie anti-fraude, de notre feuille de route anti-fraude et des indicateurs démontrant une prévention continue et améliorée sur lesquels l'entreprise s'appuie, et vous rendrez compte de ces trois éléments à l'équipe de direction principale et au conseil d'administration. Vous ne le ferez pas seul. Vous travaillerez en étroite coordination avec notre gestionnaire de l'analyse de la fraude et un gestionnaire de l'ingénierie, qui dirigent les analystes et les ingénieurs; ensemble, vous définirez la feuille de route, et vous serez la personne responsable de sa réalisation, en collaborant avec l'équipe Produit pour l'intégrer aux plans et la déployer.

Il s'agit d'un rôle concret au sens le plus important : vous serez dans les données, mènerez des enquêtes, prototyoerez la logique de détection, façonnerez la politique d'application des mesures et gérerez la réponse lorsqu'une attaque survient. Il s'agit au départ d'un poste de spécialiste individuel senior, et nous nous attendons à ce qu'il évolue : à mesure que la fonction mûrit, cette personne pourra prendre en charge des collaborateurs directs.

Ce que vous ferez

Détenir la stratégie et la feuille de route anti-fraude. Maintenir une vision claire et actuelle de nos vulnérabilités et de ce qu'elles coûtent, décider de nos priorités pour ce trimestre et le suivant, et transformer cela en une feuille de route envers laquelle les équipes d'Analyse de la fraude, d'Ingénierie et de Produit s'engagent. Soumettre les nouvelles fonctionnalités, offres et mécaniques de récompense à une révision des risques d'abus avant leur lancement, et repousser ce qui n'est pas prêt

Être le responsable ultime des indicateurs de fraude de Mistplay. Définir notre manière de mesu

Integrated Asset and facilities management;
Operation and maintenance of buildings and equipment (including district heating and cooling);

Building automation and systems;
Solutions for transportation and mobility.

Develop creative financing solutions across construction debt, land development, mezzanine and structured equity.
Maintain strong risk management, credit quality, and portfolio oversight standards.
Establish and execute regional business plans, budgets and growth objectives in partnership with executive leadership.
Represent the firm as a trusted, solution-oriented capital partner in the Ontario market.
Build the firm’s brand and visibility by engaging in industry events, thought leadership, and relationship-driven business development.

15+ years of progressive experience in commercial real estate finance, construction lending, development finance, credit or related capital markets.
Strong understanding of construction and development risk, including project feasibility, development budgets, cost-to-complete analysis, borrower equity, valuations, construction timelines and exit strategies.
Significant experience structuring and executing complex real estate financing transactions, including construction debt, land development financing, mezzanine and structured financing.

Established relationships within the Ontario commercial real estate market, particularly with developers, builders, investors, lenders and intermediaries.
Strong commercial judgment and the ability to develop creative financing solutions while maintaining disciplined credit standards.
Strategic and entrepreneurial mindset, with the ability to lead and grow a regional lending business.
Professional designations such as CFA, CPA or MBA considered strong assets.

jobs.title: Director of Financial Resilience
jobs.description:
New Destiny’s mission is to end the cycle of domestic violence and homelessness for low-income families and individuals by developing and connecting them to safe, permanent, affordable housing and services. To achieve its mission, New Destiny builds and manages housing with on-site services; offers innovative programs that assist survivors in finding and retaining affordable housing; and works to expand access to permanent housing resources for survivors. New Destiny is the largest provider of supportive housing for domestic violence survivors in New York and is a leading advocate in the effort to obtain the resources needed to end family homelessness in New York City.

General Description

The Director of Financial Resilience is a new position, created to launch and lead a department and team that assists domestic violence survivors in achieving financial stability, safety, and long-term wealth growth. This position will guide a team of three financial coaches, shape trauma-informed programming, and build partnerships with financial institutions and community organizations that expand access to resources for survivors. The Director will create a new department that will integrate a financial resilience model across New Destiny’s housing programs, with the goal of increasing the number of domestic violence survivors able to receive financial stabilization services, deepen survivors’ financial literacy and knowledge, and grow survivors’ financial health and wellness for long-term stability. This work is rooted in trauma-informed care and tailored to the experience and needs of the formerly homeless domestic violence survivors we serve.

Duties and Responsibilities

Design, implement, and evaluate financial empowerment programs, including coaching, credit repair, savings programs, asset building, debt management, and banking access.
Create curriculum for financial education and workshops and short-term financial coaching to stabilize and strengthen the economic health of survivor-led households.
Build out and execute policies and protocols for this new department, ensuring that all services being built out are survivor-centered, trauma-informed, and culturally responsive.
Develop key performance indicators to track outcomes and report to leadership and funders.
Supervise and support three financial coaches, including one-on-one supervision and performance reviews.
Provide access to training to financial coaches, including best practices and recovery from financial abuse.
Build and maintain relationships internally across departments and externally with banks, credit unions, and other financial institutions to create survivor-friendly products and services.
Partner with community organizations focusing on income security, financial independence and growth, including legal partners, eviction-prevention organizations, workforce development opportunities, and other social services to create seamless referral pathways.
Identify and pursue opportunities for matched savings and other wealth-building initiatives.
Manage program budget and ensure compliance with funder requirements.

Qualifications

A master’s degree in social work, finance, non-profit management, or a related field or equivalent experience is required.
Eight to ten years of work experience with at least three to five years in financial empowerment in a social services setting is required.
Three to five years in a supervisory role required.
Must have extensive knowledge of domestic violence dynamics and economic abuse, with experience working with trauma-informed care practices.
Experience working in or with the affordable housing industry, especially direct work with eviction prevention, preferred.
Must be a self-starter with experience in program development.
Proven success building partnerships with financial institutions and community organizations.
Must be a team player with strong communication, leadership, and data-tracking skills.
Financial coaching certifications strongly preferred (e.g., AFCPE, CFEC).
Bilingual in Spanish strongly preferred.

Compensation/Benefits

$100,000 a year with competitive benefits. This is a full-time position with a benefits package including medical, dental, vision, short disability, PTO paid holidays and 401(k). EOE

New Destiny is an equal opportunity employer and committed to diversity. Survivors of domestic violence and people who have experienced housing instability are encouraged to apply.

About Diabetes Canada

Diabetes Canada is working toward a world free from the effects of diabetes. That’s why they work together to improve the lives of those living with diabetes – sharing knowledge and resources, supporting health-care professionals to improve patient care, advocating for change through policy, and funding research to advance treatments and discover a cure.

Living with diabetes is a complex and often relentless journey, testing the resilience of every individual affected. Diabetes Canada is here to help—providing tools, resources, and support to make that journey easier.

Join us in leading with strength and compassion - so no one faces diabetes alone.

About the Role

This includes national and regional partnerships through all revenue channels including corporate sponsorships, cause marketing, point-of-sale and employee engagement. Brief Description

Role Summary

The Successful Candidate Will Be Accountable For The Execution, Funding, Servicing, Administration, Compliance, And Operational Performance Of The Insured Lending Portfolio. This Includes

Executing and administering the CMHC-insured mortgage portfolio;
Maintaining compliant funding, accurate servicing, effective risk management, and strong operations controls;
Meeting CMHC, investor, aggregator, and regulatory requirements; and
Acting as the primary link between underwriting, capital markets, finance, operations, third-party operational providers, and CMHC throughout each insured loan's life cycle.

Success in this role will depend on your ability to deliver expert-level client service, consistently fund and administer CMHC-insured transactions, and apply your expertise to create value for clients while strengthening KV Capital’s reputation as a trusted leader in the multifamily lending market.

Responsibilities

Working with KV Capital’s leadership team, you will be responsible for:

Leading all CMHC loan funding, closing, and disbursement activities
Ensuring all funding conditions, legal requirements, and CMHC program requirements are satisfied before funding;
Overseeing administration and servicing of the CMHC-insured mortgage portfolio throughout the loan life cycle;
Managing borrower payments, renewals, assumptions, amendments, discharges, and ongoing loan maintenance;
Ensuring compliance with CMHC, National Housing Act, investor, and internal policy requirements;
Maintaining strong operational controls, segregation of duties, and funding authorization protocols;
Overseeing loan onboarding, system administration, data integrity, reconciliations, and servicing records;
Monitoring portfolio performance, delinquency trends, covenant compliance, insurance coverage, and property tax status;
Managing defaults, workout strategies, enforcement actions, and required CMHC notifications;
Coordinating with aggregators, custodians, servicers, legal counsel, and other third-party service providers;
Supporting loan sales, securitization readiness, settlement, and investor reporting;
Overseeing trust accounting controls, cash movements, and funding reconciliations;
Establishing and maintaining servicing policies, procedures, controls, and quality assurance programs;
Leading and developing funding and servicing team members, including training and performance management;
Providing portfolio, funding, servicing, compliance, and risk reporting to senior management and governance committees;
Driving operational efficiency, automation, scalability, and continuous improvement initiatives; and
Acting as the primary operational liaison with CMHC on funding, servicing, compliance, and audit matters.

Requirements

Bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, Commerce, Business, Economics, or a related discipline.
5+ years of progressively senior experience in multifamily mortgage lending, with meaningful exposure to CMHC lending, funding, servicing, operations, capital markets, securitization, regulated lending environments, and third-party service provider oversight.
Professional designation or advanced credential is preferred, such as CFA, CPA, MBA, Chartered Banker, mortgage industry certification, or servicing-related qualification.
Strong knowledge of mortgage legal documentation, security registration, closing processes, and funding requirements.
Demonstrated expertise in loan portfolio administration, servicing, delinquency management, and default resolution.
Practical understanding of capital markets, loan sales, aggregators, custodians, settlement processes, and securitization requirements.
Experience developing policies, procedures, controls, governance frameworks, and quality assurance processes.
Ability to lead operational, technology, automation, and process improvement initiatives at scale.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with CMHC, aggregators, executives, auditors, investors, and service providers.
Proven ability to lead cross-functional collaboration across underwriting, servicing, finance, treasury, legal, operations, and capital markets.

Summary

About KV Capital

At KV Capital, we have established ourselves as industry leaders in real estate debt and investment, driven by our unwavering commitment to excellence, trusted partnerships, and innovative solutions. Since our founding in 2006, we have expanded our business across three connected areas of service: real estate private equity, real estate lending, and private equity investments in real estate supply chain businesses. Managing a robust portfolio of +$2 billion in funded investments, accompanied by +$1 billion in assets under management, our dedicated team of finance experts is driven by a shared goal to cultivate prosperity for our clients, investment partners, and communities. We have office locations in Edmonton, Calgary, and Toronto, and continue to expand and extend our reach nationally.

Insured Lending

KV Capital is expanding its CMHC-insured multifamily lending platform, providing insured term and construction financing solutions for multifamily and purpose-built rental properties under CMHC’s National Housing Act programs. Our platform pairs deep capital markets and securitization expertise with a disciplined, credit-aware approach to origination, delivering competitive insured financing to borrowers, sponsors, and developers across the market.

What KV Capital Offers

Performance-based and long-term incentives.
Eligible to participate in our Employee Stock Option Plan
Competitive vacation offering and flexible time off, including birthdays off and holiday office closure.
100% Employer paid benefits.
Tuition and professional development support.
Hybrid work offering

This position has a base salary range of $125,000 - $160,000 annually.

jobs.description:
At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go.

Join EY and help to build a better working world.

The opportunity

Payroll is a business-critical function, and organizations are looking for more efficient, technology-enabled ways to deliver it.

We’re looking for a senior payroll or employment tax professional who knows the market, sees where it’s going and wants to turn those insights into growth.

As a Director in EY’s Payroll Operate team, you’ll lead significant client relationships and help organizations transform how payroll is managed through EY’s managed payroll services. You’ll oversee complex payroll operations and new client transitions, bring together people, process and technology, and help build scalable solutions that improve the payroll experience.

This is an opportunity to combine payroll leadership, client delivery and commercial thinking while helping shape the growth of EY’s Payroll Operate business in Canada and contribute to the global business.

This posting does not relate to an existing vacancy. We are actively recruiting for this strategic hire to support the continued growth and development of our business.

Your Key Responsibilities

Lead managed payroll services for complex client organizations, with accountability for quality, controls and client experience.
Build strong relationships with senior payroll, HR and finance leaders and provide practical guidance on payroll operations.
Lead new client implementations and transitions, establishing effective processes, governance and service expectations.
Oversee end-to-end payroll delivery, including processing, reconciliations, reporting and payments.
Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize and automate payroll through technology and better ways of working.
Shape and grow the business by identifying market opportunities and expanding our work with Canadian and multinational organizations.
Grow client relationships and contribute to new opportunities, proposals and payroll solution design.
Develop high-performing teams through coaching, collaboration and clear leadership.

Skills And Attributes For Success

Strong knowledge of Canadian payroll and the end-to-end payroll lifecycle.
Understanding of global payroll and the ability to collaborate with colleagues across regions and countries to support organizations with global operations.
Deep familiarity with enterprise payroll and HRIS systems (e.g., ADP, Workday, Dayforce), multi-jurisdictional tax laws, and advanced data analytics/Excel proficiency
Experience leading complex payroll operations, implementations or managed services.
Ability to build credibility and strong relationships with senior clients.
A continuous improvement mindset and interest in payroll technology, automation and transformation.
Strong operational judgment with the ability to manage risk and resolve complex delivery challenges.
Collaborative leadership style with a focus on developing people and teams.

Qualifications

Typically, 10+ years of progressive payroll experience, including significant leadership responsibility.
A bachelor’s degree in business, accounting, finance, human resources or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.
Strong knowledge of Canadian payroll requirements, processes, controls and reporting.
Experience leading payroll teams, complex implementations, client relationships or significant payroll programs.

Ideally, you’ll also have,

A PLP, PCP, CPA or other relevant professional designation.
Experience in managed payroll, outsourced payroll or a shared services environment.
Experience transitioning payroll operations to a new delivery model or provider.
Exposure to payroll technology, automation, data analytics or transformation.
Experience contributing to proposals, solution design or new client opportunities.

What We Look For

We’re looking for an experienced payroll leader who knows how to deliver payroll reliably at scale while continually looking for ways to make it better. You combine strong operational judgment with a client mindset and are comfortable leading change, solving complex delivery challenges and building strong teams. You’re also excited by the opportunity to strengthen client relationships and help grow EY’s Payroll Operate business.

What We Offer

We offer a competitive compensation package where you’ll be rewarded based on your performance and recognized for the value you bring to our business. In addition, our Total Rewards package allows you to decide which benefits are right for you and which ones help you create a solid foundation for your future. Our Total Rewards package includes a discretionary bonus program, a comprehensive medical, prescription drug and dental coverage plan, a defined contribution pension plan, a great vacation policy plus firm paid days that allow you to enjoy longer long weekends throughout the year, statutory holidays and paid personal days (based on province of residence), and a range of exciting programs and benefits designed to support your physical, financial and social well-being. Plus, we offer:

Support and coaching from some of the most engaging colleagues in the industry
Learning opportunities to develop new skills and progress your career
The freedom and flexibility to handle your role in a way that’s right for you

Are you ready to shape your future with confidence? Apply today.

To help create the best experience during the recruitment process, please describe any accommodations you may need.

Inclusiveness at EY

Inclusiveness is at the heart of who we are and how we work. We’re committed to fostering an environment where differences are valued, policies and practices are equitable, and our people feel a sense of belonging. We embrace diversity and are committed to combating systemic racism, advancing gender equity and women in leadership, advocating for the 2SLGBTQIA+ community, promoting our neuroinclusion and accessibility initiatives, and are dedicated to amplifying the voices of Indigenous peoples (First Nations, Inuit, and Métis) nationally as we strive towards reconciliation. Our diverse experiences, abilities, backgrounds, and perspectives make our people unique and help guide us. Because when people feel free to be their authentic selves at work, they bring their best and are empowered to build a better working world.

EY is building a better working world by creating new value for clients, people, society and the planet, while building trust in capital markets.

Enabled by data, AI and advanced technology, EY teams help clients shape the future with confidence and develop answers for the most pressing issues of today and tomorrow.

EY teams work across a full spectrum of services in assurance, consulting, tax, strategy and transactions. Fueled by sector insights, a globally connected, multi-disciplinary network and diverse ecosystem partners, EY teams can provide services in more than 150 countries and territories.
