jobs.title: Executive Vice President of Project Management
jobs.description:
The Executive Vice President (EVP) of Project Management is responsible for leading the company’s overall project management system. This role oversees enterprise-level project strategy, portfolio planning, the execution of major projects, resource allocation, schedule control, budget management, and project delivery performance—ensuring that the company’s strategic projects and business initiatives advance efficiently and systematically toward their established goals.

The position focuses on enterprise-level project governance, the execution of strategic projects, and the management of project delivery. It serves as a key link between the Project Management Office (PMO) and various functions, including business operations, finance, technology, product development, human resources, and other business units. By establishing unified project management standards, execution mechanisms, oversight systems, and performance evaluation frameworks, the EVP enhances project delivery quality, operational efficiency, resource utilization, and cross-functional collaboration, ensuring that project outcomes remain aligned with the company’s long-term strategic objectives.

Core Responsibilities

I. Project Management Strategy and Planning
- Formulate the company’s overarching project management strategy, annual project objectives, and long-term execution plans.
- Develop a project management system aligned with the company’s corporate development strategy.
- Oversee the planning and implementation of the company’s major and strategic projects.
- Establish project management policies, execution standards, and operational guidelines.
- Continuously optimize the project management model based on evolving business needs.
- Ensure that project plans remain aligned with the company’s broader business goals.

II. Project Portfolio and Governance
- Monitor the execution of the company’s entire project portfolio and major initiatives.
- Establish mechanisms for project prioritization, approval, and decision-making.
- Oversee execution quality across all stages of the project lifecycle.
- Identify resource dependencies, scheduling conflicts, and execution risks across projects.
- Implement a project governance framework and a reporting mechanism for senior management.
- Provide regular updates on the progress of major projects to the CEO, COO, and the Board of Directors.

III. Execution Management for Major Projects
- Lead the implementation of the company’s core projects and cross-functional strategic initiatives.
- Supervise the full project lifecycle, including initiation, planning, execution, monitoring, and closure.
- Ensure that projects are delivered within the defined scope, budget, and timeline.
- Address issues such as project delays, resource shortages, and execution obstacles.
- Establish mechanisms for milestone reviews and periodic project phase acceptance.
- Drive coordination and problem-solving for complex, multi-faceted projects.

IV. Project Resource and Team Management
- Coordinate resource allocation across project managers, project supervisors, and specialized teams.
- Determine project staffing requirements and develop long-term resource plans.
- Optimize project team workloads and personnel utilization rates.
- Adjust personnel, budget, and technical resources based on project priorities.
- Establish performance management and talent development mechanisms for project managers.
- Ensure that key projects are adequately resourced for execution.

V. Project Budgeting and Cost Control
- Oversee the company’s overall project budget and capital expenditure plans.
- Review budget requirements and resource investments for major projects.
- Monitor project costs, expenses, and budget execution.
- Identify risks of budget overruns and drive corrective actions.
- Analyze project cost-benefit and return-on-investment (ROI) performance.
- Enhance project budget transparency and cost-control capabilities.

VI. Project Schedule and Delivery Performance
- Establish a unified system for project schedule management and delivery oversight.
- Monitor key milestones, project completion rates, and delivery quality.
- Develop project performance metrics and management dashboards.
- Regularly assess variances between actual project progress and planned schedules.
- Require project managers to develop recovery plans for delays and performance improvement initiatives.
- Ensure projects are delivered on time, within budget, and in accordance with requirements.

VII. Project Processes and Standardization
- Establish a company-wide project management methodology and execution standards.
- Drive the standardization of PMO management policies and project management processes.
- Optimize processes for project initiation, approval, execution, change management, and acceptance.
- Set standards for project documentation, reporting, and information management.
- Promote the consistent use of project management software and digital tools.
- Develop scalable and replicable project management best practices.

VIII. Risk and Quality Management
- Establish an enterprise-level framework for identifying, assessing, and providing early warnings for project risks.
- Oversee risks related to project scope, costs, schedules, and delivery quality.
- Address complex issues and unforeseen incidents that arise during the execution of major projects.
- Facilitate project risk assessments, root-cause analyses, and the implementation of corrective measures.
- Define standards for project quality reviews and delivery acceptance. - Mitigate the risks of project delays, budget overruns, and delivery failures.

IX. Cross-Departmental Coordination and Executive Decision Support
- Coordinate project execution across business, finance, technology, product, and operations departments.
- Resolve conflicts regarding cross-departmental resource allocation and project prioritization.
- Establish mechanisms for escalating critical project issues and facilitating management decision-making.
- Provide senior management with insights into project execution status and strategic recommendations.
- Ensure all business units are aligned with unified project objectives.
- Drive the translation of corporate strategic plans into actionable project outcomes.

X. Team Leadership and Organizational Development
- Lead the company’s project management department and Project Management Office (PMO).
- Build a talent pipeline of project managers and senior project management professionals.
- Define departmental management objectives, performance standards, and career development plans.
- Cultivate talent in project planning, execution control, and the management of complex projects.
- Enhance the professional capabilities and leadership skills of the project management team.
- Foster a project management culture characterized by high execution, accountability, and a focus on results.

Qualifications

Education
- Bachelor’s degree or higher in Project Management, Business Administration, Engineering Management, Commerce, Information Technology, or a related field.
- MBA, EMBA, or a master’s degree in a project management-related discipline is preferred.
- PMP, PgMP, or other PMI-related certifications are preferred.
- Training or background in large-scale project management, enterprise-level project governance, or PMO management is preferred.

Work Experience
- 20+ years of experience in project management, project execution, portfolio management, or corporate operations management.
- 15+ years of experience in senior project management or leading large-scale project organizations.
- Proven experience in leading multiple project teams and cross-departmental project portfolios.
- Extensive experience in managing budgets, resource allocation, schedule control, and delivery for large-scale projects.
- Experience in establishing or optimizing enterprise-level PMOs and project governance frameworks.
- Industry experience in Technology, Financial Services, FinTech, Engineering, Construction, Enterprise Software, or Professional Services is preferred.

Core Competencies
- Executive Project Management
- Strategic Project Execution
- Project Portfolio Management
- Program Management
- PMO Leadership
- Enterprise Project Governance
- Project Planning & Execution
- Project Controls
- Resource Allocation
- Budget & Cost Management
- Project Delivery Management
- Risk & Quality Management
- Performance Management
- Cross-functional Leadership
- Strategic Planning
- Organizational Development

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
- On-time Project Delivery Rate
- Project Budget Achievement Rate
- Project Cost Variance
- Key Milestone Completion Rate
- Strategic Project Execution Completion Rate
- Overall Project Portfolio Performance
- Project Delay Rate
- Project Delivery Quality Compliance Rate
- Project Resource Utilization Rate
- Return on Investment (ROI) for Projects
- Timeliness of Project Risk Resolution
- Project Change Control Compliance Rate
- PMO Process Execution Compliance Rate
- Cross-departmental Project Collaboration Efficiency
- Improvement in Project Management Efficiency
- Contribution of Project Outcomes to Corporate Strategic Goals

Billyard Insurance Group (BIG) is a leading force in the insurance industry, committed to attracting the best insurance professionals and equipping them with cutting-edge technology, tools, and unwavering support to thrive in today's dynamic insurance landscape. With a strong presence and continuous growth, we boast over 80 locations across Canada. Our dedication to excellence has earned us prestigious recognition, including being featured on Insurance Business Canada's esteemed Top Brokerages list for the past three years and securing a spot as one of Canada's Top Growing Companies in the renowned Globe and Mail's Report on Business. At Billyard Insurance Group, our mission is clear: to establish a nationally recognized insurance brokerage brand that empowers brokers and leads the digital insurance revolution.

Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the Vice-President, Technology & Digital Transformation is BIG's senior technology leader, responsible for defining and executing the enterprise technology strategy while ensuring the reliability, security and scalability of our technology environment.

This is an opportunity to influence business direction at the executive level while leading a broad technology portfolio encompassing infrastructure, cloud operations, cybersecurity, enterprise applications, software development, digital transformation and emerging technologies. You will balance long-term strategic priorities with operational performance, ensuring technology investments translate into meaningful business outcomes.

As a trusted advisor to the executive team, you will help identify opportunities to modernize operations, advance AI and automation capabilities, strengthen organizational resilience and enhance the experience of our brokers and employees.

What does the Vice-President, Technology & Digital Transformation do?

You will provide enterprise-wide leadership across BIG's technology function, ensuring our systems, infrastructure, people and investments are aligned with organizational priorities and positioned to support continued growth.

Your Responsibilities Will Include

Lead Enterprise Technology Strategy: Develop and execute a forward-looking technology strategy that supports organizational growth, operational effectiveness and long-term business objectives. Translate business priorities into clear technology roadmaps and investment plans.
Drive Digital Transformation: Identify and champion opportunities for automation, artificial intelligence, technology modernization and process improvement that enhance efficiency, strengthen capabilities and improve the broker and employee experience.
Oversee Technology Operations: Provide executive oversight of enterprise infrastructure, networks, cloud operations, systems administration and end-user support, ensuring reliable, secure and high-performing technology services.

**Description:**

**About Us:**



The Faculty of Arts \& Science is the heart of Canada’s leading university and one of the most comprehensive and diverse academic divisions in the world. The strength of Arts \& Science derives from our combined teaching and research excellence in the humanities, sciences and social sciences across 29 departments, seven colleges and 46 interdisciplinary centres, institutes and programs.

  



We can only realize our mission with the dedication and excellence of engaged staff and faculty. The diversity of opportunities and perspectives within the Faculty reflects the local and global landscape and the need for curiosity, innovative thinking, and collaboration. At Arts \& Science, we take pride in our legacy of innovation and discovery that has changed the way we think about the world.

  



The Canadian Institute for Theoretical Astrophysics (CITA) is a nationally supported research institute and a non\-profit corporation (CITA Inc.) Our mission is to foster interaction within the Canadian astrophysics community and to serve as an international centre of excellence for theoretical studies in astrophysics. We educate and develop the next generation of scientific leaders with national postdoctoral fellowships as well as postdoctoral and senior research associate fellowships, and through the supervision of undergraduate and graduate students. We are devoted to studying the origin and evolution of the universe and the many phenomena revealed by modern astronomy.

  


**About Planetary and Molecular Sensing Technologies Program**



The Eddie Goldenberg Research Chairs of Canada program is a major national initiative that supports ambitious research and accelerates translation into industrial, economic, and societal impact. Within this initiative, Professor Sara Seager holds the Eddie Goldenberg Distinguished Research Chair of Canada in Planetary and Molecular Sensing Technologies, a major research and innovation initiative focused on translating frontier science and engineering into deployed dual\-use and industrial applications. The program has two broad technical themes. The first is ultra\-sensitive molecular sensing, originally designed for the detection of organic molecules in planetary environments, with translation to Earth\-based applications. The second is planetary computer modeling and inference, including AI\-trained emulators and sparse\-data methods applicable to remote sensing from the ground and from space. The program aims to advance research toward deployed systems serving defence and dual\-use needs, environmental monitoring, agriculture, health, and space applications. This research program spans from multi academic departments within the Faculty of Arts and Science: Chemistry, Physics, CITA, and Astronomy and Astrophysics.

  


**About the Position**



Reporting to the Research Chair, the Executive Director is the most senior administrative leader of the research program. The incumbent has a pivotal leadership role in supporting the Research Chair to shape the growth and direction of the Planetary and Molecular Sensing Technologies research program. They provide strategic operational advice to the Research Chair and collaborate with University of Toronto faculty and senior staff across academic divisions and central offices to ensure the research project’s success in achieving its mission and vision within budget and timeline.

  



The Executive Director fosters and supports partnership development both within and external to the University. Working with the Research Chair, they will be executing on an expanded strategic operational plan and fundraising strategy to ensure the sustainability of the Research project.

  



The Executive Director’s responsibilities include: establishing clear short and long term objectives, identifying external funding opportunities; and monitor and assess the research progress of all streams, liaising with senior colleagues in the academic divisions and central portfolios; supporting strategic partnerships across institutional, governmental, sectoral and geographic borders; developing thematic research, policy and solutions strategies; oversight of strategic communications plans; preparation of key documents including internal and external progress/impact and financial reports; supporting and managing the governance; and implementing research and collaboration funds, allocating budgets, overseeing equipment inventory, procurements overseeing and hiring and managing staff.

  



This Executive Director is responsible for ensuring the program is delivered on time, on budget, and with full accountability across all research streams. The role serves as the primary operational interface between the scientific team and institutional administration, working closely with the Research Chair, domestic and international government agencies and industry partners, researchers and research institutions, postdoctoral fellows, technicians, graduate students, undergraduate students, and external partners.

**EXPERIENCE:**

jobs.description:
About Docker 
 Docker is the platform at the center of how intelligent software gets built. For more than a decade, Docker has helped millions of developers and thousands of organizations build, ship, and run software consistently across any environment. Today, Docker extends that same trust to the AI era. Docker Hardened Images form the foundation agentic code is built on, local and cloud Docker Sandboxes isolate where agents run, and Docker AI Governance sets enterprise-wide policy. Together, they give builders and organizations the confidence to adopt any model, tool, or agent without compromising security, governance, or control. 
 _______________________________________________________________________

 The Role 
 The Director, Developer Success Engineering leads the technical half of Docker's Developer Success team: the senior engineers who build the demos, Labspaces, workshops, tech talks and technical content that show developers what Docker can do. This role gives that team a leader who can go deep on the technology, raise the bar on technical quality, and grow senior engineers in their careers. It owns three outcomes:

 Own Docker's technical story for developers. Demos, Labspaces, reference applications and content that make AI Governance, Sandboxes, Docker Hardened Images and the core Docker experience easy to understand and adopt.

 Turn technical content into adoption and revenue. Equip customer-facing teams, Captains and partners with enablement that lands and expands accounts, and measure its impact.

 Be the developer's voice inside Docker. Bring hands-on feedback from developers, Captains and customers back to Product and Engineering so it shapes what Docker builds.

 You will be part of the DevRel team's mission for Docker to become the destination where current and future developers improve their craft, get support and find their community home. You report to the VP of Developer Success (DevRel & Docs) and lead a team of four staff and principal engineers. You work side by side with the Director, Developer Success Programmes, whose team runs the community, Captain, influencer and partner programmes your team's technical work powers.

 You'll be successful if you are an engineer at heart who loves building and explaining technology, and who wants to multiply that impact through a team. The FY27 centre of gravity is product adoption and revenue enablement, not awareness metrics alone.
 _______________________________________________________________________

 Responsibilities 
 Own Docker's technical story for developers 
 Set the technical content strategy for Developer Success, aligned with Docker's product priorities: agentic development with Sandboxes, AI Governance, Docker Hardened Images and the core Docker experience.

 Own the developer-facing product narrative for Captain briefings and launches, so the team delivers most briefings and demos itself rather than relying on ad hoc presenters.

 Lead the Labspaces catalogue as Docker's reusable demo and learning format: every strategic demo, briefing, talk and workshop is packaged once and reused across Captains, revenue, partners, events and Docs.

 Set technical quality standards for demos, code samples, reference apps and tutorials, including how they are tested, kept current with fast-moving products, and retired.

 Partner with Docs on hands-on learning content on docs.docker.com, including the Learn experience.

 Turn technical content into adoption and revenue 
 Scale the technical enablement content for customer-facing teams: tech talks, Docker Days, SDLC demos and workshops, prioritised with Revenue leadership on a regular cadence.

 Equip Solutions Engineers, Professional Services, Captains and partners to deliver Docker's story themselves, with kits that cut their demo preparation time.

 Track the impact of technical enablement on product adoption, pipeline and expansion ARR, and report it alongside the programmes team.

 Bring the team's technical depth to tier-1 events, partner work and the community programmes run by the Developer Success Programmes team.

 Be the developer's voice inside Docker 
 Build structured feedback loops from developers, Captains and customers into Product and Engineering, including pre-launch reviews of new features.

 Test new products early, report friction in the developer experience, and follow it through to fixes.

 Represent Docker credibly in technical forums: conference talks, open source communities, technical blogs and developer communities.

 Lead the team 
 Lead and grow a team of senior developer advocates and engineers: set clear goals, give technical and career coaching, and build growth paths for senior individual contributors.

 Balance the team's capacity between strategic content, revenue enablement and inbound requests through a clear intake and prioritisation process.

 Hire to fill capability gaps as Docker's product portfolio grows.

 _______________________________________________________________________

 Qualifications 
 A software engineering background, with deep hands-on knowledge of containers, Docker and modern developer workflows. You can build and debug a demo yourself.

 Working knowledge of AI and agentic development (LLMs, agents, MCP) and of software supply chain security. Experience in either is a strong plus.

 Experience leading a team of senior engineers, developer advocates or solutions engineers, and a track record of growing senior individual contributors.

 A strong technical public presence: conference talks, workshops, technical writing or open source contributions.

 Experience building technical enablement for sales, solutions or customer success teams, and tying it to adoption or revenue outcomes.

 Ability to build trusted relationships with Product and Engineering leaders, and to influence roadmaps with evidence from developers.

 Analytical and data-driven in how you prioritise and measure technical content and programmes.

 Able to coordinate across many teams and perform in a fast-moving environment; self-directed, self-driven and able to prioritise strongly.

 Strong verbal and written English communication skills.

 _______________________________________________________________________

 What to expect 
 First 30 days 
 Get to know each team member, their technical focus areas, current work and career goals.

 Get hands-on with Docker's products, especially Sandboxes, AI Governance and Docker Hardened Images, and run the team's top Labspaces and demos yourself.

 Meet key stakeholders in Product, Engineering, Revenue, Professional Services, Docs and the Developer Success Programmes team, and learn what they need from technical Developer Success.

 Live the Docker culture: humility, developer obsession, open collaboration and a bias for considered action.

 First 90 days

jobs.description:
Reporting to the Head of Product, Residential Lending (RESL), the Director, Strategic Partnerships and Partner Rewards is a strategic, relationship-oriented leader accountable for RESL's strategic partnerships and the Partner Rewards program that drives Broker and Advisor engagement.

 The role owns partnership strategy, key relationship ownership and governance for vendors supporting the Advisor and Broker channels, including the national mortgage insurers, First National (our key Broker experience partner), FCT, FNF and other RESL value chain partners. It leads joint roadmaps, service level agreements (SLAs) and commercial terms, with execution and escalations owned by the Manager, Strategic Partnerships. It also leads Partner Rewards (Broker and Advisor Rewards, Compensation Support and RESL Strategic Initiatives) through the Sr. Specialist, Partner Rewards and Strategic Initiatives.

 The Director ensures partner arrangements deliver measurable value, are well governed and align with RESL strategy, risk appetite and regulatory expectations. As a player-coach, the Director stays close to the work and leads automation and process improvements. The Director partners across Product, Sales, Sales Enablement, Marketing, Operations, Underwriting, Credit, Procurement, Finance, Treasury, Risk, Compliance and Legal, and develops a team that delivers high-quality partner, Broker and Advisor outcomes.

 Position Responsibilities: 

 Partnerships Strategy & Relationship Ownership (30%)

 Lead the RESL strategic partnerships strategy, defining the role, objectives and priorities with key partners across the RESL value chain, including First National, the national mortgage insurers, FCT and FNF.
 Serve as key owner of RESL partner relationships, with day-to-day management through the Manager, Strategic Partnerships, and define the engagement model.
 Develop joint roadmaps with strategic partners that align to product, channel and growth priorities, and track delivery against agreed milestones and outcomes.
 Identify, evaluate and recommend new partnerships and changes to existing arrangements where value, risk or fit warrants.
 Represent RESL in partner governance and cross-functional forums; partner with Product Policy, Risk and Compliance on regulatory and policy updates.

 Vendor Governance, SLAs & Commercials (20%)

 Establish vendor governance frameworks (performance reviews, scorecards, issue management, escalation paths), monitor performance against SLAs, benchmarks and commercial commitments, and drive remediation.
 With Procurement, support negotiation and renewal of commercial terms and SLAs, so pricing, fees and service levels deliver measurable value.
 Oversee contract, invoice and renewal management, hands-on where needed, to keep arrangements approved, accurate and aligned to commercials.
 Partner with Legal, Risk, Compliance, Finance and Treasury to ensure partner arrangements meet contractual, regulatory and third-party risk requirements.

 Partner Rewards (30%)

 Lead the Partner Rewards program for Brokers and Advisors, including recognition, and incentives, and supporting product teams on related analysis and execution.
 Align rewards to Bank and RESL channel strategy, growth objectives and the Advisor and Broker value proposition, and review performance, cost and outcomes.
 Support Broker and Advisor compensation discussions, including accuracy, transparency and governance, with Sales, Finance and Operations.
 Maintain strong controls over program administration, eligibility, tracking and reporting, and support resolution of escalated Broker and Advisor issues.

 Strategic Initiatives, Process Efficiency & Executive Reporting (10%)

 Lead strategic initiatives related to Partnerships, Rewards, CX and support reporting activities, such as CX reporting, Monthly Business Reviews and Product Offsites.
 Develop and present executive-ready reporting, business cases and insights on partnerships, vendors, rewards and market trends for business, Board and leadership reviews.
 Identify efficiencies within and beyond the team, and lead automation and process improvements (e.g., workflow, reporting and data automation) across partnerships, governance, rewards and reporting to reduce manual effort and improve controls, accuracy and scalability.
 Identify partner, Broker and Advisor customer experience (CX) opportunities and irritants, and drive resolution with partners and internal teams.
 Support the Head of Product in planning and executing business priorities and RESL transformation.

 Leadership, Stakeholder Collaboration & Governance (10%)

 Lead by example and develop the team, setting goals, coaching and establishing succession plan; Ensure coverage, documentation and continuity across partner relationships and program administration to reduce key-person risk.
 Lead cross-enterprise initiatives through influence, partnering with Legal, Risk, Compliance, Finance and Treasury to ensure partner arrangements and rewards programs meet contractual, regulatory and financial requirements.
 Represent the Partnerships and Partner Rewards perspective in cross-functional forums, and partner with Risk and Compliance on regulatory and policy updates.
 Demonstrate inclusive behaviours and foster a culture of accountability, collaboration and continuous development.

 Required Qualifications: 

 Strategic thinker and hands-on executor with 10-12+ years in Partnerships, Product Management or Vendor Management; RESL and mortgage experience strongly preferred, and mortgage partner ecosystem knowledge a significant asset.
 Proven experience owning strategic partner or vendor relationships, including governance, joint roadmaps, SLAs and commercial negotiations.
 Good understanding of Advisor and Broker channels, sales practices, and compensation and rewards programs in banking.
 Strong financial acumen to assess commercial terms, program costs and partner economics, with working knowledge of third-party and vendor risk management in a regulated financial institution.
 Player-coach leader who develops managers and specialists, leads by example and personally delivers in key areas such as negotiation, analysis and building materials, while maintaining strategic oversight.
 Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, building relationships at all levels, including senior executives and external partners, and developing compelling, executive-ready business cases with strong storytelling that influence cross-functional decisions.
 Strong planning and execution skills with end-to-end process orientation, managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
 Track record of delivering efficiencies, process improvement or automation that reduces manual effort and improves controls and scalability.
 University degree in Business, Finance, Marketing or a related field (MBA preferred).

 Preferred Qualifications: 

 Bilingualism (English and French) is an asset. If the successful candidate is in Québec, proficiency in both languages will be required to support clients from various provinces outside of Quebec.
 Experience with Broker or Advisor rewards, recognition, incentive or compensation programs.

 When you join our team: 

 We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want.

jobs.description:
Our Story & Purpose:

We’re Vancity, a member-owned credit union built on the principles of inclusion and social justice. Since 1946, our relentless commitment to these values has helped us challenge the status quo and break down barriers. We’ve made bold commitments to become net-zero by 2040 across all mortgages and loans, and we’re actively pursuing strategies in Indigenous banking and financial resilience for our members.
As the largest private sector Living Wage Employer in Canada, we’re proud to be consistently recognized as one of the country’s Top Employers. If you’re ready to join our team of 2,700 diverse individuals, access competitive rewards and benefits, and be part of a greater movement - apply today!

Your Role in Supporting Our Members:

As the Director, Enterprise Architecture
, you will provide strategic and people leadership for Vancity’s architecture practice, shaping the technology architecture required to deliver our business and technology strategies. You will lead and develop a team of architects responsible for defining scalable, resilient, secure, and future-ready solutions across the organization, while establishing architectural direction, standards, governance, and practices that ensure technology investments align with Vancity’s long-term business priorities. You will work closely with senior technology and business leaders to translate strategy into technology roadmaps, guide major transformation initiatives, and ensure architectural decisions balance innovation, sustainability, risk, scalability, and business value. As a people leader, you will build capability within the architecture team, establish clear accountabilities and expectations, coach and develop team members, and foster a collaborative and high-performing architecture practice.
This is a Full-time, Permanent
role and will report directly to the Senior Director, Enterprise Architecture and Transformation.
This role will enjoy hybrid working arrangements which can be fulfilled primarily from the Vancity head office location and your Lower Mainland based home office or Toronto home based office. Vancouver-based candidates may be expected to come into office at least once per week.

How You'll Make an Impact:

Leading
, coaching, and developing a team of architects, providing clear direction, performance expectations, career development, and opportunities to strengthen technical and leadership capabilities

Providing
strategic leadership and architectural direction for key business and technology initiatives, ensuring solutions align with Vancity’s enterprise strategy and long-term technology vision

Defining
, building, and maintaining architecture standards, principles, patterns, guardrails, and best practices, while establishing effective architecture governance and decision-making practices across the organization

Partnering
with senior business and technology leaders to understand business drivers, capabilities, and strategic priorities and translating them into technology strategies, roadmaps, and architectural outcomes

Providing
leadership and direction to solution, data, security, infrastructure, and other architecture disciplines, ensuring architectural decisions are aligned across the technology ecosystem

Guiding
product owners, engineering leaders, architects, designers, and developers in making sound architecture choices, including Buy vs. Build, cloud adoption, integration patterns, and real-time vs. batch solutions

Overseeing
the design and implementation of solutions across business applications and technologies based on enterprise strategy, business capabilities, security requirements, and technology standards

Providing
leadership and architectural oversight for significant transformation programs and complex technology initiatives, identifying cross-functional dependencies, risks, opportunities, and architectural considerations

Monitoring
the current-state technology portfolio and establishing roadmaps to address technical debt, aging technologies, regulatory requirements, architectural deficiencies, and misalignment with evolving business requirements

Evaluating
emerging technologies, including AI, automation, cloud platforms, modern engineering practices, fintech trends, vendor capabilities, and market changes to determine how they can responsibly enable new business capabilities and operating models

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or equivalent practical experience

10+ years of progressive technology experience, including significant experience in solution and enterprise architecture, ideally within financial services or banking environments

Demonstrated experience leading, managing, coaching, and developing architecture or senior technology teams, with accountability for performance, capability development, and delivery

Current expertise in AI, including AI-enabled architecture, AI governance, and AI spec-driven development, combined with broad knowledge of software architecture, application development, data, security, infrastructure, cloud computing, automation, and modern engineering practices

Experience establishing or maturing an architecture practice, including architecture governance, standards, principles, roadmaps, and decision-making frameworks

Strong experience influencing senior executives and business leaders and translating business strategy into technology strategy and architectural direction

Experience with cloud architecture, preferably Microsoft Azure, along with in-depth knowledge of integration patterns, APIs, microservices, event-driven architectures, and modern application architecture

Strong people leadership, communication, analytical, strategic thinking, and problem-solving capabilities, with the ability to create clarity, build alignment, navigate competing priorities, and provide direction in complex or ambiguous environments

Extra Skills That Set You Apart:

Experience with modern core banking systems and a strong understanding of the banking and fintech technology landscape

Strong knowledge of enterprise architecture frameworks and methodologies, such as TOGAF, and the ability to apply architecture practices pragmatically within a complex organization

Familiarity with Agile and modern product and software development practices and experience partnering with product and engineering leaders

You’ll Thrive Here If You Are:

A people leader who builds strong teams
- You set clear expectations, coach and develop others, create accountability, and build an environment where experienced technology professionals can do their best work.

A big-picture technology strategist
- You can translate complex business strategies into practical, scalable enterprise architectures and long-term technology roadmaps.

A trusted leader and collaborator
- You can influence senior leaders, bring together different perspectives, and provide clear direction when architectural decisions involve competing priorities or trade-offs.

Fluent in both business and technology
- You connect business drivers, member outcomes, capabilities, risk, and strategy to architectural and investment decisions.

Comfortable leading through complexity and change
- You can provide clarity in ambiguous environments while helping your team and stakeholders navigate transformation, emerging technologies, and evolving business priorities.

We value lived experience, so if you are interested in this role, we encourage you to apply even if you feel your skills don't perfectly align with those listed.

What You’ll Earn:

This role offers a salary range of $180,000 to $200,000 per annum
. The base pay offered may vary depending on factors such as relevant qualifications, skills, previous experience, and internal equity. As part of our total rewards package, employees may also be eligible for our annual incentive program, subject to program eligibility requirements.

Why You’ll Love Working Here:

A career at Vancity is more than just a job, you’re joining a tradition of change-makers who are creating lasting change for our communities. Beyond base pay, we offer a comprehensive total rewards package to ensure our employees are empowered to thrive:
Living Wage Employer
: We’re the largest private-sector Living Wage Employer in Canada and consistently ranked among Canada’s Top Employers.

Customizable Benefits
: Permanent employees receive flexible benefit packages that can be tailored annually to meet evolving needs.

Generous Vacation
: New employees start with 3-4 weeks of vacation per year, with additional days earned over time.

Extra Stat Holidays
: In addition to BC’s 11 statutory holidays, we offer 2 extra days, plus care days for personal or family illness.

Immediate Health Coverage
: Health and dental benefits begin on your hire date, with three levels of coverage to choose from.

Defined Benefit Pension
: Our retirement plan provides a guaranteed income for life, recognizing that retirement looks different for everyone.

Vancity Talent Programs:

Any information you choose to share will be stored securely and used only for recruitment and career development connected to this initiative, in line with the BC Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA). For details, please see our dedicated Talent Programs job posting.
This role is an open vacancy, and our hiring process is grounded in fairness, transparency, and inclusion. We are committed to an inclusive, barrier-free and accessible recruitment experience for all candidates. If you require any accommodations or support at any stage of the recruitment process (including the application stage), we encourage you to let us know by contacting our Talent Acquisition team at recruitment@vancity.com. jobs.description:
Harlo Entertainment owns and operates some of Toronto's most beloved hospitality and entertainment brands. The portfolio includes Shake Shack Canada, Mimi Chinese, Sunnys Chinese, Linny's, Kasa Moto, Shinji Japanese and Playbook Commons, alongside Valerie and Roses Social — the celebrated outlets at Hotel X Toronto. Each Harlo brand is distinctively crafted, and each is united by a shared commitment to warm, engaging hospitality and curated guest experiences that keep people coming back. From conceptualization to creation, Harlo takes a value-oriented approach — pairing creative vision with operational discipline to drive performance, growth, and lasting brand equity across the hospitality, entertainment, lifestyle, and technology industries.

Check out our website to learn more: www.harloentertainment.com

We are a people first culture. We strive to create great outcomes and to establish win-win partnerships through integrity, reliability, inclusivity, and great communication. Our greatest asset is our people, as they are the powerhouse behind our outcomes.

We always bring our best. We hold ourselves accountable for over-delivering on a consistent basis. We take responsibility for the outcome of our work. We find a way to make it possible. We are in the business of storytelling and remarkable experiences to create moments that matter. We ooze passion and pride in everything we do. We are relentless, driven and proud. We dig deep, we get our hands dirty. There is no challenge is too big or too small for our team.

Harlo Entertainment is looking for a highly motivated individual to join our exciting, fast-paced team as a Chief Financial Officer.

Chief Financial Officer (CFO)

As a the CFO you will act as a proactive business partner and trusted advisor to the Managing Partner, providing financial leadership and insight across the organization. The CFO is responsible for financial reporting, FP&A, banking relationships and financing, and supports the business's supply chain and brand licensing activities to drive profitable, sustainable growth.

Strategic Business Partnership:

· Bring forward insights, risks and opportunities before they are asked for.
· Translate financial and operational data into clear recommendations that support investment, pricing, growth and resource allocation decisions.
· Collaborate with the executive team to develop and implement the company's long-term strategic and financial plan.
· Lead financial evaluation of new projects, brands, ventures and acquisitions, including business cases, valuation and return analysis.
· Support the creation of new companies, including working with external counsel on organizational documents, working with the Managing Partner on accurate setup of cap tables, and managing execution of shareholder agreements.

Financial Reporting & Controls:

· Own the monthly, quarterly and annual close and deliver accurate, timely financial statements across all entities.
· Prepare consolidated reporting and management dashboards for the Managing Partner, shareholders and lenders.
· Establish and maintain strong internal controls, accounting policies and approval processes.
· Manage the annual audit or review process and relationships with external accountants and auditors.
· Oversee corporate tax planning and compliance (including HST and income tax) in partnership with external advisors.

Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A):

· Lead the annual budgeting process and rolling forecasts by company, brand and project.
· Analyze performance against budget and forecast, clearly explaining variances and recommending corrective action.
· Build and maintain financial models to support scenario planning, pricing and capital allocation decisions.
· Define and track key performance indicators, including margin, working capital and brand-level profitability.

Supply Chain:

· Partner with operations on supply chain planning, including inventory management, product costing and landed cost analysis.
· Support supplier and manufacturer negotiations, payment terms and contract review.
· Monitor inventory levels, turnover and working capital, and identify opportunities to reduce cost and improve cash flow.
· Assess and mitigate supply chain risks, including foreign exchange, tariffs, duties and freight costs.

Brand Licensing:

· Support the structuring, negotiation and financial evaluation of licensing agreements for Harlo's brands, both in-bound and out-bound.
· Oversee royalty tracking, reporting, audits and collections to ensure licensing income is accurately recorded and received.
· Work with the Managing Partner and external counsel to ensure IP and trademarks are applied for, protected and renewed, as appropriate.
· Evaluate new licensing opportunities and partners, including revenue projections, minimum guarantees and risk.

Banking Relationships & Financing:

· Serve as the primary point of contact for banking partners, lenders and financial institutions.
· Manage cash flow forecasting, treasury and liquidity to ensure the business is funded to meet its commitments and growth plans.
· Lead debt and equity financing initiatives, including credit facilities, refinancing, and investor or lender presentations.
· Ensure compliance with loan covenants and lender reporting requirements.
· Oversee insurance coverage and financial risk management.

Team Leadership:

· Lead, mentor and develop the finance and accounting team, ensuring they have the skills and resources to deliver.
· Continuously improve finance systems, processes and tools to build a scalable finance function.
· Foster a culture of accountability, accuracy and continuous improvement.

What you’ll need
Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance; MBA an asset
CPA designation
10+ years of progressive finance experience, including a minimum of 3 years at a national accounting firm and 5+ years in a senior finance leadership role (CFO, VP Finance or Controller)
Proven track record managing banking relationships and leading debt and/or equity financing
Experience in FP&A, including budgeting, forecasting and financial modelling to support strategic decisions
Experience with supply chain finance, inventory and product costing; exposure to brand licensing and royalty management an asset
Experience building internal controls and scalable financial processes across multiple entities
Strong knowledge of accounting systems, including Push Operations, Sage Intacct and ERP systems
Advanced proficiency in Excel and financial modelling
Proactive, curious self-starter who brings forward insights and recommendations, with the ability to prioritize in a fast-paced environment
Persistent in meeting reporting deadlines, with the ability to drive results from internal teams and external partners
Collaborative leader with experience building and mentoring finance teams
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present financial information clearly to the Managing Partner, lenders and investors
Exceptional attention to detail and a high standard of accuracy

What We Offer
· Competitive compensation, including comprehensive benefits, spending account and professional development program.
· Opportunity to develop skills and gain experience in multiple disciplines in a fast-paced environment.
· Dynamic and fun office culture with colleagues who share the same core values.
· Exclusive perks from our portfolio companies.
· Unlimited vacation policy.

Equal Opportunity Employer

jobs.title: Head of Business Services
jobs.description:
Madison Taylor Design is a leading multidisciplinary design firm providing architectural, landscape architecture, interior design, furniture & decorating, project management, and construction services for clients in the residential, commercial, and hospitality sectors. Our mission is to deliver high-end design solutions that blend inspiration from nature with modern and sustainable materials.

At the heart of Madison Taylor Design is our people and the experience we create together. Our core values are the backbone of how we work, lead, collaborate, and make decisions — we believe exceptional work comes from exceptional teams, built on strong culture, clear expectations, trust, and accountability. We run on the Entrepreneurial Operating System (EOS®) to create clarity, accountability, and alignment as we scale.

Summary

We are seeking a Head of Business Services to run the business side of Madison Taylor Design: finance operations, human resources administration, insurance and benefits, IT and systems, and the office. This is the seat that keeps the firm running smoothly behind the design and construction work.

As a member of our leadership team, reporting to the Integrator, you will lead our full-charge bookkeeper and administrative team.

You will oversee the monthly close and billing, prepare our monthly financial reporting, and work alongside the Integrator and our external financial advisors on forecasting and bank reporting. On the people side, you will be the first point of contact for employees and manage HR administration with the support of our outsourced HR partner.

This is a hands-on leadership role for a strong generalist: someone who is comfortable with numbers, trusted with people, and organized enough to keep many moving parts on track. Our core finance and HR processes are documented, so you’ll have a clear starting point and support as you learn our business.
Reports to: Integrator

Location: Midhurst, ON — on-site, reliably commute or plan to relocate before starting work (required)
Employment Type: Full-time, permanent
Compensation: $85,000–$100,000 annually, commensurate with experience, plus a quarterly performance bonus and profit share
Benefits: Dental care, Extended health care, Life insurance
Language: English (required)
Application Deadline: Hiring now — applications reviewed on a rolling basis

Key Responsibilities

Finance operations

Oversee the bookkeeper’s monthly close, reconciliations, and client billing, reviewing for accuracy before sign-off.
Prepare the monthly financial package for the Integrator and our external financial advisor, including division results for design, construction, and furniture.
Support the annual budget, forecast, and cash-flow planning, and prepare information for bank reporting.
Oversee payroll, HST and source deductions, and year-end coordination with our external accountants.
Monitor receivables and cash, and keep approval processes and financial controls in place.

People & human resources

Serve as the first point of contact for employee questions and concerns, handling them fairly, promptly, and confidentially.
Manage HR administration: onboarding, employment agreements, records, benefits enrolment, and compliance with Ontario employment legislation.
Coordinate recruitment and the firm-wide performance review process in partnership with department heads.
Support employee relations and workplace matters, engaging the Integrator or our outsourced HR advisor as appropriate.
Work with our outsourced HR partner to keep employment contracts, policies, and the employee handbook current.

Operations, legal & systems

Manage the company’s insurance program and employee benefits plan, including renewals, coverage, and claims.
Serve as the main contact with our legal counsel: coordinate contract reviews (client, vendor, and trade agreements, leases and employment matters), collections and disputes, and keep corporate records, annual filings, and a register of key contracts and renewal dates current.
Own office operations, IT, and software accounts (QuickBooks Online, Teamwork, Monday.com, Buildertrend, and others), and key vendor relationships.
Find practical ways to reduce administrative work through technology, automation, and AI.

Leadership

Lead, mentor, and develop the full-charge bookkeeper and administrative team, with clear expectations and accountability.
Participate actively in the leadership team, maintaining Scorecards and Rocks and contributing to weekly Level 10 Meetings through EOS®.

What You Bring

5+ years as a business, office, or operations manager with responsibility for finance and administration.
3+ years leading a small team, delegating well while keeping accountability.
Hands-on experience overseeing month-end, reconciliations, payroll, and billing in QuickBooks Online or similar.
The ability to read a profit and loss statement and balance sheet and spot an error in someone else’s work.
Experience as the first point of contact for employee relations, HR administration, and benefits, and working knowledge of Ontario employment standards.
Comfort with technology and software administration; strong Excel or Google Sheets skills.
An accounting diploma or degree, CPA progress, or HR training (CHRP/CHRL) is an asset.
Experience with an outsourced HR provider, group benefits, business insurance renewals, and working with legal counsel on contracts is an asset.
Experience in architecture, design, construction, or another project-based business is an asset.
Experience with EOS® is a significant asset.
Discretion, sound judgment, and a calm, organized approach.

Why Join Us?

Run the business side of a growing, 35-person multidisciplinary design and build firm.
Be part of a collaborative leadership team with real responsibility and decision-making authority.
Help shape the systems and processes that support our next stage of growth.
Work alongside talented designers, architects, and builders creating high-end homes across Ontario cottage country.
Competitive base salary, quarterly performance bonus, profit share, and benefits.

Please submit your resume and a brief cover letter, including an example of a process you built or improved in finance, HR, or operations, and the difference it made.

jobs.title: Director, Corporate Accounting
jobs.description:
Behind successful real estate developments is a strong accounting function that brings financial clarity, accountability, and insight to every stage of a project. A growing organization is looking for an experienced Director of Accounting
to oversee corporate and development accounting while helping strengthen financial operations across the business.

This opportunity is suited to a hands-on finance leader who enjoys solving complex accounting challenges, developing high-performing teams, and partnering with business leaders to support financial and operational decisions.

About the Role

Working directly with the Chief Financial Officer, the Director of Accounting will lead financial reporting and accounting activities across multiple business entities and development projects.

The position offers a combination of technical accounting oversight, operational leadership, and strategic involvement. You will be responsible for maintaining reliable financial information, guiding accounting professionals, and ensuring financial processes effectively support business activities.

Beyond managing daily operations, you will collaborate with leadership and project teams to improve reporting practices, strengthen financial controls, and identify opportunities to make the accounting function more efficient.

What You’ll Do

Direct accounting and financial reporting activities for multiple corporate entities, development projects, and related business operations.

Take ownership of monthly, quarterly, and annual closing processes, ensuring reporting is accurate and delivered on schedule.

Evaluate financial statements, accounting entries, reconciliations, accruals, and adjustments before final reporting.

Maintain oversight of intercompany transactions, consolidated reporting, and complex accounting matters.

Apply IFRS and ASPE requirements to ensure consistent and appropriate financial reporting.

Address technical accounting issues involving project expenditures, revenue recognition, financing transactions, and cost allocations.

Guide development accounting activities, including construction costs, work-in-progress, project commitments, and expense tracking.

Assess project financial performance by reviewing budgets, actual expenditures, cost variances, and supporting records.

Monitor development funding, cash requirements, and outstanding financial commitments to help maintain effective project controls.

Review lender draw submissions, financing documentation, and project-related financial schedules.

Coordinate year-end audits, manage accounting documentation, and work with external auditors to resolve reporting matters.

Partner with internal teams and external advisors on tax reporting, compliance, and financial matters affecting business entities.

Prepare and oversee budgets, financial projections, and performance analyses for corporate operations and development activities.

Interpret financial results and recommend practical solutions to address cost pressures and improve profitability.

Work alongside construction, development, and operational leaders to ensure financial information supports project planning and execution.

Build and develop a capable accounting team through coaching, clear expectations, and ongoing performance management.

Review existing accounting practices and introduce stronger controls, consistent procedures, and more effective reporting methods.

Identify opportunities to simplify workflows, enhance accounting technology, and reduce manual processes.

Provide financial expertise to executive leadership on business initiatives, organizational changes, and financing activities.

What You Bring

CPA designation required.

At least 7 years of progressive experience in accounting and financial reporting, with a minimum of 5 years leading or supervising accounting teams.

Proven experience in real estate development, construction, property development, or a comparable industry.

Comprehensive understanding of IFRS and ASPE, including financial statement preparation and period-end reporting.

Practical knowledge of development accounting, project cost management, construction-in-progress, and budget oversight.

Strong experience with general ledger management, account reconciliations, intercompany accounting, and financial consolidations.

Ability to oversee accounting responsibilities involving multiple entities and concurrent development projects.

Familiarity with project financing, lender requirements, construction draws, and development-related financial reporting.

Experience managing external audit requirements, internal accounting controls, and financial compliance.

Strong capabilities in financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, and evaluating project performance.

Advanced Excel skills and experience working with ERP systems and financial reporting applications.

Demonstrated success managing, mentoring, and developing accounting professionals.

Experience enhancing financial procedures, introducing reporting improvements, or supporting accounting system upgrades.

Sound analytical judgment and the ability to resolve complicated accounting and operational issues.

Strong communication skills, with the confidence to explain financial information to executives, operational teams, and external partners.

Ability to balance competing deadlines, oversee several priorities, and maintain accuracy in a busy environment.

A supportive, people-focused leadership approach with a commitment to teamwork, accountability, and continuous improvement.

Why Join

Take the next step in your accounting leadership career with an organization that offers the opportunity to influence both financial operations and business performance. This role provides direct collaboration with senior executives, involvement in a variety of development projects, and the ability to shape accounting practices while building a strong team. You'll be part of an entrepreneurial and collaborative workplace that values new ideas, professional growth, and individual contributions. The organization also offers competitive benefits, retirement savings support, professional development, and potential performance-based incentives, making this an opportunity to grow your leadership experience while contributing to the organization's continued success.

jobs.title: Managing Director
jobs.description:
Summit Search Group has been retained by a well-established Architecture and Urban Planning Firm in Winnipeg on the recruitment of a Managing Director. The firm has earned a strong reputation across the region for the quality of its design work and the depth of its relationships with public and private clients. Its portfolio ranges from private residential commissions to large-scale public landscapes, and includes parks, trails, and open space projects, municipal planning and policy work, and community engagement programs for major institutional clients.

The practice is home to a technically gifted, close-knit team of senior designers and planners who care deeply about their craft and about the communities they serve. Demand for the firm’s work is steady, its reputation is excellent, and its people are proud of what they build. The organization now looks to formalize how it is led and to bring dedicated business leadership to a practice whose creative strength has always been its foundation.

The Opportunity

This is the senior-most role in the practice, and a rare one in the Winnipeg market. The Managing Director takes full ownership of the firm as a business, with real autonomy over direction, structure, and results, and complete accountability for profit and loss. Where leaders at larger national firms often run a department within a corporate structure, this role runs the whole enterprise, shaping its strategy, its culture, and its next generation of leaders.

The incoming leader will work alongside a talented group of principals and design professionals, earning their confidence, strengthening how decisions get made, and bringing greater commercial discipline to how projects are scoped, priced, tracked, and delivered. There is meaningful design work ahead: shaping the firm’s organizational structure in partnership with the team, putting a newly developed strategic plan into motion, and building a clear path for emerging leaders. A thoughtful ramp-up is built in, so the right person can learn the business and build relationships before the real work begins. This role is based in the Winnipeg office, five days a week, with periodic travel to a satellite location.

Key Responsibilities

Run the practice as a self-directed business, setting priorities, owning financial results, and reporting at a high level to ownership on a quarterly basis.
Lead, coach, and develop a group of senior principals, fostering alignment and shared accountability, addressing difficult conversations directly and respectfully, and cultivating the next generation of firm leadership.
Take over the full range of people leadership, including compensation reviews, performance conversations, workforce planning, and the retention and engagement of a talented professional team.
Instill financial discipline across the practice, including utilization and chargeability, project pricing and margins, and rigorous tracking of scope and change, so that decisions are guided by sound numbers as well as sound design judgment.
Co-design the firm’s organizational structure with the leadership team, and lead execution of the new strategic plan across the practice.
Support senior-level business development alongside the principals who lead client relationships, represent the firm in the community, and provide a light-touch, growth-minded presence for the satellite office.

Qualifications

A background in architecture, engineering, landscape architecture, planning, land development, or a closely related design and consulting field, with enough depth in the industry to earn the respect of senior technical professionals.
A proven record of building teams and leading collaboratively, paired with the confidence to set direction and make decisions when the situation calls for it.
Demonstrated comfort with hard conversations and conflict resolution, with the interpersonal maturity to guide experienced, long-tenured professionals through change.
Strong business and financial acumen, including hands-on experience with P&L ownership, utilization, project pricing, and margin management in a project-based professional services environment.
The ability to win work, build relationships with clients and partners, and represent the firm credibly within the Winnipeg business and design community.
Winnipeg-based, with the ability to work on site five days a week; leaders currently running practices at larger firms who are seeking genuine autonomy are encouraged to apply.

For more information or to submit your resume, please reach out to Matt Erhard at Summit Search Group, matt.erhard@summitsearchgroup.com .

Summit Search Group has a strong commitment to Diversity, Equality and Inclusion. We strive for continuous development, modeling inclusive behaviors and proactively managing bias throughout our process.

We don’t flip companies; we keep them, invest in them, and rebuild them around AI, while our Venture Lab launches new AI-native products into the same markets. Named to the Inc. 5000 list of America’s Fastest-Growing Private Companies and an 8x Top Workplaces award winner, Embrace brings together top talent from around the world to build lasting products, own real outcomes, and grow with a company that plays the long game.

Job Description

This is a remote position.

Role Overview

This is an opportunity to work directly with the CEO of Embrace as Chief of Staff, leading strategic and high-impact operational projects across the portfolio, from growing and optimising businesses to strategy. You will work closely with portfolio company CEOs and the Operating Leaders across our industry groups.

Core Mandate

Partner with the CEO on strategic and high-impact operational priorities
Grow and optimize portfolio companies, applying and building Embrace's value creation playbooks
Scale AI and operating best practices across the portfolio for measurable ROI
Build the experience to take on senior leadership in the portfolio

Key Responsibilities

1. Grow & Optimize

Lead growth work with portfolio CEOs on pricing, go-to-market, and retention.
Diagnose underperformance and reset cost structure, organization, and cash flow.
Use AI and data to sharpen diagnostics on churn risk, pricing, and cost benchmarks.
Set clear KPIs for each initiative and turn what works into repeatable playbooks.

2. Portfolio Operations & AI Transformation

Set a consistent operating cadence and KPI dashboards across the portfolio.
Drive end-to-end AI automation across product, services, and internal workflows.
Prioritize AI use cases by ROI, track adoption, and build AI fluency across teams.

3. Strategy & Office of the CEO

Support corporate strategy, annual planning, and board and investor materials.
Run the leadership team's operating rhythm and lead special projects for the CEO.

4. Change Management

Lead the people side of transformation, including restructurings, leadership transitions, underperformance, and resistance to change.
Handle difficult conversations with fairness, discretion, and maturity.
Build trust with portfolio CEOs, Operating Leaders, and functional leaders.

How You'll Spend Your Time

Operations, including growth, optimization, and portfolio performance (~80%); strategy and the Office of the CEO (~20%).

Path to Leadership

You will work closely with the CEO and be mentored by Embrace's Operating Leaders. High performers will have the opportunity to move into senior leadership roles across the portfolio, with the long-term goal of leading an Embrace company as CEO.

What Success Looks Like (18–24 Months)

Measurable revenue growth and EBITDA improvement in the companies you support.
AI live in core workflows, with measurable productivity and ROI gains.
Growth and productivity playbooks driven hands-on at portfolio companies.
Short feedback loops and fast iteration on every initiative.
Change led while keeping key talent and the trust of teams and customers.
Ready to take on a senior leadership role in the portfolio.

Requirements

Ideal Candidate Profile

8+ years of progressive experience across operating roles, management consulting, or private equity operations, including hands-on operating leadership roles.
Grew and improved software/SaaS businesses, ideally with P&L or departmental-level ownership.
Proven experience managing difficult people situations during transformations and restructuring, with the maturity and presence to earn trust through change.
Strong analytical and financial skills: P&Ls, models, and business cases.
Applied AI and automation to business workflows, with measurable results.
A long-term ambition to run a company. An MBA from a top program is a plus.

Nice to Have

Industry experience in financial services, healthcare, legal, or manufacturing.
Buy-and-hold software acquirer, holdco, start-up, Series A/B scale-up, or PE-backed experience is a strong asset.

Benefits

Base salary plus attractive bonuses.
Medical, dental and vision; 401(k)/RRSP with employer match; paid time off, sick leave and holidays; job-related tuition reimbursement.
Room to grow as the team scales — this organization is being built now, and early top performers grow with it.
