jobs.title: Interim Director, Procurement
jobs.description:
IMMEDIATE INTERIM OPPORTUNITY

Interim Director, Procurement

Reports to: Associate Vice-President, Finance

Location: Virtual

Duration: 6 Months

Our client, a large and complex Canadian academic institution, is seeking an experienced Interim Director, Procurement for an initial six-month mandate.

The organization is looking for a seasoned procurement leader who can provide strong operational leadership while bringing the experience, perspective and confidence to challenge existing thinking, act as a positive disruptor and elevate the overall value, impact and reputation of Procurement across the institution.

Reporting to the Associate Vice-President, Finance and leading a team of five, the Interim Director will ensure the continued effective operation of the procurement function while helping the organization consider how Procurement can become a more strategic, progressive and value-adding partner to the broader institution.

The successful interim will bring credibility as both an experienced procurement operator and strategic advisor. They will engage and develop the existing team, build stronger relationships with internal stakeholders, challenge established practices where appropriate, and identify opportunities to improve processes, technology, supplier management, organizational risk and financial value.

THE MANDATE

The Interim Director will assume leadership of the procurement function and provide stability, direction and mentorship to the team through a period of transition.

A significant component of the mandate will be to examine how Procurement is positioned and experienced across the organization. The Interim Director will work closely with stakeholders to demystify procurement, simplify how internal clients navigate centralized procurement and build greater understanding of the value that an effective procurement function can bring to the institution.

This is not simply about maintaining the existing procurement operation. The Interim Director will be expected to challenge current approaches, identify opportunities for improvement and leave the function stronger, more professional and better positioned for the future.

KEY PRIORITIES

Operational Leadership and Team Development

Provide hands-on leadership and oversight of the procurement function and its team of five.
Ensure continuity and effective delivery of procurement activities throughout the six-month transition.
Engage, coach and support team members, bringing additional procurement expertise, knowledge and external perspective into the function.
Assess current capabilities, ways of working and opportunities to strengthen the effectiveness and professionalism of the team.
Create clarity around priorities, accountability and service expectations.

Strategic Procurement Leadership

Assess the current procurement operating model and identify opportunities to elevate Procurement from primarily a transactional function to a more strategic enterprise partner.
Develop or refine the procurement strategy and establish clear priorities for improving value, service, governance and organizational impact.
Challenge existing practices and conventional thinking, bringing external best practices and practical ideas from other large, complex organizations.
Identify opportunities to generate measurable financial and non-financial value through improved sourcing, vendor management, demand management and procurement practices.

Stakeholder Engagement and Procurement Brand

Build strong relationships across a complex academic and administrative stakeholder environment.
Improve stakeholders’ understanding of when, why and how Procurement should be engaged.
Demystify procurement policies and processes and make the function easier to navigate for internal clients.
Strengthen the internal brand and credibility of Procurement by positioning the team as pragmatic business partners rather than simply a control or compliance function.
Educate stakeholders on procurement responsibilities, processes, policies and the value of early Procurement involvement.

Policy, Process and Governance

Review existing procurement policies, procedures and governance structures and identify opportunities for modernization and simplification.
Establish clearer, more user-friendly processes that balance strong governance and risk management with an effective stakeholder experience.
Identify unnecessary complexity, duplication or friction within existing procurement processes.
Strengthen transparency, consistency and accountability across procurement decision-making.

Technology and Procurement Enablement

Review how technology is currently being leveraged across the procurement function and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, visibility and user experience.
Review the institution’s current purchase card program, associated technology and vendor arrangements and identify opportunities to improve functionality, controls, adoption and organizational value.
Assess whether existing procurement technology and processes are delivering sufficient value and identify opportunities for improvement or modernization.
Consider how automation, analytics and emerging technologies could enable a more efficient and insight-driven procurement function.

Strategic Sourcing and Collaboration

Review key supplier relationships and sourcing strategies to identify opportunities to generate additional savings and organizational value.
Explore collaborative procurement and group-buying opportunities with universities and other broader public sector organizations across Canada.
Identify areas where increased purchasing leverage, category management or consolidated sourcing could deliver improved commercial outcomes.
Bring an external market perspective on procurement models, technologies, supplier strategies and emerging practices.

Risk and Supply Chain Transparency

Assess procurement and supply-chain risks across the institution and identify areas where governance, visibility or controls could be strengthened.
Improve transparency across key supplier relationships, contractual commitments and supply-chain dependencies.
Consider emerging risks related to supplier concentration, continuity of supply, compliance, cybersecurity, sustainability and broader geopolitical or economic disruption.
Ensure procurement decisions appropriately balance financial value, service, risk and institutional requirements.

IDEAL EXPERIENCE

The successful interim will be a seasoned procurement executive who has previously led procurement within a large, complex and highly stakeholder-driven organization.

Significant senior procurement leadership experience, ideally 15+ years across progressively responsible procurement, strategic sourcing and supply-chain roles.
Previous experience leading a procurement function within a university, college, healthcare organization, government entity, Crown corporation or another broader public sector organization.
A strong understanding of public-sector procurement principles, governance, competitive procurement, accountability and transparency.
Demonstrated success developing and implementing procurement strategies that have delivered measurable savings, value creation and service improvement.
Experience transforming or elevating a procurement function beyond transactional execution toward a more strategic business-partner model.
Strong experience with procurement technology, e-procurement, purchase cards, spend analytics and technology-enabled process improvement.
Experience evaluating vendors, commercial arrangements and procurement platforms and challenging whether existing solutions continue to provide appropriate value.
Demonstrated ability to review and improve procurement policies, processes and governance without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.
Strong strategic sourcing, contract negotiation and supplier management experience.
Experience exploring collaborative procurement, consortium purchasing or group-buying arrangements would be highly valuable.
A track record of strengthening procurement teams through coaching, knowledge transfer, capability development and improved ways of working.
Exceptional stakeholder engagement skills with an ability to influence senior leaders and build credibility across decentralized and complex environments.
Experience working effectively in environments where stakeholder education, relationship building and change management are critical to improving the adoption of centralized procurement.

LEADERSHIP PROFILE

This mandate will suit a senior procurement leader who combines practical operational capability with strategic perspective.

They will be comfortable getting close enough to the work to understand what is happening while resisting the temptation to simply operate the existing model. They will ask difficult questions, constructively challenge established practices and bring solutions grounded in experience from other complex organizations.

The successful interim will be:
A positive disruptor who is comfortable challenging the status quo while bringing stakeholders with them.
Pragmatic and commercially minded, with a strong orientation toward measurable value.
Comfortable operating within the governance and accountability requirements of a broader public sector environment.
Collaborative and highly credible with senior stakeholders.
An effective coach who enjoys developing people and transferring knowledge.
Curious and externally focused, bringing ideas, benchmarks and best practices into the organization.
Able to balance strategy with execution and quickly identify where the greatest opportunities for improvement exist.
Skilled at simplifying complexity and making procurement easier for stakeholders to understand and navigate.

OUTCOMES

At the conclusion of the six-month mandate, the organization should have:

A stable, engaged and effectively led procurement team.
A clearer strategic direction and priorities for the procurement function.
Improved stakeholder understanding of Procurement and a stronger internal reputation for the function.
More effective and user-friendly procurement policies and processes.
Identified opportunities for measurable savings and increased organizational value.
A clearer roadmap for procurement technology and improved utilization of current systems.
Recommendations regarding the purchase card program, technology and vendor arrangements.
Greater visibility into supplier and supply-chain risk.
Identified opportunities for collaborative procurement and group purchasing with peer institutions.
Increased procurement capability through coaching and knowledge transfer to the existing team.
Practical recommendations for the future operating model, capabilities and leadership requirements of the procurement function.

This is an opportunity for an experienced procurement executive to make a meaningful impact over a relatively short period: stabilizing the function today while helping define what a more strategic, progressive and value-adding procurement function should look like for the future.

jobs.title: Managing Director (NAM)
jobs.description:
Description

We are seeking an experienced and entrepreneurial Managing Director
to lead one of our software businesses within TAG Software Group. As MD, you will own the P&L, set strategic direction, and drive sustained growth and profitability across the business.

Success will be measured by outcomes, raising operational excellence, scaling customer success, and building high-performing leadership teams that multiply impact. This position provides critical operational leadership to a company and potentially a portfolio of companies within a growing software vertical.

About Tag Software Group

TAG Software Group is a team of experienced investors and operators dedicated to acquiring, enhancing, and growing mission-critical software companies serving SMB, enterprise, and public sector customers.

Founded as part of a permanent home for software companies, we don’t buy to sell. Our focus is on long-term partnerships that protect your legacy, employees, and customers.

Our in-house team delivers an efficient, transparent, and seller-friendly process, ensuring speed and certainty of close. Once part of TAG, your company gains access to proven best practices, dedicated value-creation resources, and the extended ecosystem of our sister companies, including proprietary in-house technology including and — helping your business reach the next level.

Investment Approach

Unlike private equity and venture capital firms, we are Entrepreneurs who Buy, Enhance and Grow Software Businesses. That’s right; we don’t sell businesses. We form a strategic alliance with existing management teams. We recognize the dedication and perseverance required to create a firm and place a premium on customers’ and workers’ well-being over short-term goals.

Culture

Tag Software Group is more than just a place to work; we’re a team. We mean it when we say people are our greatest assets, so investing in them is our number one priority. We create an environment where our employees feel first-day-on-the-job excitement, day after day, creating a culture of high performers and collaboration. We celebrate our milestones, and we’re proud of them. We Dream Big, Stay Humble, and Stay Hungry.

Position Description

As Managing Director, you will provide strategic, operational, and financial leadership to a software business or portfolio within the Tag Software Group family. You will develop and implement the business strategy across sales, marketing, R&D, customer service, professional services, and HR. Working with the Business Unit leadership team, you will set growth objectives, lead execution, and drive operational excellence.

You will be fully accountable for business performance, profitability, scalability, and long-term customer and employee success.

Key Responsibilities

Achieve sustainable business growth by positioning the company strategically within its markets and aligning operations with long-term objectives.
Deliver measurable improvements in scalability, efficiency, and operational excellence across the business.
Drive consistent revenue growth through effective market expansion, cross-selling, and customer-focused strategies.
Ensure customer satisfaction and loyalty remain strong, supporting high retention and advocacy.
Maintain clear, market-aligned product strategies and roadmaps that balance innovation with stability, supporting both new customer acquisition and retention.
Foster an environment of innovation and technology adoption, challenging the status quo and leveraging emerging tools (including AI) to improve products, services, and operations.
Own full P&L responsibility, ensuring revenue growth, profitability, financial discipline, and long-term resilience.
Translate deep financial insight into strategic and operational decisions that maximize value creation.

jobs.title: Director, Finance
jobs.description:
POSITION DESCRIPTION

The Director of Finance is a senior finance leader responsible for the integrity, stewardship, and governance of ESA’s financial operations and financial reporting. This role ensures accurate and timely accounting, compliance with statutory and regulatory requirements, effective cash and balance sheet management, and robust internal controls. They will be responsible for all day-to-day finance operations, including functional responsibility over general accounting, accounts payable, accounts receivable, pension administration, treasury, investments.
The Director of Finance is responsible for audit readiness by ensuring robust policies, systems, and procedures are in place, and by supporting the external audit process as required.
In addition, the Director of Finance will partner with the CFO, senior leadership, and staff to improve progam or process integration to enhance efficiently and effectiveness in achieving program objectives, In relation to any system or process changes, the Director of Finance will collaborate with respective business areas to positively impact design and operational effectiveness in support of business objectives as well as financial and management reporting objectives.
ROLE DESCRIPTION

Financial Accounting and Reporting

· Provide financial and accounting leadership for ESA’s Finance function and business areas. Oversee all accounts, ledgers, and reporting systems and changes thereto, ensuring continued compliance with appropriate GAAP standards and regulatory requirements.
· Design and maintain internal controls and safeguards related to revenue (billings and receipts) and expenditures.
· Oversee the preparation and integrity of monthly, quarterly and annual financial reports in accordance with GAAP.
· Lead the month end and year end close processes, ensuring timeliness, completeness, and accuracy.
· Lead the annual ESA external financial statement audit, including planning, fieldwork and reporting while keeping the CFO apprised of any issues on a timely basis.
· Develop, maintain, and enforce accounting policies, procedures and documentation, maintaining an appropriate audit trail for the external auditors.
· Monitor and assess potential changes in NFPO accounting standards and or gaps in ESA’s accounting policies and provide data driven, clear guidance and recommendations to the CFO.
· Prepare materials for Board/A&IC briefings as part of regular quarterly meetings and/or as required.
Internal Controls, Compliance and Audit

· Design, implement, and maintain a strong internal control framework over financial reporting.
· Ensure compliance with statutory, regulatory, tax, and reporting requirements.
· Act as the primary liaison with external auditors, regulators, and other external stakeholders on accounting and control matters.
· Lead the preparation of audit schedules and support external audit activities through to successful completion.
· Identify, assess, and mitigate financial reporting and operational financial risks.
Accounts payable and Accounts Receivable

· Provide strategic and operational oversight of the accounts payable and accounts receivable functions.
· Ensure efficient, accurate, and timely processing of vendor payments and customer billings and collections.
· Establish and monitor key controls over disbursements, collections, credit management, and reconciliations.
· Oversee the management of aged receivables and support resolution of complex or escalated issues.
· Continuously improve processes to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and compliance.
· Collaborate with cross-functional business areas on review of manual journal entries.
Treasury, Cash Management & Banking

· Oversee daily cash management, bank relationships, and banking structures.
· Ensure appropriate controls over cash receipts, disbursements, and account reconciliations.
· Monitor liquidity and working capital from an operational and control perspective, in alignment with CFO direction.
· Authorize banking arrangements and ensure compliance with signing authorities and delegated limits outlined in the Organizational Authority Registrar.
Investments Oversight (Outsourced Chief Investment Officer Governance)

· Provide financial governance and oversight of ESA’s investment activities managed by an outsourced Chief Investment Officer (OCIO), in accordance with approved investment policies, mandates, and governance frameworks.
· Act as the secondary finance liaison with the OCIO to ensure the accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of investment‑related financial information and reporting. The CFO is the primary point of contact for investment-related activities.
· Review and assess investment valuations, and accounting treatments prepared under the OCIO’s management for compliance with applicable accounting standards and investment policies.
· Monitor adherence to internal controls related to investment transactions, custody, valuation, and financial disclosures, including controls executed by the OCIO and third‑party service providers.
· Coordinate with the OCIO, custodians, external managers, actuaries (where applicable), and auditors to support audit activities and regulatory reporting related to investments.
· Ensure appropriate investment disclosures are prepared for financial statements
· Support the CFO and relevant board committee by conducting a detailed review of quarterly reports provided by the outsourced Chief Investment Officer (OCIO). This includes assessing the completeness, accuracy, and clarity of reporting related to portfolio performance, asset allocation, valuation methodologies, compliance with the Investment Policy Statement, and key risk exposures.
· Liaise with the OCIO to obtain clarifications, supplemental analysis, or follow‑up information as required to support informed oversight and governance discussions at the committee level.
Pension and Other Post Employment Benefits Accounting

· Oversee accounting, reporting, and compliance related to pension plans and post‑employment benefits.
· Liaise with external actuaries, pension administrators, and external auditors on valuation, disclosures, and funding matters.
· Ensure accurate recording of pension assets, liabilities, expenses, and associated disclosures.
· Support governance and oversight of pension plans in accordance with applicable legislation and policies.
Payroll

· Provide strategic leadership and oversight over ESA’s payroll function, with operational payroll processing executed by senior payroll professionals.
· Set strategic direction, governance standards, and control expectations for payroll operations to ensure accuracy, compliance, and consistency.
· Establish and maintain ESA’s payroll policy.
· Ensure robust internal controls are designed, implemented, and operating effectively over payroll processing, payroll changes, reconciliations, and access management to ESA’s payroll system.
· Oversee payroll accounting and financial integrity, including review of payroll reconciliations and confirmation of accurate recording of payroll‑related expenses, liabilities, and accruals.
· Review and challenge escalated payroll issues, exceptions, or control matters, approving resolution approaches and escalating material risks to the CFO as appropriate.
· Sponsor continuous improvement initiatives related to payroll systems, processes, controls, and reporting to enhance efficiency, risk management, and employee experience.
People Management:

· Lead, mentor, and develop a high performing finance team.
· Set clear performance expectations and foster a culture of accountability, accuracy, and continuous improvement and customer service to cross-functional business units
Other

· Effectively represent the Finance team as a Senior Management Team Member on board committees or internal committees as required.
QUALIFICATIONS

• CPA designation required
• Strong oral and written communication skills.
· At least 10-12 years of progressive experience in accounting and finance.
· Demonstrated experience in financial reporting, internal controls, accounts payable, accounts receivable, investments and pension accounting.
• Experience supervising a team of finance professionals.
• Experience with non-government not for profit accounting and a solid knowledge and
understanding of GAAP and accounting for pensions.
• Analytic, organization, and problem-solving skills for strategic data interpretation.
• Strong emotional intelligence and self-awareness is essential.
• Strong interpersonal and communication skills required to effectively communicate complex
issues to senior leadership.
• The ability to translate complex financial concepts to individuals at all levels including finance and non-finance managers.
• Requires demonstrated listening and negotiating skills and the ability to work effectively with people inside and outside the organization to achieve the required results.
REPORTING RELATIONSHIPS

Reports to: Chief Financial Officer
Direct Reports: 3 Direct Reports
11 Indirect Reports

jobs.title: Digital Construction and Commissioning Delivery Director
jobs.description:
About Us

Worley is a global company of energy, chemicals and resources experts headquartered in Australia. We partner with our customers to deliver projects and create value across the life of their assets. With more than 40,000 employees in over 40 countries, we specialize in consulting, engineering, procurement and construction across the project lifecycle, with services extending through to operations and decommissioning. Leveraging extensive experience and AI-enabled delivery, we support customers in navigating complexity as they meet today’s needs and transition to more sustainable solutions.

Digital | Digital Project Delivery - This role can be based in any global Worley office. Please note - applicants will need to possess valid working rights for the country in which the role will be based.

Shape how the world’s energy, chemicals and resources projects are built and brought to life. As our Digital Construction and Commissioning Delivery Director, you’ll lead the team that digitally enables successful Construction and Commissioning (C&C) delivery across Worley’s global project portfolio.

Why this role matters

At Worley, digital enablement spans the full stack of people, process and technology a global EPC company needs. Reporting to the Global Head of Digital Project Delivery (DPD) and joining the DPD leadership team, you’ll set the direction for C&C digitalization and have the authority and autonomy to make it happen – owning the strategy, the technology and the corresponding processes that help our project teams deliver better outcomes for our customers. DPD is part of Digital Operations at Worley and exists to support Operations, so your work in this global role will have impact right across Worley.

This is where deep digital expertise meets senior leadership. Rather than writing code yourself, you’ll set the technical direction and lead a talented team spread across multiple locations, bringing them together to turn that vision into results on our projects. You’ll engage with functional representatives in Operations to ensure that their C&C project needs are understood and delivered upon.

Worley has placed using Advanced Work Packaging (AWP) at the centre of our project execution and a key part of the role is to support the seamless digital enablement of AWP on projects. AI is a key plank in our digital strategy, and this role plays a key part in how we adopt AI in C&C.

What You’ll Do

Set the strategy: Define the strategy for digital enablement of C&C as part of the wider DPD strategy, build the plans to deliver it, and develop strategic relationships with external technology partners who support our DPD ambition.
Own the solution: Take ownership of the C&C technology stack – tools, integrations, automation, AI, data management and reporting – across its full build-operate-support-retire lifecycle, partnering closely with other parts of the Worley digital team.
Own the approach: Own the C&C processes, defining the end-to-end workflow for digitally enabled projects in collaboration with the project delivery function.
Lead implementation: Drive adoption of the C&C digital way of working, collaborating with the DPD People and Processes team to ensure a consistent approach across project delivery.
Enable our people: Contribute to organizational change management, define the digital competency requirements for our project personnel, and support the governance framework that embeds the Worley digital approach.
Deliver standout support: Build a support culture focused on keeping our people productive, with tracking metrics that drive continuous improvement.
Lead and grow the team: Manage geographically dispersed direct and indirect reports, including subcontractors, and develop and manage the team budget in line with Company delegation of authority requirements.

What You’ll Bring

Demonstrated experience in construction and commissioning
Digital execution expertise. Strong AI skills
A proven record of directly leading and managing teams
A university degree
Experience in collaboration and working with other teams to deliver solutions
Experience developing strategies, models and frameworks, and a track record of successfully implementing new ways of working.
Experience with digital solutions on projects and awareness of the software typically used for C&C delivery. Knowledge of O3 is preferred
Thought leadership – the ability to pivot between strategic and tactical thinking and to work comfortably with new concepts and complexity.
Strong relationship skills across all levels, cultures and external parties, with the ability to present complex matters clearly and facilitate discussions with large groups.

What’s In It For You

A senior leadership role on the DPD leadership team, with real authority and autonomy over C&C digitalization.
The opportunity to shape how digital technology is used to build and commission projects on a global scale.
Building skills in deploying digital solutions in a large multinational organisation
Latitude to explore the future of C&C digital technologies with technology providers that could prove fruitful for the future of project delivery at Worley
Please note: Applicants will need to possess valid working rights for the country where the role will be based.

If you’re ready to lead the digital transformation of how we build and commission projects that matter to the world, we’d like to hear from you. Apply now.

Moving forward together

We want our people to be energized and empowered to drive sustainable impact. So, our focus is on a values-inspired culture that unlocks brilliance through belonging, connection and innovation. We’re building a diverse, inclusive and respectful workplace. Creating a space where everyone feels they belong, can be themselves, and are heard.

And we’re not just talking about it; we’re doing it. We’re reskilling our people, leveraging transferable skills, and supporting the transition of our workforce to become experts in today’s low carbon energy infrastructure and technology. Whatever your ambition, there’s a path for you here. And there’s no barrier to your potential career success. Join us to broaden your horizons, explore diverse opportunities, and be part of delivering sustainable change.

jobs.title: Director, Network Development & Operations
jobs.description:
Xplore Inc. is Canada’s fibre, 5G and satellite broadband company for rural living. Xplore is committed to the relentless pursuit of an improved broadband experience for all Canadians. Xplore is building a world-class fibre optic and 5G wireless network to enable innovative broadband services for better every day rural living, for today and future generations.

The Director, Network Development & Operations is the senior leader responsible for turning Xplore’s network architecture into an automated, scalable production network, delivering Core & Transport Network Services at a Tier-1 Telco Gold Standard and ensuring uncompromising reliability, security, and performance from the core to the customer. The role leads the teams accountable for detailed IP engineering, DWDM engineering automation, caching implementation, CI/CD, configuration management, telemetry, and operational tooling.

The Director sets the vision and operating model for network-as-code, ensuring that all IP/MPLS, DWDM, and caching configurations are deployed safely, consistently, and at scale. Under this leadership, the organization builds the automation frameworks, observability pipelines, and operational guardrails that enable high-velocity, low-risk changes across the backbone, reduce manual toil, and strengthen 24×7 operational readiness.

Working in close partnership with Network Architecture & Technology Strategy, the Director ensures that architectural intent is executed through modern DevOps practices, and brings operational insight back into standards, roadmaps, and long-term network evolution. The Director connects network development and operations directly to business outcomes and KPIs — including reliability, speed of change, customer experience, and cost efficiency — and serves as a trusted advisor to senior leadership on operational performance and automation maturity.

Key Responsibilities Include

Detailed IP, DWDM & Caching Engineering

Own detailed IP engineering across BGP, OSPF, IS-IS, MPLS, segment routing, and routing policy.
Own DWDM configuration automation, including line-system configuration templates, channel provisioning, amplifier and span parameter automation, optical telemetry integration, and operational tooling for DWDM health and performance.
Own caching platform implementation, including cache node configuration, routing and traffic-steering policies, cache peering and placement logic (as defined by Architecture), and performance tuning and hit-ratio optimization.
Translate architectural standards into deployable configuration templates and network-as-code artifacts.

Network Automation & CI/CD Pipelines

Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines for IP/MPLS/DWDM and caching configuration deployment.
Implement automated testing, validation, and rollback capabilities.
Drive adoption of network-as-code across the Core & Transport domain, ensuring all changes are executed through automated, repeatable workflows.

Telemetry, Observability & Operational Tooling

Own telemetry pipelines, dashboards, and observability tooling for Core & Transport.
Ensure real-time visibility into routing behavior, caching performance and hit ratios, DWDM optical health (OSNR, span performance, and alarms), and capacity and traffic patterns.
Partner with Service Assurance & Observability to integrate signals, alerts, anomaly detection, and automated diagnostics.

Reliability Engineering & Operational Excellence

Implement guardrails, automated checks, and configuration validation to reduce operational risk.
Lead post-incident automation improvements to prevent recurrence.

Partnership with Architecture & Execution of Architectural Intent

Implement the logical connectivity, caching strategy, DWDM design parameters, standards, and principles defined by Network Architecture & Technology Strategy.
Provide feedback loops to Architecture on operational feasibility, automation impacts, and configuration constraints.
Ensure all deployments align with long-range architectural direction and resiliency goals.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Work closely with Network Architecture & Technology Strategy; Carrier Services; Fiber, Fixed Wireless, and Enterprise teams; and NOC, SRE, and Service Assurance.

Financial & Investment Performance

Own the financial and investment performance of the Network Development & Operations portfolio, including capital and operating budgets, business cases, and return-on-investment tracking.
Drive measurable unit cost improvements (e.g., cost per bit, cost per port, cost per subscriber) through automation, standardization, and platform consolidation.
Reduce lifecycle risk by proactively managing hardware and software end-of-life and end-of-support exposure, technical debt, and refresh roadmaps across IP, DWDM, and caching platforms.
Partner with Finance, Architecture, and Procurement to prioritize investments, optimize vendor spend, and align spending with business outcomes.
Report on financial, unit cost, and lifecycle-risk KPIs to senior leadership.

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess

15+ years of experience in IP engineering, DWDM engineering automation, caching platforms, or DevOps for large-scale network infrastructure.

Technical Expertise

Strong expertise in routing protocols (BGP, OSPF, IS-IS), MPLS/segment routing, and routing policy.
Hands-on experience with DWDM systems, optical telemetry, and line-system configuration.
Experience with caching platforms (CDN nodes, edge caches, content caches).
Experience with automation tools (Ansible, Python, CI/CD frameworks).
Experience with telemetry, observability, and network monitoring systems.

Leadership & Collaboration

Demonstrated ability to lead technical engineering teams and work across Architecture, SRE, Service Assurance, and cross-functional network teams.
Strong communication skills with the ability to translate architectural intent into executable engineering workflows.

Education

Bachelor’s degree required in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience.
Master’s degree considered an asset, but not required.
Relevant industry certifications (e.g., CCNP/CCIE, DWDM/optical certifications, cloud or DevOps certifications, Agile/Scrum certifications, SRE certifications, PMP, ITIL) are considered an asset.

Condition Of Employment

As a condition of employment and in order to comply with industry related data security standards, this position is subject to the successful completion of a Criminal Background Check. Details will be supplied to applicants as they move through the selection process.

Xplore is committed to creating an accessible environment and will accommodate disabilities during the selection process. Please let your recruiter know during the selection process of any accommodation needs.

You will orchestrate the seamless onboarding of clients onto our cutting-edge AI, design performance monitoring and diagnostic playbooks that empower our Support teams, and command the resolution of complex performance escalations. :

ICES is a world-leading health research and analytics institute. With a wealth of data and analytic expertise, we create trusted evidence that has changed health policy and practice and helps ensure better health for all.

Ready to discover more with us? Join our outstanding, collaborative team where your skills, knowledge and curiosity are valued and can change the future of health care.

Introduction:

ICES is seeking a Director, Indigenous Partnerships, Data and Analytic Services to join our Indigenous Partnerships, Data and Analytic Services (IPDA) department. Reporting to the Senior Director, Strategic Partnerships and Digital Services, the Director, in collaboration with ICES leadership, is responsible for the development and delivery of the work of the department at ICES. Indigenous Partnership Development:

Accountable for developing, implementing, and managing the Indigenous Partnerships, Data and Analytics (IPDA) department at ICES. This includes facilitating the assertion of representative and diverse First Nations, Inuit, and Métis approaches, perspectives, protocols, and practices to leadership at ICES.
Effectively manage all aspects of performance management for direct reports, including coaching individuals and conducting continuous evaluations to enhance team effectiveness and alignment with departmental goals.
Utilize leadership and project management skills to ensure that departmental initiatives align with ICES' strategic objectives and community needs.

Strategy Management and Operational Planning:

Manage the design and development of an effective and ongoing strategy related to Indigenous data and partnerships. This involves advancing the harmonization of ongoing ICES scientific and corporate strategies with First Nations, Inuit, and Métis requirements and protocols.
Employ analytical and strategic planning skills to assess current practices and develop actionable plans. This includes utilizing data analysis tools and stakeholder feedback to inform strategy development and ensure alignment with community needs and organizational objectives.
Work with cross-functional teams to ensure that the strategy is responsive to evolving Indigenous data sovereignty principles, leveraging collaborative skills to engage stakeholders in the process.
Oversee departmental expenses and recovery of costs by reviewing financial reports and tracking operational expenditures and ensure budget compliance.

Leverage communication and presentation skills to effectively convey complex information, utilizing multimedia tools and resources to engage diverse audiences.
Oversee the development of internal and external capacity-building initiatives, collaborating with educational institutions and community organizations to strengthen partnerships and enhance data literacy.

Utilize networking and relationship-building skills to establish and maintain connections with key external stakeholders, ensuring that ICES remains responsive to community needs and perspectives.
Develop proposals and oversee reporting documents for funders and stakeholders

Manage, coach, and evaluate the team by providing regular feedback and facilitating team-building activities to promote collaboration and alignment with goals, utilizing performance management tools and techniques.
Foster a culture of continuous improvement by identifying training needs, organizing professional development opportunities, and mentoring team members to enhance their skills and career growth, ensuring access to relevant resources and training programs.
Utilize leadership and mentoring skills to enhance departmental effectiveness and individual growth, ensuring alignment with ICES' mission and values by creating an inclusive and supportive team environment.

Other duties as may be assigned within the scope of this position.

At least 8 years of Indigenous community and/or research experience;
Experience working with major health system and Indigenous stakeholders and leaders within Ontario;
A minimum of 5 years management experience;
Demonstrated knowledge of Indigenous cultures and histories in Canada.

Reporting to the Vice President, Client Experience and Consulting, the Director, Digital Fundraising will lead the strategy, growth and performance of Blue North's digital fundraising business.

 What’s in it for you?

Euroclear Nordics AB is now looking for Head of Core Systems to lead an experienced specialist team responsible for business-critical IT environments. Would you like to help drive this development forward? We look forward to receiving your application!

About The Role

As part of a leading provider of financial market infrastructure and post-trade services, you will work in an international environment where local expertise meets global perspectives. As Head of Core Systems, you will have overall responsibility for a team working with a business-critical mainframe environment. You will lead an experienced and close-knit team and ensure stable and secure IT operations with high availability requirements. The team consists of internal employees, consultants and external suppliers.

You will report to the Head of Infrastructure & Operations and have overall responsibility for the Core Systems team’s delivery, development and roadmap. The area includes technologies and platforms such as DB2, IMS, MQ and z/OS.

An important part of the role is to lead the team through an ongoing transformation in which technologies, platforms and ways of working are evolving. The position combines people leadership and change management with close involvement in operational matters.

We are looking for someone who has

Several years of leadership experience with people management responsibility within IT, infrastructure or operations.
Experience leading teams through change or transformation, with the ability to create a sense of stability and maintain engagement throughout the journey.
A good understanding of business-critical IT environments and the requirements associated with stability, security, structure and availability.
A solid overall technical understanding and confidence in leading and collaborating with technical specialists.
A structured and communicative approach, with the ability to work effectively with both technical teams and other parts of the organization.

It is considered an advantage if you have

Experience from banking, financial services or another regulated industry.
Experience with mainframe environments, ideally with an understanding of technologies such as z/OS, DB2, IMS or MQ.
Experience in supplier or outsourcing governance and the management and follow-up of external deliveries.
Experience working in IT environments with high security and availability requirements.

Personal qualities

You are a confident and present leader who creates trust, clarity and engagement. You are attentive and genuinely interested in your employees, while also being comfortable setting directions and making decisions.

You work in a structured and methodical way and can establish order and set priorities in a complex environment with several parallel activities. You are communicative and relationship-oriented and enjoy collaborating with both technical specialists and other parts of the organization.

To succeed in this role, you should also enjoy working in an environment characterized by change and development. You can drive change forward pragmatically while safeguarding stability, quality and confidence in day-to-day operations.

Why join us?

Join Euroclear and play a key role at the heart of the global, Nordic and Swedish financial markets. As a trusted backbone connecting more than 2,000 financial institutions worldwide, Euroclear helps safeguard the stability of global capital markets, while the Stockholm office supports critical infrastructure for Sweden’s financial system.

At Euroclear Nordics AB, you will be part of a culture that values collaboration, innovation and continuous improvement. As part of a global organization, you will have excellent opportunities to work with colleagues around the world and gain valuable insight into international financial markets.

What we offer

At Euroclear Nordics AB, you will have the opportunity to build your career at the heart of the Swedish financial market while contributing to its continued development and digitalization. As part of the Euroclear team, you will work in a dynamic and collaborative environment where your contribution matters and where you are encouraged to grow and reach your full potential.

We are committed to supporting your success through continuous learning and development opportunities, knowledge sharing and collaboration with talented colleagues across the Euroclear Group. You will join an international community representing more than 80 nationalities, united by a culture of teamwork, professionalism and continuous improvement.

Our modern office is centrally located in Stockholm with excellent public transport connections. We offer a flexible hybrid working model that combines the benefits of on-site collaboration with the flexibility of remote working, supporting a healthy work-life balance.

Beyond your day-to-day responsibilities, you will have the opportunity to take part in a vibrant workplace community with regular social activities, office breakfasts and volunteering initiatives. As part of our commitment to social responsibility, every employee is encouraged to dedicate one working day per year to volunteering or charitable activities.

In addition, we offer a competitive benefits package and look forward to welcoming you to a team where you can develop, make an impact and help shape the future of the Nordic financial market.

Euroclear is a global provider of Financial Market Infrastructure services, offering settlement, safekeeping and servicing of domestic and cross-border securities. The Group serves more than 2,400 clients worldwide and has teams across Europe, Asia, the Middle East and the Americas.

Euroclear Nordics AB is Sweden’s Central Securities Depository and plays a key role in the Swedish financial market. Through its digital infrastructure, the company enables secure and efficient registration, safekeeping and settlement of shares, bonds and other securities. Its customers include listed companies, banks and financial institutions across Sweden.

Euroclear Nordics AB has served as Sweden’s Central Securities Depository since 1971 and has been part of the international Euroclear Group since 2008.

Axya is a technology company modernizing the source-to-pay process for the manufacturing industry. Our SaaS platform streamlines and automates procurement, making it faster, simpler and more cost-effective for companies sourcing custom parts. By digitizing traditionally manual processes, Axya helps manufacturers operate with greater efficiency and competitiveness. Axya recently closed a $17 million CAD Series A funding round, a milestone that fuels our next stage of growth as we expand our team, accelerate product development and bring our platform to more manufacturers.

We are proud to cultivate an inclusive and collaborative work environment that supports innovation, growth and professional development. Axya is seeking a VP Finance to lead finance operations and guide the company through its Series B. This is a senior, hands-on role reporting directly to the CEO. You will oversee finance across Axya's two entities, secure non-dilutive funding, and prepare the company and its investors for the Series B.

Mandate And Key Responsibilities

The mandate has three components: finance operations and reporting across two entities, grants and non-dilutive financing, and pre-Series B and Series B fundraising.

Finance Operations And Reporting

Lead finance operations, month-end close, audit readiness and internal controls for both entities
Own budgeting, forecasting and runway management
Define and report key SaaS metrics, including ARR, net revenue retention, CAC payback, burn multiple and gross margin
Prepare the financial content for the board KPI pack and investor reporting
Own the finance systems
Ensure G&A and back-office costs remain in line with benchmarks for a company of Axya's revenue

Non-Dilutive Financing

Coordinate with internal teams and external stakeholders to secure and claim grants, R&D tax credits and government programs

Pre-Series B And Series B Fundraising

Build and maintain the financial model
Prepare the financial materials for the data room and the fundraising process
Maintain an up-to-date pipeline of prospective investors
Support day-to-day operations throughout the fundraising process
Participate in strategic meetings with investors, including travel as required
Support the CEO in term sheet negotiations

What We’re Looking For

Has led a company through a Series B financing, or has been closely involved in one
Background in supply chain, procurement or manufacturing technology, or has raised capital from investors in that space
Maintains a network of US-based investors relevant to Axya's Series B
Proven experience in finance operations and in investor and board reporting
Has negotiated debt and equity financing terms and can support the CEO throughout a Series B process
Willing to travel to meet investors

Being based in the US is not a requirement. Access to US investors and a willingness to travel are.

jobs.title: Vice President of Programs
jobs.description:
We’re Recruiting For…

Vice President of Programs

About the Centre 

The Confederation Centre is Canada’s National Memorial to the founders of the country. It is the result of a dream shared by all Canadians - a place where Canada’s evolution and multicultural character is celebrated and explored right where Canadian confederation began; where the talents of Canadian people are nurtured and showcased through arts, learning, and conversation. Taking up a full city block in downtown Charlottetown, the Centre includes performance venues, art gallery spaces, arts education and learning studios, and spaces for convening and conversation. 

Opened by Queen Elizabeth II in 1964 to commemorate the centennial of the 1864 Charlottetown Conference, the Confederation Centre has welcomed millions of visitors from Canada and the world to experience Canada through many lenses. Producing world-class theatre performances, gallery exhibitions, arts education, community programs, and convening opportunities for discussion on Canadian confederation, the Centre is the largest national multidisciplinary cultural institution in Atlantic Canada. 

Home to the Charlottetown Festival, which sells close to 100,000 tickets over 14 weeks each summer, the Centre employs more than 200 people and drives more than $30 million in economic activity for Prince Edward Island. The Centre is now completing the most signiﬁcant transformation in its history: a $65 million rejuvenation of the former library and archives complex, creating new facilities for the Palmer Institute for Canadian Leadership, the Arts Academy, and the Arts Innovation Hub. The Centre is governed by a national board of directors from across Canada. It is where people learn about Canada and explore the issues most important to us; it is Where Canada Connects. 

Charlottetown, Prince Edward Island 

The capital city of PEI is the birthplace of Canadian confederation, and the Confederation Centre of the Arts is Canada’s national memorial to those who met here in 1864 and proposed a union that would result in a new country three years later. Charlottetown is a beautiful place to live and work. It has a thriving cultural community with numerous attractions including arts, recreation, restaurants, parks, and the harbour. Charlottetown is home to the University of Prince Edward Island and Holland College, and welcomes roughly 1.5 million tourists every summer. Minutes away are some of the best beaches, golf courses, and natural attractions that Canada has to oﬀer. 

The Opportunity

The Confederation Centre is seeking a Vice President of Programs, to lead and support all of the Centre’s public programming. Reporting to the Chief Executive Oﬃcer, the Vice President of Programs provides leadership to the program directors and staﬀ in Theatre, Art Gallery, Arts Academy, Palmer Institute for Canadian Leadership, Archives, and the Arts Innovation Hub, to ensure sustainable operations and positive impact locally, regionally, and nationally.  

As the Centre completes the most signiﬁcant expansion in its history, its programming is growing in scale and in range. The Vice President will ensure this growth is coordinated, ﬁnancially sustainable, and aligned with the Centre’s Strategic Plan, so that every program contributes to the Centre’s national mandate and mission.  

As a key member of the senior leadership team, the Vice President serves as a trusted advisor to the CEO on program strategy, and works closely with the VP of Finance, VP of Operations and Infrastructure, and the full leadership teams in development, marketing, communications, and HR. This is an exceptional opportunity for an experienced cultural leader to shape the next chapter of a beloved national institution. 

Areas of Oversight 

• Theatre
including the Charlottetown Festival, and year-round performing arts programming
• Art Gallery
including the six gallery spaces, permanent collection, and community programming
• Arts Academy
including a host of programs in dance, musical theatre, choir, and visual arts
• Palmer Institute for Canadian Leadership
including convening programs for dialogue on Canada
• Arts Innovation Hub
including artist residencies and production support for new work
• Archives
including the organization and use of historic documents and artifacts of the Centre

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership 

Provide strategic and operational support to the leadership team across theatre, visual art, arts education, leadership and convening, and archives that advances the Centre’s national mandate and Strategic Plan
Serve as a trusted advisor to the CEO on program direction, priorities, and risk, and support the CEO and CFO in reporting to the Board of Directors and its committees
Identify and develop opportunities for collaboration across program areas, so that programs reinforce one another and engage audiences year-round, in Charlottetown and across Canada
Lead program planning for the Centre’s new and renewed facilities as they open, ensuring they are well used and well integrated with existing programs

People Leadership

Lead, support, and mentor the program directors, setting clear goals, fostering professional development, and holding the team accountable for results
Champion artistic, curatorial, and scholarly excellence, respecting the creative leadership of program directors while ensuring alignment with the Centre’s priorities
Foster a positive, inclusive, and collaborative culture across program teams, volunteers, artists, and external collaborators
Work with Human Resources on recruitment, development, and succession planning for program leadership roles

Sustainability and Fiscal Responsibility

Oversee multi-year program budgets in partnership with the Chief Financial Oﬃcer, ensuring the prudent allocation of resources across program areas
Drive entrepreneurial strategies to grow earned revenue across ticket sales, registrations, tuition, touring, and partnerships
Work with the Development team to secure philanthropic support and sponsorship for programs
Establish clear measures of audience, impact, and ﬁnancial performance, and report on results

Partnerships and Public Engagement

Build and maintain relationships with artists, cultural institutions, governments, educational institutions, community groups, and funding partners across Canada
Advance the Centre’s commitments to reconciliation and to engaging youth, newcomers, and diverse communities, working in partnership with First Nations, Inuit, and Métis communities
Serve as a spokesperson for the Centre’s programs with the media, funders, government, and the public

Operational Integration

Coordinate program calendars, shared spaces, and other resources across the Centre’s theatres, galleries, studios, and convening spaces
Work closely with Marketing, Development, Operations, Finance, and Catering & Conference Services to deliver an outstanding visitor experience
Ensure the care and stewardship of the Centre’s permanent collection and archives in keeping with professional standards

Qualiﬁcations

At least 10 years of progressive senior leadership experience in the arts, culture, heritage, education, or a related sector, including the leadership of multiple programs or departments
Proven track record leading multidisciplinary programs, such as performing arts, visual arts, education, or public engagement
Experience leading senior leaders, including artistic or creative leaders
Demonstrable experience developing and managing complex, multi-program budgets
Extensive experience with grant applications and reporting, fundraising, sponsorship, and earned revenue
Experience in strategic planning and leading change in a growing organization
Experience working with a Board of Directors
Experience managing in a unionized environment
Strong communication skills, with experience in public speaking, media relations, and stakeholder engagement
Graduate degree in the arts, arts administration, humanities, or a related ﬁeld, or an equivalent combination of education and experience
Experience working with Indigenous communities and partners is an asset
Bilingualism (French/English) is an asset

Leadership Proﬁle

Strategic, collaborative executive who brings people together across disciplines
Deep respect for artistic and creative leadership, and the judgment to balance creative ambition with ﬁnancial sustainability
Skilled at building trust, managing complexity, and leading through change
High integrity and commitment to transparency
Passionate about Canada, its evolution, and the role of the arts and public conversation in building community and understanding

Additional Information 

The Vice President of Programs, is a full-time, year-round position, beginning as soon as possible, with a comprehensive beneﬁts package and pension plan. The hiring salary range is $130,000 - $150,000 per annum commensurate with experience. Comprehensive beneﬁts include medical, dental, vision, long-term disability, and life insurance coverage. It also includes:
• Employer-matched pension plan
• Paid vacation and contingency days
• Staﬀ discounts on shows and events
• Employee Assistance Program
• Training and professional development opportunities

How to Apply

Please submit your resume with a cover letter to Sara Rogers, People & Workplace Manager at careers@confederationcentre.com, or hard copy can be mailed to Sara Rogers, Confederation Centre of the Arts, 145 Richmond Street, Charlottetown, PE C1A 1J1 

Confederation Centre of the Arts is committed to promoting a diverse workplace culture. We encourage applications from under-represented communities and persons with disabilities. When requested, we will provide accommodation for candidates throughout the recruitment and selection process.

This is a leadership role focused on setting direction, developing talent, shaping commercial strategy, and strengthening how the organization operates as we scale. The Director is expected to lead beyond the boundaries of their immediate remit, identifying broader opportunities and challenges and driving solutions that strengthen Research Services as a whole.

The Director will serve as a senior research and business partner across Scintilla, translating business priorities into action, building strong cross-functional partnerships and ensuring our people, capabilities and ways of working are positioned to meet evolving client and commercial needs across DIY, flexible support and bespoke full-service Research Services. While this role is not primarily focused on individual project delivery, the Director will remain close to the work and provide senior-level consultation and leadership on strategic, complex or high-risk engagements.

What You'll Do...

Lead a significant area of the Research Services business, setting direction and making thoughtful tradeoffs across client needs, commercial opportunity, team capacity, research quality and talent.
Shape commercial strategy in partnership with commercial leaders across Sales and Account Management, identifying areas of greatest opportunity and translating them into clear priorities that drive sustainable growth, utilization and client value across Scintilla’s research capabilities.
Lead, coach and develop a high-performing team of people leaders and researchers, creating clear accountability, strengthening leadership capability, managing performance, and building a strong pipeline of talent.
Operate with an enterprise mindset, looking beyond the immediate area of responsibility to identify opportunities, risks and ways of working that can strengthen Research Services and Scintilla more broadly.
Identify systemic challenges and proactively develop scalable solutions that improve how teams operate, collaborate and deliver, breaking down silos, and creating greater consistency and collective impact across the organization.
Lead talent and workforce planning, anticipating future capability and capacity needs and proactively shaping hiring, succession and organizational plans to support business growth.
Set and uphold a high bar for research excellence and client experience, serving as a senior research advisor on strategic, complex or high-risk engagements while empowering leaders and teams to own execution.
Build strong partnerships across Account Management, Product, Strategy and other Scintilla teams, representing the Research Services perspective and helping shape how clients move across DIY, flexible and full-service research models based on their needs and complexity.
Translate broader organizational and Scintilla priorities into clear direction for teams, creating alignment around what matters most and ensuring leaders understand both the “what” and the “why.”
Develop a strong understanding of the broader client and business landscape, identifying emerging needs, patterns and opportunities and using those perspectives to inform commercial priorities, capabilities and investment decisions.
Continuously assess how the organization should evolve as it scales, identifying opportunities to strengthen structure, capabilities, processes and ways of working across both self-service and expert-supported research.
Champion a one-team culture across Research Services, connecting people and ideas across areas, sharing knowledge and making decisions that optimize for the broader organization rather than any single team or portfolio.

Who You Are

You are an experienced consumer insights and business leader who can confidently move between research methodology, client needs, commercial strategy and organizational priorities.
You are a strong people leader who builds high-performing teams by developing talent, setting clear expectations and accountability, and providing thoughtful coaching, feedback and opportunities for growth.
You operate with an enterprise mindset, looking beyond your immediate responsibilities to identify opportunities and solve challenges that create value across the broader organization.
You are commercially minded and can translate market, client and business needs into clear priorities, thoughtful investments and sustainable growth opportunities.
You create clarity in ambiguous situations, anticipate what the business will need next and proactively mobilize people around solutions rather than waiting for challenges to become urgent.
You build trusted relationships and influence effectively across functions, recognizing that the strongest outcomes come from breaking down silos and operating as one team.
You are comfortable leading in a fast-growing, evolving environment where priorities can shift and leaders are expected to help shape how the organization works as it scales.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field.
15+ years of consumer or market research experience, including significant experience in client-facing roles.
5+ years of people leadership experience, including experience leading managers and/or teams with multiple levels of responsibility.
Demonstrated experience leading a significant business, client portfolio, research function or other complex area of responsibility.
Deep expertise in quantitative and/or qualitative research, with the ability to provide senior-level guidance across research design, methodology, analysis, storytelling and client delivery.
Experience with workforce planning, talent development, performance management, and building organizational capability.

Audit technology-related risks and controls and assist our Audit teams in addressing complex technology topics, including impacts of client artificial intelligence (AI) usage on the audits. Formal assurance on systems, processes, and controls, including Audits of Service Organization Controls (i.e., SOC 1 engagements under CSAE 3416, SSAE 18, and/or ISAE 3402), SOC 2 and SOC 3 engagements (systems security & reliability assurance), and other standards.

Experience with the identification and or evaluation of process level controls in large system transformation projects involving SAP and or Oracle.
Experience in the testing of controls in different IT environments, like SAP, Oracle, Unix, Linux, AS400, Mainframe, etc.
Experience within an external audit practice auditing client in the Financial Services, Technology and Telecom, and Mining industry.
Ability to work both, with little supervision and within a team environment.
Excellent communication skills being able to express insights, both written and orally.
Demonstrated ability to learn and succeed in a fast-paced environment.
Attention to detail and strong organization and investigative skills.
Strong understanding of business risks and audit risks.

, we never stop learning and improving | Courage

We are hiring for this position out of our Toronto, Calgary, and Vancouver offices. Successful candidates who apply outside of these areas will be expected to relocate and reside in a location that is within a commutable distance.

Role Overview

The Assistant Vice President, Third Party Risk Management (TPRM) is responsible for leading the implementation and ongoing execution of the Peoples Group TPRM framework, including ownership of the TPRM policy, supporting toolkits, inventory, and compliance tracking. This role leads and develops a team accountable for running the TPRM program, providing effective challenge to third‑party risk and criticality assessments, and ensuring regulatory requirements are met across the enterprise.

The AVP prepares regular reporting for senior management and Board committees, partners closely with Technology on the development and maintenance of the TPRM system, and works collaboratively with Legal, Procurement, Information Security, and Relationship Owners to manage third‑party onboarding, contracting, cyber risk, and ongoing monitoring. Success in this role requires strong stakeholder and conflict management skills to balance business objectives, client expectations, and regulatory obligations, as well as the ability to build productive relationships across multiple departments and drive enterprise‑wide training and compliance with TPRM requirements.

About The Day-to-day

Lead the implementation of the Peoples Group TPRM framework.
Responsible for maintaining the TPRM Policy and Framework as well as the documentation supporting TPRM toolkits (Criticality and Risk Triage, Risk Assessment Template, Due Diligence Questionnaire, Contracting Requirements, Monitoring Plans, Contingency and Exit Planning, Exception Management).
Manage a team of analysts and senior managers accountable for running the TPRM Framework. Lead the team in providing constructive challenge to the results of third-party risk and criticality assessments completed by the Relationship Owners.
Own and manage the TPRM inventory and compliance tracker.
Prepare regular reporting for the Operational Risk Management Committee, Corporate Risk Committee and Board Risk Committee.
Work directly with the Technology team on the development and launch of the TPRM system to facilitate completion of the required toolkits and inventory of required Third-Party documentation. This includes accountability for User Acceptance Testing prior to launch and for regular patches and updates from the software provider.
Successfully manage friction arising between business objectives, client expectations and regulatory requirements. Account Managers and their clients are important stakeholders in the success of TPRM. The successful candidate will be relied on to diffuse tensions when working with clients and counterparties to meet regulatory requirements for TPRM.
Develop and coordinate enterprise-wide training on TPRM requirements.
Work directly with Relationship Owners to clarify requirements for the onboarding and management of Third-Parties.
Work closely with the Legal and Procurement departments to maintain control processes and compliance requirements when onboarding new Third-Parties and executing contracts.
Coordinate with the Information Security Team to assess cyber-security control effectiveness at critical third parties.
Working across all departments within PTC, partnering with relationship owners to maintain compliance and update third-party criticality and risk assessment. Collaboratively escalating gaps with requirements and facilitating approval of waivers where appropriate.
Establishing productive relationships and working successfully with stakeholders across multiple departments is essential for success in this role.

About The Qualifications

10+ years experience working in risk management or operations at a Canadian Financial Institution, with at least 5 years of experience in a management role.
Successfully delivered enterprise-wide risk projects requiring significant change management and training across departments.
Familiarity with Software Development Life Cycle in the context of enterprise applications and experience developing requirements for risk management solutions and coordinating User Acceptance Testing.
Required experience in developing Third Party Risk Management TPRM Frameworks at Small and Medium Sized Banks (SMSBs) in Canada. Alternatively, applicants with intricate knowledge and experience in running an established TPRM framework at an SMSB or DSIB will also be considered.
Direct experience in managing OSFI expectation and regulatory findings related to TPRM and Guideline B-10 is a significant asset.
Strong communication skills, with experience presenting at senior management committee meetings and interacting directly with C-level executives at SMSBs.
Proven conflict management capabilities when working across multiple departments and stakeholders to achieve positive risk and compliance outcomes.

Peoples Group is a trusted financial services company for the innovators at the forefront of Canada’s economic future. With offices in Vancouver, Calgary, and Toronto, we are driving change by working alongside challenger banks, fintechs, brokers, and merchants to foster a dynamic and competitive financial ecosystem.

Our culture is built on four core behaviours: Grit to Grow
, Connect to Collaborate

. We believe people do not simply choose a company to work for—they choose a company that makes a positive impact in the lives of Canadians. Above all, we value people, build meaningful relationships, focus on individual strengths, and approach our work with passion.

Peoples Group offers a flexible and hybrid work environment. In this role you will work a combination of in-office and remotely from home. Typically, you'll be working regular business hours, Monday to Friday between 8:00am and 4:30pm with flexibility around start/end times.

A hybrid work environment, enabling you to balance your personal and professional life seamlessly.
