This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Director of Data Architecture based in Canada.

The Director of Data Architecture will define and lead the organization's long-term data strategy, overseeing the architecture, infrastructure, and teams responsible for managing its entire data ecosystem. You will drive the development of scalable data platforms, ensuring seamless data integration, transformation, storage, and delivery across multiple systems. Leading two specialized functions, Data Engineering and Data Operations Engineering, you will balance innovation with the reliability and performance of existing production environments. This position combines strategic leadership with hands-on technical involvement, particularly during the initial stages of team development. You will work closely with executive and engineering leaders to establish architectural standards and align data initiatives with broader business objectives. You will also play a central role in strengthening data quality, governance, security, and compliance while building a robust data foundation that supports analytics, product innovation, and business growth.

Accountabilities

Define and lead the long-term data architecture and platform strategy, overseeing data warehouses, operational data stores, and the evolution toward a modern medallion-based lakehouse architecture (bronze, silver, and gold layers).
Design, develop, and manage data lake and warehouse infrastructure, including the creation and optimization of data marts supporting analytics, product development, and business reporting.
Establish architecture standards and orchestration strategies for all data workflows, including source ingestion, web-scraping pipelines, ETL/ELT processes, and automated workflow management.
Oversee the infrastructure, administration, capacity planning, reliability, and cost optimization of data warehouses and pipelines.
Develop and enforce comprehensive data governance frameworks covering data quality, lineage, access controls, classification, retention, and auditability.
Build, lead, and scale two complementary teams: Data Engineering, responsible for developing new pipelines and architecture, and Data Operations Engineering, responsible for maintaining and optimizing existing production processes.
Define the organizational structure and leadership model as the teams grow, determining when additional management layers and operational responsibilities are required.
Remain hands-on during the initial stages by designing and reviewing pipelines, data models, and orchestration processes, while progressively empowering teams to manage execution independently.
Maintain strong technical oversight to guide architectural decisions and ensure the continuous evolution of the data platform.
Collaborate with engineering leadership and the CTO to establish technical direction, align data architecture with company-wide standards, and support strategic technology decisions.
Partner with product, analytics, data engineering, and business stakeholders to understand data requirements and translate them into effective warehouse and data mart solutions.
Establish and monitor data quality controls, lineage tracking, and auditability standards across all data pipelines.
Oversee data access policies, classification standards, and retention practices to ensure secure and compliant data management.
Ensure that compliance-sensitive and audit-relevant information is managed appropriately as data sources and customer requirements expand.

Requirements

At least 10 years of professional experience in data engineering, data architecture, or related technical fields, including a minimum of 5 years in Director- or Manager-level leadership positions with responsibility for architecture strategy and team management.
Extensive hands-on experience designing, implementing, and operating cloud-based data warehouse or lakehouse architectures, particularly with Snowflake and/or BigQuery.
Strong understanding and practical experience with medallion architecture patterns, including bronze, silver, and gold data layers.
Experience integrating multiple source systems, including MongoDB, PostgreSQL, and MySQL, and developing ingestion and ETL pipelines from diverse structured and unstructured data sources.
Experience building and managing web-scraping pipelines, background processing systems, and automated workflow orchestration.
Proven ability to establish, develop, and scale data engineering or data platform organizations, including structuring separate engineering and operations functions.
Strong knowledge of data governance frameworks, with experience establishing and enforcing standards for data quality, lineage, access management, and retention in regulated or compliance-sensitive environments.
Demonstrated ability to define technical strategy in collaboration with senior engineering leaders and influence architectural decisions across multiple teams.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to present technical strategy, platform performance, infrastructure costs, and operational risks directly to executive leadership, including the CTO.
Strong strategic thinking, organizational leadership, and problem-solving abilities, combined with the willingness to remain technically involved when needed.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience consolidating, modernizing, or re-architecting data platforms following acquisitions or significant expansions in data sources.
Familiarity with data orchestration and transformation tools such as Airflow and dbt.
Experience designing and managing large-scale web-scraping and crawling infrastructure.
Background developing data marts and self-service analytics platforms for non-technical stakeholders.
Familiarity with data observability and quality monitoring tools such as Monte Carlo, Great Expectations, Soda, or similar solutions.

Benefits

Competitive annual salary: USD 200,000 per year.
Remote work flexibility: Opportunity to work remotely from Canada.
Strategic leadership opportunity: Shape the long-term data architecture and technology strategy of a growing organization.
Team-building experience: Build, lead, and develop two specialized engineering functions while influencing organizational structure and growth.
Technical innovation: Work with modern cloud data platforms, lakehouse architectures, data orchestration, and advanced governance solutions.

About The Faculty Of Medicine

Welcome to the University of Ottawa Faculty of Medicine, the first and largest bilingual medical faculty in Canada. Our learners have access to state-of-the art facilities and specialized institutions as they learn alongside world-class physicians and scientists. Consistently ranked among the top 10 medical schools in Canada, our faculty is among the top faculties of medicine in the world for research impact in biomedical and health sciences.

Position Purpose:

As the senior administrative and operational leader for the Department of Family Medicine, the Director works in close partnership with the Chair to translate the Department’s academic mission and strategic priorities into sustainable operations. The Director provides integrated leadership across finance, human resources, education, research administration, faculty affairs, information management, facilities, communications and major projects. The role aligns people, resources, governance and service delivery across the Department, Faculty of Medicine, University, affiliated hospitals, research institutes and community teaching sites while ensuring compliance with applicable policies, agreements and regulatory requirements

Specific Accountabilities:

Operations Leadership: Sets operational priorities within the authority delegated by the Chair and the University. Approves spending and resource decisions within assigned limits, oversees agreements, and brings matters requiring higher approval forward with clear options and recommendations. Escalates significant risks promptly. Uses service standards, key performance indicators and reliable data to monitor results and report to the Chair and departmental leadership.
Planning and Strategy: Supports the Chair in developing and carrying out the Department’s strategic plan. Translates the missions of the Department, Faculty of Medicine and University into practical operating priorities and reports regularly on progress. Applies knowledge of medical education, research and the health system to departmental planning and operations.
Department Planning and Integration: Connects work across the Department, Faculty, University and community partners in line with the Chair’s direction. Brings academic and administrative leaders together, identifies cross-portfolio impacts, and turns approved priorities into coordinated and well-resourced action. Oversees the administrative systems, evidence and improvement plans needed for accreditation and quality assurance across undergraduate, postgraduate and faculty-development programs.
Governance: Supports the Chair in maintaining clear decision-making and committee processes. Prepares evidence-based recommendations, records decisions and delegated authorities, tracks implementation, and ensures committees have clear mandates, reliable information, appropriate administrative support and effective escalation paths.
Finance: Works with the Chair and both University and Departmental finance leadership to develop and manage short- and long-term financial plans for the Department and its academic units. Leads financial planning, negotiations, funding and risk management for strategic priorities, including business plans for new family medicine teaching units with government, academic and community partners.
Human Resources Management: Leads the Department’s administrative management team. Hires, supervises and evaluates direct reports; ensures they have the training and tools needed to succeed; and holds managers accountable for results. Develops the workforce plan needed to support departmental priorities, growth and community needs, in keeping with applicable University policies and collective agreements.
Accreditation, Reporting and Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI): Works with the Senior Leadership Team and academic leaders to meet CFPC accreditation standards and maintain an ongoing framework for curriculum review, program measures and quality improvement. Leads cross-department improvements that reduce duplication, close service gaps, shorten processing times and improve service. Reports to leadership committees on accreditation readiness, financial performance and CQI results, and advises on corrective action when needed.
Business Technology: Works in collaboration with University IT to set the Department’s technology roadmap and priorities based on user needs and business value. Defines business requirements, brings proposals through University approval processes, monitors technology projects and service agreements, and ensures privacy, cybersecurity, records-management and data-governance requirements are addressed by the appropriate University authorities.
Policy and Compliance: Develops and maintains departmental policies and procedures that meet University, Faculty, funder and legal requirements. Ensures staff understand their responsibilities and provides clear, timely and bilingual communication to key stakeholders.
Relationship Building and Liaison: Builds strategic relationships that support the Department’s mission and the discipline of family medicine. Acts as the main liaison with the CFPC, the Council of Ontario Universities, other family medicine programs, governments, affiliated institutions and community partners on program growth, residency duration, funding and capital needs. Represents the Department on academic, regulatory and policy bodies, advocates for sustainable funding, and brings partners together to address issues affecting family medicine education and residency training.

Knowledge, Experience and Skills:

Essential Qualifications:

Graduate degree in business administration, public administration, health administration, education administration or another field relevant to the leadership of complex academic and healthcare operations, or an equivalent combination of education and senior leadership experience.

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Applications
jobs.description:
Job Description

Toast is recruiting for a 100% employee-owned Canadian consulting engineering firm with about 1,350 people. The firm is growing from “small” to “big” and is building out its Digital Services leadership. It has just finished a Microsoft Dynamics 365 implementation. Now it needs a Director, Enterprise Applications to take the platform from “live” to “working well,” and to bring in the best practices the organization doesn’t have yet.

You’ll lead three teams of about 16 people in total: the Dynamics Centre of Excellence, Application Development, and Applications Support. You’ll have room to shape the team, put structure in place, and build the technology roadmap. The firm wants a leader with executive polish who is also happy to roll up their sleeves, and who leads by bringing people along rather than by decree.

Responsibilities

Build and own a multi-year enterprise applications strategy and technology roadmap tied to business priorities
Lead the next phase of Dynamics 365 (Finance and Operations, Project Operations, HR, Customer Engagement), working through deferred scope and getting the most value out of the platform
Assess legacy applications and decide what to modernize, consolidate or retire
Set application development standards and governance, including secure development, source control, automated testing, CI/CD and Power Platform
Be the design authority for application, integration and platform architecture, working with Infrastructure, Enterprise Architecture, Cybersecurity, and Data and Reporting
Set the support operating model, service levels and release governance that keep production stable
Own the operating and capital budgets, licensing and total cost of ownership; lead vendor selection, RFPs, negotiations and renewals
Partner with leaders in Finance, HR, Operations, Project Delivery and other functions to turn business needs into roadmaps and investment decisions
Lead, coach and develop three Team Leads and their teams, with clear roles, career paths and a collaborative, service-focused culture

Requirements

10+ years of progressive experience in enterprise applications or business systems
Expert-level Microsoft Dynamics 365 experience, ideally including Finance and Operations and Project Operations
5+ years leading application teams at a senior manager or director level
Hands-on experience leading application development, with a strong grasp of modern development best practices
A track record of running large-scale enterprise applications, such as ERP or document management, through delivery, stabilization and sustainment. You need to have led the work, not just been part of it.
Experience building technology roadmaps and governance for application portfolios
Experience managing budgets, licensing, system integrators and software vendors

Nice to Haves

Experience in a multi-office engineering, consulting, professional services or project-based organization
Knowledge of Power Platform, Azure integrations, and Microsoft Fabric or Power BI
Experience setting up a Centre of Excellence or a platform governance model
Knowledge of project-based business processes such as project accounting, resourcing, time and expense, and billing
Dynamics 365, Power Platform, enterprise architecture or ITSM certifications

Benefits

Salary listed above, plus a matching company pension and annual salary reviews
The chance to become an owner at a 100% employee-owned firm
A newly shaped leadership role where you build the team, its structure and its roadmap
Health, dental and vision coverage, a fitness allowance and mental health supports
Generous vacation, plus a paid office closure over the December holidays
Paid professional development hours, formal mentoring and parental leave top-up
Application Review

Submit your application, including your resume and cover letter, through our online portal. Our team will carefully review your qualifications and experiences. We take pride in responding promptly, so if your application aligns with our current opportunities, you’ll hear back from us with next steps. Your journey with Toast begins here, and we’re excited to see what you bring to the table!

Vetting Call

If your application is successful, we’ll schedule a vetting call with a member of the Toast team. This 30-45 minute informal conversation is designed for us to get to know you better and assess your skills. Be prepared to discuss your past projects, the challenges you’ve tackled, and the impact you’ve made. This is your chance to shine and show us why you’re a great fit for the roles we offer.

Profile Creation

Once you’ve impressed us in the vetting call, we’ll create an unbiased profile that highlights your experience while minimizing common biases. Instead, we focus on your skills, industry experience, and the impact you’ve made. This way, your profile reflects your true potential and accomplishments.

Client Submission

After crafting your unbiased profile, we submit it to our trusted clients. We work closely with these clients to ensure they understand the value you bring. Throughout their interview process, we remain by your side, providing support and guidance. Our goal is to help you navigate the hiring process smoothly and confidently, ensuring you have the best chance to secure a role that fits your skills and aspirations.

jobs.title: Data & AI Operations Director
jobs.description:
About us

 Qualio is a unified quality and compliance management platform that helps regulated organizations get products to market faster with reduced risk. Trusted by biopharma, medtech, and diagnostics companies worldwide, Qualio eliminates fragmented systems that create audit delays and compliance blind spots. Our platform enables audit readiness in weeks through multi-standard automated gap analysis and evidence reuse across ISO and FDA requirements. Qualio is ISO 27001, ISO 9001, and ISO 27701 certified, reflecting our commitment to security, quality, and privacy.

 The Qualio team is all-remote, and currently distributed across North America, Europe and Australia.

 What's the opportunity?

 The way software companies operate is being rebuilt right now, and the teams that figure out how to run AI-natively will move at a speed the rest can't match. Not by bolting a chatbot onto an existing process, but by taking workflows apart and reassembling them around what these tools can actually do.

 We've also reached the size where product, delivery, and go-to-market can no longer coordinate by proximity. The seams between them are where our leverage leaks out: a feature ships that the field can't articulate, a positioning shift lands that delivery hasn't been briefed on, a customer commitment gets made that the roadmap doesn't reflect.

 This role owns both, because they're the same problem.

 You can't rewire how a company works without seeing how the work actually flows across it.

 What will I be doing?

 Own our AI-native transformation. Partner across the organization to take our major workflows apart and rebuild them. You'll own enablement, change management, and the measurement that shows whether a new workflow is actually used and actually saves time.

 Assess the existing data infrastructure and actively make changes to improve data hygiene and maintenance in order to execute changes.

 Act as a team of one to implement sweeping operational change.

 Partner with leaders across the business, from product and engineering, to GTM, to operations, and support strategic decision making and initiative prioritization.

 Take Qualio's most ambiguous, highest-stakes business questions from "no one knows" to a decision we can act on and own the outcome.

 Bring a sharp, independent voice into company planning and our biggest capital-allocation calls.

 Partner with our finance, revenue ops, and product organizations to standardize and distribute the key operating metrics.

 Set the direction for how Qualio monetizes the AI era: agents, consumption/usage-based billing, and our APIs; with a real point of view on where the model is going, not just where it is.

 What skills do I need?

 Experience 

 8 to 10+ years of expertise in Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and NLP, with a proven track record of implementing modern Generative AI, LLMs, and Agentic workflows in SaaS environments over the last 3+ year.

 You’ve built agents or LLM-powered tools on top of company data yourself, so you know what good data for agents looks like and can guide teams building their own.

 Excellent analytical problem-solving skills with ability to unearth insights and turn them into recommendations and action plans.

 BA/BS in Economics, Math, Finance, Engineering, CS, or other quantitative field; MBA or other advanced degree a plus.

 Strong written and verbal communication skills, able to synthesize findings and concisely articulate them to an array of audiences.

 Self-starter with a demonstrated ability to adapt to a rapidly-changing environment.

 Extremely organized and structured, with a proven ability to run projects and processes from end-to-end.

 Ability to effectively build and maintain cross-functional relationships, manage multiple competing priorities, and drive projects to completion.

 Added plus if you also have exposure to monetization, pricing & packaging, or business-model design — especially in the AI/consumption era.

 Benefits

 The opportunity in helping life-saving products get to market faster

 Medical coverage (with premiums for our most popular plan fully covered for you and your eligible dependents)

 Dental and Vision coverage

 401(k) with up to 4% company matching

 Dependent Care & Health FSA, HSA, Short/Long Term Disability, Basic & Voluntary Life Insurance

 12+ weeks of Paid Parental Leave

 Flexible Time Off (FTO) policy - take time when you need it

 Generous one-time allowance for your home office setup

 Annual Learning & Development stipend

 Regular team gatherings and all-org meetups 

 A note to candidates

 Studies have shown that women and people of color are less likely to apply for jobs unless they believe they meet every single one of the qualifications as described in a job description. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive company and we are most interested in finding the BEST candidate for the job. That candidate may be one who comes from a less traditional background, and that’s okay. We would strongly encourage you to apply, even if you don't believe you meet every one of the qualifications described.

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Digital Capabilities
jobs.description:
Manulife is transforming how we deliver digital experiences across our businesses and markets. Through Digital Storefront, we are building a portfolio of enterprise digital capabilities that make it easier, faster and more effective for our segments to deliver differentiated, connected experiences for customers.

As Director, Enterprise Digital Capabilities, you will lead a team responsible for the strategy, execution, evolution, adoption and value realization of a portfolio of enterprise common capabilities that support Manulife's digital strategy across Canada, the United States, Asia and Global Wealth & Asset Management.

This is an enterprise product leadership role. You will establish the future-state vision and value proposition for assigned capabilities, understand segment needs and roadmaps, define and continuously evolve the enterprise roadmap, determine MVP and subsequent releases, and work across business, technology, experience and delivery teams to bring capabilities to market.

Working closely with peer capability leaders, you will ensure individual capability roadmaps come together as a cohesive enterprise portfolio aligned to segment strategies and evolving customer and business needs.

You will work closely with the Common Capability Collective, which brings together segment and enterprise stakeholders to identify needs, establish priorities and align investments. You will ensure capabilities solve meaningful business and customer problems, are designed for reuse across Manulife, and continue to evolve based on adoption, performance, emerging technology and changing business needs.

Success is not simply delivering a capability. It is ensuring that capabilities are adopted, generate measurable value and become stronger over time.

Position Responsibilities

Capability Strategy & Vision

Own the strategy, future-state vision and evolution of assigned enterprise digital capabilities.
Define the business and customer problems each capability is intended to solve and articulate a compelling enterprise value proposition.
Establish clear business outcomes, benefits and success measures for each capability.
Maintain an understanding of customer expectations, industry trends, competitive practices and emerging technologies to inform capability direction.
Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize and reuse capabilities across markets and businesses while enabling appropriate market differentiation.
Actively identify and embed opportunities to leverage AI, GenAI and agentic AI within enterprise capabilities and delivery practices to create differentiated customer experiences, accelerate delivery and improve business outcomes.

Roadmap & Product Leadership

Own and continuously evolve multi-year capability roadmaps that translate enterprise strategy into actionable priorities and investments.
Align capability roadmaps with segment strategies, product roadmaps, customer journeys and technology dependencies.
Define MVPs and subsequent releases that balance customer and business value, speed to market, enterprise scalability and technical feasibility.
Translate capability vision and business outcomes into clear requirements, priorities and measurable objectives for delivery teams.
Make informed prioritization and trade-off decisions based on customer value, business value, reuse potential, effort, dependencies and strategic alignment.
Partner with architecture, technology, data, experience, AI and delivery teams to ensure capabilities are designed for enterprise scale, integration and reuse.

Common Capability Collective & Enterprise Alignment

Work with the Common Capability Collective as the primary forum for gathering segment needs, identifying common requirements, establishing priorities and aligning capability investments.
Build strong partnerships across Canada, the United States, Asia, Global Wealth & Asset Management and Global functions to understand their strategies, roadmaps and evolving capability needs.
Identify commonality across segment requirements and translate individual needs into scalable enterprise solutions where appropriate.
Facilitate decisions and trade-offs when priorities differ across markets or businesses.
Maintain transparency on capability priorities, roadmaps, dependencies, delivery progress and value realization.
Ensure segment perspectives remain represented throughout the capability lifecycle—from strategy and design through implementation and ongoing evolution.

Capability Launch, Adoption & Evolution

Lead capabilities from strategy and concept through MVP, launch, adoption and ongoing maturity.
Develop capability rollout and adoption strategies in partnership with segments and delivery teams.
Work with markets and businesses to integrate enterprise capabilities into their digital experiences and roadmaps.
Identify barriers to adoption and work across teams to resolve them.
Establish feedback loops with users, segments and stakeholders to understand how capabilities are performing in practice.
Use adoption data, customer insights, analytics and stakeholder feedback to continuously improve capabilities and identify new opportunities.
Ensure capabilities evolve as customer expectations, segment requirements, technology and enterprise strategy change.

Value Realization & Performance

Define measurable outcomes and KPIs for assigned capabilities before investment and delivery.
Establish baselines and targets that enable Manulife to understand the incremental value created through common capabilities.
Track and report capability adoption, utilization, customer outcomes, business impact, operational efficiency and other relevant measures.
Demonstrate how enterprise capabilities contribute to segment and enterprise objectives.
Use performance data and insights to identify opportunities for optimization, further investment or changes in direction.
Develop clear executive-level reporting on capability performance, value realization, roadmap progress and emerging opportunities.
Ensure investment decisions continue to be grounded in measurable customer and business value.

Team & Portfolio Leadership

Lead, coach and develop a small team of product and capability resources, providing clear direction, priorities and opportunities for growth.
Work closely with peer Directors to manage enterprise digital capabilities as an integrated portfolio, aligning strategies, roadmaps, priorities, dependencies and investment decisions across capabilities.
Identify connections and dependencies across capabilities to ensure they evolve together to enable cohesive customer and business experiences.
Share resources and expertise across the capability portfolio where appropriate, dynamically aligning capacity to the highest-value priorities.
Foster consistent product management practices, ways of working and measures of success across the Enterprise Digital Capabilities team.
Create an environment of collaboration, accountability and continuous improvement across the team.

Enterprise Leadership & Communication

Act as an enterprise advocate and subject-matter leader for assigned capabilities.
Build awareness and understanding of available capabilities and the value they can create for markets and businesses.
Communicate capability vision, strategy, roadmap and value through clear and compelling storytelling tailored to executive, business and technical audiences.
Influence across organizational boundaries and build alignment among stakeholders with different priorities.
Bring together business, experience, data and technology perspectives to drive enterprise decisions.
Champion an enterprise-first mindset while recognizing legitimate market, regulatory and customer differences.
Contribute to the broader evolution of Manulife's enterprise digital capability portfolio and Digital Storefront strategy.

Required Qualifications

8+ years of experience in digital product management, capability management, digital strategy, platform strategy or related disciplines, including experience operating at a senior product leadership level.
Demonstrated experience defining product or capability vision, strategy, value propositions and multi-year roadmaps.
Experience taking digital products or capabilities from concept and MVP through launch, adoption and continuous evolution.
Strong understanding of digital platforms and enterprise capabilities, with the ability to work effectively across business, technology, architecture, data and experience teams.
Demonstrated ability to translate business and customer needs into scalable solutions and actionable product priorities.
Experience defining and measuring product or capability outcomes, including adoption, customer, operational and financial metrics.
Strong analytical skills and demonstrated ability to use data, customer insights and performance metrics to inform decisions and identify opportunities.
Demonstrated people leadership experience, including coaching and developing talent, setting priorities and effectively deploying resources across competing priorities.
Demonstrated ability to lead through both direct accountability and influence, building alignment across teams, peers and senior stakeholders in a complex matrixed organization.
Exceptional stakeholder management and influencing skills, with experience navigating complex, matrixed organizations.
Strong executive communication and storytelling skills, with the ability to simplify complex topics and articulate business value.
Demonstrated ability to build alignment across stakeholders with different priorities and requirements.
Demonstrated experience applying AI, GenAI and agentic AI to product and capability strategy, delivery and evolution—identifying and implementing opportunities to improve customer and business outcomes, accelerate delivery and increase productivity.
AI-first approach to ways of working, with demonstrated use of AI in day-to-day practices to improve analysis, research, planning, decision-making, communication and execution, and an expectation to continuously identify new opportunities to embed AI into how the team operates.
Financial services, insurance or wealth management experience is an asset.

What Success Looks Like

The Director, Enterprise Digital Capabilities will ensure Manulife's common capabilities are not simply technology investments—they are enterprise products that solve meaningful customer and business problems, are adopted across the organization and deliver measurable value.
Success means creating a clear line of sight from segment need → enterprise opportunity → capability vision → roadmap → MVP → adoption → measurable value → continuous evolution.
It also means ensuring individual capabilities do not evolve in isolation. Working with peer capability leaders, the Common Capability Collective and segment partners, the Director will help create an integrated enterprise capability portfolio in which roadmaps, investments, dependencies and resources come together to enable more connected customer experiences and accelerate delivery across Manulife.
Ultimately, the role enables Manulife to build once where it makes sense, reuse at scale, continuously improve and maximize the value of our enterprise digital investments.

When You Join Our Team

As part of our global team, we’ll support you in shaping the future you want to see.
We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want.
We’ll recognize and support you in a flexible environment where well-being and inclusion are more than just words.

jobs.title: Director, Model Inference Engineering
jobs.description:
Job Description

Thomson Reuters Labs is the global research and development division of Thomson Reuters. We bring together scientists, engineers, and domain experts to explore emerging technologies and develop state-of-the-art AI products, bridging frontier science with practical application. Labs builds and ships custom models for professional workflows requiring fiduciary-grade AI. The Thomson LLM model family was developed by training leading open-weight models on decades of authoritative Thomson Reuters content, with thousands of hours of subject-matter-expert input. Owning the model layer is how we earn trust in the most regulated, highest-stakes professional workflows.

Mariner, Thomson Reuters' custom inference platform, serves every production call to the Thomson model family and is scaling to new product integrations and business lines. This Director, Model Inference Engineering role leads and grows the team that owns the platform, working with senior technical leadership and a cross-functional team to ensure production footing, cost-tracking, compliance, and capacity planning as we scale. You'll lead the inference-engineering team and partner closely with research and product stakeholders, so the serving stack keeps pace with new model releases and product expansion.

For more on the latest model release, see the Thomson 1.0 Technical Report on Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/spaces/tri-fair-lab/publications/blob/main/Thomson_1_0_Technical_Report.pdf

Key Responsibilities

Grow the inference-engineering team: set the hiring bar, run performance and growth conversations, retain in a competitive market, and build an effective and sustainable operating rhythm (on-call, incident reviews, onboarding) as the system expands internationally.
Own delivery of Mariner's engineering roadmap: work with technical leadership, engineers, and researchers to plan and resource against objectives and key results, driving product integrations and international deployment while balancing cost/latency targets.
Scale Thomson's production footing: drive the ISO 27001 compliance path, deliver clean cost-tracking and attribution for Finance, and run GPU-capacity contingency planning so a capacity change doesn't force downtime or costly parallel running.
Represent inference-engineering tradeoffs (cost vs. latency vs. reliability) to senior leadership and cross-functional partners.
Ensure token-economics benchmarks are produced and published, showing Thomson's cost advantage over closed-model APIs when the numbers support it.

Required Qualifications

Production ML-serving depth. You've led or managed inference infrastructure for large models at real production traffic and scale, not just in a research or prototype setting, with wins delivered by teams you led that you can point to, and the fluency to hire, coach, and defend the work.
Infrastructure and cost ownership. You've owned a cost-attribution or compliance program end to end (control design, evidence collection, external audit such as ISO 27001, SOC 2, or comparable) for a production system on Kubernetes or similar.
Track record building and leading a focused engineering team, ideally growing a team from a handful of engineers rather than inheriting one at scale.
Experience balancing resource constraints. GPU capacity, region availability, and cost are active, managed constraints in this role, not abstractions.
Experience supporting external-facing or customer-facing deployments, not only internal research infrastructure.
Operational excellence in engineering teams and systems.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with common LLM-serving stacks (vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, Triton, SGLang, or similar).
Experience working with research and product stakeholders to define the engineering roadmap of a production system.
Exposure to GPU-cluster capacity planning or multi-region/multi-cloud deployment.
Familiarity with systems development languages (Rust, Go, etc.).
Exposure to a regulated or compliance-heavy production environment.

Even if you don't have all of the above requirements, we encourage you to apply to explore a mutual fit!

This posting is for proactive recruitment purposes and may be used to fill current openings or future vacancies within our organization.

What’s in it For You?

Hybrid Work Model: We’ve adopted a flexible hybrid working environment for our office-based roles while delivering a seamless experience that is digitally and physically connected.
Flexibility & Work-Life Balance: Flex My Way is a set of supportive workplace policies designed to help manage personal and professional responsibilities, whether caring for family, giving back to the community, or finding time to refresh and reset. This builds upon our flexible work arrangements, including work from anywhere for up to 8 weeks per year, empowering employees to achieve a better work-life balance.
Career Development and Growth: By fostering a culture of continuous learning and skill development, we prepare our talent to tackle tomorrow’s challenges and deliver real-world solutions. Our Grow My Way programming and skills-first approach ensures you have the tools and knowledge to grow, lead, and thrive in an AI-enabled future.
Industry Competitive Benefits: We offer comprehensive benefit plans to include flexible vacation, two company-wide Mental Health Days off, access to the Headspace app, retirement savings, tuition reimbursement, employee incentive programs, and resources for mental, physical, and financial wellbeing.
Culture: Globally recognized, award-winning reputation for inclusion and belonging, flexibility, work-life balance, and more. We live by our values: Obsess over our Customers, Compete to Win, Challenge (Y)our Thinking, Act Fast / Learn Fast, and Stronger Together.

jobs.title: Director of Computer Vision
jobs.description:
Company Overview

At Motorola Solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people. We’re a global close-knit community, united by the relentless pursuit to help keep people safer everywhere. We build and connect technologies to help protect people, property and places. Our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. Connect with a career that matters, and help us build a safer future.

Aperçu de l’entreprise

Chez Motorola Solutions, nous pensons que tout commence par nos employés. Nous sommes une communauté mondiale soudée, unie par la volonté incessante de contribuer à la sécurité des personnes partout dans le monde. Nous concevons et connectons des technologies qui contribuent à protéger les personnes, les biens et les infrastructures. Nos solutions favorisent la collaboration essentielle pour améliorer la sécurité des populations, des écoles, des hôpitaux, des entreprises et, finalement, des nations. Connectez-vous à une carrière qui compte et aidez-nous à bâtir un avenir plus sûr.

Department Overview

Motorola Solutions' innovations, products, and services play essential roles in people's lives. Our end-to-end suite of software solutions helps customers manage emergency communications, process video and evidence, and leverage cutting-edge AI-driven analytics for security and operational insights. We are industry leaders in video security and analytics, with solutions deployed in more than 120 countries across diverse environments such as school campuses, transportation systems, healthcare centers, public venues, critical infrastructure, prisons, factories, casinos, airports, financial institutions, government facilities, and retailers. Our AI-powered security solutions integrate advanced video analytics, machine learning, and embedded intelligence to enable proactive threat detection, enhanced situational awareness, and automated decision-making.

Job Description

Job DescriptionThe Director of Computer Vision will drive the technical vision, research and engineering execution for the platform, with focus on the following core areas:

Foundational Research Strategy: Define the long-term research agenda for fundamental computer vision capabilities and drive the culture of scientific excellence.
Technical Vision, Engineering Leadership, and Execution: Provide executive technical leadership to a unified research and engineering organization, defining the technical architecture, strategy, and engineering roadmap for the Computer Vision Platform. Drive execution, ensuring the seamless translation of product requirements into robust technical specifications and successful delivery of next-generation visual intelligence solutions that are highly scalable and align with overall product and business strategy.
Organizational Leadership and Talent Strategy: Manage and scale a unified computer vision research and engineering organization distributed across multiple geographies, overseeing multiple teams, and defining the strategy for recruiting, mentoring, and attracting world-class talent.
End-to-End MLOps and Deployment: Own the entire engineering lifecycle for central, reusable computer vision models and foundational AI infrastructure. This includes establishing best-in-class MLOps practices for scalable training, efficient deployment, continuous monitoring, and performance optimization across edge and cloud environments.
Performance Measurement and Continuous Improvement: Define, implement, and track key technical performance metrics (e.g., latency, throughput, model efficiency, system reliability) to measure engineering success, identify bottlenecks, and drive continuous improvement in execution and delivery.
Technical Innovation and Risk Management: Evaluate and integrate cutting-edge computer vision research and technologies. Proactively identify and mitigate significant technical risks, and lead critical engineering decisions, including build-versus-buy analysis.

Qualifications & Experience

10+ years of technical leadership experience leading computer vision teams and organizations, with a focus on building and deploying enterprise-scale platforms and solutions in production.
Technical Acumen & Deep Expertise: Deep, demonstrable expertise in computer vision, machine learning algorithms, and the end-to-end MLOps lifecycle, including 5+ years of hands-on experience building and optimizing computer vision models or as a computer vision researcher. Proven ability to engage in complex technical discussions, define the architectural vision for central, reusable AI infrastructure and models, and drive technical strategy while managing critical trade-offs.
Executive Technical Strategy & Metrics: Proven experience defining long-term technical vision, engineering strategy, and roadmaps for a large-scale platform. Expertise in defining and implementing technical metrics (e.g., latency, throughput, system reliability, model efficiency) to measure engineering excellence and drive continuous improvement across an organization.
Organizational & People Leadership: Demonstrated ability to manage and scale a unified, distributed engineering and research organization of 50 to 100 people, mentor senior technical talent, and lead multiple teams across different geographies.
Strong Analytical and Research Skills: Hands-on experience driving innovation through foundational research, working with AI performance metrics (e.g., Precision/Recall), real-time video processing, and inference optimization.
Customer-Driven Technical Leadership (Pathfinding): Track record of translating highly ambiguous product concepts and complex customer needs into clear, executable technical roadmaps and architectural specifications.
Start-up Mentality & Agility: Experience in a start-up or fast-paced environment is highly valued, demonstrating high ownership, bias for action, comfort with ambiguity, and the ability to drive 0-to-1 product development with limited resources.
Domain Knowledge: Experience in public safety, security-focused software (e.g., video security, evidence management), mission-critical systems, or emergency communications is a plus.

Target Base Salary Range: $230,000 CAD - $270,000 CAD

Consistent with Motorola Solutions values and applicable law, we provide the following information to promote pay transparency and equity. Pay within this range varies and depends on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The actual offer will be based on the individual candidate.

Note: Candidates must reside in a Canada within the Eastern (EST) or Central (CST) Time Zone.

Basic Requirements

Bachelors degree with 10+ years of technical leadership experience leading computer vision teams and organizations.

Travel Requirements

10-25%

Relocation Provided

None

Position Type

Experienced

Referral Payment Plan

No

Motorola Solutions is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status or any other legally-protected characteristic.

We are proud of our people-first and community-focused culture, empowering every Motorolan to be their most authentic self and to do their best work to deliver on the promise of a safer world. We’re committed to providing an inclusive and accessible recruiting experience for candidates with disabilities, or other physical or mental health conditions. To request an accommodation, please complete this Reasonable Accommodations Form so we can assist you.

Motorola Solutions adopte, favorise et promeut les principes de diversité, d’équité et d’inclusion. Nous encourageons et accueillons les candidatures de toutes les personnes qualifiées, quelles que soient leur race, origines ethnique, religion ou croyance, orientation sexuelle, identité et expression sexuelle, statut d’anciens combattants ou tout autre statut protégé par la Loi.

Nous sommes fiers de notre culture axée sur les personnes et les communautés, encourageant ainsi chaque Motorolan d’être la version la plus authentique de lui-même dans ses responsabilités afin de tenir la promesse d’un monde plus sécuritaire.

jobs.title: Senior Director, SEM
jobs.description:
Please note that we will never request payment or bank account information at any stage of the recruitment process. As we continue to grow our teams, we urge you to be cautious of fraudulent job postings or recruitment activities that misuse our company name and information. Please protect your personal information during any recruitment process. While Monks may contact potential candidates via LinkedIn, all applications must be submitted through our official website (monks.com/careers).

About The Role

Search has changed more in the last two years than in the previous ten. Ads now run inside AI Overviews and AI Mode, keyword lists are giving way to AI Max and Performance Max, and conversational platforms like ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot have opened as paid channels. We need a leader who sees that shift as an opportunity, not a threat.

As Senior Director, Paid Search, you will report to the VP of Paid Search and lead a group within the practice, owning performance, client relationships and talent across your book of business. You will lead a team from Account Managers through Directors, serve as paid search lead on one or two client accounts, and help define how Monks wins in an AI-first search landscape.

This is a senior leadership role: you run your accounts and team day to day, and support the VP and Group Directors in shaping the practice. Success means:

Your clients grow profitably, and we can prove the incremental impact of their search investment.
Your team operates at the frontier of AI-driven search, with clear points of view our clients and partners seek out.
Your book of business grows, through organic expansion on existing accounts and contributions to new business wins.
Your people develop into the next generation of search leaders.

Responsibilities

Strategy and AI leadership

Bring the practice's vision and roadmap, set by the VP and Group Directors, to life as strategy for your accounts, including how we plan, buy and measure across Google, Microsoft and emerging AI-driven ad surfaces.
Drive adoption of AI-powered campaign types, including AI Max for Search and Shopping, Performance Max, and AI Overviews and AI Mode placements. Build the playbooks, guardrails and testing frameworks the team uses to deploy them responsibly.
Shift the team's craft from manual execution to input governance: first-party data and conversion signals, feed quality, creative assets, brand guidelines and natural-language steering tools.
Evaluate and pilot new conversational ad channels, such as ChatGPT Ads and Microsoft Copilot placements, and advise clients on when and how to test them.
Author and publish agency POVs on the future of search, and support in award submissions and case studies.

Client leadership

Serve as paid search channel lead on one or two client accounts, owning search strategy, performance, day-to-day client communication and the account roadmap, while staying close to the platforms and the data.
Translate client business goals (revenue, profit, LTV, pipeline) into search strategies, and present them to VP- and Director-level client stakeholders, supporting C-suite presentations alongside the Group Director or VP.
Act as an escalation point and senior advisor across your group's accounts, stepping in to protect performance and relationships.
Partner with cross-channel leads (social, programmatic, retail media, SEO/GEO, analytics) on holistic media plans, including forecasting, budget allocation, testing and reporting.

Measurement and accountability

Champion measurement beyond platform-reported ROAS. Use incrementality testing, geo experiments and marketing mix modeling to prove and grow the value of search.
Ensure the team can explain performance clearly when platforms report less granular data, for example where AI Mode results are blended into campaign totals.
Own forecasting and scenario planning for your book of business.

People and practice leadership

Lead, develop and retain a team spanning Analysts through Directors. Set clear expectations, deliver regular feedback and run performance reviews.
Contribute to hiring, promotion and resourcing decisions for your team.
Upskill the team on AI tools and automation, so they spend less time on manual work and more on strategy, analysis and client value.
Build a culture of experimentation, knowledge sharing and accountability. Contribute to department-wide training and career frameworks.

Growth and commercial impact

Support new business pitches across SEM, Shopping and Performance Max, owning the search strategy component under the direction of the Group Director or VP.
Identify organic growth opportunities on existing accounts, including scope expansion, new markets and new channels.
Monitor account health and team utilization for your accounts, and flag scope, staffing and pricing needs to the VP.
Work closely with Google, Microsoft and other platform partners on beta tests, best practices and client planning.
Join in-person team meetings, client presentations and industry events as business needs arise, typically 1-2 times per quarter.

About You

The essentials:

8+ years of paid search experience, including senior leadership at an agency or in-house growth team.
3+ years of people management with at least 2 direct reports, ideally including Managers or Associate Directors.
Deep, hands-on expertise in Google Ads and Microsoft Advertising, including AI Max, Performance Max, Shopping and Smart Bidding.
Experience directing search portfolios of $1MM+ in monthly ad spend, with accountability for business outcomes, not just platform metrics.
A strong, well-reasoned POV on the future of search: AI-generated results, conversational ad surfaces, automation, and what they mean for agency value.
Working knowledge of modern measurement: conversion tracking and first-party data, incrementality and geo testing, and how MMM informs budget decisions.
A track record of presenting strategy to VP- and Director-level client stakeholders and large internal teams, with exposure to C-suite audiences.
Commercial awareness, including forecasting, scoping and spotting growth opportunities on existing accounts.
4-year college degree or equivalent work experience.

Not a Must, But a Plus

Hands-on testing of conversational ad platforms such as ChatGPT Ads or Microsoft Copilot ad formats.
Experience across YouTube, Demand Gen and App campaigns
Experience with bid management and reporting platforms such as SA360, Skai or Marin, plus BI tools like Looker or Tableau.
Familiarity with marketing mix modeling tools such as Google Meridian, or with designing geo-based incrementality experiments.
Experience leading strategy across B2B, D2C and B2C clients in multiple verticals, including regulated categories such as finance or healthcare.
Experience using AI and automation tools (scripts, LLM-based workflows, agentic tools) to scale team productivity.

This role is subject to our Return to Office (RTO) policy. If you reside within a commutable distance of one of our office locations, you will be expected to work from the office a set number of days per week. The specific details, including the number of required office days, will be in accordance with the company’s then-current RTO policy, which is subject to change from time to time.

Monks has provided a compensation range that represents its good faith estimate of what Monks may pay for the position at the time of posting. Monks may ultimately pay more or less than the posted compensation range. The salary offered to the selected candidate will be determined based on job-related factors, but not based on a candidate’s sex or any other protected status.

Salary Range$214,000—$240,000 CAD

About Monks

Monks is the global, digital-first, data-driven, unitary operating brand of S4Capital plc, where our culture centers on how we show up for the work and for one another. That begins with the commitment to strive for mastery—taking deep pride in our craft and creating work that sets the bar. In everyday execution, we drive momentum by choosing bold action rather than waiting for certainty. Above all, our teams are stronger together, bringing diverse perspectives into a unified team that communicates with clarity, trust, and mutual respect.

This commitment to craft and innovation translates directly into widespread industry acclaim: Monks was named a Contender in The Forrester Wave™: Global Marketing Services and a leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Global Digital Marketing Agencies. It ranks among Cannes Lions' Top 10 Creative Companies (2022-25) and remains the only partner featured in AdExchanger’s Programmatic Power Players list every year (2020-24). Named Adweek’s first AI Agency of the Year (2023) and The One Show’s inaugural AI Pioneer Organization (2025), Monks was also awarded Business Intelligence Group’s 2026 Excellence in Artificial Intelligence Award in the Human-Machine Interaction Team category. Additionally, Monks.Flow earned AI-based Marketing Solution of the Year at the 2026 AI Breakthrough Awards and a 2026 Global Generative AI Award in the Agentic Marketing Innovation category. Finally, Monks achieved a record-breaking number of FWAs and continues to hold the most of any partner.

We are an equal-opportunity employer committed to building a respectful and empowering work environment for all people to freely express themselves amongst colleagues who embrace diversity in all respects. Including fresh voices and unique points of view in all aspects of our business not only creates an environment where we can all grow and thrive but also increases our potential to produce work that better represents—and resonates with—the world around us.

The Vice President of Business Development is responsible for growing CGI’s business with one of Canada’s large banks in Toronto. Embedded within the client’s financial services environment, this management role leads a team of more than 60 CGI Partners and brings together client relationship leadership, business development, engagement oversight, and operational performance.  

  

The successful candidate brings a strong background in solutions\-led IT consulting and can connect the client’s business priorities with practical technology and consulting solutions. They understand the Canadian banking sector and can guide opportunities from discovery and solution shaping through proposal and delivery. Areas of focus may include digital and technology modernization, data and AI, cybersecurity and resilience, risk, regulatory change, and operational transformation.  

  

Work location: This role requires a minimum of five days per week at the client’s downtown Toronto office and/or CGI’s downtown Toronto office. This requirement may change at any time.

**Your future duties and responsibilities**


Engagement and Mission Governance  

* Oversee the successful delivery of client engagements and the evolution of end\-to\-end service offerings.
* Coordinate and monitor the quality of services delivered to clients.
* Apply the CGI Project Management Framework (CPMF), including conducting regular reviews of project and operational performance with CGI Partners and clients.
* Collaborate with internal CGI partners to deliver integrated, end\-to\-end services to clients.

  

Client Relationships and Business Development  

* Own and strengthen relationships with assigned clients.
* Build and maintain relationships with existing and prospective clients.
* Lead and manage business development activities.

  

Team and Partner Leadership  

* Oversee the assignment, recruitment, and career development of team members.
* Develop the team’s capabilities and expertise to meet client needs and respond to market changes.
* Support the health and well\-being of CGI Partners.

  

Business and Operations Management  

* Lead the team to achieve budget, revenue, and profitability targets.
* Contribute to strategic and operational planning.
**Required qualifications to be successful in this role**

* Significant experience in solutions\-led IT consulting, developing technology and consulting solutions around clients’ business needs.
* strong track record of growing strategic client accounts and leading business development in the financial services sector.
* Experience working with large Canadian banks, with an understanding of their business priorities, operating environments, and risk, security, and regulatory considerations.
* Demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships with senior business and technology executives and influence decisions across complex organizations.
* Experience leading consultative sales and pursuits, from opportunity identification and solution shaping through proposal development, negotiation, and handoff to delivery.

\#LI\-JOE13**Together, as owners, let’s turn meaningful insights into action.**  

  

Life at CGI is rooted in ownership, teamwork, respect and belonging. Here, you’ll reach your full potential because…  

  

You are invited to be an owner from day 1 as we work together to bring our Dream to life. That’s why we call ourselves CGI Partners rather than employees. We benefit from our collective success and actively shape our company’s strategy and direction.

jobs.title: Director Application, Data & Integration
jobs.description:
Director, Application, Data & Integration

Location:
Vancouver, BC

Salary Range:
$159,000 - $215,000/year

Ready to take the next step in your career with a firm that values innovation, collaboration, continuous improvement, and delivering exceptional client experiences?

Smythe LLP is seeking an experienced and strategic Director, Application, Data & Integration
to join our growing Digital Business Services (DBS) team. This is an exceptional opportunity for a technology leader who is passionate about building modern application, data, and integration capabilities while helping shape the future of technology across the firm.

This role is based in our Vancouver office, with the opportunity to work in a hybrid environment following the completion of the probationary period.

The Opportunity

The Director, Application, Data & Integration is responsible for building and leading Smythe’s enterprise application, data and integration capabilities.

The role provides technical leadership across the firm’s application landscape and establishes the engineering disciplines required to deliver secure, reliable and maintainable solutions. A key mandate is to transform how the development team works through AI-assisted engineering, automation and modern DevOps practices, driving significant improvements in development productivity and delivery speed.

The Director will also build Smythe’s data engineering and analytics capabilities and lead the integration architecture that connects the firm’s core systems. This is a capability-building leadership role supporting Smythe’s Connected Firm strategy and continued technology modernization.

In This Role, You Will

Application Strategy & Architecture

Provide technical leadership and architecture oversight across Smythe’s enterprise application landscape.
Establish application architecture, development and lifecycle standards.
Guide solution design for new applications and major enhancements.
Partner with Product Owners to translate business requirements into sustainable technical solutions.
Provide technical oversight of implementation partners and third-party development resources.

Engineering Discipline, DevOps & AI-Assisted Development

Build and mature Smythe’s software engineering practices, including development standards, source control, code review, testing and documentation.
Establish CI/CD, environment and release-management capabilities to enable controlled and repeatable deployments.
Embed application security and secure development practices throughout the software development lifecycle.
Lead adoption of AI-assisted development across the engineering team to accelerate development, testing, documentation and delivery.
Drive significant, multi-fold improvements in engineering productivity while maintaining appropriate security, quality and human oversight.
Strengthen automated testing, application monitoring and overall technical quality.

Integration & Connected Firm Architecture

Own Smythe’s integration architecture and technical integration standards.
Establish consistent approaches for APIs, interfaces and system-to-system data exchange.
Ensure integrations across the application landscape are secure, resilient, supportable and appropriately monitored.
Maintain an architectural view of how applications, integrations and data work together to support the Connected Firm.

Dynamics & DPO Technical Leadership

Provide technical leadership for Smythe’s transition to Dynamics 365 Project Operations and the broader Dynamics platform.
Work with Product Owners and implementation partners on architecture, integration and technical design.
Build sufficient internal capability to support, maintain and extend the platform over time.
Ensure Dynamics development follows Smythe’s engineering, security and application-management standards.

Data Management, Engineering & Analytics

Develop Smythe’s enterprise data architecture and technical data-management approach.
Build data engineering capabilities to integrate, transform and make trusted data available across the firm.
Establish approaches for master data, data quality, lineage and technical data controls.
Build and lead the firm’s emerging data engineering and data analytics capabilities.
Enable consistent enterprise reporting and analytics.
Partner with Product Owners and business stakeholders on data ownership and governance.

People & Capability Leadership

Build and lead capabilities spanning application development, integration, QA, data engineering and analytics.
Develop technical staff and establish clear engineering expectations and practices.
Determine the appropriate balance of internal capabilities, implementation partners and specialized contractors.
Build a culture focused on technical quality, accountability, continuous improvement and effective use of AI-assisted development.

Security, Risk & Operational Partnership

Partner with IT Operations to ensure applications and integrations meet Smythe’s security, resilience and operational requirements.
Embed security-by-design into application architecture and engineering practices.
Ensure solutions incorporate appropriate access, data protection, monitoring and operational support requirements.

What You Bring

Progressive technology leadership experience across enterprise applications, software engineering, integration and data.
Demonstrated experience building or maturing software engineering and DevOps practices.
Strong understanding of modern application architecture, APIs, integrations and cloud platforms.
Practical experience with CI/CD, automated testing, secure development and application lifecycle management.
Experience adopting modern development practices and AI-assisted development tools to materially improve engineering productivity and software delivery.
Experience with data architecture, data engineering, analytics or business intelligence.
Experience leading multidisciplinary technical teams and external technology partners.
Microsoft technology and Dynamics 365 experience is strongly preferred.
Strong communication skills with the ability to work effectively with both technical teams and business leaders.

Leadership Characteristics

The Successful Candidate Will

Be a builder, comfortable creating and scaling capabilities that do not yet fully exist.
Bring strong engineering discipline while remaining pragmatic about business delivery.
Be forward-looking in the use of AI and automation to fundamentally improve how technology is delivered.
Set high technical standards without introducing unnecessary complexity or bureaucracy.
Develop people and internal capability while using external partners effectively.
Communicate complex technical concepts clearly to business and executive stakeholders.

What Smythe Offers

At Smythe, we strive to offer a competitive salary and benefits package that accurately reflects our people’s values and ambitions. We prioritize professional development and have fostered a dynamic and progressive work culture. As a firm, our focus is on collaboration and building personal relationships with clients, mentors and peers. Learn more about what you can expect from Life at Smythe by visiting our website (www.smythecpa.com) and following us on Instagram (@lifeatsmythe) and LinkedIn (@Smythe LLP).

We thank you for your interest in joining Smythe! We will get back to you regarding any updates to your application.

jobs.title: SOX Director - ITGC
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a SOX Director – ITGC based in Canada .

The SOX Director – ITGC will lead the strategy, design, and oversight of the enterprise IT SOX compliance program, serving as the senior technical authority for IT controls. This is a hands-on leadership role covering IT General Controls (ITGCs), IT Application Controls (ITACs), and controls related to private key management and digital asset custody. Operating in a complex, rapidly evolving financial technology environment, the successful candidate will build scalable control frameworks that support modern cloud infrastructure, continuous deployment, and blockchain-native systems without unnecessarily slowing engineering teams. The role requires close collaboration with Finance, Engineering, Security, Infrastructure, Internal Audit, and external auditors. It also carries significant executive visibility, including responsibility for communicating control risks, remediation progress, and the organization's overall IT control posture to senior leadership and the Audit Committee.

Accountabilities

Own the enterprise IT SOX strategy and roadmap, covering ITGCs, ITACs, and digital asset and private key management controls across relevant entities and jurisdictions.
Develop and maintain the IT SOX control framework, including scoping methodologies, risk assessments, control design standards, testing approaches, and evidence requirements.
Determine the applications, infrastructure, wallet and custody systems, third-party providers, and service-organization dependencies that fall within the SOX program's scope.
Design practical, effective controls that align with modern engineering environments, including cloud infrastructure, continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD), and infrastructure as code.
Establish standards for management testing and evidence quality, oversee co-sourced and matrixed resources, and review the quality and consistency of their work.
Introduce AI-enabled workflows, continuous controls monitoring, and data analytics to improve assurance efficiency and move beyond periodic manual testing.
Own SOX control design and coverage across the complete private key lifecycle, including key generation, storage, access, signing and approval workflows, rotation, backup, recovery, and retirement.
Assess controls over digital asset custody architectures, including hardware security modules (HSMs), multi-party computation (MPC), multi-signature arrangements, and hot, warm, and cold wallet structures.
Evaluate segregation of duties, quorum and approval requirements, privileged access, and other safeguards within key management and custody environments.
Assess how private key and custody controls support the existence, completeness, and safeguarding of customer and corporate digital assets, including their financial reporting implications.
Evaluate controls over on-chain and off-chain transaction processing, wallet-to-ledger reconciliations, blockchain data dependencies, and relationships with third-party custodians and service organizations.
Monitor emerging digital asset risks and adapt the SOX control framework as products, blockchain networks, and custody models evolve.
Lead the assessment of control deficiencies, including root cause analysis, severity and pervasiveness assessments, and recommendations for classification as control deficiencies, significant deficiencies, or material weaknesses.
Own remediation strategies for outstanding ITGC and key management findings, driving accountability and timely resolution with Engineering, Security, and Infrastructure leaders.
Escalate significant control gaps and remediation delays to senior leadership and report progress to the Audit Committee when required.
Coordinate with Internal Audit to ensure remediated controls are appropriately documented and ready for independent validation.
Serve as the senior SOX advisor to the CFO, CISO, CTO, Controller, and Audit Committee on IT control posture, emerging risks, and remediation priorities.
Lead external auditor engagement on IT matters, including audit strategy, scoping and reliance decisions, walkthroughs, and resolution of disagreements.
Advise Engineering and Security leaders by translating audit and compliance requirements into practical technical and operational control decisions.
Collaborate with Internal Audit, Enterprise Risk Management (ERM), business process SOX leaders, and co-sourced providers to coordinate coverage across the broader assurance program.
Mentor SOX and risk professionals, strengthening technical expertise and raising the overall quality of the function.

Requirements

Professional experience: 10+ years of experience in SOX compliance, IT audit, internal audit, or external audit, with deep ITGC expertise and a demonstrated record of leading enterprise-scale programs.
Mandatory crypto expertise: Direct, hands-on experience designing, assessing, or auditing controls related to cryptocurrency private key management, wallet infrastructure, signing workflows, digital asset custody, and asset safeguarding. This is an essential requirement.
Industry background: Experience in a cryptocurrency exchange, digital asset custodian, fintech, payments company, or similarly complex and rapidly evolving technology environment.
Certifications: CISA and CPA certifications are required. Candidates holding one certification and actively pursuing the other may also be considered.
SOX and audit frameworks: Expert knowledge of ITGC frameworks, SOX Section 404, COSO, COBIT, and PCAOB standards, with the ability to make and defend decisions involving control scope, audit reliance, and deficiency classification.
Technical understanding: Strong knowledge of systems architecture, databases, cloud infrastructure, deployment pipelines, and the technical environments supporting enterprise applications.
Financial reporting awareness: Ability to connect ITGC or private key management control failures to business process controls, financial reporting risks, and potential financial statement impacts.
Auditor and executive engagement: Experience managing relationships with external auditors, with Big Four experience preferred, and presenting control matters to Audit Committees and senior executives.
International experience: Experience working across multiple legal entities, jurisdictions, or complex organizational structures.
Leadership and communication: Strong stakeholder management, mentoring, and influencing skills, with the ability to establish credibility with both technical engineering teams and senior Finance leaders.
Preferred program experience: Experience establishing or scaling an IT SOX program in a growth-stage organization or a company entering its first year of SOX compliance.
Preferred technical knowledge: Familiarity with CI/CD processes, GitLab or comparable version-control platforms, and cloud environments such as AWS and Google Cloud Platform (GCP).
Third-party assurance: Familiarity with SOC 1 and SOC 2 reliance arrangements, third-party custodians, service providers, and proof-of-reserves or similar attestations.
Compliance technology: Experience with audit and governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platforms such as AuditBoard or Workiva is an asset.
Emerging technologies: Familiarity with AI-assisted compliance tools and an interest in adopting new technologies to improve audit and assurance processes.

Benefits

Remote work: Full-time remote position, with Canada included among the eligible locations.
Annual target salary: USD $116,600–$259,700. The advertised range is a target annual salary range and may vary according to skills, experience, and the scope of the role.
Additional compensation: Eligibility for additional compensation through bonus and equity programs.
Wellness allowance: Additional wellness support is included in the compensation package.
Healthcare and retirement benefits: Medical, dental, vision, and 401(k) benefits are listed for eligible U.S. employees only; these should not be assumed to apply to Canadian employees.
Compensation flexibility: Final compensation is determined based on relevant experience, skills, and role responsibilities.
Global collaboration: Opportunity to work with international teams across Finance, Engineering, Security, and digital asset infrastructure.
Professional impact: Senior-level ownership of a complex SOX program, with direct exposure to executive leadership, external auditors, and emerging digital asset control challenges.
