What we are building
 Mimica is an AI-powered process intelligence platform enabling enterprises and individuals to reclaim their most precious resource: time. We've all seen repetitive tasks and redundant processes quietly drain productivity and creativity. Not because companies don’t want to become more efficient, but because they don’t know where to start.
 Mimica automatically analyzes your team’s work, then generates the AI agents to execute it. Our software turns everyday work into data-backed decisions, helping companies remove process bottlenecks, automate the right tasks, and upskill teams with precision and confidence.
 We’ve raised $26 million in Series B financing and are scaling fast. Backed by investors including Khosla Ventures and Paladin Capital, our proprietary AI technology is trusted by Fortune 500 companies to accelerate transformation. Mimica is recognized as a Top 100 AI Start-up by Accel and an industry Leader by the Everest Group.

 Our team 
 Behind our platform is a team of exceptionally talented people, remote-first and globally distributed across 16+ countries. We're looking for curious, collaborative people excited to solve complex problems. You'll join a fast-paced environment built on high ownership, bottom-up thinking, and transparent, open communication – helping some of the world's leading organizations transform the way work gets done with AI.

 Your mission 

 Mimica is growing fast, and so is the demand on our Platform Team. As Head of Platform, you will lead a lean but highly capable team that is the backbone of every engineering squad in the company, and you will own the infrastructure strategy, including all AI infrastructure, as we scale.
 The Platform team services the entire engineering organisation: keeping environments healthy, unblocking teams, building the infrastructure that lets everyone else move faster, and working with teams regarding SRE topics and developer experience too. As you work with us, the role will develop into designing Mimica’s infrastructure strategy at scale. The team has 4 engineers today, around 6 by the end of the year, and 10+ in 2027, so the role has the potential to grow into a “manager of managers” level as the company grows.
 This is a role with real scope: expanding to multi-region and physically separated database environments, supporting Mimica’s first installable infrastructure component for enterprise, and owning FinOps. One day you are defining the standard menu of deployment options for enterprise customers, the next you are in a security review or an architecture decision on AI infrastructure.
 We are looking for leaders with either an application development or a systems/infrastructure background.
 What matters more than your origin story is your hands-on credibility with Kubernetes, IaC, and cloud platforms, your ability to lead engineers and other leaders, and your ability to collaborate closely with Product, ML, Security, Sales and Customer Success. If you want to work in a place where your contributions are visible, your scope is broad, and the problems are real, this is the role for you.

 Part of your day-to-day 

 Own Mimica's infrastructure strategy and the platform roadmap across all products, with the final call on cloud architecture, deployment models, infra vendors and platform standards.

 Lead and grow the Platform team: Manage existing Platform and SREs, plan headcount, set goals and metrics, and design the sub-team split (Cloud & Developer Platform, Reliability & SRE, AI Infrastructure) as the team grows.

 Own all AI infrastructure, including training and serving infra, MLOps tooling, Vertex and model access.

 Maintain Mimica’s DevEx culture - improve agency for product teams without compromising on compliance, create paved roads for deployments, and identify pain points as they arise.

 Own the infra and LLM budget, forecast and unit economics, including cost attribution by product and customer and the GCP relationship.

 Own reliability across engineering: SLOs, on-call model, incident process, postmortems, DR testing and capacity planning.

 Own the CI/CD and developer platform, infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, ArgoCD, Crossplane) and observability standards (Honeycomb, Grafana, Loki).

 Work with the Platform PM, your peer, to define client needs and turn them into the platform roadmap.

 Act as the named technical owner for infrastructure in enterprise deals and security reviews, joining high-stakes sales and client calls and coaching your team to take the rest.

 Guide the craft mentors for infrastructure, MLOps and Python engineering, and set engineering-wide standards for reliability, on-call, CI/CD and craft.

 Report monthly platform health and costs to leadership, and lead the infrastructure part of technical due diligence.

 Requirements 

 Proven experience leading engineers, ideally including managing a team lead or other managers, and growing a team through hiring and sub-team design.

 Solid hands-on experience with Kubernetes, whether on GKE (preferred), EKS, OnPrem, or another managed Kubernetes service, across multiple regions.

 Proven experience with infrastructure-as-code as a core part of your platform, such as Terraform, and with ArgoCD or a comparable GitOps tool.

 A track record in owning reliability: setting SLOs and SLAs, running on-call, leading incident response and postmortems, and testing disaster recovery.

 Observability experience with at least one major platform: Honeycomb, Datadog, Grafana, or New Relic.

 Comfortable with code, and able to review architecture and prototypes hands-on.

 Experience owning an infrastructure budget, including cloud cost attribution, forecasting and cloud-provider relationships.

 Experience designing deployment models for enterprise customers (single tenant, regional, data residency) and supporting security reviews and contracted SLAs.

 Background in startups or scale-ups: you are used to ambiguity, moving fast, and wearing multiple hats.

 Strong communication and collaboration skills: you can translate infrastructure complexity into clear language for engineers, executives and clients, and you know when to say no to bespoke requests.

 Bonus / Nice to have 

 Familiarity with Crossplane, or a similar product like Config Connector.

 Experience with Temporal for workflow orchestration.

 Security and compliance experience, particularly supporting SOC 2.

 Experience supporting a funding round, including technical due diligence.

 What we offer
 💰 Generous compensation + stock options - aligned with our internal framework, market data, and individual skills.

 🧘‍♀️ Health & retirement benefits
 📖 Annual learning & development budget
 🌴 Annual workaways and regular virtual & in-person socials
 🌍 Opportunity to contribute to groundbreaking projects that shape the future of work

 Note: Some benefits may vary depending on location and role

jobs.title: Chief of Staff
jobs.description:
This role is ideally based in Toronto with hybrid working in our offices but we are open to candidates in other parts of Canada. There is some travel involved in the role, trips to Australia once per quarter and other ad hoc trips as required.

Fleet Space Technologies is a frontier technology company building the clearest 3D understanding of a mineral system before the next capital, targeting or drilling decision. Led by high-quality hard-rock seismic, Fleet integrates geology, geophysics, drilling data, geochemistry and mineralogy with geoscience expertise and machine learning, turning complex subsurface data into actionable insight.

We're looking for a Chief of Staff to report to & assist our COO who is based in Toronto to remove bottlenecks, improve operational processes, create GTM strategies for new regions and anything else that helps Fleet and our COO reach their goals.

You'll be the person Fleet Space looks to when we need to launch in a country we don't yet operate in, and the person who builds the planning rhythm, shared definitions and capacity forecasts that let us scale with rigour across the globe.

This is a builder's seat, not a VP role with a large organisation underneath it. You'll lead a small team of two to four and work with line leaders of every department and you'll personally do much of the work rather than just design it.

You'll start with training & onboarding on the ground in Australia, on the factory floor and out on a live survey in the field to understand our operations from end to end.

Adelaide, South Australia is our Global HQ, so some early mornings and late evenings are common but you are also given a lot of autonomy and flexibility around where and when you work best.

What you'll do

Build and own our country entry playbook: customs clearance and temporary imports, local agent and partner selection, entity versus partner decisions, permits, visas, crew mobilisation and field HSE
Know when a country needs a partner, when it needs an entity, and when we should walk away
Work alongside our joint venture partners on delivery, without owning their commercials
Connect manufacturing, supply chain, deployment and refurbishment as one system, connecting factory output to field demand so we are never building blind or short
Own the Geode refurbishment loop: turn time, attrition, yield and the units that get stranded in country
Set our spares, consumables and logistics strategy across regions, and manage supplier and contract manufacturer performance where it touches delivery
Design and personally run the COO's operating & reporting cadence: annual, quarterly, monthly and weekly planning, with a clear owner for every input
Create one shared definition of a survey, a deployment, a delay and a completion, and run operating reviews that surface the truth early rather than confirm it late
Build the demand and capacity model for crews, Geodes, satellites, field engineers and geoscience interpretation, turning the commercial pipeline into headcount and hardware plans our leadership can plan against
Track forecast against actual every quarter and keep making it better

What we are looking for

Chief of Staff or similar roles with a background in Operations, ideally within startup/scale up tech companies with a hardware component or mining/mineral exploration industry
Strengths in Forecasting, Executive level reporting, GTM strategy development & building out various models, systems and frameworks
Experience in companies with hardware products with responsibilities across manufacturing, supply chain, deployment, service or refurbishment
A self starter, someone that can identify and prioritise the work rather than wait for a task to be given to them
8+ years in senior operations leadership positions, with recent experience executing & delivering projects yourself rather than only overseeing others but capable of people management as well
A background in mining, mining services, geophysical survey, drilling, oilfield services or resources technology is a plus
Experience across at least three of Latin America, the Middle East, Africa, Central Asia and Australia
Start/Scale-up experience, you understand the pace and variety in the role and don’t need or want the slow corporate world
Willingness to travel globally
Professional fluency in a second language - particularly Spanish, French or Arabic - would be a real plus

About Fleet Space

Fleet Space Technologies is an Australian frontier technology company building the clearest 3D understanding of a mineral system before the next capital, targeting or drilling decision: led by high-quality hard-rock seismic, Fleet integrates geology, geophysics, drilling data, geochemistry and mineralogy with geoscience expertise and machine learning, turning complex subsurface data into actionable insight.

Founded in 2015 in Adelaide, South Australia, Fleet Space Technologies set out to bring the engineering rigour, connected hardware and computational power of the space industry to help solve mining’s hardest problems, and deliver drill predictions that stand up against ground truth.

Company Culture

As a company, we are revolutionising the exploration of new worlds with advanced space technology to build a more prosperous future for humanity.

As a culture, we are ambitious, innovative, and collaborative and we put our customers first in everything that we do.

Our company values guide us to our North Star of ambitious, collaborative success: AD ASTRA ("To the Stars!")

Add Value:
Obsessively add value for our customers
Drive Excellence:
Benchmark against the best
Agile Action:
Take Action. Independent, fast, frugal action
Seek Truth:
Be curious. Explore
Take Responsibility:
Make decisions and own them
Radical Ideas:
We are unique. We do things differently
Always Deliver:
We always find a way to get it done on time

Our Benefits Include

We have an extremely flexible work culture, with a mix of onsite, hybrid and remote workers who take time for school runs, exercise and appointments. With global teams hours can vary butiIt's about getting the work done, not what time you are at your desk.
Equity (ESOP) grants.
20 days of annual leave + 10 extra Wellness days per year.
Learning budgets.
Access to confidential Psychologist appointments via our Employee Assistance Program.
Plenty of opportunity to be part of an amazing STEM program to create the next generation of explorers.

jobs.title: Director of Product, Operations and Servicing
jobs.description:
EQ Bank is changing how Canadians experience banking, and how we serve and protect our customers is central to that mission. As Director, Product Management – Operations \& Servicing, you will set the product vision for two critical areas: Care \& Servicing (customer care tooling, agentic AI servicing, CRM, and front\- and back\-office operations) and Risk (fraud and AML systems and controls).



You will lead a team of product leaders, owning domain strategy, prioritization, and executive representation while coaching your Leads to deliver measurable outcomes. You will also be the product leader for two of the most significant workstreams in the EQ × PCF integration, customer servicing and fraud/AML. Your work will directly shape how customers are served and protected as the business grows.



### **Main Activities**



In this role, you will:



1\. Set the strategy for Operations \& Servicing


* Build and evolve a product strategy across Operations \& Servicing and Risk with a 12\+ month planning horizon, aligned to EQ Bank's overall strategy.
* Lead quarterly and annual planning, balancing investment across run\-the\-bank work, AI\-driven optimization, regulatory obligations, and strategic initiatives.
* Represent the domain in leadership and planning forums with clear, outcome\-focused updates on progress, risks, and impact.


2\. Lead and grow high\-performing product teams


* Manage Lead Product Managers, each leading a team of Product Managers, subject\-matter experts, and contract partners.
* Coach your team through regular 1:1s and development plans, and build their capability as people leaders as their teams grow.
* Set the standard for how Product partners with Design and Engineering, and build a culture of collaboration, ownership, and accountability for results.
* Build bench strength and succession, including onboarding Product Managers new to the space.


3\. Deliver measurable outcomes


* Keep high\-priority work on track, re\-prioritizing around customer value and business impact.
* Partner with Engineering and Analytics on the metrics that matter (e.g., containment, CSAT, AHT, fraud loss rate, SLA adherence) and act quickly when trends move the wrong way.
* Ensure a stable, high\-quality experience for customers and agents across care tooling, CRM, back\-office tools, and fraud/AML systems.


4\. Partner across the bank


* Build strong relationships with Legal, Compliance, AML, Security, Fraud, and Risk, engaging them early and balancing regulatory requirements with customer and business needs.
* Serve as the escalation point for complex trade\-offs that span multiple domains or functions.


5\. Lead the domain's integration workstreams


* Own product accountability for the customer servicing and fraud/AML workstreams of the EQ × PCF integration, from priorities and requirements through sequencing and delivery.
* Guide your teams through discovery, tooling decisions, and migration planning, resolving cross\-workstream trade\-offs while keeping integration and day\-to\-day delivery on track.
### **Knowledge/Skill Requirements (What you bring)**


* 10–15 years of progressive product management experience, including leading managers and senior individual contributors
* A track record of delivering measurable customer and business impact on products with large customer bases.
* Experience owning strategy and outcomes for a multi\-team domain, turning company strategy into a 12\-month\+ roadmap across more than one product area.
* Hands\-on experience or strong working knowledge of customer care/contact\-centre technology (CRM, agentic AI, self\-serve) or fraud/AML operations and controls is a strong asset.
* Strong business and technical acumen, with the ability to navigate complex dependencies across systems, vendors, and stakeholders.
* Excellent executive communication and influencing skills, including aligning senior stakeholders and control\-function partners.
* Data fluency: you build and interpret metrics and dashboards and turn insight into action.
* A people leader who hires, coaches, and develops lead\-level product talent, builds succession, and shapes a strong team culture.


Nice to have


* Experience in banking, fintech, or another regulated, high\-trust industry.
* Comfort operating across both customer care and fraud/AML domains.
* Experience delivering through a large\-scale integration, transformation, or M\&A program.

The Director BP is responsible for aligning Canada business objectives with IT & Data product roadmaps, ensuring that strategic initiatives are prioritized, funded, governed, and successfully executed. Acting as a trusted advisor, this role connects Canadian business leaders with Product Groups, Product Owners, chapters, regional teams, and global technology partners to accelerate innovation, improve enterprise performance, and support business transformation.

This position plays a critical role in driving business engagement, ensuring service continuity, strengthening cyber and data governance, and maximizing the value delivered through technology, data, analytics, automation, AI, digital products, and enterprise platforms across Danone Canada.

Key Responsibilities

Facilitate prioritization of Canadian business initiatives and ensure alignment with global, regional, and local IT & Data strategies.
Build and maintain strong relationships with business stakeholders to foster trust, collaboration, accountable ownership, and value creation.

Portfolio & Roadmap Management

Manage the Canada IT & Data product and project portfolio in partnership with Product Groups, chapters, regional IT & Data teams, and global technology partners.

Support business case development, CAPEX/OPEX planning, demand intake, and investment prioritization for strategic initiatives.
Ensure visibility, alignment, and communication of priorities across Canada business leadership, regional IT & Data, Product Groups, and delivery teams.

Value Creation & Business Outcomes

Drive adoption of products and solutions to maximize business value realization, including self-service analytics, data products, Copilot and AI capabilities, workflow automation, and fit-for-purpose tools.

Danone Canada also offers a competitive short-term incentive bonus and a comprehensive benefits package, including group insurance, group retirement plans, wellbeing account, flexible time off, true hybrid work environment, paid parental leave, and other attractive options.

jobs.title: Revenue Performance Director
jobs.description:
Dayforce is a global human capital management (HCM) company headquartered in Toronto, Ontario, and Minneapolis, Minnesota, with operations across North America, Europe, Middle East, Africa (EMEA), and the Asia Pacific Japan (APJ) region.

Our award-winning Cloud HCM platform offers a unified solution database and continuous calculation engine, driving efficiency, productivity and compliance for the global workforce.

Our brand promise - Makes Work Life Better™ - Reflects our commitment to employees, customers, partners and communities globally.

About The Opportunity

The Revenue Performance Director is a strategic performance advisor embedded within a North American sales segment, accountable for helping leadership identify where execution is constraining revenue performance and mobilizing the capabilities required to improve it.

Working at the intersection of sales strategy, enablement, coaching, operations, and execution, the role connects signals from pipeline, forecast, customer conversations, seller behavior, and leadership priorities to identify performance gaps and recommend focused responses.

This role is designed for a commercially minded partner who can develop a clear point of view, mobilize the right resources, and help sales leaders reinforce the behaviors and operating rhythms that improve pipeline health, conversion, win rate, forecast confidence, and seller productivity.

Success is measured by meaningful movement in the business, not simply by the volume of programs or content delivered.

What You’ll Get To Do

Serve as a trusted revenue performance advisor to the segment’s senior sales leader and leadership team, bringing an informed perspective on execution priorities and performance gaps and building support for the actions required to improve performance.
Develop a fact-based view of segment performance by connecting insights from Salesforce, Gong, pipeline and forecast reviews, win/loss analysis, customer conversations, seller behavior, and market conditions.
Translate complex or competing signals into clear recommendations about what is happening, why it matters, where leaders should focus, and how progress will be measured.
Partner with sales leadership to create and manage a focused quarterly roadmap tied to the segment’s most important commercial outcomes.
Diagnose the root causes of execution gaps and determine the most appropriate response, including leader coaching, seller activation, process reinforcement, targeted skill development, strategic deal support, or improved adoption of existing resources.
Translate sales strategy into observable seller and manager behaviors that can be coached, reinforced, and inspected.
Mobilize and, when needed, facilitate targeted coaching, leadership sessions, deal interventions, or skill development based on validated performance needs, leveraging specialist RAP expertise where appropriate.

Overview

The High‑Risk Portfolio Management Team (HRPMT) enhances CCB’s overall risk oversight capabilities by providing specialized expertise, advisory support, and strategic guidance for accounts exhibiting deteriorating financial performance, emerging risk indicators, or complex credit concerns. Unlike traditional credit roles, HRPMT operates in a consulting and advisory capacity
, supporting the commercial banking lines of business with expert insights to strengthen the management of high‑risk, watch‑list, and impaired accounts.

The team works closely with relationship managers, credit partners, and leadership to ensure early identification of risk, informed decision‑making, and strong discipline around the oversight of vulnerable segments of the portfolio.

Key Responsibilities

Specialized Risk Assessment & Advisory Support

Conducts advanced financial analysis and risk assessments of clients demonstrating signs of weakness or deterioration, providing the LOB with actionable insights and recommended risk‑mitigation strategies.
Offers guidance on appropriate structures, terms, and risk controls for high‑risk accounts, ensuring alignment with bank policies, risk appetite, and regulatory expectations.
Advises on complex or distressed credit situations, including covenant breaches, liquidity concerns, operational challenges, and industry‑driven pressures.
Supports LOB teams with strategies for managing watch‑list, impaired, and emerging‑risk accounts, including exit strategies, recovery pathways, and restructuring options.

High‑Risk Portfolio Oversight

Performs enhanced portfolio monitoring to detect early‑warning signals, covenant non‑compliance, or deteriorating credit trends.
Evaluates portfolio‑level performance indicators and risk concentrations, escalating concerns where appropriate and recommending corrective actions.
Assesses the overall quality of risk management practices across the high‑risk portfolio, identifying gaps and recommending improvements.

Subject Matter Expertise & Consultancy

Operates as a specialist resource to senior leaders and frontline teams, supporting decision‑making on complex or ambiguous credit scenarios.
Provides expertise for the review of high‑risk transactions, challenging underlying assumptions, and advising on risk‑aligned alternatives.
Engages with internal stakeholders to ensure consistency in the management of high‑risk exposures across the enterprise.

Governance, Reporting & Continuous Improvement

Strengthens discipline and transparency around watch‑list and impaired account management procedures.
Implements adjustments to risk oversight strategies in response to shifting market, economic, or client‑specific conditions.
Contributes to enterprise initiatives that enhance risk governance, improve monitoring capabilities, and support proactive portfolio management.

Stakeholder Engagement

Partners closely with Commercial banking stakeholders to support their management of deteriorating clients while maintaining LOB ownership of BAU underwriting and client relationships.
Supports senior leadership with insights, analysis, and recommendations to inform capital allocation decisions and risk appetite considerations.
Engages with industry peers and internal networks to stay informed on emerging risks, competitive trends, and evolving best practices.

Qualifications

7+ years of experience in credit, lending, restructuring, portfolio management, or financial analysis within a corporate or banking environment.
Strong credit qualifications, including deep knowledge of commercial credit structures, deteriorating‑credit dynamics, and high‑risk portfolio management practices.
Bachelor’s degree required; master’s degree preferred (Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, or related field).
Demonstrated ability to assess complex financial situations, identify risks, and recommend solutions aligned with risk appetite and enterprise policies.
Proven capability to operate in an advisory role, influence stakeholders, and provide expertise in non‑routine, ambiguous, or sensitive credit situations.
Strong analytical, communication, and problem‑solving skills with the ability to apply sound judgment under pressure.

Socomec Group (Socomec) is a global leader in electrical equipment engineering and manufacturing, specialized in low voltage energy performance.

About This Role

This role requires a strong understanding of the power/electrical industry and the realities of complex engineering projects, including project timelines, technical dependencies, resource constraints, and cross-functional coordination. The PMD must also bring strong people leadership and project management experience to create structure around engineering teams, remove obstacles, and allow technical leaders to stay focused on engineering and delivery.

The Project Management Director (PMD) ensures consistent, transparent, and disciplined execution of all projects across Socomec PCO North America. This includes both product development and operational initiatives, ensuring that schedules, budgets, risks, and deliverables remain aligned with business priorities and approved baselines.

The PMD ensures that multi-functional and multi-location teams operate under a unified governance framework, with clearly defined interfaces, expectations, and accountability.

At the strategic level, the role ensures schedule predictability, cost control, and risk visibility across the portfolio - providing management with the insight required to make informed and timely business decisions.

Key Responsibilities And Accountabilities

Governance & Accountability

Ensures that every project operates under clearly defined governance boundaries for scope, schedule, and budget.
Ensures that limits of delegated authority are defined, communicated, and understood by all participants.

Project Planning and Execution

Develop comprehensive project plans outlining scope, objectives, timelines, and resource requirements.
Execute project plans, monitor progress, and ensure that projects are delivered on time and within budget. Ensures that all proposed changes are assessed for cost, schedule, and risk impact before submission for approval.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including engineering, manufacturing, quality control, and external vendors. Ensures that resource assignments, time estimates, and major milestone activities are agreed upon.

Team Leadership

Lead, mentor, and motivate a multidisciplinary project team, fostering a collaborative and high-performance work environment.
Effectively communicate project objectives, expectations, and updates to team members and stakeholders.

Risk Management

Ensures that projects maintain an active risk and issue register, that mitigation and containment plans are documented, and that escalation occurs promptly whenever delivery or budget objectives are at risk.

Stakeholder Communication

Establish and maintain strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders, including senior management, clients, suppliers, and regulatory bodies.
Provide regular project updates and reports to senior management and stakeholders.
Ensures accurate, live visibility of project and portfolio status, enabling stakeholders to access progress, risks, and resource utilization through the business intelligence environment without the need for manual reporting.

Budget Management

Develop and manage project budgets
Control expenditures, and take appropriate measures to ensure that the overall business plan is achieved

Quality Assurance

Ensures that all project management activities align with the Quality Management System and that documentation supports internal and external audits.
Conduct regular reviews and audits to ensure compliance with quality standards.

Safety

Develop and promote a culture of prevention across the project team
Assess risks at the earliest stage and implement the appropriate means of prevention
Update, inform and apply safety guidelines

Essential Qualifications, Experience, And Skills

Minimum of 8-10 years of experience in project management, with a focus on high-power UPS systems or related technologies.
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Project Management, or a related field.
PMP (Project Management Professional) certification is highly desirable.
Demonstrated success in leading and delivering complex engineering projects on time and within budget.
Proven experience in project management, particularly in the field of high-power UPS systems.
Strong technical background in electrical engineering with an emphasis on power systems.
Excellent leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills.
Familiarity with relevant industry standards and regulations.
Ability to handle multiple projects simultaneously and prioritize effectively.
Successfully cultivated and managed strong relationships with key market stakeholders.
Excellent communication skills (written and verbal), interpersonal skills and networking/collaboration abilities.
Focused on the achievement of strategic goals; consistently meets or exceeds targets.
Manages risks; anticipates and communicates in advance any potential issues and their impact.

jobs.description:
Sponsor-dedicated

JOB DESCRIPTION

Working fully embedded within one of our pharmaceutical clients, with the support of Cytel right behind you, you'll be at the heart of our client's innovation. As a Principal Statistical Programmer you will be dedicated to one of our global pharmaceutical clients; a company that is driving the next generation of patient treatment, where individuals are empowered to work with autonomy and ownership. This is an exciting time to be a part of this new program.

Position Overview

The Associate Director, Epidemiological Statistical Programming serves as a senior technical leader within the Epidemiology programming function, providing functional guidance, technical expertise, and mentorship to statistical programmers while also contributing directly to complex epidemiological projects. Working with a high degree of independence, this individual translates project and scientific objectives into effective programming strategies, proactively manages priorities and deliverables, and provides expert technical consultation to team members and cross-functional partners.

The Associate Director is responsible for leading and supporting the implementation of statistical programming activities across epidemiological and real-world evidence studies, ensuring that analyses and data outputs are accurate, reproducible, consistent, and delivered to a high standard of quality. This role may provide technical oversight of internal and external programming resources, including CRO partners, and will establish and promote programming standards, efficient processes, and best practices across projects.

In addition to hands-on project responsibilities, the Associate Director will play an important role in developing programming capabilities within the team by mentoring colleagues, reviewing and advising on technical approaches, identifying opportunities for process improvement and automation, and helping ensure appropriate allocation and execution of programming work. The individual will collaborate closely with epidemiologists, statisticians, data scientists, and other cross-functional partners to support the generation of high-quality evidence across multiple therapeutic areas.

Responsibilities

As an Associate Director, Epidemiological Statistical Programming, your responsibilities will include:

Provide technical and functional leadership to statistical programmers supporting epidemiological and real-world evidence (RWE) studies, including mentoring team members, providing technical guidance, and promoting consistent, high-quality programming practices.
Lead and contribute hands-on to statistical programming activities for epidemiological studies across multiple therapeutic areas, translating study objectives, protocols, and statistical analysis plans into robust and reproducible analytical solutions.
Develop, validate, and maintain high-quality SAS and/or R programs to support the creation of analysis datasets, statistical outputs, tables, figures, and other data products required for epidemiological research and evidence generation.
Partner closely with epidemiologists, statisticians, data scientists, and other cross-functional stakeholders to determine appropriate programming approaches and ensure analyses are implemented accurately and efficiently.
Provide expert technical consultation on complex programming, data, and analytical challenges, identifying appropriate solutions and advising team members and project stakeholders on best practices.
Oversee and review programming deliverables to ensure accuracy, reproducibility, consistency, quality, and adherence to agreed timelines and standards.
Support programming activities using a variety of real-world and observational data sources, which may include administrative claims, electronic health records, registries, and other healthcare databases.
Lead or contribute to the development of analysis-ready datasets and programming specifications, including data transformations, derivation logic, quality-control procedures, and documentation necessary to ensure transparent and reproducible analyses.
Establish, enhance, and promote programming standards, reusable tools, macros, code libraries, documentation, and quality-control processes that improve efficiency and consistency across epidemiological projects.
Drive continuous improvement and identify opportunities for automation, standardization, and innovative programming approaches that enhance the scalability and quality of epidemiological programming activities.
Contribute to the planning and prioritization of programming activities across projects, proactively identifying resource needs, technical risks, dependencies, and potential challenges to successful delivery.
Support scientific deliverables including regulatory and health authority requests, publications, abstracts, presentations, evidence-generation activities, and other analyses supporting clinical development, medical affairs, and/or value and access objectives.
Ensure programming activities are conducted in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements, company policies, SOPs, data privacy requirements, and industry best practices.
Lead or contribute to the development and maintenance of SOPs, work instructions, programming conventions, and other documentation governing epidemiological statistical programming activities.
Foster strong collaboration across internal and external teams and contribute to the development of programming talent through coaching, knowledge sharing, technical review, and mentorship.

Qualifications

Here at Cytel, we want our employees to succeed, and we enable that success through consistent training, development, and support. To be successful in this position, you will have:

Bachelor’s degree or higher in Statistics, Biostatistics, Epidemiology, Computer Science, Data Science, Mathematics, or a related quantitative discipline; advanced degree is a plus.
8+ years of relevant statistical programming experience within the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, CRO, healthcare, or life sciences industry, with demonstrated experience supporting epidemiological, observational, real-world evidence (RWE), HEOR, and/or related research.
Experience with Optum and Truveta.
Advanced programming expertise in SAS and/or R, with demonstrated ability to develop, validate, and maintain complex analytical programs and reproducible programming workflows.
Strong experience working with large and complex healthcare data sources, such as administrative claims, electronic health records (EHR), patient registries, or other real-world data sources.
Demonstrated understanding of epidemiological study designs, statistical analysis methods, and the application of programming techniques to observational and real-world research.
Proven ability to provide technical leadership and guidance to statistical programmers, including mentoring colleagues, reviewing programming approaches and deliverables, and resolving complex technical challenges.
Experience leading or coordinating programming activities across multiple projects, including prioritizing deliverables, identifying risks and dependencies, and ensuring work is completed to established quality standards and timelines.
Experience overseeing and reviewing programming deliverables.
Experience with line managing a team.
Strong commitment to programming quality, reproducibility, documentation, and the development and implementation of programming standards and best practices.
Ability to work independently, exercise sound technical judgment, and effectively manage multiple priorities in a dynamic, cross-functional environment.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate complex technical concepts effectively to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Strong collaboration and leadership skills, with demonstrated ability to influence, mentor, and build effective working relationships across multidisciplinary and geographically dispersed teams.

Preferred Qualifications (Nice To Have)

Master’s degree or higher in Statistics, Biostatistics, Epidemiology, Data Science, Computer Science, or another relevant quantitative discipline.
Experience programming across multiple epidemiological and real-world data sources and/or therapeutic areas.
Experience supporting regulatory-grade RWE, regulatory submissions, health authority requests, or other evidence-generation activities.
Experience with additional programming languages, technologies, and analytical tools such as Python, SQL, Git, Unix/Linux, R Markdown/Quarto, Shiny, or similar tools.
Experience developing reusable programming tools, packages, macros, automated workflows, or other solutions that improve programming efficiency, quality, and scalability.
Experience contributing to programming standards, SOPs, work instructions, technical guidance, or organizational best practices.
Experience with cloud-based analytics platforms and/or modern data environments.

jobs.description:
OUR MISSION

At Redwood, we empower our customers with lights-out automation for their mission-critical business processes.

About Us

Redwood Software is the leading orchestration platform for the autonomous enterprise, driving business transformation at the lowest total cost of ownership. Redwood empowers organizations to intelligently automate and orchestrate mission-critical business and IT processes across complex ERP, hybrid cloud, data and emerging agentic AI systems. Through its SaaS-first automation fabric—with AI embedded across the automation lifecycle—Redwood accelerates the path to autonomous operations. Backed by 30 years of experience and trusted by more than 50% of the Fortune 50, Redwood helps organizations unlock human potential to focus on innovation, growth and what’s next.

CORE VALUES

One Team. One Redwood

Make Your Own Weather

Obsess over Customer Success

Work the Problem

Be Curious

Own the Outcome

Respect Each Other

YOUR IMPACT

As Director, Customer Education & Documentation, you will lead Redwood's global documentation and customer education practice and rebuild it for an AI-first operating model. You will inherit an established team in Canada and India and reshape it: what the team produces, how it produces it, and how its impact is measured. AI-assisted and agentic content production, a best-in-class docs-as-code platform, in-product guidance through Pendo, and training that shortens time-to-value for new customers and partners are the four pillars of the role.

You are a builder and a player-coach at the system level. You set the strategy, then redesign the workflows, roles, and tooling that deliver it.

Reinvent the Team for AI

Redesign the team's operating model, roles, and skills mix around AI-assisted and agentic content production, moving the team from writing and maintaining content by hand to designing, governing, and validating AI-generated content.
Define which content work is delegated to AI, which stays with human judgment, and how validation is performed. Publish standards for accuracy, review, and provenance that the team follows.
Build and run agentic pipelines for drafting, translation, release-note and change-driven updates, link and quality checks, and content-gap detection.
Reskill current team members, reset role definitions and career paths, and hire selectively for the capabilities the redesigned team requires.
Set measurable productivity and quality targets (cycle time from release to published content, coverage, accuracy, cost per asset) and report results.
Make content structured and machine-readable so that customers, partners, and AI assistants can consume Redwood documentation reliably.

Build Best-in-Class Docs as Code

Own the end-to-end documentation platform strategy: content in version control, authored in Markdown/MDX, built and published through CI/CD, reviewed through pull requests alongside product code.
Lead the migration from legacy authoring tools to a modern docs-as-code platform, including information architecture, content modeling, redirects, search, versioning, and access control.
Embed documentation in the product delivery lifecycle with engineering and Product: docs as a release gate, shared ownership, automated checks, and documentation updates triggered by code and API changes.
Raise API and developer documentation to the standard expected of a platform product, including OpenAPI-driven reference content.
Establish quality, style, localization, and accessibility standards, and instrument documentation with usage and effectiveness analytics.

Drive In-Product Guidance and Onboarding

Own the Pendo guide strategy: in-app walkthroughs, tooltips, announcements, and contextual help that move new users to first value faster and reduce support demand.
Partner with Product, Engineering, and Product Operations on tagging standards, guide governance, and analytics, so guides are resilient to product change and measured against adoption outcomes.
Connect in-product guidance, documentation, and training into one learning experience, so a user reaches the right content in the right place with no hand-offs.

Deliver Training That Changes Customer and Partner Outcomes

Own the global customer education strategy and its delivery through Redwood University (Skilljar): role-based learning paths, certification, instructor-led and on-demand training, and partner and implementation-partner enablement.
Design onboarding programs for new customers and partners that measurably reduce time-to-value, ramp time, and onboarding-related support and services effort.
Use AI to scale course development, localization, personalization, and assessment, while holding a high bar for instructional quality.
Evaluate and, where the case supports it, build scalable and revenue-generating education offerings, including certification and partner programs.
Define and report education outcomes: completion, certification, adoption lift, onboarding time, support deflection, and customer and partner satisfaction.

Lead a Global, Distributed Team

Lead managers and senior individual contributors in Canada and India, with a clear operating rhythm across time zones, shared standards, and consistent quality.
Coach and develop leaders, set expectations, manage performance, and build succession.
Manage the annual plan, budget, and vendor relationships for documentation, learning, and AI tooling, and make build-versus-buy recommendations.
Partner with Product, Engineering, Customer Success, Support, Professional Services, Marketing, and Partner teams to align content and training to the customer journey.
Present strategy, results, risks, and investment needs to senior executives.

Your Experience

Bachelor's degree in a relevant field (Technical Communication, Instructional Design, Education, Engineering, Computer Science, Business, or similar); master's degree preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in technical documentation, customer education, developer experience, technical content, or digital adoption for software products, including 5+ years leading managers and distributed teams. We weigh demonstrated outcomes over tenure; backgrounds in developer experience, documentation engineering, support knowledge management, and product-led onboarding are welcome.
Demonstrated experience leading a team through a major change in how it works, and delivering measurable gains in output, quality, or cost.
Hands-on fluency with AI in content production: you can describe specific workflows where AI generates content, what your team validates, how the tools fail, and how your approach has changed in the past six months. Experience designing or governing agentic content workflows in production is strongly preferred.
A docs-as-code platform you built or migrated to at scale (Git-based workflows, Markdown/MDX, documentation platforms such as Mintlify, CI/CD publishing, automated content checks), and a record of working with engineering to make documentation part of the release process. You can state the size of the content estate, the team, and the results.
Experience leading teams in India and North America, with proven practices for distributed collaboration and consistent quality.
Strongly preferred: experience with Pendo or an equivalent digital adoption platform, including guide design, tagging and governance, and analytics-based iteration.
Strongly preferred: experience running customer and partner training at scale, ideally on Skilljar or a comparable LMS, including certification and onboarding programs tied to adoption and time-to-value outcomes. If your background is elsewhere, show how you would build this capability or lead those who have it.
Ability to define metrics, instrument programs, and show business impact to executives.
Strong judgment about the trade-off between speed and accuracy in content that customers rely on for mission-critical systems.
Exceptional communication, stakeholder-management, and executive presentation skills.
Background in automation, ERP, integration, or other technically complex enterprise software preferred.
Experience with API documentation and developer experience preferred.
Experience building revenue-generating education or certification offerings preferred.

Pay Transparency:
The typical base salary range for this position is CAD $150,000 - $170,000 annually. The range represents base salary only, and does not include company bonus, incentive for sales roles, equity or benefits, as applicable. Final compensation will be determined based on the candidate's skills, experience, and relevant qualifications.

Existing vacancy

If you like growth and working with happy, enthusiastic over-achievers, you'll enjoy your career with us!

161 Bay Street (93021), Canada, Toronto,Toronto, Ontario,Director, Technical Program Management

About Capital One Canada.

For 30 years, we've been on a mission to change banking for good. We challenge the traditional bank stereotype by integrating machine learning, conversational AI and design thinking into our core operations. We're a bank a tech company would build, where your work directly shapes innovative solutions that impact millions of Canadians.

We're driven by fearless curiosity, bold innovation, and a collective of authentic people working together to redefine what's possible. Technology isn’t just part of our strategy, it is our strategy . Everything we do serves our vision and the creation of what's next.

About the Team:

Since 2014, Capital One Canada’s software studio has grown from a team of 10 to a team of over 250. We’re passionate about what we do, and we’re always on the lookout for people who want to make a difference in the world of credit through technology. We’re obsessed with doing the right thing, and we achieve that by finding innovative ways to better serve our customers.

Here are a few of the ways we’re helping people take control of their credit:

Helping customers view and monitor their credit scores with Credit Keeper
Enabling customers to view and edit their Personal Information directly in the Mobile App
Providing customers 100% certainty which credit cards they’ll be approved for before they apply, by using Quick Check™

We’re all-in on the cloud and we’re leaders in the adoption of open source, RESTful APIs, microservices, and containers. We build our own products and release them with a speed and agility that allows us to get new customer experiences to market quickly. And, as a founder-led company, we’re inspired to make, break, do, and do good.

About The Role

As a Director of Technical Program Management (TPM), you will lead an established team of TPMs to drive execution across multi-year technology roadmaps, large-scale integration strategies, and complex application convergence efforts.

This is an executive technical leadership role for an operator who excels at navigating complex enterprise matrixes, influencing engineering and business leaders, and relentlessly getting stuff done. You will simplify intricate architectural trade-offs, align cross-functional partners across Product, Engineering, Design, and Data Science, and elevate the performance of an existing TPM practice to accelerate delivery for Capital One customers.

Your Responsibilities:

Drive Execution on Complex Technical Initiatives ("Get Stuff Done")
Execute High-Stakes Programs: Take ownership of complex, multi-workstream technical initiatives—including legacy application convergence, AWS cloud architecture updates, and enterprise data migration efforts.
Unblock Delivery Teams: Roll up your sleeves to diagnose delivery bottlenecks, resolve architectural dependencies, and keep engineering teams moving at high velocity.
Relentless Accountability: Establish clear execution baselines, enforce rigorous follow-through across multi-team releases, and deliver high-impact results in a fast-paced environment.
Navigate Matrixed Organizations & Influence Stakeholders
Cross-Functional Alignment: Navigate complex enterprise structures across US and Canadian leadership, building trusted partnerships across Product, Engineering, Data Science, Design, and Risk teams.
Influence Without Direct Authority: Align competing organizational priorities, negotiate technical trade-offs with senior engineering leaders, and secure commitments across functional and reporting boundaries.
Simplify Technical Complexity: Translate intricate technical constraints, API contracts, and distributed cloud risks into crisp, executive-ready choices for leadership.
Lead & Elevate an Established TPM Practice
People Leadership & Mentorship: Lead, coach, and grow an established team of TPMs, fostering a culture of high engineering standards, continuous learning, and strong delivery ownership.
Operationalize Delivery Excellence: Define and enforce rigorous standards for project intake and delivery estimate accuracy; implement rapid escalation paths for product or business-related roadblocks; and ensure company-wide visibility into an up-to-date, stack-ranked priority list of projects.
Strategy & Engineering Alignment: Build and justify engineering-driven strategy by framing technical initiatives in clear business terms, advocating for initiatives that drive long-term value, and ensuring technical roadmaps align with the enterprise architecture vision.
Standardize Governance & Metrics: Continuously improve team practices by embedding quantitative delivery health frameworks (e.g., DORA metrics), robust CI/CD release controls, and modern Agile/SAFe operating rhythms.

Basic Qualifications:

At least 7 years of experience in Technical Program Management leading complex software, cloud, or platform engineering programs.
Proven experience managing and developing direct reports within a Technical Program Management or Engineering organization.

Preferred Qualifications:

7+ years of experience designing, building, or managing data-intensive solutions utilizing distributed computing architectures.
3+ years of experience delivering distributed systems and highly available services using cloud computing architecture (AWS preferred).
3+ years of experience delivering customer-facing, highly scalable mobile applications and RESTful microservices.
Proven track record leading complex technical integration, application convergence, or enterprise data migration initiatives.
Deep experience navigating matrixed enterprise structures and influencing VP and C-suite technology stakeholders.
Experience operating within a highly regulated environment (Financial Services, Banking, Fintech).
Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field (or equivalent practical experience).
Master’s Degree or MBA in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

Working at Capital One.

You’ll be empowered to take end-to-end ownership of your work and your career, backed by a high-performance, hybrid culture and holistic suite of benefits designed to support your whole self.

Take ownership of your own potential: Whether you’re looking to upskill, pivot into new business areas, or master your craft, you’ll have access to tools and mentorship to reach your potential and define your career trajectory.
Find your rhythm: We believe trust fosters the flexibility and autonomy required to balance personal needs with a focus on high performance. We support a hybrid model – with 3 days in the office per week – that gives room for both collaboration and personal commitments.
Benefits built for your life: We take a holistic approach to well-being, providing support for you and those who are most important to you. This includes: full coverage for spouses, domestic partners and dependents, a one-time Work From Home allowance to build your comfortable workspace, up to $3,000 in mental health coverage and up to $5,000 in annual tuition subsidies.

You’ll find that Capital One is committed to helping you thrive and evolve every step of the way.

About us

With over 200 brands sold in nearly 180 countries, we’re the world’s leading premium drinks company. From global icons like Johznnie Walker, Guinness and Tanqueray to Smirnoff and Don Julio, we create brands consumers love. Bring your passion and use your curiosity as you explore, collaborate and innovate. Together with passionate people from all over the world, you’ll test new ideas, learn and grow, and unlock a brighter, more exciting future.

Join us to create a career worth celebrating.

About The Function

Supply Chain & Manufacturing is where our brands are made, moved and delivered to the world.

With over half of our people working across more than 100 sites, this is a complex, large-scale operation that brings together production, logistics, engineering and supplier partnerships.

It’s fast-paced and hands-on, with teams working together to ensure quality, efficiency and sustainability at every stage. From sourcing ingredients to getting products into customers’ hands, you’ll play a role in delivering the brands people know and love.

Position Title: Supply Director, Canada

Location: Dunwin Drive, Toronto, Canada

Reports to: VP Supply Chain Canada

About The Role

Seeking an experienced Supply Chain professional to lead Canadian Supply Operations and drive the change needed to support Diageo Canada's ambitions with evolving customers and consumer needs.

The ideal candidate will have proven ability to lead change within supply chain operations and a strong track record of delivering against strategic objectives while maintaining high standards of execution.

They will have experience managing multiple supply chain functions with a focus on both execution and continuous improvement, as well as exceptional leadership skills with the ability to influence cross functional teams and partners.

The successful candidate will lead key Canadian Supply functions, including:

Site lead to Dunwin Keg warehouse and delivery for the entire Ontario region

Ensure continuity of supply and efficient interaction of all Demand and Supply elements for Canada.
Lead cross-functional strategic programs aimed at improving the total supply chain.
Communicate proactively with all key partners regarding the status of the Canadian Supply Chain.
Upgrade competencies within the group and organization.
Develop and implement optimized Canadian supply chain strategies in collaboration with wider North America Supply.
Build effective partnerships with Liquor Boards, Government, and trade bodies.
Sponsor strategic projects aimed at improving customer service levels, reducing operating costs, or decreasing order fulfillment lead-time.

Complexities Of Role

Ontario Guinness KEGs – lead all operational aspects of KEG warehousing and delivery in Ontario (including P&L management, Customer Service desk, LCBO relationship, Compliance and Health & Safety)
Champion the embedding of Integrated Business Planning (IBP) with all functions of
undefined

Manage Canadian Inventory profile of over $50M
Partner with both Diageo and 3rd Party Manufacturing with a Supply Plan that delivers the Canadian Sales plan

Experience / Skills Required

Preferred MBA or business degree.
Minimum of 10 years' experience in operations and supply chain management.
Demonstrated knowledge of supply chain strategy development and execution.
Proven ability to influence and network within a matrixed organization.
Comfortable working through ambiguity and being the leader to set direction and vision

Strong leadership skills with experience in building, managing, and evolving teams;

credibility at senior levels is essential.

Innovative problem-solving abilities to address business challenges.
Expertise in Advanced Planning Systems (APS) and ERP systems (SAP preferred).

Thorough understanding of forecasting and inventory planning processes; knowledge of

MPS/MRP (Master Production Schedule/Material Requirements Planning) and DRP

Flexibility is key to our success. Talk to us about what flexibility means to you, so that you’re

supported to manage your wellbeing and balance your priorities from day one.

Job Description

This is an exciting opportunity to help expand CoCounsel
, Thomson Reuters’ generative AI platform for legal professionals, into the in-house legal market. CoCounsel is already trusted across law firms for research, drafting, and review; this role will help define how the product serves general counsel, legal operations leaders, and corporate legal departments.

As Senior Director, Product Management – In-House Use Cases, you will own the discovery and definition of what CoCounsel needs to become for this customer segment. You will work directly with in-house legal teams, translate customer needs into a prioritized roadmap, and lead a team of product managers to turn that roadmap into shipped product. The role reports to the Co-Head of Product for CoCounsel Legal.

Key Responsibilities

Own the roadmap: Define and own the in-house use case roadmap for CoCounsel, translating insights from general counsel, deputy general counsel, and legal operations leaders into a focused and deliverable product plan.
Understand the customer: Develop a deep understanding of where in-house legal teams lose time, experience friction, and face risk, and translate those insights into meaningful product use cases.
Lead the team: Manage and grow a team of two to three product managers, setting priorities, reviewing work, and developing strong product judgment.
Shape the product: Identify opportunities beyond obvious automation and help define use cases that solve meaningful problems for in-house legal teams.
Deliver across the business: Partner with Engineering, Design, Marketing, and go-to-market teams to move use cases from concept through launch.
Represent the customer: Bring the in-house legal customer perspective into product roadmap and prioritization decisions.
Required Qualifications
5+ years of experience as in-house counsel or in legal operations, or 5+ years of product management experience working on an in-house-focused product.
Comfort working with generative AI and modern product tooling.
Ability to engage credibly with Engineering teams about what is realistic and feasible to build; coding experience is not required.
Strong creative instincts and genuine customer empathy.

Preferred Qualifications

jobs.title: Director, Growth Marketing
jobs.description:
About Nicola Wealth:

We have a lot to be proud of at Nicola Wealth. Our sophisticated financial planning, our diversified private investment funds and their exceptional performance, our 98% client retention rate and our award-winning culture, combine to position us as a national leader in wealth management. Recognized as a Best Managed Company and one of Canada’s Top Employers, we are dedicated to upholding our firm’s values through this phase of significant growth.

By bringing together smart, dedicated and supportive colleagues from diverse backgrounds, we deliver extraordinary client service in a values-driven work environment. The collaboration, creativity and entrepreneurial spirit we were founded on provides the opportunity for you to make a real impact and build a rewarding career. We are passionate about our business, our culture and investing deeply in your growth and development to build for the future. If you have this same drive, then let’s talk!

Purpose of the Role::

Reporting to the Vice President, Marketing & Communications, the Director, Growth Marketing
owns Nicola Wealth’s demand-generation engine, translating marketing activity into measurable, qualified pipeline and revenue. This role is accountable for the full marketing digital funnel from paid and organic acquisition through conversion, nurturing and attribution and for building the data strategy, technology and reporting foundation that makes growth predictable, efficient and repeatable. Given the considered, relationship-driven nature of wealth management, the role places particular emphasis on educating and nurturing high-value, long-consideration prospects and on demonstrating a clear return on marketing investment.

Core Responsibilities:

Pipeline Ownership & Funnel Optimization — Own the end-to-end digital marketing funnel including paid media and advisor close rate journey. Evaluate and constantly optimize marketing’s contribution to qualified pipeline; define funnel stages, diagnose drop-off, and continuously improve conversion from anonymous visitor to marketing-qualified and sales-accepted lead.
Performance Analysis & Optimization — Use the multi-touch attribution and reporting provided by the Insights function to connect marketing spend and activity to pipeline and revenue, enabling confident, data-driven decisions on where to invest. Diagnose platform performance, set up in house media as needed for always on leads.
Website & Conversion Rate Optimization (CRO) — Own the website as a conversion engine, leading a structured test-and-learn / A/B testing program to improve on-site conversion, performance and user experience.
Landing Pages, Lead Capture & User Experience — Design and optimize high-value landing pages and lead-capture frameworks — forms, offers and gated content — ensuring a seamless, trust-building experience aligned to each campaign and audience.
Paid & Organic Inbound Acquisition — Lead demand generation across paid and organic channels — search engine optimization (SEO), local SEO, and performance/paid media across search, social, display and programmatic — to grow qualified inbound traffic efficiently and at a target cost per acquisition.
Lead Nurturing & Marketing Automation — Own the marketing automation platform and build scalable nurture programs that move leads through the funnel, partnering closely with Sales on lead scoring, routing and hand-off.
Lifecycle Email Flows — Design automated, personalized email sequences that educate, build trust and prime long-term, high-consideration prospects, improving engagement and conversion across an extended buying cycle.
MarTech & Activation Stack — Own the campaign-execution technology stack — the marketing automation platform, ad and media platforms and website/CMS — and the flow of campaign data into the CRM, partnering with the Insights function on the measurement and reporting layer.
Leadership & Cross-Functional Collaboration — Lead, coach and develop the growth marketing function — team members, agencies and vendors — and partner across Sales, Content, Brand and Compliance to deliver integrated, measurable campaigns.
Customer Lifecycle Marketing (CLM) — Own lifecycle marketing across the full client relationship — onboarding, engagement, retention and deepening — extending marketing’s role beyond acquisition to nurture and grow existing client relationships.
AI Search, Content & Answer-Engine Visibility — Extend organic discovery into AI-powered search by developing Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) and Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) strategies, supported by an insight-led content foundation, so Nicola Wealth is surfaced as prospects increasingly research through search engines and AI assistants.
Other relevant and related responsibilities, as assigned and as the needs of the organization change.

Required Skills & Qualifications:

A minimum of 8 years of related work experience in growth, digital or performance marketing, including 3+ years leading teams and/or agency partners.
Completion of a bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business, Analytics, Communications or a related field required; a Master’s degree or MBA is an asset.
Certifications in relevant platforms (e.g., Google Analytics/Google Ads, HubSpot or Marketo, Meta Blueprint, or CXL/Reforge) are an asset.
Demonstrated, hands-on expertise across SEO/SEM, paid and performance media, conversion rate optimization and A/B testing.
Proven experience owning a marketing automation platform and its integration with CRM, and building lead-nurturing and lifecycle email programs.
Strong command of marketing analytics, multi-touch attribution and reporting/BI tools, with the ability to connect marketing activity to pipeline and revenue.
Familiarity with AI-powered search and answer-engine optimization (GEO/AEO), first-party data strategy and customer data platforms (CDP), and emerging discovery channels is an asset.
Experience in financial services, wealth management or another considered, regulated, high-trust purchase environment is a strong asset.
Excellent communication, collaboration and stakeholder-management skills, with a proven track record of partnering closely with Sales.
Must be legally eligible to work in Canada for any employer

Compensation & Benefits Package:

This position comes with a base salary range of $140,000 - $180,000
plus a competitive performance bonus, RRSP contribution and participation in our profit-sharing program. Base salary will be commensurate with experience, skills, and qualifications.

At Nicola Wealth, our people grow our business, delight our clients, and live our values every day. Our comprehensive compensation and benefits package reflects our appreciation for this commitment. Whether it’s participating in our profit sharing and benefit programs on day one, or the opportunity to participate in our share ownership program, our people are able to go beyond a conventional salary and bonus structure. To learn more about our complete package, visit: www.nicolawealth.com/total-rewards.

Please include both a cover letter and resume in support of your application. We are an inclusive, equal opportunity employer. For more information about this and other roles: www.nicolawealth.com/careers .

It is our priority to remove barriers to provide equal access to employment. Should you require reasonable accommodation during the recruitment process please contact us at accessibility@nicolawealth.com and we will work with you to meet your needs. All information shared during the accommodation request process will be stored and used in a manner that is consistent with applicable laws and Nicola Wealth policies.

Thank you for your interest in a career with Nicola Wealth!

jobs.title: Director, Supply Chain Management
jobs.description:
Tenstorrent is leading the industry on cutting-edge AI technology, revolutionizing performance expectations, ease of use, and cost efficiency. With AI redefining the computing paradigm, solutions must evolve to unify innovations in software models, compilers, platforms, networking, and semiconductors. Our diverse team of technologists have developed a high performance RISC-V CPU from scratch, and share a passion for AI and a deep desire to build the best AI platform possible. We value collaboration, curiosity, and a commitment to solving hard problems. We are growing our team and looking for contributors of all seniorities.

We are looking for a Director of Supply Chain Management to build and lead the operating infrastructure required to bring our products to market, scale them globally, and support them throughout their lifecycle. This role sits within the Supply Chain organization and reports to the Sr. Director, Operations & Strategic Partnerships. This role has high exposure to CEO level decisions and engagement and demonstrated leadership experience is a requirement.

This is a builder role within the Supply Chain. You will own the Supply Chain deliverables covering our cross functional go to market and customer engagement. This includes driving product certifications and market readiness, enhancing RMA and customer satisfaction processes, as well as driving our Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) process. Your job is to establish clear ownership, build scalable processes, develop the team, and create the operating mechanisms required to support a rapidly growing hardware business, working in close partnership with the other functions needed to achieve these goals.

We are not looking for someone to administer existing processes. We are looking for someone who sees ambiguity, creates structure, drives decisions, and most importantly takes end-to-end ownership. Your mandate is simple: build it, own it, and scale it.

This role is hybrid, based out of Toronto, ON; Austin, TX; or Santa Clara, CA.

We welcome candidates at various experience levels for this role. During the interview process, candidates will be assessed for the appropriate level, and offers will align with that level, which may differ from the one in this posting.

Who You Are

A builder who is comfortable entering an environment where processes and ownership are not fully defined, then turning ambiguity into a clear operating model and an executable plan.
An experienced hardware and supply chain operator who understands how Engineering, Product, Sales, Manufacturing, Quality, Finance, Legal, and customer teams connect across the product lifecycle.
A cross-functional leader who can align senior stakeholders, establish decision rights, and drive accountability without waiting for someone else to define ownership.
A data-driven and analytically rigorous decision-maker who can make sound judgments with incomplete information and maintain urgency through execution.
A people leader who develops strong teams, builds subject matter expertise, and creates a culture of ownership, transparency, and continuous improvement.

What We Need

Drive cross-functional processes and own Supply Chain deliverables for global product certification and market readiness, including certification roadmaps across products and countries, clear readiness gates, coordination with Engineering, Product, Legal, manufacturing partners, test labs, and regulatory bodies, and early mitigation of risks that could affect customer commitments or launches.
Own and mature the company’s S&OP process by connecting customer demand, Sales forecasts, supply, manufacturing capacity, inventory, and financial objectives into a disciplined operating cadence and trusted view for executive decision-making.
Build and own the end-to-end global RMA and customer operations model within Supply Chain, covering intake, triage, replacement, repair, warranty management, disposition, customer communication, service levels, escalation paths, and performance metrics, in partnership with Customer, Quality, and Engineering teams.
Establish the processes, systems, KPIs, dashboards, governance, and operating mechanisms required to scale, including measures for forecast accuracy, supply performance, inventory health, backlog, certification readiness, RMA performance, and execution against plan.
Lead cross-functional execution with Sales, Product, Engineering, Quality, Finance, Manufacturing, test labs, regulatory bodies, and customer teams. Establish clear decision rights, simplify complex workflows, identify gaps before they become business problems, and drive shared decisions through to completion while retaining Supply Chain ownership of the deliverables.

What You Will Learn

Gain broad exposure to the full operating model of a rapidly growing hardware and semiconductor business, from product development and global market readiness through supply planning, manufacturing, delivery, and customer support.
Build expertise in integrating Supply Chain-owned certification deliverables, S&OP, RMA, and customer operations into one scalable product lifecycle operating system.
Develop the leadership and operating mechanisms required to turn cross-functional complexity into clear ownership, timely decisions, and measurable execution.
See directly how operational decisions influence product launch timing, customer commitments, product quality, inventory, revenue, and the company’s ability to scale globally.
Create the foundation for a supply chain management organization that grows with Tenstorrent’s products, markets, customers, and operational complexity.

Compensation for all engineers at Tenstorrent ranges from $100k - $500k including base and variable compensation targets. Experience, skills, education, background and location all impact the actual offer made.

Tenstorrent offers a highly competitive compensation package and benefits, and we are an equal opportunity employer.

This offer of employment is contingent upon the applicant being eligible to access U.S. export-controlled technology. Due to U.S. export laws, including those codified in the U.S. Export Administration Regulations (EAR), the Company is required to ensure compliance with these laws when transferring technology to nationals of certain countries (such as EAR Country Groups D:1, E1, and E2). These requirements apply to persons located in the U.S. and all countries outside the U.S. As the position offered will have direct and/or indirect access to information, systems, or technologies subject to these laws, the offer may be contingent upon your citizenship/permanent residency status or ability to obtain prior license approval from the U.S. Commerce Department or applicable federal agency. If employment is not possible due to U.S. export laws, any offer of employment will be rescinded.
