jobs.description:
Job Description

Amazing Career Moments Happen Here

Transforming the insurance industry is ambitious, we know. That’s why at Applied, we’re building a team that shows up every day ready to learn, willing to try new things, and driven to deliver innovative software and services that make us indispensable to our customers – all within a culture built on values that make us indispensable to each other too. With 40+ years of experience in the Insurtech game, we’re not just redefining what’s achievable; we’re creating a place where amazing career moments are made possible. 

Position Overview

We're hiring a Senior Director, Product Marketing – Agency for a remote role with occasional travel, setting multi-year product marketing strategy and leading execution for the largest buyer segment in Applied's portfolio. This role owns positioning, GTM, organizational leadership, and launch outcomes, product adoption, and budget for product marketing for Applied Epic and EZLynx platforms, partnering closely with Product Management, Sales, and Content and Field Marketing to drive growth across our agency-facing solutions. This role reports to the VP of Corporate and Product Marketing.

You'll lead a Product Marketing function across the largest product surface in our portfolio, with two distinct positioning lanes in Applied Epic and EZLynx.

To keep us headed in the right direction, we're looking for people who understand winning is a team sport, who value and seek to learn from our team's diverse experiences and backgrounds, who welcome a challenge and take risks in the pursuit of creating better outcomes for our customers, and who can, at any given time, step back to laugh and have some fun.

What You’ll Do

Strategy & Vision — Set the product marketing strategy for the agency segment, aligned to Applied's portfolio strategy and corporate priorities. Own positioning, narrative, and market direction for agency buyers across Epic and EZLynx.
Team Leadership — Lead, develop, and grow a team of product marketers. Build a culture of excellence through scalable programs, outcome-based accountability, and continuous learning. Mentor talent and develop the next generation of PMM leaders at Applied.
Product Launch & GTM — Govern the launch process across the agency portfolio, ensuring cross-functional alignment with Product, Sales, Customer Success, and Demand Gen to maximize revenue and adoption impact.
Sales Partnership — Partner with Sales Enablement and CX leadership to ensure PMM output drives pipeline, competitive win rate, and adoption. Sponsor key enablement programs and own the agency-side sales narrative.
Competitive & Market Intelligence — Drive the competitive intelligence motion for the agency segment, partnering with the team's broader competitive program and contributing to portfolio-level insights.
Cross-Functional Influence — Partner with Product Management and Operations leadership as a trusted strategic advisor on roadmap, positioning, and pricing decisions for the agency portfolio.
Performance — Own and report on marketing-influenced business metrics: pipeline contribution, competitive win rate, adoption, and launch outcomes. Use data to continuously refine GTM strategy and execution.
AI-Forward Operating Model — Champion and contribute to Applied PMM's use of AI tooling, custom skills, and scalable systems to compound team impact.

We’re Excited To Learn More About You

Your experience may include:

12+ years in B2B product marketing, with 6+ years of people management experience including leading managers and other people leaders
Proven track record leading product marketing strategy and owning results for multiple product lines with distinct buyer personas, a business unit, or a major buyer segment in an enterprise SaaS or platform business
Demonstrated success building and developing PMM talent, including hiring, coaching, and growing people leaders, senior individual contributors, and lead PMMs, and building leadership succession
Strong executive presence and ability to influence and negotiate with cross-functional partners at the VP and C-suite level, reconciling competing priorities to drive business results
Experience in complex, multi-stakeholder, or regulated industries (insurance, financial services, healthcare) strongly preferred
Experience working in AI-forward marketing teams or driving AI adoption within marketing functions is a strong plus

You may have other skills or credentials, including:

Excellent written, verbal, presentation, and public speaking skills, including comfort representing the company with analysts, partners, and at industry events
Strong financial acumen and experience owning budget and headcount planning and shaping pricing strategy
Data-driven mindset with proven ability to use analytics to guide GTM strategy
Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Business, Communications, or related field; MBA a plus

Location

We know that talent comes from all backgrounds and experience levels. We encourage military members and their spouses as well as candidates without a degree or a background in tech to apply! 

When You Join Team Applied, You Can Expect:

A culture that values who you are
and recognizes that you aren’t just an employee; you are a teammate, and you matter. We thrive on the benefits of our different experiences and celebrate the uniqueness our teammates bring to work with them every day. 

We flex our time together
, collaborating remotely and in-person to empower our teams to work in the ways that work best for them. 

A comprehensive benefits and compensation package
that centers our teammates and helps them to bring their best to work every day: 

Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage 
Holiday and Vacation Time 
Health & Wellness Days 
A Bonus Day for Your Birthday 

Learn more about the people behind our products at https://www1.appliedsystems.com/en-us/about-us/jobs/

Our targeted starting base salary in the United States for this position ranges from $180,000 - $200,000 USD. To determine a new team member’s starting pay, we consider a variety of factors, including someone’s depth, breadth, and variety of experience, skills, and responsibilities. Depending on the role, team members may also be eligible to participate in additional compensation plans such as bonus and commission.

Your Security Matters:

About Solink

At Solink, our mission is to safeguard what matters most
. We provide businesses with the tools to know sooner and act faster
by transforming video security into real-time operational insights.

Our cloud-based platform integrates seamlessly with your existing cameras and systems, turning them into intelligent sensors that detect and interpret key moments. This empowers teams to make data-driven decisions, enhance security, and improve operational efficiency.

Trusted by over 35,000 locations across 60+ countries - including brands like McDonald’s and JYSK - Solink delivers clarity when it counts. Our solutions help businesses reduce shrink, optimize performance, and respond proactively to potential threats.

We're growing rapidly, earning industry recognition, and scaling with purpose. We’ve been recognized by Deloitte’s Fast 50™ and Fast 500™, Business Intelligence Group, and as one of Ottawa’s Best Places to Work. And we’re just getting started!

About The Role

Solink is looking for a (head of) Senior Director, Product Marketing and Customer Marketing to create category leadership and sharpen our positioning - accelerating adoption, differentiation, and revenue across our key products. This is a newly unified leadership role, bringing Product Marketing and Customer Marketing together so the story we tell to prospects and the story we tell to existing customers reinforce each other.

You'll own positioning and messaging, lead go-to-market strategy for major launches, run competitive intelligence and win/loss, scale sales enablement, and stand up an Analyst Relations (AR) program - while also owning how we market to and grow our existing customer base through advocacy, references, and expansion programs.

This is a senior, executive-facing role for someone who can define a category, arm a sales team to win, and build a team and function from a strong existing base of product marketers.

What You’ll Be Doing

Positioning & Messaging

Own product positioning, messaging, and narrative across Solink’s platform and key products and industries we serve.
Develop and defend a category point of view that differentiates Solink from adjacent and competing solutions.
Test and refine messaging with customers, prospects, and sales to ensure it resonates and converts.

GTM Strategy

Lead go-to-market strategy and execution for major feature and product launches, partnering with Product, Demand Gen, Sales, and Customer Success.
Build launch playbooks and processes that scale across a growing product portfolio.
Identify opportunities to grow adoption and ARPU through positioning, packaging, and GTM for new features and add-ons.

Competitive Intelligence

Own Solink’s competitive intelligence program, keeping a current, accurate view of the competitive landscape.
Run a win/loss program that turns deal outcomes into sharper positioning and enablement.
Educate internal teams - Sales, Marketing, Product - on competitive threats and how to respond to them.

Sales Enablement

Build and scale sales enablement content — battlecards, pitch decks, objection handling, and training — that drives rep proficiency and win rate.
Partner with Sales, Customer Success, and RevOps to ensure enablement keeps pace with the roadmap and competitive landscape.
Measure and improve enablement adoption and its impact on ramp time and win rate.

Analyst Relations (AR)

Build Solink’s Analyst Relations program from the ground up, establishing relationships with relevant industry analysts.
Prepare briefings, RFI/RFP responses, and positioning materials for analyst evaluations and reports.
Translate analyst feedback into product, positioning, and GTM recommendations for leadership.

Customer Marketing & Advocacy

Own customer marketing strategy - references, case studies, testimonials, and advocacy programs that support both sales, demand gen, channel and brand.
Partner with Demand Gen and Customer Success on programs that drive adoption, expansion, and retention among existing customers.
Build a scalable customer reference and advisory program to support field marketing pg growth, competitive deals and category-building efforts.

A Little Bit About You

10+ years of experience in product marketing, with meaningful experience in customer marketing, competitive intelligence, or analyst relations.
A proven track record building category positioning that differentiates a product in a competitive market.
Experience leading go-to-market strategy and execution for major product launches end-to-end.
Experience building or scaling a sales enablement function, with measurable impact on win rate or ramp time.
Comfort building new functions from scratch, including Analyst Relations or customer advocacy programs.
Strong executive communication skills, with experience presenting positioning and strategy to CMO, executive, and board-level audiences.
Experience building and coaching a team of product and/or customer marketers.

What Success Looks Like

Solink has a clear, differentiated category position that Sales, Marketing, Channel, and Product all use consistently.
Major launches land on time with strong adoption and a measurable revenue contribution.
Sales wins more competitive deals, supported by sharp, current competitive intelligence and enablement.
Solink has an active, credible presence with relevant industry analysts.
Existing customers become a growing source of references, advocacy, and expansion revenue.

Nice to Haves

Experience in physical security, video surveillance, IoT, or a related B2B technology industry.
Experience building an Analyst Relations function in a company that didn’t previously have one.
Experience scaling a product or customer marketing function as a company grows past $100M+ ARR.
Familiarity with sales enablement and customer marketing platforms (e.g., HubSpot, SalesForce, Highspot, Seismic, Gainsight).

Role Expectations

This is an M5 level role. At Solink, individuals at this level set the strategic direction for a major function, translating executive priorities into scalable execution, building organizational capability through the leaders and teams they develop, and are accountable for delivering sustained business outcomes.

In This Role, You'll Be Expected To:

Own the long-term strategy, operating model, and performance of Product & Customer Marketing, translating CMO and executive priorities into clear roadmaps and measurable outcomes.
Build and grow a high-performing team, developing future leaders and building strong marketing capability across the function.
Partner with the CMO and cross-functional executives (Sales, Product, Customer Success) to influence company-wide GTM priorities and strategic initiatives.
Establish scalable systems, playbooks, and operating rhythms — launch process, sales enablement, win/loss, AR, customer advocacy — that improve effectiveness beyond any single program.
Represent Product & Customer Marketing internally as the senior authority on positioning and category strategy, building trusted relationships across the organization.

What Success Looks Like:

Product & Customer Marketing is recognized as a strategic, executive-level function with a clear seat at the GTM table, not a service arm to Sales or Demand Gen.
The team and leaders you build operate with growing autonomy and are developing toward their own next level.
The systems and playbooks you establish scale beyond you and are adopted company-wide, outlasting any single launch or campaign.

Security Requirements

Candidates must undergo a criminal records check upon hire;
Be a Canadian Citizen (dual citizens included), or eligible to work in Canada;
Be willing to comply with Solink’s own security policies and standards.

Our Values

We do things the Solink way:

Act with URGENCY – Our customers move fast, so we do too.
Deliver with QUALITY – We sweat the details and hold a high bar.
Win with TEAM – No egos. Just outcomes, built together.
Lead with TRUST – We earn it through clarity, consistency, and care.

These aren’t just words—they shape how we hire, lead, and grow.

Why Solink?

We’re not just building tech - we’re building a place where great people do great work.

Clarity and trust: Where the role allows, we support flexibility in how and where work gets done - and we’re upfront about what’s required.
Meaningful equity: Every full-time, permanent employee has a stake in our growth.
Comprehensive benefits: Fully paid health & dental (no waiting period) + $500 health spending account.
Wellness support: Monthly reimbursement for fitness, wellness, or mental health programs.
Growth through merit: Advancement is based on contribution, initiative, and the ability to raise the bar - together.
Candid culture: Clear expectations, honest feedback, and no politics.
Social connection: From So-learns to Solink-o and So-lunches, we stay connected in ways that actually feel fun.

What To Expect From The Hiring Process

We respect your time and value transparency. Here’s a general idea of what to expect:

Intro call with our Talent Team

Role-relevant task or case (if applicable)
Final interviews with cross-functional team members
Reference Checks
Offer & onboarding 🎉

Please note: this is subject to change at any point in the recruitment process based on the needs of the business.

How To Apply

Submit your resume and a short cover letter via our [Careers Page]. Let us know what excites you about this role, and how you’d help move Solink forward.

jobs.description:
At Arctic Wolf, you won’t just watch the cybersecurity industry evolve – you'll help lead the change. Our global Pack is made up of people who thrive on solving hard problems, moving fast, and building technology that protects organizations around the world. We’re proud to be recognized by Forbes, CNBC, Fortune, CRN, Gartner Peer Insights and IDC MarketScape – but what matters most is the work behind it: delivering real outcomes for customers through award winning innovation like our Aurora Platform.

If you’re looking for meaningful work, smart teammates and the chance to make a real impact in a high-growth company that’s redefining security operations, Arctic Wolf is the right place for you!

Our mission is simple: End Cyber Risk. We’re looking for Senior Director, Product - Threat Intelligence & Detection
to be part of making this happen.   

LOCATION
: This role is open to Remote-United States, Remote-Canada, Hybrid-Eden Prairie-MN-USA, Hybrid-Waterloo-ON-CAN.

This senior product management lead role for Arctic Wolf defines and evangelizes the commercial strategy and product roadmap for threat intelligence & threat hunting along with delivering on the platform strategy to drive detection efficacy and efficiency for the latest threats keeping our customers safe. You will collaborate with Architecture, Engineering, Security Research, and cross-functional teams to align product vision with company goals, guide strategic planning, and drive innovation and outcomes in threat intelligence, threat hunting and detection engineering. You will lead initiatives to map strategy to execution, commission research, define OKRs, and maintain alignment across product lines and stakeholders. As a respected leader in the cybersecurity space, you will influence organizational structure, drive cross-team buy-in, mentor others, and represent your group with transparency and integrity.

Role Scope

Presents at stakeholder meetings to communicate the vision and alignment with corporate strategy
Works with product principals and engineering leaders to communicate strategy and high-level roadmap for threat intelligence, detections, and AI related initiatives to Leadership, PM and Engineering teams
Participates in cross-functional efforts and co-design to ensure product initiatives leverage existing security research capabilities and avoid redundant development
Decides (with Architecture and Security Research leadership) when new threat detection or intelligence capabilities are sufficiently differentiated to create new products or platforms and deliver highest value in efficacy and efficiency
Creates vision and strategy presentations and documents that address high-level cybersecurity problems, emerging threat landscapes, and AI-driven solutions
Defines and drives the strategic vision for threat intelligence and threat hunting while overseeing the incubation of breakthrough threat detection capabilities that improve effectiveness of our products (MDR, EDR) and the SOC
Leads cross-functional teams through product development, fostering a culture of experimentation, rapid iteration, threat validation, and customer-centric innovation in security
Partners with executive leadership to align threat intelligence and AI initiatives with long-term business goals, ensuring resource allocation and portfolio management driving high-impact security outcomes

Knowledge & Experience

Deep expertise in threat intelligence, threat hunting, detection engineering, and security research practices and their application to product development
Demonstrated understanding of conversational AI, large language models (LLMs), and machine learning applications in cybersecurity and threat intelligence and or detections is a plus
Collaborate and run cross-functional backlog reviews for threat intelligence and detections; participate in other product line reviews to contribute to overall organizational prioritization
Commission research into possible strategies to address customer security problems and evolving threat landscapes
Identify OKRs for threat intelligence, threat hunting and detections in support of wider corporate goals
Identify follow-up analysis and insights into emerging threat patterns and their implications for product strategy

Complexity and Problem Solving

Communicates to teams about process changes and the value these bring—provides clarity and answers questions about threat detection innovation priorities
Works with Engineering and Labs leadership to align threat intelligence, detection, and AI strategies with company direction, then breaks out specific initiatives to implement and support the strategy
Propagates priorities and "big rocks" to product principals and technical leaders to create an overall threat intelligence and detection product roadmap
Helps other product teams understand how threat intelligence, detections, and AI capabilities enable faster, more effective threat response in their solutions
Identifies projects that shift priorities and communicates with stakeholders across threat intelligence, security operations, and engineering teams

Collaboration & Interaction

Aligns cross-functional teams (Security Research, Engineering, Sales, Go-to-Market) on threat intelligence product strategies & roadmap to successfully meet the business needs
Drives buy-in and support from the SOC, security research, engineering, sales, and broader organization improving our threat intel and detection efficacy and efficiency
Creates documentation required for calibration efforts and prepares for reviews with evidence of achievements to represent the threat intelligence and detection portfolio

Required Qualifications

7+ years of progressive experience in cybersecurity, with deep expertise in threat intelligence, threat hunting, detection engineering, incident response, or security research—this is non-negotiable
10+ years of product management experience, including 3+ years at a director level or equivalent managing complex, cross-functional teams delivering enterprise security products at scale
Proven track record of taking products from strategy through successful market launch, with quantifiable results in revenue growth, customer adoption, or competitive market share expansion
Executive presence with ability to speak credibly to technical and non-technical audiences about cybersecurity strategy, emerging threats, and security innovation

Preferred Qualifications

Background in Threat Intelligence, managed security services (MSS), managed detection and response (MDR), or security operations centers (SOCs)
Experience within a fast-growth cybersecurity company or within a security labs/innovation division focused on emerging threats or technologies
Active presence and network within the cybersecurity community, threat intelligence organizations, security research ecosystem, or industry consortiums is a plus

What We're Looking For

A seasoned cybersecurity leader and product strategist who brings deep technical credibility and hands-on threat intelligence experience combined with strong executive product management acumen. You understand evolving threat landscapes and advanced adversary tactics, have direct experience with threat intelligence analysis and threat hunting, and are passionate about applying emerging AI technologies to revolutionize how organizations detect and respond to threats. You can operate effectively at the executive level, balance strategic vision with execution discipline, and drive organizational alignment on complex, multi-year threat defense initiatives. You thrive in a fast-paced, innovation-focused environment and have the credibility to influence executive decision-making on security investments.

About Arctic Wolf

At Arctic Wolf, we foster a collaborative and inclusive work environment that thrives on diversity of thought, background, and culture. This is reflected in our multiple awards, including Top Workplace USA (2021-2025), Best Places to Work – USA (2021-2025), Great Place to Work – Canada (2021-2024), Great Place to Work – UK (2024-2026), and Kununu Top Company – Germany (2024-2026). Our commitment to bold growth and shaping the future of security operations is matched by our dedication to customer satisfaction, with over 10,000 customers worldwide and more than 2,000 channel partners globally. As we continue to expand globally and enhance our technology, Arctic Wolf remains the most trusted name in the industry.

Our Values

Arctic Wolf recognizes that success comes from delighting our customers, so we work together to ensure that happens every day. We believe in diversity and inclusion, and truly value the unique qualities and unique perspectives all employees bring to the organization. And we appreciate that—by protecting people’s and organizations’ sensitive data and seeking to end cyber risk— we get to work in an industry that is fundamental to the greater good.  

We celebrate unique perspectives by creating a platform for all voices to be heard through our Pack Unity program. We encourage all employees to join or create a new alliance. See more about our Pack Unity here.   

We also believe and practice corporate responsibility, and have recently joined the Pledge 1% Movement, ensuring that we continue to give back to our community. We know that through our mission to End Cyber Risk we will continue to engage and give back to our communities.  

All wolves receive compelling compensation and benefits packages, including:

Arctic Wolf is committed to fostering a welcoming, accessible, respectful, and inclusive environment ensuring equal access and participation for people with disabilities. As such, we strive to make our entire experience as accessible as possible and provide accommodations as required for candidates and employees with disabilities and/or other specific needs where possible. Please let us know if you require any accommodation by emailing recruiting@arcticwolf.com.   View our Hiring Page to learn more about our application process.

Security Requirements

jobs.description:
Job Title:- Account Director

Work Type:- Full-Time

Work Mode:- Hybrid

Tru Inc. is hiring an Account Director for an immediate permanent opportunity. This is a senior, client-facing role for someone who has already carried a portfolio of this size and sat across the table from a client executive team.

Position Overview:-

The Account Director owns the full client lifecycle for a $3M to $5M account portfolio, serving as an executive advisor to clients and a strategic partner to internal teams. This role leads digital growth strategies across CRM, marketing automation, commerce, analytics, and related enterprise platforms. The Account Director reports to Client Services leadership.

Location:-

This is a hybrid role with some work-from-home flexibility. Preference will be given to candidates in the Greater Toronto Area, as the role follows a three-day-per-week in-office schedule to support collaboration, workshops, and client engagement. Travel to client and partner offices is required.

The Accounts You’ll Own:-

What separates this role from our Account Manager role is the size and complexity of the accounts, not the seniority of the people in the room. Account Directors carry Tru’s most complex clients:
Scale:
Enterprise accounts and multi-workstream programmes, typically $500K+ in annual value each, totalling a $3M to $5M portfolio across 6-8 relationships.
Complexity:
Three or more concurrent workstreams per account, frequently with separate budgets, separate executive sponsors, and dependencies between them.
Client organization:
Matrixed enterprises where several executives hold competing priorities, and where procurement, IT, security, and brand each have a say in what ships.
Horizon:
Multi-year programmes where the roadmap outlives any individual project, and where this year’s decisions constrain next year’s options.

Core Responsibilities:-

Portfolio Management:
Own and grow 6-8 high-value client relationships, maintaining a $3M to $5M portfolio benchmark while managing budgets, contracts, invoicing, performance, satisfaction, and escalations.
Executive Advisory & Alignment:
Build trusted relationships across a matrixed client executive group, translating competing business priorities into a single actionable digital transformation plan.
Strategic Lifecycle Planning:
Lead Quarterly Business Reviews and develop multi-year marketing and technology roadmaps aligned to measurable client outcomes.
Cross-Functional Delivery:
Partner with engineering, marketing, and delivery teams to define scope, milestones, budgets, and timelines across concurrent workstreams.
Commercial Strategy:
Own portfolio-level commercial direction: multi-year agreements, rate and pricing negotiation, commercial exceptions, and margin across the full portfolio.
Commercial Growth:
Collaborate with Business Development and Client Services leadership to shape proposals, expand accounts, and decide where Tru invests for profitable growth.
Escalation Ownership:
Act as the named escalation point for the portfolio, resolving delivery, commercial, and relationship risk before it reaches leadership.
Capability Development:
Mentor Account Managers and set the standard for client-facing practice. The Account Director group is where Tru develops its next account leaders.
Operational Discipline:
Maintain CRM accuracy and pipeline health in HubSpot to support transparent reporting, resource forecasting, and account risk management.

Technical Platform Ecosystem:-

The Account Director should bring strong conceptual and architectural awareness of enterprise technology platforms to guide client roadmaps across these areas:
Enterprise CRM & Automation:
Use Salesforce and related platforms to improve lead generation, audience data management, engagement tracking, and pipeline efficiency.
Digital Experience & Content:
Advise on Adobe Experience Cloud and CMS initiatives that create consistent customer experiences across web, mobile, and digital channels.
Composable Commerce:
Guide API-first and headless commerce strategies, including CommerceTools, to support flexible and scalable digital storefronts.
Data Analytics & Insights:
Use analytics platforms, including Google Analytics, to track performance, build reporting models, and recommend data-backed optimizations.
Search & Performance Marketing:
Advise on SEO, AEO, and paid media strategy and campaign activations and optimizations.

This role advises on platform direction; it does not configure or build. Hands-on certification is welcome but not required.

What You’ll Bring:-

Professional Experience:
6 to 9 years of progressive experience in strategic account management, technology consulting, digital marketing, or enterprise agency environments.
Portfolio Scale:
Demonstrated ownership of client relationships at $1M+ in individual annual value, or a portfolio at $3M+, with the results to show for it.
Enterprise Complexity:
Experience inside matrixed client organizations where several sponsors hold competing priorities and no single person can approve a direction alone. Managing a senior relationship at a smaller, simpler account is valuable experience, but it is not the same job.
Commercial Authority:
A track record negotiating multi-year agreements, rates, and commercial exceptions, with accountability for margin as well as revenue.
Technical Fluency:
Experience managing enterprise-scale web applications, cloud solutions, systems integrations, or digital platforms.
Executive Communication:
Strong business analysis, storytelling, negotiation, and stakeholder-management skills for senior and C-suite audiences.
Client Advocacy:
Ability to navigate matrixed client organizations and turn ambiguous requirements into structured delivery plans.
Solution Orientation:
A results-driven mindset focused on delivering value, strengthening client relationships, and exceeding expectations.
Education:
Bachelor’s degree preferred in Marketing, Information Technology, Business Administration, or a related field.

Salary Range:- $100,000- $120,000

Where This Role Leads:-

Account Director is not the top of the ladder at Tru. The path continues into client engagement leadership — holding a group of accounts rather than a portfolio, developing the Account Directors who run them, and carrying commercial accountability at the practice level rather than the account level. Account Directors who grow their portfolio and build the next group of account leaders are the people we develop into that role.

Working at Tru:-

At Tru, we put people first. We offer competitive salaries, a 100% employer-paid benefits package, and a hybrid work arrangement. Our culture is grounded in courage, entrepreneurship, diversity, and a passion for people, supported by regular team events and live gatherings that build connection beyond day-to-day work.
Our values are:-
You Talk, We Listen

Integrity at Our Core

Quality as Standard

Delivered On Time

Join Tru and help clients make measurable progress across the digital platforms that power their growth.

jobs.description:
ABOUT NEW ENERGY NEXUS
 New Energy Nexus (NEX) is an international NGO that supports climate solutions and builds a more equitable clean energy economy. Our laser focus is on clean energy entrepreneurs: providing them with funds, accelerators, and networks to thrive. They are our main audience and our agent of change.

We started in California in 2004 and now operate across China, India, Southeast Asia, East and West Africa, and Australia. We have leveraged US$5.4 billion in investment and supported more than 11,000 entrepreneurs.

 ABOUT THE ROLE & OPPORTUNITY
 The Director of Development Strategy & Operations will lead the internal engine behind New Energy Nexus' global fundraising and business development efforts. Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, this role sits at the center of NEX's development team — turning what our development and partnerships staff and country teams learn on the ground with funders into a coherent, prioritized fundraising strategy, and making sure the team is coordinated, resourced, and focused on the highest-value opportunities. 
 This is not primarily a donor-facing relationship management role. It is a strategy, team leadership, and fundraising operations role for someone who understands the business and fund development cycle deeply enough to translate frontline intelligence — what funders are signaling, what's landing and what isn't, where proposals are stalling, which markets and programs are attracting interest — into clear direction for where the team should spend its time.
 The Director will lead and develop NEX's global platform-level development team, ensuring that individual team members' skills and expertise are deployed effectively against organizational priorities, while bringing together the knowledge and fundraising capabilities of country leaders, chapter teams, and program leads. The ideal candidate has the analytical rigor and systems mindset of a strong operations leader, paired with real fluency in philanthropic and development finance fundraising, so they can be a credible internal leader and partner to a globally distributed team of fundraisers, country directors, and program leads.

 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
 Fundraising Strategy & Prioritization (50%) 
 Help develop a living, prioritized development strategy based on proposal outcomes, funder conversations, and market signals gleaned from team conversations and learnings from fundraisers, country directors, and program leads
 Synthesize funder conversations, proposal outcomes, market signals and intelligence generated across the organization into clear fundraising priorities
 Identify where NEX should be focusing time and effort across programs and geographies, based on funder appetite, pipeline strength, and organizational priorities.
 Maintain a clear view of the funding pipeline across the network — by funder, program, chapter, and stage — and flag risks, gaps, or unrestricted-vs-restricted balance issues early.
 Translate strategy into concrete guidance: which opportunities to prioritize, which proposals need repositioning, where the team is over- or under-invested.
 Serve as a thought partner to the CEO and program leads on funding strategy, drawing on patterns across markets rather than any single relationship.

 Team Coordination & Enablement (35%) 
 Lead and develop the global platform-level development team including recruiting, hiring, onboarding, coaching, and managing performance, and ensure team members' skills are effectively leveraged against NEX's development priorities.
 Translate the development strategy into a clear rolling work plan for the team, aligning ownership, resources, and timelines.
 Build strong collaboration across the global development function, bringing together the expertise and fundraising capabilities of platform-level staff, country leaders, fundraisers, and program leads to maximize collective impact.
 Run the operating rhythm of the fundraising team: pipeline reviews, proposal coordination across programs/chapters/finance/communications, and prioritization check-ins.
 Coordinate multi-country and multi-program proposals, including combining country and program inputs into a cohesive narrative and budget that aligns with broader NEX operational and growth priorities.
 Build and own a central library of fundraising collateral - pitch decks, one-pagers, case studies, program summaries, impact data - so materials for funder meetings and conference talks can be assembled quickly rather than built from scratch each time.
 Draft and maintain core funder and conference decks, adapting a standard set of modular slides/content to each audience so our fundraisers can focus their time on external relationship-building and speaking rather than deck production.
 Partner with the Chief Communications Officer to keep collateral aligned with current messaging, program updates, and brand standards.
 Provide country leads and fundraisers with the tools, templates, frameworks, and support to raise funds effectively and report consistently.
 Build feedback loops so that what is learned through funder and country-level engagement consistently makes its way back into strategy, priorities, and team planning.

 Systems, Data & Reporting (15%) 
 Accountable for the fundraising CRM and pipeline-tracking systems, ensuring data quality, consistent use across chapters, and useful reporting.
 Produce regular and ad hoc reporting and dashboards for NEX leadership on pipeline health, funder trends, and progress against platform fundraising goals.
 Standardize proposal, reporting, and stewardship templates and processes across the global platform-level team.
 Track outcomes against the fundraising strategy and refine it as new data comes in.
 Ensure fundraising protocols and internal as well as external reporting are completed on time and to consistent quality standards

 SUCCESS IN THE FIRST 6–12 MONTHS
 Success in this role will mean building a more coordinated, strategic, and effective global development function. By the end of the first 6–12 months, the Director will have:
 Established clear visibility into NEX's global fundraising pipeline, priorities, risks, and opportunities, with leadership able to make decisions based on reliable, current information.
 Built a strong operating rhythm across the global platform-level development team, with clear ownership, effective collaboration, and team members' skills deployed against the highest-priority fundraising opportunities.
 Improved coordination across platform, country, and program teams so that high-value proposals are prioritized appropriately, developed collaboratively, and submitted on time and at a consistently high quality.
 Established consistent CRM and pipeline management practices across the development function, with data being used to inform strategy, prioritization, and reporting.
 Created a well-organized, accessible library of standardized fundraising collateral and tools that enables fundraisers and country teams to move more quickly and consistently.
 Established effective feedback loops between funder and country-level intelligence, fundraising performance, and the organization's overall development strategy.

jobs.title: Director, Private Capital, Financial Services
jobs.description:
The opportunity

Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan Board (Ontario Teachers') is a global investor with net assets of ~$279 billion as of December 31, 2025. Ontario Teachers’ is a fully funded defined benefit pension plan, and it invests in a broad array of asset classes to deliver retirement security for 346,000 working members and pensioners. Our Private Capital group deploys ~$60 billion across direct private equity investments and private equity funds globally.

The Director will be a senior member of our Financial Services investment team — partnering with our Senior Managing Directors and Managing Directors to source, diligence, execute, and direct private equity investments in the Financial Services sector. This is a development seat with a clear path toward independent deal leadership for a candidate who has already built a strong foundation in private equity investing.

Who You'll Work With

Reporting to the Managing Director, the role will be part of a deal team comprising analysts, associates, principals, directors, and managing directors, supported by third-party consultants, operating executives, and legal and accounting advisors dedicated to each transaction.

The Financial Services team invests across sub-sectors including Insurance, Wealth & Asset Management, Lending, Professional Services, and Cards & Payments, with particular need to understand the regulatory, AI, and digitization themes reshaping the sector. The role will also potentially partner with colleagues in OTPP's global offices on international investment and / or cross asset class opportunities in Financial Services.

What You'll Do

Serve as a key member of deal teams — conducting industry and company due diligence, building financial models, arranging debt financing, negotiating legal documents, and preparing written recommendations for the Underwriting Committee.
Lead or co-lead individual deals and workstreams with oversight from the SMD or MD; own specific diligence streams (financial, operational, commercial, legal, tax, insurance) end-to-end.
Post-close, remain actively involved with portfolio companies — often as board observer or board member — working with management on strategy, value creation, M&A, and refinancing.
Contribute to deal flow generation through desk research, consultant relationships, operating executive networks, conferences, and relationships with management teams.
Lead sub-sector deep dives and thematic research as the team evolves its coverage strategy, including emerging AI, regulatory, and digitization themes.
Manage and develop analysts, associates, and principals on deal teams; provide direct mentorship on diligence, modeling, judgment, and communication.
Work in a highly collaborative manner, bringing a complex network of stakeholders along (Global and Sector SMDs, MDs, deal teams, Portfolio Solutions team, international office leaders, portfolio companies, etc.). Strike the appropriate balance of being a confident decision-maker and an inclusive leader.
Build a network of operating executives, CEOs, consultants, bankers, and peer sponsors; progress toward independent deal sourcing by the end of Director tenure.
Develop value creation expertise in close partnership with the SMD and MDs; contribute to portfolio company initiatives as assigned.
Exercise judgment within deal teams and surface recommendations to the MD or SMD; lead individual workstreams and, over time, full deals with oversight.
Provide disciplined thinking, sound judgment, and courage of conviction, with a willingness to take balanced, thesis-driven risk. Intervene directly and effectively when required and escalate issues early.
Work cross-functionally and collaboratively with other teams to ensure continued alignment with OTPP's mission, vision, and values — including supporting and sharing knowledge with other areas of Investments and responding to ad hoc requests.

What You'll Need

~10+ years of meaningful work experience, including several years of recent private equity investing. Active M&A in a senior role in corporate development would also be considered. Supplemented by previous experience in management consulting, investment banking, and/or corporations (preferably corporate development or similar roles).
Experience playing a lead role on deal workstreams, including conducting due diligence, leading multiple diligence streams (financial, operational, legal, tax, insurance), arranging debt financing, and negotiating documentation.
Direct investment exposure to Financial Services preferred.
Familiarity with Financial Services sector dynamics — particularly Insurance, Wealth & Asset Management, Lending, Professional Services, and Cards & Payments — and the regulatory, AI, and digitization themes reshaping them
Some experience serving on “for profit” Boards of Directors or board committees a plus.
Strong academic background, with a financial designation (MBA, CFA, CBV, or CA strongly preferred).
Experience playing a leading role in the investment process, including conducting due diligence, arranging debt financing, and negotiating documentation.
Strong negotiating skills.
Ability to balance priorities, work independently, lead projects, and thrive in a high-performance team environment.
Very strong analytical and quantitative skills to perform and guide in-depth, innovative, critical analysis.
Deep understanding of fundamental investment analysis and private equity value creation.
Strong interpersonal skills and ability to build constructive relationships with internal and external parties, particularly management teams, boards, and senior advisors.
Strong communication skills, both oral and written, including IC paper authorship and presentation.
Willingness and ability to travel across North America and globally.

What We’re Offering

Numerous opportunities for professional growth and development
Comprehensive employer paid benefits coverage
Retirement income through a defined benefit pension plan
The opportunity to invest back into the fund through our Deferred Incentive Program
A flexible work environment combining in office collaboration and remote working
Competitive time off
Our Flexible Travel Program gives you the option to work abroad in another region/country for up to a month each year
Employee discount programs including Edvantage and Perkopolis

Through our Diversity, Equity and Inclusion strategy and our Employee Resource Groups (ERGs), we celebrate diversity and foster inclusion through events for colleagues to connect for professional development, networking & mentoring. Venture outside the ordinary - TMX Careers

The TMX group of companies includes leading global exchanges such as the Toronto Stock Exchange, Montreal Exchange, and numerous innovative organizations enhancing capital markets. United as a global team, we’re connecting cross-functionally, traversing industries and geographies, moving opportunity into action, advancing global economic growth, and propelling progress. Through a rich exchange of ideas, meaningful collaboration, and a nimble operating model, we're powering some of the nation's most critical systems, fueling capital formation and innovation, bringing increased opportunity to business visionaries, product ingenuity to consumers, and career exploration to our team.

Ready to be part of the action?

Reporting to the President, CDCC, this role is a critical strategic resource focused on accelerating Post Trade's strategy and objectives. The Managing Director will drive the execution of complex, high-impact market modernization initiatives, providing dedicated delivery leadership to Post-Trade Innovations and CDCC.

The main function of this role is to provide dedicated support to Post-Trade Innovations and CDCC in delivering the Post Trade product and client centric solutions. Success hinges on a proven capital markets expert with deep knowledge of the Canadian capital markets, with an emphasis on fixed income, derivatives and repo markets knowledge, established relationships with key industry stakeholders. This expertise is vital in driving strategic development and managing complex alignment across TMX and core industry partners, including the Bank of Canada (BoC) and CIMPA participants, optimizing and aligning the Post Trade delivery strategy, with special initial focus on delivering and establishing the Canadian Collateral Management Service (CCMS) and Repo 2.0.

Reports To: President, CDCC and Co-Head, Post-Trade Services
Job Location: This role is hybrid (2-3 days/week in the office) - we are open to candidates being located in one of our Canadian office locations: Toronto or Montreal.

Key Responsibilities

Program Delivery, Stakeholder Coordination, and Optimization
Unified Product-to-Delivery Lifecycle: Partner deeply with the Product Teams across Post Trade to translate product visions, commercial goals, and market requirements into robust, executable program delivery roadmaps.
Cross-Functional Delivery Governance: Establish rigorous execution frameworks, milestones, and governance models that ensure Post-Trade Innovations, CDCC, and CDS operate in perfect lockstep.
Strategy and Delivery Support: Provide dedicated, strategic and delivery support to Post Trade Innovations, CDCC and CDS to ensure the efficient execution of the overarching Post Trade delivery strategy.
Strategic Initiative Leadership: Provide strategic support for the execution and alignment of major market modernization initiatives, specifically the Canadian Collateral Management Service (CCMS) and the Repo program.
Central Bank Coordination: Serve as the primary liaison to ensure strategic and operational alignment required for the Bank of Canada's (BoC) integration into the Post Trade framework, including the implementation of the CCP tri-party repo platform.
Market and Client Engagement: Help cultivate and maintain relationships with key stakeholders (e.g., BoC, CIMPA) to gather strategic insights, champion clearing initiatives, and validate new service proposals for Post Trade.
Internal Alignment: Ensure optimal, formalized deliveries with key internal stakeholders to efficiently advance CCMS, Repo 2.0, and other core business objectives.

Governance & Execution Frameworks
Enforce key governance, including the formal escalation path and milestone criteria.
Take direct responsibility for strategic and operational conflict resolution across CDS and CDCC business lines.

Execution & Representation
Serve as the primary coordinator for external representation with Clearstream.
Establish a strict pre-briefing protocol for client engagements to ensure unified messaging regarding value propositions.
Design and implement a mandatory, structured knowledge-transfer and cross-training program to decentralize business and product expertise.

Operational Accountability & Resource Management
Enforce mandatory participation of all dedicated resources in CCMS squad meetings and planning sessions.
Implement unified resource-tracking dashboards for visibility into team capacity and competing priorities.
Provide formal performance evaluation input to the functional leaders of dedicated resources.
Maintain authority to initiate external recruiting processes if internal resource constraints delay critical strategic deliverables.

Leadership and Guidance
Manage hiring, training and development of team members; set comprehensive objectives for individual and organizational performance and growth, enforcing accountability at all levels.
Recruit, mentor, and elevate a world-class team of delivery professionals and subject matter experts. Instill a culture of extreme ownership, high psychological safety, and continuous improvement.
Collaborate with other senior resources to ensure that objectives are aligned across all functions and business units, and create a culture of change and continuous improvement.
Challenge the status quo in a manner which inspires others to welcome change rather than create tension, leading with influence rather than authority.
Act as a culture carrier who challenges the status quo constructively. Inspire cross-functional teams outside of direct reporting lines to embrace change, collaborate transparently, and break down legacy departmental silos.
Serve as a trusted adviser to provide support and strategic guidance, or take on time critical tasks with minimal prep time.
Enhance employee engagement and culture by fostering a positive work environment, promoting employee development, and recognizing and rewarding employee contributions.

Must Have(s)

Experience: Minimum of 15+ years of progressive leadership experience in fixed income markets, both in Canada and internationally, with a specific focus on the repo market and clearing markets, alongside a proven track record of delivering enterprise-scale market infrastructure programs.
Market Knowledge: Deep expertise in the Canadian fixed income and repo markets, combined with strong analytical skills to inform and execute strategic direction.
Product Expertise: Proven experience working on complex fixed income products and market structures, including repo clearing.
Commercial Engagement: Demonstrated commercial success and hands-on experience in engaging with buy-side and sell-side firms across Canadian and US markets to address complex operational and regulatory needs.
People Leadership: Exceptional track record of managing and transforming complex teams, developing future leaders, and driving high employee engagement scores in a fast-paced environment.
Matrix Leadership: Proven experience leading cross-functional teams in a complex environment (solid-line/matrix reporting) where resources must balance functional standards with strict program delivery timelines.
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Economics, or a related technical discipline.

Nice To Have(s)

Regulatory Experience: Demonstrated experience in engaging with central banks or other regulatory bodies on market initiatives is highly desirable.
Advanced Credentials: An MBA, CFA, or advanced degree in project/program management is highly desirable.
Governance Frameworks: Direct experience designing and executing formal project governance models, including RACI frameworks, cross-organizational risk management, and formal steering committee reporting is highly desirable.
Language Skills: Fluency in English and French is an asset, given regular communications with internal teams and external stakeholders.

In the market for…

Excitement
- Explore emerging technology and innovation, as well as ventures and digital finance that shape the future of global markets! Experience the movement of the market while grounded in the stability of close to 200 years of success.

Connection
- With site hubs in some of the world’s most multicultural cities, we leverage our size and structure to create rich connections and belonging while experiencing powerful global impact through our work.

Impact
- More than a platform, we use our talents to power mission-critical systems that drive global economic advancement, innovation, and growth. As well, our employee-led Team Impact spreads social good via our giving strategy.

Wellness
- From empathetic leadership to a culture of flexibility and balance, we believe wellness at work creates the maximum yield and a stronger “we”. Plus, with a cloud-first and hybrid workstyle, as well as generous time-off and leaves, we support a life well lived!

Growth
- From a growth mindset in our work, to expansion in our business, TMX is home to action-takers energized by the achievement of ambitious growth.

Ready to enrich your career with impactful work, leaders who truly care, and the flexibility and programs to help you thrive as part of #TeamTMX ? Apply now.

jobs.description:
Shape the Future of Sales Operations at Phreesia

Title:
Director, Head of Sales Operations

Team:
Phreesia Network Solutions

Location:
Remote EST or CST in Canada or the U.S., with occasional travel required for client meetings, industry events, conferences, and team collaboration.

Why This Role Exists

Phreesia Network Solutions partners with pharmaceutical manufacturers, biotech companies, media agencies, and other life sciences organizations to activate patients and engage providers with personalized, privacy-safe communications at the moments that matter most in care. Our media programs are sold — and re-sold — every year, which means our commercial engine has to run with precision: accurate forecasts, clean pipeline data, well-designed territories and quotas, and sellers who spend their time selling.

As Director, Head of Sales Operations, you will own that engine — and modernize it. You will be the connective tissue between Sales leadership, Finance, Marketing, Client Experience, and Client Solutions — turning strategy into operating cadence, data into decisions, and friction into process.

You will scale the commercial operation with AI at its backbone, embedding AI-driven forecasting, insights, and automation across the sales workflow so the team can grow revenue faster than headcount. Reporting to the SVP, Finance & Commercial Operations, you will lead an established Sales Operations team and own the systems, analytics, and planning disciplines that allow the PNS sales organization to scale efficiently as we grow across PatientConnect, ProviderConnect, MediFind, and our expanding solution portfolio.

What You’ll Spend Your Time Doing

Lead sales planning and go-to-market design. You’ll lead annual and quarterly sales planning across territory, capacity, quota, and compensation planning — designing balanced territories and account segmentation, modeling headcount needs, setting quotas tied to forecast targets, and partnering with Finance and People teams on compensation plans that incentivize the right behaviors across new business, renewals, and upsell. You’ll also support go-to-market planning for new offerings, ensuring rules of engagement, coverage, and targets are in place at launch.
Own forecasting and pipeline management. You’ll own the forecasting process and cadence, delivering accurate, defensible revenue forecasts across new business, renewals, and expansion for a business built on annually re-sold media programs. You’ll establish pipeline hygiene standards, stage definitions, and inspection rhythms; run weekly pipeline and forecast reviews with Sales leadership; and partner with Finance on bookings-to-revenue reconciliation, campaign delivery pacing, and quarterly business reviews.
Turn commercial data into actionable insights. You’ll build and maintain the reporting suite for the business, including pipeline, win/loss, retention and renewal rates, upsell, rep productivity, and brand- and agency-level performance. You’ll deliver insights that shape strategy — identifying where we’re winning, where deals stall, and which therapeutic areas and agency relationships are growing — and present those insights to senior leadership. You’ll also define and govern a single source of truth for commercial data across systems.
Scale systems, tools, and AI capabilities. You’ll own the sales technology stack — with Salesforce as the backbone, alongside forecasting, enablement, data enrichment, and workflow tools — including administration, roadmap, integrations, and vendor management. You’ll define and execute an AI roadmap for the commercial organization, deploying AI agents, predictive analytics, and intelligent automation to improve forecast accuracy, surface deal risk and next-best actions, automate non-selling work, and increase seller productivity. You’ll drive CRM adoption and data quality, design workflows that reduce manual effort for sellers and account teams, and ensure the clean, governed data foundation that AI-driven insights depend on. You’ll also evaluate emerging AI tooling with a practical eye — piloting quickly, measuring impact, and scaling what works.
Improve deal support and commercial processes. You’ll run deal desk functions, including pricing governance, approval workflows, proposal support, and order processing in partnership with Legal, Finance, and Client Experience. You’ll continuously identify and remove friction across the quote-to-cash process and own rules of engagement across Sales, Client Experience, and Market Development.
Scale sales best practices. You’ll identify what’s working across outreach cadences, deal motions, and renewal plays and scale those practices across the team to shorten sales cycles and maximize selling time. You’ll partner closely with Sales Enablement and Training, which is owned separately, to ensure process changes, tooling, and best practices are embedded in onboarding and ongoing coaching.
Lead and develop the Sales Operations team. You’ll lead, develop, and mentor an established Sales Operations team spanning analytics, systems administration, and deal support, shaping the function’s structure as the business grows. You’ll serve as a trusted operating partner to the SVP, Finance & Commercial Operations, Client Experience, and Sales leadership, taking meaningful non-selling work off the plates of the sales team so they can focus on clients and revenue.

What Makes You a Great Fit

You will be a great fit if you are:

Bring deep, hands-on expertise with Salesforce, including administration, reporting, and process design, and ideally have experience owning a broader revenue technology stack
Have demonstrated ownership of forecasting, territory and quota planning, and sales compensation design within a quota-carrying sales organization
Bring experience in media, advertising, point-of-care marketing, life sciences, or healthcare technology; familiarity with annually renewing or re-sold revenue models is a plus
Have a strong analytical toolkit, including hands-on use of AI tools for analysis, forecasting, and workflow automation, such as Salesforce Einstein/Agentforce, generative AI assistants, or similar
Are highly proficient with Excel or Google Sheets; experience with SQL and Power BI or similar BI tools is preferred
Know how to turn complex data into a clear, compelling narrative for executives
Have a demonstrated track record of scaling a commercial function with AI and automation — identifying use cases, driving adoption, and measuring productivity impact
Bring excellent cross-functional collaboration and communication skills and are comfortable operating at both strategic and hands-on levels in a fast-growing business

We Do Have A Few Requirements To Check

Bachelor’s degree required
10+ years of experience in sales operations, revenue operations, or commercial strategy, including 3+ years leading the function or a significant portion of it
Prior people management experience

Where You’ll Work

This is a remote role, with the expectation that you’re based in EST or CST in Canada or the U.S. Occasional travel is required for client meetings, industry events, conferences, and team collaboration.

Compensation & Rewards

Base Salary: $240,000-260,000 USD or $200,000-230,000 CAD (depending on experience) inclusive of base salary and variable incentive.
A comprehensive Total Rewards package designed to support your whole life — not just your work

Who We Are

At Phreesia, we’re looking for smart and passionate people to help drive our mission of creating a better, more engaging healthcare experience. We’re committed to helping healthcare organizations succeed in an ever-evolving landscape by transforming the way healthcare is delivered. Our SaaS platform digitizes appointment check-in and offers tools to engage patients, improve efficiency, optimize staffing, and enhance clinical care.

Phreesia cares about our employees by providing a diverse and dynamic work environment. We’re a five-time winner of Modern Healthcare Magazine’s Best Places to Work in Healthcare award and we’ve been recognized on the Bloomberg Gender Equality Index. We are dedicated to continuously improving our employee experience by launching new programs and initiatives. jobs.description:
About Life360

Life360’s mission is to keep people close to the ones they love. Our category-leading mobile app, Tile tracking devices, and Pet GPS tracker empower members to protect the people, pets, and things they care about most with a range of services, including location sharing, safe driver reports, and crash detection with emergency dispatch. Life360 serves approximately 107.7 million monthly active users (MAU), as of September 30, 2026, across more than 180 countries.

Life360 delivers peace of mind and enhances everyday family life with seamless coordination for all the moments that matter, big and small. By continuing to innovate and deliver for our customers, we have become a household name and the must-have mobile-based membership for families (and those friends who are basically family).

Life360 has more than 500 (and growing!) remote-first employees. For more information, please visit life360.com.

Life360 is a Remote First company, which means a remote work environment will be the primary experience for all employees. All positions, unless otherwise specified, can be performed remotely (within the US and Canada) regardless of any specified location above.

We are AI Native

We are building an AI native company where AI is an integral part of how we build and operate. AI tool usage during interviews varies by role. You may be asked to demonstrate proficiency with AI tools, discuss how you leverage AI, or complete interview exercises without AI assistance. Your Recruiter will provide clear guidance as you move through the interview process.

Undisclosed use of AI not previously discussed with or approved by your Recruiter may impact your candidacy.

About The Team

The Data & Analytics Team (DnA) is a 60+ person organization spanning data engineering, analytics engineering, analytics/decision science, and data science/ML. The science teams are organized into two sub teams, focusing on MAU and Revenue. This role leads decision science and data science within MAU.

You and your team will be responsible for understanding the drivers behind MAU: why members come, why they stay, and why they return. The team partners with product, marketing, and engineering to put those learnings into everyday work, and that work shapes our roadmaps.

Our data is unusual for a consumer company. Life360 measures families and circles rather than individuals, so one member's behavior affects another's, which makes measurement a different problem than a standard funnel. With billions of location events, driving behavior, crash detection, and Tile and Pet GPS trackers, we get a rich picture of physical behavior that few consumer companies can build.

About The Job

This Senior Director leads MAU Analytics and Data Science.

You and your team will work across acquisition, activation, engagement, and retention on the analysis, models, and experiments behind each. A lot of what this role owns needs to be built rather than maintained: the measurement, the standards, and how the team uses AI. The team is also raising its craft, and coaching people through that is an important part of the job. Within a year, your team members will be operating at an elevated skill level, proactively bringing key questions to light, and serving as trusted advisors whom stakeholders consult for strategic guidance rather than simple task execution.

You will report to the Head of Data and work closely with counterparts leading Revenue Analytics and Data Science, and with the leaders of Data Engineering.

For candidates based in the US, the salary range for this position is $247,000 to $366,000 USD. For candidates based out of Canada, the salary range for this position is $286,000 to $339,000 CAD.
We take into consideration an individual's background, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience in determining final salary. Base pay may also vary based on geographic location, with US work locations falling into one of three geographic tiers.

Total compensation is inclusive of equity compensation in the form of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs)
, as well as a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, vision, financial, and other benefits.

What You'll Do

Lead and develop the decision scientists and data scientists on the team, and set the quality bar for both disciplines.
Own the MAU driver model and the forecast.
Own the exploratory work that drives the strategy to grow MAU.
Establish how an analysis gets scoped, run, reviewed, and written up, so its quality does not depend on who picked up the request.
Partner with your Revenue counterpart and Data Engineering leadership to define common metrics, align on experimentation standards, and introduce unified operating practices across teams.
Build the operating model that gets the team into the roadmap conversation early, with a view on what to build and what to test.
Use agents and automated analysis daily, and expect the same of the team.
Shape how the team works AI-native: what gets delegated to agents, what gets automated, and what stays human judgment.

What We're Looking For

Required Experience & Qualifications

10+ years in analytics, data science, or decision science, including 5+ years in people management in a senior leadership role.
Deep expertise in inferential and causal analytics. Able to lead ML practitioners.
Expert knowledge of engagement, retention, churn, and cohort metrics.
Experience forecasting a company-level metric and being held to it.
SQL, plus Python or R.
Experience with Databricks, third party experimentation tools (e.g. Statsig), Tableau or similar BI tools, and AI native BI tools (e.g. Hex, AI/BI).
Hands-on with coding agents (Claude Code or equivalent) in your own analytical work.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent.

Nice to Have

Familiarity with experiment design to identify and control for network effects.
Master’s degree or PhD with an emphasis in social science, psychology or other behavioral science.
Experience leading a team that reports to you but sits embedded with product and engineering teams.
Experience in a B2C subscription business.

Core Expectations

You have moved an analytics team from reactive to embedded.
You coach and develop people, and you have grown analysts into leaders.
On your teams, analysis starts from a hypothesis rather than a data request.
You have built the standards a team works from, and got people to use them.
You are curious about why people behave the way they do, not just what they did.
You decide what the team does not work on, and you can defend it.

Our Benefits

Medical, dental, vision, life and disability insurance plans (100% paid for US employees). We offer life and disability as well as supplemental plans for medical and dental for Canadian employees.
401(k) plan with company matching program in the US and RRSP with DPSP plan for Canadian employees.
Paid parental leave
Mental Wellness Program & Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for mental well-being
Generous time off: flexible PTO, companywide holidays throughout the year plus summer and winter shutdowns
Learning & Development programs
Equipment, tools, and reimbursement support for a productive remote environment.
Free Life360 Platinum Membership and Tile trackers.

AI Usage:
We use AI to help make our hiring process efficient. That said, every hiring decision is made by real Life360 hiring teams

Life360 Values

Our company’s mission-driven culture is guided by our shared values to create a trusted work environment where you can bring your authentic self to work and make a positive difference

Be a Good Person - We have a team of high integrity people you can trust.
Be Direct With Respect - We communicate directly, even when it’s hard.
Members Before Metrics - We focus on building an exceptional experience for families.
High Intensity, High Impact - We do whatever it takes to get the job done.

Our Commitment to Belonging

Life360 is an equal opportunity employer. We don’t discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status, or any other legally protected status. We believe diverse perspectives make us better, and we’re building a workplace that reflects the communities we serve. Don’t meet every qualification? Apply anyway.

Location

Brookfield Place - 181 Bay Street

Business - Infrastructure

Brookfield Infrastructure Group is one of Brookfield’s primary operating groups. The Infrastructure Group is one of the world’s largest infrastructure investors, owning and operating critical assets across the transport, utilities, energy, and data infrastructure sectors. The Group operates and manages approximately $262 billion of assets owned through its private funds and publicly listed entity, Brookfield Infrastructure Partners. Our portfolio of assets facilitate the movement and storage of energy, water, freight, passengers and data, and are located in North and South America, Europe and the Asia Pacific regions. For more information, visit: https://www.brookfield.com/our-businesses/infrastructure

Brookfield Culture

Brookfield has a unique and dynamic culture. We seek team members who have a long-term focus and whose values align with our Attributes of a Brookfield Leader: Entrepreneurial, Collaborative and Disciplined. Brookfield is committed to the development of our people through challenging work assignments and exposure to diverse businesses.

Job Description

Brookfield Infrastructure Group’s Investment teams are responsible for sourcing, evaluating and executing new investment opportunities, as well as supporting strategic and capital allocation decisions across the Group’s existing portfolio. The team evaluates opportunities across Brookfield Infrastructure’s core sectors, including data infrastructure, transport, utilities, energy and other infrastructure-related businesses, while continually assessing new sectors and investment themes.

Based in Toronto, the Vice President will be a senior member of the Infrastructure Investment team and will work closely with senior investment professionals and operating teams across Brookfield’s global platform. The role provides significant exposure to the full investment lifecycle, including investment strategy and origination, transaction evaluation and execution, due diligence, financing and structuring, investment committee processes, and ongoing portfolio and capital allocation decisions.

The Vice President will play a leadership role in developing investment theses, evaluating opportunities and driving transaction execution. This individual will oversee financial analysis and due diligence, coordinate internal and external workstreams, prepare recommendations for senior management and investment committees, and contribute to the development of new investment opportunities and business relationships.

The role is well suited to a highly motivated investment professional who combines strong commercial judgment and financial capabilities with an entrepreneurial mindset and the ability to operate effectively in a dynamic, collaborative environment.

Responsibilities

Assist in developing and implementing investment, business development and transaction strategies across Brookfield Infrastructure’s target sectors.
Lead industry, company and market research to develop investment themes, identify attractive sectors and originate potential transaction opportunities.
Develop investment theses and identify potential value creation opportunities, key investment considerations and transaction or deal structures.
Lead the financial evaluation of prospective investments, including valuation, financial modelling, returns analysis, financing considerations and scenario analysis, while overseeing work prepared by junior team members.
Working closely with Brookfield’s operating teams, lead transaction due diligence to validate the investment thesis and business plan and identify key investment risks and opportunities.
Coordinate with legal, tax, finance and other internal teams, as well as external advisors, to lead transaction execution and ensure transaction documentation and structuring are consistent with the investment thesis and business case.
Prepare and present investment committee materials, transaction recommendations, bid letters and other materials for senior management.
Support negotiations and key transaction workstreams through signing and closing.
Contribute to portfolio and capital allocation initiatives, including evaluating strategic opportunities and potential follow-on investments within existing businesses.
Build and maintain relationships with management teams, industry participants, advisors, financial institutions and other market participants to develop new investment opportunities.
Provide leadership, coaching and mentorship to junior investment professionals, fostering their technical and professional development.
Contribute to a flexible, dynamic and team-oriented culture that emphasizes collaboration, accountability and high-quality execution.
Lead special projects and strategic initiatives as required.

Qualifications & Requirements

Approximately 8–10 years of relevant professional experience, with a strong investment background and demonstrated transaction experience. Infrastructure investing experience and relevant sector knowledge are preferred.
Strong knowledge of infrastructure investing and familiarity with one or more of Brookfield Infrastructure’s core sectors, including data infrastructure, transport, utilities and energy.
Demonstrated experience evaluating and executing complex transactions, including financial analysis, valuation, due diligence, structuring and transaction documentation.
Strong conceptual and financial capabilities, with the ability to understand the broader strategic and commercial context while remaining hands-on and maintaining exceptional attention to detail.
Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills and demonstrated ability to develop well-supported investment judgments from complex or incomplete information.
Ability to work effectively in a dynamic, complex and fast-paced environment, adapt quickly and manage multiple priorities and transaction workstreams.
Strong stakeholder management, negotiation and relationship-building capabilities.
Demonstrated business judgment, leadership ability and initiative.
Superior written and verbal communication and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with senior executives, investment committees, management teams and external counterparties.
Strong organizational skills and a demonstrated ability to lead teams and deliver high-quality work within demanding timelines.
Entrepreneurial, proactive and results-oriented, with a strong sense of ownership and accountability.
Demonstrated ability to earn trust and credibility with colleagues, management teams, advisors and external partners.
Motivated by collective success and comfortable operating within a highly collaborative team environment.
Intellectual curiosity and a desire to seek new experiences, knowledge and candid feedback.
Exceptional quality standards and a continued desire to develop new approaches and insights.
Self-motivated and proactive with respect to both managing workload and ongoing professional development.
