Brookfield’s success is built on a culture of collaboration, discipline and entrepreneurship. We look for individuals who take a long-term perspective, exercise sound judgment, take ownership of their work and contribute to the success and development of the broader team.

jobs.description:
Veritree And Job Overview

veritree is an award-winning climate tech start-up based in Vancouver. Launched in 2021, our technology measures and verifies the impact of global restoration efforts from the ground up. We are on a mission to plant 1 billion verified trees by 2030, collaborating with businesses, planting organizations, and consumers who believe in the transformative power of verified restoration projects to create real and meaningful impact for the planet, nature, and people.

veritree is seeking a Director, Operations to lead our Operations team: the glue that connects our teams and initiatives. Reporting to the COO, you will own veritree's Revenue Ops, Supply Ops, Business Ops, and Business Intelligence functions. These functions empower our Revenue, Forests, Product & Engineering, and Finance teams to operate as one business.

We sell verified trees sourced from planting partners worldwide, alongside new business lines in carbon, monitoring technology licensing, and nonprofit programs. That makes our business closer to a two-sided marketplace than pure SaaS: every customer commitment depends on supply, delivery, and data lining up behind it. As we move to a new AI-native platform, our Operations team is evolving into a team of operations engineers who build the tools, automations, and data flows the business runs on.

This is a hands-on role: you'll run operations first and then evolve the systems behind it. You inherit a capable team and working systems (several of which we've outgrown) and leave behind infrastructure the rest of the company can build upon. The role starts at Director-level, with room for advancement as determined by job performance and business needs.

12 Month Key Outcomes (12m KOs)

Take the wheel: within your first 90 days, run the weekly operations cadence, own escalations across all four functions, and become the decision-maker on operational calls
Operating rhythm: set up how Operations runs for the next stage of the company: a clear meeting rhythm, defined team roles/decision rights, one agreed definition and owner for core metrics (pipeline, ACV, NRR, gross margin, tree inventory), and a 12-month operations roadmap signed off by executive leadership
Trusted data and reporting: keep commercial and delivery data clean across HubSpot, NetSuite, and the platform through go-live and beyond, and produce the monthly reporting pack and the operational metrics in board reporting from the BI stack
AI and automation: ship AI-powered tools and automations that measurably reduce manual work and save costs across the business

What You'll Do

Cross-Functional Operations

Run the operating cadence (meeting cadences, monthly business reviews, semi-annual planning) and the forums where Revenue, Forests, and Product & Engineering align on priorities
Own the deal desk with Sales, Customer Success, and Forests, so what we sell matches what we can deliver
Own the intake, prioritization, and SLA framework for operations requests from every team
Own operational readiness on the platform after go-live: close workflow gaps with Product & Engineering and lead change management
Make operational and commercial decisions within agreed guardrails (pricing, margin floors, custom deliverables), and escalate exceptions to executive leadership with a clear recommendation

Team Leadership & Development

Lead, coach, and develop the Operations team, including managers and individual contributors
Own hiring, onboarding, and ongoing performance management, in partnership with People Operations
Evolve the team into operations engineers by defining roles and scopes and building a culture that is both high-accountability and high-support

Revenue Operations

Own HubSpot as our commercial system of record, including deal stages, order and contract workflows, and clean handoffs between Sales, Customer Success, Legal, and Finance
Own the customer revenue forecast and its methodology, in partnership with Finance and Revenue leadership
Own pricing discipline: the price sheet, margin floors, and a quarterly margin and pricing review
Own lead and sales funnel, retention, and unit-economics reporting

Supply Operations

Own demand and supply planning, translating the customer forecast into tree demand by ecosystem and region and partnering with Forests on sourcing and capacity
Own order management, inventory allocation, purchase orders, and fulfillment tracking, including future obligations to customers and planting partners, so every order is delivered on time against the right supply

Business Operations

Own the processes, policies, tooling, and Operations budget that keep the business running, and decide what gets automated and what stays manual
Run the OKR process and tracker, and support annual operating planning
Own the operating model for customer and partner site visits

Business Intelligence & Reporting

Own our data warehouse and BI layer, pulling from HubSpot, NetSuite, the platform, and planting data, as the single source of truth for operational metrics
Direct the team's AI agenda, shipping internal tools, agents, and workflow automations that measurably increase output across the business

Requirements

Qualifications

Professional Requirements Or Qualifications

8+ years in operations, including 3+ years leading a multi-function operations team (at least Revenue Operations and Business Operations) at a B2B company of roughly 75 to 250 people
Experience taking a company from founder-led, ad hoc operations to a repeatable operating system
Experience owning monthly and board-level operational reporting, including the data model and BI layer behind it
Strong HubSpot fluency (you know its strengths and its limits)
Fluency in commercial metrics: NRR, cohorts, funnel conversion, CAC and payback
Experience designing operating processes (intake, SLAs, deal desk) and leading change management for systems people use every day
You have an operating system (cadence, metric tree, single-owner accountability, an intake model) and can articulate it clearly
An AI-native way of working: you already use AI and automation to ship internal tools (e.g., n8n, AI agents)
Excellent written communication, with the ability to make decisions legible to an executive team and a board

Personal Strengths

An operator first: hands-on and low ego
Calm judgment under ambiguity: we're part SaaS, part supply chain, part marketplace, and our model won't fit a template
Pragmatic about data: a high bar on definitions, without waiting for perfect data to act
You learn how a system works before you change it
Genuine passion for sustainability and nature-based solutions

Nice to Haves (not mandatory)

Experience with physical supply or fulfilment (marketplaces, logistics, agriculture)
Experience in supply planning, including demand forecasting, inventory allocation, and capacity constraints
ERP experience, including quote-to-cash
Experience in impact, sustainability, carbon, or nature-based organizations, including grant-funded work or government affairs

Benefits

Benefits & Compensation Overview

At veritree, we recognize that compensation and performance development are key to attracting and retaining top talent. Our approach is grounded in fairness, transparency, and creating opportunities for growth as both our people and business scale.

Some highlights you can expect include:

Competitive salary with a performance-driven framework that ensures fair and consistent compensation reviews, tied to individual impact and business growth
Extended health, dental, and vision benefits
Additional Health Spending Account (HSA) / Lifestyle Spending Account (LSA) to support your well-being and lifestyle interests
A variety of time-off programs, including vacation, personal days, and a 4-week remote work program each year
Employee discount with tentree, our sister company
A flexible, hybrid work environment designed for collaboration and focus-driven impact

veritree ensures that compensation is reviewed fairly and consistently, with opportunities for salary progression tied to sustained performance. As such, the salary range for this role including variable compensation is $150,000 to $180,000 CAD.

This range is positioned around the 50th-75th percentile of market data we've collected, reflecting our commitment to competitive pay. Final offer amounts are based on the individual experience and skillset of the candidate demonstrated during the recruitment process.

We reserve the >75th percentile of our salary ranges for internal employees who demonstrate sustained high performance and impact at veritree.

veritree is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a team that represents diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. All employment decisions are made on the basis of qualifications, merit, and business needs.

jobs.description:
About Beacon:

Beacon is building the essential technology infrastructure for the everyday economy: the businesses, organizations, and services that make real life work, and that mainstream tech has largely left behind. We acquire, operate, and grow vertical market software companies. They are niche, founder-built businesses serving industries that are often overlooked and too profitable to ignore.

Our model is simple: we seek out founders who have built their business by spending years understanding their market and prioritizing their customers' specific needs. We buy great businesses, invest in their continued growth, and hold them permanently, accelerating that growth with an AI-native platform built specifically for vertical market software. No mandate to cut, flip, or roll up into something unrecognizable.

We are not a financial firm. We are technology entrepreneurs and operators who believe the most important businesses in the world are already running quietly in industries most people never think about. Our job is to find them, support the people who built them, and make them better.

Beacon is backed by a diverse base of investors, with $550M+ raised to date, including General Catalyst, Lightspeed, D1 Capital, CPMG, the family offices of the founders of Stripe, DoorDash, and Ramp, and evergreen funds built for the long game.

The Role:

VieFund is a Beacon company with remote teams in Toronto, Ottawa and Vietnam. Its software is the system of record for mutual fund, segregated fund and GIC dealers in Canada: advisor tools, trades, settlements, account bookkeeping, and reporting, connected to the industry through FundServ, CANNEX and exempt-market dealer networks.

We are looking for the next technical leader of VieFund. You will own the platform end to end and work closely with the current technical team in Ottawa and Vietnam to build deep knowledge of the product, the dealers, and the operating rhythm. In the first year, you keep every dealer running through tax season, the FundServ standard change, and year-end, and you draw up the plan to move the platform off its on-prem footing, modernize it and add more value to customers with AI. You are the person who understands what is going on quickly and decides what to do about it.

You will be the technical owner of a profitable, long-held product with real customers and real seasonal deadlines, with Beacon's engineering leadership behind you and the mandate to make it better.

What You'll Do:

Own the VieFund platform end to end: architecture, codebase, database, releases, and production operations.
Build and maintain complete documentation of system behaviour, dealer configurations, and operational runbooks.
Maintain and evolve VieFund's FundServ integration, including annual standard upgrades, certification, and resolution of transaction and reconciliation issues with counterparties.
Design, build, and maintain the transaction processing, account bookkeeping, and reporting logic at the core of the product, ensuring accuracy and auditability.
Act as the final escalation point for client-facing technical issues; diagnose root causes and implement durable fixes.
Plan and deliver around the industry calendar, including tax season, RRSP and RRIF deadlines, and regulatory and standards changes.
Define and execute the technical roadmap, including the migration from on-prem infrastructure to the cloud and the adoption of modern engineering and AI-assisted development practices.
Manage production environments across hosted and client-managed Windows Server deployments, including backups, patching, security, and uptime.
Partner with hosting providers, dealers, and internal stakeholders to deliver reliable service and clear communication.
Hire, mentor, and lead engineers and contractors as the team grows.

What we are looking for:

Must have:

Deep, hands-on FundServ experience. Not just sending and receiving files: you have lived through the yearly standard change, you have debugged failures that originated at other vendors or at the fund, and you know how to work the problem when the documentation does not help.
Mutual fund transaction accounting and reporting. You understand the bookkeeping behind trades, settlements, distributions, and corrections, and you have fixed it when it was wrong.
Expert in .NET, MSSQL, and T-SQL. Much of the dealer-specific logic lives in stored procedures and scripts. You are at home there.
Windows Server management. You can stand up, patch, back up, and troubleshoot production servers, including ones you do not control.
Able to be in Ottawa at least bi-weekly for the first six months as part of onboarding. Knowledge transfer happens in person.
Judgment that does not need a committee. You will often be the only engineer in the room.
Easy to work with. Dealers call when something is wrong. The team has to trust you with the product.
Daily use of AI coding tools, and the drive to bring them into a codebase that has none.

Nice to have:

Experience migrating an on-prem system to the cloud, and the judgement to sequence it without breaking customers.
FIX protocol, for the ETF side of the business. Small part of the work, easy to pick up, but a head start helps.
Experience at a Canadian wealth or dealer platform (back office, transfer agency, or dealer software).
Experience replacing a long-tenured sole owner of a system.

Location and Working Arrangement:

Remote with ability to meet with with the teams in Ottawa and/or Toronto, Ontario. During onboarding must be able to be in Ottawa bi-weekly for the first 6 months.
Some work happens outside dealer business hours so it does not disrupt their day. Expect occasional evenings and weekends, heaviest around the seasonal peaks. Reducing this is part of the modernization mandate, but it is the reality today.

Our Values at Beacon Software

Humility: We acknowledge that the path to getting to the right answer involves being wrong along the way. We have strong beliefs which are weakly held. We actively seek new ideas and believe we can learn from anyone at any time.
Honesty: We are truth seeking in our approach to business problems. Business is a repeat game and we believe that human relationships generate alpha. We understand that trust is earned over a lifetime and can be lost in an instant.
Hunger: We play to win. We hold ourselves to high standards and will not be outworked. We take pride in having a deep sense of responsibility to ourselves, each other, our partners, and our customers. We believe to whom much is given much is expected.
Horizon: We seek to build a generational software company. This will take decades. We manage our expectations and those of our partners to take advantage of the 8th wonder of the world - compounding growth.

How We Use AI in Our Hiring Process:
To ensure transparency, we want candidates to know that Beacon Software uses Artificial Intelligence and AI-enabled tools to assist with screening, reviewing, organizing and highlighting profiles and applications that match the key requirements for each role.

AI does not make hiring decisions:
Every application is reviewed by a member of our team, and all decisions throughout the process are made by humans. We use AI to support efficiency and consistency, not to replace human judgment. We are committed to a fair, thoughtful, and equitable experience for every candidate.

The MHCW RCP, in alignment with Ontario Health-Cancer Care Ontario (OH-CCO), oversees the delivery and quality of cancer services for over 2 million residents across Mississauga Halton and Central West, including Etobicoke, Mississauga, Halton Hills, Oakville, Milton, Georgetown, Bolton, Brampton, Caledon, Malton, Orangeville, Rexdale, Shelburne and Woodbridge.

As the Regional Cancer Program Director for the Mississauga Halton Central West Regional Cancer Program, you will report to the Regional Vice President. A broad and influential leadership role that includes both a regional and programmatic mandate, you will lead regional planning and performance improvement in one of the largest regional cancer programs in the province. The Regional Director leads an inter-professional team providing system and regional leadership, relationship management, performance management and financial and risk management for cancer services across the region. Cancer Services include Systemic Treatment, Radiation Therapy, Surgical Oncology, Cancer Imaging, Pathology & Lab Medicine, Prevention, Cancer Screening, Primary Care, Psycho-social Oncology, Patient Education, and Survivorship. Additionally, the role provides integration and engagement/support for the Regional Endoscopy Services, Complex Malignant Haematology, Regional Cancer Informatics and Patient Experience across 4 hospitals partners (10 hospital sites), and 34 OSBP sites.

The Regional Director, in collaboration with the Regional Vice President and in alignment with the Ontario Cancer Plan 6, will lead the delivery of strategic initiatives to ensure quality care for patients and their families, and will play a vital role in building and sustaining excellence in regional service delivery.

Support performance oversight of the cancer system in the region (including performance of volumes, data, access safety and quality) and lead efforts to improve regional performance
Champion provincial cancer standards to ensure these are put into practice at the point of care, through dissemination of standards and compliance monitoring
Support the RVP to oversee cancer related funding within the RCP, assessing existing capacity and developing strategies to optimize regional resources
Collaborate and liaise with OH-CCO and the Regional Directors throughout the province through participation and leadership on provincial committees and projects with the goal to advance the overall care experience for persons with cancer in our community

Excellent oral and written communication skills

Funded by all levels of government, donors, and corporate partners, Dixon Hall is a multi-service, charitable organization committed to empowering the lives of the most underserved, marginalized, and at-risk communities in downtown East Toronto. As Dixon Hall approaches its centenary in 2029, significant growth in housing, real estate, and community services presents exciting opportunities to deepen its community impact, while increasing the need for strategic financial leadership, disciplined capital planning, effective risk management, and integrated operations.

The Chief Financial and Operations Officer is a newly created role that will be instrumental in supporting Dixon Hall’s continued growth and long-term sustainability. A CPA with progressive senior leadership experience in a complex, unionized, multi-site environment, the successful candidate will bring strong financial and operational expertise, including experience with real estate, capital development, and financing. Collaborative, values-driven, and influential, the CFOO will build trusted relationships with colleagues, funders, lenders, and other partners. Deliver executive-level presentations and updates to senior leadership, including project milestones, risks, and key achievements.

Bachelor’s degree in business, Finance, Economics, Technology, or related field.
10+ years of experience in Business Analysis, Operations Change, or Project Management within Corporate / Investment Banking.
Minimum 5+ years of hands-on experience with Finastra LoanIQ, ACBS and/or other core Lending platforms
VP-level experience in Business Analysis, Lending Operations, Product, Change Management, or related banking functions.
Strong hands-on experience with LIQ, ACBS or other core lending platform in a business, operational, product, or change capacity.
Deep understanding of commercial lending, including syndicated loans, bilateral loans, agency servicing, trading, and secondary loan markets.
Proven experience supporting or leading large-scale system implementations, particularly migration from legacy platforms to vendor solutions.
Strong experience writing business requirements documents (BRDs), functional specifications, process maps, gap analyses, and UAT documentation.
Strong knowledge of the end-to-end loan lifecycle, including origination, servicing, rollover, rate setting, fee processing, payments, notices, and settlements.
Strong stakeholder management experience with the ability to engage senior leaders, business users, and technology teams effectively.
Excellent analytical, problem-solving, written, verbal, and presentation skills.
Experience defining creative solutions to meet business needs.
Experience in creating training plans and training materials and in training Operations on functionalities developed by IT.

Preferred Qualifications

3+ years of hands-on experience with LoanIQ, FIS ACBS and/or legacy Loans platforms
Experience in Target Operating Model design and business process re-engineering.
Knowledge of agent bank operations, lender servicing, primary/secondary loan trading, and fee processing.
Experience with data mapping, conversion, interfaces, and reconciliations between LoanIQ and surrounding applications.
Familiarity with Agile, Waterfall, or hybrid delivery methodologies.
Exposure to tools such as JIRA, Confluence, Visio, Excel, and PowerPoint.
Experience working with global teams across Operations, Technology, Product, and Change.
Knowledge of control, audit, risk, and regulatory considerations in lending operations.
Knowledge of various application functionalities that translate across products.
Ability to identify and assess near-term business needs and advise business and technology on options and benefits.

Core Skills

LoanIQ / LIQ subject matter expertise
Business analysis and requirements gathering
Process mapping and gap analysis
Lending operations knowledge
Legacy platform migration support
Data mapping and reconciliation
Stakeholder and workstream leadership
UAT and testing support
Process improvement and automation
Executive communication and presentation skills

What Success Looks Like

Requirements are captured clearly and translated into actionable deliverables for technology and operations teams.
Legacy platform migration activities are supported effectively, with strong focus on data mapping, reconciliation, and operational readiness.
Future-state processes are well designed, controlled, and aligned to business objectives.
Stakeholders across business, operations, technology, and vendors remain aligned throughout the delivery lifecycle.
LoanIQ/ACBS/Legacy loans platform/other Peripheral system solutions are implemented or enhanced with strong operational readiness and minimal disruption.
Risks, issues, and dependencies are proactively identified and managed.

Madison Taylor Design is a leading multidisciplinary design firm providing architectural, landscape architecture, interior design, furniture & decorating, project management, and construction services for clients in the residential, commercial, and hospitality sectors. Our mission is to deliver high-end design solutions that blend inspiration from nature with modern and sustainable materials.

At the heart of Madison Taylor Design is our people and the experience we create together. Our core values are the backbone of how we work, lead, collaborate, and make decisions — we believe exceptional work comes from exceptional teams, built on strong culture, clear expectations, trust, and accountability. We run on the Entrepreneurial Operating System (EOS®) to create clarity, accountability, and alignment as we scale.

Summary

We are seeking an experienced Head of Business Services to lead the finance and people functions at Madison Taylor Design. You will oversee our financial operations, including month-end close, financial reporting, cash flow, forecasting, banking relationships, and financial controls, while also leading human resources administration with the support of our outsourced HR partner.

As a member of our leadership team, reporting to the Integrator, you will build and lead our newly hired full-charge bookkeeper and administrative team, providing the financial insight, processes, and accountability needed to support the business. This is a hands-on leadership role requiring strong technical expertise, sound judgment, and the ability to work both strategically and in the details.
Reports to: Integrator

Location: Midhurst, ON — on-site

Employment Type: Full-time, permanent

Compensation: $95,000–$115,000 annually, commensurate with experience, plus quarterly performance bonus and profit share

Application Deadline: Hiring now — applications reviewed on a rolling basis

Key Responsibilities

Finance

Oversee the monthly financial close, reconciliations, and financial statements, ensuring accurate and timely reporting.
Develop and maintain annual budgets, rolling forecasts, cash-flow projections, and divisional profit and loss reporting for design, construction, and furniture.
Oversee project and construction job costing, client deposits and retainers, monthly billing, and financial reconciliations.
Manage banking relationships, including lender reporting, covenants, and credit facilities.
Oversee payroll, HST, source deductions, and year-end reporting in coordination with external accountants.
Establish and maintain financial controls, approval processes, and accounting procedures.

Job Title

Head of Merchandise Operations & Financial Planning

About This Role

Giant Tiger is looking for a strategic merchandise leader to help shape the next chapter of our business as we strengthen our position as a Hard Discount retailer.

This is a significant merchandising leadership role with the opportunity to influence how Giant Tiger plans, operates and delivers value to Canadians. Reporting into our Executive Vice President and Chief Merchant, you will lead Merchandise Operations and Financial Planning, establishing the financial plans, operating rhythms and decision-making frameworks that guide our merchandising business. From sales, margin and inventory planning to pricing, promotions and space productivity, you will help ensure our merchandising strategies translate into disciplined execution, profitable growth and consistently low prices our customers can trust.

Giant Tiger operates differently than Canada's largest retailers. We are a Canadian-owned retailer with more than 260 stores, including a significant franchise network. Our success depends on keeping things simple, making disciplined decisions and ensuring our strategies can be executed consistently across our stores.

jobs.description:

À propos du Centre Mechtilde

Depuis 45 ans, le Centre Mechtilde accompagne et soutient les femmes et leurs enfants vivant des situations de violence conjugale, familiale ou toute autre forme de violence. Au fil des années, l'organisme a su faire évoluer ses services pour répondre aux besoins changeants des femmes et aux réalités de la société, dans une approche inclusive, accueillante et respectueuse de la diversité.

Le Centre Mechtilde offre notamment un service d’hébergement d’une capacité de 17 places, accessible 24 heures sur 24, 7 jours sur 7, ainsi que des services d'accompagnement visant à favoriser la sécurité, l'autonomie et le mieux-être des femmes et de leurs enfants. Depuis 2018, l'organisme assure également la gestion de La Maison Marie Jacque, un projet de logement communautaire comptant 31 logements, destiné aux femmes et à leurs enfants confrontés à des enjeux de stabilité résidentielle ou à un risque d'itinérance.

Pour réaliser sa mission, le Centre peut compter sur une équipe de 28 employées, réparties entre l'administration (3 personnes, incluant la direction générale), la coordination (2 personnes) et l'intervention (23 employées syndiquées). Ensemble, elles contribuent à offrir un milieu sécurisant et des services favorisant le développement de l'autonomie, la création de relations saines et l'atteinte des objectifs personnels des femmes accompagnées.

Rôle de la directrice générale

La directrice générale exerce un leadership mobilisateur, humain et stratégique, guidé par les valeurs et la mission du Centre Mechtilde et de La Maison Marie Jacque. Elle joue un rôle clé dans la consolidation, le développement et le rayonnement de l'organisme, tout en veillant à offrir un environnement sécurisant et bienveillant aux femmes et à leurs enfants. En étroite collaboration avec le conseil d'administration, les équipes et les partenaires du milieu, elle assure la pérennité de l'organisation, favorise la mobilisation des ressources et contribue à l'évolution des services en réponse aux besoins des femmes accompagnées.

Sommaire des fonctions

Sous l'autorité du conseil d'administration, la directrice générale assure la gestion globale des activités et des ressources humaines, financières, matérielles et administratives du Centre Mechtilde et de La Maison Marie Jacque. Elle veille à la qualité et à la continuité des services, encadre les équipes de gestion et assure le respect des politiques, des obligations organisationnelles et de la convention collective. Elle travaille étroitement avec le conseil d'administration à la mise en œuvre des orientations stratégiques, à la saine gouvernance et à l'atteinte des objectifs de l'organisme. Elle assure également le développement des partenariats et la représentation de l'organisme auprès des acteurs du milieu.

Tâches et responsabilités

Gestion stratégique et opérationnelle
Assurer la gestion globale des activités et des services.
Veiller à l'application des politiques, des procédures et des orientations organisationnelles.
Participer à l'élaboration des orientations stratégiques et assurer la mise en œuvre des plans d'action qui en découlent.
Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les deux coordonnatrices afin d'assurer la qualité, la cohérence et la continuité des services.
Superviser le bon fonctionnement des deux installations et veiller à une utilisation optimale des ressources matérielles.

Gestion des ressources humaines
Superviser, soutenir et mobiliser les membres de l'équipe sous sa responsabilité directe.
Assurer une gestion efficace des ressources humaines de l’organisation.
Veiller à l'application des politiques et des pratiques de gestion des ressources humaines ainsi qu'au respect des obligations de l'employeur.
Favoriser un climat de travail sain, collaboratif et respectueux des valeurs de l'organisme.
Assurer une gestion harmonieuse des relations de travail dans un environnement syndiqué, conformément à la convention collective en vigueur.

Gestion financière et administrative
Assurer une saine gestion financière de l'organisme et veiller à sa pérennité.
Superviser l'élaboration des budgets annuels et assurer le suivi des résultats financiers.
Veiller au respect des exigences des bailleurs de fonds et des obligations de reddition de comptes.
Assurer le suivi des ressources financières et matérielles en fonction des priorités organisationnelles.
Contribuer à la recherche et au maintien des sources de financement nécessaires à la réalisation de la mission.

Gouvernance et collaboration avec le conseil d'administration
Collaborer étroitement avec le conseil d'administration et sa présidence dans la réalisation des orientations et des priorités de l'organisme.
Préparer les rencontres du conseil d'administration, documenter les dossiers et transmettre les informations nécessaires à la prise de décision.
Assurer le suivi et la mise en œuvre des décisions du conseil d'administration.

Relations avec le milieu, partenariats et représentation
Développer et entretenir des relations de collaboration avec les partenaires communautaires, institutionnels et financiers.
Représenter l’organisation lors d'événements, de rencontres de concertation et d'activités officielles de l'organisme dans son milieu.
Identifier les occasions de collaboration et de développement favorisant la réalisation de la mission.
Agir à titre de porte-parole de l'organisme, selon les orientations établies avec le conseil d'administration.

Profil recherché

Diplôme universitaire de 1er cycle dans un domaine relié à l’administration, en sciences sociales (psychologie, travail social, relations industrielles), en psychoéducation ou dans un domaine connexe.
Expérience de 3 à 5 ans dans un poste de gestion similaire incluant la supervision d’employées (en milieu syndiqué, un atout) et la gestion du budget.
Expérience en gestion de budgets d’OBNL avec une approche stricte, transparente et rigoureuse.
Expérience à travailler avec des maisons d’aide et d’hébergement pour femmes victimes de violence, un atout.
Expérience à diriger une équipe de professionnelles multidisciplinaires.
Expérience de collaboration avec un conseil d’administration.
Habileté marquée pour la reddition de comptes et la gestion rigoureuse de subventions.
Capacité à optimiser les ressources financières dans un contexte limité.
Leadership positif et collaboratif.
Éthique professionnelle, bon jugement, autonomie, sens de l’initiative, sens de l’organisation, capacité à prendre des décisions difficiles, bonne capacité d’adaptation et rigueur.
Bonne maîtrise du français à l’oral et à l’écrit, et bilinguisme considéré comme un atout.
Capacité à se déplacer de façon autonome entre deux sites de travail et disponibilité pour effectuer d’autres déplacements occasionnels.

Conditions de travail

Poste permanent à temps plein avec horaire flexible ayant une moyenne de 40 heures par semaine. Disponibilité requise occasionnellement en soirée et certaines fins de semaine, lors de la tenue d’événements et de rencontres.
Salaire annuel selon la grille salariale en vigueur, à partir de 85 000 $, selon l’expérience. Une prime annuelle de rendement est offerte selon les objectifs de travail.
Possibilité de télétravail limité, de façon occasionnelle, avec une présence majoritaire en alternance sur les lieux des deux installations.
Régime d’assurance collective et régime de retraite offerts.
4 semaines de vacances par année.
12 journées de maladie par année.
11 journées fériées par année.
2 journées de congé social.
Cellulaire fourni.
Budget pour développement professionnel.
Remboursement des déplacements dans le cadre des fonctions.

Le conseil d'administration du Centre Mechtilde a mandaté la firme Tango – Solutions RH pour l’accompagner dans ce processus de dotation. Toute candidature reçue sera traitée avec la plus grande confidentialité. Seules les personnes retenues pour l’entrevue seront contactées.

Veuillez soumettre votre candidature (curriculum vitae et lettre de motivation obligatoire) au plus tard le mercredi 2 décembre à midi à l’adresse courriel suivante : apoirier@tangoRH.ca avec pour objet le titre du poste convoité.

Les candidatures retenues devront être disponibles pour une entrevue en présentiel, les 7 et 8 décembre 2026 selon l'horaire prévu, aux bureaux de Tango – Solutions RH situés au 394, boul. Maloney Ouest, bureau 106, dans le secteur Gatineau.

Dans le cadre de ce processus de recrutement, des outils intégrant des fonctionnalités d’intelligence artificielle peuvent être utilisés pour soutenir l’analyse et l’évaluation des candidatures. Ces outils servent d’appui au travail de l’équipe, sans remplacer l’intervention humaine. Tous les résultats sont révisés et validés par notre équipe.

jobs.description:
**WHO WE ARE**


GreenShield is a proudly Canadian, national non\-profit health care and insurance organization, driven by our mission of Better Health for All. We believe health care is a right, not a privilege, and we are committed to improving health outcomes, advancing health equity, and building a future where every Canadian can reach their full health and well\-being potential.


Through our unique integrated payer\-provider ("payvider") model, we offer insurance, administer benefits, and pay claims as a ‘payer’ while offering health care services such as mental health, pharmacy, telemedicine, and chronic disease management as a ‘provider’. As a non\-profit social enterprise without shareholders, we reinvest our excess earnings to directly support underserved communities. Through GreenShield Cares, we positively impacted the health and well\-being of over one million Canadians between 2020 and 2025\. What’s driving us now is the commitment to measurably impact an additional three million Canadians by 2030 – across mental health, essential medicines, and chronic disease management – through scalable initiatives that deliver meaningful change in pursuit of our mission of Better Health for All.


At GreenShield, our culture is where purpose meets passion and performance. Our teams work as one to deliver meaningful, measurable impact for the people and communities we serve.

**THE ROLE IN A NUTSHELL**

  

  

The Director, Information Security Operations is a key enterprise leader accountable for shaping and advancing GreenShield’s security strategy to safeguard digital and cyber assets in alignment with organizational objectives and risk appetite. This role continuously drives security resilience at scale, overseeing a 24/7 Security Operations Center (SOC) and leading mission\-critical functions including incident response, vulnerability and threat management, penetration testing, and cloud/application security. As a trusted advisor to senior leadership, you will define and execute the security operations roadmap, influence enterprise architecture decisions, and ensure compliance with regulatory and customer contractual requirements. You will champion operational excellence, optimize capacity and demand, and embed a culture of accountability and continuous improvement. Beyond operations, you will engage cross\-functionally, contribute to board\-level reporting and strategic planning to position Information Security as a business enabler and trusted advisor to the business.

  

Responsibilities:

* Provide strategic leadership, oversight, and operations of security technologies, controls, and platforms to protect enterprise assets and data.
* Lead cyber incident response activities, including containment, recovery, and management of incidents throughout their lifecycle, covering both internal and third\-party risks.
* Ensure regular vulnerability scans, penetration testing and red team exercises, and build/manage a threat intelligence program to proactively identify and respond to emerging threats. Champion secure software development lifecycle (SSDLC) practices, monitor remediation activities for go\-live readiness.
* Collaborate with CISO and peers to set strategic directions and roadmaps in alignment with business strategy and risk appetite
* Present security posture, threat landscape and metrics to senior audiences
* Own security operations budget and vendor strategy ensuring cost optimization and technology alignment with enterprise
* Ensure control operating effectiveness to support regulatory and compliance requirements (SOC2, ISO27001, NIST\-CSF)
* Influence enterprise security architecture roadmap
* Responsible for multi\-cloud security, and advanced threat detections capabilities for applications
* Train, develop, and coach staff; promote cross\-training and knowledge sharing; drive best practices and continuous improvement of delivery processes and user experience.
* Build high\-performing team with succession planning for senior roles.
* Subject matter expert consultation, initiative coordination, audit and compliance, board and committee reporting contribution and strategic support

 **WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR**

  

* University degree in Computer Science or equivalent.
* Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP)
* Minimum of 10 years of related experience in enterprise IT environments, with at least 5 years in a leadership role.
* Strong technical knowledge in network and endpoint security
* Knowledge in application security and hardening
* Expert knowledge in cyber incident response technologies and understanding of adversarial techniques, tactics, and procedures (TTPs).
* Proficient in security event monitoring, threat intelligence, security operations center (SOC), and incident response technologies
* Strong leadership capabilities to motivate, build, develop and lead effective teams to achieve results.
* Verbal and written communication with a spectrum of senior management, executives, users, other technical teams, external customers, to enable and influence business outcomes.
* Strong problem\-solving abilities and ability to work effectively under pressure.
* An accomplished facilitator with excellent interpersonal and communications skills that support working effectively in multi\-disciplinary and multiple location team environments.
* Experience in partnering with technology, product and program management teams.
* Highly developed planning, organizing and negotiating skills; can manage multiple tasks, meet tight deadlines and respond to changing priorities.

  

NICE TO HAVE:


* University degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science or equivalent.
* Certified Information Security Manager (CISM)
* Certificate of Cloud Security Knowledge (CCSKv4\)

At GreenShield, our culture is where purpose meets passion and performance. Our teams work as one to deliver meaningful, measurable impact for the people and communities we serve.

**THE ROLE IN A NUTSHELL**


The Director, Internal Audit Services leads GreenShield’s independent third line of defence, providing objective assurance on the effectiveness of governance, risk management and internal controls across the enterprise.


Reporting to the President \& CEO with accountability to the Board of Directors as well, the leader provides the Board, its committees and executive leadership with clear insight into significant risks, the strength of related controls and governance practices, and whether management is effectively addressing identified issues.


As GreenShield advances its strategy and further connects its payer and provider businesses, the leader ensures audit priorities reflect the changing risk environment. This includes assurance over transformation, growth, acquisitions and integration, new partnerships, and risks related to technology, cyber security, data and AI, privacy, regulatory requirements, third parties and operational resilience.


We’re looking for a credible, forward\-looking internal audit leader who brings strong professional judgment, enterprise perspective and the independence to challenge constructively. The ideal candidate can translate complex risk and control matters into clear implications for the Board and executive leadership, while building trusted relationships across the organization without compromising the objectivity of the function.


This leader will bring the discipline to maintain a strong third line of defence and the pragmatism to ensure Internal Audit Services remains relevant as GreenShield’s strategy, operating model and risk environment continue to evolve.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Lead Internal Audit Services, setting the function’s strategy, direction and operating model. Oversee its budget, resourcing approach, audit methodologies and capability priorities, with accountability for the risk\-based audit plan.
* Develop and oversee a forward\-looking audit plan that provides appropriate assurance over GreenShield’s most significant enterprise risks and reflects changes in strategy, the operating model, regulatory expectations and the external environment.
* Provide independent assurance to the Board and Audit Committee on the effectiveness of governance, enterprise risk management and internal controls.
* Ensure audit coverage addresses risks across GreenShield’s payer and provider businesses and the connections between them. Coverage includes technology, cyber, data and AI, privacy, regulatory, third\-party, partnership and operational resilience risks.
* Provide clear, timely reporting that supports decisions on material risks, control or governance gaps and audit results. Report on management’s responses and verify whether agreed actions have been completed and are effective.
* Advise the President \& CEO, executive leadership and Board committees on significant and emerging risk and control matters while preserving the independence and objectivity of Internal Audit Services.
* Escalate significant issues appropriately and lead Internal Audit Services’ preparation for and participation in Audit \& Investment Management Committee and Board meetings.
* Coordinate assurance work with Risk, Privacy, Compliance and other assurance partners while maintaining clear boundaries between management responsibilities, second\-line oversight and independent internal audit. Preserve Internal Audit Services’ independence without assuming management responsibility.
* Bring an assurance perspective to major transformation, growth, acquisitions and integration, new partnerships and changes to GreenShield’s operating model, without taking on management accountability.
* Ensure Internal Audit Services complies with applicable regulatory expectations, professional standards and the Institute of Internal Auditors’ Global Internal Audit Standards, supported by an effective quality assurance and improvement program.
* Use analytics, automation and other modern audit tools to improve the timeliness, quality and value of assurance work.
* Build and lead a skilled, diverse and high\-performing team, developing the capabilities required to address current and emerging enterprise risks and drawing on specialized expertise where needed.
* Maintain constructive relationships with external auditors, regulators, specialist providers and relevant professional networks.

 **WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR**

  

* 10\+ years of progressive internal audit, risk, assurance or related experience, including significant leadership responsibility and at least five years leading people.

jobs.title: Director of Supply Chain Programs
jobs.description:
About Jetson

Jetson is on a mission to accelerate the transition of 100 million homes across North America away from fossil fuels toward sustainable energy use. We believe in a future that is 100% electric and 100% better.

Homes are one of the largest sources of carbon emissions, yet adoption of solutions like heat pumps remains slow due to cost and complexity. Jetson is solving this by building the first fully vertically integrated home electrification company — making clean energy simple, transparent, and affordable.

We rely heavily on technology, automation, and data to scale this impact. At Jetson, we value people who are excellent at their craft, curious about new tools (including AI), and motivated to continuously improve how work gets done.

The Opportunity:

We are looking for a Director of Supply Chain Programs to build and lead programs that connect Jetson's products to their full life in the field. Jetson's product portfolio is expanding fast, and every new product needs to arrive in the field supply-chain-ready and stay supported once it's installed. Reporting to the VP of Supply Chain & Warehousing, you own Supply Chain's side of the product lifecycle: from engineering handoff through sourcing, planning, stocking, and field launch, and then through service parts, warranty, and returns for the life of the installed base. Both programs are early — Supply Chain's NPI process is a lightweight framework still taking shape, and Service has little more than a list of commonly replaced parts. This is a director-level, build-it-yourself role: you'll design the processes, cadence, and metrics, rally cross-functional partners who don't report to you, and grow a team as the need is proven out.

What You Will Do:

Overall

Operate at the level this role requires: take general, intent-based guidance and turn it into comprehensive results; bring order out of chaos; be strategic in how you approach problems while staying highly effective in tactical moments; lean into areas of need as a self-starter without waiting to be directed; and bring a mature, seasoned presence to every situation ranging from a warehouse floor to an executive readout.
Lead and manage your direct reports as the team grows — setting priorities, developing their skills, and maintaining full situational awareness of every product in flight and every active service issue, so nothing is a surprise to you or to leadership.
Know the full portfolio well enough to speak to status, risk, and next steps on any NPI or Service workstream at any time — not just the ones on your desk that week.
Deliver regular formal and informal updates — from a quick heads-up as something comes up to a structured leadership brief — so progress, risk, and blockers stay visible between scheduled checkpoints, not just at them.
Facilitate updates and conversations with stakeholders across the business that are clear, concise, accurate, and customer-centric — translating product and service complexity into language that lands with the audience in front of you.
Maintain an informative, easy-to-navigate repository for programs — launch plans, readiness status, service parts data, and decisions — using dashboards, Notion, and other tools, so anyone can find current status, documentation, and history without having to ask you directly.

New Product Introduction

Own Supply Chain's side of every new product introduction, from engineering and product handoff through supply chain readiness and field launch. Work alongside Product and Engineering, who own product development, and orchestrate Procurement, Planning, Systems, Supply Chain Operations, and field teams.
Build on Supply Chain's existing NPI framework to develop its playbook and stage-gate readiness criteria: BOM release and item setup in Arena and NetSuite, supplier quality and industrialization (with Procurement), certification and compliance, first articles, packaging and labeling, stocking plans, warehouse and 3PL readiness, and field training.
Partner with Procurement on supplier quality and industrialization for new products, setting the readiness criteria and staying involved through qualification, first articles, and the move from pilot to production.
Serve as Supply Chain's primary partner to Product and Engineering — engaged early in the development process so supply chain constraints, cost, lead times, and serviceability shape decisions before they are locked.
Work with Procurement and Jetson's in-region sourcing partners to keep development milestones, certification, and supply readiness at key contract manufacturers aligned and visible to Jetson leadership.
Represent the new-product pipeline in Jetson's Integrated Business Planning (IBP) cycle — the coordinator who brings launch timing, ramp volumes, and risks into the demand and supply plan before they land in the execution horizon.
Run NPI program cadence and reporting from the supply chain perspective — timelines, readiness status, risks, and decisions — so leadership has one current view of every product in flight.

Service

Build and own Jetson's Service supply chain from the ground up — the processes, data flows, signals, and reporting that keep installed systems running and customers whole.
Define the service parts portfolio: identify and structure commonly replaced parts by product and platform, with clean part numbers, BOM linkages, and supersession rules.
Design the service parts stocking and fulfillment model — including forward-stocking critical parts at warehouse and 3PL locations so technicians can get the right part fast — partnering with Planning on stocking levels and Supply Chain Operations on execution.
Establish service consumption signals and demand history so service parts are planned by the system rather than by memory, partnering with Planning & Systems on NetSuite and field-service system integration.
Own warranty and returns processes: claims, RMAs, failure analysis, and disposition of returned or defective material. Partner with Procurement on supplier cost recovery, and feed field failure trends back to Engineering, Product, and Supplier Quality.
Build Service reporting that gives leadership visibility into claim volumes, resolution time, parts availability, cost trends, and failure rates by product and supplier.

What You Bring:

5+ years of program management or supply chain leadership experience in hardware, durable goods, HVAC, energy, or similar physical products, including ownership of NPI or product launch programs.
Experience building or running service parts, aftermarket, warranty, or reverse logistics programs — ideally including standing one up where little formal structure existed.
A proven program management track record with structured, cross-functional processes (stage-gate, launch readiness, RCCA, or similar); PMP or equivalent is a plus.
Working knowledge of ERP and PLM systems (NetSuite and Arena a plus) and how item, BOM, and service data flow through them.
Supplier- and partner-facing experience, including working with contract manufacturers and overseas suppliers on development, certification, and quality.
Cross-functional influence — you drive accountability and alignment across Product, Engineering, Procurement, Planning, Operations, and field teams without direct authority over most of them.
Strong analytical fluency and executive presence — able to turn program status and service data into a clear narrative and decisions for senior leadership.
Comfort operating in a fast-scaling, still-forming organization where scope shifts, teams are lean, and everyone pitches in.
Experience with modern tools, including AI, to automate and make your day more efficient.

Job Type:
Full-time, Permanent

Pay:
$145,000 - $175,000 per annum

Benefits:

Dental Care, Vision Care & Life Insurance premiums fully paid by Jetson
Extended Health Care
Disability Insurance
Education Support
Parental Leave Top Up
Equity

Work Location:
In person - North Vancouver, BC, with regular travel to Jetson team, warehouse, and market locations across the US and Canada, and periodic supplier travel.

Do you feel like you don't have everything that's listed above but can still do the job? If you have the core skills and experience that we're looking for and are willing to use your talent to learn the rest, we encourage you to apply!

jobs.title: Director, Insights & Measurement, Plus Company
jobs.description:
Who We Are

At Plus Company Media, we thrive at the crossroads of creativity, strategy, and innovation. As part of a global network of 26 agencies, we connect brilliant talent with iconic brands to craft media solutions that spark conversations and deliver results. Our collaborative energy fuels bold ideas, empowers growth, and ensures we stay ahead in an ever-evolving media landscape. Working with us means tapping into a vibrant ecosystem where your expertise shines brighter and your impact reaches further.

Transparency matters to us.
For this role, you can expect a salary between $105,000-$150,000 annually, depending on experience. This is for a new vacancy.

Role Description

As the Director, Insights & Measurement
, you will be the primary analytical mind and strategic architect behind our advanced media attribution, experimentation, and business science methodologies. This role is designed for a heavyweight statistician and media measurement expert who thrives on solving the "what worked and why" for major brands.

While you will collaborate closely with our dedicated internal Data Engineering and Infrastructure teams—who build and maintain our cloud pipelines—you will own the frameworks, model designs, and causal inference methodologies. You will act as a senior leader, serving as the crucial bridge who translates complex statistical outputs (like MMM, MTA, and lift studies) into high-level strategic narratives and multi-million-dollar budget optimization recommendations for modern CMOs and CFOs.

Location: Toronto
Core Focus: 70% Attribution Methodology & Experimental Design; 30% Client Consulting, Narrative Strategy & Team Mentorship.

Key Responsibilities
Advanced Attribution & Econometric Modeling

Methodology Ownership: Lead the theoretical design, validation of custom Marketing Mix Models (MMM), Multi-Touch Attribution (MTA), and customer Path-to-Conversion frameworks.
Unified Measurement Strategy: Champion a "Unified Measurement" approach, combining macro-level MMM econometric trends with micro-level digital attribution signals to give clients a singular source of truth.
Advanced Feature Engineering & Design: Determine the data requirements, adstock transformations, and saturation curve variables needed for accurate modelling, directing data engineers on how to prepare these schemas.

Experimentation & Causal Inference

Testing Frameworks: Architect randomized control trials (RCTs), matched-market tests, and geo-lift studies to establish true incrementality and validate marketing models.
Model Calibration: Use test-and-learn results and lift studies to continuously calibrate and ground MMM/MTA models, stripping out correlation and proving true causal media ROI.

Client Consulting & Strategic Storytelling

Strategic Translation: Turn highly complex mathematical outputs, coefficient shifts, and statistical variances into clear, visual, and highly compelling business recommendations.
Budget Optimization: Guide clients on optimal media mix scenarios, flighting strategies, and cross-channel budget reallocations based on model predictions.
New Business & Growth: Serve as the measurement subject matter expert during high-profile agency pitches, articulating our advanced attribution capabilities to prospective client stakeholders.
Team Mentorship: Direct and mentor a growing team of media analysts and marketing scientists, cultivating deep methodological expertise and client-ready presentation skills.

Qualifications & Requirements Experience

6+ years of professional experience in marketing science, econometrics, data science, or advanced media analytics.
3+ years of experience specifically focused on designing and running attribution models (MMM/MTA) and designing lift/incrementality experiments.
Strongly Preferred: Direct experience working within a Media Agency, AdTech firm, or marketing consultancy.

What’s in it for you:

We Value The ‘whole You’

An innovative and entrepreneurial work environment that promotes ingenuity and individuality - with the best of colleagues, and the best of clients
Hybrid work models and flexible hours, plus a work from anywhere policy for short-term stays in other regions
Generous Vacation starting at 3 weeks + 1 extra week over the holidays
Agency summer days (exact policy differs per campus and agency)
Modern, open co-working spaces with coffee & snack bars, located in great city neighborhoods, close to shops and restaurants and easy access to public transport
Dogs allowed, dedicated Play Room to support families and Private wellness room (in select offices)
Team social events - holiday parties, seasonal gatherings, weekly happy hours, inspiring speakers and more!

We are obsessed with learning and being better humans

In-house learning & development sessions and annual career and growth conversations’
Access to internal network of opportunities across all agencies
Internal EDI group(s), programs & initiatives across Plus Company and opportunities to be involved in employee resource group(s)

Check out our EDI report here to learn more about our work and commitment towards equity.

We invest in your health and wellness:

jobs.title: Director of Procurement
jobs.description:
Xplore Inc. is Canada’s fibre, 5G and satellite broadband company for rural living. Xplore is committed to the relentless pursuit of an improved broadband experience for all Canadians. Xplore is building a world-class fibre optic and 5G wireless network to enable innovative broadband services for better every day rural living, for today and future generations.

Xplore is building a procurement function fit for a national telecommunications operator: disciplined spending, strong supplier relationships, strategic partnerships with the business, and strong governance over all external spend. The Director, Procurement will lead that build.

The successful candidate will be accountable for designing, standing up and then running Xplore's procurement capability end to end including the operating model and processes, team, the framework and the systems that underpin them. You will inherit pockets of good practice and a committed set of stakeholders, and you will be expected to turn those into a cohesive, scalable function within a defined roadmap.

Reporting to the Vice President, Strategic Supplier Partnerships, you will own tactical and strategic procurement across Xplore's network, technology, operations and corporate spend, and act as the company's senior authority on sourcing, contracting and supplier management.

Key Responsibilities Include

Build the procurement capability

Operating model. Define the target operating model for procurement at Xplore — scope, structure, decision rights and interfaces with Finance, Legal, Engineering, Network Operations, IT and the business units — and lead the roadmap to get there.
Process. Design and implement the end-to-end source-to-contract and procure-to-pay processes: demand planning, sourcing, evaluation, negotiation, contracting, purchase order management, receipting and supplier performance review. Document them, embed them and measure adherence.
Team. Assess current capability, design the team structure, and recruit, develop and retain the category management, sourcing and procurement operations talent the function needs. Build the skills, career paths and performance standards that make procurement a destination role at Xplore.
Governance. Establish the procurement governance framework: delegation of authority and approval thresholds, sourcing and tendering policy, contract standards, supplier onboarding and due diligence, conflict-of-interest and ethics controls, and the reporting cadence to the executive team and Board committees.
Systems and data. Own the procurement technology roadmap. Select, implement and drive adoption of sourcing, contract lifecycle management, supplier management and procure-to-pay tooling, integrated with Xplore's ERP and finance systems, with the data model and reporting to support spend visibility and control.
Roadmap and measurement. Define the maturity model and milestones for the function, report progress transparently, and adjust the build plan as the business evolves.

Run strategic and tactical procurement

Category management. Lead category strategies across network infrastructure (fibre, fixed wireless, satellite capacity and ground equipment, towers and structures, civil works and construction), network electronics and radio access, customer premises equipment, IT hardware, software and cloud, professional and managed services, logistics, fleet and facilities, and corporate indirect spend.
Sourcing and negotiation. Run competitive sourcing events — RFI, RFP, RFQ and reverse auctions — with rigorous total-cost-of-ownership evaluation, and lead complex, high-value negotiations on commercial terms, service levels, warranties, intellectual property and liability.
Contracting. In partnership with Legal, own the commercial terms of supply, master services, construction, licensing and capacity agreements; maintain the contract repository and manage renewals, amendments and obligations.
Supplier management. Build and maintain a supplier segmentation and performance management program — scorecards, quarterly business reviews, corrective action and continuous improvement — in close alignment with the Strategic Supplier Partnerships team's management of tier-one relationships.
Supply risk and resilience. Identify, assess and mitigate supply risk across the supplier base: financial health, concentration and single-source exposure, geopolitical and trade-compliance risk, lead times, cybersecurity and data-protection posture, and business continuity.
Value delivery. Set and deliver annual savings, cost-avoidance and working-capital targets; own spend analytics and ensure procurement data is accurate, complete and actionable for Finance and operational leaders.
Compliance. Ensure procurement activity complies with Canadian procurement, competition, trade, privacy and anti-corruption law, applicable federal and provincial program requirements (including funded broadband build obligations), and Xplore's own policies.

Lead and influence

Act as a trusted commercial advisor to the executive team and functional leaders, bringing procurement into decisions early rather than at the purchase-order stage.
Champion the value of structured procurement across the organisation and lead the change management needed to shift behaviours, adopt new processes and tools, and sustain them.
Represent Xplore externally with suppliers, industry bodies and peers, and bring market intelligence and best practice back into the business.
Model Xplore's values and build an inclusive, high-performing, accountable team.

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess

10+ years of progressive procurement, strategic sourcing or supply chain experience, including 5+ years leading a procurement function or major category portfolio at the senior manager or director level.
Telecommunications, network infrastructure or a comparable capital-intensive technology industry background, with direct experience sourcing network equipment, infrastructure construction and large managed-service or capacity agreements.
Demonstrated experience building or substantially transforming a procurement function, i.e., designing operating models, processes and governance, implementing procurement systems and growing a team
Proven track record of leading complex, multi-year, high-value negotiations and delivering measurable savings and risk reduction.
Strong command of contract law fundamentals, commercial terms and risk allocation, and experience working closely with in-house and external counsel.
Hands-on experience selecting and implementing procurement technology (source-to-pay, CLM, supplier management, spend analytics) integrated with ERP platforms.
Excellent financial and analytical skills, including TCO modelling, spend analysis and business-case development.
Outstanding stakeholder management, influence and communication skills up to executive level, with the resilience to lead change in a growing organisation.
Bachelor's degree in business, supply chain management, engineering, finance or a related field.

Preferred

Supply Chain Management Professional (SCMP) designation, CIPS, CPSM or equivalent; MBA or relevant graduate degree.
Experience in a rural or regional broadband operator, or with government-funded broadband programs and their procurement and reporting obligations.
Familiarity with ESG and supplier diversity requirements, Indigenous procurement considerations and modern-slavery reporting in Canada.
Bilingual English and French is an asset.

Condition Of Employment

As a condition of employment and in order to comply with industry related data security standards, this position is subject to the successful completion of a Criminal Background Check. Details will be supplied to applicants as they move through the selection process.

Xplore is committed to creating an accessible environment and will accommodate disabilities during the selection process. Please let your recruiter know during the selection process of any accommodation needs.
