jobs.title: Director, Capital Projects
jobs.description:
Cyclic Materials is building a resilient circular supply chain for rare earth elements and other critical materials. Through our fully integrated proprietary technology platform, we recover rare earths from end-of-life products and transform them into high-purity materials used to produce new permanent magnets. These magnets are critical to the modern economy, underpinning AI, automotive, e-mobility, electronics, semiconductor, energy, defense, and other advanced manufacturing sectors.

Founded in 2021, Cyclic Materials has rapidly become a category leader in rare earth recovery, achieving commercial operations in less than five years. We currently operate facilities in Ontario and Arizona, with further expansion underway in South Carolina. Backed by investment accounts advised by T. Rowe Price Associates, Inc., alongside strategic investors including Microsoft, Amazon, Hitachi Ventures, BMW i Ventures, Jaguar Land Rover’s InMotion fund, Energy Impact Partners, ArcTern Ventures, and Fifth Wall, we are scaling quickly and building the industrial backbone required to meet growing global demand for a secure and sustainable supply of rare earths.

We have established an extensive and growing network of commercial partnerships with global industry leaders such as Solvay, Vattenfall, Lime, and VACUUMSCHMELZE, enabling the rapid deployment of recycled rare earth materials into real-world supply chains. Joining Cyclic Materials means tackling complex and exciting challenges at scale alongside a team committed to strong execution and measurable impact. If you are motivated by building critical infrastructure and advancing the circular economy, join us and help accelerate the growth of rare earth recycling.
The Director, Capital Projects leads domestic and international capital projects for rare earth element recycling and recovery, from planning and site selection through engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, start-up, and operational
handover. Reporting to the Senior Vice President, Capital Projects, Engineering & Procurement, this role ensures projects are delivered safely, on time, within scope, and on budget while meeting technical, commercial, regulatory, and strategic objectives.
The ideal candidate brings strong leadership, strategic planning, contract negotiation, engineering, and cross-functional execution experience in a global industrial environment, with the ability to navigate complex technical, commercial, regulatory, legal, and cultural challenges in a fast-paced start-up setting. The role follows a hybrid work model, with 4 days per week in the office and 1 day per week working from home. Domestic and international travel is expected to be approximately 50%, including travel to project sites, engineering offices, vendor facilities, construction locations, partner facilities, commissioning sites, and potential new facility locations.
Key Responsibilities
Global Capital Project Execution
Lead global capital projects from initiation through completion, ensuring alignment with company strategy, growth objectives, technical requirements, and commercial priorities.
Oversee complex plant development initiatives, including planning, site selection, engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, start-up, and operational handover.
Define scope, deliverables, timelines, budgets, resources, execution plans, governance, risks, and performance metrics with internal and external stakeholders.
Deliver multiple capital initiatives safely, on time, within scope, and within budget in a matrixed global organization.

Plant Development, Engineering, and Technology
Support scopes of work for new plant builds, expansions, upgrades, and technology deployments.
Oversee bespoke physical and chemical processing plants for rare earth element recycling and recovery.
Coordinate with engineering, operations, environmental, procurement, legal, finance, strategic partnerships, corporate development, and commercial teams to ensure safe, scalable, and commercially viable plant designs.
Assess technologies that improve efficiency, recovery, throughput, safety, reliability, environmental performance, and operating costs while ensuring constructability, operability, maintainability, process safety, and commissioning readiness.

Site Selection and Due Diligence
 Lead land and site selection for new facilities, including technical, commercial, logistical, environmental, utility, infrastructure, permitting, and regulatory assessments.
Develop and apply site assessment criteria for greenfield and brownfield opportunities.
Coordinate with legal, finance, engineering, environmental, and local advisors to support due diligence, acquisition, leasing, and development decisions.

Contracts, Procurement, and Partner Oversight
Lead contract negotiation for engineering, procurement, construction, equipment supply, installation, commissioning, consulting, service, and vendor agreements.
Partner with legal, procurement, finance, and executive leadership to structure agreements that protect company interests and support successful delivery.
Evaluate and oversee contractors, suppliers, technology partners, trades, and subcontractors for capability, terms, schedules, risks, and performance.
Oversee procurement strategies for major equipment, long-lead items, specialized processing systems, materials, construction services, and commissioning support.

Governance, Risk, and Performance Control
Establish project governance, including stage-gate reviews, executive reporting, decision logs, change control, budget tracking, schedule monitoring, and performance dashboards.
Identify and mitigate risks related to technology readiness, engineering, permitting, contractors, supply chain, cost, schedule, site conditions, logistics, and regulatory requirements.
Develop contingency plans and corrective actions for emerging project risks.
Apply appropriate project delivery methods and tools, including Agile, Scrum, Waterfall, stage-gate, Monte Carlo analysis, schedule compression, and hybrid approaches where relevant.
Capture lessons learned, standardize execution practices, and document handover and operational readiness processes

Stakeholder, Team, and Communication Leadership
Coordinate effectively with internal teams, external partners, engineering firms, contractors, suppliers, regulators, authorities, and key stakeholders.
Lead cross-functional collaboration across time zones, cultures, disciplines, and geographies.
Foster a high-performance, accountable, safety-focused, and results-oriented project environment.
Communicate project status, risks, budget, schedule, required decisions, and strategic implications to executive leadership.
Ensure alignment between project execution, operational readiness, commercial priorities, and long-term growth.

Health, Safety, Environment, and Compliance
Champion a safety-first culture across site selection, engineering, construction, installation, commissioning, and start-up.
Ensure compliance with company policies, laws, regulations, permitting requirements, environmental standards, occupational health and safety requirements, and best practices.
Integrate sustainability, circular economy principles, emissions reduction, energy efficiency, water stewardship, waste minimization, and responsible materials recovery into project planning and execution.
Maintain appropriate controls for chemical handling, hazardous materials, waste treatment, process safety, and environmental protection.

Required Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline; Chemical, Mechanical, Metallurgical, Materials, Process, Industrial, or Environmental Engineering preferred.
Related business, project delivery, or technical degrees may be considered with substantial industrial capital project experience.
International MBA or globally focused MBA preferred.
PMP or Six Sigma Black Belt certification expected; PRINCE2 or equivalent international project delivery certification an asset.
Professional engineering designation such as P.Eng., PE, Chartered Engineer, or equivalent strongly preferred.
12–15+ years leading global or large-scale industrial capital projects, preferably in chemical processing, metals, recycling, mining, critical minerals, rare earths, battery materials, specialty chemicals, or advanced manufacturing.
Experience managing multiple projects across regions, time zones, regulatory environments, stakeholder groups, and matrixed global organizations.
Demonstrated expertise in budgeting, scheduling, contract negotiation, stakeholder coordination, risk mitigation, and project governance.
Experience with rare earths, critical minerals, hydrometallurgy, pyrometallurgy, solvent extraction, precipitation, chemical refining, metal recovery, e-waste recycling, battery recycling, or industrial waste valorization.
Experience developing first-of-kind, next-of-kind, modular, or repeatable plant designs and supporting pilot-to-commercial scale-up.
Experience with EPC, EPCM, design-build, owner-led delivery, equipment vendor-led delivery, and partner-led construction models.
Experience with facility due diligence, site acquisition or leasing, international teams, cultural differences, local business practices, and remote collaboration.

Skills and Competencies
Strong leadership, strategic planning, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
Excellent communication, stakeholder engagement, commercial judgment, and contract negotiation ability.
Ability to translate business strategy into practical execution plans and adapt to changing priorities under tight deadlines.
Strong understanding of industrial construction, installation, commissioning, process plant operations, and operational readiness.
Proficiency with project planning, scheduling, collaboration, and reporting tools such as MS Project, Jira, Trello, Asana, Microsoft Office, Teams, SharePoint, or similar platforms.
Familiarity with Agile, Scrum, Waterfall, stage-gate, and hybrid execution methodologies.
Fluency in English required; additional languages are an asset.

Why You Will Love Cyclic Materials

At Cyclic Materials, we're dedicated to supporting our workforce on their unique career journey
We offer a competitive compensation package including Health and Dental coverage, RRSP (Canada)/ 401K (USA) contributions and a generous paid time off program that lets you recharge
We value diversity and are committed to maintaining a workplace where everyone is respected and recognized for their contributions

The base compensation offered is determined based on the successful candidate’s relevant experience, skills, and competencies and considers internal equity.
As an Equal Opportunity employer, Cyclic Materials is committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where all individuals have an opportunity to succeed. If you require accommodation at any stage of the interview process, please email HumanResources@cyclicmaterials.earth. Applicants for roles in Canada or the United States must be authorized to work in the applicable country without current or future sponsorship from Cyclic Materials, including for an H1-B visa, F-1 visa (OPT), TN, L1-A visa, or any other non-immigrant status.

Director, Network & Security AI and Automation

We are seeking a Director, Network & Security AI and Automation to establish and lead an engineering function within Network & Security Services with two complementary mandates: applying automation and AI to improve the engineering, delivery, and operations of network and security products; and building the security tooling, controls, and operational capabilities needed to protect AI platforms, applications, and agents. Our ideal candidate combines strong network and security engineering experience with expertise in automation, AI-enabled operations, AI security, and technical leadership. You will establish reusable engineering patterns and use AIOps to strengthen operational visibility, proactive issue detection and response, and service resilience. Equally, you will lead the engineering and integration of capabilities that secure AI itself, protecting its supporting infrastructure, data access, integrations, and agent actions. Working with technology, security, and governance partners, you will translate AI security requirements into practical controls and sustainable services, with clear ownership and support models aligned to enterprise standards.

Establish and lead the Network & Security AI and Automation function, including its roadmap, delivery priorities, engineering standards, and long-term capability development across automation, AIOps, and security for AI.

What will your typical day look like?

As a Director within Deloitte’s Deal Transformation & Post Merger Integration (DT&PMI) Human Resources Due Diligence (HRDD) practice, you will play a leadership role in advising private equity investors and corporate clients on the financial, operational and strategic implications of human capital matters across complex M&A transactions.

Combining strong commercial judgment, quantitative analytical capabilities and human capital expertise, you will lead financially focused due diligence engagements to identify and quantify material transaction risks, assess historical and prospective workforce costs, and uncover opportunities for EBITDA improvement and enterprise value creation.

Your work will span complex compensation and benefits arrangements, pensions and other employee liabilities, workforce cost structures, organizational effectiveness and carve-out considerations. You will translate these findings into actionable insights that inform transaction economics, deal structuring, negotiations and post-acquisition priorities.

Beyond leading engagements, you will serve as a trusted advisor to senior client stakeholders, collaborate with multidisciplinary deal teams, mentor and develop high-performing professionals, and contribute to the continued growth of the practice.

Responsibilities

Lead Transaction Due Diligence: Direct financially focused human capital due diligence engagements, identifying and quantifying material risks, liabilities, cost exposures and opportunities that could influence transaction value, deal terms and post-closing priorities.
Assess Financial and Commercial Deal Implications: Analyze historical and projected workforce costs, including compensation, benefits, pensions, executive arrangements and transaction-related obligations, to evaluate implications for normalized EBITDA, net debt, cash flow and transaction economics.
Drive Value Creation: Identify and assess opportunities for labor cost optimization, workforce productivity, organizational effectiveness, spans and layers improvements, and sustainable EBITDA enhancement.
Lead Workforce Analytics and Financial Modeling: Direct complex quantitative analyses using workforce, payroll and financial datasets, developing robust models and defensible financial estimates despite incomplete or imperfect information.
Advise on Carve-outs and Standalone Requirements: Assess standalone operating models, workforce structures, stranded costs, incremental costs, employee transition requirements and Transition Service Agreements (TSAs).
Deliver Executive-Level Insights: Synthesize complex technical findings into clear, commercially relevant recommendations for private equity investors, corporate executives, investment teams and other transaction stakeholders.
Collaborate Across Deal Disciplines: Work closely with Financial Due Diligence, M&A, tax, legal, operational and technology advisory teams to connect human capital findings to the broader transaction thesis and diligence conclusions.
Lead Client Engagements and Develop Talent: Independently manage complex engagements, facilitate discussions with senior management, oversee delivery quality, and mentor, coach and develop high-performing teams.
Contribute to Practice Growth: Develop trusted client relationships, support business development, identify cross-functional opportunities and help expand Deloitte’s human capital transaction advisory capabilities.

About The Team

Our Human Resources Due Diligence practice is part of Deloitte’s Strategy, Risk & Transactions (SR&T) business, within the Deal Transformation & Post Merger Integration (DT&PMI) team.

We operate at the intersection of M&A, finance and human capital, helping private equity investors and corporate clients understand how workforce-related risks, liabilities, costs and opportunities influence deal value.

Our engagements combine transaction advisory, quantitative analysis and specialized human capital expertise, often in close collaboration with Financial Due Diligence and other M&A advisory teams.

Joining our growing practice offers the opportunity to advise on complex, high-profile transactions, work across diverse industries and jurisdictions, mentor and develop talented professionals, and contribute to building a differentiated advisory offering within Deloitte’s M&A business.

Enough About Us, Let’s Talk About You

Transaction Advisory and Commercial Acumen: Strong understanding of M&A transactions, investment considerations and financial drivers of deal value, with the ability to connect human capital findings to transaction economics and business decisions.
Quantitative and Financial Analytical Capabilities: Ability to interpret complex financial and workforce information, assess cost structures, build or review financial models, and evaluate implications for EBITDA, net debt, cash flow and enterprise value.
Human Capital Expertise: Strong knowledge of workforce costs, compensation, employee benefits, pensions, executive arrangements, organizational structures or other material human capital considerations. Depth in one or more specialized areas and an ability to evaluate broader implications are valued.
Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: Exceptional analytical judgment, intellectual curiosity and ability to structure ambiguous problems, challenge assumptions, and derive evidence-based conclusions from incomplete information.
Strategic and Value Creation Orientation: Ability to identify opportunities for organizational effectiveness, operating cost improvement and sustainable value creation, translating findings into actionable recommendations.
Executive Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to distill complex financial and technical matters into concise, persuasive insights for senior executives, private equity investors and deal stakeholders.
Technical Proficiency: Advanced Excel modeling and PowerPoint skills. Experience with large datasets, payroll or workforce information, or tools such as Power BI, Tableau or SQL is an asset.
Leadership and Talent Development: Ability to lead complex engagements and multidisciplinary teams, mentor professionals, provide constructive feedback, and foster a high-performing team environment.
Client Management: Ability to build trusted relationships with senior clients, manage multiple priorities and deliver high-quality work under demanding transaction timelines.
Commercial and Growth Mindset: Ability to identify client needs, contribute to business development and help grow a specialized advisory practice.

Minimum Experience

jobs.description:
Artificial Intelligence. Actual Impact. 
 At Docebo, we’re using AI to change how people learn at work—and we mean actually change it. We’re an AI-powered learning platform that helps organizations create, deliver, and manage training all in one place. But our real mission goes deeper: we help teams move faster, work smarter, and focus on the work that truly matters. Our platform is built with intelligent, time-saving tools that personalize learning, eliminate busywork, and turn training from a checkbox into a superpower. The result? Better experiences for learners and real results for businesses.

 We’re shaping the future of learning with a team that isn’t afraid to challenge the status quo. If you're excited by the idea of using AI to make work-life better for real people–you’ll feel right at home here. And it’s not just what we build, it’s how we show up. At Docebo, our values aren’t just posters on the wall—they guide how we work every day. We call it the Docebo Heart: trust by default, assume positive intent, and create space for different perspectives to thrive.

 So… what are you waiting for? Join 900+ Docebians around the world and help us reinvent the way people learn, because learning never stops.

 🚀 The Adventure Ahead
 Docebo is scaling fast, and this isn’t a "keep the lights on" role—it’s a ground-up opportunity to reimagine and build a global People Operations engine that actually works for humans. As the architect behind our operational infrastructure, you’ll operate at the intersection of high-level strategy and hands-on execution to empower 900+ Docebians across the globe, with a special focus on EMEA. You’ll partner directly with senior leaders to turn organizational complexity into clarity, designing the scalable systems, global standards, and seamless employee experiences that will fuel our next chapter of hyper-growth.

 🛠️ The Day-to-Day
 Architect & Scale People Ops: Rebuild and lead a high-performing global People Operations team, clarifying roles and workflows while designing scalable frameworks for a 900+ multi-country organization.

 Drive Strategic Partnerships: Set a multi-year People Ops vision and act as a trusted advisor to the People Leadership Team and senior executives, using data and insights to shape company-wide priorities and decisions.

 Champion Global & EMEA Compliance: Serve as our go-to expert for EMEA employment practices—navigating works councils, local labor laws, and contracts—while partnering with regional leaders to support seamless expansion into new countries.

 Optimize HR Tech & Data: Own our HR systems ecosystem (HRIS, payroll, benefits) to drive process automation, reporting accuracy, and strict GDPR and global data privacy controls.

 Lead End-to-End Delivery: Own the People Ops project portfolio from intake to adoption, applying strong project management discipline to land cross-functional system implementations and global rollouts on time.

 Elevate the Employee Lifecycle: Oversee operational excellence across every touchpoint—from hiring, onboarding, and job architecture to compensation, performance cycles, employee relations, and offboarding.

 Navigate Growth & Change: Lead with calm and clarity through rapid scaling, balancing immediate operational needs with long-term organizational design across every region and function.

 ⚡ Your Superpowers
 Bring Proven Global Scale: You have 10+ years of progressive People Operations/HR leadership in high-growth SaaS or tech, with a track record of scaling operations and restructuring teams for 1,000+ global employees.

 Think Enterprise-Wide: You possess the strategic mindset to zoom out, influence senior leaders, and set multi-year operational direction beyond your own function.

 Master EMEA Complexity: You bring deep, hands-on expertise in EMEA employment law, works councils, and navigating the nuances of cross-country HR operations.

 Execute with Discipline: You’re a project management powerhouse who thrives on delivering complex, multi-region initiatives and driving genuine stakeholder adoption.

 Optimize Systems & Data: You’ve successfully implemented and optimized HR systems at scale, pairing a detail-oriented, data-driven approach with a deep care for the human employee experience.

 Roll Up Your Sleeves: You balance long-term vision with a willingness to dive into the weeds—untangling messy processes or pressure-testing systems whenever the team needs a boost.

 Thrive in Ambiguity: You’re energized by fast-paced, evolving environments, bringing structure, momentum, and calm to complex challenges without sacrificing quality.

 Our Hybrid Work Philosophy 🤝 
 Great work can happen anywhere but coming together helps us go further. Our team spends three days a week in the office (Tuesday-Thursday) to collaborate, solve problems, and learn from each other. With flexibility the rest of the week, it’s a balance designed to help everyone do their best work and keep growing.

 Our Total Rewards Philosophy 🎉
 Our Total Rewards Philosophy centers around three core areas to reward and care for our People:
 Rewarding Impact: We lead with competitive pay to reward the impact, skills and traits that fuel our success.

 Fostering Holistic Wellbeing: We care deeply about and invest in the whole person with programs that support our people’s physical, mental, and financial well-being.

 Empowering Our Talent Culture: We build a culture of trust and empowerment by designing our rewards and benefits with transparency, equity, and flexibility, enabling our people to do their best work and stay for the long haul.

 Our Promise to You 😍
 Financial Wellness: Own a piece of Docebo through our Employee Share Purchase Plan (ESPP) at a 15% discount, plus a competitive compensation package.

 Your Well-Being, Covered: You’ll get access to health benefits, so you can get the care you need when you need it.

 Rest, Relax, Repeat: Rest and recharge with paid vacation days, two company-wide Docebo Days, floating holidays for cultural celebrations, and your birthday off!

 Family First: We provide coverage offering you time with your little one(s) so you can soak up all those precious moments. Fun fact: we had 30 Docebian babies join the family in 2025!

 Connections That Count: Connect with global communities through our Employee Resource Groups (including PRIDE, DWA, BIDOC, and Green Ambassadors) and company-wide events that keep the fun rolling all year long.

 About Docebo 💙
 At Docebo, we create seamless, AI-powered learning experiences for over 3,000 customers worldwide. We have successfully achieved two IPOs ( TSX: DCBO & NASDAQ: DCBO ), been recognized as a top SaaS e-learning solution, and are growing exponentially in the process. We're a global company, with office across North America, EMEA, APAC, and beyond. Our team is guided by five core values— Grow Together Win Together, Build with Our Customer, Clear is Kind, Own Outcomes, Progress Over Perfection —that shape everything we do. If this resonates with you, now is the perfect time to join one of the fastest-growing learning technology companies in the world.

jobs.title: Director, Product Management, Sandboxes
jobs.description:
About Docker 
 Docker has been one of the most loved brands in developer tooling, trusted by more than 20 million monthly users and over 20 billion container image pulls. From solo founders to the world's largest companies, developers rely on Docker to build, share, and run their applications across our suite of products including Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, and Docker Scout.

We are a globally distributed, remote-first team building the tools that define how software gets built and delivered. As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the sandboxed environments, verified images, and secure infrastructure that make autonomous workflows trustworthy by default.
 _______________________________________________________________________

 The Role 
 The Products Team at Docker is looking for a Director of Product Management to lead our core Sandboxes platform. You will own the vision, strategy, roadmap and execution for Docker’s sandboxes, taking this area from high-level concept design to delivery and adoption. You will manage a team of 2-3 product managers, coaching them and setting the bar for how we build. You will help shape the future of a key area of Docker, partnering with Engineering, Design, Security, and Go-to-Market leaders, and working closely with developers inside and outside of Docker, our customers, and our partners to expand our open ecosystem offering and provide value. As the company and ecosystem grow, you will build a team and a culture eager to continuously build, measure, and learn.

 To thrive in this role, you’ll need a track record of leading product teams, along with deep experience working with developers and technical knowledge of developer tools. You’ll need to know how to work with the developer community and understand the lifecycle of software development, the software supply chain, and how AI agents are safely orchestrated and deployed with sandboxes. You’ll need a relentless drive to try new things, and an eye for detail. Your long-term success will depend on your ability to set and own the product strategy and roadmap, develop great product managers, collaborate with the developer community, and scale our services. Most importantly, you’ll need to be okay with taking ownership of big objectives with big goals, leading through cross-functional teams, and maintaining a bias for action.
 _______________________________________________________________________

 Responsibilities 
 You own the product line for Docker’s sandboxes: the long-term vision, the strategy, the roadmap, the revenue, and the results.

 You lead and manage a team of 2-3 product managers. You coach them, set clear expectations and a high bar for product quality, and create the conditions for them to do the best work of their careers.

 You believe in and can articulate succinctly our customers and their pain points. You empathize with and understand the world they live in and the constraints they work through, and you make sure your team does too.

 You will engage deeply with developers and find amazing solutions that solve today’s problems while optimizing for tomorrow’s vision, including how AI agents are safely run and orchestrated.

 You enjoy building products that are easy to adopt and use. You have a keen design sensibility, and you hold your team to a standard of always looking for ways to improve usability.

 You are comfortable with ambiguity and will guide product definition, prioritization, and scope across your team, in concert with Engineering, Design, Security, and Go-to-Market leaders.

 You translate company strategy into a clear product direction and communicate it with clarity and conviction to partners and your own team.

 You present your thinking, plans, and progress to Docker’s executive leadership team, making a clear case for where to invest and why, and you incorporate their feedback into the strategy.

 _______________________________________________________________________

 Qualifications 
 You have 10+ years of product management experience, including at least 3 years managing and developing product managers.

 You have deep empathy for the needs of developers and are obsessed with talking to your users.

 You have created and deployed AI agents at scale and dealt with all the challenges and pain points of such tasks.

 You have experience building B2B, SaaS, or have a background in Public Cloud.

 You have experience working with tools in the software supply chain and/or software security.

 You can set a multi-year product vision and strategy, then break it down into small, release-able, user-valuable features that your team can deliver.

 You can explain complex ideas simply and communicate across diverse stakeholders, including presenting to executive leadership.

 You have effective written, verbal, and visual communication skills.

 You can analyze data, both qualitative and quantitative, to inform decision making, and you coach your team to do the same.

 You have a collaborative approach and the ability to lead through influence with fast-moving, distributed, cross-functional teams.

 You have experience running products at various stages of maturity, from legacy to greenfield.

 You are a coach/player. We are small and need all hands on deck. Everyone gets their hands dirty

 Visa sponsorship: Not available for this role.
 _______________________________________________________________________

 Compensation & Equity 
 All full-time roles include equity. Final compensation is determined on factors including but not limited to experience, skills, qualifications, and location.

 Canada: CA$381,472 - CA$429,156 base
 United States: $280,000 - $315,000 base

 ______________________________________________________________________

 Posting Information 
 Open vacancy: This posting is for an existing open role.

 AI in hiring: Docker may use AI-assisted tools during our recruiting process.

 Interview recordings: Candidates will be invited to opt in to interview recordings to support interviewer calibration and consistent evaluations. Recordings are optional and require explicit consent.

 ______________________________________________________________________

 Perks & Benefits 
 Remote-first by design – Work from your home, with offices in Seattle and Paris for connection and collaboration.

 Flexibility that fits your life – We trust you to manage your schedule while delivering great work.

 Time to recharge – Generous PTO, designated quarterly Whaleness Days, and a designated end-of-year Whaleness break.

 Home office support – Set up your workspace for comfort and success.

 Technology stipend – Equivalent to US$100 net per month to help support your work.

 Learning & development – Annual stipend for conferences, courses, certifications, and continued learning.

 Parental leave – 16 weeks of paid parental leave after six months of employment.

 Equity for all full-time employees – Share in Docker's long-term success as we continue to grow.

 Comprehensive benefits – Medical, retirement, and paid holidays vary by country.

 Docker swag – Because representing the whale never gets old.

 Docker is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a team that reflects a broad range of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe diverse teams build better products, make better decisions, and better serve our global community. 

 #LI-REMOTE

 Location
 Americas-based. The role must be positioned to provide effective leadership and senior stakeholder coverage across Americas working hours, while operating globally across time zones.

 Americas leadership

 A strong interest in emerging technology markets, particularly data centre, AI, Neocloud infrastructure, SaaS, or related technology sectors

jobs.description:
Who are we? 
 Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.   

A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future. 

A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work. 

 Job Summary 
 A lot of companies are still working out what AI means for how work gets done. At Equinix, this role sits at the center of that question. In this role, you’ll help decide how the company reimagines its most critical value streams leveraging AI, and how its leaders build the management habits that make the changes stick.

 The Senior Director, Process Excellence guides how Equinix reimagines some of its most critical value streams for AI transformation. Forward-deployed engineers build and deploy the solutions. This leader facilitates the work that comes before and alongside them: bringing business leaders and engineers into the same room to examine how work flows today, decide what the future flow should look like, and place AI and human judgment where each adds the most value, so the redesign starts from outcomes and decisions rather than from tools.

 The role also develops the management practices / operating system that put continuous improvement principles to work, drawing on lean principles, along with the toolset that supports them, in partnership with HR. In selected areas of focus, this leader coaches parts of the organization directly on building the operating system that sustains a culture of continuous improvement. You’ll work with business leaders, people team, and our Digital and Innovation Organization, with visibility to senior leadership.

 Responsibilities 
 Reimagining Critical Value Streams for AI Transformation
 Facilitate working sessions with business leaders and forward-deployed engineers to examine how work actually flows, find the structural bottlenecks, handoffs, and rework, and define the future flow before solutions are built
 Bring Lean, Six Sigma, BPM, and value stream thinking together with process and process mining, so the redesign is grounded in how work runs today and aimed at measurable gains in speed, quality, cost, and decision-making
 Help business leaders design for decisions and outcomes rather than tasks, build intelligence into core workflows, and place AI, automation, and human judgment where each adds the most value
 Advise senior leaders on where AI applies and where it does not, and challenge designs that only speed up an existing process
 Connect business leaders, the Digital and AI organization, and change efforts so that opportunities move from identification to deployment and adoption
 Promote always-on visibility into how redesigned processes perform, so gains are sustained and drift is caught early
 Establish a consistent approach across the enterprise to prioritizing, framing, and launching value stream redesigns

 Management Practices / Operating System
 Develop the Equinix management practices / operating system that builds from some of the best and enforces continuous improvement principles into daily use, including visual management, structured problem solving, performance management, and standard work
 Build, with partners, the toolset that supports those practices, including standards, templates, and routines that teams can adopt and adapt
 Work with HR so the practices reinforce the leadership expectations set for the company, and so the language, learning experiences, and capability pathways are consistent
 Help create the shared language and mindset that make continuous improvement part of how the company operates
 Coach selected parts of the organization on best practices for building the operating system that drives continuous improvement, with hands-on enablement in priority areas so teams and leaders can apply the practices and the redesign approach themselves
 Decide what is standard across the enterprise and what can flex by region or function, and set a deliberate path for starting the practices where they will take hold
 Embed process excellence disciplines at scale, and build communities of practice in process redesign and AI-enabled improvement so the capability spreads beyond this team
 Assess how mature the practices are across the organization, establish feedback loops on adoption and effectiveness, and refine the system based on what is learned

 Qualifications 
 Required
 12–15+ years leading enterprise-level operational excellence, process excellence, or large-scale change in complex, global organizations
 Fluency in Lean, Six Sigma, BPM, and value stream methods, and the ability to apply them to redesign how end-to-end work flows
 Working knowledge of AI, analytics, automation, and digital platforms, with the ability to translate capability into business outcomes
 Strong facilitation and coaching skills, with credibility working with senior leaders and executives
 Experience developing management practices and tools built on lean principles, and helping an organization adopt them at scale
 Deep understanding of organizational behavior and what it takes to change habits and shared language
 Comfort building something without an established playbook, balancing structure with pragmatism
 Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, or equivalent experience

 Preferred
 Hands-on experience with process or task mining
 Experience partnering with HR on capability programs
 Experience in technology, services, or infrastructure environments
 Lean Six Sigma, change management, or comparable certification

 Job Summary 
 Equinix | Build Bolder
 Build the platform that makes every Equinix engineer faster and turn that velocity into enterprise value.

 Why this role, right now
 Equinix is scaling under Build Bolder, with a stated ambition to add $100M in enterprise value by 2030. That growth runs on software, and software runs at the speed of its developers.

 This is a replacement role charter: own the developer platform, the IDE, the copilots, and the developer's voice. 

 Responsibilities 
 What you'll own
 Developer Platform — the paved road: scalable, secure, performant foundations every engineering team builds on
 IDE & AI Copilots — modern IDE integrations and AI-assisted coding that change what a day of engineering feels like
 Dev Environments — instant, reproducible environments that erase setup friction and shorten every loop
 Voice of the Developer — the listening system: gather, analyze, and act on what engineers actually need
 Quality Engineering CoE - the standards, tooling, and culture that make quality a first-class citizen across engineering. This includes: canonical test automation frameworks teams can adopt without reinventing; stable, on-demand test environments that don't become the bottleneck before every release; test data management practices that make realistic, safe data accessible at every layer; end-to-end and integration test coverage standards with visibility into gaps across the portfolio; shiftleft practices that move quality decisions earlier in the SDLC -- into design and PR, not just pre-prod; and AI-assisted testing capabilities that reduce the human cost of coverage. This is a CoE model: you set the bar, build the tooling, and raise the floor -- delivery teams own their own quality outcomes

 Your first 18 months
 0–90 days — Meet the engineers. Identify the highest-friction points in developer onboarding, environments, and tooling. Ship visible improvements. Shape platform strategy from what you learn in motion, not from a standing start
 6 months — Developers are actively using our platform, with adoption you can point to. Listening mechanisms are live and informing the backlog. The Quality Engineering team has a founding framework: one canonical test automation stack, environments that don't block releases, and a shift-left standard teams are adopting
 12–18 months — The paved road is real and most teams are on it by choice: standardized environments, test frameworks, and copilot integrations that feel like the obvious default, not a mandate. Developer velocity and satisfaction are measurable and moving. Quality gaps across the portfolio are visible, tracked, and shrinking. The platform is a competitive advantage you can tell a story about

 What's in it for you
 Scale that's rare — global, matrixed, mission-critical infrastructure; your tools touch every engineer, every day
 A start-up charter — an intrapreneurial mandate inside a company with the balance sheet to back bold bets
 AI at the center — copilots and AI-assisted development are core to the role, not a side experiment
 Measurable legacy — velocity and satisfaction gains that ladder straight into the Build Bolder value story

 Qualifications 
 What you bring
 15+ years in software engineering, including 5+ leading engineering teams
 Proven track record building developer platforms, tools, or frameworks at scale
 Deep fluency in modern IDEs, cloud dev environments, and AI-assisted development
 Strong systems thinking across backend and infrastructure layers of tooling
 A transformational leader who drives change through influence, across cultures
 Genuine empathy for the daily friction engineers face — and the drive to remove it

 If you want your work measured in how fast a whole company can build — let's talk.
 Typically requires a minimum of 15 years of related experience with a Bachelor’s degree; or 12 years and a Master’s degree; or a PhD with 8 years experience; or equivalent experience

You are as unique as your background, experience and point of view. Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered and challenged to be your best self. You'll work with dynamic colleagues - experts in their fields - who are eager to share their knowledge with you. Your leaders will inspire and help you reach your potential and soar to new heights. Every day, you'll have new and exciting opportunities to make life brighter for our Clients - who are at the heart of everything we do. 

 At Sun Life, we're driven by our Purpose: helping our Clients achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. Our values shape how we work: caring, authentic, bold, inspiring, and impactful.

 When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.

 Discover how you can make a difference in the lives of individuals, families and communities around the world.

 Job Description: 
 The Director, IT Application Audit is responsible for the oversight and delivery of risk-based internal audits across the Business Group Chief Information Officer (CIO) application portfolio and technology in Canada and the United States, and when needed in Asia. The role provides independent assurance and advisory support over business applications, data, digital delivery, enabling platforms and associated technology and cyber risk management practices. The scope includes First and Second Line activities and support for integrated business audits with significant technology components.

 Reporting to the Assistant Vice President, IT Audit, the Director leads assigned members of a geographically dispersed audit team and is accountable for high-quality audit delivery, stakeholder relationships, people development and continuous improvement of audit practices.

 What You Will Be Doing

 The scope of responsibilities includes for assigned areas the operational delivery of all IT audit work, audit plan development and coverage, IT audit universe risk assessments to ensure the adequacy of audit coverage of key risks, as well as relationship management with clients and management of the audit team.
 Identify emerging and heightened risk related to technology and cyber security in applications and technology processes, digital transformation and modernization, AI and data.
 Contribute to the development of Audit strategy and direction, and talent initiatives.
 Continuously improve audit delivery and quality through increased use of AI, data analytics and innovation.
 Plan and direct audits and special engagements following Sun Life’s Audit methodology; deliver audit reports and findings that clearly articulate the position of risks and issues.
 Provide subject matter expertise as it relates to technology, cyber and information risk management processes to other audit teams.
 Provide leadership in discussions of risk assessment, internal control and audit findings with clients.
 Actively stay engaged in the latest technologies, regulations and cyber trends.
 Manage multiple engagements and priorities concurrently, including scope, resourcing, milestones, quality review, stakeholder communication and issue escalation.
 Influence management to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of operations, risk management practices and the control environment with respect to technology, cyber and information risk management.
 Lead an audit team with a focus on building and maintaining a high-performing team of auditors, including the recruitment, administration, development and retention of staff through strong leadership and coaching.

 What You Need to Succeed

 ·    6-8+ years of leadership experience in IT, IT Audit, or related risk management or governance/control functions.
 ·    University degree or equivalent experience, plus recognized auditing (e.g., CISA, CPA, CIA), or security (e.g., CISSP) designations/certifications.
 ·    Previous people management experience, with demonstrated employee engagement results.
 ·    This role is based in Toronto and the individual is expected to work in a hybrid environment (virtual and in the office). Occasional travel to the US and rarely to Asia may be required.
 ·    In-depth knowledge of audit methodologies, system development methodologies, control frameworks, risk practices and regulatory requirements.
 ·    Exceptional understanding of application development & maintenance, technology and cyber processes, risks and controls.
 ·    In-depth knowledge of the latest application technology and security trends, best practices and industry standards.
 ·    Proficiency in cyber security risk and control frameworks and information risk management frameworks.
 ·    Strong working knowledge of risks affecting the insurance industry and financial institutions.
 ·    Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and succinctly and effectively deliver key messages verbally and in writing.
 ·    Effective listener who remains open and receptive to various viewpoints.
 ·    Confident presenter and facilitator with strong interpersonal and leadership skills to work with senior management at all levels.
 ·    Effective influencer and negotiator with the ability to effectively manage and resolve conflicts across all levels of management.
 ·    Professional presence and the ability to navigate through a matrix organization.

Communication & Stakeholder Management: Report quarterly to the Pension Committee regarding investment strategy, performance, and risk management

You are the missing piece of the puzzle

CFA charterholder and/or a graduate degree (Master's) in Economics, Finance, or Business Administration

jobs.title: Head of Marketing
jobs.description:
**About Innerlogic**

Most organizations survey their people, then wait months for the analysis. By the time the report lands, the moment to act has often passed. Innerlogic closes that gap.

We’re an employee listening platform with an agentic twist. Teams run engagement, pulse and 360 surveys on Innerlogic, and Nora, our AI analyst, turns the results into reports, insights and action plans in minutes. Enterprises use us to listen across their whole workforce. HR consultancies use us to run research for many clients at once.

Qualtrics and Culture Amp were built for a world where analysis took a team and a quarter. We’re building for one where it takes an afternoon.

We’ve just closed a funding round, moved into a new Bedford office, and are putting our full weight behind go\-to\-market. We’re a team of 8, and you’ll be our first marketing leader: the person who decides how the world hears about us.

**The role**

You’ll own the top of our funnel: who knows about us, why they care, and how many qualified conversations reach sales each month.

This is a hands\-on builder’s role. You’ll set the strategy and do much of the work yourself, from writing the positioning to launching the campaigns. You’ll have a budget for contractors and tools from day one, and you’ll decide when and where to grow a team.

We build our product with AI agents, and we expect marketing to run the same way. You’ll use tools like Claude to research markets, draft and test messaging, build campaigns and analyze results, so a small team ships like a much bigger one.

**Location:** This is a hybrid role based in our Bedford office. The team works together in person 2 days a week, so you’ll need to live within commuting distance of Halifax. We can’t consider fully remote candidates for this role.

**What you’ll do**

* **Build pipeline.** Design and run the programs that create qualified pipeline: paid, email nurture, webinars, events, partner campaigns and support for outbound. Own the numbers from first visit to marketing\-sourced pipeline.
* **Sharpen our positioning.** Define how we talk about Innerlogic against Qualtrics, Culture Amp and the rest. Own launches, messaging, sales collateral, competitive battlecards and pricing pages.
* **Market to two audiences.** Build distinct plays for HR and People leaders who buy directly, and for HR consultancies who run research on our platform.
* **Run a content engine.** Publish work that earns attention: research reports from our own data, blog, SEO and AI\-search visibility, LinkedIn and customer stories.
* **Own the brand and website.** Steward the brand and run the website as a conversion engine, working with product on design.
* **Run marketing operations.** Own the CRM and marketing automation setup, lead scoring, attribution and reporting, so we always know what’s working.

**Your first 90 days**

* Learn the product, our customers, and the deals we’ve won and lost. Talk to customers and consultancy partners.
* Deliver a positioning refresh and a 12\-month marketing plan with targets and budget.
* Launch the first repeatable pipeline program, and the reporting to measure it.

**What you bring**

* 7\+ years in B2B marketing, ideally SaaS, including at least 2 years owning demand generation or the whole marketing function at an early\-stage company.
* A track record of building pipeline from little or nothing, with the numbers to show for it.
* Excellent writing. You can produce a sharp landing page, email or one\-pager yourself.
* Product marketing instincts: you can turn a technical product into a clear story for a specific buyer.
* Comfort with data and modern tools. You run your own CRM, automation and analytics, build your own dashboards and make budget calls from them.
* You already work AI\-first. You use tools like Claude to research, write, analyze and automate, and you can walk us through a workflow you built that changed your output.
* Range. You’re happy moving from strategy to a campaign launch to fixing a form in the same day.

**Nice to have**

* Experience marketing to HR, People or employee experience buyers.
* Partner or channel marketing experience.
* HubSpot experience.
* Experience marketing an AI product.

**What we offer**

* $115,000–$135,000 CAD base salary, plus a meaningful stock option grant vesting over time.
* A real budget for programs, tools and contractors.
* Direct influence on company strategy, working alongside the founders.
* Hybrid work from our new Bedford office.
* A clear path to VP Marketing as the team grows.

**How we hire**

A short intro call, conversations with our founders and the team, and a small practical exercise. We’ll walk you through the details on the first call.

**How to apply**

Apply through Indeed with your resume and a short note on a pipeline program you built: what you did and what it produced. Links to work you wrote or launched are welcome. We review applications as they arrive and aim to have someone in the role by early 2027\.

Innerlogic welcomes applicants of all backgrounds. If you need an accommodation at any stage of the hiring process, tell us and we’ll work with you.

Pay: $115,000\.00\-$135,000\.00 per year

jobs.title: SOX Director - ITGC
jobs.description:
Building the Future of Open Finance

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

The team

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

This role sits within SOX Compliance and is the senior technical authority for IT controls in the SOX program. You will set the strategy for ITGCs, IT application controls, and the controls over private key management and digital asset custody. Internal Audit independently tests the controls you own.

You will own the ITGC SOX program, building the control framework, testing approach, and evidence standards from the ground up. This is a hands-on role with real program ownership at a crypto exchange. The technology stack spans blockchain-native infrastructure, digital asset custody systems, and on-chain and off-chain processing, and engineering changes at a pace most companies never see. The systems are complex, the deployments are frequent, and the controls are consequential.

The opportunity

Strategy & program ownership
Own the enterprise IT SOX strategy and roadmap, covering ITGC, ITAC, and digital asset and key management controls across all in-scope entities and jurisdictions.
Define the scoping methodology and risk assessment for IT SOX, including in-scope applications, infrastructure, wallet and custody systems, and third-party and service-organization dependencies.
Set control design standards and own the control framework. Design controls that fit modern engineering practices (CI/CD, infrastructure as code, cloud) and don’t slow them down.
Set the standard for management testing and evidence. Direct co-sourced and matrixed resources, and review the quality of their work.
Use AI-enabled workflows, continuous controls monitoring, and data analytics to move IT SOX from periodic testing toward scalable, automated assurance.

Private key management & digital asset controls

Own SOX control design and coverage for the full private key lifecycle: generation, storage, access, signing and approval workflows, rotation, backup and recovery, and retirement.
Assess controls over key custody architectures, such as HSMs, MPC, multi-signature, and hot/warm/cold wallet structures, including segregation of duties, quorum and approval controls, and privileged access.
Evaluate how key management and custody controls support the existence, completeness, and safeguarding of customer and corporate digital assets and their financial reporting implications.
Assess controls over on-chain and off-chain transaction processing, reconciliation of wallets to ledgers, and reliance on blockchain data and third-party custodians or service organizations.
Be the SOX authority on emerging digital asset risks and decide how the control framework should respond as products, chains, and custody models evolve.

Deficiency evaluation & remediation

Lead evaluation of control deficiencies, including root cause analysis and severity and pervasiveness assessments, and recommend classification (control deficiency, significant deficiency, or material weakness).
Own remediation strategy for open ITGC and key management findings. Drive executive-level accountability with Engineering, Security, and Infrastructure leaders.
Escalate gaps and delays directly to senior leadership. Report status to the Audit Committee as required.
Coordinate with Internal Audit so remediated controls are ready for independent validation.

Executive & external stakeholder engagement

Be the senior SOX voice to the CFO, CISO, CTO, Controller, and the Audit Committee on IT control posture, risks, and remediation.
Lead the external auditor relationship on IT matters: audit strategy, reliance and scoping decisions, walkthroughs, and resolution of disagreements.
Serve as a trusted advisor to engineering and security leaders, translating audit and control requirements into practical engineering decisions.
Partner with Internal Audit, ERM, the business process SOX lead, and co-sourced providers to align coverage across the full assurance program.
Mentor SOX and risk team members and raise the technical bar across the function.

What You Bring

10+ years in SOX compliance, IT audit, internal audit, or external audit, with deep ITGC experience and a record of owning programs at enterprise scale.
Direct, hands-on experience with crypto and private key management controls, including designing, assessing, or auditing controls over key custody, wallet infrastructure, signing, and digital asset safeguarding. This is a must-have.
Experience in a crypto exchange, custodian, fintech, or payments company with complex, rapidly evolving infrastructure.
CISA and CPA certifications required. Candidates with one who are actively pursuing the other will be considered.
Expert knowledge of ITGC frameworks, SOX 404, COSO, COBIT, and PCAOB standards, with the judgment to make and defend scoping, reliance, and deficiency-classification decisions.
Strong technical fluency in how systems, databases, cloud infrastructure, and deployment pipelines work.
Proven ability to connect an ITGC or key management failure to its impact on business process controls and the financial statements.
Experience working with external auditors (Big 4 preferred) and presenting to Audit Committees and senior executives.
Experience across multi-entity structures or multiple jurisdictions.
Exceptional communicator who earns credibility with both engineers and finance executives.

Nice to haves

Experience building or scaling an IT SOX program in a growth-stage or first-year SOX company.
Familiarity with CI/CD, GitLab or similar version control, and cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP).
Familiarity with SOC 1/SOC 2 reliance for custodians and service providers, and with proof-of-reserves or similar attestations.
Familiarity with audit and GRC platforms such as AuditBoard or Workiva.
Familiarity with AI-assisted compliance tools and willingness to adopt new technologies.

Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution.

We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

Our commitment

Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right abilities, knowledge, and skills for the job. We encourage you to apply for roles where you don't fully meet the listed requirements, especially if you're passionate or knowledgeable about crypto.

We may ask candidates to complete job-related skills or work-style assessments as part of our hiring process. These assessments evaluate competencies relevant to the role and are applied consistently across candidates for similar positions. Results are considered alongside experience and interviews, and are not the sole basis for any employment decision.

As an equal opportunity employer, we don't tolerate discrimination or harassment of any kind, whether based on race, ethnicity, age, gender identity, citizenship, religion, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

What You'll Be Doing

The Energy, Infrastructure & Transition (EIT) team provides investment banking services to existing and prospective clients across upstream and midstream energy, renewable and conventional power, utilities, infrastructure, energy transition, and climate technology. With a global coverage strategy spanning North America, Europe, Latin America, Asia, and Australia, we deliver a client-focused approach that combines mergers and acquisitions (M&A) and financial advisory services with access to debt, equity, and loan capital markets, as well as risk management and hedging solutions. As a Director, EIT, Global Investment Banking, you'll play a lead role in supporting clients through complex transactions, including M&A, strategic and capital structure advisory, debt and equity financings, and tax equity transactions. You'll work closely with colleagues across Capital Markets and our global offices to deliver thoughtful, sector-informed advice and execution support. Based in Calgary, this role has a primary sector focus on upstream and midstream energy and offers the opportunity to contribute to a market-leading platform in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. Details on your work arrangement (proportion of on-site and remote work) will be discussed at the time of your interview.

Client advisory and origination - Support business development and origination efforts by preparing client proposals and contributing ideas for equity and debt financings, mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, and other advisory mandates. jobs.title: Chief Administrative Officer (CAO) - Town of Lynn Lake
jobs.description:
About the Town of Lynn Lake, Manitoba

Surrounded by boreal forest, pristine northern lakes, and located 1,076 km northwest of Winnipeg, Lynn Lake has a population of about 600 people and offers a unique northern lifestyle with exceptional fishing, hunting, hiking, canoeing, and extensive ATV and snowmobile trails. Local amenities include West Lynn Heights School (K–12), the Lynn Lake Hospital and Clinic, RCMP Detachment, Regional Conservation Office, and an arena offering year-round programming, a fully equipped fitness centre, and all-weather roads and highways.

For a municipal administrator seeking meaningful impact, Lynn Lake offers a rare opportunity to help guide a northern community through a period of renewal, growth, and long-term sustainability. A major gold mining project is expected to bring renewed economic activity, new residents, and long-term growth opportunities for the municipality. This represents a pivotal moment in Lynn Lake’s history as the community transitions toward a time of revitalization and sustainable development.

The Opportunity

Reporting directly to Mayor and Council, the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO) is the senior administrative leader of the municipality, responsible for the effective and efficient administration of the Town of Lynn Lake. The CAO will provide strategic advice and operational leadership across all municipal functions, including administration, financial management, human resources, economic development, programs, and services. The successful candidate will be a diplomatic, results-oriented, leader with strong financial acumen, sound judgment, and the ability to build collaborative relationships with Council, staff, community members, Indigenous partners, and regional stakeholders. This is a hands-on leadership role requiring an approachable, relationship-driven, adaptable, and future-minded municipal leader committed to a northern lifestyle. This role offers a comprehensive overall total compensation package that includes furnished municipal housing, relocation assistance, northern retention bonus, benefits and pension.

Key Responsibilities

Administer the business affairs of the municipality in accordance with the Municipal Act and other statutes of the province.
Function as an effective liaison between the Council, staff, community, Indigenous groups, industry, regional and government partners.
Provide strategic advice to Mayor and Council on governance, legislation, policy, community priorities, and long-term strategic direction.
Advance community and economic development by negotiating agreements, managing mining-related and infrastructure impacts, securing funding, and supporting strategic growth opportunities –including grant opportunities for infrastructure and capital projects.
Lead the effective delivery of municipal administration, programs, services, infrastructure, and capital projects, ensuring Council decisions are implemented and residents receive responsive service.
Strengthen organizational effectiveness, transparency, and risk management through clear communication, modern administrative and digital systems, information security, records management, and process improvement.
Oversee operating and capital budgets, financial reporting, internal controls, audits, taxation, procurement, grants, borrowing, and long-term financial and asset-management planning.
Responsible for all human resource functions, including effective recruitment, employee development, performance management, labour relations, workplace safety, team engagement, and organizational culture initiatives.
Provide supportive leadership and direction to staff and management, fostering an approach focused on collaboration, effective communication, mentorship, and development.
Play a pivotal role in promoting new investment and building the community during a time of opportunity and renewed growth.

Selection Criteria

Degree in Public Administration, Business Administration, or related discipline.
Completion of the Manitoba Municipal Administrators Certificate (CMMA), equivalent training, or willingness to obtain.
3-5 years senior management experience in a municipal environment; previous CAO experience is an asset.
Empowering leader with ability to manage stress in a dynamic and evolving environment.
Strong financial management and budgeting expertise, and willingness to learn municipal financial software (ASYST).
Knowledge of municipal governance, The Municipal Act and proven ability to work effectively with elected officials, staff, and the public.
Excellent public relations, interpersonal and communication skills, coupled with the ability to negotiate, influence, and facilitate.
Exceptional relationship building skills and ability to establish credibility and trust with a diverse group of people.
Demonstrated political acumen, visionary leader, and solid decision maker with a high level of ethics, values, and integrity.
Knowledge in computer systems for business applications and capacity to blend systems, people, and process to optimize operations.
Valid Class 5 Drivers License.
Assets include community or economic development experience, and experience working in northern, rural, or remote communities.

To apply submit a resume and cover letter detailing how you meet the position requirements.

The role will translate strategy into practical execution plans, coordinate delivery across businesses and functions, and provide senior leaders with clear visibility into progress, quality, risk, and outcomes.

The role combines enterprise program leadership, data analytics, executive reporting, and identification of AI and automation opportunities. The successful candidate will work directly with complex and imperfect data, conduct targeted quality reviews, challenge scope and assumptions, identify trends and themes, and translate findings into practical recommendations. As priorities evolve, the role will apply these capabilities to other Operations Risk and Control Transformation initiatives.

Lead global risk transformation and execution

Build alignment and accountability across ELT areas, L1B teams, Process Owners, Line 2, Technology, and delivery partners through influence rather than formal authority.

Generate actionable insights

jobs.title: Director, Product Design
jobs.description:
At Replicant, we believe AI should work for people, starting with customer service. That's why we built a platform that helps contact centers resolve more requests, proactively identify issues, and improve agent performance with AI-powered conversation intelligence and AI agents that act like your best reps.

Our AI agents handle millions of calls every month for Fortune 500 companies and high-growth innovators. From processing payments to booking appointments and authenticating users, they help customers get what they need instantly, 24/7. Meanwhile, our real-time conversation insights help contact center leaders coach better and improve every interaction.

We're leading the shift from legacy systems to AI-first service, powered by large language models (LLMs) and designed for enterprise scale, security, and empathy. If you're excited by the potential of LLMs, voice AI, and building category-defining technology with a kind, ambitious team, you'll love it here.

About The Role

This role reports to the VP of Product, owns the practice outright, and comes with two designers attached – our Conversation Design Lead and a Lead / Principal Product Designer whose role you’ll define and hire.

Roughly 80% of your time goes into the work itself, and we mean owning high-leverage product design decisions rather than delivering via management of a team. You’ll be accountable for product design decisions and direction across every surface — the sales conversation, the deployments our delivery team configures, the AI agent talking to a customer, the analytics an operator reads every morning.

The other 20% is designing and running the product design practice to increase design’s leverage across the organization. We’re looking to you to help us get design right – we’ve tried to build design here twice and we’ve under-resourced it both times. Our org has grown up as sales- and engineering-led, and in this role you’ll shepherd how we grow and mature through product and design leadership. As the design practice grows into a pillar of our product function, this role grows with it.

If you want a green field to help demonstrate how powerful a force product design can be – and you want to do that while applying cutting-edge HCI to age-old problems of providing better customer service – this is the role for you.

What You'll Do

Own the whole customer experience, interface included. A customer's experience of Replicant runs from the sales conversation, through a deployment our delivery team configures, into an AI agent that talks to their customers, and back out through the analytics their operators read daily.
Set the information architecture for a converging platform. Our conversation intelligence and agent-building products grew separately and are now becoming one product. You decide what the objects are, what they're called, and how someone moves between them.
Own the design system's architecture and the rules around it. The foundation exists — components in Figma and in Storybook. What's missing is a pattern language, documented decisions about when to use what, and a contribution model engineers can build against. You set that architecture, govern it, and are accountable for it existing.
Extend design's influence past the work you do yourself. Much of the customer-facing experience here gets shaped by people outside your team: product managers, delivery engineers who configure agents, solutions engineers in demos. Raising the bar means influencing them, giving them something good enough to follow, and telling them no when it matters.
Drive rapid prototype-and-validation loops. You'll talk to internal customers, contact center operators and turn what you hear into design decisions, owning method as well as findings. You’ll create and drive a best-in-class prototype-and-validate loop.
Bring product design and conversation design together. Our product is a conversation, so we've put both disciplines in one practice. You own how they come together and the research practice underneath both.

What You'll Bring

You think in systems and journeys. Before asking which control a step needs, you ask whether the step needs to exist. You've designed across touchpoints that weren't all interfaces: a call, a handoff, an email, a conversation with a human agent.
You have a real HCI or interaction-design foundation. You can reason from first principles about how people perceive, learn, form expectations, and recover from error, rather than from patterns you've seen in other products. Voice, conversational, and graphical interfaces all sit inside our product, and we need someone who can move between them without starting over each time.
You've driven change through resistance. You've moved an entrenched team over months, not just changed one executive's mind in one meeting. You can describe what you were up against and what it took.
You lead with the human and you integrate business outcomes and thinking without being asked. You've spent time close to the PM role, or worked with product closely enough that you think that way anyway. You can point to specific decisions that changed because of a conversation you personally had with a customer.
You've governed a design system, not only built one. Contribution, documentation, deprecation, and the arguments that come with them. You can describe a time you told someone no and why. The governance matters more to us than how many components you drew.
You find the problems and set your own priorities. You identify opportunities the team hadn't seen and make the case for them. You converge without being pushed and escalate the right things at the right time.
You're AI-native in your practice. You use these tools in real design work and have earned opinions about where they help and where they degrade quality. You've built workflows or assets other people adopted.
You lead people and hold a room. Setting direction, giving hard feedback, running a critique, growing someone's craft, and hiring. You can also hold your position in front of executives and customers. Formal management experience helps; evidence that designers got better working with you matters more than a title.

Requirements

Based in a US or Canadian timezone
10+ years of product design experience, including 2-3+ at the director or principal level
Experience leading or growing designers, whether or not you had the title
Experience owning design for an enterprise or operational product

We care about the scope of what you've owned, not years on a résumé. If you're unsure whether you're at this level, apply anyway. We'd rather assess it than have you self-select out.

NICE TO HAVE

Figma fluency on the system side: components, variants, libraries, variables, tokens. Enough to hold your hire to a standard and to work in the files yourself.
Comfort moving between Figma and code (Storybook, shadcn/ui, Tailwind, or tools like Cursor and Claude Code). If you want to pick up UI-level changes yourself, that's open to you with preview environments and engineering review.
Experience designing AI or conversational products, especially where the output was non-deterministic and you had to design failure states, trust, correction, and recovery.
Experience with operational or contact center tooling.
Experience defining a design practice from close to nothing.
Experience leading designers across more than one discipline — product, conversation, content, or research.

For All Full-time Employees, We Offer

🌴 In-person connection that counts

Our Values

Replicant has three core values. It is critical that everyone who joins the team feels excited and moved by these values as every new team member makes an impact on our culture.

Blade Runners:
We take ownership and pride to influence the outcomes of our goals. We are successful, and like a Blade Runner, use the tools at our disposal to reach our objectives. Bread Makers:
