jobs.title: Director, Sales Enablement
jobs.description:
Do you believe enablement should be measured in ramp speed and revenue, not completion rates? 

 Then Jobber might be the place for you! We’re looking for a Director, Sales Enablement to be part of our Sales Enablement & Operations department.
 Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. We work with small home service businesses, like your local plumbers, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn’t like it used to be—the way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. That’s why we put the power and flexibility in their hands to run their businesses how, where, and when they want!
 Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail’s Canada’s Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada’s Technology Fast 50™, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500™ lists. With an Executive team that has over thirty years of industry experience of leading the way, we’ve come a long way from our first customer in 2011—but we’ve just scratched the surface of what we want to accomplish for our customers.

 The team: 
 Sales Enablement & Operations exists to make sure Jobber’s go-to-market org never has to choose between moving quickly and being ready. We build the systems, tools, and people development that turn strategy into execution: how we forecast and plan, how we pay and motivate, how our tech stack works for reps instead of against them, and how every seller gets better at their craft. The team is organized into peer pillars: Sales Operations, Revenue Technology, Sales Planning & Operations, and Enablement Programs.

 The role: 
 Reporting to the Sr. Director, Sales Enablement & Operations, the Director, Sales Enablement will lead Enablement Programs and make sure every seller at Jobber has what they need to win: the skills, the confidence, and the readiness to perform from day one and through every new launch. You’ll lead a team of five to six, as a peer to the leads of Sales Operations, Revenue Technology, and Sales Planning & Operations. You’re accountable for outcomes, not activity — whether reps are actually ready, whether launches actually land in the field, and whether the enablement investment shows up in ramp speed, pipeline, and revenue.

 The Director, Sales Enablement will: 
 Set the strategy for onboarding, training, certification, and coaching across the sales org, and build, manage, and upskill a team of enablement managers and practitioners.

 Own ramp programs and certification standards across go-to-market roles, and hold the bar on what “certified and ready” actually means.

 Lead enablement for new product, pricing, and process launches, building workback plans that trace every training, content, and certification milestone back from the launch date.

 Build structured, repeatable playbooks and coaching frameworks, and keep them current as products, segments, and motions change.

 Bring AI into how the team builds and delivers enablement — content creation, coaching feedback loops, practice and roleplay, knowledge access — and into what reps are taught to use in their own workflow.

 Partner with Product, Product Marketing, Sales leadership, and Customer Success so enablement priorities match what the business needs next, and launches land with sales rather than at sales.

 Define success beyond completion rates, and report on ramp time, certification pass rates, and downstream impact on pipeline and revenue.

 To be successful, you should have: 
 Extensive experience in sales enablement, revenue operations, or sales leadership, including building and running onboarding, training, or certification programs at scale.

 Demonstrated people leadership experience, including managing managers, and a track record of developing your own team’s skills alongside the field’s.

 A proven track record of leading enablement for product or pricing launches in a B2B SaaS environment, with workback plans that hold up against a real launch timeline.

 Hands-on fluency with AI tools in enablement work itself: content generation, coaching and roleplay, and knowledge management.

 Experience building structured, scalable learning frameworks rather than one-off training events.

 Strong stakeholder management with director-level and senior partners across Product, Marketing, and Sales leadership, and the ability to influence roadmap and go-to-market timing rather than only execute against it.

 Comfort operating with ambiguity and building infrastructure where none exists yet.

 Sharp written and verbal communication.

 A bias toward outcomes over activity, and the judgment to know the difference.

 Compensation: 
 At Jobber, we believe that compensation should be transparent, fair, and reflective of your experience and growth. This role has a minimum annual salary of $181,400, a midpoint of $213,500, and a maximum salary of $245,500, designed to show the progression from learning the ropes to truly excelling.
 We design our compensation to reflect each new hire’s skills, experience against the complexity of the role, ensuring a fair and competitive salary. Our range is intentionally broad to support growth and long-term impact, with fully established hires typically starting around the midpoint. The higher end of the range is reserved for those who have demonstrated deep expertise and lasting contributions, while offers below the midpoint reflect strong potential with room to develop. This approach ensures that compensation aligns with both an individual’s current capabilities and their opportunity for future growth.
 Base salary is just one part of a total compensation package that will include equity rewards, annual stipends for health and wellness, retirement savings matching, and an extended health package with fully paid premiums for body and mind. Your professional growth matters to us too! You’ll have access to a dedicated talent development program that includes career coaching and opportunities for career development.
 We believe in transparency and open conversations about compensation. If you have any questions about our approach, we’re happy to discuss them throughout the hiring process!

 Location: 
 We believe great collaboration is intentional, and sometimes that means coming together in person to build, brainstorm, and connect. To support this, the role is open to candidates based in one of our hub cities: Edmonton, Toronto, Vancouver, or Kitchener-Waterloo. 

 What you can expect from Jobber: 
 A total compensation package that includes an extended health benefits package with fully paid premiums for both body and mind, matching in RRSP, TFSA or FHSA, and stock options.

 A dedicated Talent Development team and access to coaching, learning, and leadership programs to help you grow your career, reach your goals, and unlock your full potential.

 A unique opportunity to build, grow, and leave your impact on a $400-billion industry that has no dominant player...yet.

 To work with a group of people who are humble, supportive, and give a sh*t about our customers.

 We believe that diverse teams perform better and that fostering an inclusive work environment is a key part of growing a successful team. We welcome people of diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we are committed to working with applicants requesting accommodation at any stage of the hiring process. 

 A bit more about us: 
 Job by job, we’re transforming the way service is delivered. Your lawn care provider, home cleaning service, plumber or painter could use Jobber to better connect with their customers, save time in the office, invoice faster, and get paid! We’re bringing tens of thousands of people together with technology to deliver billions of dollars a year in services to happy customers. Jobber exists to help make these small businesses successful, and when they’re successful we all win!

jobs.description:
Later is the world’s most intelligent influencer marketing company, built to give brands the confidence to create unforgettable campaigns. By combining real creator relationships, trusted intelligence, and expert guidance, Later removes fear and guesswork from one of marketing’s most visible investments.

 Built on a native, AI-powered platform and more than a decade of proprietary data—including billions of social interactions, impressions, and $2.4B+ in verified influencer-driven purchases—Later helps teams understand what will work before they launch.

 By combining trusted insight with expert guidance, Later removes guesswork from influencer marketing, enabling brands to choose the right creators, execute fully managed campaigns, and drive meaningful growth across awareness, engagement, and revenue. Trusted by leading enterprise brands including Nike, Wayfair, Unilever, and Southwest Airlines, Later bridges creativity and performance so campaigns don’t just look good—they deliver results. Learn more at later.com.

 About this position 

 We’re looking for a Director of Creator Operations to own the systems and processes that connect how Later finds, engages, and supports creators. Creators are on one side of every campaign we run, and as we bring the creator experience together across our programs, we need one leader to design how outreach, success, and support work as a single system. Later Creator is the core of this role, and the scope extends to how we support affiliate creators across Later Influence.

 You’ll own both ways we bring creators in: the sales-led motion, where our team reaches creators person to person, and the product-led motion, where outreach runs at scale through the product. Reporting to the VP of Revenue and Business Operations as part of Later’s Operations team, you’ll partner closely with the General Manager of Creator, Creator Growth, Creator Success, Creator Support, Product, and Engineering. You’ll manage one direct report, who owns HubSpot design and administration, and direct engineering and product resources on the integrations between our systems. This is a high-visibility role with regular exposure to senior leadership.

 What you’ll be doing 

 Strategy and targets 

 Own the infrastructure behind creator acquisition and engagement across the sales-led and product-led motions, from first touch through activation and campaign participation.

 Build the creator acquisition targets, and the forecast behind them, with the General Manager of Creator, so Creator Growth leadership has a number they can execute against and see coming.

 Shape funnel strategy jointly with Creator Growth: they own the number and its execution, and you own the structure, the forecast, and the target model it runs on.

 Own the roadmap for a consolidated creator engagement and tracking system, and decide what gets built and in what order.

 Turn creator funnel data into decisions on where to put outreach effort, headcount, and automation.

 Systems and integration design 

 Act as the primary integration designer between the creator product experience and the Success and Support teams that engage creators.

 Partner with Product the way a product manager would: write the requirements for engagement flows, routing, and handoffs, and work with Engineering to ship them.

 Own HubSpot as the system of record for creator marketing, engagement tracking, and the person-to-person outreach our Creator Success team runs.

 Consolidate the creator outreach tech stack: assess each tool, retire the overlap, and make the remaining systems work from one shared record of each creator.

 Own the budget for HubSpot and the other creator engagement tools, and decide where that spend goes as the stack consolidates.

 Use AI and automation to take manual work out of outreach, routing, and follow-up, and measure what it saves.

 Outreach and engagement operations 

 Own the systems behind product-led outreach to creators at scale, including segmentation, triggers, sequencing, and measurement.

 Design the routing and handoff rules that move a creator between automated outreach and a person on our team at the right moment.

 Build the engagement flows that bring affiliate and awareness creators into campaigns and keep them participating.

 Define the standards (data definitions, field governance, and service levels) that keep outreach, success, and support data accurate and trusted.

 Leadership and team 

 Lead and develop your HubSpot design and administration direct report with clear goals, regular coaching, and a growth plan.

 Set the talent bar for Creator Operations and raise it with each hire and each process you ship.

 Address performance gaps quickly and directly, in partnership with People.

 Direct engineering and product work on integrations through clear requirements, priorities, and follow-through.

 Clear blockers for the Creator Success and outreach teams before they escalate.

 What success looks like 

 Within your first 60 days, you have mapped how creators are acquired, engaged, and supported today across every tool and team, set a baseline for the creator funnel, and shipped at least one change that removes manual work for Creator Success.

 By 90 days, the plan to consolidate the creator outreach tech stack is agreed with Product and Engineering, and you have built the creator acquisition, activation, and campaign participation targets, with a forecast that the General Manager of Creator and Creator Growth leadership have signed off on.

 By 6 months, the consolidated engagement and tracking system is live for Later Creator: every creator touch, automated or personal, is tracked on one record, and routing between product-led and person-to-person outreach runs on documented rules.

 By 12 months, the creator engagement stack is consolidated onto one system that supports all of Later’s affiliate creators, and affiliate creator acquisition is growing faster than the baseline you set in your first 60 days, without added headcount. In addition, your direct report owns the HubSpot platform day to day, and Creator Operations is the team the General Manager of Creator relies on to set creator targets and forecast them accurately.

 What you bring 

 We are committed to building an inclusive, supportive place for you to do the best and most rewarding work of your career. If you identify with any of the following, we encourage you to apply!

 6-8 years in Revenue Operations, Marketing Operations, or Growth Operations, with a track record of building the systems behind a high-volume acquisition funnel.

 Experience running B2C or creator-facing outreach at scale across both product-led and person-to-person motions, including designing how the two hand off.

 Deep HubSpot experience, including designing lifecycle stages, workflows, routing, and engagement tracking for a team that works directly with customers or creators.

 A track record of designing integrations between a product and the go-to-market systems around it, working with Product and Engineering on requirements, prioritization, and release.

 Experience building targets and forecasts for a sales or outreach team that another leader executes against: you can build the model, set the number, and explain the gap.

 A record of using AI and automation to remove manual work from operations, with results you can measure.

 Experience leading through others, including managing a direct report, owning a tooling budget, and directing technical work across teams without formal authority.

 You get up to speed quickly in a new domain, break complex multi-system problems into concrete plans with owners and milestones, and own the result end to end.

 Experience with other marketing automation platforms (for example, Klaviyo, Braze, or Iterable) is a plus.

 An understanding of social platforms and how creators build audiences and earn on them is a plus.

 Experience in the creator economy, affiliate marketing, or a two-sided marketplace is a plus.

 How we work 

 We will do whatever it takes to win: We win when our customers and creators win. We bring full commitment to outcomes that matter, not just effort.

 We have no limit to our aspiration: We think big, push beyond what seems possible, and refuse to let conventional thinking set the ceiling.

 We are relentless: We keep going. Through ambiguity, setbacks, and competing priorities, we find a way forward.

 We deeply understand our business: If we don’t have the knowledge, we figure it out. We take ownership of understanding how Later works and what drives results.

 We take our work seriously, but not ourselves: We bring rigor and accountability without ego, and we make space for each other to do our best work.

 Our approach to compensation 

 We take a market-based and data-driven approach to compensation. We leverage data from trusted third-party compensation sources to help us understand the market value of a role based on function, level, geographic location, and scope. We evaluate compensation biannually, including performance and market-related factors.

 Our salaries are benchmarked against market Total Cash Compensation for the geographic location of our job posting. Compensation for some roles is structured as On Target Earnings (OTE = base + commission/variable), while for others it is structured as salary only.

 To comply with local legislation and ensure transparency, we share salary ranges on all job postings. Skills, experience, and other factors help determine the final salary we offer, which may vary from the original range posted.

 Additionally, all permanent team members are eligible to participate in various benefits plans as part of their overall compensation package.

 Salary Range: 
United States: $180k - $210k OTE

 Where we work: 

 We have offices in Boston, MA; Vancouver, BC; and Vancouver, WA. For select positions, we are open to hiring fully remote candidates. We post our positions in the location(s) where we are open to having the successful candidate be located. 

 Diversity, inclusion, and accessibility: 

 At Later, we are committed to fostering a culture rooted in an inclusion-first mindset at every level of the company, embracing the importance of hiring and building teams for culture add rather than culture fit. We openly build and maintain unbiased hiring, pay, and promotion practices to create a foundation for an equitable workplace, paving the way for systemic change.

Job Description 

 What is the opportunity? 

 Reporting to the VP, Credit Modelling & Methodology, the Senior Director, CMM Model Monitoring and Architecture will lead the strategic management of data and the technology infrastructure used for credit parameter development, performance monitoring, and external disclosures. 

 In this role, the candidate will manage a team that is accountable for the oversight of data used for Wholesale and Retail credit risk parameters.  The candidate is also accountable for the performance monitoring of stress and impairment (S&I) models for Canada (IFRS9/EWST) and the US (CECL/CCAR), parameters used in regulatory capital (AIRB), and other CMM-owned models.

 The Senior Director is a key leadership position with ownership of data governance for credit modelling and monitoring, and delivering on strategic priorities for CMM from a technology architecture perspective.  Successful execution will include close collaboration with model developers, model owners, RBC’s internal lines of defense and regulators.

 What will you do? 

 The Senior Director, supported by a team of 14 - 18, is accountable for:
 Developing, documenting, and implementing data and monitoring processes related to parameters used across RBC, including those which drive 80% of RBC’s Risk Weighted Assets as well as all credit Stress Testing & Impairment models.
 Rigorous design and execution of SOX controls related to the data used in model development and monitoring.  Partnering with other functional areas to ensure adequate data quality controls are in place on upstream data sources.
 Leading data governance activities for the CMM team, including the quarterly Data Oversight Working Group, to provide transparency into data quality in critical applications.
 Understanding and articulating strategic options with respect to data and performance production, and making strong recommendations to senior management.
 Setting and regularly assessing Objectives and Key Results for data management, infrastructure and model monitoring.
 Leading the production of external disclosures related to regulatory parameters across retail and wholesale parameters.
 Spearheading key stakeholder relationships internally and externally.  This includes coaching the team leads how to most effectively partner with colleagues in GRM, lines of business, Internal Audit, External Audit and regulators in Canada and the US.
 Driving required outcomes through anticipating and responding to constructive challenges to the output of their team.

 What do you need to succeed? 

 Must-Have 

 12 – 15+ years work experience in credit risk or a related area with model development, or on-going performance monitoring.
 Knowledge of credit risk methodology, including capital estimation, credit risk/stress testing models, and/or direct experience with Expected Credit Loss implementations.
 Substantial experience with financial models, regulatory reporting systems, and software implementation.
 Experience in managing large datasets and routine production processes subject to a rigorous control environment, and knowledge of best practices in data management.
 Experience managing teams and coordinating complex technical projects.
 Demonstrated ability to mentor and develop technical staff.
 Knowledge of Python or similar language(s).
 Knowledge of modern code development and code management best practices.
 Strong interpersonal, communication, and presentation skills, with the ability to articulate and document complex technical problems and control process for a non-technical audience.

 Nice-to-Have 

 Expertise in banking products across retail and wholesale portfolios.
 Knowledge of SAS is an asset.
 Project management and/or stakeholder coordination experience.
 Understanding of SOX controls, internal audit requirements, and regulatory compliance.

 We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

 Ability to make a difference and lasting impact

 Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team

 Build TD's perspective on the future of work, translating advancements in AI, technology, skills, and workforce models into workforce structure and role design.
 Lead workforce planning and scenario development, tying workforce plans to financial and business plans.
 Define the workforce implications of TD's business strategy, including future workforce models, critical capabilities, and workforce transformation priorities.
 Partner across HR, AI, Technology and Finance to convert future workforce insights into business-level and bank-wide strategies, roadmaps, and measurable actions.
 Lead TD's approach to work redesign, helping leaders determine how work, roles, skills, and workforce models should evolve as AI and technology reshape the enterprise.
 Establish standards and frameworks for human and AI-enabled work, including workforce implications, accountability models, governance requirements, and organizational readiness.

 Lead Skills Strategy 
 Lead skills strategy, including identifying critical skills, gaps, workforce risks, and emerging opportunities.
 Provide advice on workforce composition, investments, capability requirements, capacity, and risks.

 Research & Insight 
 Lead research and benchmarking
 Translate signals and leading practices into actionable insight, recommendations, and decision support.

 Workforce Planning & Decision Support 
 Create and deploy workforce planning methodologies and capabilities.
 Train HR, Finance and business leaders to develop high quality plans
 Oversee forecasting, scenario planning, risk assessment, and capacity insights that support better business and investment decisions.

 Job Requirements 
 10+ years of experience in workforce strategy, strategic planning, organization effectiveness, organization design, management consulting, business transformation, talent strategy, or a related field.
 Networked externally covering academia, tech firms, research organizations and industry
 Strong communication and influencing skills, with ability to challenge, simplify, and drive decisions
 Able to turn insight into solutions
 Track record of leading high-performing teams, hiring and developing top talent
 University degree in business, HR, organizational effectiveness, strategy, or a related field.

 Preferred Attributes 
 We're looking for someone who:
 Sees around corners and can translate the future into practical choices for today.
 Thinks like a strategist, executes like an operator, and follows through with discipline.
 Is energized by the intersection of workforce strategy, skills, future workforce transformation, and AI.
 Has the courage to challenge assumptions while building trusted partnerships.
 Brings ambition, grit, and a desire to win, without ego.
 Inspires leaders and teams with a clear, practical vision of what is possible.
 Moves from insight to action with urgency, persistence, and accountability.
 Balances imagination with pragmatism in a large, regulated organization.

 Who We Are: 
 TD is one of the world's leading global financial institutions and is the fifth largest bank in North America by branches/stores. Every day, we strive to make every interaction, product, and experience remarkably human and refreshingly simple for over 27 million households and businesses in Canada, the United States and around the world. More than 95,000 TD colleagues bring their skills, talent, and creativity to foster deeper relationships, ensure disciplined execution, and build a simpler, faster banking experience. TD is deeply committed to being a leader in client experience, that is why we believe that all colleagues, no matter where they work, are client facing. Together, we are reimagining what banking can be for our clients, colleagues and communities. 

 Our Total Rewards Package 
Our Total Rewards package reflects the investments we make in our colleagues to help them and their families achieve their financial, physical, and mental well-being goals. Total Rewards at TD includes a base salary, variable compensation, and several other key plans such as health and well-being benefits, savings and retirement programs, paid time off, banking benefits and discounts, career development, and reward and recognition programs. Learn more 

 Additional Information: 
We’re delighted that you’re considering building a career with TD. Through regular development conversations, training programs, and a competitive benefits plan, we’re committed to providing the support our colleagues need to thrive both at work and at home.

 Please be advised that this job opportunity is subject to provincial regulation for employment purposes. It is imperative to acknowledge that each province or territory within the jurisdiction of Canada may have its own set of regulations, requirements.

 Colleague Development 
 If you’re interested in a specific career path or are looking to build certain skills, we want to help you succeed. You’ll have regular career, development, and performance conversations with your manager, as well as access to an online learning platform and a variety of mentoring programs to help you unlock future opportunities.

 If you’re passionate about helping clients and building deep, lasting relationships, TD offers diverse career paths where you can grow your expertise and make a meaningful impact.  

 We're committed to your success and foster a respectful workplace where diverse perspectives are valued, everyone has fair opportunities to grow, and you can unlock your full potential to achieve your career goals. Here at TD, we hire and develop the best.

 Training & Onboarding 
We will provide training and onboarding sessions to ensure that you’ve got everything you need to succeed in your new role.

 Interview Process

 Accommodation

We look forward to hearing from you!

 What is the Role? 
 Telus Digital, Salesforce Practice is searching for a driven and seasoned sales professional who possesses the grit and energy to help us grow and scale. The Sales Director is responsible for leading the sales cycle, customer and solution implementation lifecycle. They are accountable for identifying and driving new opportunities with new and existing customers to meet revenue quota/targets.
 They are an experienced sales executive and have experience selling Salesforce services (product Sales will not be considered). They are strategic thinkers who uncover the desired experiences and develop the right engagement that will meet their needs. They possess technical acumen, analytical and critical thinking skills. They work closely with pre-sales, delivery experts and industry experts in order to effectively shape a deal.

They must generate leads sourced through partnerships with Salesforce, cross-sell within Telus or direct via strategic sales motions. You will work with prospects and existing customers to identify, nurture and develop opportunities. You will own the opportunity strategy and adhere to our sales processes including timely maintenance of pipeline and forecasts. You will be responsible for working closely with the Telus Digital presales and industry teams to bring the right points of views, solutions and proposals forward to customers ensuring timelines are being met.
 ● Develop and execute an account and sales plan to grow business for Telus Digital’s services.

jobs.description:
About ClearGov 

 ClearGov is building the modern financial operating layer for the public sector. 

 We help US local governments and school districts plan, budget, report, and communicate their finances with clarity and confidence. From long-term planning to financial reporting, compliance, and transparency, our platform connects the work finance teams are already doing and makes it easier to deliver for their communities. 

Today, more than 2,000 public sector organizations use ClearGov, and we continue to expand our platform and reach as we grow.

 Our Core Values 

 Be Clear & Credible  

 We are authentic in our interactions, communicating with clarity, speaking with honesty, and following through with consistency. We turn transparency into our greatest competitive advantage. 

 Be Human   

 We are human partners to our colleagues and customers and lead with consideration and kindness - making space for others to do the same. We turn empathy into a shared strength.

 Be Better Together   

 We are committed to building an inclusive community where everyone thrives. We share successes, support each other through challenges, and show up for our teammates the way we show up for our customers. We turn togetherness into our greatest advantage and collaboration into our greatest multiplier.

 Be Honourable/Honorable   

 We are responsible to our colleagues and customers. We bring our full selves to every conversation, every project, every decision, and every relationship. We act with intention, deliver on our commitments, and lead with integrity - even when no one is watching. We turn honour into the foundation that powers everything we do.

 Be Connected 

 We are culture builders where people are seen, welcomed, and celebrated. We show up in every interaction - the laughs, the wins, the hard days. We turn connection into opportunities for people to feel they belong.

 What Makes You a Great Fit 

 You take ownership and follow through

 You communicate clearly and effectively

 You're comfortable solving problems and figuring things out

 You learn quickly and adapt as things change

 You care about the team, not just your own work

 You bring a sense of humor and perspective to what you do

 About the Opportunity 

 ClearGov has built a strong product marketing foundation, with an established team supporting product launches, messaging, and sales enablement across a growing portfolio. As the company enters its next phase of growth, ClearGov is hiring a Director of Product & Solution Marketing to elevate the function from strong product-level execution to platform-and- solution-level strategy.

 Reporting to the VP of Marketing, this leader will define how ClearGov positions, packages, and brings to market a suite of 13 products across cities, counties, school districts, and special districts, each with distinct needs and buying dynamics. The Director of Product & Solution Marketing will help the company make sharper decisions about where to invest, how the products fit together, and how ClearGov expands within its customer base.

 This is a highly visible leadership role with meaningful autonomy and direct access to the executive team and board. The Director of Product & Solution Marketing will serve as a strategic partner to the VP of Marketing, CPO and CRO, translating customer and market insight into portfolio choices and measurable commercial impact.

 This leader will manage an established team of four, creating a five-person product & solution marketing organization, with the opportunity to grow the team as the function expands.

 Key Responsibilities: 

 Lead pricing and packaging strategy: Set the strategic direction for bundling, discounting, and launch pricing in partnership with Product, Finance, Revenue, and external research partners.

 Set portfolio and commercialization strategy: Define how ClearGov’s products fit together, where bundling and cross-sell opportunities exist, and how positioning and go-to-market motions should vary across customer segments.

 Shape executive decision-making: Represent product marketing with the executive team and board, connecting market, customer, and competitive insight to growth priorities and business performance.

 Lead and develop the product marketing organization: Build on the team’s subject matter expertise and strengths in messaging, launches, and enablement while expanding its capabilities in portfolio strategy, market intelligence, pricing, and commercial planning.

 Build a scalable launch and integration model: Partner with Product, Marketing, and Sales on new product / bundle launches and create repeatable approaches for positioning, packaging, and commercializing acquired products.

 Strengthen expansion motions: Partner with Revenue and Marketing leaders to improve cross-sell, upsell, and account-based growth programs across ClearGov’s customer base.

 Establish a market and customer intelligence discipline: Build competitive intelligence, win-loss analysis, and industry engagement that inform product, sales, and portfolio decisions.

 Own the market narrative and field adoption: Craft bold, outcome-based messaging that clearly differentiates ClearGov from spreadsheets and competing vendors, including sharp depositioning that sales can use in live deals. Ensure sales actually uses what the team builds by measuring content adoption, retiring assets that go unused, and tying messaging to win rates.

 Create clear measures of impact: Define how product marketing performance is evaluated and connect the team’s work to adoption, expansion, win rates, and revenue outcomes.

 Critical Skills/Experience: 

 Significant product marketing leadership experience in B2B SaaS, including recent experience at the Director or Senior Director level, or operating at a comparable scope.

 Experience owning go-to-market or commercialization strategy across a multi-product / platform portfolio, multiple customer segments, or distinct buyer personas.

 Pricing and packaging experience, including bundling, discounting, or launch pricing.

 A track record of translating customer, market, and competitive insight into positioning, portfolio, investment, or growth decisions.

 People leadership experience, including building, developing, and elevating a product marketing team.

 Strong partnership with Product, Sales, and Marketing leaders in a mid-market or enterprise sales environment.

 Executive presence and sound judgment, with the ability to operate autonomously, align senior stakeholders, and communicate strategy clearly to executives and board members.

 Comfort operating in a growing, evolving business where portfolio priorities and organizational needs continue to change.

 Experience with mid-market or lower-enterprise B2B SaaS products in the $30K–$60K ARR range and sales cycles of approximately three to four months.

 Preferred Skills/Experience: 

 Experience with programmatic growth motions such as account-based marketing, cross-sell, or upsell at scale.

 Experience with enterprise SaaS products of $75k-$250M+

 Background in GovTech, FinTech, finance, accounting, compliance, or another technical or regulated vertical.

 Experience supporting growth through M&A, portfolio expansion, or product-line integration.

 Experience building win-loss, competitive intelligence, or industry analyst programs.

 Compensation: 

 In the spirit of transparency, we are excited to share the base salary for this position is $165,000 - $200,000 USD or $155,000 - 190,000 CAD, and exclusive of fringe benefits or potential bonuses. If you are hired at ClearGov, your final base salary compensation will be determined by factors such as skills, interview performance, education and/or experience. In addition to those factors, we believe in the importance of pay equity and consider internal equity of our current team members as a part of any final offer. Please keep in mind that the range mentioned above is the full base salary for the role. Hiring beyond the base range would not be typical in order to allow for future & continued salary growth. We also offer a generous compensation and benefits package (more information on benefits listed below).

 Why Join ClearGov 

 Remote and flexible work environment

 Meaningful work that impacts communities across the United States

 Collaborative, high-performing team

 Competitive compensation and benefits

 Opportunities to grow as we scale 

 Benefits 

 Medical, dental & vision insurance

 FSA, HSA, and/or Dependent Care FSA (US)

 Life + AD&D insurance, plus short-term and long-term disability insurance (US)

 Life + disability insurance (Canada)

 401(k) (US) / RRSP (Canada) with 3.5% match

 10 company holidays

 3 wellness days

 Paid vacation time off

 Sick and safe time off

 Paid parental leave

 Paid bereavement leave

 Paid jury duty + civic service leave

 Employee assistance program

 2 summer days + annual end-of-year "Dimming of the Lights"

 Employee referral bonus program

 How to Apply 
Ready to join us? Apply online today! 

 Equal Opportunity Employer 
ClearGov is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion. We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind based on race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, age, or any other protected characteristic. Hiring decisions are based solely on qualifications, merit, and business needs.

jobs.description:
What we are building
 Mimica is an AI-powered process intelligence platform enabling enterprises and individuals to reclaim their most precious resource: time. We've all seen repetitive tasks and redundant processes quietly drain productivity and creativity. Not because companies don’t want to become more efficient, but because they don’t know where to start.
 Mimica automatically analyzes your team’s work, then generates the AI agents to execute it. Our software turns everyday work into data-backed decisions, helping companies remove process bottlenecks, automate the right tasks, and upskill teams with precision and confidence.
 We’ve raised $26 million in Series B financing and are scaling fast. Backed by investors including Khosla Ventures and Paladin Capital, our proprietary AI technology is trusted by Fortune 500 companies to accelerate transformation. Mimica is recognized as a Top 100 AI Start-up by Accel and an industry Leader by the Everest Group.

 Our team 
 Behind our platform is a team of exceptionally talented people, remote-first and globally distributed across 16+ countries. We're looking for curious, collaborative people excited to solve complex problems. You'll join a fast-paced environment built on high ownership, bottom-up thinking, and transparent, open communication – helping some of the world's leading organizations transform the way work gets done with AI.

 Mission 
 You will be the first Head of Product at Mimica, leading the product function through its next major growth phase.
 This role is about leading a product organisation as it scales with ambition and intention. You will own the macro strategy, our market positioning and product roadmap, raise the bar on product management, and introduce the structures, principles, and ways of working that help teams make better decisions and move faster with confidence.
 You’ll work closely with the CEO, CTO, Product Managers, Designers, and leaders across Engineering, Machine Learning, and Go-to-Market functions to set and align on strategy, prioritise effectively, and ensure we continue building products that deliver clear customer and business value.
 We believe the most important product decisions happen before a line of code is written. We're building the discovery muscle: understanding why customers work the way they do, what they're actually trying to accomplish, and where our technology can create outcomes they couldn't get elsewhere. Your impact as Head of Product will be to drive that shift and embed that understanding at the company level.
 It’s a rare opportunity to take on a foundational product leadership role at a well-funded AI scale-up with deep technical expertise, proprietary AI capabilities, and meaningful growth opportunities.

 Part of your day-to-day 
 Define, own, and champion the global product strategy and macro-level roadmap, including identifying gaps, shaping priorities, and long-term vision in partnership with the C-suite.

 Document and communicate the product vision and strategy to improve clarity and alignment, and turn informal decisions into clear direction.

 Mentor and develop Product Managers and Designers, and define career ladders and growth paths to assure the progression and upskilling of our team.

 Support and unblock your team when needed to maintain a healthy, sustainable, and high-performing team.

 Improve the operating model of the product function: prioritise and plan rituals; bring customer, market, and competitive insights earlier in the decision-making process and inform investment decisions.

 Align stakeholders and build consensus when priorities or opinions conflict.

 Handle executive and customer escalations and protect team focus when leadership or Sales pressure disrupts the roadmap.

 Ensure we retain a culture of strong ownership, transparency, and initiative while assuring business goals are met.

 Forecast future team capacity needs, and partner with the People team to hire top-tier talent to build an effective and well-balanced Product organisation.

 Who are we looking for 
 A product leader who has operated as Head of Product, Director of Product, or VP of Product in a comparable Scale-up environment.

 Experience building and managing one of the following technical Enterprise products or categories: data-heavy, process optimisation, AI, or automation products.

 A strong people leader with a track record of coaching and mentoring both Product Managers and Product Designers.

 Strong stakeholder management skills, particularly driving alignment between senior leaders in Engineering and Commercial functions.

 Experience in building products powered by in-house developed ML/AI technology.

 Excellent judgment on prioritization and roadmap decisions, especially when hard trade-offs are required.

 Strong product and commercial instinct, and a clear commitment to customer value.

 Confidence handling disagreement, aligning diverse stakeholders, and navigating ambiguity with maturity.

 Experience working successfully in an international and multicultural team

 Excellent written and spoken English, with the ability to communicate technical ideas clearly to different audiences. 

 Nice to have 
 A solid technical foundation or direct hands-on experience building or maintaining technical systems (eg, as a Software Engineer)

 Experience working in organisations where the product and designers were embedded into cross-functional Engineering teams.

 Experience working and leading fully remote distributed teams.

 Location 
 This is a fully remote position. We welcome candidates based across North America and Western Europe, with a preference for time zones that allow strong overlap with our teams in both regions.

 What we offer
 💰 Generous compensation + stock options - aligned with our internal framework, market data, and individual skills.
 🏢 Distributed work: Work from anywhere - fully remote, in our hubs, or a mix.
 💻 Company-issued laptop, remote setup stipend, and co-working budget
 📍 Flexible schedules and location
 ☀️ Ample paid time off, in addition to local public holidays
 🍼 Enhanced parental leave
 🧘‍♀️ Health & retirement benefits
 📖 Annual learning & development budget
 🌴 Annual workaways and regular virtual & in-person socials
 🌍 Opportunity to contribute to groundbreaking projects that shape the future of work

 Note: Some benefits may vary depending on location and role 

 ⚠️ Mimica will only contact candidates from an @mimica.ai email address. We do not request banking or sensitive personal information during the recruiting process.

jobs.description:
From our first lot in Cambridge, Ontario, to residential, commercial, and recreational developments in 18 cities across North America, Great Gulf Group has grown into a diversified real estate organization with over 45 years of experience.

While our portfolio has evolved, our commitment remains the same: building great spaces that inspire the people who live, work, and play in them. Today, our multi-faceted business spans commercial, mixed-use and residential development, construction management, software, engineering, panelized manufacturing, architecture, and hospitality.

All companies under the Great Gulf Group umbrella are united by one simple goal: the pursuit of greatness. It’s achieved every day through the passion and dedication of our people. If you’re excited to build meaningful solutions and make an impact, we’d love to hear from you!

Great Gulf Group is looking for a Vice President, Digital Platforms
to join our team in Toronto, ON
.

This is a newly created role on the business side of our marketing team, reporting to the Chief Marketing Officer. You’ll own the vision, strategy and roadmap for Great Gulf’s websites, customer portals and apps, working in close partnership with our internal IT team and leading new website builds and major re-platforms. You’ll also champion the next generation of digital tools, including applied AI and answer engine visibility.

Key Responsibilities

Vision, Roadmap & New Builds: Own the vision and roadmap for the Great Gulf Group, Great Gulf Homes and Great Gulf Resort websites, and lead new website builds and major re-platforms from strategy through launch, partnering with internal IT and external partners as needed
Customer Portals & Apps: Own the vision and roadmap for customer-facing portals and apps (e.g., homeowner and buyer portals), ensuring they integrate seamlessly with the broader website ecosystem
Cross-Functional Alignment & IT Partnership: Act as the primary business-side owner and voice for digital platforms, translating the digital objectives of Homes, Resorts, brand and IT into a single, prioritized roadmap and defining requirements in close, sustained partnership with the internal IT website development team
User Experience & Innovation: Partner with brand design and IT to optimize the user experience from discovery to sale, and identify, evaluate and champion emerging tools (dynamic site maps and floor plans, digital home renderings, virtual tours, applied AI)
Digital Foundations: Own the digital asset management (DAM) system and standards, oversee the Great Gulf domain portfolio, and own the strategy and performance of the home inventory/listing portal(s), including third-party listing integrations
Performance & Insights: Responsible for performance metrics across all digital platforms (site health, engagement, conversion, and search/answer-engine visibility), establishing clear KPIs and translating findings for the CMO and executive stakeholders
Accessibility & Data Privacy: Partner with legal, IT security and compliance to ensure websites, portals and apps meet accessibility (e.g., WCAG/AODA) and data privacy standards across all markets

Education, Experience, And Qualifications

10+ years of experience in digital platforms, website strategy or digital product leadership, ideally across multi-brand or multi-site organizations
Proven, hands-on experience leading a new website build from strategy through launch
Experience owning or closely partnering with IT/development teams to deliver web and app platforms; comfortable operating without a direct development team reporting into the role
Working knowledge of SEO and emerging AEO/GEO (generative engine optimization) practices
Experience with customer portals or apps in a consumer-facing industry; homebuilding, real estate, hospitality, or resort/travel experience is a strong asset
Familiarity with digital asset management, domain management and inventory/listing systems
A thought leader with a customer-centric approach to digital experience design and a clear point of view on applied AI (AI-assisted search, personalization, dynamic floor plans, digital home renderings)
Ability to translate business priorities into a clear, prioritized platform roadmap for a technical partner team, and to align senior stakeholders across marketing, IT and divisional business units around it
Advanced degree in business, digital strategy or a related field preferred

Work Arrangement

Hybrid role with an expectation of 4 days per week in the office

Compensation

$180,000 - $225,000; plus a short-term incentive bonus

Vacancy Status

New Vacancy

Why Join Great Gulf?

Opportunity to work for a leading real estate development company
Shape the digital experience across the Great Gulf Group, Great Gulf Homes, Great Gulf Resorts and First Gulf brands
Champion the next generation of digital tools, including applied AI and answer engine visibility
Dynamic and collaborative work environment
Commitment to sustainability and social responsibility

Interested?

We encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every qualification. If you’re the right candidate, we’ll support your growth and help you learn along the way.

Apply today and help us build what’s next.

Great Gulf Group of Companies is committed to providing a fair and equitable work environment and encourages applications from qualified women, men, visible minorities, Indigenous Peoples, and persons with disabilities. jobs.description:
President and Chief Executive Officer

NAIT

Edmonton, AB

About NAIT

For more than six decades, the Northern Alberta Institute of Technology (NAIT) has helped build Alberta. We prepare people for meaningful careers, work alongside industry to solve real-world challenges and provide the skilled talent and innovation that help our province grow.

As one of Canada’s largest apprenticeship trainers and a leading polytechnic serving more than 34,000 students and employing approximately 3,000 staff and managing an annual operating budget of $429M, NAIT has the scale, expertise and deep connection to industry to make a meaningful difference. Our proudly polytechnic approach brings education and industry together, combining knowledge with hands-on learning and preparing graduates to contribute from the moment they enter the workforce.

Position Overview

Reporting to the Board of Governors, the President and Chief Executive Officer (President) will provide strategic direction and executive leadership at a defining point in NAIT’s history. The President will build on NAIT’s strong reputation, industry relationships, committed people and unprecedented opportunity through the Advanced Skills Centre, while strengthening organizational trust, focus, financial sustainability and execution across the institution.

The next President will balance strong external advocacy with visible internal leadership. The successful candidate will engage employees and students in shaping NAIT’s future, bring clarity and discipline to institutional priorities, protect educational quality and student success, and advance major capital, philanthropic, digital and organizational initiatives.

Qualifications and Experience

The successful candidate will champion hands-on, industry-focused education, lead institutional growth and transformation, strengthen partnerships with government, industry, Indigenous communities, donors, and alumni, and ensure NAIT remains financially sustainable and positioned to meet Alberta’s evolving workforce needs. This leader will inspire a welcoming community for students, faculty, and staff while guiding major strategic initiatives, including the advancement of NAIT’s future campus and academic priorities.

The President will be a respected and engaging executive with a proven track record of organizational leadership, stakeholder engagement, strategic planning, and fostering high-performing, people-centered cultures. Experience leading complex organizations, building external partnerships, and driving meaningful change will be essential.

Additionally, the ideal candidate will bring senior executive leadership experience in post-secondary education, business, or the public sector, with a proven ability to translate strategic vision into organizational excellence, financial sustainability, and meaningful impact. They will have a strong track record of building trust, leading change, fostering constructive labour relations, supporting effective governance, and securing partnerships and funding that advance institutional priorities. A champion for student and employee success, the successful candidate will demonstrate integrity, belonging, and accountability while advocating for polytechnic education, skilled trades, and lifelong learning. They will embrace digital transformation, responsible AI, and emerging opportunities, leading with curiosity, resilience, and a commitment to creating a safe, welcoming environment where learners, employees, industry, Indigenous communities, and partners can thrive.

How to Apply

NAIT has engaged the Executive Search Firm, DHR Global, to manage this search. For more information or to apply, please send in your application to PresidentNAIT@dhrglobal.com by January 15, 2027. Applications should include a letter addressing how the candidate’s experience matches the position requirements along with a current CV.

jobs.title: Director of Network Planning, Pricing, & Revenue Management
jobs.description:
Air North, Yukon's Airline 

Founded in 1977, Air North, Yukon’s Airline, today serves destinations within the territory and connects the Yukon with southern destinations that include Calgary, Edmonton, Ottawa, Toronto, Kelowna, Vancouver, and Victoria. As we enter into our 50 th year of serving Yukoners, this has been made possible by their steadfast support, as well as investment from the Vuntut Gwitchin First Nation. All of this is reflected deeply in our business ethos, culture, and the quality of service our 500-strong team provides every day.

Our exceptional track record includes accolades such as being named one of the world’s most beloved airlines on social media by Fortune magazine, receiving recognition twice as the Best Leisure and Specialty Airline, and most recently being honored as the Best Airline in Canada by TripAdvisor's Travelers' Choice Awards. These achievements are thanks to the dedication of our remarkable team.

Our competitive salaries are joined by an enticing benefits package. This includes extensive travel perks for you and your family, encompassing over 90 airlines globally, health and dental benefits, group RRSP investment options, and profit sharing.

We are currently seeking a Director of Network Planning, Pricing & Revenue Management to shape where and when we fly, how we price it, and how we grow revenue across our network, supporting our ongoing success and the communities we serve.

The Role

The Director of Network Planning, Pricing & Revenue Management reports to the Chief Commercial Officer and is responsible for functions central to the airline’s profitability: network and schedule planning, pricing, yield management, and revenue analysis and forecasting. They direct pricing and revenue optimization initiatives, ensuring commercial decisions contribute to long-term business value, and turn strategic direction into seasonal schedules that are commercially sound and operationally achievable.

What you'll do

Network Planning & Strategy

Develop and implement short- and long-term network strategies aligned with the Company’s commercial objectives and operational capabilities
Lead network capacity planning, including aircraft utilization, route frequency, seasonal scheduling and market demand
Identify and evaluate new route and market opportunities, and assess existing routes for optimization, expansion, restructuring or discontinuation
Monitor competitors’ fleet plans, capacity, networks and schedules, and develop strategic and tactical responses to market opportunities and threats

Pricing & Revenue Management

Oversee pricing strategy and revenue management practices, including pricing structures, fare availability and inventory controls, to maximize passenger revenue and network profitability
Lead financial and commercial analysis of cost structures, price elasticity and competitive pricing to inform pricing, capacity and network decisions
Establish tools, controls and performance measures to optimize fares, inventory and revenue management outcomes
Partner across the broader commercial team, including Sales and Marketing, to develop market-specific strategies, tactical offers and revenue targets

Forecasting, Performance & Collaboration

Develop and monitor revenue forecasts, demand trends and booking patterns
Establish and track KPIs, including revenue performance, yield, load factor and route profitability, and report findings and recommendations to senior leadership
Work with commercial and operational stakeholders so that network plans are understood, achievable and implemented

Qualifications

Minimum 5 years of progressive experience in network planning, scheduling, pricing or revenue management, with demonstrated leadership experience
Experience in airline commercial strategy, with a strong understanding of airline economics and industry dynamics, including market dynamics, competitive landscape and customer behaviour
Degree in Airline Management, Business, Mathematics, Statistics or Economics would be an asset
Proven ability to turn complex commercial data into actionable insights and translate strategy into commercially sound, operationally achievable schedules
A high degree of creativity, innovation and resourcefulness in airline planning and scheduling
Strong communication and influencing skills, with the ability to build alignment across commercial, operational and senior leadership teams
Advanced proficiency in Excel, with experience using business intelligence, data visualization, and airline commercial planning tools to support network planning, pricing, forecasting and revenue management
Must be a Canadian citizen, Permanent Resident or show proof of right to work in Canada

An ideal candidate would be willing to reside in Whitehorse, Yukon, though the position is also available remotely in Vancouver, Victoria, Kelowna, Calgary or Edmonton.

jobs.title: Director, Private Capital Investments
jobs.description:
Who we are

Kilmer Group is a multi-generational platform for business development and investment, built on operational excellence, long-term stewardship, and trusted relationships. Headquartered in Toronto, we invest across three core sectors: Private Capital, Infrastructure & Real Estate, and Sports & Media, partnering with exceptional management teams to build and grow enduring businesses.

Kilmer Group has built a reputation for disciplined investment, active ownership, and creating long-term value. Our approach is grounded in partnership, integrity, and a commitment to building businesses that generate lasting impact for our partners, stakeholders, and the communities we serve.

Who we need

Reporting to the President, Kilmer Capital Partners, we are hiring a Director, Private Capital Investments. In this role, you will lead investments across the full lifecycle, from evaluating opportunities and overseeing due diligence through transaction execution, integration, and ongoing portfolio management. You will combine rigorous financial and investment analysis with practical business judgment to assess opportunities, identify risks and value creation levers, and translate insights into clear recommendations and action. Working closely with portfolio company leaders, Kilmer senior leadership, external advisors, and a team of two Managers, you will help strengthen businesses over the long term while contributing to a collaborative, transparent, and forward-looking culture within the Private Capital Investments team.

This is an existing, full-time opportunity based in the Toronto office, with periodic travel to support portfolio companies and integration activities.

What’s in it for you?

Impact and investment opportunity. You will play a meaningful role in evaluating new opportunities, shaping investment decisions, and working beyond the transaction to help portfolio companies grow and create long-term value.

Breadth and visibility. You will gain exposure to investments across a diverse range of industries rather than specializing in a single sector. Working within a small, experienced team, you will have direct access to senior leadership across Kilmer and work closely with CEOs and executive teams within portfolio companies, giving you the opportunity to see the impact of your thinking and decisions firsthand.

A broader private capital experience. You will have the opportunity to move beyond a high-volume, transaction-focused investment environment and become more deeply involved in the businesses you invest in. From diligence and integration through strategic planning, operational improvement, and ongoing value creation, you will build a broader perspective on what it takes to strengthen and grow businesses over the long term.

Leadership and influence. This role comes with real scope: leading deals, coaching and developing a team, and shaping how Private Capital Investments works together as we grow. You'll bring your own perspective and judgment to the table, build strong relationships across Kilmer and its portfolio companies, and play a meaningful role in shaping the investment function

As our new Director, Private Capital Investments, you will:

Evaluate investment opportunities.
You will lead the assessment of potential investments, combining rigorous financial analysis with commercial and operational judgment to understand the business, market dynamics, management team, risks, and long-term value creation potential. You will develop investment theses and translate your findings into clear recommendations for senior leadership and the Investment Committee.
Lead due diligence and transaction execution.
You will oversee end-to-end diligence across financial, operational, commercial, tax, legal, and strategic workstreams, coordinating internal stakeholders and external advisors. You will identify risks and opportunities, challenge assumptions, and use your findings to inform transaction structuring, negotiations, and investment decisions.
Drive integration and value creation.
You will stay actively involved after an investment closes, partnering with portfolio company leaders to support integration and identify opportunities to strengthen the business. You will bring a long-term ownership perspective to strategic planning, operational improvements, capital allocation, acquisitions, organizational development, and other initiatives that can increase enterprise value.
Monitor and strengthen portfolio performance.
You will develop a deep understanding of portfolio company performance, using financial results, operational metrics, KPIs, and market insights to identify trends, risks, and opportunities. You will oversee portfolio reporting and bring forward practical, data-informed recommendations that support better decisions and sustainable growth.
Build trusted partnerships.
You will work closely with CEOs, executive teams, Kilmer leadership, boards, lenders, and external advisors, bringing curiosity, sound judgment, and a collaborative approach to complex business challenges. You will act as a strategic partner who can ask the right questions, constructively challenge thinking, and help turn insights into action.
Lead and develop the team.
You will coach and develop two Managers, providing guidance across investment analysis, diligence, execution, and portfolio work while creating opportunities for them to expand their capabilities and ownership. You will help foster a collaborative, transparent team environment.

You bring:

The investment experience.
You have built your experience in private equity, private capital, transaction advisory, valuations, investment banking, corporate development, or another environment where you have evaluated businesses and supported complex investment decisions. You have led or played a significant role in due diligence and transaction execution, with the ability to move between detailed analysis and the broader investment thesis.
The financial and analytical expertise.
You have strong financial modelling, valuation, and investment analysis skills and can confidently assess historical and projected performance, cash flow, working capital, capital structures, and key value drivers. You know how to absorb large amounts of information, identify meaningful trends and risks, challenge assumptions, and turn your analysis into clear recommendations.
The commercial mindset.
You look beyond the numbers to understand how a business operates, competes, and creates value. You bring sound business judgment and intellectual curiosity to assessing markets, management teams, operational opportunities, and potential risks, and you can identify practical opportunities to strengthen performance and create long-term enterprise value.
The leadership skills.
You have experience guiding and developing others while remaining willing to work alongside your team in the details when needed. You set clear expectations, provide thoughtful coaching, and create an environment where people can ask questions, challenge ideas, and continue building their capabilities.
The relationship-building skills.
You can build credibility and trusted relationships with senior leaders, management teams, advisors, and colleagues across different functions. You communicate complex financial and business information clearly, ask thoughtful questions, and can constructively challenge perspectives while remaining collaborative and focused on the best outcome.
The ownership mindset.
You bring high standards for accuracy, integrity, discretion, and follow-through. You are comfortable navigating ambiguity and complex decisions, balancing independent thinking with collaboration, and taking accountability for your work from initial analysis through execution and ongoing portfolio stewardship.
The flexibility.
You are able to travel periodically to work directly with portfolio companies and support integration and value creation initiatives. A CFA, CBV, MBA, or similar designation would be an asset but is not required.

Why join Kilmer Group?

Today, Kilmer Group continues to build on decades of successful investment and business leadership offering a dynamic and supportive environment with opportunities for growth and development. Beyond our investments, we are committed to strengthening the communities where we live and work through initiatives that support sport, health, research, and community development. Joining Kilmer Group means becoming part of an organization that thinks for the long term, values partnership, and is committed to building a lasting legacy.

Join us

We recognize that no candidate brings every qualification to a role. If your experience is closely aligned with what we are looking for and you are excited by the opportunity to contribute to Kilmer Group, we encourage you to apply. We look forward to learning more about your experience and the perspective you would bring to our team.

What you can expect from our interview process

A virtual interview with a Talent Advisor to discuss your interest in joining the company and in the role. The conversation will be recorded using BrightHire, an AI-powered video interview tool. More details will be shared when you are invited to interview.
An in-person interview with the Chief Financial Officer and the Vice President, Talent and Special Projects focused on your experience, collaborative approach, and alignment with the organization and its culture.
An in-person interview with a panel of senior leaders, including the President of Kilmer Capital Partners. This interview will focus on your investment experience, technical capabilities, approach to diligence and value creation, and alignment with the direction of the Private Capital Investments team. You will also create and present a Case Study to be shared with the team.

Kilmer Group is committed to creating a workplace where people are treated with respect, supported in their development, and empowered to contribute their best work. We recognize that diverse perspectives strengthen our business and help us make better decisions for our organization, our partners, and the communities in which we operate.

We welcome applications from all qualified candidates and are committed to providing an accessible recruitment process. If you require accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.

About Us

The Western Advancement division plays a leading role in strengthening awareness of and support for the University’s mission and goals by leading alumni relations and fundraising efforts across campus and beyond. All departments within the Division build enduring alumni and public trust through understanding and support for Western University in a coordinated campus-wide effort that results in the engagement and funding needed to make an impact. There are 3 departments within the Division – Departments of Development, Alumni Relations and Advancement Operations.

The Advancement Operations department is a partner in the areas of constituent database and technology services, prospect management, research and pipeline, data analytics and storytelling, gift and pledge management, records and document management, and financial reconciliation and reporting. In addition, we provide support to the annual planning process as well as budget management, talent management and facilities support for Western Advancement.
