jobs.title: Directeur Pharmacométricien (Director Pharmacometrician)
jobs.description:
Rejoignez un poste où la science rencontre la stratégie et où votre expertise façonne l'avenir du développement de médicaments. En tant que Directeur pharmacométricien
, vous dirigerez des projets de modélisation et de simulation à fort impact au sein d'un environnement dynamique de pharmacologie clinique, de modélisation et de simulation (CPMS). Vous dirigerez des équipes, encadrerez des pharmacométriciens et fournirez des conseils stratégiques aux clients lors des étapes clés du développement. Ce poste vous offre également l'opportunité de représenter les clients dans leurs interactions avec les organismes de réglementation. Si vous aimez travailler en collaboration et relever des défis scientifiques complexes, voici votre chance d'avoir un impact significatif.
Step into a role where science meets strategy and your expertise shapes the future of drug development. As a Director Pharmacometrician
, you'll lead high-impact modeling and simulation efforts within a dynamic Clinical Pharmacology, Modeling and Simulation (CPMS) environment. You'll guide teams, mentor pharmacometricians, and provide strategic insight to clients at key development milestones. This role also offers the opportunity to represent clients in interactions with regulatory agencies. If you thrive on collaboration and solving complex scientific challenges, this is your chance to make a meaningful impact.
À propos du poste
Ce poste allie leadership scientifique et impact stratégique : vous dirigerez des analyses pharmacocinétiques de population tout en développant des approches innovantes pour à améliorer l'efficacité et la précision. Vous serez chargé de concevoir, d'analyser et d'interpréter des études de pharmacologie clinique, de fournir des conseils stratégiques aux clients et de contribuer à la rédaction de documents réglementaires ainsi qu'aux interactions avec les organismes de réglementation. De plus, vous entretiendrez les relations avec les clients, soutiendrez le développement des affaires et resterez à la pointe des avancées en pharmacocinétique et pharmacodynamique afin de favoriser l'amélioration continue.
Vos principales responsabilités comprendront, sans s'y limiter :

Diriger et réaliser des analyses pharmacocinétiques de population à l'aide d'outils et de méthodologies de modélisation avancés
Élaborer et mettre en œuvre des approches innovantes pour améliorer l'efficacité et la précision des analyses pharmacocinétiques
Concevoir, analyser et interpréter des études de pharmacologie clinique (rénale, hépatique, TQT, ADME, DDI, BE/BA, SAD, MAD, etc.) et fournir des conseils pour optimiser les stratégies d'échantillonnage pharmacocinétique et de posologie
Fournir des conseils stratégiques aux clients, en assumant la responsabilité des livrables et en élaborant des plans de pharmacologie clinique
Rédiger et réviser les rapports pharmacocinétiques ainsi que les sections de pharmacologie clinique des documents réglementaires
Représenter les clients dans les interactions avec les autorités réglementaires et contribuer au développement des affaires et à la gestion des relations

About the role
This role combines scientific leadership and strategic impact, leading population PK analyses while developing innovative approaches to improve efficiency and accuracy. You will design, analyze, and interpret clinical pharmacology studies, provide strategic guidance to clients, and contribute to regulatory documents and agency interactions. In addition, you'll foster client relationships, support business development, and stay at the forefront of PK/PD advancements to drive continuous improvement.
Your main responsibilities will include but not limited to:

Lead and conduct population PK analyses using advanced modeling tools and methodologies
Develop and implement innovative approaches to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of PK analysis
Design, analyze, and interpret clinical pharmacology studies (renal, hepatic, TQT, ADME, DDI, BE/BA, SAD, MAD, etc.) and provide guidance to optimize pharmacokinetic sampling and dosing strategies  
Provide strategic guidance to clients, owning deliverables and developing clinical pharmacology plans
Author and review PK reports and clinical pharmacology sections of regulatory documents
Represent clients in regulatory interactions and contribute to business development and relationship management

Requirements

À propos de vous
Si vous êtes un professionnel de la pharmacologie clinique motivé, fort de 10 ans d'expérience dans le développement de médicaments et la pharmacométrie, et que vous possédez un esprit analytique aigu ainsi qu'une expertise dans l'utilisation d'outils tels que NONMEM, Pirana et R pour fournir des analyses percutantes, tout en étant orienté vers le client et en étant un leader naturel qui s'épanouit dans des environnements dynamiques, alliant réflexion stratégique, excellentes compétences en communication et sens des affaires pour établir des relations et obtenir des résultats, ce poste est fait pour vous.
  Pour réussir, nous recherchons les qualités et comportements suivants :

Diplôme en sciences de la vie, en soins de santé et/ou en administration des affaires
Au moins 10 ans d'expérience professionnelle pertinente, notamment dans le développement de médicaments, la pharmacologie clinique et la pharmacométrie
Une expérience en matière de réglementation, y compris la rédaction de rapports réglementaires, est indispensable. Expérience des soumissions réglementaires, y compris les demandes d'autorisation de mise en examen (IND), les demandes d'autorisation de clinique (CTA), les réunions réglementaires et les soumissions de demandes d'autorisation de mise en marché (NDA/BLA/MAA)
Maîtrise des logiciels NONMEM, Pirana et R souhaitée 
Excellentes compétences en organisation, en négociation et en gestion financière

About You
If you are a driven clinical pharmacology professional with 10 years of experience in drug development and pharmacometrics and you bring sharp analytical thinking and expertise in tools like NONMEM, Pirana, and R to deliver high-impact insights while being client-focused and a natural leader who thrives in fast-paced environments, combining strategic thinking, strong communication, and business acumen to build relationships and drive results, this role is for you.
To be successful we are looking for the following traits and behaviors:

Life science, healthcare and/or business degree 

Minimum 10 years of relevant work experience, including experience in drug development, clinical pharmacology, and pharmacometrics 
Regulatory experience including regulatory report writing essential. Experience with regulatory submissions including INDs, CTAs, regulatory meetings and NDA/BLA/MAA submissions
Proficiency in NONMEM, Pirana, and R software preferred 
Excellent organizational, negotiating and financial skills 

Benefits

À propos d'Allucent

Notre mission est de contribuer à la mise au point de nouveaux traitements. Travailler chez Allucent, c'est retrousser ses manches et mettre à profit ses compétences, son expertise et ses connaissances uniques pour établir des partenariats avec nos clients dans leur quête de nouveaux traitements destinés à améliorer la vie des patients.
Si vous êtes passionné(e) par l'aide apportée aux clients pour le développement de nouveaux produits pharmaceutiques et biologiques, si vous avez l'esprit d'entreprise et si vous êtes prêt(e) à rejoindre d'autres leaders dans les domaines de la science, des affaires et des opérations, nous serions ravis d'en savoir plus sur la manière dont nous pouvons nous aider mutuellement à grandir.
Ensemble, nous BRILLONS. Découvrez-en plus sur nos valeurs.
Les avantages de travailler chez Allucent comprennent :

Un budget départemental dédié à la formation et à l'étude pour favoriser le développement professionnel

La possibilité de travailler télétravail/en mode hybride* selon le site
Possibilités de leadership et de mentorat
Participation à notre programme de parrainage en tant que nouvel employé ou employé existant

Programme de recommandation interne des employés financièrement avantageux

Our mission is to help bring new therapies to light. When you work at Allucent, that means rolling up your sleeves and applying your unique skill set, expertise, and knowledge to build partnerships with our clients in their pursuit to develop new, life-improving treatments.
If you're passionate about helping customers develop new pharmaceuticals and biologics; have an entrepreneurial spirit; and ready to join other science, business, and operations leaders, we would love to get to learn more about how we can help each other grow.

Vice-President, Data Centre Operations and Development

Toronto, Ontario, Canada
Full-time

Role Overview

Our client is a fast-scaling, private-equity-backed digital infrastructure business that owns and operates data centres in markets across Canada. The Vice-President, Data Centre Operations and Development will take ownership of portfolio-wide performance, uptime, customer satisfaction, growth readiness, capital allocation, and operational discipline as the organization expands its colocation, connectivity, AI, and high-density computing offerings.
This role offers a rare chance to step into a company entering a pivotal growth phase and to help steer the scale-up of one of Canada's premier digital infrastructure platforms. The right candidate will weigh operating results, commitments to customers, margin, disciplined use of capital, and where the business is headed longer term — all within a demanding, outcomes-focused setting.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

Set and drive the operating strategy across the portfolio's data centres, spanning both high-density (HD) and low-density (LD) colocation footprints.
Guide efforts to upgrade and grow product and site capabilities, working alongside engineering and design partners to unlock more sellable capacity and turn priorities into a workable, multi-site capital deployment roadmap.
Put together and roll out a first-100-days action plan covering operational readiness, the customer experience, expansion moves, tighter operational controls, and the earliest capital-spend priorities.
Stand up and manage against a solid framework of KPIs and performance metrics.
Maintain a thorough grasp of economics at both the portfolio and individual-site level — costs, margins, capital outlay, and how these track against the underlying business cases and return targets.
Plan and carry out customer relocation efforts where needed to free up larger blocks of contiguous, sellable colocation space.
Bring people together around a shared plan through clear messaging, cross-team collaboration, and fluency in the relevant industry language.

Design and Construction

Own design and construction readiness for expansion and retrofit projects — covering utility power capacity, electrical, mechanical, and architectural inputs, coordination with outside professional partners, equipment sourcing and procurement, scheduling, budgeting, permitting, and independent commissioning.

Operational Excellence

Oversee day-to-day facility operations — uptime, service-level commitments, capacity usage, change management, provisioning, upkeep of maintenance governance, commissioning readiness, handover processes, vendor relationships, and the resilience of critical infrastructure.
Balance the inventory of space, power, and cooling capacity against customer obligations, site-level economics, and room for future growth.
Keep every site aligned with applicable health and safety, security, and regulatory requirements.
Keep documentation, operating data, and reporting accurate and centralized for stakeholders — including as-builts, single-line diagrams, occupancy figures, reserved capacity, consumption data, BMS, EPMS, DCIM, maintenance logs, and trends in sellable capacity.
Uphold consistent security, compliance, and site-control protocols across access management, visitor and contractor handling, escort procedures, shipping and receiving, surveillance, zoning, monitoring, and audit and evidence readiness.
Build, maintain, and regularly test procedures for emergencies, incident response, and business continuity, including how escalations are handled, post-incident reviews, and tracking corrective actions.
Champion and track energy-efficiency programs, from reviewing power and energy usage to mechanical efficiency initiatives, free cooling, containment strategies, and other measures that lower PUE.
Provide day-to-day oversight of telecom infrastructure services, such as Meet-Me Rooms, cross-connects, points of entry, and conduit routing.

Customer Experience & Commercial Enablement

Maintain close familiarity with customer contracts, obligations, and service commitments, confirming they stay consistent with what each site can actually deliver operationally.
Oversee the processes for customer installs, service changes, and de-provisioning so they run reliably and within SLA.
Help win larger deals by turning constraints around space, power, cooling, network, and capital deployment into clear, practical input on what can be delivered, at what cost, and on what timeline for customer commitments.

Team & Organizational Development

Assemble and lead a high-performing, efficient operations organization running 24x7x365, with well-defined roles, accountabilities, and performance measures.
Spot gaps in the leadership bench and bring in the talent needed to meet strategic priorities.
Cultivate a culture built on accountability, openness, and ongoing improvement.
Establish a thorough set of standards the wider team can rally around.

Qualifications & Experience

15+ years of experience required working in data centre operations, critical facilities, construction, or infrastructure leadership, with a track record spanning multi-site 24x7x365 operations and sizeable technical teams.
A precise, methodical, and detail-oriented approach to planning, presenting, and reporting.
Direct experience with private-equity-owned companies is considered an asset.
Strong working knowledge of colocation and high-density computing environments.
Solid financial acumen, with hands-on experience in budgeting, forecasting, cost management, and planning capital deployment across multiple sites.
A history of establishing and enforcing operating standards — SOPs, MOPs, EOPs, change control, incident discipline, and maintenance governance.
Excellent communication and stakeholder-management ability, including fluency with the terminology and concepts used in this market.
Familiarity with current data centre design approaches, including high-density and direct-liquid-cooling (DLC) solutions, and what they mean for commissioning, maintenance, staffing, and day-to-day procedures.
Background with large-scale customer and data centre leasing arrangements, including power pass-through and metering structures.
Familiarity with GPU and other high-density compute systems is a plus.
Solid grounding in network infrastructure — fibre, copper, conduit, and the physical connectivity requirements that go with them.

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
Job Summary

Reporting to the Associate Vice-Principal, Finance and Administration, the Executive Director, Integrated Finance Services is accountable, within delegated authority, for the performance and coherence of the function as a whole. The Executive Director leads the development and implementation of the function’s strategy and operating model, aligned with AVP direction and approved enterprise-wide Finance strategy, and is accountable for cross-portfolio capacity and risk management, consistent service standards and controls, and the performance and development of Integrated Finance Services Directors.

The Executive Director ensures Directors have the approved frameworks, delegated authority, capability and support required to lead their portfolios or managed groups effectively and exercise their authority without unnecessary approval layers. Faculty, shared services and portfolio leaders remain accountable for academic and operational priorities, business and staffing decisions, budget approval, corrective business action and resource allocation within their delegated authorities. Integrated Finance Services supports these decisions through analysis, advice, controls and implementation of approved decisions.

The Executive Director becomes directly involved when matters exceed an individual Director’s delegated authority, require decisions across Director-led groups, remain unresolved following Director-level action, or have institutional financial, control, service or strategic implications. The Executive Director resolves matters within delegated authority and escalates institutional determinations to the AVP.

As a senior member of the Finance leadership team, the Executive Director advises the AVP on service performance, capacity, capability, risk and improvement priorities, coordinates implementation of approved Finance initiatives and represents Integrated Finance Services in designated institutional, regulatory and external forums.

The AVP, Finance and Administration retains institutional professional and people accountability for Integrated Finance Services, including enterprise-wide strategy, service standards, workforce performance and institutional service expectations. The Executive Director exercises delegated leadership and management authority within this framework.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

Finance Services Leadership and Operating Model

Leads the development, implementation and continuous improvement of the Integrated Finance Services strategy and operating model, aligned with AVP direction and approved enterprise-wide Finance strategy.
Directs and oversees Integrated Finance Services activities and ensures alignment with University financial policies and AVP direction.
Develops and recommends Integrated Finance Services standards, operating practices, performance measures and escalation protocols for AVP approval, and implements them across Director-led areas.

Resolves cross-portfolio and cross-Director service, capacity, priority and accountability conflicts and makes function-wide Finance capacity and service trade-off decisions within approved budgets, workforce plans, service expectations and delegated authority.
Determines when direct Executive Director involvement is warranted based on institutional materiality, strategic significance, cross-portfolio impact, unresolved Director-level matters or escalation requirements.

Service Performance and Standards

Maintains visibility of Finance performance across Director led groups and brings material service failures, systemic issues, structural capacity shortfalls and emerging risks to the AVP with recommended action.
Maintains relationships with designated institutional leaders to understand service expectations and identify systemic concerns, while preserving Director and Senior Manager ownership of principal portfolio Finance relationships.
Conducts periodic service reviews, using service data, client feedback, audit findings and Director-provided intelligence to identify trends, gaps and opportunities for improvement.
Develops, maintains and continuously improves the approved Integrated Finance Services performance framework and recommends changes to the AVP where needed.
Holds Directors accountable for applying approved service standards and for taking timely corrective action.
Maintains an integrated view of financial, control and service risks across Director led groups, identifies systemic issues and institutional implications, and coordinates appropriate Finance responses. Escalates institutional-level financial matters to the AVP with analysis and recommended action.
Provides timely advice to the AVP on institutional level financial pressures, structural risks and recommended responses. Supports accountable client leaders through analysis, advice and implementation support where corrective business action is required.

Capacity and Resource Management

Coordinates deployment of Finance capacity across Director-led groups and makes cross-portfolio deployment decisions within approved workforce plans, budgets and delegated authority.
Balances available capacity across all Director-led groups and makes transparent service and workload trade-offs within delegated authority.
Identifies structural capacity pressures, coordinates available responses and recommends longer-term resource or organizational changes to the AVP.
Maintains oversight of Finance workforce structure, succession risk and organizational effectiveness and advises the AVP on significant workforce or organizational design matters.

People Leadership and Finance Capability

Provides leadership, direction and coaching to Directors and establishes clear performance and accountability expectations across the Finance leadership group.
Conducts performance reviews for Directors and obtains relevant client input on integrated service delivery and relationship effectiveness.
Makes decisions and recommendations concerning the Integrated Finance Services workforce, including recruitment, workforce planning, performance, development, discipline and organization design within delegated authority.
Builds leadership capability and resilience through coaching, professional development, succession planning, and cross-portfolio knowledge sharing.
Sets Finance capability expectations and sponsors coordinated development initiatives across the function.
Fosters, promotes and drives equity and inclusion.

Transformation and Institutional Contribution

Leads implementation of approved Finance Services transformation, process standardization, automation and service-improvement priorities across Director-led areas.
Contributes to Finance governance and policy development and leads implementation of approved standards and policies across Finance Services.
Leads or sponsors implementation of significant Finance systems, operating-model changes and transformation programs and monitors adoption, performance and realization of intended benefits.
Represents approved Finance Services priorities, capabilities and accountabilities in institutional forums and external networks.
Identifies opportunities to improve the value, consistency and effectiveness of Finance Services and recommends material changes to the AVP.
Other duties as required in support of the department and/or unit.

University degree in Commerce, Business Administration, Accounting, Finance or a related field.
Chartered Professional Accountant designation or equivalent recognized professional accounting designation.

Consideration will be given to an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Talan is an international group that supports its clients in their end-to-end Data & AI transformation by combining management consulting with technological expertise.

In Americas, our multidisciplinary teams bring over 30 years of experience helping business leaders across key industries achieve measurable performance and strong ROI, designing, building, and scaling solutions that enable companies to grow more efficiently.

Job Description

Reporting to the Senior Director, SAP Presales and Alliance, the SAP Customer Solution Director is part of the SAP practice and serves as the functional design authority for clients and delivery teams. The role maintains solution continuity from the earliest pursuit and presales discussions through delivery, user acceptance testing, go-live and support, helping ensure that the solution sold remains consistent with the solution designed and delivered.

Working at the intersection of business development, presales and delivery, you translate complex business challenges into an SAP solution that can be built, estimated and aligned with the client’s industry. You own process design and the industry response, while technical architecture remains with the Solution Architect or Enterprise Architect and execution, staffing and margin remain with project management and delivery leadership. Your influence, judgement and deep SAP S/4HANA knowledge contribute directly to client satisfaction and sales growth.

Your mission consists of:

Client orientation and business value:
Lead functional solutioning for pursuits, requests for proposal and oral presentations by translating client business problems into an SAP solution that Talan can estimate and deliver.
Build and defend the value case with business stakeholders, including benefit drivers, baseline measures and the operational changes required to realize the expected value.
Advise decision-makers and, when appropriate, recommend a no-bid decision when industry fit or client readiness does not support a responsible proposal.

Business development and influence:
Define solution assumptions, scope boundaries, exclusions and functional inputs to estimates, then challenge estimates before they are incorporated into pricing.
Design and present, with Alliance and Presales teams, industry-relevant demonstrations, accelerators and proof-of-concept scenarios.
Support joint pursuits, industry positioning and engagement with SAP account teams and ecosystem partners.

Design leadership and risk management:
Act as the functional design authority, decide on process design and fit-to-standard matters, and chair or co-chair workshops focused on critical processes.
Provide a documented transition from the sold solution to the delivery team, including the assumption register, scope baseline and design intent.

Delivery excellence:

Validate the delivered design against the original value case through user acceptance testing, go-live and stabilization.
Advise the team on organizational impacts arising from process design in partnership with the change management lead.

Collaboration and practice development:
Coach functional consultants and domain leads to strengthen the team’s ability to hold credible industry conversations with clients.

Feed delivery lessons into leads, packaged offerings, accelerators and the process content used by AI-enabled delivery tools.

Aurora is on a mission to create a future of solar for all. Our award-winning software puts the power of data and technology into the hands of every solar professional to make solar adoption simple and predictable. Our software has designed millions of solar projects so far, empowering solar companies to sell, design, and install residential and commercial solar arrays accurately, seamlessly, and at scale.

We’ve been named one of "The Best Remote Companies" by BuiltIn.com and have been recognized for the second time as a Certified Green Business (CGB) with the city of San Francisco. We’re in this together to support the world’s transition to solar.

About The Team

Business Systems sits within Finance and powers how Aurora goes to market, sells, bills, and recognizes revenue. The team covers RevOps systems, usage and billing, and marketing operations. Together they support everything from first lead to cash collected for both sales-led and self-serve customers. We partner closely with Accounts Receivable, FP&A, Deal Desk, Sales, Marketing, Data Analytics and Product teams to ensure our systems evolve alongside the ways Aurora sells and monetizes its offerings. jobs.title: Head of Revenue Ops & Marketing
jobs.description:
Overview

Wrapped Media is hiring a Head of Revenue Ops & Marketing to build the engine behind our sales team. Last year was a breakout year: we grew 270% and signed brands like Disney, WestJet, McDonald’s and Scotiabank. We’re now building a team of SDRs, BDRs, and AEs and they need someone to give them great lists, great tools, great content, and a comp plan worth chasing. In addition, we need someone to own marketing which includes digital ads, trade shows, newsletters, and marketing content.

What we’re looking for

You’ve spent 5+ years in B2B sales ops, revenue ops, growth or demand gen marketing. You’ve probably worn more than one of those hats at once. The people who do well in this kind of role tend to share a few traits:
They’re builders. They’d rather set up a system once than do the same task by hand every week.
They think in pipeline, not activity. Sending an email isn’t the goal; a booked meeting is.
They’re comfortable going from a HubSpot workflow to a case study to a trade show booth in the same week.
They’re excellent communicators, both written and verbal, because a lot of this job is writing things salespeople and marketers want to read.

You don’t need to be an expert in everything below, but you should be strong in most of it and keen to learn the rest:
Cold B2B outbound email: sequences, sending infrastructure, deliverability, copy
Building and enriching lead lists
Designing sales comp plans and quotas
Sales enablement: tools, data, playbooks and content
Running a marketing newsletter
Paid ads (LinkedIn, Meta, Google)
Events and trade shows
Case studies and content development

What the job actually is

You’ll own everything that makes our sales team effective, plus the marketing that warms up the market before they call.

On the revenue ops side, you’ll build and maintain our target account and contact lists, run our cold email program, keep HubSpot clean and useful, and design comp plans and quotas for our SDRs, BDRs and AEs. You’ll also give the team the tools, data and content they need to book meetings and close deals.

On the marketing side, you’ll own our newsletter, paid ads, event and trade show presence, and the case studies and content that show what our campaigns do for brands like Disney and McDonald’s.

Some of it is fun: our product is visual, our clients are brands everyone knows, and you’ll have a lot of say in how we go to market. Some of it is detail work: data hygiene, deliverability problems, comp plan edge cases. You have to enjoy both.

You’ll report directly to our co-founder and be measured on pipeline created and meetings booked, not on how busy you look.

Your stack: Apollo for data, HubSpot for CRM, Instantly for email sends and Koncert for dials. If something better exists, we want to hear about it.

Why you should be excited

You’ll build a function from close to scratch at a company that’s growing fast. This isn’t maintaining someone else’s system.
You’ll work directly with leadership and have real influence on how we sell and market, in Canada and as we expand into the US.
We’re a modern company with modern perks: hybrid setup, benefits, Xbox and snacks in the office, and dogs are welcome.

A bit more about us

We sell advertising campaigns to marketers, typically manager through VP level. We have several products: Uber/DoorDash car wraps, in-Uber tablets, event SWARMs and more.
We have a proven outbound process, a modern tech stack, top-tier customers and case studies, and a product people remember. We need someone to scale it.

 WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

As a member of the Business Systems leadership team reporting to the Vice President, Business Systems, the Director, Data, AI & Automation Services leads Bird's enterprise data, analytics, AI, automation, and information governance services. The role is accountable for translating business strategy into a practical Data, AI & Automation roadmap that improves decision-making, project and operational performance, productivity, and responsible innovation across Bird.

The Director leads the modernization of Bird's data platform and analytics ecosystem, establishes scalable AI and automation capabilities, and advances enterprise data governance, data quality, stewardship, and data fluency. Working with executive sponsors, business leaders, Cybersecurity, Privacy, Enterprise Architecture, and delivery teams, this role ensures data and AI capabilities are trusted, secure, adopted, and measurable in business value.
 What You Will Be Working On 

 Develop and execute Bird's enterprise Data, AI, Analytics, and Automation strategy, aligned with corporate objectives and the priorities of the Business Systems leadership team, translating business strategy into measurable outcomes across decision-making, operational excellence, and innovation.

 Establish and maintain a multi-year roadmap and prioritized portfolio for data modernization, AI adoption, analytics, automation services, and information governance — sequencing initiatives by business value, risk, feasibility, and adoption readiness, and reporting quantified value realization to executive leadership.

 Establish and operationalize responsible AI governance and lifecycle controls for Generative AI, Microsoft Copilot, machine learning, predictive analytics, and intelligent automation — covering AI inventory, human oversight, third-party AI/data risk, monitoring, incident response, and decommissioning, aligned with recognized frameworks such as NIST AI RMF (Govern, Map, Measure, Manage) and ISO/IEC 42001)

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Security & IT
jobs.description:
At Klue, We’re Building the Future of Competitive Intelligence 

 We’re looking for a Security, Compliance & IT Leader 👋 

 As our Director, Enterprise Security & IT, you'll sit at the intersection of security, compliance, and IT operations. You'll be accountable for how Klue protects customer data and how every Kluebee gets equipped to do their best work. Today, these three areas sit under different teams. You'll turn them into one team with one roadmap, working alongside an Engineering org that already builds and runs our product infrastructure.

 Your Mission? To own the security and compliance posture that our customers, our sales team, and our own people rely on. That covers everything we do: from building the product, to the internal automations, to the tools we use, and how we use AI. You'll set the standard, build the systems and set the rhythm to meet it. And in the process, make the secure way, the easy way.

 What's In It for You? 

 You won't inherit a playbook. You'll write it. You'll define the operating model, the culture, and the technical direction for a brand-new function, and shape a small, sharp team of 2 from day one. You'll report directly to the CTO and work closely with the Senior Leadership Team, as well as the Engineering, Product, Sales, and People teams. You'll tackle big questions like how to govern AI agents connected to company systems, and your answers will set policy at Klue. As Klue grows, so do the team and your scope. You have the power to shape what that looks like.

 What You'll Do 
 Own security posture and incident readiness. Mature how Klue prevents, detects, and responds to security issues. Design the incident response process and governance, and make sure everyone knows their role before something goes wrong.

 Run the compliance engine. Own the annual audit cycle against SOC 2 Type II, NIST CSF, and BSIMM, plus penetration testing, from evidence collection to a successful finish. Build audit methodology and documentation that make reviews faster and less painful for the whole company.

 Be the security answer for go-to-market. Keep customer questionnaires, external assessments, and audits moving on time. Review and negotiate data protection agreements and security exhibits with customers and vendors so what we sign matches what we do.

 Govern vendors, data, and privacy. Run full-spectrum vendor reviews, including sub-processor qualification. Own DLP, data retention, and the privacy framework for an international customer base, including data subject access requests.

 Set the rules for AI and high-risk access. Own AI security governance: policies, risk acceptance, data handling, and permissioning for AI tools, agents, and integrations connected to company systems. Define and enforce access governance for high-risk systems, including admin access reviews, service accounts vs. individual credentials, and controls on sensitive logs and data.

 Make security engineering's job easier. Set the security and compliance standard for Engineering's security work. Give the team the tooling, policy, and guidelines to build against, and translate their technical work into terms leadership and customers can act on.

 Equip and enable every Kluebee. Own devices, access, and tooling across the full employee lifecycle. Manage the vendors behind our IT stack, set and hit reliability targets (SLOs) for corporate systems, and replace ad hoc fixes with repeatable processes that scale. Partner with People so onboarding and offboarding run smoothly. (Product infrastructure stays with Engineering.)

 What Success Looks Like 
 One team, one roadmap. Within two quarters, Security, Compliance, and IT operate as one team with a shared roadmap and a regular operating rhythm.

 Customers get fast, consistent answers. Questionnaires, audits, and sub-processor reviews are completed on time and in a repeatable way.

 AI and access are governed, not improvised. High-risk systems and AI tools are covered by clear, documented policy, and admin access reviews are routine, not reactive.

 Corporate systems are reliable. You define clear SLOs in your first quarter, and Klue meets or beats them.

 We're ready when it counts. Incident response governance is documented and understood, and Engineering's security engineers have the tooling and guidelines to respond fast.

 Day 1 just works. Every new Kluebee has working equipment and access on their first day, with no scrambling.

 The budget is a set of clear choices. You actively manage the function's budget and make defensible tradeoffs between tooling, vendors, and headcount.

 You're the default owner. The CTO and SLT turn to you for security, compliance, and IT. Engineering and GTM teams see you as the partner who makes their job easier, not another layer to work around.

 What You Bring 
 Must Haves 
 You've run security and compliance at a B2B SaaS company handling sensitive customer data. You're comfortable owning DLP, data retention, and privacy frameworks, and you can work through a security questionnaire or audit without panic.

 You've led IT operations for a whole company, covering equipment, access, and tooling.

 You know security frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST) and global privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA) in depth.

 You're comfortable with ambiguity and building without a playbook.

 You communicate clearly with both technical peers and non-technical leaders, and can explain a risk to an engineer and to a CEO.

 You've negotiated data protection agreements and security exhibits in vendor and customer contracts.

 You understand AI security and governance: data retention commitments, access and permissioning for AI agents and integrations, and risk acceptance for AI tooling.

 You've worked closely with product and engineering teams to turn security and compliance goals into reality.

 Nice-to-Haves 
 You've owned a DevOps and/or security engineering function inside a larger engineering org.

 You've brought previously siloed security, compliance, and IT teams together under one roof.

 You know privacy and data residency frameworks for an international customer base.

 You've managed distributed or hybrid teams.

 ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️
 Not ticking every box? That’s okay. We take potential into consideration. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be accepted in lieu of the specifics listed above. If you know you have what it takes, even if that’s different from what we’ve described, be sure to explain why in your application.
 At Klue, we're committed to building a high-performing team where people feel a strong sense of belonging, can be their authentic selves, and are able to reach their full potential. If there’s anything we can do to make our hiring process more accessible or to better support you, please let us know, we’re happy to accommodate.

 Why Klue Might Be the Perfect Fit For You 
 At Klue, you’ll push the boundaries of what’s possible. For yourself, your team, and our customers. The environment here feels more startup than corporate. You’ll roll up your sleeves, build, iterate, and level up. This is a place where your ideas matter, you can shape what comes next, and leave your mark.
 If you’re looking to join a category-defining company… where you own big outcomes, influence real customers, and work with smart, gritty people… you’ll thrive here. 

 Unlock Your Potential. Take Risks. Take Action. Innovate 

 How We Work at Klue 
 We love the balance of connection and flexibility. We work Office-First, with a hybrid touch, and work together in our vibrant offices on Mondays, Wednesdays & Thursdays to collaborate, brainstorm, and build together.
 Our main hiring hubs are in:
 🇨🇦 Vancouver (HQ) 

 🇨🇦 Toronto 

 🇬🇧 London 

 Our Commitment to You 
 High Performance Culture. We reward high performance and growth through career development, coaching, and annual performance reviews.

 Comprehensive benefits: Extended health & dental coverage that starts on Day 1. Fun perks like discounts at Goodlife and Perkopolis are gravy.

 Ownership: All full-time employees have the opportunity to participate in our Employee Stock Option Plan.

 Our Vacation Policy is Take The Time You Need. We just ask that you give notice and don’t leave your team hanging. 

 Top-tier tools. All employees will receive a Mac (or PC, if that’s your jam) and access to A+ tooling. 

 AI First. All employees are encouraged to lean into AI to work smarter and faster. Built something cool lately? Show us at our Friday Show, Don’t Tell Meetings.

 Growth / Leadership. Direct access to our leadership team, including our CEO, and opportunities to connect with incredible people across the company.

 Social connection. There’s no shortage of ways to stay connected and have fun. We get together once a year in Vancouver for a company- wide kickoff. Throughout the year our Hubs hold regular social events.

 Dog-friendly spaces. Bring your four-legged friend along in Vancouver or Toronto, as our offices are pup-approved.

 About Klue 
 We’re on a mission to help organizations stop losing winnable deals. Klue’s AI agents generate market, competitor, and buyer insights in a unified platform. We ensure it’s trustworthy, automated, and activated across every department, so they have the answers they need to own their market.
 ✨ Here’s what makes us tick:
 Klue is AI-first at its core. It’s wired deep into our internal processes and tooling, powering our small but mighty team. It drives Klue’s autonomous agents that handle the heavy lifting for customers: collecting intel, generating insights, and ensuring content is updated and available across departments. Our agents help them scale their impact, stay ahead of the market, and reclaim the time that used to be consumed by manual, repetitive busywork.

 Competitor Insights. Klue helps revenue teams win more competitive deals by turning market, competitor, and buyer signals into insights teams can actually use. Our AI analyzes calls, CRM data, and real buyer feedback to give product marketers and sellers a clear picture of what’s happening in their market and why deals are won or lost. We’re a curious, collaborative team building a platform that helps companies compete with confidence, and we’re looking for people who want to do meaningful work alongside others who care about craft and impact.

 A culture of curiosity, ownership and winning together. We’re a fast-growing, globally-distributed team based in Vancouver (with hubs like Toronto), scaling quicker than ever. We value people who own their domain, act boldly, stay curious and thrive in a collaborative, high-performance environment.

 Explore More 
 Klue Blog

 Lumentum Canada was awarded the 2022 National Capital Region’s Top Employers for the 6th consecutive year and the 2022 Career Directory Canada’s Best Employers for Recent Graduates for the 5th consecutive year. 

 The Senior Director, Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) is responsible for establishing and leading Lumentum’s global EHS strategy, policies, processes, and procedures. This role ensures that all manufacturing sites operate in compliance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements and consistently achieve Lumentum’s EHS objectives and performance standards.
 The Senior Director partners with site leadership, Operations, Facilities, Engineering, Human Resources, Legal, and other corporate functions to reduce risk, protect employees and the environment, and promote a culture of accountability and continuous improvement across the company.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Develop, maintain, and govern Lumentum’s global EHS policies, standards, processes, and procedures.
 Establish global EHS objectives, goals, metrics, and improvement priorities aligned with business and operational requirements.
 Ensure manufacturing sites implement and comply with corporate EHS requirements and applicable laws and regulations.
 Provide direction, support, and oversight to site EHS leaders and management teams.
 Monitor site performance through dashboards, reviews, audits, and management reporting; identify trends and drive timely corrective actions.
 Lead the investigation of significant incidents, near misses, and environmental events, ensuring root causes are addressed and lessons learned are shared across sites.
 Support sites in reducing workplace injuries, environmental impacts, hazardous exposures, operational risks, and regulatory non-compliance.
 Coordinate responses to regulatory inspections, notices, and enforcement matters in partnership with Legal and site leadership.
 Establish minimum EHS requirements for new facilities, expansions, equipment, processes, and acquisitions.
 Promote consistent employee training, awareness, engagement, and accountability for EHS performance.
 Provide regular EHS performance updates and risk assessments to executive management.
 Lead the development and execution of multi-year EHS improvement plans and strategic initiatives.
 Establish appropriate governance, escalation, and accountability when sites are not meeting EHS objectives or compliance requirements.

 Qualifications 
 Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Health and Safety, Occupational Safety, Environmental Science, Engineering, or a related discipline; advanced degree preferred.
 10 or more years of progressive EHS experience, including significant experience supporting manufacturing or industrial operations.
 Experience leading EHS programs across multiple sites, regions, or countries.
 Strong knowledge of applicable environmental, occupational health, and workplace safety laws and regulations.
 Demonstrated experience developing and implementing global EHS policies, standards, management systems, and governance processes.
 Experience conducting risk assessments, audits, incident investigations, compliance reviews, and corrective-action programs.
 Ability to travel internationally as required.

 Preferred Qualifications 
 Professional certification such as Certified Safety Professional (CSP), Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH), or equivalent.
 Experience in the semiconductor, photonics, electronics, or other high-technology manufacturing industries.
 Experience implementing or managing ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 management systems.
 Experience leading EHS programs during facility expansions, acquisitions, integrations, or significant operational change.
 Fluency in additional languages relevant to Lumentum’s global operations.

 What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas.  POSITION SUMMARY  
 The Director, HR Technology Governance & Project Management leads the planning, governance, project management, and vendor management disciplines that turn HR priorities into an executable technology portfolio. The role owns HR technology intake, quarterly and annual planning, portfolio prioritization, capacity planning, and delivery visibility across major HR technology initiatives.  
 The Director serves as a connective leader across HR Product, HR Systems, McKesson Technology, and HR functional teams, ensuring work is appropriately evaluated, sequenced, resourced, governed, and delivered. The role directly manages strategic HR technology vendor relationships and leads a team responsible for project management, vendor management, and portfolio execution.  

 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES  
 1. HR Technology Planning, Intake & Prioritization | 30%  
 Own the enterprise HR technology intake and planning process, including quarterly PI Planning and annual portfolio planning.  
 Establish the cadence, criteria, and governance used to evaluate incoming demand, assess capacity and dependencies, prioritize investments, and translate HR and Product priorities into an executable roadmap.  
 Maintain a transparent technology backlog and provide leaders with clear recommendations and tradeoffs when demand exceeds available capacity.  

 2. HR Technology Project Management & Delivery | 30%  
 Lead the HR technology project management capability and establish consistent standards for project planning, execution, risk management, status reporting, and delivery.  
 Direct and develop project managers responsible for medium through large, complex HR technology initiatives.  
 Maintain portfolio-level visibility into scope, timelines, dependencies, resource requirements, and delivery risks. Ensure issues are surfaced early, decisions are made at the appropriate level, and projects deliver against committed outcomes.  

 3. Portfolio Governance & Executive Visibility | 10%  
 Maintain a consolidated view of the HR technology portfolio that gives leaders clear visibility into work in flight, planned investments, capacity constraints, dependencies, and decisions requiring leadership attention.  
 Establish practical governance connecting intake, solution design, prioritization, delivery, and operational handoff.  
 Partner with HR Product leaders to translate strategy and priorities into sequencing and execution plans.  

 4. HR Technology Vendor Management | 15%  
 Directly manage key HR technology vendor relationships and lead vendor governance across the portfolio.

 Job Description: 
 About the role: 
The AVP, Security Architecture is a senior leader accountable for the enterprise security architecture strategy, governance, and evolution of security capabilities across global business and technology environments. 
The role translates business priorities, cyber risk appetite, and emerging threats into architecture direction that protects clients, employees, information, and critical services.

Working closely with the CISO, CTO, enterprise architects, and business technology leaders, the AVP leads the Security Architecture function and embeds secure-by-design, Zero Trust, and defense-in-depth principles into enterprise transformation and solution delivery.

The AVP serves as a senior security design authority within enterprise architecture governance, shapes security investment priorities, and develops a team that provides consistent architectural guidance across business units and geographies.

 What You Will Do?
Key Responsibilities:

 1. Enterprise Security Architecture Strategy and Road mapping 
 Own the enterprise security architecture strategy and target state across identity, cloud, infrastructure, networks, endpoints, applications, data, and security platforms.
 Establish multi-year security capability roadmaps aligned with business priorities, enterprise architecture, the cybersecurity strategy, and organizational risk appetite.
 Translate capability assessments, threat trends, and the NIST Cybersecurity Framework into prioritized architecture improvements, with Zero Trust and defense in depth guiding modernization.

 2. Security Architecture Function and People Leadership 
 Lead and develop the Security Architecture team, with accountability for performance, coaching, succession planning, and the skills required to support enterprise priorities.
 Define the function's operating model, engagement processes, and service expectations, providing architecture coverage across security programs and business-led technology initiatives.
 Prioritize demand and allocate capacity across strategic planning, project assurance, governance, and emerging technology work; establish coverage and knowledge-sharing practices that reduce dependence on individual specialists.
 Manage the function's operating plan, assigned budget, and resources, and build business cases for additional capacity or specialist support.

 3. Architecture Governance and Design Authority 
 Establish security reference architectures, standards, reusable patterns, and guardrails in partnership with global domain architects and enterprise security policy owners.
 Serve as senior security design authority for significant initiatives within the enterprise architecture governance process, with clear decision rights and escalation paths.
 Represent Security Architecture on enterprise technology review boards, resolve cross-domain design issues, and oversee design assurance against approved security requirements.
 Oversee recommendations for architectural exceptions, compensating controls, and remediation plans; escalate material residual risks to accountable business and risk owners through established governance.

 4. Secure Solution Design and Transformation Oversight 
 Provide security architecture oversight for major business and technology initiatives from early planning through implementation, with review effort proportionate to risk and complexity.
 Embed threat modelling, secure design reviews, and reusable security patterns into delivery practices, partnering with application, data, infrastructure, cloud, and engineering teams.
 Lead architectural direction for security transformation programs, including identity modernization, cloud security, network segmentation, application security, data protection, and cyber recovery.

 5. Security Capability Portfolio and Investment Leadership 
 Direct the strategic evolution, integration, consolidation, and retirement of security tools, services, and capabilities to address enterprise needs and reduce fragmentation.
 Shape investment priorities and present business cases that assess risk reduction, control coverage, technical feasibility, interoperability, operational capacity, and total cost of ownership.
 Maintain an enterprise view of capability gaps, overlapping technologies, lifecycle risks, and technical debt; partner with engineering, operations, procurement, and vendor management to turn roadmaps into achievable investment and delivery plans.

 6. Technology Evaluation and AI Security 
 Evaluate emerging security technologies, vendor capabilities, and service models, providing recommendations on suitability, integration, scalability, and long-term viability.
 Sponsor proofs of concept with clear success criteria for security effectiveness, technical compatibility, operational readiness, and business value.
 Define security architecture requirements and patterns for AI platforms, generative AI, and autonomous agents, addressing identity, data access, tool permissions, monitoring, and human oversight.
 Identify opportunities to use automation and AI within security capabilities, working with responsible teams to validate benefits, control effectiveness, and operational accountability.

 7. Architectural Risk and Resilience 
 Identify systemic security architecture weaknesses and drive mitigation roadmaps with accountable engineering, platform, and business technology owners.
 Translate security, privacy, regulatory, and data residency requirements into architecture requirements in partnership with Risk, Compliance, Privacy, and Legal.
 Integrate requirements for resilience, ransomware containment, recovery, logging, and monitoring into security designs, working with operational owners to establish implementation and validation expectations.
 Use findings from incidents, security testing, audits, and control assessments to improve reference architectures, patterns, and capability roadmaps.

 8. Executive Engagement and Enterprise Partnership 
 Act as a trusted advisor to the Global Chief Enterprise Architect, CISO, CTO, CIO, and business technology leaders on security architecture strategy and significant technology decisions.
 Translate complex architecture choices into clear business implications, investment options, delivery dependencies, and risk treatment recommendations for executive forums.
 Build alignment across global business units and technology functions, resolve competing priorities, and report on architecture coverage, adoption, roadmap progress, and outcomes.

 What Do You Need to Succeed? 
 Qualifications Required: 
 University degree or college diploma in cybersecurity, computer science, information technology, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
 15+ years of progressive experience in cybersecurity architecture, engineering, or related technology leadership roles, including accountability for enterprise security architecture strategy.
 Demonstrated experience leading and developing architecture or security teams, managing priorities and resources, and delivering outcomes in a complex, matrixed organization.
 Experience influencing VP and SVP stakeholders and presenting architecture strategies, investment recommendations, and risk decisions at executive forums.
 Strong knowledge across identity and access management, cloud, infrastructure, network, endpoint, application, API, and data security, including cryptography and secrets management.
 Demonstrated ability to establish enterprise architecture standards, reference patterns, governance processes, and multi-year security capability roadmaps.
 Practical understanding of Zero Trust, defense in depth, threat modelling, secure development, and frameworks such as the NIST Cybersecurity Framework.
 Experience modernizing security platforms and evaluating vendors or third-party services for technical feasibility, integration, control effectiveness, and total cost of ownership.
 Excellent communication, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills, with the judgment to balance security, business value, delivery constraints, and operational sustainability.

 Preferred skills: 
 Experience in financial services or another regulated industry with global operations and complex privacy or data residency requirements.
 Experience with hybrid and multi-cloud environments, including AWS, Azure, or Alibaba Cloud.
 Experience defining security architectures for AI, autonomous agents, automation, or other emerging technologies.
 Experience with major security transformations, technology rationalization, or mergers and acquisitions integration.
 Relevant professional certifications, such as CISSP, CISM, SABSA, TOGAF, or cloud security and architecture certifications.

 Key Outcomes and Measures of Success:

 Architecture coverage: Timely engagement on significant initiatives across business units, with consistent service coverage and review turnaround.
 Secure delivery: Greater use of approved patterns and earlier resolution of design weaknesses, reducing avoidable rework and exceptions.
 Risk treatment: Progress against remediation plans for material architectural weaknesses and timely escalation of unresolved risks.
 Portfolio effectiveness: Reduced capability duplication and technical debt, supported by documented control improvements and lifecycle cost benefits.
 Team capability: Improved skills, succession readiness, knowledge sharing, and capacity to support strategic and delivery priorities.

You'll work with dynamic colleagues - experts in their fields - who are eager to share their knowledge with you. Your leaders will inspire and help you reach your potential and soar to new heights. Every day, you'll have new and exciting opportunities to make life brighter for our Clients - who are at the heart of everything we do. 

 At Sun Life, we're driven by our Purpose: helping our Clients achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. Our values shape how we work: caring, authentic, bold, inspiring, and impactful.

 When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.

 Discover how you can make a difference in the lives of individuals, families and communities around the world.

 Job Description: 
 Lead the strategy that differentiates Group Retirement Services (GRS) in the market and connects sponsors and members with its value. As AVP, Market Strategy, Activation, & Communications you will be a key member of the Market Development leadership team, leading the GRS narrative, value proposition and go-to-market strategy. You will unite sponsor and member perspectives into a differentiated market position, strengthening awareness of GRS solutions, including its 2C (individual wealth management) capabilities. In partnership with Corporate Marketing and Communications and member marketing leadership, you will align communications and cross-functional execution while preserving partners’ accountability for member-specific strategy and execution. You will also represent GRS on key marketing strategies and initiatives across Sunlife, advancing growth, retention and member engagement through data-informed decisions and clear measures of business impact and return on investment (ROI). 

 What will you do? 

 Set the commercial go-to-market agenda: Translate GRS objectives into a roadmap for priority segments, audiences, competitive positioning, routes to market and growth opportunities. Define strategic trade-offs, recommend resource priorities and secure leadership commitment to coordinated execution. 
 Lead GRS narrative and proposition communications: Turn strategy and sponsor and member insights into differentiated value propositions and audience-specific messaging. Connect solutions, innovation and credible proof points in a consistent GRS story, validating relevance through market insight and aligning messaging standards with Corporate Marketing and Communications and enterprise requirements. 
 Establish marketing investment and performance discipline: Link investment priorities to business objectives, expected returns and measurable targets. Assess marketing’s contribution to pipeline and conversion, using ROI analysis and transparent measurement assumptions to recommend where to scale, adjust or discontinue initiatives. 
 Lead demand generation and commercial alignment: Attract and nurture prospective sponsors and activate consultant and advisor channels. Partner with Business Development on lead qualification, hand-offs, follow-up and feedback, using acquisition and conversion insights to strengthen pipeline contribution without assuming ownership of sales outcomes. 
 Align enterprise and member-level mandates: Establish shared plans, decision responsibilities and measures with Corporate Marketing and Communications, CXO and member marketing leadership. Integrate the broader member proposition into GRS positioning and sponsor-facing strategy, resolving dependencies while preserving partners’ distinct mandates and ownership of member-specific strategy and execution. 
 Shape strategic communications and market influence: Set a communications and thought-leadership agenda that reinforces GRS positioning and brings member perspectives into sponsor, consultant and advisor conversations. Guide executive messaging and external communications, aligning events, sponsorships, advertising and digital channels to market opportunities and measuring audience engagement and qualified demand. 
 Lead cross-functional launch governance: Set readiness criteria for new products, investment solutions and innovations, covering audiences, propositions, channels, commercial enablement and success measures. Align leaders on milestones and dependencies, address gaps and advance launch recommendations through appropriate decision forums. Use post-launch reviews to improve adoption and investment decisions. 
 Turn market intelligence into action: Assess sponsor needs, member insights, competitor positioning and channel feedback to identify opportunities and proposition gaps. Test strategic assumptions and bring evidence-based recommendations to GRS leadership to inform go-to-market priorities and innovation. 
 Build an entrepreneurial, accountable team: Lead and develop over 10 marketing and communications professionals, strengthening proposition development, demand generation, analytics and integrated planning. Foster ownership, proactive opportunity identification and disciplined experimentation. Shape priorities with business and enterprise partners while retaining accountability for GRS marketing outcomes and balancing strategic initiatives with ongoing business needs. 

 What do you need to succeed? 

 Commercial strategy and prioritization: Translates business objectives and market insight into segment-specific go-to-market plans and demand-generation approaches; makes clear trade-offs and focuses resources on the strongest opportunities 
 Executive presence and influence: Communicates direction with clarity and conviction, integrates diverse perspectives and exercises sound judgement to build commitment and advance decisions across organizational boundaries 
 Marketing economics and measurement: Applies investment, lead quality, funnel and ROI analysis to decisions; distinguishes activity from business impact and communicates measurement limitations transparently 
 Entrepreneurial leadership and ownership: Identifies opportunities, sets priorities and owns results; shapes direction collaboratively, makes timely, evidence-based decisions and adapts through disciplined experimentation. 
 Enterprise collaboration: Builds trusted partnerships with Corporate Marketing and Communications, CXO, member marketing leadership, Business Development, Legal and other Canadian Business Units, aligning objectives while respecting distinct accountabilities. 
 Strategic communications and narrative leadership: Translates strategy and audience insights into clear value propositions, persuasive executive communications and a cohesive GRS story, adapting messaging across channels while maintaining enterprise alignment 
 Market and member insight: Applies knowledge of GRS, the Capital Accumulation Plans (CAP) environment and the end-to-end member experience to strengthen competitive positioning. Uses member insights and evolving marketing practices to shape consumer-facing wealth management strategies that increase awareness, engagement and conversion. 
 Talent leadership: Attracts, develops and retains marketing talent, builds strategic and analytical capabilities and fosters collaboration, initiative and accountability. 
 Integrated execution and governance: Establishes effective decision forums, launch-readiness standards and performance reviews; mobilizes leaders to resolve dependencies and deliver coordinated results. 
 University degree or post-secondary education 
 10+ years of relevant industry experience, including experience within Group Retirement, Individual Wealth Management, Banking, or related financial services sectors 
 Experience leading go-to-market strategy, demand generation and marketing investment analysis 
 Experience developing consumer-facing wealth management marketing strategies informed by member insights 
 Expertise in strategic communications, value proposition development, market positioning and go-to-market leadership; banking and/or wealth management experience preferred.  
 Must be able to travel on a regular basis 
 As this position is posted in several locations, we specify that bilingualism (French, English, both oral and written) is required for Quebec only for the frequent interactions with English and French-speaking colleagues or internal partners across Canada or worldwide.  

 The Base Pay range is for the primary location for which the job is posted. It may vary depending on the work location of the successful candidate or other factors. In addition to Base Pay, eligible Sun Life employees participate in various incentive plans, payment under which is discretionary and subject to individual and company performance. Certain sales focused roles have sales incentive plans based on individual or group sales results. 

 Diversity and inclusion have always been at the core of our values at Sun Life. A diverse workforce with wide perspectives and creative ideas benefits our Clients, the communities where we operate and all of us as colleagues. We welcome applications from qualified individuals from all backgrounds.

 Persons with disabilities who need accommodation in the application process, or those needing job postings in an alternative format, may e-mail a request to thebrightside@sunlife.com.

 We are proud to be a hybrid organization that offers our employees the choice and flexibility to work from both the office and virtually based on the needs of the business, our Clients and you.

 We may use artificial intelligence to support candidate sourcing, screening, interview scheduling. 

 We thank all applicants for showing an interest in this position. Only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

 Job Description: 

 Role Summary 

 The AVP Technology Lead – Digital is a strategic technology leader responsible for enabling, scaling, and modernizing Sun Life Canada’s shared digital platforms that support secure, connected, and frictionless Client and advisor experiences. This role provides technology leadership across core digital   assets   including Secure Web, Public Web,   &   Secure Mobile, and related enablement platforms   such as client identity and access management, and   an internal   design system.   

 The role combines strategic leadership, technical oversight, people leadership, delivery execution, operational accountability, and vendor/financial management to drive technology excellence and measurable business value. The AVP partners closely with Product, Client Experience, Architecture, Cybersecurity, Operations, Engineering, and Business leaders to ensure digital   assets   are resilient, scalable, secure, reusable, and aligned to enterprise priorities.   

 This role operates in a complex, high-visibility environment where digital platform reliability, modernization, and cross-business enablement are critical to Client outcomes. The leader must be able to bring clarity to a broad mandate, make decisions in ambiguity, and build a high-performing technology organization that balances speed, stability, security, and long-term platform health.   

 What will you do? 

 1. Technology Strategy, Platform Enablement & Engineering   

 Shape, communicate, and align the digital technology strategy across   business units, ensuring it supports near-term delivery commitments and longer-term modernization objectives.   

 Partner with Business Leads, Product, Client Experience, Architecture, Cybersecurity, Operations, and Enterprise Technology to define platform roadmaps, OKRs, sequencing, and investment priorities.   

 Provide thought leadership on the evolution of shared digital platforms, including identity, web, mobile, integration, data enablement, and reusable digital capabilities.   

 Promote technology stack standards, modern engineering practices, automation, and architectural discipline, balancing build vs. buy vs. partner decisions in a complex technology ecosystem.   

 Ensure design and engineering decisions account for reusability, scalability, security, maintainability, accessibility, and technical debt reduction.   

 Create the conditions for exceptional digital experiences by enabling business and product teams with reliable, scalable, secure, and reusable platforms.   

 2. Platform Delivery & Execution   

 Accountable for end-to-end delivery of digital platform capabilities, including oversight of internal delivery teams, vendors, system integrators, and total cost of ownership.   

 Drive delivery excellence by improving velocity, quality, reliability, predictability, and agile maturity across multiple squads.   

 Track delivery metrics, identify bottlenecks, and implement targeted productivity and delivery maturity improvements.   

 Serve as the primary escalation point for platform, delivery, vendor, and dependency-related issues, enabling rapid resolution in a complex environment.   

 Ensure delivery is integrated across product, architecture,   engineering,   operations, cybersecurity, and business priorities.   

 Embed test-and-learn, automation, and continuous improvement practices to improve speed, quality, and sustainability.   

 3. People Leadership & Capability Development   

 Lead, mentor, and develop technology leaders and teams, fostering a collaborative, inclusive, accountable, and execution-focused culture.   

 Design and optimize team structures to support   clear   ownership, delivery outcomes, modernization priorities, and clear accountabilities.   

 Partner with Chapter, Engineering, Product, and Business leaders on workforce planning, role clarity, succession planning, and capability development.   

 Build internal capability in   digital   engineering,   enablement, agile delivery, vendor management, and operational excellence.   

 Coach leaders to manage performance effectively, clarify ownership, and build resilient teams through change and transformation.   

 4. Financial & Vendor Management   

 Lead budget management, including annual planning, cost tracking, capitalization, forecasting, and investment prioritization.   

 Manage strategic vendor and system integrator relationships, holding partners accountable for delivery quality, outcomes, knowledge transfer, and value realization.   

 Drive cost transparency and technology spend optimization across applications, infrastructure, security, vendor, and platform investments.   

 Identify opportunities to reduce long-term dependency on external partners while strengthening internal platform ownership and capability.   

 5. Operational Excellence, Risk & Security   

 Ensure   s tability, security, technology currency, resiliency, and end-of-life decommissioning for applications within scope.   

 Establish governance processes that balance speed of delivery with risk management, audit, regulatory, cybersecurity, and control requirements.   

 Partner with   Application   Operations to ensure effective incident management, change management, disaster recovery, and business continuity planning.   

 Proactively manage operational risk,   application   health, technical debt, and service reliability across shared digital capabilities.   

 6. Cross-Functional Collaboration & Stakeholder Engagement   

 Act as a strategic technology partner to leaders across Product, Client Experience, Business, Operations, Architecture, Cybersecurity, and Enterprise Technology.   

 Communicate   digital   strategy, delivery status, risks, trade-offs, and dependencies with clarity and transparency.   

 Represent the Digital technology function in executive forums, bringing enterprise perspective, external insight, and pragmatic recommendations.   

 Strengthen alignment between technology investments, business priorities, Client experience outcomes, and enterprise digital strategy.   

 Accountabilities   

 Align digital strategy with business objectives, Client outcomes, enterprise standards, and shared technology priorities.   

 Define and monitor roadmaps, OKRs, modernization priorities, and delivery sequencing.   

 Oversee execution across delivery teams, vendors, system integrators, and enterprise partners.   

 Establish governance, track delivery metrics, and drive productivity, quality, and reliability improvements.   

 Manage budgets, vendor relationships, and cost optimization opportunities.   

 Build and sustain a high-performing, engaged, inclusive, and platform-oriented technology organization.   

 Ensure digital platforms are secure, scalable, resilient, reusable, and positioned to support future growth.   

 What you need to succeed? 

 Qualifications & Experience   

 Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field; advanced degree or MBA is an asset.   

 10+ years of experience in senior technology leadership roles with demonstrated success delivering complex, mission-critical digital platforms.   

 Experience leading modernization and enablement of digital platforms such as identity, web, mobile, integration, or client/advisor experience platforms.   

 Proven ability to lead technology teams through transformation, platform ownership, and operating model evolution.   

 Strong financial acumen with experience managing sizable technology budgets, vendor portfolios, and total cost of ownership.   

 Strong stakeholder management, executive communication, and organizational leadership skills.   

 Experience in regulated financial services is valuable; depth in digital enablement, engineering excellence, and vendor-heavy delivery environments is prioritized.   

 As this position is posted in several locations, we specify that bilingualism (French, English, both oral and written) is required for Quebec only for the frequent interactions with English and French-speaking colleagues or internal partners across Canada or worldwide 

 Mindset & Behaviours   

 Decisive leader comfortable operating in ambiguity, complexity, and transformation.   

 Strong technical credibility with the ability to challenge architecture, delivery practices, platform decisions, and CI/CD approaches.   

 Builder mindset with equal focus on fixing, scaling, enabling, and simplifying.   

 Pragmatic, outcomes-driven decision-maker who balances speed, stability, risk, and long-term   application   health.   

 Collaborative leader who builds trust, drives momentum, and creates clarity across complex stakeholder groups.   

 Critical thinker who challenges the status quo constructively and drives continuous improvement.   

 Strong coaching orientation with a commitment to developing leaders, teams, and internal capability.   

 What’s in it for you? 
 A competitive salary and bonus program, based on market scale

 A flexible group insurance program starting on your first day of work to meet your needs and those of your family.

 Time off that allows you to focus on the moments that matter most. 20 vacation days per year.

 Our Share Ownership Program gives you the opportunity to invest in Sun Life while benefiting from employer matching contributions.

 We are proud to be included in Great Place to Work's 2026 list of Canada's Best Workplaces.
