About OBRYN GUARD OBRYN GUARD Inc. is a Canadian cybersecurity and governance, risk and compliance technology company building a cloud-based platform for continuous control monitoring, cybersecurity risk management and compliance readiness.
Our initial focus is the hospitality industry, helping hotels and multi-property organizations improve visibility into cybersecurity risk, organize evidence, identify compliance gaps, manage remediation and maintain stronger ongoing readiness for frameworks including PCI DSS, SOC 2 and ISO/IEC 27001.
We are building a global team across security, engineering, product, QA, solutions, operations and sales.

The Role We are seeking a Head of PCI DSS Advisory to lead OBRYN GUARD’s PCI DSS and payment-security advisory function.
This is a senior specialist role responsible for shaping how PCI DSS requirements are translated into practical customer workflows, platform methodology, evidence requirements, remediation guidance and hotel payment-security readiness.
You will work closely with our Head of Security, Engineering, Product, QA, Solutions and Leadership teams to ensure OBRYN GUARD’s PCI-related workflows are technically accurate, operationally practical and appropriately positioned as readiness and advisory support.
This role is particularly suited to someone with deep hands-on PCI DSS experience across complex merchant and payment environments.

Key ResponsibilitiesPCI DSS Leadership Lead OBRYN GUARD’s PCI DSS advisory methodology.
Interpret PCI DSS requirements and translate them into practical customer and platform workflows.
Support PCI DSS v4.x readiness programs.
Develop PCI control mappings, evidence requirements and remediation methodologies.
Help establish clear distinctions between automated controls, manual evidence and specialist review.
Review PCI-related platform functionality for methodological accuracy.

SAQ Readiness Support development of SAQ eligibility and readiness workflows.
Help determine what information must be collected before recommending an appropriate SAQ path.
Develop questionnaires and decision-support processes around merchant payment environments.
Identify situations requiring escalation to an appropriately qualified external assessor or QSA Company.

CDE & Payment Environment Scoping Develop repeatable methodologies for Cardholder Data Environment discovery and scoping.
Review payment flows, systems, connected environments and third-party dependencies.
Support documentation of where account data enters, moves through, is processed or may be stored.
Review segmentation, remote access, vendor access and systems capable of affecting the security of the CDE.

Hospitality Payment Security Support PCI readiness across hotel environments including:
Front desk payment terminals
PMS environments
POS systems
Restaurants and bars
Booking engines
Hotel websites
Payment gateways
Virtual terminals
Telephone reservations
E-commerce
Mobile payment environments
Spa, retail, parking and event payments
Franchise and management-company structures
Multi-property and shared-service environments

Third-Party Service Providers Review payment processor and TPSP responsibilities.
Develop shared-responsibility methodologies.
Support review of AOCs and vendor compliance evidence.
Identify gaps in third-party responsibility and evidence.

Evidence & Remediation Define acceptable PCI evidence standards.
Establish evidence freshness and sufficiency expectations.
Review customer evidence where appropriate.
Identify PCI readiness gaps.
Provide practical remediation guidance.
Support prioritization of material payment-security risks.

Product & Engineering Translate PCI requirements into product requirements.
Work with Engineering on technical feasibility.
Support Product with workflows and acceptance criteria.
Work with QA to validate PCI-related platform functionality.
Help ensure OBRYN GUARD does not incorrectly represent an automated result, integration or uploaded document as complete proof of PCI DSS compliance.

Customer & Solutions Support Support Solutions during customer onboarding and payment-environment discovery.
Participate in selected customer PCI readiness discussions.
Support complex hotel and enterprise engagements.
Review difficult PCI questions and escalations.
Help develop executive-ready PCI readiness reporting.

Required Experience Significant hands-on PCI DSS experience.
Strong understanding of PCI DSS v4.x.
Experience with merchant and payment environments.
Experience with SAQs and PCI readiness programs.
Strong understanding of CDE scoping and payment-flow mapping.
Experience reviewing PCI evidence and remediation plans.
Experience with payment gateways, processors, POS systems and third-party service providers.
Ability to interpret technical and compliance requirements and convert them into practical workflows.
Experience communicating with technical teams, leadership and customers.
Strong written documentation and methodology-development skills.

Preferred Experience Current or previous PCI SSC Qualified Security Assessor experience.
Experience working through or alongside a PCI SSC QSA Company.
Experience preparing or reviewing ROC, AOC or SAQ-related engagements.
Experience with PCI DSS Level 1 environments.
Hospitality, retail, payments or multi-location merchant experience.
ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2 or broader GRC experience.
Cloud, network, IAM or application-security experience.
Experience working with SaaS platforms or technology companies.
Certifications such as PCIP, PCI ISA, CISSP, CISA, CISM, ISO 27001 or similar are considered an asset.

jobs.title: Head of Tax
jobs.description:
Head of Tax

Writeoff Inc.
· Fully remote (Canada) · Full-time

About Writeoff

Writeoff is a fully remote, AI-native tax and accounting firm. We work with owner-managed corporations across Canada and the US, handling their bookkeeping and tax on flat monthly fees. Our stack (QuickBooks Online, TaxCycle, Claude, Aqqrue, Notion, Granola) takes care of the grunt work that buries most firms: data entry, reconciliations, chasing documents. That leaves our people doing the work that actually needs a professional: judgment, planning and owning the client relationship.
This is our first Head of Tax. Not a rung on a ladder: the seat at the table. We want someone technically strong, with SMB experience, who's tired of building somebody else's practice.

The Role

This is a player-coach role. You'll fully own Writeoff's client tax relationships and everything that comes with them: compliance, planning, CRA, and being the person founders call when it actually matters. You'll review and sign off on the work, plan the complex files yourself, and lead a small team of preparers. And because we're AI-native, you'll be expected to get creative with AI and ship useful solutions to important problems, for our clients and for how tax gets done here. You report directly to the founder, and what you build here is yours.

What You'll Do

Own tax quality

Prepare, review and file T2, T1 and T3 returns, T4/T5/T4A slips and summaries, GST/HST returns and payroll filings, all in TaxCycle
Set the review standards, checklists and workpaper conventions the team works from
Be the final word on technical positions and how we document them

Plan for owner-managers

Advise on remuneration (salary vs. dividends), SBD and association, GRIP, CDA and safe income
Lead reorganizations and planning: s.85 rollovers, holdco structures, estate freezes, pipelines, LCGE / QSBC purification
Family trust planning: setting up and running trusts in freezes, TOSI, the 21-year deemed disposition
Support SR&ED claims and other credits
Work through deal and transaction tax on asset and share sales

Lead the team

Manage and develop 1 to 2 tax preparers, reviewing their work and teaching as you go
Help us hire as the tax practice grows

Build the machine

Help design our AI-native tax workflow end to end: client intake, QBO to GIFI mapping, TaxCycle prep, review and e-filing
Turn your judgment into repeatable checklists, prompts and processes the team and our AI tools can run on

Work with clients

Own the tax relationship for your clients end to end: you're their go-to for anything tax, mostly over Slack
Handle CRA correspondence, reviews and audits
Coordinate with our US partner firms on cross-border files

What you Bring

CPA designation (required)
5+ years of Canadian tax experience with SMB and owner-managed clients, ideally in public practice
Hands-on TaxCycle experience (T1 and T2)
Real volume on T2 prep and filing: GIFI, schedules, SBD and association, year-end adjustments
T-slip prep and filing: T4, T5, T4A and summaries, plus T5018 where it applies
Trust experience: T3 returns, the expanded trust reporting rules (Schedule 15), and trusts used in freezes and family planning
Foreign reporting and non-residents: T1134, T1135, T106, NR4 and s.116
Reorg and transaction work you can scope, price and deliver: s.85 and s.86 rollovers, amalgamations, wind-ups, estate freezes, purification
Strong command of corporate and personal tax for CCPCs and their shareholders
Experience reviewing other people's work and explaining the "why" behind your comments
Comfort talking to business owners in plain language
Genuine curiosity about AI and new tools, and a willingness to change how things are done when there's a better way
Ability to juggle many clients at once in a remote, async environment

Nice to Have

CPA In-Depth Tax Course completed or in progress
Cross-border exposure: US C-corps, Delaware structures, QSBS, treaty issues, non-resident filings
SR&ED experience
QuickBooks Online experience

Compensation

Base salary: $120,000 - $150,000 CAD
, depending on experience
Benefits package included
4 weeks of vacation
Real ownership, on a real timeline.
At a traditional firm you grind ten-plus years for a shot at partner, write a cheque to buy in, and end up with a sliver and a vote. Here the path is measured in years, not decades, and the stake is meaningful. You're not renting a seat. You own part of what you build, and every client you win and every system you ship grows your piece of it.
Fully remote, anywhere in Canada, plus one in-person company offsite a year

jobs.title: Director, AI Engineering
jobs.description:
We Are

Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow.

You Are

You have spent a decade building systems that ship, not prototypes that impress in slide decks. You know the gap between a working demo and a production system that 500 engineers trust with their daily workflow, and you have closed that gap more than once. You think in platforms, not projects. When you see three teams solving similar problems in different ways, you build the shared layer that makes the fourth team move twice as fast.

You are the kind of leader who can sit with a principal engineer debugging an LLM orchestration failure in the morning and walk into an executive review that afternoon to explain why responsible AI governance is not overhead, it is how you earn customer trust at scale. You do not wait for perfect clarity. You work with what you have, make the right tradeoffs, and move the organization forward without creating chaos downstream.

At Synopsys, you will lead the engineering effort that turns agentic AI from high-potential experiments into production systems that change how semiconductor and EDA work actually gets done. The team is global, the problems are hard, and what you build will matter.

What You'll Be Doing

Own and deliver a portfolio of agentic AI programs across product engineering, semiconductor IP, applications, operations, and customer-facing teams, driving each from prototype through pilot to production deployment with clear adoption metrics
Define reference architectures for agentic workflows that combine LLMs, tool use, retrieval, orchestration, evaluation, and human oversight, setting engineering standards for reliability, testing, and release readiness that go beyond demos
Build reusable platforms and shared components including tool-use frameworks, RAG patterns, evaluation harnesses, prompt governance, model routing, and safety guardrails that reduce duplication and accelerate adoption across business units
Translate between AI technology capabilities, domain engineering realities in EDA and semiconductor workflows, product priorities, and executive goals, influencing senior stakeholders to align on tradeoffs, timelines, and risk posture
Lead, coach, and grow a team of principal engineers, staff engineers, and applied scientists, running design reviews, setting technical direction, and building a culture of ownership, pragmatism, and production discipline
Partner with infrastructure, security, legal, and compliance teams to make agentic systems observable through telemetry and tracing, secure through data controls and threat modeling, and responsible through policy and human-in-the-loop governance
Represent the AI Excellence Group with internal leaders and strategic customers to build credibility, manage risk, and ensure solutions connect to measurable business outcomes like quality improvement, cycle time reduction, and cost savings

The Impact You Will Have

Ship multiple production agentic AI deployments per year that measurably improve engineering velocity, product value, and internal efficiency across Synopsys silicon-to-systems portfolio
Establish the default standards and golden path implementations for agentic AI across the company, reducing time-to-pilot for new use cases and increasing reuse of shared components
Accelerate adoption by publishing templates, playbooks, and repeatable patterns that help teams move from idea to deployed solution without reinventing foundational infrastructure
Build organizational capability in agentic systems engineering that outlasts any single project, creating the people, practices, and platforms needed to sustain AI transformation at Synopsys scale
Reduce risk and earn customer trust by embedding observability, security, and responsible AI governance into every deployment, not as afterthoughts but as core design principles
Drive measurable business outcomes including cycle-time reduction, defect reduction, productivity gains, cost savings, and improved customer satisfaction across EDA, IP, simulation, and solver workflows
Create a high-performing team culture that attracts and retains senior technical talent and sets the bar for engineering excellence in applied AI at Synopsys

What You'll Need

10+ years of software engineering experience with a strong track record of shipping reliable production systems, not research prototypes
3+ years leading senior technical teams at the staff or principal engineer level and delivering cross-organizational programs that required influencing without direct authority
Hands-on experience with modern AI application patterns including LLMs, agents, retrieval-augmented generation, tool use, orchestration frameworks, evaluation methodologies, and production deployment workflows
Strong systems thinking across product experience, data pipelines, infrastructure, security, and operational tradeoffs, with the ability to make pragmatic decisions under ambiguity
Exceptional communication skills with both deeply technical audiences and executive or customer-facing stakeholders, able to explain complex tradeoffs clearly and drive alignment on risk and timelines
Experience in EDA, semiconductor workflows, system-level simulation, physics-based solvers, or complex enterprise engineering tools is a strong plus
Experience building internal platforms or shared services used by multiple teams, such as developer productivity tools, ML/AI platforms, or governance frameworks, is a strong plus

Who You Are

You can walk into a room where three teams are building similar agentic workflows and walk out with a plan for a shared platform that makes the fourth team move twice as fast without forcing anyone to rewrite working code
When a pilot shows promise but the eval scores are inconsistent and the latency spikes under load, you know which problems to solve now and which to instrument and monitor, because you have been here before
You push back when a roadmap is built on optimism instead of engineering reality, and you do it in a way that builds trust rather than shutting down the conversation
You can explain to a VP why responsible AI governance is not compliance theater, it is how you avoid the incident that costs customer trust, and you can do it in two sentences without losing the nuance
You hire and develop senior engineers who do not need hand-holding but do need someone who can unblock cross-org dependencies, set technical direction, and protect the team from thrash
You treat production deployments as the beginning of the work, not the end, because adoption, observability, and iteration are what turn a shipped system into a trusted one

The Team You'll Be Part Of

You will lead a team of principal engineers, staff engineers, and applied scientists within the AI Excellence Group, focused on delivering trusted, production-grade agentic AI capabilities across Synopsys. The group's mission is to turn high-potential AI opportunities into scalable platforms, repeatable patterns, and deployed solutions that measurably improve product value, engineering velocity, and internal efficiency across the silicon-to-systems portfolio, including EDA, semiconductor IP, system-level simulation, and physics-based solvers. You will partner closely with product engineering, infrastructure, security, legal, and compliance teams, and represent the group with senior leaders and strategic customers.

Rewards and Benefits

We offer a comprehensive range of health, wellness, and financial benefits to cater to your needs. Our total rewards include both monetary and non-monetary offerings. Your recruiter will provide more details about the salary range and benefits during the hiring process.

Synopsys Canada ULC values the diversity of our workforce. We are committed to provide access & opportunity to individuals with disabilities and will provide reasonable accommodation to individuals throughout the recruitment and employment process. Should you require an accommodation, please contact hr-help-canada@synopsys.com.

Canada Off-Site, Canada Off-Site Office, Canada - $194,400-$291,600

About The Role

Siemens RUGGEDCOM is a global leader in mission-critical industrial networking and cybersecurity solutions, enabling reliable communications for electric utilities, transportation, mining, energy, defense, and other critical infrastructure industries worldwide.

We are seeking a leader with entrepreneurial mindset and business-focused Head of Siemens RUGGEDCOM. In this leadership role, you will define portfolio strategy, drive profitable growth, oversee product management and R&D alignment, and ensure RUGGEDCOM maintains its technology and market leadership.

You will lead a global team of product managers, product owners, and developers while collaborating closely with portfolio management, sales, operations, finance, and regional business leaders. Combining strategic business leadership, product management excellence, and strong commercial acumen, you will act as a chief business developer who navigates complex stakeholder expectations to deliver sustainable growth and long-term customer value.

Key Responsibilities

Portfolio Strategy & Business Leadership

Drive and execute the long-term multi-year growth strategy for the RUGGEDCOM portfolio, aligned with Siemens business objectives.
Oversee overall portfolio performance, including revenue growth, profitability, market share, and return on investment.
Drive accountability for annual strategy development, operating plans, and portfolio investment decisions.
Identify and pursue growth opportunities through new markets, applications, technologies, partnerships, and acquisitions.
Product Lifecycle Management
Oversee end-to-end product lifecycle management—spanning requirement definition, R&D alignment, rigorous testing, and commercial release.
Establish and maintain market-leading product roadmaps informed by customer needs, technology trends, and competitive analysis.
Align investments and resources across the portfolio to maximize business value and customer impact based on long-term strategy.
Drive product launch excellence, lifecycle optimization, and effective management of product transitions, obsolescence planning, and portfolio rationalization.
Customer and Market Leadership
Serve as the executive voice of the customer, building strategic relationships with key utilities, EPCs, system integrators, channel partners, and industry stakeholders.
Represent RUGGEDCOM at executive customer engagements, industry forums, and strategic business reviews.
Translate market intelligence, competitive dynamics, and emerging technologies into actionable portfolio opportunities.
Cross-Executive & Operational Leadership
Build, coach, and develop a high-performing, diverse global organization.
Influence and partner with R&D leadership to align product development priorities with business objectives.
Collaborate with sales, marketing, operations, and supply chain teams to optimize product availability, cost competitiveness, lifecycle sustainability, and market penetration.
Develop business cases and investment proposals, managing key portfolio KPIs (revenue, margin, growth, market share, product vitality, and customer satisfaction) while ensuring optimized product costing.

Required Qualifications

Master’s degree preferred (minimum Bachelor's) in Engineering, Computer Science, Business, or a related discipline.
15+ years of experience in industrial technology, networking, telecommunications, automation, software, or adjacent domains, anchored by expertise in communications infrastructure, automation systems, or cybersecurity.
10+ years of leadership experience spanning Product Management, Product Lifecycle Management, Portfolio Management, or General Management.
Proven track record of leading product portfolios to drive sustained business growth across multi-market environments.
Expertise in shaping winning product strategies and driving high-impact technology roadmaps from conception to market success.
Proven ability to lead cross-functional teams and align executive stakeholders.
Strong financial and business acumen.

Preferred Qualifications

Demonstrated experience navigating harsh operational technology (OT) environments where rugged communications infrastructure is foundational.
Deep understanding of the competitive landscape within industrial networking and customer challenges.
Experience supporting critical infrastructure industries including utilities, transportation, mining, oil & gas, and defense.
Knowledge of utility communications, IEC 61850, cybersecurity, industrial Ethernet, or mission-critical networking technologies.
Track record of successfully leading organizational transformation and portfolio modernization initiatives.

jobs.title: Director of Marketing
jobs.description:
About Bells Of Steel Inc.

At Bells of Steel, our mission is to make fitness and strength training approachable, affordable, and fun. We design and manufacture high-quality strength and exercise equipment for home gym owners and fitness professionals, helping people of all experience levels achieve their goals.

We’re not your typical fitness equipment brand. We’re down-to-earth, a little cheeky, and focused on making fitness more rewarding and less intimidating. If you enjoy a fast-paced, no-BS environment and want to help shape the future of strength training, you’ll fit right in.

Our Core Values: A.C.T.

Adaptability – Raise the Bar

We challenge the status quo, learn quickly, and continuously improve. We embrace change, seek better ways of working, and take initiative to drive results.

Customer Centricity – Always Spot the Customer

Everything we do is focused on helping our customers succeed. We lead with empathy, build trust through action, and create value for both external and internal customers.

Teamwork – We Win Together

We operate with honesty, transparency, trust, and respect. We collaborate openly, take shared ownership of outcomes, and succeed as a team.

About Bells Of Steel Inc.

We’re a rapidly growing e-commerce company that designs and sells strength equipment across Canada, the USA, the UK, Australia, and now Europe, starting with Germany. We compete with the biggest names in the industry by moving fast, listening to customers, and building products that punch above their weight.

Our purpose is to make strength training accessible to all, and have fun doing it. Our 10-year target is 1 million customers made stronger, and over the next three years we’re growing to $50 million USD in annual revenue.

As we continue to grow, we're looking for a Director of Marketing

to own how Bells of Steel reaches, wins, and keeps customers in every market we serve.

This is a strategic leadership role responsible for deciding where we show up, what we say, and how every marketing dollar earns its place.

You'll own our marketing strategy, brand positioning, channel and campaign calendar, paid media strategy, creative strategy and testing, and the marketing Scorecard. You'll work closely with our founder, e-commerce, product, sales, customer service, finance, and our international teams to turn great products into growth.

You'll lead a marketing team of about 16 people across marketing operations, retention, affiliates and partnerships, social and community, creative and video, and paid search and paid social. You don't need to do it all yourself, but you need to be strong enough in each area to coach your channel owners and hold them to a high standard.

This is an AI-first role

. Over your first year, you'll lead an AI transformation across marketing: upgrading and replacing manual workflows with AI, and working with our in-house developers to build our own tools that outperform the paid software we use today.

If you're someone who reads a Scorecard like a story, moves budget toward what works and away from what doesn't, and can build a brand that real lifters trust, we'd love to meet you.

This is a hybrid role based in Calgary, with about half your time in the office and half working from home. Your office days are where the best marketing happens: in the photo studio for a shoot, on the showroom floor talking to customers, walking over to the product team to plan a launch, and lifting on the equipment you're selling.

Relocation support is available for the right candidate.

What You'll Be Doing

Marketing Strategy & Brand Positioning

Own the 1–3 year marketing strategy, tied to our company goals of $50M USD revenue by 2029 and 1 million customers made stronger.
Own our brand positioning across every market, built on our three uniques: maximum training value per square foot, function over hype, and real people with real strength.
Grow our reach with former lifters, practical beginners, parents, and professionals without losing the core lifters who built the brand.
Make sure our customer journey, from discovery to setup to training, and our 30-day money back guarantee show up consistently in every customer touchpoint.

Leadership

Lead, coach, and develop the Marketing team (~16 people) using EOS principles.
Create clarity around priorities, accountability, and execution, with KPIs for every seat.
Give every Quarterly Goal a definition of done, milestones and an owner at the start of the quarter.
Bring in outside experts where we are weak, and check their work before it ships.
Build a high-performing team capable of making excellent marketing decisions without constant executive involvement.

AI Transformation

Work AI-first, and set the standard for how the marketing team uses AI to plan, create, analyze, and report.
Lead a 12-month AI transformation across marketing: map every manual workflow, then upgrade it or replace it with AI.
Partner with our in-house developers to build internal tools that work better than our paid SaaS stack, and retire subscriptions once the replacement is proven.
Measure the results in hours saved, output per person, and software spend cut, and report them on the marketing Scorecard.
Coach every member of the team to work AI-first, and develop an AI champion within marketing.

Paid Media Strategy

Own paid media strategy across Google, Meta, Amazon, Reddit, and display.
Set targets for return on ad spend, acquisition cost, and new customer growth, and hold channel owners to them.
Make sure creative, landing pages, and offers work together from the first click to checkout.

Scorecard, Performance & Budget

Own the marketing Scorecard and adjust strategy based on results.
Set clear targets for every channel, benchmark against the industry, and dig into the stories behind the numbers.
Set and allocate the marketing budget and resources for the best return, and cut what isn't working quickly.
Write the rules for when we scale spend and when we stop it, and make a documented budget decision every week.
Work alongside Finance and Leadership on budgeting, forecasting, customer acquisition cost, and profitability.

Creative Strategy & Testing

Own creative strategy and run a standing testing program. Every test has a written hypothesis, a result and a decision, reported weekly on the Scorecard.
Set the weekly ad output target and hit it.
Own landing pages for paid traffic: build new pages for key products and campaigns, A/B test them, and report conversion rate by page.
Turn reviews, support tickets and community threads into new ad angles every month.
Stay ahead of the craft. Follow the podcasts, newsletters, creators and competitor ad libraries where new formats show up, and get the promising ones into test within weeks.

Channel & Campaign Calendar

Set our channel strategy across paid media, email and SMS, affiliates and creators, social, YouTube, community, and showrooms.
Own the annual marketing calendar and our Annual Playbook, keeping revenue teams aligned on a shared campaign cadence planned 12 months ahead.
Lead our major promotions (BFCM and more) and product launches with Product, E-Commerce, and Sales.
Own marketing results in each international market (UK, Australia, Germany, France), with a Scorecard row per market.
Make marketing for each market, not copies of North American ads: local creators, local spelling and units, local homes and seasons, local offers and delivery promises.
Own local marketing for each showroom.

What You Bring

You have your own active strength training routine and lift weights regularly
5+ years of marketing experience at a direct-to-consumer or e-commerce brand.
5+ years of experience managing people/leading a team.
An AI-first way of working. You use AI every day, have used it to replace manual work, and would rather build better tools than buy more software.
Experience building multi-year marketing strategies and brand positioning that drove measurable growth.
Hands-on depth in paid media (Google, Meta, Amazon) and a strong grasp of ROAS, CAC, LTV, and attribution.
You still open the ad account yourself. You can find a problem in Ads Manager without waiting for a report.
You have built and A/B tested landing pages and can show the results.
Experience running email and SMS, affiliate and creator, social, and content programs, and an understanding of how they work together.
Strong analytical skills. You build and read dashboards, understand the stories behind the numbers, and make budget decisions from data.
Strong creative judgment. You know great creative when you see it and can lead a creative team toward it.
Excellent leadership skills. You enjoy coaching teams, making decisions, and creating alignment across departments.
Comfortable making difficult prioritization decisions with imperfect information, following 80/20 and iterating quickly.
Experience marketing in more than one country, with creative made for each market, is strongly preferred.
Willing to travel for trade shows, content shoots, showrooms, and our international markets.

What's In It For You

Competitive salary ($110k-$145k)
Health Spending Account
Hybrid schedule: 3 days/week in a Calgary office you'll actually want to come into, the rest from home
24 paid Fridays off per year
Relocation support for the right candidate ($15k)
Employee discounts on all our equipment + $3k Home Gym Credit
2% RRSP or TFSA matching
Access to our staff gym
Opportunity to lead marketing for one of the fastest-growing strength equipment brands in the industry as it expands internationally

Equal Opportunity

Bells of Steel is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to building a diverse, inclusive workplace. If you require accommodation during the hiring process, let us know—we're happy to help.

The Pay Range For This Role Is:

110,000 - 145,000 CAD per year(Calgary)

Why You’ll Love Working Here

About Us

As Canada’s # 1 retailer of cell phones, The Wireless Kiosk @ Costco operates in every Canadian warehouse coast-coast. Our highly trained kiosk Advisors provide unbiased solutions  to some of the most engaged, affluent and loyal consumers in the country. So, it stands to reason that if we are serving the best of the best clientele, we only hire the best of the best leaders to run our business.

Director Role

Lead leaders. Shape culture. Drive transformation. Build the future!!

We view performance results as an OUTPUT.

OUTPUTS are delivered through actions, behaviors and activity – which we call INPUTS

Too often, we see sales associates and sales managers chasing outputs, which are sometimes known as KPI’s and pushing employees into “closing” customers. We have also seen that this “push” promotes solutions that do not fit what the customer actually needs. This short-term thinking approach we view as unsustainable and does not promote medium to long term growth

Our view is based upon focusing on INPUTS and we are strong believers that if you do the right thing, with the right people, in the right way, at the right time – you will invariably get the right result – the OUTPUT. We also strongly believe that OUTPUTS driven by proper INPUTS, provide the foundation for sustainable on-going growth.

The Director of Retail Operations is a leadership role which requires the right candidate to be able to operate both strategically and tactically (based upon the needs of our business) and is responsible for executing our operational go to market strategy.

Our team across the country is 600+ strong and they are the backbone of our operations. You will be responsible for leading our Western Canadian employees and growing our business through INFLUENCE, building CONSTITUENCY and showing your IMPACT through superior EXECUTION.

The key to winning at retail is the quality of our front-line people. Finding, recruiting, training and successfully onboarding is the foundation of any retailer’s success. This requires us to have hiring clarity on the profile of individual that we are looking for as well as determining who is a suitable candidate and who is not. We have found that this is key to developing and properly casting new hires into roles that match their strengths.

You will report into the Senior Director of Operation and be responsible for leading our business in 40+ locations and will be supporting 3 District Managers. This role requires you to be accountable for creating a high-performance culture where behaviors, execution and results are aligned. You will support our over-arching strategy and with the help of your leadership team, execute the tactical plan developed. You will drive organizational effectiveness (and change, where required) and ensures the creation of sustainable success by developing a strong leadership bench, identifying future talent, and guiding your teams through cyclical periods of growth, transformation, and change.

The ideal candidate must be influential and has impact when they communicate and are able to build constituency with other stakeholders and who can balance strategy with high levels of execution. The ideal candidate will also be able to challenge the status quo, can make difficult decisions, and inspire others to embrace change, while remaining focused and true to the execution of our strategy and operational plan.

What You Will Shine At

Leading and developing a team of District Managers and field leaders across a large and complex geographic region.
Driving organizational performance through strategic execution, accountability, and operational excellence.
Building leadership capability at all levels through coaching, mentorship, and succession planning.
Identifying opportunities to improve productivity, effectiveness, and business outcomes across the region.
Creating a culture of high performance, continuous improvement & accountability
Developing and executing talent strategies that attract, retain, and advance top performers.
Challenging leaders to think differently, improve execution, and raise performance standards.
Strengthening partnerships with Costco leadership through credibility, trust, and a shared commitment to delivering a world-class member experience.

Who You Are

You have 10+ years of progressive leadership experience leading large, multi-site teams through other leaders.
You have a proven track record of improving business performance through people, process, and execution.
You are an exceptional “change leader” who can create alignment, navigate ambiguity, and help teams embrace new ways of working.
You have successfully led organizational transformations, restructures, large-scale business initiatives, or performance turnarounds.
You are skilled at developing District Managers, senior leaders, and high-potential talent.
You hold leaders accountable while maintaining engagement, trust, and strong working relationships.
You inspire trust, create followership, and lead with integrity.
You have demonstrated success building leadership pipelines and developing future-ready organizations.

Your Playground

How You’ll Stand Out

Applicants should be prepared to:

Share examples of leading through significant organizational change while maintaining employee engagement and business performance.
Demonstrate how they have improved underperforming regions, districts, or business units.
Describe how they have built leadership capability and prepared future leaders for advancement.
Showcase examples of transforming team culture and creating sustainable accountability.
Explain how they have influenced senior stakeholders and aligned diverse teams behind a common vision.
Illustrate their approach to succession planning, talent reviews, and leadership development.
Share examples of making difficult decisions that strengthened long-term organizational effectiveness.

Benefits That Actually Matter

Total compensation package - $180K - $200K+
Excellent extended health benefits

This role is eligible for a discretionary variable compensation award that considers business and individual performance.

 Job Description: 
 Department Overview

 Global Technology & Solutions (GTS) enables the Bank’s strategy by delivering enterprise technology that supports clients and colleagues, protecting TD through strong fraud, cyber, technology, and physical security controls, enabling agility in response to evolving client needs and market dynamics, and supporting the delivery and execution of work across the organization. GTS is central to how TD modernizes, innovates, manages risk, and delivers secure, reliable, and differentiated experiences.

 Team Overview

 The GTS Strategy and Insights team helps shape where GTS goes next—and how we tell that story. We support GTS’ most senior technology leader and leadership team by developing fact-based analysis, executive-ready narratives, presentations, memos, and insights that help drive alignment and support decision-making for audiences including the Chief Executive Officer, the Senior Executive Leadership team, and the Board of Directors.

 The AVP - GTS Strategy and Insights will lead a team responsible for executive deliverables, strategic planning, enterprise and industry research, executive communications, and performance reporting against GTS priorities. The team sits same organization as Change Management, Communications, and Colleague Engagement, creating strong alignment between strategy, messaging, adoption, and colleague experience to ensure priorities are translated into clear narratives, practical change plans, and measurable business outcomes.

 Job Description

 Reporting to the Head, Strategy and Insights, Product Owner & Analyst Practices the successful candidate will lead the GTS Strategy function and will be accountable for influencing and shaping Senior Executive and Board-level content while overseeing the team’s day-to-day operations and delivery of high-quality analysis, insights, and strategic materials.
 This role is ideal for someone who can operate at the intersection of strategy, technology, and communication—understanding complex technology and business issues, identifying what matters, and translating that thinking into clear recommendations and executive-ready narratives.

 Key accountabilities include: 

 Lead all strategy-related deliverables required through enterprise processes or as directed by ESVP Global Technology and Solutions, ensuring each is grounded in evidence, aligned to GTS priorities, and positioned to support executive decisions.
 Lead the development, planning and communication of strategic narratives, insights, and recommendations that influence Executive and Board discussions, build alignment, and advance GTS' strategic priorities (e.g., Executive level presentations, memos, briefings and other materials for GTS Senior Leadership, Board, and/or Governance forums).
 Set the standard for clear, fact-based, outcome-oriented materials that simplify complex technology, workforce, financial, cyber, data, artificial intelligence, delivery, and regulatory topics for senior executive audiences.
 Responsible for leading the development and refresh of GTS’ short, medium, and long-term strategy, and priorities, translating strategic direction into actionable focus areas, investment ideas, and measurable outcomes.
 Develop insights on strategic issues facing GTS, including technology modernization, software delivery, artificial intelligence adoption, workforce transformation, productivity, cyber resilience, data and cloud, cost management, and regulatory priorities.
 Serve as GTS’ technology research lead by continuously drawing on external sources, including articles, books, podcasts, research, industry forums, and expert perspectives—to proactively identify leading-edge insights from across the technology and financial services landscape, raise critical awareness, and translate relevant insights into strategic deliverables, team priorities, and investment choices.
 Own performance reporting and executive insights for GTS priorities, ensuring timely, accurate, and data-driven assessment of strategic, transformation, financial, workforce, and operational outcomes to support informed decision-making and accountability.
 Drive alignment on GTS strategic priorities by influencing senior stakeholders, resolving cross-functional dependencies, surfacing risks and opportunities, and providing actionable recommendations that support executive decisions and drive measurable business outcomes.
 Lead the Strategy & Insights function, establishing priorities, allocating resources, managing strategic risks and dependencies, and ensuring successful delivery of key commitments.
 Lead, coach, and develop a high performing of team of strategy and insight specialists while fostering an inclusive and collaborative culture.

 Job Requirements

 Required: 

 Demonstrated ability to influence Senior Executives and support complex strategic decisions.
 Experience translating industry trends and external research into strategic recommendations and business outcomes for SVP+ level audiences.
 Strong analytical, problem-solving, and strategic thinking capabilities.
 Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including development of executive and Board-level materials.
 Strong business acumen and understanding of technology's role in driving enterprise outcomes.
 Proven ability to synthesize complex technical, financial, and strategic information into clear, compelling messages for senior executive and Board level audiences.
 Strong understanding of technology transformation, software delivery, artificial intelligence-enabled ways of working, data, cyber, cloud, infrastructure, digital tools, and the role of technology in enabling business strategy.
 Proven ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, workback plans, and senior stakeholder expectations in a fast-paced and ambiguous environment.
 Exceptional relationship-building, collaboration, and influencing skills, with a proven ability to align diverse stakeholders, build trusted partnerships, and drive outcomes across functions and leadership levels. Strong business acumen, with the ability to connect technology priorities to enterprise strategy, customer outcomes, colleague outcomes, risk, and financial performance.
 Experience leading teams and building high-performing, inclusive cultures.

 Preferred: 

 Experience in software engineering, technology delivery, technology strategy, architecture, product, data, cyber, or a related discipline.
 Consulting experience, particularly in strategic messaging, executive communications, technology strategy, or enterprise transformation.
 Experience supporting the Chief Executive Officer, senior executive leadership team, Board of Directors, or equivalent senior governance forums.
 Demonstrated strategic curiosity and insight, leveraging external trends, competitive intelligence, and emerging technologies to challenge thinking, shape priorities and inform GTS strategy and decision-making.
 Proven experience translating market, competitive, and technology insights into strategic recommendations that inform investment decisions, transformation priorities, and operating model evolution.

 Additional Information

 This role offers the opportunity to work directly on the strategic agenda for a large, complex technology organization; influence executive and Board-level materials; lead a small, high-performing team; and help GTS make clearer choices about where to focus time, talent, and resources.

 Who We Are: 
 TD is one of the world's leading global financial institutions and is the fifth largest bank in North America by branches/stores. Every day, we strive to make every interaction, product, and experience remarkably human and refreshingly simple for over 27 million households and businesses in Canada, the United States and around the world. More than 95,000 TD colleagues bring their skills, talent, and creativity to foster deeper relationships, ensure disciplined execution, and build a simpler, faster banking experience. TD is deeply committed to being a leader in client experience, that is why we believe that all colleagues, no matter where they work, are client facing. Together, we are reimagining what banking can be for our clients, colleagues and communities. 

 Our Total Rewards Package

Total Rewards at TD includes a base salary, variable compensation, and several other key plans such as health and well-being benefits, savings and retirement programs, paid time off, banking benefits and discounts, career development, and reward and recognition programs.  Training & Onboarding

jobs.title: Director of Operations & Development – SAPA Canada (Toronto)
jobs.description:
ABOUT SAPA CANADA

  

SAPA Canada is an independent Canadian charity that works alongside the Sudanese American Physicians Association (SAPA) to fund its work. SAPA is a physician\-led humanitarian organization that in 2025 treated 750,000 patients and served 3\.1 million meals in Sudan, Chad and Uganda, in the places most other organizations have left. Every SAPA site is run by Sudanese doctors, nurses and volunteers, nearly 2,000 of them, working in their own country under fire.

  

SAPA Canada has its own board, its own governance and its own charitable registration. It sets its own direction in Canada and chooses what it funds; its support reaches SAPA's hospitals, clinics and kitchens through funding agreements that SAPA Canada's board approves. It is in its first full year of operation, with a Year 1 operating budget approved, a growing Canadian donor base, and a Toronto/GTA Community Partnerships \& Fundraising Officer being recruited now.

  

The Executive Director leads SAPA Canada alongside a senior role in SAPA's global team. This hire is the person who runs SAPA Canada day to day: the organization needs someone whose whole job it is.

  

THE ROLE

  

The Director of Operations \& Development is SAPA Canada's most senior staff member and runs the organization day to day. You report to the Executive Director and work closely with the SAPA Canada board.

  

You own two things: that SAPA Canada is run properly as a Canadian charity (compliance, finance, governance, systems), and that it raises money in Canada (donors, campaigns, grants, and the community fundraising program). You will be the first person in this seat, so you build much of it: policies, processes, the donor pipeline, the reporting rhythm.

  

This is a builder's role in a small organization with a large mission behind it. The programs SAPA Canada funds are already running at scale; your job is to grow the Canadian side so it can fund more of them.

Run the charity


* Own CRA compliance end to end: T3010 annual return, official donation receipts, books and records, disbursement rules, and the reporting that comes with funding programs outside Canada.


* Manage finance with the bookkeeper and auditor: monthly close, cash flow, the Year 1 budget and the Year 2 budget you will build, grant and funding\-agreement reconciliation, and audited statements.


* Put the operating backbone in place: financial and HR policies, insurance, banking, donor database (Salesforce, shared with SAPA), document management and the systems a growing team needs.


* Draft and administer the funding agreements through which SAPA Canada funds SAPA programs, and the reporting that goes back to Canadian donors on how their money was used.

  

Raise money in Canada


* Build and run SAPA Canada's annual fundraising plan: individual giving, monthly donors, Ramadan and year\-end campaigns, and the stewardship that keeps donors giving.


* Manage the Toronto/GTA Community Partnerships \& Fundraising Officer and, as the team grows, further officers in other Canadian cities.


* Open institutional funding: foundations, corporate partners, and government programs where SAPA Canada is eligible.


* Hold a portfolio of major and mid\-level Canadian donors yourself, with the Executive Director on the largest relationships.


* Report monthly to the Executive Director and quarterly to the board on funds raised, pipeline, costs and what is planned.

  

Governance and the board


* Serve as board secretariat: agendas, papers, minutes, resolutions, filings, and the annual general meeting.


* Keep the board's compliance calendar and make sure every filing, renewal and policy review happens on time.


* Support the Executive Director in board recruitment and orientation.

  

Lead the team


* Recruit, manage and develop SAPA Canada staff and contractors as the organization grows.


* Work with SAPA's Global Communications \& Fundraising team on brand, campaigns, content and the donor database, so Canadian donors get the same quality of communication as everyone else and SAPA Canada never duplicates work that already exists.


* Represent SAPA Canada with partners, donors, sector bodies and government when the Executive Director does not.

  

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN YEAR ONE

  

Targets are agreed with you in your first 60 days. What we expect to see:


* 90 days: you know the books, the filings and the donor base; the compliance calendar exists; the Toronto/GTA Officer is onboarded and in market; a Ramadan 2027 plan is ready.


* Ramadan (Feb 8 to Mar 9, 2027\): SAPA Canada's first full Ramadan campaign delivered, online and in person, with every donor receipted and thanked within the month.


* 6 months: monthly financial close running on time; a Year 2 budget in front of the board; first institutional funding applications submitted; funding agreements with SAPA in place and reported on.


* 12 months: T3010 filed and audit clean; a growing monthly\-donor base; a documented donor journey from first gift to major gift; a second Canadian market scoped; and an organization that runs for a month without the Executive Director in the room.

  

WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR

  

Someone who has run a Canadian charity, or a significant part of one, and wants to build the next one from the ground up for Sudan.

  

You must have:


* Five or more years in Canadian nonprofit leadership or senior management, with direct responsibility for finances and compliance.


* Working knowledge of CRA requirements for registered charities: T3010, receipting, books and records, and the rules for funding activities outside Canada through qualifying or non\-qualifying donees.


* A fundraising record you can describe in numbers: campaigns run, donors grown, grants won.


* Experience managing a budget of at least several hundred thousand dollars, including working with a bookkeeper and auditor.


* Experience working with and reporting to a bo

jobs.description:
About the Company

Vercity

About the Role

Vercity is seeking an experienced Director, P3 Compliance & Asset Management to support the management and performance of operational Public-Private Partnership (P3/PPP) infrastructure projects. This is a senior, client-facing role for an individual who understands how P3 projects operate beyond the contract itself. The successful candidate will work across Project Company, Authority, FM provider, lifecycle, technical and commercial stakeholders to support contractual compliance, operational performance, effective governance and long-term asset outcomes. The role requires someone who can interpret complex Project Agreement requirements, understand their practical operational implications, identify emerging risks and work collaboratively with stakeholders to resolve issues before they escalate.

Responsibilities

Provide senior P3 asset management and compliance oversight across operational infrastructure projects.
Monitor performance against Project Agreement requirements, contractual obligations and governance processes.
Support Project Company in managing interfaces with Authorities, FM providers, lifecycle providers and other project stakeholders.
Review operational performance, contractual compliance, reporting and emerging project risks.
Support the interpretation and practical application of Project Agreements, FM agreements and related project documents.
Oversee and challenge FM performance, lifecycle planning and asset management activities where appropriate.
Monitor contractual notices, deductions, performance failures, relief events, variations and other compliance matters.
Support governance forums including operational meetings, management committees and escalation processes.
Identify areas of contractual, operational or asset risk and develop practical mitigation strategies.
Support lifecycle planning, asset condition, capital investment and longer-term handback/expiry readiness.
Prepare clear reporting and recommendations for Project Company boards, investors and senior stakeholders.
Work collaboratively with Vercity's broader asset management, technical and advisory teams.

Qualifications

P Eng. or relevant designation with 5-10 years experience managing P3 Assets and or commercial agreements.

Required Skills

The ideal candidate will have:

7+ years of relevant experience, preferably involving Canadian P3/PPP infrastructure.
Strong knowledge of the operational phase of P3 projects.
Experience administering, interpreting or working directly with Project Agreements and associated FM contractual structures.
Experience in asset management, facilities management, contractual compliance, Project Company management or infrastructure advisory.
Understanding of performance regimes, payment mechanisms, deductions, lifecycle obligations and contractual reporting.
Strong commercial judgement and an ability to distinguish contractual requirements from practical operational solutions.
Experience working with multiple stakeholders including public-sector authorities, developers/investors, Project Companies, FM providers and technical advisors.
Strong written communication, reporting and presentation skills.
The confidence to challenge constructively while maintaining effective long-term stakeholder relationships.
Ability to work independently and manage multiple projects and priorities.

Preferred Experience

Experience across one or more Canadian P3 sectors would be particularly valuable, including:

Healthcare
Justice and courthouses
Transportation
Education
Government and civic infrastructure
Other social infrastructure

Experience with lifecycle management, asset condition, performance monitoring.

The Person We're Looking For

This position will suit someone who is comfortable moving between the contract, the asset and the people responsible for delivering it. You should be commercially aware, pragmatic and capable of seeing the bigger picture while still understanding the detail behind contractual obligations and asset performance. Most importantly, we're looking for someone who can build credibility with clients and project stakeholders, take ownership of complex issues and help move projects toward practical, sustainable outcomes.

Why Join Vercity?

This is an opportunity to take a senior role supporting some of Canada's important infrastructure assets while working within a specialist infrastructure advisory and asset management business. The position provides exposure across multiple projects and stakeholders and the opportunity to contribute to Vercity's continued growth in the Canadian infrastructure market.

**Our Firm**


Asset Management Services (“AMS”) is the asset management practice of Agentis Capital Advisors, a global infrastructure advisory and investment platform. AMS manages more than 120 infrastructure assets representing over $35bn in enterprise value across renewables, public\-private partnerships, digital and social infrastructure. We support our clients over the life of their assets through four service pillars:

* Financial Model Management – We build, standardize, enhance and maintain the financial models behind our clients’ funds and portfolio companies
* Financial Services Management – We run the accounting, budgeting, lender compliance and financial reporting for project companies
* Operations Management – We oversee the day\-to\-day management of assets, including contract administration, performance monitoring, and board and stakeholder support
* Fund Operations \& Reporting – We maintain the fund\-level valuation models, NAV and exit calculations, and leadership and LP reporting


AMS gives private markets and infrastructure investors one consistent, auditable and trusted view of their portfolios, delivered as a managed service. Our clients include leading infrastructure funds, pension funds, developers and project companies. Our guiding principles of excellence, client success, commitment, people and entrepreneurship set us apart.

Private\-markets managers and large asset owners run their portfolios on hundreds of inconsistent models, built by different advisors in different formats. **Join a Challenger**  

  

At EQ, we're remaking banking so every Canadian gets ahead, every day. Serving nearly 4 million Canadians from coast to coast, we offer a wide variety of financial services from banking and lending, to trust and credit union solutions.  

  

We've been at this since 1970, challenging the conventions of traditional banking with smarter, faster, and more connected financial experiences.  

  

**What's kept us moving?** The people behind it all: challengers who ask better questions, push back on old assumptions, and look for a better way forward.  

  

If you're driven to help reshape how banking works for Canadians and the businesses that power our economy, this could be your next big opportunity. We can’t wait to get to know you!  

  

We can’t wait to get to know you!**The Work**
------------

  


The Senior Director, Growth and Franchise Value provides strategic leadership for the agenda to deepen relationships across Personal Banking’s combined customer franchise, spanning EQ Bank customers and PC Financial customers. The role establishes the Personal Banking approach to franchise value creation, including customer segmentation and lifetime value economics, joint value propositions and bundled offers, and channel strategy for customer growth. Working across Product, Marketing, Analytics, Loyalty, Digital and Operations, the Senior Director mobilizes cross\-functional execution and is accountable for delivering the relationship deepening and franchise growth outcomes established through the annual plan.



### **Main Activities:**

* **Franchising strategy:** Establishes and leads the multi\-year Personal Banking franchise value strategy across the combined EQ Bank and PC Financial ecosystems. Converts strategic ambition into an integrated portfolio of priorities, targets and investment choices aligned with product leaders and embedded in the annual business plan.
* **Segmentation and customer value:** Sets the strategic framework for cross\-product segmentation and customer lifetime value, identifying priority segments and directing growth investment toward opportunities with the strongest long\-term franchise economics while balancing customer value, acquisition cost and returns.
* **Plays, offers and journeys:** Provides strategic direction for franchising propositions, bundled offers and end\-to\-end customer journeys, including onboarding and early\-life experiences. Establishes targeting and offer principles within approved investment parameters to strengthen relationship depth and customer value.
* **Next\-best\-offer:** Serves as the senior business owner for the next\-best\-offer roadmap, defining strategic priorities, decision rules and business requirements for propensity and decisioning capabilities developed by Analytics, and championing adoption across channels.
* **Program delivery:** Leads the program through cross\-functional teams spanning Analytics, Marketing, Product and Digital. Establishes governance, prioritizes the highest\-value opportunities, drives disciplined test\-and\-learn execution, and ensures successful initiatives are scaled based on demonstrable incremental impact.
* **Franchise performance:** Establishes the performance framework for franchise value, including measures, baselines and management insights. Reviews performance through Personal Banking objectives and key results and quarterly business reviews, identifies emerging opportunities or performance gaps, and recommends corrective actions and investment shifts.
* **Marketing technology and data:** Sponsors the business vision and requirements for marketing technology, decisioning, journey orchestration, data and reporting capabilities required to enable a scalable next\-best\-action and offer decisioning engine, working closely with Business Enablement Technology and Digital.
* **People leadership:** Builds and leads a high\-performing team spanning strategy, channel, offer and analytics capabilities. Sets a clear mandate and priorities, develops leadership capability and succession depth, and manages resources and budget to deliver the function’s objectives.
* **Risk and compliance:** Ensures growth strategies, customer targeting and communications operate within regulatory requirements, privacy and consent obligations, and the Bank’s risk appetite. Engages Risk, Compliance, Legal and Privacy early to enable responsible, sustainable growth.

* Bachelor’s degree in business, commerce, economics, marketing or a quantitative field required; MBA or CFA designation preferred.
* 10\+ years of progressive experience in customer strategy, customer value management or cross\-sell, marketing strategy, product management or management consulting, preferably in financial services, retail or loyalty; including 5\+ years leading teams of managers and professionals.
* Demonstrated success growing multi\-product customer relationships, embedding segmentation and lifetime value models in business decisions, and building programs at scale.
* Customer segmentation and lifetime value modelling; experimental design (test\-and\-control); customer relationship management, marketing automation and decisioning platforms; journey orchestration; business intelligence tools; agile ways of working; advanced Excel and PowerPoint.

**Highclere Capital Corporation:**  

Director AML, Compliance \& Project Management
  
**Location:** Hybrid \| Department: Compliance\| Employment Type: Full\-Time
  
About Highclere Capital
  
Highclere Capital is a growing, Ontario\-based mortgage finance company focused on providing innovative lending solutions to underserved borrowers across Canada. With a sharp eye on compliance, service excellence, and responsible growth, we partner with mortgage professionals to deliver tailored financing with speed and integrity. As a remote\-first team, we’re building a culture rooted in accountability, collaboration, and a shared commitment to doing the right thing, for our brokers, our partners, and one another.
  
About the Role
  
As a member of the leadership team, the Director, AML, Compliance \& Project Management will lead Highclere’s regulatory compliance and AML/ATF programs while driving projects that strengthen governance, operational integrity, and business efficiency.
  
This position is both strategic and hands\-on, requiring the ability to interpret complex regulatory requirements, assess organizational risk, lead cross\-functional initiatives, and embed a culture of compliance and continuous improvement throughout the business.
  
Core Responsibilities
  
AML/ATF \& Sanctions Oversight
  
* Develop, implement, and maintain Highclere’s AML/ATF and Sanctions Program, including policies, procedures, and internal controls, in alignment with FINTRAC guidelines and the PCMLTFA.
* Oversee and manage outsourced AML/ATF service provider relationships, ensuring appropriate oversight, reporting, and testing.
* Conduct annual AML/ATF risk assessments, gap analyses, and program self\-assessments.
* Monitor changes in legislation, trends, and risks, and update programs accordingly.
* Liaise with regulators, industry associations, law enforcement, and internal/external auditors on all AML/ATF matters.


Regulatory Compliance
  
* Develop and maintain the corporate compliance framework, ensuring all regulatory requirements are identified, interpreted, and implemented across the business.
* Advise the Leadership Team and business units on compliance risks, policy interpretation, and remediation strategies.
* Lead the preparation for regulatory reviews/audits and ensure timely resolution of findings.
* Support ongoing training for employees on compliance and AML/ATF obligations.


Project Management
  
* Lead cross\-functional projects related to compliance, AML/ATF, and corporate priorities, ensuring initiatives are delivered on time and within scope.
* Project manage senior leadership meetings, including agenda development, materials preparation, action tracking, and follow\-up.
* Partner with business leaders to assess and manage the regulatory and operational impacts of new products, services, or process changes.
* Implement and monitor project plans, reporting progress, risks, and outcomes to senior leadership and the Board where required.
* Drive continuous improvement by embedding project management discipline, clear accountability, and technology\-enabled solutions across compliance and corporate processes.


Leadership \& Reporting
  
* Provide regular compliance and AML/ATF metrics, trends, and risk indicators to the Leadership Team and Board.
* Act as a trusted advisor to senior leadership, fostering a culture of ethical behaviour and risk awareness.


Skills \& Experience
  
Must\-Have Qualifications
  
* 8 \- 10 years in AML/ATF compliance in financial services, with direct experience in Canadian regulatory frameworks.
* Proven experience managing compliance programs, regulatory interactions, and third\-party service providers.
* Recognized AML certification (e.g., CAMS) preferred.
* Bachelor’s degree in business, law, or a related discipline.
* Demonstrated leadership in implementing compliance or AML frameworks from the ground up.
* Strong technical acumen, with the ability to leverage compliance technology platforms, data analytics tools, and digital workflows.
* Excellent communication, presentation, and relationship management skills.


Nice\-to\-Have
  
* Experience in mortgage lending, underwriting, or related credit risk functions.
* Exposure to sanctions screening systems and automated compliance tools.
* Experience leading multi\-departmental projects or technology implementations.

National Bank of Canada is building a unified Global Transaction Banking (GTB) franchise that brings together transaction banking capabilities across Commercial Banking, National Client Group, Capital Markets, Product, Technology and Operations. Together, these platforms serve an expanding base of domestic and global clients across their working\-capital and treasury lifecycles.  

GTB’s ambition is to accelerate quality deposit growth, deepen primary client relationships, increase transaction banking revenues and deliver a differentiated, scalable and client\-led experience.  

As Vice\-President, Global Transaction Banking Sales, Commercial and National Client Group, you will lead the GTB sales franchise across Commercial Banking, including specialized sectors such as Real Estate, Technology, Creative Industries and Equipment Finance, as well as the National Client Group. You will play a pivotal role in shaping GTB’s next phase of growth, with responsibility for go\-to\-market strategy, business development, sales execution and the mobilization of coverage teams across the franchise.  

You will translate GTB’s strategy into clear segment priorities, market propositions and commercial plans; identify where the Bank can win; and build the disciplines, connectivity and talent required to convert opportunity into sustainable deposits, revenue and client primacy.  

This position could be based anywhere in Canada. **Your Job**  

* Own and execute the GTB sales Deposit and Cash Management strategy for Commercial Banking and National Client Group, translating enterprise priorities into clear go\-to\-market plans by client segment, industry, geography and relationship tier.
* Build and continually refine the GTB Deposit and Cash Management commercial proposition, including the client value proposition, coverage model, referral pathways, sales plays and market activation agenda.
* Lead business\-development agenda by identifying priority markets, sectors, prospects and client opportunities; setting target lists; and establishing disciplined account and pursuit plans.

jobs.description:
About our Client:
Build Canada Homes was established by the Government of Canada in September 2025 to scale up the delivery of affordable housing across the country. Its mandate is to increase housing supply by bringing together public land, flexible financing, and development expertise to deliver more affordable and non-market housing where it is needed most.

As a federal Crown corporation, BCH was created to respond to the scale and urgency of Canada’s housing challenge. It builds on existing federal capacity while introducing a more coordinated, delivery-focused approach—working in partnership across the housing system to move projects forward and deliver results for Canadians.

This role is offers a hybrid model. They currently work 2-3 days in office and potentially 4 days in the future.

Position Scope:

The Director, Financial Planning, Analysis and Corporate Reporting lead the delivery, coordination, and continuous improvement of financial planning, analysis, budgeting, forecasting, and corporate reporting activities across Build Canada Homes and its subsidiaries (collectively, the “Corporation” or “BCH”). The role is responsible for managing financial planning cycles, consolidating budget and forecast inputs, preparing financial analyses and performance reports, and delivering timely, accurate financial information that informs operational planning, resource allocation, funding decisions, and organizational performance monitoring.

The role collaborates with internal and external stakeholders to coordinate financial inputs, monitor results, analyze variances, prepare reporting materials, and maintain alignment with established financial policies, controls, reporting requirements, and governance expectations. The Director, Financial Planning, Analysis and Corporate Reporting role applies financial expertise to manage planning processes, identify financial risks and operational issues, improve reporting practices, and deliver reliable analysis within the assigned scope of Corporate Services and Corporate Finance, Treasury & Reporting.

Responsibilities:

FINANCIAL PLANNING, BUDGETING & FORECASTING

Leads the coordination and delivery of BCH’s budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning processes within assigned scope.
Develops planning calendars, templates, assumptions, and submission requirements to promote consistent and timely financial inputs.
Consolidates financial plans, forecasts, and budget submissions from internal stakeholders to prepare integrated financial outlooks.
Analyzes funding requirements, resource needs, and cost drivers to inform operational planning and funding allocation.
Performs sensitivity analysis and financial modelling.
Provides financial advice and interpretation to internal stakeholders on budget assumptions, planning inputs, cost pressures, and financial trends.

CORPORATE REPORTING, ANALYSIS, & PERFORMANCE INSIGHTS

Leads the preparation of financial reports, dashboards, briefing materials, variance analyses, and decision-support information for leadership review.
Prepares corporate reporting materials related to financial performance, funding, cost trends, and resource utilization.
Translates complex financial information into concise reports and presentations that support management review and operational decision-making.
Develops and maintains financial models, planning tools, and reporting templates to improve efficiency and analytical quality.

FINANCIAL CONTROLS, COMPLIANCE & CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT

Leads and supervises the team responsible for the accurate and timely recording of all corporate financial transactions, including corporate operating expenditures, capital expenditures, journal entries, and general ledger activities
Oversees month-end, quarter-end, and year-end accounting close processes, ensuring completeness, accuracy, and compliance with accounting standards and organizational policies.
Identifies and addresses financial control issues, reporting risks, data quality concerns, and process gaps, escalating matters where required.
Leads the annual external financial statements audit and coordinates with finance, corporate services, legal, auditors and other stakeholders to support financial reporting, compliance and regulatory requirements.
Leads continuous improvement of accounting, financial planning, analysis, reporting, and performance management processes to enhance efficiency, accuracy, transparency, and decision support.
Evaluates financial reporting processes to identify opportunities for automation, standardization, improved controls and reduce manual effort as BCH’s operating model evolves.

Qualifications and Experience:

Post-secondary degree or diploma in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, Commerce, Economics, or a related field.
Professional accounting or finance designation, such as CPA, CFA, or an equivalent designation.
Minimum 5-10 years of experience in financial planning and analysis, budgeting, forecasting, corporate reporting, management reporting, accounting, or related finance roles.
Experience leading financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, analysis, and reporting in a complex organization.
Experience preparing financial reports, dashboards, and briefing materials for senior leadership.
Experience managing teams, priorities, timelines, and deliverables.
Knowledge of accounting, financial controls, budgeting, reporting, and performance management.
Knowledge of real estate, housing, construction, investments, or corporate finance is an asset.
Experience working with internal and external stakeholders, including auditors and regulators.
Strong analytical, financial modelling, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office; experience with ERP, financial planning, and reporting systems is an asset.
