About The Role

Camunda is seeking a hands-on frontline sales leader to lead a team of approximately six Account Executives responsible for the Majors account base in the Americas—F1000 organizations. The leader will help build a high-performing team, grow strategic enterprise revenue, and execute a partner-led motion in a high-growth market. The opportunity is to sell Camunda’s value to the world’s largest organizations as they manage critical business processes.

This role combines people leadership, complex enterprise selling, partner ecosystem execution, product and industry fluency, and disciplined operating practices. The leader will own both net-new logo acquisition and account expansion across the team.

Why This Role Matters

Lead and develop a team selling to large, complex AMER enterprises.
Build a repeatable Majors sales motion with Global Systems Integrators (GSIs), including co-selling and reseller motions.
Help customers understand how Camunda supports critical business processes and how its capabilities fit within the broader BOAT landscape.
Partner with internal teams to identify solutions, product capabilities, and pricing strategies that can accelerate revenue.
Bring strong forecast discipline and consistent Salesforce hygiene to a high-value enterprise sales motion.

What You'll Be Doing

Team leadership and hiring

Manage and coach approximately six high-performing AEs focused on the largest companies in AMER.
Identify, recruit, hire, onboard, and develop AEs with consultative, value-based selling backgrounds.
Set a high-performance bar while building an environment suited to a high-growth company.

Enterprise selling and account growth

Lead the team’s net-new logo and expansion sales motions.
Coach AEs through complex, high-value sales cycles with large enterprise customers and technical buying groups.
Help the team connect customer priorities to the value of Camunda’s platform and solutions.

Partner-led selling

Implement the Majors strategy for selling with GSIs.
Coach the team to build pipeline and solutions with partners, co-sell, sell through reseller relationships, and coordinate effectively across partner teams.

Industry, product, and cross-functional leadership

Demonstrate thought leadership and a strong understanding of why Majors customers use Camunda to manage critical business processes.
Build fluency across relevant technology areas, including BPM, RPA, iPaaS, ETL/ELT, agents/agentic capabilities, cloud computing/infrastructure, APIs, and data storage.
Partner with internal cross-functional teams to identify and deploy solutions, product functionality, and pricing strategies that support revenue growth.

Operating excellence

Ensure strong Salesforce hygiene, including opportunity stages, MEDDPICC, account plans, contract values, and win/loss data.

What You Bring

Ability and/or willingness to use our product.
At least three years of frontline sales leadership experience in SaaS.
A track record of building, recruiting, hiring, and coaching successful sales teams in the Majors segment, with experience selling to accounts with $5B+ revenue.
Demonstrated leadership of teams selling to actual enterprise customers, including F1000 organizations and complex, large-deal environments. The job description cites deals in the $1M–$20M ARR range; assess the candidate’s specific role and deal context rather than relying on deal size alone.
Experience selling a technical software platform to technical audiences, such as CIOs, CTOs, and technical architecture stakeholders.
Ability to lead both net-new logo and expansion sales.
Understanding of the BOAT software category and adjacent technology areas, including BPM, RPA, iPaaS, ETL/ELT, agents/agentic capabilities, cloud infrastructure, APIs, and data storage.

Leadership attributes

Entrepreneurial and comfortable creating structure in a high-growth environment.
Creative, adaptable, and able to exercise strong EQ while building a team and sales motion.

jobs.description:
About The Opportunity

Our client, is seeking an experienced and technically driven Director of Development and Planning
to lead the planning, feasibility assessment, design development, budgeting and coordination of its real estate development projects.

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer (COO) and working closely with the Director of Construction, the successful candidate will oversee projects from initial conception through construction and completion. This role requires a strong technical background in architecture, engineering, construction management or a related discipline, combined with extensive experience managing residential and multifamily real estate development projects.

The ideal candidate is a strategic thinker with strong financial and project management capabilities who can coordinate multidisciplinary teams, manage complex budgets and ensure projects are delivered efficiently, on schedule and in accordance with established quality standards.

Duties include but are not limited to:

Lead development planning, project evaluations and feasibility assessments, including zoning requirements, site constraints, servicing capacity, construction costs and financial viability
Establish preliminary development budgets, project schedules, key milestones and development strategies
Oversee architects, engineers, urban planners, surveyors and other professional consultants throughout the design and development process
Coordinate architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical and civil engineering plans to ensure design accuracy, constructability and cost efficiency
Oversee municipal approvals, zoning applications, site plan approvals and building permit processes
Prepare, manage and monitor comprehensive development and construction budgets, identifying variances, potential cost overruns and opportunities for savings
Collaborate with the Director of Construction on tendering, subcontractor and supplier selection, procurement, purchase orders and contractual requirements
Monitor construction progress, schedules, milestones, quality standards and overall project performance in collaboration with the Director of Construction
Review change orders, trade performance, construction deficiencies and potential cost impacts
Review monthly construction draw reports, invoices, purchase orders, progress claims and supporting financial documentation
Monitor project expenditures, committed costs and forecasts to ensure accurate financial reporting and cost control
Prepare regular project status reports, development schedules, budget updates and recommendations for senior management
Identify and escalate project risks, delays, budget discrepancies and other issues requiring management attention
Coordinate project completion, occupancy approvals and closeout activities
Maintain effective communication and collaboration with the COO, Director of Construction, finance team, consultants, contractors, lenders and other stakeholders

About You

The successful candidate will have the following:

A strong educational background or professional training in architecture, civil engineering, structural engineering, construction engineering, construction management or a related technical discipline
A university degree or college diploma in a relevant technical field is strongly preferred
10-15 years of relevant experience in real estate development, construction project management, architectural or engineering coordination, or related project delivery functions
Demonstrated experience managing complex residential or multifamily development projects from initial planning through construction
Strong understanding of architectural and engineering drawings, construction methods, building systems, municipal approval processes and construction budgeting
Proven experience coordinating multidisciplinary professional teams, consultants, general contractors and subcontractors
Demonstrated ability to prepare, manage and monitor multimillion-dollar development and construction budgets
Experience with tendering, procurement, purchase orders, construction contracts, change orders and financial reporting
Strong knowledge of project scheduling, cost controls, construction draws and cost-to-complete forecasting
Excellent organizational, analytical, problem-solving, communication and leadership skills
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and project management software
Familiarity with AutoCAD, Revit, Bluebeam, MS Project or similar technical software is considered an asset
Experience with Ontario and/or Québec municipal planning, building approvals and regulatory requirements is considered a strong asset
Bilingualism in English and French is considered an asset

About the Job

This is an exciting opportunity to join a fast-growing company in a senior leadership role with direct involvement in the planning, financial management and execution of residential and multifamily real estate development projects.

Compensation Package:

Annual base salary starting from $100,000 commensurate with qualifications and experience
Eligibility for quarterly performance-based bonuses, subject to the Company's established bonus program
Performance bonuses may be assessed based on project milestones, budget management, municipal approvals, procurement performance, construction coordination, financial reporting and overall project execution

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to play a key role in the Company's development activities while working closely with senior management and construction leadership.

How To Apply

Please apply by clicking the “Apply Now” button below and follow the instructions to submit your résumé. You can also apply by submitting your résumé directly to jobs@clapersonnel.ca. If you are already registered with us, please contact your Senior Recruiter. Please quote job 19636
.

Each submission is reviewed by an experienced recruiter to ensure a thoughtful and equitable evaluation of every candidate.

Thank you for your interest in this role. One of our Recruiters will be in touch with you if your profile meets the requirements for the role and the expectations of our clients. Please note that all candidates must be permitted to work in Canada to be considered for this opportunity.

 The Regional Director of Investments is a senior investment leader responsible for enabling regional growth, strengthening Investment Counsellor and client-facing business development efforts, and ensuring our team delivers high-quality investment management, fiduciary oversight, and regulatory compliance across the assigned portfolio/jurisdiction.

 This role partners closely with Investment Counsellors, Market Leaders, other Regional Directors, and internal business partners to support growth objectives, deepen client relationships, improve sales effectiveness, and allow our team of professionals to deliver an exceptional client experience. The Regional Director of Investments brings technical investment expertise, strong judgment, and strategic leadership to help teams identify opportunities, prepare for prospect and client conversations, develop investment solutions, and execute business development strategies in a disciplined, compliant, and scalable way.
 The role also provides guidance on regional performance, investment governance, portfolio oversight, reporting, change management, training, and strategic initiatives that support client, business, and enterprise priorities.

 Key Accountabilities 

 Business Development & Growth Enablement 
 Actively supports regional and market-level business development efforts by partnering with Investment Counsellors, Market Leaders, Relationship Managers, and other business partners to identify growth opportunities, strengthen referral activity, and improve prospect conversion.
 Develops and maintains strong internal and external networks and referral sources to support growth across the assigned portfolio or jurisdiction.

 Investment Leadership & Technical Expertise

 Governance, Risk & Compliance

 Reporting, Analytics & Business Insights

 Breaks down complex business problems and uses data and insights to provide practical, action-oriented recommendations.

 Change Management, Training & Enablement 
 Leads and supports change management initiatives, including readiness assessment, planning, stakeholder engagement, communication, execution, evaluation, and sustainment.
 Oversees the design, development, and implementation of tools, training, frameworks, and communications required to deliver business results.
 Identifies business needs and designs or delivers training programs to support investment professionals, client-facing teams, and regional leaders.
 Leads communication strategies that positively influence behaviour, drive adoption, and improve consistency of messaging across teams.
 Collaborates across BMO to align communications, tools, training, and business development support.

 Stakeholder Leadership & Collaboration 
 Builds effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders and ensures alignment across teams.
 Fosters strong internal and external networks and works across multiple teams to achieve business objectives.
 Influences how teams and groups work together to support client outcomes, business growth, and operational effectiveness.
 May consult to or serve on committees, task forces, governance forums, or strategic working groups.
 Acts as a senior specialist resource across the enterprise and contributes thought leadership on investment, business development, and regional growth priorities.

 Operational & Program Leadership 
 Leads or participates in the design, implementation, and management of core business and group processes.

 Reporting directly to th CISO, The Director, Cybersecurity Program Management leads the planning, governance, and delivery of the organization’s cybersecurity program. Reporting directly to the CISO, this role translates security strategy into an integrated portfolio of initiatives with clear priorities, accountable owners, budgets, milestones, and measurable outcomes. The Director works across Cyber, IT, Risk, Compliance, and business teams to resolve dependencies, manage delivery risks, and ensure security investments address business and regulatory priorities.

 This is a delivery-focused leadership role requiring direct involvement in execution, issue resolution, and stakeholder management, alongside accountability for program governance and performance.

 You’ll partner closely with IT, Cyber Ops, DevOps, Risk, and Compliance to strengthen our security posture and ensure it remains scalable, resilient, and aligned with business priorities.

 What You’ll Do 

 Minimum of 10 years of professional experience in financial services or the financial industry is required, including substantial responsibility for cybersecurity, technology, risk, or transformation program delivery.

 Demonstrated experience leading a cybersecurity program or portfolio, with accountability for delivery planning, governance, resources, executive reporting, and outcomes.

 Proven ability to manage multiple complex cybersecurity initiatives simultaneously and resolve cross-functional dependencies in a regulated environment.

 Experience managing program budgets, delivery forecasts, vendors, and internal or external delivery teams.

 Experience working with CISOs, senior IT leaders, business executives, Risk, Compliance, Internal Audit, and control owners.

 Understanding of financial industry regulatory expectations, audit processes, risk management, and the evidence needed to demonstrate remediation.

 Project or program management certification, such as PMP or PgMP, is preferred. Cybersecurity certifications such as CISSP, CISM, or CRISC are an asset.

 Knowledge and experience with NIST framework

 What You’ll Bring to the Table 

 Strong program and portfolio management skills, including prioritization, planning, dependency management, financial oversight, issue resolution, and benefits tracking.

 Sound understanding of cybersecurity concepts, controls, governance, and operational priorities, with the ability to translate technical issues into business decisions.

 Executive communication and facilitation skills, including concise reporting on risk, delivery progress, investment needs, and decisions required.

 Ability to hold stakeholders accountable, negotiate priorities, and influence delivery across teams outside the direct reporting line.

 Hands-on leadership style, with the judgment to address execution details while maintaining visibility of the overall program.

 Strong analytical, organizational, and people leadership skills, supported by proficiency with project tracking, reporting, and collaboration tools.

 Preferred Background 

 Experience leading cyber transformation, security improvement programs, regulatory remediation, or enterprise security initiatives within financial services. Experience building program governance and delivery practices and presenting to executive, risk, or security committees is particularly valuable.

 What Success Look Like 

 Cybersecurity priorities translate into funded, achievable delivery plans with clear ownership, milestones, and measurable outcomes.

 The CISO/CTO and governance committees have reliable visibility into program performance, financial position, risk, and decisions required.

 Delivery risks and dependencies are identified early, corrective actions are implemented, and material issues are escalated promptly.

 Audit and regulatory commitments are delivered with appropriate evidence and validation; completed initiatives transition effectively to operational owners.

 Education + Experience 

 Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or a related field required; Master’s degree preferred.

 Relevant certifications are highly valued (AWS Certified Security – Specialty, CISSP, CISM, OSCP, GSEC, etc.).

 Experience working in regulated industries (finance, fintech, or similar) strongly preferred.

jobs.title: Director, Cash Management
jobs.description:
Job Description 

 What is the opportunity? 
 This Director-level position provides strategic leadership and operational oversight for cash management operations supporting RBC's global Capital Markets and Retail nostro accounts. The role combines deep technical expertise in intraday liquidity risk management with leadership capabilities to manage complex stakeholder relationships across Corporate Treasury, trading desks, operations teams, and external financial market infrastructures. The incumbent is responsible for ensuring operational excellence in daily cash positioning, developing and maintaining contingency playbooks, and establishing robust measurement and monitoring frameworks that support regulatory compliance and enterprise liquidity risk management objectives.

 What will you do? 

 Intraday Liquidity Management & Operations 
 Provide strategic oversight and direction for the monitoring of cash flows as they relate to trades, transactions, and payments required for accurate positioning, forecasting, and funding of nostro accounts globally under prescribed guidelines and procedures
 Ensure operational capabilities for frequent monitoring of payment and settlement flows during the day while managing the timing of liquidity outflows where possible, including real-time monitoring and escalation procedures to Designated Liquidity Managers
 Demonstrate ability to identify and estimate unsettled items through intraday nostro reconciliation to determine additional intraday liquidity requirements at any point in time
 Monitor and track all time-sensitive payments (TSP) throughout the day and ensure timely settlement, including managing delays or promoting payments to improve intraday liquidity position with FMIs as permitted
 Monitor cash balances at FMIs to ensure positions remain within both maximum long and short intraday position limits where established
 Oversee daily maximum intraday liquidity usage observation and reporting to oversight functions within reasonable timeframes
 Lead the compilation of cash flow forecasts for funding and intraday collateral needs, demonstrating capabilities to forecast key intraday liquidity risk items for large time-sensitive payments

 Risk Management & Controls 
 Act as subject matter expert for FMI relationships, including FMI operating procedures, rule books, credit requirements, and understanding of business line FMI usage in support of Recovery and Resolution requirements
 Identify cash flow errors or potential value at risk to the Bank and manage to resolution or escalate to senior management with clear recommendations
 Ensure monitoring and management of intraday liquidity resources made available to resolve intraday demands, including demonstrating ability to transfer cash from central bank accounts or pledge/lodge collateral at discount windows
 Maintain reporting to show available cash or collateral at the start of the day and real-time if requested to oversight functions
 Oversee the monitoring of total value of time-sensitive payments settled each day and the timing and recurrence of material TSP
 Ensure compliance with prescribed risk appetite requirements, limits, and thresholds; report and escalate excesses to any established metrics in a timely manner

 Strategic Planning & Contingency Management 
 Maintain the operational aspects of intraday FMI playbooks to document scenario and procedural response strategies and escalation of intraday events in times of stress in coordination with local and enterprise Liquidity Contingency Plans
 Lead the development of contingency playbooks and support asset monetization strategies to ensure timely access to liquidity resources
 Provide leadership in the review and acknowledgment of liquidity stress testing and parameter documents as subject matter expert prior to GRM review and approval
 Support Corporate Treasury and Capital Markets Treasury in establishing appropriate liquidity buffers for intraday liquidity risk based on stress parameters

 Stakeholder Management & Reporting 
 Deliver high-quality subject matter expertise to Retail and Capital Markets teams in relation to projects and ad hoc requests involving the funding and liquidity of nostro accounts
 Effectively interact with and provide leadership engagement with TS Funding & Liquidity Trading Desk, Account Managers, Branches, Trading Operations staff, and correspondent banks in the handling and resolution of inquiries and discrepancies
 Update and deliver daily and monthly reports to Traders, Corporate Treasury, Capital Markets Treasury, and senior management in a timely manner
 Provide data to support the monitoring, measuring, and reporting of material intraday liquidity risk exposures potentially on a real-time basis as agreed with Corporate Treasury
 Lead/coordinate efforts with IT partners and Model Development Owners to ensure supplied data is accurate and complete

 Systems & Process Improvement 
 Apply expert knowledge of Treasury Operations systems (CLM, IntelliMatch, Rimm, RATS, Prowide, BESS) and external systems (CDSX, CARS, LYNX, ACSS) to effectively calculate and manage the bank's current, overnight, and forward positions
 Lead the identification of departmental system or process changes to streamline and improve service and efficiency
 Identify service gaps provided by Cash Management to internal clients as well as service gaps from correspondent banks and make recommendations to senior management for improvement
 Support the process of creating, updating, and maintaining desk procedures and operational documentation

 Leadership & Team Development 
 Provide leadership and direction to cash management teams, fostering a strong commitment to teamwork, open two-way communication, and positive staff morale
 Ensure strict adherence to policies and regulatory requirements across the team
 Uphold the reputation of RBC and Operations at all times and ensure timely escalation of operational risk or loss events, control deficiencies, and risks

 Regulatory & Compliance 
 Ensure compliance with OSFI Liquidity Adequacy Requirements Chapter 7 - Intraday Liquidity Monitoring Tools and all applicable regulatory requirements
 Participate in the review of the material FMI list and provide relevant attestations as outlined in policy requirements
 Support regulatory submissions and intraday liquidity reporting requirements

 What do you need to succeed? 

 Required: 
 10+ yrs of experience with advanced understanding of Cash Management processes, procedures, and intraday liquidity risk management principles
 Extensive knowledge of Capital Markets and banking operations/trading activity
 Deep understanding of market infrastructure including Settlement Agents, Nostro Agents, Clearing Houses, and Large Value Payment Systems
 Comprehensive understanding of operational risks, impacts, and controls in a capital markets environment
 Proven leadership experience managing complex operational processes and teams
 Strong knowledge of BCBS Principles for Sound Liquidity Risk Management and OSFI regulatory requirements

 Preferred: 
 Professional designation (CTP, CFA, FRM) or equivalent advanced degree
 Experience with regulatory stress testing and recovery/resolution planning
 Background in both Capital Markets and Retail banking operations
 Experience managing relationships with central banks and major FMIs

 What’s in it for you? 
 We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual. 
 A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits, competitive compensation, commissions, and stock where applicable
 Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team
 Opportunities to do challenging work

 Access to a variety of job opportunities across business and geographies

jobs.title: Director, Portfolio Management
jobs.description:
WHY JOIN US?

At AstraZeneca, we are dedicated to being a Great Place to Work, where you are empowered to push the boundaries of science and unleash your entrepreneurial spirit. With an ambitious goal of delivering 20 new medicines by 2030, there is no better place to make a difference in medicine, for patients, and in society.

Join us on this exciting journey to pioneer the future of healthcare. Our inclusive culture champions diversity and collaboration, and we are always committed to lifelong learning, growth, and development. As part of our team, you'll contribute to groundbreaking advancements that will shape a healthier future for people everywhere. Be a catalyst for change at AstraZeneca, where your work will have a real impact on improving people's lives.

Recognizing the importance of individualized flexibility, our ways of working allow employees to balance personal and work commitments while ensuring we continue to create a strong culture of collaboration and teamwork by engaging face-to-face in our offices 3 days a week
. Our head office is purposely designed with collaboration in mind, providing space where teams can come together to strategize, brainstorm and connect on key projects.

About AISI

AstraZeneca AI for Science Innovation (AISI) is driving the convergence of artificial intelligence and life sciences at enterprise scale. AISI brings together data foundations, AI and machine-learning technology, strategic partnerships, process reinvention, and business-facing AI to accelerate drug discovery, development, and delivery. Success depends on connecting and scaling existing capabilities, promoting reuse, and translating innovation into measurable scientific, patient, and enterprise value.

The Opportunity

The Director, Portfolio Management will lead the design, governance, and continuous improvement of AISI's portfolio management capability across strategic initiatives, AI and data platforms, external partnerships, projects, suppliers, managed services, and operational investments. The role ensures that strategy is translated into an executable portfolio, investments and resources are directed to the highest-value opportunities, delivery performance is transparent, and financial and operational risk, and compliance governance are embedded throughout the portfolio lifecycle.

Operating at the intersection of AISI leadership, scientific and therapeutic-area stakeholders, Data Science, Engineering, Finance, Procurement, HR, and external partners, the Director will establish scalable ways of working, strengthen evidence-based decision-making, and deliver outcomes through cross-functional teams and managed-service providers. The role sits within AISI Operations and reports to the Head of AISI Operations.

Scope And Core Accountabilities

Portfolio Strategy, Planning, and Governance

Translate AISI strategy and scientific priorities into an integrated portfolio of investments, initiatives, platforms, products, partnerships, and operational services.
Establish and continuously improve demand intake, assessment, value-based prioritization, funding, resource allocation, stage-gate review, delivery assurance, and benefits-realization processes.
Maintain an integrated portfolio view, identifying opportunities to stop, sequence, accelerate, consolidate, reuse, or scale initiatives as priorities and evidence evolve.
Lead portfolio governance forums and provide clear executive reporting on investment, demand, delivery health, dependencies, risks, issues, decisions, capacity, financial performance, and expected value.
Develop standardized dashboards and management information that enable timely, transparent, evidence-based decisions without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.

Financial and Investment Management

Partner with Finance and senior leaders to manage long-term investment planning, business cases, budgets, forecasts, and Run and Change expenditure.
Oversee forecast-versus-budget analysis, variance management, accruals, cross-charges, resource recharges, purchase orders, and supplier-related financial commitments.
Ensure financial information is accurate, timely, transparent, and connected to portfolio priorities, delivery milestones, and benefits realization.
Define and track financial and non-financial value measures, including scientific impact, speed, adoption, reuse, risk reduction, productivity, and enterprise scalability.

Operating Model and Process Excellence

Design and evolve the portfolio operating model, decision rights, governance forums, escalation pathways, and RACI frameworks required to manage a complex, global portfolio.
Drive standardization, simplification, automation, and continuous improvement across portfolio, project, financial, supplier, contracting, resource, onboarding, and service-management processes.
Introduce fit-for-purpose Agile, Lean Portfolio Management, Design Thinking, incremental delivery, and hybrid governance practices where appropriate.
Ensure processes are practical, adopted, and supported by reliable data and fit-for-purpose tools, including ServiceNow, Azure DevOps, and portfolio or financial-management platforms.

Partnership, Contracting, and Supplier Governance

Provide end-to-end portfolio oversight of strategic alliances, AI and data partnerships, technology providers, suppliers, and managed services.
Partner with Legal, Procurement, Finance, Privacy, Information Security, and technical leaders across the contracting lifecycle, from intake, due diligence, term-sheet development, and negotiation through execution, performance review, renewal, and exit.
Implement supplier and partner governance through scorecards, service-level agreements, periodic business reviews, delivery-quality measures, commercial-health monitoring, risk mitigation, and value-for-money assessments.
Ensure partner commitments, dependencies, milestones, financial obligations, and benefits are integrated into portfolio planning and reporting.

Resource and Capacity Management

Lead resource and capacity-management practices across projects, products, platforms, partnerships, and operational services.
Oversee workforce planning, allocation, utilization, people recharges, onboarding, and prioritization of scarce scientific, AI, engineering, and portfolio-management capabilities.
Work with functional leaders to identify capability gaps, resolve constraints, improve onboarding, and align internal and external capacity with strategic priorities.

Risk, Compliance, and Delivery Assurance

Establish portfolio-level approaches to risk, issue, dependency, assumption, and decision management, ensuring material concerns are identified early, escalated appropriately, and managed through resolution.
Provide oversight of scope, schedule, cost, quality, benefits, adoption, operational readiness, and delivery performance across the portfolio.
Ensure portfolio activities and external arrangements comply with relevant pharmaceutical and technology requirements, including data governance, GDPR and privacy, information security, intellectual property, procurement, ethical, quality, and regulatory frameworks.
Anticipate and manage delivery underperformance, supplier failure, commercial disputes, IP complexity, changing priorities, financial pressure, data and technology dependencies, and regulatory constraints.

Stakeholder Engagement and Change Enablement

Build trusted relationships with AISI and Enterprise AI leaders, therapeutic and scientific areas, Data Science, Engineering, Finance, Procurement, Legal, HR, Operations, and external partners.
Facilitate alignment on priorities, investment choices, delivery expectations, trade-offs, and accountabilities across a global matrix organization.
Communicate complex portfolio, financial, commercial, and delivery matters clearly to senior leaders and diverse stakeholder groups.
Champion adoption of portfolio standards, transparent governance, and collaborative delivery while preserving the speed and experimentation required for AI innovation.

Leadership

Lead and develop high-performing portfolio management, governance, and business-operations capabilities, directly and through matrix teams and managed-service providers.
Create a culture of accountability, collaboration, customer focus, continuous improvement, reuse, and measurable value delivery.
Set clear standards and build scalable capabilities from the ground up, enabling consistent ways of working across functions and geographies.
Contribute to AISI functional strategy and operating model evolution as the organization, technology landscape, and partnership ecosystem mature.

Essential

Qualifications and Experience

Bachelor's degree in business, technology, finance, life sciences, project management, law, data science, or a related discipline; a Master's degree or equivalent extensive professional experience is preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience across portfolio management, program or project management, business operations, financial management, alliance or partnership management, supplier governance, contracting, or a related discipline in a complex global organization.
Demonstrated experience leading portfolio management and process-transformation initiatives, including demand intake, value-based prioritization, governance, investment planning, resource allocation, delivery assurance, and benefits realization.
Strong financial acumen, including business-case development, long-term planning, investment tracking, forecasting, budget management, accruals, variance analysis, cross-charges, purchase orders, and resource recharges.
Experience managing suppliers, strategic partners, external collaborations, or managed services, including contracts, service levels, performance, commercial risk, value for money, and issue resolution.
Experience designing and implementing operating models, decision rights, governance forums, processes, RACI frameworks, dashboards, and management information.
Proven success influencing senior leaders and delivering through cross-functional teams, matrix structures, third parties, and managed-service providers.
Ability to operate with limited direction in ambiguous, fast-moving environments and make sound decisions that balance scientific and strategic value, risk, cost, capacity, compliance, and delivery feasibility.
Exceptional written, verbal, influencing, relationship management, and organizational skills.

Desirable

Experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, healthcare, life sciences, or another highly regulated technology environment.
Working knowledge of AI and machine-learning ecosystems, data partnerships, cloud platforms, digital products, technology platforms, and platform-based delivery models.
Understanding of pharmaceutical research and development and how AI, data, platforms, and external partnerships create scientific and competitive advantage.
Experience establishing or scaling portfolio management, alliance management, PMO, or business-operations function.
Experience with Agile, Scrum, SAFe, Lean Portfolio Management, Waterfall, Design Thinking, or hybrid delivery approaches.
Experience with ServiceNow, Azure DevOps, and comparable portfolio, project, financial, procurement, or service-management tools.
Knowledge of data governance, privacy, information security, intellectual property, quality, regulatory compliance, and IT risk management.
Professional qualifications such as PMP, PRINCE2, MSP, Scrum, SAFe, or equivalent portfolio, program, commercial, or supplier-management credentials.

Leadership Capabilities

Strategic thinking: Connects scientific and enterprise strategy to investment choices, delivery priorities, and measurable value.
Enterprise perspective: Optimizes across the portfolio, promotes reuse and scalability, and avoids isolated solutions.
Execution discipline: Establishes clear governance and follows through to achieve reliable delivery and benefits realization.

jobs.description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What You'll Be Doing

Our product team brings together business, data, and technology expertise to deliver meaningful solutions that create value for clients and the business. As a Senior Director, Product Owner, you'll set the vision and direction for your Squad, ensuring priorities align with Crew strategy and broader organizational goals. You'll develop and manage a strategic product roadmap, translate complex business and client needs into clear backlog priorities, and lead release planning to deliver impactful outcomes. You'll work closely with partners across Crews, Squads, and business units to manage dependencies, resolve issues, and keep delivery on track in a complex environment. You'll also help strengthen product practices by mentoring other Product Owners, championing continuous improvement, and promoting delivery excellence across teams.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. You'll have the flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you'll spend 1-3 days per week on-site, while other days will be remote.

How You'll Succeed

Product strategy and vision - Set and champion the Squad’s vision, goals, and priorities, ensuring alignment with Crew strategy and broader business objectives. Build and communicate a strategic product roadmap that maximizes client and business value.
Backlog and delivery leadership - Build, prioritize, and manage a complex Squad backlog by translating business and client needs into actionable user stories and requirements. Lead release and delivery planning, assess outcomes, and reprioritize work to respond to changing needs.
Risk and dependency management - Anticipate, navigate, and resolve risks, issues, and dependencies across Squads and business units. Ensure work is delivered within established frameworks, guardrails, and compliance requirements.
Cross-functional collaboration - Partner with Crew Leads, Crew Technology Leads, Chapter Leads, Agility Coaches, Squad members, stakeholders, and external partners to drive progress and achieve shared outcomes. Build strong relationships across teams to support decision-making and delivery.
Thought leadership and continuous improvement - Provide mentorship to other Product Owners and share best practices that strengthen product delivery across teams. Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that enhance efficiency, effectiveness, and product outcomes.

Who You Are

You act like an owner. You thrive when you're empowered to take initiative, go above and beyond, and deliver results.
Your influence makes a difference. You know that relationships and networks are essential to success. You inspire outcomes by sharing your expertise.
You give meaning to data. You enjoy investigating complex problems and making sense of information. You communicate detailed information in a meaningful way.
You embrace and advocate for change. You continuously evolve your thinking and the way you work in order to deliver your best.
You can demonstrate experience in product ownership, strategic roadmap development, backlog management, agile delivery, stakeholder management, and navigating complex cross-functional dependencies in data, technology, or analytics-focused environments. It’s an asset if you bring experience in decision science, machine learning, optimization, product analytics, technical strategy, or consulting.
You have a degree/diploma in computer science, engineering, mathematics, statistics, economics, operations research, physics, or a related quantitative discipline. Equivalent experience is also valued.
You know that details matter. You notice things that others don't. Your critical thinking skills help to inform your decision making.
You live your values. You bring high standards, genuine care to your relationships, and want to grow with an employer that shares your values and brings out your best.

What CIBC Offers

jobs.description:
At eBay, we're more than a global ecommerce leader — we’re changing the way the world shops and sells. Our platform empowers millions of buyers and sellers in more than 190 markets around the world. We’re committed to pushing boundaries and leaving our mark as we reinvent the future of ecommerce for enthusiasts.

Our customers are our compass, authenticity thrives, bold ideas are welcome, and everyone can bring their unique selves to work — every day. We're in this together, sustaining the future of our customers, our company, and our planet.

Join a team of passionate thinkers, innovators, and dreamers — and help us connect people and build communities to create economic opportunity for all.

eBay is a global marketplace connecting millions of buyers and sellers across more than 190 markets. People come to eBay to discover unique and pre-loved goods, pursue their interests, and grow businesses. Our purpose is to connect people and build communities to create economic opportunity for all.

About The Team And The Role

Low Cost Shipping is a key strategic initiative focused on delivering a more affordable, competitive, and sustainable shipping experience for eBay and Depop customers. By employing lower shipping costs to offer compelling customer pricing, the initiative aims to drive adoption, influence customer behavior, and unlock new growth opportunities, all while strengthening operational efficiency and long-term unit economics.

This role leads the economic architecture of the low cost shipping business. You will own the business recommendation on pricing, subsidy, unit economics, contribution, and the economic conditions required to launch, expand, or change course.

The role sits at the intersection of customer behavior and physical network economics: understanding how cost changes with parcel flow and density, how buyers and sellers respond to price, and whether lower shipping prices create incremental marketplace activity rather than simply subsidizing existing transactions.

What You Will Accomplish

Manage the end-to-end economic model for low cost shipping, including partner rates, network costs, buyer pricing, subsidy, contribution, and fixed and variable investment
Understand economics at the level that decisions are actually made: by market, parcel flow, customer cohort, partner, and network stage rather than relying on blended averages
Define buyer-facing pricing and subsidy recommendations that balance adoption, incrementality, contribution economics, and the long-term path to structurally lower shipping cost
Establish the economic thresholds that determine when the business should STOP, SLOW, or EXPAND, including break-even volume, density, utilization, and subsidy requirements
Develop a deep understanding of price sensitivity, incrementality, cohort response, and experiment outcomes; continuously update the economic thesis as customer behavior becomes observable
Distinguish incremental marketplace value from shipment substitution. Determine whether pricing changes are creating incremental conversion, frequency, GMV, or low-ASP TAM rather than simply moving existing volume or buying adoption
Build scenarios and sensitivities that show how partner rates, flow mix, density, node utilization, customer behavior, and network design change the economics and required investment
Translate the analysis into clear business recommendations for senior leaders on pricing, investment, network expansion, partner economics, and market sequencing

What You Will Bring

Deep quantitative fluency and the ability to personally work through complex financial, operational, customer, and network data rather than relying solely on prepared analysis. SQL or equivalent analytical capability is strongly preferred.
Strong understanding of pricing, elasticity, experimentation, incrementality, unit economics, contribution economics, and sensitivity analysis
Experience building economic models where customer behavior and cost structure interact — ideally in marketplaces, logistics, transportation, consumer pricing, or another network business
Ability to distinguish correlation from causality and design or interpret experiments that can support pricing and investment decisions
Strong commercial judgment: able to translate detailed analysis into a recommendation, identify the few assumptions that actually drive the answer, and state what evidence would change the recommendation
Ability to challenge partner cost structures, operating assumptions, forecasts, and internally generated business cases rather than treating supplied inputs as fixed
Demonstrated ability to influence Finance, Product, Analytics, Growth, Operations, and senior leadership without direct authority
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience; advanced quantitative training is useful but not required

How We Will Measure Success

Success means we can answer, with increasing confidence: what does each parcel flow actually cost, what customer price changes behavior, how much subsidy is required, how much demand is incremental, and at what volume and density the network becomes structurally advantaged.

The role succeeds when better economics allow us to sustainably lower customer shipping prices and unlock incremental marketplace activity — not simply when low cost shipping volume increases or the modeled P&L improves.

Additional Details

C$142,000 - C$189,600

Base pay offered may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, including location, skills, and experience. The total compensation package for this position may also include other elements, including a target bonus and restricted stock units (as applicable) in addition to a full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits (including RRSP eligibility, various paid time off benefits, such as PTO and parental leave). Under the leadership of the Vice President, Relief, the Senior Director, Relief leads the development, quality standards and implementation of services that the Canadian Red Cross mobilizes during the immediate onset of an emergency operation in Canada. These services must be designed and implemented in consideration of the diverse nature of communities in Canada and in partnership with all levels of governments and authorities, inclusive of First Nation leadership.

In this role, you will:

Provide vision, strategic direction, oversight, and management of programs, ensuring alignment with the organization's mission, vision, and strategic priorities.
Develop and implement program strategies, including program design, planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation, ensuring adherence to organizational guidelines, and best practices.
Establish performance metrics and accountability frameworks to assess outcomes.
Review program performance and impact and use findings for program improvement, learning, and innovation.
Maintain strategic partnerships with stakeholders, including government agencies, NGOs, donors, and local communities, at national and international levels, to ensure effective coordination, collaboration, and support for program activities.
Ensure compliance with organizational policies, donor requirements, and accountability standards, and ensure appropriate risk management measures are in place for program implementation.
Lead strategic change initiatives that drive program and service transformation.
Provide leadership in emergency response and preparedness efforts, including providing technical expertise, and contributing to rapid assessments and decision-making and leadership to the field operations.

What we are looking for:

Qualifications include a minimum of 12 years experience and a university degree in social sciences, public administration, program management, business administration, human services or a related field and/or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Requires advanced expertise in strategic leadership, business growth, and organizational initiatives, with broad knowledge of diverse business issues, and involves coordinating leadership to set and achieve long-term objectives.
Leadership and senior management experience, with the ability to provide strategic direction, mentor and motivate a diverse team, and promote a culture of collaboration and innovation.
Experience leading multiple programs, service areas, or functional teams in a complex organizational environment with the ability to identify and implement best practices, pilot new approaches, and leverage technology and data for program impact.
Ability to develop, forecast and manage program budgets; implement, allocate and monitor expenditures; report on budget performance and variances to ensure financial accountability.
Experience optimizing operational processes and program efficiency.
Ability to address highly complex, abstract problems with visionary thinking, develop innovative solutions with long-term strategic impacts, and assess and mitigate risks.
Communication, influence, persuasion and negotiation skills to promote complex and sensitive ideas, facilitate consensus and commitment with strategically important contacts or groups in sensitive, contentious, and political or controversial situations.
Ability to establish and maintain strategic partnerships with government agencies, NGOs, donors, local communities, and to navigate complex political and cultural contexts.
Proficiency in standard computer applications (Microsoft Office Suite), data analysis tools, etc.

Working Conditions:

Ability to adapt to frequent and often urgent changes in priorities, and make decisions under pressure, work at an unpredictable pace.
Potential for responding to disaster areas, as well as difficult and unstable conditions (environmental, physical, social, etc.) and uncomfortable conditions (noise, odors, smoke, humidity, vulnerable beneficiaries). These stressful rapidly changing environments with limited information to make decisions have the potential to affect the physical and psychological state of the responders on site.
Will be required to work extended hours during peak periods on short notice.
In a large-scale emergency, provide direct operational leadership to field teams.
As we work with and support people (managers, colleagues, beneficiaries/customers, volunteers, donors and external partners) and communities in Canada and around the world, applicants whose first language is not English may be required to perform the responsibilities of the role in English.

You will own the firm's recurring deliverables end to end, from input collection and analysis through quality review and on-time release. You should be as comfortable in a financial model as you are mapping a process, writing an SOP or driving an open item to completion across teams.

jobs.title: Director of Business Development
jobs.description:
BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT DIRECTOR

Fort McMurray, Alberta

(Relocation Assistance Available)

About Fort Mcmurray Airport Authority (fmaa)

The Fort McMurray International Airport (YMM) is owned and operated by the Fort McMurray Airport Authority. YMM

connects the world to Fort McMurray Wood Buffalo. The airport is a major economic driver for the region, with an economic

impact of over $290 million, supporting 40+ businesses and 500 jobs on the airport campus.

In 1999, the Regional Municipality of Wood Buffalo (RMWB) created the Regional Airport Commission to take ownership of

the airport from the federal government. The Fort McMurray Airport was later incorporated as an Airport Authority in

December 2009. The first Airport Authority Board was formed in January 2010, to become the Fort McMurray Airport Authority

(FMAA). The newly formed organization acquired the airport from the RMWB.

Today, the FMAA is an independent not-for-profit non-share capital corporation which owns and operates the Fort McMurray

International Airport. FMAA provides critical transportation services, creating local jobs, procuring local goods and services

and offering commercial land leasing opportunities. All surplus revenue generated from commercial activities is reinvested

back into airport operations and infrastructure to ensure compliance with safety, security and environmental regulations.

About The Role

Reporting to the CEO, the Director, Business Development is responsible for identifying and advancing opportunities that

strengthen the Fort McMurray International Airport’s revenue, connectivity, and long-term sustainability. The Director will

lead business development activities across aviation and non-aviation revenue streams, including air service development,

commercial leasing, land development, concessions, advertising, parking, and strategic partnerships.

As part of a small and collaborative airport leadership team, the Director will work closely with Operations, Finance,

Infrastructure, Communications, and other functional areas to assess opportunities and move viable initiatives from concept

through negotiation and implementation. The role will also build productive relationships with airlines, tenants,

government, tourism organizations, economic development partners, Indigenous communities, and businesses throughout

the Wood Buffalo region.

The ideal candidate will be commercially minded, relationship-focused, and comfortable moving between strategy and

hands-on execution. They will understand how to develop a persuasive business case, negotiate agreements, manage

several opportunities at once, and represent the airport professionally within the community and aviation sector. Success

will require initiative, sound judgment, persistence, and an ability to identify practical opportunities that align with the

airport’s operational capacity, regulatory obligations, and community mandate.

Key Responsibilities

BUSINESS AND COMMERCIAL DEVELOPMENT

Develop and implement a business development strategy aligned with the airport’s strategic and financial priorities.
Identify new aviation and non-aviation revenue opportunities that support long-term financial sustainability.
Assess the commercial feasibility, financial return, operational impact, and strategic fit of potential opportunities.
Prepare business cases, market assessments, proposals, presentations, and recommendations for senior leadership and the Board.
Lead commercial negotiations and support the development of leases, licences, service agreements, and partnership arrangements.
Monitor market trends, competitive activity, regional development, and changes within the aviation sector.
Maintain a business development pipeline and provide regular reporting on opportunities, progress, risks, and results.

COMMERCIAL PROPERTIES AND REVENUE

Identify opportunities to increase revenue from airport land, terminal space, concessions, advertising, parking, and related services.
Market available commercial land and facilities to prospective tenants, developers, and business partners.
Support tenant attraction, lease renewals, expansions, and the ongoing development of the airport campus.
Build strong relationships with airport tenants and identify opportunities to improve services and commercial performance.
Review commercial agreements and recommend adjustments based on market conditions, performance, and organizational priorities.
Collaborate with Finance to develop revenue forecasts, pricing models, and return-on-investment assessments.

AIR SERVICE DEVELOPMENT

Build and maintain relationships with existing and prospective airline partners.
Identify opportunities to retain, restore, or expand passenger and cargo air services.
Develop route-specific business cases using passenger, market, economic, and community data.
Coordinate airline presentations, route development proposals, and airport familiarization activities.
Work with regional partners to demonstrate market demand and strengthen the airport’s value proposition.
Monitor passenger trends, airline performance, schedules, capacity, and regional travel patterns.
Support collaborative marketing initiatives that increase awareness and use of available air services.

PARTNERSHIPS AND STAKEHOLDER RELATIONS

Attend industry events, trade shows, conferences, and community activities.
Develop relationships with municipal, provincial, and federal government representatives and agencies.
Work with tourism, economic development, Indigenous, industry, and community organizations on shared priorities.
Identify grants, funding, sponsorship, and partnership opportunities that support airport development.

Fort McMurray Airport Authority (FMAA) Business Development Director

Act as a primary point of contact for prospective commercial partners and guide opportunities through internal review.
Promote the airport’s contribution to regional connectivity, economic development, employment, and investment attraction.

LEADERSHIP AND ORGANIZATIONAL SUPPORT

Contribute to strategic planning, annual business planning, budgeting, forecasting, and organizational reporting.
Establish measurable business development targets and monitor performance against approved plans.
Coordinate cross-functional project teams to evaluate and implement approved commercial initiatives.
Ensure business development activities comply with airport policies, contractual obligations, and applicable regulations.
Prepare reports and presentations for senior leadership, the Board, partners, and other stakeholders.
Manage external consultants, brokers, contractors, or service providers when required.
Provide leadership, coaching, and direction to assigned employees or project resources.
Perform other duties as required.

Skills And Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in business administration, Commerce, Marketing, Economics, Aviation Management, or a related field.
7+ years of progressive experience in business development, commercial management, economic development, real estate, tourism, transportation, or aviation.
Experience developing and implementing business development or revenue-generation strategies.
Demonstrated ability to identify opportunities, prepare business cases, and move initiatives from concept to implementation.
Experience negotiating commercial agreements, leases, partnerships, or service contracts.
Proven ability to develop productive relationships with businesses, government, community organizations, and senior decision maker stakeholders.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including proposal writing and executive-level presentations.
Ability to manage multiple projects and opportunities within a small, resource-conscious organization.
Strong judgment and ability to balance commercial objectives with operational, regulatory, and community considerations.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office, customer relationship management systems, and business reporting tools.
Airport, airline, transportation, commercial real estate, land development, or public-sector experience is preferred.
Knowledge of the Regional Municipality of Wood Buffalo, or resource-based regional economies is considered an asset.
Experience working with Indigenous communities and organizations is desired.
Ability to travel and attend occasional evening or weekend meetings and events.
Ability to obtain and maintain an Airport Restricted Area Identification Card and any other required security clearances.

We encourage interested candidates to apply through MNP’s official recruitment process. For more information about this opportunity or

to submit your resume in confidence, please contact Gena Griffin at gena.griffin@mnp.ca with FMAA BDD in the subject line. All inquiries

and applications will be handled with the highest level of confidentiality. We appreciate the interest of all candidates; however, only those

selected to move forward in the recruitment process will be contacted. To support a fair and confidential recruitment process, candidates

are asked to direct all inquiries through MNP and not contact Fort McMurray Airport Authority or its employees directly.

jobs.description:
Come make your difference in communities across Canada, where authenticity, trust and making connections is valued – as we shape the future of Canadian retail, together. Our unique position as one of the country's largest employers, coupled with our commitment to positively impact the lives of all Canadians, provides our colleagues a range of opportunities and experiences to help Canadians Live Life Well®.

At Loblaw Companies Limited, we succeed through collaboration and commitment and set a high bar for ourselves and those around us. Whether you are just starting your career, re-entering the workforce, or looking for a new job, this is where you belong.

Come make your difference in communities across Canada, where authenticity, trust and making connections is valued – as we shape the future of Canadian retail, together. Our unique position as one of the country's largest employers, coupled with our commitment to positively impact the lives of all Canadians, provides our colleagues a range of opportunities and experiences to help Canadians Live Life Well®.

At Loblaw Companies Limited, we succeed through collaboration and commitment and set a high bar for ourselves and those around us. Whether you are just starting your career, re-entering the workforce, or looking for a new job, this is where you belong.

Role Mandate

The Director, Technology & Transformation leads the technology and product capabilities that turn the Marketing & Brands vision into practical solutions and measurable business outcomes. This leader will shape and drive the technology roadmap, bringing hands-on technical depth, strong product instincts and a solution-focused approach to MarTech, AI and emerging technologies.

Leading Transformation Operations and Transformation Solutions, the Director will lead a motivated, accountable team and drive delivery across complex organizational boundaries. Working closely with Loblaw Technology & Analytics (LT&A), Loblaw Digital and business partners, this leader will own solutions from concept through adoption, influence delivery commitments and remove barriers to progress. The role complements enterprise technology teams while taking clear ownership of Marketing & Brands technology outcomes.

Core Responsibilities

Technology & Product Leadership: Translate business priorities into product and technology roadmaps; define the right solutions, evaluate build-versus-buy choices and technical trade-offs, and guide design, integration and delivery. Bring the technical depth to prototype, troubleshoot or build targeted solutions when needed.
Roadmap Execution & Accountability: Own roadmap milestones, priorities, dependencies and outcomes. Create urgency, resolve blockers, challenge delivery assumptions and hold teams and partners accountable for commitments, implementation and measurable results.
MarTech, AI & Innovation: Advance marketing platforms, data-enabled capabilities, automation and practical AI use cases. Evaluate new technologies, test solutions quickly and scale capabilities that improve marketing effectiveness, efficiency and customer experiences.
Cross-Functional Influence & Solution Delivery: Build commitment across LT&A, Loblaw Digital and business teams without direct authority. Articulate solution value, navigate competing priorities, secure decisions and resources, and drive partners toward shared delivery outcomes.
Transformation Operations & Solutions: Lead an integrated operating model across intake, prioritization, product ownership, solution development, delivery readiness and adoption. Establish clear roles, effective governance and visibility into performance without adding unnecessary process.
People Leadership & Change: Build trust through consistency, transparency and follow-through. Motivate and develop the team, raise performance standards, empower problem-solving and lead the people and process changes required for successful technology adoption.

Key Skills & Capabilities

Deep technical and product fluency across modern software platforms, integrations, MarTech ecosystems and AI-enabled solutions; able to get hands-on when needed.
Strong solution orientation, with the resourcefulness to turn ambiguous problems into practical, scalable solutions and completed outcomes.
Proven roadmap ownership and execution discipline across multiple complex workstreams and delivery dependencies.
Ability to influence, persuade and secure cross-functional commitments without formal authority, including in environments with competing priorities.
Commercial and product judgment to connect user needs, feasibility, adoption and technology investment to business value.
Motivating people leadership, with the ability to earn trust, coach talent, address performance and drive sustainable change.

Experience

8-10+ years of progressive experience in technology, technical product leadership, software delivery or technology transformation, including people leadership.
Demonstrated experience shaping, building or implementing technology products and solutions, with credible hands-on technical experience.
Experience delivering complex roadmaps through engineering, product and business partners, including teams outside direct reporting lines.
Experience with MarTech, enterprise platforms, automation, AI or related digital capabilities.
Experience leading teams through change, improving delivery performance and building a culture of ownership and accountability.

his position provides strategic and operational leadership for the organization’s application development, software engineering and application management capabilities. jobs.description:
About Earthdaily

EarthDaily is revolutionizing the way we understand and monitor our planet. Through cutting-edge Earth Observation technology and geospatial analytics, we provide unparalleled insights for industries ranging from agriculture to mining, insurance, and government intelligence. Our mission is to build the world’s most advanced change detection system to capture, analyze, and interpret global shifts in near real-time.

OUR CREW

Our global, distributed team represents a variety of business lines and is made up of business development, sales, marketing and support professionals, data scientists, software engineers, project managers and finance, HR, and IT professionals. We are currently looking for an experienced, Vancouver-based Director, Revenue Operations to join our crew!

READY TO LAUNCH?

Do you want to join the Revenue team at one of the most exciting space companies at the forefront of global change detection and monitoring? The Director, Revenue Operations will be accountable for supporting revenue generation and will own EarthDaily’s end-to-end revenue operations function. You’ll drive growth by building the conditions that make revenue predictable, scalable from a process and systems perspective, and efficient across all EarthDaily product markets. This is a Vancouver-based hybrid position that requires regular in-office work.

PREPARE FOR IMPACT!

Reporting directly to the Chief Revenue Officer as a member of the Revenue Team, the Director, Revenue Operations will work in close partnership with Finance, Marketing, Analytics and Data, and support teams. You’ll influence the full revenue generation lifecycle by understanding and analyzing each market and its revenue generation process, including the market’s level of maturity and market forces, pipeline generation, deal execution, pricing governance and forecasting accuracy. You’ll use those insights as inputs to scalable systems and processes that enable and unify our sales teams to perform and achieve revenue objectives at scale. You’ll provide insights on pricing and yield governance and oversee CRM and technology administration, forecasting and analytics, quota and commissions management, and workflow standardization, so the sales team’s day-to-day work is accurately tracked, efficiently executed and aligned with revenue objectives. Success requires the operational discipline and expert knowledge to impact revenue attainment through processes, systems, data and sales alignment.

Key Responsibilities

Revenue Operations Planning

Analyze and seek to understand the revenue growth strategies for each LoB aligned with goals, market opportunities, and product roadmap across all data and analytics products
Partner with the CRO and other executive/finance members to understand annual/quarterly revenue targets and consider revenue operations plans, resources, and processes required to achieve targets
Define and continuously refine revenue operations strategies/revenue engine across LoB verticals/customer segments and channels by understanding all sources of revenue including direct sales, partnerships, system integrators, consultancies, and other indirect revenue channels.
Collaborate with product and marketing to understand product positioning, pricing strategy, and demand generation activities that maximize revenue impact
Present new revenue operations yield opportunities to the CRO on an ongoing basis

Revenue Forecasting and Analytics

Own the revenue forecasting process, ensuring consistent methodologies, pipeline stage definitions, and reliable projections for executive and board-level reporting
Establish consistent forecast methodologies and pipeline stage definitions and lead quarterly revenue reviews with variance analysis
Partner with finance to maintain a single source of truth for revenue performance across the organization

CRM, Revenue Tools, and Workflow Standardization

Serve as the functional owner of CRM and revenue management platforms, ensuring accurate opportunity codification, pipeline integrity, data hygiene and synchronization across platforms
Design and implement standardized revenue workflows — covering lead-to-close, deal approvals, contract management, and renewals — with documented process playbooks
Identify and eliminate process gaps and workflow inefficiencies that create revenue leakage or slow deal cycles
Establish governance frameworks that ensure cross-team compliance with revenue policies and commercial standards
Leverage CRM and analytics tools to surface pipeline health, win/loss trends, and revenue concentration insights for leadership
Manage data accuracy and synchronization across third-party sales tools and internal platforms to ensure a single, reliable source of commercial truth

Revenue Optimization

Maintain an understanding of each LoB’s account portfolio – including customer goals, contract structures, buying patterns, and decision-making dynamics – to identify and suggest revenue maximization opportunities within the customer lifecycle
Review customer, partner, reseller agreements to ensure they are aligned with revenue operations objectives
Identify and develop tools and processes to operationally manage high-value prospects and new revenue channels
Work with the sales team to ensure complete and accurate use of systems and processes for efficient pipeline progression, deal support, and movement through the sales cycle across the commercial organization
Analyze and influence strategies to yield greater revenue within the existing customer base through processes, systems, data and sales alignment

Product Pricing

Develop and maintain the pricing policy framework, including list pricing structures, discount authorization levels, and yield optimization guidelines
Standardize pricing governance and deal approval processes to ensure margin integrity across all commercial transactions
Conduct regular yield reviews and implement corrective adjustments to address revenue erosion or market misalignment

Renewals and Marketing Operations Support

Oversee standards for renewals within revenue operations, ensuring structured timelines, clear accountability, and accurate tracking of renewal pipeline and outcomes
Support marketing by providing pipeline data, lead management process guidance, and commercial feedback to improve demand generation effectiveness

Commissions Program Management

Design, administer, and continuously refine the commissions and incentive compensation program to align sales behaviors including prospect to lead conversion for SDRs and revenue attainment for Account Executives and Commercial Directors
Ensure commission structures incentivize the right mix of new business, renewals, and expansion revenue in line with company growth priorities
Partner with finance and HR for accurate, timely commissions processing and conduct annual plan reviews benchmarked against market norms.

Team Leadership and Cross-functional Partnership

Build and lead a high-performing revenue operations team with a culture of data integrity, process discipline, and continuous improvement
Own the program to onboard new team members ensuring rapid immersion in tools, quotas, commissions, and process standards
Serve as the primary cross-functional partner to finance, legal, product, and marketing on all revenue operations matters

YOUR PAST MISSIONS

Bachelor’s degree in finance/accounting, science, technology, business, or relevant field
MBA or Advanced degree preferred
10+ years of progressive experience in revenue operations, sales operations, or commercial finance
Prior experience in technology, SaaS, data, or analytics markets strongly preferred
Proven track record building and scaling revenue operations functions including revenue forecasting in a growth-stage environment
Experience owning CRM platforms and managing multi-platform commercial tech stacks
Proven success designing and managing commissions frameworks and incentive compensation programs
Experience developing pricing policies, yield management processes, and deal governance frameworks – an asset
Experience building and managing channel or partner-based revenue programs – an asset

YOUR TOOLKIT

Strong commercial acumen with analytical rigour
Deep proficiency with CRM platforms (e.g., Salesforce, HubSpot) and revenue analytics and forecasting tools
Strong analytical and financial modelling skills with a solid command of SaaS revenue metrics (ARR, NRR, churn, renewal rates)
Data-driven approach to pipeline management, forecasting, and revenue analytics
Excellent negotiation, communication, and executive presence skills to coach and maximize deal value
Ability to design and implement scalable processes, governance frameworks, and workflow standards
Excellent cross-functional collaboration and communication skills, including executive-level presentation abilities
A systems-thinking approach to ensure accuracy and quality of data
Ability to design incentive compensation structures that drive the right commercial behaviors

Your Compensation

Base Salary Range: $145,000 to $190,000 CAD annually

The range is based on Vancouver, BC-derived compensation for this role. Individual placement in the range is determined based on many factors, including experience, skills, and qualifications. The top end of the range is typically reserved for individuals that meet or exceed all required qualifications and show demonstrated experience and expertise in all responsibilities of the role.

OUR SPACE

We’d love to welcome you to our world of software for space. We have a shared passion for building production critical systems that generate near real-time views of Earth from satellites that power real-world applications like disaster mitigation, environmental monitoring and crop yield improvements.

This is a hybrid role, with regular in-office work and collaboration required. Standard hours are 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday to Friday, with occasional evening or weekend work. Occasional travel to be expected (2-4 times per year)

WHY EARTHDAILY ANALYTICS?

Competitive compensation, full benefits and flexible time off
Be part of a meaningful mission as part of one of Canada’s most innovative space companies that are developing sustainable solutions for our planet
Work from home opportunities (hybrid)
Great work environment, team and one of the best office locations in Vancouver (right over the water in the Vancouver Convention Centre)
Company subsidized lunches, lunch & learns and Friday afternoon social hours
