jobs.title: Director of Customer Success
jobs.description:
There is an immediate need for a Director of Customer Success
located in the Greater Toronto Area, Ontario (Mississauga head office; field-based across the GTA and Southern Ontario)
at SupraITS
. If you have led account management and customer-facing technical teams in a managed services or technology services business, and you want to own retention, growth, and customer experience across an entire customer base, then this position is for you.

Company Overview

ABOUT SUPRA ITS

Founded in 1999, Supra ITS has grown into a globally trusted IT partner, delivering world-class Managed IT, Cybersecurity, Digital Transformation, Application Services, and Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) Services. Headquartered in Mississauga, Supra ITS operates with 650+ employees worldwide, including Network Operations Centers (NOCs) in Canada and India, ensuring 24/7 IT support and seamless service delivery.

Supra ITS provides a full spectrum of IT solutions, including server and network management, private cloud, disaster recovery, service desk support, and advanced security services. With a security-first approach and SLA-driven commitments, Supra ITS takes complete ownership of IT services, allowing clients to focus on growth while ensuring uninterrupted operations.

A vendor of established track record, Supra ITS is dedicated to long-term client success through tailored, scalable IT solutions. Canon Canada’s strategic investment in Supra ITS strengthens this commitment by integrating Canon’s cutting-edge technologies with Supra’s agile IT services. This partnership fosters innovation, enhances efficiency, and accelerates digital transformation, providing customers with superior IT solutions that are scalable, secure, and customer centric.

For more information, visit www.supraits.com.

Team Overview

This is your opportunity to join a dynamic company with a team that works very well together and has solid organized structures in place. Supra is rebuilding its Managed Services customer organization around a pod model: every customer has a named Account Manager who owns the relationship and the revenue, paired with a Customer IT Manager (CITM) who acts as the technical co-pilot for architecture, security, and the technology roadmap. The function spans Canada and India: a Senior Account Manager, Account Managers, and an Account Executive in Canada, Account Managers in India, and CITMs in both countries, together covering Supra’s managed services customer base.

YOU ARE!

You have built and led customer teams that own a number.
You have run account management, customer success, or client services in a managed services, cloud, or technology services business, and you know how to turn a team of relationship owners and technical advisors into one accountable unit that renews, grows, and keeps customers.

You understand recurring revenue in your bones.
Gross and net revenue retention, MRR movements, renewal rates, margin, and cost to serve are the numbers you manage by. You can explain to a CFO why an account is at risk a quarter before it shows up in churn, and you can explain to an Account Manager exactly what to do about it.

You lead from the field.
You are the executive your largest customers know by name. You show up for the quarterly reviews that matter, you run the saves personally when they are big enough, and you coach your team by doing the work alongside them, not from a dashboard.

The Director of Customer Success leads Supra’s Managed Services customer organization in Canada and India: the Account Management team (Senior Account Manager, Account Managers, Account Executives) and the Customer IT Manager (CITM) team. You own retention, growth, and customer experience across the full managed services base: gross and net revenue retention, renewals, expansion, customer health, the quarterly business review and technology roadmap cadence, and the coverage model that assigns every customer a relationship owner and a technical co-pilot. You hire, develop, and hold the team accountable to a weekly scorecard, act as executive sponsor for the largest and most at-risk accounts, and represent the voice of the customer in pricing, service catalogue, and delivery decisions. The role reports to the Senior Vice President, Sales
, based in Canada.

This is a leadership role based at Supra’s Mississauga office with significant customer-facing time. Supra is a hybrid workplace, but this position is expected to be in front of customers or with the team most of the week: executive sponsorship visits, quarterly business reviews for Tier A accounts, and ride-alongs with Account Managers across the GTA and Southern Ontario. Time working from home will be limited. Periodic travel to Supra’s India operations is expected to lead the India-based Account Managers and CITMs. A valid Ontario driver’s licence and access to a reliable vehicle are required.

Key Responsibilities Leadership of the Account Management and CITM Teams

Lead, hire, develop, and performance-manage the Account Management team (Senior Account Manager, Account Managers, Account Executives) in Canada and India and the CITM team in both countries.
Run the pod model: every customer has a named Account Manager and, where warranted, a CITM; books are balanced, seats are filled with the right people, and accountability for each account is unambiguous.
Set role charters, cadences, and the weekly scorecard for every seat; run the weekly team meeting, quarterly planning, and one-on-ones in Supra’s operating rhythm.
Build the career ladder and coaching plan from Associate Account Executive to Senior Account Manager and across the CITM track.

Retention, Growth, and Book Economics

Own gross and net revenue retention, renewal rate, and expansion bookings for the entire managed services base; build the annual revenue plan for the base by account and forecast it monthly.
Own the renewal pipeline: no renewal is a surprise, every agreement is opened early, and rate and margin are protected.
Drive roadmap-led expansion across the portfolio (managed security, cloud and infrastructure, Microsoft, application and AI services, hardware) by making the annual technology roadmap the standard for every Tier A and Tier B account.
Manage cost to serve: coverage ratios, Canada and India seat mix, and the use of programmatic coverage for the long tail.

Customer Health, Risk, and Saves

Own the customer health system: RAG status, risk register, early-warning signals from service, financial, and relationship data, and the save playbook.
Act as executive sponsor for Tier A accounts and personally lead saves on the largest at-risk accounts with the Account Manager and CITM.
Run monthly account reviews with leadership covering at-risk accounts, renewals, and expansion pipeline.

Customer Experience And Operating Cadence

Own the quarterly business review and roadmap cadence across the base: standards, materials, quality, and completion, with Supra’s delivery and service desk leaders aligned behind them.
Be the voice of the customer inside Supra: feed customer requirements into pricing, packaging, service catalogue, and delivery decisions, and close the loop with customers on what changed.
Lead the transition plan as accounts move between seats: warm handoffs, no changes inside 90 days of a renewal, at-risk accounts handled last, and customer communication framed as added accountability.

Collaboration Across Supra

Partner with Sales on new-logo handover into account management, with Delivery and Operations on service performance and escalations, and with Finance on billing, contracts, and MRR reporting.
Work with the Microsoft and vendor alliance functions to bring partner programs and funding into customer roadmaps.
Work with People and Culture on hiring plans, compensation plans, and onboarding for the customer teams.

Reporting and Governance

Own the customer success scorecard and present it weekly to leadership: GRR, NRR, renewals, QBRs held, roadmap conversion, pipeline, customer health, and seat capacity.
Maintain accurate account data in ConnectWise and the CRM as the single source of truth for the customer base; re-segment the base quarterly as accounts grow, shrink, or change risk.

Qualifications & Skills

Education & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent experience; an MBA is an asset.
Minimum 12 years in technology account management, customer success, or client services, including at least 5 years leading customer-facing teams at a managed services provider, cloud or technology services company, or similar recurring revenue business.
Proven record of owning retention and growth targets for a large recurring revenue base and of building or rebuilding an account management function.
Experience leading distributed teams across countries, ideally including India-based staff.

Industry & Commercial Knowledge

Deep understanding of managed services economics: MRR, gross and net revenue retention, renewal and pricing strategy, margin, and cost to serve.
Strong working knowledge of the managed services portfolio (service desk, infrastructure and cloud, managed security, Microsoft 365 and Azure, projects, emerging AI services) and the ability to lead a customer conversation about a technology roadmap alongside a CITM.
Familiarity with ConnectWise or a comparable PSA and CRM, and with running a team on a weekly scorecard (EOS or similar operating system experience is an asset).

Leadership & Soft Skills

Executive presence with customers and credibility with technical teams; comfortable with CIOs, CFOs, and owners in person.
Proven people leader: hires well, coaches in the field, sets clear expectations, and acts on performance.
Commercial judgement and the integrity to recommend what the customer needs over what is easiest to sell.
Disciplined operator: builds the cadence, owns the numbers, and reports without being chased.

Connect. Grow. Thrive Together.

This role will have a portfolio of responsibilities related to architecture, strategy, and planning, and will have oversight of the activities of several very senior and experienced technical leaders.

The Senior Director, Enterprise Architecture is accountable for owning and driving architectural solutions across the enterprise, inclusive of line-of-business (LOB), Enterprise IT, and corporate solutions. This role drives the creation and adoption of Teranet’s multi-year IT roadmap. The IT roadmap drives multi-year IT investment decisions and broadly impacts technology spending of ~ $25M (excludes people costs) per year to deliver business value across the enterprise.

All system, technology, and solution architects in Teranet, across the enterprise, will report to this role. As such, this position will have a widespread impact on the business capabilities delivered in partnership with the Registry & Property Solutions, Financial Solutions, Enterprise IT, Information Security, and other departments at Teranet.

Develop IT strategy that maintains alignment between business and IT and which will drive
multi-year IT investment decisions.
Contribute to the development of the company’s strategic roadmap.
Lead Teranet’s enterprise-wide IT roadmap, defining the future-state architecture and transformation of technology, people, organizational design, and processes.
Contribute to the execution of digital transformation efforts.
Define the technology solution and environment roadmaps to ensure capacity and scalability as demand and usage evolve within the business.
Have visibility and understanding of the entire technology landscape.
Identify, assess, and communicate risks related to the roadmaps, to strategic IT initiatives, and to Teranet’s business from emerging technology trends.
Participate, as required, in executive- and board-level discussions on technology and strategy.

Manage a team of architects responsible for creating technology solutions to business problems, developing new business capabilities, and providing technical direction to implementation teams.

Mentor and manage team members to achieve program targets and goals.

Oversee the time management, prioritization, and effectiveness of all team members.

Chair the architecture board responsible for reviewing and approving architecture, technology, and design decisions across the enterprise.
Partner closely with and maintain regular touchpoints with key partners, including product development, customers, finance, PMO, vendors, and delivery teams.
Manage the allocation of architecture resources to various initiatives.
Create and communicate solutions to various business problems.
Oversee adherence to the architecture strategy, principles, and framework throughout IT.
Lead the definition and validation of architecture principles and standards.
Ensure systems are architected to be secure and resilient through the effective application of architecture principles across the domains of Business, Application, Data, Integration, Technology/Infrastructure, and Security.
Communicate architecture standards to all stakeholders and ensure standards are published, updated, and followed.

jobs.description:
Who we are

At Aquila, we invest in category-defining B2B/B2G software companies globally, acting as a thought-partner, striving for the success of our companies in the long term. We are a well-managed, profitable company that operates like a startup with the financial backing of a parent company. For our people, this means limitless possibilities.

We are unapologetically unique, pivoting to respond to the needs of the multiple markets we operate in. We have ambitious goals, and we are looking for genuine contributors with integrity, energy, flexibility, and loyalty. We are investing in building future leaders who can take an idea and make things happen.

About Campana Systems

Campana Systems, a Gemini Group company within Aquila, develops specialized software solutions for AAA and CAA auto clubs across North America. Founded in 1988 and headquartered in Waterloo, Ontario, Campana has built long-standing relationships with organizations that rely on its technology to manage their operations and deliver services to their members.

Our AXIS platform brings together membership management, customer relationship management, emergency roadside assistance, travel services, and business intelligence in an integrated suite of solutions. Looking ahead, we are focused on evolving our technology, strengthening our platform capabilities, and finding new ways to help our customers work more efficiently and deliver better member experiences.

Who we need

Reporting to the General Manager, we are hiring a Director, Technology to lead the evolution of Campana Systems’ technology strategy, architecture, infrastructure, and AXIS platform. In this newly created role, you will own the technology roadmap from strategy through execution, with accountability for modernization priorities, investment decisions, platform reliability, and measurable business outcomes. You will lead the Architecture and Infrastructure & Security teams, partner with the Director, Development, and establish the technical direction and capabilities needed to deliver on our product vision while supporting the customers who depend on our technology.

This is a fully remote role open to candidates across Canada, with working hours of 8:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Eastern Time.

What’s in it for you

Shape a meaningful transformation . You will have the autonomy to challenge established approaches, make consequential technology decisions, and guide the evolution of a business-critical software platform. You will see the impact of your work in stronger platform capabilities, improved delivery, and better customer experiences.

Build what comes next. You will lead experienced teams while shaping the standards, capabilities, and ways of working needed for the future. From strengthening engineering practices to developing technical leaders, you will have the opportunity to build a more effective technology organization and see the results of your leadership.

Grow your executive influence. You will work directly with the General Manager and contribute to decisions that connect technology investments with customer needs and business growth. Backed by Aquila and the broader Constellation Software network, you will have opportunities to expand your leadership experience and pursue broader responsibilities over time.

As our new Director, Technology, you will

Own the technology roadmap
. You will turn the product vision into a multi-year strategy with clear priorities, investments, milestones, and measurable outcomes. You will balance modernization, technical debt, customer commitments, and platform stability, taking accountability for delivery and results. You will establish architectural standards, technology governance, and engineering priorities. Partnering with the Director, Development, you will strengthen technical decision-making, CI/CD, automation, and delivery practices across Canadian and offshore teams.
Lead platform modernization.
You will define a phased approach to evolving AXIS, including its legacy Rocket UniVerse architecture. You will determine what to retain, integrate, replace, or modernize, guiding decisions on APIs, application architecture, CRM, data capabilities, and cloud or hybrid environments while protecting the reliability customers depend on.
Turn innovation into impact.
You will identify opportunities to improve CRM capabilities, business intelligence, reporting, and operational efficiency through AI, automation, and better use of data. You will evaluate feasibility and business value, establish priorities, and work with technical teams to turn promising initiatives into measurable results.
Strengthen security and reliability.
You will oversee infrastructure, hosting, cybersecurity, disaster recovery, and platform resilience. You will reduce technology risk, strengthen operational controls, and advance security and compliance readiness, including SOC 2-related requirements.
Build and grow technical capabilities.
You will lead the Architecture and Infrastructure & Security teams, develop talent, strengthen accountability, and identify capability gaps. You will improve collaboration with Development and Product to ensure teams have the direction and support needed to execute the roadmap.
Connect technology to business priorities.
You will partner with the General Manager on technology investments, budgets, resources, and strategic decisions. You will communicate risks and trade-offs, measure progress, and contribute technical leadership to customer conversations when needed.

You bring

The senior technology leadership.
You have led technology strategy, architecture, and technical teams within an enterprise software business, with accountability for investment decisions, organizational performance, and business outcomes. You bring the judgment to set direction, establish priorities, and deliver results through technical leaders and cross-functional teams.
The platform modernization expertise.
You have led the evolution of complex, business-critical software, navigating legacy architecture, technical debt, and customer dependencies. You know how to assess what to retain, replace, or integrate, develop a phased modernization roadmap, and introduce new capabilities without compromising reliability.
The technical depth.
You bring strong expertise in enterprise architecture, APIs, integrations, data platforms, and cloud or hybrid environments, along with an understanding of infrastructure, cybersecurity, and disaster recovery. You can establish technical standards, evaluate emerging technologies, and guide decisions that strengthen platform performance, security, and scalability.
The experience driving innovation.
You have improved engineering practices and delivery performance across distributed teams, including those outside your direct reporting structure. You understand CI/CD, automation, and modern development practices, and can identify practical opportunities for AI, analytics, and business intelligence that deliver measurable value.
The business acumen.
You connect technology decisions to customer needs, financial priorities, and long-term business growth. You can evaluate investments, communicate complex trade-offs, and align senior leaders while staying close enough to the technology to challenge assumptions and guide execution.
The influence.
You develop strong technical leaders, establish accountability, and build cross-functional, cross-location collaboration. You are comfortable making difficult decisions, navigating competing priorities, and owning outcomes in an environment where you have the autonomy to shape what comes next.

Why join?

Axis Campana and Aquila are part of Constellation Software Inc., one of Canada's largest and most successful software companies and its most successful technology stock over the last 10 years [TSE: CSU].

Our entrepreneurial culture, lean environment, and people come together to form a dynamic organization where purpose drives our growth. This is a place where high performance and hard work are rewarded, where leaders are grown, and where the best ideas win. With the autonomy to be creative and curious, we collaborate and iterate to achieve real impact in the communities we support.

We spend our days asking questions and challenging the status quo, manipulating our structure, roles, and internal operations in order to stay ahead in a competitive landscape.

If you share our growth mindset, relationship-focused approach, and high moral fibre, you will thrive at Aquila.

Compensation

At Campana and Aquila, we believe compensation should be transparent, fair, and reflective of both experience and impact. The salary range for this role is CAD $150,000 to $200,000 plus bonus.

Compensation is determined based on skills, experience, and the scope and complexity of the role. We value open conversations about compensation and are happy to discuss our approach at any stage of the hiring process.

Apply now.

Diversity and inclusion are not mere words on paper to us. We welcome and appreciate candidates with a range of backgrounds and experiences. If you have most of the qualifications we are seeking, and want to play an integral role in our success, apply to express your interest.

What you can expect from our interview process:

A virtual interview with a Talent Advisor to discuss your interest in joining the company and in the role. The conversation will be recorded using BrightHire, an AI-powered video interview tool. More details will be shared when you are invited to interview.
An interview with the General Manager to discuss your technology leadership experience, approach to platform modernization, architectural decision-making, and ability to connect technology strategy to business outcomes.
A final virtual interview with the Portfolio Manager and members of the technology leadership team to explore your approach to leading transformation, collaborating across teams, and building the capabilities needed to execute the technology roadmap.

All employment decisions are made based on qualifications, merit, and business needs. We welcome and encourage applications from people with disabilities and accommodations are available on request.

Job Title: HEAD OF PEOPLE INTEGRATION PLANNING

Harbour Air is preparing for an exciting period of change as we work through the proposed acquisition of Pacific Coastal Airlines, and we are looking for an experienced people leader to lead the planning and coordination of the people side of this work. Reporting to the VP, People, Culture & Safety, the Head, People Integration Planning will develop and lead the people integration roadmap, ensuring we are thoughtful, coordinated and well prepared across culture, organization design, talent, communications, employee experience, systems, policies and processes. This is a hands-on role: in addition to setting direction, you will personally drive project management and day-to-day integration work to deliver a single, aligned organization. Working closely with senior leaders across both Harbour Air and Pacific Coastal Airlines, you will bring structure, clarity and momentum to a complex, highly visible body of work.

WORK HOURS:
Office hours (evenings and weekends as needed around key milestones)
LOCATION:
Vancouver with occasional travel to Harbour Air and Pacific Coastal Airlines locations
TERM:
12-Month Contract
DEPARTMENT:
People, Culture & Safety
REPORTING TO:
VP, People, Culture & Safety
COMPENSATION:
Competitive salary, full medical and dental and other industry benefits including interline flight partners

Responsibilities and Expectations

Integration Strategy and Governance

Develop and maintain the overall People Integration strategy, roadmap, milestones and priorities.
Establish clear governance, workstreams, accountabilities, dependencies and decision points across People & Culture.
Lead and coordinate the People Integration team and ensure deliverables stay on track.

Project Management and Delivery

Provide hands-on project management of the people integration: build and manage detailed integration plans, timelines, task tracking, status reporting and RAID (risks, actions, issues, decisions) logs.
Identify key people risks, dependencies and opportunities and ensure they are appropriately escalated and addressed.
Establish meaningful measures and reporting to monitor progress, risks and people outcomes.

HR Systems, Policies and Processes

Lead and coordinate the integration of HR systems, processes, policies and procedures across both organizations, including harmonization of policies, payroll and HRIS, and the retirement or consolidation of duplicate practices, to create one aligned organization.
Work directly with functional owners and subject matter experts at both companies to map current-state processes, identify gaps and conflicts, and drive decisions and implementation through to completion.

People Readiness, Organization Design and Talent

Lead people readiness planning and integration across organizational design, talent, compensation, benefits, policies, processes, systems, employee experience and culture.
Support organizational design and workforce planning for the future organization.
Develop approaches to talent retention, critical roles, leadership transitions and employee engagement through the integration.

Culture, Communications and Employee Experience

Ensure appropriate consideration is given to both organizations' cultures, strengths and ways of working.
Work closely with Communications and business leaders to ensure people-related messaging is thoughtful, timely and aligned.

Stakeholder Partnership

Partner with the senior leadership teams of both Harbour Air and Pacific Coastal Airlines to understand and address people impacts and integration priorities.
Build strong working relationships with senior leaders at both organizations, facilitating joint planning, alignment and timely decision-making.
Partner with legal and other advisors as required throughout the transaction and integration process.

Ad hoc Projects and Other Duties

May be asked to carry out additional tasks, projects, or responsibilities as required, in alignment with the scope and level of the position, to meet changing business needs.

Qualifications/Assets

EDUCATION

Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business or a related field, or a comparable combination of education and experience. A professional designation (e.g., CPHR) or project management certification (e.g., PMP) is an asset.

IDEAL EXPERIENCE

Significant senior HR/People leadership experience, ideally with experience supporting a merger, acquisition, integration or significant organizational transformation.
Demonstrated hands-on project management and integration delivery experience, including coordinating the alignment of systems, processes, policies and procedures across organizations.
Experience harmonizing HR policies, payroll and HRIS, and supporting organizational design and workforce planning, is an asset.
Experience partnering with senior leaders, legal and other advisors through a transaction is an asset.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, & CAPABILITIES

Strategic Planning – Builds clear roadmaps, milestones and priorities; brings structure to complex and ambiguous work.
Project Leadership – Manages detailed plans, timelines, task tracking, status reporting and RAID logs hands-on.
Judgment & Discretion – Handles confidential and sensitive people matters with care.
Business Acumen – Balances employee experience with operational and organizational needs.
Relationship Building – Builds trust and strong working relationships with leaders across both organizations.
Influence – Influences senior leaders, navigates competing priorities and keeps people moving forward.
Clear Communication – Exceptional written and verbal communication; works with Communications to keep messaging thoughtful, timely and aligned.
Systems Thinking – Sees how culture, structure, talent, systems, policies and processes connect, and manages dependencies across workstreams.
Change Leadership – Brings a thoughtful, practical and collaborative approach to change.
Commitment to Safety – Keeps safety as top priority throughout the integration.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) and project management tools.

Harbour Air is North America's largest seaplane airline, a quintessential west coast experience offering up to 300 daily scheduled flights, charters, and scenic tours highlighting British Columbia’s coast and beyond. Our people are the backbone of our organization, and we are committed to creating a culture that inspires one another to achieve extraordinary success. **Key Responsibilities**

**Financial Leadership and Reporting**

* Lead the finance and accounting function, including controllership, accounts payable, accounts receivable, credit and financial analysis.
* Ensure accurate and timely monthly, quarterly and annual financial reporting.
* Strengthen accounting policies, internal controls, approval processes and financial documentation.
* Oversee month\-end and year\-end close, reconciliations, audits, tax filings and intercompany reporting.
* Provide the President and leadership team with clear financial analysis and practical recommendations.

**Cash Flow, Treasury and Risk**

* Take ownership of cash flow, liquidity and working\-capital management.
* Maintain reliable cash flow forecasts and identify potential constraints before they affect the business.
* Oversee collections, payment planning, customer terms and financial commitments.
* Manage banking relationships, credit facilities, lender reporting and funding requirements.
* Develop and oversee the company’s foreign\-exchange and financial risk\-management strategy.

**Planning and Business Performance**

* Lead budgeting, forecasting and financial planning.
* Monitor results against budget and investigate significant variances.
* Develop meaningful financial and operational performance indicators.
* Improve costing and profitability analysis across customers, transactions, services and business lines.
* Support pricing, capital allocation, financing and growth decisions through financial modelling and analysis.

**ERP and Process Improvement**

* Lead the company’s ERP implementation from a finance and business perspective.
* Define financial, reporting, control, workflow and data requirements.
* Coordinate with internal stakeholders, consultants and implementation partners.
* Oversee data readiness, testing, training, documentation and system adoption.
* Reduce reliance on manual reporting and improve the accuracy and efficiency of financial processes.

**Team Leadership**

* Assess and develop the finance team, clarify responsibilities and identify capability gaps.
* Coach and support the Controller and other finance team members.
* Establish clear expectations, reporting timelines and standard operating procedures.
* Build a collaborative and accountable finance function capable of supporting the company’s growth.

**Required Qualifications**

* CPA designation in good standing and a bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, business administration or a related discipline.
* Minimum of ten years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including senior leadership responsibility.
* Demonstrated experience leading a finance function and developing accounting and finance professionals.
* Strong technical knowledge of financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, cash flow, working capital and internal controls.
* Experience managing banking relationships, credit facilities, funding requirements, treasury activities and foreign\-exchange exposure.
* Demonstrated experience leading an ERP implementation, finance transformation or significant systems\-improvement initiative.
* Strong commercial and analytical judgment, with the ability to translate financial information into clear business recommendations.
* Excellent communication and stakeholder\-management skills, including experience working directly with owners or executive leadership.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in a privately held, entrepreneurial or high\-growth organization.
* Experience supporting multi\-entity or cross\-border Canadian and U.S. operations.
* Experience in an inventory\-intensive, margin\-driven or operationally complex business.
* Industry exposure to metals, steel, trading, manufacturing, distribution, transportation, freight, logistics or warehousing.
* Familiarity with commodity pricing, inventory costing, customer\-credit risk and working\-capital\-intensive operations.

**Candidate Profile**

The ideal candidate is a practical, commercially minded finance leader who is comfortable moving between strategy and detailed execution. They can build structure in a growing organization, develop people, improve systems and provide leadership with reliable financial information for decision\-making.

**About Minga**

 **Minga means community**. It’s the belief that we achieve more together than we ever could alone. At Minga, joining our team isn't just about a new role, it's about joining a collective that is deeply invested in your growth, your impact, and your connection to the people around you.

  

We’re building the Student Behavior Platform schools can’t live without, and we’re having fun doing it.

  

We are a tight\-knit group of curious, low\-ego humans who genuinely enjoy the "we" over the "me."


* **Supportive Growth:** You aren’t on an island. You’ll have the autonomy to do your best work and a community that has your back every step of the way.
* **Shared Ownership****:** Whether at our Kelowna HQ or remote, you’re a vital part of a team that cares as much about the people as the product.
* **Real Impact:** Everything we do supports the educators and students we serve, creating a ripple effect of connection in schools everywhere.
  


**Ready to be part of the community?**  

Come help us make school life better for everyone.  



  

**The Role**



We’re not just hiring for a position, we’re adding a teammate

  

Minga is scaling, and we need a finance leader who sees the whole business. As VP of Finance, you’ll own more than the numbers. You’ll own the commercial engine behind them: the contracts we sign with school districts, the metrics we report to our board, the comp plans that motivate our sellers, and the forecast that ties it all to our operating plan.

  

Reporting to our COO, Pam Boyko and sitting on the Leadership Team, you’ll partner with Sales, Customer Success, Account Management, Product and People to turn data into decisions. You’ll lead and mentor a small team today and decide how the function grows, while helping to build the systems that let finance, legal and revenue operations scale with us.

  

This role is for a builder. If you love being the person who makes a growing company run smarter and with less risk, keep reading.

* Lead financial planning, forecasting, budgeting and monthly reporting
* Build and own the annual operating plan and headcount plan, linked directly to the revenue and bookings forecast
* Own revenue modelling, cash planning and scenario analysis
* Maintain strong internal controls, compliance and cross\-border (Canada/US) tax readiness
* Lead a team of two direct reports, Corporate Accountant and Accounting Manager
  


**SaaS metrics and board reporting**


* Own the source of truth for ARR, gross and net revenue retention, churn, bookings and pipeline\-to\-revenue
* Deliver a monthly metrics package to the Leadership Team
* Prepare board deck metrics and investor updates
* Run cohort, churn and expansion analysis, and track unit economics (CAC, payback, LTV, gross margin)
* Support investor relations: shareholder communications, investor requests and data room maintenance

* Engage and manage outside counsel, including scope and legal spend
* Manage disputes, demand letters and litigation with counsel
* Act as corporate secretary: board and shareholder resolutions, minute book and corporate records
* Manage the cap table: equity grants, option plan administration, vesting records and FMV / 409A valuations


**Business insurance and risk**


* Own our insurance program: general liability, cyber, E\&O, D\&O and employment practices
* Manage the broker relationship and annual renewals
* Issue certificates of insurance and handle additional\-insured requests for district contracts and RFPs
* Manage claims when they come up


**Sales compensation and commissions**


* Partner with sales and CX leadership on annual comp plan design, quota setting and plan documents
* Run monthly commission calculations, approvals and the payroll handoff
* Manage clawbacks, splits, SPIFs and resolve commission disputes fairly and quickly


**Pricing governance and deal desk**


* Own the discount approval matrix and the policy for non\-standard terms
* Support Sales on complex district and multi\-year deals as our deal desk lead

  


**What We Require ✅**


* CPA designation
* 8\+ years of finance and accounting experience, including 4\+ years in a leadership role
* A track record of financial leadership in a scaling SaaS, technology or high\-growth company
* Deep FP\&A experience: modelling, forecasting, budgeting and reporting
* Fluency in SaaS metrics and how they connect to the P\&L and board story
* Experience in revenue recognition, internal controls and cross\-border tax
* Hands\-on experience with commercial contracts, redlines and managing outside counsel
* Experience designing or administering sales commission plans
* Comfort with financial systems (QuickBooks, NetSuite or similar) and spreadsheets that others can trust
* Clear communicator who can explain the numbers to a board, a seller or a new hire

  


**Bonus Points For**

* EdTech, K\-12, public sector or local government experience (district procurement, RFPs and contract terms)
* Corporate secretary, cap table or equity plan administration experience
* Experience supporting M\&A activity on the buy side and/or sell side (e.g., due diligence, deal preparation, or post\-acquisition integration)
* Insurance program or risk management experience

  


**Who You Are**

* A builder at heart: you love creating and improving systems that make a difference
* A trusted partner who balances people, process and business needs
* Commercially minded: you’d rather help a deal close safely than say no
* Curious and adaptable: you ask great questions, listen deeply and pivot quickly

jobs.description:
**Job Description:**


ONNI Group is hiring a Head of Interior Design in Vancouver

  

Join one of the largest privately owned real estate companies in North America.

  

For over half a century, we’ve been building communities for people to live, work, and play — spanning real estate development and construction, commercial property ownership and management, hospitality, and a growing presence in venture capital and technology. Our expertise reaches across major North American cities including Los Angeles, Seattle, Chicago, Phoenix, Toronto, and Vancouver. To date, we’ve developed, built, and now own or manage well over 50 million square feet of residential, office, retail, and industrial space — including more than 15,000 homes and 11,200 rental apartments — with another 28 million square feet underway across our markets. Employing thousands of people across North America, Onni continues to diversify beyond our real estate roots, including through Grey Owl, our technology company delivering managed IT, AI\-driven security, and smart building solutions to commercial properties across North America.


In 2009, Onni entered the hospitality space with Level Hotels \& Furnished Suites, and our portfolio has since grown to various hotels in Vancouver, Chicago, and Seattle, with plans to add and grow more. We’ve also expanded into dining, with restaurant concepts including Capo \& The Spritz and Solette in Vancouver and Chicago, Fora in Chicago’s Fulton Market, and Dialtone, our coffee\-by\-day, wine\-by\-night concept.


At Onni, you’ll learn from experienced professionals across every part of our business, take on real responsibility early, and have clear room to grow — whether your path is in commercial real estate, hospitality, or the technology and innovation shaping what comes next.

 **Perks \& Benefits:**


Onni operates a full\-time, work\-from\-the\-office culture — vibrant, dynamic, and fun, with an open floor plan built on our belief in the strength of in\-person interaction and collaboration. We do not offer remote or hybrid work arrangements, although employees do enjoy the added perk of up to three work\-from\-home days per month, depending on business needs. We take pride in our office culture, and our team members enjoy ONNI’s open\-floor environment, complete with a fantastic kitchen and lunch area with espresso and coffee machines and appliances, and a 24\-hour gym — just steps away from Vancouver’s vibrant Yaletown and Downtown neighbourhoods, and a short walk from the Granville and Yaletown\-Roundhouse (Canada Line) SkyTrain stations. Employees also enjoy an exciting calendar of employee events throughout the year — including quarterly team\-building events, Pemberton trips, summer boating days, sports day, an annual holiday party, watch parties for major sporting events like FIFA and the Olympics, and other seasonal celebrations throughout the year, plus early office closures before statutory holidays and weekends, along with regular office events like food trucks and local favorites, and the following perks and benefits::

* Competitive pay and a comprehensive benefits package.
* Benefits include company\-paid extended health care, dental care, vision care, life insurance, critical illness, and critical life insurance.
* Annual education allowance.
* Generous referral program.
* Fun and collaborative company culture with lots of team\-building events.
* Local discounts at restaurants, clothing stores, personal training, and more.
* Free access to a fully equipped gym.
* Friends and Family rates for hospitality brands.

 **What You Will Do**

jobs.title: Director of Marketing
jobs.description:
**About Bells of Steel Inc.**


At Bells of Steel, our mission is to make fitness and strength training approachable, affordable, and fun. We design and manufacture high\-quality strength and exercise equipment for home gym owners and fitness professionals, helping people of all experience levels achieve their goals.


We’re not your typical fitness equipment brand. We’re down\-to\-earth, a little cheeky, and focused on making fitness more rewarding and less intimidating. If you enjoy a fast\-paced, no\-BS environment and want to help shape the future of strength training, you’ll fit right in.

 **Our Core Values: A.C.T.**

**Adaptability – Raise the Bar**  

We challenge the status quo, learn quickly, and continuously improve. We embrace change, seek better ways of working, and take initiative to drive results.

**Customer Centricity – Always Spot the Customer**  

Everything we do is focused on helping our customers succeed. We lead with empathy, build trust through action, and create value for both external and internal customers.

**Teamwork – We Win Together**  

We operate with honesty, transparency, trust, and respect. We collaborate openly, take shared ownership of outcomes, and succeed as a team.

**About Bells of Steel Inc.**
-----------------------------


We’re a rapidly growing e\-commerce company that designs and sells strength equipment across Canada, the USA, the UK, Australia, and now Europe, starting with Germany. We compete with the biggest names in the industry by moving fast, listening to customers, and building products that punch above their weight.


Our purpose is to make strength training accessible to all, and have fun doing it. Our 10\-year target is 1 million customers made stronger, and over the next three years we’re growing to $50 million USD in annual revenue.


As we continue to grow, we're looking for a **Director of Marketing** to own how Bells of Steel reaches, wins, and keeps customers in every market we serve.


This is a strategic leadership role responsible for deciding **where we show up, what we say, and how every marketing dollar earns its place.**


You'll own our marketing strategy, brand positioning, channel and campaign calendar, paid media strategy, creative strategy and testing, and the marketing Scorecard. You'll work closely with our founder, e\-commerce, product, sales, customer service, finance, and our international teams to turn great products into growth.


You'll lead a marketing team of about 16 people across marketing operations, retention, affiliates and partnerships, social and community, creative and video, and paid search and paid social. You don't need to do it all yourself, but you need to be strong enough in each area to coach your channel owners and hold them to a high standard.


This is an **AI\-first role**. Over your first year, you'll lead an AI transformation across marketing: upgrading and replacing manual workflows with AI, and working with our in\-house developers to build our own tools that outperform the paid software we use today.


If you're someone who reads a Scorecard like a story, moves budget toward what works and away from what doesn't, and can build a brand that real lifters trust, we'd love to meet you.


This is a hybrid role based in Calgary, with about half your time in the office and half working from home. Your office days are where the best marketing happens: in the photo studio for a shoot, on the showroom floor talking to customers, walking over to the product team to plan a launch, and lifting on the equipment you're selling.


Relocation support is available for the right candidate.

**What You'll Be Doing**
========================

**Marketing Strategy \& Brand Positioning**
-------------------------------------------

* Own the 1–3 year marketing strategy, tied to our company goals of $50M USD revenue by 2029 and 1 million customers made stronger.
* Own our brand positioning across every market, built on our three uniques: maximum training value per square foot, function over hype, and real people with real strength.
* Grow our reach with former lifters, practical beginners, parents, and professionals without losing the core lifters who built the brand.
* Make sure our customer journey, from discovery to setup to training, and our 30\-day money back guarantee show up consistently in every customer touchpoint.

**Leadership**
--------------

* Lead, coach, and develop the Marketing team (\~16 people) using EOS principles.
* Create clarity around priorities, accountability, and execution, with KPIs for every seat.
* Give every Quarterly Goal a definition of done, milestones and an owner at the start of the quarter.
* Bring in outside experts where we are weak, and check their work before it ships.
* Build a high\-performing team capable of making excellent marketing decisions without constant executive involvement.

**AI Transformation**
---------------------

* Work AI\-first, and set the standard for how the marketing team uses AI to plan, create, analyze, and report.
* Lead a 12\-month AI transformation across marketing: map every manual workflow, then upgrade it or replace it with AI.
* Partner with our in\-house developers to build internal tools that work better than our paid SaaS stack, and retire subscriptions once the replacement is proven.
* Measure the results in hours saved, output per person, and software spend cut, and report them on the marketing Scorecard.
* Coach every member of the team to work AI\-first, and develop an AI champion within marketing.

**Paid Media Strategy**
-----------------------

* Own paid media strategy across Google, Meta, Amazon, Reddit, and display.
* Set targets for return on ad spend, acquisition cost, and new customer growth, and hold channel owners to them.
* Make sure creative, landing pages, and offers work together from the first click to checkout.

**Scorecard, Performance \& Budget**
------------------------------------

* Own the marketin

jobs.description:
Our Purpose 

 Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential. 

 Title and Summary 

Director, Risk Management 

Overview:
Mastercard is a global technology company in the payments sector. We power payments and provide products and services for individuals and industries all around the world. Our people, technology, data and brand provide the capabilities that drive our success. We believe in connecting people to priceless possibilities.

As a company, we know that our success is driven by the skills, experience, integrity and mindset of the talent we hire. By building an inclusive, world-class culture, our employees have once-in-a-career opportunities to be a part of teams that have a greater impact on our community and our world. We invite you to join our team to find out how you too can start something priceless. 

Role Description:
The Digital Asset Risk & Compliance team is looking for a Director, Operational Risk & Controls to help build and operate Mastercard’s Second Line operational risk and control capabilities for digital assets.
The role will establish a consistent approach to identifying, assessing, monitoring and reporting operational risks across Mastercard’s digital asset strategy, products and operations. The Director will partner with the First Line to establish and maintain effective controls, risk and control self-assessments, control testing and monitoring in line with Mastercard policies and standards.
The Director will also support BVNK’s integration into Mastercard by aligning operational risk frameworks, controls, governance and reporting while preserving the ability of the business to grow and innovate.

Role:
Digital Asset Operational Risk & Controls
• Build and operate the operational risk and controls capability for Digital Assets and BVNK.
• Partner with the First Line to identify material operational risks and establish effective controls, monitoring, and escalation.
• Lead risk assessments, RCSAs, control reviews, and issue management across digital asset products, operations, technology, and third-party providers.
• Assess control effectiveness and identify emerging risks, control weaknesses, and opportunities for improvement.
• Establish practical and scalable approaches to monitoring, testing, reporting, and remediation
Governance, Reporting & Business Partnership
• Integrate operational risk considerations into strategy, product development, operating model decisions, and business growth.
• Establish governance and reporting that provides management with a clear view of risks, controls, issues, and required actions.
• Partner across Product, Technology, Operations, Finance, Compliance, Security, and Risk to support responsible growth.
• Provide independent challenge while helping the business develop practical and scalable solutions.
• Promote a strong risk and control culture across Mastercard and BVNK.

BVNK Integration
• Build the long-term operational risk and controls capability for Digital Assets as part of BVNK's integration into Mastercard.
• Assess current-state practices and identify priority enhancements based on business growth, risk profile, and regulatory expectations.
• Align governance, RCSAs, control monitoring, testing, issue management, and reporting with Mastercard standards.
• Track integration commitments and remediation plans through completion.
• Drive simplification, scalability, and automation of operational risk and control activities.

All About You:
• Experience in Operational Risk, Controls, Audit, Compliance, Risk Management, or a related discipline.
• Demonstrated ability to build and enhance risk and control frameworks, including risk assessments, controls, testing, monitoring, and issue management.
• Strong understanding of Second Line oversight, independent challenge, governance, and risk appetite.
• Ability to identify material risks, assess control effectiveness, and drive practical improvements.
• Experience partnering across business, product, operations, technology, and risk functions.
• Strong stakeholder management and ability to influence without direct authority.
• Ability to simplify complex issues and translate them into clear actions, decisions, and reporting.
• Comfortable operating in ambiguity, building new capabilities, and driving execution.
• Interest in digital assets, payments, fintech, and emerging financial technologies. 

Mastercard is a merit-based, inclusive, equal opportunity employer that considers applicants without regard to gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, disabled or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We hire the most qualified candidate for the role. In the US or Canada, if you require accommodations or assistance to complete the online application process or during the recruitment process, please contact reasonable_accommodation@mastercard.com and identify the type of accommodation or assistance you are requesting. Do not include any medical or health information in this email. The Reasonable Accommodations team will respond to your email promptly. 

 Corporate Security Responsibility 

All activities involving access to Mastercard assets, information, and networks comes with an inherent risk to the organization and, therefore, it is expected that every person working for, or on behalf of, Mastercard is responsible for information security and must:
 Abide by Mastercard’s security policies and practices;

 Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed;

 Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and

 Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.

In line with Mastercard’s total compensation philosophy and assuming that the job will be performed in Canada, the successful candidate will be offered a competitive pay based on location, experience and other qualifications for the role and may be eligible to participate in a discretionary annual incentive program. This posting reflects one or more current openings on our team.

Toronto, Canada: $138,000 - $221,000 CAD

Job Description 

 What is the opportunity? 
 Operational Risk Controls and Governance (ORC&G) acts as trusted advisors and subject-matter experts for the Capital Markets businesses and COO groups on risk mitigation practices, providing guidance to front line units on controls best practices.

 We are looking for an eager and high-performing individual to oversee the maintenance of an effective operational risk management program within CM. This role will focus on controls assurance by ensuring the consistent application of the Operational Risk Framework and associated policies in the business, and supporting a culture of risk ownership, awareness and management in the business and functions.   

 In addition to supporting the broader operational risk mandate, this role will have the unique opportunity to gain exposure to every business and control function within RBC Capital markets, and to work directly with Senior CM leaders by managing the full end to end governance of the North American New Business Committees, as well as supporting ongoing efforts to establish clear and concise reporting.

 What will you do? 
 Strategic Risk Governance & Change Management: 
 CM-sponsored Change Initiatives: Participate in the end-to-end detailed risk assessment process for CM change initiatives through input into and membership of the NBC, IRP, and PAR processes, per procedures outlined in the CM Risk Assessment of Change Initiatives procedures document, and the NBC Standing Order;
 Review post-NBC control documentation status, to ensure that new or amended controls that were required to support an NBC-approved initiative have been implemented and are confirmed to be effective, either through design review of controls or through robust post-implementation reviews of NBC initiatives;
 Monitor North American NBC pipeline via periodic meetings with NBC Secretaries to review conditionally approved, in progress papers, items placed on hold, and performing escalation with CM stakeholders where required;
 Oversee the execution of periodic product risk assessments and post-implementation review for CM initiatives;
 Lead and co-ordinate remediation for Second Line of Defense (2LOD) and Internal Audit (3LOD) Findings assigned to ORC&G, ensuring timely closure of issues and action plans.

 Operational Risk Event (ORE) Management: 
 Oversee the capture, analysis, and reporting of Operational Risk Events and Issues/Actions across Capital Markets, working closely with Line of Business leads and Managers to ensure compliance with Enterprise Policy and Standing Order requirements.
 Lead thematic reviews of OREs to identify areas that may warrant highlighting in management reporting or additional control evaluation/enhancement/new control creation;
 Establish governance frameworks and oversight mechanisms for the capture, analysis, and reporting of Operational Risk Events and Issues/Actions across Capital Markets, ensuring compliance with Enterprise Policy and Standing Order requirements and driving consistency in ORE management practices;
 Set strategic direction for 1st Line of Defense (LOD) guidance in managing and mitigating operational risk, establishing clear accountability frameworks and ensuring alignment and consistency in the regional execution of operational risk tools, processes, and practices with the Global ORC&G approach;
 Oversee the development, delivery, and continuous enhancement of enterprise-wide training and awareness programs to embed a control-conscious culture and ensure clear understanding of control ownership, internal control management principles, and expected conduct, behaviours, roles, and responsibilities across the business;

 Enterprise Policy & Change Governance: 
 Support the Managing Director ORC&G through participation in projects to review and implement new enterprise policies that impact Capital Markets in North America, which may include assisting in the establishment of procedures/guidelines, liaising with internal and/or external parties to understand requirements and define parameters;
 Lead engagement with the appropriate Centre of Governance groups to provide input into the development of new/changed enterprise policies, clarifying proposed requirements in order to initiate discussions with the in-scope business units to assess the impact on the CM business processes and controls;
 Provide interpretation and guidance to broader ORC&G Team on Enterprise Methodology changes impacting Controls Management, Risk and Control Self Assessment (RCSA), OREs and Issues Management.

 Reporting: 
 Direct the development and production of monthly and quarterly Operational Risk reporting, including trend analysis, executive commentary, and business insights to support Regional, Legal Entity, and Line of Business governance reporting requirements; 
 Synthesize ORE data, control assurance results, assessment findings, and emerging risk trends into strategic insights and recommendations for senior leadership, identifying areas warranting executive escalation, policy intervention, or enterprise-wide action;
 Establish analytics and management information standards to support informed decision-making and governance across the operational risk portfolio;
 Oversee and review information consolidation for ad-hoc regulatory reporting/regulator information requests, as required.

 Relationship Management: 
 Spearhead engagement with CM Senior Management, Business and Functional Heads in matters relating to the internal risk and control environment.
 Represent ORC&G at the New Business Committee

 What you need to succeed? 
 Minimum Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant experience in Finance, Engineering, Science or Math desirable
 7 - 10 years of experience in Project Management, Risk Management, Audit and/or Financial Services industry
 Strong knowledge of trading and supporting systems used within Capital Markets. 
 Proven people management & development skills; ability to work effectively in a project team environment, demonstrated facilitation and leadership skills, strong listening and interview skills.

 Detailed understanding of RBC Capital Markets organizational structure (front office sales and trading, middle office, product control, BCS, regulatory/compliance, etc.)
 Self-motivated, able to work independently and within a team
 Ability to prioritize, plan and execute work to meet tight deadlines
 Strong innovative, problem-solving and analytical skills; a self-starter capable of functioning in an autonomous manner. 
 Capable of building strong relationships with clients and stakeholders across the enterprise

 We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. Hungry For Life International exists to bring about physical and spiritual change in the world.  Through global partnerships and community-focused initiatives, we support leaders and communities to cultivate spiritual vibrancy and human flourishing.  Our team is passionate, mission-driven, and committed to serving with integrity and excellence.

Position Summary

The Director of Finance and Administration provides strategic leadership and oversight for all financial, administrative, compliance, and human resource functions of the organization.  Reporting directly to the Managing Director, this role ensures strong financial stewardship, effective internal controls, and alignment of operations with Hungry For Life’s mission, values, and strategic objectives.  The Director is a key member of the executive leadership team and contributes both professionally and spiritually to the life of the ministry.

Direct and manage all financial plans, practices, and policies.

Prepare and manage annual budgets, forecasts, and cash-flow projections.
Supervise preparation of financial statements, management reports, and regulatory filings.
Coordinate annual external audits and ensure compliance with GAAP/IFRS.
Oversee donation processing, fund accounting, donor-designated funds, and grant compliance.
Manage banking relationships and investment strategies.
Ensure compliance with Canadian charity tax law and other relevant regulations.

jobs.description:
Chief Operating Officer (COO)

Who We Are

Great banking should feel effortless. The kind where things just work, the right information is easy to find, and the next step feels natural. At YNCU, we’re focused on making banking simpler, more intuitive, and more useful in the moments that matter. So instead of making people think about how banking works, we make it feel like it just does. That’s one of the ways we show care.

YNCU was created by working people and small business owners who pooled their money to make affordable financial services available to one another. They weren’t just customers—they were our founders. That spirit still shapes how we work today.

Innovation is part of our history, too. Credit unions helped introduce some of Canada’s earliest banking innovations, and that mindset continues at YNCU. We’re always looking for unmet needs, better ways to serve members, and simpler experiences that make banking easier to understand and use.

What You’ll Be Doing

In 2026, YNCU announced a new strategic vision guiding the organization into 2026 and beyond, marking the beginning of its next chapter of growth, clarity, and shared purpose. The strategy sharpens YNCU’s focus on the people who build, protect, and care for communities.  This direction builds on the credit union’s recent growth, including the integration of Comtech Fire Credit Union, and reflects YNCU’s commitment to relationship-driven, community-focused banking.  As part of this direction, YNCU will deepen member relationships through personalized financial advice, simplify the way members interact with their credit union across digital and in-branch experiences, and tailor products and services to better meet the needs of those who serve others every day.

Consistent with providing Your Neighbourhood Credit Union’s (YNCU) Members with the right financial services to live life, dream big and achieve financial success, the Chief Operating Officer (COO) provides strategic leadership and oversees the organizations operations strategy including retail and commercial delivery, marketing, brand, product, member experience, operational excellence and credit administration.

The COO drives alignment collaboration across YNCU by standardizing sales, service and operational practices, removing barriers to execution, and enabling shared business success.   This role accelerates sales performance through strong leadership, coaching and accountability and a culture of continuous improvement as well as operational excellence and regulatory compliance. The COO leads member operations including payments, operations and agent deposit processing.

In addition, the COO will oversee marketing, product and brand strategy across all channels for YNCU to deliver meaningful product and campaign leadership to drive member growth and sustainable business performance.

Leadership and Strategy

Actively and collaboratively participate in YNCU’s strategic planning process with the Chief Leadership Team and the Board of Directors and work closely with peers to develop and implement long and short-term plans to bring the Strategic Plans to life.  Be an advocate for internal culture, new initiatives, and transformation.
Provide strategic leadership and guidance to all functional areas of the Credit Union related to operational excellence and member experience.
Provide leadership to assigned Team Members through effective goal setting, delegation, and communication, and drive the achievement of goals in responsible business areas.
Ensure the execution of established goals with Team Members and monitor progress toward and sustainability of achieving set goals.
Conduct performance reviews as required, and formulate and implement corrective actions as needed
Facilitate the design of career development and training plans for each direct report to include coaching, motivation and support

Member Experience

Develop and implement a Member Centric business strategy to deliver outstanding Member experience across the entire Member journey.
Ensure a high quality, service-driven environment through service standards and initiatives that continuously enhance services for Members including the establishment and implementation of measurable performance benchmarks to gauge Member loyalty/satisfaction. 
Act as the Chief Complaints Resolution Officer for YNCU and act in any government relations activities on behalf of YNCU and own the Market Code of Conduct.
Champion and evolve the NPS program at YNCU, including target-setting and action planning.
Partner with our marketing team to understand Member insights and research and translate to meaningful strategies to continuously improve the Member experience. 
Lead sales enablement: supporting the Chief Member Experience Officer and Chief Commercial Officer and the distribution teams to deliver exceptional advice conversations to members.
Develop and support the frontline in the development of programs that support pipeline management, leveraging YNCU’s investment in Salesforce CRM.

Operational Excellence, Process Improvement & Project Management

Champion procedural enhancements, support systems, resources and activities that are focused on exceptional Member experience.
Provide first-line support to retail branch operations to resolve in-branch issues, business interruptions or management concerns.
Ensure operational policies and procedures and reviewed, modernized and have meaningful job aids and workflows for our staff.
Apply continuous improvement methodologies to YNCU’s operations processes and procedures.
Project management leadership for organizational projects or changes to ensure stakeholder management, resource requirements, timelines and budgets are met.

Marketing

Lead integrated brand and marketing strategy to support growth in membership, deposits, and lending.
Oversee digital marketing, campaign management, content strategy, and market research.
Build strong brand positioning aligned with the credit union’s cooperative mission and community presence.
Drive data-driven marketing and personalized member engagement.

Product Innovation

Work in partnership with retail, commercial and wealth channel leaders to share Member experience feedback and partner on product evolution and innovation to meet Member needs.
Lead business case development and feasibility assessments for new product initiatives.

Operations and Payments

Lead the Member support and payment services team to ensure efficient and timely service to our branch teams. 
Accountable for payment processing, investment administration, estate administration and all payment services for YNCU.

Lead the commercial and retail credit administration teams, ensuring timely and accurate support to commercial and retail distribution teams.
Keep abreast of ind
ustry changes as they relate to payments modernization and open banking. Participate and manage any changes to payment products and services driven by industry or third parties.

Other

Actively and collaboratively participate in the annual budget process to ensure alignment of department with YNCU goals and objectives and create effective business plans.
Facilitate risk mitigation and ensure compliance with all regulations pertaining to Member Services.
Stay informed of trends and changes in Member Experience, products and services and provide reports to the Chief Leadership Team. Monitor local, regional and national economic, financial, industry and political events which could impact YNCU.
Prepare reports, participate in meetings, with the Board of Directors and serve on committees as required, and represent and promote YNCU at external functions.
Perform other duties as required.

This position is for an existing vacancy within our team.

What we are looking for:

Post secondary diploma, degree and/or certification in business, finance or a related program, or equivalent business experience
Minimum ten (10) years of senior level experience in financial services predominantly in the areas of financial services operations.  Experience with retail branch network. 
Strong knowledge of the Credit Unions Act and Regulations, Credit Union By-laws and Policies
Working knowledge of applicable government regulations and legal requirements
Sound knowledge of economic and financial trends
Effective understanding and use of Microsoft Office (Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint)
Must have a valid Ontario driver's license and reliable available vehicle
Must meet bonding requirements

The compensation offered to the successful applicant for this role will be determined by the candidate’s relevant skills and experience and internal equity. More information about our total rewards package will be available during the hiring process.

At YNCU, you are more than an employee. You are part of a purpose driven team that strengthens local communities and champions the credit union difference. We believe banking locally matters, and every day our team helps members build stronger financial futures through personalized advice, trusted relationships, and community support.

As a people first organization, we are committed to an environment where employees feel supported, valued, and empowered to grow. Through professional development, wellness initiatives, volunteering, and collaborative team experiences, we invest in our people because they are at the heart of everything we do. Programs like our Good Neighbours Employee Volunteer Program and Monthly Staff Donation Draws give employees a direct voice in supporting the causes that matter most to them and their communities
