jobs.title: Director, Supply Chain - Canada
jobs.description:
Job Location: Laval, Quebec, CAN

Job Requisition ID: 15804

Join our global diversified pharmaceutical company enriching lives through our relentless drive to deliver better health outcomes to our patients. We are all in it together to make a difference. Be a part of a culture that doesn't just wait for change but actively creates it—where your skills and values drive our collective progress and impact.

We are looking for a trustworthy and respectful individual who consistently does the right thing. Someone who is imaginative and proactive, with a keen eye for what is possible. A perceptive and adaptive person who is action oriented. We need a disciplined, focused, and accountable team member. If you embody these values, come join our company and help us shape the future.

General Responsibilities

Provide strategic and operational leadership for the Supply Chain Planning function across Canada. The primary objective of the role is to ensure reliable, customer-focused product supply while optimizing inventory investment, manufacturing capacity, and overall supply chain performance.

The incumbent is responsible for establishing and implementing integrated demand, supply, inventory, and production planning processes to support business growth, customer service, financial objectives, and the overall supply chain strategy.

The incumbent provides leadership to the Planning teams across two Canadian manufacturing sites, as well as the Commercial Planning team, which works closely and regularly with the business units.

The Supply Chain Planning function plays a central role within the organization, connecting commercial strategy with manufacturing operations and supply execution. The incumbent works closely with Business Leadership, Quality, Procurement, Manufacturing, Commercial Operations, Business Intelligence, Finance, Regulatory Affairs, Logistics & Distribution, Human Resources, and Global Supply Chain Leadership.

As a leader of leaders, the incumbent directly supervises five employees across three locations and is responsible for building organizational capabilities, fostering collaboration, and developing a high-performing planning organization.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the Demand Planning function and process for Canada, ensuring the development of robust, data-driven forecasts aligned with commercial strategy and market dynamics.
Lead the Supply Planning function and process for Canada, ensuring product availability and appropriate alignment between demand, supply, production capacity, and inventory.
Oversee Inventory Management and Planning, balancing customer service, working capital, inventory health, and obsolescence risks.
Lead the Production Planning function across two Canadian manufacturing sites.
Own the Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) and Integrated Business Planning (IBP) processes, ensuring alignment between Commercial, Finance, Operations, and Supply Chain.
Monitor and improve key planning and supply chain performance indicators, including forecast accuracy, forecast bias, inventory levels, obsolescence, backorders, and customer service levels, including fill rate.
Partner with Logistics & Distribution teams to optimize end-to-end product flow and ensure customer requirements are consistently met.
Contribute to annual budgeting, strategic planning, and quarterly financial forecast updates, including financial assumptions related to inventory and supply.
Develop and implement supply chain planning strategies that support business growth, operational resilience, cost optimization, and customer service objectives.
Identify and lead initiatives to improve planning processes, systems, data quality, and organizational effectiveness.
Participate in the Global Supply Chain Planning Leadership Team, contributing to global standards, transformation initiatives, and best-practice sharing.
Collaborate strategically with Commercial, Finance, Quality, Procurement, Regulatory Affairs, Human Resources, Logistics & Distribution, and Operations leaders.
Work closely with manufacturing sites to ensure alignment between production plans, manufacturing capacity, raw materials, and operational requirements.
Lead talent development, performance management, employee retention, and succession planning activities within the Planning function.
Foster a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, collaboration, and customer-centric decision-making.

Education And Experience Requirements

A minimum of a Bachelor's degree in Science, Engineering, Business Administration, Supply Chain Management, or a related discipline is required.
An advanced degree in Science, Engineering, Business Administration, Supply Chain Management, or a related field is considered an asset.
A minimum of ten (10) years of relevant supply chain experience within the pharmaceutical, life sciences, or healthcare industries.
Demonstrated experience leading supply chain planning activities at both the manufacturing site level and across multiple sites at an organizational level.
Significant people leadership experience, including developing high-performing teams and building organizational capabilities.
Experience developing and implementing integrated, end-to-end, customer-centric supply chain strategies and innovative solutions that improve service, inventory management, costs, and operational resilience.
Demonstrated ability to operate effectively within a matrixed, multinational organization and influence senior leaders and stakeholders without direct reporting authority.

Core Competencies

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent proficiency in Excel, PowerPoint, SAP and supply chain planning systems.
Professional certifications such as APICS/ASCM, CSCP, Lean, Six Sigma, or equivalent are considered assets.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills (French and English).
Strong executive presence, with a demonstrated ability to clearly communicate complex supply chain issues and strategic recommendations to senior leadership.

Total Rewards

The range of starting base pay for this role is $145,000 to $180,000. Actual starting pay will be based on a wide range of factors including, but not limited to, relevant skills, experience, qualifications, education and location. In addition to base pay, this position is eligible for participation in our annual bonus program.

What We Have To Offer Employees

Annual bonus plan
Health insurance coverage upon start date
Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP & DPSP) for qualifying employees
Competitive vacation policy
Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) for qualifying employees
Employee Recognition Program
Full-service cafeteria with weekly lunch specials; free coffee and tea
Free onsite gym
Free parking
Electric vehicle parking
Tuition reimbursement
Years of Service Awards
Employee Referral Program
Maternity Leave top-up

Version française

Nous recherchons une personne digne de confiance et respectueuse, qui agit toujours de manière intègre. Une personne imaginative et proactive, ayant un bon sens des opportunités. Une personne perspicace et adaptable, orientée vers l’action. Nous avons besoin d’un membre d’équipe discipliné, concentré et responsable. Si vous vous reconnaissez dans ces valeurs, joignez-vous à notre entreprise et contribuez à façonner l’avenir.

Responsabilités générales

Assurer le leadership stratégique et opérationnel de la fonction de planification de la chaîne d’approvisionnement pour le Canada. L’objectif principal du poste est d’assurer un approvisionnement fiable et axé sur les besoins des clients, tout en optimisant les investissements en stocks, la capacité de fabrication et la performance globale de la chaîne d’approvisionnement.

Le ou la titulaire du poste est responsable de l’établissement et de la mise en œuvre de processus intégrés de planification de la demande, de l’approvisionnement, des stocks et de la production, afin de soutenir la croissance de l’entreprise, le service à la clientèle, les objectifs financiers et la stratégie globale de la chaîne d’approvisionnement.

La personne assure la direction des équipes de planification de deux sites de fabrication canadiens, ainsi que de l’équipe de planification commerciale, qui collabore étroitement et régulièrement avec les unités d’affaires.

La fonction de planification de la chaîne d’approvisionnement occupe une position centrale au sein de l’entreprise, assurant le lien entre la stratégie commerciale, les activités de fabrication et l’exécution de l’approvisionnement. Le ou la titulaire collabore étroitement avec la direction des unités d’affaires, les équipes de la qualité, des achats, de la fabrication, des opérations commerciales, de l’intelligence d’affaires, des finances, des affaires réglementaires, de la logistique et de la distribution, des ressources humaines ainsi qu’avec la direction mondiale de la chaîne d’approvisionnement.

À titre de gestionnaire de gestionnaires, la personne supervise directement cinq employés répartis dans trois emplacements. Elle est responsable du développement des capacités organisationnelles, de la promotion de la collaboration et de la mise en place d’une équipe de planification hautement performante.

Responsabilités principales

Diriger la fonction et le processus de planification de la demande pour le Canada et la Russie, en assurant l’élaboration de prévisions rigoureuses, fondées sur les données et alignées sur la stratégie commerciale et les réalités du marché.
Diriger la fonction et le processus de planification de l’approvisionnement pour le Canada, afin d’assurer la disponibilité des produits et un alignement adéquat entre la demande, l’approvisionnement, la capacité de production et les stocks.
Superviser la gestion et la planification des stocks, en maintenant un équilibre entre le service à la clientèle, le fonds de roulement, la saine gestion des stocks et les risques d’obsolescence.
Diriger la fonction de planification de la production dans deux sites de fabrication canadiens.
Assumer la responsabilité du processus de planification des ventes et des opérations (S&OP) et de planification intégrée des activités (IBP), en assurant l’alignement entre les équipes commerciales, les finances, les opérations et la chaîne d’approvisionnement.
Assurer le suivi et l’amélioration des principaux indicateurs de performance de la planification et de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, notamment la précision des prévisions, les biais de prévision, les niveaux de stocks, l’obsolescence, les commandes en souffrance et le niveau de service à la clientèle, y compris le taux de satisfaction des commandes.
Collaborer avec les équipes de logistique et de distribution afin d’optimiser le flux des produits de bout en bout et de veiller à ce que les besoins des clients soient satisfaits de façon constante.
Contribuer à l’élaboration des budgets annuels, à la planification stratégique et aux mises à jour trimestrielles des prévisions financières, notamment en ce qui concerne les hypothèses financières liées aux stocks et à l’approvisionnement.
Élaborer et mettre en œuvre des stratégies de planification de la chaîne d’approvisionnement qui soutiennent la croissance de l’entreprise, la résilience opérationnelle, l’optimisation des coûts et les objectifs de service à la clientèle.
Cerner et diriger les initiatives visant à améliorer les processus de planification, les systèmes, la qualité des données et l’efficacité organisationnelle.
Participer à l’équipe mondiale de direction de la planification de la chaîne d’approvisionnement et contribuer à l’établissement de normes mondiales, aux initiatives de transformation et au partage des meilleures pratiques.
Collaborer de façon stratégique avec les dirigeants des fonctions commerciales, des finances, de la qualité, des achats, des affaires réglementaires, des ressources humaines, de la logistique et de la distribution ainsi que des opérations.

jobs.title: Director, Supply Chain
jobs.description:
Headquartered in Toronto, Polar Racking Inc. is a North American leader in the design, engineering and manufacturing of PV mounting systems. We are at the forefront of PV innovation, leading the industry in cutting edge design with a focus on continuous innovation. Our vision is to deliver the highest value to our clients at the lowest cost per kWh. To support this, the company has a diversified portfolio of ground mount and carport products for the commercial and utility scale markets. This, coupled with our unique suite of engineering collaboration tools, technical services and installation support allow us to deliver turnkey solutions that are modular, lighter, and quicker to install. We support our North American and Caribbean clients from our locations in Toronto, Calgary, and US.
  
  

**The Opportunity:**  

We are seeking a strategic and execution\-focused Director of Supply Chain to lead end\-to\-end supply chain operations in a manufacturing environment specializing in metal parts fabrication. This role requires deep technical fluency, strong commercial acumen, and the ability to build resilient, cost\-effective supplier networks. A mechanical engineering background is strongly preferred due to the technical complexity of the components and manufacturing processes involved.
  
  

The Director of Supply Chain will oversee procurement, strategic sourcing, supplier development, contract negotiation, production planning, inventory management, and quality alignment across the supply base.
  
  

**Key Responsibilities:**  

Strategic Leadership
  
  

* Develop and execute a comprehensive supply chain strategy aligned with operational and financial objectives.
* Lead sourcing initiatives for metal components, machined parts, fabricated assemblies, and related materials.
* Build long\-term supplier partnerships while driving cost optimization, risk mitigation, and performance improvement.
* Establish KPIs to monitor supplier performance, cost efficiency, delivery reliability, and quality metrics.


Technical \& Operational Oversight
  
  

* Evaluate and source metal fabrication suppliers including machining, welding, stamping, casting, and finishing processes.
* Interpret and review technical drawings, specifications, and GD\&T to ensure supplier capability alignment.
* Collaborate closely with Engineering and Quality teams to support NPI (New Product Introduction) and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Ensure suppliers adhere to established quality control systems and regulatory standards.


Contracting \& Commercial Management
  
  

* Lead high\-value contract negotiations, including pricing models, long\-term agreements, and performance clauses.
* Manage supplier contracts to ensure compliance, cost competitiveness, and risk protection.
* Develop cost models and conduct should\-cost analyses for fabricated and machined components.


Quality \& Compliance
  
  

* Implement and maintain robust supplier quality management processes.
* Conduct supplier audits and capability assessments.
* Partner with Quality Assurance to manage corrective actions, root cause analysis, and continuous improvement programs.


Team Leadership
  
  

* Build and lead a high\-performing supply chain team.
* Develop succession planning and talent development strategies.
* Foster cross\-functional collaboration across Engineering, Manufacturing, Finance, and Sales.


**Core Competencies:**  

* Strategic sourcing and cost modeling
* Technical literacy in metal fabrication processes
* Supplier development and risk management
* Negotiation and commercial structuring
* Quality systems and compliance management
* Data\-driven decision\-making
* Executive communication and leadership


**Qualifications:**  

* 10\+ years of progressive experience in supply chain leadership within a manufacturing environment.
* Demonstrated experience sourcing metal fabricated and machined parts.
* Proven success in complex contract negotiations.
* Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and technical specifications.
* Strong understanding of quality control methodologies (e.g., ISO standards, Six Sigma, SPC, PPAP).
* Experience managing global supplier networks.


Preferred
  
  

* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering (strongly preferred).
* MBA or advanced degree in Supply Chain, Operations, or Engineering.
* Experience in vertically integrated or engineered\-to\-order manufacturing environments.
* Background in lean manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives.


Why Polar Racking?
  
  

Join our team and become part of a dynamic company at the forefront of the renewable energy sector. In addition to competitive compensation, we offer a comprehensive benefits package including RRSP contributions, generous vacation time, and the opportunity for career growth.
  
As a valued member of our team, you'll also enjoy perks such as a company vehicle and a collaborative, fun work environment where innovation and teamwork are celebrated. If you're passionate about making a positive impact in the world while working with a supportive team, we invite you to apply and embark on an exciting journey with us.
  
We value an innovative, diverse workplace where all colleagues feel empowered to be their authentic selves. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

jobs.description:
Blacksmith Agency

Marketing
Full time
Remote (USA, Canada or South Africa)

About The Role

Blacksmith Agency runs PPC and SEO for clients across multifamily, B2B and technical verticals. As Director of Performance Marketing you lead that department. The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist report to you and they are the specialists in their channels. Right now nobody owns this function, which is the whole reason this seat is open.

This is a management seat, not a senior individual contributor one.
You will not be building campaigns, and on technical SEO your strategist will know more than you do. That is the arrangement, not a gap. You carry channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale. The strategists carry the execution of it, and you carry whether the department delivers.

What You Own

The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist: their quality bar, their development, their reviews, and the call when someone is not going to get there.
The standard the work is held to. What a good audit looks like, what gets checked before work leaves the agency, how an account is reported. You write it and you hold two specialists to it.
Client results across the whole function, including whether our reporting is honest. Nobody here is auditing attribution and GA4 accuracy today.
The escalation when an account is at risk. You diagnose it, you direct the strategist who fixes it, and you are on the call with the client.
Channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale.
What we tell sales we can credibly deliver, before it gets sold.
The hiring plan for the department, and first-round interviews for your own team, within about a quarter.

What You Need

Strategists or specialists who have reported to you, where their reviews, their development and the decision when someone was not working out were yours. Managing accounts is not this.
7+ years across paid media and SEO. Owning one channel while sitting beside the other does not count here.
Enough depth in Google Ads, GA4, Search Console, Meta and Microsoft Ads to tell good work from work that merely looks good. That is a lower bar than doing it and a higher bar than reading a report.
One account you turned around that you can talk through: the metric, the figure before, the figure after, and why the change worked. Whose hands were on the keyboard matters far less than whether the diagnosis was yours.
Comfortable being the client-facing owner when an account is underperforming. That call comes to you, not to the strategist.
Agency experience carrying many accounts at once.

Please do not apply if

Nobody has ever reported to you, or you have never owned someone's review or had to performance-manage anyone.
You have only ever run one channel.
All of your experience is in-house on a single brand.
What you actually want is to keep building campaigns yourself. That is not a lesser ambition, it is a different job, and this is not it.

None of these are preferences we bend on. They are how we screen, so applying anyway costs you an hour and gets you a no.

Process

Three conversations, then a decision. A thirty minute screen with our recruiter, a first round with the founder this seat reports to, and a final. No take-home project and no panel interview.

How To Apply

Four fields at the link, then a short 6 minute Predictive Index assessment. Use the same email throughout. No cover letter.

jobs.title: VP, Enterprise Sales
jobs.description:
About CoLab

At CoLab, we help mechanical engineering teams bring life-changing products to market years sooner.

We build AI for engineers designing cars, medical devices, and jet engines. Products this complex aren't sketched and sent to production. Teams spend months on iterations, reviews, and tests, predicting how every part performs before anything is built. CoLab is where those reviews happen, and we capture the rationale behind every change. Other tools show what changed between versions. Only CoLab knows why. That's how our AI helps manufacturers like Bobcat, Triumph Motorcycles, and GE Appliances make better decisions, eliminate rework cycles, and get to market faster.

Proudly based in St. John's, Newfoundland, CoLab started with one customer in 2018. Since then we've raised a $72M Series C, been named the 57th fastest growing company in North America by Deloitte (Fast 500™), signed multi-year AI partnerships with companies like Bombardier, and grown to a team of 250+.

About the Role

CoLab is hiring a highly motivated VP of Enterprise Sales to scale our enterprise sales team and the process behind it during a critical phase of growth. You will report to our SVP of Sales and lead enterprise teams, whose Account Executives sell deals from $25K to $500K and upwards of $1M to Fortune 500 manufacturers in automotive, industrial, heavy machinery, medical device and consumer products.

CoLab sells into engineering and design teams, not just procurement or supply chain. These are complex, multi-stakeholder deals with long cycles and no pre-existing budget line, so this person needs to be a strong closer and a stronger coach.

What you'll do

You will own enterprise new-logo and expansion revenue and build the repeatable system that lets the team scale.

Lead and coach enterprise teams.
Run a weekly coaching cadence, review deals in depth, and sit in on key calls to raise how reps run complex, multi-threaded cycles.
Recruit, develop, and retain top talent.
Provide effective coaching, career development, and performance management, and set clear expectations and scorecards.
Own the number.
Set quotas and territories, drive pipeline coverage, and deliver an accurate forecast to the SVP of Sales.
Inspect and refine the sales process.
Dive into the pipeline, drive daily improvements, and enforce consistent stage criteria, mutual action plans, and deal reviews using a methodology such as MEDDPICC.
Be a hands-on player/coach.
Lead by example: jump on intro calls, step into enterprise negotiations, and help close the largest accounts.
Expand within existing customers.
Identify upsell and cross-sell opportunities to grow business with the current client base.
Sell value to engineering buyers.
Help reps build business cases around design error cost, review cycle time, and quality, and engage engineering leaders and executive sponsors.
Collaborate cross-functionally.
Work with BDRs and Marketing on pipeline and account targeting, and Customer Engineering and Product on technical selling.
Report with accuracy.
Use Salesforce (and other tools) to report sales performance, pipeline movement, and forecasts to the senior leadership team.
Share market feedback and experiment.
Monitor customer, market, and competitor activity, feed insights to internal partners, and test new sales strategies to improve ARR and sales efficiency.

What you'll bring

10+ years of B2B SaaS sales, including 4+ years leading enterprise sales teams (Director or VP level), ideally with experience multiple teams and managers ( frontline managers to Director).
A track record of closing six-figure deals, ideally $500K+ and up to $1M, with multiple stakeholders and long sales cycles.
Experience selling into technical buyers and complex organizations, using consultative methods in undefined product categories where educating the buyer and creating budget is essential.
Experience scaling a sales organization through a high-growth phase and building process that outlasts you.
Strong executive presence and the ability to build trust quickly with skeptical C-suite and VP-level stakeholders.
A disciplined forecaster with a working command of Salesforce and a formal methodology (MEDDPICC, Challenger, or similar), and the judgment to adapt it.
A coach first: you can step into an existing team of experienced reps and earn credibility by improving how they sell, including in remote or hybrid environments.
A builder's mindset: you see what's missing, create it, and don't wait for a playbook or permission.
No ego, high drive, and a fast learner who seeks feedback and works well cross-functionally. Values of Kindness & Respect, One Team One Mission, and Better Everyday come naturally.

Nice to have

Experience selling into manufacturing, aerospace and defense, automotive, or industrial customers, and comfort with engineering buyers (CAD, PLM, design review).
Experience selling AI, engineering software, or design-collaboration tools.
Experience selling a mix of SaaS, services, and hardware.
Prior experience inheriting an established team, not only building one from scratch.
Familiarity with Salesforce, Gong, and a modern sales-tech stack.

Why CoLab and the details

This is a chance to lead the enterprise sales team at a company already selling complex deals to Fortune 500 manufacturers, at a critical phase of growth. You will shape the team, the process, and how CoLab sells to engineering organizations.

jobs.title: Head of Accounts
jobs.description:
About Orium

Orium builds smart, modern commerce solutions that help enterprise brands move faster and stay ahead.

By bringing together AI, data, and composable systems, we create experiences designed for collaboration between people and intelligent agents— helping our clients work more efficiently, adapt quickly, and gain a long-term competitive edge.

With more composable launches than any firm in the Americas and deep expertise across commerce architecture, we partner with leading technology providers to deliver scalable solutions that evolve with our clients and accelerate time to value.

We blend systems thinking, data-driven design, and intelligent delivery, embedding AI and agents into our own teams to move faster, reduce friction, and co-create with greater precision. The result: adaptive, cross-channel experiences that keep our clients ahead of what’s next.

About The Opportunity

Orium is entering a new phase of growth, where expanding and deepening existing client relationships is as critical as acquiring new ones.

We’re hiring a Head of Accounts to define and lead how we grow, manage, and scale our current client portfolio. This is a strategic leadership role responsible for transforming account management into a disciplined, insight-driven, and AI-enabled function that consistently drives customer lifetime value. This role owns the account growth engine end-to-end: team leadership, commercial outcomes, and the operating discipline needed to convert expansion opportunities and ensure Orium has a repeatable approach to account planning, forecasting, and sales operations.

You will manage Account Managers and work closely with Delivery, Line of Business Owners, Marketing, and Sales leadership to ensure current accounts are actively managed, forecasted, and expanded, bringing structure to how Orium grows existing relationships through account playbooks, expansion plans, quarterly forecasts, and bookings targets.

This person must be a strong consultant in their own right — someone who can sit across from a client’s VP of Digital or CTO, understand their business challenges, and map those challenges to commercial opportunities without relying on internal subject matter experts to carry the conversation. They should be comfortable leading strategic planning discussions, challenging a client’s assumptions, and building a case for investment based on business outcomes.

A core mandate of this role is scaling the practical use of AI across the account management function to improve team efficiency, effectiveness, and quality, and to help clients connect AI-enabled opportunities to measurable business outcomes. This means going beyond process improvement. This role uses AI to surface account risks early, identify the right commercial move at the right moment, and turn account data into revenue action.

Responsibilities

Personal Account Ownership

Carry a personal portfolio of 5–8 priority accounts, serving as the primary commercial relationship owner and demonstrating the standard of account management the team is expected to deliver.
Drive expansion and renewal conversations at meaningful deal sizes ($200K–$500K+), personally navigating complex client organizations, building multi-stakeholder relationships, and closing commercial opportunities.
Use personal account work to model the consultative selling, objection handling, and proactive commercial engagement the broader team is being coached to develop.

Account Growth & Portfolio Strategy

Own the strategy for growing Orium’s existing client portfolio, with accountability for expansion revenue and lifetime value.
Identify, prioritize, and drive expansion opportunities across accounts, , including cross-LOB expansion (Commerce to DXP, DXP to Agentic), partner-driven joint plays (commercetools, Stripe, Contentstack), transition of project-based clients into ongoing optimization or managed service relationships, and long-term partnership growth.
Establish account-level growth strategies for priority clients, including relationship mapping, opportunity hypotheses, and commercial targets.
Partner with Sales, Delivery, and LOB leaders to convert account insights into executable growth plans.
Monitor account health, client satisfaction, delivery performance, and commercial potential to proactively manage risk and opportunity.
Elevate client relationships to executive-level partnerships, positioning Orium as a long-term strategic advisor.
Frame AI as a driver of customer outcomes, helping clients understand how AI can support measurable business goals such as increased revenue, improved conversion, lower operational costs, better customer experiences, and faster execution.

Account Operating Model & Playbooks

Define and implement Orium’s account management playbooks, including standards for account planning, business reviews, relationship management, renewal motions, expansion planning, and risk mitigation.
Create a consistent operating rhythm for managing current accounts across the business.
Establish clear expectations for how account teams identify opportunities, document account intelligence, manage stakeholders, and progress expansion conversations.
Improve visibility into account activity, pipeline, and next steps across Orium’s leadership team.
Build scalable playbooks, templates, and tools that improve consistency without adding unnecessary complexity.

AI-Enabled Account Management

Design and implement an AI-enabled account management function that increases scale, quality, and efficiency. This would focus on outcomes such as: earlier risk detection, faster opportunity identification, and higher conversion across the portfolio.
Embed AI and agentic workflows across account research, opportunity identification, forecasting, and meeting preparation. Use these to surface next best actions, track client sentiment, and flag at-risk accounts before they escalate.
Develop reusable, AI-supported assets such as account plans, growth frameworks, and expansion playbooks.
Build and operationalize AI-assisted workflows, including account research, meeting preparation, follow-up, and opportunity tracking that raise the consistency and quality of account team output.
Replace manual tracking with automated account monitoring and AI-prioritized action lists, so no expansion opportunity or at-risk account goes unnoticed.
Connect AI initiatives in client accounts to measurable outcomes. Articulate value in terms of revenue growth, reduced churn, improved conversion, and faster time to value.
Define and track success metrics such as increased opportunity conversion, improved forecast accuracy, and reduced manual effort.

Sales Operations for Current Accounts

Own day-to-day sales operations for existing accounts, including bookings targets, pipeline hygiene, opportunity tracking, and quarterly forecasting.
Lead the account forecast process, ensuring bookings projections are accurate, current, and tied to concrete client opportunities.
Partner with cross-functional leadership to track bookings performance, forecast gaps, and account-level revenue opportunities.
Ensure CRM data and account records are complete, accurate, and useful for decision-making.
Develop reporting that gives leadership clear visibility into account performance, expansion pipeline, forecast confidence, and commercial risks.

Team Leadership & Function Building

Manage and develop the account management team, including Account Managers, CSM-commercial hybrids, and Client Partners, providing clear priorities, development support, and accountability, with a focus on commercial thinking, opportunity development, and client engagement.

jobs.description:
About Us

SickKids Foundation, with over 50 years of philanthropic impact is Canada's largest charitable funder of child health research, learning and care, raising over $200 million last year. As a national charity, SickKids Foundation invests in national and international initiatives to benefit children in Canada and around the world. As the fundraising partner to The Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids), we are aligned in supporting Precision Child Health (PCH), the future of tailoring medicine to each child's unique traits so SickKids can diagnose faster, treat smarter, and predict better.

We are driven by our core values of integrity, collaboration, excellence, innovation, and inclusion, with goals of delivering a superior donor experience, investing in our people and culture, driving innovative and sustainable fundraising, and disrupting the market through data and technology.

SickKids Foundation is committed to an inclusive culture by embedding equity, diversity and inclusion in our policies, practices, and behaviours. We aim to build awareness and skills in this area, both internally and with our partners. Our commitment extends to creating a safe, positive work environment. For details on our Equity, Diversity & Inclusion commitment, please click here.

We’re committed to attracting and retaining passionate individuals to help create a healthier future. That’s why SickKids Foundation is looking for a new Associate Director, Data Engineer.

Description Of The Position

Reporting to the Director, Data Science & Engineering, the Associate Director, Data Engineer designs, builds, and operates enterprise-grade data platforms that deliver trusted, well-governed data across SickKids Foundation. The role will help establish and evolve a production-grade cloud platform using medallion architecture principles, with a focus on reliability, data quality, cost efficiency, and scalable delivery.

As a senior hands-on technical contributor, you will set engineering standards, support platform incident response, enable self-serve analytics and AI-powered data products, and provide specialized technical guidance to data and analytics partners across the Foundation.

You will

Design, build, and operate enterprise-grade data engineering platforms using modern cloud technologies such as Microsoft Fabric, Snowflake, and Databricks, aligned to bronze, silver, and gold medallion architecture principles.
Build and maintain robust, idempotent ETL/ELT pipelines with embedded validation, data quality checks, clear lineage, and repeatable delivery workflows.
Design data models and semantic layers that make trusted data accessible for analytics, reporting, and self-serve business intelligence.
Establish platform observability through query profiling, cost attribution, utilization metrics, alerting, and SLO/SLA monitoring; lead day-to-day response to data availability and performance incidents.
Define and enforce coding standards, CI/CD patterns, and Infrastructure-as-Code practices to support consistent, secure, and scalable platform deployment.
Partner with business stakeholders, Data & Analytics, IT/Infrastructure, and Security teams to translate requirements into reliable platform capabilities and support appropriate access, governance, and compliance.
Enable AI and advanced analytics use cases, including natural-language querying and AI-powered data products, by partnering with stakeholders to identify and deliver high-value opportunities.
Stay current with developments in cloud data platforms, AI, and emerging engineering practices, bringing relevant advancements into the platform roadmap and providing technical guidance to analysts, BI developers, and engineering partners.

Qualifications

While we know that for any job posting no one candidate will possess the qualifications being sought in equal measure, below is an outline of the qualifications we believe are important for a candidate to bring to the position or for the successful candidate to develop while in the role:

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Systems, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
5-7 years of hands-on data engineering or platform engineering experience, ideally spanning the full lifecycle of architecting, building, and operating production data platforms.
Deep technical expertise with modern cloud data platforms such as Microsoft Fabric, Snowflake, or Databricks and strong knowledge of medallion/lakehouse architecture.
Strong data modelling and database design skills for analytics and business consumption, including dimensional modelling and semantic layers for self-serve BI.
Hands-on experience developing production-grade ETL/ELT pipelines and working with data quality, governance, CI/CD, and Infrastructure-as-Code practices.
Experience establishing observability, performance monitoring, reliability standards, and incident-response practices in production data environments.
Working knowledge of AI and advanced analytics tooling, including approaches that support natural-language querying and AI-powered data products.
Strong technical judgment, problem-solving, communication, and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across technical and non-technical stakeholder groups.
Knowledge of foundational data domains, business processes, and enterprise applications is an asset.

We’re looking for a passionate individual who is interested in moving the dial and making a difference. We are an environment that looks to attract hardworking and committed people; people who want to challenge themselves and grow with a globally recognized brand that continues to change the world. If this describes you, consider joining our team. We look forward to reviewing your application.

$99,297 - $124,121; with the ability to progress to a maximum of $142,739 with demonstrated experience and proficiency. To ensure fair and equitable pay at SickKids Foundation, placement on the salary range will be based on your years of experience, skills, and qualifications relevant to the Associate Director, Data Engineer role.

To help you lead in the fight for kids’ health and to support your health, wellness, and career growth, in addition to competitive compensation, we offer a comprehensive benefit package (includes a flex benefit plan), tuition reimbursement, flexible work arrangements, pension plan and birth parent/parental top up – to name a few!

At the heart of CSA Group is a vision: making the world a better, safer, more sustainable place. It's been part of our mission for nearly one hundred years: from the first engineering standard for railway bridges developed in 1919, to more than 3,500 standards, codes & related products today.

Job Summary

Responsible for leading treasury and cash flow management for the Canadian Standards Association (CSA), overseeing tax planning, administration, and compliance, and ensuring accurate accounting, reporting, and internal coordination related to CSA's investments and its interest in a separately governed investment entity.

Principal Duties & Responsibilities

Investment Reporting & Governance Coordination

Serve as liaison with the separately governed investment entity to ensure accurate accounting, reporting, and reconciliation of CSA's interest in, and transactions with, the investment entity.
For CSA’s investment portfolio, manage relationships with external investment consultants, asset managers, custodians, and banking partners.
Prepare and/or review investment-related account reconciliations, schedules and supporting documentation for monthly, quarterly and annual financial reporting.
Coordinate with the investment entity, custodians, external investment managers, auditors and other service providers to obtain timely and accurate information required for CSA accounting and reporting.

Treasury, Cash Flow & Capital Management - Canadian Standards Association

Lead CSA's treasury operations and enterprise cash-flow management, including short- and medium-term liquidity forecasting.
Develop and maintain rolling cash-flow forecasts to ensure CSA has sufficient liquidity to meet operating, capital and strategic requirements.
Determine CSA's near-term funding needs and coordinate cash movements, contributions, distributions or other transfers with the investment entity in accordance with approved governance and authorization processes.
Manage CSA banking and treasury relationships, bank accounts, signing authorities and treasury controls.
Optimize CSA's operating cash balances and short-term liquidity within approved policies and risk parameters.
Develop liquidity management policies, cash reserve parameters and contingency funding plans for CSA.
Monitor counterparty exposure, interest rates, credit conditions and currency developments relevant to CSA's treasury activities.
Prepare treasury and liquidity reporting for executive management and the Board, including cash forecasts, liquidity headroom and key risks.

Tax Strategy, Planning, Administration & Compliance

Lead and coordinate CSA's tax planning, administration and compliance activities, working with external tax and legal advisors as appropriate.
Develop and maintain tax policies, internal controls and governance processes.
Assess tax implications of transactions between CSA and the investment entity, including investment income, distributions, capital movements, financing arrangements and restructurings.
Oversee corporate tax compliance, including income tax returns, information returns, withholding taxes, indirect taxes and applicable foreign reporting obligations.
Coordinate tax provisions and related financial statement reporting and audit support.
Monitor relevant Canadian and international tax developments and advise management on implications for CSA. Pension compliance
Lead the financial and regulatory compliance activities for CSA's Defined Benefit (DB) and Defined Contribution (DC) pension plans, ensuring adherence to applicable legislation, plan provisions, and regulatory requirements.
Oversee the financial administration of CSA's pension plans, including monitoring pension contributions, special payments, and funding obligations to ensure compliance with plan policies and regulatory requirements.
Work closely with Payroll, Human Resources, and external actuaries to validate pension calculations, contribution requirements, and funding transactions.
Monitor pension regulatory developments and funding requirements, including those established by the Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario (FSRA), and advise management on implications for CSA.
Support pension-related accounting, financial reporting, audit requirements, and disclosures associated with CSA's pension obligations.

Preferred Education & Experience

University degree in Accounting, Finance or a related field; CPA designation strongly preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in treasury, accounting/financial reporting and tax, ideally in a complex organization.
Strong experience in cash-flow forecasting, liquidity management, banking and treasury operations.
Experience accounting for investments and/or interests in separately governed entities and coordinating information from external managers, custodians or administrators.
Strong knowledge of financial reporting, internal controls, corporate taxation and treasury governance.
Knowledge of foreign-exchange risk management and hedging is an asset.
Experience preparing materials for senior management and Boards or Board committees.
Critical and innovative problem-solving ability and strong attention to detail.
Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills.
Demonstrated ability to lead across multiple finance disciplines and develop a high-performing team.

Reaching customers in over 100 countries worldwide, our portfolio includes: fire detection & alarm, communications & security, mass notification, nurse call, and building automation & smart technologies.

Mircom’s mission is to save lives and protect property by providing a line-up of innovative and advanced solutions which are scalable to satisfy diverse user demands, from small buildings to the largest complexes. Our unwavering commitment to North American manufacturing enables us to offer the highest quality and best competitive value across our vast range of products and solutions.

Summary:

Mircom is seeking an experienced and dynamic Director of Quality & Continuous Improvement to lead and oversee all aspects of quality across the organization, including product design and development, manufacturing and testing, supply chain, sales, service, and corporate processes. Reporting directly to the President & CEO, this senior leadership role carries an enterprise-wide mandate to ensure that our products and services meet the highest quality standards and regulatory requirements. The ideal candidate will have extensive experience in quality management, deep expertise in ISO standards and continuous improvement methodologies, and a strategic mindset to drive the company's quality objectives forward while fostering a culture of excellence throughout the organization.

Key Responsibilities:

Organizational Quality Leadership

Develop and implement a comprehensive quality management strategy that covers all facets of the organization, including product design, development, manufacturing, testing, sales, service, and corporate functions, with an unwavering emphasis on safety.
Maintain and continuously strengthen ISO 9001 compliance and maturity toward world-class quality standards, ensuring that quality practices align with organizational growth and Mircom's mission to deliver best-in-class solutions
Own and continuously mature the Quality Management System (QMS) across all departments to ensure a consistent, rigorous, and holistic approach to quality assurance.
Integrate Six Sigma, Lean, and other continuous improvement methodologies to systematically reduce defects and enhance overall product quality.
Support process improvement and automation initiatives to reduce variabilities and enhance manufacturing processes, anchored to key performance indicators including Cost of Poor Quality, Scrap Rate, First Pass Yield, Return Material Authorization rate, and Customer Satisfaction scores.

Leadership

Lead and manage the quality team, providing expert guidance on quality tools and techniques, mentorship, support, and training to ensure high performance and professional development.
Prepare and present clear, data-driven quality reports to the President & CEO and senior management, highlighting key performance indicators, quality improvement initiatives, and recommendations.
Manage and strengthen cross-functional relationships with stakeholders across product management, product development, operations and sales; serve as the voice of quality at the senior leadership level.
Challenge the status quo, negotiate quality objectives, and communicate progress toward continuous improvement goals with transparency and confidence.
Establish a framework for resolving quality-related problems quickly and efficiently, ensuring that root causes are rigorously addressed and preventive actions are systematically implemented.
Use data analytics to monitor key quality metrics, identify trends, and drive evidence-based continuous improvement initiatives.

People Development

Mentor and support team members to foster a culture of quality, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Develop and deliver comprehensive training programs to enhance team skills and knowledge in quality management, defect data analysis, root cause and corrective action (RCCA), and continuous improvement methodologies.
Invest in ongoing training programs for cross-functional staff to ensure adherence to quality standards and foster a sustained culture of continuous improvement.

Compliance

Ensure rigorous adherence to regulatory requirements and industry standards through comprehensive auditing processes, with a strong focus on ISO compliance.
Plan, execute, and oversee internal and external audits to assess compliance with quality standards and identify areas for improvement.
Develop and implement inspection and audit strategies to ensure comprehensive, systematic coverage of all manufacturing processes and quality management systems.
Address audit findings and implement structured corrective actions to resolve issues and prevent recurrence.
Implement robust risk management processes to identify and mitigate potential challenges in quality assurance, safety, and compliance efforts across the organization.

Continuous Improvement

jobs.description:
About CaptivateIQ

CaptivateIQ is transforming the way companies plan, manage, and optimize sales performance.

We started with incentive compensation management and are now expanding our platform to solve broader enterprise performance management challenges. Recognized by analysts like Gartner, Forrester, and G2 and backed by investors including Sequoia, ICONIQ, Accel, and Sapphire Ventures, we help high-growth companies like Netflix, Figma, and Stripe drive revenue performance with flexibility and insight.

We’re building a category-defining platform at the intersection of finance, sales, operations, and AI. We’re looking for ambitious builders to help shape what comes next.

About The Role

As Senior Director of Engineering for Incentive Compensation Management (ICM), you’ll lead the engineering organization behind our flagship product that customers rely on to pay their teams accurately and motivate performance. You’ll lead managers across multiple teams and set the technical direction for making ICM AI-native without compromising the accuracy and trust our customers depend on.

This role combines product thinking, technical leadership, and organization building. You’ll partner closely with Product, Design, GTM, and executive leadership to turn ambiguous opportunities into scalable products, and you’ll shape the engineering culture and structure that delivers them.

The Problems You’ll Solve

Making ICM AI-native. Decide where AI creates real customer value in plan design, calculation, and payout workflows, and build the quality and evaluation practices that make those features trustworthy.
Scaling a system where correctness is non-negotiable. Customers pay real people based on our calculations. You’ll balance speed of delivery with reliability, performance, and data integrity at enterprise scale.
Evolving the organization with the product. You’ll develop managers, clarify ownership, and adapt structure and process as the product matures.

What You'll Do

Set the strategy

Own the engineering strategy for ICM, aligned with company priorities, customer needs, and long-term platform direction
Identify new opportunities and guide product evolution, including the thoughtful application of AI to create differentiated customer workflows

Lead the organization

Recruit, grow, and inspire engineering managers and senior technical leaders
Build a culture of ownership, velocity, and continuous improvement
Design team structures and processes that evolve with product maturity

Raise the technical bar

Guide architecture decisions that balance speed, scalability, reliability, and maintainability
Stay close enough to the work to spot risks, challenge assumptions, and raise quality across the organization. You don’t need to write production code, but you do need to earn the respect of the engineers who do.

Drive execution

Create alignment and clear priorities across Engineering, Product, Design, and GTM
Make thoughtful tradeoffs and help teams move quickly while holding a high quality bar

What You'll Bring

15+ years of software engineering experience, including 6+ years leading managers and multi-team engineering organizations
A track record of building and scaling high-performing teams
Experience owning products end to end and scaling existing systems
Hands-on experience shipping AI/ML-powered product features, ideally LLM-based, including how you measure and maintain their quality. Experience applying AI to improve how engineering teams work is a plus.
Strong technical instincts across product architecture, infrastructure, reliability, and developer experience
A close partnership with Product and Design, and a focus on customer outcomes beyond engineering
The ability to create clarity for teams in fast-moving, ambiguous environments
Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, including experience working with executive leadership

Nice to have: Experience in enterprise B2B SaaS, finance or compensation systems, or other domains where calculation accuracy and auditability matter.

Why You'll Love This Role

You’ll own a flagship product in a category CaptivateIQ helped define and drive the next generation of AI-native capabilities
You’ll operate with significant ownership and influence across product and engineering strategy
You’ll work alongside deeply collaborative product, design, and engineering leaders
You’ll join a high-growth company with strong product-market fit and ambitious expansion plans
You’ll have the opportunity to shape not only products, but the engineering culture and organization that builds them

Benefits

Comprehensive Healthcare: 100% coverage for medical, dental, and vision for all FTEs, with roughly 75% coverage for dependents
Flexible Time Off: Flexible vacation days plus quarterly mental health days to ensure you have the space to recharge
Annual Stipends: Dedicated funds for your professional development and caretaking needs
Work Anniversary Bonuses: Annual bonuses to celebrate your milestones and contributions to the CaptivateIQ team that grow as your tenure does
Retirement Savings (US-Only): A 401(k) plan to help you invest in and secure your future
Premium Tools: The latest Apple hardware to empower you to do your best work
Inclusive Community: Active Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) that celebrate shared identities and support our DEI goals by fostering an environment where diverse talent thrives

About the faculty/service: Facilities

Facilities services are characterized by a dynamic and creative growing team where the winds of change are blowing, offering people like you opportunities to use your leadership and innovation skills to contribute to the achievement of their inspiring mission: to deliver best in class research infrastructure, reshape campus life and student experience, and provide a sustainable environment for students, researchers, teachers and community.

uOttawa’s facilities encompass three main sites that are comprised of over 600,000 square meters of building space (over 6.4 million square feet), 42.5 hectares of grounds, 125 buildings and 4,500 beds in 11 residences. There are over 150 employees in Facilities, including Project Managers, Energy and Commissioning Specialists, Mechanical and Electrical Engineers, Architects, and space Planners. The facilities capital and operating expenditures are in the range of $100M for the University’s $2.0 billion assets under management. The 20-year Capital spending plan envisions $4.0 billion of new investment highlighted by uOttawa launch of project Top Shelf, a $300 million capital investment to build a new facility for the Faculty of Health Sciences at uOttawa’s River Campus, as well as a tower at the Roger Guidon campus to house uOttawa’s new Advanced Medical Research Center (AMRC).

Position purpose:

Reporting to the Associate Vice-President, Facilities, the incumbent provides strategic leadership, direction, and oversight of the University's facilities operations and maintenance activities to ensure the safe, reliable, efficient, and sustainable operation of its physical infrastructure in support of the University's teaching, research, and institutional objectives. Develops and implements strategies to drive operational excellence, organizational effectiveness, financial sustainability, and continuous improvement. Ensures the effective stewardship and lifecycle management of the University's physical assets through optimized resource utilization, risk-informed maintenance and infrastructure renewal strategies, while safeguarding operational resilience and business continuity.

In this role, your responsibilities will include:

Strategic Leadership and Operational Stewardship : Plans, directs, and oversees all aspects of the University's 24/7 facilities operations and maintenance programs, establishing strategic priorities, operational frameworks, and performance standards to ensure the effective stewardship of a physical asset portfolio valued at more than $3 billion. Ensures the delivery of safe, reliable, sustainable, and high-quality facilities services through effective governance, sound resource management, operational risk mitigation, and a commitment to institutional excellence and continuous improvement.
Operational Excellence and Service Delivery Optimization : Provides strategic leadership in the development, evaluation, and continuous optimization of facilities operations and maintenance service delivery models through performance benchmarking, reliability engineering, process improvement, resource optimization, and the implementation of industry best practices. Establishes comprehensive performance management frameworks, service standards, and key performance indicators to drive operational efficiency, accountability, service quality, and value for money, while ensuring alignment with the University's strategic and operational priorities.
Organizational Leadership, Workforce Effectiveness and Talent Development : Provides strategic leadership and direction to a diverse, multi-disciplinary, and multi-unionized workforce through the extended management team, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, operational excellence, and continuous improvement. Ensures the effectiveness of organizational structures, workforce planning, succession management, leadership development, employee performance, and labour relations strategies to maintain a highly skilled, engaged, and adaptable workforce capable of meeting current and emerging institutional needs.
Critical Infrastructure Reliability and Continuity of Operations : Provides strategic oversight of the University's mission-critical infrastructure, building systems, central utility plants, and essential operational services to ensure their safe, reliable, efficient, and uninterrupted operation on a 24/7 basis. Establishes operational reliability standards, preventive and predictive maintenance strategies, system redundancy requirements, and contingency measures to minimize infrastructure failures, mitigate operational disruptions, and safeguard the continuity of teaching, research, and other essential University activities.
Regulatory Compliance, Occupational Health and Safety, and Operational Risk Management : Establishes and oversees comprehensive governance, risk management, and compliance frameworks to ensure facilities operations and maintenance activities meet applicable legislation, regulatory requirements, technical standards, and University policies. Provides strategic leadership in identifying, assessing, and mitigating operational, technical, environmental, and occupational health and safety risks, while fostering a proactive culture of regulatory compliance, workplace safety, and organizational accountability.
Financial Leadership and Resource Stewardship : Provides strategic leadership in the development, management, and optimization of the University's facilities operations and maintenance budgets, ensuring effective financial planning, resource allocation, expenditure control, and long-term financial sustainability. Establishes financial performance objectives and resource optimization strategies, evaluates operational investment opportunities, and ensures the efficient and responsible utilization of financial, human, and material resources in support of institutional priorities and service delivery requirements.
Emergency Preparedness, Infrastructure Resilience and Business Continuity : Provides strategic leadership in developing and implementing operational emergency preparedness, infrastructure resilience, and business continuity strategies to protect critical facilities and essential University services. Ensures the establishment, testing, and continuous improvement of emergency response procedures, infrastructure contingency plans, and operational recovery capabilities to minimize service disruptions and support the University's ability to respond effectively to emergencies, infrastructure failures, and other significant operational events.
Asset Lifecycle Management and Infrastructure Renewal : Provides strategic leadership in the assessment of infrastructure conditions, operational performance, asset reliability, and lifecycle maintenance requirements to support the sustainable management of the University's physical assets. Collaborates with institutional planning and capital investment stakeholders to identify, assess, and prioritize deferred maintenance, infrastructure renewal, and asset replacement requirements based on operational risk, asset criticality, lifecycle costs, and long-term institutional objectives.
Innovation, Digital Transformation and Operational Modernization : Leads the continuous modernization and transformation of facilities operations through the strategic evaluation and adoption of emerging technologies, digital asset management solutions, advanced building automation, predictive maintenance practices, and data-driven decision-making. Promotes innovation, process optimization, and organizational adaptability to enhance operational reliability, workforce productivity, service delivery effectiveness, and long-term operational sustainability.
Capital Project Integration and Operational Readiness : Provides strategic direction and oversight to ensure that operational requirements, lifecycle costs, asset maintainability, system reliability, and long-term sustainability considerations are effectively incorporated throughout all phases of capital projects, from initial planning and design through construction, commissioning, and project transition to operations. Collaborates with capital planning and project delivery teams to establish operational acceptance standards, ensure effective knowledge transfer, and facilitate the safe and efficient integration of new and renewed infrastructure into the University's ongoing operations and maintenance programs.
Institutional Collaboration, Executive Advisory and External Representation : Serves as a senior operational advisor to University leadership on matters relating to facilities operations, infrastructure performance, operational risks, resource requirements, and emerging industry developments. Establishes and maintains effective strategic relationships with academic and administrative leaders, research stakeholders, external partners, and professional associations to align facilities services with institutional priorities, promote service excellence, and represent the University's interests in relevant industry forums and professional networks.
Energy Management, Environmental Sustainability and Climate Resilience : Provides strategic leadership in the optimization of energy and utility management, the improvement of operational resource efficiency, and the integration of environmentally sustainable practices across the University's facilities operations. Collaborates with institutional sustainability and infrastructure planning stakeholders to advance energy conservation, greenhouse gas emissions reduction, climate adaptation, and long-term environmental performance objectives while maintaining operational reliability, service quality, and financial sustainability.

Professional Engineers Ontario license, member in good standing or having a recognized accreditation in facility management would be an asset.

The Director, Enterprise Financial Management leads organization-wide financial consolidation, corporate accounting, financial governance and external reporting. Reporting to the Vice President, Finance, IT and Risk, this role establishes common accounting policies, timelines, standards and reporting requirements across all lines of business, and provides executive leadership to the Finance, Audit and Investment Committee, and the Board of Directors with a complete view of the organization’s financial position.

Reporting and leadership

Reports to the Vice President, Finance, IT and Risk.
Directly supervises 5-6 finance staff, including the Senior Manager, Payroll & Benefits, AP/Payments Manager and Senior Financial Analyst.
Provides organization-wide functional direction for budgeting, period close, audit preparation, journal-entry standards, financial controls and reporting requirements.

What you’ll be doing

Enterprise financial reporting and close

Lead the consolidated month-end and year-end close for YWCA BC and YW Housing Society, including organization-wide timelines, reporting standards, intercompany eliminations and review of submissions from line-of-business finance teams.
Prepare and review consolidated monthly, quarterly and annual financial reporting for the VP Finance, executive leadership, the Finance, Audit and Investment Committee, and the Board.
Analyze organization-wide results, budget-to-actual variances, trends and emerging risks, and translate them into clear recommendations and an integrated financial narrative.
Establish organization-wide journal-entry standards and conduct risk-based reviews of entries to identify unusual transactions, inconsistent accounting treatment, control gaps and recurring errors.
Set accounting policies and reporting requirements for restricted contributions, deferred revenue, consolidation and other technically significant matters.

Budgeting, forecasting and financial sustainability

Lead the annual budget process and development of a multi-year forecast by establishing assumptions, timelines, standards, templates and system requirements.
Coordinate and review submissions from program-area Finance Directors, consolidate the final budget and forecast, and identify enterprise-wide surpluses, shortfalls, funding pressures and financial risks.
Review material business cases and pro formas for consistency with organization-wide assumptions, accounting policies, cash-flow requirements and long-term financial sustainability.

Audit, treasury and compliance

Plan and lead the external financial statement audit and other organization-wide assurance engagements, including auditor communications, information requests, proposed adjustments and significant findings.
Manage cash flow and oversee investments by monitoring balances, projecting liquidity needs and reviewing investment activity against policy.
Oversee Canadian charity and tax compliance, including GST, T3010, T4A and T5007 requirements, and support technically significant funder and government reporting matters.
Approve payments, credit card issuances and limit requests within delegated authority and organizational policy.

Systems, controls and continuous improvement

Administer finance-system governance, including the chart of accounts, financial dimensions, workflows, user access and approval structures; support effective integration with payroll and other enterprise systems.
Develop and improve finance policies, processes and internal controls, including segregation of duties, role-based access, audit trails and fraud-prevention measures.
Lead finance projects such as system enhancements, process automation and new program setup, with clear implementation, training and transition plans.
Investigate and resolve material discrepancies in accounts, reconciliations and reporting, and ensure corrective action prevents recurrence.

People leadership and collaboration

Lead, coach and develop the payroll, payments and financial analysis team through clear priorities, work review, performance management and development planning.
Partner with other Finance Directors and program leaders while maintaining clear accountability: program-specific analysis, budgeting, forecasting and funder reporting remain with the responsible line-of-business Finance Director.
Explain complex financial information clearly to executives, directors, managers, staff, auditors, funders, banks and external advisors, and resolve disagreements constructively.

Required education and experience

Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation and a bachelor’s degree in business, accounting or a related field.
9-11 years of progressively responsible financial management experience, including senior leadership responsibility in a complex, multi-program or multi-entity environment.
Strong knowledge of Canadian Accounting Standards for Not-for-Profit Organizations, including restricted contributions, deferred revenue, consolidation and intercompany accounting.
Demonstrated experience leading consolidated close, external audit, organization-wide budgeting and multi-year forecasting.
Experience supervising and developing a finance team, assigning and reviewing work, and managing performance.
Advanced financial systems and Excel capability; experience governing a modern cloud accounting system such as Sage Intacct is an asset.

Required capabilities

Sound independent judgment and the ability to design practical approaches where established guidance is limited.
Strong knowledge of internal controls, approval workflows, segregation of duties, fraud prevention and financial risk management.
Ability to build and test financial models, assess assumptions and communicate implications for cash flow and long-term sustainability.
Knowledge of Canadian charity and tax compliance, including T3010 and GST requirements; familiarity with T4A and T5007 reporting is an asset.
Executive-level communication skills, including the ability to present financial results and recommendations to senior leadership, Board committees and the Board.
Collaborative leadership style with the confidence to challenge assumptions, establish enterprise standards and support program-area teams.

Working conditions

Based in Vancouver, with hybrid work arrangements supported where operationally appropriate.
Regular computer-based work involving detailed financial statements, reconciliations, spreadsheets, budgets and forecasts.
Periodic extended hours during month-end, year-end, budget and audit cycles to meet critical deadlines.
