jobs.title: Vice President of Finance
jobs.description:
About Stone Tile International

Stone Tile International Inc. (STI) is a national supplier of luxury natural stone, porcelain, slab and wood surfaces to designers, architects, builders and homeowners. Headquartered in Toronto with divisions in Montreal, Calgary and Vancouver, STI operates six product divisions (Stone Tile, Porcelain Tiles, 12MM, Stone Slabs, Wood and Gallery) through a network of showrooms, galleries and warehouses. STI is entering its next stage of growth and is building a finance leadership team to match.

The Role

This is a new role at STI, and a chance to transform how the business uses its numbers. The VP of Finance will tell STI’s financial story: what is driving results, where the opportunities and risks are, and what leaders should do next. You will build the data, metrics and AI-enabled tools that make that story fast and reliable, and use them to move the needle on margin, cash and growth across six product divisions and four regions.
You will own planning, forecasting, performance reporting, cash and financial controls, and lead the accounting function through the Director of Accounting. You will also be the first point of contact for contracts and legal matters, own IT infrastructure, oversee import compliance, and manage corporate insurance and governance, with guidance from the CFO. We are looking for a highly credentialed finance leader with real estate exposure, who is as comfortable in front of the executive team as in the data.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Storytelling and Insight

•    Turn financial results into a clear, compelling story for the President, CFO, executive team and ownership: what happened, why, and what to do about it.
•    Deliver a monthly management pack built around insight and action, not just tables of numbers.
•    Design visual dashboards that show performance by division, region, product and customer at a glance.
•    Lead monthly performance reviews with division and regional leaders and drive corrective action where results fall short.

Data, Metrics and AI-Enabled Finance

•    Define STI’s core financial and operating KPIs (margin, inventory turns, cash conversion, sales productivity, occupancy cost) and a single source of truth for each.
•    Build a modern finance data and reporting stack that connects ERP, sales and inventory data.
•    Identify and implement AI and automation across finance: forecasting, variance analysis, reporting, reconciliations and AP/AR, with sound controls.
•    Replace manual, spreadsheet-driven work so the team spends its time on analysis and decisions.

Financial Controls

•    Own STI’s financial control framework, including approval limits, segregation of duties and authorization of spend.
•    Review and challenge the internal controls designed and maintained by the Director of Accounting, and close gaps.
•    Ensure controls keep pace as processes are automated and new systems are introduced.

Planning and Forecasting

•    Own the annual budget process, delivering a board-ready budget before the fiscal year begins in April.
•    Build and maintain a rolling 12–18-month forecast by product division and by region.
•    Develop scenario and sensitivity models for volume, cost, margin, headcount and capital decisions.

Business Partnering and Margin Reporting

•    Act as the finance partner to sales, operations and division and regional leaders on margin, product mix and inventory.
•    Report on pricing and margin performance and help manage it, working with the Director, Supply Chain, who owns day-to-day pricing.

Import Compliance and Trade

•    Oversee compliance with regulations and administration for importing goods into Canada, including customs, duties and tariffs, with day-to-day administration by the Director of Accounting.
•    Monitor foreign trade policy, tariffs and geopolitical events, and model their impact on landed cost, sourcing, FX and margin.
•    Brief the CFO and executive team on trade risks and recommend responses.

Contracts and Legal

•    Own the review of contractual documents, such as purchase orders and contracts from general contractors, customer and vendor agreements, from a legal and business perspective, with guidance from the CFO.
•    Act as the first point of contact for general legal matters, resolving where appropriate and escalating to the CFO.

Cash, Working Capital and Treasury

•    Produce and manage a 13-week cash flow forecast and longer-range cash plan.
•    Set and manage targets for inventory, customer credit terms and collections.
•    Manage day-to-day banking, covenant monitoring and foreign exchange exposure, within CFO policy.

Real Estate and Capital Investment

•    Lead the financial analysis for real estate decisions: new or relocated showrooms and warehouses, lease renewals, lease versus buy, and occupancy cost by location.
•    Maintain a lease and property portfolio view, including commitments, renewal dates and occupancy costs as a share of revenue.
•    Build business cases for capital expenditures, new product lines and major hires, and track post-investment returns.

Insurance and Corporate Governance

•    Manage the corporate insurance program, including coverage reviews, renewals, claims and the broker relationship, within CFO direction.
•    Support corporate governance across STI’s entities, including corporate records, resolutions and annual filings.

IT Infrastructure and Support

•    Own IT infrastructure and support, including managed service providers, hardware and software, user support and cybersecurity, with guidance from the CFO.
•    Build a technology roadmap that supports finance transformation and the wider business.

Acquisitions

•    Lead financial due diligence on acquisition targets with the Director of Accounting, under the direction of the CFO.
•    Help integrate acquired businesses into STI’s reporting, controls, systems and processes.

Leadership and Transformation

•    Lead, coach and develop the Director of Accounting and build a finance team that is analytical, data-fluent and business-facing.
•    Set a finance transformation roadmap and deliver measurable improvements in speed, accuracy and insight.
•    Ensure a fast, reliable month-end close feeds planning and reporting.

Success in the First 12 Months

•    A monthly management pack and dashboards the executive team relies on to make decisions.
•    Agreed KPIs with one source of truth, reported consistently by division and region.
•    At least two AI or automation use cases live in finance, with time saved and accuracy gains measured.
•    An approved FY budget, rolling forecast and 13-week cash forecast in place and trusted.
•    Financial control framework reviewed, with gaps identified and closed.
•    A clear process for contract review and legal escalation, and a trade and tariff impact model in use.

Qualifications

•    CPA designation required; an MBA and/or CFA charter is a strong asset.
•    12+ years of progressive finance experience, including 5+ years leading FP&A, commercial finance or corporate finance at a senior level.
•    Exceptional financial storyteller: proven ability to present to executives, ownership and lenders and turn analysis into decisions.
•    Track record leading finance transformation, including data, BI/dashboard and automation or AI initiatives.
•    Strong data skills: modern BI tools (e.g., Power BI), advanced modelling, and comfort working with large data sets.
•    Experience reviewing commercial contracts (e.g., construction and general contractor agreements, purchase orders) from a legal and business perspective.
•    Knowledge of import regulations, customs and tariffs, with a strong grasp of foreign trade policy and geopolitical risk.
•    Experience overseeing financial controls, corporate insurance and IT infrastructure.
•    Real estate exposure: lease analysis, property investment or real estate finance, and lease accounting.
•    Acquisition due diligence and integration experience is an asset.
•    Public company or public sector experience is an asset.
•    Multi-location, multi-entity Canadian experience; distribution, wholesale, retail or building products experience is an asset.
•    French is an asset.

Working Conditions

•    Based at the Toronto head office, with some travel to Montreal, Calgary and Vancouver
•    Presents regularly to the executive team and external stakeholders
•    Extended hours during budget, year-end and audit periods as required

We thank you for your interest; however, only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted. No agencies please.

Job Description

What makes this role important at Ipsos?

As a Vice President, you will serve as a senior quantitative research leader and trusted advisor to clients. You will work with senior stakeholders to translate complex business challenges into clear learning agendas, testable hypotheses, and rigorous research methodologies that drive decision-making and business impact.

This role requires deep expertise in quantitative research design, advanced statistical techniques, and quantitative best practices. You must be comfortable thinking on your feet, providing methodological guidance in real time, and confidently defending analytical approaches with clients and colleagues. Beyond delivering insights, you will help shape the questions that matter, determine how they should be tested, and translate findings into strategic recommendations.

Our ideal candidate is an intellectually curious and commercially minded research leader who combines methodological excellence with strategic thinking, client advisory skills, and a passion for turning evidence into action.

This is a highly quantitative role. Candidates must possess significant hands-on experience designing, executing, and interpreting advanced quantitative research studies and analyses. Experience managing quantitative projects alone is not sufficient; successful candidates will have personally applied advanced analytical techniques and statistical methods throughout their careers. Individuals whose experience is primarily qualitative should not apply.

What You Can Expect To Be Doing

Lead the design of complex research and advisory engagements that address critical client business challenges and contribute to business growth.
Translate client issues and strategic questions into learning agendas, testable hypotheses, and robust research methodologies.
Apply advanced analytical techniques and methodological best practices to ensure research is insightful, innovative, and fit for purpose.
Serve as a senior advisor to clients, helping them interpret findings, evaluate strategic options, and make informed decisions.
Lead the development of reports, presentations, workshops, and executive-level recommendations that move beyond reporting results to driving action.
Collaborate across Ipsos service lines to bring the full breadth of Ipsos expertise to clients and identify opportunities for integrated solutions.
Contribute to business development activities, including proposal development, thought leadership, and identifying opportunities for growth within existing and prospective client relationships.
Build Ipsos' reputation internally and externally through subject matter expertise, innovation, thought leadership, and market presence.
Coach and mentor researchers at all levels on research design, analytical thinking, storytelling, strategic consulting, and client management.

Client Management Responsibilities

Acts as a senior trusted advisor to client leadership teams, providing strategic counsel on research, insight generation, and business decision-making.
Leads complex client conversations involving methodology, interpretation, business implications, and challenging or ambiguous situations.
Anticipates client needs and proactively recommends research and advisory solutions that address emerging opportunities and risks.
Builds and maintains senior-level relationships that contribute to long-term partnerships, business retention, and revenue growth.
Supports and coaches team members in managing client relationships and navigating difficult stakeholder situations.

Study Lead Responsibilities

Oversees the design and execution of complex research programs from hypothesis development through final recommendations.
Guides methodological decisions and analytical approaches, ensuring technical rigor and alignment with client objectives.
Leverages advanced quantitative techniques, segmentation, modeling, forecasting, and other analytical approaches, as appropriate.
Synthesizes findings across multiple data sources to identify patterns, implications, and strategic opportunities.
Leads development and delivery of executive-level reporting and presentations that connect research findings to business outcomes.

Employee Management Responsibilities

Manages and develops researchers and team leaders, providing ongoing coaching, mentorship, and performance development.
Builds team capabilities in research design, analytical methods, strategic thinking, consulting skills, and client advisory.
Creates an environment that encourages innovation, collaboration, continuous learning, and methodological excellence.
Identifies and develops future leaders within the organization.

STRATEGIC THINKING EXPECTATIONS

Serves as a strategic leader for client accounts and research engagements.
Demonstrates hypothesis-driven thinking and the ability to connect business objectives with research solutions.
Quickly assesses complex situations, identifies key issues, and develops practical paths forward.
Balances methodological rigor, client realities, commercial considerations, and organizational priorities.
Anticipates emerging trends, risks, and opportunities and helps shape Ipsos' approach to addressing them.
Influences strategic direction for clients, projects, and the broader business through evidence-based recommendations and thought leadership.

This might be the job for you if you have:

8-10+ years of experience in market research, insights, consulting, or a related field.
Deep expertise in quantitative research methodologies and advanced analytical techniques.
Proven ability to transform complex business questions into actionable research programs and testable hypotheses.
Strong understanding of research best practices and the ability to select, defend, and communicate methodological approaches.
Exceptional critical thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to think on your feet in high-stakes client situations.
Demonstrated success advising senior client stakeholders and leading complex engagements.
Strong storytelling and communication skills, with the ability to connect data to strategic business decisions.
Experience coaching and developing high-performing teams.
Strong commercial acumen and experience contributing to business development and account growth.
Bachelor's Degree required; Master's degree considered an asset.
Experience with advanced analytical platforms and statistical software such as SPSS, R, Python, or equivalent.

If you don’t meet 100% of the requirements, we encourage all who feel they might be a fit for the opportunity to apply. We may consider a variety of backgrounds for a particular role and are also committed to considering candidates for available positions throughout our organization, not just the one you’re applying to!

In accordance with NY/CO/CA/WA law, the estimated base salary range for this role is $105,000 CAD to $115,000 CAD. Your final base salary will be determined based on several non-discriminatory factors which may include but are not limited to location, work experience, skills, knowledge, education and/or certifications.

What’s In It For You

At Ipsos you’ll experience opportunities for Career Development, an exceptional benefits package (including generous PTO, healthcare plans, wellness benefits), a flexible workplace policy, and a strong collaborative culture.

Benefits

To find out more about all the great reasons to work at Ipsos, how we’re making an impact around the world, and more about our benefits and employee programs, please visit:

Why Work at Ipsos | US

Commitment to Diversity

Ipsos recognizes the necessity of building an inclusive culture that values each employee’s individuality and diverse perspectives. For more than 40 years, our mission has been to generate and analyze data about society, markets, brands, and behaviors to provide our clients with the insights that elevate their understanding of the world. This could not be fulfilled without Ipsos’ diverse employees who compile and analyze this data—they are the essence of who we are and what we do.

We are committed to providing equal opportunity to all employees, creating an environment that promotes inclusion, and enabling employees from all walks of life to flourish. Ipsos is An Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, or any other protected class and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability.

About Us

Ipsos is one of the world’s largest research companies and currently the only one primarily managed by researchers, ranking as a #1 full-service research organization for four consecutive years. With over 75 different data-driven solutions, and presence in 90 markets, Ipsos brings together research, implementation, methodological, and subject-matter experts from around the world, combining thematic and technical experts to deliver top-quality research and insights. Simply speaking, we help the biggest companies solve some of their biggest problems, serving more than 5000 clients across the globe by providing research, data, and insights on their target markets. And we are proud of our continuous efforts in making Ipsos the best place to work!

jobs.title: Technology Director - Global Sourcing Technology, Supply Chain
jobs.description:
Requirements

Description & Requirements

Technology Director | Global Sourcing Technology

Who we are

lululemon is an innovative performance apparel company for yoga, running, training, and other athletic pursuits. Setting the bar in technical fabrics and functional design, we create transformational products and experiences that support people in moving, growing, connecting, and being well. We owe our success to our innovative product, emphasis on stores, commitment to our people, and the incredible connections we make in every community we're in. As a company, we focus on creating positive change to build a healthier, thriving future. In particular, that includes creating an equitable, inclusive and growth-focused environment for our people.

About This Team

Global Supply Chain Technology delivers the platforms and capabilities that power lululemon’s supply chain—from raw material innovation and development, costing, sourcing, quality, sustainability and traceability, trade, logistics, and distribution technology. Our team works in close partnership with core business units to ensure that our supply chain remains agile, efficient, and responsive to ever-evolving market demands. By continuously innovating and refining our technological solutions, we enable best-in-class supply chain operations to service our Guests and our stores. This collaborative approach ensures we provide exceptional experiences and support lululemon’s growth in every community we serve.

The role

We are seeking a Technology Director to define and execute the multi year strategy for modernizing and transforming lululemon’s global sourcing technology ecosystem. This leader will shape the strategic roadmap, elevate costing and sourcing platform capabilities, advance AI driven decisioning, and ensure operational excellence across the systems that connect lululemon to its global vendor base.

You will own all aspects of technology for Global Sourcing—architecture, engineering, security, QA automation, operations, and delivery—and oversee a globally distributed team across North America and India. You will be accountable for the platforms that support approximately 300 raw material (RM) and finished goods (FG) vendors globally, and will partner with Enterprise Architecture and Engineering on the technology evolution required to support enterprise initiatives. This role requires a seasoned leader with a proven record of developing a strong leadership bench, managing complex solutions, and thriving in complex, fast paced, and highly collaborative environments.

This Role Oversees Technology Solutions Supporting

Product costing and should-cost modelling (materials, labor, overhead, landed cost)
Sourcing execution (quoting and RFQ, vendor award, capacity allocation and booking)
Purchase order management and order lifecycle for raw material and finished goods
Supplier collaboration portals and vendor-facing self-service
Partner connectivity (vendors, mills, agents, service providers)
Integration frameworks (EDI, APIs, event-driven architecture)
Master data and data quality for cost
Sourcing analytics, margin visibility, exception management, and operational dashboards

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership & Roadmap

Define and deliver a multi year global sourcing technology strategy that enhances scalability, reliability, and speed to market.
Translate business needs into an actionable engineering roadmap incorporating modernization, cloud migration, supplier collaboration, and responsible AI adoption.
Partner with business Directors, Sr. Directors, and VPs across Global Sourcing and Costing to define, deliver, and support the strategic roadmap.
Enroll cross functional technology partners in the strategic vision for Global Sourcing, and lead the creation and expansion of new capabilities that align with our strategic goals.

Platform & Architecture Modernization

Modernize existing costing and sourcing platforms and integrate next generation capabilities (costing engines, sourcing execution suites, or equivalent).
Drive transformation toward API-first, event-driven, and scalable integration architectures across the global vendor base.
Lead design and implementation of secure, resilient, and responsible data management and governance frameworks for material, vendor, and cost master data.
Partner with Enterprise Architecture and Engineering on technology evolution that supports enterprise initiatives.

Engineering Leadership

Lead globally distributed engineering, QA automation, delivery, and support teams; develop managers and future-ready technical leaders.
Serve as the escalation point for Technology Managers to support delivery, making thoughtful decisions on the fly and constantly clearing roadblocks.
Raise engineering standards around quality, observability, security, and system reliability.
Build high performing, diverse teams with a culture of inclusion, transparency, and continuous improvement, and support career progression and stretch opportunities across the Global Sourcing technology area.

Operational Excellence

Oversee delivery, operations, and vendor/partner management across sourcing and costing systems, and own the relationship with key vendor partners.
Manage budgets for strategic initiatives and baseline opex for Global Sourcing technology, ensuring clear ROI and optimization of total cost of ownership.
Drive root cause analysis, systems reliability, service maturity, and measurable operational improvements.

Innovation & AI Enablement

Introduce AI-driven decision support for should-cost modelling, quote analysis, capacity allocation, vendor performance, and exception management.
Champion ethical, transparent, and responsible use of AI in sourcing and vendor-facing operations.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, related field, or commensurate relative experience.
15+ years of experience in technology, including 4+ years in a senior leadership position such as a Technology Manager or Technology Director.
Experience leading large scale initiatives and modernization efforts for supply chain platforms, with highly valued experience in costing and sourcing areas.
Proven success delivering transformations in areas such as product costing, sourcing execution, purchase order management, supplier collaboration, or vendor connectivity.
Strong background in integration architectures (API platforms, EDI, message streaming, event-driven design).
Hands-on experience with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP).
Proficiency in programming languages such as Python or Java and familiarity with data engineering patterns.
Demonstrated ability to manage large budgets and deliver high-impact technology programs.
Exceptional communication, storytelling, and executive influencing skills.
Continuous learning mindset that stays on the leading edge of sourcing and supply chain technology solutions that can bring value to the organization.
Experience with AI/ML use cases in supply chain, sourcing, or costing.
Understanding of apparel or consumer goods product development, raw materials, and global vendor management processes.
Experience working with distributed teams across multiple time zones and a global vendor base.

Success Metrics

Improved cost accuracy, margin visibility, and speed of costing cycles.
Reduced sourcing and purchase order cycle times, with fewer manual touches per order.
Improved reliability, uptime, and SLA performance of sourcing and costing systems.
Strong engagement scores and leadership development of global teams.

Must Haves

Acknowledges the presence of choice in every moment and takes personal responsibility for their life.
Possesses an entrepreneurial spirit and continuously innovates to achieve great results.
Communicates with honesty and kindness and creates the space for others to do the same.
Leads with courage, knowing the possibility of greatness is bigger than the fear of failure.
Fosters connection by putting people first and building trusting relationships.
Integrates fun and joy as a way of being and working, aka doesn’t take themselves too seriously.

additional notes

Applicants must be authorized to work for ANY employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time for this role.

Compensation And Benefits Package

lululemon’s compensation offerings are grounded in a pay-for-performance philosophy that recognizes exceptional individual and team performance. The typical hiring range for this position is from  $190,400 - $249,900  annually; the base pay offered is based on market location and may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and internal equity. As part of our total rewards offering, permanent employees in this position may be eligible for our competitive annual bonus program and equity offerings, subject to program eligibility requirements.  

At Lululemon, Investing In Our People Is a Top Priority. We Believe That When Life Works, Work Works. We Strive To Be The Place Where Inclusive Leaders Come To Develop And Enable All To Be Well. Recognizing Our Teams For Their Performance And Dedication, Other Components Of Our Total Rewards Offerings Include Support Of Career Development, Wellbeing, And Personal Growth

Extended health and dental benefits, and mental health plans
Paid time off
Savings and retirement plan matching
Generous employee discount
Fitness & yoga classes
Parenthood top-up
Extensive catalog of development course offerings
People networks, mentorship programs, and leadership series (to name a few)

Note: The incentive programs, benefits, and perks have certain eligibility requirements. The Company reserves the right to alter these incentive programs, benefits, and perks in whole or in part at any time without advance notice.

jobs.title: VP of Product & Data
jobs.description:
KYBER1

Location:
Remote-first (CA preferred)
Engagement:
Contract-to-hire or bootstrap-friendly, with a full-time path for the right person

About KYBER1
KYBER1 is an early-stage commerce media company that helps retailers and other data owners turn consented first-party customer and transaction data into media revenue. Commerce media is one of the fastest-growing categories in advertising, but activation is concentrated in a handful of giant networks. We serve everyone else: the thousands of retailers and data-rich organizations with valuable first-party signals and no practical, governed way to bring them to market.
Our platform takes a partner from raw commerce data to activation-ready audiences: ingesting and normalizing first-party signals, resolving identity deterministically, gating PII before it becomes a liability, building audiences aligned to real buying behavior, and activating them across approved channels, including directly to AI planning and buying agents through the open Ad Context Protocol (AdCP). We are agentic by design, in the product and in how we run the company: agents do real work here, and a small team ships what used to take departments.

The Role
We're looking for a VP of Product & Data to own the product function at KYBER1 and drive it from architecture and ambition into shipped, revenue-generating features. While hands-on in the early days, this is a key strategic role, and you will lead product strategy with input from our C-suite and advisors. It's a great opportunity to build something from scratch with huge upside for businesses and advertisers. If you're an ad tech nerd with ideas about the future of agentic advertising, and someone who loves to build, this is an ideal role for you.
You'll partner directly with our Lead Engineer to run one unified execution loop: you turn the platform strategy and roadmap into a small number of clearly defined use cases, translate each one into user stories, and work closely with engineering on agile and agentic execution.
Because we're a startup, we're flexible on how we start working together. We're open to a contract-to-hire arrangement or a bootstrap-style engagement, and a full-time opportunity with equity is on the table for the right talent.

What You'll Do
Set product strategy and vision. Define where KYBER1's product goes across Audience Extension, KYBER1 Sales, Audience Activation, and the Agentic/AdCP ecosystem, working directly with founders and advisors to turn a strong technical thesis into a sequenced, buildable plan.
Partner with engineering on overall architecture. Sit alongside our Lead Engineer as the other half of technical and product leadership, shaping system design and technical roadmap decisions together, not handing off a spec and waiting to see what comes back.
Bring an innovative, AI-forward product point of view. Push our thinking on where agentic commerce and AI-driven advertising are headed and use agents themselves as leverage in how the team builds and ships product.
Move fast and ship. Translate strategy into a prioritized backlog, use cases, and tickets engineering can pick up right away, and keep a lightweight cadence, like a weekly build review, that turns ideas into shipped product quickly.
Drive the near-term proof points: the real-data pilot campaign and match-rate reporting, closing the consent & governance gap with legal/ops, the second partner integration, and the AdCP beta, all sequenced as one flywheel, not a menu of parallel projects.
Own data and privacy requirements. Translate consent terms, data-share agreements, and PII-gating rules into concrete engineering specs: what fields are permitted, what gets redacted or tokenized, and what identity resolution and audience segmentation decisions follow from that.
Work the ad tech and commerce-media specifics: partner and retailer data integrations, DSP/clean-room mechanics, identity and match-rate reporting, and the taxonomy that makes audiences usable to buyers and agents.
Help hire and mentor the product and data function as it grows beyond you.

What We're Looking For
8+ years of product management experience, including meaningful time owning a product area with full accountability for outcomes, not just roadmap input.
Product background in ad tech, ideally including programmatic advertising, DSP/SSP mechanics, or attribution.
A demonstrated record of shipping, concrete examples of turning strategy into a roadmap, and a roadmap into things that went live.
Experience in privacy and data-heavy products is a strong plus: consent and data-governance frameworks, identity resolution, clean rooms, CDPs, or audience/segmentation data.
Retail or commerce media experience is ideal, understanding how retailers and data owners think about monetizing first-party data.
Comfortable writing detailed specs and tickets yourself, not reliant on a separate business-analyst or PM-ops layer to translate your thinking into something engineering can build.
Strong technical fluency to partner directly with engineering: you don't need to write production code, but you need to speak the language of APIs, data pipelines, and identity graphs credibly.
Startup DNA: biased toward action, comfortable with ambiguity, and energized by building in a fast, low-process environment.
Collaborative by nature: comfortable pitching in outside your lane, and just as invested in the team's wins as your own
Clear communicator who can explain technical trade-offs to non-technical stakeholders

Nice to Have
Experience taking a product from zero to one at an early-stage company
Familiarity with emerging agentic ad standards such as the Ad Context Protocol (AdCP), or with agentic/LLM-driven products more broadly
Experience operating inside a retail media network or commerce media business specifically
Background working with identity graphs, clean rooms, or match-rate/attribution reporting as a proof metric
Experience partnering with legal/ops to close data-share or consent agreements without stalling engineering momentum

What We Offer
A ground-floor seat at a commerce media startup where your product decisions become the company's foundation
Flexible engagement to start (contract-to-hire or bootstrap), with a full-time offer, including equity, competitive salary, health benefits, unlimited PTO and fully remote
Direct access to founders and real influence over product and technical strategy
A genuinely agent-native way of working: high leverage, low bureaucracy, and a standard we hold everywhere, assume an agent is on the other side, and that it is choosing whom to trust

To apply, reach out to jobs@kyber1.com

KYBER1 is an equal opportunity employer, committed to building a diverse team. All qualified applicants will be considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.

jobs.title: Project Controls Director
jobs.description:
Overview

The Project Controls Director provides senior leadership and strategic direction for the planning, execution, governance, and continuous improvement of project controls across major projects, programs, portfolios, or enterprise-level workstreams.

This role is accountable for ensuring effective integration of cost control, planning and scheduling, earned value, forecasting, change management, reporting, systems, and performance analysis. The Project Controls Director leads project controls teams, establishes standards and expectations, provides oversight of reporting quality and data integrity, and supports senior leadership in making informed decisions related to project performance, risk, recovery, and delivery outcomes.

The role requires strong technical expertise in project controls, proven leadership capability, stakeholder influence, and the ability to operate at both strategic and execution levels.

Your role

Lead the overall strategy, execution, and continuous improvement of project controls functions across assigned projects, programs, portfolios, or business areas.
Establish, maintain, and oversee project controls processes, standards, procedures, and governance expectations.
Provide leadership and direction for cost control, planning and scheduling, earned value, forecasting, change control, reporting, and performance management activities.
Ensure project controls practices are integrated across cost, schedule, scope, risk, finance, commercial, and reporting functions.
Lead the development and delivery of reliable project performance reporting, including cost performance, schedule performance, earned value, variance analysis, forecasts, trends, and corrective action plans.
Oversee the Cost Performance Report process and ensure reporting is accurate, timely, consistent, and fit for leadership decision-making.
Identify key project performance variances, risks, issues, and trends, and lead the development of corrective action plans with project teams.
Challenge forecasts, schedules, assumptions, variances, and performance narratives to ensure clear visibility of project delivery risks and opportunities.
Provide senior advisory support to project leadership, functional leadership, alliance partners, clients, finance, commercial teams, and executives.
Lead implementation and oversight of change control processes, including trend management, approved changes, potential claims, and impacts to cost, schedule, scope, and forecast.
Support alignment between project controls, finance, commercial, project management, and delivery teams to ensure consistent project performance visibility.
Build, organize, and lead functional project controls teams, including planners, schedulers, cost controllers, reporting analysts, and project controls specialists.
Provide coaching, mentoring, direction, and performance feedback to project controls staff.
Support capability development, succession planning, and growth of project controls talent across cost and planning career streams.
Promote standardization, governance, data integrity, reporting discipline, and continuous improvement across project controls practices.
Support system implementation, process improvement, reporting enhancements, and integration between project controls systems and finance or enterprise systems.
Represent project controls in senior leadership discussions, client meetings, project reviews, governance forums, and business planning activities.
Ensure project controls teams operate effectively, collaboratively, and in alignment with business priorities, client commitments, and project delivery objectives.

Other Aspects (if Applicable)

May lead project controls across multiple projects, portfolios, programs, or strategic enterprise initiatives.
May provide functional leadership to cost controllers, planners, schedulers, reporting analysts, and project controls specialists.
May represent project controls in executive reviews, client meetings, alliance forums, governance reviews, and business planning discussions.
May lead or support project recovery planning, forecast challenges, schedule recovery, change control escalation, claims discussions, and commercial impact reviews.
May support enterprise standardization, reporting improvements, data integrity initiatives, system implementations, and capability development across project controls.
Expected to operate as a trusted advisor to senior leadership and as a role model for project controls professionalism, governance, collaboration, and accountability.

About You

Post-secondary education in engineering, business, commerce, finance, accounting, project management, or a related discipline.
Professional certification or designation such as PMP, PMI-SP, PSP, EVP, AACE, CPA, MBA, CFA, or equivalent is considered an asset.
Typically requires 15+ years of relevant project controls, project management, cost control, planning, scheduling, reporting, commercial, or project delivery experience.
Typically requires 5–10 years of experience leading project controls teams or multidisciplinary project delivery teams.
Experience supporting large, complex engineering, construction, nuclear, energy, infrastructure, or major capital projects is preferred.
Experience leading integrated project controls across cost, schedule, earned value, change, forecasting, reporting, and performance management.
Experience advising senior leadership on project performance, delivery risks, trends, forecasts, recovery plans, and corrective actions.
Experience working with clients, alliance partners, project teams, finance, commercial teams, and executive stakeholders.
Experience developing, implementing, or improving project controls processes, governance, systems, reporting frameworks, or performance management practices.
Nuclear project experience is considered an asset.

est un leader nord-américain en conception durable et en fabrication avancée de systèmes sur mesure de traitement de l’air et de refroidissement liquide. Nous offrons des solutions innovantes et écoénergétiques à des secteurs tels que les centres de données hyperscale, les établissements de santé, les laboratoires pharmaceutiques, les salles blanches pour semi-conducteurs, les fabricants de batteries pour véhicules électriques et les installations en sciences de la vie.

Sommaire du poste

Relevant de la Directrice de site, le ou la Directeur(trice) des opérations assure la gestion, la coordination et l’optimisation des activités de production, de logistique et de planification de l’usine de Saint-Hubert. Cette personne veille à l’atteinte des objectifs de santé et sécurité, qualité, livraison, productivité et coûts, tout en développant les équipes et en structurant les processus pour soutenir la croissance de XNRGY. Elle collabore entre autres avec l’ingénierie, la qualité, l’approvisionnement et les ressources humaines.

Principales responsabilités

Leadership et gestion des opérations

Diriger les activités de production, de logistique et de planification et assurer leur coordination.
Décliner les orientations de la Directrice de site en objectifs, plans d’action et indicateurs mesurables.
Instaurer une cadence de gestion opérationnelle : suivi des KPI, rencontres de performance et escalade des enjeux.
Anticiper les risques, contraintes de capacité et besoins liés à la croissance du site.

Gestion de la production

Assurer l’exécution du plan de production et le respect des standards de qualité, des délais et des coûts.
Optimiser l’utilisation des effectifs, des équipements et des espaces de production.
Identifier les goulots d’étranglement et déployer des actions correctives durables.
Collaborer avec l’ingénierie manufacturière, les méthodes et la qualité pour améliorer les procédés.

Planification et ordonnancement

Superviser la planification à court, moyen et long terme selon la demande, les capacités et les matériaux disponibles.
Améliorer la fiabilité des échéanciers, l’adhérence au plan et la prévisibilité des livraisons.
Coordonner les changements de priorités avec les équipes commerciales, projets et approvisionnement.
Optimiser l’utilisation des outils ERP et MRP pour la planification manufacturière.

Logistique et flux de matériaux

Superviser la réception, l’entreposage, la gestion des stocks, l’alimentation des lignes et l’expédition.
Assurer la disponibilité des matériaux et améliorer l’exactitude des inventaires et la traçabilité.
Optimiser les flux physiques et informationnels et réduire les déplacements et les délais.
Collaborer avec l’approvisionnement pour prévenir les ruptures et résoudre les contraintes de composants.

Gestion et développement des équipes

Encadrer, mobiliser et développer les gestionnaires de production, logistique et planification.
Fixer des attentes claires, suivre la performance et renforcer l’autonomie et la responsabilisation.
Maintenir une présence active sur le terrain et favoriser une culture de collaboration et de respect.
Collaborer avec les RH à la planification des effectifs, à la relève et à l’engagement des employés.

Santé, sécurité et qualité

Faire de la prévention SST une priorité dans les décisions et les pratiques quotidiennes.
Assurer le respect des procédures, des exigences réglementaires et des standards de fabrication.
Collaborer avec les fonctions SST et Qualité pour réduire les incidents, non-conformités et reprises.

Baccalauréat en génie industriel, génie mécanique, gestion des opérations ou domaine connexe.
Au moins 10 ans d’expérience manufacturière, dont 5 ans en gestion des opérations.
Expérience de gestion d’équipes multidisciplinaires en production, logistique et planification.
Expérience en fabrication sur commande (Make-to-Order) ou Engineer-to-Order, un atout.
Expérience en croissance ou transformation opérationnelle, un atout important.
Maîtrise des principes Lean, des ERP/MRP et des indicateurs de performance.
Excellente maîtrise du français et de l’anglais pour collaborer avec les différents sites.

Leadership mobilisateur

Orientation résultats
Vision transversale
Rigueur opérationnelle
Résolution de problèmes
Gestion du changement
Collaboration
Présence terrain

La Directrice de site conserve la responsabilité stratégique et globale de l’établissement, notamment la performance financière, les investissements majeurs et les relations corporatives. Le ou la Directeur(trice) des opérations est responsable de l’exécution quotidienne et de la performance des fonctions de production, de logistique et de planification, dans le cadre des orientations établies par la Directrice de site.

Salaire concurrentiel avec programme de bonification
Assurances médicales, dentaires et de soins de la vue
REER
Programme d’aide aux employés
Vacances payées
Équipe dynamique, ouverte au changement et à l’innovation
Installations modernes à la fine pointe de la technologie (Industrie 4.0)
Contribution à une industrie verte soutenant la révolution de l’IA
Environnement en forte croissance où l’esprit entrepreneurial est valorisé
Milieu de travail inclusif et favorable à la diversité
Opportunités d’avancement — XNRGY favorise la mobilité interne
Bornes de recharge électrique disponibles sur le site

, nous nous engageons à bâtir un milieu de travail diversifié et inclusif. The organization is seeking an accomplished Chief Operating Officer (COO)
to join its senior leadership team to lead the continued development and growth of its operations. Reporting to the CEO, the COO will have broad responsibility across manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, logistics, service, facilities and operational excellence. This executive will translate an ambitious growth plan into an operating model that is scalable, disciplined and built for global markets. They will pair strategic perspective and commercial acumen with hands-on credibility to engage deeply with engineering, external partners and the production floor.

Enterprise-level impact.
A true seat at the senior leadership table, with the mandate to design the operating model that will carry the business through its next phase of growth.

Lead operations for technology where quality, reliability and on-time delivery have a direct bearing on patient outcomes.

A global platform.

Key Responsibilities

Develop and execute the company's operational strategy in alignment with its broader strategic plan and long-term growth objectives.
Provide executive leadership across manufacturing, production planning, supply chain, sourcing, procurement, inventory, warehousing, logistics and service operations.
Lead the strategic relationship with the company’s contract manufacturing partners, including contract negotiation, capacity planning, scaling new products into full-rate production, and sourcing and setting up operations in other jurisdictions.
Establish operational KPIs and performance management systems while driving continuous improvement, scalability, efficiency and profitability.

Partner with Engineering, Quality and Sales on new product introductions, design transfers and commercialization.

Oversee global service and customer support operations, including order fulfillment and aftermarket service and help grow recurring service revenue. Support international service expansion through partnerships, training, and service infrastructure development.

The successful candidate will be a seasoned operations executive with significant experience in a regulated medical technology environment, ideally within a growing manufacturing organization. jobs.title: Director, Preconstruction and Sales Operations
jobs.description:
Polar Racking Inc. is a North American leader in the design, engineering and manufacturing of PV mounting systems. We are at the forefront of PV innovation, leading the industry in cutting-edge design with a focus on continuous innovation, with a vision to deliver the highest value to our clients at the lowest cost per kWh. Our diversified portfolio of rooftop and ground mount products for the residential, commercial, and utility scale markets, coupled with our unique suite of engineering collaboration tools, technical services, and installation support, allows us to deliver turnkey solutions that are modular, lighter, and quicker to install. We support our North American clients from our locations in North America.

The Director, Preconstruction & Sales Operations leads the work that turns qualified sales opportunities into commercially sound, technically coordinated, and execution-ready projects. The role owns the preconstruction process, including estimating, proposal development, pricing governance, risk review, and the handoff from Sales to Operations.
This is a hands-on leadership position for someone with experience in technical sales and project operations. You will align customer commitments with engineering requirements, supplier capacity, installation needs, and project schedules, while developing the team and processes needed to support growth.

Responsibilities:

Preconstruction leadership

· Lead projects from opportunity qualification through bid submission, contract award, and formal handoff to the delivery team.
· Establish bid/no-bid criteria and project review gates based on profitability, customer requirements, technical feasibility, capacity, and commercial risk.
· Coordinate preliminary layouts, design inputs, foundation assumptions, site information, quantities, and installation requirements with Engineering and Operations.
· Develop preconstruction schedules and identify long-lead materials, supplier constraints, site risks, and required customer decisions before commitments are made.
· Evaluate alternatives that improve cost, constructability, schedule, or customer value, with technical validation by the responsible engineering team.

Estimating and commercial management

· Lead the estimating function and set standards for takeoffs, cost models, supplier quotations, contingencies, and documented pricing assumptions.
· Review material, foundation, installation, freight, duty, currency, and other project costs with the appropriate functional leaders.
· Oversee proposals so that scope, exclusions, deliverables, payment milestones, warranties, and schedule assumptions are clear and consistent.
· Recommend pricing and negotiate commercial terms within delegated authority; escalate margin exceptions and material contractual risks to leadership and legal counsel as appropriate.
· Maintain cost benchmarks and compare bid assumptions with actual project outcomes to improve future estimates.

Sales operations and customer support

· Set consistent processes for opportunity qualification, proposal requests, quote turnaround, approvals, and customer follow-up.
· Maintain CRM discipline and provide reliable reporting on pipeline, forecast bookings, bid status, conversion, and expected project start dates.
· Partner with Sales and Business Development on strategic pursuits, technical presentations, and negotiations with developers, EPC contractors, and other customers.
· Align proposal workloads and expected awards with Engineering, Supply Chain, and Operations capacity.
· Resolve technical and commercial questions during the sales cycle and ensure customer commitments are documented and achievable.

Operational readiness and project handoff

· Coordinate procurement plans, supplier lead times, delivery sequencing, and preliminary installation schedules before project release.
· Lead structured handoff meetings supported by approved scope, budgets, drawings, assumptions, commitments, risk registers, and key milestones.
· Confirm that unresolved design inputs, scope gaps, and customer dependencies have assigned owners and resolution dates.
· Support Operations during early execution and significant scope changes; incorporate lessons learned into future bids and processes.
People leadership and process improvement
· Build and coach the preconstruction, estimating, and sales operations team; set responsibilities, workload priorities, and performance expectations.
· Introduce practical templates, dashboards, and approval workflows that improve accuracy and reduce avoidable rework.
· Promote respectful communication, accountability, and timely decisions across departments.

Qualifications:

· Bachelor’s degree or diploma in engineering, construction management, business, or a related discipline; an equivalent combination of relevant education and experience will be considered.
· Typically 10 or more years of progressive experience in preconstruction, estimating, technical sales, project management, or operations within solar, renewable energy, construction, structural systems, or engineered products.
· At least 5 years of people leadership experience, with responsibility for team performance, budgets, and cross-functional delivery.
· Demonstrated experience connecting technical sales with project execution, including bids, pricing, contract negotiations, and project handoffs.
· Strong understanding of project costing, gross margin, commercial risk, procurement, logistics, construction scheduling, and change management.
· Ability to interpret technical drawings, specifications, bills of materials, and scope documents and work effectively with engineering specialists.
· Experience with CRM and ERP systems, advanced Excel analysis, and project scheduling or reporting tools.
· Strong negotiation, presentation, decision-making, and organizational skills, with the ability to manage several concurrent pursuits.
· Ability to travel to customer, supplier, and project locations in Canada and the United States, as required by the role.
· Experience with solar racking, trackers, steel fabrication, foundation systems, or EPC project delivery.
· Knowledge of Canadian and US construction markets, cross-border supply chains, and international sourcing.
· Experience building or scaling an estimating or preconstruction department.
· PMP, relevant estimating credentials, or P.Eng. licensure would be an asset. P.Eng. is not required for this commercial and operational leadership role; professional engineering approvals remain with appropriately licensed professionals.

Why Polar Racking?

Join our team and become part of a dynamic company at the forefront of the renewable energy sector. In addition to competitive compensation, we offer a comprehensive benefits package including RRSP contributions, generous vacation time, and the opportunity for career growth.
As a valued member of our team, you'll also enjoy collaborative, fun work environment where innovation and teamwork are celebrated. We value an innovative, diverse workplace where all colleagues feel empowered to be their authentic selves. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

Relay is a digital banking platform that gives self-made business owners the tools and know-how to be great with money—bringing clarity, confidence, and control to every dollar earned, so they can turn hard work into lasting success. We do this by replacing financial guesswork with real visibility, transforming cash flow from a constant source of stress into a clear signal owners can use to run stronger, more resilient businesses.

Relay's performance marketing team runs one of the most analytically sophisticated paid programs in the SMB fintech space — operating across paid search, paid social, affiliate, CTV, and direct mail with a $2-3M monthly budget. Your mission: make every dollar work harder, build the measurement infrastructure to prove it, and grow a team that can execute at the pace Relay moves.

What You'll Be Doing

Own Relay's full paid media portfolio — paid search, paid social, affiliate, CTV, linear TV, and direct mail. Set channel strategy, budget allocation, and performance targets across brand and performance objectives. Hold the team accountable to both.
Directly manage and develop a team of performance marketers, owning hiring, leveling, performance management, and growth pathways while coaching on channel mechanics, creative strategy, and business impact.
Lead Relay's TV and CTV strategy, partnering with Brand and Creative on messaging and measurement. Build the attribution infrastructure that connects upper-funnel investment to downstream efficiency.
Drive paid search and paid social programs with a bias toward continuous experimentation — audience segmentation, creative testing, bidding strategy, and landing page optimization across both PLG and sales-assisted conversion paths.
Own the affiliate program end-to-end, including partner recruitment, commission structure, compliance, and performance management. Identify non-obvious distribution partners in the SMB ecosystem.
Work with the data team to build and maintain Relay's measurement infrastructure across paid channels — media mix modeling, multi-touch attribution, and incrementality testing. Own the methodology and use it to strengthen decision making.
Own paid media budget modeling, pacing, and forecasting, partnering with Finance on plans that hold up under scrutiny and flex intelligently as performance data comes in.

Who You Are

8+ years in performance marketing or paid media, with at least 2 years managing a team, ideally at a high-growth SaaS, fintech, or subscription business.
You've owned a multi-million dollar monthly paid media budget and can walk through how you've allocated across channels, how your thinking evolved, and what you'd do differently.
You are an expert in attribution — you can walk through an incrementality test you've designed, a media mix model you've commissioned, or an attribution debate you've settled. You don't accept last-click as an answer.
Deep hands-on fluency in at least two of: paid search, paid social, CTV/programmatic, or affiliate — with working knowledge across the rest.
You've driven acquisition into both PLG and sales-assisted funnels and understand how channel mix, creative, and landing experience need to flex depending on which motion you're feeding.
Strong communicator who can translate channel data into business narrative — you've made a budget ask to a CFO or CEO that landed.
SQL and AI-fluent in how you and your team work — using it to accelerate analysis, creative iteration, reporting, and audience research.

Bonus Points

Experience in a regulated industry (fintech, healthcare, insurance) — you know how to run aggressive acquisition programs within compliance constraints
Experience marketing to small business owners or self-employed professionals
Experience with direct mail as an acquisition channel
A public POV on performance marketing, attribution, or media strategy

The Interview Process

Stage 1: 45-minute video call with a member of the Talent team
Stage 2: 60-minute video call with the VP of Marketing
Stage 3: 60-minute Live Scenario with the Marketing team
Stage 4: Values interview with a member of the Leadership team

Our Compensation Approach

We believe Relayers should feel rewarded for the impact they have on our mission and growth. Compensation follows impact. As impact increases, compensation grows, and we do not limit compensation changes to a once-a-year review cycle.

The annual salary range for this role is $207,000 CAD to $253,000 CAD.

For candidates who demonstrate full readiness for the defined scope of the role, the typical starting salary is $230,000 CAD. Offers below this point reflect candidates we believe can grow into the full scope of the role with support and development. Offers above this point reflect impact that meaningfully exceeds the role’s defined expectations or an expanded scope from day one.

We encourage you to have a conversation with your recruiter and ask questions about compensation throughout the hiring process. For more information on our compensation philosophy and perks and benefits, visit our Candidate Hub.

Why Relay Might Be the Perfect Fit For You

You push relentlessly for reinvention: You're always asking "how can this be better?" -- in your work, in your craft, in yourself. Comfort is a signal to push harder, not coast. You'd rather build something better than defend something familiar.
You crave autonomy: We trust our team with big challenges and the freedom to solve them. If you’re someone who takes initiative, is comfortable taking risks, and seeks input when needed, you’ll find the freedom here empowering.
You own your work: You take pride in your work, follow through on commitments, and feel a deep sense of responsibility for outcomes, not just tasks.
You build with AI, not just use it: You're actively embedding AI into how you work, pushing what's possible, and bringing your team along with you.
You care about impact, not noise: You care deeply about the substance of your work. You measure success by results, not recognition, and you let your work speak for itself.
You’re energized by complexity and ambiguity: You enjoy tackling problems that don’t come with a playbook. You’re comfortable building from scratch, iterating as you go, and collaborating to shape the best path forward.
You seek out feedback: You see directness as respect, not criticism. You actively seek input, sit with hard truths, and use feedback as fuel for improvement.
Small businesses are why we're here: Relay exists to help them thrive -- and that mission has to resonate with you.

Join Us

We're looking for people who are relentless, curious, and care deeply about the work. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't perfectly match the job description -- your perspective and drive matter more. We welcome diverse backgrounds and people who think critically, challenge the status quo, and want to help small businesses thrive.

jobs.description:
About SandboxAQ

SandboxAQ is a high-growth company delivering AI solutions that address some of the world's greatest challenges. The company’s Large Quantitative Models (LQMs) power advances in life sciences, financial services, navigation, cybersecurity, and other sectors.

We are a global team that is tech-focused and includes experts in AI, chemistry, cybersecurity, physics, mathematics, medicine, engineering, and other specialties. The company emerged from Alphabet Inc. as an independent, growth capital-backed company in 2022, funded by leading investors and supported by a braintrust of industry leaders.

At SandboxAQ, we’ve cultivated an environment that encourages creativity, collaboration, and impact. By investing deeply in our people, we’re building a thriving, global workforce poised to tackle the world's epic challenges. Join us to advance your career in pursuit of an inspiring mission, in a community of like-minded people who value entrepreneurialism, ownership, and transformative impact.

About The Team

The SandboxAQ AI Generation Engine (SAIGE) team’s mission is to accelerate SandboxAQ’s mission of “Deep Impact at Scale”
with a focus on quantitative AI and rapid innovation. More specifically, the SAIGE team aims to:

Build next-generation AI capabilities that establish SandboxAQ as the global pacesetter in quantitative AI.
Identify, incubate, prototype, and launch new AI products for high-potential and longer-term use cases, proving (or disproving) their viability as high-impact, highly profitable business lines.

The SAIGE team operates on the following principles: Prototype with Velocity, Explore Boldly, Fail Smart, Learn Fast, Look Forward, and Share Knowledge.

Our current top priority use case is leveraging AI and LQMs to solve some of the most impactful problems in the Finance and Insurance industries.

The Opportunity

As The Director Of Product Management For The AI Generation Engine (SAIGE), You Will Be The PM Lead For The Team And a Key Partner To Engineering, Research, And User Research. You Will

Own the product strategy and execution for our efforts in Finance & Risk Modeling, partnering closely with financial services and insurance customers to understand their workflows, risk models, and decision-making processes.
Lead rapid prototyping and innovation across a broad range of new ideas and domains, driving 0→1 product discovery, experimentation, and incubation of high-potential use cases.
Operate in a highly ambiguous, fast-changing environment, providing clarity on priorities, making pragmatic trade-offs, and ensuring we ship impactful prototypes and products.

This role is ideal for a seasoned product leader who is energized by uncertainty, enjoys working across disciplines (UXR, engineering, research, business), and is excited to build new AI and quantitative products from the ground up.

Key Responsibilities

Lead product strategy in Finance & Risk Modeling

Own the product vision, roadmap, and execution for our Finance/Risk portfolio, with a focus on financial services and insurance (e.g., portfolio risk, capital modeling, risk analytics, underwriting, and related workflows).
Develop a deep understanding of customer contexts, including current tools, models, and data flows (e.g., portfolio / risk modeling systems, vendor platforms, internal analytics stacks).
Partner with quantitative researchers, ML engineers, and domain experts to translate customer problems into clear product requirements and model/data needs.
Define success metrics and validation strategies to compare our approaches against existing PML/ERM and portfolio views, and to demonstrate differentiated value.

Drive rapid prototyping and 0→1 innovation

Identify, evaluate, and prioritize new AI / LQM use cases across multiple domains (beyond Finance/Risk), from early signals to clearer opportunities.
Lead 0→1 product discovery: problem framing, hypothesis development, lightweight customer validation, and rapid iteration on prototypes.
Work with engineering and research to scope experiments that are small enough to move quickly but meaningful enough to answer key questions.
Establish and champion a rigorous but pragmatic approach to ruthless prioritization, ensuring the team focuses on the highest-impact opportunities.

Build strong customer and stakeholder relationships

Serve as a trusted product partner to senior stakeholders at key customers (e.g., heads of risk, portfolio managers, actuaries, CROs), speaking credibly about risk models, scenarios, and portfolio decisions.
Lead customer conversations from initial discovery through pilot definition and ongoing adoption, connecting customer needs to the SAIGE roadmap.
Communicate progress, learnings, and recommendations clearly to internal and external stakeholders, including executives.

Essential Skills & Experience

You are a senior product leader who is comfortable at the intersection of AI, quantitative modeling, and financial risk
. You thrive in ambiguity, enjoy working closely with deeply technical teams, and can just as easily go deep on models and data as you can on customer needs and business outcomes. You are proactive, low-ego, and collaborative, and you don’t need rigid structure to have impact.

10+ years of product management experience, with substantial time spent on complex B2B or platform products; at least several years operating at a senior / staff / principal / director level (e.g., L7-equivalent scope).
Deep Experience in financial services and/or insurance, especially in one or more of:
Risk modeling (e.g., portfolio risk, capital modeling, asset-liability management, market/credit risk, or insurance risk)
Financial simulation or scenario analysis
Portfolio analytics or decision support tools

Demonstrated ability to work closely with quantitative and engineering teams:
Past experience in building AI / ML products or capabilities
Comfortable discussing models, data pipelines, and trade-offs with engineers and researchers.
Able to translate between technical details and customer/business value.

Proven track record of 0→1 product work:
Identifying new opportunities and shaping them from idea to prototype and early product.
Working through high ambiguity, incomplete information, and changing constraints.

Strong ruthless prioritization skills: can define clear frameworks, make hard trade-offs, and say “no” to good ideas to focus on the best ones.
Exceptional customer-facing skills:
Confident leading discovery and roadmap conversations with senior stakeholders.
Skilled at uncovering real needs behind stated requirements and pressure-testing problem statements.

Demonstrated ability to drive execution without heavy process or structure:
Self-directed, proactive, and comfortable creating structure where needed rather than waiting for it.
Experience in environments with shifting priorities and evolving strategies.

Strong collaboration and communication:
Experience working tightly with UXR, design, engineering, and research.
Clear written and verbal communication across technical and non-technical audiences.

Alignment with SandboxAQ values and the SAIGE principles around rapid prototyping, learning, and shared ownership.

Highly Desired Skills & Experience

Direct experience building products involving AI / ML, foundational models, quantitative models, or LLM/agentic systems.
Hands-on exposure to risk tools and vendor platforms (e.g., risk engines, portfolio analytics systems, or modeling platforms used in insurance and financial services).
Experience in both:
A high-growth startup or new product incubation context, and
A large, complex environment (e.g., Big Tech, major financial institution), giving you a strong sense of how to navigate stakeholders and scale impact.

Educational background in a quantitative or technical field (e.g., computer science, mathematics, physics, statistics, engineering, finance, or similar).

If you’re excited by the idea of shaping the future of quantitative AI, building products with real impact in finance and insurance (and possibly other domains), and leading 0→1 innovation in a highly cross-functional team, we’d love to hear from you.

Why Join Us?

We offer a comprehensive and competitive benefits package designed to support your health, financial well-being, and life outside of work.

Compensation: Competitive base salary, performance-based incentives or bonuses (where applicable), and equity participation.
Benefits: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and dependents with generous employer premium contributions, retirement savings with company matching, paid parental leave, and inclusive family-building benefits.
Work-Life Balance: Flexible paid time off, company-wide seasonal breaks, and support for flexible work arrangements that enable sustainable performance.
Career Development: Opportunities for continuous learning and growth through on-the-job development, cross-functional collaboration, and access to internal learning and development programs.

SandboxAQ Welcomes All

We are committed to fostering a culture of belonging and respect, where diverse perspectives are actively sought and valued. Our multidisciplinary environment provides ample opportunity for continuous growth - working alongside humble, empowered, and ambitious colleagues ready to tackle epic challenges.

jobs.title: Head of Product – AI Native
jobs.description:
Qui sommes-nous ?

Pivot est une startup québécoise qui simplifie la gestion des opérations pour les restaurants.
Adoptée par des restaurants gastronomiques et des chaînes comme A&W, Boustan et Poulet Rouge, notre plateforme aide les restaurateurs à gérer leurs horaires, leurs équipes, leurs pourboires et leur paie.

Notre ambition : éliminer les tâches répétitives pour permettre aux restaurateurs de se concentrer sur leur équipe et leurs clients.

Et on croit que l'IA change complètement la façon d'y arriver. Pas en ajoutant de l'IA aux fonctionnalités existantes, mais en repensant ce que le restaurateur devrait encore avoir à faire lui-même. C'est là que tu entres en jeu 🚀

Le rôle

Tu seras notre Head of Product : un team of one, responsable de bâtir le produit, mais aussi la fonction produit de Pivot. Tu travailleras directement avec nos deux fondateurs, qui portent la vision produit, tu relèveras de notre CTO et tu formeras un tandem avec notre Head of Engineering. Ceci est un poste hybride où vous vous joindrez au bureau trois jours par semaine (mardi, mercredi, jeudi).

Tes missions

Comprendre les problèmes qui comptent :
Aller à la rencontre des restaurateurs, remonter des demandes individuelles aux problèmes fondamentaux qu'elles révèlent et challenger les hypothèses, les leurs comme les nôtres.
Concevoir des produits AI-native :
Partir du résultat recherché plutôt que des interfaces existantes, et déterminer ce que la technologie peut prendre en charge et ce qui mérite réellement une intervention humaine.
Prototyper et valider rapidement :
Matérialiser les idées en prototypes, simulations et expérimentations, et les valider avec les clients avant d'investir en développement.
Roadmap et priorisation :
Bâtir une roadmap guidée par la valeur client et les priorités d'affaires, définir les MVP qui démontrent la valeur et décider ce qui mérite notre énergie maintenant.
Préparation pour l'ingénierie :
Avec le Head of Engineering, définir les grandes capacités nécessaires et leur séquencement, et t'assurer que les initiatives sont mûres avant le développement.
Mesure et itération :
Mesurer l'adoption et la valeur créée, puis ajuster les priorités selon les résultats plutôt que suivre un plan figé.
Bâtir la fonction produit :
Mettre en place une démarche légère de découverte, de conception et de validation. Pas de bureaucratie, pas de processus pour le plaisir d'avoir des processus.
Challenger la vision :
T'imprégner de la vision des fondateurs, l'enrichir avec ce que tu apprends sur le terrain et la challenger quand il le faut.

Tu dois être aussi à l'aise à discuter de stratégie avec les fondateurs qu'à passer une heure avec un restaurateur pour comprendre ce qui a mal tourné pendant son service du samedi soir.

Ton profil

Expérience solide en Product Management (PM senior, Lead PM ou Head of Product), idéalement en startup ou en SaaS.
Tu as déjà contribué à concevoir, lancer et commercialiser des produits numériques.
Tu utilises déjà intensivement l'IA dans ton travail : recherche, analyse, prototypage, automatisation.
Bonne compréhension des nouvelles possibilités de l'IA et de la façon de les appliquer à la conception produit.
Capacité à passer rapidement d'un problème à une hypothèse, à un prototype, puis à une validation client.
Excellent jugement d'affaires et capacité à faire des choix.
Assez à l'aise techniquement pour collaborer étroitement avec une équipe d'ingénierie.
Le leadership nécessaire pour challenger des fondateurs ambitieux et faire converger les décisions.
Autonomie, sens de l'organisation, et autant d'intérêt pour la stratégie que pour l'exécution.
À l'aise dans un environnement startup où les priorités évoluent et où ton travail a un impact direct.

Un vrai + si tu as de l'expérience en restauration, dans des produits intégrant l'IA ou en automatisation intelligente.

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ?

Un rôle de leadership, profondément hands-on, avec une influence réelle sur la stratégie produit et les décisions de l'entreprise.
Une collaboration directe avec deux fondateurs issus de la restauration, notre CTO et notre Head of Engineering.
L'occasion de bâtir une fonction produit de A à Z, avec une grande autonomie.
Une équipe qui utilise déjà l'IA au quotidien pour repousser ce qu'une petite équipe peut accomplir.
Un produit qui simplifie le quotidien des restaurateurs et de leurs équipes.
Une équipe engagée qui valorise les discussions franches, le partage et l'initiative.
Des bureaux chaleureux dans le quartier Saint-Henri, près du canal de Lachine.
Un environnement dog-friendly : ton chien est le bienvenu !
Salaire allant de 100 000 $ à 120 000 $ CAD.

Processus d'embauche

Entrevue en visio avec notre CTO
Échange sur ton approche produit et ta façon d'utiliser l'IA
Entrevue avec Yannick et Jérôme, cofondateurs
Vérification des références
Offre

Comment postuler ?

Tu préfères comprendre pourquoi un problème existe plutôt que simplement développer une fonctionnalité pour le résoudre ? On aimerait te rencontrer.
Envoie ton CV et ta lettre de motivation à yannick@pivotapp.ca. Dans ta lettre, dis-nous pourquoi ce défi t'intéresse et comment l'IA influence aujourd'hui ta façon de concevoir des produits.

Viens construire la suite de Pivot avec nous 🤝
