jobs.description:
CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER (CFO)

Bujou Group | Founding Executive Opportunity

Location: Calgary, Alberta
Employment Type: Full-Time | Executive Leadership
Compensation: Competitive Executive Salary + Equity Participation
Reports To: Chief Executive Officer

About Bujou Group

Bujou Group is a diversified Canadian business group operating across real estate development, investment management, construction, hospitality, property management, and marketing.

Through our portfolio of companies, including Precedent Developments, Bujou Capital, Bujou Construction Management, Bujou Properties, and Bujou Studios, we are building an integrated platform focused on creating, managing, and growing long-term enterprise value.

We are entering a significant stage of expansion with the launch of the Bujou Mutual Fund Trust (MFT), an investment platform initially offering two funds focused on strategic real estate equity investments and mezzanine lending.

As we establish this investment platform and continue expanding our operating businesses, we are seeking an experienced Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to join our executive leadership team.

The Opportunity

This is a unique opportunity to take on a founding executive role in the launch and growth of Bujou Capital’s investment platform, while assuming financial leadership across the entire Bujou Group.

The CFO will be responsible for the financial strategy, management, reporting, and oversight of all Bujou Group companies, with a particular emphasis on establishing and managing the financial operations of the Bujou Mutual Fund Trust and its underlying investment structures.

The successful candidate will play a central role in launching our two initial investment funds, establishing institutional-quality financial infrastructure, supporting capital formation, and positioning the group for significant long-term growth.

We are seeking more than a traditional corporate finance executive. Our ideal candidate has experience operating at the C-suite level within an investment firm, asset management company, private equity platform, real estate investment firm, or capital markets organization.

As an early member of the executive leadership team, the CFO will have meaningful influence over the financial structure and growth of the organization, with equity-based compensation providing an opportunity to participate in the long-term value being created.

Key Responsibilities

1. Bujou Mutual Fund Trust & Investment Management

This will be the most significant and strategically important component of the role.

* Lead the establishment and ongoing financial management of the Bujou Mutual Fund Trust and its two initial investment funds.
* Oversee fund accounting, financial reporting, cash management, capital deployment tracking, and investment performance reporting.
* Establish appropriate financial systems and reporting processes across the MFT, Master Limited Partnership, and underlying investment entities.
* Manage net asset value calculations, investment valuations, investor capital accounts, distributions, and financial reconciliations.
* Develop and maintain fund-level financial models, cash flow projections, liquidity forecasts, and performance reporting.
* Coordinate with external fund administrators, auditors, tax professionals, legal counsel, and regulatory advisors.
* Establish financial controls, reporting standards, and governance procedures appropriate for a growing investment management platform.
* Support fund capitalization, investor due diligence, financial disclosures, and capital-raising initiatives.
* Ensure financial and operational reporting obligations are met in coordination with legal and regulatory advisors.

2. Group-Wide Financial Leadership

* Assume executive responsibility for financial management across all Bujou Group companies and subsidiaries.
* Oversee corporate accounting, budgeting, forecasting, treasury, tax planning, and financial reporting.
* Develop consolidated financial statements and group-wide financial performance reporting.
* Manage intercompany transactions, capital allocation, and financial structures across operating entities.
* Establish financial controls and reporting systems that support operational efficiency and scalable growth.
* Provide strategic financial guidance to the CEO and executive leadership team.
* Oversee banking relationships, credit facilities, debt management, and corporate liquidity.
* Identify opportunities to improve profitability, capital efficiency, and long-term enterprise value.

3. Capital Markets & Corporate Finance

* Support the development and execution of Bujou Group’s long-term capital strategy.
* Work alongside executive leadership to structure financing arrangements, investment transactions, and strategic partnerships.
* Develop sophisticated financial models for acquisitions, developments, investment opportunities, and corporate transactions.
* Support institutional and accredited investor due diligence, financial presentations, and investment reporting.
* Evaluate debt and equity financing alternatives to optimize capital structures across the group.
* Build relationships with financial institutions, investment partners, lenders, and professional advisors.
* Support future investment fund launches and the expansion of the Bujou Capital investment platform.

4. Real Estate Investment & Development Finance

* Oversee financial analysis and reporting for real estate development, acquisition, and investment projects.
* Evaluate project feasibility, projected returns, financing structures, cash flows, and investment performance.
* Monitor development budgets, construction financing, loan covenants, and project-level financial exposure.
* Support investment decision-making through comprehensive financial analysis and risk assessment.
* Work with the executive team to establish consistent financial reporting across the real estate portfolio.

5. Executive Leadership & Organizational Growth

* Help establish the financial infrastructure required to support Bujou Group’s evolution into a sophisticated investment and operating platform.
* Build and lead internal finance and accounting teams as the organization expands.
* Establish relationships with external accountants, auditors, fund administrators, and other financial service providers.
* Participate in executive-level strategic planning, corporate structuring, and growth initiatives.
* Contribute to the development of new investment products, funds, and operating businesses.

Qualifications & Experience

Preferred Experience

* Previous experience as a CFO, VP Finance, Head of Finance, or senior financial executive within an investment firm, private equity firm, asset management company, real estate investment platform, or capital markets organization.
* Demonstrated experience managing investment funds, pooled investment vehicles, limited partnerships, or similar investment structures.
* Strong understanding of fund accounting, investment valuations, capital structures, investor distributions, and financial reporting.
* Experience supporting capital raises, investment transactions, and institutional or accredited investor relationships.
* Knowledge of Canadian investment fund structures, taxation, and applicable securities regulatory requirements.
* Experience with real estate investment, development finance, private credit, or alternative investments is highly advantageous.

Professional Qualifications

* CPA designation strongly preferred.
* CFA designation, MBA, or equivalent advanced financial qualifications considered a significant asset.
* Typically 10+ years of progressive financial leadership experience, including senior management or executive responsibility.
* Advanced financial modelling, forecasting, and analytical capabilities.
* Experience establishing and scaling financial operations within growing or entrepreneurial organizations.
* Strong financial governance, risk management, and strategic decision-making capabilities.

The Ideal Candidate

We are seeking a financially sophisticated executive who combines institutional investment experience with an entrepreneurial mindset.

The successful candidate will be comfortable operating at both the strategic and operational levels—developing capital strategies and advising on multimillion-dollar transactions while also taking ownership of the financial systems, controls, and reporting required to support a growing organization.

They will recognize the opportunity to help establish a new investment platform from its inception and will be motivated by the prospect of building a long-term business rather than simply managing an existing finance department.

Experience in capital markets or investment management at the executive level will be a significant differentiator.

Compensation & Long-Term Opportunity

We recognize that attracting an experienced financial executive requires an opportunity that reflects both the responsibilities of the position and the value they will contribute to the organization.

The compensation package will include:

* Competitive executive base salary, commensurate with experience and qualifications.
* Equity-based compensation, providing participation in the long-term growth and success of the business, subject to an agreed structure.
* Opportunity to become a founding member of the leadership team responsible for establishing Bujou Capital’s investment platform.
* Significant influence over the financial strategy, corporate structure, and future expansion of Bujou Group.
* A long-term executive leadership opportunity within a growing, diversified Canadian business group.

The specific compensation and equity structure will be negotiated based on the successful candidate’s experience, qualifications, and expected contribution.

Why Join Bujou Group?

Bujou Group is at an important inflection point.

With established operating businesses and the launch of our mutual fund trust and initial investment funds, we are creating a platform designed to connect real estate investment, development expertise, and long-term capital management.

For the right executive, this position represents an opportunity to help build the financial foundation of an investment business from its earliest stages, contribute directly to its growth, and participate in the value created along the way.

We are looking for a CFO who wants to help build an investment firm, not simply manage its finances.

How to Apply

Qualified candidates are invited to submit their résumé and a brief introduction outlining their executive financial leadership experience, particularly within investment management, private equity, capital markets, or real estate investment.

All applications will be handled confidentially.

jobs.title: Directeur des Produits | Chief Product Officer
jobs.description:
À PROPOS DE POWER FACTORS

Power Factors est un fournisseur de logiciels et de solutions qui mène la nouvelle génération de l'énergie propre avec Unity, l'une des suites de gestion de l'énergie renouvelable (REMS) les plus complètes et les plus largement déployées sur le marché. Avec plus de 300 GW d'actifs éoliens, solaires et de stockage d'énergie gérés dans le monde, plus de 600 clients et 18 000 sites, Power Factors gère 25 % des données mondiales sur les énergies renouvelables.*

Unity REMS de Power Factors couvre l'ensemble de la chaîne de valeur de l'énergie, de la supervision et du contrôle à l'analyse des marchés. Cette suite d'applications ouvertes, fondées sur les données, permet aux acteurs des énergies renouvelables de collaborer, d'automatiser les flux de travail critiques et de prendre des décisions plus éclairées afin de maximiser le rendement de leurs actifs. Les acteurs du secteur bénéficient d'un accompagnement de bout en bout, avec des solutions pour le SCADA et le PPC, la supervision centralisée, la gestion de la performance, la gestion commerciale des actifs et la gestion des interventions sur le terrain.

Grâce à sa vaste expertise métier, Power Factors propose à grande échelle des analyses issues de l'IA, afin que les entreprises puissent optimiser leurs actifs, libérer leur croissance et prendre de meilleures décisions alors que le monde accélère sa transition vers une énergie propre. Power Factors lutte contre le changement climatique par le code.

Hors Chine et Inde

À PROPOS DU POSTE

Power Factors est une entreprise de logiciels de référence dans son secteur, au service de l'industrie des énergies renouvelables. Nous recrutons un Directeur des Produits (Chief Product Officer, CPO) chargé de piloter la stratégie, les processus et la performance produit sur l'ensemble de notre portefeuille, et de transformer la gestion de produit en un véritable modèle de responsabilité (« ownership »).

Notre ambition est que chaque produit soit dirigé par un product owner qui comprend le chiffre d'affaires qu'il génère, le coût de sa conception et de son exploitation, ainsi que le rendement qu'il apporte. Le CPO développera cette capacité, inspirera l'équipe pour qu'elle l'adopte et sera responsable des résultats. Il s'agit d'un engagement pluriannuel pour façonner le prochain chapitre de l'entreprise.

Un partenariat essentiel

Le CPO et le Directeur de la Technologie (CTO) sont les deux moitiés d'un même moteur. Le CPO est responsable de ce que nous construisons et pourquoi : stratégie, valeur client, priorisation, résultats commerciaux et compte de résultat (P&L) des produits. Le CTO est responsable de la manière dont les produits sont construits et livrés : ingénierie, architecture et exécution du développement. Le succès repose sur des objectifs partagés, une confiance mutuelle et un rythme opérationnel commun qui transforme la stratégie en produits livrés, adoptés et rentables. Les candidats doivent démontrer une expérience avérée de partenariats exceptionnels avec des responsables technologiques.

Vos missions

Piloter la stratégie produit. Définir et communiquer une vision claire, centrée sur le client, ainsi qu'une feuille de route pluriannuelle qui renforce notre leadership dans les énergies renouvelables
Bâtir une culture de product ownership. Faire évoluer l'organisation vers une responsabilité produit assumée, chaque owner étant responsable des résultats, et non des seules livraisons
Mettre en place un suivi du P&L. Collaborer avec la Finance pour offrir à chaque product owner une visibilité transparente sur le chiffre d'affaires, la marge et la structure de coûts, et prendre sur cette base les décisions d'investissement, de tarification et d'arrêt de produits
Promouvoir l'excellence en gestion de produit. Instaurer des processus rigoureux et évolutifs pour la découverte, la priorisation, l'élaboration des feuilles de route, le lancement et la gestion du cycle de vie, avec des indicateurs clairs
Travailler en partenariat avec le CTO. Co-construire le modèle opérationnel, le calendrier de planification et les droits de décision entre produit et développement, et arbitrer conjointement les compromis
Collaborer avec l'ensemble de la chaîne commerciale. S'aligner avec les Ventes, le Marketing, le Succès Client et les Services sur le positionnement, le packaging, la tarification, l'adoption et la fidélisation
Rester proche des clients et du marché. Échanger avec les propriétaires, exploitants, gestionnaires d'actifs et investisseurs ; suivre la réglementation, la technologie et la concurrence ; identifier des opportunités de croissance, y compris des partenariats et des fusions-acquisitions
Développer les leaders. Recruter, accompagner et fidéliser une organisation produit performante ainsi qu'un vivier de futurs dirigeants
Contribuer en tant que dirigeant. Siéger au comité exécutif (ELT), participer à la définition de la stratégie de l'entreprise et rendre compte de la performance produit au PDG et au Conseil d'administration

Votre profil

Maîtrise fonctionnelle

Contributions démontrées et vérifiables en tant que responsable produit senior : produits que vous avez conçus, développés à grande échelle, repositionnés ou redressés, et résultats commerciaux obtenus
Capacité avérée à concevoir et à faire fonctionner des processus de gestion de produit, et à renforcer les compétences et l'esprit d'ownership d'une équipe
Aisance commerciale : expérience de la responsabilité ou de l'influence sur le P&L d'un produit, la tarification et le packaging, et prise de décisions d'investissement fondées sur les données
Historique de partenariats solides et collaboratifs avec la direction de l'ingénierie
Excellentes qualités de communication, capacité à inspirer, à influencer et à responsabiliser

Expertise du secteur des énergies renouvelables

Connaissance approfondie du secteur des énergies renouvelables, par exemple en matière de performance des actifs, d'exploitation, de finance ou de logiciels pour l'énergie. Nous étudierons aussi les profils de dirigeants produit exceptionnels capables d'apprendre rapidement, mais une expertise sectorielle approfondie est un véritable atout

Exposition au Conseil d'administration (souhaitée, non obligatoire)

Expérience préalable au sein d'un comité exécutif et auprès d'un Conseil d'administration. Nous accueillons volontiers les leaders en devenir dont le parcours et la motivation montrent qu'ils sont prêts à franchir cette étape

Qui vous êtes

Un expert de votre métier, avec un impact avéré et l'humilité de continuer à apprendre
Animé par l'envie de faire la différence et motivé par la mission d'accélérer la transition vers les énergies renouvelables
Enthousiaste à l'idée de rejoindre un leader de sa catégorie et prêt à vous engager sur le long terme
Un bâtisseur et un pédagogue, qui fait grandir son entourage

Comment le succès sera mesuré

Des product owners disposant d'une visibilité claire sur le P&L et assumant leur responsabilité sur l'ensemble du portefeuille
Un processus de gestion de produit mature et appliqué de manière cohérente
Une croissance mesurable du chiffre d'affaires produit, de l'adoption, de la fidélisation et de la marge
Un partenariat de grande confiance et à haute vélocité avec le CTO, ainsi qu'une équipe produit engagée et fidélisée

LA VIE CHEZ POWER FACTORS

Nous sommes une entreprise de développement logiciel agile : assez grande pour avoir un impact, assez petite pour aller vite et exécuter dans un secteur en pleine croissance. Nous sommes une équipe de talents audacieux et ingénieux, animés par les résultats. Nous sommes passionnés par l'idée de rendre le monde meilleur. Nous recherchons des personnes ambitieuses et humbles pour nous aider à réaliser notre plan.

POURQUOI NOUS REJOINDRE

En rejoignant l'équipe de Power Factors, vous ferez partie d'un groupe dynamique de personnes innovantes et motivées, engagées à avoir un impact positif. Chaque jour, votre travail contribuera directement à l'avancement des solutions d'énergie propre et au soutien des initiatives mondiales de durabilité. Notre culture est profondément ancrée et se reflète dans notre façon de travailler ensemble : engagés, consciencieux et collaboratifs. Avec de nombreuses opportunités d'évolution professionnelle, Power Factors vous accompagne dans votre développement alors que nous menons la transformation du secteur de l'énergie.

EMPLOYEUR GARANTISSANT L'ÉGALITÉ DES CHANCES

Power Factors est un employeur garantissant l'égalité des chances, engagé à rassembler une main-d'œuvre diversifiée et à entretenir une culture inclusive. Toutes les candidatures qualifiées seront examinées sans considération de race, de couleur, de religion, de sexe, d'orientation sexuelle, d'identité de genre, d'origine nationale, de handicap ou de statut d'ancien combattant.

About Power Factors

Power Factors is a software and solutions provider leading the next generation of clean energy with Unity, one of the most extensive and widely deployed renewable energy management suites (REMS) in the market. With over 300 GW of wind, solar, and energy storage assets managed worldwide across more than 600 customers and 18,000 sites, Power Factors manages 25% of the world's renewable energy data.*

Power Factors' Unity REMS supports the entire energy value chain, from monitoring and controls to market analytics. The company's suite of open, data-driven applications empowers renewable energy stakeholders to collaborate, automate critical workflows, and make more informed decisions to maximize asset returns. Energy stakeholders receive end-to-end support, including solutions for SCADA & PPC, centralized monitoring, performance management, commercial asset management, and field service management.

With deep domain expertise, AI-powered insights are delivered at scale so businesses can optimize assets, unlock growth, and make smarter decisions as the world rapidly transitions to clean energy. Power Factors fights climate change with code.

Outside China and India

About The Role

PowerFactors is a category-leading software company serving the renewable energy industry. We are hiring a Chief Product Officer to own product strategy, process and performance across our portfolio, and to transform product management into a true ownership model.

Our ambition is for every product to be run by a product owner who understands the revenue it generates, the cost to build and serve it, and the return it delivers. The CPO will build that capability, inspire the team to embrace it, and be accountable for the results. This is a multi-year commitment to shape the company's next chapter.

The Critical Partnership

The CPO and Chief Technology Officer are two halves of one engine. The CPO owns what we build and why: strategy, customer value, prioritization, commercial outcomes and product P&L. The CTO owns how it is built and delivered: engineering, architecture and development execution. Success depends on shared goals, mutual trust, and a joint operating rhythm that turns strategy into shipped, adopted, profitable product. Candidates should show a track record of exceptional partnership with technology leaders.

What You Will Do

Lead product strategy. Define and communicate a clear, customer-driven vision and multi-year roadmap that extends our leadership in renewables
Build a product-owner culture. Evolve the organization from to accountable product ownership, with each owner responsible for outcomes, not outputs
Establish P&L oversight. Partner with Finance to give every product owner transparent visibility of revenue, margin and cost structure, and to make investment, pricing and sunset decisions on that basis
Drive product management excellence. Institute disciplined, scalable processes for discovery, prioritization, roadmapping, launch, and lifecycle management, with clear metrics
Partner with the CTO. Co-create the operating model, planning cadence and decision rights

jobs.title: Head of Growth
jobs.description:
Company Description
Mills builds AI-powered tools that simplify construction scheduling and daily workflows for general contractors and subcontractors. The platform brings scheduling and project coordination into a single, streamlined workspace, reducing complexity across projects with many moving parts. Mills’ AI agents are designed to automate repetitive tasks, helping contractors avoid time-consuming follow-ups and manual updates. By reducing administrative overhead, Mills enables construction teams to focus more on execution and delivering high-quality work. The company is committed to making construction operations more efficient, predictable, and easier to manage.
Role Description
The Head of Growth is a full-time, hybrid role based in Toronto, ON, with flexibility for part-time work from home. This role is responsible for defining and executing Mills’ growth strategy, including setting customer acquisition targets, identifying key market segments, and optimizing the end-to-end growth funnel. Day-to-day responsibilities include leading growth marketing initiatives, running experiments across channels, overseeing performance metrics, and collaborating closely with sales, product, and customer success teams. The Head of Growth will design and iterate on go-to-market campaigns, build and manage growth-related processes, and use data to inform decisions on pricing, positioning, and messaging. jobs.title: Vice President, Marketing
jobs.description:
Cosmetic Physician Partners (CPP) is the largest practitioner-owned medical aesthetics network in the US. Founded in 2022, we have grown to 80+ clinics across the US. We are profitable, have already returned more than $60M to our investors, and are majority owned by our doctors, nurses and employees. No private equity.

Our model is simple: great practitioners lead their clinics, and CPP gives them the leadership team, support services and brand to grow faster than they could alone. We are looking for leaders who want to help write the next chapter.

MISSION

Own CPP’s marketing strategy and make it happen in every clinic. Set CPP clinics apart in the minds of consumers so our network grows faster than our peers, and do it in a way that our physicians, practice managers and marketing team trust and get behind.

THE ONE THING THAT MATTERS MOST

CPP owns its clinics, but we treat our physicians and practice managers like owners. This person earns their trust and the trust of our marketing team. Trust is earned by showing up with a sharp strategy, knowing digital inside out, rolling up your sleeves to deliver results, and building a team people want to be part of.

KEY OUTCOMES

1. Earn the trust of our physicians and practice managers

Partner, not vendor:
Build real working relationships with physicians and practice managers, and treat them like the owners they act as. Understand each clinic’s goals, patients and local market before recommending anything.
Speak their language:
Translate marketing into what clinics care about: new patients, rebooking, revenue per provider and return on spend. Explain the why behind every plan in plain terms.
Show up:
Visit clinics regularly, run clear monthly performance reviews and follow through on every commitment. Bad news early, good news with data.
Clinic-level guidance:
Give clinics practical playbooks they can run locally, and coach practice managers who are less familiar with marketing.

2. Earn the trust of our marketing team

Lead by example:
Be the person who can do the work, not just review it. Credibility comes from walking the talk.
Clear direction:
Set clear priorities, targets and ownership so everyone knows what winning looks like and how their work moves the numbers.
Back your people:
Remove roadblocks, give honest feedback, and give credit generously. Build a fun, drama-free team culture aligned with CPP values.

3. Clinic-level marketing strategy

Local brand positioning:
For each clinic, define how it stands out in its local market: who its patients are, what it is known for, and how it beats local competitors.
Clinic marketing plans:
Build a marketing plan for every clinic with the channels, budget and targets it needs to grow, created together with its physicians and practice manager.
Local presence:
Grow each clinic’s reputation in its community through reviews, local search, social media, events and referral partners.
Growth levers:
Drive both new patient acquisition and retention of existing patients (rebooking, visit frequency, loyalty) clinic by clinic.
Network advantage:
Use CPP’s scale, shared playbooks and annual promotional calendar to make every local brand stronger, and decide where in-house beats agencies.

4. Lead our digital marketing team

Lead digital experts:
Lead a team of digital marketing professionals across paid media, SEO, web, CRM and design. Know the craft deeply enough to coach and challenge each of them.
Set clear goals:
Set goals and targets for each person and channel, tied to clinic results like new patients and rebooking, and review progress with the team regularly.
Clear the path:
Help the team work through challenges, from underperforming campaigns to tech and data issues, and make the call when trade-offs are needed.
Translate digital:
Explain what is happening in plain language to physicians, practice managers and business operators: what we did, what it delivered and what comes next. No jargon.
Measurement:
Make sure tracking and dashboards are in place so results are clear and trusted by everyone.
AI in marketing:
Keep building AI into our marketing stack, from content and creative to targeting, reporting and patient journeys. Test new tools fast and scale what works.

5. Hands-on execution

Walk the talk:
Personally build campaigns, review ad accounts, write briefs and fix what is broken. This is a player-coach role.
Ship fast:
Launch, measure, learn and adjust quickly. Deliver results in months, not quarters.
Roll out at scale:
Take what works in one clinic and roll it out across the network, including new and acquired clinics.
Best practices:
Benchmark top-performing clinics and standardize what drives results.

6. Build and support teams

Build the team:
Hire, develop and retain a high-performance team of employees and contract partners.
Develop people:
Coach team members to grow in their roles, with regular 1-on-1s, clear goals and honest feedback.
Manage partners:
Hold agencies and vendors to clear targets, and bring work in-house where it makes sense.

WHAT YOU BRING

Experience:
10+ years in marketing, with 5+ years leading teams. Healthcare, medical aesthetics or wellness a strong plus.
Nice to have:
Multi-location consumer services experience, and agency-side experience.
Relationship skills:
A track record of earning the trust of operators, owners or clinicians who do not report to you, and getting them on board with change.
Strategic and digital depth:
Proven ability to build a marketing strategy and personally run digital channels to measurable growth.
Hands-on mindset:
Comfortable going from a board-level plan to the details of an ad account in the same day.
Data-driven:
Fluent with marketing analytics and comfortable making decisions from numbers, while staying close to people.
Communication:
Clear, simple and direct in writing and in person. French is a plus but not required.
Adaptable:
Thrives on change. Our business moves fast and priorities shift, and you adjust quickly without losing momentum.
AI-forward:
Excited about AI and already using it in your own work. You see it as a way to do more, faster and better.
CRM agnostic:
Experience with any major CRM or marketing automation platform. We care about results, not tools.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN YEAR ONE

Trusted by clinics:
Physicians and practice managers see you as a partner and ask for your input.
Trusted by the team:
The marketing team is engaged, clear on its targets and retaining its best people.
Clear plan:
A network-wide marketing strategy and budget is in place and understood by clinics.
Measurable growth:
New patient growth and patient retention are tracked monthly and trending ahead of target.

WHY JOIN CPP

Compensation:
Competitive package including health and dental benefits, and free medical aesthetic services from our network.
Equity:
Significant equity upside as we grow.
Fast growth:
Build alongside a proven leadership team in a profitable, fast-growing business.
Clear direction:
Very clear goals on what success looks like.
Culture:
We are clinic first, with a strong culture that values its people. A fun, drama-free workplace that rewards those who help build it.

PERKS & BENEFITS

RRSP Matching Program – Support for your long-term financial goals.
Summer Fridays – Enjoy half-day Fridays during the summer.
Comprehensive Benefits – 100% employer-paid base benefits plan.
Hybrid Work Environment – Flexibility to work both remotely and in the office.
Aesthetic Treatments – Access to treatments at our clinics.
Office Perks & Events – Snacks and refreshments, monthly team lunches, and quarterly team events.

jobs.description:
Level:
M4 | Proficient

Location:
Ottawa, ON | Hybrid

Reports To:
Victoria Wnek, VP, Operations

Type:
Permanent | Full-Time

About Solink

At Solink, our mission is to safeguard what matters most
. We provide businesses with the tools to know sooner and act faster
by transforming video security into real-time operational insights.

Our cloud-based platform integrates seamlessly with your existing cameras and systems, turning them into intelligent sensors that detect and interpret key moments. This empowers teams to make data-driven decisions, enhance security, and improve operational efficiency.

Trusted by over 35,000 locations across 60+ countries - including brands like McDonald’s and JYSK - Solink delivers clarity when it counts. Our solutions help businesses reduce shrink, optimize performance, and respond proactively to potential threats.

We're growing rapidly, earning industry recognition, and scaling with purpose. We’ve been recognized by Deloitte’s Fast 50™ and Fast 500™, Business Intelligence Group, and as one of Ottawa’s Best Places to Work. And we’re just getting started!

The Role

As Director, Operations
, you'll own Solink's end-to-end sales-to-deployment operating model, from the moment a deal closes to the point a customer is live, supported and generating recurring revenue. Our Deployment function has grown in scale, complexity and strategic importance, and this role exists to lead it into its next chapter.

You'll lead a team across three focus areas: Deployment Execution, Optimization & Automation, and Operations Enablement. You'll be accountable for the overall function and driving major automation and process-improvement initiatives and partnering with senior leaders across the organization to improve planning, quality, scalability and accountability.

This is an opportunity for an operations leader who's energized by building systems that scale, raising the bar on execution and connecting operational performance directly to ARR growth.

What You’ll Do

Own the sales-to-deployment operating model: Define and continuously improve how work flows from Sales through Deployment to Support, including handoffs, planning, capacity, quality standards and accountability at every stage.
Lead and develop a high-performing leadership team: Lead Managers across Deployment Execution, Optimization & Automation, and Enablement & Cross-Functional. Set clear goals, coach for growth and build a leadership bench that can scale with the business.
Drive operational transformation: Lead major automation, tooling and process-improvement initiatives that increase throughput, reduce cycle time and improve the customer deployment experience.
Deliver on ARR: Ensure deployments are executed on time and at quality so that contracted revenue converts to recurring revenue predictably. Own the metrics, forecasting and reporting that connect operations to financial outcomes.
Partner across the organization: Work closely with senior leaders in Sales, Customer Success, Support, Product and Finance to align on planning, resolve cross-functional friction and make Deployment a strategic lever for the business.
Establish governance and operational rigour: Set the standards, SOPs, KPIs and reporting cadence that give leadership clear visibility into deployment health, capacity and risk.
Oversee partner and field strategy: Guide how Solink works with installation partners and field resources, including partner enablement, performance management and relationship health.
Serve as the senior escalation point: Own resolution of high-impact customer and operational escalations, and turn recurring issues into systemic fixes.

Role Expectations

This is an M4 level role. At Solink, individuals at this level serve as a strategic advisor within a department, who is confident acting as their executive leader’s right hand within their functional area and is able to set cross-functional direction in collaboration with departments within the organization.

In this role, you'll be expected to:

Set the vision and multi-quarter roadmap for the Deployment function and translate it into clear priorities for your managers.
Operate with a high degree of autonomy, making decisions that shape how the function runs and how it interacts with the rest of the business.
Influence senior stakeholders across functions, building alignment on shared goals, processes and trade-offs.
Balance near-term delivery with long-term investment in automation, tooling and scalability.
Build a culture of ownership, quality and continuous improvement across the Deployment team.

What success looks like:

Deployment cycle times, on-time delivery and quality metrics improve measurably, and ARR from new deals is realized faster and more predictably.
Key automation and process-improvement initiatives are delivered, reducing manual effort and allowing the function to scale without proportional headcount growth.
Sales, Deployment, Support and other partners operate from a shared planning model with clear handoffs, visible accountability and fewer escalations.

What You Bring

Must-Have:

8+ years in operations, deployment, implementation or professional services, including 3+ years leading managers or multi-team functions.
A proven track record of designing and scaling an end-to-end operating model in a high-growth B2B technology, SaaS or hardware-enabled services environment.
Demonstrated success leading process-improvement and automation initiatives with measurable impact on efficiency, quality or revenue.
Strong analytical and business acumen, with experience owning KPIs, capacity planning and operational reporting tied to financial outcomes such as ARR.
Excellent cross-functional leadership and communication skills, with the credibility to influence senior leaders and drive alignment.

Nice-to-Have:

Experience in physical security, video surveillance, IoT or other field-deployed technology.
Experience managing installation partner or channel networks across multiple regions.
Familiarity with operations tooling and automation platforms (e.g., Salesforce, HubSpot, NetSuite, Asana, Jira, n8n or similar).
Background in Lean, Six Sigma or other formal continuous-improvement methodologies.

Security Requirements

Candidates must undergo a criminal records check upon hire;
Be a Canadian Citizen (dual citizens included), or eligible to work in Canada;
Be willing to comply with Solink’s own security policies and standards.

Compensation

The compensation range for this role is $156,696-195,870 CAD and includes a base salary plus a performance-based variable component.

We determine compensation based on the experience, skills, and impact you bring to the role.

For this position, we are hiring within the Proficient
range. Candidates in this range will demonstrate the ability to serve as a strategic advisor within their department, confidently acting as the senior leader's right hand within their functional area and setting cross-functional direction in collaboration with other departments across the organization.

Our Values

We do things the Solink way:

Act with URGENCY – Our customers move fast, so we do too.
Deliver with QUALITY – We sweat the details and hold a high bar.
Win with TEAM – No egos. Just outcomes, built together.
Lead with TRUST – We earn it through clarity, consistency, and care.

These aren’t just words—they shape how we hire, lead, and grow.

Why Solink?

We’re not just building tech - we’re building a place where great people do great work.

Clarity and trust: Where the role allows, we support flexibility in how and where work gets done - and we’re upfront about what’s required.
Meaningful equity: Every full-time, permanent employee has a stake in our growth.
Comprehensive benefits: Fully paid health & dental (no waiting period) + $500 health spending account.
Wellness support: Monthly reimbursement for fitness, wellness, or mental health programs.
Growth through merit: Advancement is based on contribution, initiative, and the ability to raise the bar - together.
Candid culture: Clear expectations, honest feedback, and no politics.
Social connection: From So-learns to Solink-o and So-lunches, we stay connected in ways that actually feel fun.

What To Expect From The Hiring Process

We respect your time and value transparency. Here’s a general idea of what to expect:

Intro call with our Talent Team
Behavioural interview with a member of People & Culture
Hiring Manager interview with this role's manager
Cross-functional panel interview
Reference Checks
Offer & onboarding 🎉

Please note: this is subject to change at any point in the recruitment process based on the needs of the business.

How To Apply

Submit your resume and a short cover letter via our [Careers Page]. Let us know what excites you about this role, and how you’d help move Solink forward.

NOTICE: Solink
uses artificial intelligence (AI) to screen, assess, and/or select candidates for this position.

Solink is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. If you require accommodation during the selection process, please let us know.

Oakville, Ontario, a community of more than 244,000 residents, stands out as a place where both people and business thrive. Located in the west end of the Greater Toronto Area, the town blends economic strength with an exceptional quality of life, making it one of Canada’s most desirable places in which to live and invest. It consistently ranks among the country’s most livable communities and has been recognized for seven consecutive years as one of Site Selection magazine’s top 20 Canadian locations for investment.

Oakville offers ready access to domestic and global markets, strengthened by its proximity to leading post‐secondary institutions that provide talent, research capacity, and industry partnerships. Located only 30 minutes from downtown Toronto, Oakville combines exceptional connectivity with strong academic links that support innovation and business growth.

Oakville offers a lifestyle that ranks among the best in Canada, with established neighborhoods, acclaimed schools, abundant parklands, and a strong sense of community. Quality of life is a defining feature, attracting business leaders, entrepreneurs, and employees who value a place where both work and life can thrive. This blend of natural beauty, vibrant amenities, and supportive community spirit makes Oakville a destination of choice for living, working, and growing.

With a 2026 operating budget of $458 million, a capital budget of over $344 million and over 1,700 permanent and part-time staff, the Town of Oakville is committed to meeting the needs of our residents and business community by delivering efficient and effective services that reflect their community values.

Inspire our Future as our Chief Administrative Officer

About The Role

Royal York Property Management is hiring a highly experienced Director of Operations to lead and strengthen the day-to-day operations of a growing, service-driven property management company.

This is a senior leadership role with responsibility across people, process, service quality, financial discipline, technology, compliance, vendor management, and execution.

The Director of Operations will oversee managers and operational departments, improve performance, enforce service standards, strengthen reporting, and build scalable systems across the business.

Royal York manages single-family residential rental homes, which means operations involve owners, tenants, maintenance issues, rent payments, complaints, legal timelines, vendors, communication standards, and service expectations. The right candidate must be able to lead in a fast-moving environment where accountability, documentation, customer experience, and operational discipline all matter.

This role has the potential to grow into a COO-level position for the right person.

Lead managers, team leads, and operational departments

Enforce service standards across maintenance, leasing, collections, complaints, escalations, and customer communication
Strengthen rent collection, payment follow-up, receivables discipline, and financial accountability
Improve documentation, compliance, legal escalation, and risk-control processes
Build dashboards, scorecards, reporting systems, and management routines

Work with CRM systems, automation, AI tools, customer portals, dashboards, and third-party platforms

Manage vendors, service providers, software vendors, and cross-company partnerships
Control costs while protecting service quality, compliance, collections, and customer experience

Required Experience

10+ years of operations leadership experience
5+ years in a senior operations role managing managers, department heads, or multiple operational teams
Experience leading a high-volume, people-heavy service operation
Experience overseeing teams of 50+ people, either directly or through managers, team leads, contractors, vendors, or distributed operational staff
Strong experience with customer experience, service delivery, process improvement, team accountability, and operational performance
Experience with collections, payment follow-up, receivables, financial accountability, or payment-related operating controls
Strong judgment around documentation, compliance, escalation, risk control, and operational discipline
Experience with CRM systems, dashboards, workflow tools, reporting, automation, or AI-enabled systems
Experience managing vendors, partners, external service providers, software vendors, or cross-company relationships
Ability to work with technical teams and translate business needs into clear system, workflow, automation, or reporting requirements

Education Requirement

Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree preferred
Preferred fields of study include Business Administration, Operations Management, Management, Finance, Accounting, Economics, Real Estate, Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Information Systems, Technology Management, or a related field
MBA, Master’s in Management, Master’s in Operations, or similar graduate degree is considered an asset

Property management

jobs.title: Chief Executive Officer
jobs.description:
About The Company

The Northwest Territories Power Corporation (NTPC)
is the primary public electricity utility serving the Northwest Territories and plays a critical role in supporting the territory's economic development, community well-being, and energy security. As a crown corporation wholly owned by the Government of the Northwest Territories through NT Hydro, NTPC is responsible for generating, transmitting, and distributing electricity across one of the most geographically vast and operationally challenging jurisdictions in North America. The organization provides power to more than 43,000 residents across 27 communities and manages a diverse portfolio of hydroelectric, diesel, natural gas, solar, wind, and battery storage assets. With more than $650 million in assets and approximately 151 MW of generating capacity, NTPC operates a geographically dispersed and operationally diverse utility system across the Northwest Territories.

For more information, please download the full position profile: NTPC CEO Position Profile.pdf

Position Overview

Reporting to the Board of Directors, the President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) is responsible for providing the strategic, operational, financial, and cultural leadership required to guide the Northwest Territories Power Corporation (NTPC), Northwest Territories Hydro (NT Hydro), and their subsidiaries. The CEO will ensure the organizations effectively fulfill their commercial and public-service mandates while aligning with the strategic priorities of the Government of the Northwest Territories and the evolving needs of residents, communities, businesses, and industrial customers across the North.

The CEO will provide the leadership required to advance NTPC's mandate as the Northwest Territories' leading electricity utility while supporting the priorities of the Board of Directors and shareholder. Operating at the intersection of public policy, utility operations, infrastructure investment, and economic development, the CEO will guide the organization through a period of significant transformation as it addresses aging infrastructure, increasing energy demand, major capital investment requirements, and the transition toward a more sustainable and diversified energy future. This will require a strategic yet pragmatic leader who can establish a clear long-term direction while remaining accessible, hands-on when required, and closely connected to the operational realities of delivering critical utility services across the North.

Working within a highly regulated and publicly accountable environment, the CEO will balance the operational and commercial requirements of the Corporation with broader territorial priorities. This includes advancing strategic initiatives related to system reliability, affordability, renewable energy integration, Indigenous partnerships, economic development, and long-term energy security, while ensuring strong financial stewardship, operational excellence, and organizational performance. Preparing NTPC for future growth will be a central leadership mandate, requiring the CEO to ensure the Corporation has the people, leadership capacity, systems, infrastructure, partnerships, and financial readiness required to respond to increasing demand and emerging opportunities across the Northwest Territories.

The successful candidate will bring the judgment, political acumen, and stakeholder leadership required to navigate a complex operating environment and build trusted relationships with government, regulators, Indigenous governments, communities, customers, employees, and industry partners. Beyond delivering operational and financial results, the CEO will be expected to foster a culture of safety, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement while positioning NTPC for long-term operational, financial, and environmental sustainability and ensuring the reliable delivery of affordable energy to communities across the Northwest Territories.

Education And Experience Requirements

Education and Professional Background

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, commerce or other related discipline.
Significant senior leadership experience within the utility sector or a similarly complex, capital-intensive, highly regulated environment.
Experience leading organizations with significant operational, infrastructure, stakeholder, and public accountability requirements will be highly valued.
Minimum of eight years of direct management experience, in a unionized work environment.
Previous experience providing advice to and receiving direction from a Board of Directors.

WORK ARRANGEMENT

The role is based at NTPC’s head office in Hay River and requires a visible leadership presence within the organization and community. Regular travel to Yellowknife and NTPC’s regional plants, offices, and communities throughout the Northwest Territories is required. This may include travel by small aircraft and extended stays due to weather or operational requirements. The demands of the role may also require work outside normal office hours.

RECRUITMENT PROCESS

We welcome conversations with individuals interested in learning more about this unique leadership opportunity. To explore the role in confidence, please contact a member of our Executive Search team at MNP.

To apply, please submit a résumé and cover letter in confidence through MNP's online application portal or directly to the contacts below. All inquiries and applications will be managed through MNP to ensure a fair, confidential, and consistent recruitment process.

The Northwest Territories Power Corporation is committed to building a representative workforce and values the contributions of Indigenous peoples. Qualified Indigenous candidates are encouraged to self-identify during the application process and may be eligible for consideration under NTPC's Indigenous Employment Policy.

We thank all applicants for their interest; however, only those selected to move forward in the process will be contacted.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Technical Development Lead, Device
jobs.description:
BlueRock Therapeutics, a wholly-owned and independently operated subsidiary of Bayer AG, is a leading engineered cell therapy company pioneering a new generation of cellular medicines. Utilizing our proprietary CELL+GENE™ platform, we direct cellular differentiation and genetically engineer cells to create transformative therapies for patients suffering from neurological and ophthalmological diseases.

Founded in 2016, BlueRock is at the forefront of the convergence of cell biology and genetic engineering. Our mission is to harness pluripotent stem cell technology and gene editing to deliver authentic, functional cell therapies that address the root causes of disease and offer hope to millions of patients worldwide.

What Are We Doing?

Our foundational science enables the generation and directed differentiation of universal pluripotent stem cells into authentic, functional cells for allogeneic cellular therapies.

We are passionate about realizing the promise of cell and gene therapy, shaping the future of regenerative medicine, and delivering new therapies to patients with limited or no treatment options.

Who is BlueRock?

BlueRock Therapeutics LP is a clinical stage cell therapy company harnessing the power of cell therapy to create a pipeline of new medicines for people suffering from neurological and ophthalmic diseases. Two of our novel investigational cell therapies, bemdaneprocel (BRT-DA01) for the treatment of Parkinson’s disease and OpCT-001 for the treatment of primary photoreceptor diseases are clinical stage programs. BlueRock was founded in 2016 as a joint venture of Versant Ventures and Leaps by Bayer. Our culture is defined by the courage to persist regardless of the challenge, the urgency to transform medicine and deliver hope, integrity guided by mission, and community-mindedness with the understanding that we are all part of something bigger than ourselves.

What Are We Doing?

Our foundational science harnesses the ability to create and then direct the differentiation of universal pluripotent stem cells into authentic, functional cells that can be used as allogeneic cellular therapies to treat a broad array of diseases. We can also further engineer these cells, enabling them to produce enzymes, antibodies, and other proteins for additional therapeutic benefit.

We are passionate about delivering on the promise of cellular and gene therapy, shaping the future of cellular medicine, and delivering new therapies to millions of patients with treatment options.

We are seeking individuals who are collaborative, thrive in a fun and dynamic culture, and are steadfast in the commitment to advance cutting-edge cellular therapies to impact patients’ lives.

Description Of Position

This role is responsible for providing strategic and technical leadership for the development and execution of potential delivery device systems supporting the company’s combination cell therapy portfolio. In addition, this role serves as the single point of accountability for program-level technical development, ensuring alignment from early development through clinical stages and commercialization readiness. The individual will bring deep expertise in medical device development and commercialization, integrated with biologics/cell therapy development, to enable successful delivery of complex combination products.

This leader will work cross‑functionally with Device Development, Clinical Development, Regulatory Affairs, Quality, and External Manufacturing teams to ensure device solutions are robust, scalable, regulatory‑compliant, and aligned with patient, clinician, and business needs.

Responsibilities

Strategy & Leadership

Define and lead the medical device development strategy aligned with the company’s cell therapy pipeline and long‑term platform vision.

Act as a core leader for combination product development, ensuring strategic alignment across various technical areas.

Serve as the primary technical leader in governance forums.

Act as a thought leader in device‑enabled cell therapy delivery, monitoring emerging technologies, standards, and competitive approaches.

Produce Development Oversight

Lead integration of device options into an overall program strategy

In partnership with functional leadership, oversee device development activities including but not restricted to: user needs, design inputs/outputs, risk management, verification & validation, and design transfer

Ensure device designs are compatible with sterile, GMP, and scalable manufacturing environments while meeting international or region-specific standards.

Program Leadership

Drive integrated development plans and timelines ensuring execution across a matrixed organization

Partner with Regulatory Affairs to define and execute U.S. and global regulatory strategies for combination products (e.g., FDA CDRH/CBER interactions).

Support regulatory submissions including IND‑enabling device sections, IDEs, 510(k), PMA, De Novo, and combination product filings as applicable.

Partner with various stakeholders to ensure devices meet real‑world clinical workflows and adoption requirements

Ensure compliance with ISO 13485, ISO 14971, 21 CFR Part 820, and applicable combination product regulations.

Minimum Requirements

Advanced degree (MS, Ph.D., or equivalent) in Biomedical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Materials Science, or related discipline.
12+ years of progressive experience in medical device development, with senior leadership experience in biotech, medtech, or combination product environments.
Demonstrated success leading complex device programs from concept through commercialization.
Hands‑on experience with combination products, drug‑device or biologic‑device integrations strongly preferred.
Deep knowledge of medical device regulatory frameworks and design control requirements.
Track record of building and leading high‑impact technical teams.
Experience managing external development partners, CDMOs, and device vendors.
Strategic thinker with strong execution discipline
Collaborative, strategic leader who thrives in cross‑functional matrix organizations
Clear communicator with the ability to influence at executive and board levels

jobs.title: Head of Retention & Customer Experience
jobs.description:
Head of Retention & Customer Experience

Own customer retention, reduce churn, and maximise customer lifetime value across two growing DTC pet brands.

Job Overview
We’re looking for an experienced Head of Retention & Customer Experience
to lead the retention strategy and customer experience function for a profitable, fast-growing direct-to-consumer pet brand.
You’ll take full ownership of everything that happens after a customer's first purchase, including subscription management, email and SMS marketing, post-purchase journeys, customer experience, and retention analytics.
Reporting directly to the founder, you’ll lead a Customer Experience Manager and oversee an external retention agency. Your focus will be improving customer lifetime value (LTV), reducing churn, increasing repeat purchases, and building a scalable retention function across two brands.
This is a fully remote, full-time independent contractor position for candidates based outside the United States.

Annual Base Compensation:
US$115,000–US$145,000
Performance Bonus:
15–20% of base salary after the trial period.
About the Company
Our client is a profitable DTC pet brand generating more than US$50 million in annual revenue
through Shopify, Amazon, and Chewy.
The business has built its growth on strong paid acquisition and product performance. A second brand has recently launched, creating an opportunity to expand into a new customer base.
Retention has previously been managed by a lean internal team supported by an external email and SMS agency. This role will establish one senior owner responsible for the entire post-purchase customer journey and retention performance across both brands.
The company is focused on scaling from US$50 million or more toward nine-figure annual revenue.

Key Responsibilities
1. Own the Subscription Programme
Manage the subscription programme through Loop across both brands.
Develop and optimise subscription offers, billing cadence, bundles, and customer portal experiences.
Improve subscription retention, save rates, and customer lifetime value.
Build and optimise cancellation prevention, save, and win-back flows.
Identify opportunities to reduce subscription churn and increase recurring revenue.

2. Lead Email and SMS Retention Strategy
Set the overall email and SMS marketing strategy.
Direct the retention agency's campaign calendar, automated flows, targets, and results.
Ensure agency activities align with retention and revenue objectives.
Review campaign performance and identify opportunities to improve engagement, repeat purchases, and customer value.
Hold the agency accountable for measurable results rather than campaign execution alone.

3. Own the Post-Purchase Customer Journey
Oversee the customer experience from the first purchase through repeat purchases and long-term loyalty.
Identify opportunities to improve the post-purchase journey.
Evaluate and implement loyalty, referral, and VIP programmes where supported by the numbers.
Develop initiatives that strengthen customer relationships and encourage repeat purchases.
Ensure retention initiatives support both customer satisfaction and business profitability.

4. Lead Customer Experience Operations
Manage and develop the Customer Experience Manager.
Establish customer service policies covering refunds, replacements, and exceptions.
Ensure customer experience decisions balance customer satisfaction with business margins.
Provide clear guidelines for handling customer concerns and escalations.
Improve service consistency and operational efficiency across both brands.

5. Build Retention Analytics and Reporting
Develop a reliable retention data and reporting structure.
Track key performance indicators, including:
Cohort retention.
Repeat purchase rate.
Customer lifetime value (LTV) by brand and acquisition channel.
Subscription churn and save rates.
Build weekly retention scorecards to monitor performance.
Use customer and cohort data to identify the biggest opportunities for improvement.
Translate findings into clear priorities and measurable action plans.

6. Lead Retention Reviews and Build Processes
Conduct monthly retention performance reviews with the CEO.
Present results, key trends, challenges, and recommended actions.
Establish standard operating procedures (SOPs) for retention and customer experience operations.
Document strategies, workflows, policies, and performance expectations.
Build a scalable retention function that supports the growth of both brands.

Required Experience & Qualifications
Senior-level experience in DTC retention, lifecycle marketing, or CRM.
Proven experience independently owning a retention function.
Hands-on experience managing subscription programmes and improving churn, save rates, and customer lifetime value.
Experience directing an external email and SMS agency, including strategy, targets, performance reviews, and results.
Strong understanding of post-purchase customer journeys, repeat purchase behaviour, and customer retention.
Experience managing customer experience teams or leading a Customer Experience Manager.
Ability to establish customer service policies covering refunds, replacements, and exceptions while protecting business margins.
Strong analytical skills and experience using cohort data to identify retention opportunities.
Ability to translate performance insights into clear strategies and measurable actions.
Strong leadership, communication, decision-making, and process development skills.
Must be based outside the United States
and available to work full-time contractor hours.

Compensation & Engagement
Annual Base Compensation:
US$115,000–US$145,000, depending on experience.
Performance Bonus:
15–20% of base compensation after the trial period.
Engagement:
Full-time independent contractor.
Payment:
Monthly invoicing.
Location:

jobs.title: SVP, Product
jobs.description:
About Toptal

Toptal is a global network of top talent in business, design, and technology that enables companies to scale their teams, on-demand. With $200+ million in annual revenue and team members based around the globe
, Toptal is the world’s largest fully remote workforce.

We take the best elements of virtual teams and combine them with a support structure that encourages innovation, social interaction, and fun. We see no borders, move at a fast pace, and are never afraid to break the mold.

Position Description:

As SVP, Product, you will shape the vision as to where Toptal’s products and platforms go next and then drive the execution to build them. This is the most senior product role in the company. You will report to the Chief Executive Officer, sit on the executive team, and work collaboratively with our Engineering, Design, Finance, Marketing, New Businesses, Professional Services, and Customer leaders. AI is not a line item on your roadmap. It is the roadmap.

You should be Toptal’s foremost expert on what AI means for products and platforms. That means real depth in fine-tuning and post-training, agent design and evaluation, and the economics of running models in production, along with the judgment to know which applies to us. Work directly with our AI researchers rather than through them. We expect both the AI agenda and the product strategy to originate with you. We will react to your plan rather than hand you ours.

This is a hands-on role. You will write your own specs and pull your own data. When you think an agent could take over a piece of work, you will build a rough version and find out whether it holds up before anyone budgets for it. You will sit in product reviews and say what you actually think. We move fast, and we need Product setting the pace. You will own and set the standards for the hiring bar for the product team, bringing in talent that will advance Toptal to the next level.

Your remit runs across the business: the core platform, the talent and client experiences, the internal systems that run it, the products we take to market, and the data and AI platform underneath them. You will work hand in hand with Engineering on the platform all of it runs on, fold acquisitions and new products into the portfolio, and know growth marketing cold, because how a product reaches the market is part of building it.

Product is yours to shape at blazing speed: scoping, sizing the teams, planning headcount, and defining the role and the bar for every seat. None of that is beneath the role, and we are not interested in someone who thinks these tasks can be done properly by handing them off to HR. Hiring is the highest-leverage work you do, and we want someone who is visibly excited about landing an A player and treats an open seat as urgent. Your own dedication and hard work will set the tone, and the people you bring in should be inspired to do the best work of their careers on this team. We are looking for the person who will define what an AI-native product organization looks like and then run it successfully.

This is a remote position. Resumes and communication must be submitted in English.

Responsibilities:

The following information is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or required skills.

AI and agentic product

Own Toptal’s AI product strategy: where agents and models belong across the marketplace, the talent and client experiences, our internal systems, and the products we take to market, along with the business outcomes they carry.
Decide what we build with AI and what we do not, including build-versus-buy on models and tooling and the packaging and pricing of AI-enabled products.
Make AI quality measurable through evals, acceptance bars, and review loops, and partner with Engineering on the platform as its most demanding customer.
Rebuild how Product works using AI, raising the output and judgment of every product manager through AI-assisted discovery, research, prototyping, and analysis. Product managers have to want this rather than comply with it, and creating that pull is on you.

Portfolio and operating model

Own the vision, strategy, and multi-year roadmap for the whole portfolio: what we build, what we sunset, and how investment is distributed across growth, platform, and operational leverage.
Establish the product operating model and the metrics behind it, so decisions are made on evidence and user research rather than opinion.
Own the product integration of acquisitions and new products, and act as a senior voice of the customer for both talent and clients.

Team and accountability

Decide what a product team should look like now that the roles have blurred, where the product manager believes they can design and code, the engineer believes they can do product and design, and the designer believes they can code and do product.
Own resourcing and workforce planning, and hit time-sensitive hiring commitments.
Review the product work directly, develop people against a clear bar, and raise it as the organization grows.

Qualifications and Job Requirements:

Bachelor’s degree is required, preferably in a technical discipline (Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems). Masters is strongly preferred.
At least 15 years of proven software Product Management experience.
At least 8 years of experience leading Product organizations, including experience leading other product leaders (managing managers).
Proven ability to raise the level of a product organization through the people you hire and develop.
Proven ownership of resourcing and workforce planning, with a hiring track record you can quantify. You have made the hard calls when someone was not clearing the bar.
Experience owning an entire product portfolio at a high-growth technology company, with accountability for business outcomes and not solely delivery.
Demonstrated success setting product strategy at the executive level and translating it into an executable roadmap across multiple teams and domains.
Experience leading AI-enabled products, with a focus on delivering measurable business outcomes.
Deep, hands-on command of modern AI as a product discipline: agentic architectures, harness and orchestration design, retrieval, context engineering, fine-tuning, and evaluation, along with the economics of running models in production. You have shipped these yourself.
Further ahead on AI than the executives around you, able to teach it, and proven at moving an organization to adopt something it was not asking for.
Growth marketing fluency. You understand acquisition, activation, conversion, and retention well enough to build for them.
Experience with marketplace, platform, or two-sided business models is a strong plus.
Prior experience working as a Software Engineer is a strong plus.
Comfortable working with SQL or spreadsheets to analyze data, as well as conducting research with internal and external users.
Ability to creatively craft solutions through data and a user-centric approach.
Be meticulous and have a high bar for quality when writing user stories, brainstorming technical approaches, and testing a feature before it is released.
Be humble, willing to learn, and do whatever is needed to help us accomplish our goals.
Outstanding written and verbal communication skills.
Experience using agile development methodologies with globally distributed teams and the ability to keep up with a fast-paced and global company.
Ability to work in a fast-paced, rapidly growing company and handle a wide variety of challenges, deadlines, and a diverse array of contacts.
You must be a world-class individual contributor to thrive at Toptal, and you will not be here just to tell other people what to do.

Listed on CyberJobs.cc, a job board for cybersecurity jobs from the team behind AITraining.jobs.

Tonic.ai has been de-identifying sensitive data since 2018, and hundreds of enterprises use our products, among them eBay, UnitedHealth Group, Qualcomm, Commonwealth Bank, and Mercor. Our customers hand us some of the most sensitive data they have: production databases, patient and financial records, and increasingly the email, chat, documents and code that AI labs want to train on.

That makes security part of what we sell, not just how we operate. Every deal runs through a security review, every customer asks how their data is protected, and the AI tools our own team uses every day raise new questions faster than most policies can keep up. We're looking for a Head of Security who can own all of it.

Why This Role, Why Now

Our customers are getting bigger and more regulated, and our products now sit in the middle of AI training-data deals where the buyer, the seller and their lawyers all want proof that the data was handled safely. The bar for our own security program is rising with them. What keeps deals moving is a security leader who can pass the audit, answer the questionnaire, get on the call with a customer's CISO, and keep our own house in order at the same time.

That's this job. You'll be Tonic's senior security leader, working directly with our founders, engineering, DevOps, sales and legal. You'll own the program end to end, setting the strategy and doing much of the hands-on work yourself.

What You'll Do

Own our SOC 2 program end to end: scoping, evidence collection, control remediation, and the auditor relationship.
Keep our practices aligned with GDPR, HIPAA, and the security commitments in our customer contracts.
Partner with engineering to build security into the development lifecycle, from design review through release, so products ship securely and on time.
Run vulnerability management across our code, dependencies, and infrastructure, including pen tests and remediation tracking.
Secure and govern our AWS, GCP, and Azure environments (IAM, configuration, logging, hardening), working closely with DevOps and backend engineers.
Act as the customer-facing security expert. Own security questionnaires and RFP responses, and join sales calls when a customer wants to go deep.
Work with legal on contract negotiations and security redlines.
Run corporate security and IT: endpoint management and laptop hardening, EDR monitoring, and incident response.
Own identity and access management and vendor risk management across the company.
Set and maintain policies and guardrails for employee AI use, including LLM platforms, coding assistants, and MCP connectors, covering access controls, data handling, and vendor review of AI providers.
Keep those AI policies current as the landscape moves, so the team can adopt new tools quickly and safely.

What We're Looking For

Several years leading security at a B2B software company, with a record of building programs rather than inheriting them.
SOC 2 audits owned end to end, plus working knowledge of GDPR and HIPAA.
Hands-on experience securing AWS, GCP, and Azure. You can read an IAM policy, spot a misconfiguration, and fix it with the engineer who owns it.
Experience embedding security in the development lifecycle and running vulnerability management without becoming the team that slows everything down.
Comfort in front of customers. You can answer a 300-question security questionnaire, hold your own on a call with a customer's CISO, and work through redlines with legal.
Experience running corporate security and IT: endpoint management, EDR, incident response, IAM, and vendor risk.
AI-native workflow. You use AI tools yourself, understand where they create real risk, and can write guardrails that people actually follow.
Self-direction. You'll be the security leader, and you'll need to make sound, risk-based calls without waiting for someone to tell you what to do.
Clear communication with very different audiences, from an engineer debugging a finding to an executive weighing a tradeoff.

Nice to Haves

Experience at a data infrastructure, privacy, or AI company.
Experience selling into regulated industries such as healthcare and financial services.
Experience with ISO 27001, HITRUST, or FedRAMP.
Experience securing software that customers deploy in their own environments, alongside SaaS.
Experience at an early-stage or fast-growing company.

What Success Looks Like

In your first month, you'll learn our products, infrastructure, and current controls, take over the security questionnaire queue, and build a clear picture of our biggest risks. By the end of your first quarter, you'll own the SOC 2 program and auditor relationship, have a prioritized roadmap across product, cloud, and corporate security, and have AI-use policies in place that the team actually follows. After that, you'll help shape how security grows at Tonic, including whether and when we hire next.

Why Join

You'll own security at a company where security is part of the product, not a back-office function.
You'll work directly with our founders, with a real say in how the company handles risk and makes commitments to customers.
You'll get close to the AI training-data market and help set the bar for how sensitive data should be handled in it.
You'll shape AI governance in real time, at a company whose own business is making data safe for AI.
Competitive compensation and equity.

401k plan with employer contribution

Remote-friendly work environment
