APPLICATION DEADLINE

November 13, 2026, for Best Consideration

POSITION

Staff Regular

SALARY RANGE

$235,000-$275,000

The Clarice Overview

The Clarice Smith Performing Arts Center (The Clarice) at the University of Maryland (UMD) is part of the College of Arts and Humanities (ARHU) and is the academic and artistic home of the School of Music (SOM); the School of Theatre, Dance, and Performance Studies (TDPS); the Michelle Smith Performing Arts Library (MSPAL); and The Clarice’s own artistic platform Clarice Presents (CP). At the time of its construction, the 318,000-square-foot facility on 17 acres of land was the largest construction project undertaken by the State of Maryland, and remains one of the most complex projects in recent Maryland state history.

The Clarice opened in 2001 and is named in honor of visual artist and philanthropist Clarice Smith (1933-2021). From its founding, The Clarice was conceived as a “creative village” that brought a robust series of outside artists and performers to campus, supported the academic and performance programs of SOM and TDPS and collaborations with MSPAL, and built bridges between UMD and its surrounding community. The Clarice, through its dynamic outreach programs, manifested UMD’s commitment to meaningfully contribute to those communities through the arts and the encouragement of cultural citizenship. The Clarice continues to strengthen its role as the central home for performing arts at UMD, supporting the academic and performance needs of SOM and TDPS, ensuring the excellence and social relevance of all of its programs, and enhancing its leadership position in the field despite the political and financial headwinds for the arts in this country.

The Clarice hosts more than 1,000 public performances and events each year, the majority featuring the artistry of SOM and TDPS students and faculty. The Clarice’s artistic platform, Clarice Presents (CP), offers uniquely integrated performances, digital, civic and community engagement programming. MSPAL, often in partnership with CP and M‐NCPPC, also presents events at The Clarice. All presentations and events are supported by the administrative, production management, and technical staff of The Clarice.

Professional staff across artistic planning, operations, and finance report to the Executive Director, who works in close collaboration with College senior leadership, academic partners, and marketing, communication, and development staff.

Position Summary/Purpose

Reporting directly to the Dean of the College of Arts and Humanities, the Executive Director is ultimately responsible for the management of The Clarice’s staff, operations, facilities, budget, and fundraising. In these roles, the position balances educational, public, and financial priorities to ensure that operations and programming simultaneously enhance The Clarice’s stature as a national leader among performing arts presenters and contribute meaningfully to the resident academic units’ missions; reflect the values of collaboration, belonging, and community; and align with the goals of the college and institution. In collaboration with the Directors of the resident academic units, the position is responsible for the Clarice’s artistic programming and works to ensure that this programming and other initiatives respond to curricular needs. The Executive Director works alongside Directors of the School of Music; the School of Theatre, Dance, and Performance Studies; and the Michelle Smith Performing Arts Library, as well as the Executive Director of Arts for All to develop and refine a strategic and innovative vision that enhances the curricular experience for faculty and students, engages the campus, connects with the community, and further enhances the reputation of the University of Maryland. The Executive Director should bring significant knowledge of the changing performing arts landscape and a fierce dedication to collaborative leadership models. The Executive Director meets monthly with the Dean and annually with the Provost and Dean to ensure that the performing arts have a campus and community-wide agenda and impact. For more detailed information about The Clarice please visit this website.

jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Director, Client Support and Enablement based in Canada.

As Director, Client Support and Enablement, you will lead the strategy, development, and execution of customer support and enablement operations for enterprise clients within a growing SaaS environment. You will oversee service reliability, platform adoption, and the overall customer experience, ensuring clients receive timely, effective support throughout their journey. Combining strategic leadership with operational execution, you will build and scale a high-performing team, establish service standards, and implement processes that support sustainable growth. Working closely with Account Management, Product, Engineering, Launch, and Ad Operations, you will drive seamless collaboration and continuous platform improvement. You will also leverage analytics, automation, and AI-powered tools to improve efficiency, anticipate customer needs, and strengthen service delivery. This is an opportunity to shape a critical customer-facing function within an innovative technology business serving leading enterprise retail media partners.

Accountabilities

Customer Support Strategy: Define and lead the overall Customer Support and Enablement (CSE) strategy, including the team's mission, service catalog, operating model, responsibilities, and collaboration frameworks with Account Management, Launch, and Ad Operations.
Team Leadership and Development: Recruit, build, and manage a high-performing support and enablement team. Establish clear responsibilities, support career development, manage performance, and foster a culture of accountability and continuous learning.
Scalable Support Operations: Implement a pooled support model with a centralized service queue and cross-training practices to ensure consistent account coverage, even during employee absences or team transitions.
Workforce Planning: Develop multi-year staffing, resource allocation, coverage, and technology plans to support business expansion across new retail partners and geographic regions while maintaining service quality.
Service Level Management: Establish, monitor, and report on service-level agreements (SLAs), resolution times, ticket backlogs, and quality standards. Own ticket prioritization, escalation procedures, operational runbooks, and service performance across all accounts.
Incident and Escalation Management: Lead communications during critical Sev-0 and Sev-1 incidents, ensuring timely updates to enterprise clients and internal stakeholders. Oversee root-cause analyses (RCAs) and ensure findings and corrective actions are documented and shared.
Operational Coverage: Collaborate with Ad Operations to establish clear support coverage models for urgent requests and after-hours incidents.
Client Training and Enablement: Lead customer education initiatives, including platform demonstrations, training sessions, FAQs, product guides, and communications about platform updates and new features.
Help Center Management: Own the Help Center and its development using tools such as Freshdesk, including knowledge base architecture, documentation, article creation, and publishing strategies designed to improve self-service and reduce support ticket volume.
Platform Adoption: Monitor feature adoption and platform engagement after launch, identify low-usage patterns, and collaborate with Account Management and Product teams to improve adoption and customer outcomes.
Performance Reporting: Oversee weekly campaign pacing and advertiser reporting, as well as monthly ticket-trend analysis. Translate operational data into actionable insights for leadership and enterprise clients.
Client Onboarding and Transition: Partner with Launch and Account Management teams to ensure new retail partners experience smooth implementations and effective transitions from launch into ongoing support.
Technology and Tooling Ownership: Own the support technology ecosystem, including Freshdesk, Jira, and related platforms. Guide tooling decisions, integrations, and data flows to ensure efficient operations.
Product Feedback and Feature Requests: Manage feature-request intake, identify recurring customer issues, and translate ticket trends into prioritized recommendations for Product and Engineering.
Product Readiness: Collaborate with Product teams on supportability reviews to ensure new features are properly documented, supported, and ready for customers before release.
AI and Automation: Identify and implement AI-powered tools and automation opportunities to increase team capacity, streamline workflows, improve reporting, and enhance client communications without compromising service quality.
Strategic Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work alongside leaders in Account Management, Launch, and Ad Operations to drive shared outcomes, including account health, customer retention, renewals, and launch quality.
Executive Client Engagement: Bring support performance and platform adoption insights into quarterly business reviews (QBRs) and executive-level discussions with major retail partners.

Requirements

At least 10 years of experience in customer support, customer success, technical account management, or platform operations within a SaaS or advertising technology environment.
At least 3 years of people management experience, including team recruitment, performance management, coaching, and career development.
Proven track record of building, scaling, or managing a customer support function, including defining its operating model, service standards, SLAs, escalation paths, runbooks, and reporting frameworks.
Hands-on experience managing customer support technology platforms such as Freshdesk, Zendesk, or similar solutions, alongside Jira or comparable project management tools.
Demonstrated ability to make strategic technology and tooling decisions that improve support efficiency and operational performance.
Experience leading major incident communications and conducting root-cause analyses (RCAs) for enterprise customers.
Strong analytical capabilities, with the ability to interpret ticket volumes, service-level performance, resolution times, and platform adoption metrics to guide operational decisions.
Experience implementing and managing pooled support models, centralized ticketing systems, or follow-the-sun support operations.
Proven experience developing customer education programs, training initiatives, knowledge bases, or Help Centers.
Familiarity with AI-powered tools and automation solutions, particularly for improving team productivity, reporting, operational workflows, and customer communications.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and confidently with senior executives, enterprise clients, and internal stakeholders.
Strong leadership and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build collaborative relationships and influence cross-functional teams.
Exceptional organizational and problem-solving abilities, with a proactive approach to identifying recurring issues and implementing long-term solutions.
Ability to balance strategic planning with hands-on operational management in a fast-paced, evolving business environment.
Strong customer-centric mindset, with a commitment to service excellence, platform adoption, and long-term client satisfaction.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in retail media, commerce media, or programmatic advertising environments.
Familiarity with advertising platforms and ecosystems such as Meta, Google, Criteo, and Display & Video 360 (DV360).
Experience supporting enterprise retail media networks or complex advertising technology platforms.
Understanding of campaign operations, advertiser reporting, and retail media performance metrics.

Benefits

Job Summary

The Director, Large Reactor Deployment reports to the Vice President, Nuclear Development Division and provides strategic leadership and direction for assessing and advancing large nuclear generation opportunities. As a member of SaskPower's Senior Management team, this role plans, organizes, directs and controls large nuclear development activities to advance project readiness and align departmental work with SaskPower's strategic goals and objectives.

The position leads an integrated development program spanning commercial negotiations, site assessment, engineering studies, regulatory planning, Indigenous and public engagement, policy and planning. As the initiative progresses, the role will also oversee scheduling, construction planning, project management, vendor relationships and project controls.

The Person

The Director, Large Reactor Deployment is a strategic and results-oriented leader with extensive experience advancing or delivering large-scale industrial or energy projects. They can integrate technical, regulatory, commercial, public policy, engagement and organizational considerations into clear priorities and credible recommendations.

The ideal candidate builds trusted relationships across SaskPower and with external partners, communicates effectively with senior decision-makers and affected parties, and remains effective in a complex and continually changing environment. They demonstrate sound judgement and accountability when managing significant budgets, confidential matters, competing interests and organizational outcomes. They lead long-term planning and decision-making, anticipating future needs, risks and impacts across the organization and the public

Key Accountabilities

Provide strategic leadership and direction for large nuclear development, including technology evaluation, site assessment, engineering studies, regulatory readiness, and project readiness.

Establish the development strategy and roadmap, and lead integrated planning for scope, budgets, schedules, resources, risks and interdependencies.

Allocate human, financial and material resources and establish appropriate financial, administrative and project controls.

Lead site assessment activities and integrate regulatory, Indigenous rights and engagement, public engagement, engineering and commercial considerations into project development.

Oversee development-stage contracts, vendor relationships and major advisory arrangements, and establish effective partnerships with nuclear operators, technology vendors, contractors, utilities and government.

Develop recommendations on reactor technology, site and investment options, considering technical, regulatory, commercial, affordability and engagement requirements.

Coordinate contributions from Engineering, Regulatory Affairs, Procurement, Indigenous Relations, engagement teams and other internal partners.

Provide the Vice President, Executive, Board of Directors and government committees with recommendations and presentations regarding project strategy, budgets, schedules, risks and investment considerations.

Lead negotiations and collaboration with private-sector, utility and government partners within approved authorities and direction.

Anticipate, resolve and prevent departmental and project issues using sound judgement, practical solutions and appropriate escalation.

Lead managers, employees, embedded contractors and consultants; establish clear accountabilities and support employee engagement, performance and succession planning.

Foster a strong nuclear safety culture grounded in a questioning attitude, accountability, teamwork and sound decision-making.

Other related duties as assigned.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

Degree in Engineering, Business Administration, Social Sciences, Humanities or another related discipline.

Related professional designation(s) and/or certification(s) would be considered an asset.

Ten (10) years of extensive experience leading the development, planning or delivery of large-scale industrial or energy projects, with demonstrated expertise in multidisciplinary leadership, project governance, scheduling and risk management.

Knowledge of large nuclear reactor development, including technology assessment, site evaluation, engineering interfaces, lifecycle requirements and the transition from feasibility studies to investment and execution readiness.

Understanding of the Canadian nuclear regulatory framework and applicable assessment and licensing processes.

Understanding of electricity supply planning, transmission and grid integration considerations associated with large generating units.

Knowledge of major-project development and delivery models, including governance, scheduling, risk management, commercial relationships and contracting.

Ability to establish and maintain effective relationships with nuclear operators, technology vendors, contractors, utilities, government, Indigenous Relations and other internal and external parties.

Ability to provide strategic direction, integrate multidisciplinary work and lead effectively through uncertainty and change.

Excellent negotiation, facilitation, communication, presentation and decision-making skills.

Ability to manage complex and highly confidential matters with sensitivity and professionalism.

Ability to lead and develop managers, employees, contractors and consultants while establishing accountability for safe, timely and cost-effective execution.

Demonstrated skill in SaskPower's competencies.

Lead the Global People Operations function and team
Work with the Exec Team to set the strategy and operating standards for People Operations across North America and India, and build a function that scales with the business.
Manage, coach, and develop a distributed team of three across multiple time zones and regions. Own hiring, leveling, and succession within People Operations, and raise the bar on how the team delivers in both regions.
Own service delivery across North America and India
Be accountable for People Ops service delivery across regions (HRIS and people systems, onboarding and offboarding, and the full employee lifecycle), with your team running day-to-day execution.
Set consistent, documented processes that work the same way in all regions, and keep policy, documentation, and records accurate and accessible.

Partner with legal, payroll, and external consultants in each region, own relationships with statutory bodies and auditors, and oversee POSH Internal Committee responsibilities.

Partner with leadership on org and talent strategy
Act as a strategic people partner to senior and functional leadership, advising on org design, workforce planning, and talent strategy at a company level.
Guide leadership effectiveness and organizational health, and support reorgs and scale-ups as a change partner.
Bring people data and analytics (attrition, engagement, span/layer, representation) to leadership as insight-led recommendations, not just administrative support.
Own compensation, performance, and people programs
Own the design and governance of compensation across regions, including annual reviews, equity refresh cycles, and market benchmarking (including India-market benchmarking against local tech and GCC employers).
Own the frameworks for performance, leveling, and engagement, and set the cadence the team runs them on.
Shape and localize global people programs, including engagement surveys, career frameworks, recognition, and total rewards.

The North America and India people teams operate as one function, with consistent, documented processes across regions.
Statutory compliance run clean in both regions, with zero major findings.
Senior leaders view you as a trusted partner, not only as a transactional HR contact.
Clear, consistent frameworks for leveling, performance, and compensation are in place across regions.
Engagement and attrition metrics improve year-over-year.

12–15+ years of progressive HR / People Operations experience in multi-country, high-growth tech environments.

This role directly owns Walmart US, Kroger, Publix, HEB, Trader Joe’s and Harris Teeter, leads the e-commerce channel including Amazon, and supports the Costco business in partnership with the VP of Strategic Accounts, with the long-term goal of owning the Club channel.

2. E-Commerce

Partner with Brand and Commercial Strategy & Insights on retail media and digital programs at strategic accounts.
Identify and evaluate new e-commerce and direct-to-consumer opportunities.

3. Costco Support & Club Channel

Work alongside the Sales & Marketing Admin Assistant on Costco admin, reporting and day-to-day account execution.
Build Club channel knowledge, buyer relationships and program expertise in preparation for taking full ownership of the Club channel.
Long term, own the Club channel, including strategy, annual plans, item and program management, and growth targets.

4. New Business Development

Build and manage the new customer and channel pipeline, with priority targets set in partnership with the SVP of Commercial.
Lead new customer pitches, new item presentations and listing negotiations from first meeting through to first order.
Evaluate new channel opportunities for strategic fit, profitability and supply capacity before committing resources.
Set new business priorities and commercial terms within the approved trade budget.
Track pipeline progress and conversion, and report new customer sales against plan.

5. Account Coverage & Operations

Shape and evolve the coverage model for assigned accounts, building direct customer relationships and internal capability over time.
Own the operating model for retailer portals, promotional planning, deductions and paperwork alongside the Sales Analyst.

Strategic account and e-commerce sales vs. FY27 AOP.

Trade ROI and forecast accuracy (sales input) for assigned accounts.

Proven record of winning new customers and listings, and of building joint business plans with national retailers.

Experience in the Club channel, ideally Costco, and in building direct customer coverage and internal account management capability.
Strong command of trade management, promotional analytics, retailer portals and syndicated data (Circana / NielsenIQ).

Matrix360 is a social impact business helping to build the commercial real estate and development (CRED) industry – an industry responsible for creating and building our cities and communities.

At Matrix360, we are the champions of diversity and equity in the CRED industry.

We firmly believe in providing equal access and opportunities to all individuals, ensuring accommodation and inclusion in every aspect of employment, services, programs, and activities.

If you require accommodation or this information in an alternative format at any stage of the search process, contact us at info@matrix360.ca or 416 703 3400.

About Our Client

Raising the Roof (RTR) is a nationally registered charity with the primary goal of delivering long term solutions to homelessness in Canada. Previously to 2020 the organization was known for their toque campaign as well as contributions to homelessness awareness and research. In response to the magnitude of today’s homelessness crisis, RTR has pivoted to focus primarily on homelessness prevention through the development and operation of affordable rental housing. Their portfolio has grown significantly since this work began in 2020 with 70 units in operation by the end of 2024 and over 400 units currently under development.

Most of the units in operation are located in the GTA. Other communities within which RTR has active development sites or operating units include Orillia, Barrie, Sudbury, Winnipeg and St. John’s. The goal is to one day develop and operate housing across all provinces and territories in Canada.

They operate a mix of market and affordable units across a range of different profiles with corresponding tenant acuity, affordability and levels of support. In each community we serve, RTR forms a partnership with at least one housing provider partner – typically a non-profit group that will refer tenants, provide support services and (sometimes) provide property management services. RTR has some head lease arrangement but predominantly holds leases directly with tenants and hires contractors accordingly to manage the needs of the tenants and real estate operations.

For more information about our client, please connect with us.

Senior Director, Finance

On behalf of our Client, a growing not-for-profit housing platform and national charity, we are seeking a Senior Director, Finance to provide strategic financial leadership and operational oversight for the organization as they expand their national affordable housing development and operating portfolio.

In this newly created role, you would build out and lead the finance function while working closely with the Director of Housing Development & Operations, and the Director of Strategic Initiatives & Partnerships to support the planning, financing, and delivery of housing projects across Canada.

The successful candidate will be a highly motivated team player, with the ability to work in a dynamic and fast-paced environment. They will be able to work collaboratively with multiple internal/external teams. The ideal candidate will be someone who enjoys putting structure in place while staying hands-on and close to the day-to-day.

Base salary for this position is $120k - $150k based on level of industry experience and exposure, plus a fully remote working style, comprehensive benefits and vacation. Our client is an advocate for equity and diversity and recognizes the importance of leadership engagement within its framework.

Responsibilities

1. Strategic Financial Leadership

Serve as a key strategic advisor to the Executive Director and Board of Directors on financial sustainability, capital strategy, and organizational growth.
Develop long-term financial strategies aligned with the company's mission to prevent homelessness through housing development.
Support multi-year financial modelling for the organization’s housing pipeline and operating portfolio.
Provide financial leadership support in evaluating new development opportunities, acquisitions, and strategic partnerships.

2. Housing Development Finance and Capital Structuring

Work with the Director of Housing Development & Operations to ensure financial feasibility and sustainability of development projects.
Supports the structuring of affordable housing development projects across multiple provinces.
Supports the creation of development pro-formas, project budgets, and operating projections.
Supports the structuring and management of complex capital stacks, including:

3. Housing Portfolio Financial Management and Operations

Leads financial management of the organization’s housing asset portfolio, including operating budgets, reserves, and long-term financial sustainability.
Oversees portfolio-level financial reporting and performance metrics.
Ensure appropriate financial planning for capital repairs, lifecycle costs, and reserve funds.
Work closely with the Director of Housing Development & Operations to ensure effective financial transition from development to operations.
Leads in the areas of managing project risk, finalizing construction budgets, contingency management, and development partner oversight.

4. Social Finance and Innovative Capital

Lead strategies for utilizing social finance tools to support housing development and portfolio growth.
Work collaboratively with the senior leadership to identify new capital partnerships, explore innovative financing mechanisms, develop opportunities for impact investment.
Oversee the development of financing structures such as community or social bonds, impact investment vehicles, loan guarantees and credit enhancement, program-related investments from foundations.

5. Financial Management and Organizational Operations

Oversee all financial operations including accounting, reporting, budgeting, investment strategy, and cash flow management.
Lead annual budgeting and multi-year financial planning processes.
Leads in the areas of treasury management, construction draw management, debt covenant monitoring, interest rate risk management.
Ensure accurate financial reporting across programs, housing developments, and partnerships.
Strengthen financial systems to support a growing national housing developer.

6. Human Resources Policy Compliance and Organizational Administration

Ensure compliance with employment legislation, workplace regulations, and organizational HR policies.
Oversee implementation and monitoring of HR policies including compensation frameworks, benefits administration, and workplace practices.
Support the Executive Director and leadership team in maintaining strong HR governance and organizational risk management.
Work with senior leadership to support workforce planning as the housing development pipeline and portfolio expand.

7. Governance, Compliance and Risk Management

Ensure compliance with charitable regulations, funding agreements, lender requirements, and financial reporting standards.
Lead annual audits and relationships with external auditors.
Maintain strong internal controls and financial governance practices.
Support the Board Finance and Audit Committee with clear financial reporting and risk oversight.
Contribute to enterprise risk management related to development, operations, finance, and HR.

8. Collaborative Leadership

Guide the strategic growth of Raising the Roof’s housing development portfolio.
Align financial, operational, and partnership strategies to support project delivery.
Coordinate capital planning, development pipelines, and partnership development.
Support organizational growth while balancing impact, financial sustainability, and risk management.

Qualifications

CPA designation required (CPA, CA, CMA, or CGA)
5+ years of progressive financial leadership experience.
Strong knowledge of ASPE accounting and charitable reporting standards
Senior financial leadership experience in affordable housing, real estate development, non-profit housing, or social infrastructure sectors considered an asset.
Demonstrated experience structuring financing for housing or real estate development projects.
Experience managing housing operations or real estate portfolios.
Experience working with social finance instruments and blended capital models.

jobs.description:
Guru Studio is a creative\-driven entertainment company and an industry leader in animated storytelling. For over twenty years, our studio has brought to life some of the most recognizable and beloved children’s properties in the world.

  

We’re always looking for passionate and committed talent, so come join our dynamic and growing team!

  

Guru is proud to offer our team members meaningful learning and developmental opportunities! You will work alongside a wide range of talent in a positive and supportive environment where we want to see success in each individual.

  

We're looking for a talented and experienced **Director of IT** \- come join our team!

  

The Director of IT will supervise and manage the IT department’s daily and long\-term operations to allow for growth in a fast paced and rapidly expanding internationally renowned animation studio. This role is a management position for a very sophisticated tech\-based company and requires clear and effective leadership and visionary thinking. This role reports to the VP of Technology.  



  

**Duties and Responsibilities include but will not be limited to:**

 **Management \+ Supervision**


* Manage a department of IT professionals in their day to day operational functions and all of their responsibilities including server, desktop, and communications infrastructure, ensuring a reasonable level of in\-studio IT support is available during regular business hours.
* Set goals and milestones for all IT staff. Review their performance and report to the VP of Technology.
* Liaise with all heads of production and business operations to ensure IT department’s efforts are coordinated to meet everyone’s needs (get information on studio upcoming projects, determine production resources needs, communication and delivery requirements and issue and follow up on all appropriate tasks).

  

  

**Facility Infrastructure Planning**


* Ensure all physical services (leased space, electrical, HVAC, floor load etc) at the studio and in the data centre are able to support IT equipment and services and that the equipment is compatible and fully integrated with physical services.
* Manage all budget needs for the IT department: create, present and revise purchase orders, follow up on approvals, ensure purchasing documentation is digitized, recorded and stored in a central repository, maintain IT inventory lists.
* Budget for, acquire and maintain appropriate licenses for all software needed for production and business operations.
* Maintain studio growth plan with the President, the VP of Technology and VP of Finance and Business Affairs.
* Gather and organize purchasing research with guidance from relevant IT personnel.
* Prepare projected equipment cost information for studio project bidding purposes.
* Implement, manage and supervise IT desktop ticketing systems.
* Schedule IT all operations including: personnel, technical maintenance, internal meetings and finance and budget related deadlines.
* Ensure regular maintenance and upgrades are done to all IT infrastructure to ensure a secure and well\-functioning IT environment.
* Work with studio stakeholders to implement any studio expansion or move.

  


**Knowledgebase**


* Maintain IT documentation/wiki (oversee, coordinate and arrange information input and creation of diagrams, organize the structure of documentation/wiki, propose new sections).
* Create and Maintain IT procedures and policies (coordinate with the input from the VP of Technology).
* Guru methodology asks for employees who will go above and beyond; in staying informed on upcoming technologies, most cost\-effective vendors and taking the initiative in implementing forward thinking planning within each department.
  


**Qualifications**


* Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).
* 5\+ years of progressive experience in IT infrastructure and operations, including 1–2\+ years in a senior management or director\-level role.
* Previous experience working in an animation, VFX, gaming, or post\-production environment is considered a strong asset.
* Deep expertise in enterprise server architecture, high\-speed networking, SAN/NAS storage, render farms, cloud/hybrid workflows, and multi\-OS environments (Linux, Windows, macOS).
* Strong familiarity with 2D/3D creative software pipelines (e.g., Maya, Houdini, Nuke, Harmony, Adobe Creative Cloud) and managing enterprise software licensing.
* Hands\-on experience overseeing physical data center requirements (electrical, HVAC, floor load) and leading studio office expansions or relocations.
* Proven track record managing IT helpdesk ticketing systems, asset inventories, preventative maintenance schedules, and studio security/IP protection standards (such as TPN compliance).
* Extensive experience negotiating vendor contracts, managing purchase orders, and forecasting equipment costs for project bidding.

Executive Director

Description

The Homelessness Society of the Bow Valley (HSBV) is a community-based charity with a mission to foster a Bow Valley community where everyone has access to safe, warm shelter and programs that support their needs.

HSBV provides a low barrier shelter and programs with the goal to build trust and facilitate individuals' access to the local system of care. We are seeking an Executive Director to join our team and help lead the organization’s continued growth and local impact.

Summary

The Executive Director for the Homelessness Society of the Bow Valley is responsible for the successful leadership and overall management of the organization in accordance with the strategic direction, and policies set by the Board of Directors. This position reports to the Board of Directors and will oversee and participate in program operations, public relations, and financial management.

The Executive Director is responsible for ensuring that the organization is operated in compliance with the Government of Canada Charities Directorate, Government of Alberta Societies Act, Municipal Regulatory Bodies, Public Health Department, the Occupational Health and Safety Act, the Employment Standards Act and other mandated legislative requirements. The Executive Director must present the organization in a professional and respectful manner, and model organizational values for all team members.

Responsibilities

Organizational Leadership & Strategy

Clearly articulate and uphold the vision, mission, values, and strategic direction of the organization.
Ensure that the Board’s directives, policies, strategic plan, and organizational vision are effectively operationalized across all levels.
Support the Board in the development and execution of the strategic plan, organizational policies, and long-term planning.
Lead system mapping and identification of wise practices to inform strategic direction and internal improvements.
Support the Board in planning and executing the Annual General Meeting (AGM) and other meetings as required.

Board Relations & Governance

Act as a key liaison between the Board and staff, fostering strong, transparent communication.
Support Board operations and ongoing Board development and engagement.
Provide insight and recommendations to the Board for organizational growth, risk management, and sector trends.
Support convening of Board members and Board onboarding and offboarding processes.

Operations & Compliance

Oversee day-to-day operations, ensuring they align with organizational goals and values.
Maintain an open, collaborative, and mission-focused management approach.
Ensure compliance with all relevant legislation and regulations, including but not limited to Occupational Health and Safety, Canada Revenue Agency’s Charities Directorate, and Alberta Corporate Registry.
Identify and implement technologies and systems to streamline operations and maximize impact.

Financial Management & Administration

Oversee organizational finances and bookkeeping to ensure strong financial health and transparency.
Support the streamlining of financial management systems and processes
Collaborate with bookkeepers, accountants, and auditors to support preparation and completion of annual audits.
Oversee administrative systems, including file organization, digital and physical record storage, and general office management.

People & Culture

Oversee and support the Program Manager, including participation in hiring and staff performance reviews.
Provide leadership in all human resources functions, including recruitment, onboarding, training, and performance management.
Ensure all HR practices reflect a commitment to equal opportunity, accessibility, and inclusion.
Foster a team culture rooted in equity, diversity, inclusion, and psychological safety.
Promote staff wellbeing and encourage ongoing professional development.

Programs & Impact

Collaborate with team members to guide program design, including defining goals, eligibility, referral pathways, and performance metrics.
Conduct and disseminate annual program reports using the established evaluation and measurement framework.
Suggest and implement strategies for program enhancement based on research and community engagement.
Build and maintain meaningful relationships with community partners, shelters, and change makers in the homeless-serving sector.

Fund Development & External Relations

Oversee fundraising strategies and lead donor engagement, cultivation, and stewardship efforts.
Support identifying and securing long-term, stable funding sources.
Support the planning and execution of fundraising and community engagement events.
Develop and maintain strong relationships with key external stakeholders, including funders, government partners, community organizations, and media.
Represent the organization publicly, advocating for its mission, programs, and impact.

Requirements

Over 5 years of experience in the non-profit sector as well as the human services or related field, preferably in leadership and management.
Experience working with a Board of Directors.
A recent police criminal reference check and vulnerable sector search.
Must be able to work flexible hours.
Demonstrated leadership skills with the ability to lead compassionately with empathy, and purpose.

Confident, personable and approachable.

Collaborative leadership style.

We’re seeking a leader who puts people first, with a proven background in dental operations and an understanding of the daily realities of running successful clinics, developing strong Clinic Managers and driving business performance.

You’ll bring together leadership, business insight and practical operational support to make a meaningful impact across your region—creating exceptional experiences for patients and team members while supporting sustainable growth.

The Opportunity

Anytime Dental clinics are designed around accessibility and convenience, with extended hours, seven-day operations and same-day care that make it easier for patients to access the dentistry they need.

As Regional Director, you’ll work closely with Clinic Managers, Doctors and Support Office partners to strengthen leadership, improve performance and identify opportunities across your portfolio of clinics.

Success in this role means being present in your clinics, understanding their businesses and developing leaders who can turn opportunities into action. Regular travel between clinics throughout the Toronto and East Region, including Scarborough and Barrie, is an essential part of this role.

What Great Looks Like

You understand that strong regional performance starts with strong local leadership. You invest time in your Clinic Managers, coach them through challenges, build their confidence and hold them accountable for the results they own. You know when to step in, when to ask the right questions and when to empower your leaders to find the answer themselves.

You’re equally comfortable with the business side of dental operations. In this role, you will:

Develop strong leaders: Coach Clinic Managers to lead their teams, understand their businesses and take ownership of performance. Build succession plans and develop future leaders.
Turn insights into action: Review financial and operational results, identify trends and gaps, and translate KPIs into clear priorities and practical action plans.
Drive clinic performance: Support improvements in production, collections, scheduling, treatment acceptance, hygiene optimization, patient retention and profitability.
Deliver sustainable growth: Partner with clinic leaders to achieve budgets, annual plans and growth objectives while maintaining a strong patient experience.
Build engaged teams: Create a culture of accountability, collaboration and trust where people feel supported and understand what success looks like.
Partner with Doctors: Build trusted relationships with Doctors and clinical teams to align operational support with clinic needs and patient care.
Lead change: Help teams successfully adopt new programs, processes and ways of working, collaborating with Support Office partners to remove barriers and maintain momentum.

You look beyond the numbers to understand what drives a clinic’s results—and coach your leaders to recognize opportunities, address challenges and know where to focus next.

What You Bring

Required: Previous operational leadership experience within the dental industry, including direct responsibility for dental clinic operations, team leadership and business performance.
At least five years of progressive dental leadership experience, including experience overseeing multiple clinics or locations.
A strong understanding of dental clinic workflows and performance drivers, including scheduling, production, collections, treatment acceptance, hygiene optimization and patient retention.
A demonstrated track record of coaching Clinic Managers, developing leaders and building strong, engaged teams.
Strong business and financial acumen, with experience using KPIs, budgets and operational reporting to guide decisions and improve results.
The ability to identify business opportunities, prioritize effectively and translate plans into measurable results.
Exceptional communication, relationship-building and problem-solving skills, with confidence partnering with Doctors, Clinic Managers and Support Office teams.
The ability to balance strategic thinking with practical operational support in a fast-paced, evolving environment.
Availability and flexibility to travel regularly between clinics throughout the Toronto and East Region, including Vaughan, Scarborough and Barrie.

Above all, you enjoy developing leaders. You measure your success by the strength of the leaders and teams you build around you and the results they achieve.

Anytime Dental is redefining access to dental care through modern clinics, comprehensive dentistry, extended hours, weekend availability and same-day care. Our network includes established clinics, newly built locations and clinics experiencing significant growth, creating opportunities to shape teams, develop leaders and support businesses at different stages of their journey.

Anytime Dental is part of Passion Dental Group, a growing dental organization committed to creating exceptional experiences for both patients and team members. Our clinics and leaders are supported by dedicated teams across Operations, People & Culture, Marketing, Accounting & Finance, Learning and Clinical Development, creating strong partnerships between our clinics and Support Office.

We’re also proud to be Great Place to Work Certified

Ready to bring your dental operations experience to a role where you can develop leaders and make an impact across the Toronto and East Region? Apply today and help build the next chapter of Anytime Dental.

 About 1Password 
 At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work. 

 If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future. 

 As Senior Director, Corporate Counsel, you’ll oversee 1Password’s Corporate Legal function and provide strategic legal guidance across a broad range of matters. Reporting to the VP, Legal & General Counsel, you’ll play a key role in supporting 1Password’s growth, M&A activity, international expansion, financing activities and corporate and subsidiary governance. This role also oversees compliance, equity, litigation, intellectual property and marketing matters.

 You’ll partner closely with leaders across Finance, Marketing, People, Corporate Development and other business functions. This role requires a pragmatic, business-minded lawyer who can operate effectively in a fast-paced environment, manage complex projects, and provide clear advice on matters involving multiple stakeholders and jurisdictions.

 This is a remote opportunity within the United States and Canada.

 How we’re using AI today 
 On the Legal team, AI helps us move faster without sacrificing quality. We use it to draft and review commercial agreements, implement negotiation playbooks, and prepare the groundwork for legal review. AI also helps us stay on top of regulatory developments, synthesize research across jurisdictions, and identify risks in novel situations like new product launches or partnership structures. The result is a team that can operate at higher volume with greater consistency, while creating more time for the judgment calls, collaboration, and meaningful decisions that matter most.

 What we're looking for: 
 Juris Doctor with active bar membership in Canada or the United States and at least 10 years of relevant experience, including time at a nationally recognized law firm and ideally a mix of late-stage private and public company work. Experience in technology or SaaS is preferred.

 Experience leading or supporting mergers and acquisitions, including due diligence, negotiations, transaction documentation, and post-closing integration.

 Strong knowledge of corporate governance, securities laws, entity management and experience preparing for or managing public company compliance.

 Experience advising on international expansion, including subsidiary formation and regulatory requirements across multiple jurisdictions.

 Experience supporting financing transactions and related securities law compliance.

 Ability to identify legal and business risks, develop practical mitigation strategies, and communicate recommendations clearly to senior stakeholders.

 Experience managing external counsel and coordinating cross-functional teams on complex legal matters.

 Excellent judgment, written and verbal communication skills, and attention to detail.

 A practical, collaborative, and solutions-oriented approach to legal work.

 Ability to manage competing priorities independently while maintaining a high standard of execution.

 What you can expect: 
 Lead the legal workstreams for mergers and acquisitions, including due diligence, negotiations, drafting and reviewing transaction documents, and coordinating with external advisors and internal stakeholders.

 Advise on legal considerations and regulatory requirements related to international operations and expansion.

 Oversee corporate entities, corporate records, and related governance processes, including the incorporation and ongoing management of global subsidiaries

 Provide guidance on corporate governance matters, including developing and implementing corporate policies and procedures.

 Support Finance on a variety of matters, including insurance renewals, tax planning, financial statements, employee equity, commission plans, and other strategic projects.

 Review marketing materials and advise on applicable compliance requirements.

 Develop and deliver compliance training programs for employees on relevant legal and regulatory topics.

 Identify legal risks across the organization and develop strategies to mitigate those risks.

 Manage litigation and dispute resolution matters, including overseeing external counsel, developing case strategies, and supporting negotiations.

 Manage 1Password’s intellectual property portfolio, including trademarks, copyrights, and patents.

 Serve as a trusted legal partner to leaders across the business, balancing thoughtful risk management with the needs of a fast-moving company.

 USA-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $269,000 USD and $404,000 USD, plus immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, 401k and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

 Canada-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $234,000 CAD and $351,000 CAD, plus immediate participation in 1Password’s generous benefits program (health, dental, RRSP and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set.

 This posting is for an existing vacancy. 

 Our culture 
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first. 

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results. 

 How we work with AI 
We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.

We believe in the power of remote work, but recognize that in-person connection is important to help us achieve our mission. While we are a remote-first company, travel for in-person engagement is a part of almost all roles, and we require our employees to be ready and willing to take part. Frequency will depend on role and responsibilities, and may include, but is not limited to: annual department-wide offsites, team meetings, and customer/industry events.

We welcome all individuals and do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity and expression, race, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, colour, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, marital status, pregnancy, sex, citizenship, education, languages spoken or veteran status. Be yourself, find your people and share the things you love.

Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work. 

 If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future. 

 As the Senior Director, Implementation, you’ll report to the Vice President, Customer Success and set the strategic and operational direction for 1Password’s implementation and professional services function. You’ll lead a team responsible for helping customers across Small and Medium-sized Businesses (SMB), Commercial, and Enterprise segments adopt 1Password successfully, improve time to value, and achieve measurable outcomes.

 How we’re using AI today 
 Across GTM, we’re transforming the way we work with AI. We expect every seller, CSM, and team member to become a power user, using it daily to work smarter and move faster. AI is already embedded in how we operate – from real-time coaching that sharpens how we sell and interact with customers, to surfacing insights that help us anticipate needs – creating more time for meaningful customer engagement. If you’re excited to reshape how you think, make decisions, and drive growth with AI, you’ll feel right at home here.

 This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US.

 What we're looking for: 
 Bring 10+ years of experience in professional services, customer onboarding, or implementation, including at least 5 years in a leadership role, with experience in cybersecurity and Software as a Service (SaaS) environments.

 Demonstrate a strong background in technical implementations, systems, infrastructure, and integrations for complex customers.

 Apply experience from implementation, professional services, solutions architecture, or technical account management environments.

 Scale onboarding and implementation programs across SMB, Commercial, and Enterprise customer segments.

 Build capacity-planning models and use utilization, delivery performance, and other Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to guide decisions.

 Combine strategic thinking with a willingness to engage directly in complex customer situations, team challenges, and operational details.

 Influence senior leaders and cross-functional partners through clear communication, sound judgment, data, and a strong understanding of customer and business needs.

 What you can expect: 
 Define and execute the strategic vision for implementation and professional services, including the launch and evolution of scalable services offerings.

 Lead, coach, and grow a cross-functional team of Solutions Architects, Onboarding Specialists, Project Managers, and Implementation Specialists.

 Establish scalable playbooks, frameworks, and processes that improve onboarding, implementation quality, customer adoption, and time to value.

 Partner with Sales, Customer Success, Product, Marketing, and Operations to create effective transitions from pre-sale activities through customer implementation.

 Oversee implementation delivery across customer segments, ensuring projects meet scope, timeline, quality, and outcome expectations.

 Use data and reporting to monitor project health, capacity, utilization, customer outcomes, and opportunities for improvement.

 Serve as an escalation point for complex implementation challenges while leading change initiatives that strengthen team effectiveness and customer results.

 USA-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $192,000 USD and $264,000 USD. This role is also eligible for immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, 401k and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

 Canada-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $182,000 CAD and $250,000 CAD. This role is also eligible for immediate participation in 1Password’s generous benefits program (health, dental, RRSP and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set.

 This posting is for an existing vacancy. 

 Our culture 
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first. 

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results. 

 How we work with AI 
We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.

 This approach extends to our hiring process—candidates are welcome to use AI tools responsibly and thoughtfully during the application process. To us, this means we do ask that you join live interviews without using AI tools so we can get to know how you communicate, solve problems, and collaborate with others.

 Our approach to work 
We recognize the power of both in person collaboration and remote work. Some roles are designated as remote-first, with an expectation that individuals work from their homes majority of the time, while others are designated as in-office roles, with an expectation of being on-site on a regular basis. We recognize that certain roles benefit from regular, in-person connection to support collaboration, team cohesion, and customer engagement.

For all roles, occasional travel may be required. This includes things like: department-wide offsites, quarterly department meetings and periodic customer events. These events are typically held in varying locations across Canada, USA and/or EMEA. In leadership roles, you can expect to travel once per month on average.

Note: All go-to market roles will have an in-person onboarding in Toronto. 

 What we offer 
We believe in working hard, and rewarding that hard work through our benefits. While not an exhaustive list, here is a glance at what we currently offer: 

 Health and wellbeing 
👶 Maternity and parental leave top-up programs
🩺 Competitive health benefits
🏝 Generous PTO policy 

 Growth and future 
📈 RSU program for most employees
💸 Retirement matching program
🔑 Free 1Password account

 Community

🏆 Peer-to-peer recognition through Bonusly
🌎 Remote-first work environment
 *Some roles in our GTM team are currently being hired for in-person hybrid work in Toronto and Austin. These roles will specify on the posting. 

 You belong here. 

 1Password is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive, diverse and equitable workplace that is built on trust, support and respect. We welcome all individuals and do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity and expression, race, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, colour, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, marital status, pregnancy, sex, citizenship, education, languages spoken or veteran status. Be yourself, find your people and share the things you love. 

 Accommodation is available upon request at any point during our recruitment process. If you require an accommodation, please speak to your talent acquisition partner or email us at nextbit@agilebits.com and we’ll work to meet your needs. 

 Remote work is a part of our DNA. Given that our company was founded remotely in 2005, we can safely say we're experts at building remote culture. That said, remote work at 1Password does mean working from your home country. If you've got questions or concerns about this, your talent partner would be happy to address them with you.

Who We Are 
 AeroVect is transforming ground handling with autonomy, redefining how airlines and ground service providers around the globe run day-to-day operations. We are a Series A company backed by top-tier venture capital investors in aviation and autonomous driving. Our customers include some of the world’s largest airlines and ground handling providers.  We are hiring a Strategic Account Director to own and grow one of AeroVect’s largest airline accounts. You will lead the day-to-day customer relationship, secure funding for deployments, and manage commercial agreements. You will work directly with AeroVect’s leadership and the customer’s operations, finance, procurement, and executive teams.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role dedicated to a single strategic customer. You will personally lead business reviews, negotiate commercial agreements, and follow through on the customer decisions needed to keep deployments moving.

 You Will 
 Own the account plan, including revenue targets, expansion opportunities, budget timelines, and key customer decisions.

 Build relationships across the customer’s operating teams, budget owners, procurement, and senior leadership. Develop executive sponsorship beyond individual contacts.

 Lead pricing, contract negotiations, and renewals with AeroVect’s leadership, Finance, and Legal. Work with Product, Engineering, and Operations to validate scope and service commitments.

 Run customer business reviews covering operating results, deployment progress, commercial opportunities, and decisions required.

 Maintain an accurate account forecast and track contractual milestones, payment status, and commercial risks. Evaluate expansion requests against delivery capacity, support costs, and margins.

 You Have 
 10+ years of experience in strategic account management, enterprise sales, or commercial leadership, with direct responsibility for large enterprise customers.

 A track record of growing accounts through signed, funded agreements and deployed products or services.

 Experience navigating complex buying organizations, capital budgets, procurement processes, and contract negotiations.

 The ability to build relationships with frontline operators and senior executives, and lead substantive discussions about business performance and investment decisions.

 Exceptional financial and commercial judgment.

 Clear written and verbal communication, including executive presentations.

 Strong follow-through across customer and internal teams. You are comfortable personally handling the details needed to move an account forward.

 Experience selling and deploying robotics, industrial automation, or other technology used in industrial operations.

 Experience owning a major enterprise account in the airline / airport industry.

 Atlanta-based, with availability for regular in-person meetings and visits to customer locations.

jobs.title: Director of Human Resources

 People strategy and leadership

AIG Canada has launched careers and developed future leaders for 60 years. 

 Client Director

The team serves these important clients and their broker partners through an elevated, personalized experience – our client-centric framework drives a consistent experience and best practice, while allowing flexibility to meet the client’s needs. 

 What you need to know:  
 AIG Canada has an exciting opportunity for a Client Director to join our Client Engagement Team.  Reporting to the Head of Distribution, Canada and based out of the Toronto office, the responsibilities will involve management of key client relationships focused on client retention and new business growth.  A successful candidate will have proven ability to align and influence internal and external stakeholders, is an effective communicator, has the ability to build commitment, and is tolerant of ambiguity.  What you'll need to succeed:  
 10+ years of experience, including proven client relationship / management experience 
 Experience in P&C Insurance 
 Ability to build relationships, internally and externally 
 Ability to influence brokers, clients, peers, senior executives and staff 
 Ability to manage complex global insurance relationships

High performers move from the ELP program into a CEO or C-suite role within a Banyan operating company, or into a leadership role at Banyan Software HQ.

 Real operating reps, not case reps. You carry a genuine initiative inside a live business and leadership-level stretch assignments, decisions that show up in a P&L.

 Graduating or recently graduated from a top MBA program. This cycle is not open to first-year MBA students.
