jobs.title: VP Sales & Marketing (Bilingual Eng/Fre)
jobs.description:
Banyan Software is the best permanent home for software businesses that serve specialized industries, their employees, and their customers. With a buy-grow-and-hold-for-life approach and a permanent capital base, Banyan acquires and grows companies worldwide, honoring founder legacies and helping portfolio companies modernize through shared AI expertise and operational discipline. Founded in 2016, Banyan operates more than 120 portfolio companies across North and South America, Europe, and APAC, and has appeared on the Inc. 5000 list for six consecutive years. The Banyan Software Foundation, endowed with $100 million in Banyan stock, leverages technology to build a greener and more equitable world.

 VP Sales & Marketing (Bilingual Eng/Fre) 

 Reports to: CEO, NovoLogik
 Location: Saint-Jérôme, Quebec, Canada
 Work model: Hybrid-flexible

 About NovoLogik

 NovoLogik provides electronic medical record and practice management software for orthodontic and dental clinics. Its OrthoNovo and DentoNovo platforms bring patient engagement, scheduling, billing, documentation, and imaging together into a single system of record that clinical teams use every day. NovoLogik has been the leading technology provider for orthodontic practices in Quebec for over 20 years, and it is extending that position into new markets across Canada.

 The Opportunity

 NovoLogik has never had a dedicated sales and marketing function. This role exists to build it, starting from a blank page rather than a broken process.

 NovoLogik holds a leading position in its core Quebec orthodontic market and has built a growing, loyal base of dental customers, with high retention and an expanding product set. There is real room to grow, both within existing customer relationships and in new markets across Canada, though building on that position requires a true commercial function, which does not exist today.

 This is a high-volume, relationship-driven commercial motion, not an enterprise field-sales role. Success looks like a functioning CRM, a real marketing engine, a handful of well-chosen industry conferences, new outbound campaigns, and disciplined follow-through on renewals and account growth.

 Because NovoLogik is a small, lean organization, this role also carries general operational and administrative responsibility beyond the commercial mandate. You will partner directly with NovoLogik’s CEO on commercial strategy and priorities.

 Why NovoLogik

 You’re building, not maintaining. This is NovoLogik’s first dedicated sales and marketing leadership hire. Process, tooling, team structure, and positioning are yours to define.

 Real ownership from day one. You are not inheriting a team or a process. You decide what to build first and how, with full accountability for the outcome.

 A business built to grow. NovoLogik holds a leading position in its core market and a sticky, system-of-record product used daily by clinical teams. The growth opportunity in front of you is real.

 A permanent home, not a flip. Banyan acquires and holds its companies indefinitely. You are building something meant to last, not preparing a company for a near-term sale.

 Meaningful scope, fast. In a small, lean organization, your decisions are visible and consequential from day one.

 Direct executive access. You will work closely with NovoLogik’s CEO and with Banyan’s Operating Group on commercial strategy, marketing investment, and growth support.

 What You Will Own

 Go-to-Market Build

 Select and implement a CRM, and establish the sales operating rhythm that goes with it.

 Define and prioritize the ideal customer profile and target segments, starting with the existing customer base.

 Build out marketing collateral, refresh the website in partnership with Banyan’s marketing team, and launch initial outbound campaigns, including SEO and SEM.

 Sales Execution

 Run the full sales cycle: qualify inbound leads, deliver demos, negotiate, and close.

 Own the revenue number from day one as an individual contributor until the team justifies its first hire.

 Build day-to-day sales process and reporting discipline to support the function’s growth.

 Customer & Market Expansion

 Shape product packaging and account-growth opportunities across the existing customer base, in partnership with NovoLogik and Banyan leadership.

 Represent NovoLogik at relevant industry conferences and build a cadence of customer visits, including in English-speaking parts of Canada.

 Build the commercial foundation to extend NovoLogik’s presence beyond Quebec.

 Team Building

 Build the business case for NovoLogik’s first account executive hire as pipeline volume warrants it, in partnership with Banyan.

 Hire, ramp, and mentor new sales talent as the function grows beyond a single seat.

 Operational Leadership

 Take on general operational and administrative responsibilities as needed in a lean organization.

 Identify and drive opportunities to professionalize processes across the business.

 Cross-Functional Partnership

 Work directly with NovoLogik’s CEO on sales strategy and go-to-market execution.

 Partner with Banyan’s Operating Group on go-to-market resourcing, marketing support, and growth priorities.

 What We’re Looking For

 Must-Haves

 Proven, quota-carrying B2B sales experience with a track record of consistently meeting or exceeding revenue targets.

 Professionally proficient in both English and French, spoken and written, sufficient to lead business conversations in either language.

 Demonstrated experience building or scaling a sales and marketing function, including process, tooling, and early execution, not purely analytical or advisory work.

 Comfort owning the entire sales cycle (qualifying inbound leads, running demos, negotiating, closing) without an existing SDR team or outbound infrastructure.

 Able to work on-site in Saint-Jérôme, Quebec on a regular basis.

 Comfort operating as a generalist in a small, lean organization, including administrative and operational responsibilities outside the core commercial mandate.

 Nice-to-Haves

 MBA.

 Experience selling into healthcare, dental, or another regulated or professional-services vertical.

 Experience building volume-driven sales or marketing motions rather than closing a small number of large, bespoke deals.

 Working marketing fluency (SEO/SEM, website strategy, campaign management) to help stand up NovoLogik’s first demand-generation motion.

 Experience selling on-premise or hybrid-deployment software rather than pure cloud/SaaS.

 Vice-président(e), Ventes et Marketing (bilingue anglais/français) 

 Relève de: PDG, NovoLogik
 Lieu: Saint-Jérôme, Québec, Canada
 Mode de travail: Hybride flexible

 À propos de NovoLogik

 NovoLogik propose des logiciels de dossiers médicaux électroniques et de gestion de cabinet pour les cliniques dentaires et orthodontiques. Ses plateformes OrthoNovo et DentoNovo réunissent en un seul système de référence l’engagement des patients, la prise de rendez-vous, la facturation, la documentation et l’imagerie, utilisés quotidiennement par les équipes cliniques. Depuis plus de 20 ans, NovoLogik est le principal fournisseur technologique pour les cliniques d’orthodontie au Québec, et étend maintenant cette position à de nouveaux marchés partout au Canada.

 Le Défi

 NovoLogik n’a jamais eu de fonction dédiée aux ventes et au marketing. Ce poste consiste à la bâtir à partir de zéro, plutôt qu’à corriger un processus déjà en place.

 NovoLogik occupe une position de leader dans son marché orthodontique de base au Québec et a développé une clientèle dentaire fidèle et croissante, avec un taux de rétention élevé et une offre de produits en expansion. Il existe un réel potentiel de croissance, tant auprès de la clientèle existante que dans de nouveaux marchés à travers le Canada, mais pour en tirer parti, une véritable fonction commerciale doit être mise en place, ce qui n’existe pas encore aujourd’hui.

 Il s’agit d’une approche commerciale à haut volume et axée sur les relations, et non d’un rôle de vente terrain de type entreprise. La réussite se traduit par un CRM fonctionnel, un véritable moteur marketing, quelques conférences industrielles bien choisies, de nouvelles campagnes de prospection et une discipline rigoureuse dans le suivi des renouvellements et de la croissance des comptes.

 NovoLogik étant une organisation petite et agile, ce rôle comporte également des responsabilités opérationnelles et administratives générales, au-delà du mandat commercial. Vous travaillerez directement avec le PDG de NovoLogik sur la stratégie commerciale et les priorités.

 Pourquoi NovoLogik

 Vous bâtissez, vous ne maintenez pas. Il s’agit du tout premier poste de direction en ventes et marketing chez NovoLogik. Les processus, les outils, la structure d’équipe et le positionnement sont entièrement à définir.

 Une réelle prise en charge dès le premier jour. Vous n’héritez ni d’une équipe ni d’un processus. Vous décidez quoi bâtir en premier et comment, avec une pleine imputabilité des résultats.

 Une entreprise bâtie pour croître. NovoLogik occupe une position de leader dans son marché de base et possède un produit de référence, intégré au quotidien par les équipes cliniques. Le potentiel de croissance devant vous est bien réel.

 Un foyer permanent, pas une revente rapide. Banyan acquiert ses entreprises pour les conserver indéfiniment. Vous bâtissez quelque chose destiné à durer, et non à préparer une entreprise pour une vente à court terme.

 Une portée significative, rapidement. Dans une organisation petite et agile, vos décisions sont visibles et ont un impact dès le premier jour.

 Un accès direct à la direction. Vous collaborerez étroitement avec le PDG de NovoLogik et avec le groupe des opérations de Banyan sur la stratégie commerciale, les investissements marketing et le soutien à la croissance.

 Ce Que Vous Prendrez en Charge

 Mise en place de la stratégie de mise en marché

 Sélectionner et déployer un CRM, et établir la cadence opérationnelle des ventes qui l’accompagne.

 Définir et prioriser le profil de client idéal et les segments cibles, en commençant par la clientèle existante.

 Développer du matériel marketing, actualiser le site Web en partenariat avec l’équipe marketing de Banyan, et lancer les premières campagnes de prospection, y compris le référencement (SEO) et la publicité payante (SEM).

 Exécution des ventes

 Gérer l’ensemble du cycle de vente: qualifier les pistes entrantes, effectuer les démonstrations, négocier et conclure.

 Assumer la responsabilité du chiffre d’affaires dès le premier jour, à titre de contributeur individuel, jusqu’à ce que le volume justifie la première embauche.

 Mettre en place les processus de vente et la rigueur de suivi au quotidien pour soutenir la croissance de la fonction.

 Expansion de la clientèle et du marché

 Façonner l’offre de produits et les occasions de croissance de comptes au sein de la clientèle existante, en partenariat avec la direction de NovoLogik et de Banyan.

 Représenter NovoLogik lors de conférences industrielles pertinentes et établir une cadence de visites clients, y compris dans les régions anglophones du Canada.

 Bâtir les fondations commerciales permettant d’étendre la présence de NovoLogik au-delà du Québec.

 Développement de l’équipe

 Bâtir, en partenariat avec Banyan, la justification d’affaires pour la première embauche d’un ou d’une représentant(e) des comptes, selon le volume du pipeline.

 Recruter, intégrer et encadrer de nouveaux talents en vente à mesure que la fonction se développe au-delà d’un seul poste.

 Leadership opérationnel

 Assumer des responsabilités opérationnelles et administratives générales selon les besoins d’une organisation agile.

 Repérer et mener des initiatives de professionnalisation des processus à l’échelle de l’entreprise.

 Collaboration transversale

 Travailler directement avec le PDG de NovoLogik sur la stratégie de vente et l’exécution de la mise en marché.

 Collaborer avec le groupe des opérations de Banyan sur les ressources de mise en marché, le soutien marketing et les priorités de croissance.

 Ce Que Nous Recherchons

 Exigences essentielles

 Expérience éprouvée en vente B2B avec quota, assortie d’un historique constant d’atteinte ou de dépassement des objectifs de revenus.

 Compétence professionnelle en anglais et en français, à l’oral comme à l’écrit, suffisante pour mener des conversations d’affaires dans les deux langues.

 Expérience démontrée dans la mise en place ou le développement d’une fonction de vente et de marketing, incluant les processus, les outils et l’exécution initiale, et non uniquement un rôle analytique ou consultatif.

 À l’aise de gérer l’ensemble du cycle de vente (qualification des pistes entrantes, démonstrations, négociation, conclusion) sans équipe de représentants au développement des ventes (SDR) ni infrastructure de prospection existante.

 Capacité à travailler sur place à Saint-Jérôme, au Québec, de façon régulière.

 À l’aise d’agir comme généraliste au sein d’une organisation petite et agile, incluant des responsabilités administratives et opérationnelles en dehors du mandat commercial principal.

 Atouts

 MBA.

 Expérience de vente dans le secteur de la santé, dentaire, ou dans un autre secteur réglementé ou de services professionnels.

 Expérience dans la mise en place d’approches de vente ou de marketing axées sur le volume, plutôt que la conclusion d’un petit nombre de transactions importantes et personnalisées.

 Aisance pratique en marketing (SEO/SEM, stratégie Web, gestion de campagnes) pour aider à mettre en place la première fonction de génération de demande de NovoLogik.

 Expérience de vente de logiciels sur site ou en mode hybride, plutôt qu’en mode infonuagique (SaaS) pur.

jobs.title: ASSOCIATE DIRECTOR / DIRECTOR– FUND INVESTMENTS
jobs.description:
We are banking at another level. 

 Choosing BDC as your employer means working in a healthy, inclusive, and skilled workplace that puts forward the best conditions to bring together unique teams where employees are empowered to act. It also means being at the centre of ambitious economic and financial projects to see further and to do things differently, to fuel the success of Canadian entrepreneurs.

 Choosing BDC as your employer also means: 
 Flexible and competitive benefits, including an Employee Savings and Investment Plan where BDC matches part of your voluntary contributions, a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, a $750 wellness and health care spending account, to name a few   

 In addition to paid vacation each year, five personal days, sick days as necessary, and our offices are closed from December 25 to January 1 

 A hybrid work model that truly balances work and personal life

 Opportunities for learning, training and development, and much more... 

 Explore the BDC Way in our Culture Book 

 POSITION OVERVIEW 

 BDC Capital 

 With more than $6 billion under management, BDC Capital is the investment arm of BDC and a strategic partner to Canada’s most innovative and high-potential companies. As Canada’s largest and most active technology investor, BDC Capital provides equity, venture capital, and growth and transition capital to help Canadian entrepreneurs build globally competitive companies.

 BDC’s Defence Platform will mobilize an additional $6 billion in financing, investment and advisory solutions to support Canadian businesses and strengthen Canada’s defence and security ecosystem. Within the Platform, BDC Capital is investing through direct and indirect strategies to accelerate defence innovation, strengthen Canadian capabilities and support technologies with defence-focused or dual-use applications.

 Reporting to the Managing Director, Fund Investments, the  Associate Director / Director, Fund Investments  will play a leading role in sourcing, underwriting, executing and managing investments in venture capital and private equity funds aligned with Canada’s defence and national-sovereignty priorities.

 Your primary focus will be the Defence Fund Investments mandate. You will also contribute to BDC Capital’s broader fund-investment activities across stages, sectors and regions in Canada.

 You will lead substantial components of the investment process, develop and defend investment recommendations, manage selected GP relationships and portfolio responsibilities, and guide Associates and Analysts. You will combine institutional fund-investing judgment with a growing understanding of dual-use technologies, defence markets, procurement pathways and the Canadian and allied defence ecosystem.

 CHALLENGES TO BE MET 

 Investment Sourcing and Underwriting 
 Help source and assess high-quality venture capital and private equity fund investment opportunities, with a particular focus on defence, dual-use and deep technology.
 Lead significant components of GP due diligence, including assessment of investment strategy, team, track record and attribution, portfolio construction, sourcing capabilities, fund economics, terms, risks and expected returns.
 Analyze underlying portfolios and pipelines to assess strategy execution, concentration, market exposure and alignment with BDC’s mandate.
 Prepare investment memoranda and present and defend recommendations to the BDC Capital Funds Investment Committee.
 Guide Associates and Analysts in the analysis and execution of investment opportunities.

 Transaction Execution and Portfolio Management 
 Participate in negotiations with fund managers and work with Legal and other internal teams on LPAs, side letters and investment documentation.
 Manage an assigned portfolio of fund investments and maintain strong relationships with GPs.
 Monitor financial performance, portfolio developments, organizational changes, strategy execution and emerging risks.
 Develop recommendations on re-ups, amendments, consents and other portfolio decisions.
 Assess portfolio construction, concentration, pacing, cash flows and risk/return trends to inform future capital allocation.
 Represent BDC, as appropriate, on LPACs and other investor-governance forums.

 Collaboration and Market Presence 
 Collaborate closely with BDC Capital’s Fund Investments and direct-investing teams and with colleagues across BDC involved in the Defence Platform.
 Develop relationships with fund managers, institutional investors and other ecosystem participants and represent BDC Capital at relevant industry events.
 Share market intelligence and insights that support BDC’s broader investment and strategic objectives.
 Coach and support the development of Associates and Analysts.

 Defence and Dual-Use Specialization 

 Prior defence-investing experience is an asset, not a prerequisite. We are looking for an a person with the curiosity, judgment and commitment to develop meaningful expertise in Canada’s defence and dual-use investment ecosystem.
 Develop strong knowledge of dual-use and defence technologies, defence procurement cycles, deep-tech commercialization and the role of prime contractors, integrators and government customers.
 Assess fund managers’ defence-sector expertise, networks, technical-diligence capabilities and ability to support portfolio companies in accessing Canadian and allied defence markets.
 Evaluate relevant indicators including procurement traction, technology and manufacturing readiness, supply-chain resilience and commercial-market potential.
 Contribute to defence-specific portfolio monitoring and reporting, including financial performance, strategic alignment and material risks.
 Build relationships across the Canadian and allied defence, investment, government and innovation ecosystems.

 WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR 
 5–7 years of relevant investment experience, including at least 2 years of direct experience underwriting and/or managing venture capital or private equity fund investments, or in a closely related institutional manager-selection role.
 Strong understanding of venture capital and/or private equity fund structures, economics, performance analysis and portfolio management.
 Experience leading significant components of investment due diligence and developing recommendations for an investment committee or equivalent decision-making body.
 Familiarity with fund documentation and commercial negotiations.
 Strong financial, analytical, written and verbal communication skills.
 Sound investment judgment, intellectual curiosity and the ability to manage multiple workstreams with appropriate autonomy.
 Strong relationship-management skills and the ability to work effectively with senior internal and external stakeholders.
 Bachelor’s degree in business, finance, economics, science, engineering, law or another relevant discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
 Fluency in both Canadian official languages (English & French) is an asset.

 #INDHP

 Proudly one of Canada’s Top 100 Employers and one of Canada’s Best Diversity Employers, we are committed to fostering a diverse, equitable, inclusive and accessible environment where all employees can thrive and feel empowered to bring their whole selves to work. If you require an accommodation to complete your application, please do not hesitate to contact us at accessibility@bdc.ca.

 While we appreciate all applications, we advise that only the candidates selected to participate in the recruitment process will be contacted.

jobs.title: Director of Pricing & Monetization
jobs.description:
About Blue J

Blue J is the leading generative AI solution for tax professionals and one of Canada's fastest-growing AI companies. Headquartered in Toronto, we're a high-growth B2B SaaS company building industry-leading tax research software that helps accountants find accurate answers to complex tax questions with greater speed and confidence, supporting workflows across compliance, advisory, training, tax writing, and more.

Backed by a $176M USD Series E funding round, we're scaling rapidly across North America and the UK while continuing to push the boundaries of what's possible with AI. By combining advanced technology with deep tax expertise, we empower tax professionals to work more efficiently, make better decisions, and deliver greater value to their clients.

A Note on Location

We are excited to meet with qualified candidates and are grateful for everyone's interest. This is a remote position open to candidates anywhere in Canada, with occasional travel to our Toronto office as needed. All candidates must be eligible to work in Canada.

To help you get off to a great start, we bring all new team members together for their first three days of onboarding. If you’re based outside of our local commuting area, Blue J will arrange and cover your travel and accommodation.

The Opportunity

Reporting To The VP, GTM Strategy & Operations, The Director Of Pricing & Monetization Will Lead Pricing And Packaging Analysis And Recommendations At Blue J. You'll Explore The Questions That Shape Our Commercial Strategy

Who are our customers, and how do their needs differ?
How do they get value from Blue J, and how should our pricing reflect it?
How should our offering evolve as our product portfolio and customer base expand?

You'll collaborate with Finance, Product, Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, and Revenue Operations, and regularly present recommendations to the executive team.

You'll draw on experience in finance, FP&A, or a related analytical field to turn complex data into clear, actionable recommendations. You'll build models, conduct analysis, and communicate findings to stakeholders with different perspectives and priorities, helping the team reach decisions and bring pricing and packaging changes to market.

What You’ll Be Doing

Pricing & Packaging Strategy

Lead analysis and develop recommendations for Blue J’s pricing and packaging structure, including plans, tiers, bundles, and add-ons.
Evaluate how our pricing model can evolve as we launch new products and capabilities and serve a broader range of customer segments.
Identify value metrics that align what customers pay with the value they receive.
Develop principles and guidelines for discounting, promotions, renewals, and price changes.
Build and maintain a prioritized monetization roadmap in partnership with GTM and Product leadership.

Financial Modeling & Analysis

Build business cases and financial models to assess how pricing and packaging changes affect acquisition, conversion, expansion, retention, and customer lifetime value.
Partner with Finance on revenue forecasting and scenario planning related to pricing decisions.
Analyze deal, usage, and customer data to understand willingness to pay, actual prices paid, and discounting patterns.
Measure the impact of pricing initiatives on annual recurring revenue (ARR) and margins, and share results with leadership.

Customer & Market Insights

Develop segmentation frameworks based on customer needs, behaviours, and willingness to pay.
Conduct qualitative and quantitative research, including customer interviews, surveys, win/loss analysis, and churn analysis, to test pricing assumptions.
Monitor competitive pricing and SaaS and AI monetization trends, identifying developments relevant to Blue J’s strategy.

Experimentation & Implementation

Design pricing and packaging experiments with clear hypotheses, success measures, and safeguards for customer trust and retention.
Collaborate with relevant teams to implement approved changes across configure, price, quote (CPQ) systems, billing, and reporting.
Develop rollout and transition plans for new and existing customers, and provide training and resources for Sales and Customer Success.
Establish post-launch measurement plans and refine approaches based on results and feedback.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Communication

Establish a regular process for pricing reviews and decisions, with clear responsibilities across Finance, Product, and GTM.
Present recommendations to executive leadership, clearly explaining the supporting evidence, trade-offs, and potential impacts.
Advise Sales and Customer Success leadership on deal structures and pricing questions.

What You Offer Blue J

7+ years of experience in pricing, monetization, FP&A, strategic finance, or revenue strategy, ideally within B2B SaaS.
Experience analyzing, recommending, and implementing pricing or packaging changes.
Deep analytical and financial modeling skills, with a strong command of SaaS metrics and subscription economics (ARR, NRR, churn, CAC, LTV, gross margin).
Experience with a range of pricing models, such as seat-based, usage- or consumption-based, value-based, and hybrid approaches.
Comfort working directly with large datasets; proficiency in SQL and advanced spreadsheet modeling; experience with AI and BI tools.

About Blue J

Blue J is the leading generative AI solution for tax professionals and one of Canada's fastest-growing AI companies. Headquartered in Toronto, we're a high-growth B2B SaaS company building industry-leading tax research software that helps accountants find accurate answers to complex tax questions with greater speed and confidence, supporting workflows across compliance, advisory, training, tax writing, and more.

Backed by a $176M USD Series E funding round, we're scaling rapidly across North America and the UK while continuing to push the boundaries of what's possible with AI. By combining advanced technology with deep tax expertise, we empower tax professionals to work more efficiently, make better decisions, and deliver greater value to their clients.

A Note on Location

Primarily remote, but you must live within driving distance of our Toronto office. You’ll join us in person for every quarterly and occasionally for team get-togethers (typically 1–3 visits per quarter).

To help you get off to a great start, we bring all new team members together for their first three days of onboarding. If you’re based outside of our local commuting area, Blue J will arrange and cover your travel and accommodation.

About The Team

Blue J’s technology creates value when tax professionals can easily discover, trust, and incorporate it into their work. The Tax Pro Engagement pillar owns that experience, including onboarding, search, collaboration, account management, purchasing, integrations, and core customer workflows.

As Director of Engineering, you will set the pillar’s technical and organizational direction, lead multiple product-engineering teams, and partner with Engineering and Product leadership to shape priorities and measure customer value.

You will initially immerse yourself in our product, architecture, customers, and codebase while contributing to technical design and complex problem-solving. Over time, your focus will shift toward scaling the teams, leaders, systems, and practices supporting the pillar.

The Opportunity

We are looking for a Director of Engineering that will guide the evolution of Blue J’s platform architecture and help our engineering teams deliver high quality products at speed. This role is ideal for someone who is a strong system designer, deeply experienced with building SaaS platforms, and energized by helping teams navigate technical complexity.

The ideal leader combines deep systems expertise with strong product instincts and a genuine commitment to user experience. They will champion the end user, challenge assumptions, and help identify new product possibilities that may not yet be obvious.

You will work closely with product, engineering, and research to define product direction, build reliable and scalable systems, and ensure our teams have the tools and infrastructure they need to ship confidently and frequently. jobs.description:
Location 

Brookfield Place - 181 Bay Street 
 Business - Energy 

 Brookfield Energy operates one of the world’s largest publicly traded platforms for sustainable energy. Our energy portfolio consists of hydroelectric, wind, utility-scale solar, distributed generation and storage facilities in North America, South America, Europe and Asia. Our operating capacity totals over 35,000 megawatts and our development pipeline stands at approximately 200,000 megawatts. Our portfolio of sustainable solutions assets includes our investments in Westinghouse (a leading global nuclear services business) and a utility and independent power producer with operations in the Caribbean and Latin America, as well as both operating assets and a development pipeline of carbon capture and storage capacity, agricultural renewable natural gas and materials recycling. 

 Brookfield Energy is the flagship listed energy company of Brookfield Asset Management, a leading global alternative asset manager with over $1 trillion of assets under management. 
 To learn more about the Brookfield Energy group, visit  https://www.brookfield.com/about-us/capabilities/energy. 

 Brookfield Culture 

 Brookfield has a unique and dynamic culture.  We seek team members who have a long-term focus and whose values align with our Attributes of a Brookfield Leader:  Entrepreneurial, Collaborative and Disciplined.  Brookfield is committed to the development of our people through challenging work assignments and exposure to diverse businesses. 

 Job Description 

 The Regional HSS&E Director within the Brookfield Energy’s North American Asset Management team will serve as the subject matter expert to provide prompt, quality HSS&E assistance to the Asset Management team and Brookfield Renewable portfolio companies within the region, actively supporting Brookfield’s commitment to HSS&E excellence and to be industry leaders in risk management and incident prevention. This role serves as a key member of the regional senior leadership Asset Management team and as an extension of the Brookfield Renewable Corporate HSS&E team, providing expert advice and leadership to enable safe, sustainable growth across multiple countries in the region.

 The HSS&E Director will be responsible within the region for leading and coordinating HSS&E-related due diligence activities, gap analyses, audits, investigations, business support requirements, subject matter expertise and assistance with applicable policies, processes, procedures and regulations.

 The ability to forge strategic relationships with internal and external stakeholders will be a critical success factor in the role, as will the ability to influence without direct authority.

 Key Responsibilities 

 Lead, coach and serve as the HSS&E subject matter expert on behalf of the regional Asset Management team, while fostering collaboration between Corporate HSS&E, Asset Management and portfolio companies.
 Support regional portfolio companies in effectively implementing HSS&E programs and processes, as part of an HSS&E Management System, that meet the requirements of Brookfield HSS&E standards and ensure compliance with the appropriate regulatory requirements & legislation.
 Serve as subject matter expert for HSS&E program implementation with newly acquired businesses/assets.
 Assist investment teams by leading HSS&E due diligence initiatives for potential acquisitions/investments within the region.
 Coordinate and conduct HSS&E gap analyses for all newly acquired businesses.
 Assist Asset Managers and new portfolio companies and in the planning, coordination, and performance of Asset Condition Assessment inspections to ensure newly acquired assets meet Brookfield safety standards and provide a safe working environment for employees and contractors.
 Provide portfolio companies with support to help define strategies and action plans for the implementation of recommendations from HSS&E gap analyses, Asset Condition Assessments, audits and incident investigations.
 Coordinate & streamline HSS&E-related reporting from regional portfolio companies to Brookfield Corporate HSS&E.
 Coordinate and, as necessary, participate in HSS&E Detailed High-Risk Incident Investigations, HSS&E audits, and other HSS&E-related assessments and program monitoring activities across the Brookfield Renewable businesses.
 Coordinate and provide HSS&E training and coaching on the Brookfield HSS&E program, standards and requirements for asset management teams, newly acquired businesses, and key portfolio company leadership, line management, and HSS&E staff.
 Assist in collecting and reporting leading/lagging HSS&E metrics and KPIs for use in Corporate HSS&E reporting.
 Maintain up-to-date data and supporting information on portfolio companies and HSS&E-related initiatives within the region using appropriate Corporate HSS&E data management and reporting systems.
 Participate in developing HSS&E standards, guidance and training materials for the safe and effective operation of new asset classes using new technologies

 Requirements 

 The successful candidate will hold a minimum relevant degree qualification in Health & Safety, or a related discipline.
 Minimum 10+ years of Health & Safety experience in a fast paced, dynamic environment, preferably in the renewables sector.
 Knowledge of pertinent standards, laws, regulations and practices and the ability to interpret and advise on their application.
 Experience in complex safety incident investigations within high-risk environments, with experience in root cause analysis methodologies.
 Demonstrated ability to influence, without authority, at all levels.
 Proven experience supporting geographically dispersed teams and projects in fast-paced and often high-risk working environments involving asset construction / operations.
 Track record of driving cultural change and continuous improvement in health & safety.
 High level of English language capability, both spoken and written.
 Proficient with Microsoft applications with specific experience/capability in drafting professional, clear and succinct HSS&E-related assessments, standards, procedures, etc.
 Ability to plan, multi-task and prioritise a large and varied workload.
 Experience in a multi-national global environment.
 Personal attributes – credible, calm, knowledgeable and authoritative leadership style. Pragmatic, solutions focused, strong communicator with resilience, strong judgement and high integrity.
 A willingness to ‘roll up one’s sleeves and get work done’.
 Flexibility to travel to operational and construction sites and other business locations globally, as required.

 Capco is looking for a Sales Enablement Lead – North America to play a key role in strengthening sales effectiveness, shaping strategic opportunities and driving growth across our US and Canadian businesses. Working closely with regional leadership and reporting to the Global Sales Enablement Lead, you will combine strategic thinking with hands-on execution — supporting high-value pursuits, challenging commercial approaches and delivering practical initiatives that improve how we sell. This is a highly visible, collaborative role for someone who understands how consulting business is won, can engage credibly with senior leaders and has the drive to turn ideas into tangible results.

 Drive Strategic Pursuits and Improve Win Rates 

 Lead and shape priority pursuits, from opportunity strategy and solution development through proposals, commercial discussions and executive presentations.

 Challenge deal strategies, sharpen differentiation and strengthen client value propositions.

 Bring together the right expertise across Capco to develop compelling, commercially sound solutions.

 Facilitate pipeline and deal reviews, win strategy sessions and pitch preparation for major opportunities.

 Capture lessons from wins and losses to improve future deal performance.

 Lead and support sales education initiatives that strengthen sales confidence, develop practical selling skills and build growth capabilities across career levels.

 Design and deliver targeted learning, coaching and hands-on development for client-facing teams.

 Strengthen capabilities in opportunity origination, consultative selling, solution shaping, storytelling and strategic account growth.

 Work with regional leaders to identify capability gaps and address them through practical interventions.

 Build commercial confidence and embed effective sales behaviours into everyday client engagement.

   

 Make Selling More Effective 

 Develop practical playbooks, tools and guidance that improve effectiveness across the sales lifecycle.

 Champion AI-enabled sales productivity, identifying opportunities to simplify work, improve quality and reduce duplication.

 Drive the adoption and effective use of knowledge assets and reusable sales content.

 Translate successful sales approaches into repeatable practices that can scale across the business.

 Work with sellers to identify friction points and deliver improvements that make a tangible difference.

   

 Connect Expertise and Unlock Growth

 What We're Looking For 

 We are looking for a growth-minded, credible and action-oriented sales professional who understands how consulting business is won and actively collaborates across the leadership team to help Capco succeed. 

 You will bring:

 15+ years of consulting and financial services experience, ideally gained through client-facing consulting, business development, strategic sales or delivery roles.

 Commercial judgement and confidence to challenge senior stakeholders, test assumptions and strengthen deal strategies.

jobs.title: Director, Insurance Operations
jobs.description:
At CI, we see a great place to work as one that is a safe place for everyone to have a voice, where people are empowered to take ownership over meaningful work, where there is an opportunity to grow through stretching themselves, where they can work on innovative products and projects, and where employees are supported and engaged in doing so.  

CI Financial is seeking a Director, Insurance Operations to lead the modernization and ongoing performance of our Canadian individual life insurance Operations function.

This role combines daily operational leadership with a significant transformation mandate. You will strengthen case progression and carrier advocacy, build actionable Operations Intelligence, improve operational data and technology, develop differentiated advisor service, and lead an established team through sustained change.

This opportunity is suited to an insurance operations leader who has personally delivered meaningful change while remaining accountable for people, service quality, and daily results. 

 What You Will Do: 
 Lead the daily performance and modernization of Insurance Operations.
 Assess current services, processes, systems, operational data, capacity, and cross-functional handoffs.
 Lead the development and phased implementation of an approved future operating model aligned with CI’s insurance growth, advisor-support, and client-service priorities.
 Build Operations Intelligence that turns pipeline progression, aging, service levels, capacity, carrier performance, and financial information into clear actions and decision-ready recommendations.
 Strengthen case ownership, underwriting follow-up, carrier advocacy, escalation, delivery, placement, and oversight of complex, high-value, or aging cases.
 Develop practical pre-submission navigation and complex-case routing while preserving clear boundaries between operational support, insurance advice, and underwriting authority.
 Design differentiated advisor and in-force service models, including enhanced support where internal involvement adds meaningful value.
 Define operational technology, data, automation, and self-service requirements in partnership with Technology teams and vendors.
 Deliver practical improvements within the current operating environment while longer-term modernization work proceeds.
 Assess future capability requirements and recommend the team design, development priorities, and resources required to deliver the approved operating model.

 Specific modernization priorities, sequencing, performance measures, and resource requirements will reflect the operating baseline, business priorities, available resources, and appropriate approval processes.

 What You Bring: 
 At least 7 years of progressive experience specifically in Canadian individual life insurance Operations, including a minimum of 3 years in a formal operational people-leadership role with direct accountability for people, workload, service quality, capacity, priorities, and escalations.
 Strong knowledge of Canadian individual life insurance products, carrier practices, application processing, underwriting requirements, medical and financial evidence, issue, delivery, placement, and in-force servicing.
 Proven experience modernizing an operation while continuing to deliver effective daily service.
 Experience implementing meaningful process, service, data, or technology improvements that achieved sustained adoption and measurable results.
 Strong analytical and commercial judgment, including the ability to challenge incomplete data, establish credible measures, and translate findings into action.
 Practical experience defining business requirements and working with Technology teams or vendors through assessment, testing, implementation, adoption, and post-launch improvement.
 Experience leading an established team through material change with respect, clarity, and accountability.

 Bilingual English and French capability is preferred but not required. CLU, MBA, or relevant insurance, business, operations, technology, or change-management credentials are considered assets.

 What Will Make You Successful 
 You are equally comfortable reviewing an aging case queue, challenging unreliable reporting, working with carriers, coaching experienced employees, and presenting recommendations to senior leadership.
 You can modernize an operation without losing control of daily service.
 You create useful intelligence from imperfect data rather than waiting for perfect systems.
 You simplify and clarify processes before attempting to automate them.
 You respect institutional knowledge while challenging practices that no longer serve the business.
 You understand that launching a change is not the same as achieving sustained adoption.

 Why This Role Is Different 
 This role combines leadership of an established operation with the opportunity to define and implement its next stage.
 You will help build stronger operational intelligence, improve case progression, modernize technology and data, develop differentiated service, and strengthen the capabilities required for the future.
 Candidates may currently hold a Director or Senior Manager role. Demonstrated scope, operational accountability, and evidence of sustained delivery will matter more than current title or employer type.
 Relevant experience may come from an MGA, national insurance account, life insurer, wealth-management insurance operation, or insurance transformation role with prior operational accountability.

 The Operating Model You Will Help Build 
 The role will help establish stronger operational visibility, case ownership and escalation, differentiated advisor support, practical pre-submission navigation, and priority process and data improvements.
 The specific sequence will reflect the operating baseline, business priorities, cross-functional dependencies, and approved resources. Success will be visible in how the operation performs, how the team works, and how consistently improvements are used in daily practice.

 Work Arrangement 
 Occasional travel may be required based on business needs.
 This role follows our in office work model and requires employees to be onsite four days per week to support collaboration and business needs.

The ideal candidate is expected to apply a risk-based, value-added approach that aligns with international audit standards, strengthens governance, and upholds compliance with regulatory, contractual, and corporate-specific requirements.
 The Director of Internal Controls will be based at CI’s head office 15 York Street, Toronto, Ontario, and will oversee a team and internal control specialists and external consultants.

 WHAT YOU WILL DO: 
 Liaison between the company, internal audit, external audit, and Mubadala Capital (CI’s parent) in corporate audit projects.
 Ensure the effectiveness of CI’s internal controls over financial reporting (“ICFR”) by maintaining and executing the ICFR program.
 Support internal and external auditors in their audit duties – ensure all requests are delivered in line with agreed timetable.

 Conduct sample checks as part of the ICFR program to provide assurance over controls and risk mitigation measures, including sustainability of controls implemented by business management to address audit issues.

 Leading the management testing program areas such as scoping, scheduling, stakeholder management, workpaper review, etc., in communication with relevant stakeholders.
 Ensure that documentation supporting audit testing is sufficient, competent, and relevant to support conclusions.
 Identify risk, controls and process weaknesses, document main control points and provide evidential support for report recommendation.

 Monitor management’s implementation of audit recommendations and maintain a tracking system to ensure timely resolution and accountability.
 Prepare and present reports with well-documented observations, risk ratings, and practical recommendations to Management and the Compliance Committee.
 Elevate the importance of internal controls through training and technical assistance on internal controls, risk management, compliance, and audit readiness, and coach team through the methods for evidence and retaining evidence of controls.

 Bachelor's Degree in Accounting, Finance, Internal Audit or any other related fields.

 At least 2 – 3 years of leadership experience.
 Self-driven and self-managed with the ability to work independently, prioritize tasks, and meet established deadlines.
 Strong project management skills.
 Preferred but not required: CISA or CIA Credentials.
 Fundamental understanding of core Information Technology processes and systems.
 Knowledge of internal control concepts and frameworks (COSO), Sarbanes-Oxley standards, and auditing processes.
 Extensive experience in auditing Sarbanes Oxley (SOX) IT General Controls (ITGC), IT Automated Controls (ITAC), including testing the completeness and accuracy (C&A) of key reports supporting business processes.
 Experience with testing various systems and technologies, such as ERP systems, cloud technologies, and other enterprise applications.
 Strong attention to detail and accuracy in data validation and record keeping.
 Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate and resolve discrepancies.
 Strong interpersonal and influencing skills and communication, reports and/or analytics, internal controls, compliance controls, knowledge and exposed to IT, back office and/or marketing operations, preferably in the online gaming industry.
 Superior written and verbal communication, listening and presentation skills to effectively communicate with individuals at all levels of an organization.
 Exceptional interpersonal, negotiating and influencing skills to achieve win-win solutions.
 Demonstrated leadership and strong commitment to collaboration and teamwork with proven success inspiring teams to high levels of performance and engagement.
 Proficient with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint).

 Team player, collaborative, approachable, supportive, positive, open, patient, diplomatic and respectful.
 A confident, proactive and results-oriented individual with the demeanor, maturity, and intellect required to quickly establish trust and credibility.
 Exceptional interpersonal, listening, and conflict management skills. High EQ and self-awareness.
 High level of tact, discretion, and diplomacy in dealing with highly sensitive and confidential matters.
 Influencer, able to persuade others to action without absolute authority.
 Not afraid to express opinions and provide feedback in a balanced and constructive manner.
 Highest personal standards of integrity; strong work ethic, diligent, reliable and trustworthy.
 Organized, focused, and flexible in managing competing priorities; able to manage multiple complex issues, lead change management, drive multiple projects, work independently and deal with ambiguity.

 About This Role 
 The primary responsibility of this role is to lead leasing activities for a premier office portfolio located in Downtown Toronto. The portfolio consists of three assets totaling approximately 2.2 million square feet. The Vice President, Leasing will also support the Senior Vice President, National Leasing in managing the Greater Toronto Area (GTA) office leasing team, ensuring the successful execution of leasing mandates across the REMS-managed portfolio.

 Working closely with the Senior Vice Presidents of National Leasing, regional REMS leasing professionals, and brokerage partners, the Vice President will play a key role in developing and implementing leasing strategies across office assets ranging from Class AAA to Class C.  As part of an integrated real estate services platform, REMS operates within a highly collaborative environment.  Summary of Essential Job Functions

Reporting to the Managing Director, Subsidiary and Sustainability Reporting, you will lead CPP Investments’ group company financial reporting, legal entity management, subsidiary audits, and corporate accounting activities.

You will oversee financial reporting, regulatory compliance, and internal controls across global group companies, while strengthening governance, financial integrity, and operational efficiency. jobs.title: Director, Partner Solution Engineer
jobs.description:
About Docker 
 Docker has been one of the most loved brands in developer tooling, trusted by more than 20 million monthly users and over 20 billion container image pulls. From solo founders to the world's largest companies, developers rely on Docker to build, share, and run their applications across our suite of products including Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, and Docker Scout.

We are a globally distributed, remote-first team building the tools that define how software gets built and delivered. As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the sandboxed environments, verified images, and secure infrastructure that make autonomous workflows trustworthy by default.
 _______________________________________________________________________

 The Role 
 As Docker continues its rapid growth, we're seeking an inspiring and experienced Director of Partner Solution Engineering to lead a world-class team. Docker helps organizations solve complex challenges in modern software supply chains, security governance, and AI-driven development. This role offers the opportunity to shape how our strategic partners, including ISVs, CSPs, SIs, and VARs, adopt and deliver transformative technologies that make developers more productive and secure.

 As Director of Partner Solution Engineering, you will lead a high-performing technical organization responsible for driving partner enablement, joint go-to-market initiatives, and technical excellence across Docker's partner ecosystem. You will collaborate closely with Partner Sales, Technical Alliances, Product, and Engineering to develop scalable technical partnership strategies that help partners successfully integrate, sell, and deliver Docker's platform. Your focus will be on enabling your team to drive partner technical readiness, co-innovation, and mutual customer success while building repeatable models for partner engagement at scale.
 _______________________________________________________________________

 Key Responsibilities 
 Leadership & Team Development 
 Lead, develop, and inspire a team of Partner Solution Engineers, ensuring professional growth and high performance across multiple partner segments (ISVs, CSPs, SIs, VARs).

 Build and scale the Partner SE organization to support Docker's expanding partner ecosystem and geographic coverage.

 Foster a culture of innovation, collaboration, and continuous learning focused on partner success and technical excellence.

 Coach, mentor, and empower your team to engage effectively with diverse partner organizations and communicate complex technical concepts clearly.

 Partner Enablement & Technical Strategy 
 Establish repeatable processes and programs for partner technical enablement, including scalable learning paths, certifications, technical deep-dives, and integration workshops.

 Design and deliver both 1:1 strategic enablement for key partners and 1-to-many programs that drive adoption across the broader partner ecosystem.

 Create technical content, integration guides, architectural diagrams, reference architectures, and enablement videos tailored for partners.

 Develop partner-specific technical sales plays, solution validation frameworks, and proof-of-value methodologies that highlight Docker's differentiated value.

 Joint Go-To-Market Execution 
 Partner with the Partner Sales organization to drive joint account planning, co-selling opportunities, and "sell-with" and "sell-through" motions.

 Guide partners through solution design, technical validation, and evaluation processes to achieve joint customer success and sales goals.

 Support product positioning and technical validation during joint sales engagements, ensuring clarity on what's GA and ready for delivery.

 Define and track metrics for partner technical readiness, engagement quality, and revenue impact.

 Product & Alliance Collaboration 
 Collaborate with Product and Engineering teams to share Voice of the Partner, influencing roadmap priorities and co-building initiatives.

 Guide beta/EAP program participation with strategic partners, gathering feedback on new features and integration requirements.

 Work closely with the Technical Alliances team on roadmap alignment, technical integrations with CSPs and ISVs, and partner-driven feature requests.

 Champion regional partner technical needs and priorities in internal planning discussions (FedGov, EMEA, APAC).

 Cross-Functional Leadership 
 Collaborate with Field SEs to ensure alignment with market-specific requirements, share learnings, and avoid duplication of effort.

 Partner with Marketing to support partner events, conferences, webinars, and demand generation programs.

 Work with Sales leadership to define partner success metrics, performance standards, and technical excellence measures.

 Represent Docker at partner events and conferences as a technical expert and evangelist.

 Operational Excellence 
 Create an environment of continuous improvement focused on partner outcomes, operational excellence, and scalable processes.

 Develop internal enablement programs that enhance partner SE capabilities and share best practices across teams.

 Establish tools, systems, and workflows that enable efficient partner engagement and measurement.

 Build strong feedback loops to iterate on enablement strategies based on data-driven insights and partner performance.

 _______________________________________________________________________

 Qualifications 
 Required 
 8+ years of experience leading technical partner engineering, partner solutions, or pre-sales teams for distributed systems, developer platforms, or cloud infrastructure companies.

 Proven success in guiding teams that support channel partnerships, strategic alliances, and joint go-to-market initiatives.

 Minimum of 5 years in management, including hiring, mentoring, and scaling high-performing partner-facing technical teams.

 Deep understanding of partner ecosystems including ISVs, CSPs (AWS, Azure, GCP), Systems Integrators, and VARs.

 Strong experience in software supply chain security, security governance, DevOps, DevSecOps, or developer productivity technologies.

 Deep technical understanding of containerization, cloud-native architectures, CI/CD pipelines, and developer tools.

 Demonstrated ability to build scalable partner enablement programs (technical learning paths, certifications, workshops).

 Excellent communication and executive presentation skills, with the ability to build trust across technical and business audiences at both partner and customer organizations.

 Strong strategic thinking with proven ability to influence cross-functional teams and drive complex initiatives.

 Preferred 
 Operational experience with Docker, Kubernetes, or similar container-based platforms.

 Experience with application security principles and securing the software supply chain, including SBOMs, image scanning, and secure delivery pipelines.

 Background in software development, scripting, or infrastructure-as-code.

 Experience enabling developer productivity through coding assistants, AI integrations, or AI agent development.

 Familiarity with partner operations tools including Salesforce and enablement platforms like MindTickle.

 Experience working in both direct and channel sales models, understanding the nuances of partner-led vs. partner-assisted sales.

 Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field (or equivalent experience).

 Willingness to travel (~30% expected) to support key partner engagements and events.

 _______________________________________________________________________

 What Success Looks Like 
 30 Days 
 Successfully onboard, gaining familiarity with Docker's platform, partner ecosystem, and partner go-to-market strategy.

 Establish relationships with your team, Partner Sales, Technical Alliances, Field SE leadership, and key cross-functional partners.

 Begin shadowing partner calls, reviewing existing enablement materials, and understanding current partner technical capabilities.

 Learn tooling (Salesforce, Looker, Docker platform, PRM) and connect with internal stakeholders.

 90 Days 
 Develop and align a 12-month strategic plan with Partner Sales, Technical Alliances, and Product leadership.

 Begin executing key initiatives focused on improving partner technical readiness, enablement program quality, and joint sales effectiveness.

 Lead enablement sessions for selected strategic partners and support joint-account planning activities.

 Produce initial partner-facing technical content and establish your voice as a technical leader in the partner ecosystem.

 1 Year 
 Scale and enable a high-impact Partner Solution Engineering organization that drives measurable partner success and revenue growth through the channel.

 Own the technical strategy for one or more partner segments with documented processes, metrics, and success stories.

 Become a trusted advisor across Partner Sales, Product, Engineering, and Technical Alliances by championing partner insights and technical excellence.

 Demonstrate quantifiable improvements in partner technical closure rates, joint sales velocity, and partner satisfaction scores.

 Build a reputation as a thought leader in the partner ecosystem, representing Docker effectively at partner events and conferences.

 _______________________________________________________________________

 Why Join Docker 
 Docker is at the forefront of developer productivity and software supply chain security. As Director of Partner Solution Engineering, you'll have the opportunity to:
 Shape the technical strategy for how Docker scales through its partner ecosystem

 Build and lead a world-class team of Partner Solution Engineers

 Work with industry-leading partners including major cloud providers, security vendors, and global system integrators

 Influence product direction based on partner and customer insights

 Make a measurable impact on Docker's growth through the channel

 Collaborate with passionate, talented teams across Sales, Product, Engineering, and Alliances

 This is a high-impact leadership role for someone who thrives at the intersection of deep technical expertise, strategic partnership development, and team building. If you're excited about enabling partners to deliver exceptional outcomes for joint customers while building a best-in-class Partner SE organization, we'd love to hear from you.

 Visa sponsorship: Not available for this role.
 _______________________________________________________________________

 Compensation & Equity 
 All full-time roles include equity. Final compensation is determined on factors including but not limited to experience, skills, qualifications, and location.

 Canada: CA$327.6K– CA$468K OTE 
 United States: $226.1K – $323K OTE 

 ______________________________________________________________________

 Posting Information 
 Open vacancy: This posting is for an existing open role.

 AI in hiring: Docker may use AI-assisted tools during our recruiting process.

 Interview recordings: Candidates will be invited to opt in to interview recordings to support interviewer calibration and consistent evaluations. Recordings are optional and require explicit consent.

 ______________________________________________________________________

 Perks & Benefits 
 Remote-first by design – Work from your home, with offices in Seattle and Paris for connection and collaboration.

 Flexibility that fits your life – We trust you to manage your schedule while delivering great work.

 Time to recharge – Generous PTO, designated quarterly Whaleness Days, and a designated end-of-year Whaleness break.

 Home office support – Set up your workspace for comfort and success.

 Technology stipend – Equivalent to US$100 net per month to help support your work.

 Learning & development – Annual stipend for conferences, courses, certifications, and continued learning.

 Parental leave – 16 weeks of paid parental leave after six months of employment.

 Equity for all full-time employees – Share in Docker's long-term success as we continue to grow.

 Comprehensive benefits – Medical, retirement, and paid holidays vary by country.

 Docker swag – Because representing the whale never gets old.

 Docker is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a team that reflects a broad range of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe diverse teams build better products, make better decisions, and better serve our global community. 

 #LI-REMOTE

If you're driven to help reshape how banking works for Canadians and the businesses that power our economy, this could be your next big opportunity. 

We can’t wait to get to know you! 


Purpose of the Job
The Vice President, Integration Management Office (IMO) is accountable for the end-to-end execution of the Bank's enterprise integration, bringing two established Canadian banking businesses together into a stronger, more efficient and more competitive combined bank. The IMO holds one integrated master plan, central value case objectives & realization, and a central view of program budget, setting the standards, decision gates, data and reporting that delivery teams work to. The IMO operates through a matrix of employees and consultants across the Bank, with the central programme office team and dedicated consultants reporting directly to the Vice President.
This is a cross-bank role. The Integration Management Office is the connective tissue between the Executive Leadership Team, the executive sponsors who own each workstream's outcomes, the Board and its committees, the Bank's regulators, and the vendor providing transition services. The Vice President sets the cadence, the control structure and the reporting spine those audiences rely on, and converts complexity into decisions and execution plans.
The role is deliberately broad rather than deep. Executive sponsors drive the substance within their own domains; the Vice President is accountable for the integrity of the whole across critical path, value case, risk management, and outcome accountability, including the judgment of when to verify, escalate, problem solve, or hold the line rather than absorb the work centrally.
