 Model organizational values and commitments to diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility in leadership, collaboration, and decision-making.

 Requirements:

 You are a strategic and collaborative leader with substantial experience in learning, evaluation, research, or impact management, ideally within an international nonprofit, philanthropic, or social justice environment. You combine strong analytical capabilities with participatory and equity-centered approaches, and can translate complex evidence into practical improvements and compelling narratives for diverse audiences. The following qualifications and experience are expected:

 At least 9 years of progressive experience leading learning, evaluation, research, or impact functions.

 At least 5 years of people management experience, including setting direction, supporting staff development, and building effective teams.

 Demonstrated experience designing and implementing learning agendas and/or outcomes frameworks and ensuring their adoption by program teams.

 Strong understanding of participatory, equitable, and trust-based approaches to evaluation and learning, with a willingness to challenge conventional practices that may reinforce unequal power dynamics.

 Familiarity with feminist, decolonial, or other community-led approaches to research, evaluation, and impact measurement.

 Expertise in mixed-methods research, combining qualitative storytelling with quantitative analysis and synthesis across diverse programs or portfolios.

 Demonstrated ability to develop theories of change and practical learning and outcomes frameworks.

 Experience training and coaching program staff to integrate learning and data practices into their work.

 Proven ability to build a learning culture and facilitate reflection, collaboration, and evidence-informed decision-making across an organization.

 Exceptional facilitation, communication, and writing skills, including the ability to present complex findings to senior leadership, Board members, and donors.

 Strong commitment to equity, children's and young people's rights and wellbeing, and ethical data collection and storytelling.

 Ability to lead cross-functional initiatives, build trusting relationships, and support equitable participation and shared accountability.

 Experience working with grassroots, community-based, or youth-led organizations and individual changemakers across different regions is preferred.

 Familiarity with child and youth development, rights-based approaches, ecosystem perspectives, or life-course frameworks is an advantage.

 Experience in change management, strategy development, or organizational transitions is beneficial.

 An advanced degree in a relevant discipline or equivalent professional experience is preferred.

 Experience building or restructuring a learning, evaluation, or impact team is an asset.

 Familiarity with data and knowledge management systems, AI tools, grants management platforms, or CRM systems is desirable.

 Knowledge of Salesforce and its use for grants, data, or learning management is an advantage.

 Fluency in an additional language, particularly Spanish or French, is preferred.

 Knowledge of gender justice and/or climate justice, including relevant issues, stakeholders, and approaches to measuring change, is beneficial.

 Experience gained through lived experience, community work, or non-traditional professional paths is welcomed.

 Benefits:

 Annual salary range of $105,000–$140,000 for US-based candidates, depending on experience. Compensation for international hires is locally benchmarked according to location, benefits, and experience.

 Full-time, exempt position.

 International candidates outside the US and UK may be engaged through an Employer of Record, with benefits aligned with local employment laws.

 Comprehensive private healthcare coverage, including medical, dental, and vision insurance.

 Generous paid time off, including annual leave, enhanced sick leave, wellbeing days, sabbatical leave, and family-friendly leave.

 Flexible working arrangements, including remote, hybrid, and compressed work schedules.

 Pension contributions.

 Employee Assistance Services.

 Professional development opportunities, including training, collaboration, mentorship, and access to professional development funds.

 Team-building activities and social committees.

 Additional benefits may be available depending on the employee's location.

 An international, collaborative, and inclusive working environment focused on meaningful social impact.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Product Growth
jobs.description:
Define and execute product growth strategy: Own the overall product growth vision and roadmap, identifying opportunities to increase customer acquisition, activation, adoption, retention, and revenue across the platform.

 Orchestrate hybrid growth strategies: Partner closely with Sales to develop and optimize the product-led and sales-assisted growth model. Identify product usage signals that indicate when customers are ready for sales engagement and translate these insights into actionable playbooks that generate qualified pipeline.

 Drive customer activation: Design and optimize in-product experiences that help new customers reach value quickly, reduce friction during onboarding, and improve time-to-value.

 Accelerate customer expansion: Develop product-led expansion strategies and engagement loops that encourage deeper adoption, increased product usage, and stronger multi-product retention across the customer base.

 Grow self-service revenue: Lead the self-service growth strategy across transactional and subscription-based products, with a particular focus on measurement solutions, subscription upgrades, and seamless in-product purchasing experiences.

 Lead cross-functional teams: Manage and develop a multidisciplinary Growth team spanning Engineering, Design, and Data Science, with direct leadership responsibility for a Principal Product Manager.

 Build an experimentation culture: Establish a fast-paced, data-driven approach to product experimentation, enabling teams to test ideas, measure results, learn quickly, and continuously improve customer experiences.

 Own growth metrics and performance: Define, monitor, and report on key performance indicators, including activation rates, product adoption, expansion revenue, and net revenue retention (NRR).

 Leverage data and customer insights: Use product analytics, customer research, and behavioural data to identify growth opportunities, understand customer friction, and inform strategic decisions.

 Scale AI-powered products: Support the expansion of AI-driven product offerings by identifying opportunities to improve customer engagement, adoption, and monetization.

 Collaborate with executive leadership: Work closely with the Chief Product Officer and other senior stakeholders to align growth priorities with broader business objectives and deliver measurable commercial impact.

 Optimize growth across revenue models: Balance transactional and recurring revenue strategies while improving conversion, monetization, customer lifetime value, and long-term retention.

 Requirements:

 8–12+ years of product growth experience within B2B SaaS organizations, with a strong track record of developing and executing successful product-led growth strategies. Experience in vertical SaaS is a significant advantage.

 Demonstrated experience building and scaling hybrid product-led and sales-led growth models, with a practical understanding of how to align self-service customer journeys with sales-assisted acquisition and expansion.

 Strong expertise in customer activation, product adoption, and expansion strategies, including designing user journeys that improve time-to-value, engagement, and long-term retention.

 Experience managing both transactional and subscription-based revenue models, with a solid understanding of conversion optimization, monetization, and recurring revenue growth.

 Proven ability to lead product growth initiatives and manage strategic roadmaps that deliver measurable business results.

 Strong experimentation capabilities, including designing, launching, and evaluating product experiments, defining success criteria, and making data-driven decisions in fast-moving environments.

 Excellent understanding of product growth metrics, including activation rates, adoption, expansion revenue, customer retention, and net revenue retention (NRR).

 Strong analytical skills and the ability to independently investigate product performance, interpret data, and translate findings into actionable growth strategies.

 Experience with product analytics and CRM platforms such as Amplitude, HubSpot, Snowflake, or comparable analytics and data warehouse solutions.

 Experience building, launching, or scaling AI-powered products is a valuable advantage.

 Demonstrated ability to lead and develop cross-functional teams, including Engineering, Design, and Data Science, particularly in matrixed environments where influence and collaboration are essential.

 A hands-on leadership approach, with the ability to work alongside teams, provide strategic direction, remove obstacles, and support execution.

 Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to present complex strategies and performance insights clearly to executives, technical teams, and analytical stakeholders.

 Strong strategic thinking, adaptability, and commercial awareness, with the ability to balance customer needs, product quality, and business growth objectives.

 Candidates must be based in Canada or the United States.

 Benefits:

 Competitive compensation: Annual compensation range of $250,000–$300,000 USD, with location-based adjustments. Final offers depend on experience, seniority, demonstrated impact, and relevant market benchmarks.

 Flexible paid time off: Flexible vacation arrangements designed to support work-life balance.

 Additional time off: The first week of employment is dedicated to paid time off, allowing new employees to recharge before starting. Employees also receive one Friday off each month.

 Company-wide holidays: Paid company shutdown during the week between Christmas and New Year's Day.

 Healthcare coverage: In the United States, 80% of employee benefits premiums are employer-paid. In Canada, extended healthcare and dental insurance premiums are 100% employer-paid.

 Retirement savings: Access to RRSP matching in Canada and 401(k) matching in the United States.

 Parental support: Generous parental leave policies to support employees and their families.

 Remote-first culture: Flexibility to work remotely while collaborating with a distributed team.

 Home office support: Financial assistance through a home office setup stipend.

 Internet and phone allowance: Additional support for remote working expenses.

 Professional development: Learning and development opportunities to support continuous career progression and professional growth.

 Annual company retreat: Opportunities to connect with colleagues through company-wide retreats and team-building activities.

 Weekly paydays: Employees receive their pay every Friday.

 Growth opportunities: Join an ambitious, financially established technology business at an exciting stage of expansion, with opportunities to make a significant strategic impact.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Revenue Operations
jobs.description:
Lead revenue planning and forecasting: Own bookings forecasts, pipeline definitions, forecast categories, deal inspection, and pipeline health, ensuring consistent and reliable revenue visibility.

 Establish the revenue operating rhythm: Lead pipeline reviews, forecast calls, and revenue reporting for monthly business reviews, quarterly business reviews, and board materials.

 Oversee go-to-market planning: Drive territory design, customer segmentation, quota allocation, and sales capacity modeling.

 Manage sales compensation and deal operations: Provide input into compensation plan design and oversee accurate, timely payouts with appropriate financial controls. Manage deal desk processes, approvals, contract structures, and non-standard terms in collaboration with Strategic Finance.

 Own marketing operations: Oversee the marketing technology stack, pipeline reporting, and performance measurement.

 Build an AI-forward GTM roadmap: Partner with Sales and Marketing leaders to translate business priorities into a sequenced roadmap of AI-powered workflows and agents, determining where to build, buy, or configure solutions.

 Drive AI adoption and measurable impact: Set delivery milestones, monitor adoption, and report outcomes such as pipeline improvements, shorter sales cycles, and increased forecast accuracy.

 Own Salesforce architecture and governance: Set standards for the platform's core data model, architecture, sandbox environments, release processes, and complex development work.

 Maintain data quality and integration standards: Establish clear field definitions, validation rules, data hygiene practices, and correction processes. Partner with Analytics and Finance to ensure reliable data flows into the warehouse and business intelligence tools.

 Lead and develop the Revenue Operations team: Manage and grow a team of approximately 6–8 professionals across Sales Operations, Marketing Operations, Salesforce, and AI development, with clear accountability, coaching, and hiring practices.

 Set priorities and align cross-functional teams: Establish a transparent intake process, communicate roadmap priorities and trade-offs, and coordinate delivery expectations across Sales, Marketing, Client Operations, and Finance.

 Provide technical leadership: Stay closely involved in complex technical challenges, prototype new solutions when needed, and review architecture and implementation work while empowering the team to deliver independently.

 Requirements:

 At least 10 years of experience in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, or Go-to-Market Operations within a high-growth B2B SaaS or fintech environment.

 At least 4 years of experience leading teams and managers, with a track record of developing talent and scaling operational functions.

 Deep expertise in Salesforce architecture, data modeling, release management, and platform governance, including the ability to assess when to build, buy, or configure solutions.

 Strong financial and analytical capabilities, including revenue forecasting, bookings, unit economics, sales compensation modeling, and executive- or board-level reporting.

 Technical fluency with SQL, modern data warehouses, workflow and orchestration tools, and large language model (LLM) and agent-based technologies.

 Experience governing a shared technology platform used by administrators and developers across multiple business units, including setting standards for data definitions, architecture, and release management without direct authority over all users.

 Demonstrated hands-on experience using AI to transform go-to-market operations, supported by specific tools, implementations, and measurable business outcomes.

 Strong change management and stakeholder influence skills, with the confidence to establish priorities, manage competing demands, and address operational or data-quality issues with senior leaders.

 Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present complex initiatives clearly, lead executive discussions, and communicate decisions, risks, and business impact.

 A growth mindset, strong builder mentality, and comfort operating in an evolving environment with ambiguity and competing priorities.

 Nice to have:

 Experience with Python, agentic coding tools, or AI development workflows.

 Familiarity with modern data technologies such as Snowflake, dbt, and business intelligence or semantic-layer platforms.

 Experience with conversation intelligence or sales commission management tools.

 Background in payments, payroll, vertical SaaS, or businesses involving complex financial transactions and a combination of SMB and enterprise customers.

 Experience in the entertainment industry.

 Experience building a Go-to-Market Engineering or AI development function from the ground up.

 Benefits:

 Competitive annual base salary for Canada-based candidates ranging from CAD 183,500 to CAD 252,500, depending on location, experience, and role level.

 Unlimited paid time off.

 Remote work flexibility from anywhere in Canada or the United States.

 Health and dental benefits.

 Up to CAD 2,025 toward home office technology and equipment.

 Employer matching of up to 2% toward an RRSP or 401(k), depending on location.

 Learning and development opportunities.

 Up to CAD 67.50 toward monthly internet or cell phone services.

jobs.title: VP, Marketing
jobs.description:
As VP of Marketing, you will oversee the complete marketing function, establishing its strategic priorities, operating processes, budget, and performance framework. You will be responsible for building a measurable growth engine, strengthening customer relationships, supporting revenue generation, and ensuring consistent market positioning across all channels. You will combine strategic leadership with hands-on execution while working closely with cross-functional teams.

 Marketing Strategy and Performance

 Develop and own the annual marketing strategy, operating plan, budget, and vendor management processes.

 Establish marketing performance scorecards with clear KPIs, targets, and leading and lagging indicators.

 Track and report marketing-sourced and marketing-influenced pipeline, bookings, revenue, and retention.

 Own marketing attribution, lead scoring, lead handoff processes, and data quality across marketing automation and CRM platforms.

 Present marketing performance and strategic priorities during executive reviews and quarterly business reviews.

 Optimize the marketing technology stack, manage vendor spending, and ensure all marketing accounts and assets remain under company ownership.

 Align marketing priorities and service-level expectations with other departments on a quarterly basis.

 Demand Generation and Revenue Growth

 Develop and execute demand generation campaigns and account-based marketing programs to generate qualified pipeline.

 Lead customer expansion, adoption, and retention initiatives in collaboration with Customer Success.

 Translate product value propositions into business-case tools and ROI materials that support sales conversations.

 Build and maintain a database of measurable customer outcomes demonstrating the value delivered by products and services.

 Maintain proposal and RFP content libraries, including materials supporting public-sector and government opportunities.

 Conduct win/loss analysis and share insights with Sales, Product, and marketing stakeholders.

 Product and Sales Marketing

 Partner with Product teams on product positioning, naming, packaging recommendations, and launch readiness.

 Develop and maintain product sheets, presentations, demonstration materials, customer case studies, and competitive battlecards.

 Ensure consistency and accuracy across all customer-facing marketing and sales materials.

 Lead co-marketing initiatives with technology and channel partners.

 Equip Sales and Customer Success teams with relevant messaging, competitive intelligence, and business-value materials.

 Events and Customer Engagement

 Develop an annual event strategy and calendar, establishing investment cases and measurable ROI targets for each initiative.

 Manage national and regional conferences from planning through execution, including meetings, booths, customer receptions, and follow-up activities.

 Organize webinars, virtual events, and customer conferences.

 Support internal company events, including annual employee conferences.

 Measure event performance through meetings generated, pipeline contribution, costs, and post-event ROI reporting.

 Brand and Communications

 Lead brand positioning and refresh initiatives, ensuring consistent brand standards across all communication channels.

 Own social media strategy, public relations, thought leadership, industry awards, and customer recognition programs.

 Maintain accurate and consistent external company profiles across directories, analyst platforms, and industry data sources.

 Support employer branding initiatives and recruitment-related communications.

 Website and Digital Marketing

 Lead website redesign initiatives and oversee ongoing website performance, including traffic, conversion rates, and lead quality.

 Own search engine optimization (SEO) strategy and improve visibility across traditional search engines and AI-powered search tools.

 Manage customer newsletters, email marketing campaigns, and digital engagement programs.

 Internal Communications and Market Intelligence

 Manage the company intranet and oversee its content and updates.

 Develop leadership newsletters and company-wide internal communications.

 Coordinate customer surveys through a centralized process to ensure feedback is collected, analyzed, and acted upon.

 Transform competitive intelligence and market insights into actionable messaging, sales enablement materials, and product recommendations.

 Produce market intelligence reports following major industry conferences.

 Collaborate with Product and Sales to define ideal customer profiles and market segments across healthcare, military, corrections, and higher education.

 Represent the voice of the customer in product development, positioning, and pricing discussions.

 AI-Enabled Marketing

 Lead AI adoption across the marketing function, implementing AI-first workflows for research, content creation, campaign management, personalization, and reporting.

 Develop and deploy practical AI tools and agents, including workflow automation within marketing automation and CRM platforms.

 Establish quality assurance, brand safety, and data privacy standards for AI-generated content and marketing activities.

 Measure and communicate the productivity, efficiency, and performance improvements achieved through AI adoption.

 Strengthen brand visibility across AI-powered search platforms and answer engines.

 Team Leadership and First-Year Delivery

 Align team responsibilities and individual strengths with strategic growth initiatives to maximize marketing effectiveness.

 Review existing marketing vendors and tools, identifying opportunities to optimize spending and improve efficiency.

 Establish baseline marketing performance metrics and deliver an initial marketing scorecard within the first 90 days.

 Develop an annual marketing plan and budget supported by clear investment cases and measurable objectives.

 Lead a brand refresh and website redevelopment, ensuring delivery within agreed timelines and budgets.

 Build a library of at least 10 quantified customer success stories and establish an active customer reference program.

 Increase content production and campaign execution capacity through effective AI adoption.

 Requirements:

 The ideal candidate is a results-driven B2B marketing leader with substantial experience in enterprise software or technology environments. You should combine strategic marketing expertise with hands-on execution capabilities, demonstrating a proven ability to generate measurable pipeline and revenue growth. Strong product knowledge, analytical skills, and practical experience implementing AI-powered marketing workflows are essential.

 At least 7 years of B2B marketing experience within software, SaaS, or technology organizations.

 Demonstrated success delivering measurable business results, including improvements in marketing-generated pipeline, revenue, conversion rates, or customer retention.

 Proven ability to lead strategic marketing initiatives from planning through execution and measurable outcomes.

 Hands-on experience building demand generation campaigns and implementing pipeline attribution using marketing automation platforms and Salesforce or comparable CRM solutions.

 Strong execution capabilities, including personally creating content, developing campaigns, managing marketing automation tools, and analyzing performance data.

 Ability to make data-driven decisions, provide actionable recommendations, and take ownership of strategic and operational outcomes.

 Strong product marketing expertise, including the ability to understand complex enterprise software, deliver product demonstrations, and communicate customer ROI.

 Practical experience using generative AI tools in daily marketing operations, including building or deploying AI-powered workflows or agents and demonstrating measurable improvements in productivity, quality, or results.

 Experience leading major marketing transformation initiatives, such as brand repositioning, brand refreshes, product launches, or rebuilding a marketing function.

 Proven experience managing industry conferences and events as measurable business investments, with clear pipeline and ROI objectives.

 Familiarity with marketing technology and analytics tools, including:

 Marketing automation platforms.

 Salesforce or comparable CRM systems.

 Website content management systems (CMS).

 Web analytics and campaign performance tools.

 Strong communication, leadership, and stakeholder management skills.

 Ability to coordinate cross-functional initiatives and collaborate effectively with geographically distributed teams across different time zones.

 Preferred Qualifications:

 Previous experience managing and developing a marketing team.

 Experience marketing both on-premise and cloud-based software solutions.

 Background in healthcare technology, healthcare foodservice, or clinical nutrition.

 Registered Dietitian credentials or professional experience working closely with dietitians are considered a strong advantage.

 Experience marketing to healthcare systems, government organizations, or military buyers within complex, multi-stakeholder sales environments.

 Experience working in private equity-backed or holding-company software environments.

 Previous responsibility for internal communications alongside external marketing activities.

 Benefits:

 Competitive annual base salary ranging from $115,000 to $140,000, depending on experience.

 Additional annual performance-based bonus.

 Employee benefits package.

 Fully remote working arrangement, with the position open to candidates in Canada.

 Opportunity to lead and shape the overall marketing strategy of an established enterprise technology business.

 Significant ownership and influence over marketing operations, brand positioning, and revenue growth initiatives.

 Opportunity to drive AI adoption and introduce innovative marketing technologies and workflows.

 Collaboration with executive leadership and cross-functional teams.

 Exposure to diverse industries, including healthcare, government, military, corrections, and higher education.

 Opportunity to make a measurable impact within a growing technology organization.

jobs.title: VP, People
jobs.description:
People Strategy & Culture: Define and continuously evolve the people strategy in alignment with business objectives, growth plans, and long-term organizational priorities. Advise the CEO and executive leadership team on organizational health, talent risks, leadership effectiveness, and culture-related decisions. 

 Organizational Effectiveness: Translate company values into practical operating principles, leadership expectations, and decision-making frameworks. Develop organizational health assessments and action plans to improve employee engagement, leadership effectiveness, and business performance. 

 People Operations: Lead the People function's operating model, including team structure, resource allocation, prioritization, and service delivery. Build scalable HR processes, operating rhythms, and decision-making frameworks that support organizational growth. 

 People Metrics & Analytics: Establish and monitor key people indicators, including employee engagement, retention, recruitment effectiveness, and performance outcomes. Develop dashboards and reporting systems that translate workforce data into actionable business insights. 

 Remote & Distributed Work: Develop and continuously improve remote and hybrid work strategies, ensuring consistency, fairness, collaboration, and strong performance across geographically distributed teams. 

 Talent & Leadership Development: Oversee recruitment, onboarding, performance management, learning and development, succession planning, and employee retention. Coach managers to strengthen their leadership capabilities, establish clear expectations, provide meaningful feedback, and build accountable teams. 

 Mergers & Acquisitions: Lead HR due diligence for acquisitions, mergers, and strategic transactions. Develop and implement post-acquisition integration plans covering organizational design, change management, employee communications, and talent retention. 

 Employee Communications: Own the internal communications strategy and annual communication plans. Lead executive and organizational messaging to ensure transparency, alignment, and employee engagement during periods of growth and transformation. 

 Cross-functional Leadership: Partner with business leaders to align people initiatives with operational priorities, strengthen organizational capacity, and ensure effective execution of company-wide initiatives. 

 Requirements: 

 Significant experience in a senior People leadership position, ideally at VP or Senior Director level, within a scaling technology or SaaS organization backed by private equity or venture capital. 

 Proven ability to build a People function and establish scalable HR systems, processes, and operating models, preferably from an early-stage or developing organizational structure rather than inheriting a mature function. 

 Experience managing Canadian or cross-border workforces, particularly across Canada and the United States. 

 Strong business acumen and the ability to translate people strategies into measurable business outcomes. 

 Demonstrated expertise in organizational design, workforce planning, organizational effectiveness, and change management. 

 Experience leading HR due diligence and post-acquisition people integration during mergers, acquisitions, or strategic transactions. 

 Strong understanding of talent acquisition, employee engagement, performance management, leadership development, succession planning, and retention strategies. 

 Experience developing people analytics frameworks, dashboards, KPIs, and reporting systems to support data-driven organizational decisions. 

 Proven ability to lead and support remote and geographically distributed teams, creating effective collaboration practices and a strong organizational culture. 

 Exceptional communication, influencing, stakeholder management, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to advise and challenge senior executives. 

 Sound judgment, discretion, and the ability to navigate complex employee relations and organizational challenges. 

 A pragmatic, hands-on leadership style, combining strategic vision with operational execution, adaptability, and a strong sense of ownership. 

 Benefits: 

 Competitive compensation package based on experience, qualifications, and market benchmarks. 

 Employee stock options, providing an opportunity to participate in the company's long-term growth. 

 Comprehensive health benefits. 

 Flexible working hours and a remote-friendly working environment. 

 Three weeks of paid vacation annually. 

 Seven additional life leave days. 

 Two dedicated Level Up days for professional development. 

 One paid volunteer day per year. 

 Summer Fridays to encourage work-life balance. 

 Company-wide closure during the December holiday break. 

 Paid parental leave. 

 CAD $2,000 annual wellness and home office allowance. 

 CAD $5,000 annual professional development allowance. 

 Opportunities to experiment with innovative technologies and AI-powered tools. 

 An inclusive, collaborative, and performance-driven culture that encourages autonomy, accountability, professional growth, and new ideas.

jobs.title: Director, Brand & Growth - Mntd
jobs.description:
Knix is an award-winning intimate apparel and activewear brand that is re-inventing intimates for real life. Through our innovative products and our engaged community, we are empowering people everywhere to be unapologetically free.  Launched in 2013, we are one of the fastest-growing intimate apparel brands in North America and are globally recognized as an innovator within the apparel space.  We reach over 3 million customers through our online stores, Knix retail locations across North America and channels such as wholesale and Amazon.  We are revolutionizing the apparel industry with our best-in-class customer experience, innovative products and brands Knix, Kt by Knix, and Mntd.  Come join us if you are looking for a purpose-driven and authentic career!


MNTD is looking for a highly entrepreneurial, commercially minded brand leader to help build the next stage of the business.
This is a broad, hands-on leadership role for someone who knows how to build a brand and grow a business at the same time. You will own the day-to-day performance of MNTD while shaping how the brand shows up in the market, from growth strategy and digital marketing to campaigns, retail, partnerships, storytelling, customer experience and commercial planning.
You will operate with the speed and resourcefulness of an early-stage business, while having access to the capabilities, infrastructure and expertise of the broader Knix organization.
The right person is equally comfortable developing the strategy, reviewing a P&L, briefing a creative campaign, managing an agency, evaluating paid media performance, building a retail or brand partnership and jumping in to solve an executional problem when needed.
This role requires someone who creates momentum rather than waits for direction. You should be excited by ambiguity, motivated by growth and comfortable moving between big-picture thinking and detailed execution.

jobs.title: Director, Cloud Engineering
jobs.description:
Who We Are; What We Do; Where We’re Going
 
Magnet Forensics is a global leader in the development of digital investigative software that acquires, analyzes, and shares evidence from computers, smartphones, tablets, and IoT-related devices. We are continually innovating so our customers can deploy advanced and effective tools to protect their companies, communities, and countries.
 
Serving thousands of customers globally, our solutions are playing a crucial role in modernizing digital investigations, helping investigators fight crime, protect assets, and guard national security.
 
With employees based around the world, Magnet Forensics has been expanding our global presence. As a part of Magnet Forensics, you can expect to make a difference in the world, no matter what role you play. You’ll be supported through learning and development, not to mention an incredible team with unbelievable talent and integrity. 
 
If you think you would be the right person to join our team working towards this goal, we would love to hear from you! 


Role Overview
The Director, Cloud Engineering is responsible for the strategy, operation, security, governance, and financial stewardship of Magnet's cloud platform and shared engineering services. This Leader partners closely with Engineering, Product, UX, Security, IT, Compliance, Finance, and Go-to-Market teams to ensure our cloud platform enables rapid product innovation while meeting the highest standards for reliability, security, compliance, and cost efficiency.

This role combines technical acumen, operational excellence, cloud strategy, AI enablement, Financial Operations ("FinOps") discipline, vendor management, and organizational leadership. 
 
This is a highly visible leadership role responsible for ensuring Magnet's cloud platform remains secure, reliable, compliant, cost-effective, and capable of powering the next generation of digital investigation products.
 
NOTE: Candidates must reside in Canada.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Database & Operations
jobs.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

 What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

 Position Summary (Purpose of job):   

 The Sr. Director (M5) leads major divisional functions or corporate sub‑functions, providing enterprise‑level strategic direction, long‑range planning, and operational leadership across multiple related disciplines. This role analyzes external business environments to anticipate trends, influence strategy, and recommend growth opportunities for the business unit. It directs second‑level managers and Directors, ensuring operational excellence, cross‑functional integration, and execution of high‑impact initiatives. The Sr. Director is financially accountable for operating plans, budgets, and forecasts, and manages complex organizational performance across services, programs, and customer outcomes. 
 As a senior enterprise advisor, the Sr. Director interfaces with VPs and executive leaders to shape integrated business strategies and ensure alignment of products, solutions, and capabilities with organizational priorities. The role leads talent pipelines, strengthens leadership benches, and manages significant conflicts and disciplinary matters. It drives continuous improvement, optimizes cross‑functional workflows, and ensures strategic communication across stakeholder groups. The Sr. Director represents the function internally and externally, advancing McKesson’s mission through innovation, strategic influence, and enterprise stewardship. 

 Key Responsibilities:   

 Direct development and execution of integrated business strategies, partnering with VPs and senior executives to shape enterprise outcomes. 
 Lead strategic planning, prioritization, and delivery of large‑scale initiatives across multiple sub‑functions or locations. 
 Establish functional standards, governance processes, and performance metrics to ensure value delivery and regulatory alignment. 
 Oversee implementation of high‑impact technology, operational, and process improvements that enhance efficiency and customer satisfaction. 
 Serve as primary advisor to senior leadership on modernization, automation, cloud, and transformation strategies. 
 Manage divisional budgets, capital planning, cost‑reduction initiatives, investment decisions, and financial transparency efforts. 
 Direct vendor strategy, contract negotiations, service‑level oversight, and lifecycle management across platforms. 
 Lead long‑range workforce planning, organizational design, and leadership development programs. 
 Drive cross‑functional change leadership, ensuring communication and adoption of major transformation initiatives. 
 Provide thought leadership by assessing emerging trends, developing executive recommendations, and challenging conventional approaches. 

 Minimum Job Qualifications (Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities):  

 Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience; typically 13+ years of professional experience with 6+ years of diversified leadership, planning, communication, and people‑management responsibilities. 

 Highly advanced knowledge of enterprise operations, strategic planning, and cross‑functional leadership across large, complex organizations. 
 Expertise in governance frameworks, performance measurement, and enterprise risk and compliance programs. 
 Ability to direct multi‑disciplinary teams and serve as a senior advisor on technology, architecture, product, or operational strategy. 
 Advanced financial management skills, including budgeting, capital planning, cost optimization, and ROI analysis. 
 Executive‑level communication and storytelling skills for influencing VPs, C‑suite leaders, and external partners. 
 Strong capability to drive enterprise transformation, manage ambiguity, and resolve complex organizational conflicts.

 Senior Director, Network Operations

This leader will drive the maturation of people, process, and technology while delivering resilient, scalable, and business-aligned network services.

jobs.title: Sr. Director, HR Global Operations
jobs.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

 What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

 Position Summary 

 The Senior Director, HR Global Operations, provides strategic direction, integrated leadership, and end-to-end accountability across multiple HR Operations disciplines. Reporting to the Vice President, Employee Care, this role leads Benefits Operations, Talent Acquisition Operations, Workforce Administration (e.g., reduction in force, personnel records management), and specialized HR operational support.
 This role is an enterprise and operational leader, not the primary subject-matter expert or day-to-day practitioner within each discipline. The Senior Director leads through functional leaders and subject-matter experts, setting strategy, priorities, governance, performance expectations, and resource direction while ensuring each area maintains the technical depth required for effective delivery.

 The Senior Director translates enterprise HR strategy into an integrated HR Operations agenda and holds the collective organization accountable for accurate, timely, compliant, and employee-centered service delivery. The role creates the HR Operations technology and continuous improvement strategy, identifies cross-functional dependencies, resolves competing priorities, removes barriers, and ensures matters requiring specialized expertise are owned and addressed by the appropriate functional leader.

 As the senior HR Operations leader, the position advises HR and business leadership on service delivery, operational risk, workforce needs, process effectiveness, and employee experience. The role partners across Employee Care, HR Centers of Excellence, HR Technology, HR Business Partners, Legal, Privacy, Payroll, Finance, and other enterprise functions to strengthen controls and advance scalable solutions.

 Organizational Scope
 Benefits Operations
 Talent Acquisition Operations
 Special Workforce Actions Team (aka Workforce Administration)
 Specialized HR operational support, including Global Mobility & Immigration

 Leadership Model:  The Senior Director is accountable for overall strategy, integration, governance, prioritization, performance, resource direction, and talent across the portfolio. Functional leaders remain accountable for subject-matter expertise, technical decisions, and day-to-day execution within their respective disciplines.
 Key Responsibilities

 Portfolio Strategy and Leadership 
 Establish and execute the multi-year strategy and operating model for HR Operations, aligned with enterprise HR priorities, workforce needs, and business objectives.
 Set shared direction across Benefits, Talent Acquisition, Workforce Administration, and other assigned capabilities, relying on functional leaders for discipline-specific design and execution.
 Translate enterprise HR programs and policies into coordinated operational priorities.
 Define decision rights, service boundaries, escalation paths, and cross-team dependencies.
 Advise senior HR and business leaders on operational priorities, service trends, risks, capacity, and investment needs.

 Integrated Service Delivery 
 Direct overall delivery and continuous improvement across the portfolio, holding functional leaders accountable for their respective areas rather than personally owning discipline-level execution.
 Establish common governance, service standards, and operating rhythms while preserving appropriate functional ownership.
 Reduce fragmentation, strengthen handoffs, and improve the end-to-end employee and leader experience.
 Ensure complex matters are routed to the appropriate experts, resolved through clear escalation, and elevated for leadership decisions when required.
 Balance enterprise consistency with business, workforce, and jurisdictional requirements.

 Governance, Risk and Performance 
 Establish portfolio-level policies, controls, performance expectations, and governance practices that enable consistent execution and appropriate risk management.
 Convene and align Legal, Privacy, Payroll, HR Centers of Excellence, and other experts to identify and mitigate operational, regulatory, financial, and employee experience risks.
 Maintain leadership visibility into service performance, material risks, control issues, recurring defects, and remediation plans.
 Set organizational goals and measures across quality, timeliness, accuracy, customer experience, risk, capacity, productivity, and cost.
 Make cross-functional priority and resource decisions based on business need, service demand, risk, and expected value.

 Operational Excellence and Transformation 
 Sponsor modernization and simplification through process redesign, automation, analytics, AI-enabled capabilities, and improved self-service.
 Set cross-functional priorities with HR Technology and enterprise teams while functional leaders define detailed requirements and lead implementation within their disciplines.
 Identify opportunities to consolidate fragmented processes, eliminate unnecessary manual work, and create scalable practices.
 Use operational data, employee feedback, case trends, and control outcomes to direct continuous improvement.
 Develop operating plans, resource strategies, budget recommendations, and investment priorities for the organization.

 People and Organizational Leadership 
 Lead, coach, and develop a multi-disciplinary organization through functional leaders and senior subject-matter experts, preserving clear technical ownership within each discipline.
 Set clear expectations for ownership, collaboration, customer orientation, decision-making, and accountability.
 Build leadership capability, organizational depth, and succession readiness across Canadian HR Operations.
 Create an inclusive, high-performing environment in which leaders are empowered to make decisions and accountable for results.
 Assess portfolio-wide capability and make decisions on structure, roles, skills, capacity, and resource deployment as business needs evolve.

 Executive and Cross-Functional Partnership 
 Translate complex operational issues, risks, and trends into decision-ready recommendations for senior leaders.
 Influence priorities and solutions across teams where direct authority may not exist.
 Represent HR operational requirements in enterprise planning, transformation, and governance forums.
 Lead initiatives requiring coordination across multiple HR disciplines and stakeholder groups.

 Minimum Job Qualifications 
 Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.
 Typically, 13+ years of progressive professional experience in HR operations, shared services, employee services, talent acquisition operations, HR transformation, or a related discipline.
 Typically, 6+ years of diversified leadership, planning, communication, organization, and people-management experience.
 Demonstrated experience leading a portfolio of HR disciplines or operational teams through managers, functional leaders, and senior subject-matter experts; deep practitioner expertise in every discipline is not required.
 Experience establishing operating models, governance practices, operational policies, performance measures, budgets, and service-delivery standards.
 Demonstrated success leading complex, cross-functional transformation or continuous-improvement initiatives in a large, matrixed organization.
 Strong understanding of HR operational risk, controls, data privacy, and compliance considerations, with the judgment to engage the appropriate experts.
 Ability to use data, service insights, and cost-benefit analysis to guide priorities and improve organizational performance.
 Executive-level communication and influence skills, including the ability to frame decision-ready recommendations.

 Preferred Qualifications 
 Experience leading HR operations or supporting a geographically distributed workforce.
 Broad leadership exposure across two or more of the following: Talent Acquisition, Employee Care, Global Mobility, HR Case Management, or HR Shared Services.
 Experience leading HR service-delivery transformation, process automation, analytics, or AI-enabled operational improvement.
 Experience managing vendor-supported HR services or third-party relationships.
 Experience partnering with HR Technology teams on platform enhancements, integrations, workflow optimization, or digital employee experiences.
 Bilingual English and French capability is an asset where relevant to the supported workforce.

 Critical Leadership Capabilities 
 Portfolio leadership: Sets shared direction across distinct disciplines, enables functional experts to lead their areas, and holds leaders accountable for integrated results.
 Enterprise and country-level perspective: Connects enterprise HR strategy with Canadian workforce and operational requirements.
 Operational judgment: Balances employee experience, service, cost, risk, and compliance while engaging experts for technical decisions.
 Executive influence: Communicates complex operational topics clearly and provides actionable recommendations.
 Transformation leadership: Leads teams through operating-model, technology, and process change.
 Systems thinking: Understands how HR policies, processes, technologies, data, and services interact across the employee lifecycle.
 Talent leadership: Builds organizational capability, develops leaders, and strengthens succession depth.
 Data-driven management: Uses performance measures, service trends, risk indicators, and employee insights to shape decisions.

jobs.title: Directeur(trice), Conformité et éthique / Director, Compliance & Ethics
jobs.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care. 

 What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you. 

 ENGLISH DESCRIPTION FOLLOWS 

 Modalités de travail: Il s’agit d’un poste hybride qui exige que les candidat(e)s travaillent sur place au moins 2 jours par semaine dans notre bureau de Montréal. Les autres jours peuvent être travaillés à distance, selon les besoins de l’équipe et de l’unité d’affaire.

 À propos du poste (sommaire): 

 Relevant de la vice-présidence, Conformité et éthique (Canada), le ou la directeur(trice), Conformité et éthique exerce un rôle de leadership stratégique et est responsable de la mise en œuvre, de la supervision et de l’amélioration continue du programme de protection des renseignements personnels et de conformité de McKesson Canada.

 La personne titulaire du poste dirige les initiatives liées à la protection des renseignements personnels, à la conformité, à l’éthique et à la gouvernance afin de protéger l’organisation, de soutenir la croissance de l’entreprise et de favoriser une culture d’intégrité et de responsabilisation. Elle fournit une orientation stratégique sur les questions de protection des renseignements personnels, de réglementation, d’éthique et de conformité, et collabore avec les différentes unités d’affaires afin de cerner et d’atténuer les risques, de renforcer les contrôles et d’assurer le respect des lois, règlements, obligations contractuelles et politiques de l’entreprise applicables.

 La personne titulaire du poste est responsable de l’exécution et de la supervision des principaux volets du programme, notamment les programmes de protection des renseignements personnels, de conformité et d’éthique; la gouvernance des politiques; les évaluations des risques; la surveillance de la conformité; les enquêtes; la gestion des incidents liés à la protection des renseignements personnels; la formation et la sensibilisation; la gestion des mesures correctives; les relations avec les organismes de réglementation; ainsi que la production de rapports destinés à la haute direction. Elle traduit les objectifs stratégiques en solutions d’affaires concrètes qui favorisent une croissance responsable tout en assurant une gestion efficace des risques.

 La personne titulaire du poste dirige et développe une équipe de professionnel(le)s de la protection des renseignements personnels et de la conformité, et agit comme conseillère de confiance auprès des leaders de l’entreprise. Elle supervise les processus de gouvernance, notamment les évaluations des facteurs relatifs à la vie privée (EFVP), les initiatives de protection des renseignements personnels dès la conception et les programmes de surveillance de la conformité. Elle collabore également avec les Services juridiques, les Ressources humaines, l’Audit interne, la Conformité d’entreprise, la Sécurité de l’information, la Gouvernance des données et d’autres fonctions afin d’améliorer l’efficacité organisationnelle et la maturité du programme de conformité.

 Pour réussir dans ce rôle, il faut faire preuve de réflexion stratégique, d’un excellent jugement, d’une grande capacité d’influence au sein de l’organisation et d’un solide sens des affaires, ainsi que d’une capacité à diriger le changement dans un environnement complexe et hautement réglementé.

 Vos responsabilités: 

 Leadership stratégique et gouvernance 

 Mettre en œuvre les priorités de la fonction et superviser l’exécution de la stratégie de McKesson Canada en matière de protection des renseignements personnels et de conformité au moyen des programmes, initiatives et ressources confiés à la fonction.
 Fournir une expertise spécialisée et une orientation stratégique aux leaders des équipes d’affaires et des différentes fonctions en matière de protection des renseignements personnels, de conformité, d’éthique et de gouvernance.
 Piloter des initiatives visant à renforcer la culture de conformité, la prise de décisions éthiques, la responsabilisation et la sensibilisation aux risques.
 Collaborer avec les leaders de l’entreprise afin d’intégrer les principes de protection des renseignements personnels, de conformité et de gouvernance à la planification des activités, aux initiatives de transformation et aux processus opérationnels.
 Assurer le leadership et la supervision des instances de gouvernance et des activités de production de rapports.
 Évaluer, promouvoir et diriger l’adoption responsable de technologies émergentes afin de renforcer l’efficacité des programmes de conformité, de protection des renseignements personnels et de gouvernance, d’améliorer la surveillance et l’efficacité opérationnelle, et de permettre à l’organisation de concentrer davantage ses efforts sur les priorités à fort impact fondées sur les risques, tout en respectant les attentes réglementaires et éthiques.
 Établir les priorités de la fonction et superviser l’affectation des ressources afin d’assurer une mise en œuvre efficace des programmes, l’alignement organisationnel et l’évolution continue du programme de conformité.
 Diriger des initiatives de changement organisationnel visant à renforcer les capacités en matière de conformité, les pratiques de gouvernance ainsi que l’adoption, par les équipes d’affaires, des exigences liées à la conformité et à la protection des renseignements personnels.

 Supervision du programme de protection des renseignements personnels et de conformité 

 Diriger la mise en œuvre, le fonctionnement et l’amélioration continue des principales composantes du programme de protection des renseignements personnels et de conformité de McKesson Canada.
 Exercer une influence sur les cadres de gouvernance, les normes, les politiques, les procédures et les contrôles liés à la protection des renseignements personnels, à la conformité et à l’éthique, ainsi qu’aux pratiques connexes de gouvernance de l’information, et contribuer à leur évolution.
 Soutenir l’intégration de nouvelles unités d’affaires, d’acquisitions, de produits, de services et d’initiatives stratégiques aux cadres établis de conformité et de protection des renseignements personnels.
 Promouvoir les principes de protection des renseignements personnels dès la conception et superviser les processus de gouvernance en la matière à l’échelle de l’entreprise, notamment les évaluations des facteurs relatifs à la vie privée (EFVP), les examens de l’utilisation des données, les consultations en matière de protection des renseignements personnels et les évaluations des risques connexes.

 Gestion des risques, surveillance et enquêtes 

 Diriger les évaluations des risques liés à la protection des renseignements personnels et à la conformité afin de cerner les risques émergents, d’évaluer l’efficacité des contrôles et d’élaborer des stratégies d’atténuation.
 Superviser les activités de surveillance, d’audit et d’évaluation fondées sur les risques afin de cerner de façon proactive les tendances, les vulnérabilités et les possibilités d’amélioration.
 Superviser les enquêtes et les évaluations portant sur des préoccupations potentielles en matière de protection des renseignements personnels, d’éthique, de conformité ou de réglementation, et veiller à ce que les situations soient examinées, résolues et documentées de façon appropriée.
 Veiller à l’élaboration, à la mise en œuvre, au suivi et à la communication des plans de mesures correctives et préventives par l’intermédiaire des mécanismes de gouvernance appropriés.
 Surveiller l’évolution de l’environnement réglementaire et évaluer ses répercussions sur l’organisation ainsi que les stratégies d’intervention appropriées.

 Relations avec les organismes de réglementation et les parties prenantes externes 

 Soutenir la gestion des demandes de renseignements, des enquêtes, des audits et des inspections réglementaires ainsi que des obligations en matière de production de rapports.
 Collaborer avec les Services juridiques et les parties prenantes des différentes unités d’affaires afin de gérer les risques réglementaires et d’assurer des réponses cohérentes à l’échelle de l’organisation.

 Formation, communications et culture 

 Diriger les programmes de communication, de sensibilisation et de formation en matière de protection des renseignements personnels et de conformité afin de promouvoir une conduite éthique et le respect des exigences réglementaires.
 Favoriser une culture dans laquelle chacun(e) se sent à l’aise de signaler ses préoccupations et renforcer la sensibilisation, à l’échelle de l’organisation, aux mécanismes de signalement, aux obligations de conformité et aux responsabilités en matière de protection des renseignements personnels.
 Collaborer avec les Ressources humaines, les Services juridiques, la Sécurité de l’information, l’Audit interne et les leaders de l’entreprise afin d’offrir des formations efficaces et de mettre en œuvre des initiatives visant à renforcer la culture organisationnelle.

 Gouvernance des données et soutien aux objectifs d’affaires 

 Collaborer avec les équipes de Gouvernance des données, de Sécurité de l’information et des Technologies ainsi qu’avec les leaders de l’entreprise afin de renforcer la gouvernance de l’information, la gestion responsable des données, la protection des données et les pratiques d’utilisation responsable des données.
 Favoriser l’innovation au sein de l’entreprise en fournissant des conseils pratiques et fondés sur les risques en matière de protection des renseignements personnels et de conformité, afin de soutenir les initiatives stratégiques et les objectifs opérationnels.
 Promouvoir des normes de gouvernance cohérentes dans l’ensemble des unités d’affaires tout en conciliant les exigences réglementaires et les besoins de l’entreprise.

 Rapports et analyses 

 Présenter à la haute direction des rapports stratégiques et des recommandations portant sur la conformité, la protection des renseignements personnels, l’éthique et les risques.
 S’appuyer sur des indicateurs, des tendances et des analyses pour évaluer l’efficacité des programmes, soutenir la prise de décisions et favoriser l’amélioration continue.
 Communiquer à la direction les risques émergents, le rendement des programmes et les recommandations stratégiques.

 Gestion d’équipe 

 Constituer, diriger et développer une équipe hautement performante grâce à l’accompagnement, au développement des talents, à la planification de la relève, à la gestion du rendement et à l’engagement des employé(e)s.
 Établir les priorités, affecter les ressources et favoriser la responsabilisation afin d’atteindre les objectifs d’affaires.
 Promouvoir au sein de l’équipe la collaboration, l’innovation, l’amélioration continue et le développement professionnel.

 Exigences de base: 

 Baccalauréat ou expérience professionnelle équivalente.
 De 8 à 12 ans ou plus d’expérience progressive en protection des renseignements personnels, conformité, éthique, gestion des risques, affaires réglementaires, gouvernance, soins de santé ou dans un domaine connexe.
 Au moins trois ans d’expérience en leadership, incluant des responsabilités en matière de développement des talents et de réalisation d’initiatives complexes à l’échelle de l’entreprise.

 Capacité démontrée à exercer une influence auprès des membres de la haute direction et à diriger des initiatives interfonctionnelles complexes.
 Solide sens des affaires et excellentes capacités en matière de planification stratégique, de leadership du changement et d’efficacité organisationnelle.
 Excellentes aptitudes en communication, en animation, en présentation, en négociation et en gestion des relations.
 Capacité éprouvée à concilier la gestion des risques et l’atteinte des objectifs d’affaires dans un environnement hautement réglementé.

 Compétences et expérience privilégiées: 

 Maîtrise ou autre diplôme d’études supérieures pertinent.
 Titre professionnel en protection des renseignements personnels (CIPP/C, CIPM ou l’équivalent).
 Solide connaissance des lois canadiennes sur la protection des renseignements personnels, de la réglementation du secteur des soins de santé, des cadres de conformité et des principes de gouvernance.
 Bilinguisme (français et anglais).

 About the Role (Job Summary): 

 The Director, Compliance & Ethics reports to the Vice President, Compliance & Ethics (Canada) and serves as a strategic leader responsible for the implementation, oversight, and continuous improvement of McKesson Canada’s Privacy & Compliance Program.

 The Director leads privacy, compliance, ethics, and governance initiatives that protect the organization, support business growth, and foster a culture of integrity and accountability. The role provides strategic guidance on privacy, regulatory, ethics, and compliance matters, partnering across business units to identify and mitigate risk, strengthen controls, and ensure compliance with applicable laws, regulations, contractual obligations, and company policies.

 The Director is accountable for the execution and oversight of key program elements, including privacy, compliance, and ethics programs; policy governance; risk assessments; compliance monitoring; investigations; privacy incident management; training and awareness; corrective action management; regulatory engagement; and executive reporting. The role translates strategic objectives into practical business solutions that enable responsible growth while managing risk.

 The Director leads and develops a team of privacy and compliance professionals and serves as a trusted advisor to business leaders. The role provides oversight of governance processes, including Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs), privacy-by-design initiatives, and compliance monitoring programs, while collaborating with Legal, Human Resources, Internal Audit, Enterprise Compliance, Information Security, Data Governance, and other functions to enhance organizational effectiveness and compliance maturity.

 Success in this role requires strategic thinking, sound judgment, organizational influence, business acumen, and the ability to lead change in a complex and highly regulated environment.

 What You'll Do (Responsibilities): 

 Strategic Leadership & Governance 

 Implement functional priorities and oversee the execution of McKesson Canada’s Privacy & Compliance strategy through the programs, initiatives, and resources assigned to the function.
 Provide subject matter expertise and strategic guidance to business and functional leaders on privacy, compliance, ethics, and governance matters.
 Drive initiatives that strengthen compliance culture, ethical decision-making, accountability, and risk awareness.
 Partner with business leaders to embed privacy, compliance, and governance principles into business planning, transformation initiatives, and operational processes.
 Provide leadership and oversight for governance forums and reporting.
 Evaluate, promote, and lead the responsible adoption of other emerging technologies to strengthen compliance, privacy, and governance program effectiveness, enhance oversight, improve operational efficiency, and enable greater focus on high-impact, risk-based priorities while aligning with regulatory and ethical expectations.
 Establish functional priorities and oversee resource allocation to ensure effective program delivery, organizational alignment, and continued compliance program maturity.
 Lead organizational change initiatives that strengthen compliance capabilities, governance practices, and business adoption of compliance and privacy requirements.

 Privacy & Compliance Program Oversight 

 Lead the implementation, operation, and continuous improvement of key components of McKesson Canada's Privacy & Compliance Program.
 Influence and support governance frameworks, standards, policies, procedures, and controls related to privacy, compliance, ethics, and associated information governance practices.
 Support the integration of new business units, acquisitions, products, services, and strategic initiatives into established compliance and privacy frameworks.
 Champion Privacy by Design principles and oversee enterprise privacy governance processes, including Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs), data use reviews, privacy consultations, and privacy risk assessments.

 Risk Management, Monitoring & Investigations 

 Lead privacy and compliance risk assessments to identify emerging risks, evaluate control effectiveness, and develop mitigation strategies.
 Oversee risk-based monitoring, auditing, and assessment activities to proactively identify trends, vulnerabilities, and opportunities for improvement.
 Oversee investigations and assessments relating to potential privacy, ethics, compliance, or regulatory concerns and ensure matters are appropriately reviewed, resolved, and documented.
 Ensure corrective and preventive action plans are developed, implemented, monitored, and reported through appropriate governance channels.
 Monitor changes in the regulatory environment and assess organizational impacts and response strategies.

 Regulatory & External Stakeholder Engagement 

 Support regulatory inquiries, investigations, audits, inspections, and reporting obligations.
 Collaborate with Legal and business stakeholders to manage regulatory risk and ensure consistent organizational responses.

 Training, Communications & Culture 

 Lead privacy and compliance communications, awareness, and education programs that promote ethical conduct and regulatory compliance.
 Foster a speak-up culture and support organizational awareness of reporting mechanisms, compliance obligations, and privacy responsibilities.
 Partner with Human Resources, Legal, Information Security, Internal Audit, and business leaders to deliver effective training and culture-building initiatives.

 Data Governance & Business Enablement 

 Partner with Data Governance, Information Security, Technology, and business leaders to strengthen information governance, data stewardship, data protection, and responsible data use practices.
 Enable business innovation by providing practical, risk-based privacy and compliance guidance supporting strategic initiatives and operational objectives.
 Promote consistent governance standards across business units while balancing regulatory requirements and business needs.

 Reporting & Analytics 

 Deliver strategic compliance, privacy, ethics, and risk reporting and recommendations to senior leadership.
 Leverage metrics, trends, and analytics to evaluate program effectiveness, support decision-making, and drive continuous improvement.
 Communicate emerging risks, program performance, and strategic recommendations to management.

 People Leadership 

 Build, lead, and develop a high-performing team through coaching, talent development, succession planning, performance management, and employee engagement.
 Establish priorities, allocate resources, and drive accountability to achieve business objectives.
 Promote collaboration, innovation, continuous improvement, and professional development across the team.

 Basic Requirements: 

 Bachelor's degree or equivalent business experience. 
 8-12+ years of progressive experience in privacy, compliance, ethics, risk management, regulatory affairs, governance, healthcare, or related disciplines. 
 Minimum 3 years of leadership experience with responsibility for talent development and delivery of complex enterprise initiatives. 
 Experience identifying and leveraging emerging technologies to drive innovation, improve organizational effectiveness, strengthen risk management, and enable business growth in a regulated environment.
 Experience leading regulatory interactions, investigations, audits, monitoring programs, and risk assessments.
 Demonstrated ability to influence executive stakeholders and lead complex cross-functional initiatives.
 Strong business acumen, strategic planning, change leadership, and organizational effectiveness capabilities.
 Excellent communication, facilitation, presentation, negotiation, and relationship management skills.
 Proven ability to balance risk management with business enablement in a highly regulated environment.

 Preferred Skills/Experience: 

 Master's degree, or other relevant advanced degree.
 Privacy designation (CIPP/C, CIPM, or equivalent).
 Strong knowledge of Canadian privacy laws, healthcare regulations, compliance frameworks, and governance principles. 
 Bilingual (French/English).
