jobs.title: VP, People
jobs.description:
Rewind is a service that protects the critical data that powers businesses of all sizes. Our focus is on backing up data that lives in the cloud - in apps like Jira, GitHub, Confluence and Shopify. We are backed by Insight Partners, Inovia, Bessemer and Atlassian Ventures and are proud to be recognized as one of Canada's 50 fastest growing technology companies ( 2023 Deloitte Fast 50 ). We invite you to read our startup story to learn where we came from and where we’re going.
 Read about our mission, story and values here.
To find out more about our perks, click here.
Some of our Blogs might help you get a better understanding of what we do here. You can find them all here.
 Thriving at Rewind: 
 We embrace the fast-paced, ever-changing nature of startup life. If you love working with speed, agility, and creativity, you’ll feel right at home here. Here's what it takes to succeed with us:
 Team-First Mentality: We put teamwork at the core of everything we do, believing that we are better when we are together. Success is shared, and when the team wins, we all win.

 Performance-Driven Mindset: We are proactive, goal-oriented, and focused on delivering tangible, high-quality results. We go beyond meeting expectations - we aim to exceed them.

 Flexible Work-Life Approach: We encourage balance and understand the need to recharge. While we stay agile for urgent needs, we make sure there's time to recover and enjoy life.

 Customer Centricity: Our commitment to customers shapes everything we do. We listen, build relationships, and innovate - from our dedicated customer support team to our engineers, everyone at our company is focused on solving problems that matter most to our users.

 Taking Initiative: We value ownership and proactive problem-solving. We encourage team members to think creatively, take ownership, and lead improvements. Your ideas and actions drive our success.

 We Make Time for Fun: We work hard and make time to enjoy the journey. It’s not just about hitting milestones—it’s about making the experience rewarding along the way.

 Rewind's mission is to help businesses protect their most valuable digital assets. As we
 continue to scale, we are building the systems, leadership capabilities, and operating practices
 that enable us to grow intentionally while maintaining our culture and values.
 The Vice President, People, leads the design and execution of people strategies and systems that scale with the business. This role ensures our people practices, leadership capabilities, and operating model enable high performance, clear accountability, and sustained growth.

 You are accountable for translating Rewind's values into durable systems, meaningful people
 metrics, and a consistent operating cadence that supports how the company attracts, develops, and retains exceptional talent. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who enjoys building structure where it matters, challenging assumptions, and building culture.

 What You'll Do 
 People Strategy & Culture Stewardship
 Set and evolve Rewind's people strategy in support of company goals, growth plans, and long-term sustainability.

 Act as a trusted advisor to the CEO and executive team on organizational health, talent risks, leadership effectiveness, and culture decisions.

 Translate Rewind's values into operating principles, decision frameworks, and leader expectations.

 Partner with leaders to maximize the effectiveness of distributed teams and leverage the benefits of hybrid work.

 Develop and implement organizational health assessments and action plans that strengthen leadership effectiveness, employee engagement, and business performance.

 People Operations & Execution
 Own the operating model of the People team, including structure, capacity,prioritization, and delivery standards.

 Design and implement people processes and operating rhythms that support effective planning, decision-making, and execution across the organization.

 Align People team priorities with company objectives and business needs.

 Establish clear forums and cadences, including talent reviews, leadership reviews, and retrospectives that connect people insights to business decisions.

 Ensure leaders across the company have clarity on expectations, accountability, and follow-through as the company scales.

 People Metrics & Organizational Insights
 Define, track, and continuously improve People team KPIs, including engagement, retention, hiring effectiveness, and performance outcomes.

 Develop and maintain dashboards and reporting that connect people metrics to business outcomes and provide actionable insights to leaders and the executive team.

 Use people data and operational insights to inform discussions regarding organizational capacity, productivity, workforce planning, and organizational health.

 Provide strategic recommendations and action plans based on trends and emerging risks.

 Remote-First & Distributed Work
 Own and evolve Rewind's remote and hybrid work strategy to ensure clarity, equity, and consistency across teams.

 Design systems and norms that support strong performance, collaboration, and connection in a distributed environment.

 Regularly assess what is working, what is not, and where adjustments are needed as the company grows.

 Talent, Performance & Leadership
 Oversee talent acquisition, onboarding, performance management, learning and development, and succession planning.

 Coach leaders to be strong people managers who set clear goals, provide meaningful feedback, and hold themselves accountable.

 Support leadership development with a focus on execution, trust, and growth.

 Ensure performance management practices are consistently applied, including timely feedback, development plans, and decisive action when expectations are not met.

 Mergers, Acquisitions & Organizational Change
 Lead HR due diligence activities for mergers, acquisitions, and strategic transactions.

 Develop and execute people integration strategies, including organization design, change management, communications, and talent retention plans.

 Partner with business leaders to ensure seamless organizational transitions and achievement of business objectives.

 Employee Communications & Change Management
 Develop and execute the company's employee communications strategy and annual communications plan.

 Draft and oversee executive and organizational communications that support change initiatives, reinforce company values, and strengthen employee engagement.

 Ensure consistent, transparent, and timely communication during periods of growth and transformation.

 This role is open for candidate located in Ontario. 

 What You'll Bring 
 Proven experience in a senior people leadership role (VP or Senior Director level) in a scaling technology or SaaS organization that is PE or VC backed.

 Demonstrated success building and scaling people functions and operating models.

 Have built the People function, rather than inheriting a mature one

 Experience in a Canadian or cross-border (Canada and US) workforce

 Strong business acumen with the ability to connect people strategies to business outcomes.

 Demonstrated expertise in organizational design, change management, and organizational effectiveness.

 Experience leading M&A due diligence and post-acquisition integration.

 Experience supporting remote and distributed teams.

 Exceptional communication, influencing, and relationship-building skills.

 Sound judgment and the ability to navigate complex people and organizational situations.

 A pragmatic, hands-on approach and the ability to balance strategic thinking with operational execution.

 Compensation Philosophy 
The actual base salary will vary based on various factors, including market and individual qualifications objectively assessed during the interview process. 
 In some cases, we’re open to hiring at a higher level for the right person and are committed to paying competitively and fairly.
 If your experience is closer to an earlier career stage, we may still consider your application. In that case, we would evaluate the role at a different level within our levelling framework.
 Pay is just one part of the overall compensation at Rewind.

 Why join Rewind 
 At Rewind, you’ll help shape the future of data protection for thousands of businesses. We’re performance-driven, innovative, and not afraid to challenge what’s possible. You’ll join a team that values trust, accountability, and respect for people’s time — and encourages every employee to experiment, think critically, and grow.
 We support innovation through experimentation — including smart use of AI tools — and believe the best ideas come from those who aren’t afraid to push boundaries.

 How Rewind Will Support You 
We know that enjoying the journey is just as important as reaching our goals. We work hard to create a positive, inclusive environment where fun and laughter are part of our everyday routine. We also offer a variety of benefits to support your success both at work and in your personal life which includes but is not limited to: 
 Flexible work hours

 Employee stock options

 Health benefits

 3 weeks vacation

 7 life leave days

 2 Level Up days for professional development

 1 volunteer day

 Summer Fridays and office closed during the holiday break in December

 Paid parental leave

 $2000/year wellness/home office allowance

 $5000/year professional development allowance

 Rewind is committed to building an inclusive, supportive place for you to do the best and most rewarding work of your career. We value how each new hire is an opportunity for us to bring in a different perspective, and we are always eager to further diversify our company. We strongly encourage candidates of all different backgrounds and identities to apply.

 AI Usage 
 Our recruitment process may include the use of artificial intelligence–enabled tools to help manage and review applications efficiently. These tools assist our team, but hiring decisions are ultimately made by human reviewers.

jobs.title: VP, Revenue Operations
jobs.description:
Location: This role can be based anywhere in Canada (excluding Quebec) as a fully remote position. For candidates located in the Vancouver, BC Lower Mainland, there is flexibility to work remote, hybrid, or onsite at our Surrey headquarters. This role is also open to candidates in the USA as a fully remote position.

 Please note that employment is contingent upon the successful completion of reference checks and background checks.

Safe Software is looking for a VP, Revenue Operations to join our Revenue Operations team. As VP, Revenue Operations, you will design and enforce the operating model our entire go-to-market organization runs on, reporting directly to the Chief Revenue Officer and presenting regularly to the board. This is a builder’s mandate: the CRM isn’t fully configured, the forecasting process is mostly informal, the Rules of Engagement are still being written, and the AI tooling stack is unevaluated. You’re not fixing a broken system — you’re building the one Safe’s revenue org will run on for years. We have an immediate opening and are excited to find the right candidate to join our team. 

 About The Team 
 As a part of the Revenue Operations team, you’ll build and lead a function that’s still taking shape — RevOps analysts, a Sales Enablement team, and a broader GTM Enablement capability, five to seven hires in total. Safe builds FME, the only All-Data, Any-AI Enterprise Integration Platform, trusted by 25,000+ enterprise customers in 125+ countries to bring their data to life. Profitable, growing, and scaling toward $250M ARR with a clear path to $700M, Safe is building a multi-motion revenue engine — direct field, inbound and outbound BDR, partner channel, EMEA, and Canada — and it needs a single operating authority to keep those motions from colliding. That’s this role. You’ll report to the CRO and work daily with VP Sales East, VP Sales West, and the EMEA leader, each of whom has strong opinions and moves fast.

 What You’ll Be Doing 
 As VP, Revenue Operations, you will operate at all altitudes — one week presenting forecast accuracy to the board, the next telling a VP Sales their deal doesn’t meet the bar to advance stage, regardless of how the conversation started. Both are the job.

 Rules of Engagement — Ownership & Accountability 
 Write the rules everyone will actually operate inside. Safe is building a multi-motion revenue engine — direct field, inbound BDR, outbound BDR, partner channel, EMEA, Canada — and without clearly defined and enforced Rules of Engagement, those motions conflict, accounts get double-touched, partners get burned, and trust between functions collapses. You write it, socialize it across every stakeholder (including strong-willed VP Sales leaders who will push back), get it approved by the CRO, and enforce it through process design and CRM configuration.

 Define territory and account ownership. Who owns what account, what happens at renewal, how partner and direct conflict is resolved, and what triggers an escalation to the CRO.

 Set lead routing and BDR handoff standards. How inbound and outbound leads are qualified, assigned, accepted, and rejected, with SLA definitions for each stage and accountability for every gate.

 Design the partner co-sell and channel conflict policy. Clear rules for when the partner leads, when direct leads, and how sourcing credit is allocated, reviewed and agreed with the Partner Leader and EMEA Leader at launch.

 Hold the qualification gates. Define MEDDPICC field requirements by stage, what must be true before a deal advances, and what RevOps will kick back regardless of who is asking.

 GTM Enablement 
 Close the ramp gap. At Safe’s current hiring pace across AEs, BDRs, SEs, CSMs, and partners, the difference between a 30-day ramp and a 90-day ramp is a material revenue number — this role owns closing that gap.

 Build the function, not just the content. The Sales Enablement team reports directly into this role. You’ll build it, hire against a capability scorecard, and hold the team accountable to ramp and productivity outcomes, not just content creation.

 Design role-based onboarding. Structured, milestone-gated onboarding tracks for every GTM role — AE, BDR, SE, CSM, and partner — with clear ready-to-carry-quota certification criteria and a defined ramp timeline per role.

 Own the sales methodology and playbook. The single source of truth for how Safe sells — pitch structure, discovery framework, objection handling, competitive positioning, and deal execution standards — updated quarterly with input from the field and calibrated against win/loss data.

 Turn Gong data into a coaching loop. Use Gong and other tooling to create a systematic feedback loop from deal recordings and call reviews to enablement content updates, so the playbook reflects what actually wins, not what the last training deck said.

 Revenue Architecture & AI-Native GTM Stack 
 Give the CRO one version of the truth. Build the weekly, monthly, and quarterly forecasting process — call accuracy, coverage ratios, deal velocity — so the CRO walks into every board meeting with zero surprises.

 Own the numbers that matter. Pipeline model, funnel metrics, win-rate analytics, rep productivity, CAC payback, and NRR by segment and vertical, owned by you, trusted by the board.

 Evaluate and integrate the AI-native GTM stack. CRM (HubSpot), conversation intelligence (Gong), outbound automation, intent data, and agentic AI workflows — owning use-case prioritization, adoption, and value realization across the revenue org. AI architecture, security review, and governance decisions are made in partnership with IT and Engineering.

 Enforce data governance with teeth. Own the data model in CRM, ensuring field hygiene, account hierarchy, and MEDDPICC field consistency across every pod, globally.

 Executive Leadership & Cross-Functional Authority 
 Earn credibility through data, not hierarchy. Working with high-performing, highly opinionated VP Sales leaders is a feature of this role, not a bug — you’ll push back on a VP Sales who wants to move a deal to the wrong stage, enforce an ROE that a regional leader finds inconvenient, and do it in a way that preserves the relationship.

 Present to the board and hold up under questioning. You’ll present pipeline health, forecast accuracy, and GTM efficiency metrics directly to Safe’s board — output that’s clear, accurate, and defensible, from someone who can handle hard questions from investors without flinching.

 Own the cross-functional cadence. Finance, Marketing, CS, Product, and Legal all have legitimate interests in how the GTM org operates — you mediate those interests and own the QBRs, planning cycles, and headcount models that keep the org moving in the same direction.

 Leadership & Impact 
 This is single-threaded ownership of the operating system, not a shared function. You set the Rules of Engagement, own the forecasting methodology, and hold budget and vendor authority over the RevOps and Enablement tooling stack. When a VP Sales and the model disagree, the model doesn’t move without your sign-off — and you carry that authority directly to the CRO and, on a regular cadence, to the board.
 The board stops asking why the number moved. Forecast accuracy becomes predictable enough that variance is the exception the CRO has to explain, not the norm.

 The rules hold under pressure. Rules of Engagement survive contact with a strong-willed VP Sales who wants an exception — and when they don’t, that’s a deliberate call you made, not a gap they found.

 RevOps becomes a real team. What starts as a single-person mandate becomes a functioning function of RevOps, Enablement, and analytics talent that other departments route through by default.

 GTM tooling delivers measurable outcomes. AI and automation investments are evaluated against clear success criteria — rep productivity, pipeline data quality, forecast accuracy, and adoption rates — before scaling. Pilots that don't meet the bar are discontinued; those that do are operationalized.

 Qualifications, Skills, and Competencies 
 Safers come from a variety of backgrounds with a diversity in skills and knowledge. That said, we find that those who are most successful in this role have experience with the following areas.
 Required skills: 
 10–15+ years in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, or GTM Strategy at a scaling B2B SaaS company, at VP or Senior Director level with direct board-level exposure

 Experience building and enforcing a Rules of Engagement framework across multiple GTM motions, including the hard conversations with sales leaders who push back

 A track record presenting pipeline health, forecast, and GTM efficiency metrics directly to a board or equivalent investor group

 Experience holding strong field sales leaders accountable through data and rigor rather than hierarchy

 People leadership experience — hiring, developing, and holding accountable a multi-functional team spanning RevOps analysts and sales enablement

 Ownership of the full RevOps stack — CRM architecture, forecasting model, territory design, quota mechanics, and tooling evaluation

 Strong analytical range: comfortable building a bottoms-up coverage model, explaining CAC payback to a CFO, and translating rep-level data into a board-ready narrative

 Hands-on experience evaluating, piloting, or deploying agentic workflows or AI-assisted tooling in a live GTM environment — including the ability to assess feasibility, data readiness, and security requirements before committing to production

 Deep HubSpot or Salesforce architecture experience, including data model and process enforcement design

 Effective communication skills

 Desired skills / Bonus points: 
 Background in data, infrastructure, or integration software

 Experience with MCP, Salesforce Agentforce, Clay, or similar agentic GTM infrastructure at production scale

 Experience navigating a PE-backed or founder-owned growth inflection from $100M to $250M+

 Familiarity with partner channel economics and co-sell Rules of Engagement design

 Experience building a RevOps function from solo operator to a team of 3–5

 A Bachelor’s degree in a related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience

 About Safe Software 
 Safe Software transforms organizations with FME, the only All-Data Any-AI Enterprise Integration Platform connecting all your data, anywhere, at any velocity. 
 With over 30 years of expertise and 25,000+ enterprise customers across 125+ countries, we simplify your data journey, wherever it leads.
 Founded in 1993, Safe is headquartered in Surrey, BC with over 300 team members and counting. We’re always looking for talented individuals with diverse backgrounds who are determined to learn and grow. Are you ready to join the team?

 Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion 
 Safe Software is an equal opportunity employer and we truly believe that innovation and strength begin with diversity and inclusion. 
 We welcome all candidates regardless of race, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, ability, disability, national or ethnic origin, political belief, religion, or family status. 
 Should you require accommodations during the recruitment process, please contact hr_dept@safe.com.

 Notice Regarding Use of Automated Tools in Hiring 
 At Safe Software, we use automated tools to help us process applications and identify qualified candidates. These tools may assist in screening resumes and summarizing interview content based on the information you provide. This helps our team review applications efficiently while ensuring every candidate is considered based on the requirements of the role.
 Please be assured that the final hiring decision is always made by a member of our team. For more information on how we protect your privacy, please see our policy. If you have questions about this process, please contact us at hr_dept@safe.com.

jobs.title: AVP, Emerging Risk Management & Strategic Risk Initiatives
jobs.description:
You are as unique as your background, experience and point of view. Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered and challenged to be your best self. You'll work with dynamic colleagues - experts in their fields - who are eager to share their knowledge with you. Your leaders will inspire and help you reach your potential and soar to new heights. Every day, you'll have new and exciting opportunities to make life brighter for our Clients - who are at the heart of everything we do. 

 At Sun Life, we're driven by our Purpose: helping our Clients achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. Our values shape how we work: caring, authentic, bold, inspiring, and impactful.

 When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.

 Discover how you can make a difference in the lives of individuals, families and communities around the world.

 Job Description: 
 About the role 

 At the intersection of strategy, risk management and execution, the AVP, Emerging Risk Management & Strategic Risk Initiatives leads enterprise-wide capabilities and strategic initiatives that strengthen Sun Life's ability to anticipate, assess and respond to evolving risks. The role provides second-line leadership for emerging risk management, AI risk governance, risk culture and selected strategic risk initiatives. Working across Business Groups, Corporate Functions and Risk teams, the AVP translates strategic direction, external developments and internal risk signals into forward-looking insights, practical governance and risk management actions that support risk-informed decision-making across the organization. The role is flexible and future-focused, leading the development and implementation of operating models, methodologies, governance structures and management reporting that turn emerging or conceptual issues into practical and sustainable risk management capabilities. 

 What you'll need to succeed 

 More than 10 years of progressive experience in risk management or a related discipline, preferably within a major federally regulated financial institution.
 Significant experience leading enterprise-wide initiatives and influencing senior stakeholders across multiple businesses, functions and jurisdictions.
 Demonstrated people or functional leadership experience, including leadership through matrix reporting relationships.
 Expert knowledge of risk management within a large, complex financial institution.
 Strong understanding of first-line and second-line risk management accountabilities and the respective roles.
 Demonstrated ability to develop and execute enterprise strategies, operating models and multi-year transformation roadmaps.
 Proven ability to lead through influence across a federated or matrix organization and gain alignment among senior stakeholders with competing priorities.
 Has led or has exposure to the development of AI risk governance models in an organization
 Strong business and industry acumen, with the ability to assess complex and sensitive risk matters and provide pragmatic recommendations.
 Demonstrated experience developing executive and committee reporting that translates complex risk information into clear implications and decisions.
 Strong knowledge of regulatory expectations and leading practices relating to risk.
 Experience translating enterprise policy and methodology into first-line execution guidance.
 Strong knowledge of Sun Life’s products, businesses and operational risk environment.
 Exceptional written, verbal and presentation skills, including the ability to communicate with and influence senior executives.
 Strong change leadership, communication, negotiation, and decision-making capabilities.
 Demonstrated sound judgment and ability to operate autonomously in complex and ambiguous situations.
 University degree in business, risk management, finance, technology or a related discipline; a relevant graduate degree or professional designation is preferred.

 What you'll be doing 

 Risk Management Framework and Associated Governance  
 Identify where emerging risks, AI or other evolving risk management capabilities may require changes to the Risk Management Framework, risk taxonomy, policies, standards or related governance.
 Work with the AVP, Enterprise Risk Management and relevant policy owners to recommend and support appropriate changes while maintaining clear accountability with the applicable framework or policy owner.

 AI Risk Governance and Oversight  
 Lead the development and ongoing evolution of the second-line approach to AI risk governance and oversight, including the target operating model, governance forums, roles and accountabilities, escalation pathways and management reporting.
 Bring together relevant risk and policy owners to support coordinated identification, assessment and oversight of risks arising from AI across the Enterprise.
 Provide second-line risk advice, oversight and challenge on material AI initiatives, including risks arising as AI systems become more capable, autonomous or influential in business decision-making.
 Monitor developments in AI technology, regulation and industry practice and assess implications for Sun Life’s risk governance and capabilities.
 Support the integration of AI risk considerations into existing risk frameworks, policies, governance and business processes in partnership with accountable owners.

 Enterprise Reporting and Decision Support  
 Provide senior management and the Board with clear, decision-relevant reporting on emerging risks, AI risk governance, risk culture and other strategic risk priorities within the role’s mandate.
 Develop and maintain meaningful indicators, scorecards and analysis to identify trends, changes in exposure and areas requiring management attention.
 Prepare high-quality materials for senior leadership, committees and working groups.

 Emerging Risk Management and Strategic Risk Initiatives and Enterprise Preparedness 
 Lead the ongoing development, execution and enhancement of Sun Life’s Emerging Risk Management program, including horizon scanning, risk identification, assessment, prioritization, monitoring and reporting.
 Develop forward-looking insights on changes in the external environment, emerging technologies and evolving risk themes that could materially affect Sun Life’s strategy, risk profile or resilience.
 Lead the enterprise Risk Culture program, including its framework, assessment methodology, monitoring, reporting and continuous improvement roadmap.
 Partner with Business Groups, Human Resources and other Corporate Functions to embed risk culture considerations into relevant business and people practices.
 Lead and/or work with the AVP, Enterprise Risk management on risk interconnectedness analysis to understand how material risks, business activities and critical dependencies interact and where interconnections could amplify risk or impact.
 Convene leaders and subject-matter experts to identify material intersection points, dependencies, concentration points and potential blind spots.
 Use scenario analysis, discovery workshops and tabletop exercises, where appropriate, to test preparedness and identify gaps in decision rights, playbooks, capabilities, dependencies or resilience.

 Data & Records, Innovation and Risk Enablement 
 Support the Risk function in meeting applicable records management and OSFI E-21 data risk management requirements by strengthening how risk data and records are governed, managed and used, in partnership with EORM leadership and relevant data and information owners.
 Partner with Corporate Risk Operations and other EORM teams to advance data, technology and innovation initiatives that support strategic risk priorities.

 Leadership, Partnerships and Team  
 Build strong relationships across Business Groups, Corporate Functions and Risk teams and bring together diverse perspectives to advance complex or evolving risk priorities.
 Lead and develop a high-performing team, establishing clear priorities and accountabilities across direct, matrixed and project-based resources.  Currently supervises one manager who reports to this role, including setting objectives, providing ongoing coaching and feedback, and managing performance and development.
 Build team capability in strategic thinking, risk assessment, analytics, stakeholder engagement and execution.
 Provide senior-level risk advice and leadership on other strategic, emerging or ad hoc risk management priorities as required.

 Forward-Looking Regulatory and External Environment Insight  
 Monitor emerging regulatory and supervisory developments relevant to the role’s mandate and assess their potential implications for enterprise risk management.
 Work with relevant Risk, Compliance and Corporate Functions to develop a common understanding of material developments and potential enterprise implications.
 Identify developments that may require changes to risk governance, frameworks, methodologies, capabilities or oversight and provide EORM leadership with forward-looking insight to support preparedness.

 What's in it for you: 

 Being a member of the Sun Life family, a group of people united by our Purpose: to help Clients and Employees achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives.
 In 2024, Sun Life ranked among the top 100 most sustainable global corporations by Corporate Knights for the 15th consecutive year, leading Canadian insurers.
 We are proud to be on the 2024 Best Workplaces in Canada list by Great Place to Work.
 We’re also listed as one of the Best Workplaces for Women and Best Workplaces with Most Trusted Executive Teams.
 Our unique Sabbatical Program gives you the opportunity to take up to 6 weeks off, every five years.
 Care Days available for self-care or care of others (i.e., family or others you may support) and Sick Days to support your well-being.

 The Base Pay range is for the primary location for which the job is posted. It may vary depending on the work location of the successful candidate or other factors. In addition to Base Pay, eligible Sun Life employees participate in various incentive plans, payment under which is discretionary and subject to individual and company performance. Certain sales focused roles have sales incentive plans based on individual or group sales results. 

 Diversity and inclusion have always been at the core of our values at Sun Life. A diverse workforce with wide perspectives and creative ideas benefits our Clients, the communities where we operate and all of us as colleagues. We welcome applications from qualified individuals from all backgrounds.

 Persons with disabilities who need accommodation in the application process, or those needing job postings in an alternative format, may e-mail a request to thebrightside@sunlife.com.

 We are proud to be a hybrid organization that offers our employees the choice and flexibility to work from both the office and virtually based on the needs of the business, our Clients and you.

 We may use artificial intelligence to support candidate sourcing, screening, interview scheduling. 

 We thank all applicants for showing an interest in this position. Only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

155,000/155 000 - 225,000/225 000

jobs.description:
You are as unique as your background, experience and point of view. Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered and challenged to be your best self. You'll work with dynamic colleagues - experts in their fields - who are eager to share their knowledge with you. Your leaders will inspire and help you reach your potential and soar to new heights. Every day, you'll have new and exciting opportunities to make life brighter for our Clients - who are at the heart of everything we do. 

 At Sun Life, we're driven by our Purpose: helping our Clients achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. Our values shape how we work: caring, authentic, bold, inspiring, and impactful.

 When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.

 Discover how you can make a difference in the lives of individuals, families and communities around the world.

 Job Description: 
 The incumbent is responsible for the oversight and delivery of risk-based internal audits across areas relating to global Technology Infrastructure, Cyber and Physical Security, Digital & Data, and Technology & Cyber Risk Management. The audit scope is global and covers both First and Second Line of Defence processes and controls. The role reports to the AVP, IT Audit, and leads a global team of 5+ individuals.

 What will you do: 

 For assigned areas, the scope of responsibilities includes the operational delivery of all IT audit work, audit plan development and coverage, IT audit universe risk assessments to ensure adequate audit coverage of key risks, as well as client relationship management and management of the audit team.
 Identify emerging and heightened risks related to technology and cyber security that affect the company.
 Contribute to the development of audit strategy and direction.
 Continuously improve audit delivery and quality through increased use of AI, data analytics and innovation.
 Plan and direct audits and special engagements following Sun Life’s Audit methodology; deliver audit reports and findings that clearly articulate the position of risks and issues.
 Provide subject matter expertise as it relates to technology, cyber security and information risk management processes to other audit teams.
 Provide leadership in discussions of risk assessment, internal control and audit findings with clients.
 Stay actively engaged with the latest technologies, regulations and cyber trends.
 Influence management to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of operations, risk management practices and the control environment with respect to technology, cyber security and information risk management.
 Lead a global audit team with a focus on building and maintaining a high-performing team of auditors, including the recruitment, administration, development and retention of staff through strong leadership and coaching.

 What You’ll Need to Succeed

Zafin is an AI platform company helping regulated institutions modernize how critical work is designed, governed, and delivered. Our technology enables organizations to move faster while maintaining the governance, accountability, and control required in highly regulated environments.

 Our portfolio includes Zafin AIOS, an agent orchestration platform for governed AI work; the Zafin Banking Platform, which helps banks modernize product, pricing, offers, billing, loyalty, and relationship management; and Zafin IO, an integration platform that connects data, systems, and workflows across complex enterprise environments.

 Headquartered in Toronto, Canada, Zafin partners with leading financial institutions across North America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Asia-Pacific. As AI transforms the future of financial services, we're building the platforms that help regulated organizations adopt AI responsibly and at scale.

 What is the Opportunity?

 Lead the FinOps function. As Director, FinOps (Cloud Financial Management), you will shape and advance Zafin’s cloud financial management strategy. You will build and lead a scalable FinOps function that delivers measurable, sustainable cost savings while safeguarding platform reliability, security, and engineering productivity.

 Shape cloud investment decisions. You will define how Zafin manages and optimizes cloud investments across its banking technology platforms. Working with Engineering, Cloud Operations, Product, and Finance, you will strengthen financial accountability, increase cost visibility, and embed cost-conscious decision-making across technology and business operations.

 Apply AI and automation. You will use AI-driven analytics, automation, and intelligent cost monitoring to improve forecasting, identify optimization opportunities, detect spending anomalies, and strengthen cloud financial governance.

 Deliver sustainable business value. Your leadership will improve cloud cost efficiency and financial predictability, ensuring Zafin’s cloud investments generate lasting value.

 What Will You Do?

 Define and lead Zafin’s FinOps strategy, governance framework, and cloud cost optimization program across Microsoft Azure and platform services.

 Deliver measurable cloud savings through resource optimization, improved utilization, cost avoidance, and stronger financial accountability.

 Lead cloud budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis, and financial reporting to increase cost visibility and improve predictability.

 Partner with Engineering, Cloud Operations, Product, and Finance to embed cost-efficient practices in architecture, infrastructure, and operational decisions.

 Optimize Azure infrastructure spending across compute, storage, networking, AKS/Kubernetes, Reserved Instances, and observability services.

jobs.title: Director of Ecommerce Growth
jobs.description:
At Hadley Designs, we believe early learning should be joyful, screen-free, and filled with connection.
 Founded by Becca Hadley, a former teacher and mom who began creating hand-drawn learning tools at her kitchen table, we’ve grown into a leading early childhood education brand trusted by millions of parents, grandparents, and teachers. Our products are developmentally sound, emotionally engaging, and intentionally designed to help children ages 3–8 grow curious, confident, and resilient.
 We serve busy, intentional families who are tired of screens and want more meaningful ways to teach and connect with their kids. From educational posters to busy books, handwriting guides to emotional learning kits, every product is crafted with care and rooted in research.
 Our vision is bold: to become the most trusted children’s brand in the world, present in millions of homes, and passed down for generations, while reaching $100 million in annual revenue by 2030.
 Today, Hadley Designs is an approximately $25 million ecommerce brand selling across Amazon, Shopify, TikTok Shop, and other channels. We've built a strong foundation, an established customer base, and a talented team of specialists. Now, our next chapter is about building a repeatable, profitable growth engine that can take us from $25 million to $100 million and beyond.
 We're looking for an entrepreneurial Director of Ecommerce Growth who has helped scale ecommerce brands before and knows how to turn growth opportunities into measurable business results. Someone who can see the bigger picture, connect the dots across channels, align talented teams, and determine where to invest, what to scale, and what to stop.
 This is an opportunity to take meaningful ownership of our growth strategy, build systems that consistently generate profitable demand, and help shape the next stage of Hadley Designs.

 Role Overview 
 The Director of Ecommerce Growth is responsible for building and leading Hadley Designs' next phase of profitable growth, developing a repeatable demand generation engine that can scale our business from $25 million to $100 million and beyond.
 This is a hands-on growth leadership role that combines strategic thinking, financial accountability, and cross-functional execution. We're looking for someone who thinks like an entrepreneur, understands the economics of scaling an ecommerce brand, and knows how to turn promising opportunities into profitable, repeatable growth systems.
 We've built a talented team of specialists across Amazon, Shopify, TikTok Shop, paid media, creative, and affiliate marketing. The Director of Ecommerce Growth connects the dots between these functions, aligning priorities, coordinating execution, removing bottlenecks, and ensuring our investments translate into measurable business results.
 This person doesn't need to be the best specialist in every channel, but they must know how to lead specialists, challenge assumptions, diagnose performance, and make the entire growth engine more effective. They take ownership of growth initiatives from strategy through execution, without relying on the CEO to drive every decision.
 The role is channel agnostic. We don't care whether our next major growth opportunity comes from Meta advertising, Amazon external traffic, Shopify, TikTok Shop, creator partnerships, AI-powered content, or an entirely new channel. What matters is identifying where the greatest opportunities exist, validating them through disciplined experimentation, and allocating resources toward what produces profitable, incremental growth.
 Equally important is knowing what not to pursue. The Director of Ecommerce Growth must be willing to challenge existing strategies, stop underperforming initiatives, and redirect resources toward higher potential opportunities.
 The vision: Build a diversified, scalable, and profitable growth engine that consistently generates new customer demand, turns successful experiments into repeatable systems, and operates without requiring the CEO's daily involvement, ultimately helping Hadley Designs become a $100 million brand by 2030.

Metrics that You'll Own 
 Incremental Contribution Profit: Generate at least $1,000,000 in annual incremental contribution profit from growth initiatives, after all attributable variable marketing and program costs.
 Incremental Demand Generation Revenue: Generate at least $7,000,000 in annual incremental revenue through paid media, affiliate marketing, creator partnerships, and new acquisition channels, regardless of whether customers purchase through Amazon, Shopify, or TikTok Shop.
 Marketing Efficiency Ratio (MER): Achieve a minimum 3.0x blended MER across the defined growth portfolio, while meeting contribution profit targets. Final target subject to validated channel economics.
 Growth Experiments: Execute at least 1 meaningful growth experiments per month (12 annually), each with a documented hypothesis, an approved budget, contribution profit target, performance review, and predefined stop criteria.
 Scalable Growth Engines: From the list of 12 growth experiments, at least 3 new experiments are repeatable, profitable growth engines annually, each generating at least $25,000 in incremental monthly revenue with positive contribution profit for three consecutive months.

 Primary Objectives 20% BIG ROCKS – These must be done first and at all costs.
 Build a Repeatable, Profitable Demand Generation Engine: Develop and scale sustainable sources of customer acquisition and revenue across Amazon, Shopify, TikTok Shop, paid media, affiliates, and emerging channels, prioritizing incremental contribution profit over revenue alone.
 Integrate and Lead Cross-Functional Growth Execution: Align existing specialists across creative, paid media, ecommerce, affiliates, and analytics around shared priorities. Own execution plans, remove bottlenecks, and ensure growth initiatives deliver measurable results without requiring the CEO's daily involvement.
 Own Growth Strategy and Marketing Investment Efficiency: Evaluate marketing performance using contribution margin, MER, acquisition costs, and incremental revenue. Determine where to allocate resources, what to double down on, and what to reduce or stop to maximize profitable growth.
 Build a Disciplined Growth Experimentation System: Identify new growth opportunities, launch at least 1 measurable experiment monthly, and systematically evaluate results. Turn winning experiments into repeatable, scalable growth systems while quickly discontinuing underperforming initiatives.
 Optimize Affiliate, Influencer, and Cross-Channel Demand Generation: Develop a profitable creator and affiliate strategy that connects TikTok Shop, Amazon, Shopify, and paid media. Ensure winning creator content, partnerships, and emerging AI opportunities are integrated into the broader growth strategy rather than operating as isolated programs.

 Regular Work Activities 80% – These must be done ongoing daily/weekly after the BIG ROCKS are complete. 
 GROWTH STRATEGY & PERFORMANCE 
 Monitor growth performance across Amazon, Shopify, TikTok Shop, paid media, affiliates, and emerging acquisition channels.
 Identify opportunities to increase profitable revenue through improved customer acquisition, conversion rates, offers, retention, and demand generation.
 Evaluate competitive strategies, emerging marketing trends, AI technologies, and new acquisition channels to identify opportunities worth testing.
 Maintain a prioritized pipeline of growth opportunities based on potential financial impact, resources required, and probability of success.
 Challenge existing strategies and recommend where to increase investment, improve execution, or discontinue underperforming initiatives.
 MARKETING ECONOMICS & CAPITAL ALLOCATION 
 Own the performance of the growth investment portfolio, including budgets, incremental revenue, marketing costs, and contribution profit.
 Review marketing efficiency ratio (MER), customer acquisition costs, conversion rates, and contribution margins across relevant channels.
 Work with Finance and Analytics to validate attribution, incremental performance, and profitability.
 Allocate approved marketing and experimentation budgets toward the highest potential growth opportunities.
 Identify inefficient spending and make timely decisions to scale, optimize, or stop initiatives.
 Ensure marketing investments are evaluated based on actual business outcomes rather than attributed revenue or platform ROAS alone.
 CROSS-FUNCTIONAL GROWTH LEADERSHIP 
 Coordinate growth initiatives across Shopify, Amazon, TikTok Shop, paid media, creative, affiliates, and analytics.
 Establish clear priorities, responsibilities, deadlines, and measurable outcomes for cross-functional growth projects.
 Lead weekly growth meetings focused on performance, bottlenecks, opportunities, and decisions.
 Ensure creative strategies, offers, customer acquisition campaigns, and product launches are aligned across relevant channels.
 Remove execution bottlenecks and hold initiative owners accountable for delivering results.
 Connect insights and winning strategies between teams so successful ideas can be tested and scaled across channels.
 GROWTH EXPERIMENTATION & EXECUTION 
 Launch and oversee at least 1 meaningful growth experiment monthly, each with a documented hypothesis, budget, owner, and success criteria.
 Coordinate experiment execution through existing specialists, internal teams, and external partners.
 Review results and distinguish meaningful performance improvements from temporary fluctuations or attribution noise.
 Document learnings and make clear decisions to scale, improve, continue testing, or stop each initiative.
 Turn successful experiments into repeatable growth systems with clear ownership and operating procedures.
 Maintain a centralized growth experiment tracker and prioritized testing roadmap.
 AFFILIATE, INFLUENCER & CREATOR GROWTH 
 Oversee the strategy and profitability of the affiliate and influencer program across TikTok Shop, Amazon, and Shopify.
 Evaluate creator acquisition, activation, retention, commissions, samples, incentives, and program economics.
 Direct the affiliate operations team to improve creator productivity and program profitability.
 Identify opportunities to develop high-value creator partnerships and expand creator driven demand generation.
 Ensure winning creator content is systematically shared with paid media teams and tested across appropriate channels.
 Integrate affiliate marketing, creator content, and AI influencer strategies into the broader growth engine.
 AGENCY, PARTNER & TEAM MANAGEMENT 
 Evaluate, select, and manage external marketing agencies, technology providers, and strategic growth partners.
 Establish clear performance expectations, financial targets, and accountability for outside partners.
 Lead growth initiatives through existing channel specialists without creating unnecessary management layers.
 Identify talent gaps and recommend additional resources when supported by clear financial opportunities.
 Develop systems and team capabilities that reduce dependence on the CEO for daily growth decisions.
 SYSTEMS, ANALYTICS & AI 
 Work with Analytics to maintain reliable marketing performance dashboards and growth scorecards.
 Ensure marketing and financial data is accurate, actionable, and consistently measured across channels.
 Use AI and automation to accelerate market research, competitive analysis, creative testing, reporting, and growth execution.
 Identify repetitive growth workflows that can be automated or delegated.
 Maintain documentation, SOPs, and historical experiment results so successful strategies can be repeated and improved.
 REPORTING & ACCOUNTABILITY 
 Weekly Growth Scorecard: Revenue, incremental contribution profit, MER, marketing spend, active experiments, emerging winners, underperforming initiatives, and recommended actions.
 Weekly Growth Meeting: Review performance with relevant specialists, resolve bottlenecks, assign priorities, and make decisions without requiring the CEO to lead the discussion.
 Monthly Growth Investment Review: Evaluate the growth portfolio, recommend budget reallocations, and identify opportunities to scale or discontinue.

jobs.title: Director, Computational DMPK (Drug Metabolism & Pharmacokinetics)
jobs.description:
Deep Origin is a biotechnology company building an operating system for science that transforms how life science research is conducted. Our AI-powered platforms simulate biology, streamline R&D workflows, and enable scientists to model complex biological systems at scale. 
 Deep Origin leads the PREDICTS consortium, funded by ARPA-H under the CATALYST program, to build in silico models that predict human drug safety and toxicity. As part of this work we are scaling our capabilities in whole-human modeling and predictive toxicology. 

About the role
 Deep Origin is building VHAT, the Virtual Human Avatars of Toxicology. VHAT takes a molecule, a dose and a patient population and predicts organ-level human toxicity before a compound is synthesized or dosed. Metabolism sits at the heart of that chain. What a drug becomes, which enzymes act on it and how fast they act determine what each organ is exposed to, and every predicted metabolite is screened for its own off-target and organ liabilities. The Metabolism group builds four connected models: drug-metabolizing enzyme, site of metabolism, metabolite structure, and enzyme kinetics. As the group’s leader, you will own those models, mentor the team that builds them, and drive integration of their predicted parameters into the physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model that governs exposure across the VHAT.

 Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment Visa at this time.

jobs.title: Senior Director, People Operations
jobs.description:
A LITTLE BIT ABOUT Boldr
 Boldr is the first global B-Corp dedicated to delivering world-class Client experiences while creating
 access to dignified, meaningful work in communities around the world.
 We are a global team, united by our desire to connect diverse people with common values for boldr
 impact.

 LET’S START WITH OUR VALUES
 Excellent. Being excellent at what we do sets us apart. It happens when we care about our work and how it lands, set clear standards, and hold each other accountable. We don't stop at meeting the standard; we keep raising the bar.
 Authentic. Real connection happens when we show up as our best, truest selves, help others dothe same, and stand by each other through the harder times.
 Curious. Curiosity keeps us innovative. Better understanding comes from asking helpful questions, seeking to understand before we act, and building on each other's thinking.
 Dynamic. Growth is central to our purpose, and it only happens in dynamic environments where we stay flexible, adaptable and open.
 Empathetic. Great partnerships happen when we take the time to understand the people we work with, our teams, our clients and our communities, for better outcomes for each.

 WHAT IS YOUR ROLE
 As Senior Director, People Operations, you are the operational and governance backbone of Boldr's People function. You own the systems, rewards, and standards that let a five-country division run with consistency and care.
 Three connected disciplines roll up to you across the Philippines, South Africa, Mexico, Canada, and the United States:
 People Operations and Systems: the employee lifecycle, our HRIS (Rippling), people data, service delivery, and self-service.
 Total Rewards: compensation and benefits, Living Wage governance, pay equity, and job banding.
 Business Partnering: ER cases and investigations, multi-country labor law compliance, risk and audit, and the policies and handbooks that keep us fair and consistent.

 This is a role for a builder and an operator. The longer-range strategic agenda, organizational design, performance strategy, and strategic business partnering, sits with the VP and grows alongside our People Success team. Your mandate is to make the backbone genuinely excellent: scalable processes that do not rely on heroics, clean and trustworthy data, sound compliance across every jurisdiction, and a team member experience that reflects our values wherever people work.
 You report to the VP, People, and you are one of the leaders the rest of the division depends on to keep the engine running as we scale.

 WHY DO WE WANT YOU
 We are looking for an impact-driven operator who can give a fast-growing, five-country division the backbone it needs to scale without breaking. Someone who builds systems that last, holds a high bar on compliance and fairness, and still keeps the human center in every process they design.
 You will protect organizational health, bring calm and consistency to sensitive moments, and make the everyday experience of working at Boldr feel reliable and fair in every country we operate in. We do all of this so our team members can thrive as we grow.

 WHAT WILL YOU DO
 People Operations and Systems
 Own the employee lifecycle end-to-end: onboarding, changes, and offboarding, delivered consistently across all five countries.
 Lead Rippling as our HRIS and system of record; design and maintain clean workflows, self-service, and service delivery (ticketing and knowledge base).
 Establish data integrity and reporting discipline: headcount, attrition, and the people data leaders rely on to decide well.
 Partner closely with Payroll to protect accuracy and timeliness in every jurisdiction.
 Modernize People infrastructure through automation and sound system design, so support scales without manual workarounds.

 Total Rewards
 Own compensation and benefits governance across all geographies, anchored to our Living Wage philosophy as the pay floor.
 Direct compensation cycles with rigor and clarity: timelines, manager enablement, auditability, and clear communication.
 Oversee job banding and pay structures using our market data source (Payfactors), keeping pay equitable and defensible.
 Steward pay equity and transparency norms that build trust while managing risk appropriately.

 Employee Relations
 Oversee sensitive ER cases, investigations, grievances, and disciplinary matters through the Business Partnering team, and personally lead the most complex cases, with consistency, fairness, and empathy.
 Build the ER frameworks and manager guidance that keep outcomes fair and well-documented across countries.
 Serve as a trusted, high-integrity escalation point on difficult people matters.

 Compliance, Risk, and Governance
 Ensure compliance across all five countries and both operating models: Managed Outsourcing and Global Employment (EoR).
 Own records, audit, and data protection for People data.
 Translate local labor realities into sound, consistent decisions, flag clearly where in-country counsel is needed, and engage and consult with counsel on these matters.
 Build the governance and risk frameworks that let us scale responsibly.

 Policy Development and Maintenance
 Own the development, maintenance, and governance of People policies and employee handbooks.
 Keep policy current with changing labor law in each jurisdiction, and consistent with our values and B Corp commitments.
 Make policy clear, accessible, and genuinely useful to managers and team members, not just technically compliant.

 Team Leadership and Stakeholder Partnership
 Lead and develop the People Operations, Total Rewards, and Business Partnering teams; set clear goals, coach for growth, and build a culture of service excellence.
 Own the budget for People Operations, Total Rewards, and Business Partnering, including people, systems, and vendor costs, and ensure it meets company requirements.
 Establish clarity on decision rights, service levels, and escalation paths, so it is clear how People decisions get made here.
 Partner with the VP, the Talent Acquisition and People Success pillars, Business Operations, Finance, and client-facing teams to keep the backbone aligned to the business and company strategy.

jobs.title: Director of Software Engineering (Canada)
jobs.description:
At Flosum, we are building the world's best software for the modern enterprise. Our team is passionate about crafting elegant, high-performance products that delight our customers and set a new bar for engineering excellence. We combine deep expertise in cloud-native development with a relentless focus on quality, speed, and innovation. Every line of code we ship is built to scale, built to last, and built to make a real difference for the businesses that rely on us.
 We are a company where technologists lead, ideas win on merit, and shipping great software fast is a core value—not a slogan. If you believe world-class engineering teams are the ones that move quickly and build things right, you'll feel at home here.
 About the Role
 We are hiring a Director of Software Development to lead a team of 10 engineers building and scaling our Node.js and Salesforce-integrated products. This is a hands-on leadership role for a technical architect at heart who can compress delivery schedules, drive developer velocity, and own the performance of the overall solution. You will be the single point of accountability for turning our roadmap into shipped software—on time, at quality, and at scale.
 What You'll Own
 Lead, coach, and grow a team of 10 full-stack developers across Node.js services and Salesforce customizations.
 Drive measurable improvements in developer velocity using DORA metrics: lead time, deployment frequency, change failure rate, and MTTR.
 Compress delivery schedules by breaking epics into small, independently shippable slices and challenging inflated estimates with data.

 With over 80 years serving Saskatchewan, Auto Electric Service Ltd. (AES) is a locally owned wholesale distribution company serving the automotive, agriculture, industrial, heavy-duty, and retail markets.
 Since 1943, we have built our reputation on strong customer relationships, extensive product availability, industry expertise, and dependable service. As we continue to grow, we are looking for an experienced business development leader to help build and lead our Agriculture & Industrial market segment.
 The Opportunity
 We are looking for a Director of Business Development – Agriculture & Industrial who understands the Saskatchewan market, knows the needs of agriculture and industrial customers, and has the experience to turn opportunities into long-term business.
 This is a hands-on growth role with the opportunity to help build a business segment from the ground up. You will identify where AES can win, develop new customer relationships, secure strategic accounts, help determine the products and solutions our customers need, and develop a practical strategy for sustainable and profitable growth.
 Initially, you will be heavily involved in direct business development and account acquisition. As the Agriculture & Industrial segment grows, you will help recruit, coach, and lead a team of Client Solutions Partners to support continued expansion.
 What You'll Do
 Identify and develop new business opportunities within Saskatchewan's agriculture and industrial markets.
 Build relationships with owners, procurement teams, maintenance leaders, operations leaders, and other key decision-makers.
 Lead strategic opportunities from initial discovery and proposal through negotiation, implementation, and repeat business.
 Develop and execute plans to grow strategic accounts and expand AES's share of customer business.
 Gather customer and market insight to identify product gaps, new product opportunities, and changing customer needs.
 Work closely with Purchasing, Assortment Optimization, Operations, Logistics, Marketing, and branch teams to support new products and customer programs.
 Help develop pricing, territory coverage, sales campaigns, account acquisition strategies, and go-to-market plans.
 Negotiate pricing, freight, payment terms, and service expectations while maintaining a strong understanding of profitability and cost to serve.
 Build and maintain a strong sales pipeline, forecasts, account plans, and customer information within our CRM.
 Track segment performance, identify opportunities or challenges, and take action to achieve sales and profitability goals.
 Recruit, coach, and develop Client Solutions Partners as the Agriculture & Industrial segment grows.
 Provide field coaching, account support, pipeline reviews, and clear performance expectations for the sales team.
 Represent AES professionally with customers, suppliers, and industry partners throughout Saskatchewan.

jobs.title: Account Director (Performance Marketing Agency)
jobs.description:
This job posting is available in English and Canadian French. Please scroll down for the French version. 
 Cette offre d’emploi est disponible en anglais et en français (Canada). Veuillez faire défiler pour la version française. 
 ________________________________
 Remote - U.S. & Canada Only | Full-Time 
 Compensation: 
 $80K - $130K USD (U.S.-based candidates)
 $80K - $130K CAD (Canada-based candidates)
 We’re Not Looking for Generic Account Leadership. We’re Looking for a Performance Marketing Leader. 
 Level Agency is hiring an Account Director with deep performance marketing agency experience — someone who knows how to lead client relationships, connect strategy to execution, and drive measurable business outcomes.
 You may be a current Account Director at a performance marketing agency. Or, you may have started hands-on in paid media, analytics, or campaign management before moving into account leadership. Either way, you understand what great performance marketing looks like because you’ve worked close enough to the work to know what actually moves results.
 You can speak credibly about Google Ads. You understand how media, SEO, creative, data, CRM, websites, CRO, and reporting all connect. You know how to spot issues before they become client escalations. And you’re confident enough to lead a room without making it about your title.
 You’re especially strong when the path to conversion is complex — where lead quality, pipeline, sales alignment, landing pages, and conversion journeys matter as much as media efficiency.
 This is not a “status call and recap email” role. This is for someone who can connect client business goals to marketing strategy, push back with purpose, and lead a focused book of accounts with depth — rather than spreading their attention across a high-volume roster with limited depth.
 This Isn’t for Everyone. 
 We’re building something rare: a place where growth, truth, and high performance go hand-in-hand.
 You’ll thrive here if: 
 ✅ You’ve led client relationships in a performance marketing agency environment.
✅ You understand how modern marketing channels work together — media, SEO, creative, data, CRM, website, CRO, and analytics.
✅ You can speak credibly about Google Ads and paid media strategy.
✅ You care about client business results, not just campaign metrics.
✅ You can lead a focused book of clients deeply, not manage a huge roster shallowly.
✅ Your default is “I’ll handle it,” even when the work sits slightly outside your lane.
 And you’ll struggle here if: 
 ❌ Your experience is primarily brand, creative, ecommerce, or DTC without deeper performance agency experience.
❌ You’ve only managed accounts at the surface level across a very large client load.
❌ You need a narrow job description to know what you should own.
❌ You protect scope before you protect the outcome.
❌ You can’t speak credibly about channel strategy beyond talking points.
 About Level
 We’re an AI-powered performance marketing agency — built for precision, designed to scale, and powered by a scientific mindset. At Level, we blend strategy, media, creative, and machine intelligence to deliver outcomes that matter. Every time. At scale.
 We’ve been named one of Pittsburgh’s Best Places to Work and an Inc. 500 Fastest-Growing Company. Our clients span B2B, education, healthcare, financial services, ecommerce, and more.
 Your Role (and Impact)
 As an Account Director, you’ll lead performance-driven client relationships across a focused book of accounts. You’ll sit at the intersection of client strategy, marketing execution, internal team leadership, and business impact.
 You’ll be the person clients trust to tell them the truth, the person internal teams count on to create clarity, and the person who keeps strategy tied to measurable outcomes.
 You’ll:
 Lead Performance Strategy: Translate client business goals into multi-channel marketing strategies that drive measurable growth.
 Own Client Relationships: Build trust with senior stakeholders through clear communication, proactive thinking, and sharp strategic recommendations.
 Connect the Marketing Ecosystem: Help clients understand how paid media, SEO, creative, data, CRM, websites, CRO, and reporting work together to improve performance.
 Bring Paid Media Fluency: Speak credibly about Google Ads, paid social, and media performance — even when you’re not the person making every in-platform change.
 Spot Issues Early: Dig into performance trends, ask better questions, and catch problems before they become client escalations.
 Push Back with Purpose: Challenge client assumptions when needed — always in service of the performance goal, never ego, scope protection, or control.
 Manage a Deep Book: Lead a focused portfolio of accounts with enough depth to truly understand each client’s business, performance drivers, and risks.
 Guide Internal Teams: Partner with media, SEO, creative, analytics, and strategy teams to keep work moving, priorities clear, and outcomes aligned.
 Tell the Story in the Data: Turn reporting, dashboards, and performance analysis into insights clients can act on.
 Own the Details: Keep budgets, forecasts, timelines, documentation, and communication sharp and accurate.
 Requirements
 Must-Haves
 5+ years in a performance marketing agency. You have agency experience rooted in performance, paid media, and measurable outcomes — not primarily brand, creative, or ecommerce-only work.
 Account leadership experience in a performance environment. You are either currently an Account Director at a performance marketing agency or you started in marketing, paid media, analytics, or campaign management before transitioning into account leadership.
 Google Ads fluency is required. You can speak credibly about Google Ads and understand what to investigate when performance shifts, lead volume drops, or conversion quality changes.
 Modern marketing ecosystem understanding. You understand how paid media, SEO, creative, data, CRM, websites, CRO, and analytics connect to drive outcomes.
 Paid media strategy depth. You understand how media channels work together, especially search and social, and can translate performance signals into strategy.
 Client leadership experience. You’ve managed client relationships, led strategic conversations, and presented recommendations to senior stakeholders.
 Focused account management experience. You’re used to leading a meaningful book of clients deeply — roughly 3 to 8 accounts — rather than spreading your attention across a high-volume roster with limited depth.
 Experience with meaningful media spend. You’ve worked with clients spending at least $50K/month in media per client; $100K+/month is strongly preferred.
 Business-first mindset. You talk about revenue, pipeline, lead quality, conversion paths, customer journeys, and business outcomes — not just CTRs, CPCs, and platform metrics.
 Low ego, high ownership. You’re willing to build the dashboard, chase the answer, clean up the ambiguity, or step into the gap when the team needs it.
 Strong Preferences
 B2B, lead generation, or complex-sale experience. Experience with longer buying cycles, pipeline quality, sales alignment, or non-DTC conversion paths is a major plus.
 Meta, LinkedIn, SEO, CRM, CRO, or other channel fluency. You don’t need to be an expert in every channel, but you should understand how they work together.
 Experience in financial services, healthcare, education, SaaS, or other considered-purchase verticals.
 Comfort with dashboards, reporting tools, Google Analytics, and data visualization.
 Experience mentoring account team members or coordinating cross-functional delivery teams.
 AI Expectations
 At Level, AI is a skillset — not a shortcut. In this role, you’ll be expected to:
 Use tools like ChatGPT, Midjourney, Claude, and Perplexity to improve how you work
 Share your prompts, process improvements, and ideas with the team
 Experiment regularly and refine your workflows over time
 Embrace discomfort as part of the learning process
 Apply AI tools to increase your speed, clarity, and creativity — not to replace thoughtful work
 AI should make you sharper, faster, and more strategic. It should never replace judgment, taste, accountability, or a strong point of view.
 Our Core Values
 No Ego, All In 
We don’t do “that’s not my job.” We win together, step in where needed, and care more about the outcome than the org chart.
 Better Every Day 
We want the feedback — even when it stings. We test, learn, adapt, and keep raising the bar.
 Relentless for Results 
Activity is nothing without outcomes. We care about the work that moves the business forward.
 Driven by Truth 
We challenge assumptions, follow the data, and tell clients what they need to hear — not just what is easy to say.
 Perks & Benefits
 At Level, we support our people across the U.S. and Canada with benefits designed to promote flexibility, wellbeing, and long-term growth.
 Fully remote across the U.S. & Canada, plus monthly WFH stipend and Summer Fridays
 Generous time off, including unlimited PTO (U.S.), competitive vacation (Canada), and parental/family leave options
 Comprehensive health benefits, mental health support, and company-paid disability & life coverage
 Employer retirement contributions (401(k) in the U.S., RRSP match in Canada)
 Quarterly performance reviews and career advancement opportunities
 Remote First
 This role is open to U.S. and Canada residents and is fully remote. We are unable to sponsor visas at this time.
 Level Is Built on Inclusion
 We are committed to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging. Level is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer — we celebrate what makes you, you.
 Ready to Apply?
 Click below to submit your resume. You’ll also answer a few thoughtful questions, so take your time.
 We care more about how you think, how you lead, and how you create impact than whether your path has been perfectly linear.
 Let’s build something together.

 Télétravail – États-Unis et Canada seulement | Temps plein 
 Rémunération: 
 80 000 $ à 130 000 $ US pour les personnes candidates basées aux États-Unis
 80 000 $ à 130 000 $ CA pour les personnes candidates basées au Canada
 Nous ne cherchons pas un leadership de comptes générique. Nous cherchons un leader en marketing de performance.
 Level Agency recrute un ou une Account Director possédant une solide expérience en agence de marketing de performance — une personne capable de diriger les relations clients, de relier la stratégie à l’exécution et de générer des résultats d’affaires mesurables.

Dans tous les cas, vous comprenez à quoi ressemble un excellent marketing de performance, parce que vous avez été assez près du travail pour savoir ce qui fait réellement avancer les résultats.

 Ce n’est pas un rôle de « status call et courriel de récapitulation ». Ce rôle s’adresse à une personne capable de relier les objectifs d’affaires des clients à la stratégie marketing, de challenger avec intention et de diriger un portefeuille de comptes ciblé en profondeur — plutôt que de disperser son attention sur une longue liste de clients gérés en surface.
 Ce poste n’est pas pour tout le monde. 
 Nous bâtissons quelque chose de rare: un endroit où la croissance, la vérité et la haute performance avancent ensemble.
 Vous allez vous épanouir ici si: 
 ✅ Vous avez dirigé des relations clients dans un environnement d’agence de marketing de performance.
✅ Vous comprenez comment les canaux marketing modernes fonctionnent ensemble — médias, SEO, création, données, CRM, site Web, CRO et analytique.
✅ Vous pouvez parler de Google Ads et de stratégie médias payants avec crédibilité.
✅ Les résultats d’affaires des clients vous importent plus que les simples indicateurs de campagne.
✅ Vous pouvez diriger un portefeuille ciblé de clients en profondeur, plutôt que gérer une énorme liste en surface.
✅ Votre réflexe naturel est « je m’en occupe », même lorsque le travail dépasse légèrement votre champ habituel.
 Et vous aurez de la difficulté ici si:
