jobs.title: Director of Public Practice
jobs.description:
Director of Public Practice

4-Day Work Week | Leadership Role | Winnipeg, Manitoba

McLenehan and Associates Chartered Professional Accountants
$140,000 Base Salary | 32-Hour Week, Even in Busy Season | Lead the Department, Shape the Firm

WHY YOU'LL LOVE WORKING HERE

4-Day Work Week
Four 8-hour days. In public practice. Through busy season. Yes, really.
Competitive Salary
$140,000 base. Full-time pay for a 32-hour week.
Real Authority
You run the public practice department: the people, the production, the processes, and the quality standard. You report to the owner, and no one else.
Generous Time Off
3 weeks of vacation plus a paid week during the December holidays.
Paid Growth
Firm-funded professional development and your annual CPD, covered.
RRSP Matching
Contribution matching to support your long-term financial security.
Comprehensive Benefits
Prescription, dental, and vision coverage.

THE OPPORTUNITY

Most senior roles in public practice follow the same script. You carry the team, but someone else makes the decisions. You review files until nine at night in March. You are told the firm values balance, and then busy season arrives and the promise quietly expires.

This one is different.

McLenehan and Associates CPAs is a growing Winnipeg-based accounting firm serving hundreds of incorporated Canadian small businesses, from monthly bookkeeping and year-end compliance through to Fractional CFO and Virtual Controller services. Our people like the work they do and the people they do it with. And our 4-day work week has proven, for years, that high standards and a full life outside the office are not in conflict.
Until now, the final review of year-end files, the delivery of finished work to clients, and the day-to-day leadership of our public practice team have run through Mike McLenehan, the firm's owner. As the firm has grown, that has made Mike the bottleneck, and it has kept him from the work only an owner can do: strategy, growth, and building the firm. That changes with this hire.

We are putting Directors in place who hold full responsibility for their departments. A Director of Business Development and a Director of People and Culture are already in their seats. The Director of Public Practice is an important addition to that leadership team, taking ownership of the department at the centre of the firm: year-end preparation, corporate tax, and personal tax.

This is the senior seat that experienced CPAs talk about but rarely find: a firm with 500 to 600 incorporated business owner clients, a department of Managers, Assistant Managers, Senior Accountants, and Accountants ready to report to you, a proven 4-day work week, and an owner who is ready to hand you the department and support your decisions.

To be clear, this is not a role that takes you out of the work. You will review files, you will sit across from business owners and deliver their results, and you will hold ultimate responsibility for the quality of everything that leaves the department. What is different is that you will also own the system that produces that work: the workflow, the capacity planning, the processes, and the people.

We are not looking for someone to grow into this role. We are looking for someone who has already done this work: reviewed the files, led the people, sat with the owners, and run a busy season. Someone who wants to do it inside a firm that respects their time and their judgment.

If that describes you, keep reading.

WHAT YOU'LL EARN

Base Salary:
$140,000

Work Week:
Four 8-hour days. 32 hours. Year-round, including personal tax season and corporate year-end peaks

Time Off:
3 weeks of vacation plus a paid week during the December holidays

Retirement:
RRSP contribution matching

Health Benefits:
Prescription, dental, and vision coverage

Professional Development:
Annual CPD covered, plus firm-funded development in leadership and advisory skills

Reporting Line:
Directly to Mike McLenehan, the firm's owner. No layers in between

Location:
In-office, Winnipeg. This is a senior leadership role and the team is here

Public practice has trained most senior CPAs to quietly accept that a strong salary comes bundled with a brutal spring. Here, the salary is full-time and the week is 32 hours. Work out what that does to your effective hourly rate compared with your last busy season, and then keep reading.

THE DEPARTMENT YOU'LL LEAD

The clients

500 to 600 incorporated, owner-managed Canadian small businesses: trades, professionals, retailers, contractors, and holding companies. They are building something meaningful, they want advice they can act on, and they want to hear it from someone who speaks their language.

The work

Year-end compilation and review engagements, corporate tax returns (T2), personal tax returns (T1), and owner-manager tax planning: compensation planning, corporate structures, and the purchase and sale of a business. We do not perform audit engagements. The department exists to deliver compliance work of a consistently high standard and to turn that work into advice our clients value.

The team

The department is made up of Managers, Assistant Managers, Senior Accountants, and Accountants. You lead all of them. Your Managers share responsibility with you for quality assurance and quality review on every file, and you hold ultimate responsibility for what leaves the department. Mike's partner sign-off remains on client deliverables.

Your tools

CCH iFirm for practice management and iFirm Tax for every T1 and T2. CaseWare with Jazzit financial statement templates for year-end preparation. QuickBooks Online across most client files. You will have a strong voice in what we adopt next.

How we will work together

Strategy, hiring, compensation, processes, budgets, and software are decided together, you and Mike. Implementation is yours, and so is the result. Mike will be alongside you for the first several weeks of file reviews and client meetings until you are calibrated to the firm's standard, and then his involvement shifts to partner sign-off, the most complex matters, and the strategic decisions you bring to him.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Lead the Public Practice Department

Own the production system for year-end preparation, corporate tax, and personal tax: workflow, capacity planning, scheduling, and deadlines across the full year, including T1 season and corporate year-end peaks
Design, document, and continuously improve the department's processes so that quality and turnaround do not depend on any one person, including you
Set and monitor the department's KPIs, including turnaround time, budget versus actual on files, deadlines met, and review points, and report on them regularly to Mike
Lead the department's software and workflow improvements in iFirm, CaseWare, and the tools around them, in coordination with the firm's leadership team

Quality Assurance and File Review

Hold ultimate responsibility for quality assurance and quality review across the department, working with your Managers, who share the review workload with you
Review year-end compilation and review engagement files, corporate tax returns (T2), and personal tax returns (T1) before they reach the partner for sign-off, with a focus on the complex, the unusual, and the high-stakes
Uphold the firm's quality standards and professional requirements on every file, and know when an issue needs to be escalated
Coach preparers and reviewers through your review notes so the same issues stop recurring. Your goal is fewer review points every season, not more

Client Delivery and Advisory

Meet with business owner clients to deliver finished year-end results and tax returns, and explain them in plain language the owner can act on
Provide financial and tax advice on owner-manager matters: compensation planning (salary versus dividends), corporate structures, purchase and sale of a business, and CRA correspondence
Identify opportunities where clients would benefit from deeper advisory services, and coordinate with our Director of Business Development to grow those relationships

People Leadership

Lead and develop the department's Managers, Assistant Managers, Senior Accountants, and Accountants across the full people cycle: hiring input, onboarding, training, coaching, performance evaluations, and career development
Build the bench: develop Senior Accountants into reviewers and Assistant Managers into Managers, and make the department stronger every quarter
Work with our Director of People and Culture on recruiting, performance management, and career pathways for the department

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE: YOUR FIRST 90 DAYS

Month 1 (Days 1 to 30): Learning the firm

You know our clients, services, systems, and standards well enough to hold a credible advisory conversation
You have met one-on-one with every member of the department and understand their strengths, goals, and development needs
You are shadowing file reviews and client meetings alongside Mike and calibrating to the firm's quality bar
You have mapped the department's current workflow from client request to partner sign-off and identified where it slows down

Month 2 (Days 31 to 60): Taking the Reins

You and your Managers are completing file reviews independently on standard files, with Mike involved only on complex matters
Workload planning, scheduling, and day-to-day leadership of the department run through you
You are joining client meetings and beginning to lead them
You have agreed a set of department KPIs with Mike and begun reporting on them

Month 3 (Days 61 to 90): Fully Operational

The department's production and quality review run through you and your Managers, and Mike's role has narrowed to partner sign-off and the most complex files
You own the team: performance management, development plans, and hiring input are yours
You are delivering finished work and advice to clients independently
You have a documented plan for the coming busy season that does not depend on Mike's review capacity

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

You must have:

Chartered Professional Accountant designation (CPA), in good standing
7+ years of Canadian public practice experience, including several years reviewing files prepared by others
Deep, current expertise in compilation and review engagements, corporate tax (T2), personal tax (T1), and owner-manager tax planning
Proven experience leading a team of accounting professionals in public practice, including managing Managers or Senior Accountants who review the work of others
The presence and judgment to sit across from a business owner, hold the conversation, and give advice they trust
A track record of running a busy season: planning capacity, managing a team's workload, and meeting competing deadlines without dropping the standard

You will stand out if you have:

Experience as the final reviewer in a firm, or as a Senior Manager or Principal with responsibility for a department's production and quality
Hands-on experience with CaseWare and Jazzit, CCH iFirm and iFirm Tax, and QuickBooks Online, or comparable tools
Experience designing or implementing workflow and process improvements in a growing firm, and measuring the results
Exposure to advisory work beyond compliance: cash flow, budgeting, business purchase and sale, or CFO-level conversations

WHO YOU ARE

Top performers will recognize themselves in this list:

You have the technical judgment to be the last word on a file, and the self-awareness to know when to pick up the phone and talk it through
You think in systems. When a file goes sideways, you fix the file and then you fix the process that let it happen
You find genuine satisfaction in a clean file, and equal satisfaction in coaching the person who prepared it
Your review notes teach; they do not just correct
Business owners relax when you walk into the room, because you speak their language, not just the Income Tax Act's
You can hold a high standard and a warm relationship with the same person at

jobs.description:
About Powerfleet

Powerfleet (Nasdaq: AIOT; JSE: PWR) is a global leader in the artificial intelligence of things (AIoT) software-as-a-service (SaaS) mobile asset industry. With more than 30 years of experience, Powerfleet unifies business operations through the ingestion, harmonization, and integration of data—regardless of source—and delivers actionable insights to help companies meet their strategic objectives around Safety, Compliance, Efficiency and Sustainability. Our people-first culture and relentless innovation empower customers to achieve measurable, sustainable business improvements. Powerfleet serves over 2.6 million subscribers across more than 48,000 customers in 120 countries, with commercial operations across every major continent.

Position Overview

The Collections Director leads the North American collections function and is accountable for cash delivery, forecasting, collectability analysis and resolution of complex customer balances. This is not a traditional collections role. The position requires significant research and cross-functional problem solving, including locating historical contracts, resolving billing and credit issues, and obtaining evidence that sold devices are active on the data platform.

Key Responsibilities

Lead, coach and develop a team consisting of one Collections Manager and six Collections Analysts, with clear account ownership, priorities and escalation paths.
Responsible for enforcing corporate processes
Consolidate disjointed collections teams and processes across North America into a consistent operating model with standardized reporting, documentation and customer treatment.
Lead the implementation and adoption of the Advanced Collections module in Microsoft Dynamics 365, including workflows, work queues, account segmentation, notes, promise-to-pay tracking and management reporting.
Oversee negotiations and resolution strategies for large and complex customers, including accounts affected by incorrect billing, disputed charges, legacy arrangements and credits to be issued.
Partner with Billing and other teams to prioritize research and corrective actions based on value, aging, customer impact, collectability risk and expected cash recovery.
Coordinate research of historical contracts, amendments, billing records and operational data needed to substantiate amounts due and resolve customer disputes.
Work with operational and data-platform stakeholders to obtain evidence that devices sold to customers are active, deployed or otherwise supported by system data.
Own the North American collections forecast, including expected timing, risks, assumptions and major account dependencies.
Maintain the cash target file and ensure timely, accurate input by the collections team, with clear tracking of actual results against forecast and target.
Prepare and present monthly executive reporting on specific customer accounts, including collectability, unresolved issues, expected cash timing, credits, dependencies and recommended next steps.
Identify recurring causes of delayed payment and partner with upstream teams to reduce preventable billing, contracting, data and process issues.

Qualifications And Experience

10+ years of experience in collections with Enterprise Fortune 1000 company.
Progressive experience in collections, accounts receivable, order-to-cash, credit or finance operations, including leadership of multi-level teams.
Demonstrated success resolving large, complex or disputed customer balances through research, negotiation and cross-functional coordination.
Strong experience in collections forecasting, customer collectability analysis and executive-level reporting.
Experience leading process consolidation or finance transformation across multiple teams, business units or geographies.
Experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 collections capabilities or a comparable enterprise platform; Advanced Collections implementation experience is preferred.
Strong analytical and commercial judgment, with the ability to connect contracts, billing records, credits, customer history and operational data into clear conclusions.
Advanced Excel skills and experience using reporting or business intelligence tools.
Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.

Measures of Success

Achievement of cash targets and improved forecasting accuracy.
Reduction in aged and unresolved balances, particularly for high-value and complex accounts.
Timely resolution of billing errors, credits, disputes and supporting-evidence requirements.
Effective adoption of Dynamics 365 Advanced Collections and consistent North American processes.
Clear, decision-ready executive reporting on customer collectability and collection risk.

Note:
This description summarizes the primary responsibilities of the role and may be adjusted as business needs evolve.

The base salary range for this full-time position is [CAD $140, 000 – $150, 000]
, with eligibility for additional variable compensation. Final compensation will be determined based on experience, skills, and location.

Equal Employment Opportunity Statement

Powerfleet is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive and accessible workplace where all individuals are treated with respect and dignity. We prohibit discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, or any other protected characteristic under applicable Canadian human rights legislation.

With over 30 years of expertise, we empower organizations worldwide to unify operations by ingesting, harmonizing, and integrating data from any source—transforming it into actionable insights that save lives, time, and money.

Our end-to-end solutions help businesses monitor, manage, and optimize everything from warehouse assets to connected vehicles, driving safety, efficiency, and sustainability across the supply chain. But we are more than just a technology company—our people-centric approach fosters innovation and long-term success for our customers.

jobs.description:
ABOUT US

JOB DESCRIPTION

BGIS is a leading provider of customized facility management and real estate services. With a combined team of over 10,000 professionals worldwide, we relentlessly focus on enabling innovation through the services we deliver. We actively seek new opportunities that drive innovation for our clients’ businesses. Globally, we manager over 320 million square feet of client portfolios across 30,000+ locations in North America, Europe, Middle East, Australia, and Asia. For further information, visit www.bgis.com .

OUR CULTURE

At BGIS, our culture is built on three foundational pillars:

Culture of Care: We deeply care for each other, our clients, partners, and the communities we serve.
High Performing Teams: We go Above and Beyond to deliver exceptional services. INTEGRITY, OWNERSHIP, RESPONSIVENESS, INITIATION, VISIBILITY, DRIVE, and INTEGRATION are core to high performance.
Unwavering Commitment to Sustainability: We conduct every action with a focus on preserving our earth.

SUMMARY

For the assigned region(s), the Regional Director
is accountable for operations, financial management and meeting service delivery obligations in a specified Geographical region that includes several facilities, employees and clients.  This role is expected to understand, coach and train the team in all regulatory and client requirements.  In addition, this role is also responsible for contributing to strategic and account management plans and objectives and people leadership. 

This role will work in collaboration with all key BGIS departments to ensure full support of all activities and play a key role in our INTEGRATED approach to operating buildings.   

Opportunities for Development:  

At BGIS we are committed to the development of our people – offering them opportunities to learn and grow into various roles.  Success in the role offers Team Members the opportunity to explore various roles – some include:  

On Account and expanded Operational Leadership
Facility Management Office roles to support accounts,
Project Management leadership roles to lead and execute projects

KEY DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

Health, Safety, Environment & Security

Follow and apply all Health and Safety and Emergency Response, aligned with both BGIS and Client expectations.to ensure safety of all employees and building occupants. 
Work in collaboration with BGIS Health Safety and Environment Teams for support and direction on key programs to emphasize Safety Culture 
Accountable for meeting all internal and external health, safety, environment and security-related requirements 
Accountable for the safe delivery of all work performed  

Account Management

Continuously engages clients in discussions to understand and anticipate needs, identify and recommend additional services   
Provides input and contributes to the development and execution of strategic account expansion plans 
Recommends additional pull-through services 
Participates in and contributes to quarterly business reviews 
Contributes to contract renewal and business development activities 
Contributes to account governance  
Adherence to Contract Specific MSA (Master Service Agreement)  
Manages the BGIS ECE Program for the specific client group 
Responsible for results and action plans related to the Likely to Recommend Survey.  

Client Relationship Management

Accountable for achieving client satisfaction objectives for the assigned region(s) 
Accountable for developing and maintaining effective relationships with clients, managing client expectations 
Position level of client representatives with whom this position typically interacts with include those at the senior management level 
Acts as the focal point of escalation for issues pertaining to facilities within assigned region(s) 

Region/Portfolio Budget Development & Management

Assume financial responsibility for facility operations, including budget management. 
In partnership with finance, responsible for the development of budgets (O&M, Transaction, capital projects and rent), and be able to support and explain approach to the client and the account team.  
Using financial reports, perform monthly budget, analyze and re-forecast allocations as necessary. 
Meet annual targets as per contractual performance and client financial targets / indicators. 
Identify cost-saving opportunities and develop strategies to maximize financial resources. 
Track and report on budget positive or negative trends performance regularly 
Participates in, provides recommendations, and contributes to continuous improvement projects to achieve efficiency gains and cost savings 

Portfolio Management

Accountable for operations management for the portfolio of facilities within the assigned region(s) 
Leads the operations and maintenance activities of a portfolio of facilities along with the execution of the portfolio’s programs 
Oversees the completion and submission of capital plans 
Creates and implements short to mid-term plans for the assigned region(s) 
Provides input into strategic plans   
Collaborates with relevant stakeholders to optimize facilities within assigned region(s) and continuously create value for the client. 

Service Delivery Management

Work in collaboration with Central Work Order Management Team to ensure all work is being completed as outlined in the MSA 
Monitor work order progress and ensure tasks are completed within established timelines. 
Work with Account Governance Teams to maintain accurate records of work orders and associated costs. 
Streamline and manage work order processes to optimize efficiency. 
Prioritize and assign work orders based on urgency and impact on facility operations. 
Accountable for meeting all service obligations for the assigned region(s) 
Oversees the delivery of all service obligations 
Accountable for meeting established metrics/key performance indicators.  Leads the operations team in the development and implementation of action plans to remediate gaps, where applicable, to ensure objectives are met. 
Accountable for ensuring compliance to all legislated, corporate and industry-related requirements and guidelines including but not limited to environmental, health and safety, and building standard requirements 

Risk Management, Emergency Preparedness and Business Continuity Planning and Execution

Accountable for safeguarding the client against emergencies and risks by ensuring emergency preparedness, risk management, disaster recovery and business continuity plans are developed and that relevant stakeholders are trained to ensure proper execution 
Oversight and engagement in Emergency Management 

Regulatory Compliance

Accountable for ensuring all regulatory compliance requirements have been met and all related documentation are created and maintained 
Ensure compliance with corporate and legislated policies, procedures, practices and guidelines related to environmental, building code and issues by applying cursory knowledge of legislation related to these areas 

Project Management

Accountable for on-time, on-budget and quality delivery of facility management projects for the assigned region(s) 
Collaborates with clients and internal stakeholders to identify project opportunities and priorities, develop and implement projects 
Oversees the development and execution of project plans for portfolios within assigned region(s) 

Procurement

With Support from BGIS Strategic Sourcing and Vendor Management Leadership – follow BGIS Vendor Performance and Relationship Management Program protocols  
Collaborates with Procurement and Supply Chain Administration teams to source and qualify vendors, source and procure goods and services. 

Continuous Improvement

Collaborates with stakeholders and contributes to efficiency gains   through activities including but not limited to identifying and implementing best practices; reviewing, refining and/or developing, implementing processes, technologies and sustainable practices, and leveraging self-perform wherever possible.  Implements related enhancements for the assigned region(s) 

Leadership and Recognition

Accountable for employee-oriented activities including but not limited to employee engagement, development and performance management, hiring and retention, compensation recommendations 
Employee Satisfaction Scores and employee recognition (development and implementation of action plans to improve ESAT scores) 
Day to day support and team oversight/management 

Collaboration with BGIS Self Perform Teams delivering Best Quality Services to Buildings 

Work in collaboration with BGIS teams in Janitorial, Project Management and TechnicalServices or any other areas where work is directly performed by BGIS to maximize efficiency and the best customer service in the buildings / portfolios  
Work together with these teams to ensure work is completed 

Technology to Support your Success. 

Leverage technology such as work order system, vendor monitoring tools, BAS and CMMS scheduling tools to deliver effective service to clients.  
Mentor staff in vendor management and the effective use of technology for vendor relationships. 
Provide guidance to team members on the effective use of technology for financial management and career progression. 
Other duties as assigned 

KNOWLEDGE & SKILLS

Community college diploma preferably in business administration
More than 10 years of facility management work experience
Highly skilled at account management
Highly skilled at facility operations management
Highly skilled at client relationship management with demonstrated ability in building and managing relationships with client representatives at the senior management level
Highly skilled at managing service delivery and meeting service delivery obligations
Skilled at managing budgets
Fully developed communication, influence, persuasion and negotiation skills
High degree of client service orientation and sense of urgency
Highly skilled at leading and engaging a team of individuals
Skilled at vendor management
Highly skilled at emergency management, emergency preparedness and business continuity planning and execution
Possesses a sustainability mindset and seeks to incorporate sustainable practices within assigned portfolio where possible
Expert level knowledge of health and safety requirements. Possesses a high degree of safety mindset
Maintains current knowledge of and highly skilled at implementing facility management services best practices
Expert level knowledge of current building standards and requirements
Possesses a continuous improvement and quality mindset along with a desire to continuously seek and incorporate innovative practices and technologies in order to deliver value to the client

Licenses and/or Professional Accreditation

One or more of the following would be considered an asset:

Certified Facility Manager from International Facility Management Association
Certified Property Manager from Institute of Real Estate Management
Facility Management Administrator Designation from Building Owners and Managers Institute
Real Property Administrator Designation from Building Owners and Managers Institute

This is a regular, full-time position with a salary range of $110,000 - $138,000 per annum. The starting salary will be based on the successful candidate’s competencies, including but not limited to experience, education and performance related to this role.

jobs.title: Engineering Transportation Consulting - Director of Operations - Canada
jobs.description:
At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

Are you a visionary leader ready to shape the future of transportation infrastructure across our Canada geography? Do you embrace innovative solutions to provide our clients and communities with the very best from a worldwide delivery team? If you are - come join our purpose-driven team where innovation, sustainability, and people-first leadership drive everything we do.

This is a fast-paced role reporting directly to the Executive Director of Operations and will have direct reports inclusive of Department Leaders, Managers of Projects, and select others. The successful candidate will bring a collaborative approach to cultivating partnerships with a wide range of cross-functional teams and leaders from finance, sales and people partners including HR, Talent Acquisition, Health & Safety, and Jacobs Employee Network (JEN) leaders.

This role can be based in any of our major Canadian offices, (Toronto, Vancouver/Burnaby, Calgary, Ottawa) and as a people leader you will be in our offices, projects sites or client offices 3 days a week as per our hybrid policy. You will need the ability to travel across Canada to meet our clients and your Jacobs colleagues.

In this role, you will

Grow our market presence through strategic partnerships and strong client relationships, working closely with sales partners, regional technologists, and design-build teams.
Apply strong business and financial insights to achieve key performance objectives and identify opportunities for sustainable growth.
Foster collaboration across the enterprise while coaching, mentoring, and developing future talent.
Champion attraction and retention initiatives, cultivating a culture of care, belonging, and professional growth that supports high engagement and low attrition.

Here's what you'll need

Minimum 12 years in leadership roles in engineering consulting operations focused on infrastructure and/or transportation markets
Engineering or business degree
Proven success delivering large, complex projects and programs
Strong financial acumen, including P&L accountability
Experience driving operational improvement and sustainable growth
An inclusive, people-focused approach with a passion for coaching, developing talent, and fostering high-performing teams
Ability to balance strategic priorities, adapt to changing needs, and execute effectively in a dynamic environment
Commitment to advancing global and digital delivery capabilities
Strong understanding of transportation market trends, clients, and design-build delivery

If you're passionate about building strong teams, fostering growth, and making a meaningful impact across Canada. Please submit a resume tailored to this opportunity, along with a one-page statement of interest addressing the following questions

Innovation, People, Culture & Inclusion

If selected for this role, how would you build a culture that promotes innovation, inclusion, collaboration, and accountability? How would you develop talent, strengthen leadership capability, foster diversity of thought, and create an environment where people are engaged and empowered to perform at their best?

Delivery Excellence, Operational Performance & Profitability

How would you drive delivery excellence, operational effectiveness, and profitable growth across the business? What strategies would you implement to improve project execution, increase margins, optimize resource utilization, and leverage global delivery capabilities?

Posted Salary Range Minimum

171,000.00

Posted Salary Range Upper

277,650.00

The base salary range for this position is $171,000.00 to $277,650.00. This range reflects the minimum and maximum target for new hire salaries for the position across British Columbia, Canada locations. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

We value collaboration and believe that in-person interactions are crucial for both our culture and client delivery. We empower employees with our hybrid working policy, allowing them to split their work week between Jacobs offices/projects and remote locations enabling them to deliver their best work.

Your application experience is important to us, and we’re keen to adapt to make every interaction even better. If you require further support or reasonable adjustments with regards to the recruitment process (for example, you require the application form in a different format), please contact the team via Careers Support.

jobs.title: Director, Program Management
jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 275237

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

Purpose

The Director, Program Management reports into the VP, Delivery & Portfolio Management supporting a large-scale program within the [Canadian Banking] portfolio. This role is accountable for the end-to-end and day-to-day management of the program including managing program objectives, execution, risk mitigation, issue escalation and enabling activities between governance, design, delivery, and support workstreams. As the Director, you will ensure program strategy and objectives are fulfilled within the established timelines and manage and mitigate risks. You will be responsible for implementing new ways of working and operating models, and ensuring the successful delivery of projects within scope, on time, and within budget.

Is this role right for you? In this role you will perform:

Project Leadership: Provide strategic direction and leadership to cross-functional teams, ensuring alignment with ScotiaTech’s strategic goals and business objectives.
Strategic Planning: Collaborate with senior leaders and our external consulting partner to define and drive the strategic roadmap of initiatives, identifying key opportunities and potential risks. Responsible for establishing and managing integrated plans in collaboration with the project delivery team. Identify key stakeholders and involve subject matter experts as required.
Effective Communication: Consistently interact professionally with clients both in business and technology to manage project expectations and deliverables within allocated timelines and budget.
Risk Management: Implement robust project management methodologies and processes to identify, assess, and mitigate project risks, ensuring successful project delivery. Escalate critical issues and drive decision-making and accountability by supporting cross-functional executive and senior management forums to align on opportunities, challenges and required actions.
Stakeholder Engagement: Build and maintain strong relationships with key stakeholders, including business leaders, technology teams, and external partners, to ensure alignment and transparency throughout project lifecycles.
Agile Leadership: Work in an agile delivery environment, drive maturity in Agile practices and effectively collaborate with product, engineering, business and other partners.
Resource Management: Manage project budgets, resource allocation, and vendor relationships to optimize project outcomes while controlling costs.
Quality Assurance: Monitor and ensure the quality of project deliverables, adhering to industry best practices and regulatory requirements.
Continuous Improvement: Champion a culture of continuous improvement, identifying opportunities to enhance project management practices and streamline processes.
Manage Priorities: Effectively manage changing priorities, project risks and issues along with impact and mitigation plans. Facilitate change requests for major impact on scope, schedule, resourcing, and budget.
Reporting and Documentation: Prepare and present regular project status reports and documentation to senior management, providing insights and recommendations for decision-making.
Talent Development: Mentor and develop project management professionals within the team, fostering a culture of growth and excellence. Build a high-performance environment and implement a people strategy that attracts, retains, develops, and motivates the team by fostering an inclusive work environment and using a coaching mindset and behaviours; communicate vison/values/business strategy; and manage succession and development planning for the team.
Understands how the Bank’s risk appetite and risk culture should be considered in day-to-day activities and decisions
Create an environment in which their team pursues effective and efficient operations of their respective areas in accordance with Scotiabank’s Values, its Code of Conduct and the Global Sales Principles, while ensuring the adequacy, adherence to and effectiveness of day-to-day business controls to meet obligations with respect to operational, compliance, AML/ATF/sanctions and conduct risk.

Skills

Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed in this role? We'd love to work with you if you have:

Bachelor's degree in Business, Technology, Project Management, or equivalent experience; MBA or PMP certification is a plus
Strong Project Management background with experience in Agile, hybrid, and waterfall programs, optimizing cross-team workflows for velocity and quality
Minimum of 10 years of project management experience, with a track record of successfully managing complex technology transformation in banking or digital business sector, with specific experience in [CB]
Hands-on experience in working in an agile delivery environment; exposure to business agility is a plus
Proven ability to navigate ambiguity, drive strategic change, and influence senior stakeholders
Strong leadership skills and the ability to motivate and inspire cross-functional teams at all levels of the organization
Experience with Enterprise Delivery Frameworks
PMP or equivalent certification
PM at a Canadian bank
Exceptional communication, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills
Strong analytical and data-driven decision-making skills
Proven experience in strategic planning and portfolio management
Knowledge of regulatory and compliance requirements in the financial industry
Results-driven mindset with a focus on delivering business outcomes
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic, and changing environment
12+ years leading large-scale business/technology programs
10+ years establishing and championing program governance, PMO practices, or agile delivery frameworks
7+ years managing and developing high-performing teams

The Workplace

We are technology partners who help the business transform how our employees around the world work
We have an inclusive and collaborative working environment that encourages creativity, curiosity, and celebrates success!
You'll get to work with and learn from diverse industry leaders, who have hailed from top technology companies around the world
We foster an environment of innovation and continuous learning
We care about our people, allowing them to design how they work to deliver amazing results
We offer a competitive total rewards package, including a performance bonus, company matching programs (on pension & profit sharing), and generous vacation

Location(s): Canada : Ontario : Toronto

Scotiabank is a leading bank in the Americas. Guided by our purpose: "for every future", we help our customers, their families and their communities achieve success through a broad range of advice, products and services, including personal and commercial banking, wealth management and private banking, corporate and investment banking, and capital markets.

jobs.title: Head of Content Design
jobs.description:
Asana is looking for a Head of Content Design to lead and grow our content design practice across the company. You'll manage a team of content designers working across our portfolio of products: Agentic Work Management, Service Management, Client Management, and Command. You'll set the standard for how Asana speaks to customers on every surface, from a settings page to a conversation with an AI Teammate. In this player-coach role, you'll lead the practice, develop senior practitioners, and take on some of the highest-stakes writing projects yourself while collaborating with the Asana Design leadership team to shape both what we make and how we make it.

We design the future of teamwork. Asana has a bold, ambitious mission: help humanity thrive by enabling the world's teams to work together effortlessly. Our design team is at the heart of that mission.

Asana Design is an inclusive and collaborative community. We're a diverse group of designers from different backgrounds (product, brand and content design, design operations, producers, motion design, film, copywriting). We are a team that loves combining research, data insights, and peer feedback into a human-centred design process to produce designs that are core to the power of our applications. We partner with people across Asana to create our product, shape our brand, and drive greater impact through design. We use design to solve challenges and create experiences that customers love. We also take the time to get weird and have fun along the way.

We believe every designer should have the opportunity to grow and learn by utilizing their strengths and nurturing their interests.

This role is based in our Vancouver office with an office-centric hybrid schedule. The standard in-office days are Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday. Most Asanas have the option to work from home on Wednesdays. Working from home on Fridays depends on the type of work you do and the teams with which you partner. If you're interviewing for this role, your recruiter will share more about the in-office requirements.

What You’ll Achieve

Lead, coach, and grow a team of content designers by setting clear expectations, developing their craft and careers, and building a team with a clear mission and measurable outcomes.
Own the end-to-end quality of content across Asana's portfolio of products, including Agentic Work Management, Service Management, Client Management, and Command.
Define and evolve Asana’s product voice, terminology, and content standards, building scalable systems—such as guidelines, patterns, design-system content, and tooling—that empower every product team.
Establish Asana’s AI voice by defining the voice and tone for AI Teammates and agents, developing conversation design patterns, and distilling characteristics that make humans and agents feel like one team.
Partner with Design, Product Management, Engineering, Research, and Product Marketing leaders to integrate content strategy into roadmap decisions and make content design a visible, measurable part of how Asana ships.
Collaborate with Marketing and Brand Creative to ensure a cohesive voice and tone across the entire customer journey.
Lead high-impact content design initiatives, including flagship launches, AI and conversational experiences, cross-product naming, and information architecture.
Partner with Research and Data Science to validate content decisions through experiments and user studies, advocating for content improvements backed by evidence.
Shape how the broader Asana Design organization operates as a member of its leadership team, including evolving design and content workflows alongside AI-assisted product development.

About You

Demonstrates curiosity about AI tools and emerging technologies, with a willingness to learn and leverage them to enhance productivity, collaboration, or decision-making
10+ years of experience designing content for digital products, including 4+ years managing content designers or UX writers and developing senior and lead-level practitioners.
Proven track record of running a day-to-day content design practice—setting priorities across multiple teams, driving consistency, shipping products, and advocating for content design best practices cross-functionally.
Demonstrated ability to build influence with Product, Engineering, and Marketing leaders so content design is embedded early in decision-making rather than treated as a final review step.
Hands-on expertise in UX writing and content strategy for web and mobile products, covering microcopy, nomenclature, information architecture, accessibility, user education, and launch content.
Experience designing content for conversational or AI-powered experiences, paired with a clear point of view on how products should communicate when systems generate language.
Experience creating, governing, and scaling voice and tone guidelines and content systems—including AI content tooling—that cross-functional teams actively adopt.
Proficiency in leveraging both quantitative and qualitative research to inform, make, and defend content decisions.
Clear, persuasive written and verbal communication skills, with experience presenting to executives and cross-functional leadership.

At Asana, we're committed to building teams that include a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills, as this is critical to helping us achieve our mission. If you're interested in this role and don't meet every listed requirement, we still encourage you to apply.

What We’ll Offer

Our comprehensive compensation package plays a big part in how we recognize you for the impact you have on our path to achieving our mission. We believe that compensation should be reflective of the value you create relative to the market value of your role. To ensure pay is fair and not impacted by biases, we're committed to looking at market value which is why we check ourselves and conduct a yearly pay equity audit.

For this role, the estimated base salary range is between $180,000-$205,000. The actual base salary will vary based on various factors, including market and individual qualifications objectively assessed during the interview process. The listed range above is a guideline, and the base salary range for this role may be modified.

In addition to base salary, your compensation package may include additional components such as equity, sales incentive pay (for most sales roles), and benefits. If you're interviewing for this role, speak with your Talent Acquisition Partner to learn more about the total compensation and benefits for this role.

We strive to provide equitable and competitive benefits packages that support our employees worldwide and include:

Mental health, wellness & fitness benefits
Career coaching & support
Inclusive family building benefits
Long-term savings or retirement plans
In-office culinary options to cater to your dietary preferences

These are just some of the benefits we offer, and benefits may vary based on role, country, and local regulations. If you're interviewing for this role, speak with your Talent Acquisition Partner to learn more about the total compensation and benefits for this role.

Learn More About Our Team

About Us

Asana is a leading platform for human + AI collaboration. Millions of teams around the world rely on Asana to achieve their most important goals, faster. Asana has been named to Fortune's Best Workplaces for 7+ years and recognized by Fast Company, Forbes, and Gartner for excellence in workplace culture and innovation. We offer an exceptional office-centric culture while adopting the best elements of hybrid models to ensure that every one of our global team members can work together effortlessly. With 13+ offices all over the world, we are always looking for individuals who care about building technology that drives positive change in the world and a culture where everyone feels that they belong.

We believe in supporting people to do their best work and thrive. Our goal is to ensure that Asana upholds an environment where all people feel that they are respected and valued, whether they are applying for an open position or working at the company. We provide equal employment opportunities to all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Head of Frames
jobs.description:
Location:
This hybrid role requires 3 days on-site at our Burnaby, BC office and 2 days remote per week.

Welcome to Specsavers
– where we’re not just about eyecare and eyewear, but changing lives through better sight. Ranked the 5th Best Workplace™ in Canada and 12th globally by Great Place to Work®, we’re proud of our optometrist-owned model that makes high-quality, eyecare and eyewear accessible to all Canadians.

Founded 40 years ago in the UK by visionary husband and wife optometry duo Doug and Mary Perkins, Specsavers has remained privately owned since day one. Today, we are a $7.8 billion global business with over 45,000 colleagues across more than 2,700 retail optical locations.

In Canada, our support office is based in Burnaby, BC. Since entering the market in 2021, we’ve been scaling rapidly, now with over 270 locations nationwide. With advanced clinical equipment and a wide range of affordable, high-quality eyewear, we’re transforming the way Canadians experience eyecare.

If you’re passionate about making a difference and want to be part of a values-driven organization, join us as we continue to grow. Together, we can change lives through better sight.

What You’ll Do

The Head of Frames supports the Product Proposition Director in the planning and execution of the Canadian frame strategy. They will define and manage the frame portfolio, monitor performance, and maximize sales and margins. Strengthening the relevance, quality, and commercial performance of the frame range is central to this role.

Key Responsibilities

Product Portfolio Management

Effective range management performance support
Development of frame strategy to ensure alignment of range with business needs and Marketing strategy.
Planning and implementation of frame product launches and discontinuations, including management of obsolescence risks.
Ensure frame product quality is consistent and meets agreed commercial and technical standards.
Provide clear frame product guidance and support to relevant cross-functional teams.

Product Communications & Marketing

Collaborate in defining the Product Comms strategy and deliver to the highest standard.
Liaise with Marketing/PR to ensure consistent and credible communications are issued to external stakeholders (mainly Marketing and PR campaigns).
Build understanding of and pride in the frame portfolio through clear, compelling product communications.

Data Analysis and Reporting

Support the Product Proposition Director and the wider team through timely and effective analysis of frame sales, range performance, product mix, and margin.
Act as the “customer champion” in the development of the frame range, using factual and anecdotal evidence to evolve the range and its architecture.
Gather and synthesize input from partners, user groups, and cross-functional stakeholders to strengthen the frame range.
Ability to work cross functionally with local and global teams, internal and external
Demonstrated ability to build strong professional relationships with partners and colleagues, including Marketing, Retail and Finance leadership and supporting teams.
Proactively demonstrates and encourages team collaboration within the Product and Supply Chain teams locally and globally.
Maintain high levels of engagement with suppliers, licensors and other key external stakeholders.

What We’re Looking For

10 years’ experience in product, category, or portfolio leadership roles, ideally within frames, eyewear, or a related consumer product category.
Customer focused and highly organized: genuinely enjoys engaging with different interlocutors at all levels.
Demonstrated capacity to determine priorities, meet strict deadlines and effectively balance competing demands and the ability to work under pressure both independently and as a member of a team. Great attention to detail.
Excellent written, verbal and interpersonal communication skills with the ability to prepare and present reports and documentation of high quality and integrity and the capacity to deal with a wide range of clients and staff.
Demonstrated capacity to exercise sound judgment, initiative, diplomacy, tact and discretion and proven ability to handle information, and materials in a confidential and appropriate manner.

Nice to have

Experience within the optical, eyewear, frames, or healthcare product sector.
Able to demonstrate a proven track record of delivering innovative frame products, ranges, and portfolio solutions.
Able to demonstrate a genuine passion for the Products we sell.

Compensation:
$160,000 - $180,000 base salary, plus quarterly bonus, profit sharing, and benefits. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience.

Speccies’ Benefits

5 weeks of vacation and 1 paid volunteer day per year
1 extra paid day off plus an eyecare voucher to celebrate your birthday.
Health and dental benefits, RRSP matching and a Healthcare Spending Account active from your first day.
Mental health and wellbeing support, including $3,000 annually for practitioner care and access to our Employee Assistance Program.
Quarterly bonuses, based on your performance.
Annual Profit Share program to recognize your part in Specsavers’ success.
Free parking, access to the building gym, and a fully stocked kitchen with snacks and coffee/tea.
On‑site wellness offerings in-office, including RMT and yoga sessions.
Team and company social events, including holiday and annual celebrations.

Behaviours We Value

Collaborative: We work together as one Specsavers to deliver on our purpose
Curious: We question, explore, and seek out diverse perspectives to develop our knowledge and understanding
Courageous: We challenge the status quo, we experiment with good ideas, and we are brave, bold, and fast in our decision making
Compassionate: We care, support, and help each other
Commercial: We treat money wisely and make decisions that are good for our customers, our partners, our people and for the long term

We hope that in applying with us, you value these things as well!

Our Hybrid Work Model

Experience the best of both worlds. At Specsavers, we embrace a hybrid approach that balances in-office collaboration with the flexibility to work from home. We come together in office three days a week to connect, innovate, and keep our culture thriving.

Equal Opportunity Employer

At Specsavers, we are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. We believe that a diverse team enriches our work environment and enables us to achieve our goals. We are an equal opportunity employer and encourage candidates of all backgrounds and abilities to apply. If you believe you can contribute to our mission and vision, we welcome your application, even if you don't meet every qualification listed. We value the unique skills and perspectives each individual brings to our team.

Accessibility and Accommodations

We are committed to creating an inclusive and accessible workplace. If you require accommodations at any stage of the application or interview process, please let us know by contacting us at careers.ca@specsavers.com . We will work with you to meet your needs and ensure a fair and equitable experience.

jobs.title: Director, Major Capital Projects
jobs.description:
Career opportunities are presented in the language received.

The Saskatchewan Health Authority (SHA) is the largest employer in the province, with more than 45,000 staff and physicians and an annual operating budget exceeding $5 billion. As Canada’s largest fully integrated provincial health system, the SHA is responsible for delivering high-quality, patient-centred health care to 1.18 million residents across Saskatchewan.

With an extensive provincial footprint, the SHA oversees a network of 245 facilities, including 64 hospitals and approximately 9,000 long-term care beds. Its services span acute and hospital-based care, long-term care, mental health and addictions, primary health care, public health and community-based programs. Through a single, integrated health system, the SHA is working to improve how care is coordinated and delivered, strengthen population health outcomes and build a more consistent and sustainable health system in partnership with patients, providers and health system partners.

Reporting to the Executive Director, Capital Planning and Major Capital Projects, the Director, Major Capital Projects provides strategic leadership and oversight for complex capital initiatives that advance organizational priorities and support provincial health system objectives. The Director plays a key role in Saskatchewan’s health care system, ensuring the effective planning, delivery and execution of major capital projects. The Director provides leadership across the project lifecycle, ensuring effective governance, stakeholder engagement, risk management, resource alignment, and stewardship of public resources. The Director works collaboratively with operational leaders, system partners, government stakeholders, and project teams to advance project delivery, remove barriers, and achieve successful outcomes.

The successful candidate will be an accomplished capital projects leader with a demonstrated track record of planning and delivering large-scale capital initiatives, ideally within a health care or similarly complex environment. They will bring a strong understanding of the full capital project lifecycle, including strategic planning, business case development, procurement, design, construction and commissioning, along with the financial and operational acumen required to oversee significant capital budgets and a diverse project portfolio. A collaborative and engaging leader, they will be skilled at building high-performing teams, establishing effective governance structures and fostering productive relationships with a broad range of stakeholders. They will demonstrate the ability to navigate competing priorities, manage risk and drive results, while ensuring sound stewardship of public resources and advancing broader health system objectives.

To Apply

To fill this position, Saskatchewan Health Authority has partnered with leadership advisory firm Odgers. Applications are encouraged immediately and should be submitted at https://careers.odgers.com/en-ca/32328

We thank all those who express an interest, however only those chosen for further development will be contacted.

Odgers is deeply committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion in all the work that we do. Permanent - Full Time

We generate more than just power for the people of Saskatchewan. We also offer some of the best jobs in the province. Our challenging careers will help you grow, while being surrounded by a team committed to safety, openness, collaboration and accountability. Apply no later than 12/13/2026 to be considered for this opportunity.

Job Summary

The Director, Large Reactor Deployment reports to the Vice President, Nuclear Development Division and provides strategic leadership and direction for assessing and advancing large nuclear generation opportunities. As a member of SaskPower’s Senior Management team, this role plans, organizes, directs and controls large nuclear development activities to advance project readiness and align departmental work with SaskPower’s strategic goals and objectives.

The position leads an integrated development program spanning commercial negotiations, site assessment, engineering studies, regulatory planning, Indigenous and public engagement, policy and planning. As the initiative progresses, the role will also oversee scheduling, construction planning, project management, vendor relationships and project controls.

The Person

The Director, Large Reactor Deployment is a strategic and results-oriented leader with extensive experience advancing or delivering large-scale industrial or energy projects. They can integrate technical, regulatory, commercial, public policy, engagement and organizational considerations into clear priorities and credible recommendations.

The ideal candidate builds trusted relationships across SaskPower and with external partners, communicates effectively with senior decision-makers and affected parties, and remains effective in a complex and continually changing environment. They demonstrate sound judgement and accountability when managing significant budgets, confidential matters, competing interests and organizational outcomes. They lead long-term planning and decision-making, anticipating future needs, risks and impacts across the organization and the public

Key Accountabilities

Provide strategic leadership and direction for large nuclear development, including technology evaluation, site assessment, engineering studies, regulatory readiness, and project readiness.
Establish the development strategy and roadmap, and lead integrated planning for scope, budgets, schedules, resources, risks and interdependencies.
Allocate human, financial and material resources and establish appropriate financial, administrative and project controls.
Lead site assessment activities and integrate regulatory, Indigenous rights and engagement, public engagement, engineering and commercial considerations into project development.
Oversee development-stage contracts, vendor relationships and major advisory arrangements, and establish effective partnerships with nuclear operators, technology vendors, contractors, utilities and government.
Develop recommendations on reactor technology, site and investment options, considering technical, regulatory, commercial, affordability and engagement requirements.
Coordinate contributions from Engineering, Regulatory Affairs, Procurement, Indigenous Relations, engagement teams and other internal partners.
Provide the Vice President, Executive, Board of Directors and government committees with recommendations and presentations regarding project strategy, budgets, schedules, risks and investment considerations.
Lead negotiations and collaboration with private-sector, utility and government partners within approved authorities and direction.
Anticipate, resolve and prevent departmental and project issues using sound judgement, practical solutions and appropriate escalation.
Lead managers, employees, embedded contractors and consultants; establish clear accountabilities and support employee engagement, performance and succession planning.
Foster a strong nuclear safety culture grounded in a questioning attitude, accountability, teamwork and sound decision-making.
Other related duties as assigned.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

Degree in Engineering, Business Administration, Social Sciences, Humanities or another related discipline.
Related professional designation(s) and/or certification(s) would be considered an asset.
Ten (10) years of extensive experience leading the development, planning or delivery of large-scale industrial or energy projects, with demonstrated expertise in multidisciplinary leadership, project governance, scheduling and risk management.
Knowledge of large nuclear reactor development, including technology assessment, site evaluation, engineering interfaces, lifecycle requirements and the transition from feasibility studies to investment and execution readiness.
Understanding of the Canadian nuclear regulatory framework and applicable assessment and licensing processes.
Understanding of electricity supply planning, transmission and grid integration considerations associated with large generating units.
Knowledge of major-project development and delivery models, including governance, scheduling, risk management, commercial relationships and contracting.
Ability to establish and maintain effective relationships with nuclear operators, technology vendors, contractors, utilities, government, Indigenous Relations and other internal and external parties.
Ability to provide strategic direction, integrate multidisciplinary work and lead effectively through uncertainty and change.
Excellent negotiation, facilitation, communication, presentation and decision-making skills.
Ability to manage complex and highly confidential matters with sensitivity and professionalism.
Ability to lead and develop managers, employees, contractors and consultants while establishing accountability for safe, timely and cost-effective execution.
Demonstrated skill in SaskPower’s competencies.
Must have a continuing record of professional development.

A suitable combination of relevant education and experience may also be considered.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Medical Science Liaison Head
jobs.description:
Kyowa Kirin is a fast-growing global specialty pharmaceutical company that applies state-of-the-art biotechnologies to discover and deliver novel medicines in four disease areas: bone and mineral; intractable hematologic; hematology oncology; and rare disease. A Japan-based company, our goal is to make people smile by delivering breakthroughs where no adequate treatments currently exist, working from drug discovery to product development and commercialization. In North America, we are headquartered in Princeton, NJ, with offices in California, Massachusetts, and Ontario

Summary Of Job

The Senior Director, Kyowa Kirin North America (KKNA) Medical Science Liaison Head provides strategic and operational leadership for Medical Science Liaison teams across KKNA therapeutic areas. This role establishes the enterprise MSL vision, operating model, and annual and long-range strategic plans; drives consistent, high-quality field execution; and develops field medical leadership capabilities. The Senior Director ensures that scientific exchange, external stakeholder engagement, and medical insights advance Medical Affairs and organizational priorities while meeting the highest standards of scientific integrity, ethics, and compliance. The role serves as a senior Medical Affairs leader and strategic partner, ensuring that field medical perspectives inform evidence generation, launch readiness, lifecycle planning, and organizational decision-making. Through a dotted-line relationship with the Global Head of Medical Strategic Capabilities and Scientific Exchange, the role ensures alignment of KKNA MSL strategy and execution with the Global Field Medical operating model and standards, while addressing regional needs and applicable local requirements.

Essential Functions

Leadership and Organizational Management

Lead, coach, and develop MSL Directors, Associate Directors, and MSLs across therapeutic areas, establishing clear accountabilities, leadership expectations, succession plans, and talent-development priorities.
Build and sustain a high-performing, inclusive, and collaborative field medical organization capable of operating effectively across therapeutic areas and within a complex matrix environment.
Establish a performance-management framework that aligns team objectives, field execution standards, and outcomes with Medical Affairs priorities.
Regularly evaluate organizational and individual performance, provide timely feedback, and implement development or improvement plans as appropriate.
Define the MSL capability framework and proficiency expectations; identify organizational capability gaps; and oversee development plans that strengthen scientific expertise, insight generation, stakeholder engagement, and communication effectiveness.
Ensure MSL teams remain current on product data, clinical evidence, scientific literature, industry developments, and regulations governing field medical activities.
Lead organizational change and the adoption of new capabilities, technologies, processes, and ways of working that enhance field medical effectiveness.

Strategic Planning and Execution

Lead the development, prioritization, and execution of annual and long-range MSL strategies, operating plans, and budgets in alignment with therapeutic area, Medical Affairs, and enterprise objectives.
Establish thought leader and healthcare professional engagement strategies that support meaningful scientific exchange and address defined medical and patient needs.
Translate organizational priorities into clear field medical objectives, execution standards, resource plans, and measurable outcomes.
Allocate people, budget, and technology resources based on strategic priorities, scientific opportunity, patient need, and anticipated field medical impact.
Identify emerging opportunities and risks and recommend adjustments to strategy, operating plans, and resource deployment.

Scientific Exchange, Stakeholder Engagement, and Medical Insights

Provide leadership to MSL teams in building trusted scientific relationships with thought leaders, healthcare professionals, academic institutions, and other relevant external stakeholders.
Ensure that external scientific exchange is evidence-based, balanced, responsive to stakeholder needs, and conducted in accordance with applicable policies and standards.
Establish expectations and processes for the systematic collection, synthesis, escalation, communication, and application of field medical insights to ensure these inform evidence-generation plans, medical strategy, educational priorities, launch readiness, lifecycle planning, and organizational decision-making.
Evaluate the quality and strategic relevance of stakeholder engagement and medical insights, not solely the volume of activity.
Represent the MSL function in senior internal and external forums, as appropriate.

Cross-Functional and Enterprise Leadership

Serve as the senior MSL function partner to Medical Directors, Global Medical Affairs, Clinical Development, Research, Franchise, Commercial, Market Access, and other relevant leadership teams.
Clarify roles, decision rights, and ways of working between MSL teams and cross-functional partners.
Provide senior leadership with clear recommendations regarding field medical priorities, capabilities, organizational design, resource requirements, risks, and opportunities.
Champion the strategic value of the MSL organization and communicate its contribution to Medical Affairs and enterprise objectives.

Performance, Impact, and Continuous Improvement

Own the MSL performance and impact framework, including the selection, implementation, monitoring, and communication of quantitative and qualitative measures that demonstrate execution quality, stakeholder value, insight impact, and progress against strategic objectives.
Use data, analytics, and field intelligence to guide resource allocation, identify performance trends, and improve MSL effectiveness.
Provide senior leadership with timely, balanced assessments of risks, resource needs, and opportunities.
Sponsor continuous improvement initiatives that strengthen MSL processes, systems, governance, and stakeholder experience.

Governance, Ethics, and Compliance

Set and model high standards and ensure that MSL activities adhere to applicable laws, regulations, policies, standard operating procedures, and Medical Affairs governance requirements.
Ensure teams receive appropriate training and understand their individual accountability for compliant execution.
Identify, escalate, and address compliance, quality, operational, or reputational risks associated with field medical activities and partner with Legal, Regulatory, Compliance, and other control functions to strengthen governance and resolve identified gaps.

Education

A doctoral level scientific or clinical degree, such as MD, PharmD, or PhD, is preferred. A relevant advanced degree or professional qualification in the life sciences, nursing, pharmacy, medicine, or a related discipline is required.

Experience

A minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in Medical Affairs or field medical leadership.
At least five years of experience leading managers and geographically dispersed medical teams.
Demonstrated success developing and executing field medical strategy across multiple therapeutic areas, products, or lifecycle stages.
Experience managing budgets, organizational resources, operating plans, and competing strategic priorities.
Proven ability to partner with senior cross-functional and global leaders in a complex matrix organization.
Demonstrated experience leading organizational change, capability development, and continuous-improvement initiatives.
Experience supporting launch readiness, evidence generation, medical insights, and lifecycle planning is strongly preferred.
Prior field medical or MSL experience is preferred

Leadership Competencies

Demonstrated enterprise leadership, strategic thinking, and sound judgment.
Ability to translate organizational priorities into clear objectives, operating plans, execution standards, and resource decisions.
Proven success leading leaders, building high-performing teams, developing talent, and strengthening succession pipelines.
Ability to guide teams through ambiguity, complexity, growth, and organizational change.
Exceptional executive communication, influencing, and stakeholder-management skills.
Ability to build alignment across a complex multinational matrix while maintaining scientific integrity and appropriate Medical Affairs independence.
Strong business and financial acumen, with disciplined execution and accountability for outcomes.
Demonstrated ability to identify organizational risks and opportunities and present clear, evidence-based recommendations to senior leadership.
Cultural sensitivity and the ability to establish trust and consensus across diverse teams and stakeholders.
Strong commitment to patient needs, scientific excellence, continuous learning, and talent development.

Non-Technical Skills

Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment while managing ambiguity effectively. Commitment to the highest ethical, legal, regulatory, and scientific standards. Demonstrated professionalism, sound judgment, and scientific integrity. Passion for personal learning and professional development. Cultural sensitivity and adaptability within multinational organizations.

Physical Demands

Normal office or remote-working environment with prolonged sitting and extensive computer work.
Ability to drive or fly to meetings and business activities.

Working Conditions

The position requires up to 50% of domestic and international travel, including occasional weekend commitments.

Compensation And Benefits

The anticipated base salary range for this position is $290,000 to $325,000
. The actual base salary offered may vary based on relevant experience, skills, qualifications, education, applicable licenses and certifications, job-related knowledge, location, and business and organizational needs.

Salary is one part of the total compensation package. Kyowa Kirin North America offers:

401(k) with company match
Annual bonus program
Paid time off and holidays, including summer and winter shutdowns, sick days, and volunteer days
Medical, dental, prescription drug, and vision coverage
Health savings account (HSA) and flexible spending account (FSA) programs
Well-being and work-life programs
Life and disability insurance
Concierge services
Long-term incentive program, subject to job level and performance
Pet insurance
Tuition assistance
Employee referral awards

The compensation and benefits described in this posting apply to candidates hired in the United States. Candidates hired outside the United States are eligible for compensation and benefits in accordance with their local market.

Integrity and Equal Employment Opportunity

KKNA and all of its employees have an obligation to act in accordance with the law and with integrity in all our operations and interactions.

It is the policy of Kyowa Kirin North America, Inc. to provide equal employment opportunity to all qualified persons without regard to race, religion, creed, color, pregnancy, sex, age, national origin, disability, genetic trait or predisposition, veteran status, marital status, sexual orientation or affection preference or citizenship status or any other category protected by law.
