jobs.title: Director of Finance And Operations
jobs.description:
About the role

Few Director roles hand you both finance and operations, and a mandate to rebuild them with AI tools. You get access to the engineering team for improvements implementation. This role has both, plus stock options, so you own a stake in the outcome.

Positrace is rebuilding how finance and operations run, and you lead it. You own the processes where the two meet, across Canada and Mexico, and you lead an AI-first transformation and tool automation across operations and finance processes.

This is a builder's seat. You get an engineering team that ships what you specify, an in-house data and AI platform, and executives who want the change. If you have transformed a process end to end and want a first Director role with real scope, this is it.

You report to the COO , with a dotted line to the CFO for finance, and have direct access to CEO.

What you will own

Hands-on first
You run every core process yourself a few times before you change, delegate or automate it. You will know the business from the inside, and your notes become the procedure and the automation spec.

Finance
Month-end close and controls.
Own/supervise close for three entities to a calendar, reduce time to close.
Tax and compliance calendar.
One calendar for Canada and Mexico, and nothing filed late.
Billing and collections.
Invoices that tie to the ledger and payments that apply themselves.
Cash and treasury operations.
Instrumented and automated, starting with a 13-week forecast that refreshes itself.
Reporting and planning automation.
Designed with the CFO, so the management pack assembles itself from the ledgers.
Audit readiness.
Audit-ready by fiscal 2027 year end.

Operations
Procurement and suppliers.
Vendor management and forecasting for hardware and connectivity in two countries.
Quote approval and deal margin automation.
You set the margin and payback rules; the system checks every quote.
Inventory, warehouse and logistics reporting.
Two warehouses, and stock that matches the count.
Procedures and governance.
Every process written down, owned and followed.
Operating cost management and control.
Spend that ties to the ledgers, and savings you can show.

Systems and automation
Billing platform.
You are the business process owner. Engineering builds; you set the rules and sign off every change.
AI automation.
Built with the CTO's team on Cortex, our in-house AI platform. Finance first, then operations.
Ledger and ERP path.
Yours to recommend: build our platform into an accounting-grade subledger, or move to a full ERP.
One system of record per process.
No parallel spreadsheets.

Team
You lead the operations team and the finance teams in both countries. The Controller reports to you. Automate first, hire second.
You work alongside the CFO, who leads lenders, the board, tax strategy and accounting policy. You prepare, the CFO reviews and signs, and you learn the capital side from the seat next to it.

Who you are

Must have

At least 5 years in audit at a Big 4 or national firm, and a CPA designation. We see audit as the school.
At least 2 years of hands-on finance work in industry, at a software or hardware company. This is where you learned to manage and to deliver change fast.
Multi-subsidiary experience: you have closed and consolidated across entities.
Finance experience at a company with at least CAD 20 million in revenue, where automation is a necessity.
One transformation you led from start to finish, with a before and an after to show.
You build with tools yourself: AI scripting, workflow automation.
You have managed people and are ready to lead managers.
You document what you own, so others can run it without you.
Based in Metro Vancouver, or relocating, working from our Burnaby office and able to travel to our Mexico office.

Good to have

A recurring-revenue business model, ideally one that also ships hardware.
Cross-border, multi-currency accounting, especially Canada and Mexico.
Spanish is a nice to have, but AI translation will help you otherwise.
Procurement, inventory or field-operations exposure.

This is likely your first Director role. We care more about what you have changed, and how fast your scope has grown, than about the size of your last title. If you have the first five and the drive, we want to hear from you.

What we offer

Finance and operations in one seat.
Breadth that most Director roles do not offer.
Stock options.
You share in the value you help build.
Room to build.
An engineering team, an in-house data and AI platform, and leaders who want the old way replaced.
A seat at the table.
You sit on the senior leadership team and work directly with the CEO.
Scope that grows as you deliver.
You take on the role in phases, and each one you land opens the next.
Salary range:
CAD $150,000 to $180,000 per year, plus stock options and benefits.
Location:
Burnaby, BC (Metrotown). You work from our Burnaby office and travel to our Mexico office in Guadalajara as needed.

About Positrace and how to apply

Positrace builds fleet management software: GPS telematics, connected cameras and asset tracking for commercial fleets in Canada and Mexico. We have been in business for 19 years, and thousands of vehicle fleets trust Positrace every day. We are founder-led and profitable, with teams in Burnaby and Guadalajara.

To apply, send your résumé and a short note, one page at most, describing one process you transformed: what it was, what you changed, and the measured result.

Positrace is an equal-opportunity employer. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates.

jobs.description:
UNITED WAY BC IS PROUD TO BE RECOGNIZED AS ONE OF CANADA'S TOP 100 EMPLOYERS FOR 2026 !

ABOUT US – WHY WE’RE HERE:

Across British Columbia, communities are facing urgent and complex social challenges. United Way BC is committed to delivering lasting, community-driven impact in partnership with diverse populations across the province including Indigenous communities whose territories we live and work on. From Vancouver Island to the Lower Mainland, and across the Thompson Nicola Cariboo, Southern Interior, Trail and District, and East Kootenay regions, we walk alongside communities to create meaningful and equitable change. 

Our mission
is to strengthen vital connections that support people in need in our communities. 

Our vision
is to create a healthy, caring and inclusive community. 

How do we deliver on our mission and vision – by delivering resources and support for those who need it most, and by living our values of being collaborative, compassionate, strategic, responsive, accountable, and inspiring. 

For a more in-depth to look into our work and programs, please visit: www.uwbc.ca.

ABOUT YOU:
You're a strategic technology and data leader with at least seven years of progressively responsible experience, including three years leading teams. You've developed enterprise technology and data strategies and overseen cloud, applications, cybersecurity, BI and data governance. You've also led change and adoption of new tools, including AI and automation, with the right safeguards. You manage budgets and vendors with confidence, and you advise senior leaders in clear, practical terms. As an inclusive, collaborative leader, you build trusted relationships across a hybrid, multi-location organization. A degree in a related field, or equivalent experience, is required. Experience in nonprofit, public-sector or unionized settings, and with platforms such as Microsoft 365, Azure, Power BI and Salesforce, is an asset.

JOB PURPOSE:
The Director, Information Technology & Business Intelligence is UWBC’s most senior technology professional and the principal partner to the Chief Financial & Technology Officer (CFTO) on all technology and data matters. Accountable to the CFTO, the Director is trusted to set strategy, manage budgets and run operations for Information Technology (IT) and Business Intelligence (BI), and to lead the team and external partners in delivering reliable services, trusted information and effective technology adoption.

The Director sets priorities, standards and resource allocations; decides on vendors, risk mitigation and staffing; recommends enterprise strategies and significant investments to the CFTO; and escalates matters with significant organizational, financial, security, privacy or reputational implications. Working with senior leadership and with finance, fundraising, community impact and regional teams, the Director champions innovation while balancing provincial consistency, regional needs, staff capacity and responsible stewardship.

The role requires broad knowledge of technology strategy and governance, cybersecurity and privacy, cloud and enterprise applications, BI and data stewardship, and technology financial and vendor management, together with the judgment to direct specialists and external partners. It also requires inclusive leadership of change, innovation and people, and the ability to build trusted cross-functional relationships.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Strategy and advisory

Lead an integrated technology, data and digital strategy and adaptable roadmap that drives innovation, aligning investments, architecture and governance with organizational priorities, capacity, cost, risk and long-term value.

Advise senior leadership on significant technology, data, cybersecurity and digital opportunities and risks, translating complex issues into clear options and recommendations.

Agree priorities with business leaders, retaining business ownership of process changes and outcomes and escalating unresolved priorities or material risks.

Champion innovation by assessing and introducing technologies, automation and AI through practical use cases, controlled pilots and measured results, with privacy, security, human oversight and monitoring.

Contribute to organizational planning and represent UWBC with technology partners and external stakeholders.

IT operations and enterprise systems

Oversee reliable, secure and integrated infrastructure, cloud, networks, devices, telecommunications, enterprise applications and end-user services against defined service standards, measured by service availability and incident response times.

Govern technology and application selection, integration and lifecycle management, with clear business and technical ownership, documentation, and asset, licensing, access and configuration controls.

Cybersecurity, risk and resilience

Lead cybersecurity and technology risk management, including identity and access controls, secure use, risk assessment, mitigation and reporting across operations and investments, measured by security and recovery readiness, including tested recovery.

Ensure recovery, backup and incident-response capabilities are documented, tested and aligned with business continuity priorities.

Lead responses to significant disruptions and cybersecurity incidents, advising senior leadership on material risks.

With designated organizational leaders, define technology responsibilities for privacy, information management and enterprise risk, including retention and disposal, third-party data handling and privacy-incident escalation, in line with applicable privacy legislation such as BC’s Personal Information Protection Act.

Business intelligence, analytics and data governance

Deliver the BI and analytics plan with business owners, prioritizing dashboards, reporting and forecasting that support planning, operations, fundraising and community-impact decisions, measured by BI usage and data quality.

Oversee data architecture, integration and governance, setting ownership, quality and access standards that protect sensitive information.

Build data literacy through practical training so teams can use reports, shared definitions and reliable information in decisions and evaluation.

Projects and change

Lead cross-functional initiatives collaboratively, with clear executive sponsorship, business ownership, outcomes, scope, resources, milestones and success measures, delivering on time and cost.

Resolve competing operational, technical, financial, security and stakeholder needs, developing new approaches where existing practices fall short.

Co-design improvements with staff and business owners, leading readiness, process redesign, communication, training and post-launch support, sequenced to staff capacity to sustain adoption of new systems and tools.

Evaluate outcomes with business owners against agreed adoption, service, staff-time, data-quality, cost and risk measures, and recommend changes where benefits are not sustained.

People leadership

Lead integrated IT and BI functions, setting clear responsibilities, priorities, service expectations and performance objectives and allocating capacity across operations and initiatives.

Coach employees and leaders, and oversee recruitment, performance, engagement, development, succession and knowledge continuity.

Build an inclusive, collaborative, accountable and service-oriented culture and strong working relationships across UWBC, measured by team engagement and retention.

Financial and vendor management

Manage operating and capital budgets, project costs, capacity and funding needs, measured by budget performance against plan. Recommend significant investments and improve value from licensing, subscriptions and services.

Oversee vendors, consultants and managed services, including selection, contracts, renewals and performance, with corrective action where needed.

Ensure technology procurement and expenditures comply with organizational policies.

Qualifications and requirements: Education

University degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Administration, Data/Analytics or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education, training and relevant professional experience.

Advanced education or certification in technology governance, cybersecurity, data management, cloud or project management is an asset.

Experience

At least seven years of progressively responsible technology, digital or BI/data experience, including three years leading technology, data or multidisciplinary teams.

Demonstrated experience developing enterprise technology, digital or data strategies and overseeing operations, cloud, applications, cybersecurity, technology risk, BI and data governance.

Demonstrated experience leading technology implementations and cross-functional change, including AI or automation, through staff engagement, process redesign, training and sustained adoption, with measurable benefits and safeguards.

Experience managing budgets, contracts, vendors and external service providers.

Assets: experience in complex, multi-location, nonprofit, public-sector or unionized environments; and experience integrating or deriving insight from CRM, financial or ERP systems and modern data platforms, such as Microsoft 365, Azure, Power BI, Salesforce and Microsoft data warehouse technologies.

working conditions:

Works with confidential, sensitive and security-related organizational information, balancing concurrent strategic, operational and stakeholder priorities and making timely decisions on emerging risks and issues.

Works in a hybrid, multi-location environment with occasional travel within British Columbia.

Occasional work outside regular business hours may be required in connection with significant system implementations, service disruptions or cybersecurity incidents.

Other related duties as assigned.

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
About Nuvollo

Founded in 2010 and headquartered in Toronto, Nuvollo Corp has established itself as a leader in delivering secure, high-performance cloud and IT infrastructure solutions to businesses across North America. A fast-growing cloud company focused on managing and operating business critical systems such as Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) requiring high availability, secure and predictable environments. Nuvollo’s commitment to reliability, compliance, and customer-centric service has allowed it to build long-standing relationships with clients in highly regulated industries such as healthcare, finance, and professional services.

In August 2025, Nuvollo expanded its North American platform through the acquisition of a U.S.-based business, strengthening its market presence and broadening its service capabilities. As the company continues its strong growth trajectory, Nuvollo is focused on strengthening its leadership team and building the internal capabilities needed to scale. A key priority is enhancing its financial management, strategic planning, and reporting functions to support continued expansion, integration activities, and investor reporting.

Snowdon Partners
, a leading mid-market private investment firm, has recently made an important investment in Nuvollo, and has partnered with them to launch a search for a Director of Finance
. This role represents a unique opportunity to build and lead a finance function in a growing private equity-backed business.

The Role

Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer, working closely with the private equity CFO, and managing a team of four (4) direct reports, the Director of Finance serves as the company’s financial quarterback and is a key member of the leadership team, participating in strategic discussions and supporting all areas of the business.

The ideal candidate will not only build and implement accurate and timely financial reports, tailored KPIs, and actionable insights to drive the business forward, but will also develop best-in-class budgeting and forecasting tools, and lead multi-currency, multi-country consolidation, an exciting opportunity to shape the company’s financial reporting capabilities. Given the recent private equity investment in the company, this role will operate at a slightly faster pace than traditional director of finance positions, providing direct exposure to the private equity CFO and investors, and offering genuine participation in strategic decision-making.

Who You Are

The successful candidate is a hands-on accounting and finance leader with extensive experience in multi-currency, international consolidation and a strong track record of building scalable financial processes. You know that growth and management start with getting the basics right-timely, accurate reporting and robust controls – but you also understand that true financial leadership extends to driving strategy, supporting growth, and navigating complex international operations. You are energized by change, resilient in the face of challenges, and skilled at identifying which initiatives will deliver lasting impact.

You will dive into Nuvollo’s financial results, lead consolidation across multiple currencies and international entities, and work closely with the team to develop KPIs, reporting frameworks, best-in-class budgeting and forecasting tools. Your experience supporting acquisitions, integration initiatives, or international cross-selling efforts will allow you to contribute meaningfully to strategic growth opportunities as Nuvollo continues to scale. You show up as your authentic self, approaching new challenges with purpose, energy, and enthusiasm, and are motivated by the opportunity to shape Nuvollo’s financial future in a dynamic, fast-growing environment.

What You Will Build

Reporting and controls:
using data, you will build actionable insights and enhance our executive team’s visibility and decision-making.
Manage the company’s financial accounts.
Identify, create, and implement financial controls.
Develop Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and create management dashboards to allow management to track performance of critical data points.
Prepare annual budgets and update with actual results throughout the year.
Prepare monthly and quarterly reporting packages, including year-to-date performance and projected year-end results.
Prepare compliance reports and financial packages for lender partners.
Become the “go-to” leader internally for financial performance data.

Financial accounting and cash management:
as our financial quarterback, you will ensure our accounting is always up to date and our cash position is optimized, balancing growth requirements and opportunistic capital deployment with real-time cash constraints.
Compile, close, and prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements (Income Statement, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow), as well as discussion materials presenting key performance trends for management decision-making.
Verify staff accountants’ work to ensure quality of data entry to the general ledger.
Prepare backup schedules for annual third-party accounting audit procedures.
Verify weekly bank reconciliations and take necessary actions to proactively manage the company’s cash flow.
Develop cash flow forecasts to manage cash requirements for growth investments.
Track equipment purchases, improvements, dispositions, and work with operations teams to optimize fixed asset management.
Manage and oversee working capital accounts, including invoicing and receivables, supplier payments, and prepaid expenses.

International operations & growth enablement:
as Nuvollo continues to expand, you will strengthen our ability to manage international growth and support sales.
Lead multi-currency, multi-entity consolidation and reporting.
Ensure compliance with international accounting standards and local regulations in jurisdictions where Nuvollo operates.
Build scalable reporting processes that allow management to track performance across countries and business entities.
Partner with leaders to provide financial analysis supporting international cross-selling initiatives and expansion opportunities.
Contribute financial integration support for acquisitions in new markets.

Information technology:
while reviewing and assessing processes, you will integrate technology into our financial practices to help Nuvollo become more effective as an organization.
Ensure integration of ERP and CRM solutions with our accounting systems in collaboration with the finance group of Snowdon Partners.
Act as key liaison during implementation of new software solutions and lead change management with the Nuvollo team.
Identify and implement a scalable ERP platform.
Identify and implement automation solutions for recurring accounting activities, such as A/P automation, payroll single-point management, and field expense tracking.

High-performing team:
you will lead a strong team of accounting staff.
Build, foster, coach, and mentor a highly engaged accounting team.
Create an environment to develop, attract, and retain top talent.
Introduce best practices and instill a mindset of continuous improvement.

Strategic planning:
as the company’s finance leader, you will have the mandate to integrate long-term thinking into Nuvollo’s financial management practices, ensuring soundness and scalability are part of our ethos.
Support the senior leadership team in developing the company’s strategic plans.
Lead long-term financial planning, including forecasting and budgeting.
Performance management: analyze and make recommendations regarding service lines, staff utilization, operations, volumes, and profitability.
Provide executive leadership and financial oversight for procurement, and vendor management activities, ensuring purchasing strategies, supplier relationships, and spending decisions align with the company's financial, operational, and strategic objectives.

Tax management:
you will maintain our standing with the relevant tax authorities.
Work with the company’s external accountants to prepare and file year-end tax declarations.
Prepare and file other tax declarations as required.
Prepare documentation for and provide support during government audits.

Your Profile

You hold a bachelor’s or master’s degree in accounting and a Canadian CPA designation, with a minimum of 8 years experience in a similar leadership role.
You demonstrate a strong understanding of GAAP/ASPE and have consistently applied superior technical accounting knowledge in prior roles.
You have prior experience working within an IT/MSP business (preferred).

jobs.description:
**Join a Challenger**  

  

At EQ, we're remaking banking so every Canadian gets ahead, every day. Serving nearly 4 million Canadians from coast to coast, we offer a wide variety of financial services from banking and lending, to trust and credit union solutions.  

  

We've been at this since 1970, challenging the conventions of traditional banking with smarter, faster, and more connected financial experiences.  

  

**What's kept us moving?** The people behind it all: challengers who ask better questions, push back on old assumptions, and look for a better way forward.  

  

If you're driven to help reshape how banking works for Canadians and the businesses that power our economy, this could be your next big opportunity.  

  

We can’t wait to get to know you!

### **Purpose of the Job**



The Vice President, Enterprise Risk Management is a senior member of the CRO’s leadership team and serves as the CRO and Deputy CRO’s primary partner on enterprise risk governance, leading the second\-line ERM function and the continued development and operation of a forward\-looking risk management program aligned with regulatory expectations and commensurate with EQ Bank’s size, scope and complexity.  

  

The VP, ERM will provide the vision and roadmap to further embed ERM across the organization, working closely with business leaders to strengthen risk management capabilities while providing independent oversight and effective challenge on strategic and business decisions. The role will oversee the Bank’s enterprise\-wide view of risk, including its Board\-approved Risk Appetite Framework, management and reporting of key risks, and reporting to the Board and Enterprise Risk Management Committee (ERMC), while supporting the CRO and Deputy CRO in interactions with OSFI and other regulatory stakeholders.  

  

The VP, ERM will also lead the risk management aspects of integration of PC Financial with EQ Bank and build a high\-performing ERM team that is nimble and innovative, enabling EQ Bank to achieve its strategic objectives while operating within its risk appetite.



### **Risk Governance**

* Lead the risk governance program. This covers owning and maintaining EQ Bank’s ERM framework, policy inventory, the annual review cycle, committee charters, escalation protocols, and coordinating policy submissions for ERMC.
* Act as the primary day\-to\-day point of contact with OSFI for the Risk function. Coordinate supervisory meetings, information requests, reviews, and follow\-up questions across the bank.
* Monitor OSFI guidance and regulatory developments affecting risk, capital, and liquidity. Assess their impact, lead the Bank's readiness plans, and promote a strong risk culture through clear accountability and training.
### **Risk Reporting**

* Own the CRO's quarterly reporting to the ERMC and the Board. This covers the enterprise risk dashboard, top and emerging risks, and the risk profile against appetite.
* Run ERMC as its secretariat and content lead. Set agendas, bring together reporting on credit, financial, operational, compliance and strategic risks, and track decisions and actions.
* Turn complex, multi\-risk information into short, decision\-focused insight for both committees. Bring forward material issues, top\-risk assessments, and thematic deep dives so leaders can act early.
* Prepare the CRO and Deputy CRO for committee discussions, and manage the Board risk agenda, follow\-up actions, and the annual risk governance calendar.
* Keep improving the reporting suite through better data, more automation, and a consistent risk taxonomy across the enterprise.
### **Risk Identification \& Assessment \& Risk Appetite Monitoring**

* Lead the annual enterprise\-wide risk assessment. Identify, assess, and rank material and emerging risks with the business lines and second\-line partners, and use the results to set the top\-risk inventory and ICAAP risk coverage.
* Run the annual refresh of the Risk Appetite Framework and Statement. Recalibrate metrics, limits, and early warning indicators to reflect the strategic plan, the financial forecast, stress testing results, and changes in the business, including the PC Financial portfolios.
* Steer the refresh through governance from management review to ERMC endorsement and Board approval. Cascade the approved appetite into business\-line limits and policies.
* Monitor risk appetite metrics against Board and management limits throughout the year. Report position and trends to ERMC and the Board.
* Run the escalation and remediation process for limit breaches and amber trends, including root\-cause analysis and tracking of corrective actions.
### **Risk \- Integration Management Office (IMO) and Convergence for PC Financial**

* Lead the risk workstream of the PC Financial integration. Coordinate second\-line oversight of integration milestones, synergy delivery, and the associated risks.
* Drive the convergence of PC Bank's risk frameworks, policies, limits, reporting, and controls onto EQ Bank's enterprise standards. Make sure combined\-entity reporting is accurate and complete.
* Lead the OSFI reporting related to IMO \& Convergence activities for the entire bank.
### **Let's Talk About You!**

* A university degree in Finance, Business, Economics or a quantitative field. A graduate degree (MBA or Master's) or a professional designation such as CFA, FRM, PRM or CPA is an asset.
* Minimum of 15 years of experience in a financial institution in a leadership capacity and at least 10 years’ experience in the ERM function leading quantitative teams
* Broad and deep experience in various risk functions, including credit, operational, market, stress testing and IRRBB
* Deep knowledge of OSFI expectations, including Corporate Governance, E\-21, B\-20, CAR, LAR and ICAAP. Direct experience managing supervisory relationships
* Has built a high\-performing team: recruits, trains, and mentors talent to drive employee retention and engagement. Provid

jobs.title: Director, Inventory Planning & Replenishment
jobs.description:
About The Role

Reporting to the Interim CEO, Performance & N9NE, the Director, Inventory Planning & Replenishment
is responsible for improving product availability and inventory health by ensuring the right approved products are available in the right quantities and locations, at the right time. The Director builds reliable forecasting and replenishment processes and drives effective use of Streamline demand-planning software while balancing customer service and inventory investment.
The Director leads planning and replenishment for Performance and N9NE and develops common planning methods with Source. This is a hands-on leadership role: it combines operating accountability, team development and planning-process improvement with strong cross-functional coordination across Customer Service, Purchasing, Warehousing and Logistics. The Director partners with Source's planning lead on common methods and Streamline adoption; Source retains its planning and replenishment execution and existing reporting structure.
The immediate priorities are reliable replenishment, effective use of Streamline and stronger internal capability.

Main Responsibilities

Forecasting

•Build rolling demand and supply plans from sales history, commercial input, product plans and supplier constraints. Test commercial assumptions and translate agreed demand into inventory requirements.
•Measure forecast error and bias at relevant replenishment horizons. Separate underlying demand, projects and growth assumptions; reconcile intercompany demand to avoid double-counting.
•Lead the demand-planning review with Sales and Product as part of the monthly planning cycle, reviewing and adjusting forecasts for trends, projects, promotions and new items.
Replenishment and inventory health
•Own Performance/N9NE replenishment plans and decisions within delegated limits: which approved items to buy or transfer, how much, when and where. Work with Purchasing and Operations to ensure approved replenishment plans are executed and exceptions are resolved.
•Maintain planning parameters, including lead times, safety stock, service targets, minimum/maximum levels, order cycles and supplier minimum order quantities (MOQs).
•Manage shortage, excess, slow-moving and obsolete inventory exposure. Recommend recovery, transfer and run-out actions; escalate material cash commitments, write-offs and service trade-offs.
•Use ABC/XYZ segmentation to set differentiated service levels, planning parameters and inventory policies.

Demand planning / Streamline ownership

•Establish the planning rules and logic for Streamline, including forecasting and replenishment parameters, workflow design, testing, user training and adoption. Maintain internal ownership after go-live.
•Partner with Source on its planning workflows and adoption. Work with IT, the implementation provider and named data owners on technical delivery, data validation and issue resolution.
•Manage planning milestones and issues, validate licence needs against actual workflows and test replenishment outputs. Embed routine planning in Streamline, with documented exceptions and overrides.

Review discipline and common methods

•Run weekly replenishment reviews and a practical monthly demand, supply and inventory review for Performance/N9NE. Present service, inventory and cash trade-offs for business-leader decisions.
•Lead agreed KPI definitions, planning controls and Streamline methods with Source. Sequence improvements against the agreed work plan and available capacity.

Inventory network planning

•Set and manage inventory-transfer rules within approved service and inventory targets; agree transfer frequency with Operations, balancing availability, inventory investment and freight cost.
•Evaluate hub-and-spoke replenishment with Operations and implement the agreed inventory-planning approach.
•Define stocked versus non-stocked item strategy by location.

Product lifecycle inventory planning

•Translate supplier lead times, minimum orders, production availability, container constraints and warehouse capacity into inventory plans. Purchasing and Operations retain supplier-order follow-up and physical execution.
•Develop first-buy, launch-stock, phased-receipt and run-out plans with Product and commercial teams. Quantify inventory exposure before commitments; Product/Sourcing retains product and supplier decisions.

People, knowledge and reporting

•Develop assigned planners, assess capacity and establish documented workflows and backup coverage. Capture critical operating knowledge and strengthen the team’s independence.
•Publish an inventory and availability scorecard with root causes, actions and owners. Work with Finance to validate benefits and with data owners to resolve planning-data issues.

Knowledge and Experience

•Typically, 8–12+ years of relevant demand, inventory or replenishment planning experience, including people leadership and cross-functional change.
•Proven improvement in availability and inventory health in multi-location distribution, imported finished goods, furniture, building products or a comparable inventory-intensive business.
•Hands-on delivery of planning-platform implementation or adoption. Streamline experience is an asset; broader planning and implementation capability is essential.
•Strong command of forecasting, safety stock, supplier lead times, service targets, order constraints, multi-location replenishment, working-capital trade-offs, ERP data and analytical tools.
•Experience establishing practical demand/supply reviews, developing planners and working constructively with Sales, Product, Purchasing, Operations and Finance.
•Relevant degree or equivalent experience; relevant planning or supply-chain certification is an asset. Ability to work from Burnaby and travel to Canadian and U.S. operating locations as required.
•A practical, hands-on builder who combines analytical depth with commercial judgement. The Director respects existing expertise, challenges assumptions constructively, explains decisions clearly and develops capability that stays with the organisation.

jobs.title: Director of Solution Architecture
jobs.description:
At PwC Canada, we're transforming the way we work—and the way our people and clients experience technology. Our Products & Technology team builds the digital products, enterprise applications, and AI-enabled platforms that power the firm and shape the future of professional services. We're a community of solvers combining technology, data, and human ingenuity to deliver sustained outcomes that matter. We're looking for a Director of Solution Architecture to lead our established team of Senior Solution Architects—a technically deep, business-savvy leader who can set direction, grow and develop talent, and partner with senior leaders across the firm to turn ambitious ideas into reality. Reporting to the Architecture and Development Leader, you will lead PwC Canada's Solution Architecture practice within Products & Technology. You will take ownership of our established team of Senior Solution Architects, elevate their performance, and grow the team's capabilities as our technology ambitions expand. The team designs AI-enabled products, enterprise applications, and platforms used across the firm's lines of service, ensuring our solutions are secure, scalable, resilient, aligned with enterprise architecture standards—and deliver real business value. This is a hands-on architecture leadership role. While your focus is on design and technical direction rather than execution, you'll be expected to understand the technology from the inside. You'll go deep into architecture diagrams, integration designs, data flows, platform configurations, and the realities of how solutions are implemented, engaging with technical trade-offs at a practitioner level. Your credibility with the team and with stakeholders will come from genuine technical depth and a willingness to go hands-on with architecture and implementation details when the situation calls for it, not from high-level concepts alone. Equally, this role operates at the intersection of business and technology. You'll be a trusted advisor to business stakeholders and organizational leaders, translating complex challenges into clear technology solutions, influencing strategic direction, and communicating in terms that resonate with executives. You'll also help shape how PwC Canada adopts emerging technologies, including generative and agentic AI.

The Opportunity

As a Director of Solution Architecture, unlock your potential and embrace the chance to drive meaningful outcomes that’ll elevate your career. Your role will include, but isn’t limited to:

Provide architecture oversight for digital products, enterprise applications, and AI-enabled solutions from ideation through production
Lead solution design decisions, balancing reusable platform components with business-specific needs
Guide the architecture of enterprise applications—including SaaS platforms, ERP, CRM, HR, finance, and collaboration systems—ensuring effective integration, extensibility, and alignment with our broader technology ecosystem
Go hands-on with architecture and technical implementation details when needed—working through complex integration patterns, data flows, platform configurations, or design problems alongside the team
Advise on the adoption of emerging technologies, including generative and agentic AI
Manage, coach, and mentor an established team of talented Senior Solution Architects, elevating performance and fostering a culture of technical excellence and continuous learning
Grow the team's capabilities over time—identifying skill gaps, developing talent from within, and recruiting new members as the practice expands
Evolve team structure and define new roles as the practice grows and technology priorities shift
Partner with Enterprise Architecture, Data, Security, and Risk teams to ensure solutions align with firm standards
Participate in architecture review boards and technology governance forums, advising on governance requirements, risk assessments, and policy exceptions
Contribute to PwC's broader architecture community—locally and across the global PwC network

What You’ll Bring

Your skills, knowledge, and experiences are what set you apart. Here’s what we look for:

Experience in technology roles, including significant time in solution or enterprise architecture, with extensive experience designing and delivering solutions within large, complex organizations
Proven experience leading, developing, and growing a team of Senior Solution Architects—setting technical direction, elevating performance, and fostering a high-performance culture, including in an Agile/DevOps environment
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science or Computer Engineering
Azure Cloud Platform certifications (Solutions Architect or Developer) preferred; TOGAF certification
Strong technical depth as an architect—able to engage with the technology from the inside, work through implementation-level details, and go hands-on with architecture and design when the situation requires it
Enterprise application architecture, including SaaS and COTS platforms (ERP, CRM, HCM, finance, collaboration, workflow), integration patterns (APIs, iPaaS, event-driven), and configuration vs. customization trade-offs
Cloud-native architectures on Azure (AWS/GCP nice to have), including containerization and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes) and DevOps practices such as CI/CD pipelines and infrastructure-as-code
Generative AI and agentic AI solution design, including LLM integration, RAG patterns, and responsible AI practices
Enterprise software architecture and design patterns, including service-oriented, event-driven, and microservices architectures; data architecture and persistence strategies (RDBMS, NoSQL); and Big Data, analytics, and AI/ML architecture
Security-by-design, privacy, and compliance considerations, plus vendor and product evaluation, including RFP processes, proof-of-concepts, and total-cost-of-ownership analysis
Demonstrated experience advising and partnering with senior business leaders on technology strategy and investment decisions; experience in professional services or consulting environments is an asset
This role does not require professional engineering licensure and is not classified as a formal engineering position under provincial regulatory definitions. While individuals with a P.Eng designation are welcome to apply, the responsibilities of this role do not involve the practice of professional engineering as defined by applicable legislation.

This position ensures continuity and upholds our standards of excellence following the departure of a valued team member.

The salary range for this position is $196,000 - $246,000. The posted salary range represents the expected hiring range for PwC locations in major city centres. Given our national recruiting approach, ranges may vary for positions in other locations. At PwC Canada, base salary is determined by your skills, experience, qualifications and work location. In addition to base salary, eligible employees may have opportunities to participate in variable incentive pay programs which are designed to reward individual and firm-wide achievements. We are committed to offering competitive compensation and adhere to all relevant pay transparency legislation. During the hiring process, our Talent Acquisition team will provide details about our comprehensive total rewards package.

Why you’ll love PwC

We’re inspiring and empowering our people to change the world. Powered by the latest technology, you’ll be a part of diverse teams helping public and private clients build trust and deliver sustained outcomes. This meaningful work, and our continuous development environment, will take your career to the next level. We reward your impact, and support your wellbeing, through a competitive compensation package, inclusive benefits and flexibility programs that will help you thrive in work and life. Learn more about our Application Process and Total Rewards Package at: https://jobs-ca.pwc.com/ca/en/life-at-pwc

PwC Canada acknowledges that we work and live across Turtle Island, on the land that is now known as Canada, which are the lands of the ancestral, treaty and unceded territories of the First Nations, Métis and Inuit Peoples. We recognize the systemic racism, colonialism and oppression that Indigenous Peoples have experienced and still go through, and we commit to allyship and solidarity.

We’re committed to providing accommodation throughout the application, interview, and employment process. If you require accommodation to be at your best, please let us know during the application process.

The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in recruiting is just getting started, so we know you have questions about how and why we use it. At certain points during our recruiting process, we rely on AI to improve your experience. This could be during resume review or curating personalized job recommendations, asking you clarifying questions via a chatbot or during our interview scheduling to improve your experience. Our use of AI helps ensure we combat bias by evaluating candidates equally and fairly, without seeing identity information, such as your name, or gender for example). AI also helps us better predict successful hires by reviewing all applicants for a role and the relationship between your skills, experience and likely success at PwC Canada. While AI supports parts of our recruitment process, final hiring decisions always involve human review. This focus on data, innovation, growth and excellence are key leadership priorities for the Vice President, Information Technology Services (VP). Our Client’s formal leaders are accountable, together with fellow leaders, for the overall accomplishment of Our Client’s strategic priorities including its Mission, Vision and Values and its Strategic Plan. As a key member of Our Client's senior leadership team, the Vice President will provide strategic leadership across enterprise technology, digital transformation, data strategy and advanced analytics. The incumbent will oversee the modernization of technology infrastructure, applications and platforms, including cloud adoption and emerging technologies, while ensuring robust cybersecurity, data governance, regulatory compliance and enterprise risk management. Working collaboratively across Our Client's Group, the VP will align technology investments and initiatives with organizational priorities, enhance the experience of Subscribers/customers (internal and external), and serve as a trusted advisor to the CEO, senior leadership team and Board committees on technology strategy, innovation and risk.

The combination of what works well and modernizing/sustaining structures and processes to enable resilience and support innovation in meeting customer needs, through advancing digital and analytics capabilities will ensure Our Client’s ability to leverage the power of information for improvement.

The successful candidate will bring a minimum of eight years of progressive senior leadership experience, with demonstrated expertise in enterprise technology strategy, financial and operational management, technology governance, cybersecurity and digital transformation. Experience leading complex modernization initiatives, including cloud adoption, data strategy, advanced analytics and legacy system transformation, will be important, as will a proven ability to build high-performing teams, oversee strategic technology investments, manage vendor relationships and deliver complex projects. The ideal candidate will possess strong business acumen, executive presence, sound judgement and exceptional communication skills, with experience advising Boards, senior leaders and diverse stakeholders. A bachelor's degree in information technology, business, engineering, healthcare or a related field is required, (a master's degree being preferred) and professional designations such as CISSP, CISA or PMP considered assets. jobs.title: Director of FP&A
jobs.description:
Company Background

Our client is North America’s largest lawn care franchisor, serving more than 800,000 households across approximately 1,000 territories across a majority of U.S. states and Canadian provinces. The group combines a franchise network with substantial company-owned operations and provides lawn care services and mosquito/tick control.

The business has moved from a founder-led environment to a private equity-backed one while continuing to be led by its existing management team. To support this next stage, finance is undertaking two major initiatives: modernizing its infrastructure, tools and ERP systems, and establishing a consistent monthly reporting cadence for private equity investors and the Board of Directors.

Role Overview

Reporting to the CFO, this role will lead consolidated reporting of actual results, budgets and future forecasts across the group. The immediate priority is to own Board, executive and lender reporting, working closely with accounting and business leaders and taking ownership of the tools and processes developed an in process 100 day plan engagement to lay foundations for reporting. Over the next 24 months, the role will also play a significant part in finance transformation, particularly initiatives affecting reporting and FP&A.

This is a player-coach role. At the company's current size, the leader of FP&A must be hands-on, building the models, reporting packages and processes personally, while also setting the standard for how the business thinks about financial performance. The successful candidate will be expected to develop a strong financial culture across the organization, partnering with operators to build their financial acumen and equip them to manage the business through its next phase of growth.
On an ongoing basis, the successful candidate will serve as a key finance partner to the CFO and operating leaders. As the business grows and its needs evolve, the successful candidate will build the FP&A function, including its team, responsibilities and recurring planning and reporting cadence.

Role & Responsiblities

Management and Board Reporting
Own consolidated and business-level reporting across franchising and corporate operations in Canada and the US in a timely manner, including visibility of bank accounts and cash balances across entities and currencies.
Align with the CFO, executive team and PE fund on reporting needs, key metrics and presentation.
Develop a recurring reporting package covering financial performance, operational KPIs, budget variances and management commentary.
Translate results into clear insights, risks and recommended actions.

Budgeting, Forecasting and Financial Modeling
Streamline and lead the annual budget, rolling forecast and long-range planning processes with the respective business teams and consolidate the results for Board/Executive reporting.
Build and maintain an integrated three-statement financial model (by business stream; as well as consolidated) covering the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow.
Ensure driver-based budgeting linked to operational KPIs and business priorities.
Partner with business leaders to challenge assumptions, assess resource needs and improve forecast accuracy, building their ownership of the numbers.
Develop scenario and sensitivity analyses to support strategic and operating decisions.
Own a rolling 13-week cash forecast and longer-term liquidity projections.

Business Performance and Profitability Analysis
Establish consistent financial and operational KPIs across business units and help operators understand and act on them.
Use the integrated financial model to analyze profitability by business stream, entity, branch and geography, as appropriate.
Assess revenue growth, margins, labour productivity, overhead and cost allocations.
Identify opportunities to improve profitability and track delivery against agreed initiatives.

Lender Reporting and Covenant Monitoring
Develop and own the recurring lender reporting package, including covenant calculation templates and supporting schedules.
Establish reliable data sources, review procedures and accountability for timely submissions.
Forecast covenant compliance and available headroom, flagging potential constraints early.
Identify challenges or gaps affecting delivery of lender reporting and implement practical recommendations.
Partner with accounting and operations to improve working capital and cash conversion.

Finance Transformation and Automation
Play a significant role in the 24-month finance transformation roadmap, helping rebuild the finance function through modern technology, improved processes and automation.
Lead one or more transformation workstreams affecting reporting and FP&A, including budgeting, forecasting and financial analysis.
Partner with accounting, IT and business leaders to evaluate and implement planning, reporting, consolidation and business intelligence tools.
Define FP&A requirements for the future ERP and related systems, including data structures, reporting dimensions and integration needs.

Culture and Business Partnership
Lead by example, personally building and owning the core models, reports and analyses while setting the standards and habits that raise the bar for the finance function.
Develop a financial culture grounded in accountability, data-driven decision-making and a shared understanding of what drives profitability, cash flow and growth.
Build financial acumen among operators through coaching, training and accessible tools, helping them read their own P&Ls, KPIs and budget variances and take ownership of results.
Mentor and develop the future FP&A team, defining roles, standards and career paths as the function grows.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, economics or a related field; CPA, CA, CFA or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive FP&A, corporate finance or finance leadership experience, ideally in a private equity-backed, multi-entity or multi-location service business.
Proven experience owning Board, investor and lender reporting, including covenant monitoring and compliance forecasting.
Advanced financial modeling skills, including integrated three-statement models, driver-based budgets and scenario and sensitivity analyses.
Hands-on experience with ERP, planning and business intelligence tools, and a track record of automating reporting and improving finance processes.
Demonstrated ability to coach and influence non-finance leaders, building financial acumen and accountability across operating teams.
Strong communicator who can present to a Board and private equity sponsor and translate complex results into clear, actionable insights.
A hands-on, player-coach mindset: comfortable building the work personally while developing a team and a finance culture.
Experience in franchise, seasonal or cross-border (Canada and U.S.) businesses is an asset.

Join us in redefining healthcare — so it doesn’t just survive, it thrives. To learn more about PointClickCare, check out Life at PointClickCare and connect with us on Glassdoor and LinkedIn.
 
About the Team
The People Strategy & Transformation (PST) is PointClickCare's HR strategy, organizational design, and portfolio management pillar. The team includes HR Business Partners, Organizational Design & Effectiveness, People Experience, and the HR Strategy & Enablement function, with a dotted-line partnership to Internal Communications. PST is responsible for ensuring HR's work across every Center of Excellence is planned, resourced, sequenced, and tracked against business outcomes — spanning a portfolio of Pillar Initiatives, Cross-Pillar Projects, and Program Roll-Ups delivered across all four HR solution groups.
 
Position Summary:
The Director, People Strategy and HR Portfolio (Project) Management s is the VP, People Strategy & Transformation's strategic thought partner in building and running PointClickCare's HR Portfolio Management Office (HR PMO) — co-designing the strategy, governance model, capacity methodology, and dashboard reporting that let HR plan, resource, and track its work against business outcomes. This is a net-new function: no HR PMO currently exists at PointClickCare, and this role will design these mechanics in partnership with the VP rather than operate a system someone else has already built.

Operating with significant design authority but without direct reports or final decision rights on cross-functional trade-offs, this role earns influence through the credibility of the mechanics it builds and runs. It operates across all four HR solution groups without formal authority over any of them, serves as the VP's thought partner on HR strategy and the HR SLT prioritization process, and convenes HR initiative stakeholders and Internal Communications to coordinate how HR's work reaches the business.
 
Key Responsibilities:
Design and run the HR Portfolio Management Office’s core operating mechanics
Design and maintain the capacity management methodology, including the heat map model and the oversubscription thresholds used to flag resourcing conflicts across HR COEs
Own and run the Portfolio Council governance cadence end to end — intake, capacity check, tier assignment, publish, mid-quarter check, and close-out
Build and maintain the integrated HR initiative dashboard, ensuring data currency and accuracy across every active Pillar Initiative, Cross-Pillar Project, and Program Roll-Up
Example deliverable: a quarterly Portfolio Council capacity heat map showing every HR COE’s current initiative load, used to approve or defer new initiative intake
Serve as strategic thought partner to the VP, People Strategy & Transformation
Co-design the HR SLT prioritization process and criteria used to evaluate and sequence HR initiatives each planning cycle
Co-design the OKR and scorecard measurement architecture — what gets measured, how it rolls up, and the cadence it runs on
Co-author and stress-test the HR Strategy on a Page, contributing independent analysis before it is finalized by the VP
Example deliverable: a documented HR SLT prioritization framework — criteria, weighting, and process — adopted for the FY28 planning cycle
Own capacity management and project plan oversight across the full HR initiative portfolio
Track progress against committed business outcomes, not activity completion alone, across every active HR initiative
Maintain consistent project plan structure, milestone tracking, and dependency mapping in partnership with each initiative’s named Delivery Lead
Proactively surface cross-COE capacity collisions and resourcing conflicts before they reach Portfolio Council
Example deliverable: a consolidated project plan view across all active Program Roll-Ups, flagging dependency risk before it affects a committed milestone
Convene HR initiative stakeholders and Internal Communications on a recurring cadence
Establish and run a recurring go-to-market coordination cadence bringing together initiative Delivery Leads and Internal Communications
Sequence the timing and stakeholder readiness of HR initiative rollouts to the business, avoiding duplicate or conflicting messages landing in the same window
Maintain a shared go-to-market calendar visible to HR SLT, showing what is launching, when, and to whom
Example deliverable: a quarterly HR go-to-market calendar sequencing every planned initiative rollout to the business, reviewed and approved by HR SLT before the quarter begins
Represent HR in enterprise planning and governance forums
Serve as the primary operational liaison to the Strategic Delivery Office, aligning HR’s initiative classification and intake practices to enterprise taxonomy
Represent HR’s initiative portfolio and capacity picture in the Corporate Strategy Group’s quarterly planning cadence
Flag enterprise-level dependencies or conflicts affecting HR’s ability to deliver against committed priorities
Example deliverable: HR’s consolidated initiative and capacity submission into the Corporate Strategy Group’s quarterly planning sprint, reflecting current Portfolio Council status
 
Required Skills & Qualifications:
10–15 years of experience in program/portfolio management, management consulting, or a PMO leadership capacity, including demonstrated experience designing — not only operating — portfolio governance, capacity management, or OKR measurement systems
A track record serving as a strategic thought partner to a senior leader, with evidence of shaping that leader's thinking rather than only executing direction
Demonstrated experience operating in matrixed, cross-functional environments without formal authority over the teams being coordinated
Strong data and dashboard fluency — comfortable architecting reporting tools and the metrics model behind them, not just maintaining an existing build
Executive-level communication skills — this role prepares materials for and interacts directly with VP-level stakeholders across every HR pillar
Experience convening cross-functional stakeholder groups to coordinate sequencing and alignment on complex, multi-team initiatives
 
Preferred Experience:
Experience building a PMO or governance function from scratch, in a design capacity, rather than operating within an already-mature one
HR domain experience, including familiarity with COE structures and business-outcome-linked workforce initiatives
Experience partnering with internal communications or marketing functions on coordinated, multi-stakeholder rollouts

This role will provide strategic leadership for target\-state architecture, technology standards, governance, and enterprise architecture decision\-making across the organization. jobs.title: Regional Director, Digital Assets Sales & Commercialization, North America
jobs.description:
Our Purpose 

 Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential. 

 Title and Summary 

Director, Digital Assets Sales & Commercialization, North America 

Overview

Mastercard is seeking a highly strategic, commercially focused, and externally oriented Director, Regional Commercialization, Digital Assets to lead the growth, market expansion, and commercialization of Mastercard's BVNK solution across NAM Region. This sales executive will play a critical role in establishing Mastercard's leadership position in next-generation payments by driving adoption of Mastercard's stablecoin capabilities and BVNK-powered solutions.

He/she will define and execute the regional go-to-market strategy, shape ecosystem partnerships, and drive revenue growth across financial institutions, fintechs, payment service providers, marketplaces, digital merchants, and emerging payment innovators.

The successful candidate will serve as Mastercard's expert sales leader for accelerating the adoption and usage of MA’s BVNK solution opportunities, working closely with BVNK Senior Sales leadership, MA Regional Sales and Product leadership and account management teams, market development and MA Move teams to originate, structure, and accelerate strategic opportunities. The role requires balancing commercialization execution with long-term ecosystem development and strategic market expansion.

This is a highly visible expert sales role requiring deep expertise in payments, digital assets, cross-border flows, stablecoins, fintech ecosystems, and platform commercialization.

Role

The Director, Regional Commercialization, Digital Assets will be accountable for driving market adoption, revenue growth, and ecosystem expansion for BVNK and MA’s digital asset solutions across NAM Region.

The role serves as the BVNK expert sales leader connecting BVNK’s solutions, Mastercard's capabilities, and regional customer opportunities.

Key Responsibilities 

Strategic Leadership & Commercialization 

• Define and execute the regional commercialization strategy for Mastercard's BVNK- powered solutions and stablecoin offerings 

• Collaborate with MA account teams to advance pipeline generation, strategic partnerships, client acquisition, and revenue realization. 

• Establish regional priorities, target segments, and market expansion strategies 

Revenue Growth & Market Expansion 

• Lead targeted regional sales efforts focused on MA customer segments including financial institutions, fintechs, PSPs, remittance providers, marketplaces, merchants, and digital economy participants. 

• Develop and govern a robust pipeline of high-value opportunities while supporting deal progression from origination through contract execution, retention and growth. 

• Sponsor strategic pursuits and executive-level client engagements for priority opportunities. 

• Drive achievement of revenue, transaction volume, and market adoption goals across the region. 

• Identify new market opportunities, geographic expansion priorities, and emerging use cases that create sustainable growth. 

Executive Client Engagement 

• Evangelize BVNK and MA’s digital assets and stablecoin-based payment solutions. 

• Build and maintain executive relationships with key Account Managers, clients, and ecosystem partners. 

• Provide stablecoin expert sales for strategic client discussions, executive briefings, workshops, and solution design engagements. 

• Support regional sales teams in navigating complex opportunities and executive-level negotiations. 

Strategic Partnerships & Ecosystem Development 

• Identify emerging partnership opportunities that accelerate adoption of Mastercard and BVNK’s digital asset capabilities. 

• Monitor competitive, regulatory, and market developments and translate insights into commercialization strategies. 

Product & Market Development 

• Partner with BVNKs product teams to inform client insights, competitive analysis, product strategy, roadmap prioritization, market readiness decisions, and future product investments. 

• Develop regional growth strategies around key digital asset use cases, including: 

 • Stablecoin-enabled cross-border payments 

 • Remittances 

 • Merchant payouts and settlement 

 • Treasury and liquidity management 

 • B2B payments 

 • Disbursements 

 • Marketplace payouts 

 • Wallet funding and cash-out solutions 

• Assess market readiness and prioritize opportunities by country, client segment, use case, and revenue potential. 

All About You 

Required Qualifications 

• Significant experience leading commercialization, business development, product, or growth initiatives within payments, digital assets, fintech, cross-border payments, or financial technology. 

• Demonstrated ability to originate, negotiate, and close complex strategic partnerships and enterprise opportunities. 

• Deep understanding of the payments and financial services landscape across NAM Region. 

• Experience engaging and influencing C-level executives and senior decision-makers. 

• Ability to lead through influence across highly matrixed global organizations. 

• Strong executive presence with exceptional communication, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills. 

• Demonstrated success operating within rapidly evolving and ambiguous market environments. 

• Ability to translate emerging technologies and market trends into commercial business opportunities. 

• Willingness to travel across the region. 

Preferred Qualifications 

• Experience in digital assets, stablecoins, blockchain-based payment infrastructure, or crypto-financial services. 

• Experience commercializing emerging or nascent payment technologies at scale. 

• Strong network across the banking, fintech, digital commerce, and payments ecosystem within the region. 

• Experience developing market-entry strategies and scaling new business lines globally or regionally. 

• Background in consultative sales, strategic partnerships, product leadership, or general management. 

Success Measures 

Success in this role will be measured by: 

• Achievement of regional digital asset revenue and business growth objectives. 

• Strategic pipeline creation, conversion, and closed revenue. 

• Expansion of Mastercard's stablecoin and BVNK-powered solution adoption. 

Mastercard is a merit-based, inclusive, equal opportunity employer that considers applicants without regard to gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, disabled or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We hire the most qualified candidate for the role. In the US or Canada, if you require accommodations or assistance to complete the online application process or during the recruitment process, please contact reasonable_accommodation@mastercard.com and identify the type of accommodation or assistance you are requesting. Do not include any medical or health information in this email. The Reasonable Accommodations team will respond to your email promptly. 

 Corporate Security Responsibility 

All activities involving access to Mastercard assets, information, and networks comes with an inherent risk to the organization and, therefore, it is expected that every person working for, or on behalf of, Mastercard is responsible for information security and must:
 Abide by Mastercard’s security policies and practices;

 Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed;

 Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and

 Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.

In line with Mastercard’s total compensation philosophy and assuming that the job will be performed in Canada, the successful candidate will be offered a competitive pay based on location, experience and other qualifications for the role and may be eligible to participate in a discretionary annual incentive program. This posting reflects one or more current openings on our team.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Enterprise Data Management
jobs.description:
About Versapay

Versapay is the platform that rewires AR by removing barriers to collecting and reconciling B2B payments, providing end- to-end cash flow clarity, ensuring businesses can manage working capital on their terms. By closing the loop for finance teams and their business systems, customers, and payment activity into a single intelligent ecosystem, Versapay transforms money matters into a data-driven advantage. With 10,000 customers and 5M+ companies transacting, Versapay facilitates 110M+ transactions and processes $300B+ in payments volume annually.

About The Role

We are looking for a strategic, builder-minded Senior Director of Enterprise Data Management to own and execute Versapay’s enterprise data strategy at a pivotal moment in our evolution. This leader will drive the convergence of our transactional, operational, behavioral, relational and intent data layers into a unified operational backbone — the foundational unlock for AI- powered product features, semantic data models, externalized data products, and autonomous AR workflows.

This is a high-visibility, high-impact role directly tied to our product and commercial roadmap, with a clear mandate and executive alignment behind it.

What You’ll Do

Data Strategy & Architecture

Define and drive Versapay’s enterprise data strategy, aligning the data roadmap to product, AI, and commercial objectives.
Lead the architectural convergence of our transactional, operational, and analytical data layers into a unified, bi-directional operational backbone.
Own a multi-year data maturity roadmap with clear milestones across architecture, semantics, governance, and accessibility.
Champion a business-first data modelling philosophy: canonical hierarchies, enterprise ontologies, and shared metric catalogues that allow humans and AI agents to interpret data consistently.

Data Governance & Quality

Operationalize data governance as a first-class concern — automated classification, RBAC enforcement, platform SLAs, and certified data objects.
Formalize the Enterprise Data Catalogue, replacing institutional knowledge with a searchable, self-service discovery layer.
Deploy and maintain an executive data health dashboard to provide ongoing visibility into the health and integrity of our data estate.
Enforce the data procurement gate, ensuring new tools and systems are reviewed and classified before entering the estate.
Build and own the Enterprise Data Asset Registry to enable secure, frictionless data sharing internally and with commercial partners.

AI Enablement & Agentic Readiness

Drive data infrastructure readiness to support Versapay’s AI roadmap — from ML pipelines and LLM serving layers to agentic serving tiers.
Establish formal schema contracts and semantic modelling standards that guarantee deterministic outputs for safe, scalable agent deployment.
Partner with Product and Engineering to enable agentic capabilities: reverse data flow, predictive model productization, and real-time data serving.
Govern data and AI exposure — ensuring sensitive data stays within approved platforms and all external data products meet strict quality, lineage, and privacy standards.

Data Accessibility & Commercialization

Evolve the function from ad hoc data requests to a design-first, product-oriented organization with a governed, discoverable asset registry.
Operationalize external data products for commercialization, delivering clear value to customers within consent and compliance frameworks.
Partner with the commercial team on data product strategy — turning Versapay’s proprietary network data into defensible, recurring revenue.
Expand self-service data access for internal teams while protecting compute capacity and governance standards.

Team Leadership

Lead and grow the Data Platform Team, building a high-performing function with clear ownership across data strategy, engineering, consumption, AI compute; in tight partnership with the Embedded Analytics Team, Risk and Compliance.
Act as the cross-functional bridge between Product, Engineering, Commercial, Finance, and Legal/Compliance- ensuring data serves every function from a shared, trusted foundation.
Build a culture of data discipline — standardizing how information is captured and governed so insight is consistent, discoverable, and trusted across the organization.
Represent the data function at the executive level, partnering closely with the CTO and contributing to the broader AI and product roadmap.

Required

What You Bring

10+ years of experience in data leadership, with at least 5+ years at the Director level owning enterprise data strategy, architecture, or governance.
Demonstrated track record of modernizing and unifying complex, multi-source data environments at scale — ideally in a SaaS, fintech, payments context.
Deep expertise in modern data stack: cloud data warehouses (Snowflake preferred), lakehouse architectures, ETL frameworks, and semantic/canonical modelling.
Strong evidence of application of AI and ML infrastructure — including how data governance, observability, and semantic standards underpin safe, scalable AI deployment.
Proven ability to build and lead high-performing technical teams and partner effectively across Product, Engineering, and Commercial functions.
Experience governing data for commercial use: external data products, consent frameworks, lineage standards, and privacy compliance.
Exceptional communication skills — able to translate complex data and architectural concepts for executive audiences and build alignment across functions.
Experience with managing the cost of data warehouses and cost forecasting.
Experience in hiring and managing talent across the entire data food chain – from BI and Analytics to Data Engineering to CI/CD of data platforms.

Preferred

Experience with agentic AI architecture, MCP, or LLM serving layers and the data requirements that underpin them.
Familiarity with AR/AP automation, payments, or working capital platforms and the data models they generate.
Track record of commercializing data as a product — packaging data assets, building external APIs, or creating data-sharing programs with partners.
Experience managing data maturity transformations with structured roadmaps, measurable milestones, and executive visibility.
Hands-on experience with AWS-native data infrastructure (Glue, SageMaker, Bedrock) alongside Snowflake and modern BI tooling.
Background in a PE-backed, high-growth SaaS environment.

As the University's senior finance executive, the Vice-President, Finance & Administration provides strategic leadership that strengthens financial sustainability, drives enterprise transformation, and enables long-term institutional growth.

This is an exceptional opportunity to lead a broad and impactful portfolio spanning finance, information services, human resources, and facilities and sustainability services. As MacEwan's senior financial executive, the VPFA & CFO will contribute to enterprise-wide strategy, champion operational excellence, lead transformative initiatives, and identify innovative approaches to revenue generation, resource optimization, and long-term financial resilience. With responsibility for financial stewardship, enterprise risk management, capital planning, strategic resource allocation, and the systems that support these functions, the VPFA & CFO will help position the University for its next phase of growth and success.

Working closely with students, faculty, staff, government, unions, and community partners, the VPFA & CFO will help shape an institution with significant momentum, ensuring MacEwan University continues to deliver an exceptional student experience while achieving its bold ambitions for the future.
