Success in this role requires more than financial expertise. It calls for a collaborative, forward-thinking leader who thrives in complex environments, builds trusted relationships across diverse constituent groups, and inspires innovation and continuous improvement.

The ideal candidate is an accomplished executive who combines strategic vision with sound judgment, collaborative leadership, and exceptional relationship-building skills. They will bring deep financial expertise, a strong record of leading complex organizations through growth and change, and the ability to serve as a trusted advisor on financial stewardship, enterprise risk, governance, and institutional strategy. They combine strategic vision with exceptional financial acumen and are recognized for challenging assumptions, identifying opportunities, and delivering meaningful organizational change.

They have demonstrated success leading enterprise-wide transformation across finance, human resources, information technology, and other administrative functions, building integrated teams that work collaboratively toward shared institutional outcomes rather than operating in functional silos.

A confident and forward-thinking leader, they inspire trust through integrity, transparency, and accountability while fostering a culture of innovation, continuous improvement, and evidence-informed decision-making. They are an effective collaborator who builds strong relationships across diverse constituent groups and thrives in complex, highly regulated environments.

The successful candidate will be passionate about developing people, building organizational capacity, and helping position MacEwan University for continued success and long-term impact.

Relevant university degree required and Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation highly preferred. Equivalent senior financial leadership experience as the organization's chief financial executive may be considered.

Demonstrated success leading enterprise transformation, organizational redesign, technology-enabled modernization, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Demonstrated success leading finance and administrative functions, including financial stewardship, budgeting, forecasting, enterprise risk management, and organizational transformation.
Demonstrated success leading multidisciplinary portfolios that include finance, human resources, information technology and other corporate services.
Experience providing strategic advice to executive leadership and boards within complex governance environments.
Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary portfolios and build high-performing teams through periods of growth and change.

 Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential. 

 Title and Summary 

Director, Global AI Thought Leadership 

Who is Mastercard?

Mastercard is a global technology company in the payments industry. Our mission is to connect and power an inclusive, digital economy that benefits everyone, everywhere by making transactions safe, simple, smart, and accessible. Using secure data and networks, partnerships and passion, our innovations and solutions help individuals, financial institutions, governments, and businesses realize their greatest potential.

Our decency quotient, or DQ, drives our culture and everything we do inside and outside of our company. With connections across more than 210 countries and territories, we are building a sustainable world that unlocks priceless possibilities for all.

Overview
The AI & Data Office is responsible for the strategy, acquisition, evaluation, and responsible use of AI and data capabilities that power innovation and operations across Mastercard. It defines the enterprise AI and data vision, develops shared capabilities, and helps the business realize value from AI and data responsibly and at scale. 

The Director, AI Thought Leadership, will report to the Vice President, AI Thought Leadership and partner with AI product, engineering, and SMEs, to cultivate a unified narrative for Mastercard’s AI solutions and position. Within the AI & Data Office, the AI Thought Leadership team shapes Mastercard's internal and external perspective on artificial intelligence and its impact on our business, our customers, and on commerce, business, and society. The team develops original insights, executive narratives, and thought leadership programs that strengthen Mastercard's reputation as a trusted leader in applied AI and execute on Mastercard's AI positioning to strengthen engagement with customers, stakeholders, and employees, and reinforce Mastercard's unique role in the evolving AI landscape

Role
• Monitor AI and data technologies landscape, their application, and industry trends to identify emerging opportunities, risks, and implications for Mastercard and its customers.
• Develop original thought leadership, research, and points of view on topics such as AI adoption, trust, economy, workforce transformation, and the future of commerce.
• Create flagship content including research reports, whitepapers, executive briefs, articles, presentations, keynote materials, and webinar content, building towards an AI-driven AI content studio. 
• Lead the end-to-end thought leadership lifecycle, including research, content development, stakeholder coordination, reviews, approvals, publication, and ongoing content refresh.
• Measure the impact of thought leadership programs and continuously improve content effectiveness, audience engagement, and business outcomes.
• Partner with executives and cross-functional teams across AI & Data, Products, Marketing, and Communications to deliver through leadership programd and activation through speeches, bylines, presentations, customer briefings, executive workshops, facilitation sessions, strategic discussions, and thought leadership programs.
• Represent Mastercard at industry events, customer forums, analyst engagements, and external thought leadership opportunities.

All About You
The ideal candidate for this position should demonstrate:
• Experience in thought leadership, market research, management consulting, technology research, journalism, publishing, editorial strategy, or a related field.
• Strong understanding of artificial intelligence, machine learning, generative AI, agentic systems, data strategy, responsible AI, and enterprise AI adoption trends including evaluating emerging technologies and their business and socio-economic implications
• Track record producing high-quality research, reports, articles, or executive content and translating complex technology topics for business audiences.
• Effective project and production management skills, with experience coordinating complex publications from planning through review, approval, and delivery.
• Strong market research and analytical capabilities, able to synthesize large volumes of information into clear viewpoints.
• Exceptional writing, editing, and storytelling abilities, and leading the use of AI tools to accelerate and amplify thought leadership work.
• Experience working with senior executives, technical subject matter experts, communications and marketing. 
• Knowledge of payments, technology, financial services, or digital commerce preferred.
• Ability to operate independently in ambiguous and rapidly evolving environments.

• Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed;
• Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and 
• Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines. 

Mastercard is a merit-based, inclusive, equal opportunity employer that considers applicants without regard to gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, disabled or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. As Director, Data Engineering for the Public Markets and Alternate Assets (PMAA) team, you will build and publish the enterprise market data products that power investment strategies across our public markets and alternate assets businesses. Partnering closely with your business-aligned product owner, you will lead a talented team of data engineers and analysts and own the end-to-end lifecycle of PMAA data, from vendor and internal feeds through to trusted, well-documented data products used by investment teams, analytics platforms and AI agents. You will set the technical direction for a modern AWS data platform, establish the semantic and knowledge graph foundations that connect data across asset classes, and ensure every data product meets the standards of timeliness, quality, licensing compliance and control that investment decisions demand. 

 The Team 

 CPP Investments invests across public and private markets, supported by technology and data capabilities that enable informed investment decisions and long-term value creation.

 Within PMAA, this role leads market data engineering and the development of enterprise data products that support investment professionals, quantitative and research teams. The team works with investment, product, architecture, technology and governance partners to deliver reliable, accessible and AI-ready market data.

 Accountabilities 
 Define and execute the multi-year data engineering strategy and roadmap for PMAA market data products, partnering with the product owner to align priorities with investment needs and enterprise architecture standards.
 Own the target-state AWS data platform architecture across ingestion, storage, processing, orchestration, governance and consumption, making design and build-versus-buy decisions that balance scalability, resilience, security and cost.
 Lead the development and adoption of enterprise data products across public and private markets, including pricing, reference data, corporate actions and benchmarks, with clear ownership, data contracts, service levels and documentation.
 Establish semantic data capabilities, including RDF knowledge graphs on Amazon Neptune, and enable governed access to AI-ready data through Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, agent skills and Amazon Quick.
 Ensure reliable, timely and secure data delivery through observability, automated quality controls, incident management, AWS Lake Formation, data lineage and market data licensing and entitlement controls.
 Lead agile roadmap delivery and engineering excellence, embedding CI/CD, infrastructure as code, automated testing and reusable frameworks while engaging senior stakeholders, investment teams and strategic technology and data partners.
 Build, coach and develop an inclusive, high-performing engineering team, fostering accountability, collaboration, continuous learning and career growth.

 What You Bring 
 Undergraduate degree or college diploma in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics or a related field; a graduate degree is an asset.
 10+ years of progressive experience in data engineering, data platforms or software engineering, including 5+ years leading engineering teams, with demonstrated success delivering enterprise-scale, cloud-native data platforms and leading complex agile programs.
 Strong understanding of capital markets, investment management and market and reference data, including experience with major data vendors, licensing, entitlements and usage controls; private markets experience is an asset.
 Advanced AWS architecture expertise equivalent to Solutions Architect – Professional, including security, IAM, networking, resilience and cost optimization, together with hands-on technical depth in Apache Spark (PySpark or Scala), AWS Glue or EMR, Airflow/MWAA, AWS DMS and Amazon RDS/Aurora.
 Expertise in enterprise data product design, AWS Lake Formation governance, data contracts, service levels and consumption patterns, along with RDF, SPARQL, ontology design, Amazon Neptune, MCP servers, agent skills and AI-assisted analytics using Amazon Quick.
 Ability to guide engineering teams across cloud-native development, data quality, observability and delivery practices. Experience with lakehouse technologies, Python, SQL, CI/CD, infrastructure as code, data cataloguing, financial ontologies, Amazon Bedrock or GraphRAG is an asset; relevant AWS certifications are also assets.
 Inclusive people leadership, sound judgment and strong communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to investment professionals and executives, influence stakeholders and manage strategic vendor partnerships.

 You are motivated to contribute to something larger than yourself, approach complex challenges with rigor, and hold yourself to  high standards in a collaborative, performance-driven environment.   

 We provide colleagues with cutting-edge AI tools, dedicated learning time, and practical support to help them deliver with greater impact.

 Inclusion & Accessibility 
 CPP Investments is committed to  equitable access to employment and building a workforce that reflects diverse talent and perspectives. If you require accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.   

 Attention: Protect Yourself from Fraud 
 CPP Investments is committed to a secure and transparent recruitment process. We will never ask candidates for payment or financial information at any stage of hiring. All legitimate opportunities are posted on our careers page, and communications will come from our applicant tracking system, Workday.  

 CPP Investments may use AI tools to help screen and assess applicants by analyzing resumes and applications for relevant skills and experience. These tools support, but do not replace, human decision-making.

jobs.description:
About The Role

Within Global Customer Experience (GCX), our mission is to advance the HelloFresh customer relationship from reactive resolution to proactive, trust-building service. The compensation function sits at the heart of that mission: it is the mechanism through which the business acknowledges failures, restores customer confidence, and, when done well, turns a bad experience into a reason to stay.

The Associate Director, Customer Compensation & Policy is responsible for the global strategy, architecture, and governance of how HelloFresh compensates customers across all markets and brands. This is not a policy maintenance role. It is a strategic function that sits at the intersection of customer economics, operational data, behavioral experimentation, and cross-functional influence.

You will own one of the most financially material and customer-sensitive levers in the business. You will shape a multi-year roadmap and hold peers in Operations, Technology, Finance, and Market Leadership accountable for the quality of inputs that determine how well and how efficiently we recover customer trust.

The ideal candidate brings a rare combination: analytical rigor sharp enough to architect a global compensation engine from first principles, and the executive presence to drive adoption across a complex, multi-market organization without formal authority over most of the people they need to move.

What You'll Own

Global Compensation Strategy & Engine Architecture

Own the end-to-end strategic vision for how HelloFresh categorizes customer errors and determines compensation across all markets, brands, and contact channels.
Lead the design and continuous evolution of the compensation engine: along with Tech, you’ll define the the rules, thresholds, segmentation logic, and automation frameworks that govern recovery decisions at scale.
Define the principles that govern trade-offs between customer generosity and cost discipline and translate those principles into operational rules that hold across market complexity and brand variation.
Partner with Technology to ensure the compensation engine is scalable, auditable, and capable of supporting dynamic, AI-assisted decisioning as the product evolves.

Experimentation & Behavioral Economics

Set the global roadmap for compensation experimentation: A/B testing across offer types, value levels, channel timing, and segmentation variables.
Apply behavioral economics frameworks to compensation design understanding how recovery offers shape long-term retention, repurchase behavior, and brand perception, not just immediate satisfaction.
Define the measurement framework for experimentation: what constitutes a successful test, what confidence warrants global rollout, and how results are synthesized into durable policy change.
Partner with Analytics & Insights to ensure test design, sample integrity, and rollout analysis meet a rigorous standard of evidence.

Financial Stewardship & Cost Governance

Own the global compensation P&L line: tracking spend by market, error category, customer segment, and channel — and holding yourself accountable to defined cost-per-incident and avoidable-contact targets.
Identify and close financial leakage: cases where compensation is being issued without policy justification, at incorrect values, or at the wrong frequency.
Build the reporting infrastructure that makes compensation economics visible to GCX leadership, market GMs, and Finance — with the granularity and context needed to drive decisions.
Define the right balance between cost optimization and customer lifetime value investment: not just 'spend less' but 'spend where it earns back.

Fraud Policy & Global Governance

Own the global fraud and abuse prevention framework: the policies, detection logic, thresholds, and escalation paths that protect the business without creating friction for genuine customers.
Lead the governance rhythm for policy: quarterly reviews, market exception management, escalation adjudication, and framework versioning across a multi-brand, multi-market environment.
Act as the final authority on complex, cross-market policy gaps — resolving ambiguity with speed, consistency, and strategic clarity rather than routing decisions upward by default.
Maintain global standards while creating principled space for market-level adaptation where local context genuinely requires it.

Cross-Functional Leadership & Stakeholder Accountability

Represent the compensation function in senior forums translating customer economics into requirements that peers in Operations, Technology, Finance, and Market GMs must respond to.
Hold cross-functional partners accountable for the upstream data quality, operational accuracy, and system reliability that the compensation engine depends on.
Drive adoption of policy changes across markets and brands, building communication and change management plans that make new frameworks land — not just launch.
Influence at VP and Director level across multiple functions; escalate only strategic blockers, not routine alignment.

What You'll Bring

Education

MBA or equivalent postgraduate qualification required.
Undergraduate degree in Economics, Business, Engineering, or a quantitative discipline.

Experience

8–12 years of progressive experience in customer strategy, pricing, operations, or a directly adjacent domain with meaningful exposure to global, multi-market environments.
Demonstrated track record of owning a financially significant operational lever and managing it with both analytical precision and strategic judgment.
Prior experience leading and developing teams; comfort operating as a senior individual contributor and a people leader simultaneously.
Background in subscription commerce, logistics, or consumer-facing operations strongly preferred. Familiarity with the economics of customer recovery in high-volume, low-margin environments is a distinct advantage.

Technical & Analytical

Advanced proficiency in SQL and data analysis; able to build and pressure-test the analytical models that underpin policy decisions without delegating the logic to others.
Fluency with experimentation methodology: test design, statistical significance, holdout analysis, and the translation of results into policy not just reporting.
Experience working with or alongside engineering teams to define product and system requirements for rules-based or AI-assisted decisioning tools.
Comfort with financial modeling: building the business case for compensation investment, forecasting spend impact, and tracking actuals against plan.

Leadership & Influence

Senior executive presence: able to walk into a GM, COO, or CFO conversation with a clear point of view, defend it under pressure, and leave with alignment.
A credible voice with peers and upward stakeholders not because of title, but because of the quality of analysis and clarity of communication.
Structured and decisive under ambiguity: able to make a defensible call with incomplete information and adjust as evidence develops.
Genuinely collaborative across markets and functions able to hold people to standards without damaging the relationships needed to sustain them.

What we offer

Box Discount-Amazing discounts on 1 box per week! 75% discount on weekly HelloFresh and Chefs Plate meal kits AND 50% off weekly Factor meal box.
Health & Wellness-Health & Dental benefits from day 1, a Health Spending Account, unlimited access to the Headspace app to meet your self-care needs, and 25% discount on GoodLife fitness memberships!

Vacation & PTO-Time off is also an important part of self-care! We offer generous vacation and PTO to help you create a good work-life balance.
Family Benefits-A parental leave top-up program for expectant parents.
Growth & Development-We support your career progression, provide development opportunities, and invest in your continued learning through our organization wide L&D fund.
Work Hard & Have Fun-From team socials to engaging company days, you’ll have plenty of opportunity to experience the fun!
Diversity & Inclusion Initiatives- With impactful ERG’s like FreshPride, Women Empowered and LIMES, we are committed to our diversity, equity & inclusion efforts.

Flexible Hybrid Approach

At HelloFresh, we know that flexible work arrangements are essential in enabling you to do your best work, while balancing your personal and life needs. Offering remote work flexibility, along with the opportunity to interact and collaborate in the office are all a part of creating a great employee experience.

To meet these needs, we are pleased to provide Flexible Hybrid work. Flexible Hybrid is a people-first approach that is based on choice, trust, personalization, and empowers teams to choose when and how often they work from the office and work from home, in addition to team days and company days. This means a minimum of 3 days in office per week.

HelloFresh Canada uses AI-integrated technology to help us process and evaluate applications more efficiently. This includes tools that screen and assess candidate qualifications based on the requirements for this role. While these tools assist our workflow, all final selection decisions are made by our hiring team.

jobs.title: Finance Director
jobs.description:
Established in 1937, Marquis, a division of Lakeside Book Company, offers integrated print and logistics solutions to thousands of content owners in Canada, the United States, and Europe. Today, our team includes more than 600 employees in six business locations across Canada: Montmagny, Quebec City, Louiseville, Sherbrooke, Georgetown, and Toronto. Marquis is at the heart of our industry's action due to the company's mastery of new technologies, sense of innovation, and privileged relationships with our customers.
  
  

**Salary:** Starting $150/hour
  
  

**JOB SUMMARY:**  

The Finance Director is responsible for providing strategic and operational financial leadership for Marquis Book Printing Inc., overseeing the accounting and financial planning and analysis (FP\&A) functions. The role ensures the integrity, accuracy, and timeliness of financial information while translating financial and operational results into insights that support business performance, investment decisions, and long\-term growth. Based in Canada, the Finance Director leads the Marquis finance team and partners closely with Lakeside Book Company’s U.S. Corporate Finance organization to support consolidated reporting, planning, financial governance, and cross\-border business initiatives.
  
  

**KEY JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:**  

* Provide overall leadership and direction for Marquis Finance, establishing priorities, financial objectives, and operating practices that support business strategy and performance.
* Lead and develop the Accounting Manager, FP\&A Manager, and Credit Supervisor, setting clear expectations, strengthening capabilities, and ensuring effective coordination across accounting, reporting, planning, and analysis.
* Oversee the integrity and timeliness of Marquis financial reporting, close, consolidation, intercompany accounting, and financial controls through the Accounting Manager; ensure significant accounting matters and risks are appropriately escalated and resolved.
* Provide executive oversight of financial planning and analysis, including annual budgets, periodic forecasts, long\-range plans, financial models, KPI reporting, profitability analysis, and business cases through the FP\&A Manager.
* Provide financial oversight and strategic support to the Credit function, partnering with the Credit Supervisor to monitor accounts receivable performance, customer credit risk, collections effectiveness, and working capital. Support the development of policies, processes, and strategies that strengthen credit management and minimize financial exposure.
* Partner with Marquis and Lakeside Book leadership to evaluate financial performance, identify risks and opportunities, assess strategic investments and capital projects, and recommend actions to improve profitability, cash flow, and operational effectiveness.
* Oversee financial governance and compliance for Marquis in Canada, including application of the accounting framework applicable to statutory and consolidated reporting (ASPE and/or IFRS, as applicable), internal controls, audit requirements, and applicable federal and provincial tax obligations; coordinate with external auditors and tax advisors as appropriate.
* Provide oversight of treasury, cash flow, working capital, banking relationships, and foreign currency considerations, including intercompany balances and transactions, in partnership with the Accounting Manager and Lakeside Book Corporate Finance.
* Serve as a key finance partner in the cross\-border relationship with Lakeside Book U.S. Corporate Finance, aligning reporting, forecasting, policies, processes, and financial analysis to support consolidated business needs.
* Support Marquis integration and continuous improvement initiatives, including finance process harmonization, systems and ERP initiatives, reporting enhancements, and opportunities to strengthen efficiency, controls, and decision support across Marquis and Lakeside Book.
* Build strong relationships with operational and functional leaders, including Plant Leadership, and ensure the FP\&A Manager provides effective financial support to the Marquis Plant Finance Manager and manufacturing operations.
* Perform other related duties as assigned.


**SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS:**  

* Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field; equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
* 10\+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including leadership responsibility in a manufacturing, multi\-entity, or similarly complex business environment.
* Demonstrated experience leading accounting and FP\&A functions, including financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, financial modeling, cash flow management, and business performance analysis.
* Strong knowledge of Canadian accounting and financial reporting requirements, including the ability to interpret and apply the accounting framework relevant to the organization’s statutory and consolidated reporting.
* Working knowledge of Canadian federal and provincial tax requirements, including GST/HST and other applicable sales tax obligations, and experience partnering with external tax and audit advisors.
* Experience with multi\-entity accounting, consolidation, intercompany transactions, foreign currency considerations, and partnership with finance teams across national borders.
* Strong business acumen and demonstrated ability to translate complex financial and operational information into clear recommendations for senior leadership.
* Experience in manufacturing finance, including cost drivers, inventory, working capital, capital investment, and operational performance metrics.
* Proven ability to lead, coach, and develop finance professionals and to influence stakeholders across functional and organizational boundaries.
* Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and experience with ERP and financial reporting systems; experience with NetSuite or other en

Job Description 
 You will be working on a flexible hybrid schedule as part of Fidelity’s dynamic working arrangement. 

 The work location for this role is 483 Bay Street in Toronto until approximately late 2026, when the work location will change to the new Mississauga office at 3 Robert Speck Parkway. 

 Current work authorization for Canada is required for all openings. 

 At Fidelity, we’ve been helping Canadian investors build better financial futures for over 35 years.  We offer individuals and institutions a range of trusted investment portfolios and services - and we’re constantly seeking to find new and better ways to help our clients.  As a privately owned company, we boldly embrace innovation in all areas as we continue to grow our business into the future. 

 Working with us means you’ll be part of a diverse and dedicated group of people who make a real difference for our clients and communities every day. You’ll have a wide range of opportunities to grow and develop your career in an inclusive environment where you’ll feel valued and supported to be your best - both personally and professionally. 

 How You’ll Make an Impact 
 The Director, Architecture & Technology Strategy reports to the Vice President, AI and is responsible for shaping and executing the enterprise architecture and technology strategy for Fidelity Investments Canada. The role provides strategic and people leadership across enterprise, domain, solution and data architecture, ensuring these capabilities evolve in support of the firm's business priorities, technology modernization and AI ambitions. 

 The successful candidate will combine strong strategic thinking, technical depth and business partnership skills. They will work closely with senior business and technology leaders to translate enterprise priorities into target-state architecture, technology capabilities, standards and multi-year roadmaps that support long-term growth, operational resilience and transformation. 

 A critical part of the role is close partnership with Fidelity International (FIL). The Director will maintain visibility into evolving FIL strategies, standards, platforms and capabilities and work collaboratively with international partners to shape a joint Canada-FIL roadmap, identifying where Canada should adopt, extend, contribute to or influence enterprise capabilities. 

 The Director leads and develops the Architecture teams, strengthening the maturity of the function, its operating model, governance practices and technical capabilities. They work closely with Business, AI, Engineering, Security, Risk and Governance partners on key strategic initiatives, ensuring enterprise architecture supports modern engineering practices, technology modernization and the adoption of advanced analytics, generative AI and agentic AI while maintaining appropriate security, resilience and control. 
 Translates long-term business objectives into target-state architecture, technology capabilities, standards and investment priorities and establishes a clear multi-year technology roadmap. 
 Defines and maintains enterprise architecture direction across business, application, integration, data, cloud and technology domains, ensuring alignment between business strategy and technology decisions. 
 Shapes enterprise technology strategy, providing strategic guidance on technology investments, platform selection, modernization opportunities and emerging technologies while balancing innovation, resilience, security and cost efficiency. 
 Establishes and continuously matures architecture governance, principles, reference architectures and decision-making practices to enable consistent, pragmatic and effective technology decisions. 
 Partners with Engineering and Technology leaders to identify and prioritize technology modernization, technical debt reduction, technology lifecycle management and architectural simplification. 
 Ensures AI and emerging technology requirements are incorporated into enterprise architecture, data architecture, integration patterns and platform strategy, supporting the adoption of generative AI, agentic AI and AI-enabled software development. 
 Leads, develops and matures the Architecture function, establishing clear accountabilities, operating practices and decision rights across enterprise, domain, solution and data architecture teams. 
 Hires, coaches, mentors and develops leaders and technical talent and establishes clear goals, development plans and performance expectations. 
 Builds a culture of strong technical leadership, collaboration, accountability, continuous learning and constructive challenge. 

 What We’re Looking For 
 University degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Systems, Data, Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience. 
 10+ years of progressive experience in technology, enterprise architecture or technology strategy, preferably in financial services or another complex regulated environment. 
 At least 5 years of people leadership experience managing technical subject matter experts and people managers. 
 Demonstrated experience defining and executing enterprise architecture and technology strategies, leading multidisciplinary technical teams and partnering with senior business and technology leaders on major transformation and modernization initiatives. 
 Experience building and maturing architecture capabilities, establishing architecture standards, governance practices and technology roadmaps in complex organizations. 
 Experience working in a global organization and developing enterprise architecture or technology capabilities across regions; financial services experience strongly preferred. 
 Relevant enterprise architecture, cloud or data management certification such as TOGAF, AWS, Snowflake or CDMP. 

 The Skills Set You Bring 
 Deep understanding of enterprise architecture and technology strategy, with the ability to connect business strategy to technology capabilities, architectural direction and investment decisions. 
 Strong knowledge of modern cloud and data platforms, including Snowflake and AWS, and the architecture patterns required for scalable, secure enterprise technology capabilities. 
 Strong knowledge of enterprise, domain, solution and data architecture, including application design, integration patterns, data modelling, semantic layers and enterprise information architecture. 
 Strong understanding of technology modernization, architecture governance, technical debt management, technology lifecycle management and enterprise architecture standards. 
 Broad knowledge of enterprise architecture across applications, integration, cloud, security and technology domains and experience establishing target-state architecture and multi-year technology roadmaps. 
 Strong understanding of how enterprise architecture and modern engineering practices enable AI, machine learning, generative AI, agentic AI and AI-enabled software development at enterprise scale. 
 Demonstrated ability to build and mature architecture practices, develop technical talent and establish effective operating models and decision-making frameworks. 
 Exceptional leadership, interpersonal, communication, presentation and relationship-management skills, including the ability to influence senior business, technology and international stakeholders. 
 Strong strategic judgement, analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to evaluate emerging technologies, balance short-term delivery with long-term direction and lead through ambiguity

37.5

 TD is committed to providing fair and equitable compensation opportunities to all colleagues. Growth opportunities and skill development are defining features of the colleague experience at TD. Our compensation policies and practices have been designed to allow colleagues to progress through the salary range over time as they progress in their role. The base pay actually offered may vary based upon the candidate's skills and experience, job-related knowledge, geographic location, and other specific business and organizational needs.

 As a candidate, you are encouraged to ask compensation related questions and have an open dialogue with your recruiter who can provide you more specific details for this role.

 Job Description: 
 This role is an executive member of the Bank’s second line of defense Operational Risk Management function, which specializes in fraud, insider and conduct risk management as Head of Governance, Policy/Framework, Reporting and Risk Insights, and Emerging Risks. This role is Enterprise-wide, and works closely with Oversight teams in Canada and the U.S. to maintain Fraud, Insider and Conduct risk policies and frameworks, governance committees, and board reporting.  Their team is also responsible for emerging fraud, insider and conduct risks, as well as QA and Enablement for the broader fraud, insider and conduct risk team.

Job Description
 Depth & Scope: 
 Provides management leadership by hiring the best talent, setting goals, developing staff, managing employee performance and compensation decisions, promoting teamwork and handling any/all disciplinary actions, as required
 Owns, manages and evolves the Fraud, Insider and Conduct Risk Frameworks, Policies & Standards to set a consistent and appropriate suite of controls for managing such risks within risk appetite and in line with regulatory expectations, and in consideration of the customer experience and customer friction.
 Responsible for risk profiles, board reporting, RAS measures
 Owns and drives Fraud, Insider and Conduct risk governance committees in conjunction with the Heads of Fraud, Insider and Conduct Risk Oversight
 Reviews policy conformance, and assesses risk acceptances against the policies
 Oversee the design and execution of ORM programs across the team, through maintenance of job aids and tools/templates, and review of the quality of the artifacts being maintained across the team
 Centralized the initial review of emerging risks, through consideration of the changing fraud, insider and conduct risk and threat environment and evolving schemes.  This may be done through as the initial point of contact for CRA's / NBPA's, or other emerging threat/risk work
 Responsible for regulatory compliance management, and compliance monitoring and testing for our team
 Responsible for maintenance of our own team's controls, RCSA, interaction models and RACI's
 Builds and maintains effective relationships with business partners and control function partners, establishing credibility by understanding the business/control, their needs, strategic priorities and challenges
 Partners with key stakeholders to drive fraud, insider and conduct risk management strategy in alignment with organizational and business objectives and risk appetite
 Supports internal and external audits and regulatory examinations
 Reports and escalates risk issues, events and breaches to executive management and risk committees
 Partners with senior management and oversight leads on the reporting and presentation of fraud, insider and conduct risk, trends and key developments to the board, regulators and other key stakeholders
 Fosters a culture of fraud risk management awareness and accountability for fraud, insider and conduct risk management, including identification, prevention, detection and response/reporting of such risks
 Promotes and fosters a strong culture of integrity, ethics and regulatory compliance and provides independent oversight of the management of such risks
 Maintains positive, honest, transparent and constructive relationships with regulators

 Education & Experience: 
 4-year degree or equivalent experience; post graduate degree preferred
 15+ years related experience required with deep subject matter expertise in Insider, Fraud and Conduct Risk Management and Banking
 Experienced professional with technical knowledge of fraud, insider and conduct risk threats, risks and controls, and experience in the Banking industry (across the customer lifecycle from account opening, financial and non-financial transactions, fraud controls and case managers, and suspicious activity reporting)
 Ability to attract, inspire, coach, train and lead; bring out the best in team members
 Strong knowledge of banking regulations and industry standards (e.g., OSFI, OCC, FRB, FDIC)
 Excellent leadership, project management and stakeholder communication skills

Vice President, Finance and 
Administration / Chief Financial Officer

Division: Finance and Administration

 Position Summary 

Our post-secondary education client is seeking an accomplished and 
strategic financial executive to serve as its next Vice 
President, Finance and Administration / Chief Financial Officer.

As the chief financial and administrative officer and a member 
of the President’s Cabinet, the CFO provides executive 
leadership, strategic direction, and institutional stewardship 
for the school's financial operations, administrative services, 
public safety, and facilities.

This position ensures the responsible management of 
institutional resources while advancing the school's mission, 
vision, and strategic priorities. Serving as a trusted advisor 
to the President, the CFO helps shape institutional strategy, 
provides sound financial counsel, and partners with executive 
leadership to maintain the school's fiscal strength, operational 
effectiveness, and long-term sustainability.

The successful candidate will bring an institution-wide 
perspective and contribute to college-wide initiatives, 
organizational culture, governance, strategic planning, and 
executive decision-making.

 Executive Leadership Philosophy 

The school's Vice Presidents serve as institutional leaders 
first and functional leaders second. As members of the 
President’s Cabinet, they share responsibility for advancing the 
school's mission through collaborative leadership, strategic 
planning, innovation, and responsible stewardship of public 
resources.

The CFO will balance financial discipline with innovation, 
operational excellence with exceptional customer service, and 
long-term sustainability with the evolving needs of students, 
employees, and the community.

Success will be measured not only by the performance of assigned 
departments, but also by meaningful contributions to the overall 
effectiveness, reputation, and future of the college.

 Core Executive Responsibilities 

 Cabinet and Strategic Leadership 

• Serve as an active member of the President’s Cabinet and 
executive leadership team.

• Advise the President on strategic, financial, operational, and 
organizational matters.

• Participate in institutional planning, executive 
decision-making, and policy development.

• Collaborate across divisions to advance college-wide 
initiatives and strategic priorities.

• Represent the school before governmental agencies, financial 
institutions, professional organizations, and community 
partners.

• Develop long-range financial and operational strategies that 
support the school’s Strategic Plan.

• Evaluate emerging trends, risks, and opportunities affecting 
higher education and public finance.

• Champion innovation, continuous improvement, and responsible 
resource management.

 Organizational Leadership 

• Recruit, develop, mentor, and evaluate executive leaders and 
management staff.

• Build high-performing teams committed to operational 
excellence and continuous improvement.

• Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, inclusion, 
professionalism, and exceptional customer service.

• Promote employee engagement, leadership development, and 
succession planning.

• Establish measurable goals and performance expectations 
aligned with institutional priorities.

 Stewardship and Governance 

• Ensure responsible stewardship of the college’s financial, 
physical, and operational resources.

• Support the Board of Regents through executive reports, 
recommendations, and presentations.

• Develop and implement policies, administrative regulations, 
and business practices that strengthen institutional 
effectiveness.

• Ensure compliance with federal and state laws, accreditation 
standards, Board policies, and administrative regulations.

• Maintain effective systems of internal control, enterprise 
risk management, and institutional accountability.

 Division Leadership Responsibilities 

 Financial Leadership 

• Serve as the college’s chief financial officer and principal 
advisor to the President on financial strategy, fiscal 
sustainability, and institutional stewardship.

• Provide executive leadership for all financial operations, 
ensuring the integrity, transparency, and long-term health of 
the college’s financial resources.

• Deliver financial analysis and recommendations that support 
informed decision-making by the President, Cabinet, and Board of 
Regents.

• Through the Controller and Finance team, provide strategic 
oversight for:

• Budget development and administration

• Accounting and financial reporting

• Payroll administration

• Treasury, cash, investment, and debt management

• Annual financial audits and internal controls

• Financial forecasting and analysis

• Grant accounting and financial compliance

• State and federal financial reporting

• Financial systems and business process improvement

 Procurement and Administrative Services 

• Provide executive leadership for procurement and 
administrative support operations, ensuring services are 
efficient, compliant, transparent, and customer-focused.

• Promote responsible stewardship of public resources while 
supporting operational effectiveness and service to the college 
community.

• Through the Executive Director of Procurement and 
Administrative Services, oversee:

• Purchasing and procurement

• Contract administration and competitive solicitations

• Vendor relations

• Administrative services

• Auxiliary enterprises, including the campus bookstore, café, 
and merchandise store

• Shipping and receiving

 Facilities Management 

• Provide strategic leadership for the planning, maintenance, 
operation, preservation, and improvement of the college’s 
physical assets and campus environment.

• Ensure facilities remain safe, functional, attractive, and 
supportive of teaching, learning, student engagement, and 
community use.

• Through the Executive Director of Facilities Management, 
oversee:

• Facilities maintenance and operations

• Custodial services and utilities management

• Preventive and deferred maintenance

• Capital improvement, construction, and renovation projects

• Campus infrastructure

• Sustainability initiatives

• Space utilization and facilities planning

 Public Safety 

• Provide executive oversight of the school’s public safety and 
emergency preparedness functions, fostering a secure environment 
for learning and institutional operations.

• Collaborate with institutional leadership and external 
agencies to maintain a comprehensive approach to campus safety 
and emergency management.

• Through the Executive Director of Public Safety, oversee:

• Campus security

• Emergency preparedness and response

• Business continuity planning

• Safety compliance

• Threat assessment and risk mitigation

• Emergency communications and crisis response

 Minimum Qualifications 

 Required

standing.

• Master’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, 
Accounting, Public Administration, Higher Education 
Administration, or a closely related field.

• At least eight years of progressively responsible executive 
leadership experience in finance and administration.

• At least three years of senior leadership experience within 
higher education, government, or another similarly complex 
organization.

• Demonstrated experience leading multiple administrative 
divisions and managing complex organizational budgets.

• Demonstrated ability to provide strategic leadership, manage 
organizational change, and build collaborative relationships

education institution.

The successful candidate will demonstrate the ability to:

• Provide visionary executive leadership while maintaining 
strong fiscal stewardship.

• Develop and communicate long-term financial strategies that 
advance institutional priorities.

• Analyze complex financial and operational issues and develop 
practical, sustainable solutions.

with external stakeholders.

• Lead organizational change with transparency, professionalism, 
and integrity.

• Interpret and apply applicable laws, regulations, accounting 
standards, and Board policies.

mentoring, and succession planning.

• Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, collaboration, 
continuous improvement, and exceptional customer service.

• Exercise sound judgment and maintain the highest standards of 
ethics, professionalism, and confidentiality.

jobs.title: Deputy Director, Data Value
jobs.description:
Government Digital Service

Location Bristol, London, Manchester

Job grade SCS Pay Band 1

Contract type Permanent

Working pattern Flexible working, Full-time, Job share, Part-time, Compressed hours

Salary £86,000 - £117,800

Closing date Mon 30 Nov 2026

Reference 489478

Profession Digital, Information Technology

Apply now

You'll build a clear, trusted view of where data is making a difference across government and where it isn't, so leaders can choose with evidence instead of anecdote.

Why now?

AI is raising the stakes on data, and leaders need to know where their investment will pay off. At the moment there is no single, agreed way to show that across government.

We need one answer to a simple question. What is data worth to citizens, to services, to the economy and to national security? Then we need to use that answer to make better decisions.

It can be done. Others have already published practical guides to valuing data, covering how to take stock of it, assess it and put a value on it. We want to do the same, properly, for government.

Where you'll work

You'll be part of the Government Digital Service (GDS), the digital centre of government. We're home to GOV.UK and the Incubator for AI (i.AI), we lead the Government Digital and Data function, and we have more than 1,000 colleagues across London, Bristol and Manchester.

Job Description

What you'll do

Take stock of what government owns. Oversee a joined-up view of public data assets, including inventories, asset intelligence and valuation. Start with the assets that matter most to national infrastructure, public services and citizen-facing products.
Build the yardstick. Set up methods to judge the potential and the realised value of data assets and data-enabled products across their whole life, including where revenue could safely be raised to support public services.
Be the authority on 'value'. Decide what counts as data value, from economic and operational to assurance and risk reduction, and make it consistent and comparable across departments and portfolios. Advise senior leaders on how value is understood, evidenced and explained.
Show where it's working. Use that evidence to see where data creates the most value and where attention or investment should go next.
Help leaders make the call. Give senior decision-makers value-led evidence on priorities, sequencing and investment, so they can see what to scale, redirect, pause or stop. Base it on the whole system, not on one success story.
Keep citizens and users in the room. Make sure their view is built into every prioritisation and investment decision, working closely with Product, Portfolio and Strategy colleagues.
Follow the value through. Build value into decisions before, during and after delivery. Track how it changes over time, from performance and adoption to longer-term outcomes, and feed what you learn back into future choices.
Work safely in sensitive places. Operate within legislative, regulatory, governance and national security frameworks. Make visible the value that data brings in national security settings, where it often shows up as assurance, resilience or reduced risk.
Tell the story. Turn complex activity across government into clear, credible insight for senior leaders, and help the organisation move from one-off case studies to a system-level view of impact.
Lead a rigorous team. Lead the teams and partners working on data value, insight and asset intelligence, set a high bar for quality and professionalism, and help build a culture where decisions follow evidence.
One boundary. You provide evidence and analysis for commissioning, roadmap and portfolio discussions. You don't own delivery or benefits realisation in departments.

What Success Looks Like

A clear, trusted view of data value across government, built on comparable evidence of use, adoption, outcomes and benefits. Senior leaders can see where data is delivering and where they need to step in.
One system-wide definition of public value from data, covering citizen, service, economic and national outcomes, that shapes priorities, architecture and product decisions.
Valuation methods that let leaders compare data assets and products and decide when to scale, invest, pause or close.
A lifecycle approach, so value shapes decisions before, during and after delivery and feeds the next round of strategy, architecture and product priorities.
A story that senior leaders believe, moving us from one-off case studies to a system-level understanding of impact.

The honest bit

Valuing data across a whole government is hard, and the method is still being built. You'll be setting it up as well as using it, so expect plenty of debate about what counts as value and who decides.

Person specification

This role is for you if...

Role

You've helped very senior people make big decisions using data and evidence, and you can tell the difference between being busy and making a difference. You'll thrive in this role if you have:

Treated data as a strategic asset at a senior level, shaped how it is valued and accessed, and influenced decisions across a portfolio, a system or a whole organisation.
Used evidence to help senior leaders decide. You've brought information together from many sources to guide priorities, sequencing and investment in complicated settings.
Shown sharp analytical judgement. You can tell delivery activity, adoption and real outcomes apart, and you don't mistake progress for impact.
Influenced senior stakeholders by turning complex data, analysis or performance information into clear insight that makes trade-offs and risk-aware decisions easier.
Worked in governed, risk-aware settings, such as legislative, regulatory, assurance or security-sensitive ones, and understand that value can show up as assurance, resilience or reduced risk as well as delivery.
Worked across boundaries and in ambiguity, bringing policy, delivery, technical and operational teams together around one view of performance and value.

Bonus points

You're curious. You've taught yourself something, built something or written about something, at work or in your own time, and you'd enjoy telling us about it.

jobs.title: Portfolio Finance Director
jobs.description:
Job Summary

About the Turner Portfolio

The Turner Portfolio is part of Volaris Group, an operating group of Constellation Software PLC (TSX:CSU), a listed acquirer and permanent owner of vertical market software businesses. We are a global, fast growing portfolio of around 20 operating companies and around 1,200 employees worldwide, with a distinct focus on three key verticals. A portfolio team of around 35 people supports three vertical teams of around five people each, and each vertical is looking to expand globally through sustained M&A activity.

Job Description

Purpose of the role

The Finance Director owns the production of the portfolio's numbers: consolidation, quarterly reporting to group, compensation calculations and the financial mechanics of acquisitions, to a standard that survives challenge.

The role reports to the VP, Portfolio Operations, who owns the portfolio's operating cadence, planning direction and automation mandate. The Finance Director is the technical authority beneath that: the person who makes the numbers right, on time, every time, and whose reading of the numbers shapes what the portfolio says about itself. This is not an operating company CFO seat; each operating company keeps its own ledgers and local finance lead. The job is to make 20 sets of operating company data consolidate cleanly into one trusted picture, and to leave the finance community stronger than it was found.

Key Responsibilities

Portfolio reporting

Own the monthly consolidation of results across all operating companies and production of the portfolio management reporting pack.
Own the mechanics of the quarterly reporting cycle to group: the numbers, the standard operating ratios the group manages by, and variance analysis against plan and prior submission.
Contribute significantly to the reporting narrative: trend analysis, observations across the operating companies, and the so-what behind the numbers, feeding the commentary the VP, Portfolio Operations owns.
Flag risks in the numbers early and with a recommended action, not after the quarter has closed.

Planning and compensation

Run the mechanics of the annual budget and rolling forecast with operating company finance leads, to the planning direction set by the VP, Portfolio Operations.
Own the calculation, modelling and reconciliation of the group's leadership bonus scheme and operating company leader compensation across the portfolio; interface to Volaris Group central finance on methodology.

Treasury and banking

Manage the portfolio's debt cycles and the relationships with external banks, alongside intercompany funding and the movement of cash across the group.
M&A and integration finance
Own financial integration from signing: day one reporting onboarding, group chart of accounts mapping, and earn-out and deferred consideration tracking.
Track investment performance across the portfolio: investment case tracking against the diligence model post close, and regular IRR analysis and reporting on every acquisition.
Provide the finance workstream for portfolio transitions, including the clean financial separation of businesses moving to other operating groups or verticals.

Finance community and capability

Lead the community of finance leads across the operating companies: standards, cadence, training on the group's methodology, and succession for weak or vacant seats.
Implement automation and AI in reporting production within the VP, Portfolio Operations' automation mandate, so the team spends its time on interpretation, not collation.

Controls and compliance

Own the coordination of statutory audit, tax and intercompany requirements with group finance and operating company finance leads; own management fee and recharge mechanics for the portfolio.
Maintain a control environment appropriate to a listed group without importing bureaucracy the operating companies do not need.

Candidate profile

With the new era of AI and automation upon us, we are looking for someone who is very curious and can adapt: a track record of using technology to improve systems and processes, so less time is spent on repeatable transactional work and more on critical thinking and value-add.

Essential

Qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA, CIMA, CPA or equivalent) with eight or more years of postqualification experience, including group consolidation and management reporting personally owned in a multi-entity environment.
Has produced and stood behind quarterly reporting in a listed or equivalently demanding environment: numbers that hold up under scrutiny.
Fluency in software economics: recurring revenue, attrition, licence and services mix, and the operating ratios that follow from them.
Hands-on M&A finance: completion mechanics, chart of accounts mapping, earn-outs and deferred consideration, post-close integration.
Has led a small team and influenced finance leads they did not line manage. Comfortable in a decentralised model where authority comes from credibility, not control.
Precise, concise communicator whose numbers need no caveats.

Desirable

Experience inside Constellation, Volaris or a comparable serial acquirer of vertical market software.
Multi-currency and multi-GAAP/IFRS exposure (IFRS, US GAAP), with North American and European entities.
Experience administering leadership bonus or incentive schemes.

What We Are Not Looking For

A controller who stops at the ledgers. The operating companies run their own; this role interprets as well as produces.
Someone who reports problems rather than resolving them.

SALARY AND ADDITIONAL PAY*

Base salary range: $156,000 - $225,000

Other compensation: This position is eligible to participate in the discretionary company bonus plan.

Individual compensation packages are based on various factors unique to each candidate, including skill set, experience, qualifications and other job-related reasons

How We Assess

Beyond experience, we assess every candidate against our A-Player behaviours: the standard every member of the portfolio is held to. For all team members these are Drives Outcomes, Owns It, Elevates Others, Thinks Critically and Acts Decisively, Communicates with Impact, and Pursues Self Growth. Because this role leads a team, we also look for the people leadership behaviours that sit on top: Builds Awesome Teams and Creates Unshakable Trust. Expect the selection process to explore these with specific examples from your own experience, and to treat each as a balance; overdone is as telling as underdone.

Job Description

You will be working on a flexible hybrid schedule as part of Fidelity’s dynamic working arrangement.

The work location for this role is 483 Bay Street in Toronto until approximately late 2026, when the work location will change to the new Mississauga office at 3 Robert Speck Parkway.

Current work authorization for Canada is required for all openings.

At Fidelity, we’ve been helping Canadian investors build better financial futures for over 35 years. We offer individuals and institutions a range of trusted investment portfolios and services - and we’re constantly seeking to find new and better ways to help our clients. As a privately owned company, we boldly embrace innovation in all areas as we continue to grow our business into the future.

Working with us means you’ll be part of a diverse and dedicated group of people who make a real difference for our clients and communities every day. You’ll have a wide range of opportunities to grow and develop your career in an inclusive environment where you’ll feel valued and supported to be your best - both personally and professionally.

How You’ll Make An Impact

The Director, Architecture & Technology Strategy reports to the Vice President, AI and is responsible for shaping and executing the enterprise architecture and technology strategy for Fidelity Investments Canada. The role provides strategic and people leadership across enterprise, domain, solution and data architecture, ensuring these capabilities evolve in support of the firm's business priorities, technology modernization and AI ambitions.

The successful candidate will combine strong strategic thinking, technical depth and business partnership skills. They will work closely with senior business and technology leaders to translate enterprise priorities into target-state architecture, technology capabilities, standards and multi-year roadmaps that support long-term growth, operational resilience and transformation.

A critical part of the role is close partnership with Fidelity International (FIL). The Director will maintain visibility into evolving FIL strategies, standards, platforms and capabilities and work collaboratively with international partners to shape a joint Canada-FIL roadmap, identifying where Canada should adopt, extend, contribute to or influence enterprise capabilities.

The Director leads and develops the Architecture teams, strengthening the maturity of the function, its operating model, governance practices and technical capabilities. They work closely with Business, AI, Engineering, Security, Risk and Governance partners on key strategic initiatives, ensuring enterprise architecture supports modern engineering practices, technology modernization and the adoption of advanced analytics, generative AI and agentic AI while maintaining appropriate security, resilience and control.

Translates long-term business objectives into target-state architecture, technology capabilities, standards and investment priorities and establishes a clear multi-year technology roadmap.
Defines and maintains enterprise architecture direction across business, application, integration, data, cloud and technology domains, ensuring alignment between business strategy and technology decisions.
Shapes enterprise technology strategy, providing strategic guidance on technology investments, platform selection, modernization opportunities and emerging technologies while balancing innovation, resilience, security and cost efficiency.
Establishes and continuously matures architecture governance, principles, reference architectures and decision-making practices to enable consistent, pragmatic and effective technology decisions.
Partners with Engineering and Technology leaders to identify and prioritize technology modernization, technical debt reduction, technology lifecycle management and architectural simplification.
Ensures AI and emerging technology requirements are incorporated into enterprise architecture, data architecture, integration patterns and platform strategy, supporting the adoption of generative AI, agentic AI and AI-enabled software development.
Leads, develops and matures the Architecture function, establishing clear accountabilities, operating practices and decision rights across enterprise, domain, solution and data architecture teams.
Hires, coaches, mentors and develops leaders and technical talent and establishes clear goals, development plans and performance expectations.
Builds a culture of strong technical leadership, collaboration, accountability, continuous learning and constructive challenge.

What We’re Looking For

University degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Systems, Data, Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
10+ years of progressive experience in technology, enterprise architecture or technology strategy, preferably in financial services or another complex regulated environment.
At least 5 years of people leadership experience managing technical subject matter experts and people managers.
Demonstrated experience defining and executing enterprise architecture and technology strategies, leading multidisciplinary technical teams and partnering with senior business and technology leaders on major transformation and modernization initiatives.
Experience building and maturing architecture capabilities, establishing architecture standards, governance practices and technology roadmaps in complex organizations.
Experience working in a global organization and developing enterprise architecture or technology capabilities across regions; financial services experience strongly preferred.
Relevant enterprise architecture, cloud or data management certification such as TOGAF, AWS, Snowflake or CDMP.

The Skills Set You Bring

Deep understanding of enterprise architecture and technology strategy, with the ability to connect business strategy to technology capabilities, architectural direction and investment decisions.
Strong knowledge of modern cloud and data platforms, including Snowflake and AWS, and the architecture patterns required for scalable, secure enterprise technology capabilities.
Strong knowledge of enterprise, domain, solution and data architecture, including application design, integration patterns, data modelling, semantic layers and enterprise information architecture.
Strong understanding of technology modernization, architecture governance, technical debt management, technology lifecycle management and enterprise architecture standards.
Broad knowledge of enterprise architecture across applications, integration, cloud, security and technology domains and experience establishing target-state architecture and multi-year technology roadmaps.
Strong understanding of how enterprise architecture and modern engineering practices enable AI, machine learning, generative AI, agentic AI and AI-enabled software development at enterprise scale.
Demonstrated ability to build and mature architecture practices, develop technical talent and establish effective operating models and decision-making frameworks.
Exceptional leadership, interpersonal, communication, presentation and relationship-management skills, including the ability to influence senior business, technology and international stakeholders.
Strong strategic judgement, analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to evaluate emerging technologies, balance short-term delivery with long-term direction and lead through ambiguity

We are seeking an exceptional, strategic finance leader to serve as Finance Director for our Canada team, overseeing a business generating $250+ million in revenue across Real Estate Management Services, Markets, and Leasing. You'll drive financial planning and reporting while shaping the corporate strategy and vision for Canada, working hand-in-hand with leadership to translate financial insight into decisive action. The ideal candidate understands commercial real estate and professional services, exceptional partnering skills, and high level corporate finance.

This role is based out of JLL's Corporate office in Toronto and requires being in-office 4 days/week (flexibility to work remote one day/week). The Finance Director leads a small team and plays a key role on JLL Canada's Executive Leadership team. You will work closely with leaders across all business lines and report into a Global Finance team.

What your day-to-day will look like
:

Strategic Financial Leadership

Serve as the primary strategic finance partner and advisor to the Country CEO, country business line leaders, country functional leaders, and regional/global finance leadership.
Lead the preparation, management, consolidation, and delivery of the annual financial plan, reforecasts, and long-range planning efforts.
Drive proactive, data-informed decision-making across all stakeholder groups.
Translate global business line strategy into local Canada priorities, providing the financial insights and analysis that connect country-level execution to business line direction and identify opportunities to support revenue growth and margin improvement.
Oversee the integrity of all financial processes within your scope of responsibility.
Bridge discussions between business leadership and technical finance teams to inform, guide and influence business decisions

Performance Management & Reporting

Develop pipeline reporting and key performance metrics for business and service lines.
