jobs.title: Director, Client Enablement Analytics
jobs.description:
BMO Capital Markets is a leading, full-service financial services provider. We offer corporate and investment banking, treasury management, as well as research and advisory services to clients around the world. #bmocapitalmarkets

Mandate:

We are looking for an individual who has built out a metrics and reporting program for a client onboarding function that enabled removing bottlenecks and unlocking revenue.

The Client Enablement team is responsible for onboarding new clients and enabling them to successfully transact quickly and accurately, with high-touch service both internally and externally. The Client onboarding process encompasses Intake, Regulatory/Jurisdictional/Product Approval Compliance, Trade Reporting Compliance, Credit Line Setup, Legal Agreement (e.g. ISDA) Negotiation, Account Opening, and Electronic Setups. The group fulfills key governance requirements and plays a central role in how quickly and effectively clients are onboarded and enabled to transact with BMO Capital Markets.

Reporting to the Managing Director & Head of Client Onboarding, Client Tax Governance, and Client Operations, the Director is a senior leader who will build and lead the onboarding analytics and reporting agenda for Capital Markets, bringing a proven track record of turning operational data into commercial insight in this space. The role links client onboarding and client enablement processes to revenue, connecting onboarding milestones such as KYC, legal documentation, credit, and account set-up to client activation and revenue outcomes, and delivers the insights needed to speed up and improve the end-to-end client experience. The role will also report on selected cross sell analytics. The Data and Analytics team aggregates data from across Capital Markets systems into outcome-driven visualizations and reporting that drive insights, enable day-to-day evidence-based decision making, and support targeting for increased revenue generation.

This role will:

Working with senior leadership, set the vision and roadmap for onboarding and client enablement analytics, defining the metrics, KPIs, and reporting that matter most to senior business and operations leaders.
Provide hands-on leadership of a small team as people manager while building reports.
Link onboarding and client enablement processes to revenue, quantifying the commercial impact of cycle time, bottlenecks, and backlog on client activation and revenue realization.
Deliver insights that accelerate onboarding, reduce friction for clients and Front Office partners, and prioritize process, data, and technology improvements.
Lead stakeholder engagement with senior leaders across Front Office, Operations, AML/KYC, Legal, and Technology, translating business questions into automated reporting and data visualizations.
Provide data analytics, data governance, and data tools and technology leadership that will support Capital Markets, Client Enablement, and strategic transformation initiatives.

Key Accountabilities:

Lead the onboarding analytics and reporting strategy, establishing an end-to-end view of the client onboarding and client enablement lifecycle from client request through account activation.
Build and maintain an onboarding-to-revenue framework that links onboarding milestones (KYC, legal documentation, credit, and new accounts) to client activation, trading activity, and revenue.
Define, capture, measure, and report KPIs and SLAs (e.g., cycle time, aging, backlog, throughput, and first-time-right) that support defined business objectives.
Deliver executive-ready dashboards and data visualizations that provide actionable insights to senior business partners and governance forums.
Use data to identify bottlenecks, root causes, and improvement opportunities, and recommend solutions that speed up and improve onboarding and the client experience.
Partner with senior stakeholders to lead requirements gathering, with a focus on delivering desired business outcomes.
Provide subject matter and technical leadership in data profiling and analysis that supports Client Data Strategy and enterprise initiatives.
Champion data governance so that data is fit for purpose and meets business, usability, and data quality requirements and standards.
Drive the maturation of operational process efficiencies using automation, AI, and technology.
Mentor and develop analytics talent, fostering a culture of curiosity, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Ensure adherence to BMO privacy and confidentiality requirements (legal, compliance and operational risk).

Authorities:

Accountable for the onboarding analytics and reporting roadmap, including prioritization of reporting and insight requests.
Accountable for defining and governing onboarding KPIs, metric definitions, and the onboarding-to-revenue methodology.
Responsible for providing insightful data visualizations and executive reporting.
Responsible for BAU oversight; ensuring reports are built and breaks/issues with existing reports and/or processes are addressed in a timely manner.
Make recommendations on, and lead implementation of, process automations and improvements.

Scope & Impact:

This role has direct or indirect impact on the following:

Client Onboarding
AML/KYC
New Accounts
Legal
Tax Operations
Front Office groups
Client Enablement and client experience
Data Governance

Cross Functional Relationships:

Lines of business in Capital Markets (Global Markets and I&CB)

Front Office coverage and sales leadership; Business Management and Finance (revenue and client activity data)

Capital Markets Client Static Data, Client Onboarding, KYC/AML

Operations: Middle and Back Office teams

Corporate Support: Compliance, Legal, Technology

Knowledge & Skills:

Knowledge:

Completion of an applicable university degree and/or relevant professional designation is required.
10+ years of data, analytics, and reporting experience within the financial services industry, including progressive leadership responsibility (Data Visualization, Data Analysis & Profiling, Reference & Master Data).
Proven track record of building analytics and reporting capabilities that link operational processes to revenue and business outcomes.
Strong understanding of Capital Markets client onboarding, KYC/AML, legal documentation, credit, and account set-up processes.
Experience leading business process automation and transformation initiatives.
Solid understanding of data management practices (data visualization, data analysis, data profiling, matching, cleansing, mastering, and exception management).

Skills:

Proven ability to translate complex data into clear, executive-ready insights and recommendations that drive decisions.
Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills with senior leaders across business lines.
Experience with analyzing and manipulating data sets using data analytics tools and technologies.
Experience applying AI tools (e.g., Copilot) to analytics and reporting.
Experience using a variety of reporting and analytics tools (e.g., Power BI, DAX, M, Python, Splunk, Dataiku, Databases)
Excellent communication skills – written and verbal, including presenting to senior executives.
Ability to maintain strong attention to detail while meeting deadlines.
Collaborative leader who demonstrates initiative, is proactive, and client-focused.
Strong troubleshooting, analysis and problem-solving skills.
Proven ability to collaborate and build strong relationships with colleagues across business lines.

Working Conditions:

This role operates within an office environment with minimal exposure to discomfort or risk of ill health.

Fast paced and dynamic – work to deadlines.

Manage multiple tasks and work streams concurrently.

Salary:

The salary range for this role is $150,000 up to $170,000 CAD (subject to the candidate meeting the specific skills, experience, education, and qualification requirements)

Salary:

Pay Type:

Salaried

The above represents BMO Financial Group’s pay range and type.

Salaries will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and qualifications for the role, and may include a commission structure. Salaries for part-time roles will be pro-rated based on number of hours regularly worked. For commission roles, the salary listed above represents BMO Financial Group’s expected target for the first year in this position.

BMO Financial Group’s total compensation package will vary based on the pay type of the position and may include performance-based incentives, discretionary bonuses, as well as other perks and rewards. BMO also offers health insurance, tuition reimbursement, accident and life insurance, and retirement savings plans. To view more details of our benefits, please visit: https://jobs.bmo.com/global/en/Total-Rewards

About Us

At BMO we are driven by a shared Purpose: Boldly Grow the Good in business and life. It calls on us to create lasting, positive change for our customers, our communities and our people. By working together, innovating and pushing boundaries, we transform lives and businesses, and power economic growth around the world.

As a member of the BMO team you are valued, respected and heard, and you have more ways to grow and make an impact. We strive to help you make an impact from day one – for yourself and our customers. We’ll support you with the tools and resources you need to reach new milestones, as you help our customers reach theirs. From in-depth training and coaching, to manager support and network-building opportunities, we’ll help you gain valuable experience, and broaden your skillset.

To find out more visit us at https://jobs.bmo.com/ca/en

BMO is committed to an inclusive, equitable and accessible workplace. By learning from each other’s differences, we gain strength through our people and our perspectives. jobs.description:
Titre :
Directeur(-trice), Technologie, infrastructure et mise en œuvre

Lieu de travail :
Partiellement virtuel/hybride (Canada)

Type d’emploi :
Permanent à temps plein

La Croix-Rouge canadienne, organisation sans but lucratif des plus réputées et inspirantes au monde, vient en aide aux personnes et aux communautés dans le besoin au Canada et partout dans le monde et leur donne les moyens de renforcer leur résilience. À titre d’organisation figurant au palmarès des Meilleurs employeurs au Canada en 2026
, elle s’engage à offrir un milieu de travail accessible, diversifié, inclusif et sans obstacle.

Relevant de la direction principale, Planification et activités philanthropiques, au sein du service de Philanthropie de la Croix-Rouge canadienne, la personne retenue assurera un leadership stratégique en vue de créer l’écosystème de technologies et de données du service. En s’appuyant sur les travaux fondamentaux réalisés jusqu’à maintenant, elle supervisera l’évolution continue des systèmes, des outils et des structures de gouvernance propres au service afin de concrétiser les objectifs de croissance des revenus du service de Philanthropie.

Elle dirigera les équipes responsables de l'analyse des systèmes opérationnels et du développement Web; à cette fin, elle définira l'orientation stratégique et opérationnelle et veillera au respect des priorités du service. Elle travaillera également en étroite collaboration avec la direction du service de Philanthropie, et d’autres unités opérationnelles (Groupe technologique, Finances), afin d’arrimer la stratégie et la gouvernance en matière de technologies et de données avec les besoins opérationnels.

Enfin, elle se tiendra au courant des tendances du domaine pour mettre à profit l’intelligence artificielle et les technologies émergentes, tout en veillant à faire évoluer continuellement la feuille de route technologique afin de faire progresser les priorités stratégiques du service de Philanthropie.

Tâches et responsabilités

Diriger et encadrer les équipes responsables de l’analyse des systèmes opérationnels et du développement Web, en définissant les orientations, en renforçant les capacités grâce à la planification du perfectionnement et des effectifs, et en accompagnant les membres des équipes dans leur développement de carrière.
Définir l'orientation stratégique et opérationnelle de l'écosystème de technologies et de données du service de Philanthropie, en traduisant les priorités en feuilles de route et plans concrets.
Agir à titre d’administratrice ou d’administrateur des données au sein du service de Philanthropie, en mettant en place une structure de gouvernance encadrant l’utilisation des données et des technologies, ainsi que la gestion des processus et des produits, conformément aux normes de gouvernance de l’organisation.
Collaborer avec la direction du Groupe technologique, du service des Finances et d’autres équipes au sein du service de Philanthropie afin d’arrimer la stratégie technologique, les normes et la gouvernance avec les besoins opérationnels changeants.
Diriger la gestion du changement dans le cadre d’initiatives technologiques et opérationnelles, en anticipant les points de résistance, en favorisant l’adhésion et en assurant l’adoption.
Gérer le budget ainsi que les relations avec les fournisseurs, en veillant à la reddition de comptes et au rendement des investissements technologiques du service.
Élaborer des dossiers d’analyse et les présenter à la haute direction afin d’obtenir le financement, les ressources et le soutien de l’organisation nécessaires à la réalisation des initiatives clés.
Se tenir à l’affût des tendances du secteur et des technologies émergentes, notamment l’intelligence artificielle, en adaptant des stratégies pertinentes afin de soutenir la croissance des revenus et l’atteinte des priorités stratégiques du service de Philanthropie.
Établir et mettre à jour les pratiques exemplaires, les normes et les cadres de gouvernance qui renforcent la maturité en matière de données et de technologies à l'échelle du service.
Cerner, évaluer et atténuer les risques liés aux opérations ou aux systèmes, en veillant à la mise en place de pratiques appropriées en matière de gouvernance et de conformité.

Profil recherché

Posséder au moins de 8 à 12 ans d'expérience professionnelle pertinente ou une combinaison équivalente d'études et d'expérience en administration des affaires, en développement des affaires, en opérations, en analyse des données, en gestion de l'information ou dans un domaine pertinent, y compris de 5 à 7 ans d'expérience en gestion de personnel en ayant démontré sa capacité à diriger des équipes dans le cadre de changements et de transformations organisationnelles.
Posséder une expérience professionnelle dans le secteur sans but lucratif constitue un atout considérable; la connaissance du marketing, de la collecte de fonds ou de la vente constitue un atout.
Pouvoir conceptualiser et harmoniser des stratégies et les concrétiser en plans opérationnels complets et cohérents qui permettent de rapprocher les tâches quotidiennes des objectifs opérationnels du service de Philanthropie.
Pouvoir synthétiser des renseignements complexes et les communiquer à divers groupes de parties prenantes, en ayant de solides compétences en matière de persuasion, de négociation et de recherche de consensus.
Avoir prouvé sa capacité à planifier et à réaliser des projets de transformation technologique, organisationnelle ou en matière de données de moyenne à grande envergure.
Avoir une grande compréhension des systèmes de gestion des relations avec la clientèle (CRM) et des technologies plus générales liées à la collecte de fonds ou au marketing numérique (p. ex. plateformes de dons, outils de marketing par courriel et par message texte, traitement des dons).
Posséder une bonne connaissance du cadre réglementaire applicable au secteur caritatif canadien en matière de traitement des données, notamment la protection des données et de la vie privée, le consentement à la communication de renseignements et les obligations de conservation de dossiers à des fins fiscales (LPRPDE, LCAP, norme de l’ICP, ARC, etc.)
Pouvoir travailler efficacement dans un environnement complexe aux priorités multiples et parfois conflictuelles.
Avoir de l’expérience en gestion de budgets et de relations avec les fournisseurs.
Maîtriser les applications de base de la suite Microsoft Office.
Maîtriser l’anglais à l’oral et à l’écrit; la maîtrise du français constitue un atout.

Conditions de travail

La personne travaille selon un modèle hybride prévoyant une combinaison de travail en personne et à distance.
Le travail se déroule dans un environnement en évolution rapide où les priorités et les échéances changent souvent.
Il implique d’interagir avec des parties prenantes dans des situations délicates ou très stressantes.
Il exige un souci du détail, une grande concentration et la capacité de traiter une importante quantité d’informations.
Il exige de s’adapter à des changements dans l’ordre des priorités, de prendre des décisions sous pression et de parvenir à effectuer ses tâches à un rythme imprévisible.
Il exige le respect de multiples échéances conflictuelles.
L’emploi prévoit des déplacements dans des zones sûres, mais pourrait parfois contraindre la personne à évoluer dans des conditions difficiles.
Étant donné que nous offrons des services à des communautés et que nous travaillons avec des personnes (gestionnaires, collègues, clientèles, bénévoles, bailleurs de fonds et partenaires externes) partout au Canada et dans le monde, la personne retenue pourrait devoir assumer les responsabilités de son poste en anglais même s’il ne s’agit pas de sa langue maternelle.
Admissibilité à travailler au Canada : Nous invitons toutes les personnes qualifiées qui peuvent être employées au Canada à présenter leur candidature. Les personnes qui n’ont pas la citoyenneté ou la résidence permanente du Canada sont encouragées à examiner attentivement leur visa pour savoir si elles sont en mesure d’occuper le poste pour lequel elles présentent leur candidature. Pour obtenir de plus amples renseignements, veuillez consulter notre Foire aux questions.

The Director, AI & Automation is a senior business transformation leader accountable for setting the direction for, and leading the identification, prioritization, and delivery of, artificial intelligence, generative AI, intelligent automation, and digital workflow solutions across Procurement and the broader Operations organization. The role will translate enterprise and business priorities into a scalable portfolio of initiatives that simplify work, improve decision-making, strengthen controls, and create measurable operational and financial value.

Working under DIO-centered governance and in continuous partnership with DIO leadership and the DIO organizations, this role will own the business AI and automation roadmap and lead business initiatives from discovery and business-case development through solution design, deployment, adoption, and value realization. No AI or automation initiative will advance outside established DIO engagement, intake, architecture, platform, data, Information Security, and Cybersecurity processes. The Director will connect business process expertise with approved enterprise platforms and technical capabilities, including AI assistants and agents, machine learning, robotic process automation, workflow automation, intelligent document processing, process mining, analytics, and low-code solutions.

The role will serve as a strategic partner to Procurement, MCE, GDC, and other Operations senior leaders, leading the redesign of priority processes and scaling practical solutions that reduce manual effort, cycle time, cost, and operational risk. All opportunities, experiments, pilots, and production deployments will be planned and executed with DIO engagement and in alignment with enterprise architecture, Information Security, Cybersecurity, privacy, data governance, Responsible AI, and change-management requirements

Responsibilities

AI & Automation Strategy and Portfolio

Set the vision for and own a multi-year AI and automation roadmap aligned with Procurement, MCE, GDC, and broader Operations priorities
Partner with DIO leadership to apply its established intake and assessment process to identify, size, prioritize, and sequence opportunities based on business value, feasibility, risk, data readiness, security requirements, and scalability
Own business cases, delivery plans, resource requirements, investment asks, and benefit targets for the portfolio, with clear accountability and executive decision points
Monitor market and enterprise technology developments and advise senior leadership on practical use cases that address defined business problems rather than technology-driven experimentation

Business Partnership and Process Transformation

Serve as a trusted advisor to Procurement and Operations leaders to shape strategic priorities, map end-to-end processes, identify root causes, and redesign work before automating it
Direct focus toward high-value opportunities across source-to-pay, supplier management, contracting, risk and compliance, planning, project delivery, asset operations, and shared operational services
Partner with MCE and GDC leadership to improve productivity, throughput, service levels, data quality, cost performance, and execution predictability
Lead discovery efforts and ensure business needs are translated into clear process, data, user, control, and technology requirements

DIO-Led Governance, Partnership, and Solution Delivery

Serve as the primary business leader and counterpart to DIO leadership and DIO product, engineering, architecture, data, security, and platform teams, ensuring DIO is engaged from initial opportunity identification through planning, delivery, production approval, and ongoing support
Co-develop solution strategies and delivery roadmaps with DIO within DIO governance and using DIO-approved enterprise capabilities, including generative AI, agentic AI, machine learning, RPA, workflow, intelligent document processing, process mining, and low-code tools
Provide business leadership across the full lifecycle—discovery, prototyping, design, testing, deployment, stabilization, support transition, and continuous improvement—while DIO provides the required technology governance, architecture, security, and platform engagement
Direct and align business subject-matter experts, DIO teams, Information Security, Cybersecurity, vendors, implementation partners, and managed-service providers to deliver on scope, schedule, quality, security, and value commitments

DIO-Centered Governance, Information Security, and Responsible AI

Operate within DIO-owned governance, design standards, documentation requirements, stage gates, decision rights, and operating routines; do not initiate or advance AI and automation work without the appropriate DIO engagement and approvals
Ensure Information Security and Cybersecurity are engaged through DIO at the earliest stage and maintain alignment throughout design, testing, deployment, monitoring, and change management
Ensure solutions comply with DIO requirements for enterprise architecture, approved platforms, cybersecurity, information security, privacy, data governance, records management, legal and regulatory obligations, and Responsible AI
Partner with DIO, Information Security, and Cybersecurity leadership to define controls for human oversight, identity and access, data protection, testing, model and output quality, exception handling, monitoring, incident response, and issue escalation
Provide transparent reporting to executive, business, and DIO stakeholders on portfolio health, dependencies, risks, approvals, costs, benefits, adoption, and operational performance

Adoption, Capability Building, and Value Realization

Lead stakeholder, communication, training, and adoption strategies that embed new ways of working and deliver sustained business outcomes
Champion AI and automation fluency across Procurement and Operations through playbooks, reusable patterns, communities of practice, and role-based learning
Establish baselines and own value tracking across productivity, cycle time, cost, quality, compliance, user experience, adoption, and capacity released for higher-value work
Deliver executive-ready recommendations, portfolio updates, and value-realization reporting to senior leadership; take decisive action when initiatives are not delivering expected outcomes

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Operations, Supply Chain, Procurement, Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience
Typically, 10+ years of progressive experience in AI, intelligent automation, digital transformation, process excellence, product or program management, or technology-enabled operations, including leadership of complex cross-functional initiatives
Demonstrated experience identifying, prioritizing, and delivering AI and automation use cases from concept through production, adoption, and value realization
Working knowledge of generative AI, AI agents, machine learning, RPA, workflow automation, intelligent document processing, process mining, analytics, APIs, and low-code platforms
Experience improving end-to-end business processes and translating operational needs into business requirements, solution designs, implementation plans, and measurable outcomes
Strong understanding of DIO-centered technology governance and the role of enterprise architecture, Information Security, Cybersecurity, data governance, privacy, controls, testing, monitoring, and Responsible AI across the solution lifecycle
Proven ability to partner with senior business leaders, technology organizations, process owners, vendors, and geographically distributed teams in a global matrixed environment
Excellent business-case development, program leadership, analytical problem-solving, facilitation, executive communication, and stakeholder-influence capabilities

Preferred Qualifications

Advanced degree in Business, Operations, Supply Chain, Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, or a related field
Experience applying AI and automation in Procurement, source-to-pay, supplier management, infrastructure delivery, data center, engineering, construction, or asset-intensive operations
Experience with enterprise platforms and ecosystems such as Microsoft Azure and Power Platform, Copilot, UiPath, ServiceNow, Celonis, Oracle, Coupa, or comparable technologies
Experience with Lean, Six Sigma, process reengineering, product management, agile delivery, or enterprise change-management methods
Relevant certification in AI, automation, cloud, process mining, project or product management, change management, or process improvement

jobs.description:
Embark on a rewarding career with Sobeys Inc., celebrated among Canada’s Top 100 employers where your unique contributions drive success.

Role Summary

The Director, Digital Experience Platforms (DXP) is accountable for the strategy, engineering delivery, operations, reliability, and evolution of all customer-facing digital experience platforms across Empire banners. This role leads the technology execution of web, mobile, content, search, UX platform capabilities, and front-end engineering ecosystems, ensuring seamless, scalable, secure, and high-performing customer experiences.

The Director serves as the primary technology counterpart to Digital Experience, Digital Product, Customer Engagement, Commerce, and Banner teams, translating business vision into enterprise-grade digital capabilities. The role is responsible for balancing innovation, delivery velocity, operational excellence, and platform sustainability while enabling a product-led operating model.

Accountabilities & Responsibilities

Digital Experience Platform Leadership

Own the end-to-end technology strategy, roadmap, delivery, and operation of all digital experience platforms across web, mobile, and customer-facing digital channels.
Define the future-state architecture and capability evolution roadmap for DXP technologies including Adobe Experience Manager (AEM), front-end platforms, mobile applications, search technologies, design systems, and supporting digital services.
Ensure platform capabilities support enterprise digital commerce objectives, customer experience strategies, and banner-specific priorities.
Establish technology standards, engineering practices, and governance frameworks for front-end and customer experience platforms.

Engineering Delivery & Execution

Lead multiple engineering teams responsible for:
Customer websites
Mobile applications
Front-end engineering
Search and discovery platforms
Design systems
Content delivery platforms
AEM ecosystem

Drive delivery of strategic initiatives through Agile product teams.
Ensure predictable execution, release readiness, and high-quality software delivery.
Partner with Product and Business teams to define roadmaps, priorities, and release strategies.

Digital Experience Reliability & Operations

Own availability, performance, scalability, and resilience of all digital experience platforms.

Disaster recovery
Capacity planning

jobs.title: Directeur ou directrice de l’ingénierie – Solutions thermiques pour centres de données / Senior Director of Engineering - Data Center Thermal Solutions
jobs.description:
À propos de Smardt

Leader mondial des refroidisseurs centrifuges sans huile, Smardt développe des solutions de gestion thermique écoénergétiques destinées aux environnements critiques, notamment les centres de données IA et hyperscale, les établissements de santé et les installations industrielles et commerciales.

Présente aux États-Unis, au Canada, en Allemagne, en Chine et en Australie, Smardt compte plus de 1 200 employés. Nous misons sur l'innovation, la fiabilité et la performance pour contribuer à un avenir plus durable.

Profil recherché

Nous recherchons un(e) leader technique pour développer et diriger notre expertise en solutions thermiques pour centres de données. Vous définirez la stratégie technologique, la structure d'ingénierie, la feuille de route des produits et les partenariats stratégiques pour répondre aux besoins des clients hyperscale, de colocation et d'infrastructures IA haute densité.

Vous dirigerez le développement et l'intégration de solutions de refroidissement liquide et à air, notamment les systèmes CRAC, CRAH, les murs de ventilateurs, les solutions modulaires et les systèmes de contrôle.

En collaboration avec les clients et partenaires, vous identifierez les nouvelles technologies et les occasions de marché afin de développer des solutions innovantes, évolutives et commercialement viables.

Vos responsabilités

Stratégie et développement de l'expertise

Développer l'expertise de Smardt en solutions thermiques pour centres de données, notamment le refroidissement liquide, les systèmes CRAC/CRAH, les murs de ventilateurs et les contrôles intégrés.
Définir les normes techniques, les priorités d'investissement et la feuille de route technologique.
Développer le portefeuille de solutions de refroidissement des salles informatiques en complément des refroidisseurs et systèmes de rejet de chaleur existants.
Développer des technologies exclusives et de la propriété intellectuelle pour répondre aux besoins des clients et se démarquer de la concurrence.
Recruter, encadrer et diriger une équipe multidisciplinaire d'ingénieurs en thermique, mécanique, systèmes fluidiques et automatisation.
Conseiller la direction sur les occasions de marché, les risques techniques et les investissements stratégiques.

Architecture thermique et innovation

Diriger la conception et le développement de solutions intégrées de gestion thermique pour centres de données.
Superviser le développement du refroidissement liquide direct aux puces, des unités de distribution de liquide de refroidissement (CDU), des circuits secondaires, des échangeurs de chaleur et des systèmes de pompage.
Assurer l'intégration des solutions de refroidissement des salles informatiques aux infrastructures du bâtiment, notamment les réseaux d'eau glacée, les refroidisseurs et les systèmes de rejet de chaleur.
Optimiser la performance, l'efficacité énergétique, la fiabilité, la redondance et la facilité d'entretien.
Transformer les besoins des clients hyperscale, de colocation et IA/HPC en solutions évolutives et commercialement viables.
Évaluer les nouvelles technologies et déterminer les solutions à développer à l'interne ou avec des partenaires stratégiques.
Adapter les produits des sociétés du groupe aux marchés desservis par Smardt, conformément aux certifications et exigences des clients.

Exécution des projets et commercialisation

Superviser le cycle complet de développement, de la conception et modélisation jusqu'aux prototypes, essais, validation, qualification et lancement.
Collaborer avec les équipes de fabrication, qualité, chaîne d'approvisionnement et service pour assurer la sécurité, la fabricabilité, la fiabilité et la rentabilité des solutions.
Mettre en place des revues de conception, des protocoles d'essais et des processus de gestion des risques et d'actions correctives.
Développer des processus d'ingénierie évolutifs permettant la commercialisation et le déploiement mondial des produits.

Relations clients et partenariats

Agir comme expert technique auprès des exploitants hyperscale, des fournisseurs de colocation, des firmes de génie-conseil, des fabricants d'équipement (OEM) et des partenaires technologiques.
Participer à l'architecture des solutions, aux propositions techniques, aux projets pilotes, aux essais d'acceptation et à la mise en service.
Anticiper les besoins technologiques des clients et les intégrer à la feuille de route des produits.
Représenter Smardt lors d'événements de l'industrie, de groupes techniques et de partenariats stratégiques.

Qualifications Recherchées

Plus de 10 à 15 ans d'expérience progressive en génie mécanique, thermique, CVAC-R ou systèmes fluidiques, dont une expérience significative en refroidissement de centres de données.
Expérience démontrée en développement, intégration ou commercialisation de solutions thermiques critiques : refroidissement liquide, CRAC, CRAH, murs de ventilateurs ou technologies connexes.
Excellente compréhension des architectures de refroidissement des centres de données et de leur intégration aux réseaux d'eau glacée et systèmes de rejet de chaleur.
Expérience reconnue en création d'équipes d'ingénierie, gestion multidisciplinaire et développement de produits complexes.
Expérience de direction en ingénierie ou comme gestionnaire principal(e) capable de créer et diriger une nouvelle fonction.

Compétences techniques

Maîtrise des technologies de refroidissement liquide direct aux puces, CDU, CRAC, CRAH, murs de ventilateurs et systèmes d'eau glacée.
Connaissance des exigences thermiques des infrastructures IA/HPC haute densité, de la gestion des flux d'air, de la redondance et de la fiabilité.
Expertise en transfert de chaleur, thermodynamique, mécanique des fluides et systèmes hydroniques.
Capacité à évaluer le dimensionnement des CDU, les débits, les pertes de pression, les échangeurs de chaleur et les systèmes de contrôle.
Capacité à lire et interpréter les plans techniques, schémas de tuyauterie et d'instrumentation (P&ID), devis et données de performance.
Expérience en CAO, simulation CFD et modélisation, un atout.
Expérience en développement d'équipes, qualification de fournisseurs, partenariats technologiques et commercialisation de produits.
Excellent jugement technique, leadership, gestion de projets et aptitudes en communication avec les clients et les équipes.

Formation

Baccalauréat en génie mécanique, génie thermique ou domaine connexe.
Diplôme d'études supérieures, un atout.

Ce que nous offrons

Rémunération concurrentielle.
Assurances collectives, incluant soins médicaux et dentaires, dès le premier jour.
Programme de cotisation équivalente au REER ou au 401(k), selon le pays.
Environnement de travail international et collaboratif offrant des possibilités de développement professionnel.

Équité en matière d'emploi

Smardt souscrit au principe de l'égalité des chances en emploi et favorise un milieu de travail inclusif et diversifié, où chaque personne est traitée avec dignité et respect.

Nous ne pratiquons aucune discrimination fondée sur la race, la couleur, la religion, le sexe, la grossesse, l'orientation sexuelle, l'identité de genre, l'origine nationale, l'âge, le handicap, les renseignements génétiques, le statut militaire ou d'ancien combattant, l'état matrimonial ou tout autre motif protégé par les lois applicables.

Dans le cadre de son processus d'embauche, Smardt peut effectuer des vérifications des antécédents conformément aux lois applicables.

Smardt n'accepte pas les candidatures non sollicitées provenant d'agences de recrutement. Aucun honoraire ou frais de référencement ne sera versé sans entente de services préalablement signée.

As a global leader in oil-free centrifugal chiller technology with an expanding portfolio of thermal management solutions, Smardt is dedicated to delivering high-efficiency and energy-saving systems for mission-critical environments worldwide, from AI and hyperscale data centers to health care, industrial and commercial facilities. We operate manufacturing facilities in the US, Canada, Germany, China, and Australia, with a team of over 1200 employees. With a focus on reliability, performance, and environmental stewardship, Smardt continues to redefine industry standards through advanced engineering and a commitment to a more sustainable future.

What We're Looking For

You will build and lead Smardt’s data center thermal solutions capability, defining the technology strategy, engineering organization, product roadmap and strategic partnerships required to serve hyperscale, colocation and high-density AI infrastructure customers.

You will lead the development and integration of comprehensive data center cooling solutions, including liquid cooling, CRAC, CRAH, fan walls, modular solutions, thermal management and controls, complementing Smardt’s established chiller and heat rejection portfolio.

You will engage directly with customers and industry partners to anticipate emerging technology requirements, identify market opportunities and translate these into differentiated, scalable and commercially viable solutions. Lead product and technology development from concept through validation, industrialization and commercialization, determining where Smardt should develop proprietary capabilities versus leverage strategic partnerships.

What You'll Do

Develop IP’s to solve challenging customer problems and differentiate vs competition

Advise executive, R&D, product and commercial leaders on market opportunities, technical risks and capability-building priorities.

Engineering Execution and Commercialization

Own the engineering lifecycle from concept, modeling and design through prototyping, performance and reliability testing, verification, qualification and launch.

jobs.title: Director, Delivery CX AI
jobs.description:
Director, CX AI Delivery 
 Who We Are 
 Welcome to TELUS Digital — where innovation drives impact at a global scale. As an award-winning digital product consultancy and the digital division of TELUS, one of Canada’s largest telecommunications providers, we design and deliver transformative customer experiences through cutting-edge technology, agile thinking, and a people-first culture
 With a global team across North America, South America, Central America, Europe, Africa, and APAC, we offer end-to-end expertise across eight core service areas: Digital Product Consulting, Digital Marketing Services, Data & AI, Strategy Consulting, Business Operations Modernization, Enterprise Applications, Cloud Engineering, and QA & Test Engineering.

 From mobile apps and websites to voice UI, chatbots, AI, customer service, and in-store solutions, TELUS Digital enables seamless, trusted, and digitally powered experiences that meet customers wherever they are — all backed by the secure infrastructure and scale of our multi-billion-dollar parent company.

 Location & Flexibility 
 This role will operate remotely in the United States or Canada OR be based out of one of our major North American office locations - Charlottesville, VA, Durham, NC, Columbus, OH, Boston, MA, Toronto, ON, or Vancouver, BC.
 This role may involve travel of up to 25% to contact center and client locations.

 The Opportunity 
 We are seeking a Director, CX AI Delivery: a consultant and delivery expert who can turn complex contact center and AI programs into predictable, measurable outcomes. You will lead delivery across our CX AI portfolio, spanning Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) platforms, conversational and agentic AI, agent assist, and CX intelligence, and serve as a trusted advisor to client executives. You will manage a portfolio of client engagements (generally ~$15–20M in revenue), directly lead delivery, product, and engineering leaders, and step in to stabilize and recover programs when needed.

 This is a delivery-first leadership role with an AI lens. You will bring the rigor of a seasoned delivery executive together with a working command of how AI is changing CX: from AI-driven routing and virtual agents to copilots, knowledge, and agentic automation. You will help clients adopt these capabilities responsibly, at scale, and in iterative releases that get value into production quickly. You will also help evaluate vendor and partner solutions and decide how and when new tools enter the ecosystem.

 This position reports to the Managing Director, CX AI Delivery and typically manages 8–12 direct reports, including senior managers, managers, and principal-level delivery and technical leaders. It is primarily evaluated on delivery success, client and team feedback, forecast accuracy, portfolio profitability, and growth of key accounts. This is an opportunistically billable position.
 Responsibilities 
 Strategic Account Governance & Growth 
 Be the executive partner. Act as the primary escalation point and strategic advisor for client executives, ensuring TELUS Digital is viewed as a “Doctor” (consultative partner), not a “Waiter” (order taker).

 Run portfolio health. Drive the commercial success of a ~$15–20M portfolio, leading Quarterly Business Reviews that connect delivery progress to the client’s long-term CX and business goals.

 Grow organically. Identify expansion opportunities in existing accounts by understanding client pain points and bringing a relevant point of view on CX and AI. Support renewals, upsell, and expansion in partnership with strategic sales and customer success teams.

 Extend into managed services and advisory as the practice matures: shape Day 2 support models, operational readiness, and advisory engagements that keep clients engaged after go-live.

 Delivery Excellence & Risk Mitigation 
 Lead a global, multidisciplinary team across multiple concurrent workstreams, ensuring product, engineering, and delivery leaders operate as a cohesive unit to deliver measurable outcomes.

 Manage risk proactively. Identify “red” and “yellow” programs early; step into recovery situations to provide clarity, reset expectations, and stabilize teams and client relationships.

 Push for iterative delivery. Favor smaller releases and faster cycles over big-bang launches, especially for AI capabilities where learning in production is essential.

 Optimize delivery models, balancing onshore/offshore teams, automation, and repeatable assets to improve margins and scalability.

 Manage vendor and partner ecosystems. Work with CCaaS and AI platform partners (e.g., Genesys, Google, AWS, Zendesk, Five9, ElevenLabs, Cresta, Parloa) to deliver joint solutions as well as surrounding services in the client ecosystem.

 Partner on pre-sales. Support the commercial team to shape innovative solutions and lead scoping, estimation, and handoffs into delivery so engagements start with clear requirements and goals.

 Leadership & Talent Development 
 Coach and mentor delivery, product, and engineering leaders on leading their own teams and navigating complex client dynamics.

 Build a high-performance culture with regular 1:1s and performance reviews grounded in radical candor and growth, delivering feedback upward, across, and down with grace and clarity.

 Raise the bar on talent. Participate in senior-level hiring, contribute to the Delivery Playbook, and build career paths and skill development (including AI and platform certification pipelines).

 Operational & Financial Stewardship 
 Own portfolio financials: gross margin, utilization, and effective billable rates.

 Forecast accurately. Maintain precise revenue and resource forecasts so the business can plan hiring and growth with confidence.

 Influence with data. Use reporting language, data visualization, and storytelling to influence internal and external decisions and inspire confidence in stakeholders.

 Collaborate across the business with peers and practice leaders to improve internal processes and operational efficiency, and bring energy to moments that matter: new relationships, key presentations, and recovery situations.

 Qualifications 
 10+ years in the technology industry, including 4+ years in a senior leadership role in a professional services, consulting, or agency environment.

 Proven record managing a diverse portfolio of client accounts (ideally $10M+ in annual revenue) with a focus on retention and organic growth.

 Experience delivering large-scale CX or contact center transformations that influenced VP- and C-level decision making.

jobs.description:
About ClearGov 

 ClearGov is building the modern financial operating layer for the public sector. 

 We help US local governments and school districts plan, budget, report, and communicate their finances with clarity and confidence. From long-term planning to financial reporting, compliance, and transparency, our platform connects the work finance teams are already doing and makes it easier to deliver for their communities. 

Today, more than 2,000 public sector organizations use ClearGov, and we continue to expand our platform and reach as we grow.

 Our Core Values 

 Be Clear & Credible  

 We are authentic in our interactions, communicating with clarity, speaking with honesty, and following through with consistency. We turn transparency into our greatest competitive advantage. 

 Be Human   

 We are human partners to our colleagues and customers and lead with consideration and kindness - making space for others to do the same. We turn empathy into a shared strength.

 Be Better Together   

 We are committed to building an inclusive community where everyone thrives. We share successes, support each other through challenges, and show up for our teammates the way we show up for our customers. We turn togetherness into our greatest advantage and collaboration into our greatest multiplier.

 Be Honourable/Honorable   

 We are responsible to our colleagues and customers. We bring our full selves to every conversation, every project, every decision, and every relationship. We act with intention, deliver on our commitments, and lead with integrity - even when no one is watching. We turn honour into the foundation that powers everything we do.

 Be Connected 

 We are culture builders where people are seen, welcomed, and celebrated. We show up in every interaction - the laughs, the wins, the hard days. We turn connection into opportunities for people to feel they belong.

 What Makes You a Great Fit 

 You take ownership and follow through

 You communicate clearly and effectively

 You're comfortable solving problems and figuring things out

 You learn quickly and adapt as things change

 You care about the team, not just your own work

 You bring a sense of humor and perspective to what you do

 About the Opportunity 

 We are seeking a hands-on Vice President, Financial Planning & Analysis to own enterprise-wide planning, forecasting, and performance analytics for a growth-stage SaaS business. This is not a purely oversight role, the VP, FP&A will be in the models directly, building and stress-testing scenarios, and translating the numbers into decisions. Reporting to the CFO, this person will be a key partner to executive leadership and business unit owners, and will play a central role in the company's next chapter of growth.

 We're looking for someone who wants to build, not just review, someone as comfortable inside the mechanics of a model as they are presenting its output to the CFO and board. 

 Key Responsibilities: 

 10+ years of progressive finance experience, including FP&A leadership, with a track record of being genuinely hands-on in the model — not several layers removed from it.

 Direct experience in a SaaS or recurring-revenue business, fluent in ARR, NRR, churn, cohort, and unit economics analysis.

 Strong financial modeling and scenario-planning skills — able to build complex models from scratch and pressure-test assumptions in real time.

 Exposure to an exit, sale process, recapitalization, refinancing, or similar transaction, with a working understanding of what "diligence-ready" actually looks like.

 Executive presence — able to move fluidly between deep model work and clear, confident presentation to the CFO and board.

 Strong judgment about what's urgent, what's important, and what can wait — able to prioritize across competing asks from the CFO, business leaders, and the sponsor.

 Nice-to-haves: 

 M&A diligence or post-acquisition integration experience.

 CPA, CFA, or MBA.

 Prior experience building or scaling an FP&A function from a less mature state.

 Compensation: 

 In the spirit of transparency, we are excited to share the base salary for this position is $200,000 - $240,000 USD and $185,000 - $225,000 CAD and exclusive of fringe benefits or potential bonuses. If you are hired at ClearGov, your final base salary compensation will be determined by factors such as skills, interview performance, education and/or experience. In addition to those factors, we believe in the importance of pay equity and consider internal equity of our current team members as a part of any final offer. Please keep in mind that the range mentioned above is the full base salary for the role. Hiring beyond the base range would not be typical in order to allow for future & continued salary growth. We also offer a generous compensation and benefits package (more information on benefits listed below).

jobs.title: Vice President, Finance & Business Operations
jobs.description:
CONTEXT
  
At Make\-A\-Wish® Canada, we’re redefining how the world perceives wishes through our transformative new brand platform: Wishes Are Medicine. Grounded in research, this platform recognizes what we’ve long known to be true — that wishes have measurable healing power. When prescribed alongside medical treatment, wishes reduce stress, elevate endorphins, limit emergency room visits, and deliver lasting health benefits.
  
With more than 3,500 children still waiting and a new child diagnosed with a critical illness in Canada every two hours, our mission has never been more urgent — and there are many more prescriptions to fill.
  
To meet this challenge, we’ve launched our new three\-year strategic plan — Wishes Are Medicine: One Team, One Mission — focused intentionally on financial sustainability, mission impact, and operational excellence. When a child is facing a critical illness, a wish isn’t just a moment of joy — it’s a medically supported turning point. Studies show that children who receive a wish are 2\.5 times less likely to have unplanned hospital visits and 1\.9 times less likely to need the ER, with 100% of physicians agreeing that a wish can be a pivotal moment in treatment.
  
At Make\-A\-Wish Canada, you can play a lead role in bringing these powerful prescriptions to life. Where Wishes Are Medicine, transformation becomes a pathway to healing at scale — and this role is your opportunity to architect that future.
  
Our ambition to reach more children and families requires a strong financial and operational foundation. As Vice President, Finance \& Business Operations, you will help shape that foundation, bringing strategic leadership to financial planning, investments, risk, governance and the services that enable our organization to thrive. You will turn insight into action, strengthen how resources are invested and managed, and help build a more resilient, disciplined and mission\-driven organization.
  
At Make\-A\-Wish Canada, you’ll join a team united by a shared mission and an unwavering sense of possibility. Every role — whether advancing fundraising, brand, operations, or technology — helps fuel the same trajectory: transforming how hope and healing come to life for children and families nationwide. If you’re ready to help build a future where every eligible child receives the wish that helps them heal, we invite you to read on.
  
ROLE OVERVIEW
  
We’re seeking a Vice President, Finance \& Business Operations, a strategic and forward\-thinking leader who will help shape the next chapter of Make\-A\-Wish Canada. This is more than a finance role; it’s an opportunity to strengthen the financial and operational foundation that will enable our mission to grow sustainably.
  
As a key member of our Senior Leadership Team, and reporting to the Senior Vice President, Transformation \& Operations, you will bring together financial strategy, business operations, analytics, risk and governance to strengthen how we plan, invest and make decisions. You’ll provide the insight and discipline to steward our resources responsibly, improve organizational performance, and build the capabilities needed to support sustainable growth and greater mission impact.
  
If you bring financial acumen, business curiosity and enterprise thinking, and believe the strongest organizations pair ambition with discipline, this is your opportunity to help build the foundation from which our mission can grow and bring the power of Wishes Are Medicine to more children and families across Canada.
  
WHAT YOU WILL DO
  
**Shape Financial Strategy:** Lead budgeting, forecasting, multi\-year financial planning, and financial modelling. Translate insights into scenarios and recommendations that guide sustainable, mission\-aligned decisions over a three\-to\-five\-year time horizon.
  
**Steward Assets and Investments:** Oversee financial assets, treasury, and investment portfolio performance in accordance with policy, ensuring disciplined stewardship and informed decision\-making.
  
**Strengthen Governance and Reporting:** Provide clear financial reporting to the Board of Directors and Senior Leadership Team, support the Finance \& Audit Committee, and ensure sound governance, audit readiness, and compliance with CRA and other regulatory obligations.
  
**Advance Enterprise Risk Management:** Maintain the enterprise risk register, strengthen internal controls, and lead business continuity and disaster recovery planning to protect the organization’s assets, reputation, and long\-term sustainability.
  
**Modernize Financial Capability:** Build stronger modelling, analytics, systems, and processes that improve forecasting, performance visibility, operational efficiency, and organizational decision\-making.
  
**Lead Business Services:** Oversee property management, leases, contracts, insurance, and related business services. Balance operational efficiency and financial sustainability with investments in organizational capability and a safe, supportive workplace.
  
**Oversee Gift and Donation Administration:** Ensure sound systems and processes for restricted giving, endowments, estates, and other complex giving structures, coordinating closely with development teams to support stewardship and compliance.
  
**Advise and Partner:** Serve as a trusted advisor to the Senior Vice President, Transformation \& Operations, the CEO, and leadership colleagues on finance, risk, and business operations. Bring an enterprise lens to strategic planning and execution.
  
**Guide and Develop Talent:** Build, coach, and lead a high\-performing Finance and Business Operations team, creating clarity, accountability, collaboration, and opportunities for growth.

The Alberta Public Service works to build a stronger province for current and future generations. We make a difference in the lives of Albertans through rewarding career opportunities.

Ministry Of Advanced Education

The Ministry of Advanced Education in Alberta is responsible for overseeing the post-secondary education system. It plays a vital role in supporting universities, colleges, polytechnic institutions, and apprenticeship programs across the province.

In addition, the Ministry works to align education with the needs of Alberta’s economy by promoting skills development, research, and innovation. It collaborates with educational institutions, industry partners, and communities to prepare students for successful careers and to contribute to the province’s economic and social growth.

Overall, the Ministry of Advanced Education plays a critical role in shaping Alberta’s future by strengthening its workforce and supporting lifelong learning opportunities for all residents.

To learn more about the Ministry of Advanced Education in Alberta and what it has to offer, follow this link: Advanced Education | Alberta.ca

Role Responsibilities

Reporting to the Executive Director, Financial Services, the Director, Financial Operations & Projects, leads and continuously improves the Ministry’s financial and procurement operations, systems, and processes to support strategic business objectives.

Working in a complex and evolving environment, the Director manages competing priorities, develops innovative solutions, and adapts strategies to achieve results. The role requires strong leadership, problem-solving, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills to balance interests and build consensus.

The Director provides advice and guidance to senior management, executives, the Deputy Minister, and the Minister, influencing decisions and ensuring alignment between Ministry and Government priorities. Sound judgement, diplomacy, and the ability to navigate politically and financially sensitive issues are essential.

Job Responsilbilites

Lead the Financial Operations & Projects team in the review of current systems, processes and procedures with a Save view to assessing the potential risk of the current controls and providing options for the enhancements that could be implemented to strengthen the financial controls protecting Ministry assets as well as protecting the integrity of its financial reporting controls.
Work with program areas across the department to support procurement and contracting by assessing risks, providing alternatives and identifying business solutions that meet program area needs within the parameters of prudent business and government policies and trade agreements.
Recommend options and actions to improve affordability, value for money, and alignment with government priorities.
Develop ministry-wide financial operation processes to facilitate the efficient and effective delivery of department business.
Develop innovative approaches to new and existing financial systems, and support program financial teams.
Ensure all Ministry users have access to the required automated tools and privileges to perform their duties effectively and efficiently while balancing internal controls and segregation of duties.
Manage human resource issues (e.g., recruitment, performance management, professional development plans, and supervision).
Promote a cooperative attitude between Financial Services and program areas to ensure that the review of internal controls are completed to improve the financial and procurement processes and reduce risk in the programs and divisions of the Ministry.
Provide financial advice and guidance to all levels of line management throughout the Ministry, assisting them to resolve complex management issues and ensuring that they comply with Treasury Board, Service Alberta and internal AE policies.

APS Competencies

Competencies are behaviors that are essential to reach our goals in serving Albertans. We encourage you to have an in depth understanding of the competencies that are required for this opportunity and to be prepared to demonstrate them during the recruitment process.

Drive for Results
- The position takes and delegates responsibility for outcomes, uses variety of resources to monitor own performance standards, acknowledges even indirect responsibility, commits to what is good for Albertans even if not immediately accepted and reaches goals consistent with APS direction.

Creative Problem Solving
- The position engages the community and resources at hand to address issues, engages perspective to seek root causes, finds ways to improve complex systems, employs resources from other areas to solve problems and engages others and encourages debate and idea generation to solve problems while addressing risks.

Agility
- The position identifies and manages required change and the associated risks, identifies alternative approaches and supports others to do the same, proactively explains impact of changes, anticipates and mitigates emotions of others, anticipates obstacles and stays focused on goals and makes decisions and takes action in uncertain situations and creates a backup plan.

Develop Networks
- This position builds trust to fairly represent every party, uses network to identify opportunities, establishes credibility and common purpose with a range of people, actively represents needs and varying groups, creates strategic impression by inspiring and connecting with values and beliefs.

Systems Thinking
- This position takes a long-term view towards organization’s objectives and how to achieve them, takes holistic long-term view of challenges and opportunities, anticipates outcomes and potential impacts, seeks stakeholder perspectives, works towards actions and plans aligned with APS values and works with others to identify areas for collaboration.

This link will assist you with understanding competencies.

Qualifications

Required:

A University graduation in a field related to the position assignment, supplemented by five years progressively responsible experience.
CPA or legacy designation (CA, CMA, CGA).
Related experience or education may be considered as an equivalency on a one for one basis.

Assets

Relevant legislation, regulations and policies, specifically the Financial Administration Act, Government Accountability Act, Government Organization Act, Fiscal Responsibility Act, Treasury Board Directives, etc.
Demonstrated experience with financial operations and management within a public sector environment.
Government strategic and policy directions as they relate to the Ministry's mandate and initiatives.
Ministry business plans, programs, deliverables and initiatives and related financial issues.
Strategic, business, operational, fiscal and human resource planning and accountability processes used in AE and GoA.
The political environment within which the Ministry operates and the decision-making processes of Government.
Clients and stakeholders affected by Ministry legislation, policies and initiatives, including relevant committees, advisory groups and senior representatives.
Best practices associated with financial accountability, continuous improvement and quality assurance.
Thorough knowledge of business-related software and automated financial systems.

Minimum recruitment standards outline the minimum education and experience required for appointments to a job classification.

Notes

Term of Employment – Full-time

Candidates may be considered on a secondment basis, subject to approval from their home position/department. There may be an opportunity for the appointment to be extended beyond the initial term.

jobs.description:
Role purpose

The Director, Product Strategy & Growth is accountable for the strategic direction, growth, profitability, and lifecycle management of an assigned product portfolio. The role translates customer, market and business insight into a focused portfolio strategy, investment roadmap and commercialization plan that strengthen market position and deliver measurable value for customers, distribution partners, and the business. As a senior product leader and people leader, the Director brings together teams across Product, Distribution, Marketing, Digital, Technology, Operations, Finance, Legal, Risk and Compliance to make sound portfolio choices, accelerate execution and ensure products remain relevant, sustainable, and differentiated.

Key accountabilities:

Strategy and portfolio ownership:

Own and continuously refine the long-term strategy, value proposition and investment roadmap for the assigned portfolio, aligned to enterprise and business priorities.
Manage the full product lifecycle, including ideation, validation, development, launch, optimization, modernization, rationalization and, where required, responsible exit or run-off.
Maintain a focused and relevant product shelf that supports growth, client retention, member value, operational sustainability, and market differentiation.
Translate strategic priorities into clear choices, sequenced roadmaps, investment recommendations, and measurable outcomes.
Structure complex or ambiguous business opportunities into evidence-based assessments and business cases that clearly articulate customer and business value, financial implications, operational impacts, risks, dependencies, and tradeoffs.

Customer, market, and competitive insights:

Champion the voice of the customer by incorporating sponsor, member, advisor and distribution insights into product strategy, design, and prioritization.
Use customer research, market intelligence, competitive analysis, emerging trends, and performance data to identify unmet needs, growth opportunities, and portfolio risks.
Define the customer and business problems to be solved and ensure product decisions are grounded in evidence, clear hypotheses, and expected outcomes.
Monitor developments in technology, regulation, healthcare, benefits, and adjacent markets to anticipate changes that may affect the portfolio.

Growth, commercialization, and performance:

Lead commercialization and go-to-market strategies that strengthen positioning, enable distribution, and improve adoption, engagement, revenue, and profitability.
Partner with Sales, Marketing and Distribution to develop compelling value propositions, sales narratives, launch plans and client-facing materials.
Establish and regularly review portfolio scorecards covering customer outcomes, adoption, growth, revenue, profitability, operational health, risk, and strategic value, with clear accountability for delivering agreed portfolio outcomes
Use performance insights to recommend investment, optimization, pricing, remediation or exit decisions and communicate progress to senior leadership.

Product and delivery leadership:

Lead major product initiatives from opportunity assessment and business case through delivery, launch and benefits realization.
Set strategic priorities and desired outcomes for cross-functional delivery teams, ensuring resources remain focused on the highest-value opportunities.
Guide discovery, experimentation and validation using customer research, concept testing, analytics, and other fit for-purpose methods before significant investment is made.
Partner with Digital, Technology, Design and Operations leaders to create integrated experiences and scalable solutions; provide direction on scope and minimum viable product decisions.
Identify and evaluate opportunities to use AI, automation, data, and emerging digital capabilities to improve customer value, operating effectiveness, or business performance.
Lead the strategic management of external product partners and vendors, working with Procurement and business partners on selection, contracting, renewals, service expectations, performance, and ongoing strategic alignment.
Ensure product launches and material changes are operationally ready, with appropriate contracts, policy provisions, processes, training, communications, controls, and distribution enablement in place.

Risk, governance and regulatory stewardship:

Own product governance for the assigned portfolio and ensure material product, customer, contractual, operational, financial, and regulatory risks are understood and managed.
Work closely with Legal, Compliance, Risk, Privacy, and other control functions to obtain required approvals and ensure products and communications meet applicable requirements.
Bring forward clear decisions, trade-offs, and recommendations when risk, customer value, economics, or delivery feasibility are in tension.
Maintain appropriate documentation, controls, decision records, and escalation paths across the product lifecycle.

Enterprise leadership and talent development:

Build strong relationships and influence across functions and levels to align stakeholders, resolve ambiguity, and move complex decisions forward.
Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team, setting clear expectations and building strength in strategic thinking, commercial acumen, customer insight, and execution.
Create an inclusive, accountable, and learning-oriented team environment that encourages constructive challenge and sound decision-making.
Represent the portfolio in senior leadership discussions, capabilities presentations, distribution forums, client meetings, advisory boards, and industry events as required.
Lead strategic initiatives spanning the broader product organization or business where enterprise priorities require cross-portfolio leadership.

Measures of success:

Clear portfolio strategy and roadmap with demonstrated alignment to business priorities.
Measurable improvement in customer value, adoption, growth, profitability, retention, and/or strategic differentiation, as appropriate to the portfolio.
Disciplined investment choices supported by evidence, transparent trade-offs, and defined success measures.
Reliable delivery of priority initiatives, with effective management of scope, dependencies, risks, and benefits realization.
Strong product governance, partner performance, and lifecycle management.
An engaged, capable team with clear accountability and succession depth.

Qualifications and experience:

Required:

Undergraduate degree in business, finance, marketing, health, technology or a related field, or equivalent experience.
Typically, 8+ years of progressive product, strategy, innovation, or commercialization, including leadership of complex cross-functional initiatives.
Demonstrated experience in financial services, insurance, group benefits, health, wellbeing, disability, or other regulated industries.
Demonstrated experience developing product or portfolio strategies and translating them into executable roadmaps, business cases, and measurable outcomes.
Demonstrated ability to apply product and strategic capabilities across different portfolios, quickly build subject matter expertise and lead effectively as business priorities evolve.
Strong commercial and financial acumen, including experience assessing product economics, investment tradeoffs, and portfolio performance.
Proven ability to lead through influence in a highly matrixed and regulated environment.
Experience leading, coaching, and developing people and building effective teams.
Excellent executive communication skills, including the ability to simplify complex issues, frame decisions and deliver clear recommendations.

Preferred:

Experience in group benefits, health, wellbeing, dental and/or disability products, including employer-sponsored solutions.
Experience managing strategic partnerships, vendors, or ecosystem-based propositions.
Experience with digital product development, customer experience design, agile delivery, and data-informed experimentation.
Working knowledge of relevant compliance, privacy, risk, and product governance practices.

Leadership capabilities:

Strategic and enterprise thinking:
Connects market, customer, and business signals; makes choices that strengthen long-term enterprise value.
Customer and growth orientation:
Balances customer outcomes with commercial discipline and sustainable portfolio growth.
Decision quality:
Uses evidence, judgment, and clear trade-offs to make timely recommendations in ambiguous situations.
Influence and collaboration:
Builds alignment across diverse stakeholders without relying solely on formal authority.
Execution and accountability:
Turns strategy into priorities, mobilizes teams, and follows through on measurable outcomes.
Innovation and adaptability:
Challenges established approaches, learns quickly and responds effectively to changing conditions.
People leadership:
Sets a clear direction, coaches for growth, and creates an inclusive, high-performance environment.
Technology and data fluency:
Uses technology, analytics, and emerging capabilities to improve products, experiences, and decisions.

Decision authority:

Full people and resource management accountability within the assigned team, in accordance with organizational policies and delegated authority.
Recommend portfolio strategy, investment priorities, product launches, significant enhancements, remediation, rationalization and exit decisions to senior leadership.

Define desired outcomes, minimum viable product parameters, and scope guardrails for assigned initiatives.
Direct minor product enhancements and lifecycle actions within approved strategy, budget, risk appetite, and governance requirements.
Manage approved budgets, business cases, financial commitments, and partner performance for the assigned portfolio.
Make implementation and operating decisions within delegated authority and escalate material issues, risks, or trade-offs as required.
Own product risk and governance decisions within the assigned portfolio, in partnership with the appropriate control functions.

Working conditions:
