jobs.description:
Director, Accounting & Finance

Toronto, ON (Hybrid – Tuesdays and Thursdays in Toronto office)

$125,000–$150,000 base salary, plus benefits and RRSP matching

Our client is an established organization with a small Canadian team and long-tenured employees. They are looking for a Director, Accounting & Finance to take ownership of full-cycle accounting and financial reporting. Reporting to the Executive Director, you will supervise one direct report and work closely with finance colleagues across the broader organization.

This is a hands-on role for a CPA who enjoys preparing the numbers and explaining them to leadership. You will manage the monthly close, oversee payroll and help the team transition to Workday Financial and its integration with ADP. The organization is targeting a January 2027 start. They offer very good work/life balance, 12 sick days and an office closure between Christmas and New Year’s. Some weeks you will only be expected to go into the office one day per week, but mostly it will be two days. This is a very hands-on Director role, so you should be prepared to handle bank reconciliations, journal entries, HST filing and more.

Responsibilities

Manage the monthly and year-end close, including journal entries, general ledger reconciliations and the preparation of financial statements. Prepare monthly management reports and explain variances against budget.
Oversee accounts payable and accounts receivable, manage day-to-day banking and complete bank reconciliations.
Record investment transactions, reconcile holdings to investment statements and prepare monthly investment reports. Review distribution approvals and complete the related accounting and reconciliations.
Oversee Ontario payroll through ADP. Review and approve each pay run, verify salary changes and ensure payroll information flows accurately between Workday and ADP.
Coordinate the annual audit, prepare working papers and financial schedules, and respond to questions from external auditors.
Prepare monthly GST/HST returns and coordinate withholding tax reporting, annual information returns and other regulatory filings with external advisers.
Review accounting policies, approval procedures and the segregation of duties. Help improve processes as the team transitions to new systems.
Supervise and develop one direct report whose current focus is accounts receivable. Help identify opportunities for that role to take on more financial analysis over time.

Requirements

Canadian CPA designation and a bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance or a related field.
At least eight years of progressive accounting experience, including hands-on responsibility for full-cycle accounting, bank reconciliations and monthly financial reporting.
Preference will be given to individuals with Workday and ADP experience.
Strong understanding of audit preparation, internal controls and payroll oversight.
Advanced EXCEL skills and the ability to investigate discrepancies, explain findings and manage competing deadlines.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, sound judgment when handling confidential information and the ability to guide a direct report while managing your own accounting work.

This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Director of Sales, Enterprise based in Canada.

The Director of Sales, Enterprise will lead enterprise revenue growth across North America, driving new business acquisition and expanding relationships with strategic customers. This leadership role combines sales strategy, team development, and hands-on involvement in complex, high-value SaaS transactions. You will manage and coach a team of Account Executives while building a predictable, scalable enterprise sales engine. Working closely with senior executives and cross-functional teams, you will strengthen go-to-market execution and expand the organization's presence in the Life Sciences sector. The role requires strong commercial judgment, executive relationship-building skills, and the ability to navigate lengthy, multi-stakeholder sales cycles. You will help shape enterprise sales performance in a fast-growing, innovative software environment.

Accountabilities

Drive enterprise revenue growth: Own and execute the North American enterprise sales strategy, achieving new business annual recurring revenue (ARR) targets and expanding market share across strategic accounts.
Develop sales strategy: Establish structured approaches for complex enterprise sales cycles, including account planning, opportunity qualification, stakeholder mapping, and deal execution.
Lead and develop the sales team: Manage, mentor, and coach Account Executives through hands-on guidance, performance management, and ongoing professional development.
Support strategic deals: Engage directly in high-value opportunities, helping the team develop deal strategies, build executive relationships, navigate procurement, negotiate commercial terms, and close business.
Build executive relationships: Develop and maintain relationships with senior decision-makers across pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device organizations in the United States and Canada.
Manage pipeline and performance: Maintain a healthy enterprise pipeline, monitor sales metrics, and identify ways to improve conversion rates, deal progression, and overall sales effectiveness.
Expand market opportunities: Identify and pursue new enterprise accounts across North America, developing targeted strategies and strengthening market positioning within the Life Sciences industry.
Collaborate across departments: Work closely with Marketing, Product, Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, and Revenue Operations to align go-to-market initiatives and address complex customer needs.
Oversee forecasting and reporting: Lead pipeline reviews, revenue forecasting, and sales reporting, providing senior leadership with visibility into opportunities, risks, and expected performance.

Requirements

8+ years of experience in B2B SaaS sales, with a focus on enterprise accounts.
At least 3 years of experience in sales management or leadership, including managing, coaching, and developing Account Executives.
Proven record of achieving and exceeding enterprise sales targets in North American and global markets, including closing complex, high-value SaaS deals.
Experience selling SaaS solutions to Life Sciences organizations or within Quality Management, Compliance, or other highly regulated industries.
Strong understanding of the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device sectors, including international regulatory and compliance requirements such as FDA, EMA, and GxP.
Extensive knowledge of complex enterprise sales cycles, including multi-stakeholder decision-making, executive-level engagement, procurement, and contract negotiations.
Strong business acumen and the ability to communicate technical capabilities in terms of measurable business value to C-level executives and senior decision-makers.
Hands-on leadership approach, with the ability to guide teams through discovery, qualification, value-based selling, negotiation, and closing.
Strong analytical skills and experience with revenue forecasting, pipeline management, and sales performance metrics.
Ability to balance strategic planning with direct sales involvement in a dynamic, fast-growing environment.
Availability to work primarily Eastern Time (ET) hours to collaborate effectively with internal teams.
Nice to have: Experience selling Quality Management Systems (QMS) or compliance software; experience scaling enterprise sales teams and processes in early- to mid-stage SaaS companies; familiarity with Salesforce-native SaaS products and go-to-market environments.

Benefits

Opportunity to lead enterprise sales strategy and develop a high-performing Account Executive team.
Exposure to strategic customers in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device industries.

Description

Director Strategy and Delivery Real World Late Phase

Syneos Health® is a leading fully-integrated life sciences services organization built to accelerate customer success. We partner with innovators at every point across the drug development and commercialization continuum, helping them navigate complexity, anticipate change and accelerate progress.

Our Clinical Solutions team members act with a drug development mindset, applying their years of experience and deep expertise to truly understand customer needs and represent those in the solutions we shape.

Whether you join us in a Functional Service Provider partnership or a Full-Service environment, you’ll collaborate with passionate problem solvers, innovating as a team to help our customers achieve their goals. We are agile and driven to deliver – for one another, our customers, and, most importantly, for those in need.

Discover what your 25,000 future colleagues already know:

Why Syneos Health

We are passionate about developing our people, through career development and progression; supportive and engaged line management; technical and therapeutic area training; peer recognition and total rewards program.
We are committed to building an inclusive culture – where you can authentically be yourself. Central to this is our purpose – Driven to Deliver – which captures the passion of our colleagues to show up each day and shape solutions that have the ability to dramatically impact someone’s life.
We are continuously building the company we all want to work for and our customers want to work with. Why? Because we know that when we bring together smart colleagues from across the world, we can shape the future of healthcare, driving impact for customers and defining the pace of patient progress.

Job Responsibilities

Job Summary

The Director, Strategy & Delivery, Real World Late Phase (RWLP), independently leads customer engagements from pre-award strategy through study delivery. The role combines ownership of study strategy, proposal development and bid defenses with operational and financial oversight of assigned studies, programs and portfolios. The Director partners with Business Development and Medical Strategy to secure new business, support account growth and ensure that proposal commitments translate into achievable delivery plans.

The Director develops practical delivery solutions for non-interventional and interventional late-phase research, including prospective and retrospective observational studies, registries, postmarketing safety and effectiveness studies, pragmatic studies and long-term follow-up. Working with Business Development, Medical, Epidemiology, Biostatistics and other functional leaders, the Director translates evidence needs into feasible study plans, budgets and delivery commitments. The role is accountable for customer satisfaction, study and portfolio performance, and the development of assigned teams.

Strategy and customer engagement

Lead strategy for assigned RWLP opportunities, aligning customer evidence needs with study design, data availability, country requirements, operational feasibility and budget.
Lead proposal development and writing and bid defense preparation, including delivery models, country and site strategy, staffing, assumptions, timelines, budgets and risk mitigation. Coach team members to present their expertise and proposed solutions clearly.
Partner with Business Development and account leaders to develop customer relationships, identify follow-on opportunities and demonstrate RWLP capabilities through credible delivery commitments.
Ensure an effective transition from proposal to delivery, with clear ownership of commitments, assumptions, scope, resources and customer expectations.

RWLP study design and delivery

Apply working knowledge of interventional and non-interventional study designs, including cohort, case-control and cross-sectional studies; prospective and retrospective registries; chart reviews; pragmatic trials; postmarketing studies; and extension or long-term follow-up programs.
Partner with Epidemiology, Biostatistics and Medical to assess whether proposed populations, endpoints, follow-up schedules and data sources can answer the study objectives. Translate scientific recommendations into operational plans without substituting for specialist scientific accountability.
Assess delivery options using primary data collection, secondary data sources or a combination of both, including electronic health records, claims and existing registries. Identify data access, completeness, linkage, consent and site-workflow requirements with the relevant specialists.
Oversee feasibility, country and site selection, startup, recruitment, retention, monitoring, data collection and closeout. Adapt delivery to routine care and site capabilities while meeting protocol and applicable quality requirements.
Ensure monitoring and oversight are proportionate to study design, data risks and applicable requirements. Coordinate safety reporting, vendor oversight and event adjudication where required by the protocol.
Oversee assigned studies and portfolios against scope, timeline, quality and financial commitments. Review performance trends, resolve escalations and lead recovery plans with clear owners and deadlines.

Operational leadership and people management

Lead portfolio reviews and governance discussions; identify recurring delivery issues, capacity constraints and opportunities to improve execution across studies.
Partner with functional and resource leaders to forecast demand, allocate staff and balance workload, skills, continuity and cost across the assigned portfolio.
Provide line management for designated employees where assigned, including recruitment, onboarding, objective setting, coaching, performance reviews, development planning and succession planning.
Assess employee readiness for assigned responsibilities, identify training needs and oversee project handovers and role transitions. Address performance concerns with HR and the appropriate functional leaders.
Develop project leaders and cross-functional teams, clarify accountability and promote consistent delivery practices. Maintain defined decision rights with the ODL and functional leadership under the approved operating model.

Financial performance, quality and compliance

Own financial oversight for assigned studies and programs, including budget review, forecasting, resource utilization, profitability, scope management and timely change orders. Resolve variances with project teams and Finance.
Apply Good Pharmacoepidemiology Practices (GPP), Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and applicable local requirements according to study classification and activities. Work with Regulatory and Quality to confirm the appropriate framework.
Ensure compliance with company procedures, contractual commitments and applicable customer requirements. Coordinate ethics review, informed consent or approved waivers, privacy and data governance requirements with the responsible functions.
Maintain oversight of quality risks, deviations and corrective and preventive actions; support audit and inspection readiness and timely resolution of findings.
Use delivery metrics, customer feedback and lessons learned to improve RWLP processes, proposal assumptions, budget models and execution.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in life sciences, nursing, public health, epidemiology or a related discipline, or equivalent education and related experience. An advanced relevant degree is preferred.
Extensive relevant research experience within a CRO, pharmaceutical, biotechnology or comparable research organization, including demonstrated leadership of RWLP programs. Direct experience delivering both non-interventional and interventional late-phase studies is required.
Demonstrated understanding of observational and interventional study designs, routine-care research, primary and secondary data collection, and their operational implications.
Working knowledge of GPP, GCP and applicable global and local requirements for late-phase and non-interventional research, with the ability to apply the appropriate framework with specialist support.
Proven experience leading proposals, bid defenses and senior customer discussions, and translating evidence objectives into feasible, appropriately costed delivery plans.
Demonstrated portfolio or multi-study oversight, operational problem-solving, financial forecasting, resource planning and scope management.
Experience developing staff and leading cross-functional teams. Direct people-management experience is required where the role includes line-management accountability.
Ability to work effectively with Medical, Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Regulatory, Safety, Data Management and technology partners; sufficient therapeutic-area knowledge to lead credible customer discussions and identify when specialist input is needed.
Strong communication, presentation, negotiation and decision-making skills; ability to manage competing priorities and resolve issues with senior stakeholders.
Proficiency in core business and project-management tools; fluency in English; willingness to travel approximately 25%, consistent with business needs.

Critical Skills

RWLP strategy and delivery; study-design literacy; customer engagement; bid defense leadership; portfolio oversight; people development; resource planning; financial management; risk-based quality oversight; cross-functional decision-making.

US Experience Requirements

At least eight years of relevant research experience, including at least seven years managing studies, with demonstrated experience leading RWLP programs across interventional and non-interventional research.

jobs.title: Director, Patient Access & Channel Strategy
jobs.description:
Aperçu

Build the connections that bring innovation to patients.

Scientific progress creates possibilities. Helping patients access treatment takes people who can connect the dots—between support programs, reimbursement, pharmacies and the partners who deliver medicines.

At Incyte Canada, we are looking for an Associate Director / Director, Patient Access & Channel Strategy to strengthen those connections across oncology, hematology, immunology and dermatology. As our portfolio evolves and we prepare for upcoming launches, you will shape how patients access our therapies, building the programs, partnerships and capabilities to support them.

Patient Support Programs will be at the heart of your mandate. You will lead their strategy and delivery, strengthen our distribution partnerships and develop our pharmacy and channel approach. Working closely with colleagues across Market Access, Medical, Finance and Legal, you will turn complex challenges into practical solutions, combining strategic vision with the willingness to get into the detail and make things work.

We are looking for a builder, a thoughtful negotiator and a relationship leader. Someone who brings structure to ambiguity, earns trust across a complex healthcare ecosystem and takes ownership from strategy through execution.

An opportunity to shape a critical capability for Incyte Canada, and help patients access the innovation we work to deliver.

The Associate Director/Director, Patient Access & Channel Strategy is responsible for the strategic leadership, development, and execution of best-in-class Patient Support Programs (PSPs), trade relations, supply chain, and pharmacy/channel strategy supporting Incyte Canada's oncology/hematology and immunology/dermatology portfolio.

This role oversees a complex ecosystem of PSPs, vendors, wholesalers, distribution partners, pharmacies, and Group Purchasing Organizations (GPOs), ensuring seamless patient access to innovative therapies. The incumbent serves as the primary point of contact for Supply Chain within Canada, acts as the Quality Assurance (QA) Ambassador for the affiliate, and represents the organization externally with the Health Products Stewardship Association (HPSA).

In addition, the incumbent holds accountability for budget oversight and financial governance across PSP, trade, and channel-related activities. Working cross-functionally with Government Affairs, HEOR/Reimbursement Strategy, Private Insurance, Medical, Legal, Finance, and other key stakeholders, the incumbent drives operational excellence, compliance, and continuous improvement while delivering patient-centric solutions at scale.

Reporting to the Senior Director, Market Access & Government Affairs, this position will be filled at the Associate Director or Director level depending on the successful candidate's experience and demonstrated readiness for the full scope of commercial, pharmacy, and GPO responsibilities described below.

Essential Functions Of The Job (Key Responsibilities)

Patient Support Program Leadership (Primary Focus)
Own PSP strategy, performance, and day-to-day program integrity across the oncology/hematology and immunology/dermatology portfolios
Scale and adapt PSPs ahead of anticipated public reimbursement wins and upcoming launches
Set and monitor KPIs for program effectiveness, patient outcomes, and vendor performance; lead vendor selection, onboarding, and governance
Act as Incyte Canada’s internal Quality Assurance (QA) Ambassador for PSP operations — overseeing SOP adherence, supporting inspection readiness, and championing continuous improvement across vendor-delivered programs

Channel Strategy & Innovation

Build a multi-year channel and PSP strategy roadmap aligned to portfolio evolution
Continue to assess and refine the foundational infrastructure (governance, SOPs, vendor framework, KPIs)
Develop and maintain the business case for additional headcount and/or ongoing vendor support as scope is validated; lead hiring/onboarding as resources are approved

Cross-Functional Integration

Partner with Government Affairs, HEOR/Reimbursement Strategy, and the Private Insurance lead to ensure channel, trade, and pharmacy strategy reflects and reinforces active pCPA negotiations, CDA-AMC/INESSS outcomes, and payer strategy
Partner with Medical for Real World Evidence (RWE) generation
Provide a channel/trade lens into pricing and contracting strategy for both in-line and pipeline assets

Financial & Vendor Governance

Own PSP, trade, and channel-related budgets; manage forecasts, variance, and ROI reporting in partnership with Finance
Ensure cost-effective, compliant vendor management across PSP, trade, and GPO/pharmacy relationships, including short-term external vendor/agency engagements where internal capacity is still being built
Trade Relations & Supply Chain (Outsourced Vendor Management)
Own wholesaler and distribution partner relationships and commercial agreements
Negotiate and renew trade terms, ensuring uninterrupted product flow for publicly reimbursed, privately reimbursed, and pCPA-negotiated brands
Serve as the primary point of contact for Supply Chain in Canada; oversee 3PL operations, forecasting, and distribution planning
Where internal capacity is constrained, engage and manage external vendors/agencies to maintain trade and supply chain continuity
Serve as Incyte Canada’s liaison to the Health Products Stewardship Association (HPSA), ensuring compliance with environmental stewardship and product-return obligations tied to the wholesaler and distribution network
Pharmacy Strategy & Group Purchasing Organizations (As Strategic Build-Out)
Develop and execute Incyte Canada's pharmacy channel strategy across retail, specialty, and hospital pharmacy
Build and manage relationships with relevant GPOs and hospital shared-services organizations, prioritized around hospital-administered/infused oncology products and pipeline
Lead GPO and hospital contract negotiations in partnership with Legal and Finance, ensuring alignment with PMPRB pricing rules, the Competition Act, and Incyte's compliance framework
Assess buy-and-bill vs. PSP-mediated distribution models for infused and hospital-administered assets as they approach launch
Coordinate with the Private Insurance lead where pharmacy/specialty network strategy intersects with private payer plan design

Qualifications (Education, Experience & Competencies)

Education & Experience

Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences, Business, or related field; advanced degree an asset
Significant pharmaceutical/biotech experience leading Patient Support Programs at scale
Experience in trade relations, wholesaler management, and Canadian pharmaceutical distribution/supply chain
Experience with pharmacy channel strategy and/or GPO negotiation strongly preferred, ideally including hospital-administered or infused specialty products and buy-and-bill models
Working knowledge of Canadian public (CDA-AMC, INESSS, pCPA, PMPRB) and private reimbursement frameworks
Experience managing external vendors/agencies as an extension of a lean internal team; prior people-leadership experience, or demonstrated readiness to build and lead a team, considered an asset

Core Competencies

Program management rigor, particularly for PSP operations at scale
Commercial negotiation skill, with wholesalers, GPO/hospital counterparts, and vendors
Ability to operate with significant ambiguity, sequence competing priorities, and build structure from a limited existing foundation
Vendor and cross-functional stakeholder management, including managing agency/vendor resources as short-term capacity
Compliance and risk-awareness in a regulated, PMPRB-governed pricing environment
Collaborative mindset — able to identify and act on synergies with adjacent Market Access functions (e.g., Private Insurance)

Additional Requirements

Bilingualism (French and English) considered an asset.

Disclaimer

The above statements describe the general nature and level of work performed and are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, or skills required. Management reserves the right to modify the role as needed.

Résumé du poste (fonction principale)

Le/la directeur(trice) associé(e)/directeur(trice), Accès aux patients et stratégie des canaux, est responsable de la direction stratégique, du développement et de la mise en œuvre de programmes de soutien aux patients (PSP), de relations commerciales, de chaîne d’approvisionnement et de stratégies pharmaceutiques et de canaux de distribution de premier ordre, soutenant le portefeuille d’oncologie/hématologie et d’immunologie/dermatologie d’Incyte Canada.

Ce poste supervise un écosystème complexe comprenant des PSP, des fournisseurs, des grossistes, des partenaires de distribution, des pharmacies et des organismes d’achats groupés (GPO), afin d’assurer un accès fluide des patients aux thérapies innovantes. Le titulaire agit à titre de principal point de contact pour la chaîne d’approvisionnement au Canada, assume le rôle d’ambassadeur de l’assurance qualité (AQ) pour la filiale et représente l’organisation à l’externe auprès de la Health Products Stewardship Association (HPSA).

De plus, le titulaire est responsable de la supervision budgétaire et de la gouvernance financière des activités liées aux PSP, aux relations commerciales et aux canaux de distribution. En collaboration étroite avec les équipes des Affaires gouvernementales, de l’HEOR/Stratégie de remboursement, de l’Assurance privée, des Affaires médicales, des Affaires juridiques, des Finances et d’autres parties prenantes clés, il favorise l’excellence opérationnelle, la conformité réglementaire et l’amélioration continue tout en offrant des solutions axées sur les patients à grande échelle.

Fonctions essentielles du poste (principales responsabilités)

jobs.description:
The AVP, Delivery Excellence & Transformation sets the strategy for how Technology plans, resources and delivers work, bringing together program and project management, Agile practices and AI-enabled transformation to improve predictability and business outcomes. The role aligns quarterly delivery planning with enterprise planning, funding and governance. Accountabilities span development of delivery leaders and professionals, and ownership of delivery platforms, workforce planning, internal and external resource allocation, and strategic staffing and delivery partnerships.

The AVP leads enterprise-wide delivery transformation, defining and implementing an AI-enabled delivery model that simplifies processes, redefines roles and controls, and embeds new ways of working. The mandate is to remove unnecessary complexity and deliver measurable business outcomes through effective AI adoption.

What You Will Do

Lead program and project management, Scrum Master and Agile Coaching practices, setting standards and driving continuous improvement across traditional and Agile delivery.
Develop delivery leaders and professionals through career pathways, coaching and practical AI skills.
Align quarterly delivery planning, including PI Planning and Big Room Planning, with enterprise priorities, funding and governance; partner with platform leaders to address dependencies, readiness gaps and prioritization decisions. Partner with business, technology and corporate leaders to clarify accountabilities and align delivery practices with enterprise requirements.
Lead enterprise-wide adoption of the AI-enabled delivery model, challenging established practices, eliminating low-value work and simplifying processes, roles and controls; build commitment to change and align adoption with enterprise standards.
Own delivery tools for project and resource tracking, ensuring reliable data and integrated, automated reporting.
Establish delivery performance measures and validate AI benefits against baselines, using evidence to guide improvement and investment decisions.
Own Technology workforce planning, talent intake and internal and external resource allocation, aligning skills and capacity with funded demand.
Manage Engineering operating expense forecasts and savings commitments, translating realized productivity gains into workforce and sourcing decisions.
Manage strategic staffing and delivery partnerships, setting contractual expectations for quality, productivity, AI adoption and security; work with Procurement, Legal and Architecture on commercial terms and remediation.
Challenge the status quo, remove unnecessary complexity and focus on outcomes over process.
Develop people, build commitment to change and lead effective AI adoption.
Exercise sound financial judgment and hold teams and partners accountable for measurable business results.

What You Will Bring

Experience leading Program and Project Management and Agile delivery practices in a complex enterprise, developing leaders and professionals, and driving continuous improvement across traditional and Agile approaches.
Expertise in enterprise and quarterly delivery planning, including aligning priorities, funding, capacity and dependencies; sound judgment in applying project management, SAFe, Scrum and Lean practices to business needs.
Demonstrated success redesigning processes, roles and controls through AI and automation, with practical knowledge of generative and agentic AI adoption and evidence of measurable benefits beyond tool deployment.
Strong workforce planning, resource allocation and financial acumen, including operating expense forecasting, savings realization and management of internal and external technology capacity.
Experience managing strategic technology staffing and delivery partnerships, including sourcing, commercial negotiations, contractual expectations and partner performance.
Experience owning delivery-platform requirements and adoption, establishing reliable data and performance measures, and validating productivity and delivery improvements against baselines.
Proven experience leading enterprise-wide transformation, with strong executive communication and cross-functional influence to build commitment, navigate resistance and sustain adoption. A change-oriented mindset and strong bias for simplifying complexity, challenging the status quo and delivering measurable business outcomes.

At Baycrest Hospital, older adults receive specialized post-acute inpatient care informed by deep expertise in aging and brain health, delivered with compassion and clinical excellence.

The Finance Department provides financial planning, accounting, financial reporting, budgeting support, regulatory reporting, treasury, and financial management services in support of Baycrest Hospital operations. Reporting to the Vice President, Finance and CFO, the Director, Financial Accounting and Systems Integration works as a partner with the Director, Finance and provides leadership for Baycrest Hospital's financial accounting, reporting, compliance, and financial systems functions.

The Director is responsible for ensuring the integrity, accuracy, and timeliness of financial information through the effective management of accounting operations, financial reporting, accounts payable, accounts receivable, capital accounting, internal controls, regulatory reporting, audit coordination, and compliance activities.

The Director serves as the Finance lead for major technology, systems, and business transformation initiatives impacting financial operations, reporting, controls, data management, and decision support capabilities. Working collaboratively with Information Technology, Human Resources, Payroll, Decision Support, operational leaders, project teams, and external partners, the Director ensures Finance requirements are appropriately incorporated into the planning, design, implementation, integration, testing, and optimization of enterprise systems and related business processes.

The Director works collaboratively with Payroll and Human Resources to support the integrity, governance, integration, reconciliation, reporting, and analysis of workforce-related financial and operational data.

MIS Submissions

Monitors data quality, reporting integrity, and compliance with reporting standards and recommends corrective actions as required.

Leads annual external audit activities and serves as the primary liaison with auditors for assigned hospital operations and reporting areas.
Coordinates audit requests and ensures timely completion of audit schedules, supporting documentation, analyses, recommendations, and action plans.
Identifies financial, operational, reporting, compliance, and system-related risks and develops mitigation strategies where appropriate.
Supports organizational risk management initiatives through strong financial oversight, governance, and accountability practices.

Identifies opportunities to improve financial processes, compliance activities, reporting capabilities, systems functionality, internal controls, and operational effectiveness.

jobs.description:
Our client is a long-established, privately held organization operating a multi-site, customer-focused business across retail, wholesale, distribution, logistics and related services. The company has grown significantly and built a strong reputation through operational excellence, long-term relationships and a commitment to continuous improvement. Its culture is highly collaborative, performance-oriented and grounded in servant leadership, with leaders expected to be accountable, approachable and engaged while fostering an environment focused on teamwork, accountability and results.

Reporting to the President and Chief Executive Officer, the Vice President, Finance leads the organization’s Finance and People & Culture functions and serves as a key member of the senior leadership team. This is a highly operational leadership role for a finance executive who takes an active interest in how the business runs and enjoys working directly with leaders and teams across the organization. Leading accounting, financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, data analysis, credit, cash flow, working capital and financial controls, the Vice President will provide timely and meaningful insight into performance. The role’s financial responsibilities also extend to a related property business that owns most of the organization’s operating locations, together with a small portfolio of other commercial properties.

Working closely with ownership and business leaders, the Vice President will strengthen visibility into sales, margins, expenses, inventory and profitability; enhance planning, reporting and decision support; and help drive greater consistency across financial processes, systems and controls. By engaging directly with the business and developing a firsthand understanding of operational challenges, the Vice President will help translate financial and operational insight into practical improvements in performance.

A key priority will be supporting the continued adoption and optimization of a recently implemented enterprise system, improving the quality and accessibility of financial and operational data, and helping business leaders leverage analytics to make better decisions. The successful candidate will also bring an active interest in artificial intelligence and a commitment to ongoing learning, working with leaders across the organization to identify practical applications that improve productivity, decision-making and business performance.

In addition to leading Finance, the Vice President will provide executive oversight to the People & Culture function. Working closely with the Senior Director, People & Culture, this leader will help ensure the organization’s talent, leadership and organizational capabilities support its strategic and operational priorities. The Vice President will strengthen a capable, service-oriented team across both functions while building the processes and discipline necessary to support future growth.

The ideal candidate is a finance leader with demonstrated success leading accounting and finance functions in a complex, customer-focused business. Experience in retail, wholesale distribution or another operationally complex, inventory-intensive environment would be highly relevant. Collaborative, humble, credible and highly hands-on, this servant leader will be equally comfortable rolling up their sleeves to work through complex issues as they are coaching and developing others. They will bring strong business judgment, intellectual curiosity and a practical problem-solving approach, with the ability to identify root causes, navigate ambiguity and translate analysis into action. Experience with ERP system optimization and enhanced reporting through data analytics will be highly valued.

Based in Metro Vancouver, this is an exceptional opportunity to make a meaningful impact within a respected privately held organization. Working closely with ownership, senior leadership and teams across the business, the successful candidate will build on a solid foundation and help position the company for continued success.

At Sun Life, we're driven by our Purpose: helping our Clients achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. Our values shape how we work: caring, authentic, bold, inspiring, and impactful.  



  

When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.  



  

Discover how you can make a difference in the lives of individuals, families and communities around the world.  



  

**Job Description:**

**Role Summary**

  

You will represent the Security Architecture team across our enterprise architecture and technology community, shaping how security is designed into everything we build including the AI systems now reaching production.  



  

This is a senior, influence\-led role. You will prioritise the strategic concepts and capability sets that matter most, align security to the architecture process and the NIST framework, and advance technology modernisation and defense\-in\-depth across multiple clouds and on Prem.  



  

You will set direction for a substantial security technology stack including: cloud security posture and workload protection, endpoint detection and response, SIEM, secrets and privileged access management, data protection, application security and perimeter defense and make strategic decisions on the future of the technology stack  



  

**What will you do?**

  

* Partner with global domain architects to review enterprise architecture patterns and guardrails, ensuring security is designed in rather than retrofitted.
* Evaluate and recommend emerging technologies, providing technical and thought leadership through proofs of concept and business cases that demonstrate value.
* Represent security technology and capability strategy at senior executive forums and enterprise technology review boards.
* Provide architecture and design expertise on enterprise projects and security initiatives, including cross\-domain functions, and certify domains in line with architecture governance.
* Lead the strategic evolution of security capabilities with a zero\-trust\-first approach, working alongside delivery teams.
* Define the security architecture for AI adoption covering AI and agentic systems, the data that feeds them, and the platforms that host them. This includes model and agent governance, AI security posture management, data\-classification controls for training and inference, guardrails against prompt injection and model misuse, and secure\-by\-design patterns for AI\-enabled products.
* Set a modernised approach to security tooling, services and capability sets, focused on technical feasibility across emerging technologies, controls and functions.
Drive multi\-cloud consistency, ensuring controls, telemetry and posture management extend uniformly across all cloud providers rather than clustering around the best\-covered one.  
* 

  

**What will you need to succeed?**

  

**Experience**
--------------

* Minimum 7–10 years in information security architecture, engineering and design.
* Proven ability to navigate complex organisations across the security, network, infrastructure and global architecture stack.
* Proven experience migrating and upgrading core security technologies as part of an evolving security and infrastructure stack, including API security, web filtering, cloud security, email security and endpoint security.
Experience managing third\-party security service providers in delivering security services.  
* 

  

**Technical depth**
-------------------

* Strong knowledge of core security domains: endpoint, cloud, infrastructure, perimeter and data protection.
* Multi\-cloud security architecture across at least two major providers, with an appreciation of how native controls and third\-party platforms differ in coverage.
* Working knowledge of the modern security toolset CNAPP/CSPM, EDR/XDR, SIEM, secrets management, privileged access management, SSE/CASB, WAF and perimeter protection, database activity monitoring, and SAST/SCA/DAST in the pipeline.
* AI security: familiarity with AI and LLM threat models (such as the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications), AI governance frameworks (such as the NIST AI Risk Management Framework), AI security posture management, model and agent identity, and the data\-security implications of AI adoption.
Pragmatic understanding of security problems as a mix of technology and process, with the ability to pursue solutions at multiple levels throughout the organisation.  
* 

  

**Leadership and communication**
--------------------------------

* Expert presentation and communication skills, written and verbal.
* People leadership experience preferred, including the ability to engage, mentor, coach and develop.
* Extensive knowledge of information security principles, best practices and industry standards.
Self\-starter, strategic thinker, negotiator and consensus builder.  
* 

**Education**

* University degree/college diploma in related discipline(s) or equivalent co\-op work experience,
Professional designation in IT security (such as CISM, CISSP, CISA) preferred

jobs.description:
JOB TITLE:
Director, Finance and Business Intelligence
STATUS:
Permanent, Full Time
LOCATION:
Home Office Based
Candidates are required to reside in the province of Ontario or National Capital Region, maintain a private and safe workspace, and have a high-quality internet connection.
HOURS OF WORK:
35 hours/week (regular office hours)
GRADE:
Grade 11
The hiring range for this position ranges from $166,261.26 to $182,887.39, with the opportunity to grow within the broader salary range as you advance in your role.

About Us

Workplace Safety & Prevention Services (WSPS) is a not-for-profit organization committed to protecting Ontario’s workers and businesses. It serves more than 174,000 member firms and 4.2 million workers across the agricultural, manufacturing and service sectors. A proud partner in the province’s occupational health and safety system and a trusted safety advisor since 1917, WSPS has a rich history of making workplaces safer.

Our focus on healthy workplaces extends to our own strong safety culture. We’re committed to helping employees thrive in a remote-first world, and we’re honoured to be recognized as a Great Place to Work for two consecutive years for 2024 and 2025.

Why Work with WSPS

As a member of our team, you'll benefit from a compensation package aimed at keeping you happy, healthy, motivated and safe. Highlights include:
Make a meaningful impact by supporting our mission to protect Ontario’s workers and businesses
35-hour work week
Flexible working arrangements within the province of Ontario
Comprehensive life and health benefits (100% company paid Health & Dental)
Defined Benefit Pension Plan
Generous vacation and leave entitlements (including paid time off over Christmas and New Year's, paid parental leave benefits)
Internet allowance
And more!

Role

Reporting to the CFO and Vice President, Corporate Services, this position is responsible for the strategic planning, leadership and oversight of the Finance, Accounting and Business Intelligence functions. The Director, Finance and Business Intelligence will work as a member of the Senior Leadership Team (SLT) to support the achievement of the WSPS strategic plan. As future focused leader, this role plays an integral part in formulating best practices and process improvements while leveraging technology and tools for financial planning, accounting services, financial and business reporting.

Responsibilities

Note: Percentages refer to approximate % of time spent on each area, over the course of a given year.
1. TEAM LEADERSHIP, DEVELOPMENT AND ADMINISTRATION (20%)

Provide leadership to Finance, Accounting and Business Intelligence managers. Guide and coach team members to effectively perform and achieve objectives.
Ensure the development of a highly skilled, knowledgeable, and motivated workforce in the team.
Ensure team structures, positions and skills are appropriate for delivery of the team’s and organization’s mandate.
Provide the necessary training, resources, and support to ensure that team members are continually developing and enhancing their capabilities.
Evaluate and lead the team through succession planning to ensure continuity in roles.
Review and analyze engagement results with a focus on solutions to increase employee engagement in satisfaction in the department. Assure strong employee engagement/satisfaction results in the department.
Collaborate with the team to ensure clear understanding and alignment related to changes within the organization.
Reinforces the WSPS vision and employees’ connection to that vision.
Lead multi-disciplinary project teams as needed.
Upholds and promotes ethical standards, integrity, and a strong sense of corporate responsibility as per WSPS policies and procedures.

2. RELATIONSHIP BUILDING (20%)

Develop strong customer and stakeholder relationships with all divisions/business units in the organization to support financial management, business intelligence processes, and continuous improvement efforts at WSPS.
Act as a liaison between WSPS and the Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development (MLITSD), representing WSPS’ interests while developing collaborative and effective relationships.

3. LEADERSHIP OF ACCOUNTING SERVICE DELIVERY (20%)

Lead the team responsible for the design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of internal controls to safeguard the assets of WSPS and to mitigate business risks.
Review existing/new/proposed accounting policies to assess adherence to GAAP and well as consider operational impacts.
Oversee the preparation of monthly, quarterly and annual internal and Board of Director financial statements, as well as preparation of annual external financial statements, ensuring the format and disclosure within statements are effective for decision-making, while adhering to GAAP requirements.
Identify areas for improvement in current systems required to comply with TPA reporting requirements and partner with appropriate functional areas to implement improvements.
Participate in TPA audit relating to both financial information provided to the Ministry and reporting of performance indicators.
Ensure effectiveness and efficiency of internal monitoring processes that assess accounting transactions for validity, completeness, accuracy and adherence to all government directives and WSPS policies to minimize risk of loss.
Ensure procurement policies and procedures comply with government directives.
Ensure consistent training and advice on procurement activities are communicated across the organization, including monitoring of emerging requirements as mandated by government for implementation and compliance.
Act as liaison with government agencies on procurement reporting requirements.
Participate in the design and management of an investment strategy to achieve strategic and financial goals of WSPS, including meeting cash flow requirements, while adhering to parameters set by government directives and internal policies.

4. LEADERSHIP OF BUDGETING, FINANCIAL REPORTING AND AUDIT PROCESS (20%)

Ensure the implementation of an accurate, efficient, and timely annual budget process and provide leadership to the organization in the preparation of an annual budget that adheres to ministry requirements.
Serve as liaison between WSPS and the Ministry for financial planning and Transfer Payment Agreement (TPA) reporting related matters.
Provide guidance to the executive and senior leadership teams during the budgeting process to achieve a balanced budget.
Ensure the implementation of an accurate, efficient, and timely forecasting process, including reporting to senior management in support of effective decision-making.
Oversee the preparation of forecast and spending reports, ensuring they are effective in communicating the organization’s financial position, highlighting any areas of risk, and recommending mitigation strategies.
Provide advice and develop recommendations on financial management practices across the organization.
Oversee monthly and quarterly variance analysis and develop recommendations for achieving a balanced budget at year-end.
Oversee analysis and develop recommendations on sales, contribution margins and pricing strategies.
Lead development of Ministry reporting packages, including annual business plan and quarterly reports, ensuring they meet all requirements.
Work closely with the external actuary in the annual employee future benefits valuation process to ensure accurate data is reflected in the valuation results and the reports are available for year-end audit and budgeting purposes.
Oversee the team leading the audit preparation process to ensure audit process and procedures performed are effective and efficient and to identify areas where documents/procedures can be updated to facilitate a more efficient audit process.
At year end audit, ensure appropriate documentation/supporting documents are available for auditor’s review and act as liaison between auditor and other WSPS departments where ownership of supporting information/documents does not lie within Corporate Services.
Stay current on financial standards for Not-for-Profit Organizations to ensure financial record systems are maintained in accordance with the Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), as well as the designated standards of the government bodies.

5. LEADERSHIP OF BUSINESS INTELLIGENCE (20%)

Oversee the collection, synthesis and analysis of data and metrics to inform senior management decision making, priority setting and investment strategies.
Regularly assess processes and systems used for the collection, synthesis, and analysis of data to promote effectiveness and efficiency.
Oversee the preparation of ministry reports ensuring all requirements are met, highlighting areas of potential under performance, and developing recommendations to address.
Oversee development of reporting tools, including dashboards and scorecards, that provide useful and timely information for decision making, as well as measure and report on the impact and value of WSPS activities.
Report on key performance metrics that show progress WSPS’ strategy and mandate and communicate the results across WSPS.
Oversee development and application of a WSPS framework for acquiring business intelligence on the market, industry, and our customers, to inform decision-making and business planning. Framework includes quantitative measurements, customer feedback and environmental scans.
Develop and promote tools and best practices for project management with a view to develop competencies across the organization.
Oversee project management professionals to ensure effective support of enterprise-wide or high priority projects to ensure effective, timely and efficient implementation.

5. CONTRIBUTES TO A HEALTHY AND SAFE WORK ENVIRONMENT (at all times)

Adhere to WSPS policies, procedures, process fact sheets, guidelines, and business rules.
Contribute to the promotion of a healthy & safe culture through modelling and following WSPS health, safety and wellness policies and practices.
Act as a role model internally and externally by demonstrating knowledge of health and safety and wellness practices, weighing options for sound risk management decision making.

Skills & Experience

Minimum

Bachelor’s degree in business or related field, or minimum of 5 years of related experience in financial management.
Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) Designation
5-7 years progressive management experience with emphasis on financial planning and reporting, exposure to senior management decision making, developing talent, and managing budgets.
Experience leading across multiple teams to deliver service excellence.
Excellent collaboration skills to effectively engage with internal and external stakeholders.
Excellent oral and written communication, including ability to present complex concepts in simple business-oriented terms.

Preferred

10+ years progressive management experience in a not-for-profit environment
Experience leading positive change and seeking out continuous improvement.
Understanding Transfer Payment Agreement model and requirements
This position requires frequent travel within the Mississauga area and thus it is preferred that candidates live within 75km of WSPS’ Mississauga Head Office.

Additional Requirements

Candidates are required to reside in the province of Ontario (or National Capital Region), maintain a private and safe workspace, and have a high-quality internet connection.
Provide an original criminal background check at your own expense prior to commencing work with WSPS. The criminal record check document must have been issued no more than 30 days prior to first day of employment.
To support success in building connections, inclusion and collaboration, a minimum level of in person presence for the purposes of meetings is required for all team members as of July 2026:
Divisional Meetings on a quarterly basis.
Team Meetings on a month

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
About UJA Federation Of Greater Toronto

At UJA Federation of Greater Toronto, our vision is to lead the most vibrant Jewish community in North America — a community characterized by its diversity, unity, compassion, generosity and commitment to Jewish values. Together with our philanthropic, volunteer and professional leadership, we're changing lives.

As one of North America's leading Jewish non-profits, UJA Federation of Greater Toronto works to preserve and strengthen the quality of Jewish life in Greater Toronto, Canada, Israel and around the world. UJA advances this mission through fundraising, planning, and research focused on our strategic pillars: fighting poverty and improving well-being, growing Jewish education and identity, countering antisemitism and hate, and strengthening connections with Israel and Jewish communities worldwide.

About The Opportunity

At a pivotal time for UJA Federation of Greater Toronto, the Chief Financial Officer serves as a strategic partner to the President & CEO, Chief Operating Officer, Board, and senior leadership team. Building on a stable financial foundation and a capable finance team, the CFO is responsible for advancing finance into a forward-looking enterprise function focused on planning, resource allocation, decision support, organizational performance, and long-term financial sustainability. Initially, the CFO will work closely with the existing team to understand how work is currently performed, strengthen accountability and capability, and create the foundation for a more scalable and strategic finance function. The role exists to ensure that financial insight, forecasting, scenario analysis, performance measurement, and resource allocation effectively support organizational priorities and decision-making. The CFO will develop trusted relationships across professional leadership, Board and committee members, lay leaders, donors, partner agencies, and other key stakeholders, while leading improvements in analytics, systems, data, and processes that strengthen organizational effectiveness and scalability. Success in this role will depend on sound judgment, strong relationships, and the ability to build alignment across a complex stakeholder environment.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Lead the Finance function across UJA entities and operating activities, with accountability for financial stewardship, planning, reporting, controls and team performance.
Own and lead the annual budget process and strengthen multi-year planning, forecasting and scenario analysis, aligning financial plans with strategic priorities.
Lead resource allocation, reserve strategy and long-term sustainability planning, helping leadership assess competing priorities and strengthen UJA's financial resilience.
Oversee investments and organizational assets, working with relevant Board committees and advisors to ensure sound governance, risk management and long-term stewardship.
Lead financial reporting and discussions with the Board and relevant committees, providing clear context, insight and recommendations to support decision-making.
Oversee the annual audit, internal controls, governance and compliance with internal requirements and external obligations, including CRA requirements.
Ensure financial or other risks are appropriately identified, understood and addressed.
Lead, mentor and develop the finance team, establishing clear accountabilities, succession depth and a culture of ownership and continuous improvement.
Champion systems, data and process improvements and strengthen financial acumen across the organization.

Qualifications:

CPA designation.
Senior financial leadership experience, ideally as a CFO or equivalent, within a complex organization with multiple stakeholders and competing priorities.
Demonstrated success as a strategic partner to a CEO, senior leadership team and Board, with the judgment to influence effectively without relying solely on formal authority.
Proven ability to succeed in a consensus-driven environment and build alignment across stakeholders with differing perspectives and priorities.
Board experience is highly valued, particularly with philanthropic or community organizations that combine fundraising with meaningful operating activities.
Track record of developing high-performance finance teams, developing leaders and leading thoughtful organizational change without creating unnecessary disruption.
Strong governance, investment oversight, risk and analytical capabilities, with the ability to translate financial information into clear implications and choices for non-financial stakeholders.
Strategic in orientation while sufficiently hands-on to understand the function, people and processes during a period of transition and evolution.
Passion for UJA’s mission and an appreciation for the complexity of serving a broad and highly engaged community.

jobs.title: Interim Director, Financial Planning & Analysis
jobs.description:
IMMEDIATE INTERIM OPPORTUNITY

Interim Director, Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A)

Duration: 3 Months

Reports: Chief Financial Officer

Location: Downtown Toronto (Hybrid)

Our client a North American professional services organization with multiple locations is seeking an experienced financial planning & analysis professional to lead a small team through a critical budgeting process. This individual will play a key role in guiding the organization through a complex budgeting and forecasting cycle while bringing greater structure, discipline, and insight to the overall financial planning process.

This is a highly hands-on assignment requiring an individual who is comfortable working directly in the details, partnering closely with operational and finance stakeholders, and supporting a team through a demanding planning period. The successful candidate will be equally comfortable rolling up their sleeves in Excel while providing strategic recommendations on process improvement, automation, and future-state planning capabilities.

Key Mandate

The Interim Director will be responsible for stabilizing, coordinating, and enhancing the organization's budgeting and forecasting processes while identifying opportunities to simplify workflows, improve data quality, and introduce practical technology solutions.

Key Responsibilities

Lead and manage the organization's annual budgeting and forecasting process.
Provide day-to-day leadership, coaching, and support to a team of four FP&A professionals.
Work directly with budget owners and operational leaders to develop, validate, and challenge assumptions.
Consolidate and analyze budget submissions, identifying risks, opportunities, and variances.
Develop financial models and scenario analyses to support decision-making.
Ensure budget timelines, milestones, and deliverables are achieved.
Perform detailed hands-on analysis and modelling within a largely Excel-based environment.
Improve the consistency, accuracy, and transparency of financial reporting and forecasting.
Identify process bottlenecks and inefficiencies within the current budgeting framework.
Recommend practical opportunities for automation, simplification, and technology enablement.
Partner with senior leadership to provide meaningful insights into financial performance and future outlook.
Support the development of a roadmap for a more scalable and sustainable FP&A function.

Desired Experience

10+ years of progressive finance, FP&A, and business planning experience.
Previous experience serving as an Interim Director, FP&A Director, Finance Director, or equivalent senior finance leadership role.
Demonstrated success leading large-scale budgeting and forecasting cycles in complex organizations.
Strong people leadership experience with the ability to motivate and develop teams during periods of change.
Advanced Excel modelling skills and experience working in less structured finance environments.
Proven ability to create structure and discipline in processes that have evolved organically over time.
Experience implementing reporting, planning, or performance management improvements.
Exposure to budgeting and forecasting technologies, FP&A platforms, Power BI, automation tools, or similar solutions is considered an asset.
Strong communication and stakeholder management capabilities.

Ideal Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate is not a pure strategist nor a pure analyst. They are a pragmatic finance leader who can quickly earn credibility, work collaboratively with the existing team, and balance immediate execution with longer-term process improvements.

They bring experience navigating ambiguity, are comfortable operating in Excel-based planning environments, and have a track record of introducing practical innovations that improve efficiency, accuracy, and decision-making without overcomplicating processes.

Expected Outcomes After 90 Days

Successful completion of the budgeting and forecasting cycle.
Improved forecasting accuracy and reporting consistency.
Enhanced structure, accountability, and governance within the planning process.
Increased confidence among stakeholders in financial plans and assumptions.
Identification of practical automation and technology opportunities.
Clear recommendations for future-state FP&A processes and tools to support scalability and improved decision-making.

jobs.title: Director of Information Technology
jobs.description:
POSITION DESCRIPTION

Athletica Sport Systems Inc. is a global leader in the design, manufacturing, and installation of dasher board and arena systems, and the Preferred Rink Equipment Supplier of the NHL® and AHL®. Guided by our philosophy of “Safety through Innovation,” we have completed more than 3,000 projects worldwide from our headquarters in Waterloo, Ontario and operations in Minneapolis, London, and Vancouver.

Athletica is seeking a Director of Information Technology to join our leadership team in Waterloo. Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, this role owns technology, systems, and data across Athletica and its operating entities, supporting daily operations, organic growth, and acquisitions. The successful candidate will build and lead a growing IT team, stay hands-on while it matures, and lead the clean-up and cloud migration of our Epicor ERP, the technology side of a move to a new facility within 18 months of hire, and completion of our Microsoft Dynamics CRM implementation.

Key Responsibilities

Strategy and budget: Translate business strategy into a sequenced technology roadmap with the CFO and leadership team, and manage the IT operating and capital budget, licensing, and vendor contracts.
Team: Staff, structure, and develop the IT team to meet business needs, using skills assessments to set hiring and training priorities and to engage outside partners. Stay hands-on while the team matures.
Epicor improvement: Own Epicor Kinetic end to end. Lead the clean-up and improvement of the existing implementation, including workflows, customizations, reports, and data quality, and standardize setups across entities.
Epicor platform: Keep Epicor current and supported, and lead the planned move from on-premises to Epicor in the cloud.
Epicor expertise: Build and train the IT team toward deep Epicor expertise and act as the conduit to outside specialists, including Six S Partners, reviewing designs, testing deliverables, and approving releases.
Manufacturing modernization: Keep operations on efficient, effective tools. Work with Operations, Engineering, and Projects to implement Epicor capabilities and technology such as barcode scanning, shop floor data collection, and mobile tools, and support Finance, which owns costing, with reliable system data.
Security & controls: Maintain role-based security in Epicor and other core systems, enforce segregation of duties and change management, and support financial controls and audits. Build a practical cybersecurity program covering multifactor authentication, endpoint protection, backup and recovery testing, and incident response.
Microsoft 365 & infrastructure: Own the Microsoft 365 environment and set direction for infrastructure and security, including which workloads stay on-premises and which move to the cloud.
Facility transition: Plan and lead the technology side of the move to the new facility, including network, telephony, shop floor connectivity, and cutover planning that limits disruption to production, installs, and shipping. Lead the expected Microsoft tenant reorganization, and sequence it with the Epicor upgrade and cloud migration.
CRM: Own Microsoft Dynamics CRM. Complete the partial implementation with sales, service, and finance leaders, fix data quality, simplify workflows, and integrate with Epicor and Microsoft 365.
Projects & platforms: Determine what project management capability Epicor and Dynamics already provide before recommending new platforms, and replace ad hoc spreadsheets and email processes with system workflows the business adopts.
Data, reporting & AI: Establish data ownership and standards, and set the reporting approach, including Power BI dashboards for bookings, backlog, margin, labor, capacity, and installs. Lead AI tool use, with Claude as the primary tool and Microsoft Copilot in limited use, within the company AI usage policy, and deploy a few high-value analytics and AI use cases.
M&A integration: Own the systems workstream for acquisitions, from diligence through integration, using a repeatable playbook for data migration, access setup, and process standardization.
Executive partnership: Translate how work happens across the business into system configurations, lead rollouts with training and post-go-live support, and represent technology with the board, banks, investors, and senior leadership.
Other duties as required

POSITION REQUIREMENTS

Education & Certifications:
·      Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
·      Certifications such as PMP, ITIL, CISSP, Microsoft, or Epicor are an asset.

Knowledge, Experience, and/or Technical Skills:
·      10+ years of progressive IT experience, including 5+ years leading an IT team in a manufacturing environment (required).
·      Hands-on experience with Epicor or another full-featured manufacturing ERP, including upgrades and role-based security design (required). Entry-level accounting packages do not qualify.
·      Experience with Epicor Kinetic, including on-premises to cloud migration, is a strong asset.
·      Working knowledge of manufacturing and financial processes, from bills of materials and routings to inventory, work in process, and the general ledger (required).
·      Microsoft 365 administration experience, including a tenant reorganization or migration (required).
·      Working knowledge of Microsoft Dynamics CRM, Power BI, and SQL.
·      Knowledge of IT general controls and cybersecurity practices, with experience supporting financial audits.
·      Experience delivering major technology projects, such as an ERP upgrade or facility move, with limited disruption to operations.
·      Proven ability to lead and develop a junior team, hire for skill gaps, manage vendors, and explain technical matters to business leaders.
·      Experience with multi-entity environments, acquisition integration, and applying AI tools is an asset.

Work Environment, Hours & Travel:
·      This role is based on-site at our Waterloo, Ontario facility, with occasional remote work at the discretion of the Chief Financial Officer.
·      Occasional travel is required to support other business units (Minneapolis, MN; London, ON; Vancouver, BC).
·      Standard full-time office hours, Monday to Friday, with flexibility for after-hours work during upgrades, cutovers, the facility move, and urgent incidents.
·      Some time on the production floor should be expected.

Compensation & Benefits:
·      Annual salary range: $120,000 to $150,000 CAD, commensurate with experience and qualifications.
·      Full-time, permanent position with eligibility to participate in Athletica's benefits program.
·      Opportunity to lead technology modernization at a global market leader.
