jobs.title: Director Data Platform Governance
jobs.description:
Director Data Platform Governance
Toronto, Canada (Hybrid)
Full Time

Position Overview
The Director of Data Platform Governance is responsible for establishing, operating, and continuously improving the Digital Technology governance capabilities that ensure Enterprise Data Platform and related governance tooling ecosystem are controlled, integrated, secure, scalable, traceable, and fit for enterprise use. This includes platform governance standards, certified EDP table usage, metadata, catalog, lineage, data quality monitoring, lifecycle controls, automation, bots, agents, and other tools and services that support governed data creation, certification, publication, and consumption.
The role provides DT leadership for the technical enablement, enterprise integration, architecture and security alignment, platform controls, and operational reliability of this tooling ecosystem. SimpleMDG is a key Data Governance capability sitting on top of SAP, and the Director ensures it is integrated and governed consistently with EDP, SAP, downstream platforms, and other governance-enabling tools across the enterprise technology landscape. The Director also works closely with Technology Architects to ensure proper data flow, lineage, traceability, and integration patterns across the Enterprise Data Platform.
The Director works in close alignment with Business Transformation Data Governance through a shared agenda, agreed priorities, and clear ownership boundaries. Business Transformation Data Governance and business data owners remain accountable for business definitions, semantic layer, approval workflow design, mandatory business rules, reference data certification, stewardship logic, and business adoption, while DT ensures those decisions can be embedded consistently across platforms, workflows, tools, certified data assets, data products, and consumption layers.

Key Responsibilities

1. Enterprise Data Platform Governance and Certified Data Consumption
Establish, operate, and continuously improve DT governance standards for the Enterprise Data Platform, ensuring that data products are created and consumed using certified EDP tables where available.
Define platform-level controls, metadata, lineage, traceability, catalog, and data product governance expectations for EDP assets and consumption layers.
Partner with Business Data Governance and DT delivery teams to embed certified data consumption, lineage, controls, and governance checkpoints into delivery standards and ways of working.
Work with Technology Architects to ensure proper data flow, integration patterns, certified consumption paths, lineage, and traceability across the Enterprise Data Platform.
2. Governance Tooling Ecosystem Enablement
Provide DT leadership for the implementation, integration, controls, security, scalability, and operational reliability of the governance tooling ecosystem, including SimpleMDG, metadata and catalog solutions, lineage tools, data quality monitoring, automation, bots, agents, and related platform services.
Ensure governance tools are connected appropriately across SAP, EDP, downstream platforms, workflows, and consumption layers so that business-approved governance decisions can be executed consistently.
Maintain clear ownership boundaries by enabling business-led configuration decisions while ensuring the technical design, integration, access, auditability, and sustainability of the tools.
3. Master Data Platform Enablement and Enterprise Integration
Support business-led master data governance model by ensuring master data capabilities are technically enabled, integrated, secure, scalable, and aligned with enterprise architecture and data platform standards.
Ensure governed and certified master data can be integrated, exposed, monitored, and consumed appropriately across SAP, SimpleMDG, EDP, downstream enterprise applications, and certified data products.
Maintain lineage, traceability, metadata, issue visibility, platform controls, and certified consumption paths for master data from source systems through EDP and downstream usage.
4. Data Quality Monitoring, Controls, and Issue Visibility
Enable data quality monitoring, profiling, dashboards, scorecards, preventative controls, and issue visibility across EDP and related governance tooling.
Ensure business-defined rules, thresholds, and quality expectations can be technically implemented, measured, and monitored across platforms and consumption layers.
Partner with BT Data Governance, business stewards, Data Product Owners, and DT teams to support root-cause analysis, remediation tracking, and continuous improvement of data quality controls.
5. Metadata, Catalog, Lineage, and Data Intelligence
Establish and operate technical metadata, catalog, lineage, discovery, classification, and transparency capabilities for EDP and related data assets.
Ensure BT-owned business definitions, glossary content, critical data elements, and certification decisions are made visible and usable through platform tools, catalogs, workflows, and data products.
Work with Technology Architects and EDP teams to maintain end-to-end lineage and traceability from source systems through certified EDP tables, data products, and consumption layers.
6. Data Lifecycle, Archiving Governance, Retention, and Platform Compliance Controls
Operate technical lifecycle, data archiving governance, retention, archival, disposition, and compliance controls for EDP and related data platforms in alignment with enterprise policy, legal, regulatory, audit, and information governance requirements.
Ensure enterprise data remains manageable, controlled, compliant, traceable, and cost-efficient throughout its lifecycle, including active use, retention, archiving, and disposition across platform and consumption layers.

Required Qualifications
• Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Business, Supply Chain, or related discipline.
• 12+ years of progressive experience in Data Management, Data Platforms, Master Data Management, or Enterprise Information Management
• 5+ years leading data platform or MDM organizations.
• Strong expertise in SAP Master Data structures and business processes.
• Hands-on experience implementing and operating SAP MDG and/or SimpleMDG.
• Experience leading enterprise data quality initiatives.
• Experience enabling governance operating models and stewardship programs through platform capabilities
• Strong understanding of ERP transformation programs.
• Experience managing enterprise-scale cross-functional initiatives.

Preferred Qualifications
The ideal candidate demonstrates strong expertise in:

• Enterprise Data Platform governance, including certified data assets, governed consumption layers, platform standards, controls, and auditability.
• Data product and certified consumption governance, including ownership visibility, certification practices, guardrails, and governance checkpoints across data products and analytics use cases.
• Metadata, catalog, lineage, and data intelligence capabilities, including traceability, classification, discovery, and transparency across source systems, EDP, data products, and consumption layers.
• Data quality monitoring and control frameworks, including profiling, dashboards, scorecards, preventative controls, issue visibility, and remediation tracking.
• SAP, SimpleMDG/SAP MDG, and master data platform enablement, including integration across SAP, EDP, enterprise applications, analytics platforms, and downstream consumption layers.
• Enterprise integration and lifecycle governance, including source-to-consumption data flows, integration patterns, retention, archiving, compliance, and platform controls.
• Governance-enabling tooling and enterprise transformation, including workflow automation, bots, agents, metadata/catalog tools, lineage tools, data quality platforms, ERP transformation, and enterprise-scale data platform change.
• Critical enterprise data domains and operating models, including supply chain, customer, commercial, and other core data domains, with clear distinction between business-owned governance decisions and DT-owned platform enablement.

The successful candidate will demonstrate:

• Pragmatic execution, solves complex business and data problems and turns governance concepts into measurable results.
• Business process orientation, understands how trusted data supports operational execution, performance, analytics, and decision-making.
• Enterprise mindset, connects platform governance, certified data consumption, and data quality to business outcomes and transformation priorities.
• Influential leadership, builds alignment across Business Transformation, Digital Technology, Data Product Owners, architects, and senior stakeholders.
• Change and adoption focus, drives practical adoption of governance standards, platform controls, tooling, and ways of working.
• Continuous improvement discipline, improves data quality, platform reliability, governance effectiveness, and operational efficiency.

jobs.title: Director, Security Architecture
jobs.description:
You are as unique as your background, experience and point of view. Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered and challenged to be your best self. You'll work with dynamic colleagues - experts in their fields - who are eager to share their knowledge with you. Your leaders will inspire and help you reach your potential and soar to new heights. Every day, you'll have new and exciting opportunities to make life brighter for our Clients - who are at the heart of everything we do.

At Sun Life, we're driven by our Purpose: helping our Clients achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. Our values shape how we work: caring, authentic, bold, inspiring, and impactful.

When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.

Discover how you can make a difference in the lives of individuals, families and communities around the world.

Job Description:

Role Summary

You will represent the Security Architecture team across our enterprise architecture and technology community, shaping how security is designed into everything we build including the AI systems now reaching production.

This is a senior, influence-led role. You will prioritise the strategic concepts and capability sets that matter most, align security to the architecture process and the NIST framework, and advance technology modernisation and defense-in-depth across multiple clouds and on Prem.

You will set direction for a substantial security technology stack including: cloud security posture and workload protection, endpoint detection and response, SIEM, secrets and privileged access management, data protection, application security and perimeter defense and make strategic decisions on the future of the technology stack

What will you do?

Partner with global domain architects to review enterprise architecture patterns and guardrails, ensuring security is designed in rather than retrofitted.
Evaluate and recommend emerging technologies, providing technical and thought leadership through proofs of concept and business cases that demonstrate value.
Represent security technology and capability strategy at senior executive forums and enterprise technology review boards.
Provide architecture and design expertise on enterprise projects and security initiatives, including cross-domain functions, and certify domains in line with architecture governance.
Lead the strategic evolution of security capabilities with a zero-trust-first approach, working alongside delivery teams.
Define the security architecture for AI adoption covering AI and agentic systems, the data that feeds them, and the platforms that host them. This includes model and agent governance, AI security posture management, data-classification controls for training and inference, guardrails against prompt injection and model misuse, and secure-by-design patterns for AI-enabled products.
Set a modernised approach to security tooling, services and capability sets, focused on technical feasibility across emerging technologies, controls and functions.
Drive multi-cloud consistency, ensuring controls, telemetry and posture management extend uniformly across all cloud providers rather than clustering around the best-covered one.

What will you need to succeed?

Experience

Minimum 7–10 years in information security architecture, engineering and design.
Proven ability to navigate complex organisations across the security, network, infrastructure and global architecture stack.
Proven experience migrating and upgrading core security technologies as part of an evolving security and infrastructure stack, including API security, web filtering, cloud security, email security and endpoint security.
Experience managing third-party security service providers in delivering security services.

Technical depth

Strong knowledge of core security domains: endpoint, cloud, infrastructure, perimeter and data protection.
Multi-cloud security architecture across at least two major providers, with an appreciation of how native controls and third-party platforms differ in coverage.
Working knowledge of the modern security toolset CNAPP/CSPM, EDR/XDR, SIEM, secrets management, privileged access management, SSE/CASB, WAF and perimeter protection, database activity monitoring, and SAST/SCA/DAST in the pipeline.
AI security: familiarity with AI and LLM threat models (such as the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications), AI governance frameworks (such as the NIST AI Risk Management Framework), AI security posture management, model and agent identity, and the data-security implications of AI adoption.
Pragmatic understanding of security problems as a mix of technology and process, with the ability to pursue solutions at multiple levels throughout the organisation.

Leadership and communication

Expert presentation and communication skills, written and verbal.
People leadership experience preferred, including the ability to engage, mentor, coach and develop.
Extensive knowledge of information security principles, best practices and industry standards.
Self-starter, strategic thinker, negotiator and consensus builder.

Education

University degree/college diploma in related discipline(s) or equivalent co-op work experience,
Professional designation in IT security (such as CISM, CISSP, CISA) preferred

What's in it for you?

A competitive salary and bonus program, based on market scale
A flexible group insurance program starting on your first day of work to meet your needs and those of your family.
Time off that allows you to focus on the moments that matter most. 20 vacation days per year.
Our Share Ownership Program gives you the opportunity to invest in Sun Life while benefiting from employer matching contributions.
A warm, supportive, and inclusive culture.

jobs.description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An Overview Of This Role

As Director, Analytics Engineering, you'll lead a team of 8 and report to the VP of Data & Insights. You set direction across the data organization, stay close enough to the work to guide technical decisions credibly, and partner with Data Engineering, Data Science, IT, and business leaders.

You Will Have Three Mandates

Build trusted, AI-ready self-service. Deliver a semantic model that answers business questions correctly, with the telemetry, evals, and model flexibility to prove it and keep costs in check.
Set the strategy for how GitLab accesses data. Own the data models, BI tools, and AI access patterns (Claude, MCP servers, Slack agents) that put trusted data in everyone's hands.
Build data applications the whole company relies on. Ship production-grade apps that combine trusted data, APIs, and AI to answer questions dashboards can't.

What You'll Do

Build and own a trusted semantic model, with governed metrics and business definitions, that answers business questions consistently across every tool
Build evals and ground-truth datasets that measure answer quality, and use them to drive improvements and catch regressions
Instrument telemetry to see who uses the semantic model and AI tools, what they ask, and where they get stuck
Build a model-selection harness so GitLab can route work across LLMs and stay flexible on cost and quality
Own data modeling and curated datasets for self-service, with the ownership, data contracts, testing, and documentation that make them AI-ready
Define the AI data access strategy: when to use BI, Claude, MCP servers, or Slack agents, with the governance and security to keep access trusted and reliable
Own the enterprise BI and self-service tools strategy (e.g., Tableau, Omni), including evaluation, adoption, and cost
Build self-service capabilities, such as Claude skills, documentation, and guided workflows, that help people find and use data on their own
Build and own company-wide data applications, from Claude-built single-page apps to apps inside BI tools, that combine Snowflake data, API calls, AI-powered deep dives, and write-back to Postgres or Snowflake
Set engineering standards for data apps (security, authentication, testing, deployment, and monitoring) so they're reliable at company scale
Set a long-range roadmap tied to company strategy, and a lightweight operating model that balances urgent stakeholder needs with investment in reusable data products and tech-debt reduction
Hire, coach, and retain a high-performing team of 8: build career paths, develop leaders, distribute ownership, and recognize great work
Act as customer zero for GitLab and GitLab Duo in data workflows, sharing feedback with Product and Engineering

What You'll Bring

12+ years in analytics engineering, data engineering, or BI, including 5+ years leading teams and 2+ years managing managers or senior leads
Deep expertise in data modeling and semantic layers (e.g., dbt Semantic Layer, Snowflake semantic views, LookML, Cube), and expert dbt, including testing and CI/CD across a multi-team project
Hands-on experience building LLM-powered data access (text-to-SQL, agents, MCP servers), including evals and telemetry for answer quality, and advanced use of AI coding agents such as Claude Code
Expert SQL and strong Snowflake experience; working knowledge of Python
Strong data governance experience: data quality, lineage, certified datasets, and access controls (RBAC, row access and masking policies)
Track record of leading cross-functional data initiatives from strategy through adoption and measurable business impact, including enterprise BI and self-service at scale
Systems thinker who sees how models, pipelines, and architecture decisions connect, and designs for second-order effects
Exceptional communicator who writes clear technical specs, sets a clear vision, makes trade-offs visible, and influences executives and peers across the company
Pragmatic in ambiguity: makes sound decisions on emerging technology and ships the right next version rather than waiting for the ideal end state
Able to use GitLab, thrive in an all-remote, asynchronous company, model GitLab's remote working competencies, and work in line with GitLab's values

Nice to Have

Experience with LLM routing or gateway tools and managing model costs
Experience with Tableau, Omni, or a BI platform migration
Experience with web app development (e.g., React, TypeScript) and Postgres
Experience owning finance or revenue-critical data (e.g., ARR, consumption) where accuracy and auditability are non-negotiable

About The Team

Analytics Engineering makes GitLab's data trusted, easy to find, and ready for anyone to use, whether they ask a dashboard, Claude, or a Slack agent. We own the curated data models, the semantic layer, the self-service tools, and the data applications that let teams answer their own questions.

AI is changing how people get to data. Questions that once went through an analyst now go straight to AI tools, so the answers are only as good as the data models and business definitions behind them. Our job is to make those answers correct, consistent, and measurable.

jobs.description:
Who We Are Is What We Do.

Deel is the all-in-one payroll and HR platform for global teams. Our vision is to unlock global opportunity for every person, team, and business. Built for the way the world works today, Deel combines HRIS, payroll, compliance, benefits, performance, and equipment management into one seamless platform. With AI-powered tools and a fully owned payroll infrastructure, Deel supports every worker type in 150+ countries—helping businesses scale smarter, faster, and more compliantly.

Among the largest globally distributed companies in the world, our team of 7,000 spans more than 100 countries, speaks 74 languages, and brings a connected and dynamic culture that drives continuous learning and innovation for our customers.

Why should you be part of our success story?

As the fastest-growing Software as a Service (SaaS) company in history, Deel is transforming how global talent connects with world-class companies – breaking down borders that have traditionally limited both hiring and career opportunities. We're not just building software; we're creating the infrastructure for the future of work, enabling a more diverse and inclusive global economy. In 2024 alone, we paid $11.2 billion to workers in nearly 100 currencies and provided healthcare and benefits to workers in 109 countries—ensuring people get paid and protected, no matter where they are.

Our momentum is reflected in our achievements and customer satisfaction: CNBC Disruptor 50, Forbes Cloud 100, Deloitte Fast 500, and repeated recognition on Y Combinator's top companies list – all while maintaining a 4.83 average rating from 15,000 reviews across G2, Trustpilot, Captera, Apple and Google.

Your experience at Deel will be a career accelerator. At the forefront of the global work revolution, you'll tackle complex challenges that impact millions of people's working lives. With our momentum—backed by a $17.3 billion valuation and $1 B in Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) in just over five years—you'll drive meaningful impact while building expertise that makes you a sought-after leader in the transformation of global work.

About The Studio

Deel is one of the fastest-growing companies in the world, and we're building the brand and creative studio to match. We make global campaigns, partnerships, film, design, and social at real scale, for businesses and for workers in almost every country there is.

We're looking for someone exceptional to raise the bar on what we make. This is a hands-on role. You'd set the standard by making the work.

The role

Deel is a truly global, people-first brand, and it's taking off. We're looking for a creative director who works at the front edge of AI-native production across video and design. Most AI creative work is technically impressive and creatively empty. Some of it is good work that used AI somewhere in the pipeline. We think there's a real discipline in between, and we want you to build it here. You'd define how we make this work, and you'd prove it by making it. This is a hands-on role.

What You'll Make

AI-native creative. Work where generative tools are central to how it's made, at a standard the category hasn't reached.
The stack. Our AI creative tooling and the workflows around it, including the principles for where we don't use it.
Video and motion. Brand films, campaign work, and product storytelling that blend traditional and AI-led production.
A repeatable method. Something the rest of the team can use, so the capability outlives any one project.

What You Bring

At least ten years across video, motion, or design, with direction as well as production.
Recent work made or directed with generative AI that stands up as creative work first.
Deep knowledge of the current tooling, and clear judgment about where it breaks.
Proven ability to build a workflow other people can actually use.
A point of view on likeness, disclosure, and provenance. We take these seriously.

What Would Set You Apart

A reel with range across live-action, motion, and generative work.
Experience establishing an AI practice inside a creative team.
A public point of view on AI in creative work.

Who You'll Work With

You'll sit inside the creative studio and work alongside our Creative Director, the video and motion teams, and the brand designers who'll build on what you establish.

How We Work

We're a studio, not a request queue. People here make things rather than manage from a distance. We use AI seriously, and we're deliberate about where we don't.

jobs.title: Director - Finance, Data & Analytics
jobs.description:
About The Foundation

At the St. Joseph’s Health Centre Foundation we are committed to continuing to transform St. Joe’s as a leading community hospital that delivers the best care experiences to Toronto’s west end. We are guided by our mission to inspire philanthropy from our community and raise the funds needed to support that transformation.

St. Joe’s has provided care for millions of people in Toronto’s west end for more than a century. Today it is one Canada’s busiest community teaching hospitals, looking after a vibrant community of over half a million.

The Foundation has grown in recent years to be a leading community hospital foundation with a strong and engaged board of directors. We are looking for a new team member to help with gift management and donor engagement that helps to deliver the best care possible for our community.

About The Position

The Director, Finance, Data & Analytics provides strategic and operational leadership across financial management, business intelligence, fundraising analytics and organizational performance for the Foundation.

As the Foundation enters an ambitious next phase of campaign growth, this role will be responsible for ensuring that the organization has the financial discipline, data infrastructure and insights required to support informed decision-making and maximize fundraising performance.

Working closely with the President & CEO, VP, Operations, Senior Leadership Team and fundraising leaders, the Director will connect financial and fundraising data to provide a clear, timely and actionable view of organizational and campaign performance.

The Director will be the Foundation’s lead resource for financial reporting, fundraising analytics, campaign intelligence, data quality and performance reporting, ensuring that leaders have the information they need to identify opportunities, manage risk, allocate resources and achieve campaign objectives.

The successful candidate will combine strong financial expertise with an analytical and business-oriented mindset, an understanding of fundraising and donor data, and the ability to translate complex information into clear insights and recommendations.

Key Areas of Responsibility

Financial Leadership & Management
Lead the Foundation’s financial planning, budgeting, forecasting and reporting processes.
Prepare timely, accurate decision-useful financial reports for the President & CEO, Senior Leadership Team, Finance Committee and Board.
Monitor financial performance against budget and provide analysis of material variances, trends, risks and opportunities.
Lead the annual budgeting and collaborate on the business planning process with the VP, Operations and Senior Leadership Team.
Oversee cash flow, investments, receivables, payables and other core financial management activities.
Lead the annual audit and maintain strong financial controls, policies and procedures.
Ensure appropriate financial oversight of designated funds, restricted gifts, commitments and disbursements.
Work closely with external accounting and investment partners as required.
Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards, regulatory requirements and Foundation policies.
Campaign & Fundraising Analytics
Own the development and ongoing management of the Foundation’s campaign reporting and fundraising analytics framework.
Partner with fundraising leadership to establish clear definitions, methodologies and performance measures for campaign pipeline, proposals, asks, commitments and revenue.
Develop and maintain campaign dashboards that provide management and Board-level visibility into campaign progress and future potential.
Provide analysis that identifies emerging gaps, opportunities and trends and supports proactive campaign management.
Develop forecasting models to support campaign revenue projections and scenario planning.
Work with fundraising leaders to assess portfolio capacity, prospect movement and pipeline sufficiency.
Translate fundraising data into concise insights and recommendations for the Senior Leadership Team, Campaign Leadership, Finance Committee and Board.
Data Strategy, Quality & Business Intelligence
Serve as the Foundation’s internal lead for data strategy, data governance and business intelligence.
Establish standards for data quality, consistency, definitions and reporting across financial and fundraising systems and oversee implantation with Database Manager.
Partner with fundraising and operations teams to improve the use of Raiser's Edge NXT and other systems as strategic management tools.
Identify opportunities to automate reporting and improve data accessibility.
Develop and maintain dashboards and reporting tools using appropriate business intelligence platforms.
Connect financial, fundraising, donor and operational data to provide a more complete picture of organizational performance.
Establish appropriate data governance, privacy, security and access practices in partnership with organizational leadership.
Identify technology and systems improvements that will increase efficiency, insight and fundraising productivity.
Prospect & Donor Intelligence
Support the fundraising team with data-driven prospect identification, qualification and prioritization.
Develop reporting to help assess prospect capacity, relationship activity, portfolio composition and movement through the fundraising cycle.
Partner with fundraising leadership to identify gaps in prospect pipelines and opportunities for portfolio development.
Support analysis of donor behaviour, giving patterns, retention, upgrades and other trends that inform fundraising strategy.
Organizational Performance & Decision Support
Working with VP, Operations develop a consistent framework of organizational KPIs aligned with the Foundation’s strategic and business plans.
Provide analysis to support resource allocation, staffing decisions, event and program performance, fundraising investments and operational planning.
Identify trends and insights across revenue, expenses, fundraising activity and organizational performance.
Prepare clear, concise analysis and visualizations for leadership and Board audiences.
Act as a strategic thought partner to leaders, moving beyond reporting results to helping the organization understand what the data means and what action it should inform.
Leadership, Collaboration & Continuous Improvement
Lead continuous improvement of financial and fundraising reporting processes.
Provide leadership and coaching to the administration team, including the Database Manager.
Identify opportunities to streamline workflows, automate repetitive activities and improve organizational efficiency.
Contribute to a culture of accountability, curiosity, continuous learning and evidence-informed decision-making.
Provide leadership and coaching to staff, contractors or external resources supporting finance, data and analytics.

Qualifications & Experience

CPA designation.
7+ years of progressive experience in finance, financial management, analytics, business intelligence or a related field.
Experience working in a nonprofit, healthcare, fundraising or similarly complex environment is an asset.
Demonstrated experience developing budgets, forecasts, financial models and management reporting.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate data into clear business insights.
Experience with CRM and fundraising databases; experience with Raiser's Edge NXT is an asset.
Experience developing dashboards and reporting using tools such as Power BI or equivalent is an asset.
Experience working with large or complex datasets and improving data quality and reporting processes.
Strong understanding of data governance, privacy and information management.
Excellent communication skills and the ability to present financial and analytical information clearly.
Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively.
Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Strategic, curious and improvement-oriented.

At Tangerine, we’re redefining banking. As Canada’s leading digital bank, we thrive on innovation, agility, and bold thinking, tackling every challenge head-on with leading technology and the unstoppable power of collaboration.

Our client-obsessed teams deliver flexible, accessible banking solutions, breakthrough products, and award-winning service. Beyond banking, we’re committed to making an impact in the communities we serve and across our organization. We foster a culture built on integrity, inclusion, and fearless ambition – where diverse perspectives are valued, and people are empowered to do their best work.

Are you ready to disrupt the status quo? Do you crave challenges that push boundaries? If you’re a high performer looking to accelerate your career and reimagine the banking landscape, this is your moment.

Let’s shape the future of banking together!

The Director, Wealth Strategy & Research will lead the development and execution of strategic initiatives that shape the future of our wealth offerings. This role carries enterprise-level accountability, executive decision support, and stakeholder influence across the organization. The Director will serve as a thought leader, driving insights that inform product strategy, market positioning, and long-term growth.

Is this role right for you? In this role, you will be:

Define and execute the Tangerine Wealth product roadmap in alignment with business strategic objectives.
Provide strategic insights and recommendations to senior executives, influencing enterprise priorities and business decisions.
Represent Tangerine Wealth in executive forums and prepare board reports, C-suite briefings, and steering-committee updates.
Work closely with market research and competitive intelligence teams to identify actionable insights to inform product development and business decisions.
Continuously monitor the traditional wealth, digital wealth, and fintech landscape for emerging trends, competitor moves, regulatory developments, and technology innovations.
Translate research findings into actionable strategies that drive innovation and client-centric solutions.
Develop and manage structured frameworks for competitor benchmarking, client segmentation, pricing, and go-to-market strategies.
Build data-driven business cases for new initiatives, products, or partnerships.
Support annual and multi-year strategic planning cycles with market input, scenario analysis, and post-implementation reviews to capture lessons learned.
Establish KPIs, scorecards, and dashboards to track progress against strategic objectives.
Maintain decision-support tools and intelligence repositories for timely stakeholder updates.
Produce thought-leadership pieces, white papers, and briefing notes to inform executives and strengthen external positioning.
Distill complex research and analysis into clear recommendations, dashboards, and strategic presentations for senior leadership.
Build and maintain strong relationships with senior leaders, cross-functional teams, and external partners, and coordinate input for major decisions to ensure alignment between insights, strategy, and execution.
Champion process optimization, knowledge-sharing, and adoption of best practices by creating templates, playbooks, and standardized deliverables for strategy projects.
Lead and develop a high-performing team, fostering collaboration, empowerment, and continuous improvement.
Championing a client- obsessed culture
Leveraging a growth mindset, embracing learning and continuous improvement
Contributing to a dynamic workplace fostering trust, integrity and inclusion
Removing obstacles to drive momentum across teams
Leading a high performing team through times of change
Supporting teams through transformation activities

Skills

Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed in this role? We'd love to work with you if you have:

AI fluency
A craving to contribute to a high-performing team
Ability to drive results in periods of change
Track record of fostering an inclusive culture
10+ years in strategy, research, corporate development, or management consulting, ideally within financial services or fintech.
Strong quantitative and qualitative research capabilities, with deep expertise in the North American wealth management space.
Proven ability to translate insights into actionable strategies and drive cross-functional alignment.
Excellent executive-level communication and presentation skills, with comfort working under tight deadlines on high-visibility projects.
Highly organized, self-directed, and able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-changing environment.

What's in it for you?

You will be part of a diverse, inclusive, and purpose driven community of client- obsessed innovators who move fast, push boundaries, and celebrate big together.
We are creating something game changing and you get to make your mark on it.
You will have access to thousands of online and in person learning experiences at your fingertips to elevate your career and accelerate your development.
From competitive benefits to programs that support your wellbeing and financial goals- we invest in you today and in your future.*

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Chief Financial Officer

Regional Municipality of Wood Buffalo | Fort McMurray, Alberta

Aplin is proud to partner with the Regional Municipality of Wood Buffalo (RMWB)
in the search for an accomplished and strategic Chief Financial Officer (CFO)
to join its senior leadership team.

Reporting directly to the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO), the CFO will provide executive leadership across Financial Services, Procurement, and Assessment and Taxation. This is an opportunity for a forward-thinking financial executive to influence the Municipality's long-term financial strategy, strengthen governance, and contribute to a business-focused, accountable, and data-driven organization.

The successful candidate will be a confident and decisive executive who brings deep financial expertise, strong business acumen, and exceptional communication skills. They will demonstrate sound judgment, a collaborative leadership style, and the ability to navigate the complexity of a large public-sector organization while building credibility with Council, senior leadership, employees, and key stakeholders.

The Opportunity

As a key member of the senior leadership team, the CFO will:

Lead the Municipality's financial strategy, long-term planning, budgeting, financial reporting, and governance.
Provide strategic financial advice and recommendations to the CAO, Council, and senior leadership.
Oversee Financial Services, Procurement, and Assessment and Taxation, ensuring effective and accountable service delivery.
Champion operational excellence, financial sustainability, continuous improvement, and informed decision-making.
Build and lead high-performing teams while fostering collaboration, transparency, and accountability.
Present complex financial information clearly and confidently to Council and other stakeholders.

The Ideal Candidate

We are seeking an accomplished financial leader who brings:

A minimum of 15 years of progressive financial or corporate services leadership experience, including five years at a senior management level.
A CPA designation and a degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related discipline. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
Strong financial acumen, strategic planning capabilities, and experience leading complex, multidisciplinary functions.
Knowledge of public-sector accounting standards, financial governance, and municipal administration.
Exceptional communication, interpersonal, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate complex financial matters into clear, practical recommendations.
A collaborative, decisive leadership style and the confidence to operate effectively in a dynamic, politically sensitive environment.

Candidates with broader public-sector experience or a combination of public- and private-sector leadership experience are encouraged to apply, provided they possess the relevant financial and governance expertise.

Why Consider This Opportunity?

This position offers the opportunity to work directly with a business-minded CAO, influence strategic decision-making, and make a meaningful contribution to one of Alberta's most economically significant municipalities.
The Municipality offers a competitive executive compensation package, including a cost-of-living allowance and relocation assistance if necessary.

We believe diverse teams build stronger companies, and we welcome applicants from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. To be considered, applicants must be legally entitled to work in Canada, including holding any required permits. jobs.title: Vice President, Finance - St. Francis Xavier University
jobs.description:
St. Francis Xavier University is located in Mi’kma’ki, the ancestral and unceded territory of the Mi’kmaw people. We honour their enduring stewardship and commit to advancing reconciliation through learning, reflection and action. We are all Treaty People.

St. Francis Xavier University (StFX) is one of Canada's leading primarily undergraduate universities, recognized for excellence in teaching, research, community engagement, and student success. Located in Antigonish, Nova Scotia, StFX offers an immersive learning environment through its Faculties of Arts, Science, and Education; the Gerald Schwartz School of Business; the Rankin School of Nursing; and the Coady Institute. Home to approximately 5,000 students, 250 faculty members, and 460 staff, the University is supported by an engaged global alumni network of more than 50,000. StFX is known for fostering intellectual growth, leadership, service, and lifelong connections while advancing its commitment to community development and social justice.

StFX is seeking a forward-thinking, inclusive, and collegial leader to serve as its next Vice President (VP), Finance. This is a significant leadership opportunity at an important time for StFX and the Canadian post-secondary sector. Building on a proud tradition, a strong sense of community, and a deeply held commitment to student success, the University is looking to advance its priorities with creativity and focus on emerging opportunities to enhance resilience, invest strategically, and expand the University’s capacity to achieve its goals. The VP will help shape thoughtful, forward-looking choices that strengthen StFX’s long-term position.

Reporting to the President and Vice-Chancellor and serving as a key member of StFX’s executive leadership team, the VP, Finance will provide strategic financial leadership, oversight, and stewardship in support of the University’s academic mission, distinctive student experience, and long-term sustainability. In close partnership with the Academic Vice President and Provost, senior leaders, the Board of Governors and the broader University community, the Vice President will bring an enterprise-wide perspective to financial planning, budgeting, resource allocation, risk, and institutional priorities.

The Vice President leads Financial Services, including Accounts Payable, Financial Reporting, Procurement Services, Student Accounts and Risk Management, and will position the portfolio as a trusted, responsive partner to the University. Combining strong financial acumen with integrity, sound judgment and a collaborative approach, they will advance modernization, evidence-based decisions, and service excellence, while empowering a high-performing team.

The successful candidate will bring senior financial leadership experience in complex organizations, with a track record of improving financial performance, and a post-secondary education in finance, business or a relevant discipline. A Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation is required. Higher education experience and experience in a unionized environment is an asset. The VP combines strong financial acumen across strategy, capital planning, cash flow, treasury, debt and risk with sound knowledge of accounting, fund accounting, financial reporting, controls and governance. Knowledge of post-secondary reporting requirements and government funding is preferred. They will have demonstrated success leading change, improving operations, advising executives and boards, communicating complex matters clearly, and building trust across diverse stakeholder groups. Experience supporting collective bargaining, complex contracts, government funding, partnerships or asset strategy is an asset.

To learn more about St. Francis Xavier University, please visit: https://www.stfx.ca/

StFX is committed to upholding the values of equity, diversity, inclusion and accessibility. StFX encourages applications from members of groups that have been historically disadvantaged and marginalized, including Indigenous persons (especially Mi’kmaq), racialized persons (especially African Nova Scotians), persons with disabilities, those who identify as women and/or 2SLGBTQIA+ and any others who would contribute to the diversity of our community.

If you are a member of one of these underrepresented groups, we invite you to self-identify on your cover letter or resume.

StFX is committed to the elimination of barriers to participation for persons with disabilities. If you require an accommodation(s) to participate in the application, interviewing or selection process, please contact Georgia Jones at gjones@royerthompson.com.

Please submit a combined resume and cover letter online by clicking “Apply.”
For further information about this opportunity, please contact Erica Armstrong (earmstrong@royerthompson.com), or Dr. Dominique Roche (droche@royerthompson.com) in confidence.

Full-Time Position: Director of Finance
Location: Hillside Pines Home for Special Care, Bridgewater, NS
Industry: Not-for-Profit, Long Term Care

Hillside Pines has an immediate opening for a Director of Finance. Hillside Pines is a person-first long-term care facility located in the beautiful South Shore area of Nova Scotia. Nestled in the heart of Bridgewater, we offer opportunities for meaningful work as part of a team creating the future of long-term care.

Position Summary
Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer (CEO), the Director of Finance will lead the home’s finance function while serving as a trusted business partner to senior leadership. This role combines strategic leadership with operational oversight and will play a key role in shaping the home’s financial future.

The successful candidate will oversee financial planning, maintenance of accounting, payroll and budgeting systems, including financial management, financial reporting, internal control, budgeting, and forecasting. In addition, they are responsible for ensuring accurate and timely production of statements and analysis to keep Hillside Pines on target financially and within budget.

Key Responsibilities
• Oversee all financial operations, including budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, and cash flow management.
• Ensure accurate accounting records, internal controls, and compliance with generally accepted accounting principles, government regulations, and funding requirements.
• Prepare and present monthly financial statements and analysis to the CEO and Board of Directors.
• Lead the annual budgeting process and coordinate year-end audits and external reporting requirements.
• Oversee payroll administration, employee benefit programs, pension contributions, and statutory remittances.
• Manage resident billing, trust accounts, accounts payable, accounts receivable, and capital project accounting.
• Ensure compliance with Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Workers' Compensation Board (WCB), insurance, and other regulatory obligations.
• Develop and maintain financial, payroll, and administrative policies and procedures.
• Collaborate with leaders across the organization to support operational planning, financial stewardship, and continuous improvement initiatives.
• Participate as a member of the senior leadership team and support the organization's mission, values, and commitment to quality care.

Requirements
What We’re Looking For
• Bachelor's degree in accounting or business administration.
• CPA designation, active and in good standing (preferred but not mandatory)
• Must be bondable and able to provide relevant documents
• Minimum of 5+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including leadership responsibility.
• Advanced knowledge of Sage 300 computerized accounting programs, and other software programs related to payroll (Payworks), Microsoft Word and Excel.
• Strong experience with budgeting, forecasting, financial modelling, and business partnering.
• Solid understanding of accounting operations, financial reporting, internal controls, and cash management.
• Demonstrated success leading process improvements, systems implementations, or automation initiatives.
• Experience partnering with senior leadership and/or a Board of Directors.
• Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with a collaborative approach and the ability to thrive in a team-focused workplace.
• Proven ability to thrive in a busy and sometimes high-pressure office setting while working independently and meeting deadlines.
• Ensures the privacy and dignity of residents, families and staff are protected and information treated in confidence.

Hours of Work - Monday to Friday 8-4 with occasional evenings related to elder functions.
Work Location – In Person

Hiring Manager’s Note - We’re looking for someone who is both strategic and hands-on — a finance leader who wants to understand how the Home operates, build strong relationships across the leadership team, and help shape the next chapter of financial and operational growth within the Home.

How to Apply
Please email your current resume and salary expectations to: Elizabeth Eberendu, CEO at ceo@hillsidepines.com

jobs.title: Associate Director S&OP Excellence and Planning Analytics
jobs.description:
Earlier this year, Unilever announced an agreement to combine its Foods business with McCormick & Company, creating a scaled global flavour powerhouse. The proposed combination would bring together iconic Foods brands, including Hellmann’s and Knorr, with McCormick’s portfolio to create a global leader across spices, seasonings, condiments and complementary food categories, supported by strong retail and foodservice platforms. McCormick brings more than 135 years of heritage, a presence in 150+ countries and territories, and a portfolio of trusted brands. The transaction remains subject to regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions, with completion estimated for mid-2027.

Job Purpose

This role exists to strengthen how the North America Foods business plans, decides, and delivers across demand, supply, inventory, service, cost, and business waste. As Associate Director, S&OP Excellence and Planning Analytics, you will lead the planning excellence and analytics agenda that connects business ambition with practical, reliable operating plans. You will help build a more resilient, data-driven, and collaborative supply chain that enables trusted Foods brands to serve customers and consumers with confidence. This is inclusive of planning technology, analytics, and process.

You will be part of a team that believes planning is more than a process. It is a critical way of bringing people together, making better decisions, and creating the conditions for sustainable growth.

Key Responsibilities

In this role, you will lead the development and continuous improvement of integrated planning and sales and operations planning practices across North America Foods (Retail and Foods Solutions; US and Canada). You will partner closely with Demand Planning, Supply Planning, Material Planning, Manufacturing, Finance, Customer Development, Marketing, and senior Supply Chain leaders to ensure the business has clear plans, strong governance, reporting/tools, and actionable insights to support growth, service, efficiency, and transformation.

Lead a team of WL1s/2s to drive the sales and operations planning excellence agenda. Ensure robust process and technology are in place to ensure demand, supply, inventory, service, cost, and financial assumptions are connected through clear business rhythms and decision-making forums.
Partner with integrated planning teams to identify risks, opportunities, and gaps within planning technology/process and drive improvement plans. Identify / build business cases or drive cross functional process improvement.
Strengthen integrated planning capability by improving processes, tools, routines, governance, and ways of working across the North America Foods planning community.
Lead planning performance management, including the maintenance and creation and use of clear measures, scorecards, dashboards, reports, and insights that help teams make faster and better decisions. This can include modifying existing dashboards due to new business insights
Drive continuous improvement, simplification, and standardization across planning processes to improve reliability, reduce complexity, and support scalable ways of working.

jobs.title: Director, Finance
jobs.description:
Finding the right finance leader for a stadium is about more than producing accurate financial statements. It's about finding someone who can thrive in a fast-paced, event-driven business where concert nights can run late, operational decisions happen in real time, and leadership teams rely on financial insight to drive strategy. This role is ideal for a senior finance leader who loves getting into the details, building strong teams, and turning complex financial information into a clear business story.

Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the Director, Finance of BC Place is an experienced business and people leader responsible for providing financial oversight, direction, and leadership across the organization. Working closely with the Finance team, senior leadership, and operational stakeholders, this role ensures best-in-class financial reporting, analysis, controls, and compliance while helping drive strategic business decisions.

This is a highly visible leadership role within a dynamic venue and events environment. No two days are the same at BC Place. One day you may be leading the annual budgeting process, negotiating financial terms within a major contract, or presenting forecast updates to executives. The next, you may be overseeing event settlements following a sold-out concert that wrapped long after most offices have turned off the lights.

The successful candidate is a strong accounting professional first and foremost. They bring deep technical expertise, exceptional analytical capabilities, and the ability to translate financial results into meaningful business insights. They are equally comfortable reviewing complex reconciliations, coaching a finance team, supporting negotiations, and presenting strategic recommendations to executives.

What You Will Do

Lead all day-to-day financial operations for the BC Place, including oversight and integration of shared services accounting functions.
Ensure the accuracy, integrity, and completeness of financial records across all departments.
Oversee general ledger management, account reconciliations, and month-end and year-end close processes.
Deliver accurate, timely, and meaningful financial statements and management reporting.
Lead the annual budgeting, forecasting, capital planning, and long-range financial planning processes.
Provide detailed financial analysis, operational reporting, and business insights that support strategic decision-making.
Analyze operating trends, financial performance, and key business drivers to identify efficiencies, risks, and opportunities for improvement.
Oversee event settlement preparation, review, analysis, and presentation while ensuring accuracy and strong client relationships.
Manage recurring billings, accounts receivable performance, credit management, and revenue reconciliation activities.
Lead capital asset management activities, including additions, disposals, write-downs, and maintenance of the capital asset register.
Ensure payroll processes are completed accurately and on time through effective procedures, support, and training.
Manage the annual external audit process and maintain strong relationships with auditors and external stakeholders.
Maintain and continuously improve financial policies, procedures, workflows, and internal controls.
Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards and maintain financial reporting in accordance with PSAB requirements.
Provide financial guidance on contracts, leases, supplier agreements, sponsorship agreements, and other commercial arrangements.
Support leadership with contract reviews, negotiations, and financial risk assessments.
Advise senior leaders on financial impacts, emerging issues, and opportunities affecting business plans and budgets.
Build, mentor, and develop a high-performing finance team while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and excellence.
Partner with leaders across the organization to support operational success, strategic initiatives, and long-term business objectives.
Be prepared to support an events-based operation where concert and event schedules may occasionally require evening work and late-night financial oversight.

What You Will Bring

CPA designation is required.
University degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, or a related discipline. A combination of education and experience may also be considered.
7+ years of progressive finance and accounting leadership experience, ideally including Controller-level responsibilities.
Proven success leading and developing finance teams within complex, multi-stakeholder organizations.
Deep technical accounting expertise with strong knowledge of financial reporting, internal controls, and accounting standards.
Experience with PSAB reporting standards is strongly preferred.
Demonstrated excellence in financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, and analytical reporting.
Advanced financial modeling and business analysis capabilities with a natural curiosity for understanding the "why" behind the numbers.
Experience leading month-end and year-end close processes in fast-paced operational environments.
Strong audit management experience and ability to ensure compliance while driving process improvements.
Experience managing capital assets, contract reviews, lease accounting, and financial implications of commercial agreements.
Exposure to risk management and contract negotiations is considered an asset.
Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
Strong communication and presentation skills with the ability to influence and build credibility with executives, operational leaders, clients, and external partners.
A collaborative leadership style paired with strong business judgment and decision-making skills.
Ability to balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution.
Comfortable working in an events-driven environment where business needs occasionally extend beyond traditional office hours.
Passion for building efficient processes, creating strong controls, and helping an organization make informed decisions through data and financial insight.

This is a unique opportunity for a finance leader who enjoys rolling up their sleeves, leading through complexity, and partnering with a business that operates at the intersection of live events, operations, and community impact. jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
About Jim Peplinski Capital

At most companies, finance supports the business. At Jim Peplinski Capital (JPC), finance is our business.

For over 35 years, Jim Peplinski Capital has financed and managed the vehicles and equipment Canadian businesses run on. We combine capital, fleet expertise and technology to help our clients get the most from the assets that keep them moving. Now we're building the next generation of fleet management, with ambitious growth plans and the balance sheet to pursue them.

We're looking for a steady, strategic, and commercially minded CFO to partner with the President and Executive Team on the decisions and execution that shape our future.

About The Role

Reporting directly to the President, you'll lead JPC's Finance, Credit and Risk function and serve as a trusted partner to the Executive Team. Two leaders report to you, a Finance Manager and a Credit Manager, along with their teams.

This is not a back-office finance role. As a lender and fleet manager, how we fund, price and manage risk is how we compete, and you'll own it. That covers capital and liquidity, funding and banking relationships, pricing and return on capital, portfolio risk and credit discipline, financial reporting and planning, and accounting, controls and compliance.

You'll shape how JPC funds its growth, manages risk, allocates capital, and you'll build the people and systems we need to scale. It's hands-on leadership: you set the direction, and you’ll roll up your sleeves when the work calls for it.

What You’ll Do

Team Leadership. Build, mentor and develop high-performing Finance and Credit teams with a culture of sound judgment, ownership, accountability and practical problem solving.
Capital, Funding and Liquidity. Ensure JPC has the capital, liquidity and funding structure to support growth. You'll manage banking relationships, funding facilities, interest rate exposure, covenant compliance and lender reporting, and build capacity ahead of where the business is going.
Residuals and Portfolio Risk. You'll own concentration limits, provisioning and credit performance across the portfolio. Collaborating with our VP, Asset Management, you'll set and monitor residual assumptions.
Credit and Adjudication. Keep credit discipline strong while finding practical ways to say yes to good business. You'll be the second set of eyes for the Credit Manager on the decisions that need it.
Financial Reporting and Planning. Deliver accurate, timely reporting to the President, Board and lenders. You'll lead budgeting, forecasting and planning, and provide the Executive Team the insights to make better decisions faster.
Accounting, Compliance and Controls. Own accounting, lease accounting, tax, audit, treasury and financial controls, plus our regulatory program, including FINTRAC and AML.
Client engagement. Work directly with clients on the decisions that matter most, from structuring deals to managing delinquencies and payment workouts, balancing a strong relationship with protecting the portfolio.
Commercial Judgment. Bring financial rigor to decisions on new products, services and partner programs. You'll lead negotiation of key commercial agreements and embed financial and risk thinking across JPC.
Systems & Technology: Own the finance and credit systems that support our growth, driving automation and building a scalable foundation for reporting, adjudication and accounting.

What We’re Looking For

You have 12+ years of progressive finance experience, including senior leadership. Experience in fleet management, automotive and/or equipment finance or specialty lending is a strong asset. Bank or boutique, we care about the depth of your experience, not the logo. A CPA is preferred but not required for candidates with deep experience as a CFO or senior finance leader in a lending business.

You Also

Have built teams, developed strong leaders, and held them to a high standard.
Understand banking, lending, capital structure and liquidity management.
Have excellent financial, accounting and commercial credit judgment.
Are an expert in assessing financial performance, cash flow, leverage and creditworthiness.
Turn financial information into clear recommendations and decisions.
Can protect the balance sheet without losing sight of the customer and commercial opportunities.
Take ownership, challenge assumptions and make decisions.

Why You’ll Love It At JPC

A real partnership. You'll work directly with the President, Executive Team and Board. We're privately held, so decisions get made quickly, and you'll be part of making them.
Autonomy to build. You'll have the autonomy to build our Finance, Credit and Risk function, influence strategy and create processes that scale.
A chance to shape the industry. You'll help define how commercial fleets are financed and optimized.
A team that plays to win. You'll join a talented, fast-moving group that values ownership, high standards and trust.
Strong rewards. Competitive compensation, a performance bonus, and comprehensive benefits from day one.

Job Description:

Additional Job Description

Department Overview

TD Commercial National Accounts services the unique needs of public and private Canadian businesses, customizing a broad range of products. The Financial Institutions Group within National Account is an industry leading team focused on providing best-in-class products and services to firms in the financial services sector. As part of the FI team the Director, Credit Execution guides and leads a team of Associates and Associate Directors whose job is to assist with structuring credit proposals and analyzing the risks associated with lending facilities for new and existing business clients that borrow in excess of $ 25 million. The Director, Credit Execution is part of the senior management group for a business banking unit and reports directly to the AVP, Credit Management, Commercial National Accounts.

Job Description

In the role of Director, Credit Execution ("DCE"), you are principally responsible for managing the credit and operational risk for an industry-specific commercial / junior corporate loan portfolio. You are a subject matter expert and have the ability to analyze and understand complex credit proposals, including multi-lender situations. You can anticipate and assess the risks associated with entering into a lending relationship under a wide range of economic scenarios and ensure solicitor-prepared loan agreements are relevant, supportive and competitive for the bank and our clients on an ongoing basis. You will assess, analyze and perform due diligence in support of all applications, approving credits within delegated limits and making recommendations on all others. You will interface with TD's risk management group on a regular basis to ensure that your understanding of the Bank's risk models and pricing platforms allows you to effectively interpret and apply policy. Recognizing that your credibility and influence with them is based on the credit proposals that are well-crafted and presented by your team, you make the development of your Associates' and Associate Directors' risk evaluation skills your primary priority. Thus, you will establish yourself as a trusted business leader who is sought after for guidance regarding matters relating to the credit facilities that are supporting the clients’ business strategy. You support your Unit’s efforts to meet their business development targets by recommending credit packaging alternatives and actively discuss credit solutions with internal TD partners, external professional advisors, and other lenders as appropriate. You feel comfortable in a team based business environment where you are expected to balance risk management objectives with our ongoing business building targets.

Job Requirements

Education/Accreditations:

Undergraduate/Graduate degree in business or relevant professional designation.

Other Qualifications/Skills/Experience:

Successful DCEs have the proven ability to understand the economic and industry specific circumstances that will impact the long term viability of their clients, leveraging them to structure solid credit solutions. Through their coaching expertise and experience as a mentor, they effectively impart their experience on a team of Associates and Associate Directors, developing these individuals to be better equipped to structure credit proposals and evaluate business risks. In addition to your undergraduate/graduate degree in business or relevant professional designation, you will ideally have proven your suitability for this role with at least 5 years experience in a combination, and / or Manager Commercial Credit roles in a banking environment. You have well developed analytical, relationship management, credit structuring, coaching, and negotiation skills, and have a personal goal to expand them further in this role. Your passion for enhancing the customer experience guarantees that we provide credit solutions that serve the best interests of both the bank and our client.

TD is one of the world's leading global financial institutions and is the fifth largest bank in North America by branches/stores. Every day, we strive to make every interaction, product, and experience remarkably human and refreshingly simple for over 27 million households and businesses in Canada, the United States and around the world. TD is deeply committed to being a leader in client experience, that is why we believe that all colleagues, no matter where they work, are client facing. About Toronto Community Housing Corporation
  
  

Toronto Community Housing Corporation (“TCHC”) is the largest social housing provider in Canada and the second largest in North America. We are wholly owned by the City of Toronto and operate in a non\-profit manner. TCHC provides homes to over 41,000 low and moderate\-income households in 88 of Toronto's neighbourhoods, with 93,000 tenants from many different backgrounds with a diversity in age, education, language, mental and physical ability, religion, ethnicity and race. We are an essential part of the City of Toronto's fabric and social system.
  
  

Our over 2,000 employees work to achieve our vision of quality homes in vibrant communities where people are proud to live and work.
  
  

**Vacancy Type:** Full\-time Permanent
  
**Salary Range:** $165,001\.67 \- $198,002\.01
  
**Work Details (Days/Hours):** Monday – Friday, 36\.25 hours per week
  
Hybrid Eligible Yes
  
**Affiliation:** Non\-Union: Management/Exempt
  
Division and Department CEO Office
  
**Number of Vacancies:** 1
  
**Existing/New Job:** New
  
**Grade:** 10
  
Vacancy Status Existing Vacancy
  
**Candidate List or Eligibility List:** Candidate List
  
  

What we offer
  
In addition to competitive compensation and a rewarding career where you can truly make a difference, we offer a comprehensive package that meets the various needs of our diverse employees, including:
  
* Ability to participate in inclusive employee\-led networks to educate, inspire, amplify voices, build relationships and provide development opportunities;
* Minimum four (4\) weeks of paid annual vacation days, increasing with years of service;
* Four (4\) paid personal days;
* Defined benefit pension plan with OMERS, includes 100\-per\-cent employer matching;
* Health and dental benefits, including a health spending account available upon your start date;
* Employee and family assistance program;
* Maternity and parental leave top up (93% of base salary);
* Training and development programs including tuition reimbursement of $1500 per calendar year;
* Fitness membership discount.


**Work location:** This job offers the opportunity to work from home as part of a hybrid work arrangement. This arrangement will allow you to work some days at a TCHC work location (Metro Hall – 55 John Street and/or 729 Petrolia Road) and the rest of the time from home. The amount of time required to work at a TCHC work location is flexible, while considering operational and service delivery requirements.
  
  

Make a difference
  
As the Director, Corporate Compliance and Enterprise Risk, you have a unique opportunity to build and operate TCHC’s corporate compliance function while shaping the future of enterprise risk management. Reporting directly to the President \& CEO, you will develop practical frameworks, tools, and reporting that enable leaders to identify, assess and manage significant risks and compliance obligations.
  
As a trusted advisor to leaders across TCHC and to the Board of Directors, you will bring clarity to complex and emerging risks and inform enterprise\-wide decisions. Your advice will strengthen transparency and accountability while ensuring leaders remain responsible for their processes, risks, controls, and corrective actions.
  
Through coaching, facilitation and fit\-for\-purpose solutions, you will build risk and compliance capability across TCHC, helping TCHC make informed decisions and ultimately deliver better outcomes for tenants and communities.
  
  

What you’ll do
  
Corporate Compliance
  
* Design, establish and operate a corporate compliance model that enables divisions to identify and manage legislative, regulatory, shareholder, funding, policy and other obligations.
* Develop practical compliance tools, guidance, learning resources and reporting that business units can apply within day\-to\-day operations.
* Partner with compliance owners to clarify obligations, assess exposure, address capability gaps and develop proportionate improvement plans.
* Monitor changing requirements, coordinate enterprise\-level compliance insights, and support escalation of significant compliance matters.


Enterprise Risk Management (ERM)
  
* Shape and operate TCHC’s existing enterprise risk management model, including common risk language, assessment practices, risk appetite and tolerance, the enterprise risk profile and reporting cycle.
* Facilitate enterprise and cross\-divisional risk identification, assessment, prioritization and response planning with executives, risk owners and subject\-matter leaders.
* Support risk owners in developing proportionate responses, indicators and monitoring approaches, while ownership of risks, business processes and actions remains with management.
* Integrate internal controls as one component of ERM by advising leaders on controls that support the treatment of priority risks and by helping them evaluate whether those controls remain fit for purpose.


Risk Advisory and Capacity Building
  
* Provide concise, risk\-based advice on the enterprise risk profile, significant compliance obligations and emerging risks.
* Prepare and present integrated compliance and ERM reporting that supports executive and Board discussion, direction, and oversight while distinguishing management\-owned corrective actions.
* Support appropriate escalation of significant risk or compliance matters and track management commitments for executive and Board visibility.
* Coach executives, leaders, risk owners and staff in risk\-informed decision\-making and compliance management.
* Build sustainable capability through workshops, training, templates, communities of practice and decision supports.
* Lead, coach and develop team, setting priorities and quality expectations.


What you’ll need
  
* An undergraduate degree in Risk Management, Business Administration, Public Administration, Law, Compliance, Finance or related discipline.
* A recognized professional designation
