jobs.title: Director of Information Technology
jobs.description:
Position:
Permanent, full-time
Location:
Montréal, Quebec
Base Salary:
Up to $190,000 +bonus + benefits
Environment:
Onsite (5 days/wk)

Position Overview

Hammehr invites applications for the role of Director, Information Technology on behalf of our client for a full-time permanent opportunity.
Our client operates more than 60 telecommunications retail locations across Quebec, Ontario and New Brunswick, alongside business-services, device-repair and refurbished-device operations. With plans to exceed 100 locations, including through acquisitions, the business needs reliable store systems and a technology plan that supports expansion.

Reporting directly to the President and CEO, you will lead the IT and automation team, manage technology suppliers and oversee the budget and roadmap. The immediate work includes stabilizing point-of-sale systems and holding providers accountable, alongside longer-term decisions about POS, ERP and data platforms. Expect direct involvement in operational issues, executive decisions and occasional travel to Ontario and New Brunswick stores.

What You'll Do

Keep point-of-sale systems, payments, store connectivity and carrier portals available, coordinating incident response and producing a root-cause report within 48 hours of any store outage
Schedule production changes outside store opening hours, respect peak-period change freezes and require tested rollback plans
Manage service providers across hosting, infrastructure, POS, telecommunications and software, negotiating service levels, credits and exit terms and reviewing performance quarterly
Stabilize the current POS environment, lead POS and ERP platform decisions, define the data platform and deliver a three-year technology roadmap
Oversee Microsoft 365 and SharePoint governance, Entra single sign-on, multifactor authentication, access controls, endpoint protection, recovery-tested backups and technology measures supporting Quebec privacy compliance
Maintain a company-owned registry of systems, accounts, domains, licences and devices, working with Finance to manage spending and remove unused subscriptions
Integrate acquired stores into the technology environment and support the systems needed by business-services, repair and refurbished-device operations
Lead and develop the IT and automation team, chair the IT committee and present technology options, costs and risks to executives

Basic Qualifications

Experience leading IT across a multi-site retail, telecommunications or distribution business, including direct responsibility for POS and store infrastructure during peak trading periods
Technical experience diagnosing and managing Windows Server, networking, Microsoft 365, Entra ID, SharePoint, backup and security environments, including remote-access platforms such as RDS, TSplus or Citrix
Experience managing IT service providers against contractual service levels, addressing underperformance and assessing provider replacement when needed
Delivery of at least one POS, ERP or CRM migration from business analysis through go-live
Spoken and written French and English, including the ability to explain technical options, costs and operational risks to non-technical leaders

Preferred Qualifications

Experience integrating store technology following acquisitions
Experience using Azure, Power BI or APIs for reporting, data integration or automation
Familiarity with telecommunications retailer systems and carrier portals

The Challenges

Immediate store-service issues compete with longer-term platform decisions and acquisition integration; priorities must account for both trading continuity and future requirements
Production changes must fit outside opening hours and around peak-period freezes, with recovery plans tested before deployment
Accountability spans internal staff and external providers, requiring clear service expectations and escalation when delivery falls short

Your Impact

Store teams and customers experience fewer technology interruptions, with clearer explanations and corrective actions when outages occur
Executives have a clearer view of technology costs, risks and investment priorities, supported by accountable suppliers and reliable asset records
New locations and acquired stores can connect to a more consistent, secure technology environment, reducing disruption as the business expands

-----------------------------------------

Poste :
Permanent à temps plein
Lieu :
Montréal, Québec
Salaire de base : Jusqu’à 190 000 $ + prime + avantages sociaux
Mode de travail :
En présentiel, 5 jours par semaine

Aperçu du poste

Hammehr vous invite à poser votre candidature au poste de directeur ou directrice des technologies de l'information pour une occasion permanente à temps plein chez notre client.Notre client exploite plus de 60 magasins de télécommunications au Québec, en Ontario et au Nouveau-Brunswick, ainsi que des activités de services aux entreprises, de réparation et de vente d'appareils reconditionnés. L'entreprise prévoit dépasser les 100 établissements, notamment par des acquisitions. Elle a donc besoin de systèmes fiables en magasin et d'un plan technologique capable de soutenir cette expansion.

Relevant directement du président et chef de la direction, vous dirigerez l'équipe TI et automatisation, gérerez les fournisseurs technologiques et superviserez le budget et la feuille de route. Les priorités immédiates comprennent la stabilisation des systèmes de point de vente et le respect des engagements des fournisseurs, en parallèle des décisions à plus long terme concernant les plateformes de point de vente, de gestion intégrée et de données. Le poste exige une participation directe à la résolution des problèmes opérationnels et aux décisions de la direction, ainsi que des déplacements occasionnels dans les magasins de l'Ontario et du Nouveau-Brunswick.

Vos responsabilités

Assurer la disponibilité des systèmes de point de vente, des paiements, de la connectivité des magasins et des portails des opérateurs, coordonner la réponse aux incidents et produire un rapport d'analyse des causes dans les 48 heures suivant toute interruption de service en magasin
Planifier les changements en production en dehors des heures d'ouverture, respecter les gels de changements durant les périodes de pointe et exiger des plans de retour arrière testés
Gérer les fournisseurs d'hébergement, d'infrastructure, de systèmes de point de vente, de télécommunications et de logiciels, négocier les niveaux de service, les crédits de service et les clauses de sortie, puis évaluer leur rendement chaque trimestre
Stabiliser l'environnement de point de vente actuel, piloter le choix des plateformes de point de vente et de gestion intégrée (ERP), définir la plateforme de données et mettre en œuvre une feuille de route technologique sur trois ans
Superviser la gouvernance de Microsoft 365 et de SharePoint, l'authentification unique avec Entra, l'authentification multifacteur, les contrôles d'accès, la protection des postes de travail, les sauvegardes avec tests de restauration et les mesures technologiques soutenant la conformité aux exigences québécoises de protection des renseignements personnels
Tenir un registre centralisé des systèmes, comptes, domaines, licences et appareils appartenant à l'entreprise, et travailler avec les Finances pour gérer les dépenses et éliminer les abonnements inutilisés
Intégrer les magasins acquis à l'environnement technologique et soutenir les systèmes nécessaires aux services aux entreprises, à la réparation et à la vente d'appareils reconditionnés
Diriger et développer l'équipe TI et automatisation, présider le comité TI et présenter à la direction les options technologiques, leurs coûts et leurs risques

Qualifications requises

Expérience en direction des TI dans une entreprise de commerce de détail, de télécommunications ou de distribution comptant plusieurs établissements, avec une responsabilité directe des systèmes de point de vente et de l'infrastructure en magasin durant les périodes de pointe
Expérience technique en diagnostic et en gestion d'environnements Windows Server, de réseaux, de Microsoft 365, d'Entra ID, de SharePoint, de sauvegarde et de sécurité, y compris des plateformes d'accès à distance comme RDS, TSplus ou Citrix
Expérience en gestion de fournisseurs de services TI selon des engagements contractuels, en correction des écarts de rendement et en évaluation du remplacement d'un fournisseur lorsque nécessaire
Réalisation d'au moins une migration de système de point de vente, de gestion intégrée (ERP) ou de gestion de la relation client (CRM), de l'analyse des besoins d'affaires à la mise en service
Maîtrise du français et de l'anglais, à l'oral et à l'écrit, incluant la capacité d'expliquer les options techniques, les coûts et les risques opérationnels à des dirigeants non techniques

Qualifications souhaitées

Expérience d'intégration des technologies de magasins à la suite d'acquisitions
Expérience avec Azure, Power BI ou les API pour la production de rapports, l'intégration de données ou l'automatisation
Connaissance des systèmes utilisés par les détaillants en télécommunications et des portails des opérateurs

Les défis du poste

Les incidents en magasin, les décisions de plateformes à long terme et l'intégration des acquisitions se disputent le temps et les ressources disponibles; les priorités doivent tenir compte de la continuité des activités et des besoins futurs
Les changements en production doivent être réalisés en dehors des heures d'ouverture et respecter les gels prévus durant les périodes de pointe, avec des plans de retour arrière testés avant le déploiement
La prestation des services repose à la fois sur l'équipe interne et sur des fournisseurs externes, ce qui exige des attentes claires et des mécanismes d'escalade lorsque les engagements ne sont pas respectés

Votre contribution

Les équipes en magasin et la clientèle subissent moins d'interruptions technologiques, et les incidents donnent lieu à des explications claires et à des mesures correctives
La direction dispose d'une vue plus claire des coûts, des risques et des priorités d'investissement technologiques, appuyée par un suivi rigoureux des fournisseurs et un inventaire fiable des actifs
Les nouveaux établissements et les magasins acquis s'intègrent à un environnement technologique plus uniforme et sécuritaire, ce qui réduit les perturbations pendant l'expansion de l'entreprise

Partner with Project Managers and Leadership to provide financial input into planning and prioritization
Identify and mitigate financial risk while ensuring compliance with policies and standards

What You Bring

CPA designation (CA, CMA, or CGA legacy designations accepted)
8 to 12 years of progressive finance experience, including 3 to 5 years in a senior finance leadership role

jobs.description:
Director, Strategy Lead, Patient Centered Outcomes (PCO)

Reports to Practice Area Lead, Patient Centered Outcomes

Job Summary

Our Director, Strategy Lead, Patient Centered Outcomes (PCO) is responsible for supervision of the pyschometrics service area unit within PCO to oversee and advise on the development and execution of clinical outcome assessment (COA) studies. Specifically, these studies will focus on supporting our clients’ COA strategy in clinical trials and non-interventional/observational studies. The PCO team supports studies of instrument development, psychometric evaluation (classical and modern methods), and analysis of COA-based study endpoints (e.g., longitudinal modelling, survival analysis, trial exploration, missing data & intercurrent event adjustment).

The majority of the work in this team is regulatory-focused. Therefore, the role involves generating evidence for submission to federal regulators at the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and European Medicines Agency (EMA) and occasional interaction with other international regulators. Experience with regulatory agencies is essential for this role.

Essential Duties

Primary duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Collaborating with business development, marketing, and other service areas to build greater awareness of OPEN Health Group’s (OHG) PCO team capabilities
Leading the development of proposals and proactively engaging in seeking new opportunities
Managing and mentoring of mid-level and junior team members
Overseeing the design and execution of COA studies that align with international scientific standards and regulatory authority recommendations
Overseeing and advising on the development of study documents (such as study proposals, protocols, statistical or psychometric analysis plans, technical reports, and study presentations) and supervising psychometric and/or quantitative analyses to meet the study objectives
Leading or advising on the COA-focused strategy for client interactions/submissions with regulatory agencies (FDA, EMA)
Representing OHG as a COA thought leader and subject matter expert through extramural scientific activities such as: presenting research findings to clients and other external stakeholders, development of presentations at scientific congresses, developing and delivering COA-related educational content (via webinars, scientific congress short courses, etc.), serving as a peer-reviewer, and collaboration with established scientific organizations (ISPOR, ISOQOL, C-PATH) through sub-committee or task force participation. It is anticipated that these extramural scientific activities to will represent approximately 15% of the time spent in this role.

Required Experience, Skills, And Qualifications

Masters degree or PhD in Biostatistics or Psychometrics, or a relevant science (e.g., Health economics, Health Services Research, Public Health, Epidemiology, Pharmacoeconomics, or Psychology)
8+ years of experience in a consulting, pharmaceutical, or industry setting
Strong experience in COA/patient-reported outcomes research: COA instrument development/psychometric validation, quantitative analysis of COA-based clinical study endpoints, measurement strategy advising, and regulatory dossier development and submissions
Proven track record of interacting with regulatory agencies (FDA, EMA, PMDA) and/or health authorities
History of effective leadership of a global team, including strong skills in mentorship of early career professionals
Strong familiarity with current analytic methods used in COA development and validation, including an understanding of appropriate methodology applications and ability to review and interpret results
Extensive working knowledge of relevant regulatory guidance on COAs
Strong communicator (both written and verbal) with attention to detail and accuracy
Strong organizational and project management skills, including the ability to juggle a number of different projects and work to deadlines
Strong experience in business development and ability to generate organic growth opportunities
Well-developed problem-solving skills and a genuine interest in delivering high-quality deliverables
Highly proficient in MS365 including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams and Outlook

At OPEN Health, we connect visionary minds, pioneering science, and advanced technology to drive real impact. By uniting people, science, and technology, we activate new opportunities for biopharma innovation. Our expertise across medical affairs and market access unlocks faster, smarter routes to market. We are committed to improving patient outcomes worldwide. To learn more, visit www.openhealthgroup.com.

 Edelman is looking for a Senior Vice President, Health Digital to help shape the future of digital marketing for some of the world's leading pharmaceutical brands. Sitting at the intersection of Edelman Health and Edelman Digital, this is an opportunity to lead sophisticated, integrated digital strategies that connect healthcare brands with patients, caregivers, and healthcare professionals in meaningful ways.

 We're looking for a strategic digital leader who understands the complexities of pharmaceutical marketing and knows how to bring together creativity, technology, data, and regulatory expertise to deliver results. You'll serve as a trusted advisor to senior clients, lead multidisciplinary teams, and help build connected digital experiences that drive business impact.

 If you're energized by solving complex challenges, shaping digital innovation in healthcare, and building high-performing teams, we'd love to hear from you.

 You bring a strong point of view on the evolving digital landscape, from omnichannel engagement and personalized content to emerging search technologies and social platforms. You're equally comfortable advising senior executives, identifying growth opportunities, and bringing together specialists across disciplines to turn ambitious ideas into measurable results.

 What We're Looking For
 10+ years of health digital marketing experience within an agency environment, with a bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience.

 Proven success leading digital strategy for complex, large-scale pharmaceutical accounts, with a strong understanding of omnichannel marketing and customer experience.
 Expertise in developing integrated digital ecosystems spanning websites, CRM, paid media, search, social, and emerging digital technologies.

jobs.title: Director, Global Technology & Operations Strategy & Transformation
jobs.description:
The Director, Global Technology & Operations Strategy & Transformation will help shape and execute strategic priorities across Global Technology & Operations (GTO), with a significant focus on leading the AI program and translating strategy into measurable business outcomes.

 The Director will lead the AI program across GTO, bringing together strategy, business case development, funding, program governance, technical delivery, adoption, and value realization. This includes managing AI program funding, ensuring funding is directed to the appropriate initiatives and teams, and maintaining visibility into how initiatives are progressing against delivery commitments, defined success criteria, and approved budgets.

 Working closely with the VP of GTO and senior stakeholders across Business, Technology, Enterprise AI, Finance, and Risk, the Director will provide an integrated view of the AI program, drive accountability across teams, identify areas requiring leadership attention, and enable informed decisions on priorities, funding, execution, and outcomes.

 The Director will also help shape how GTO delivers its AI agenda, establishing approaches to prioritize and sequence initiatives, accelerate execution, and scale reusable AI capabilities across segments and countries. This includes helping establish a practical path from opportunity identification through development, production, and adoption, while focusing resources on initiatives that can deliver the greatest strategic and business impact.

 Position Responsibilities
 GTO Strategy & Transformation: Partner with the VP of GTO and senior leaders to translate strategic priorities into executable strategies, roadmaps, initiatives, and measurable outcomes. Connect priorities across teams, identify opportunities and risks, and provide insights and recommendations to support executive decision-making.
 AI Program Leadership & Governance: Lead the end-to-end AI and Automation program across GTO, establishing a single integrated view of initiatives, priorities, dependencies, funding, and outcomes. Establish program governance and operating rhythms and work across Product Owners, Segment Leads, Technology, and business and functional partners to drive execution, alignment, and accountability.
 AI Strategy, Prioritization & Delivery Approach: Help define how GTO identifies, assesses, prioritizes, sequences, and delivers AI initiatives. Develop practical prioritization and delivery approaches that consider strategic alignment, business value, delivery readiness, scalability, complexity, funding requirements, dependencies, and risk. Continuously assess the portfolio to ensure resources remain focused on the highest-value opportunities and identify where initiatives should be accelerated, repositioned, or deprioritized.
 Business Case & AI Program Funding: Lead the planning, mobilization, and partner engagement required to develop business cases for AI execution and future funding, including cost-benefit analysis, expected outcomes, success criteria, delivery requirements, and risk considerations. Manage AI program funding and recommend allocation or reallocation across initiatives and teams based on strategic priorities, expected value, delivery readiness, and performance.
 Delivery Excellence, Performance & Value Realization: Oversee AI initiatives across technical delivery, business outcomes, adoption, success criteria, budget utilization, risks, and dependencies. Assess whether initiatives are delivering against their original commitments, drive accountability for results, and identify where intervention, reprioritization, or funding adjustments are required. Ensure realized outcomes can be traced back to approved business cases and defined success measures.
 Executive Reporting & Stakeholder Management: Provide the VP of GTO and senior leadership with a consolidated view of the AI program, including roadmap progress, funding utilization, delivery performance, value realization, risks, dependencies, and decisions required. Maintain effective engagement across sponsors, segments, Technology, Enterprise AI, Finance, Risk, and other partners, translating complex information into clear executive insights and recommendations.
 AI-Driven Transformation & Reusable Capabilities: Identify opportunities to fundamentally redesign processes and ways of working through AI and Automation, moving beyond incremental improvements. Drive the development, reuse, and adoption of scalable AI capabilities, standards, playbooks, and common approaches that accelerate delivery and reduce duplication across GTO.

 Required Qualifications
 8+ years of experience across strategy and transformation, technology, AI, program management, product management, or related disciplines, with demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional programs.
 Demonstrated experience leading large-scale AI, Automation, technology, innovation, or transformation programs, including program governance, prioritization, funding, delivery oversight, and performance management.
 Strong strategic and analytical capabilities, with demonstrated experience translating strategy into prioritized programs, roadmaps, business cases, funding recommendations, and measurable outcomes.
 Strong financial acumen, including experience developing and evaluating business cases, cost-benefit analysis, managing budgets and funding, establishing success measures, and assessing value realization.
 Strong understanding of AI platforms and modern AI solution patterns, with sufficient technical fluency to understand delivery plans, challenge assumptions, assess dependencies and risks, and engage credibly with Technology and AI leaders.
 Strong program leadership capabilities, including the ability to oversee multiple concurrent initiatives, establish governance and delivery frameworks, manage complex dependencies, and drive disciplined execution across Business and Technology teams.
 Exceptional executive communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to synthesize complex strategic, financial, business, and technical information into clear insights, recommendations, and decisions for senior leadership.
 Demonstrated ability to influence and challenge senior stakeholders, drive accountability without direct authority, create structure in ambiguous environments, and manage competing strategic priorities.
 Demonstrated use of AI productivity tools and agentic workflows to accelerate analysis, synthesis, reporting, decision-making, and content development.

 Preferred Qualifications
 Experience leading or managing an enterprise-scale AI, Automation, technology, innovation, or transformation program, including prioritization, funding, delivery, and value realization.
 Experience establishing program governance, portfolio prioritization frameworks, business cases, executive reporting, and value-realization models.
 Familiarity with enterprise AI architecture, MLOps/LLMOps, AI evaluation, Responsible AI, model governance, and the considerations involved in moving AI solutions from development into production.
 Experience scaling reusable AI capabilities across multiple teams, business segments, or geographies.
 Experience partnering directly with senior executives on strategy, funding, program performance, prioritization, and enterprise transformation.
 Financial services or other highly regulated industry experience strongly preferred.

Job Description 

 What's the opportunity? 

 We're looking for a product leader to own the roadmap for RBC's internal agentic AI platform end-to-end — from intake and prioritization through delivery and measurement. As Director, Product Strategy & Roadmap, you will decide what ships and when, ground those decisions in user value and adoption evidence, and own the product experience and analytics that make the platform usable and valuable at scale.

 You will bring rigour to prioritization, fluency in agentic AI, and the credibility to partner with engineering on how the roadmap gets built — without owning the technical implementation.

 Your responsibilities will include: 
 Roadmap ownership: Maintaining and communicating a rolling 12-month roadmap with clear, evidence-based prioritization rationale

 Stakeholder intake: Capturing, assessing, and prioritizing feature requests from business lines, users, and leadership against a consistent value bar

 User experience: Owning the end-to-end product experience across the platform — how users discover, adopt, build with, and get value from it — including the self-service builder, templates, and connector catalog as part of a coherent whole.

 Product analytics: Building and maintaining adoption dashboards, usage telemetry, and value-realization measurement to drive decisions

 Delivery partnership: Partnering with engineering on acceptance criteria, backlog, and delivery quality, staying engaged to protect the user outcome

 Responsible AI in practice: Embedding the safety, governance, and transparency standards set by the AI Group's Safety and Responsible AI function into the roadmap and release gates

 Market awareness: Conducting competitive and market analysis to inform platform direction

 You're our ideal candidate if you: 
 Have 8+ years of product management experience, including 3+ in AI/ML products or enterprise platforms

 Have a strong product-experience and design sensibility — able to shape how users discover, adopt, and succeed with a product, not only what features it has.

 Have a deep working understanding of agentic AI: LLMs, tool-use, MCP connectors, RAG, and multi-agent orchestration

 Have owned and delivered a product roadmap with measurable adoption outcomes

 Are strongly analytical — able to define and track adoption metrics, build dashboards, and interpret telemetry

 Have the technical fluency to partner with engineers on architecture decisions without writing code

 Have agile delivery expertise: backlog grooming and acceptance-criteria definition

 Have financial services awareness, or the ability to develop it quickly - understanding banking end-users (advisors, analysts, operations staff) and their workflow needs

 Nice to have: 
 Bachelor's or Master's in Computer Science, Engineering, Business, HCI, or a related discipline

 Product management certification (AIPM, Pragmatic Institute, CSPO, or SAFe)

 Experience building developer platforms, APIs, or self-service builder tools

 Familiarity with AI governance frameworks (NIST AI RMF, OSFI E-23, or equivalent)

 Experience with prompt engineering, model evaluation, or fine-tuning in production

 Background at a fintech, regtech, or major bank digital team

 Drive AI transformation at one of Canada's largest and most respected financial institutions, with exposure to senior leadership across RBC

 Be part of a newly formed, high-impact function within RBC's AI Group alongside experienced transformation leaders

 A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits, competitive compensation, commissions, and stock options where applicable

 Leaders who support your development through coaching and managing opportunities

 Ability to make a difference and lasting impact from a local-to-global scale

 RBC's AI Group is the AI accelerator for RBC, with a focus on driving the shift from early-stage AI projects to scaled, client outcomes that amplify the impact of RBC's people. Neo is fast-forwarding the green energy transition by manufacturing the critical building blocks of modern, sustainable technologies. Our advanced industrial materials - including magnetic powders and magnets, specialty chemicals, metals, and alloys - enhance efficiency and performance in everyday products and next-generation innovations.

Neo operates three business segments: Magnequench, Chemicals & Oxides, and Rare Metals. With a global footprint, we have eight manufacturing facilities across China, the United States, Germany, Canada, Estonia, Thailand, and the United Kingdom, along with a dedicated research and development centre in Singapore.

Be part of a global organization driving innovation and sustainability. At Neo, you will have the opportunity to contribute to meaningful work while growing your career in a collaborative and dynamic environment.

Join us in shaping a cleaner, more sustainable future.

Role Overview:

Neo is seeking a Director to strengthen how we manage internal controls, policies and continuous improvement across its global business. This role combines ownership of the finance policy and controls environment with delivery of practical, cross-functional improvement initiatives. The Director will work with Corporate and regional Finance, IT, operations, senior management and external advisors, and will lead the Manager, Finance Systems & Data Governance and work closely with external service providers.

What you will do:

Lead the continued development and elevating Neo’s internal control environment, including control ownership, documentation, evidence standards, issue assessment and remediation tracking.

Manage external advisors by agreeing scope, evaluating recommendations and deliverables, monitoring timelines and ensuring follow-through.
Provide clear updates to senior management on control matters, remediation and transformation projects; coach the Finance Systems & Data Governance Manager.

Experience in public-company SOX level internal controls, risk advisory, internal audit, finance transformation, including building or materially improving programs — not solely testing established controls.
Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional projects and influencing stakeholders across functions and geographies.
Experience developing or maintaining finance policies, SOPs, control documentation, risk/control matrices or governance processes.
Strong understanding of financial reporting processes, IT-dependent controls, spreadsheets/end-user computing and segregation of duties.

jobs.description:
ROLE: SENIOR DIRECTOR, SOCIAL & CREATIVE STRATEGY

DEPARTMENT: CREATOR & SOCIAL

LOCATION: TORONTO, HYBRID ONSITE

Company Overview

Salt is a North American marketing agency that creates connected experiences through creative, digital & media innovation.

Our mission is to “Earn The World’s Attention” and Salt is built to find, develop, execute, and amplify the ideas that are worthy of our clients’ audiences. We’ve structured our agency to do what’s right for our clients – to connect different perspectives, to work across mediums, and to focus on delivering meaningful, effective results.

We’re committed to living up to the values in our name. “Salt of The Earth” means we value collaborative, humble, hard-working people here. We’re looking for people who are as smart as they are kind because we believe the right talent and the right culture help us do what’s right for our clients.

Role Overview

We are looking for a hybrid social strategist who balances creative vision with deep analytical rigor to guide our social and creator-led initiatives. In this role, you will act as the strategic engine for client accounts—building sharp social playbooks, scoping complex programs, consulting and collaborating with internal teams and translating performance data into clear creative direction and effective strategy.

We are looking for someone who understands social because they have actively helped shape brands’ social presences, understand how to identify culturally relevant opportunities, know how to source strategic creator partners, cultivate communities, and evolve a brand’s social approach in real time based on data and insights.

You will consult closely with our influencer execution team on strategy and creator alignment (without managing day-to-day execution) and provide strategic and creative leadership to our internal social and creator teams The ideal candidate blends high-level brand strategy with strong creative insights, deep platform knowledge, cultural curiosity, and advanced measurement fluency to prove business impact. You should have a point of view on where social is going – not just where it has been – and be excited to help both Salt and our clients push the boundaries of what brands can do in the space.

Responsibilities

Strategic Planning & Client Advisory

Develop comprehensive social playbooks, channel architectures, audience strategies, and creative frameworks for client accounts.
Turn complex brand briefs, cultural shifts, platform behaviours, and audience insights into actionable, provocative creative briefs.
Identify culturally relevant niches, communities, behaviours, and emerging opportunities where brands can credibly participate and create disproportionate impact.
Develop concise, compelling POVs on emerging social behaviours, platform changes, cultural trends and industry shifts, helping clients understand what is changing, why it matters, and how they can stay ahead of the curve.
Partner with account and executive leads to build clear scopes of work (SOWs), define deliverables, and estimate strategic/creative resource allocation.
Serve as a senior strategic voice in client presentations, campaign launches, client advisory conversations, and pitch initiatives.

Analytics, Measurement & Reporting

Guide brands through the full lifecycle of building and cultivating a social presence, from defining the initial strategy and content/platform model through ongoing optimization, experimentation, and growth.
Design robust measurement frameworks and KPI models tailored to client goals across brand awareness, engagement, and conversion.
Own and oversee monthly, quarterly, and post-campaign reporting—synthesizing data from social listening, native analytics, paid performance data, and attribution tools into clear executive summaries.
Look beyond topline metrics to understand why content is or is not working, and train teams to do the same.
Build a culture of test-and-learn across client work, using performance signals to sharpen creative output in real time.
Extract actionable insights from performance data to directly inform future creative iterations and strategic pivots.

Creative Support & Influencer Consultation

Bring a strong social and performance-led POV to creative conversations
Consult with and advise the dedicated influencer team on campaign strategy, target creator personas, and content themes to ensure strategic alignment (hands-off on logistics and campaign management).
Partner with creative teams to advise on creative social strategy on active programs.
Guide and support internal social content creators, videographers, and editors to ensure output stays grounded in platform best practices and strategic goals.
Evaluate emerging platforms, viral trends, and AI-assisted creative workflows to continuously elevate agency output.

Experience & Qualifications

Experience: 8+ years in social strategy, creative strategy, or digital analytics within an agency or high-growth brand environment.
Measurement Expertise: Advanced fluency with social analytics tools, social listening platforms, and performance reporting frameworks; proven ability to turn raw data into narrative insights.
Strategic Versatility: Direct experience authoring client-facing social playbooks, creative briefs, and campaign scoping models.
Consultative Approach: Proven ability to advise dedicated execution teams (e.g., influencer management, production) without needing to own project logistics.
Creative Mentorship: Experience coaching and inspiring internal content creators to elevate their output while maintaining strategic discipline.

Perks & Benefits That Set Us Apart

We don’t just talk about balance, growth, and culture, we build for it:

Work-Life Flexibility: Hybrid setup, up to 28 paid days off and winter holiday shutdowns
Comprehensive Coverage: Health, dental, and vision plans, plus Salt Bucks to spend on what matters to you—wellness, RRSPs, or extra time off.
Growth-Driven Culture: Dedicated Salt Days, top-tier learning access, and formal leadership development.
Celebration-First Mentality: Legendary team trips, seasonal socials, and Salt Swag that reps your squad.
Real Rewards: Referral and new business bonuses, exclusive lifestyle perks, and personalized wellness options.
Culture of Belonging: DEI programs, active ERGs, and a workplace where every voice counts.

What We Stand For

Salt of the Earth: We lead with humility, honesty, and heart—always.
Do What’s Right: No shortcuts. We choose integrity over ease, every time.
Earn Your Salt: We roll up our sleeves, chase results, and celebrate the journey.
Make Things Better: We’re solution-seekers, always pushing for smarter ways forward.
Seek Different Perspectives: Diversity fuels our thinking. Inclusion drives our impact.

The anticipated annual base salary range for this position is $150,000–$160,000. Individual compensation within this range is determined based on job-related factors such as experience, skills, level of responsibility, internal equity, and business needs. This range represents the expected base salary for this role and does not include other elements of SALT’s total rewards program.

You will lead and mentor a team of high performing data scientists and shape our growth strategy through empirical studies and experimentation. This role is resourceful, analytically rigorous, with extensive experience leading data science teams and a passion for solving product problems.

This role is a mix of consulting know-how (problem solving, thought leadership, communication), analytical proficiency in statistics, data science and machine learning, agentic workflows, and, when required, hands-on proficiency in SQL/Python programming, visualization methods and technologies, and data engineering / infrastructure.

This role is responsible for leveraging data science to assess risks, improve underwriting, detect fraud, and optimize pricing models while unlocking valuable insights, optimize processes, and inform decision-making. By implementing advanced analytics and ensuring data integrity, this role enables the organization to make informed decisions, streamline operations, and ultimately provide better coverage and services to policyholders while managing risks effectively.

What will you do :

Model Development & Deployment

Managing a data science project from end-to-end, including collaborating with partners and stakeholders to understand the business problem, obtaining data, defining an experimental design, setting up a model building pipeline, overseeing a team of data scientists to build necessary models, and working with a team of developers to implement models and managing a monitoring process
Developing and maintaining predictive models using advanced ML/AI techniques. Building Supervised and unsupervised learning models LLM workflows and agents.
overseeing the development of analytical products and machine learning models, AI models, LLM workflows and agents, building and enabling analytics infrastructure including production model deployment, as well as Non Prod experimentation, deployment and testing

Leadership & Cross-Functional Collaboration

Driving change within team and across broader Data & Analytics the importance of learning our business and the respective to help aid in our building the best solutions – be a business expert.

Research & Innovation

We’re excited to share that JDRF Canada is now Breakthrough T1D.

We’re the same organization, with the same mission and determination to realize a world free from type 1 diabetes (T1D) – just with a new name and look that reflects what the T1D community needs now and next.

It’s an exciting time to join Breakthrough T1D as we continue to break barriers to help people better manage the disease and enjoy full, healthy lives. Curing T1D is and always will be our north star and we will not stop until breakthroughs get us to a world free from T1D.

Breakthrough T1D is searching for an experienced leader in Information Technology for the role of National Director, Information Technology.

If you’re a strategic, innovative and collaborative leader who would like to lead the next chapter of the organization’s digital evolution by developing and delivering a multi-year information technology strategy, roadmap and portfolio aligned with Breakthrough T1D’s strategic priorities, please read on to see if this is the right fit for you.

Here’s what your primary responsibilities would be:

Works with the Senior Leadership Team to develop and execute a multi-year IT and digital strategy, roadmap and investment portfolio aligned with organizational priorities and supported by business cases, resource plans, budgets, performance measures and clear accountabilities.
Leads Breakthrough T1D’s responsible AI strategy and portfolio, including governance, approved-use standards, privacy and security controls, vendor due diligence, human oversight, staff education, prioritized use cases and benefits measurement.
Provides planning, resourcing, oversight and accountability for the IT portfolio, including enterprise applications, infrastructure, digital platforms, data and analytics, cybersecurity, service delivery and technology-enabled innovation.
Partners with business leaders to assess needs, select solutions and oversee the design, implementation and integration of technologies that support mission delivery, research collaboration, fundraising, advocacy and organizational operations.
Develops, implements and maintains Breakthrough T1D’s cybersecurity framework, policies and controls, aligned with organizational risk, privacy and data sovereignty requirements and applicable standards.
Leads the enterprise data and analytics strategy, including data ownership, quality, classification, integration, retention, privacy, governance, reporting and the development of trusted organizational and constituent insights.
Builds, motivates and retains a highly engaged, customer-centred information technology team aligned with Breakthrough T1D’s values, vision and strategic priorities.

Here’s what we’re looking for:

Knowledge/Skills/Experience
Bachelor’s degree in computer science, information systems, business technology or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
A minimum of seven (7) years of progressive leadership experience across information technology, digital transformation, project and portfolio management, enterprise applications, infrastructure, cybersecurity, data and service delivery, including experience leading complex enterprise-wide initiatives and multidisciplinary teams.
Demonstrated experience managing IT environments with cybersecurity, privacy, and data sovereignty requirements comparable to those of federally Canadian organizations.
Demonstrated experience leading enterprise digital transformation involving cloud platforms, enterprise architecture, systems integration, digital products, vendor ecosystems and organizational change.

Applies sound judgment, initiative and a strong sense of organization and urgency in a changing environment.
Communicates complex information clearly and credibly to technical and non-technical stakeholders, senior executives and governance bodies.
Demonstrates strong business analysis, project and financial management capabilities and a record of leading successful cross-functional initiatives.

Project, program, technology governance, security or service management certification is an asset.
Translates organizational strategy and stakeholder needs into practical technology priorities, investment decisions and outcomes.

Breakthrough T1D is the leading type 1 diabetes (T1D) research and advocacy non-profit organization in Canada. As we drive toward curing type 1 diabetes, we help to make every day better for the people who live with it.

Breakthrough T1D is committed to investing in the most promising research, advocating for progress by working with governments to address issues that impact the T1D community, and supporting individuals living with this disease.

Job Description:

Role Summary

The AVP Technology Lead – Digital is a strategic technology leader responsible for enabling, scaling, and modernizing Sun Life Canada’s shared digital platforms that support secure, connected, and frictionless Client and advisor experiences. This role provides technology leadership across core digital assets including Secure Web, Public Web, & Secure Mobile, and related enablement platforms such as client identity and access management, and an internal design system.

The role combines strategic leadership, technical oversight, people leadership, delivery execution, operational accountability, and vendor/financial management to drive technology excellence and measurable business value. The AVP partners closely with Product, Client Experience, Architecture, Cybersecurity, Operations, Engineering, and Business leaders to ensure digital assets are resilient, scalable, secure, reusable, and aligned to enterprise priorities.

This role operates in a complex, high-visibility environment where digital platform reliability, modernization, and cross-business enablement are critical to Client outcomes. The leader must be able to bring clarity to a broad mandate, make decisions in ambiguity, and build a high-performing technology organization that balances speed, stability, security, and long-term platform health.

What will you do?

Technology Strategy, Platform Enablement & Engineering
Shape, communicate, and align the digital technology strategy across business units, ensuring it supports near-term delivery commitments and longer-term modernization objectives.
Partner with Business Leads, Product, Client Experience, Architecture, Cybersecurity, Operations, and Enterprise Technology to define platform roadmaps, OKRs, sequencing, and investment priorities.
Provide thought leadership on the evolution of shared digital platforms, including identity, web, mobile, integration, data enablement, and reusable digital capabilities.
Promote technology stack standards, modern engineering practices, automation, and architectural discipline, balancing build vs. buy vs. partner decisions in a complex technology ecosystem.
Ensure design and engineering decisions account for reusability, scalability, security, maintainability, accessibility, and technical debt reduction.
Create the conditions for exceptional digital experiences by enabling business and product teams with reliable, scalable, secure, and reusable platforms.
Platform Delivery & Execution
Accountable for end-to-end delivery of digital platform capabilities, including oversight of internal delivery teams, vendors, system integrators, and total cost of ownership.
Drive delivery excellence by improving velocity, quality, reliability, predictability, and agile maturity across multiple squads.
Track delivery metrics, identify bottlenecks, and implement targeted productivity and delivery maturity improvements.
Serve as the primary escalation point for platform, delivery, vendor, and dependency-related issues, enabling rapid resolution in a complex environment.
Ensure delivery is integrated across product, architecture, engineering, operations, cybersecurity, and business priorities.
Embed test-and-learn, automation, and continuous improvement practices to improve speed, quality, and sustainability.
People Leadership & Capability Development
Lead, mentor, and develop technology leaders and teams, fostering a collaborative, inclusive, accountable, and execution-focused culture.
Design and optimize team structures to support clear ownership, delivery outcomes, modernization priorities, and clear accountabilities.
Partner with Chapter, Engineering, Product, and Business leaders on workforce planning, role clarity, succession planning, and capability development.
Build internal capability in digital engineering, enablement, agile delivery, vendor management, and operational excellence.
Coach leaders to manage performance effectively, clarify ownership, and build resilient teams through change and transformation.
Financial & Vendor Management
Lead budget management, including annual planning, cost tracking, capitalization, forecasting, and investment prioritization.
Manage strategic vendor and system integrator relationships, holding partners accountable for delivery quality, outcomes, knowledge transfer, and value realization.
Drive cost transparency and technology spend optimization across applications, infrastructure, security, vendor, and platform investments.
Identify opportunities to reduce long-term dependency on external partners while strengthening internal platform ownership and capability.
Operational Excellence, Risk & Security
Ensure stability, security, technology currency, resiliency, and end-of-life decommissioning for applications within scope.
Establish governance processes that balance speed of delivery with risk management, audit, regulatory, cybersecurity, and control requirements.
Partner with Application Operations to ensure effective incident management, change management, disaster recovery, and business continuity planning.
Proactively manage operational risk, application health, technical debt, and service reliability across shared digital capabilities.
Cross-Functional Collaboration & Stakeholder Engagement
Act as a strategic technology partner to leaders across Product, Client Experience, Business, Operations, Architecture, Cybersecurity, and Enterprise Technology.
Communicate digital strategy, delivery status, risks, trade-offs, and dependencies with clarity and transparency.
Represent the Digital technology function in executive forums, bringing enterprise perspective, external insight, and pragmatic recommendations.
Strengthen alignment between technology investments, business priorities, Client experience outcomes, and enterprise digital strategy.

Accountabilities

Align digital strategy with business objectives, Client outcomes, enterprise standards, and shared technology priorities.
Define and monitor roadmaps, OKRs, modernization priorities, and delivery sequencing.
Oversee execution across delivery teams, vendors, system integrators, and enterprise partners.
Establish governance, track delivery metrics, and drive productivity, quality, and reliability improvements.
Manage budgets, vendor relationships, and cost optimization opportunities.
Build and sustain a high-performing, engaged, inclusive, and platform-oriented technology organization.
Ensure digital platforms are secure, scalable, resilient, reusable, and positioned to support future growth.

What you need to succeed?

Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field; advanced degree or MBA is an asset.
10+ years of experience in senior technology leadership roles with demonstrated success delivering complex, mission-critical digital platforms.
Experience leading modernization and enablement of digital platforms such as identity, web, mobile, integration, or client/advisor experience platforms.
Proven ability to lead technology teams through transformation, platform ownership, and operating model evolution.
Strong financial acumen with experience managing sizable technology budgets, vendor portfolios, and total cost of ownership.
Strong stakeholder management, executive communication, and organizational leadership skills.
Experience in regulated financial services is valuable; depth in digital enablement, engineering excellence, and vendor-heavy delivery environments is prioritized.
As this position is posted in several locations, we specify that bilingualism (French, English, both oral and written) is required for Quebec only for the frequent interactions with English and French-speaking colleagues or internal partners across Canada or worldwide

Mindset & Behaviours

Decisive leader comfortable operating in ambiguity, complexity, and transformation.
Strong technical credibility with the ability to challenge architecture, delivery practices, platform decisions, and CI/CD approaches.
Builder mindset with equal focus on fixing, scaling, enabling, and simplifying.
Pragmatic, outcomes-driven decision-maker who balances speed, stability, risk, and long-term application health.
Collaborative leader who builds trust, drives momentum, and creates clarity across complex stakeholder groups.
Critical thinker who challenges the status quo constructively and drives continuous improvement.

What’s in it for you?

We are seeking a Director, Planning, Procurement & Inventory to lead the enterprise function that turns customer demand into a credible, executable supply plan, secures material availability, and optimizes inventory across regions and fulfilment models.

This is an opportunity to bring Demand Planning, Supply and Production Planning, Tactical Procurement, and Inventory into one connected operating model. You will lead through significant organizational and ERP-enabled change while improving customer service and working capital together.

This position is located in London, Ontario, and will be onsite.

Lead enterprise planning and SIOP. Own demand planning, forecasting, executive SIOP, the approved enterprise supply plan, planning risk, and cross-functional escalation across regions and businesses.
Strengthen supply and production planning. Lead master production scheduling, MRP, material-availability management, shortage recovery, and planning logic across Make-to-Stock, Engineer-to-Order, Configure-to-Order, and aftermarket flows.
Direct tactical procurement and inventory governance. Lead tactical buying, supplier-delivery performance, purchasing master data, inventory strategy, service-level policy, E&O governance, record accuracy, and inventory improvement.
Own Procurement Planning & inventory business processes through ERP transformation. Lead relevant Order-to-Cash and Procure-to-Pay workstreams from design and testing through cutover, adoption, stabilization, process governance, and master-data health.
Build one capable enterprise organization. Establish a common KPI architecture, management cadence, decision rights, standard work, talent development, succession coverage, and an everyday continuous-improvement operating system.

A bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Operations, Business, or a related field.
Progressive leadership of enterprise planning, tactical procurement, and inventory in a complex manufacturing environment.
Demonstrated leadership across a combination of Make-to-Stock, Engineer-to-Order, Configure-to-Order, and aftermarket or service-parts planning.
Direct ownership of Demand Planning and an executive S&OP or SIOP process that drove cross-functional decisions.
End-to-end leadership of a major ERP business-process transformation covering design, testing, cutover, adoption, and stabilization.

Experience leading substantial tactical buying and multi-site or multi-region inventory, with evidence of improved service, supplier delivery, inventory productivity, and record accuracy.
Experience with Infor LN or a comparable enterprise ERP, APICS CPIM or CSCP certification, Lean or Six Sigma certification, or deployment of VES, DBS, Lean, or a comparable operating system.

You will shape how demand, supply, procurement, inventory, commercial requirements, manufacturing execution, customer service, logistics, finance, and technology connect around one enterprise plan. The Financial Advisory Team at Teneo

Teneo’s global Financial Advisory business advises corporates, creditors and other financial stakeholders in situations of financial stress and distress. No two situations are the same. Our advice and approach is tailored to each situation and each client. At Teneo, we believe such occurrences present new opportunities for our clients. Opportunities to restore value, raise new capital, pivot in a new direction and ultimately, identify certainty amidst chaos. Teneo partners with clients to find viable opportunities that will protect and enhance value and help them to build strategies that will most benefit their business and/or investment goals.

Integrating the disciplines of financial advisory, management consulting, investor relations, strategic communications, government affairs, risk analysis and talent advisory, Teneo’s global Financial Advisory team guides companies and their stakeholders through periods of uncertainty and stress. We help address the challenges a business faces, whether that is targeted performance improvement to Financial Advisory, or delivering a route to recover value, our focus is delivering certainty from uncertainty.

Teneo is expanding its already established global Financial Advisory footprint, now in Canada. The Canadian Financial Advisory team will join forces with the already established Strategy and Communications platform which has offices in Toronto, Montreal and Calgary. We are hiring at several levels.

The Role – Associate Director, Toronto

This is an excellent opportunity to work alongside our established team who will support you to utilise and enhance your advisory skills and experience. You will work alongside some of the most experienced practitioners in the field advising the boards, management teams, lenders and shareholders of companies which are underperforming and/or facing any financial stress.

As an Associate Director / Director in the team, you will have the opportunity to work and lead on a diverse range of engagements across all sectors, with plenty of responsibility for leading workstreams, managing junior staff and supporting Directors and Managing Directors in client-facing delivery.

Key Responsibilities

Client Service

Preparation of engagement letter(s) and ensuring adherence to all compliance requirements.
Manage parts or all of the engagement, providing support to the Managing Director/ Director (or often directly to Senior Managing Director) in managing external stakeholders.
Managing insolvency engagements under the Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act, the Companies’ Creditors Arrangement Act and other statutes.
Support management teams in preparing and challenging business plans, short term cash flow forecasts and Financial Advisory plans.
Providing comprehensive financial restructuring and cash management services to identify working capital and other cash flow improvements.
Reviewing and stress-testing integrated business plans, budgeting and forecasting models using a fact-based, data driven approach, including KPI definition, data visualization, reporting automation and touchless forecasting.
Establishment or enhancement of company finance functions and processes.
Develop, analyse and present Financial Advisory options using input from other teams, e.g. insolvency or tax analysis, sector and financial modelling. Liaise with the Company’s legal advisors to understand key aspects of legal documentation and also drive any documentation processes (term sheets, waivers, loan documentation etc.)
Apply an understanding of engagement economics.
Apply an understanding of financial and risk management.

Knowledge Acquisition

Build client relationship skills, sector knowledge and continue to develop leadership skills.
Continue to build technical expertise, broader business advisory and people management skills.
Understand the market, topical issues and our Financial Advisory propositions.

People and Leadership

Support practice and talent development.
Provide on-job coaching and development to staff.
Develop junior staff outside of jobs through appraising and mentoring.
Support wider Financial Advisory training initiatives.
Manage diverse teams within an inclusive team culture where people are recognised for their contribution.

Business Development

Start to own elements of business development including actively supporting business development activities, building and expending your own contact network and supporting Director/ Managing Director/Senior Managing Director-led marketing and sales activities.
Participate in existing business development programmes and key client accounts.
Identify opportunities to expand engagments as well as opportunities to provide wider Teneo services to existing clients.
Take responsibility for leading marketing initiatives aimed at specific channels to market, or events.

Key Skills & Experience

Qualified accountant (CPA or equivalent), both time and exam qualified.
Financial Advisory experience gained either as an advisor within a professional services company, consultancy or investment bank; as an analyst in a debt or special situations funds. An understanding of debt markets, banking, loan agreements and other relevant financial and legal documentation.
Understanding of financial statements and related data to assess historical financial performance and future outlook for client companies and prospects.
Good understanding of the Financial Advisory marketplace, its trends, and key players (principals and advisors).
Very strong analytical skills, including: business analytics, business planning, short term cash flows, financing options. A basic understanding of insolvency legislation and practice is not a prerequisite but helpful.
Excellent interpersonal skills.
Strong project management skills, with ability to lead mid-large teams and develop people.

What We Offer

As a Teneo employee, you'll enjoy unique benefits including flexible time off policy; medical, dental, and vision coverage; long-term disability, and life insurance; RRSP plan with corporate matching; team events; snacks; and other perks.

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

Teneo is an equal opportunity employer and promotes a diverse and inclusive workplace. Teneo considers all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, creed, national origin, age, sex, marital status, ancestry, disability, veteran status, gender identity, genetic information, or sexual orientation or any other status protected by applicable law.

Total Compensation Package

Expected compensation for Associate Director is CAD110,000 - CAD160,000 plus annualized bonus. Expected compensation for Director level is CAD150,000 - CAD200,000 plus annualized bonus.

RRSP match, healthcare coverage and a broad range of additional benefits and perks.

About Teneo

Teneo is the global CEO advisory firm. We partner with our clients globally to do great things for a better future.

Drawing upon our global team and expansive network of senior advisors, we provide advisory services across our five business segments on a stand-alone or fully integrated basis to help our clients solve complex business challenges. Our clients include a significant number of the Fortune 100 and FTSE 100, as well as other corporations, financial institutions, and organizations.

Our full range of advisory services includes strategic communications, investor relations, financial transactions and restructuring, management consulting, physical and cyber risk, organizational design, board and executive search, geopolitics and government affairs, corporate governance, ESG and DE&I.

Nobis is a Canadian-founded global performance luxury outerwear brand known for combining technical innovation with refined design. With distribution across North America, Europe, and Asia, Nobis operates through a mix of direct-to-consumer, wholesale, and international partnerships, including a joint venture in Asia.

About the Role

We are hiring a Director of Finance to lead financial strategy and operations across Nobis and the InnoVision Group, its parent company. This role sits at the intersection of global operations, multi-channel growth (DTC and wholesale), and financial discipline. It requires a leader who can balance strategic thinking with rigorous cash flow management and operational efficiency.

As the business continues to evolve across multiple markets and channels, we are focused on strengthening our financial foundation: enhancing visibility, improving cash flow discipline, and ensuring sustainable, profitable growth.

We are looking for someone who doesn’t wait to be asked. You will get close to the business, understand how every team operates, and use that knowledge to turn finance into a true partner in decision-making.

Financial Strategy & Planning

Lead annual budgeting, forecasting, and multi-year financial planning
Support leadership with scenario modeling, investment analysis, and strategic decision-making
Provide financial insight to support growth initiatives while maintaining discipline on profitability

Reporting & Performance

Deliver timely, accurate financial reporting with clear, actionable insights
Drive visibility into performance by channel and market
Identify opportunities for margin improvement, cost optimization, and operational efficiency

Operations & Cash Management

Oversee core finance functions including AP/AR, payroll, and product costing
Own cash flow planning, liquidity management, and working capital optimization
Maintain and strengthen internal controls and financial processes

Business Partnership & Initiative

Proactively engage with teams across the business, including sales, merchandising, product, operations, marketing, and e-commerce, to understand how they work and what drives their results
Take initiative to identify risks, opportunities, and improvements before they are raised, and bring forward recommendations, not just reports
Act as a trusted finance partner to leadership and department heads, translating numbers into clear, practical guidance

Global Partnerships

Oversee financial operations and reporting across international JVs and distributors, particularly in Asia
Partner with global stakeholders to ensure alignment, transparency, and accountability

Systems, Infrastructure & AI

Lead ongoing development and optimization of financial systems (NetSuite preferred)
Enhance dashboards and reporting tools to support data-driven decision-making
Adopt AI tools responsibly to improve workflows and generate insight, with verification of every output before it informs a decision

jobs.title: Head of Machine Learning
jobs.description:
Company Description
Uyir Lab is an AI research lab focused on making AI agents accurate in underrepresented languages, as they are truly spoken in everyday life. The lab addresses gaps in dialects, code-mixing, and cultural context for languages that are widely spoken but barely present on the web, starting with Tamil and expanding to Sinhala, Punjabi, Swahili, Hausa, Amharic, Fula, Oromo, Javanese, Bhojpuri, and more. Uyir Lab’s approach combines consented voice data from native speakers, deep linguistic mapping, and proprietary models like Nila for Tamil, delivered via a “Language Brain” layer that plugs into existing AI agents. As AI takes on critical work in sectors such as banking, health, and customer service, Uyir Lab’s mission is to reduce costly misunderstandings and give every language a life in AI, working closely with agent builders, native speakers, and community partners.
Role Description
The Head of Machine Learning is a full-time remote role leading the design, development, and deployment of language-focused ML systems across Uyir Lab’s growing portfolio of models and languages. This position oversees end-to-end machine learning pipelines: defining research directions, shaping model architectures, guiding experimentation, and driving productionization of models for real-world AI agents. The role includes managing and mentoring a multidisciplinary ML team, collaborating with data engineers and linguists to build high-quality datasets, and ensuring robust evaluation for dialect-aware, culturally grounded performance. The Head of Machine Learning partners with product and engineering teams to integrate Uyir Lab’s “Language Brain” into external applications, sets technical standards for scalability and reliability, and contributes to strategic decisions about new languages, platforms, and partnerships.
Qualifications

Strong foundations in Computer Science, including algorithms, data structures, distributed computing, and software engineering best practices.
Expertise in Machine Learning and Data Science, covering model development, training at scale, evaluation, optimization, and experimentation workflows.
Specialized experience in Natural Language Processing (NLP), particularly for low-resource or multilingual settings, including sequence models, transformers, and representation learning.
Hands-on skills in Pattern Recognition, statistical modeling, and signal processing methods relevant to speech, text, and multimodal data.
Proficiency with modern ML ecosystems (e.g., Python, PyTorch or TensorFlow, Hugging Face, ML Ops tools) and cloud-based training infrastructure.
Demonstrated experience leading ML or research teams, setting technical direction, and delivering production-ready models in collaboration with product and engineering.
Background in building or improving language technologies (ASR, MT, chatbots, dialogue systems, or language understanding) is highly beneficial.

You will help take our clients along a transformative journey in their thinking about what is possible with data and AI. This will result in large\-scale engagements with direct links to the C\-suite. You will run early discovery, define solutions, shape SOWs, and represent Datatonic’s offerings in the market.


You do not need to manage people, but you must be exceptional with **technical and business stakeholders**, able to build trust quickly, and comfortable presenting at C\-suite and architect levels.

**What You’ll Do**

### **Pre\-Sales Leadership**

* Lead early discovery alongside Sales: understand business pain points, qualify opportunities, and translate ambiguity into structured technical narratives.
* Take an insight\-led approach to bring industry best practices in data and AI to shape and guide clients’ strategic transformations
* Architect data, ML, and GenAI solutions on Google Cloud.
* Own scoping, estimation, and writing of Statements of Work and RFP responses in collaboration with Sales and Delivery.
* Support RFP responses, solution reviews, and deal strategy for opportunities and accounts $1m\+.

### **Strategic Advisory**

* Facilitate client workshops on AI strategy, platform modernization, and GenAI readiness, with a lens toward bringing our clients along on a transformative journey in their approach to data and AI.
* Build POVs and architecture options that balance business value, feasibility, and cost.
* Act as a trusted advisor for our clients across data platforms, MLOps, Generative and Agentic AI, and application design.

### **Thought Leadership, GTM \& Vertical Expertise**

* Represent Datatonic on site at client, at events, conferences, partner sessions, and executive dinners
* Work with our GTM team to create industry\-relevant content (decks, briefs, POVs) tailored for **Telecommunications, FSI, Media, and Agencies** and help shape our offering by surfacing patterns, reusable architectures, and packaged solutions.
* Work with the Office of the CTO and our Architecture delivery team to establish standards, handbooks, and technical best practices for data and agentic deployments.
* Enable Sales and Delivery teams on industry trends, discovery patterns, and Datatonic accelerators.

**What You Bring**

* 7–12 years of experience in data, analytics, ML, or cloud engineering/architecture, including in large scale digital/data/AI transformations, with at least 3 years in a pre\-sales or client\-facing advisory role.
* Strong knowledge of cloud\-based architectures (including infrastructure, data architecture, governance), application design, and Generative and Agentic AI concepts and deployments.
* Hands\-on depth in **GCP is ideal**, but strong AWS/Azure SAs with a proven ability to cross\-skill to GCP quickly will be considered.
* Excellent written and verbal communication; able to simplify complex technical ideas for business leaders.
* A consultative sales approach with experience shaping deals over **$1M**.
* Comfortable presenting to C\-suite, negotiating trade\-offs, and influencing stakeholders.
* Ideally, a track record in at least one of our verticals: **Telecommunications, FSI, Media, and Agencies**

**What Success Looks Like (first 12 months)**

* Consistently shaping and winning large scale data and AI transformations for our biggest clients.
* Recognized by Sales as the go\-to technical partner for complex pursuits.
* Recognized by Delivery for the accuracy of SOW scoping and technical leadership when needed.
* Trusted by strategic accounts as a value\-driven advisor.
* Strong contribution as a thought leader to vertical narratives, events, and Datatonic’s GTM.

 As part of the Group Risk Management team, the Associate Director, Global Risk Analytics is responsible for the conceptual design, development, and ongoing maintenance of the mathematical models used for the measurement and capitalization of the market risk of RBC's trading portfolio.

on a permanent full-time basis within our Finance team. This position is a hybrid
opportunity and is based in Saskatoon, SK
.

As the Associate Vice President, Corporate Finance, you'll provide leadership across Financial Planning & Analysis, Corporate Accounting, Treasury & Credit and Risk & Insurance ensuring the function delivers strong financial stewardship, insight and support for FCL’s enterprise priorities. This is an opportunity to influence executive decision-making, build high-performing teams, and help strengthen FCL’s long term financial performance.

What you’ll do:

Lead Corporate Finance as an integrated, high performing function, ensuring alignment across Financial Planning & Analysis, Corporate Accounting, Treasury, Credit and Insurance while fostering strong collaboration, clear accountabilities, operational excellence and strong business partnerships across FCL.
Serve as a key strategic partner to the Vice President Finance, helping translate enterprise priorities into action while providing trusted advice and independent financial perspective that supports sound enterprise decision-making, capital allocation, and long-term organizational performance.
Oversee enterprise financial planning and analysis, financial reporting, and controllership ensuring accurate financial information, meaningful business insights, and disciplined financial stewardship.
Guide treasury, credit, and financial risk strategies to support FCL's long-term financial sustainability and strategic objectives.
Champion strong governance and financial controls while driving continuous improvement across Corporate Finance.
Provide leadership for Corporate Finance led strategic initiatives and support broader enterprise initiatives as required, ensuring strong Corporate Finance alignment, support and execution.
Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing leadership team while fostering a culture of collaboration, performance, accountability, and continuous improvement across Corporate Finance.

Who you’ll work with:

The Team:
Reporting to the Vice President, Finance, you'll lead a diverse team of finance leaders, including the Director, Corporate Accounting, Director, Financial Planning & Analysis, Senior Manager, Treasury & Credit and Manager, Risk & Insurance. You'll work closely with the Vice President Finance and Leaders across FCL to advance enterprise and Finance priorities while ensuring Corporate Finance provides strong financial leadership, insight and support to the organization.

Why it matters:

We help local Co-ops grow and thrive by offering a range of professional services, including marketing, market research, information technology, human resources, accounting, risk management and business development.

Who you are:

You are looking for a career in Finance and:
Have 15+ years of progressive finance leadership experience across multiple disciplines, including Financial Planning & Analysis, Corporate Accounting, Treasury, Corporate Finance, Capital Planning, or Risk Management.
Have a degree in Business or Commerce. An MBA, CFA, CBV or equivalent advanced designation considered an asset.
Hold a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation.

Competitive salaries, short-term incentives, a comprehensive benefits package, and an employer-contributed pension plan.
Encouragement to take advantage of learning opportunities to grow and develop as a Team Member.
As a co-operative, we do business differently. We believe in working together to serve Western Canadians, delivering profits back to our communities and investing in sustainable growth. To learn more about who we are and what we offer, visit www.fcl.crs.
