Reporting to the CEO, the Vice President will provide enterprise-wide leadership across Finance and corporate services, while serving as a trusted advisor to the CEO, Board of Directors, and senior leadership team.

The organization delivers essential services to a large and diverse client base. Behind every service are countless financial, operational, and strategic decisions that turn resources into meaningful impact. As Vice President, Finance, the successful candidate will ensure the financial strength, insight, and discipline needed to advance the mission and support long-term sustainability.

This is an exceptional opportunity for an accomplished finance executive who combines strategic insight with operational leadership and wants to influence meaningful outcomes in a purpose-driven organization. More than a functional leader, the Vice President will be a key enterprise partner, helping shape strategy, support growth, and position the organization for continued success in a complex operating environment.

The Mandate

The mandate extends well beyond traditional financial stewardship. As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, the VP will help shape organizational strategy, support evidence-based decision-making, and ensure the long-term sustainability of an organization delivering critical services.

In partnership with the CEO, Board, and senior leadership team, the VP will provide strategic financial leadership across planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, treasury, audit, risk management, and compliance. They will ensure financial resources are aligned with organizational priorities while maintaining the discipline and accountability the mission requires.

A key priority will be supporting the organization through a period of growth and change. Using financial insights and performance data, the VP will help evaluate opportunities, inform strategic initiatives, and optimize the deployment of resources in a complex funding and operating environment. Success will require balancing long-term vision with disciplined execution and sound financial management.

Beyond finance, the VP will provide executive oversight of key corporate services, including procurement and facilities, ensuring effective stewardship of organizational resources and infrastructure. The role will also lead efforts to strengthen internal capabilities, foster collaboration across departments, and build a high-performing, engaged team.

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to evolve the finance function from a trusted service provider into an even more proactive strategic partner and to enable data-driven decision-making across the organization. Success will be measured not only by financial outcomes, but also by the ability to influence strategy, support growth, and contribute to long-term sustainability and impact.

Leadership and Stewardship

The organization is seeking a VP Finance who leads with maturity and earns trust through action. This is not a role for someone who relies on title or tenure to get things done. The culture here rewards people who show up prepared, communicate clearly, and follow through.
Operates with humility, credibility, and sound judgment
Brings a practical, solutions-oriented mindset
Communicates clearly and influences at all levels
A good partner to the program managers – asking what they need before explaining what the number say
Leads with integrity, accountability, and transparency

Ideal Background

The successful candidate will bring experience in social services, healthcare, the boarder public sector, or the not-for-profit sector. Those who understand the operational, funding, and stakeholder dynamics of publicly funded organizations will be particular well positioned for success.
A CPA designation and progressive senior finance leadership experience.
Experience leading finance within a complex, multi-stakeholder organization.
A strong understanding of financial planning, financial reporting, treasury, governance, risk management, and internal controls.
Experience working with Boards and senior executives in a strategic advisory capacity.
The ability to translate financial information into actionable business insights.
A collaborative leadership style and a reputation for building strong relationships across an organization.

Why This Role

This is a rare opportunity to combine executive-level impact with genuine purpose. As a strategic partner to the CEO and Executive Leadership Team, the Vice President, Finance will help shape decisions that influence the organization’s direction, sustainability, and growth.

The successful candidate will join an organization at an exciting point in its journey, with the opportunity to strengthen financial stewardship, support strategic priorities, and help position the organization for continued success. The organization measures its success not only by financial performance, but by the positive impact it has on the people and communities it serves.

If you are ready to make a meaningful impact and help shape the future of a mission-driven organization, we encourage you to apply in confidence.

Development and use of business and financial analytics to support operations decisions.
Effective use of financial accountability and reporting systems.
Application and use of internal controls.
Development of organization, program, or product budgets.
Experience leading organization-wide financial planning efforts and establishing process timelines and deliverables.
Knowledge and application of generally accepted accounting principles.

Preferred Qualifications

Technical Skills:

Advanced degree (Master’s or higher) in Business, Finance, Accounting, Public Administration, Economics, or a related field.
Professional certification such as CPA, CMA, CGFM, or CGMA.
Demonstrated leadership of enterprise-level financial planning and analysis functions, including forecasting, scenario modeling, and development of data-driven insights used for strategic decision-making.

Experience leading large-scale financial system implementations, upgrades, or integrations across multiple divisions.

Leadership Experience

Demonstrated success managing and developing leaders and teams, including performance management, coaching, and succession planning.
Proven experience driving organization-wide process improvements or operational transformation efforts within a large organization (approx. 500+ employees).
Experience representing financial information to executive leadership, legislative bodies, oversight agencies, or public audiences, with the ability to explain complex financial content to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Demonstrated ability to build and maintain effective partnerships with internal divisions, external agencies, and community or governmental stakeholders.
Experience fostering an inclusive, respectful, and equity-driven workplace, including working effectively with individuals from diverse backgrounds and ensuring equitable operational and leadership practices

This will include, but is not limited to, verification of degrees and licensures, state and federal criminal history checks, and a review of tax filing and payment history. All individual income tax filing and payment obligations must be current prior to interviewing for this position.

jobs.title: Senior Director, GTM AI Product Leader
jobs.description:
Job Description

We are looking for a Senior Director to own the AI roadmap and strategy for our go-to-market organization: Sales, Customer Success, Professional Services, and Partnerships. You will partner with our segments and RevOps to decide where AI creates the most value across the customer lifecycle, and work with Engineering to deliver it through a deliberate mix of best-in-class SaaS platforms (such as Salesforce, Gong) and custom-built solutions where off-the-shelf products fall short.

You will work with internal stakeholders to define the problems worth solving, prioritize ruthlessly, and measure adoption and business impact. You will be the accountable leader for how AI shows up in the way we sell, onboard, deliver, retain, and grow with customers and partners.

Key Responsibilities

GTM AI strategy and roadmap

Define and own a multi-year AI vision and a quarterly roadmap spanning Sales, Customer Success, Professional Services, and Partnerships.
Identify, size, and prioritize AI use cases by revenue impact, productivity gain, cost to serve, and feasibility.
Establish clear principles for build vs. buy vs. configure, and make those calls transparently with business cases and total cost of ownership.
Align the GTM AI roadmap with company strategy, revenue targets, and the broader enterprise AI and data strategy.
Rationalize and govern overlapping tools and prevent AI sprawl across the GTM organization.
Run discovery, prototyping, pilots, and scale-up with clear success criteria and stage gates.

AI Across The GTM Functions

Sales: AI for prospecting and account research, lead and opportunity scoring, call and meeting intelligence, deal inspection and forecasting, proposal and RFP generation, pricing and quoting guidance, and rep coaching and ramp.
Customer Success: AI for health scoring and churn prediction, renewal and expansion signals, automated QBR and meeting prep, sentiment and call analysis, onboarding acceleration, and proactive risk alerts.
Professional Services: AI for scoping and estimation, project planning, knowledge retrieval, delivery acceleration, resource allocation, utilization, and margin improvement.
Partnerships: AI for partner identification and tiering, co-sell and pipeline insight, partner enablement, and ecosystem performance analytics.
Design cross-functional workflows that connect these motions, such as handoffs from sales to onboarding to delivery to renewal, so AI improves the whole customer lifecycle rather than isolated steps.

Adoption, change management, and value realization

Own adoption by partnering with Revenue Operations, enablement, and functional leaders on training, playbooks, and incentives so tools become part of daily work.
Define and report a KPI framework covering usage, productivity, pipeline and win rate, forecast accuracy, retention and expansion, services margin, and partner-sourced revenue.
Quantify ROI and report outcomes to executive leadership on a regular cadence.

Governance, data, and responsible AI

Work with Legal, Security, Privacy, and IT to set guardrails for AI use with customer and partner data, including access controls, data residency, model usage policies, and auditability.
Ensure AI outputs are trustworthy and that humans remain appropriately in the loop for high-stakes decisions.
Partner with Data and Analytics on data quality, definitions, and a shared source of truth.

Leadership and operating model

Build and lead a team of product managers and business analysts, and influence a broader matrixed group of Engineering, Data, and GTM Operations partners.
Establish intake, prioritization, and governance processes so GTM leaders (CRO, CCO, Services, Partnerships) jointly steer the roadmap.
Act as the executive-level voice on GTM AI, internally and externally, including with vendors, analysts, and peer companies.

Required Qualifications

12+ years of experience in product management, GTM operations or strategy, sales or revenue technology, or related roles, with 5+ years leading teams.
Demonstrated success owning a technology roadmap that serves revenue-generating teams, ideally across more than one of Sales, Customer Success, Professional Services, and Partnerships.
Deep working knowledge of the GTM technology stack, including Salesforce and conversation intelligence tools like Gong, and how data flows between systems.
Hands-on experience delivering AI/ML or generative AI solutions into production, including a practical understanding of LLMs, agents, retrieval, prompt and workflow design, evaluation, and cost management.
Strong build-vs-buy judgment, vendor management experience, and comfort building business cases.
Proven ability to drive change and adoption among frontline revenue teams and senior business leaders.
Excellent executive communication, with the ability to translate between technical teams and business stakeholders.
Analytical rigor and a bias toward measurable outcomes.

Preferred Qualifications

Prior experience as a sales, customer success, or services practitioner or leader, or in a hybrid GTM + product role.
Experience with Salesforce platform capabilities (Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Agentforce or equivalent AI features), data cloud or warehouse integrations, and Gong or similar conversation intelligence tools.
Experience in a B2B, enterprise, or professional-services-oriented environment with long sales cycles and complex account structures.
Familiarity with partner ecosystems, co-sell motions, and channel programs.
Experience establishing AI governance and responsible-AI practices.

This posting is for proactive recruitment purposes and may be used to fill current openings or future vacancies within our organization.

What’s in it For You?

Hybrid Work Model: We’ve adopted a flexible hybrid working environment for our office-based roles while delivering a seamless experience that is digitally and physically connected.
Flexibility & Work-Life Balance: Flex My Way is a set of supportive workplace policies designed to help manage personal and professional responsibilities, whether caring for family, giving back to the community, or finding time to refresh and reset. Industry Competitive Benefits: We offer comprehensive benefit plans to include flexible vacation, two company-wide Mental Health Days off, access to the Headspace app, retirement savings, tuition reimbursement, employee incentive programs, and resources for mental, physical, and financial wellbeing.

Social Impact: Make an impact in your community with our Social Impact Institute. We offer employees two paid volunteer days off annually and opportunities to get involved with pro-bono consulting projects and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives.

Toronto, Ontario, Canada

37\.5

TD Securities
**Pay Details:**

150 000 $/$150,000 \- 160 000 $/$160,000 CAD
This role is eligible for a discretionary variable compensation award that considers business and individual performance.
TD is committed to providing fair and equitable compensation opportunities to all colleagues. Growth opportunities and skill development are defining features of the colleague experience at TD. Our compensation policies and practices have been designed to allow colleagues to progress through the salary range over time as they progress in their role. The base pay actually offered may vary based upon the candidate's skills and experience, job\-related knowledge, geographic location, and other specific business and organizational needs.


As a candidate, you are encouraged to ask compensation related questions and have an open dialogue with your recruiter who can provide you more specific details for this role.


**Job Description:**

TD Securities ("TDS") provides a wide range of capital market products and services to corporate, government and institutional clients through Global Transaction Banking ("GTB"), Corporate and Investment Banking ("CIB"), and Global Markets ("GM"). The firm works with clients around the world, focusing selectively and strategically on key global financial centers: Toronto, Montreal, Calgary, Vancouver, New York, London, Singapore, and Tokyo. www.td.com


GTB is a key growth business within TDS that provides the opportunity to make an impact with top tier organizations. We offer innovative solutions and treasury advisory services on large and complex liquidity, payments, and trade and working capital finance needs. The business constantly changes with macroeconomic conditions, unprecedented levels of innovation, interest rate environments, and Foreign Exchange ("FX") movements. Accordingly, GTB continues to invest and innovate to support our clients' evolving needs.


GTB is comprised of three business lines: Trade \& Working Capital ("TWC"), Corporate Cash Management ("CCM"), and Financial Institutions ("FI"), which are underpinned by dedicated support functions, including GTB Risk \& Control, Product Management, Client Solutions, Data \& Analytics, and Deposit Portfolio Management. TWC is made up of Global Core Trade Finance ("GCTF") and Structured Trade \& Export Finance ("STEF"), which is comprised of Export \& Agency ("EAF") Finance and Working Capital Solutions ("WCS").


**Global Core Trade Finance (GCTF):**

* Clients principally include Fortune 500 and 100 companies with head offices located in North America and Europe, as well as key financial institutions.
* Develops client centric solutions to remove or reduce payment risk or facilitate working capital by employing traditional trade finance products (Standby Letters of Credit / Guarantees, Import Letters of Credit, Export Letters of Credit, or Documentary Collections) associated with our clients' domestic business needs or foreign sales and purchases.
* Supports strategic foreign banks and their clients' needs in North America \& UK and acts as a trusted partner to mitigate risks in our markets.
* Works closely with internal TD internal partners to provide "One\-TD" solutions to our clients.

**Job Description:**

Reporting directly to the Managing Director, and Head of Global Core Trade Finance , the candidate will be responsible for providing GCTFFinance product coverage, structuring advice, and risk mitigation solutions to a portfolio of Canadian domiciled, multinational corporates and for driving product penetration within assigned market. Proactivity, flexibility, technical product expertise, and origination discipline are required to deliver value from prospecting and pitching through deal structuring and execution. As a key product partner, the VP interacts with a wide variety of internal stakeholders including industry heads and sector leads within CIB and partners across credit management, GM, and GTB. A collegial and team\-oriented view of success is very important to allow the candidate to fit into the team. Having an entrepreneurial mindset is critical to manage through ambiguity and change associated with growing a business.


**Requirements:**

This role is suited to a detail\-oriented individual with a client\-centric focus, and a strong understanding of and demonstrated judgement related to credit structuring, execution, and risk. At Ontario Health, we are committed to developing a strong organizational culture that connects and inspires all team members across the province. Our vision is that together, we will be a leader in health and wellness for all. Our mission is to connect the health system to drive improved and equitable health outcomes, experiences and value. How we work together is reflected through our five values: integrity, inspiration, tenacity, humility and care. 

What Ontario Health offers:  

Role

At Ontario Health, your growth and well-being aren’t just supported—they’re celebrated every step of the way. Here, you have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact while shaping a fulfilling and sustainable career. Based on your role, you may receive:

Comprehensive health coverage from day one, with fully paid medical, dental, and vision benefits to support you and your family’s health
Flexible health care or wellness spending accounts, plus an inclusive program to support your overall well-being
A premium defined benefit pension plan, ensuring long-term financial security
Competitive vacation entitlement that encourages time to rest and recharge
Three personal days and two float days annually, providing added flexibility to support work-life balance, in addition to vacation days
Ongoing learning and career development opportunities designed to help you grow, advance, and thrive in your profession
A collaborative, values-driven workplace where integrity, care, humility, inspiration, and tenacity shape everything we do
Opportunities to participate in Communities of Inclusion, fostering belonging, equity, and the sharing of diverse perspectives across our team

Want to make a difference in your career?  Consider this opportunity. 

As Director, Planning and Implementation, you will lead health system strategies that respond to regional needs and advance integrated, equitable care. Reporting to the Vice President, System Strategy, Planning, Design and Implementation, you will turn strategic priorities into achievable program plans and oversee their implementation and evaluation.

Lead a cross-functional team and collaborate with regional and provincial partners across health sectors to close system gaps, strengthen coordination and deliver results. You will be accountable for your portfolio’s planning, team performance, and day-to-day program operations.

This regional role supports the health care needs and priorities of the North East Region.

Here Is What You Will Be Doing

Drive regional strategy: Assess health care needs, set priorities and lead integrated planning, implementation and evaluation aligned with provincial and regional strategies and Ontario Health’s Strategic Plan and Annual Business Plan.
Turn evidence into action: Work with regional colleagues to identify data sources and analysis that inform decisions, strengthen planning, and improve performance. Embed health equity principles and priorities throughout planning processes.
Build partnerships across sectors: Establish committees and communities of practice, engage internal and external partners, and connect regional and provincial teams to address system barriers, resource needs and accountability gaps.
Advance integration and innovation: Represent the portfolio on regional committees and other collaborative bodies, champion best practices and integrated care models, and recommend program improvements and funding allocation priorities informed by emerging health system issues.
Lead people and operations: Guide and manage staff, oversee day-to-day program operations, and ensure work follows accepted best practices, government and ministry directives, and regional policies and procedures.
Deliver measurable results: Establish regional goals and implement initiatives to achieve them. Monitor, evaluate, and report on activities against performance objectives set by the CRO.

Education And Experience

Here is what you will need to be successful:

Master’s degree in health or business administration, or equivalent education/experience.
7 years of work experience in the public or private health care sector.
5 years of experience leading or managing teams directly or indirectly, using relationship-building and management skills, with a solid background in managing staff to achieve corporate objectives.
Solid background in integrating large, complex initiatives in a changing environment, with advanced project management skills and the ability to manage multiple concurrent projects.

Knowledge And Skills

Business acumen: Apply business principles and systems thinking in health care, including financial and human resource management, organizational dynamics and governance, strategic planning, risk management and quality improvement.
Stakeholder engagement and relationship management: Develop networks, alliances and multiple external collaborative relationships that support department performance. Collaborate across functions and boundaries, find common ground with an expanding range of stakeholders, identify key issues, and accommodate key players’ needs on joint projects with external parties or units.
Communication and interpersonal skills: Highly developed verbal and written communication skills to provide and obtain complex, technical or sensitive information effectively, clearly, concisely and logically, at an appropriate level and in an appropriate format. Prepare and deliver presentations on technical and/or sensitive information to diverse audiences. Listen well, encourage open communication, and respond appropriately to others’ needs, feelings and capabilities with tact, compassion, sensitivity, and respect.
Judgement and negotiation: Exercise sound judgement on sensitive and contentious issues and negotiate consensus on complex policy strategies.
Strategic planning and risk management: Align department tasks and objectives with corporate goals, establish clear targets and measures to track progress, evaluate outcomes and adjust direction as appropriate.
Change management: Actively embrace change initiatives to improve department performance and use varied methods to help employees respond positively to change.
Health care planning and system design: Expert knowledge of planning models and approaches, with an understanding of the health care system and environment. Scan for ideas, best practices and system-wide trends, and effectively select options, plan, implement and evaluate health care policies and/or programs.
Program development and innovation: Develop new insights and apply innovative solutions to improve the organization. Foster creative thinking and innovation, and design and implement new or cutting-edge programs and processes.
Health sector and community knowledge: Knowledge of Ontario’s health sector and workforce trends; in-depth knowledge of local health issues, priorities and needs in the context of broader health care policy and system development trends; and knowledge of the needs of Indigenous peoples in urban and community settings and Francophone communities.

jobs.description:
Job Description

Toast is recruiting on behalf of one of the world's largest professional services firms, with thousands of people across Canada advising organizations on audit, tax, and advisory work. Their Data & AI practice is one of the fastest growing parts of the firm, driven by strong demand from clients across sectors who want to modernize their data platforms and put AI to work at scale. They are looking for a Director to lead the growth and delivery of Google Gemini Enterprise solutions, owning client engagements from AI strategy through to enterprise-wide implementation while working closely with Google Cloud to build and take joint offerings to market.

Responsibilities

Act as a trusted advisor to senior client stakeholders, including CIOs, CTOs, CDOs, and CFOs, guiding their AI transformation agendas
Lead AI strategy engagements, including maturity assessments, Gemini Enterprise roadmaps, and operating model and governance design
Translate complex business challenges into clear AI-enabled opportunities and value cases
Architect end-to-end Gemini Enterprise solutions covering data integration and grounding, agentic workflows, and security and compliance frameworks
Provide technical oversight across data, AI/ML, and cloud engineering teams to keep delivery cohesive
Advise on scalable deployment models and enterprise integration with ERP, CRM, and collaboration platforms
Lead large-scale AI programs from pilot through enterprise rollout, owning quality, timelines, and value realization
Build reusable assets and accelerators, such as use cases, reference architectures, and deployment playbooks, to scale delivery
Build and manage strategic relationships with Google Cloud, aligning client needs with product roadmap evolution
Co-develop joint solutions and go-to-market offerings with partners and contribute to capability development
Support business development and complex pursuits, including solution shaping, proposals, and pricing models
Present Gemini Enterprise solutions to executive audiences, turning technical concepts into clear business narratives
Drive client-facing storytelling on agentic AI, productivity gains, and ROI
Contribute to thought leadership and market positioning in AI transformation

Requirements

10+ years in consulting, technology, or AI/data leadership roles
Proven track record delivering enterprise AI or cloud transformation programs
Expertise in enterprise AI architecture and design
Strong expertise in generative AI and LLMs, enterprise data architecture, and cloud platforms, with experience on GCP considered an asset
Experience engaging and influencing C-suite stakeholders
Ability to shape, position, and close complex deals
Demonstrated success contributing to business development and revenue growth
Experience with the Google Cloud ecosystem and strategic alliances
Exposure to AI agents, agentic workflows, and enterprise AI governance frameworks
Track record building repeatable consulting offerings and intellectual property

Benefits

Compensation listed on the posting is for base salary only. Total salary includes base salary + annual bonuses.
Comprehensive Total Rewards program
Lead a flagship Google Gemini Enterprise practice inside one of the fastest growing teams at the firm
Shape how major Canadian organizations across sectors adopt generative and agentic AI, moving them from pilot projects to enterprise-wide rollouts
Work directly with Google Cloud to influence product roadmaps and build joint offerings that reach clients across the country
Build the playbooks, reference architectures, and IP that will define how the firm delivers AI transformation for years to come
Application Review

Submit your application, including your resume and cover letter, through our online portal. Our team will carefully review your qualifications and experiences. We take pride in responding promptly, so if your application aligns with our current opportunities, you’ll hear back from us with next steps. Your journey with Toast begins here, and we’re excited to see what you bring to the table!

Vetting Call

If your application is successful, we’ll schedule a vetting call with a member of the Toast team. This 30-45 minute informal conversation is designed for us to get to know you better and assess your skills. Be prepared to discuss your past projects, the challenges you’ve tackled, and the impact you’ve made. This is your chance to shine and show us why you’re a great fit for the roles we offer.

Profile Creation

Once you’ve impressed us in the vetting call, we’ll create an unbiased profile that highlights your experience while minimizing common biases. Instead, we focus on your skills, industry experience, and the impact you’ve made. This way, your profile reflects your true potential and accomplishments.

Client Submission

After crafting your unbiased profile, we submit it to our trusted clients. We work closely with these clients to ensure they understand the value you bring. Throughout their interview process, we remain by your side, providing support and guidance. Our goal is to help you navigate the hiring process smoothly and confidently, ensuring you have the best chance to secure a role that fits your skills and aspirations.

jobs.title: VP Technology and Innovation Partners
jobs.description:
Dayforce is a global human capital management (HCM) company headquartered in Toronto, Ontario, and Minneapolis, Minnesota, with operations across North America, Europe, Middle East, Africa (EMEA), and the Asia Pacific Japan (APJ) region.

Our award-winning Cloud HCM platform offers a unified solution database and continuous calculation engine, driving efficiency, productivity and compliance for the global workforce.

Our brand promise - Makes Work Life Better™ - Reflects our commitment to employees, customers, partners and communities globally.

About The Opportunity

Dayforce is the AI-powered people platform. One platform for HR, Pay, Time, Talent, and Analytics, with AI built into how work gets done. Partners are central to that strategy. The AI capabilities, data, and solutions our partners bring to the platform extend what Dayforce AI can do for customers and accelerate how fast we grow.

That is changing what our technology ecosystem does for the business. Partners are moving from integrations that sit next to the platform to AI-enabled solutions we resell, transact, and build on together. That shift touches revenue, product strategy, and how Dayforce competes.

The VP, Technology and Innovation Partners owns the strategy, performance, and commercial outcomes of Dayforce’s technology partner ecosystem across five areas: ISV partners Dayforce resells, including Go1, Emburse, Docusign, Aquera, etc.; ISV partners with certified connectors on the Dayforce Exchange across Pay and Benefits and HR and Talent; the Microsoft partnership; In Country Payroll partners; and Dayforce Build.

This is a leader-of-leaders role with a number attached. You will be accountable for resell bookings, partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline, marketplace revenue, and the quality of the integrations and solutions partners deliver. You will lead an established team of four senior leaders who own the Microsoft alliance, In Country Payroll, Pay and Benefits ISVs, and HR and Talent ISVs. You will operate as a peer to the leaders of our Services Delivery and Community pillars. We are looking for a leader with the commercial, go-to-market, and technology depth to run all of it as one business.

Work is what you do, not where you go. For this role, we are open to remote work and can hire anywhere in the US or Canada.

What You’ll Get To Do

Business Ownership and Growth

Carry the technology partner number. Own resell bookings, partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline, and marketplace revenue, with clear accountability to the CRO organization.
Scale software resell. Grow attach of resold partner solutions to core Dayforce deals. Set the margins, pricing, packaging, and commercial terms that make resell a material, predictable revenue line.
Make the Exchange transactable. Share ownership with Product of moving the Dayforce Exchange from referral-only to transactable. Own the partner commercial model, partner onboarding, and partner readiness.
Make partners a growth engine for Dayforce AI. Build the partner strategy that extends the AI-powered people platform. Bring in the AI partners, agents, and solutions that deepen what Dayforce AI delivers for customers and create new revenue.
Own the portfolio. Decide which partners we resell, which we integrate and refer, which we co-build with, and which we retire. Close gaps in the Dayforce offering through build, partner, or buy recommendations with Product and Corporate Development.

Microsoft

Serve as executive sponsor for Microsoft, supporting the alliance lead who owns the day-to-day relationship across partnership, sales, and product teams.
Grow Dayforce’s position as a strategic HCM and payroll partner in the Microsoft ecosystem, across Azure, Dynamics 365, Copilot, and Teams.
Build and run a joint HCM, Pay, and ERP go-to-market with Microsoft and the SI partners that deliver it, including marketplace, co-sell programs, and field-to-field engagement.
Lead AI co-innovation that turns Microsoft technology into differentiated Dayforce AI capability.

Global Payroll and In-Country Partners

Own the strategy and performance of the In Country Payroll network that delivers and extends Dayforce global payroll.
Set standards for coverage, service quality, compliance, integration, and customer experience, and hold partners to them.
Rationalize and expand country coverage based on customer demand and deal pipeline.
Work with Product and Operations to deliver one consistent global payroll experience, whether Dayforce or a partner runs the payroll.

Dayforce Build

Dayforce Build is the platform customers and partners use to build integrations, extensions, and new capabilities on Dayforce. Partners are already building in it. This role turns that early momentum into a scaled partner ecosystem.

Own the partner strategy and growth of Dayforce Build, sharing ownership of the platform roadmap with Product and Engineering.
Move partner builds, including AI-powered extensions and agents, from proof of concept to production, certified, and in market.
Recruit and grow the ISVs, SIs, and developers building on the platform, including through the Dayforce Developer Community.
Connect what partners build to the Exchange, the resell program, and field go-to-market so builds turn into revenue.
Set quality, security, and certification standards for everything partners build on Dayforce.

GTM and Field Execution

Build repeatable joint go-to-market motions with priority partners: co-sell plays, joint campaigns, enablement, and account mapping.
Drive field adoption of resell and partner solutions across segments.
Equip Dayforce sellers with the positioning, pricing, and proof points to attach partner solutions to core deals, so partner attach is a default consideration rather than an exception.
Partner with Marketing on ecosystem launches, events, and partner showcases.

Leading the Team

You will lead four senior leaders, each running a distinct motion. Your first job is to make them operate as one ecosystem.

Microsoft Alliance owns the day-to-day Microsoft relationship, co-sell, and joint GTM.
In Country Payroll owns the global payroll partner network, coverage, and service quality.
Pay and Benefits ISVs owns the partners that extend Dayforce Pay and Benefits through connectors and resell.
HR and Talent ISVs owns the partners that extend Dayforce HR and Talent through connectors and resell.
Coach, develop, and raise the bar across the team. Have a clear point of view on strengths and gaps within your first quarter.
Establish one scorecard and operating rhythm across all five areas, balancing long-term platform strategy against near-term revenue.

Technology and Product Influence

Serve as the technical voice of the partner ecosystem inside Dayforce.
Partner with Product and Engineering on integration architecture, APIs, connector certification, and partner developer experience.
Partner with Product on the Dayforce AI roadmap, so partner AI capabilities complement and extend what Dayforce builds.
Scout emerging technology and AI partners that expand the Dayforce platform and create new revenue.

Executive and Cross-Functional Influence

Operate as a trusted counterpart to executive leadership across Sales, Product, Engineering, Marketing, Legal, and Finance.
Negotiate complex resell, revenue share, and strategic partner agreements, and hold partners accountable through data, not sentiment.
Present performance, risk, and opportunity directly to the executive team with clarity and conviction, including in forums with sponsor visibility.
Executive exposure to the CRO, Product, and Technology organizations, and to Microsoft executive leadership, as a matter of routine, not exception.

Skills And Experience We Value

15+ years in enterprise software, with at least 7 years leading technology partnerships, alliances, or ecosystem businesses, and meaningful time spent carrying a number.
A track record of growing partner revenue, including resell or OEM models, with specifics: bookings delivered, attach rates moved, marketplace revenue grown.
Direct experience scaling a SaaS marketplace, app ecosystem, or developer platform program, ideally including the move to a transactable model.
Deep experience with Microsoft or another hyperscaler: co-sell programs, marketplace, and executive sponsorship.
Strong commercial judgment. You have structured and negotiated complex resell, revenue share, and strategic partner agreements.
Enough technical depth to lead conversations on APIs, integration architecture, cloud platforms, and AI with engineering teams on both sides.
A clear point of view on how AI is reshaping software ecosystems, and experience bringing AI partners and solutions to market.
Experience leading senior leaders who each run a distinct business and making them operate as one team.
Familiarity with HCM, payroll, ERP, or an adjacent enterprise platform category.
Comfort operating in a private equity-backed environment, with the pace, transparency, and accountability that entails.
Highly analytical and metrics-driven, at ease in complex matrixed environments and in front of an executive audience.

What Would Make You Stand Out

Global payroll experience is a strong advantage.
Prior PE-backed experience is a strong advantage.

What’s In It For You

Dayforce is fueled by the diversity of our talented employees. We are an equal opportunity employer and consider and embrace ALL individuals and what makes them unique. We believe our employees should be happy and healthy, with peace of mind and a sense of fulfillment.

We encourage individuals to apply based on their passions.

Dayforce encourages personal and professional growth. We offer excellent time away from work programs, comprehensive wellness initiatives and recognition through competitive pay and benefits.

With a commitment to community impact, including volunteer days and our charity, Dayforce Cares we provide opportunities for you to thrive both in your career and personal life. Our focus is not just on your job but on supporting you to be the best version of yourself.

This job posting is for an existing vacancy

Artificial intelligence may be used in the screening, assessment, or selection of applicants for this position.

Dayforce is committed to providing accommodations for applicants with disabilities throughout the recruitment process. If you require an accommodation, please contact us at accessibilty@dayforce.com.

About The Salary Ranges

Please note that the salary range mentioned in this job description should serve simply as a guide. The final compensation offered may vary based on a variety of factors, including bonuses and/or incentives, or a candidate’s experience, skills, budget and location. Our company is committed to providing a fair, equitable, and competitive package that reflects the value an individual brings to the organization.

Proficiency in English is required for this position as this role will regularly interact with English-speaking stakeholders, co-workers, managers and/or clients across the world. Further, our back office support teams, including but not limited to Human Resources, are primarily English speaking. Employees need to be able to communicate with these departments in English to appropriately administer their business relationship. Due to the significant high volume of interactions with these English-speaking co-workers, managers, stakeholders and/or clients, which is inherent to this position, it is not possible to reorganize the company's activities to avoid this requirement.

Fraudulent Recruiting

Beware of fraudulent recruiting. Legitimate Dayforce contacts will use an @dayforce.com email address. We do not request money, checks, equipment orders, or sensitive personal data during the recruitment process. jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
About The Company

The Northwest Territories Power Corporation (NTPC)
is the primary public electricity utility serving the Northwest Territories and plays a critical role in supporting the territory's economic development, community well-being, and energy security. As a crown corporation wholly owned by the Government of the Northwest Territories through NT Hydro, NTPC is responsible for generating, transmitting, and distributing electricity across one of the most geographically vast and operationally challenging jurisdictions in North America. The organization provides power to more than 43,000 residents across 27 communities and manages a diverse portfolio of hydroelectric, diesel, natural gas, solar, wind, and battery storage assets. With more than $650 million in assets and approximately 151 MW of generating capacity, NTPC operates a geographically dispersed and operationally diverse utility system across the Northwest Territories.

For more information, please download the full position profile: NTPC CFO Position Profile.pdf

Position Overview

The ideal candidate is an accomplished executive with a proven track record leading finance, treasury, risk management, regulatory affairs, and capital planning functions within large, complex, and highly regulated organizations. Experience within the utility, energy, infrastructure, natural resources, transportation, or broader public-sector sectors will be highly valued. They will bring deep expertise in long-term financial planning, capital allocation, enterprise risk management, and organizational performance, alongside a demonstrated ability to support critical investment decisions where commercial outcomes, public accountability, and long-term sustainability must be carefully balanced.

The successful candidate will possess the strategic perspective and business judgment required to help guide NTPC through a period of infrastructure renewal, energy transition, and economic development across the Northwest Territories. As a trusted advisor to the CEO, Board of Directors, and the Audit & Risk Committee, they will bring the credibility to navigate complex relationships with government, regulators, Indigenous governments, lenders, and other key stakeholders.

They will be equally comfortable evaluating major capital projects, supporting regulatory and rate-setting processes, identifying new business opportunities, and helping shape the Corporation's long-term strategic direction. As a leader, the preferred candidate will build strong teams, develop future leaders, and create an environment characterized by accountability, safety, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

With exceptional communication skills and executive presence, they will confidently represent NTPC in boardrooms, government forums, regulatory proceedings, and stakeholder engagements. Above all, they will be motivated by the opportunity to contribute to a purpose-driven organization whose success directly supports the energy security, economic prosperity, and long-term sustainability of communities across the Northwest Territories.

Education And Experience Requirements

Education and Professional Background

CPA designation, MBA, or other relevant postgraduate degree.
Minimum of 10 years of progressive financial leadership experience.
Extensive management and supervisory experience, preferably within a utility or similarly complex operating environment.
Demonstrated experience leading financial management functions, including planning, reporting, analysis, and performance oversight.
Experience working effectively with executive leadership teams, regional leaders, and diverse stakeholder groups.

WORK ARRANGEMENT

The role is based at NTPC’s head office in Hay River and requires a visible leadership presence within the organization and community. Travel to Yellowknife, regional plants, offices and communities throughout the Northwest Territories will be required.

The position requires visits to regional and area plant and office locations, which may involve travel in small aircraft and the possibility of extended travel due to weather conditions. Work pressures and demands often require work outside of normal office hours. In this role, you must maintain the confidentiality of all Corporation information that comes to the incumbent’s attention as a result of their employment with the Northwest Territories Power Corporation.

RECRUITMENT PROCESS

We welcome conversations with individuals interested in learning more about this unique leadership opportunity. To explore the role in confidence, please contact a member of our Executive Search team at MNP.

To apply, please submit a résumé and cover letter in confidence through MNP's online application portal or directly to the contacts below. All inquiries and applications will be managed through MNP to ensure a fair, confidential, and consistent recruitment process.

The Northwest Territories Power Corporation is committed to building a representative workforce and values the contributions of Indigenous peoples. Qualified Indigenous candidates are encouraged to self-identify during the application process and may be eligible for consideration under NTPC's Indigenous Employment Policy.

We thank all applicants for their interest; however, only those selected to move forward in the process will be contacted.

The CFO Centre Canada is actively looking for CFOs to join our team. You’ll be a local, or at least an adopted local in the region.

Become Part of Our Dynamic Portfolio CFO Team

Start an amazing new career as a portfolio CFO supporting exciting fast growth businesses. If you’re a top-quality Chief Financial Officer and you’re looking for something different, or you’re an independent CFO who’s already made the break from corporate life, or a working or returning CFO parent who wants more work flexibility and work life balance, then read on, this might be for you

What we do?

We’re looking for top quality CFOs who are looking for a new challenge. Joining the CFO Centre will allow you the opportunity to provide CFO services to ambitious small to mid-size businesses with revenues of $2-$100 million. Our model provides them with a flexible, affordable option to acquire this skill set from a business whose purpose is making a real difference to our worldwide client base. Whether you come from corporate, SME, independent, parent returning to work background – we have opportunities that will allow you to achieve work flexibility and work life balance.

The CFO Centre Canada has thrived since it was established in 2011, catering to clients across 10 regions nationwide with a powerhouse team of nearly 125+ CFOs, and we're primed for exponential growth in the coming year. The CFO Centre Canada is part of the CFO Centre Group, which began its journey in the UK in 2001.

Today the global CFO Centre Group:

Is the number 1 provider of part-time CFOs
Operates globally from 90+ locations in 18 countries and 5 continents
Has over 750+ colleagues all across the globe, including Canada, UK, USA, Netherlands, Germany, Ireland, Belgium, Italy, Australia, New Zealand, Hong Kong, Singapore,Dubai, India, and South Africa.

What sets us apart?

We define and deliver the numbers that really matter. We help clients identify figures that drive real impact—not just in business, but in their lives. Whether it's fostering growth, facilitating acquisitions, streamlining operations, or enabling desired lifestyles.

What Makes a Successful Portfolio CFO?

Our team consists of highly experienced, like-minded CFOs with hands-on CFO experience. Together we build and nurture a portfolio of diverse clients while you enjoy variety, freedom, and work-life balance.

You can create a successful portfolio CFO career with The CFO Centre if you are energetic, have entrepreneurial drive, and care deeply about helping business leaders thrive.
The life of a portfolio CFO is not just about changing the lives of our clients, it’s about helping you find meaning in your career as well.

You’ll work on a self-employed basis

With the full support from our wider operational team and your fellow CFOs, supporting you to build your portfolio client base.

Access to global support network

You can get the best of both worlds – 750+ global CFOs to support each other. That’s an incredible amount of knowledge and experience to share.

Dedicated regional support team

To work closely with, giving you strategic capability. Building you bespoke campaigns and building your portfolio.
Enjoy comprehensive onboarding, mentoring and a global network of colleagues to share best practices and client experiences.

Do you have experience in some of the following?

Selling/exiting businesses
Identifying risks
Reviewing Business plans
Sourcing funding
Improving systems and controls
Implementing KPI reporting
Increasing profit
Improving cash flow
Tightening up compliance
Optimizing tax and legal
Driving strategic direction of a business
Mergers and acquisitions

The ideal candidate will possess the following:

Be a self-starter with ambition, energy, and a ‘can do’ attitude
Fully engage with our ‘purpose’ of wanting to make a real difference to our clients
Desire to work closely as part of a team together with our Regional Directors in a collegiate environment
Exceptional interpersonal and relationship-building skills
Track record of excellence, achievement, and entrepreneurial drive
Desire to work directly with business owners, with a passion for making a real difference
Well networked
Confidence and gravitas
Excellent presentation skills
Able to develop a strong alignment with the company’s culture
The role is self-employed whilst operating in a defined model. You must be able to support yourself financially during the build-up phase

What do you need to have?

You have worked as a CFO for a minimum of 5+ years during your finance career – commercial and strategic
You are highly networked and love to meet new people, develop business and ensure client satisfaction.

Desired Accreditations

Qualified with one of the major accounting institutes CPA, CA, CMA or equivalent
MBA asset
You are highly networked and love to meet new people, develop business and ensure client satisfaction.

jobs.description:
⠀

The Director, Defense Portfolio Strategy reports to the Chief Strategy Officer and directly supports the CSO's enterprise mandate to identify and unlock growth above the underlying market rate. Defense is CAE's largest such opportunity, and this role carries the analytical and transactional workload behind it.

The Defense & Security business unit owns its strategy. This role does not duplicate or adjudicate it. Instead, the Director works on the questions that sit above and across the operating plan — where CAE should allocate capital and capability within the Defense domain, which adjacencies merit entry, what the enterprise should build, buy, or partner for, and how the Defense portfolio should evolve to deliver above-market growth.

The Director operates as a full member of the corporate strategy team. The above-market growth mandate is enterprise-wide and held by the CSO; this role brings dedicated defense-domain depth to it, working alongside colleagues whose expertise spans other domains and functions. Portfolio work remains collective — the addition here is capacity and depth against a specific CEO-level priority, not a redrawing of scope.

Key Responsibilities

Portfolio Strategy and Capital Allocation

Quantify the gap between the Defense market's underlying growth rate and CAE's growth ambition, and maintain a live view of which portfolio moves close it — with what confidence, on what timeline, and at what capital cost.
Develop CAE's point of view on where Defense capital and capability should be deployed to generate above-market growth, and where they should not.
Assess portfolio adjacencies, capability gaps, and whitespace across the Defense domain, framing entry, expansion, and exit questions for executive decision.
Build the build / buy / partner logic for capabilities the Defense portfolio requires.
Contribute the Defense lens to enterprise portfolio reviews and capital allocation discussions alongside corporate strategy colleagues covering other domains.
Develop investment cases for new markets, segments, and capability plays, in partnership with the business unit strategy team.

M&A and Partnership Pipeline

In Collaboration With The Strategy Team Colleagues

Build and actively cultivate a pipeline of acquisition and partnership candidates aligned to the Defense portfolio thesis, maintaining live relationships well ahead of any formal process.
Maintain a standing view of the defense industrial landscape — who is consolidating, who is available, where valuations are moving.
Partner with Corporate Development through diligence and execution; support integration planning where strategic rationale must be preserved.
Evaluate teaming, joint venture, and partnership structures as alternatives to acquisition.

Technology Enabler Pipeline

Identify, map, and cultivate relationships with startup, scale-up, and pre-IPO companies whose technologies could accelerate CAE's Defense capabilities or threaten its positions.
Maintain an ongoing landscape view of emerging technologies relevant to simulation, training, and mission readiness.
Create structured pathways from early engagement through pilot, commercial partnership, investment, or acquisition.
Connect CAE to relevant venture, accelerator, and defense-innovation ecosystems, sharing that access across the strategy team.

Market Intelligence and Enterprise Contribution

Bring outside-in intelligence on defense budgets, procurement trends, geopolitical shifts, and competitor moves into both business unit and corporate strategy discussions.
Contribute to enterprise strategy work beyond Defense where domain insight is relevant — this is a shared-team role, not a single-vertical one.
Prepare executive-level analysis and briefing materials for the CEO, Executive Committee, and Board.
Support Government Relations and business unit leadership with strategic context for key customer engagements.

This Role Succeeds Through Partnership Rather Than Authority

With the Defense & Security business unit — the BU owns its strategy and operating plan. The Director brings portfolio and transaction perspective to that work and takes the BU's market reality into enterprise portfolio decisions. Joint work products, jointly presented.
With corporate strategy colleagues — a peer contributing defense depth to a shared team agenda, drawing on colleagues' functional and domain expertise in turn. Enterprise portfolio work remains collective.
With Corporate Development — origination and strategic framing from this role; transaction execution led by Corporate Development.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's or postgraduate degree in Business, Strategy, Economics, Engineering, International Relations, or a related field; MBA an asset.
12+ years in corporate strategy, corporate development, management consulting, or defense/aerospace industry roles.
Demonstrated experience with portfolio strategy, capital allocation, or build/buy/partner decision-making in a complex global organization.
Strong command of defense markets, government procurement, and allied defense spending dynamics.
Direct experience with M&A origination, partnership development, or technology scouting.

Preferred Qualifications

Track record of earning influence without formal authority, and of working effectively as a peer within an established team.
Strong financial, analytical, and commercial judgement.
Comfortable operating with ambiguity, across multiple time horizons, in a fast-moving environment.
Excellent written and verbal communication, including executive-level presentation and narrative skill.
Ability to obtain and maintain required security clearances.

Benefits

Group Insurance.
Telemedicine Employee and Family Assistance Program.
Employee Stock Purchase Plan.
Group RRSP.
CAE Pension Plan/Defined Benefit Plan.
Sabbatical Leave.
Flex Time.
Enhanced Parental Leave.

We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients. 

 At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute. 

 To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com 

 What you’ll be doing 

 As a member of the Enterprise Real Estate and Workplace Experience team, you’ll help shape a modern, connected, inclusive, and high-performing workplace experience across CIBC’s real estate portfolio, including flagship and enterprise environments. As a Director, Workplace Strategy, you’ll lead the evolution, translation, and implementation of CIBC’s Global Workplace Experience Strategy across workplace transformation projects. You’ll provide strategic advice, develop workplace standards and enablement approaches, and use research, data, and team member feedback to help reimagine how we work. You’ll partner with leaders across Real Estate, Human Resources, Design, Technology, and other key functions to align workplace strategy with business priorities, future workforce needs, and enterprise transformation goals. You’ll also prepare clear recommendations and insights for senior leaders to support decision-making and the delivery of CIBC’s future workplace strategy. 

 At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. You’ll have the flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you’ll spend 1-3 days per week on-site, while other days will be remote. Details on your work arrangement will be discussed at the time of your interview. 

 How you’ll succeed 
 Lead workplace strategy execution – Translate CIBC’s Global Workplace Experience Strategy into practical design strategies, standards and enablement approaches for real estate transformation projects across the portfolio. 
 Provide strategic advice – Partner with leaders and project teams to apply workplace experience principles, align initiatives to enterprise priorities, and recommend solutions that improve the workplace experience and support the future of work. 
 Use insights to inform decisions – Conduct market research, evaluate internal and external trends, and use employee feedback and workplace data to identify opportunities, inform recommendations, and strengthen strategic planning. 
 Support change and enablement – Develop materials, approaches, and change tactics that help leaders and team members adapt to evolving workplace environments and new ways of working. 
 Build strong partnerships – Work closely with partners across Enterprise Real Estate, Human Resources, Design, Technology, Corporate Security, Events, Retail, and Facilities Management to support coordinated planning and successful implementation. 
 Present to senior leadership – Prepare clear, compelling findings, business cases, and recommendations for senior leaders and executive forums, highlighting benefits, risks, dependencies, and considerations for decision-making. 

 Who you are 
 You can demonstrate 10 years of experience in workplace strategy, strategic planning and real estate transformation, and change enablement. You have experience in workplace design, employee experience, operating model change, or enterprise transformation in a large, complex organization. 
 You have a degree or diploma in a relevant field. It’s an asset if you have education or experience related to workplace strategy, business strategy, design, organizational change, or real estate. 
 You’re future focused. You look beyond the moment and help shape strategies that will make a difference today and tomorrow. You identify opportunities to evolve the workplace in support of business and workforce priorities. 
 You’re analytical. You give meaning to data and research. You enjoy investigating complicated problems, identifying trends, and turning insights into clear, practical recommendations. You have well-developed communication and presentation skills, both written and verbal. 
 You’re influential. Your influence makes a difference. You build credibility with senior leaders and partners and help bring about change by sharing your expertise and recommendations in a clear and thoughtful way. 
 You’re collaborative. You’re motivated by collective success and work effectively across functions to bring people together, align priorities, and deliver shared outcomes. 
 You’re a caring and accountable leader. You have experience developing strategic team goals, creating clarity around priorities and ways of working, and coaching others to support strong performance and growth. 
 You live your values. You bring high standards, genuine care to your relationships, and want to grow with an employer that shares your values and brings out your best

 At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.

jobs.title: Vice President, Analytics & Health Outcomes
jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE

GreenShield is a proudly Canadian, national non-profit health care and insurance organization, driven by our mission of Better Health for All. We believe health care is a right, not a privilege, and we are committed to improving health outcomes, advancing health equity, and building a future where every Canadian can reach their full health and well-being potential.
Through our unique integrated payer-provider ("payvider") model, we offer insurance, administer benefits, and pay claims as a ‘payer’ while offering health care services such as mental health, pharmacy, telemedicine, and chronic disease management as a ‘provider’. As a non-profit social enterprise without shareholders, we reinvest our excess earnings to directly support underserved communities. Through GreenShield Cares, we positively impacted the health and well-being of over one million Canadians between 2020 and 2025. What’s driving us now is the commitment to measurably impact an additional three million Canadians by 2030 – across mental health, essential medicines, and chronic disease management – through scalable initiatives that deliver meaningful change in pursuit of our mission of Better Health for All.
At GreenShield, our culture is where purpose meets passion and performance. Our teams work as one to deliver meaningful, measurable impact for the people and communities we serve.

THE ROLE IN A NUTSHELL

Reporting to the SVP, Product, Experience & Health Outcomes, the Vice President, Analytics and Health Outcomes is a strategic senior leadership role responsible for turning GreenShield’s data into actionable insights, measurable outcomes, and clear narratives that inform priorities, support decision-making, and demonstrate impact. This leader will work across the organization to connect analytics and insights to enterprise priorities and measurable impact in a way that helps leaders understand what is happening, why it matters, and where to act.

This role will be responsible for:

Lead enterprise analytics and outcomes capabilities, ensuring data is used to inform priorities, guide investment decisions, and measure impact across the enterprise.
Translate complex data into clear insights, narratives, and recommendations that help executives, product teams, clinical leaders, clients, and partners understand where to act and how to create measurable value.
Build scalable measurement practices that help GreenShield assess performance, outcomes, and impact across its portfolio.
Develop clear, evidence-based insights for internal and external stakeholders to demonstrate impact.
Partner cross-functionally to embed analytics and outcome measures into planning, decision-making, client insights, and performance management.
Use data-driven insights to support better experiences, decisions, and outcomes.
Provide thought leadership on data quality, governance, privacy, responsible AI, and scalable analytics practices, working closely with Technology and enterprise data teams to ensure the right data foundations are in place.
Build and lead a high-performing team that combines analytical depth, business judgment, storytelling, and a practical orientation toward measurable outcomes.

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

15+ years of progressive analytics experience in health care, benefits, insurance, consulting, or a related field, including senior leadership accountability for analytics, insight generation, and business impact.
Proven ability to turn data into insight, insight into action, and action into measurable business, customer, and health outcomes.
Exceptional storytelling skills, with the ability to translate complex analysis into simple, credible, executive-ready narratives for internal leaders, clients, partners, and external audiences.
Business-oriented analytics leader who can ask the right questions, define the right measures, challenge assumptions, and connect data to decisions that improve performance and impact.
Experience building outcome frameworks, dashboards, scorecards, insights, analytics products, or executive reporting that drive decision-making.
Advanced analytics expertise, including predictive modelling, segmentation, measurement design, statistical analysis, data visualization, and practical application to business, customer, and health outcome questions.
Strong advanced analytics capability, including familiarity with AI and machine learning applications.
A collaborative, practical, and outcomes-focused leadership style, with the ability to operate at both strategic and execution levels in a fast-moving environment.

WHAT WE OFFER

Base Salary:
Range exempt
Offer positioning:
Determined using relevant experience, skills, internal equity and current market data.
Additional compensation:
Eligible for a discretionary target bonus.
Total rewards:
Health and dental coverage, retirement savings, paid time off and well-being support (up to $10,000 per year for mental health).
Posting disclosures:
This is for an existing vacancy.
Work model:
Hybrid

THE CULTURE

We believe a career should be meaningful. Not just a means to earn a living. Our culture is one where everyone's voice is heard and valued. Because that’s what it takes to create better health for all. We dare to challenge the status quo. And we’re driven by people who have challenged theirs. We believe that your workplace should empower you to be the best version of yourself. That’s why we provide a place where you can be inspired, challenged, and rewarded.

Where your growth means our growth.
Where your voice is heard and valued.
Where your work has purpose. And purpose matters.

We believe our people are critical to our overall success. Inclusivity makes us a stronger, smarter and more informed organization. Being intentionally inclusive of diverse backgrounds, perspectives and experiences will enhance our company culture to positively impact how we support our communities. A career at GreenShield isn’t just about personal achievements, it's about making a difference together.
