jobs.description:
Work Location:

Toronto, Ontario, Canada

Hours

37.5

Line Of Business

TD Securities

Pay Details

$155,000 - $215,000 CAD

TD is committed to providing fair and equitable compensation opportunities to all colleagues. Growth opportunities and skill development are defining features of the colleague experience at TD. Our compensation policies and practices have been designed to allow colleagues to progress through the salary range over time as they progress in their role. The base pay actually offered may vary based upon the candidate's skills and experience, job-related knowledge, geographic location, and other specific business and organizational needs.

As a candidate, you are encouraged to ask compensation related questions and have an open dialogue with your recruiter who can provide you more specific details for this role.

Job Description

Role mandate

Lead the Applied AI and Innovation capability for TD Securities and build a high-performing team of applied AI specialists. Identify advances in AI that matter to the business and translate them into practical capabilities that can be tested, proven, and deployed in capital markets workflows.

This is a business-led senior technical leadership role requiring deep AI expertise, strong product judgment, and a pragmatic delivery mindset. The role connects emerging models, methods, and research with complex business problems and works across business, quantitative, data, engineering, and control teams to deliver measurable value.

Strategy and technical direction

Set the applied AI strategy, technical direction, and priorities across generative AI, agentic systems, decision intelligence, multimodal models, retrieval, reasoning, and human-agent operating models for TD Securities.
Assess research and industry developments in generative AI, agentic AI, machine learning, retrieval, reasoning, multimodal models, and related technologies, for practical relevance, then translate the most promising capabilities into experiments, product strategies, operating models, and value opportunities.
Determine where advanced AI provides a material advantage over conventional analytics, rules, or automation, avoiding unnecessary complexity.

Applied AI delivery and value creation

Identify and prioritize high-value opportunities; develop business cases, value hypotheses, adoption plans, measurable baselines, and value-realization frameworks.
Lead applied scientists in designing, building, testing, and improving AI solutions for complex, knowledge-intensive and analytical workflows.
Establish standards for experimentation, benchmarking, statistical rigor, error analysis, robustness, documentation, reproducibility, and production readiness.
Develop or adapt models and methods when existing solutions do not meet requirements for performance, latency, privacy, explainability, control, or cost.
Drive rapid prototyping while ensuring successful solutions can be engineered, governed, scaled, monitored, and supported in production.

Technical leadership

Provide senior technical oversight across model selection and adaptation, fine-tuning, retrieval-augmented generation, agent orchestration, knowledge and semantic methods, tool use, planning, memory, context management, hybrid retrieval, reranking, evaluation, and inference optimization.
Design robust agentic and retrieval systems, spanning tool use, planning, memory, context management, hybrid retrieval and reranking, while proactively addressing scaling, data quality, evaluation blind spots and inference cost.
Set rigorous experimentation and evaluation standards, including controlled ablations, multi-seed testing, statistical significance, red teaming and contamination controls to ensure solutions are reliable and production-ready.
Anticipate and mitigate scaling bottlenecks, evaluation blind spots, data quality issues, model risk, security concerns, and inference cost.
Challenge architecture and model choices; lead design reviews and resolve significant trade-offs with Engineering, Data, Architecture, Technology, and control partners.

AI products and capability development

Apply product-management disciplines to AI capabilities, including vision, roadmaps, lifecycle management, prioritization, adoption, and value tracking.
Work directly with quantitative practitioners, traders, bankers, risk specialists, data scientists, and engineers to frame problems and design practical AI solutions.
Establish reusable AI components, evaluation frameworks, implementation patterns, and technical standards that accelerate delivery across teams.
Apply AI to information extraction and synthesis, decision support, workflow automation, quantitative and analytical tasks, client intelligence, risk analysis, and other complex processes.
Partner with engineering and delivery teams to move validated prototypes into reliable production capabilities.

People and capability leadership

Build, lead, and develop a multidisciplinary applied AI team with a high bar for technical quality, scientific rigor, engineering discipline, and measurable impact.
Lead through technical credibility by authoring design documents, running architecture and technical reviews, and setting expectations for code, experiments, and system quality.

Governance, risk, and responsible adoption

Partner with Risk, Compliance, Legal, Information Security, Technology, and enterprise AI governance teams to ensure responsible, controlled, auditable, and explainable adoption.
Define guardrails, escalation paths, adoption controls, measurement routines, and governance artifacts for AI products and agentic workflows, while preserving clear human accountability for material decisions.

Decision authorities

Prioritize the AI product and transformation portfolio with front-office sponsors and enabling partners.
Determine which emerging capabilities warrant experimentation and which prototypes have sufficient evidence to progress toward production.
Recommend investments in models, tooling, platforms, compute, talent, and external partnerships.
Escalate material risk, control, data, compliance, or technology dependencies to the appropriate accountable partners.

The Role Shares Responsibilities And Decision Interfaces With

Front Office leaders for opportunity prioritization, workflow design, commercial impact, adoption, and value realization.
Data Product teams for reusable, business-ready data; semantic context; quality; lineage; provenance; metadata; and AI-ready information structures.
Technology and Architecture for secure implementation, integration, platform alignment, resiliency, production readiness, and sustainable support.
Risk, Compliance, Legal, Information Security, and enterprise AI Governance for control design, policy alignment, approvals, responsible AI, and auditability.
Finance and Business Management for business cases, budgets, benefits tracking, operating leverage, and value realization.
Operations, Change Management, Human Resources, and Learning for workflow change, adoption, training, role impacts, and capability building.
Product and Delivery partners for execution planning, backlog prioritization, stakeholder engagement, success metrics, and delivery discipline.
Approved universities, research institutes, vendors, and open-source communities for collaboration, talent pipelines, and knowledge exchange.
Key measures will balance technical quality, adoption, and realized business impact:
Realized value from AI-enabled products, capabilities, and workflow transformation, including productivity, decision quality, revenue support, risk insight, or control effectiveness.
Delivery of approved roadmap milestones, business cases, benefits plans, and strategic transformation objectives.
Adoption, outcome improvement, reliability, and production performance of deployed AI capabilities.
Number, maturity, and reuse of AI components, evaluation frameworks, implementation patterns, workflows, and skills.
Team growth, talent development, stakeholder confidence, and cross-functional delivery effectiveness.
Portfolio, project, cost-centre, and value-realization targets to be confirmed.
This role is generally not directly client-facing. It creates client and shareholder value by improving how front-office teams serve clients, identify opportunities, make decisions, manage risk, and execute work.
Improves the speed, quality, and consistency of client coverage through AI-enabled insights, workflow tools, and decision support.
Reduces manual effort and accelerates access to relevant business context and information.
Supports revenue generation and relationship management by helping teams prepare more effectively and act on insights faster.
Simplifies fragmented workflows and embeds intelligence into day-to-day processes.
Strengthens control, transparency, and consistency through governed, explainable, reusable AI capabilities.

Education

PhD strongly preferred in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Statistics, Mathematics, Operations Research, Engineering, Physics, or a related quantitative discipline. A research-intensive master’s degree may be considered with an exceptional record of applied technical leadership.

Experience And Technical Capabilities

Typically 8+ years of progressive experience in applied AI, machine learning, data science, quantitative research, or advanced analytics, including leadership of multidisciplinary technical teams.
Demonstrated success translating research into robust, production-used systems in complex, regulated, or high-consequence environments.
Deep expertise in several areas such as large language models, natural language processing, retrieval and reasoning, agentic systems, multimodal learning, graph methods, time-series modelling, causal inference, optimization, reinforcement learning, or probabilistic modelling.
Expert command of experimental design, statistical inference, benchmarking, ablation studies, error analysis, model evaluation, reproducibility, contamination controls, and scientific peer review.
Strong hands-on fluency in Python and modern AI/ML ecosystems, with the ability to review code, experiments, model behaviour, architecture, and data pipelines.
Strong understanding of production AI architecture, including feature and data pipelines, vector and graph retrieval, model serving, APIs, distributed compute, cloud platforms, MLOps and LLMOps, observability, security, latency, resiliency, and cost optimization.
Technical depth to challenge designs, assess feasibility and risk, resolve architecture trade-offs, and partner credibly with data, engineering, quantitative, and technology teams.
Experience building and developing applied science or research teams, including talent assessment, mentoring, organizational design, and capability building.
Ability to engage credibly with quantitative practitioners, engineers, data scientists, risk specialists, traders, bankers, and senior technology leaders.
Capital markets or financial-services experience strongly preferred; experience with market, client, transaction, research, risk, or unstructured financial data is advantageous.
Executive communication skills to explain technical findings, uncertainty, limitations, and investment choices precisely without oversimplification.

Who We Are

TD Securities offers a wide range of capital markets products and services to corporate, government, and institutional clients who choose us for our innovation, execution, and experience. With more than 6,500 professionals operating out of 40 cities across the globe, we strive to make every interaction, product and experience remarkably human and refreshingly simple. Join MUFG, where being inspired is expected and making a meaningful impact is rewarded.

Overview

The role supports the Financial Risk function within MUFG Canada Risk Management, with a focus on the production, analysis, governance and continuous enhancement of liquidity risk, market risk, credit risk and interest rate risk in the banking book reporting. Reporting to the Financial Risk Vice President, the incumbent is responsible for preparing and maintaining recurring risk reports, supporting ECL and portfolio credit risk analysis, monitoring risk appetite and limit metrics, maintaining EUC and procedure documentation, and assisting with committee materials for IRC, ECC, Liquidity Risk and Market Risk governance forums. The role requires excellent technical capability, including advanced data analysis, Excel/Power Query/VBA automation, source-data reconciliation, AI literacy and the ability to responsibly leverage AI-enabled tools to improve reporting efficiency, data quality, trend analysis, control effectiveness and management insight. The incumbent must demonstrate strong knowledge of the underlying risk metrics, data sources such as OVS extracts, Bloomberg and internal reporting files, and the ability to translate complex technical outputs into clear, audit-ready commentary and management materials.

Key Accountabilities

Risk reporting, analytics and governance support - responsibilities include:

Prepare, analyze and maintain recurring Financial Risk reports across liquidity risk, market risk, credit risk and IRRBB, including Liquidity Early Warning Indicators, Liquidity Limit Dashboard, Liquidity Stress Testing, daily and monthly liquidity monitoring, VaR, stress testing, DV01, sensitivity measures, portfolio concentration, IFRS 9 ECL, Watchlist inputs, Risk Appetite metrics and interest rate risk analytics.
Compile and validate source data from OVS extracts, Bloomberg, internal risk files, Treasury reports, Middle Office data, Finance inputs, facility and commitment data, exposure reports and locally maintained EUC tools to support recurring production and independent review of risk metrics.
Support the preparation of IRC, ECC, Liquidity Risk, Market Risk and other governance materials by compiling metrics, drafting commentary, preparing exhibits, explaining drivers, documenting assumptions and ensuring materials are accurate, complete and delivered within required timelines.
Perform review and challenge of report outputs, investigate material movements or exceptions, document rationale, reconcile data back to source systems, and escalate breaches, data issues or control concerns in accordance with applicable procedures.

Support for stakeholders - responsibilities include:

Coordinate with Treasury, Middle Office, Finance, Operations, Compliance, business lines, regional risk teams and Head Office to obtain data, validate assumptions, clarify methodology, and support timely completion of Financial Risk deliverables.
Provide support, oversight and guidance to first line and independent risk monitoring functions on risk reporting, risk appetite monitoring, limit usage, breach escalation and remediation tracking.
Support audit, regulatory and internal review requests by maintaining clear evidence, audit trails, version logs, approvals and supporting documentation for recurring reporting processes.
Monitor relevant regulatory, Head Office and regional risk requirements and assist in translating them into local policies, procedures, controls, testing approaches and reporting processes.
Support the review and enhancement of local risk policies, procedures, EUC documentation and user manuals, including documentation for EWI, liquidity limits, LST, market risk reporting, RFR-linked submissions and ECL processes.
Assist with annual recalibration and methodology review processes for liquidity risk metrics, EWI thresholds, LST assumptions, local limits and other Financial Risk measures, including coordination with ALRMO, Head Office and first line stakeholders.
Identify opportunities to automate, streamline and strengthen recurring reports, tracking logs, confirmations and control processes while maintaining appropriate governance, documentation and change management.

Technical Skills

Excellent technical skills, including advanced Microsoft Excel capability with complex formulas, Power Query, pivot tables, data validation, reconciliations, financial modelling, VBA/macros and automation techniques used to streamline recurring risk reporting processes.
Strong knowledge of liquidity risk metrics and reporting, including Early Warning Indicators, Liquidity Stress Testing, liquidity limits, limit utilization, funds position, cash-flow analysis, contingency funding plan inputs, liquidity risk appetite measures, threshold recalibration and breach/escalation monitoring.
Strong knowledge of market risk metrics and analytics, including VaR, stress testing, DV01, sensitivity analysis, limit monitoring, market data validation, rate and spread movements, exposure drivers and recurring market risk reporting packages.
Strong knowledge of credit risk and ECL analytics, including IFRS 9 ECL, exposure and commitment utilization, portfolio concentration, industry and obligor analysis, facility data, credit exposure trends and credit risk appetite reporting.
Working knowledge of IRRBB concepts and tools, including interest rate sensitivity, earnings and economic value perspectives, repricing profile analysis, scenario-based impacts, assumptions review and coordination with regional or Head Office stakeholders on IRRBB methodology and tool development.
Ability to source, extract, reconcile and analyze data from multiple internal and external risk systems, Treasury and Middle Office files, Finance inputs, facility and commitment reports, shared-drive repositories, SharePoint sites and locally maintained EUC tools.
Advanced data analytics capability, including the ability to work with large and complex data sets, identify data quality issues, perform variance and trend analysis, reconcile outputs across systems, design repeatable controls, and convert raw data into meaningful risk insights and executive-level commentary.
Practical knowledge of AI-enabled productivity and analytics tools, with the ability to responsibly leverage AI to support data validation, report drafting, process documentation, variance investigation, coding assistance, workflow automation, knowledge management and management reporting, while maintaining appropriate human review, confidentiality and control standards.
Ability to identify and implement opportunities for automation, AI-assisted analysis and process improvement in recurring reports, EUC tools, tracking logs, confirmations, procedure manuals, management materials and control evidence repositories.
Experience preparing high-quality committee, management and audit materials, including metric dashboards, variance explanations, trend summaries, breach or exception commentary, methodology notes, procedure documentation and evidence packages.
Sound understanding of financial risk concepts, governance expectations and control requirements, including liquidity risk, market risk, credit risk, IFRS 9 ECL, IRRBB, risk appetite metrics, stress testing, concentration risk, EUC governance and risk measurement methodologies.

Experience & Abilities

Minimum of 3 years of banking, risk management, treasury, finance, audit, data analytics or related financial services experience; experience in a second line risk management function is preferred.
Demonstrated ability to prepare, analyze and explain recurring risk reports and supporting materials across liquidity risk, market risk, credit risk and IRRBB, including EWI, LST, liquidity limits, VaR, stress testing, DV01, sensitivity measures, ECL, commitment utilization, concentration, risk appetite and governance reporting.
Strong technical aptitude and curiosity, with a proven ability to learn new systems, adopt emerging technologies, use AI-enabled tools responsibly, and translate technical outputs into practical risk management conclusions.
Strong analytical, investigative and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify data issues, explain key drivers, assess materiality, reconcile outputs to source data, validate AI-assisted outputs and recommend practical control or reporting improvements.
Effective written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to draft concise commentary, document rationale, present results, and coordinate deliverables with stakeholders at different levels.
Ability to manage multiple recurring deadlines, maintain strong attention to detail, preserve accurate audit trails, and ensure technology-enabled improvements remain transparent, controlled and well documented.

Education & Training

University degree in finance, economics, mathematics, accounting, business, risk management, data analytics, computer science, information systems or a related discipline.
Post-graduate education, professional designation or progress toward a designation such as FRM, CFA, CPA, MBA, data analytics certification, AI-related training or equivalent risk/finance certification is considered beneficial.
Additional training in liquidity risk, market risk, credit risk, IFRS 9, regulatory reporting, data analytics, automation, responsible AI use, prompt engineering, model/EUC governance or technology risk controls is considered an asset.

jobs.title: AVP, Enterprise Digital Capabilities
jobs.description:
We are seeking a strategic, collaborative and product-minded leader to join our team as Assistant Vice President (AVP), Enterprise Digital Capabilities. This role is a key leader in Manulife's multi-year transformation to modernize and converge our digital ecosystem across Canada, the US, Asia and Global Wealth & Asset Management.

At the heart of this role is a simple objective: identify what is common across our digital experiences, build it once as an enterprise capability, and enable markets and segments to reuse and extend it to accelerate their own digital roadmaps.

Manulife has established a strong portfolio of reusable enterprise digital capabilities that support our Digital Storefront transformation and broader unification ambitions. The next opportunity is to expand and scale this portfolio to accelerate the unification strategies and roadmaps of our segments and advance One Manulife experiences across the enterprise. The AVP will lead this evolution – working across segments to identify where common capabilities can create the greatest incremental value, bringing together requirements to ensure capabilities are designed for enterprise reuse, defining adoption and rollout strategies, and establishing a federated model where capabilities can be developed globally or contributed by segments and scaled for broader enterprise benefit.

The AVP will own the strategy and evolution of this portfolio — identifying new opportunities for reuse, prioritizing investment, establishing strong product management disciplines, driving adoption, optimizing existing capabilities and ensuring that each enterprise investment continues to deliver measurable value.

A critical part of the role is leading the Common Capability Collective, bringing together digital and product leaders from across the enterprise to identify common needs, align roadmaps, determine where enterprise investment can eliminate duplication and accelerate delivery, and create a shared view of capability priorities.

This is an enablement role, not ownership of individual market or segment experiences. The AVP will partner closely with Digital Storefront and segment digital leaders to understand their roadmaps and determine how enterprise capabilities can help them deliver faster, with greater quality, consistency and efficiency.

The AVP will operate in a two-in-a-box partnership with a complementary Global Technology leader, jointly shaping the business and technology evolution of enterprise digital capabilities. Together, they will ensure capabilities are scalable, secure, reusable, well-integrated and designed for long-term enterprise value.

 Position Responsibilities 

 Enterprise Capability Strategy & Portfolio 

 Own the strategy, roadmap and ongoing evolution of Manulife's portfolio of reusable enterprise digital capabilities.
 Establish a clear view of the capabilities required to support digital convergence across markets, segments and channels.
 Continuously identify common business and customer needs that can be solved once and reused across the enterprise.
 Assess existing segment capabilities for opportunities to scale them globally rather than rebuilding equivalent solutions.
 Prioritize enterprise investment based on customer value, segment demand, reuse potential, strategic alignment and economic benefit.
 Maintain a multi-year capability roadmap aligned to Digital Storefront, segment roadmaps and Manulife's broader digital strategy.
 Ensure the portfolio remains focused and sustainable by rationalizing overlapping capabilities, technology and licenses where appropriate.

 Common Capability Collective & Federated Leadership 

 Lead the Common Capability Collective, bringing together Digital Storefront and product leaders from across the enterprise to jointly shape capability priorities and investment.
 Create transparency across segment roadmaps to identify shared needs, opportunities for reuse and potential duplication before investment occurs.
 Establish a federated model that enables capabilities to originate within segments where appropriate and subsequently evolve into reusable enterprise capabilities.
 Build alignment around enterprise standards and shared capabilities while preserving segment accountability for their own customer experiences and business outcomes.
 Create clear decision rights, funding principles, ownership models and governance for the creation and evolution of common capabilities.

 Product Management & Capability Evolution 

 Establish strong product management disciplines across the enterprise capability portfolio, including product vision, roadmaps, adoption, performance measurement and lifecycle management.
 Ensure every capability has clear customer and business outcomes, ownership, success measures and an evolution roadmap.
 Use segment feedback, performance data and emerging customer needs to continuously improve capabilities.
 Drive adoption and reuse across markets and segments, ensuring enterprise investments translate into meaningful acceleration of local roadmaps.
 Ensure capabilities are designed for extensibility so segments can meet differentiated market needs without unnecessarily duplicating core functionality.
 Manage capabilities through their full lifecycle, including investment, enhancement, optimization, consolidation and retirement.

 AI Enablement & Optimization 

 Establish an AI-by-default approach to the development and evolution of enterprise digital capabilities.
 Identify opportunities to embed AI directly into capabilities to improve customer experiences, decisioning, personalization and digital effectiveness.
 Apply AI and automation across the capability lifecycle to accelerate development, testing, implementation, operations and ongoing optimization.
 Partner with Technology and enterprise AI teams to identify emerging AI capabilities that can be productized and reused across the organization.
 Continuously evaluate opportunities to reduce manual effort, improve quality and accelerate time to market through AI-enabled capabilities and ways of working.

 Enterprise Integration & Technology Partnership 

 Co-lead the enterprise capability portfolio in close partnership with Global Technology through a two-in-a-box leadership model.
 Define business requirements and product priorities while partnering with Technology on architecture, engineering, security, scalability and technical lifecycle management.
 Ensure enterprise capabilities are designed to integrate effectively across Manulife's digital ecosystem and can be consumed by multiple platforms, markets and channels.
 Promote API-enabled, modular and reusable approaches that reduce point-to-point solutions and technology duplication.
 Ensure platform and technology decisions support long-term reuse, interoperability and enterprise scale.

 Business Value & Benefits Realization 

 Establish a clear value proposition and business case for enterprise digital capabilities and the overall portfolio.
 Quantify and track the value generated through reuse, including delivery acceleration, avoided duplicate investment, license consolidation, operational efficiency, improved customer experience and reduced ongoing support costs.
 Demonstrate how building once and reusing at scale compounds speed, quality and efficiency with every additional implementation.
 Partner with Global Marketing Strategy, FP&A, Technology and segment teams to track expected and realized benefits.
 Use adoption, utilization, performance and financial data to inform ongoing investment and portfolio decisions.

 Adoption & Enterprise Enablement 

 Partner with segment digital leaders to understand upcoming priorities and proactively identify enterprise capabilities that can accelerate their roadmaps.
 Establish clear onboarding, documentation, implementation patterns and support models that make enterprise capabilities easy for teams to adopt.
 Build awareness and understanding of available capabilities across the organization to increase reuse and prevent unnecessary reinvention.
 Create feedback loops with consuming teams so capabilities continue to evolve based on real implementation and customer needs.
 Champion a culture of reuse and enterprise thinking while recognizing the differentiated needs of individual markets and businesses.

 Required Qualifications 

 Bachelor's degree in Business, Digital, Technology, Marketing or a related discipline; MBA or master's degree preferred.
 10+ years of experience in digital product management, digital transformation, enterprise capabilities, platforms or related leadership roles.
 Demonstrated experience building and scaling reusable digital products, platforms or capabilities across a complex, federated organization.
 Strong understanding of modern digital ecosystems, including APIs, cloud platforms, identity, personalization, search, content, data, analytics, experimentation and customer experience technologies.
 Experience establishing product management disciplines and managing a portfolio of digital products or capabilities through their lifecycle.
 Demonstrated ability to identify opportunities for reuse, simplify complex technology landscapes and translate enterprise investment into measurable business value.
 Strong understanding of AI and automation and their application to digital products, customer experiences and delivery.
 Proven ability to influence and align senior stakeholders across business, marketing, product and technology organizations without relying solely on direct authority.
 Experience operating successfully in a global, federated environment with competing priorities and varying levels of digital maturity.
 Strong strategic, commercial and analytical skills, with the ability to connect technology and capability decisions to customer outcomes, delivery acceleration and financial value.
 Exceptional communication and leadership skills with the ability to translate complex digital concepts into clear business outcomes.

 What Success Looks Like 

Success in this role means Manulife increasingly builds once and benefits many times.

Segments are able to deliver their digital roadmaps faster because proven enterprise capabilities are readily available rather than repeatedly designed, procured and built. Capabilities originating in one part of Manulife can be scaled for the benefit of others. Duplicate technology and investment decline. Adoption and reuse increase. AI and automation continuously improve how capabilities are built, operated and consumed.

Over time, Manulife develops a growing portfolio of reusable digital capabilities that compounds the value of each investment — accelerating delivery, improving quality and customer experience, reducing duplication and creating sustainable enterprise-scale benefits.

 As part of our global team, we’ll support you in shaping the future you want to see.
 We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want. 
 We’ll recognize and support you in a flexible environment where well-being and inclusion are more than just words.

Job Role - Market Unit Leader – Financial Services | Data, Analytics & AI (Senior Director)

Job Location – Toronto, ON

Job type – Full-time

Choosing Capgemini means joining a company where you can shape your career, collaborate with talented colleagues across the globe, and help some of the world’s leading organizations unlock the value of technology.
We are looking for an accomplished Financial Services consulting and sales leader to drive the growth of our Data, Analytics and AI business across strategic Banking, Capital Markets, Wealth Management and Insurance clients.
This is a senior leadership opportunity for someone who combines deep Financial Services expertise, executive client relationships, consulting sales leadership and a strong understanding of Data & AI transformation. You will own strategic client growth, build and expand executive relationships, shape large-scale transformation opportunities, and work across Capgemini to bring the best of our Data, Analytics and AI capabilities to our clients.

What You’ll Lead

Own and drive the growth strategy for a Financial Services Data, Analytics and AI consulting portfolio.
Lead sales and account growth across named strategic Financial Services clients, with responsibility for large-scale consulting opportunities and engagements.
Build trusted relationships with C-suite executives, senior business leaders and technology decision-makers.
Identify, shape and convert new opportunities while expanding existing strategic engagements.
Act as a senior advisor to clients on their Data, Analytics, AI and digital transformation priorities.
Lead complex pursuits from opportunity identification through solutioning, executive presentations, commercials and closure.
Partner with solution, delivery, alliance and account teams to develop differentiated, outcome-driven propositions.
Lead commercial negotiations and the development of Statements of Work for strategic engagements.
Build senior-level relationships across the Financial Services ecosystem and strengthen Capgemini’s market presence.
Partner with staffing and Talent Acquisition teams to ensure successful fulfillment and delivery of critical client demand.
Provide leadership, mentorship and people care for consulting teams supporting the portfolio.

What We’re Looking For

We are looking for a proven leader with a combination of consulting, technology, Financial Services and business development experience, including:
Significant experience in IT services, consulting sales, sales enablement or account growth within Banking, Capital Markets, Wealth Management or Insurance.
Proven experience leading and closing IT consulting engagements with annual values exceeding $25M+.
Strong executive relationships and an established network within the Financial Services industry.
Deep understanding of one or more Financial Services domains, including:
Commercial Banking
Payments & Treasury

Cards

Capital Markets

Strong negotiation, communication and stakeholder-management capabilities.
Experience working successfully across global and multicultural organizations.
Prior technology delivery or program leadership experience is an advantage.
Bachelor’s degree required; MBA or equivalent advanced degree preferred.

Why This Role

This is more than a traditional sales position. It is an opportunity to shape a strategic Financial Services market, influence major client transformation agendas, build executive relationships and grow a significant Data & AI consulting business.
If you have built trusted relationships within Financial Services, led complex technology consulting pursuits, and know how to turn emerging technologies such as AI and Data into meaningful business outcomes, we would like to hear from you.

jobs.description:
If this post is up, we are still hiring—even if LinkedIn says applications are no longer accepted.

Position:
Director of Client Strategy
Type of Role:
Full time, remote anywhere in Canada
Reports To:
Managing Director
Compensation:
$115,000 - $130,000 CAD + performance pay
On Target Earnings (OTE):
>$150,000 CAD

About The Company BuildGood is a fundraising growth agency. We help nonprofits change the way they find new donors, retain them longer, and grow lifetime value, building a system that creates moments of generosity from first-time giver to legacy leaver.

Our approach is rooted in understanding why people give. Generosity grows when people feel motivated—when giving supports their identity, creates a sense of connection, and makes supporters feel competent and effective in their giving. We design fundraising systems around building donor motivation and leading first-time donors to become committed supporters.

We partner with nonprofits across North America to grow durable revenue, from donor acquisition and direct mail to digital fundraising, retention, and mid-level giving. Our work blends brand and direct response.

Is This Job For You? Do you get fired up about turning client relationships into long-term, high-impact partnerships?

Do you understand what it takes to grow fundraising and be responsible for revenue targets, and know
how to help others turn that understanding into stronger strategies and better results?

Are you energized by leading a team of Strategists and Account Managers, challenging their thinking, building their confidence, and helping them manage client relationships well?

Can you look at a client’s fundraising program, identify the biggest opportunities, and help your team build a clear plan for growth?

Are you comfortable leading important client conversations, addressing concerns directly, and making the case for renewing or expanding a partnership?

And do you want to build a high-performance client strategy function at a fundraising agency that’s genuinely changing how nonprofits grow?

We’re looking for someone who combines deep fundraising knowledge with strong account management and people leadership. You’ll lead the team that owns our client accounts, set the standard for strategy and client experience, and take responsibility for keeping and growing those partnerships.

What We Offer A workplace that values your need for autonomy, competence and connection
An entrepreneurial culture that places a premium on rigor and accountability
A teamwork environment built on both humour and challenging each other to continuously improve in our craft
Meaningful work that directly influences how organizations grow
Attendance at the Build Good Summit, Canada’s premiere fundraising conference
Work from home anywhere in Canada
4 weeks vacation
Summer Fridays (Fridays off in June, July, and August)
Generous professional development budget
Group Retirement Savings Plan (GRSP)
Flexible Spending Account (HSA)
Performance pay based on meeting goals and targets

What You’ll Do

You will own the strategy and execution for how our client team grows and protects BuildGood’s client portfolio. Your focus will be on client success, retention, renewals, expansion, and the profitability of each account—ensuring our work delivers measurable fundraising results, gives clients a clear reason to deepen their partnership with us, and generates a healthy profit for BuildGood.

You will set the direction for BuildGood’s client strategy function and lead the team responsible for putting it into practice. You’ll manage our Fundraising Strategists and Account Managers, set the standard for fundraising strategy and account management, and own all renewals and expansion across the client portfolio.

Every account will have a clear growth plan that connects the client’s fundraising goals with the work, investment, and decisions needed to achieve them. You’ll help your team build those plans, hold them accountable for progress, and ensure clients understand the value of our work and where the partnership can go next.

You’ll lead through your team while participating directly in strategic reviews, important client conversations, renewals, and escalations. You’ll work closely with the Managing Director, who provides commercial leadership and sets pricing, margin, and other business parameters.

Your main responsibilities:
Lead, coach, and develop BuildGood’s Fundraising Strategists and Account Managers through regular 1:1s, account reviews, clear performance expectations, and professional development.
Review and challenge the fundraising strategy across the client portfolio. Review and challenge recommendations to ensure they reflect donor insights, performance data, and the client’s goals.
Own and iterate the Total Fundraising Review & Revenue Roadmap, our flagship diagnostic, forecasting and planning process at the beginning of each new client relationship built on our Brand → Demand → Expand and Fundraising FlywheelTM IP.
Work closely with the Creative Director to ensure the work we deliver is outstanding—grounded in a strong fundraising strategy, built around donor insights, and executed with exceptional craft. Together, review key campaigns and deliverables, challenge work that falls short, and coach the team toward a consistently high standard.
Ensure every account has a documented growth plan covering fundraising priorities, measurable goals, recommended investment, renewal timing, relationship risks, and opportunities to expand the partnership.
Make annual planning and Quarterly Fundraising Reviews the foundation of account management, ensuring each review leads to clear recommendations, decisions, and next steps.
Hold the team accountable for executing account plans, monitoring results, and adjusting strategy when performance or circumstances change.
Own renewal planning and execution across the portfolio. Maintain a clear renewal calendar and forecast, prepare the team, and lead renewal conversations within the commercial parameters agreed with the Managing Director.
Identify and advance opportunities to expand client partnerships where additional BuildGood services or investment would help the client achieve its fundraising goals.
Monitor account health using fundraising performance, client feedback, engagement, and relationship strength. Act early when results, trust, or renewal prospects are at risk.
Serve as the senior escalation point for client challenges. Lead the response, coordinate the right people, communicate clearly with the client, and follow through to resolution.
Ensure client strategies, presentations, and reports are clear, credible, and useful. Help the team explain what happened, what it means, and what should happen next.
Partner with creative, data, digital, production, and project management leaders to ensure work follows the agreed strategy and meets client expectations.
Own the profitability of each client account. Monitor account revenue, delivery costs, scope, and resource use against agreed profit targets. Address scope creep and unprofitable work early, and work with the Managing Director on pricing, staffing, or scope changes needed to protect profit while delivering excellent client results.
Partner with the Managing Director to ensure commitments made during the sales process carry through into onboarding and account planning.
Hire and onboard members of the client strategy team, and build consistent practices that help the team deliver strong work with greater independence.
Establish regular client feedback and use it to improve account management, service quality, and the client experience.
Serve on BuildGood’s Leadership Team, participating in weekly leadership meetings and quarterly in-person sessions.

Skills & Experience Significant experience in nonprofit fundraising strategy, direct-response marketing, and fundraising agency account management, typically gained over 7 or more years.
At least 5 years of experience managing and developing a team, including setting expectations, coaching performance, hiring, and handling difficult conversations.
Deep knowledge of direct-response fundraising across disciplines and channels, with the ability to connect acquisition, retention, monthly, mid-level, and legacy giving into a coherent growth strategy.
Demonstrated success managing client relationships and leading account planning, renewals, and expansion.
Strong analytical judgment: you can interpret fundraising performance, identify the underlying issues, and turn findings into clear recommendations.
The ability to evaluate other people’s strategies and coach them toward stronger thinking and better work.
A consultative approach: you ask good questions, make complex information understandable, and present recommendations with confidence.
Credibility with senior nonprofit leaders and experience navigating concerns, competing priorities, and difficult client situations.
Commercial awareness: you understand how scope, pricing, and resource decisions affect account profitability.
Experience using CRM and project management tools to maintain visibility into account plans, commitments, risks, and renewal opportunities.
Significant agency experience is required.

The Hiring Process

Send an email to hr@buildgood.com
Subject Line: Application – Director of Client Strategy
In the email, briefly share why you want to work with BG, why it’s a good fit, and a link to a song that gets you excited about fundraising
If you have LinkedIn, include a link to your profile
Attach your resume (we’ll read it) and don’t attach a cover letter (we won’t read it)
In addition, fill out this screening form. If you haven’t filled out this form, we consider the application incomplete.

We can’t guarantee that we will get back to every single applicant. If you have not heard from us two weeks after you apply, please assume that you were not included in the final field of applicants.

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
Director of Finance — Landmark Full-Service Resort, Atlantic Canada
$100,000 CAD base + bonus program | Relocation required | Retained search

The step you've been waiting for:

You're the Assistant Director of Finance at a full-service hotel. You already run the close. You already build the forecast. You already answer the questions the DOF gets credit for. What you don't have is the title, the seat on the Executive Committee, and the mandate that comes with them.
This is that seat.
Our client — a celebrated, century-old full-service resort in Atlantic Canada, operated by one of the country's largest hotel owner-operators — has retained Global Hospitality to find its next Director of Finance. We are not screening for a lateral move. We are looking for a strong #2 ready to be the #1.
The property
Two hundred–plus keys. Multiple food and beverage outlets. Championship golf. A full conference centre and spa. A four-season resort with real complexity — the kind of P&L that makes a finance leader, not the kind that babysits one.
Ownership is midway through a substantial capital reinvestment: guestrooms, restaurants, public spaces, and a significant new wellness amenity that extends the property's year-round demand. You will not inherit a static budget. You will help underwrite, monitor, and post-audit the spend that reshapes this asset.
The role
Reporting directly to the General Manager and serving on the Executive Committee, you will own:
All accounting functions and internal controls
— accuracy, timeliness, and compliance across the balance sheet
Financial statements, forecasts, and annual budgets
— prepared, defended, and delivered on time
Capital project finance
— ROI modelling, critical-path budget tracking, post-completion audits
Leadership of Accounting, Purchasing, Receiving, and IT
— hiring, coaching, and developing the team
Strategic partnership with department heads
— translating numbers into decisions for leaders who don't speak finance
Audit readiness, brand reporting, permits, licences, contracts, and insurance compliance

Credit and receivables management
, chairing the bi-weekly credit meeting

What we're looking for:

Progressive financial leadership in full-service hotels or resorts
— this is non-negotiable. Multi-outlet F&B, banquet, and rooms exposure matters here.
Current Assistant DOF, Controller, or Assistant Controller at a full-service property, with team leadership experience
Command of hotel accounting: reconciliations, AP, AR, payroll, budgeting, forecasting
Strong systems proficiency and genuine analytical range
Impeccable integrity, sound judgment, and the discretion the role demands
CPA is an asset, not a requirement

Our client's most successful hires in this seat have been strong second-in-commands who committed to two to three years
and used the role as the platform it is.

The life:

This is a rural, coastal posting — and that is the point.
Picture a walkable seaside town: locally owned restaurants, working harbours, a beach with the warmest swimming in the region, whale watching offshore, and a commute measured in minutes rather than lanes of traffic. It is a place where a professional salary buys a materially better standard of living than it does in a major market, and where the resort is the centre of community life rather than one building among thousands.
It is also genuinely remote. We are candid about that with every candidate, and you should be candid with yourself. The people who thrive here want it — the quiet, the seasons, the space, the community. If that describes you or your family, few opportunities in Canadian hospitality offer more.

Housing:
Company-owned townhouse rentals are available to help you land — two-bedroom units at $1,550–$1,750 per month. Convenient, close, and one less thing to solve during relocation.
Compensation
$100,000 CAD base salary plus participation in the bonus program, with a full benefits package.
Apply in confidence
Global Hospitality is retained on this search. All inquiries are handled in strict confidence, and no information is shared with our client without your explicit permission.

Joshua Platz | Global Hospitality Search Consultants
joshua@globalhospitality.com

jobs.title: Director, Delivery Planning and Implementation Support
jobs.description:
Apply by:
Monday, November 9, 2026 11:59 pm EST

From strategy to implementation. From ideas to impact.

The Ministry of Education is seeking a strategic and collaborative leader to serve as Director, Delivery Planning and Implementation Support. This is a unique leadership opportunity to shape how the ministry translates priorities into action by ensuring effective delivery planning, implementation, evaluation and results/performance management for complex, high-profile initiatives. Working at the intersection of policy, strategy and execution, you will lead a branch responsible for helping transform new ideas into practical actions and measurable outcomes while providing the evidence, insights and accountability frameworks needed to support continuous improvement. As a trusted partner to senior leaders across the ministry, you will play a pivotal role in advancing government priorities and driving meaningful change across Ontario's education system.

A career in the Ontario Public Service is driven by a passion for creating a stronger Ontario.

We foster a diverse and inclusive workplace where employees have the resources and opportunities, they need to be fulfilled and inspired to move Ontario forward.

About the job

Reporting to the Assistant Deputy Minister, Strategic Policy and Planning Division, you will:
lead a team responsible for delivery planning, implementation support, evaluation and results/performance management for key ministry priorities and initiatives
work across the ministry to translate policy decisions into practical implementation plans, measurable outcomes and sustainable change
provide strategic advice to executives on implementation risks, delivery performance, evaluation findings and opportunities for course correction
establish evidence-based approaches to evaluate the effectiveness of education initiatives and inform continuous improvement and decision making
build strong partnerships with ministry leaders, stakeholders and partners to support successful implementation of government priorities and delivery of measurable change
champion collaboration, engagement, equity, inclusion, accessibility, excellence and employee well-being within the branch, division and ministry

What you bring to the team

Executive Leadership

You are seasoned people leader with expertise in:
strategic and team leadership influencing people, promoting improved program development and delivery
supporting learning, capacity building and innovation around common purpose, while fostering a culture of collaboration, inclusion, equity and excellence
demonstrating and building resiliency and flexibility while leading and motivating high-performing teams in a fast-paced, highly visible demanding environment
guiding teams through change, complexity and evolving strategic priorities while promoting employee wellbeing and engagement

Relationship Management and Political Acuity

You are an effective communicator, and consensus builder with proven abilities in:
fostering collaborative internal and external relationships to promote a seamless integration of program design and service delivery
demonstrating executive presence, influence and political acuity while delivering strategic and confidential advice to senior leaders, and when collaborating with internal and external stakeholders
working collaboratively with colleagues and stakeholders to advance shared priorities and manage complex issues
managing complex, politically sensitive issues within the context of multiple interests, with high public profile and scrutiny

Job Knowledge

You are an influential program leader with proven abilities in:
program implementation, including designing and executing logic models, theories of change and delivery plans that translate policy decisions into measurable outcomes
program evaluation methods, strategies and frameworks to assess effectiveness, generate evidence and support continuous improvement
results and performance measurement and management, including the development of indicators, outcomes, reporting frameworks and accountability mechanisms
using data, evidence and analytical insights to assess results, identify risks and inform strategic course corrections

Don't meet every qualification?

If you're excited to work for the Ontario Public Service but don't think you meet all the criteria, please still consider applying. We recognize no one person might have every qualification in this job ad, and you just might be the right candidate!

How we support diversity, inclusion and accessibility

We are building an inclusive workforce that reflects the communities we serve. We encourage everyone interested in working with us to apply, including people with disabilities, Indigenous, Black and racialized individuals, as well as people from all ethnicities, cultures, sexual orientations, gender identities and gender expressions.

Our hiring process is accessible, consistent with Ontario's Human Rights Code and the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, 2005. We are working to prevent and remove barriers in our hiring processes and can offer accommodation to address specific needs related to Code-protected grounds such as disability, family status and religion. For more information about accommodation during the hiring process please contact ExecutiveAccommodations@ontario.ca . All information discussed related to accommodation will be kept confidential.

jobs.description:
Location: Toronto- Hybrid (3 days onsite per week)

Yonge-Eglinton

Department: Finance

Status: Full-Time Permanent

Salary Range: $140,000-$150,000 annually

This role supports the healthcare brands across the FH Health portfolio (Pollin Fertility, Perennial and Wellness Haus). FH Health was founded by tech entrepreneurs to support Canada’s pandemic response with innovative healthcare solutions. We’ve since evolved into a leading health-tech company that transforms traditional clinic experiences by integrating diagnostics and care through technology. We are proud to support a portfolio of healthcare brands:

Pollin Fertility-A next-generation fertility centre revolutionizing patient experience, safety, and outcomes through advanced technology.
Perennial – Integrated primary and wellness care brought directly to retirement residences, improving seniors' health and quality of life.
Wellness Haus – A physician-led clinic blending evidence-based medicine with cutting-edge wellness care.

Learn more:
www.fhhealth.com
www.pollinfertility.com
www.perennialcare.ca

About the Role

We are seeking a strategic and hands-on Director of Finance to lead and scale our finance function and support the growth and expansion of the business. This role will serve as a key member of the leadership team, partnering closely with the executive team to drive financial performance, support growth initiatives, and shape the company’s long-term strategy. This role will also champion process improvements, automation, and the adoption of modern financial technologies, including AI-driven tools, to transform and elevate the finance function. The successful candidate will bring a forward-thinking, digitally savvy approach to optimizing workflows, enhancing reporting, and enabling smarter, faster decision-making.The ideal candidate is a designated CPA with strong analytical capabilities and a proven track record of building high-performing teams, optimizing financial operations, and enabling data-driven decision-making in a high-growth environment.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Leadership & Strategy
Act as a strategic advisor to the executive team on financial planning, growth, and expansion initiatives
Lead the development of long-term financial strategy aligned with corporate objectives
Translate business strategy into actionable financial plans and performance metrics
Support capital planning, fundraising, and investor relations as needed

Financial Planning & Analysis
Oversee budgeting, forecasting, and financial modeling across all business units
Review financial results and identify key drivers, risks, and opportunities
Develop insights on profitability levers, cost optimization, and revenue growth
Establish KPIs and dashboards to enable real-time, data-driven decision-making
Partner with operations and clinical leaders to align financial and business strategies

Financial Reporting & Controls
Oversee monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reporting processes
Ensure accuracy and integrity of financial statements in accordance with ASPE
Strengthen internal controls, policies, and financial governance frameworks
Lead audit processes, tax compliance, and coordination with external advisors
Accounting & Finance OperationsProvide oversight of day-to-day accounting operations, including A/R, A/P, payroll, inventory management and treasury
Drive process improvements, automation, and scalability across finance functions by leveraging modern technologies, including AI, to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and insight generation
Ensure compliance with regulatory, tax, and payroll requirements
Oversee financial operations across a multi-entity organizational structure

Team Leadership
Lead, mentor, and develop the finance team, fostering a culture of accountability and continuous improvement
Build and scale the finance function to support company growth and expansion
Promote cross-functional collaboration across departments
Act as a change agent to reimagine and modernize the finance function from the ground up, delivering strategic insights and building a nimble, high-impact team

Qualifications

CPA designation (required) in good standing
8–12+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including leadership roles
Experience in healthcare, technology, or high-growth environments
Strong background in financial planning & analysis, reporting, and operational finance
Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders and drive strategic initiatives
Experience with ERP systems (preferably Odoo) and financial reporting tools
Deep understanding of ASPE and IFRS standards
Exceptional analytical, communication, and leadership skills
Hands-on, adaptable, and comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment

Why Join FH Health (Perennial, Pollin and Wellness Haus)?

You’ll be joining a mission-driven, fast-growing organization that’s reimagining healthcare with innovation at its core. This is a unique opportunity to play a leadership role in shaping the financial future of a company making a meaningful impact on patients’ lives.

Apply Now

We look forward to learning more about you. If you're a strategic finance leader passionate about driving growth and innovation in healthcare, we encourage you to apply.

FH Health is an equal opportunity, affirmative action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.If you are an individual with a disability and require a reasonable accommodation to complete any part of the application process, or are limited in the ability or unable to access or use this online application process and need an alternative method for applying, you may contact careteam@perennialcare.ca for assistance.We thank all applicants in advance for their interest in this position, however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.
